55fd3e69d089025ea4159569c578bdbd1f313eb0.summary: backend/src/prompts.ts now trims oldContent and newContent during blockRegex parsing instead of during processFileBlock replacement. This prevents exact-match failures when diff blocks contain leading or trailing whitespace. src/project-files.ts updates the failure console.log message for clarity. musings.knowledge.md adds a documentation scraping use case.

e70163a8da801e05f0e15515be27fc7ec7fa81b6.text: The assistant now double-checks which files it is editing to prevent mistakes. This small internal update helps ensure changes are applied to the correct places.

5fceb4b0ecc20b0427785ac56bc33a937cb7b0dc.text: The system now waits for background tasks to finish before moving on. This helps catch and log errors more reliably. No visible change for users.

577e1c040c68dcbce71dc95d22c9bb6d5b3d014a.text: The assistant now asks your device for file contents only when it needs them, instead of loading everything at once. This makes the experience smoother and more responsive.

6aaacb83f0deaf00e1d48a0a9439d7db0b96a5e2.text: The tool now requires exact text matches to make changes. Minor formatting differences may prevent updates.

8fad941fdb5fb5178e1941254fd0f004758db45a.text: The assistant now knows to ask for documents and save new information when you correct it. This internal update helps the system learn from your feedback.

61b9683c28dea64cc30c796fae17563fef072e58.text: The AI assistant received clearer instructions on how to compare and update text. This small internal change helps it make more accurate edits automatically, without needing user input.

87039279e416c3fb0aaf2508c93640520f190f84.text: The assistant now reviews your previous conversation when creating code updates. This helps it make more accurate changes based on what you already discussed.

73828a089d30eb253a342e6962ea65ab33ecf8c4.text: Stopping an AI response now saves the partial text instead of discarding it.

9b4c3d5ac8f9c3c713c8f1ec132fd1010b14a866.text: Developers removed an outdated set of instructions from the assistant's internal setup. This small, behind-the-scenes cleanup helps the system run more smoothly but changes nothing for users.

81a382a67ebe7b8a223c6e3d0f92061c41cd24af.title: System prompt restructured with explicit recommendations
81a382a67ebe7b8a223c6e3d0f92061c41cd24af.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts restructures the project files section, replacing a dense paragraph with a bulleted Recommendations list. Adds guidance to batch-read multiple files in a single read_files call for request understanding. Scope limited to backend system prompt. The read-before-edit constraint remains, now isolated as a distinct bullet.

096d1a96d78558f81d5e4b0e43fc3b2bb33b8a15.title: Refactor knowledge system prompt structure and guidelines
096d1a96d78558f81d5e4b0e43fc3b2bb33b8a15.summary: Moved Knowledge section to end of system prompt in backend/src/system-prompt.ts. Expanded content types to include project mission and user intent, while adding explicit exclusions for verbose or redundant documentation. Updated guidelines to enforce conciseness, command verbs, and markdown usage for better agent performance.

b25cd0e15f031f492bb4523ec6895aafacc6ffef.title: System prompt instructs to update knowledge.md on user corrections
b25cd0e15f031f492bb4523ec6895aafacc6ffef.summary: Added instruction to `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` directing the agent to update `knowledge.md` files when users identify mistakes. This ensures recurring errors are documented as concise rules to prevent repetition. The change applies to the core system prompt logic.

82d0436228457243a2775ac34a323e046eb83c6b.title: ChatStorage generateChatId uses date-time format
82d0436228457243a2775ac34a323e046eb83c6b.summary: ChatStorage.generateChatId replaces random Date.now() base36 ID with ISO date-time string YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS plus random suffix. Improves chat file name readability and sorting. Internal storage mechanism change in src/chat-storage.ts. Existing random IDs remain valid.

3f43fe6515c06f08cd87f5f1f8f2373a8ce5523a.title: Clarify system prompt editing instructions
3f43fe6515c06f08cd87f5f1f8f2373a8ce5523a.summary: Updated <editing_instructions> in backend/src/system-prompt.ts to explicitly state that <file> blocks are applied automatically, removing the need for manual user copying. Added a constraint forbidding instructional comments like '// Add this line' in generated code, ensuring edits are direct and clean.

122ee89d87e5519937008129f0e0add084d67079.title: Add file-based debug logging and fix duplicate file processing
122ee89d87e5519937008129f0e0add084d67079.summary: New `backend/src/debug.ts` introduces `debugLog` and `clearDebugLog` for file-based logging to `debug.log`, gated by `DEBUG_MODE`. `backend/src/prompts.ts` uses a `processedFiles` Set to prevent duplicate `processFileBlock` calls for the same path. `backend/src/server.ts` clears the log on startup. `.gitignore` excludes `debug.log`. `musings.knowledge.md` documents edit/diff block issues.

331565164e8842901c5761a1dda5086e8dff01f8.title: ESC key stops generation in CLI
331565164e8842901c5761a1dda5086e8dff01f8.summary: Escape key interrupts active response generation in CLI. Sets raw mode stdin listener; checks `stopResponseRequested` flag in `sendUserInputAndAwaitResponse`. Prevents assistant message persistence on abort. Limited to `src/index.ts`.

93b51b725ff797219f3a6932d29f8e1e8ef023df.title: Refine indentation analysis in backend prompt
93b51b725ff797219f3a6932d29f8e1e8ef023df.summary: Updated `backend/src/prompts.ts` to require explicit analysis of indentation style (spaces/tabs), level size, and nesting depth instead of assuming fixed spacing. Instructions now emphasize exact character-for-character matching for `<old>` blocks, including empty lines, and mandate maintaining original indentation in `<new>` blocks. This internal refinement targets the backend prompt logic to improve string replacement accuracy.

cc5b0e70c3f3f370e8df9fa7b15bb414a674f9b7.title: Revert debug log expansion and file deduplication in prompts.ts
cc5b0e70c3f3f370e8df9fa7b15bb414a674f9b7.summary: Reverts experimental debug logging expansion in backend/src/prompts.ts, restoring standard indentation and removing verbose message length tracking. Disables automatic clearing of debug logs in backend/src/server.ts to preserve initial issue context. Removes processedFiles deduplication logic and uniqueChanges mapping, restoring direct file processing and raw change return.

5522df008b2f33b9591fd27e97d8565826f7c260.title: prompts.ts: Fallback file change record when diff empty
5522df008b2f33b9591fd27e97d8565826f7c260.summary: Added fallback logic in `processFileBlock` to push a change record with original content if `changes` array remains empty. Prevents silent omission of file state when regex-based diff detection yields no matches. Scope limited to `backend/src/prompts.ts`. Mechanism ensures `changes` always contains at least one entry for processed files, overriding subsequent `updatedContent === oldContent` check.

331565164e8842901c5761a1dda5086e8dff01f8.text: Pressing the Escape key now stops the assistant from generating a response. This change applies only to the command-line tool and does not affect other interfaces.

93b51b725ff797219f3a6932d29f8e1e8ef023df.text: The assistant now checks spacing and line breaks more carefully before editing text. This helps it keep your formatting exactly as you wrote it.

3f43fe6515c06f08cd87f5f1f8f2373a8ce5523a.text: The assistant now applies text edits automatically, so you do not need to copy changes yourself. It also avoids adding confusing notes inside the text, keeping the result clean.

81a382a67ebe7b8a223c6e3d0f92061c41cd24af.text: The assistant's internal instructions were updated to make it read multiple files at once. This helps it understand requests faster and more accurately.

096d1a96d78558f81d5e4b0e43fc3b2bb33b8a15.text: The assistant's internal instructions were updated to make it more direct and concise. This helps it follow your commands better and avoid unnecessary chatter.

82d0436228457243a2775ac34a323e046eb83c6b.text: Chat names now use the date and time instead of random letters. This makes them easier to read and sort.

122ee89d87e5519937008129f0e0add084d67079.text: The system now avoids processing the same file twice, which reduces errors. It also includes internal debugging tools to help staff track issues.

5522df008b2f33b9591fd27e97d8565826f7c260.text: A small internal fix ensures the system always records a file's current state, even if no changes are detected. This prevents missing information in the background.

7ef6008be01238433d0b1dac7904d18eb65a41e5.title: Refactor message schemas and disable file update user messages
7ef6008be01238433d0b1dac7904d18eb65a41e5.summary: Extracted `MessageContentObjectSchema` in `common/src/actions.ts` to simplify `MessageSchema` content union. In `src/index.ts`, commented out `addUserMessage` call triggered by file updates. Scope limited to core shared types and main entry logic. This temporarily suppresses automatic user message injection for file changes.

06993d11e296a7c4db9157eec76ee4a1bba3956e.title: Fix duplicate file updates in promptClaudeAndGetFileChanges
06993d11e296a7c4db9157eec76ee4a1bba3956e.summary: Moved `parseFileBlocks` call outside the `while` loop in `backend/src/prompts.ts`. Prevents redundant processing of tool results on each iteration. Adjusted `currentFileBlock` clearing logic inside the stream chunk loop. Added debug logging to `processFileBlock`.

11c333b428e1d271ff26c184562d3b7c7aef5ed8.title: Fix consecutive user messages in CLI chat
11c333b428e1d271ff26c184562d3b7c7aef5ed8.summary: Refactored `manicode` in `src/index.ts` to extract `addUserMessage` helper. Fixes bug where consecutive user inputs were not properly merged if previous message lacked string content type check. Ensures `messageHistory` correctly appends to last user message or pushes new one. Scope limited to CLI chat history logic.

2edfac49059f0f236e622e58f9ba59f67f9e5d16.title: ChatStorage persists sessions in .manicode/chats
2edfac49059f0f236e622e58f9ba59f67f9e5d16.summary: New `ChatStorage` class persists chat sessions as JSON files in `.manicode/chats`, replacing in-memory `messageHistory`. `src/index.ts` initializes storage per project root, creating chats with unique IDs and updating them on user/assistant messages. Added `.manicode` to `.gitignore` to exclude local chat data.

2dff45aa3a1ddd412902953aa8b97dcc418b81e4.title: musings.knowledge.md wish list
2dff45aa3a1ddd412902953aa8b97dcc418b81e4.summary: Added 'Wish list' section to musings.knowledge.md. Lists desired features: full terminal command access, arrow key message scrolling, and rigorous prompt testing suite. Internal documentation update only.

5fd3d84cf5204db3f6b4448086f22aa00225c9f1.title: Add file reading loop prevention to system prompt
5fd3d84cf5204db3f6b4448086f22aa00225c9f1.summary: Added 'Efficient File Reading and Analysis' section to `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to prevent agents from entering infinite loops by repeatedly reading the same files. Instructions now require checking conversation history for prior reads, planning file access logically, and summarizing gathered info before editing. Removed 'recently read' exception from edit pre-read rule in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` and deleted debug `console.log` from `backend/src/prompts.ts`.

d7253e2b83d450eab89dd2c8dc70a13689b8e930.title: Add knowledge conciseness guidelines and strict file diff error
d7253e2b83d450eab89dd2c8dc70a13689b8e930.summary: System prompt in backend/src/system-prompt.ts now enforces concise knowledge updates, integrating new info into existing sections rather than creating detailed minor-change sections. knowledge.md reflects this by stripping verbose descriptions from Main Components and Important Files. Backend prompts.ts replaces silent failure on missing file content with a thrown Error in processFileBlock, and reduces log noise by logging message counts instead of full payloads.

1e26174866393cc9c169f4d4d79c3214c2528fcb.title: backend start script use ts-node
1e26174866393cc9c169f4d4d79c3214c2528fcb.summary: backend/package.json start script now runs ts-node src/server.ts. Original node dist/server.js renamed to start-js. common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts sendAction now returns result of sendMessage. Prevents server restarts while websocket connected.

4b3edc7eee72aa55a274b36f9281093957978009.title: Rename assistant to Manny across system prompt, knowledge, and CLI
4b3edc7eee72aa55a274b36f9281093957978009.summary: System prompt, knowledge.md, and src/index.ts replace generic 'assistant' references with 'Manny'. backend/src/system-prompt.ts adds conditional read_files logic for recently read files. knowledge.md documents Claude AI as Manny's underlying engine. src/index.ts renames claudeResponse to mannyResponse and updates CLI prompts.

8b1c95d0741afd8a5a89608d2d8615889295a1d5.title: Agent persona named Manny; file-read loop guard
8b1c95d0741afd8a5a89608d2d8615889295a1d5.summary: System prompt in backend/src/system-prompt.ts names the agent 'Manny' and adds friendly/professional traits. Replaced verbose 'Efficient File Reading' section with concise <important_instruction> block forbidding re-reading files before editing. Adds 'or you have recently read the file already' exception to initial read requirement.

73b3e16cdc03da2402d2a3eed7e3bbec76b073f1.text: The free AI assistant now lets users choose how much effort it spends thinking before answering. This option applies only to the free tier and takes effect on the next message sent, without needing to restart the program.

cc2e698cf6c70dfad256e440be039d256a163222.text: The tool no longer allows linking a ChatGPT account to boost the AI's thinking power. If you used this link, the planning and review commands now run on the model you already selected, ignoring the extra account. You will notice the command to connect the account is gone, and the AI's reasoning stays on the standard service instead of switching to the linked one.

28663a3cb73ad6b81408aa9cf131a8edf1f1f5ba.text: The assistant now has a save-chat button that writes the whole conversation to a file, fixing the old limit where saving only worked for short chats. If you type /export, it creates a readable text file, or a raw data file if you name it with.json. The assistant also stopped rewriting its own memory after a short break, so it no longer forgets what you were just working on.

ce02985fc2dae21a5d6635d933952781273e3b33.text: Typing /copy now saves your entire chat history to your computer's clipboard so you can paste it elsewhere. If you connect from a remote server, the system will automatically trim large chunks of technical output to fit within strict size limits, but local connections copy the full conversation.

3dc7ec2306d94243ab2ba83ab457b59bcd4713c1.text: You can now manage your queued messages directly within the interface. By pressing Ctrl+Q, a dedicated screen opens where you can edit, reorder, or delete any messages waiting to be sent. This gives you full control over your message list before sending, replacing the previous need to manage the queue indirectly.

dc18d1a2063a92cc1939648a0280c0847a662c73.text: The app now includes a new command that shows how much memory the program is using and lists the process IDs for any running terminal tasks. This helps diagnose issues where background tasks might be stuck or not closing properly. Users will see this information appear in the chat when they type the new command.

175ea48e5f9acebbb528cd76425d4f268f0d947c.text: A new command lets users connect their own AI accounts by entering the name of a secret code stored on their computer. This feature is currently built but not active for general users yet. Once enabled, it allows people to use their own AI services without the app's usual login checks or ads.

4b2b9ba193f215d52fdda833622d4929ab3b2be8.text: The system now protects the assistant's most recent actions from being cut off when saving space. This ensures the AI does not forget what it just looked up or did, even if the conversation gets very long. You will notice the assistant stays focused on your current task instead of suddenly losing track of what it was doing.

385a99b3d9437720f257e7edf99fc5570dfe8fa1.text: A new 'pilot' version of an ad delivery method was added. It is not live yet; the code just prepares for it. When used, pilot offers will stay separate from main test results.

8ae0c9c1da31404dd515238cb4e196c13c2872fc.text: The system now detects when the AI assistant gets stuck repeating the same task list without making progress. After three repetitions, it nudges the assistant to move forward; after six, it stops the response to save your session limits. This applies specifically when using the GLM model.

1217a53754489ef6be6257b36a25fcd8d4edb110.text: Programs using this service can now be set up to let you move an ongoing conversation to a different AI provider, but only when you explicitly choose a new connection. This capability is built into the software's foundation but does nothing yet until an application enables it. You will not notice any change today.

b0ec8028c8fa97b1e285eb8739988689b8520e7d.text: The command list now checks names and short forms for both start-of-word and middle-of-word matches using one shared rule. This prevents duplicate suggestions and ensures consistent highlighting. The change is live for CLI users typing partial commands.

02e98eb553ef6474710195bcf76d8659282ce708.text: When you restart a session in the command-line tool, it now creates a unique identifier for that new conversation instead of reusing the previous one. This prevents the new chat history from overwriting the old one in your saved records. The change is active immediately for anyone using the tool.

44616e1e8cbc975b693b136b98b301ccc157d7d1.text: The price of the Solar Pro 4 model doubled from 5 to 10 starting September 14, 2026. This change is live and affects anyone using that specific model. You will notice the higher cost when checking your usage or receiving a bill.

72627b4a8b54f0f2fb08b872d0ad770891b87e24.text: The billing system now records exact hours used by paid subscribers, separate from full-day totals used for future cost estimates. This small update is active today but invisible to customers, as it only improves internal data accuracy for finance teams.

4897491493104492eafbdca91dfd2ccda3c00020.text: The test system now hides sensitive login keys in a temporary, private file instead of showing them in the project folder or command history. This change affects the automated checks that run against the live service. A person watching the test logs would simply see the checks pass without the secret keys being visible in the recorded steps.

98e174e577d764b45973ff8a4091cb3b3d6196d8.text: The free version of this coding assistant now lets you type a command to open a personal account page in your web browser. This page shows your daily activity history over the past year and your recent usage totals. If your computer cannot open a web browser automatically, the command will simply print the web address for you to copy and paste.

51e6c7bcf02623bda9cd8faa187aad7ffeaad37e.text: The system now has a standard way to organize data about how much it costs to serve paying subscribers, including current spending and future estimates. This change only sets up the internal structure for this information; it does not create any visible reports or dashboards for you to see yet. No new features are active today, so you will notice no changes to your subscription or billing.

0e7e3934db90c7866404ed431039233bc6f1a628.text: The command-line tool now checks for your project folder more carefully. If that folder is not ready yet, it shows the full file path instead of crashing. This makes the tool more stable while it is starting up.

990e923559d61a9fd04f94fc5f330ae24f0c8f97.text: The app now schedules daily credit resets based on your local time zone instead of a fixed Pacific time. If you travel or change your time zone, your next refill might arrive earlier or later than usual. You will see 'Updating balance...' instead of a countdown if the scheduled time has passed but the server hasn't confirmed the new balance yet.

1fe7bfe3bb89a5f39ce493861f57c861565e81ed.text: When you are blocked from starting a new chat session because you have reached your plan's limit, the system now tells you exactly how many chats you are allowed to run at the same time. This helps you understand why your request was refused instead of leaving you to guess. This improvement is live for users on plans with specific concurrency limits.

aa93519f568da1f67f76245d2f2c9e8724ad9ebb.text: The fee charged to accept sponsored compute offers is now adjustable via server configuration, replacing the fixed two-dollar price. This change is internal and affects only the backend setup for specific ad campaigns. Regular users will notice no difference unless the server setting is explicitly changed.

ebc17a50dc3d760f6d6eb023df4abc508e1dbd9f.text: The app can now show a yearly payment option for subscription plans. This change is in place but does nothing yet because the yearly payment setup is not finished. Once enabled, you will see a yearly price that refreshes your usage limits monthly.

dedd70d5414f7b9b98050623b74a4fa850669e1b.text: The assistant can now view images in your project directly, rather than seeing unreadable text. This works only if your setup allows local file access; otherwise, it behaves as before. Large images are rejected to save space.

a7ea9ca1fdbf59aea2aedd91b557f4416f19695b.text: This change sets up the internal plumbing to track a new ad display experiment. It currently does nothing visible to users, as the system is just ready to receive and check the data. Once the experiment actually starts, it will ensure that only properly formatted records are saved, preventing messy data from breaking the tracking system.

a8d0c1a83f4dc3677069dec06aca8a2aa3bdfb20.text: Solar Pro 4 is back to charging per use instead of being free, effective today as servers update. The discount from the provider continues, but the free promo ended. People using this model will see costs return.

a784cf2d81b03b3074f794fb5acdcfcb18ef35fd.text: The system now assigns people signing up for the shared subscription plan to see either monthly or yearly pricing, based on a fixed rule. This split is built and ready, but it does nothing yet until turned on. If active, a person would see one price option consistently, never the other.

5f024bab305902dc778d74b92756ae6c96cb42f4.text: New advertisers can now run up to $200 in unpaid ads before their service stops. If the bill reaches $100, the company begins asking for payment while the ads keep running. This change applies to new ad accounts using a saved card.

af898dcad679dbbd27389aef8a674cee31d58d43.text: The system now lets a saved task switch from the default service to your own personal account key exactly once. It blocks any attempt to switch back or change the key while the task is paused or resuming. This protects your data and billing from unexpected changes. Most people will not notice anything unless they try to alter the settings of an existing task.

4aa36c7b25c32bdc0605e5abfc8529e306dc4dd7.text: The app now recognizes three new spots for ads on iPhones. These include spaces after a message in the chat and coding tools. This setup is currently invisible to users and only tells the system where ads are allowed to appear.

bf468de5940335611a1669118edb2540e6618f6e.text: The wait time before a computer session ends increased from ten to fifteen minutes. This change also added invisible markers to help the system correctly identify specific browser tabs and repeated actions. These new markers are currently inactive and will only work once the rest of the system is updated to use them.

2570b57ebdbf98f703cd9515379d76615eb48e4a.text: The promotional banners shown in the desktop app now feature a cozy nighttime desk scene and emphasize flexible pricing instead of daily usage limits. This update is currently in place but does not appear live yet; existing users will continue to see the old banners until the campaign is refreshed.

f48d871ed62bc99da5c8486f58e5847750fcb2fd.text: The AI assistant behind chat now uses a different thinking model that reasons more deeply. This change is live today. Regular chat users might notice slightly more thoughtful responses, though the visible interface remains unchanged.

cc9069e251e8fedd5784c688ce78ccfecd76815f.text: The command-line tool now displays a specific web link for sponsored tasks, but only when the task explicitly requests it. You will see this link appear as plain text below the task description, allowing you to copy it directly. This change protects your agreement by keeping the main task text unchanged while adding the necessary link separately.

6bfe1fe6644c350a1d13259cd4141c316e57e1ac.text: When the server pauses new paid desktop sessions, the app now shows a clear message saying the pause is temporary and the assistant is working fine. This stops people from thinking the system is broken and switching to a different option. The update applies to desktop sessions and is live today.

4cb83e770ab4290df3813b4526fcd55978f5a323.text: People using sponsored tasks on Linux can now save their work without errors, because the system protects the project's history while allowing new entries. If a task is rejected, the screen shows a clear sentence explaining why, instead of confusing computer codes. These fixes are active today.

c8894546fb126b852322d188c60fd21efc9a0faa.text: Older desktop versions that could not resume paid time without charging again now show a clear update request instead of blaming the model. This applies only to desktop users on those older versions, and the new message is in place but does nothing until the desktop app reads it.

5f45bd81450eb50ba253ec315e067f798771d98a.text: Starting September 9, 2026, the Solar Pro 4 product price drops to zero Freebucks. This change affects only customers viewing this specific product. They will see the new free price and tagline immediately, while past prices remain recorded for accounting.

df46a33ebe7178f9f9a56740f859e846215f982d.text: Solar Pro 4 now sends requests to a different server route to help the provider debug issues. This change is live today. Users will not notice any difference in speed, cost, or output quality.

b816aed976efe357204d4878122710062c89ec89.text: The desktop app now tracks each usage claim as a one-time pass. If a claim expires or is used, the app must save a new pass before trying again. This prevents double-spending. The change is not live for users yet; it only prepares the data structures.

abd1eed4ab8de4111232935a21962b5a03ff5a33.text: Pressing a key to close the introductory message no longer accidentally starts a paid session. This fix affects new customers on paid plans who see the welcome card. Additionally, clicking on model options you cannot afford now displays a message about upgrading instead of doing nothing.

e9ebac6cb68071c635ef41d4d6807073a57b513c.text: The ad network now receives the real customer's internet address instead of the server's address. This helps Imprezia show and track ads correctly. The change is ready but does nothing until the main system starts sending the customer's address.

17106e2e4b02aee3ffa07db72fad3327df43b1b2.text: The command-line tool now ensures that if a session ends unexpectedly, it keeps the chat active so you can retry the refund process. This prevents losing credit for unused time due to network glitches. You will see a message on the landing screen confirming how many credits were returned to your wallet.

04578916f453fcab40ef1d5dac060e94ab126108.text: The command-line model picker now marks models that currently carry an extra charge with a small badge and a tooltip. The tooltip explains the extra amount, how long the busy-hour price lasts, and when the normal price returns, shown in the person's local time. People choosing a model during the priced window will see this instead of the old sentence under the model name.

3e63daca691768e95055f250f95cdf1404b251ad.text: The command-line tool no longer blocks you after a certain daily spending limit. Instead, it might briefly pause between requests to manage usage. The old 'monthly usage left' display is gone.

6e661ec6984d33a02c3a592348b160d68dacfee3.text: The text on the 'Earn' page changed to reflect a new reward system. Instead of mentioning levels or sessions, it now says 'Earn Freebucks · engage with a promoted post'. This update ensures the instructions match the current way to earn credits.

4972f1e7a75e6c7f2421c55040c0746c9e5d97da.text: A small fix ensures that users in specific countries or with certain account statuses are no longer incorrectly blocked from using their remaining free credits. If you had free credits but were told you had 'used all of today's free usage', you should be able to spend them now. This change is live.

c4093bf714387f3c5bda94d19d5181c0543054e1.text: The command-line tool now shows monthly waiting times in days, like '26 days,' instead of confusing hours like '622h 18m.' It also fixes a bug where hitting a spending limit displayed raw dollar amounts instead of the number of free sessions used. This affects free-tier users who hit their monthly or daily caps, making the reset timing and usage limits easier to read.

872fc2305848cdcdd0e5d4199e211b9f82831fe1.text: Advertisers can now see specific reasons when their ads fail to show due to location settings. Instead of a generic error, they will see whether their own country rules blocked a viewer or if the system could not determine the location. This helps them distinguish between intentional exclusions and technical placement failures.

253ee6c497c3d67371a7cddabfeacaebb19e308a.text: During free trial periods, using a promoted AI model no longer eats into a user's daily spending limit. This fixes a bug where the free model was still counting against the budget, causing users to get locked out of other tools. The change is live.

a4b3d0fa55c77663581617e15840fb467c110159.text: The system now handles highlighted words in sponsored headlines more strictly. If an advertiser marks more than one word for emphasis, the entire headline appears as plain text without any highlighting. This prevents confusing symbols from showing up in terminal-based views. Advertisers must now highlight only a single word to see the special formatting.

76a5696e5fdd93b9dc8dded8d2d0c8fac82937ab.text: The app now selects GLM 5.3 Flash by default instead of DeepSeek V4 Flash for new users, though previous choices remain unchanged. Limited-tier accounts keep DeepSeek V4 Flash because GLM requires earned credits. This update also fixed a display bug where GPT-5.6 Luna and Gemini 3.8 Flash incorrectly showed unavailable hours.

fb0ab0941b7c17b23b57e0d950f836d852c4d912.text: For accounts on the Freebucks pay-as-you-go meter, the command-line welcome screen now shows clearer labels for daily credits, wallet balance, and monthly dollar allowance, replacing old session-limit warnings. A bug that made the first-time intro reappear on every launch was fixed, so the intro now stays dismissed. These changes are live today.

6c846b9d1e27bda1da35cfbe900f062eefb7e2b2.text: Accounts on the pay-per-use plan now see a one-time welcome card and a balance meter in the command-line tool. The model list groups pay-per-use options together and sorts them by cost. The status bar shows remaining credits instead of a session count.

4ac0d8ab8584d5ada8c2f0bda35ab6b7c974e02f.text: Restricted accounts in unsupported regions or on VPN can now pick the deepest reasoning model. The text interface now shows remaining balance instead of a session count for models that cost money. This change is live today.

02ec3583806e4bf811825a7f7bc3a1082c4583d3.text: The product added full-screen and banner ads for a paid subscription plan. These ads will appear to Freebuff Pro customers after they finish a task or while they are typing, showing the plan's daily limit and monthly cost. The new images and text are ready to serve, but they do not appear today until the ads are turned on.

e8a3c7930b8024d099e2c2abf75ff582798a73c9.text: The GPT-5.6 Luna model is no longer locked behind a paid subscription for everyone. If you have a full-access account, you can now use it by spending your regular premium credits. However, limited-access accounts still cannot use it unless they have a specific paid plan.

e6c61f451394b49df437af776c496a0365474fd6.text: The command-line tool now shows the temporary free price for the Solar Pro 4 model during the Labor Day weekend promo. Users will see the cost drop to zero and the description update automatically when the promo starts and ends. The change applies to the model selection menu, keeping the displayed price accurate without needing a manual update.

b9d72aecc22730807ca4c2d450c9f9b1c0c6739b.text: This change adds hidden tracking to a specific type of sponsored ad, recording how long the close button stays disabled and whether that wait finished. It affects only the internal reporting system, so regular visitors will see no difference on the page. The new data lets the ad team see if the wait encourages clicks or just annoys people.

7d386183ac1fba92b91d0fd6116ed7f61dbacd6d.text: This update clarifies how the app displays the date for your next monthly reward. It now correctly shows this date even if you have scheduled a cancellation, as long as your plan is still active. If you cancel or your plan ends, any unspent monthly rewards remain available until the next period would have started, rather than disappearing immediately.

b8a55e9b61345917b0f8b470e4c02ab4f4956d4f.text: The system now defines a paid compute grant that requires a $2 acceptance fee and caps internal compute at $0.50, but it stays inactive until the server is configured. Separately, the software stopped writing secret access keys into error logs when lookups fail. Advertisers and operators see no visible change yet, while the logging fix quietly reduces the risk of credential leaks.

f3857f1b81fa3b21e59eba6564a47a8edb64c5f3.text: The system now has a safer way to explain blocked ad placements to advertisers, using approved plain reasons instead of internal test or allocation details. It also sets a $10.00 default maximum cost-per-click bid for self-serve advertisers, and a manager can only lower that ceiling. These rules are in place today, but no visible change is promised until the rest of the system starts using them.

d573b4d0977a99b5bea28768a03e3731c51343f5.text: A new measurement system is in place to test two different ways of showing Supabase ads to eligible users. It sorts people into groups and tracks their first interaction to ensure fair comparisons, but it does not change what ads appear today. This setup is ready for future analysis but currently has no visible effect on user experience.

7b211367021e612630a9c1040fea39abdc157e45.text: The AI assistant now strictly blocks its own ability to change files or run commands when you select 'Plan' mode. Previously, it could still accidentally edit your code despite instructions not to. You will notice the assistant only suggests changes and waits for you to approve them before doing any work.

8870810f21a3f99ee8e7f349bd10e1dce92488d2.text: People in limited regions using the website can now pick the cheapest chat model, which costs less than the other options they had. This change does not affect the mobile app or computer programs, which still show the same short list of choices. The premium model remains locked behind a paid plan, but it now appears as a locked option on the screen instead of being hidden completely.

219a700815b8cd4d3e19ae9761b2127a53a669e0.text: The system now checks if data reports are fully complete before saving them, preventing truncated information from being recorded as fact. It also uses a more secure method for verifying digital signatures and improves the speed of tracking user activity limits. These are internal reliability updates, so regular users will not notice any immediate changes to the interface.

f25d4059b88ff4bdca2e120522d0970fb8d2d103.text: The command-line tool now displays a monthly spending allowance for eligible accounts, showing the total limit, amount used, and remaining balance. This information appears only for accounts where the system supports monthly tracking, preventing confusion for legacy accounts. The displayed usage figures may lag by up to one hour behind real-time activity.

3160888e27f2fb25238fef56ff8e67b9d8d1f5ea.text: Test data for sponsored ads now includes a logo by default, while one specific 'failed' state keeps it blank to check both layouts. This helps developers ensure the ad cards display correctly, but it does not change what you see in the live app today.

9f81f91397709452f3b757a035fb9e93d0ab9454.text: Gemini 3.8 Flash is available again for free users after performance issues were fixed. The change also ensures paying subscribers have a daily limit on this model to prevent excessive costs. Free users can use the model normally, while subscribers will see a cap on how many times they can use it each day.

6470ff421860de64df4196f6891f11470625bce0.text: The ad system now tracks how long it takes for sponsored content to appear on a user's screen and assigns a unique ID to each viewing event to prevent double-counting. This affects the data collected by the ad service, allowing for more accurate performance reporting and deduplication of retry attempts. Users will not see any visual changes or interface updates.

7c5cc043fcad67cd82f362c61bc4c82cae553a78.text: Starting prices for Plus and Pro plans changed to offer larger discounts on more expensive tiers. Plus subscribers now see $6 off instead of $3, and Pro subscribers see $15 off instead of $3. This makes the first-month savings feel more meaningful for higher-priced plans.

7faa16471f65d093f3535980864182ff79dac50a.text: The consent prompt for sponsored tasks is now a single sentence instead of a long form. This change applies to the desktop application, so a user would see just the advertiser's name and one line of text asking for permission, with yes or no buttons.

6b1963707ad3659f9d2308535dff59f317cd8174.text: Sponsored proposals now omit 'Co-Authored-By' lines from their commits. This affects only sponsored proposals, keeping repository history clean. Users will see these commits lack the AI attribution trailer previously added by default. This feature is live today.

7bdce0946bbc83e804efd99fca98fa2d99b90e19.text: Solar Pro 4 is now available for limited access and costs no sessions for full access. Desktop users running GPT-5.6 or Gemini 3.8 can only open one tab at a time until a previous tab stops being used for 10 minutes. This prevents the system from mixing up which tab used the service.

d4ee9ca285c94e9348a7da806a9d2b7ecc69807b.text: The command-line tool can now show a small, expandable panel for sponsored content. This feature is live for eligible users, who can press a specific key combination to reveal more details about the ad. The panel automatically closes when a message is sent or when a full-screen overlay appears, and it will not open if the terminal window is too short to display it fully.

38b9fb0ffb5f0f14035dcf78969d153d7b0acfd8.text: For people using the command-line tool, accepting a sponsored task now opens a safety screen that asks for confirmation before running anything on their computer. If you press the wrong key, the task does not start, and you can back out without any changes being saved. This feature is live today but does not appear on Windows.

18eee2a9d4ab53dcf63a34e2a5b113f86b86f469.text: The system stopped showing a secondary dollar spending limit alongside your main Freebucks meter. This change affects users who see the Freebucks balance, removing a confusing number that made it look like dollars ran out first. You will notice a cleaner interface that only displays your actual Freebucks limit.

7b65652ad9decd202054622a7fbe267cc7c11201.text: Added tracking fields to record viewer location tier and decision-outbox status on every ad request, regardless of routing flags. This change is internal to the logging system and has no immediate effect on how ads are served or displayed to end users. It provides data for engineers to analyze traffic patterns and system behavior without altering the user experience.

9b16ec41446c36cc56ac43f225aa3b720d29d848.text: A hidden security check that stopped account data from being erased too early was removed. This internal cleanup affects only the system's background processes, so regular users will not notice any change in how the app works.

c6a7eae9e05dad4f07be5d34298dcecf93ed08bd.text: The system now records extra details about ad requests, like a unique tracking number and a fixed group assignment for each user. This change is for internal analysts measuring future ad experiments. Regular users will see no difference in the ads they receive today because these details are only saved for reporting, not used to choose which ads to show.

2cd4966460ec52724504da1424e2aaa7f56b6e95.text: The system now better recognizes specific ad breaks and distinguishes between those that interrupt content versus those that do not. This change helps ensure daily limits on disruptive ads are applied correctly, preventing interruptions for non-disruptive formats. These updates are currently in place but have not yet been activated for users.

60123cbaaa09113e6f314b9c877df53e41165095.text: The system now assigns a unique identifier to ad acceptance events based on the proposal number. This prevents duplicate records if the system retries a transaction. No visible change for users today.

ebb4deb34adc86dfaa1b4584d98edaf6db889f3d.text: This update fixes a delay when you cancel a task before it starts. Previously, if you stopped a request early, the system might keep waiting for the server to respond, ignoring your cancel command for a while. Now, the system stops immediately when you cancel, so the task ends right away without lingering.

8221e333895c0933b2ab58d669ac40272c339eb8.text: A hidden rule now prevents paid subscribers from spending past their daily limit, ensuring the subscription's cap is strictly enforced. The system also separates daily allowances from permanent balances, though this data structure is not yet visible to users.

892f79590b0dbbf4753d4f66051c8b3d8af7a3ce.text: The system now keeps a tally when it refuses to show an ad due to traffic limits or missing permissions. This record intentionally leaves out personal details like names or locations, so privacy stays protected. No one will see this change yet, as it only prepares the background logging structure for future analysis.

56dbe402f41689aa095fa05026ddd53037ff462d.text: The system now sets a one-day limit for how long a task started on your computer can report its status. This prevents stuck tasks from ignoring late updates, so a job that finishes after a long pause will still show the correct result. This rule is in place but does not change visible behavior until the next system update.

f27429b2728f0614353df3194a77b493d0444e18.text: The desktop app now admits it has not yet tested four advanced tasks involving real user actions, like opening a pull request. This change affects internal quality reports, not the app itself. You would notice nothing; it just stops the system from falsely claiming these features are fully verified.

6edee52fa9c4ab5511163f99269dd8613f0669f2.text: The software now uses your computer's built-in security tools to keep sponsored tasks safely separated from your main files. This protection is active immediately on Mac and Linux, but tasks are blocked on Windows. You will notice tasks running smoothly on supported systems without risking your personal data.

26a3a70dac0329050970baa5e1d585b22c8ada9a.text: The app's privacy notices now match the new policy effective September 2. Users see that agent traces are included in data used for the service, and that restricted partners may evaluate connected cloud repositories or code used with models labeled for AI training. The old pop-up banner is gone.

dd1d934b7418b612d453d52e5fc2091011923dbc.text: The standard AI model used by the command-line tool has switched to a faster, cheaper option for all users. If you previously chose the old default model, the tool will automatically move you to the new one, though you can still manually select the old model if you prefer deeper reasoning. This change is active immediately.

9b2ca33ed534768e4860d8b6949da3934abf2d81.text: Starting September 2, 2026, people who have already paid for a subscription will no longer see internal promotional messages about that subscription. This is a small internal adjustment, not a change to the advertising system itself. Paying for a subscription does not remove other ads from the service.

2a6cd7375ba0be59db222123a7294c0982ad0453.text: A small internal update lets the system share its current list of throwaway email addresses with other security tools. This list is used to block sign-ups from known disposable email providers. Nothing changes for you today; this just helps the system keep its spam filters up to date.

7f41c17658f1631e318a9aa7b0e4d9bd26ad58da.text: The app now shows a specific message if a local task cannot run because the desktop consent window is missing, directing users to open the app instead of claiming the operating system is unsupported. It also blocks file paths starting with a tilde (like ~/file) to prevent security boundary errors. These updates are live for users running local sponsored tasks.

3975224904d989f60ad8db9139bf51b7390e67c0.text: The terminal now shows cards for sponsored offers. You can accept, dismiss, or report them using specific text commands instead of keyboard shortcuts. This prevents typing in the main box from accidentally triggering card actions.

e47bf5c35bbc5397a02ad2dc1074907ad4fdf225.text: The company prepared a new slot for their own promotional ads, but it is currently switched off, so no customers will see any changes today. Once enabled, eligible users in specific regions might see these internal promotions before paid ads appear. The team added a tracking label to measure how often this new slot is available for each request.

c10a9f304bd1337ad48ef2b2294d38af5e460dab.text: The text shown to subscribers about their usage limits was updated to correctly say 'weekly' instead of '5-day'. This change ensures the displayed information matches the actual rules, which changed on August 31st. Subscribers will now see accurate wording when viewing their account details.

6a4ad1d04afdcc25bf6aea1e3503199ae65e39c3.text: The newer Muse Spark assistant option now appears in the browser-based free tier list, replacing the older version. Existing conversations using the old option finish normally, but new chats will use the updated assistant. This change applies only to the web interface, not the desktop or command-line tools.

f2ddf900349a34acf802d7645accc70840d0a4f3.text: The web search tool now has a 'deep research' mode for complex questions. Instead of showing a list of links, it sends a team of AI agents to read pages and write a cited summary. This costs money ($0.30–$2) and takes up to 6 minutes, so it is off by default and only used when specifically requested.

d227b0349fd05b02d6d5a0f0c628783996fbf89d.text: A new tracking field was added to record how email searches end for identity checks. This affects only internal data analysts monitoring specific ad conversions. Nothing changes for regular users, and the field does nothing yet until analytics tools read it.

5d679590800f31569758fe1002a5ef087668f7b7.text: The site switched the hidden thinking tool that helps answer questions on the free chat page to a cheaper system, saving thousands of dollars weekly. Regular visitors will see no change in how answers appear or load, though the underlying brain powering those detailed responses is now different. This update is live today.

a71de944590b9d02d5c182133e8c17de5e600db0.text: The GLM v5.3 flash model now defaults to its deepest thinking mode. Previously, it used a shallower mode that had stopped working properly, resulting in almost no reasoning. This affects anyone using this specific model in the command-line tool. They will notice the assistant takes longer to reply but provides much more thorough and logical answers.

48b5fee79a1016800772e01eafa8ceb3db346f98.text: Free daily use limits for accounts outside supported regions were restored to six sessions. This change is live and gives users in limited mode back the MiMo access they had before the recent cut. They will notice more free coding hours available each day.

3b8fa14a1010363bb909958213fa8beea9c31a30.text: The system now recognizes a specific digital tag that links a website banner click to a payment. This tag is only used when the payment is confirmed and verified, preventing fake click records. The underlying list of available AI models was cleaned up without changing which models are offered. This update is in place but has no visible effect on the user interface today.

a90d9c446543900a2ec75675fe03844a537ac3f1.text: The assistant now decides when to shorten long chat histories based on the specific model it is using. For most models, it waits one hour of inactivity and only shortens if the conversation is large enough to save meaningful space. For DeepSeek Flash, it shortens after just 15 minutes of inactivity, matching how quickly that model loses its memory cache.

01bf3cd467fb1a2700c866b3097fff745b3c0f5b.text: Free account holders now see three usage counters in the command-line tool: today, week, and month. This matches the layout paid subscribers already see. The change is visual only; the week and month numbers track usage but do not yet stop you from working if you go over them.

e1792f99509f9abc40904b9f4dad683d57510329.text: Ads now count as 'viewed' only if half their pixels stay visible for one full second while the app is active. Scrolling the ad out of view or switching apps resets the timer immediately, rather than pausing it. This ensures advertisers pay for actual views, not just ad placements, across web and desktop apps.

0d2d7a08594e7172e82d0f59a6a4c8a6bcc001b4.text: Solar Pro 4's daily one-use limit is lifted for Freebuff users. The AI now shares your regular premium allowance instead of locking you to a single chat. This change is live today.

321907165f73f9a66f780f275f38e27092f87aa9.text: The ad system can now show your own ads before the outside company's ads, but only for a small group of high-value customers. This feature is currently turned off, so nobody sees any change yet. When turned on, it replaces the outside company's ad with yours for a set percentage of requests.

70f1d8d632956affcf4ef483ae0c317dfd8d9403.text: The app now automatically sets this AI model to 'high' reasoning effort instead of leaving it blank, which previously caused it to get stuck in endless loops while performing complex tasks. This change applies only to people using the built-in service, not those connecting their own API keys. Most people will just notice the model stops repeating itself and finishes tasks correctly.

12f8f2bb5b72969b7114cec9f24ae47e7e5e4500.text: The tool now correctly counts text used in conversations, stopping it from double-counting saved information. This change affects how usage is displayed on your account page, showing accurate totals instead of inflated numbers for heavy users. You will see cleaner, easier-to-read figures for your token usage, with large numbers abbreviated (like '1.5M') for better visibility.

dcc6b662d492759a0776826bd0ee32e36480baa4.text: The daily spending limit for ad placements can now go up to $5,000 instead of $50. Advertisers building campaigns will see a wider range of choices on the budget slider, with finer adjustments available at lower amounts. This change is live and applies to all placement campaign builders.

7bcf9ba0b06d17819d238906d0d0436fa1eb432e.text: The system now has a shorter way to display time limits, such as showing '24 hrs' instead of '24 hours'. This change helps keep information tidy in smaller spaces on the screen, like lists or small cards, where longer words might make things look cramped. It is not active for customers yet; it is just a new option ready to be used later.

fcb16dec8af815505ae1dcc2d4f8be9c907fc814.text: A specific AI model is now restricted to one chat session per day. This change is live today and applies to users selecting this particular model. If you try to start a second session, the system will block it and display a notice that the model is experimental.

6341ef3af85281a213d98d6fab35e502e544dbd5.text: The system now automatically identifies where an ad should appear when the request itself is incomplete. This prevents ad clicks from failing and showing an error page instead of the advertiser's site. The fix applies to ads placed below the chat window and older command-line chat ads.

f3e97864f5d12d3df41f0bc10e08b5afd66dd101.text: The account status labels shown to users are now kept separate from the private rules that decide those labels. This change is live today. Users will not notice any difference in how the service works or looks.

091a224cd3b63af11dbded3dea62c726a669d112.text: A small internal update lets the evaluation system skip its own file-tracking step and rely on a safer external method, mainly affecting sponsored tests. It also blocks attempts to access files outside the designated project folder. This change is live for internal evaluations but invisible to regular users.

443f19f0eae03bcbc0dfb3ac6a5cd869fb9dcbae.text: Typing a skill name alone now opens a text box for adding instructions, matching the interview feature's behavior. Submitting blank runs the skill unchanged. The bottom bar shows live memory usage, and new messages queue correctly during active responses.

21d3b7668e7f43c2bcfbcd065b1915ae4329f6d3.text: If you invite friends or keep up a daily streak, you now get extra daily chats on the top-tier plan instead of a special model unlock. Lower-tier subscribers still see the old reward option in the banner. This is live today.

94eb1cfce38c1ccd0f91a5a7a1e66013863eabbb.text: The system gained rules to choose different ad sources based on a reader's country, but these rules are currently switched off. Nothing changes for readers today. When enabled later, people in specific regions will see bonus ads from the publisher's own inventory when paid ads run out.

c3521fd87fc4c8f683e73c08251772dc976ca8ec.text: The system now requires a specific digital signature before it will erase a user's account data. This signature acts as a strict permission slip, ensuring that deletion only happens after the advertising platform confirms the account was suppressed. This change is not live for users today; it is an internal safeguard currently being put in place.

f9b0815704eb34ebed2b8852b1a27c4902664d58.text: The system now tracks spending limits for free credits across daily, weekly, and monthly periods. This helps the command-line tool display accurate remaining balances and per-model prices to subscribed users. The update is live but currently serves as a data structure for the interface; users will see clearer budget information once the display logic fully integrates these new limits.

477b0e47facf165557cca9b60a070dacc3f6f9d9.text: This small fix helps paid subscribers who choose a premium model in the command-line tool. Before this update, the system sometimes forced these users back to a basic, limited model when starting a chat, ignoring their paid plan. Now, the tool respects the subscription status, so paid users see and use the premium model they selected.

fd3c20c290bf78152ecc86ab7ba9191f420ca1ea.text: The command-line assistant now starts with a different default model that gives deeper reasoning and no longer limits you to two sessions a day. This change is live for anyone using the free version. You would notice the new model listed first in the menu and the daily usage warning for it removed.

94288ad24bcefe362692ded7a3a8c692a503ff16.text: One fast AI model was removed from the free multi-tab premium list for desktop users. This model is now the cheapest option available, so running three tabs at once costs less than the models already on the list. Users will not see a change in price or speed, but the list now strictly follows the rule of only including models that are safe to run simultaneously without high cost.

d88c688727818ebcf7ce9bdcdcc18ba16d7946a2.text: A new safety rule for ad pricing is now in place. If an operator tries to set a custom minimum price per click that is invalid or zero, the system will automatically reject it and enforce the standard one-dollar floor. This protects advertisers from accidental under-billing and ensures consistent pricing across the platform.

8542dfe658589b2433a7d039b031d1e0eab1be07.text: Rules were added to cap how much credit advertisers can use before paying, limiting the window to 3-10 days and a $5,000 ceiling. These rules also require 14 days of account history and 3 successful payments before any credit increase. This is currently just a setup step; the limits do not affect advertisers until the system starts using these rules.

31e6e831630f42720b61aa08561daa941dbf4ed3.text: The system now counts usage tokens correctly by not double-counting saved information. Users checking their recent activity stats will see accurate totals instead of inflated numbers. This fix is live and affects how usage data is displayed.

a67e89052816db2de4de5bc42c4b6c318f91797a.text: Paid subscribers can now run more desktop applications at the same time, up to three high-quality models and eight standard ones. Free accounts keep their old limit of one high-quality and three standard sessions. This change is live and removes the previous restriction that accidentally kept paying customers to free-tier limits.

e5d41741aeca4ae11989042f2af1647b94c11e41.text: The deep-thinking assistant now offers three explicit levels of reasoning effort instead of a single hidden setting. Most users will see no change, as the default was set to the deepest option to match previous behavior. However, those who manually select the lowest level will notice the assistant stops showing its step-by-step thinking process entirely.

6ace1d00c9409518218bbf90225391e9002a5b21.text: Free ad campaigns now spread their daily budget across the whole day instead of dumping it all at once. This stops the ads from arriving in predictable hourly bursts, so the timing feels random rather than like a metronome. The change applies only to when ads are offered, ensuring that if you click an ad, your action is never rejected just because the timing looked suspicious.

1f35b8067456bba14e902e3018e6c41545b2a64e.text: The system can now record a limited set of numbers about how well ad choices work, without saving any private details or links. This affects only the internal reporting team and is not live today because the code that uses this new record type has not been connected yet.

4a9013b2a97bd2bade3e61b99f3deb7814094eb0.text: The system now tags external ad conversion reports with their source: 's2s' for secure server-to-server connections or 'client' for browser-based reports. This helps internal monitoring tools filter and route data correctly. The change is live but invisible to users; it only affects how engineers track and debug these reports.

8f390e940d2f9457ea52bca4567f727f0a049277.text: The system now automatically separates hidden planning notes from the final answer when they accidentally mix together. This helps people using certain third-party services that fail to sort these notes correctly. If you look at the chat, you will no longer see confusing tags or internal thoughts displayed as normal text.

72fffec8570aebd6a07ae1fce403fcdedee01dbd.text: The free tier now lets you use the GLM 5.3 Flash model without daily limits. This change is live and applies to standard free users, removing previous usage caps because this model costs less than others already allowed. You will notice you can use this specific AI model more frequently without hitting a stop.

3623ca3ffeb9e8ed71a65207075c1d4d18e639f3.text: The limit for ad variations per campaign increased from ten to twenty-five, allowing the system to test more headlines and descriptions simultaneously. Advertisers will notice their campaigns automatically selecting the most effective wording based on click-through data, without needing to manually approve each new variant.

cb3ef3135c27c68f08c1c3e92290607a08732afc.text: The daily limit on using GLM 5.3 Flash has been removed. Free plan users can now use this model as often as their overall allowance permits. Billing for this model now routes through a new gateway.

02f42768b0bc73acb01625d4d082a2f6f72d497e.text: Subscribers in restricted regions can now see and select the models included in their paid plan, instead of being forced back to the free option. The list of available models updates immediately when you open the selection menu, showing your paid choices alongside the free ones.

42989afa85b9d0c2cf43c220309ef9f05951d3bb.text: A fast AI assistant model is now available at all times, rather than only during off-peak hours. This change corrects a previous restriction that accidentally increased costs by forcing traffic to a more expensive alternative. Users who select this model will no longer see a 'paused' label during peak times and can use it continuously.

ec3142a4e62ca638acd914b68a3842d4e8c347f3.text: A small internal update lets the team swap in a fake connection when testing how the assistant responds to messages. This helps them catch bugs more easily before releasing fixes. Regular users won't see any change in how the app looks or works today.

590e6d257bf4128557f1e5823077c586bb424138.text: Ads that are winding down now spread deliveries evenly over every hour instead of letting quiet periods build up a burst of spending. This stops advertisers from wasting their budget in a single minute or at midnight, ensuring a smoother, more predictable pace. The change is live today.

2f4829e864d268f1cd6987537fd7956f6c67d0dc.text: The Freebuff subscription ad is now in place and does nothing yet. It appears when no other ad is available, showing a price pulled from the current subscription catalog to prevent mismatches with checkout. This change is internal and has no immediate effect on users.

f68e7ca5489c3652786a98440b44dc36b95d9176.text: The system can now gradually lower the daily ad limit for free campaigns over a set period, rather than dropping it all at once. This change is in the code but does nothing yet, as it has not been connected to any active campaigns. If used, advertisers would see their ad delivery slow down smoothly over several days instead of stopping abruptly.

0591414315966ad5f2442f39de7c0ca6a9478558.text: The default spending limit for advertisers who save a card was lowered from $250 to $100. This affects new postpaid accounts and limits how much they can spend on placements before paying. The change is live today.

9188c032117f7f2326e7bec8afb0a1bc62c33c1a.text: Ad placement rules now decide whether to show a user's own ads based on each request rather than the user's identity. This means the same person might see different ad sources at different times, depending on the specific request. The change is live and applies to all ad requests using this routing method.

bd5c18ff73257a748a3bd0e402e25af4c012649f.text: Paid accounts in restricted regions can now access GLM 5.3 Flash, fixing a bug where they paid for plans but received no access to the models those plans cover. Daily limits were also reduced to prevent the larger plan from being a pure linear buy over three smaller ones. This change is live.

38feaebb146a689d5dbf3a38b322e7db2e63f071.text: The company added a safety system to test which advertising partner earns the most money, but they kept the test switched off. This internal setup affects only the ads shown to people, and nothing will change for you today because the new rules do nothing until a human turns them on.

4ff202b7d262eb975b755a5da73965c661801cc6.text: The server now sends a direct link and message when you run out of free AI time. This helps you find the right upgrade page without guessing. You will also see your daily limit listed in hours instead of sessions.

47c4bf8cf7f311a30adfb47f4ca09d914cc3ce9a.text: Advertisers who save a credit card now get a $250 spending credit and face a $1 minimum price per click. If an account goes negative, the system automatically charges the saved card to pay it off, showing up as a 'payment' on the statement. These limits are live today.

adbcb4e4a515334bd3f46580fe8188ba3d27bf84.text: The referral bonus rules changed for advertisers. Previously, bonuses were matched in stages after $250 and $500 was spent. Now, the $500 bonus only unlocks after $100 is spent on a live, reviewed campaign.

b3e1d17c5a89e05ad7692f0dd70466a97851a3c7.text: The software now limits how many times it reports the same error to the analytics service. This prevents billing spikes if a program gets stuck repeating the same mistake. Users will not notice any change in how the program works, but the company will avoid paying for millions of duplicate error reports.

e30c58d37ea03426da0f01a727c5acff3895a462.text: If you pick a model that has been permanently removed from the free tier, the tool now shows a clear message saying it is gone and suggests a replacement. Before, it might have looked like the model was just busy or unavailable for an hour, causing you to waste time retrying a pick that will never work. This change is live for the command-line tool.

6f7cf660e827d750b278497432eebfa763ca58e5.text: The app can now show ads on the new-tab screen, not just in chat. The system checks the ad source's website address before requesting an ad, and if that address is wrong, the ad source blocks the request. Users might see an ad on the new-tab page if the account is enabled; if blocked, the page loads without an ad and no error message appears.

5c250334a319ef47c7ae2d5653ec7f062e1eead1.text: New rules for a launch promotion were added to the system, but the promotion is not live yet. Once active, advertisers who spend $250 or $500 will receive matching credits, and those who refer new advertisers will get $500 after the referred account spends $500. These promotional credits will expire after 60 days and cannot be used for other purchases.

9f0de8454bcac2ea8898d1f6592c488da4942f7b.text: Ads from Imprezia no longer show the ad network's name as the destination. This change is live for Imprezia ads. Users see no destination name under the ad, though clicking still works normally.

c359f63c20bbc0f7d23fb950af7764257b6ec274.text: When the service blocks a request because a model is busy, it now shows the exact time zone for the return window instead of guessing from the server's clock. This affects people using the command-line tool or checking support replies, who would notice the time labeled 'UTC' or their local zone. The change is live today.

cb53f476e75fa8151b31fc9ae263d0aa59281d5d.text: A new cancellation menu now asks subscribers to pick from a short list of reasons. The beta pricing warning is also standardized to show that leaving means losing a special three-times lower rate.

28d0514641dc8804ec29db0727c13bb9f2bc2ca1.text: Paid plans now add to free daily limits instead of replacing them. Subscribers see a combined total, so five free plus four paid equals nine sessions. The panel and model lists show matching numbers, including for accounts exempt from limits.

b11ec75a04ede2ef903e89bbe41fb5080514e102.text: The system now sends separate numbers for your free daily sessions, so your app can show them without accidentally counting them twice. This helps people on plans that include a daily free session allowance. You would see your free session count displayed more accurately in your usage dashboard.

907cda721501e4f656b82ef0bf61e19af07926ef.text: The command-line tool now remembers your account details when switching screens, so the usage panel stays visible instead of disappearing and reloading. This affects all active users of the tool. You will notice a smoother experience with fewer visual glitches when checking your remaining limits.

54790e3a6614fea67d6dabd01fd367fabb684dc8.text: The coding assistant now records a few private, summary statistics about your project's size and history when you use it. This information helps the team understand how the tool works across different projects, but it strictly prevents the recording of your actual code, file names, or project details. You will not notice any change in how the assistant behaves or what it shows you.

72f1310353bddeacfee88d760a6193527ff69dd2.text: Starter and Pro plan members can now use premium models for every daily session, rather than having a smaller limit than their total allowance. The confusing warning text about this restriction has been removed from the interface. This change is live today.

8238d829cad6ce2b95694de923e6e58c9a240e5d.text: The service now tracks a dollar limit for AI costs alongside the existing session limit. This applies to all paid plans. You will see a new spending cap on your plan details, but the system does not yet block you if you reach it.

a733b317c1e05ace5fe868e3d4f52d300dbd018c.text: Free access to the GLM 5.2 model now limits each person to one session per day, ending the previous unlimited referrals. This stops people from creating fake accounts to get excessive free time. In the command-line tool, the message that used to promise more daily sessions for inviting friends now disappears once that one-session limit is reached.

10218ba5aa9794a3327524cc1922daa9f3e39ce1.text: The app now shows specific hours when time-restricted models are open, helping you plan usage instead of just blocking access. A new system is ready to mark certain models as paid-only, but no models are currently assigned to it, so this part has no effect today. Free users see no change; paid users will see clearer availability times.

ed41bbe6cce57a22a3d03f3a69848063615c385c.text: The written guide for a specific data field was corrected to accurately describe what information it holds. This change affects the internal instructions for the system's communication layer. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the product behaves.

9066513a775a950c3c5f620141e41cd8ebfc76b3.text: Desktop tabs holding a chat slot now release it after ten minutes of inactivity, freeing the connection for other windows. This affects limited-tier accounts where one tab blocked access for an hour. You will notice the chat model picker becoming available again in other tabs without needing to close the idle window.

cb3ea78eda6ea14b43bc1624d0e854fdd9a898d0.text: The ad system now includes GitHub as a supported platform for engagement campaigns. Since starring a repository does not produce a shareable link like a comment does, users must submit a screenshot to prove they completed the action. This change is live and applies to anyone running GitHub ad campaigns.

81dc44a30b2de783596bce9e6c8192a674be6a23.text: Two new settings were added to the system's internal log to track how ads are paid for and if outside payments are allowed. These settings are currently inactive and do nothing yet. They are meant for internal teams to later record money-related rules without exposing private advertiser details.

dc2947f208c695a64f1781053d8afe1a3968a40a.text: This small update helps people using OpenRouter see the exact reason a chat response failed, rather than just a generic error. Instead of seeing 'Provider returned error', you will now see the specific message from the provider, such as why a request was refused. This change is live and affects only those using OpenRouter as their chat provider.

9043277365c41dd3d8c20f4d192b64d879823dce.text: The app stopped offering pre-written replies for sponsored posts. Users must now type their own comments. This prevents the feed from looking like a bot wrote it.

7a65d914646cc0f2883efcbc94971198e8064c16.text: The app fixed a mistake in the message shown when a free model is busy. Users who see a 'model unavailable' warning will now get the correct time when the model returns, instead of a confusing mix of office hours and the wrong time zone.

8d2fe1d276001824281f633df332852e67e82564.text: The service now blocks sign-ups from five specific email addresses known to be used by automated spam accounts. These addresses were identified because they send fake requests that real people never make. Ordinary users will notice no change, but anyone trying to register with these five email domains will be refused.

061b2465fb339069a9a7b09081c6125a5919a574.text: The command-line assistant now picks GPT-5.6 Luna as the starting choice for full-access plans, replacing DeepSeek V4 Flash. DeepSeek models pause during peak hours, so that model may become unavailable when traffic is highest. A hidden system update prepares for future subscription downgrades, but it does nothing yet.

836022e5e8a479b8330a80261070e80b636da639.text: Previously, adding a model to the weekly usage list accidentally restricted it to one open tab at a time, causing errors for many users. Now, the usage list and the tab limit list are separate, so models can be metered without losing multi-tab support. This fix is live today and prevents the 'Another tab is using the hosted model' error for affected accounts.

8bf398cd72689f7ca4bea6eb14ad7a7b162763ee.text: DeepSeek V4 Flash is now free to use without limits for full-access members, sharing this status with MiMo. Limited-tier members see no change, as their options remain the same. The updated notice confirms these two models no longer count against daily session caps.

0b60b7df7979a111f67629386bd2a64f36885060.text: The coding assistant now receives a short summary of a project's history, like the current branch and number of contributors, instead of the full list of every file change. This stops the assistant from crashing when it opens a very large project. The change is live and affects all projects the assistant analyzes.

989208414f3649ca01ab3b87500917770ddcf204.text: A new field was added to the ad logging system to track the outcome of the preceding Gravity attempt. This change is in place but does nothing yet, as no code reads this field. It will allow internal teams to observe recovered inventory without exposing campaign details.

1bbdc9e90d4becb32401d13293d9cbd7c9a5841c.text: A small internal update ensures that staff members and a specific test account always see ads from the company's own network. Regular users are unaffected, as their ad experiences remain based on standard random selection. This change is active immediately for the designated internal email addresses.

01b15151126e71919675bb0ab8972e1720377b12.text: The default AI model for new users has switched to a cheaper option to save money during peak hours. This change is live today. Users will notice the assistant uses a different model by default, which may respond slightly differently but costs less to run.

d9e94b083c24c9e1fa9655b0e55f5cdfc6506865.text: The limit that allowed only three conversations a day with one specific AI model has been removed, so it now shares the same daily allowance as other models. This change is live and affects anyone using that model, who will notice they can have more conversations before hitting their daily cap.

1a069f10a6dcb5116116520f285a565bc7e658ac.text: The system stopped checking a specific list of email addresses to decide who could see test advertisements. Now, a single setting controls whether these internal promotional ads appear in real apps. This change is live and affects only the partners managing the ad accounts, as they no longer need to manually add their email addresses to a list before testing.

4fa5ea05a929de13ec11d3f1a4549953efa6c09b.text: The ad management dashboard is now live for advertisers, showing real campaign data instead of fake placeholders. A new safety filter automatically removes hidden text tricks from ad copy to keep the display clean. The system now tries to show internal ads to 10% of users before selling space to outside networks.

41eb6446627cc703eeb8323efaf1e6477204a06d.text: The ad system now has a stricter gate for showing internal test ads to real people. Regular users will not notice any change, as the feature remains off by default. Only specific email addresses added to a private list can see these test ads, and only when they use a special link. This prevents accidental exposure of unfinished or promotional content to the general public.

4140a604bcff8120f0e60c1cd20258bdbb9e6cd0.text: The app stops showing a confusing '0 of 4' message for accounts with unlimited access. Instead, the text disappears entirely, so the screen correctly matches the 'unlimited' status. This fix is live today and affects only users whose accounts bypass standard usage limits.

79ca37b5008dc6dfe804a8b7bb002be7d4435abf.text: The command-line tool now shows longer wait times for quota resets, displaying days alongside hours instead of just hours and minutes. Internal cleanup of how the tool tracks nested tasks and formats command outputs makes the code clearer for developers, with no visible change to users. These updates are live in the latest version.

695d4d15676d9937d172ccf87909013085942be1.text: DeepSeek's higher-priced hours now only apply on weekdays. On Saturdays and Sundays, the cost stays at the lower rate all day. Subscribers who use DeepSeek will see this reflected in their billing.

ac2a035d604166a86390a7272dd56b60efd8a556.text: Free users now get the faster DeepSeek model by default instead of the deeper reasoning one. The advanced model is still available but limited to one session per day and unavailable during peak hours. The switch happens automatically, so free users see the faster model load first, while the advanced option remains accessible for occasional complex tasks.

2b718cc3be65d5704cf71390e398c989c1641b84.text: The ad system now tracks clicks and earnings more precisely, but this new reporting is currently switched off. Advertisers will not notice any changes yet. This update also prepares the system to handle specific ad placements on the desktop.

990ae116fee764e1daf72f0fda57880cf3d369b7.text: The daily limit for one-hour sessions with the premium DeepSeek V4 Pro model has been removed. This change is live today and affects users who select this specific model. Instead of being restricted to a single session per day, users can now use V4 Pro as often as their overall premium allowance permits, matching the usage rules for other premium models.

7895583a6c3216d4a977080028483c8b65fc9d3d.text: Ad spending limits now reset at midnight Pacific Time, matching when user quotas refresh. This prevents ads from running before daily funds are officially available. The change applies to advertisers and reporting systems, though it may not be visible immediately.

b2efafdc0d4a0bf860ea5dd9581c8d754a664087.text: The system now recognizes a new, restricted AI model that behaves differently from the standard version, preventing accidental mix-ups. This change affects only internal administrators and does not alter the experience for regular users.
