923de567621991a2f4d90fe7bcfcf4fd016a24ca.text: The system now allows specific technical details about ad loading times and success rates to be recorded for internal monitoring. This change affects only the engineering team's ability to track ad performance, not the ads themselves. Users will not notice any difference in how ads appear or function.

098dd053d11a6338dae3f4abd62996a0c18982aa.text: The tool that labels AI agents now uses a simple list instead of complex rules to find names. This change is internal and only affects how agents are labeled in the command-line interface. You will not notice any difference in your experience, as the names displayed remain the same.

5a504c380ad0497547ff88e63624d6101795cc92.text: The DeepSeek V4 Pro model is now available at all hours of the day, ending its previous pause during peak times. This change applies to all users and means the model will no longer automatically switch to a faster, less capable alternative when demand is high. The change is live today.

84c46ec290a6e544a29a30189b87a2fa1fa4ec90.text: The $60 Pro subscription plan is now hidden from the public catalog. This change is live today. New customers will no longer see the Pro option on the checkout page, though existing accounts remain unaffected.

95e94c20aecc773fd13da69de9eebff40f6436bb.text: Signed-in users are now randomly split into groups to test a new advertising partner. Those in the test group see ads from the new partner first, while others see the old partner first. This helps compare revenue between the two groups.

592d93f5d9e627a00fa4db4e1d1e8ca7662421a0.text: Two sample posts on the website now show their real view and share counts instead of leaving those numbers blank. This change is live today for anyone viewing the site. The data was manually copied from the social platform because it cannot be fetched automatically.

9d0e435b3802e4b6b833c1ed349d604e5b804f0d.text: A new coding assistant option is live today, but only for people using the service through a web browser or cloud interface. It is currently free and can handle very long conversations, but the company has set a strict spending limit to protect against unexpected charges if the price changes. Users of desktop software or command-line tools will not see this new option.

ed706ca47d476c9a68e7302b22b3c615dd522dd1.text: The tool now defaults to a different model for complex tasks, replacing the previous fast option. During busy hours, the fast model pauses and traffic automatically routes to the new default to prevent accidental switches to unlimited plans. You will notice the new model appears at the top of the selection list, and daily usage limits for another model have doubled.

0b697402591b23688e8fff0b8861d7b427190e2e.text: The ad banner on the landing screen now displays the advertiser's headline text. Previously, this text was hidden when a button label existed. The total height remains unchanged, but the description gets shorter to make room. This affects viewers of first-party ads.

2a3c3c791364d4f39c2c61d80162909cd199cd29.text: Freebuff now offers three paid plans that give you a set number of chat sessions each month. If you buy a plan, your session count changes to match that plan's allowance instead of the free tier limits. This affects only people who purchase a subscription; free users see no change today.

6c1591f8a5caf4b189e75bea718139d506c0b121.text: The default AI model switched to DeepSeek V4 Flash, and MiniMax M3 is now free to use without limits. GPT-5.6 Luna and DeepSeek V4 Pro now have daily usage caps, with V4 Pro restricted to off-peak hours. These changes are temporary measures to manage rising provider costs.

aefe67a7bd41d1b8cce4e53d39f9e22677aaf630.text: The model selection list now has a hidden setting to freeze its clock at a specific time. This helps test checks run reliably, stopping results from changing based on the time of day the tests happen. Normal users see no difference, as the list still updates in real time.

105640d21d124ff1dd6a7ccd7df06fffb9a5c34f.text: The assistant can now create accounts for outside services like databases or payment tools directly, skipping the need for you to visit a signup page. This only happens if you explicitly say yes to creating an account, and it applies to services that support this feature. If a service does not support it, the assistant will still give you the normal setup link.

b9ace3f9b2782eb321dd299ec9972689f3e08daa.text: A policy banner covering the bottom of marketing pages disappeared early on August 20. A new ad showcase section now displays exact likes and replies for specific posts, but omits repost and view counts because those numbers cannot be retrieved automatically.

3f3cb3851705ca43846d8a13c2c12a7ebfe94a38.text: Freebuff accounts no longer get a smaller daily spending limit during DeepSeek's peak pricing hours. This affects users who previously hit these reduced caps, meaning their standard allowance now applies at all times. The change is live today.

b4e5713b824dff395fcf7112cfc5ccae94429984.text: Approved advertisers can now publish ads immediately without a staff member checking each one first. Regular users will see ads appear faster, while staff must now manually spot-check the new listings instead of approving them one by one.

1e69baf9bf0ba91e9f693f1a6942e2b92c880783.text: The software now recognizes file paths written in a specific Linux-style format when running on Windows, converting them to the format Windows expects. This affects agents using Git Bash on Windows. If a file path starts with a single slash, the system translates it to a standard Windows drive path, ensuring files are found correctly. This change is live.

ffed5e29d2c86da974e22ca462675bb334d3212c.text: A small fix improves how the software creates new folders on Windows cloud systems. Previously, the program sometimes failed if the folder appeared slightly late. Now, it tries again briefly before giving up. This reduces random errors when saving files.

2e3e3f6691f3de16b7b0b5ddcb1612c553a382de.text: The cost of using standard AI models is now free, and the lowest possible score for your account is zero instead of a negative number. This change is live today. If you looked at your account, you would see that your score can no longer drop below zero, and using standard models no longer lowers your score.

b378f994a87f43adea2fa4fed651663f2b89b08e.text: Ads on the platform are currently free, but the system now stops any campaign from running longer than seven days. Advertisers will see a fixed end date appear when they create an ad, even if they did not pick one. This prevents anyone from leaving a free ad running forever.

08a8371fb064793ba00624c528e8738489aea268.text: Every message sent to the assistant now costs one point of trust, regardless of which model is used. Previously, standard models were free while premium ones cost more. This change makes spending predictable for users earning points through engagement, ensuring every interaction deducts a single point.

9311890b70d198454df8e25b72df2d064854dc48.text: The model picker now shows a countdown for DeepSeek V4 Pro during peak hours. Previously, the option just greyed out with no explanation. You will see exactly when the model becomes available in your local time.

8c034b5f9242c0bb48b8021f96eeb2e159096d16.text: The system now rejects links to the ad post itself when checking for proof of engagement. This stops people from bypassing the requirement to actually comment on the post. Users trying to submit the post's own link will now see an error asking for the specific link to their comment.

7b1bde13e85e50fb7f0ca7675ebf8c29788ec464.text: The model picker now shows separate usage counts for models with stricter daily limits, preventing misleading headers. This affects premium users selecting DeepSeek models in the command-line interface. You will see the correct remaining uses for each model instead of a single shared count.

7dcb4fb1e09cbd72bb0d86409739ff616bc6d472.text: The system now limits each person to five new web projects per day and allows only two active sandboxes running at once. These caps apply everywhere and take effect immediately. Most people will not notice any difference because the limits are set higher than typical usage, but they prevent a few heavy users from filling up the shared computing space.

b5111f885a8e3b737cffff102f353444ea860ada.text: The ad system now correctly marks posts that a human reviewer has flagged as blocked, fixing a bug where these posts would not display their status to advertisers. New data is also in place to show real examples of boosted posts and view count ranges on the advertiser landing page, but this showcase feature does not appear to the public yet.

1470aa4e189c2d0347843109e5ec86dbab395402.text: The database health alerts previously stopped running if the system lacked certain permissions, leaving a blind spot for a month. Now, the alerts always run and report how much of the database activity they could not see. This change is live today and ensures operators get visibility into potential issues instead of a misleading 'all clear' signal.

e73d39fff1ab55bc2c2615d60efd7129afa5c7fc.text: The command-line tool now points to the faster-paying 'Trust' feed instead of the slower referral page. This helps rate-limited users earn more sessions quickly. You will see a single, consistent message across all apps inviting you to 'Earn Trust for more sessions.'.

187b1e916c06bd3ab87208ac647577fb4b9f6b03.text: The ad pricing rules were clarified to ensure advertisers are billed a fixed daily subscription rate rather than a variable cost per interaction. Advertisers will see their dashboard display a set daily fee and a maximum number of engagements, instead of calculating charges based on actual activity.

ba0e40bacf53a1ffa8dfcf0db6ab7b0da43b139a.text: The command-line tool now sends a browser-like identity to ad networks instead of a server label, matching what was sent during the ad auction. This prevents ad networks from flagging your impressions as suspicious bot traffic. You will not notice any visual changes; this is a small internal fix that ensures ads are counted correctly.

24de8d9513fd0584a4a18a73f3d3ca5e7e54a1bf.text: The ad submission form now accepts website links without the 'https://' prefix. Previously, pasting a link like 'x.com/profile' caused the submit button to do nothing or show a confusing error. This fix lets advertisers sign up successfully using plain links, matching how people typically copy and paste web addresses.

8da51dc0eaecae13822690e91ea90a9038bd9dc6.text: Freebuff replaced the default model for limited-access users with MiMo 2.5, because DeepSeek V4 Flash was paused due to upstream pricing changes. This affects only users in restricted regions or those using VPNs, who will now see MiMo 2.5 as their automatic choice when starting a session. Full-access users continue using DeepSeek V4 Flash without any change.

89832d9b3ade452149cf8e9658bd4537107fc5e7.text: The system now checks if a user's plan includes DeepSeek models before applying peak-hour spending limits. This change affects users on limited plans who only use other models like MiMo 2.5. They will notice their spending caps remain normal during peak hours, as those restrictions no longer apply to them.

d20038cb58001e360bbcfb30960817b202e8993a.text: The spending dashboard now separates model creators from bill payers. This prevents costs from being incorrectly attributed to the wrong company. The change is in place but does nothing yet.

5f72959fab4202f5b667112c914282bcc195fb9b.text: The command-line tool now estimates message length locally instead of waiting for a remote service, which speeds up each step. It also safely includes your personal saved instructions from your home folder, ensuring the tool sees them just like its own list does. These updates are live for command-line users.

cef358330ebed218abe3c1d8df88a8d4bb8315db.text: Fixed a billing glitch for free-tier users. When the system swapped in a cheaper AI model, it mistakenly charged credits to accounts with zero balance. Now, these automatic swaps correctly remain free, preventing errors.

7129d45870e6486850aca5729015b555653ca7d1.text: Freebuff changed how many free chat sessions people get each day. Premium users now start with four instead of five, while users in limited regions start with three instead of six, but everyone can earn up to seven sessions by completing tasks like engaging with ads. Advertisers can also now buy daily campaigns starting at ten dollars, with each user interaction costing fifty cents.

695a52ed5a16bd3c3482682e2f84b29ac47c5190.text: The system now strictly limits spending for accounts flagged as high-risk, capping them at twice their daily allowance. Previously, these accounts could exceed their limit by finishing an already-open session; now, new requests are blocked once the hard cap is reached. Regular accounts and internal users remain unaffected.

eb2eb5ec4b15f2b31cee2ff7c6870aef398526aa.text: The option to send activity data to a custom address is gone. Only the standard, pre-set location for this data now works. If you previously used a custom address, your data will no longer reach it.

2d370c194f127b56a4273462587f7589a557b834.text: The system now waits for all background tasks to finish before sending attached images. This prevents errors that could freeze chat threads when multiple actions happen at once. Users will experience smoother conversations with media attachments.

6c49e12dc09c72d510ee13940ea543ef19b418e5.text: Free desktop users previously saw 'out of credits' errors that stopped the app from choosing its next action. This update allows the automatic decision-making feature to work correctly for them without using up their allowance. Users will notice their tasks continuing smoothly instead of halting unexpectedly.

2fa82f2e26c68a2e750dcdd3515855e661d05577.text: The team moved the rules for counting days into one shared spot. This affects the reports that track ad income and free credit spending. Without this, those reports might accidentally miss or double-count transactions made right at the end of the day.

ae35b542f1b2cc0e6e455ef9effa1cdb9ad4c818.text: Singapore users can now spend up to $5 a day for free, up from 50 cents. This change went live today. If you are in Singapore, you will notice you can use the service more before hitting a daily limit, because the system now blocks specific spam email addresses instead of restricting everyone in the country.

192cb715a3ae26a1deee15731d0ddd86560fe262.text: The desktop app now records when a user clicks the sign-in button, not just when they finish. This helps the team see if people try to log in but fail, without guessing from incomplete data. Nothing changes for you yet; this is just a background measurement tool.

f97ca5511b01eba2552e9be7d7332194f5118ca3.text: The system stopped charging a penalty for email addresses from major privacy providers like Proton and Apple. If you use one of these addresses, your account is no longer treated as a suspicious bot farm. This change is live today.

ad5d3005fb7f08e572e6fe8323303b26497795e1.text: This is a small internal update that adds two new tracking points for the desktop app. It helps the team measure how often old conversations are automatically archived and how often message delivery issues change status. Users won't see anything new, but the team can now better understand these background processes to improve stability.

6eb9bf8e4038d432a370d0186b0d124fe912fabe.text: The system now cleans up its saved memory before pausing. If a task was started but not finished when the pause happened, that incomplete step is removed. This prevents the system from getting confused when it restarts, so it can pick up right where it left off.

cef314aab409b9198cc4f5665e4a52da528c4eb4.text: The command line tool now points directly to the referral status page instead of the general earnings dashboard. The button label changed to "Open referral status" to match the new destination. This update is live and helps people find their referral details faster.

190ac96c3428bfbd1ea3ffbdeaf77659f088a902.text: The copy command now falls back to a size-limited method when standard clipboard tools are missing, preventing silent failures. It also cancels old copy attempts when new text is selected to avoid restoring stale data. If a background process hangs, it is forcibly stopped to keep the interface responsive.

43db7ec34405a23491b376662bf243226a136619.text: The system stopped using an internal tool that checked if database requests were taking too long. This change is for the engineering team, not the customers. People using the app will not see any difference, because this was just a cleanup of the background code that watches performance.

871d75810e6732f65067d4bd6faec927c529332d.text: Free accounts now have a daily spending limit based on their region and account details, replacing a flat fifty-dollar cap. Users in restricted countries or with disposable email addresses will hit this lower limit faster, stopping new sessions from starting once reached. This change is live and aims to curb abuse without banning honest users.

80bc9c895dd73f9996ae18af67432e9ae1b09181.text: The system now removes incomplete action requests from chat history before sending it to the AI, preventing errors when resuming old conversations. This change is active in the background for all users interacting with the AI assistant. You likely won't notice a visual difference, but the assistant will be more stable and less likely to get stuck or crash after an interrupted task.

7c219be7ef6d60e088fcfa9fcd566a798153d57b.text: The system now gives specific reasons for limited access to accounts flagged for VPNs, certain locations, or suspicious email domains. Affected users will see a message telling them to turn off their VPN to restore normal limits, rather than a generic capacity error. This change is live and applies only to these specific flagged groups.

5db7a544be7c5ec414b833a4cb295fa8511b1b8c.text: Accounts with very small spending limits now face a stricter cutoff. If a user from a restricted country or a flagged email domain spends more than twice their allowed limit, the assistant stops responding mid-task to prevent excessive costs. This change is live today.

c0e5740f4ee47c3c7dd3fe6f890b2fc5b26b34d7.text: A background update fixes how the system reads images sent to AI models, specifically handling a new format for image data. This affects users who upload pictures in chats, ensuring those images are correctly understood by the AI. It is live now. Most users won't notice a change, but it prevents errors when sending images through certain AI providers.

603b0d994dece07838c774cb022529dee7a28f1d.text: When you use the keyboard to select the dashboard link, it now highlights in a bold color instead of adding a symbol that pushed text around. This stops the button from visually overlapping the 'Copy invite link' text next to it. The daily streak dots also changed back to clearly filled and hollow circles, so you can instantly see which days you've completed.

a801ecf452f6262853055d6aafb484bf3a74ec3c.text: The label for the GPT-5.6 Luna option changed from 'Balanced' to 'Strong all-around'. This affects only the text shown when choosing a model in the command-line tool. Users will see the new description immediately.

0029f0a29f01837307120b1212694ffaa2899474.text: Free accounts using privacy tools like VPNs now get a lower daily spending limit of fifty cents. This change applies only when starting a new session, so users on these networks will notice they cannot open a second session after using up that small amount until the next day. Regular users without these privacy tools are unaffected.

c7ddc18ceedc4938f6df6f859c14e98de8ad0562.text: The model selection menu now lists the most capable option first, matching the default choice. This applies to people using the full-access version. They will see the recommended model at the top of the list instead of the faster, simpler one.

d9ee7bfc3e52b9156522bc86250fc7376f9fe955.text: The command-line app now recommends the stronger AI model by default for people with full access. If that model’s daily allowance runs out, the app automatically switches to the always-available fast model so a conversation can still start. People may notice the main suggestion and its label change, while limited-access users keep the fast model as their default.

e43fdc88870d851ec92b669dbba00bd5ffe17d0d.text: When the main assistant is busy, it now automatically switches to a different, stronger model instead of the previous one. This change is live today and affects web, cloud, and chat users. You would notice that if an image is sent during this switch, the system still understands it, even though the new model cannot see images directly, because the system describes the image to it first.

0d865059f023cea0d49fd9dce302ed1762f196c8.text: The sign-up form now demands an answer to every question, removing the old ability to skip parts. If the system fails to save your answers, a temporary safety net lets you leave the page to avoid a frustrating loop. This safety net lasts only one day, so it helps during short glitches but does not allow skipping the form when everything works.

fe30ebff1d8856788874e037cf2b741f95b6ead3.text: New accounts must finish a quick setup form before using the free tier. If you skip it, the command-line tool now stops with a clear message telling you to complete the form on the website, rather than showing a confusing retry countdown. This rule applies only to accounts created after a specific start date; older accounts remain unaffected.

bab9f2907dff6c3f090b3ba645f64c91e95e997e.text: The sign-up questionnaire changed. New users now see a question about paid subscriptions, and the 'Where did you hear about us?' list combines Instagram and TikTok into one option while removing Discord and blogs. The coding experience question now uses a slider instead of a list of choices. These changes affect the questions people answer when they first create an account.

a5b6b0cf4ef9fbf7f6cf529e803601f243cd1b0f.text: Freebuff Web users in outer regions can now create up to ten new projects per day, up from three or five. This change stops people from getting locked out after a few setup errors, since failed attempts no longer count against the daily total. Only the number of projects you can start changes; you still can only run one assistant at a time.

b07e38d987cc4aa41a1c0fea1a2502a462f0f50f.text: The text tool no longer stops you from sending messages if you haven't answered initial setup questions. Instead, the website now shows a simple pop-up form once when you log in, which you can safely ignore. This change affects all free accounts, making it easier to start working without being blocked by mandatory questions.

a0a9a4c80ae8b8aba38b449aa29ad9e214633c43.text: The system now knows about three new AI models (DeepSeek Pro Max, DeepSeek Flash Max, and Luna Max) that can handle very long conversations. These models are not visible in the standard menus or lists for most accounts. Only accounts that have been specifically set up to use these models can request them directly by name; others will not see them as options.

364433c460916d2de22bf35956dfa0f9f5e8edff.text: The list of available thinking levels now includes a 'minimal' option. This change only updates the internal settings menu; you will not see this new option in the app yet.

4da4570dc9d90c75467c5d5541882cd919481bf0.text: The web app now has a switch for a session recording tool. It is not active yet because the recording service is not connected. Developers can set this up later to watch how visitors use the site.

44212cc2816aedc01e2239edb193a18909727871.text: Freebuff users now see a clear message stating the service ran out of provider usage and needs a refill, instead of being prompted to buy credits. This change is live and ensures free users are not mistakenly billed or directed to purchase credits when the upstream providers are exhausted.

84f4ca34cd7481a4d5bc577ebf5d7343b385650a.text: Small internal cleanup for the command-line tool. The text on the referral banner is now locked to a fixed width so the buttons do not slide around when navigating with the keyboard. A redundant line about earning sessions was removed because that information already appears elsewhere.

3a66664e54bc6ebb3dcc9dd073e45769a85d045f.text: The build process now recognizes an alternative version of the interface engine for specific Linux systems. This prevents errors when creating the executable for those machines. Developers building the tool will see a smoother compilation step, but end users will notice no change in the application's behavior.

c235ded0aec8696b8af0e9fbb9e7fe1529e8bf1f.text: A small change now lets mouse clicks on the title of the queue preview open the full list of waiting messages. This only works when the window is wide enough to show the hint text. If the window is too narrow, the hint disappears and clicks do nothing.

00e5fa83a7e86d744e826cef0021ee41b4ccce17.text: The system now tracks how much work an AI agent does and when it needs to shorten its memory to fit more information. This change is for people building applications with the software toolkit. They can now set up their apps to receive these specific updates automatically, though nothing visible changes for regular users yet.

90ca26c0745bcbbcd40ea7ac385c031977d328cc.text: The service now automatically blocks free-tier accounts that try to resell access by routing traffic through Cloudflare's network. This action is only taken if the request passes a strict security check at the network edge, ensuring legitimate users are not accidentally banned. Regular paid users and internal tools see no change, while the abusers simply get blocked.

389f40a9a9a113232c22a5e93ee40d01a4ee7b08.text: The app now searches more carefully for the command-line tool Git for Windows installs on your machine. People who installed Git without admin rights, or on a drive other than C:, will no longer see false 'bash not found' errors. The fix is live today.

b9810f1556b1ad235441f5bea1278b948d119973.text: A new list of messages explains why someone cannot create an account, such as using a VPN or trying too many times from one network. This helps people understand the problem instead of thinking the website is broken. The list is ready to use, but the website does not show these messages yet.

db9b6fc11799d1756d2b434b432c8da1f6422046.text: The command-line assistant now offers free access to several new models, including a limited trial of Claude Fable 5. This update also ensures the assistant follows user-selected reasoning effort levels for Luna and prevents accidental routing to paid services during the free trial. These features are live today for command-line users.

44177dad55f47ee36c17c8c98b60c95202fa9ab1.text: The program now uses one shared list of rejection reasons instead of keeping its own copy, so it always agrees with the server. This change only affects the text-only version of the assistant; the desktop app still has its own separate rules for extra open windows. Users will not see any difference today, as this is just an internal cleanup to prevent future errors.

85fe163fd7843afe7dc3d07df57d2ac8eade07c4.text: The free AI assistant swapped one test model for another and deleted three old test entries. Regular users see no change because these were only visible to internal staff for testing. The new model is live for that internal group, while the old ones are fully removed.

97ea5981ff9943999d24543fa28dd5cc6fe5654a.text: The streak display now sends exact counts of filled and empty slots to the desktop app, which draws its own circles instead of using text dots. This change is internal plumbing and does not affect what anyone sees today.

a6f9f6f9f36afe33900b80d4df2d61d646a8460f.text: This update ensures that the system accurately tracks token usage even if a response cuts off before sending the final data. It affects anyone using the assistant to generate long responses, preventing silent accounting errors. Users won't see a visual change, but their usage records will now be complete and correct, with a new field available to track complex reasoning tokens.

837519d09bdafee951022bd77b63e5cfc25ecc7e.text: During the active GLM 5.2 promotion, the terminal interface now displays extra daily session limits and the promotion's end date. A new button opens the rewards page directly in your browser, while the page address remains visible for copying in restricted environments. This only appears for users who already earned access through referrals or bounties.

1b28a1b851243771ec6e1433673df5e676496f9c.text: The free web assistant now uses a simpler single-loop setup for its models, which changes how it manages long conversations. When the assistant reads files, it now correctly limits the view to specific lines instead of guessing or hitting errors. This affects only users of the free web version, and they will notice the assistant handling large files more reliably without false error messages.

9ddaa67d28223f14873db3c78e8fd0fbf98608c1.text: Alerts that warned engineers about slow database queries now ignore normal daily traffic swings. Engineers will stop getting woken up by routine changes in request timing and trip counts. This is live today.

ab5e182182a84b9df51cc00e8cdf96ce75d4bc0f.text: The internal speed limits for database requests were reset to match actual current speeds, replacing older, unrealistic targets. This change is live today but only affects the monitoring tools used by the engineering team, not the service itself. Regular users will not notice any difference in performance or behavior.

7a29686a3dc1313a85ce61f22d76bc18a78de3f5.text: A new one-hour limit for sign-in codes is now shared between the command-line tool and the desktop app. This prevents the two from timing out at different times, which previously caused confusing errors. The change is in place but does nothing yet, as the apps have not switched to using this shared limit.

0bbfdeb6b0c850151bbedd015b31cd6c99f9e2a8.text: The research assistant sometimes stopped after finding information, giving no final answer. A small instruction was added to force it to continue until it writes a summary. This applies to all research tasks. You will notice fewer blank or incomplete responses.

702b43bf6fbd41be7405bc3e02773f21a7888d37.text: The free version of the assistant now uses a different method for completing tasks. This change applies to free users and affects how the tool handles requests, as the previous method failed to finish work correctly on basic models. Users will see the assistant complete more of their requested tasks without stopping early.

bb7dbadf40439cd9a5159185a4d1a242b68f74ac.text: The system now spots requests from outside programs that use our main assistant as a simple text generator, without its usual tools. This helps us understand how these programs behave, but we are not blocking them yet because many regular users also make similar requests. Nothing changes for you today; this is just background tracking to help us make better rules later.

d800f61ca0291aa9270a75e454fb1a4a8ce09712.text: The system now separates database warnings into two types: alerts for performance drops and reports for exceeding cost limits. This ensures that only genuine regressions trigger urgent notifications, preventing alert fatigue from chronic overages. Developers will receive fewer, more actionable alerts when database performance suddenly worsens compared to previous baselines.

4e79ce476b22c73f06a2ca9fe5210d83d1c325ed.text: The coding assistant can now read only parts of large files instead of loading entire documents, and it automatically summarizes older conversations to save memory. This new behavior is disabled by default, so nothing changes for you unless you specifically enable the new 'Buffy' agent. If you do use it, you'll notice the assistant is faster and more efficient at handling complex tasks.

92a6961b894204c5620f9dd77cd2606e54b9a397.text: Typing commands in the text box now updates suggestions instantly, preventing the system from inserting the wrong text when you press Enter or Tab. Additionally, users can mark specific helper instructions to be hidden from the AI's automatic choices, ensuring they only run when explicitly requested.

87acd39098734f870266915e02267851c4cd4a4f.text: The service now checks whether free requests come from outside its official apps. If they do, the system answers them using a cheaper, free model instead of spending money on premium processing. This change protects the company's budget but does not affect people using the official software.

405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.text: On Windows, the tool now saves a record of its startup immediately, before its automatic recovery system activates. This prevents the recovery system from deleting the startup record if security software stops the tool during launch. Users will notice that the next time they restart the tool, it can correctly identify the previous session was interrupted, rather than treating it as a fresh start.

55258aabc4592ed2e90fc5d99fd7ae1e8a7bf10b.text: The command-line tool no longer turns on a specific Windows recovery feature by default. This stops security software from mistakenly blocking the program's startup. The feature stays off unless a tester manually switches it on for checking issues.

0f112dfc17a5d2dfc4419d5c4471a7cb8b49276c.text: The program now quietly reports when its background helper fails to start on Windows machines. This helps the support team spot rare glitches that stop commands from running. Regular people will see no change in how the program works, as this only adds invisible tracking for the developers.

e455a7f11d4caa461b258678a9a3bb975da44860.text: On Windows, the program now sends instructions to a helper through a short-lived temporary file instead of a direct connection. This stops the program from crashing after running several commands in a row. You will just see the program stay open and work reliably.

fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.text: The command-line tool now displays the exact reasoning level it will use for each model. This update ensures the visible label matches the server's actual behavior, preventing confusion when a model's effort setting is fixed or adjusted. You will see a new text suffix next to model names in the selection menu, showing whether the model runs with low, medium, or high reasoning effort.

25d69d5854023aae6361a9dbe09ab23090638563.text: Muse Spark 1.2 now displays 'Queue' instead of '1M context' in the model picker. Hovering reveals a tooltip explaining that if the queue is too long, requests automatically switch to GPT-5.6 Luna after a 10-second wait. This change affects users selecting Muse Spark 1.2, ensuring they are aware of the potential delay and fallback behavior before making a request.

372bcb13336cfa7eb8060b1b80208c8a9884fb9f.text: A new AI model is now available on the website, but not on the desktop app or command-line tool. Because Meta limits this model to one request per second for everyone, the website will show a wait screen if it is busy, while other platforms would simply fail. This change is live for web users today.

95f7ba2869aed9e0bd0ef259d86becf75a4ac23e.text: The team added a rulebook for how long database tasks should take, but it is not active yet. Nothing will change for you today because no system is checking these limits against real traffic. It is a safety net for the engineers to catch slow-downs later.

e93edfe8d2d61a6b285ed4e7614d50a8c9de8e29.text: The command-line tool now checks your active session more efficiently by skipping redundant data it already has, reducing unnecessary network traffic. Additionally, the system now tracks which specific step an AI agent is taking to better manage resources, though this tracking is currently internal and not visible to users.

956dcf938814d5da8af5f2c1c1216f14d1bcd769.text: In regions with restricted model access, users who earned a specific reward can now use it to run the GLM 5.2 model. Previously, the system automatically switched this choice to a basic model, wasting the reward. This fix is live and ensures earned credits work as expected in those areas.

ba0d1c06f45f11e6259d8d3c03aee844a0b60a97.text: A small safety limit now stops the assistant from waiting too long for a quick command to finish. If the assistant asks for a wait time longer than ten minutes, the system automatically shortens it to ten minutes. This helps you avoid staring at a frozen screen when a command hangs, but it does not affect tasks meant to run in the background or those set to wait indefinitely.

c7445e24582aabfa1c2f45c2108982511769385a.text: A specific free AI assistant model has been removed from the free service. People using the free version can no longer choose or use this model, though it remains available for paid users or those with their own API keys. If you were using the free version, you won't see this model in the list anymore.

a47be121a650358f747794cf743870e75d35e6b3.text: Two tools that previously disrupted the automated quality-check process have been renamed to prevent them from running during these checks. This internal fix ensures that engineers see a complete and accurate summary of test results. You will not notice any change to the software's visible features.

dd1e2cfc9f90b5c1b0c2e056e7eecf45ae0c7cd5.text: The command-line tool now fixes a hidden setup problem in its background data storage. This change is internal and affects no visible features. Users will notice nothing, as the tool simply continues working correctly without relying on a fragile startup order.

6059b884a999ffb281a0c15913c659f9bc6f5308.text: When the command-line tool loses its connection while trying to take over a session, it now lets you try again immediately instead of forcing you to restart the program. This applies to people using the CLI who hit common temporary network errors like timeouts or server busy messages.

3a8cc3135b1201b6403abb26762a309b269c8119.text: The command-line tool now tracks whether a failed request might have already taken effect on the server. If the outcome is unclear, it blocks immediate retries to prevent duplicate actions. Users will see specific error messages and a countdown timer when connection issues occur.

9bf66ff09f2303f7bc13ebb134678c45869f2e30.text: When free-tier accounts hit a server capacity limit, the assistant now shows 'high demand — in line, starting soon...' instead of a generic 'retrying...' message. This change is live and affects only free-mode users during peak load, providing clearer context for the wait.

adf5bef2be7cd107b6fdefb43b9e9e6fffadf1d7.text: The system now tracks two very expensive AI models, marking them as restricted so they do not appear in the standard free list. This change is for internal accounting; the models are hidden from general users to prevent accidental high costs. No visible feature changes for regular users.

383fb0ceededb4056d40b1f6db984a321b7feb21.text: The terminal screen now shows the weekly streak with simple dots that older fonts can display, instead of symbols that often appeared as empty boxes. The streak also keeps a clear gap beside the headline, so the words and the count no longer run together. The change is live today.

2e0d17a8eb3b3bf8b25564ff44b3338348cbfc63.text: The team added tracking points to measure how people use the new website builder's setup steps and guided tours. This change is internal only, so regular users will not notice any difference in how the site looks or works today.

4f9fad7460a17948620ee4c82d02a3ddb4bba868.text: A new safety check is now in place for the desktop app's 'use it here' button. If you click this button to move a session from a device you cannot reach, the system now verifies the exact target before closing it. This prevents old or wrong buttons from accidentally ending a different open window. This rule is active today to protect your sessions.

4d3c46a551d4e0e3f37e902090ea267ec9b9ab5e.text: Three email domains were added to a list of blocked services today. New sign-ups using proxyvpn.cn, impact.qd.je, or fincy.qd.je will be rejected. Regular users are unaffected, and real internet providers were carefully kept on the allowed list.

f28ecce37f526a75beecd2e0c8d82da50630abba.text: Two free assistant options, MiMo Pro and an extra GLM 5.2 path, are gone from the model picker in the web, CLI, and desktop apps as of today. Users who previously chose MiMo Pro will now see only the standard MiMo option. GLM 5.2 remains available only to those who earn access by referring friends, and it no longer shares the daily free credits that other premium models use.

d1c94381b39773dbd68e9c7ebbd4909724179110.text: The command-line tool now runs shell commands through a separate helper program, which prevents them from interfering with the interactive terminal. This change is live for interactive command-line use, ensuring stable focus and input states during execution.

60dd01fe109f976b0e1e7eea23b9bd0e3ba67b6e.text: People who usually only get basic access to the AI can now use the GLM 5.2 model, but only if they have earned a specific reward through a bounty program. If you have this reward, the app will show you an active button to start a chat; if you do not, the button stays locked.

12660b067482362d977d9d423b6a2c107ad0c76c.text: The assistant now automatically retries when it finishes 'thinking' without generating a visible answer, preventing silent failures. This affects all users interacting with the assistant, who will see a brief 'retrying' indicator instead of an error or blank response. The fix is live.

af3257b3b7d7a81bde74a67d84d9a683478b684d.text: The desktop app now records every instance where a task fails to recover. This change helps support teams spot rare errors without guessing from partial data. You will not notice any difference in the app's behavior.

32b7907dfe18e9fd79fac194172c07fcc816edda.text: The program's background helper now tells the main app it is finished before cleaning up its own leftover parts. This stops the app's display from freezing on Windows when closing tasks. If the helper fails, the app now shows a clear message telling you to restart or change your terminal window.

32405d54b26ef83e80be7c091a8c9610c6bf3b8a.text: The program now strictly blocks a command from starting if it cannot first secure the terminal screen. This protects Windows users from losing control of their window when running tasks, though headless setups remain unaffected. You will notice the program simply refuses to launch the command rather than crashing or freezing the screen if the terminal is busy.

817391fb58001b3bc24fbc42be479676d265d7d0.text: When the main assistant hands a task to a helper assistant, the helper now always receives the exact same conversation history, regardless of how the task was triggered. This internal fix ensures helpers have consistent context and prevents errors from old or duplicate messages. Users will not notice any visual changes, but background tasks may run more reliably.

cfefab1485351974f3ed0461c9d4797fbb251c9d.text: The command-line tool now checks version labels on its saved files more carefully. If a label looks broken or old, the tool ignores it and fixes itself instead of trying to use it. This stops the tool from getting stuck on bad update data.

f56844fd118df56422c40c55968c247d6253c562.text: Windows users of the command-line tool now get a safety check while it runs another program. The tool temporarily turns off extra mouse and window-focus signals that could otherwise appear as stray text over the screen. The change is active now, and the visible effect is a cleaner screen during command runs.

8c9929fa0f77987bcfd64f0625b68a97cf9dc17b.text: The software's internal testing process now uses the correct built-in file extractor on Windows. Previously, the test might fail because the wrong extractor misread the file location. This change is only for the testing environment, so regular users will not notice any difference in their experience.

5423683dc8558497f5168a3e65a61e9a5e01e0ad.text: The free Fable assistant now uses its own model for code review, and it no longer tries to call a different, less capable model when it needs to think harder. This change is live and affects free Fable users. They would notice faster responses, because the system stops making wasted attempts that previously failed or timed out.

59b71a2329ee96e2378ae589e09694cfa02eee4a.text: The assistant now delivers its step-by-step instructions as a temporary message that disappears after the current task, rather than keeping it permanently visible. This change prevents the system from wasting memory by trying to save the old, permanent instructions. It is live today, and you will notice smoother, more efficient responses from the assistant.

8f24a429cd6addf8fb858155634ef5241fea86b4.text: The system now allows AI assistants to hold twice as much conversation history in memory before summarizing it. This change is active today and applies to most models, though some specific models retain a smaller limit. Users will notice the assistant maintains better context during long chats, remembering earlier details without prematurely compressing the conversation.

7335066f45ad29fa39ad3f09fa84c45ab1aca737.text: The website's chat assistant now connects directly to the DeepSeek service instead of using a slower, third-party route. This change is live for chat users today. You will not notice any visual differences, but the system's internal routing is more efficient.

ef5190fe8024ca729df82dfa11c847354a3ca279.text: The command-line tool now remembers if a faster version crashed on your computer, stopping it from trying that version again. It also stops asking Windows for screen colors, which prevented antivirus software from blocking the tool. These fixes help Windows users run the tool without security warnings or repeated crashes.

0251dddf1475cf3bd2449b2fe3f4cb429903459d.text: The error message shown when a request stops after five minutes of silence has been updated. Previously, it blamed the user's internet connection, assuming the server was always sending regular signals. Now, it acknowledges that a slow start on our side could also cause the delay. This helps users avoid troubleshooting their own network when the issue is actually with the service.

3e5be71544b2879899a0dea5162bf6f7e8195bcb.text: The free tier's model list now shows a 'Buffy the Claude Fable 5' option when the company has spare capacity for it. This option appears and disappears based on server availability, not your choice. If you pick it and capacity runs out mid-task, the system automatically switches to a standard free model to keep your work going.

6e1168a960e83d3c2651c6765b504f45f0d091b9.text: The cloud planner now uses a newer, better model for everyone. This change is live today and affects all users who use the cloud planner. You will notice the planner gives you better and faster answers, and it no longer uses a more expensive option for paid plans.

13b1cfee56ea86d90e68a05afbb0399cc5c062a5.text: The assistant's memory shortcut broke for one specific model, making it re-read everything each turn. Now it keeps the shortcut intact, so that model responds faster and cheaper. Only users on that model notice it.

f388f14e2b1dcafb2a95799598ceb7e7ac511c24.text: The text prompting you to press Enter to choose a model has been removed from the menu. This change affects anyone selecting an AI model and makes the screen less cluttered. You will notice the model options appear in narrower boxes with more empty space around them.

612e2a39e0355c12169f3dd37ce5e3bf09942e02.text: A new rule now cleans up chat titles. It removes quotes and periods, and cuts text longer than sixty characters. This applies to all chat surfaces. You will see tidier, shorter labels in your chat list.

e183deaed6c794aacff15662a87d41c98e3201d1.text: Small internal change. Adds heartbeat rules for the desktop app's multi-tab mode. Nothing happens yet; code does not use these rules.

b1f68e07ef57b84fe337023718d350a96ec2305b.text: Free mode no longer offers the Kimi K2.7 Code model, blocking all requests for it. This change stops older software versions from accidentally using expensive resources, protecting the free service budget. Users will notice Kimi is gone from the list, and DeepSeek V4 Flash is now highlighted as the better, faster free option.

a5cb80f3d735b96b63f2fc075689ab4ed9955056.text: The command-line assistant now forces every new session to start on DeepSeek V4 Flash if your saved preference was an older model like MiMo 2.5. This change is live. You will see the assistant open on the newer model automatically, though you can still manually select the older one if you prefer.

3a7b54b212bfe45eafb19525bbf52041f9b3a6c9.text: The software switched its terminal assistant to a cheaper, faster model to prevent accidental charges on free accounts. This change is live today and applies to users running the terminal tool on a free plan. A person would notice that their usage now bills against the same model as the main assistant, avoiding surprise costs.

7c831448a6e554c45b87894487ebe7421385045f.text: Windows computers now ignore a hidden Linux bridge when looking for the command tool. This stops confusing errors for people who have that bridge installed but not set up. The fix is active today.

ab4919394f7cd07cc1f360e48f04b600a1f6d40a.text: If you manually select a new model while an old session is still active, the system now automatically ends that old session to switch to your choice. You will see a message confirming the previous session ended and the new model is active. This prevents the common issue where your selection appeared ignored because the system was stuck on the old model.

ef75fd7a27e09c75d822efcfdaa28b023a03e31f.text: A small cleanup to the command-line screen where you pick an AI model. If you are building a daily habit for less than a week, the screen no longer shows a note about the reward you have not earned yet, which stops that text from pushing the model list off the screen on small windows. The list now shows one specific model first, moving it ahead of another option so it is easier to find.

31ac8a0f82d45b3a6f82a46a9be1a4c6b8ad3b11.text: The free coding assistant now blocks new connections if too many people use it from the same network address. Current sessions continue working, but new users see a message saying the network is full and should try again later. This change is live today.

d5ca1376e2a658169fc355905b29159d5af6a85a.text: The command-line tool now lists a newer, faster free assistant model dated July 31. People who previously saved the older MiniMax model as their default will have their setting switched to this new one automatically. When opening the model list, a "NEW" badge appears next to the new choice, and a short note suggests switching if the user is still on the old model.

f3e3cce8abe081a471cdf9fbd525426f7fba600f.text: The model picker in the command-line tool now keeps the recommended model visible and selected when access is limited or when the list expands. This prevents the screen from hiding models or moving the cursor unexpectedly as account details load. The change is live in the current release.

254c227edee9d656de7fc74312468062e17f7a1e.text: If you try to change models while a session is still running, the command line tool now shows a message explaining the change was blocked and tells you to end the session first. Before this, the tool quietly kept the old model, leaving you confused about why your choice did not apply. This fix is live today.

0cda526a6c5bbf6cab64dafb874a9774ac1a4299.text: Windows users will now see fewer missing files when searching large projects. The tool previously failed to exclude build folders on Windows, wasting its search limit on junk data. Now, it properly ignores those folders to save room for source code. If a search still hits the limit, the tool warns that results might be incomplete instead of showing zero files.

6cc0c94c19331c4a4009587d3b698916f00f9f0a.text: The referral program dropped its old level system and now gives one extra daily chat session for each new person you invite. This change only applies if you invite someone who has had a GitHub account for at least four months. You will not see a difference today because the feature is still being set up.

c22abe9a8900d52fac3c91bd1d12f407e631be0c.text: A small internal price limit for one free AI model was raised to stop the service from rejecting requests. This affects users who pick that specific free model on the Freebuff plan. They will simply be able to use it again without seeing a 'no endpoints found' error.

bfead8065f4f0e68f6247fa51973c73185d00525.text: A new free AI model is now available for the Freebuff service. It provides high-quality reasoning without charging extra, but it is restricted to OpenAI's direct servers to prevent accidental high fees. Users of Freebuff can select this model today, though it does not affect paid Codebuff users.

5b8b58dbe1bc8498ac86a6e8aaa8e6311e86331f.text: The limit on free coding sessions earned by inviting friends was removed today. For full-access members, the app now shows the total number of sessions earned instead of a capped fraction, meaning each new friend adds another daily session without hitting a ceiling.

1ba142d747a1c095f2be79abe6b6adefad0c2a28.text: Desktop users can now open three free model tabs at once instead of unlimited, though paid models still allow just one. The app now shows exactly how many slots you have used and when the next one frees up. This helps you avoid errors if you try to open a new tab while another device or project is already using your capacity.

9f80be02582ab23c45aa4fd7adf8370b2613ad92.text: Kimi K2.7 Code was removed from the free model picker because its usage cost exceeded the free tier budget. This affects users who previously selected Kimi: it no longer appears in the list of available choices. The server still recognizes the model to prevent errors for existing sessions, but new selections are blocked.

faee98a2042d0b024219330c1f6ae2f6df89cff0.text: A small layout tweak was made to the model selection screen in the command-line tool. When a model can analyze images, a short "· Images" label now appears at the end of its description on the same line. This prevents the label from pushing the text onto a new line, keeping the menu neat and compact.

f377278c442149319ba818d05791b4012b9cf3b5.text: The default free assistant model switched from MiniMax M3 to DeepSeek V4 Pro. This change is live today for people using the command-line tool. When opening the model list, the new model appears first, and a warning about data usage for training now sits on its own line below the name instead of being hidden on small screens.

ac163119e1412375e526494c81ec179739f4ced4.text: Browser-based AI tools now default to a cheaper, more efficient model for new users, making long sessions less costly to run. The old, more expensive models are still available but appear smaller and less prominent in the selection menu. This change is currently being prepared for release, so users will not see the new default until the update goes live.

dde3b3223f5082e1ce6c3d890dfaee4a1c5e91f4.text: The text-based interface now places the session counter inside the model selection box to prevent the screen from shrinking. Warnings and hours appear centered below the model name, giving the highlighted row more breathing room. This visual cleanup is live and helps you see all available options without scrolling.

d281d6eedd789ca6b8590df20edb4388379408f4.text: The app now always sends a reply for every tool request, even when the result is just a picture. This stops errors that could happen when the assistant tried to use a tool that returned only an image. You likely won't notice anything, as it just makes the app more reliable.

9b8ffc8ef8c48601dc234a57e45ebc83b498a5f5.text: The assistant's planning step now uses a different underlying brain. A new experimental option was also added for a specific advanced tier, but it is marked as potentially using your data for training and is not yet active for general use. Regular users will see slightly different planning behavior, with no other visible changes.

6fbfd71dd51c396171b911b5fc3894984e0a3dd9.text: Codebuff's paid 'Lite' mode now uses a different AI model to make it faster and cheaper. The internal test scores are also more reliable now because the system checks results with two different AI judges instead of relying on one that might silently fail. Free users are unaffected and will not notice any changes.

075723dbdc661304e710e2b305277f3acfef3101.text: A specific AI model previously limited to one use per day now draws from a shared daily allowance, allowing more frequent access for eligible users. However, the system prevents this model from being set as a default, so it will not auto-load on fresh visits. This change is live today.

801a9d02c935e19c2f9529d1330b0de6eac555c4.text: The tool that runs terminal commands now skips its extra text-summarizing step when the result is short. This speeds up everyday checks and saves computing costs. If you ask it to run a quick command, you will see the full, unedited result immediately instead of waiting for a condensed version.

9b8e85b8d0d50bfc0c1bffe9caa17eee7798d1bf.text: The desktop app now records a separate signal when it goes quiet because it is waiting for a background command to finish. This prevents those normal waits from being mistaken for frozen sessions in the reliability data. The change is live for desktop app telemetry, but you will not notice any difference in how the app behaves.

0ff93e746badad951717b0a70386bf5b24701517.text: The system now removes broken conversation records where a tool request was left unanswered. This fixes a hidden error that could stop all future replies in chats using strict providers like DeepSeek. If you had a conversation that suddenly refused to answer, it should work again.

cb202d14e1327ee923368b2dc099364b372dac68.text: The new planner limits blank cloud projects to five per day, resetting at midnight Pacific time. This prevents heavy use of computing resources by people who start projects without connecting a code repository.

622a2a2228556af643a2addd266099af434504f5.text: The desktop app now quietly counts which features people actually use. This happens only when a person deliberately opens a tool, and it records just once per session to keep data clean. Regular users will not see any change in the app's look or behavior, but the company will get a clearer picture of what tools matter to them.

3c92d4e7bd963920744771f9af70a7740f5db53b.text: The chat assistant now automatically shortens long conversation histories before each reply to prevent errors when switching to models with smaller memory limits. This affects all chat users and prevents the assistant from crashing or refusing to answer after a model change. The feature is live and runs silently in the background.

8e2ef71f5db6f210951e6086acaa0618bf80e055.text: The small, fast helpers that run commands or search files now use a newer, slightly pricier brain to work better. If you use an older version of the app that hasn't updated, the helpers keep using the old brain so nothing breaks for you yet. You won't notice any changes right now, as this just improves how the helpers think under the hood.

086e7bfc29fc3edd9f62a2eddbdc8821ff71b409.text: When the tool fails to start a task, it now shows the raw reason to the support team instead of hiding it. Support can see the exact error message in their logs. Customers see no change.

ef69165e2f7db1192f722d33574d63f4d4bc8f4a.text: The one-time free credit grant for new accounts is now off. New users who sign up with a linked GitHub account no longer receive those initial credits. This is live today.

c731787cd02fea9b5d37c9e5e6fb06c0e3897045.text: The command-line tool now waits a bit longer before trying to reconnect after a failure, and it varies the waiting time slightly so all users don't try at once during an outage. This change is active now and helps keep the service stable, so you might notice fewer connection errors if the main server goes down.

3b621851400cd86740de15406b74d8f020832c01.text: A weekly bonus of free AI model uses now increases based on how long a user has maintained a daily streak. This applies to full-access users, who will see their bonus amount grow from one use per week up to four uses per week as their streak reaches 28 days.

99f8bdf7238772049723aee6d133b9e2af05e10c.text: The chat assistant now picks sign-up links from its own search results instead of typing them from memory. This stops it from making up web addresses or sending you to a company's main page when you need an account key. The fix applies to the free coding tool chat and is live now.

ed223e710e22a010882d619831743d1c66d4ce9c.text: The AI assistant now handles sudden internet disconnects during long responses. If the connection drops, the system keeps the partial answer and automatically resumes from that point instead of crashing. This change is active today.

04bceb38336bd18978e6c75daa2b1451b3f51c8d.text: The assistant's internal memory cleaner now skips official logging and estimates text length locally, making each step faster. It also keeps memory intact for thirty minutes after a pause, preventing unnecessary rewrites. This change is live and affects all agent runs, but users will only notice slightly quicker responses.

ff555dfc23f4037715103ed7983c5e934eae5555.text: The rules for drawing the streak progress dots moved to a shared spot, so the command-line tool and the desktop app now use the exact same logic. You would see the same visual style in both places: the dots fill up to seven days, then a plus sign appears to show you have gone beyond that, and the text always says 'day' instead of 'days'.

21e20ab6257f3141ddca47ec45624e70688a4bc1.text: The system removed a specific signal that previously told the desktop app when a user was blocked due to having too many tabs open, rather than hitting a daily limit. This change only affects the desktop application. Users will no longer see a specific 'close a tab' message if they are blocked; instead, they will see a general limit warning.

2d3b8b08b30dd13c6590106ec5eb4720ffd18215.text: The paid version of the HY3 Atlas assistant now connects to a different service called OpenRouter instead of its previous direct connection. This change affects only users paying for the HY3 Atlas tier. They might notice a slight difference in response speed or availability, but the underlying model remains the same.

7f0aadcf9dac5265474b698062f1d51776223fd8.text: The system now allows multiple web container addresses to be listed together, separated by commas. This setting is currently just a rule for how data is formatted and does not change how the application behaves for end users yet.

19ef71044ca314d9713b6f291ef272abbcc58724.text: The system no longer checks a specific list of web addresses used to connect to internal tools. This change only affects the software's internal setup rules, not the features people use. Regular users will see no difference in how the app looks or behaves.

c11ed01ddcbcb4bb5477850724e03e3bce8441e5.text: The team added a new AI model, Laguna S 2.1, to the system's internal list. This model is currently hidden from regular users and restricted to a special 'god-mode' testing group. Ordinary customers will not see or use it yet, as it is being tested for stability before any wider release.

6a8bd574f8f06b5f519397bf8b066709ab784545.text: Added a new hidden option for internal testing that routes a specific AI model through a different service provider. This change is not visible to regular users and does not affect the current live experience. It allows the team to compare performance between two connection methods without changing what customers see.

aff0092445df1aceda16b73f9435f9121831fa44.text: The command-line tool now saves chat history more reliably, preventing crashes when data is too large or tangled. It also limits warning messages to once every five minutes, so your screen stays clear during long sessions.

21d02b63f7a0e4b97b0e825243a70231d24de6fc.text: A small internal change added a hidden testing path for the GLM 5.2 model via CrofAI. It only works for staff using a special developer mode to check this new provider separately. Regular users will not see this option or notice any difference in the product today.

de58a616b9b0ca15d0fba59c68fe8b7e19ef2fb5.text: The desktop app now quietly records when a task goes silent for too long. This note is for the team to measure how often it happens, so they can decide later if a fix is needed. You will not see any change in the app.

92ff02610686d5d9fc79060254e0ba759de87c76.text: The free coding tool's main menu now hides extra text and logos if your terminal window is too short or narrow, keeping the screen from looking cluttered. This change is live and affects anyone using the command-line tool. You would also notice the description for the Kimi coding model now includes '& Slow'.

31731d4b275ad637ad19e9531442b3f5acaa8d7f.text: The system now records specific details when an AI response gets cut off or hits a length limit, helping engineers track how often these interruptions happen and if the AI successfully recovers. This change is internal for the engineering team and does not affect the end-user experience today, though it improves the reliability of future fixes for stream interruptions.

6501764d584c609c88de49fbb649c5b5f055c3d9.text: The assistant hides its internal cleanup notes from you. It still shows when this work starts and ends. This stops clutter while letting you see why it pauses briefly.

74ee22bd83306ec1e06b515b52e03e43a31b41cd.text: Daily session allowance for premium and limited plans increased from five to six. This applies to premium subscribers and limited-mode users (outside full-access countries or via VPN). They will see the new cap reflected in help text and the app interface.

ff901fe20bad843eac69657fe3f446d4285af737.text: When the assistant stops writing mid-answer because the network drops or it runs out of thinking room, the program now notices this and quietly asks the assistant to try again, up to three times. People using the command-line tool will see a brief 'retrying' message instead of the conversation ending unexpectedly.

4b03dcbd2a7791366306ab976dba52fd9659b6d6.text: The system now records when a new user sends their first message, helping track where they came from. This works across all platforms (web, desktop, mobile). Users won't see any changes, but marketing teams can now measure which ads or pages lead to actual usage.

908988675e48fa01e64a50b5f9ac2410d06900dd.text: The command-line tool now correctly hides the 'context-pruner' assistant, regardless of how its name is formatted. This change is active today. If you previously saw this hidden assistant's activity in your chat history, it will be removed from view when you reopen the conversation.

35474f6bf77e51e4dbcf3773cbb0ebf5c30d6fe7.text: The command-line tool now has a single, clear rule for stopping an active task. Whether you press a key, switch chats, or log out, the system correctly halts the current work and prevents stray data from corrupting your new session. This is live today and prevents rare glitches where old responses might leak into a new conversation.

9262d077baa57360516b372dae789cd193f7a15a.text: A new daily limit of six sessions was added for free web-based AI models. This affects only people using the web browser interface, not those using the command-line tool. Users will notice they can no longer start more than six new chat sessions per day with these specific free models.

e78563f1e523d46e46a3234eeb84bb3e77cb9b4b.text: The chat application now keeps your conversation active while browsing history or switching views. Previously, navigating away reset the session state. This change is live today. Users experience smoother navigation without losing their current chat context.

ea226cb387463c614ad636bf2fa368cca721099c.text: The assistant now stops guessing when asked to fetch documentation. It rejects blank or invalid search terms and cuts off results exactly at a smaller, fixed limit instead of silently raising them. This applies immediately to anyone using the documentation lookup tool.

b6199c08ae729268fb8e37886fe7608ee7c7c17c.text: The command-line tool now labels your session count as 'this week' or 'today' depending on your account's reset schedule. It also prepares the display to show how many free sessions come from referrals or streaks. This change is live for the weekly reset logic, but the detailed breakdown data does not appear yet because the server does not send it.

8785289028f63c9a6d0f34de8380e3de400c1f3c.text: One specific AI model now uses daily free credits instead of being unlimited. The screen shows the exact number of uses left, pulled directly from the service rather than a fixed guess. If you run out of premium credits, the app automatically switches you to an unlimited model so you can keep working.

16931ade9e64c9e5a453642da335cf4b08ed6093.text: The software now records which model is active and when that session starts and ends. This data is prepared for apps that manage multiple sessions, but it does nothing yet because no app reads it today. You will not see any changes in the product.

6655cc5ad6e660c64cbca9251ef019eecf59dde9.text: The command-line tool now correctly shows if a task is still running, even if you switch screens or close the chat window while it works. Previously, the status might falsely appear as 'idle' or stopped, hiding the fact that the system was still busy. This small fix ensures you see accurate progress updates.

1328a3f288ed36e8ee37a3aac1b8ca1efff52cd6.text: The system now separates basic model names from complex setup data to prevent errors in the desktop application. This change is internal and fixes a technical conflict, so people will not notice any visible difference in how the app looks or works.

4ccefe89dc731502797440fa56faa60e1417f9eb.text: The system's internal logic for identifying valid AI models was reorganized to resolve a technical conflict. This change ensures the model recognition feature remains stable and accurate without altering how it functions. Users will not notice any difference in the application's behavior.

94f0f052111d7430d1cc973c9653333d045e5f6d.text: The text-only version of the MiMo 2.5 Pro model now correctly refuses image inputs, preventing failed requests. The system dynamically checks model capabilities instead of using a fixed list, ensuring new models are handled correctly without accidentally blocking their features.

ed5c777e9ea95739a4f2484a600d096304e6a3e3.text: The note describing how streak rewards work was updated to say they add time to a shared pool instead of giving out separate sessions. This change only affects the internal description and does not alter the actual reward amount. Users will see no difference in their streak bonuses.

1b952b35d6dac171d48c8e0fd7daf70c873a40b5.text: The app now reports which command-line tool it finds on your computer when you launch it. This helps the support team diagnose setup issues if the tool is missing or blocked. You will not see any changes in the interface.

c931d187e9c094739c6acc86ec1c583dc9319d51.text: The system now lets trusted background services act on behalf of a specific signed-in user. Ordinary accounts cannot do this; only pre-approved service accounts can. Regular users will notice no change, but apps using these special services can now correctly attribute actions and data to the end-user rather than the service itself.

191fd58e6fbdcd4f428da59d556490c152d2361f.text: The tool now sends specific internal performance numbers about how it manages conversation memory to a separate operational dashboard. This data bypasses standard privacy filters to ensure technical staff see exact figures, but it stays hidden from general usage reports. Regular users will not notice any changes in their experience.

ef2019f26ece398825b6dbe8451e9b5aec3be563.text: The command-line tool now stops new free sessions if you hit today's spending limit, while letting current sessions run. Affected users see a message explaining the block and when it resets. This is live today.

10fb028c168f112636f95dc76cc992a67819940e.text: The tool that reads files now has a strict total limit on how much text it can return in one go, rather than cutting off individual files. This means if you ask it to read many large files, it will stop early and tell you to ask for fewer files at once. This change is live and affects anyone using the file-reading feature.

a793b16ecd43ca8d61e002222b2c9f8f8614880b.text: The special offer for the free assistant now appears inside the scrolling menu of options, rather than as a separate block below it. This affects people using the free tier. When you open the menu, you will see the offer as part of the list of choices, and you can move through it using the arrow keys just like you do for the model names.

464115e810f97affdcebc6f7e5485d3664c6956c.text: The program now stops an assistant's response if you start a new chat or switch to an old one. This prevents the previous, unfinished response from accidentally overwriting the text of the chat you just opened. You will notice that switching chats no longer corrupts or mixes up your saved conversation history.

7dbf452bebddc6dd0ea8d46809d425a182a44753.text: The 'KAT Coder Pro V2' AI model is gone from the free model picker because the provider retired it. Limited-region web users who previously used it now share the general session pool without its special exemption.

d24c97e0aa12993c710b9495edbe6315550f9910.text: The application now sends a standard web browser identity to ad networks instead of its internal tool signature. This prevents ad providers from blocking requests as suspicious. Developers will see consistent ad delivery across all platforms.

47ef2af4ac5eb7f77c5ae2be02f77801fabf9490.text: The command-line tool now quietly records how often it shows ads during answers. This helps the company measure ad placement without storing every user's conversation. You would see no change in the tool's appearance or speed.

9ef7e7f28943c8ab971309b595bafd08d00d7b3a.text: The command-line tool now downloads updates through corporate network filters and resumes interrupted downloads from where they stopped. If a download fails, it keeps the existing working program instead of breaking it. This affects users installing the tool on restricted networks.

739b605e24c6307c71c81c8323b3f38563a76ec1.text: The software now uses the official, permanent name for a specific fast, low-cost AI model instead of its temporary testing name. This affects the small background helpers that scan files, browse the web, or run commands. You will not notice any visual changes, but these helpers now use the stable version of the model, ensuring they keep working correctly as the testing version is retired.

ae87d9cee86c3c4665a0447b4c8cef653c739b76.text: The code that decides where to place small ads within the assistant's answers was moved to a shared location. This change affects desktop app users, who will see up to four unique ads repeated every two sections of text. The new tracking events are in place but do nothing yet.

879cc9e68d329f65c252f1f1473f5d0b37dccd15.text: A small internal fix stops the assistant from ending a conversation too early when certain reasoning models send leftover thinking tags. It affects people using those specific models, who would notice the assistant continuing to answer instead of stopping abruptly.

4beca76c6485fa3c57a3716650a0eecd996044b4.text: A new rule was added to limit signup credits to GitHub users with accounts older than four months. This change is currently in the system but has no effect yet. Users will not notice any difference today.

bc264d00cf190d86d2953e9937afc68c3b371446.text: Three new AI models are now available in the free web browser tool. The tool also shows exact session limits for these models. This change is active.

2f0296cf9937bb0bc0256849868e81c193f0f472.text: The command-line tool now fetches ads in small batches of four as needed, rather than grabbing eight upfront for every message. This change is live today. Free users will see a slight reduction in unnecessary ad requests and potentially faster initial load times, though the visual appearance of the ads remains largely unchanged.

1d64a9f44880ccf58e335af1efb24a93ec923831.text: The command-line tool now correctly identifies when you switch away from or back to its window, preventing false triggers from unrelated text. This means the screen will accurately dim or brighten the interface to reflect focus, and the cursor blink will only activate when the terminal supports it. The fix is live today for all command-line users.

c4c5dcd66aaa42cd023a0ad0c146feacf180ebc9.text: After seven straight days of using the service, you now get one extra free chat every day, rather than only on the seven-day mark. This applies to everyone, though premium members also get a special weekly bonus. You will see the extra chat available in your daily limit.

e1ce92184215843f83e268d758011594a4a0c8a5.text: The program now saves progress faster by copying only the parts that change. This stops the text from freezing on screen during long sessions. You will notice smoother updates as the assistant works.

33192e18252182b6f101ffe9191d2da5fb230c57.text: The free coding assistant can now use a newer Kimi model again, which was previously hidden due to slow responses. This change is live for users in the full mode regions (US, Canada, UK, EU, and select others). You would notice this model listed as an option for coding tasks, and you can now attach images to it, unlike with some other free models.

8e3f104307089d0da674ad22011f2114b5bcf71d.text: The system now adds a special setting when running commands on Windows to stop background processes from trying to open a terminal window. This affects people using the software's assistant to run commands on Windows machines. They will see fewer unexpected terminal pop-ups or errors when the assistant runs tasks quietly in the background.

d049aa594eaa6ffe79276ee9358921814f6e3077.text: The system now accepts more ways to set up agents that can create other agents. Previously, it only allowed one specific method, causing setups using alternative approaches to fail. This change is live and affects anyone configuring these agent templates, removing unnecessary errors for valid setups.

0a6df5765585fe3da17d92272fbce28be74bc127.text: The tool now shows small advertisements inside the assistant's text replies, not just at the top of the screen. This applies only to free users, who will see up to eight ads scattered throughout longer answers. The ad above the input box remains, but now rotates separately from the ones inside the text.

bd3b19ed76cf17a16e45df2e329ee5e84b7b6883.text: The software now stops background tasks more reliably and prevents visual glitches in the terminal interface. This affects people using the command-line assistant, who will no longer see strange characters appearing over the screen when running certain tools.
