f0d966458519ffa59de0fbce27fad27f0ac7a047.text: The team removed a separate helper program that used to carry out some assistant tasks outside the main service. This was an internal cleanup, so the app and website behavior did not change and users should not notice anything. An old setting that could enable that helper still exists, but it no longer controls anything.

0deed0f9ae60e3d338e71d7077fe4180e21277f4.text: The tool now uses a simpler method to manage terminal settings on Windows, avoiding security software false alarms. This change is live and affects Windows users, ensuring the application runs smoothly without triggering unnecessary alerts.

4afa065433a1f7c99574755052324ab24fc7bd1c.text: A new model is now available in the web interface. It is not available in the command line or desktop app. This is a small internal change to limit the rollout.

758fdbfedc1bd8c31dee38e5fdf17ae71b7cb67c.text: The command-line tool now saves your conversation history in the background instead of pausing your typing to write it to disk. This stops the interface from freezing up during very long chats. The final save when you exit still happens immediately to ensure nothing is lost.

e40725574901bc9196b956db9113351627654769.text: The free and lite versions of the assistant now use a newer AI model for all tasks. Users on these plans will see responses generated by the updated model instead of the older, faster one. The change is live today.

d0de3f5b1cbd70534b9d6c36f0dfc9c77ae8f92b.text: Three new AI models now show a 'TEST' badge in the selection menu, warning that they might be unreliable. This applies to everyone using the model picker. Separately, a background tracking point was added for the cloud sign-up page, but it does not change what visitors see.

c59bde7fe2f90f0e25b0ce36a1d8856ec8ccfa5f.text: The free command-line tool now shows advertisements between your conversation messages, instead of rotating them in a single fixed spot. These ads appear after the assistant finishes answering, spaced out over several exchanges. The tool also gained a safety feature for Windows users that automatically cleans up the screen if the program crashes.

5ab9f24e10c3cafc301fe1eb3838c0c54008806f.text: The AI assistant now correctly translates its internal tool descriptions into a format the counting service understands, preventing errors when listing complex options. This fix applies to the agent's runtime logic. A non-programmer would notice fewer unexpected failures when the assistant tries to use tools that accept multiple types of input.

778ce13d412dcf87de7eec8b2732d27aa9c35c3a.text: The system now calculates the size of conversation history more accurately by measuring actual content instead of its raw text format. This prevents images from being incorrectly counted as massive blocks of text. The assistant can now handle longer conversations or larger screenshots without mistakenly deleting older messages to fit within its memory limits.

f8b3b17b3ed642b2fb5d7bea14d33db9aa340651.text: The name of the screen where you pick a model changed from 'waiting room' to 'landing screen' to better match what it actually does. This affects the command-line tool's interface, but you will not notice any change in how it works or looks.

2a0165cd6654c96138ebf48279da6271d3edb8d9.text: The system now recognizes blank labels as missing, forcing a default setting for specific tools. This fixes a hidden glitch in how data is described to the AI. Regular users will not notice any difference, as this is a small internal safety check.

7f595c4c0634c855c18f0cfb325c173392e3bd61.text: The text shown when starting a free session was updated. Instead of saying you are 'in the waiting room' or 'next in line', it now says 'Your free session is still being set up. Try again in a moment.' This applies to people using the free version who encounter a brief, rare delay when starting a session.

10ec4e5ad003a6c5bd72ba98ad322469581d3d69.text: The tools that let the assistant read and change files are no longer restricted to the current project folder. This allows the assistant to access files anywhere on the system, including absolute paths. Users will notice the assistant can now successfully open or modify files outside the project directory, whereas it previously refused such requests.

bd166f455bc3bee08e35e0cc212e4da6fbbe4f15.text: The assistant now automatically tries again if a brief network drop cuts off its connection to the server. This helps people using the assistant on unstable networks or specific setups where connection resets happen. They will see fewer sudden failures and no error messages for these short interruptions.

f7828c2c4b5a55de46b00f0484ed047e091d0964.text: The assistant now runs its work on a separate, always-on computer instead of inside the main database. This change applies to Freebuff, Codex, and Claude Code requests, making the streaming responses smoother and less prone to connection drops. It is live today for these services, meaning the assistant handles long tasks more reliably.

f65992d39adda73162606b55c07b364ca8afa181.text: The command-line tool now stops waiting for a server response after twenty seconds. This prevents the loading screen from freezing indefinitely if the connection hangs. If the request times out, the tool logs the error and automatically tries again after a short delay.

dc8f236d73ec651b392b4dbb09a8826258f12666.text: The service now quietly tells Reddit when a new person first tries the product and again when they return after one, seven, or twenty-four days. This helps the advertising team measure how well Reddit ads bring back customers. Regular users will see no change in the product itself, as this background reporting only happens if the company has set up their Reddit advertising account.

030a4c60e51b5da6ad04a6ac3e3470a7ce53b874.text: The system now tracks when users see ads in the chat interface to help compare different ad formats. This affects only people using the web chat, and it is not active for them yet. The tracking is set up to measure ad clicks and views, but the ads themselves have not changed or started showing differently.

cee618d4b5a9d00053d9955262595b276fd7ea1e.text: When the free trial time runs out, the program now pauses instead of trying to send messages that will be rejected. It keeps the messages waiting and automatically sends them if the session becomes active again. This only affects people using the free version.

8151087175d6205542190ed092126bdd19ae4130.text: The command-line tool now keeps your typed message at the front of the list if the free session ends right as it tries to send, rather than losing it. If the message fails to send because the session is gone, you will see an error on screen instead of the message looking like it went through. This change applies only to the free tier of the tool.

a07d73d1f0bdd5f9c47d64423d3837d59bcb2309.text: Codebuff's software tools now check where to send data when they run, rather than using an address fixed when the tool was built. This prevents a common error where tools running on remote servers try to contact a developer's local computer and fail. Developers who use these tools in cloud services will see fewer connection errors.

671c093077dc5cd74ab2b1892c7c134d84c8fbd8.text: The chat tool now saves your complete conversation history instead of deleting older messages after a certain point. It also uses a separate summary file to load your chat list faster. If you open your history, you will see all your past chats and the full text of older messages.

effaebabd70b475f18cd90481cc6cbc88c5ff9e3.text: The command-line assistant now saves your conversation to your computer the moment you send a message and repeatedly while it works. If your terminal closes unexpectedly, you won't lose that turn. When you reopen it, the assistant displays your last message and shows a note that the reply was interrupted.

4f5a72d6b85c9521b28248e359c11719cf6d55c4.text: A shared tool now prepares log records for storage, ensuring they stay within size limits and do not crash due to complex data structures. This applies to all system logs. You will not notice any immediate change in the application's behavior, as this is an internal maintenance update.

77cfee986c1b3e6fd7fffc5b37bb7c4028a30446.text: You can now stop the assistant while it is searching files, loading web pages, or running commands. Pressing stop immediately cancels the current task and closes any background programs it started. This change is live today for the assistant's built-in tools.

85ccc41bab5e0ee15d2cd97f2230055f4f2984b2.text: Freebuff Desktop now enforces a one-tab limit for all models on the LIMITED tier, while the FULL tier keeps its existing premium-bucket concurrency rule. If a LIMITED user tries to open a second tab, the app will show 'close a tab' instead of 'daily limit'.

0eb5e08fac20277f02c9f486b6176610e73431da.text: A new limit now allows users on the basic web plan in certain regions to create only one project per day. This cap resets every night at midnight Pacific time. If you are in this group, you will see a message preventing you from starting a second project until the next day.

b88380a4c48c5a1dfe12d788f62d794c5df7db57.text: The chat history tool now saves your conversation in a way that prevents a crash from destroying the record. It also shows a clear 'corrupted' warning for any broken files instead of hiding them, and starting a new chat or clearing history now creates a fresh folder so old conversations are never overwritten.

b10e9ab1644601375492fa771f2acd2088b27429.text: The software now combines the assistant's internal reasoning with its action requests into a single message when sending to DeepSeek V4. This fixes a validation error that previously blocked the model from processing these combined steps correctly. Users interacting with DeepSeek V4 will notice fewer failed requests during conversations that involve complex thinking and tool use.

d304465cf1503c0d27dc79e6ffaf252657fe922c.text: The desktop app now records when you see or click a sponsored ad in the chat history. This change is in place but does nothing yet, as the app does not currently display these ads. You will notice no difference until the ads feature is fully turned on.

b4989d0c77187ca908ff2417b1dfd4e68be25818.text: This small update fixes how the referral banner and waiting room display when the screen is short. It affects people using the command-line tool. Previously, if the window was too small, the text and buttons would overlap and look messy. Now, those sections keep their full size, so nothing gets squashed or hidden.

92a719efa08071eb2c6f0eb67079416304201adb.text: The desktop app now records every action for the first few users who open it, instead of randomly ignoring 99% of them. This helps the team see the true number of people launching the app and logging in. You would notice nothing; this only changes how the company counts usage behind the scenes.

9e61e4b90860c77829c87b675c5a7f002276ef9d.text: Previously, if a helper service failed to start, the assistant would show a vague 'connection closed' error and stop working completely. Now, the system captures the specific error message from the failed service and disables only that service's tools. This means the assistant continues to function normally using its other tools, while showing a clear reason for the missing feature.

e6af6ff08ba0ed02b362aae22b208e554fd5f74a.text: The software now remembers a working copy of custom instructions alongside its text version. This prevents rare crashes when the system tries to run these instructions. Developers building custom agents will see fewer unexpected errors, though the change is internal and requires no action from you.

425e9cb485d05a34b93c2abdf22a8e980fc2effb.text: The system now records a note each time it tries to create a name for a new chat. These notes track how long it took and if it worked, helping the team see performance issues. Regular users will notice no change, as this is only for internal monitoring.

454dcd2c72790576154d4ed6cc68d96bf47dad96.text: This small internal update lets the software accept new instructions while it is already working, without forcing it to stop and restart. It affects the underlying system that runs automated tasks. If you use a tool built on this system, you might notice it can now react to mid-task updates, though this feature is only available if the specific tool has been set up to use it.

a60a6abccdfcbbe6d3a72c17ed86dbc03810876a.text: Two changes arrived. Pressing Tab now places the highlighted command into the text box without running it, letting you add extra options; use arrow keys to pick items and Enter to run. Also, a new reward system grants an extra session for every seven-day streak, though it stays off until the company turns it on.

c7df706d4a2306da3d645b3d5091a718f0b057bc.text: When a user has used the command-line tool for seven days straight, a short note now appears under the model picker. This note explains the weekly reward for keeping the streak going, but it only promises a specific advanced model if that model is actually available to the user at that moment. This prevents the tool from advertising a reward that the user cannot currently claim.

b3c3decd0afb7d08f0ab70a80070a316c1547bab.text: The assistant now checks for new instruction files on your computer first, instead of using an old memory of them. If you add or update these files while working, the assistant sees the changes immediately. This helps users who manually install new skills or edit existing ones during a session.

8a96d48d79d02c951416f047ba4d2b269407b584.text: The software now counts the minutes a user spends actively working in the command-line tool. This tracking only happens for users on the Freebuff plan and only starts after the interactive screen is fully loaded. Users will not see any change, but the company now records how long each active user stays engaged.

ca8ddb859a773965c2058c74e401c818650f92d9.text: The coding assistant now skips the waiting room. When you pick a model, you go straight into the chat. This change is live today.

15c9fe6c7e7bff8436ca2e3f48cb699de7d56c55.text: In the desktop app, you can now only run one session at a time for certain advanced models, though simpler models allow unlimited tabs. If you try to open a second window with an advanced model, the app will block it and offer to switch to or close the existing session.

dd3e1e6aa9ef1bd11f446bb4cca0ceaf1ac3e89b.text: The referral banner now adjusts its size when the screen is narrow. Previously, the 'Copy Invite Link' button could get squished and cut off, and long text would not wrap correctly. Now, the button stays fully visible and the text flows properly.

979954f98423e67c331525052c100358fa1f97a4.text: The program now counts when a sign-in attempt starts, fails, times out, or is cancelled. This helps the team see how many people get stuck trying to log in from the command line versus the pop-up window. You will not notice any change in how the sign-in works.

5824dc1d4e6d9948220ac83e68c0254f775f08c7.text: Test bots now wait for any of several startup messages instead of just the logo. This fixes flaky checks on automated servers that sometimes show text instead of graphics. Regular users see no change.

eebd6089f2b07ee217e4367ccdf074effed29364.text: On the model selection screen, keyboard navigation now reaches the referral banner's buttons. Arrow keys move past the model list to the invite and switch options, letting people use them without a mouse. The change is live today.

55f61ffc60b73ecdfb31f8d649e85e4ff3086c0b.text: Users on the limited plan can now see a new banner in the command-line tool when they have a referral code. Instead of advertising a weekly unlock, this banner quietly shows how many daily free sessions they have earned by inviting friends, up to a daily limit. The banner layout was also fixed to prevent text overlapping, making the referral progress easier to read.

ec42536f50943a38138d63621738bf4a4e5bfa8f.text: The referral banner now hides itself for accounts that do not qualify for premium perks. It moved to sit below the daily streak line and replaced the plain web address with a button that copies the invitation link to your clipboard. The button now sends friends to a page that greets them by your name.

1bac5606860ccd893adeb9188103fde0d2bb93f6.text: The app now hides a special AI model from the main menu, showing it instead in a separate banner for people who have invited friends. If you refer friends, you earn one-hour sessions with this model each week, capped by a limit. The banner changes appearance depending on whether you have unlocked the reward or need to invite more people.

3e442f817a080ee0f2ac2ecd86193db9e2c7349f.text: The command-line tool now remembers a unique anonymous tag on your computer, so it can tell that your early visits before signing in came from the same person. When you log in, or when the tool restores a previous session, it records a login event. This fixes a reporting bug where returning users appeared to abandon the sign-in process.

95a1156a6015112ed1b82cb897df77395b0fd5b0.text: The model selection screen now displays a 'Press Enter' hint when the recommended option is highlighted. This helps people using the command-line interface know they can confirm their choice by pressing the key. The hint only appears on the main recommended option to keep the layout clean.

750dc9aaa60a81d5716bfe47380a859dd7159720.text: The planning and review commands no longer block people who haven't linked a ChatGPT account. They now run on the model you have selected. If you did link ChatGPT, the tool still hands the deep-thinking step to that account. This change is live today.

c0d984a61fa18c7fdb06b8132b63d3134abf5816.text: The tool now remembers the free model offer even after you use a session, so the banner stays visible when you return to the start screen. It also fixes a bug where text on a green button became invisible. These changes are live and affect anyone using the command-line interface.

538768ba9aaf73180427a125c12e05edf67fbbd6.text: The command-line interface now shows a daily reset timer for premium models even when you haven't used any yet. Previously, this countdown only appeared after you started using your sessions. This change affects only full-access premium users, letting them see exactly when their daily model allowance refreshes right from the start.

59f2ba13cee05f37282e74d3738adfe15633ef31.text: The automatic test that checks if the command-line tool starts correctly now tries three times instead of once. This helps prevent false failures when the test computer hangs briefly on startup, especially on Windows. Real crashes still fail immediately, so developers won't miss actual bugs.

b9439256f51364c82f6d6a551a213ae995a8813c.text: The waiting room screen now shows the large text logo when the model list is collapsed on medium-sized terminal windows, filling empty space. This change is live and affects CLI users with terminals at least 26 rows tall who keep the model list closed.

d38aa87d8f52653a6efbd545aba736173cf07a89.text: The system now correctly labels which specific assistant is thinking when multiple helpers work together. This fixes a bug where the label was wrong, meaning tools that display the thought process can now show the right name next to each thought. The change is live and affects anyone watching the assistant's reasoning steps.

a94090ee7b615e9cb447b239791b4a5fb1dde283.text: Paid Lite plan users now use a different AI engine for basic tasks. Free plan users and those who manually pick a specific model see no change. This update is live today.

692bf102f5e653d85d43fc32883c4d8366c537ef.text: The free coding tool's help pages were reorganized to put all instructions in one central place. New questions were added to explain which models are available based on your location and how the service pays for itself through ads. This is live now for anyone using the free version, though it only changes what you read in the manual, not how the tool works.

a4f5d94ecbd0e09f41c432abf7115b65eb498f3e.text: The command-line tool now sends usage data to the server even before you log in, rather than waiting until you are authenticated. This helps the company track how many people start using the tool versus those who complete registration. You will not notice any changes in your workflow or see new features, as this is a background data collection update.

2e94bb23cc19832c25dad3b04883f71a44fdd998.text: For premium users, the daily session count and reset timer now appear directly in the model selection menu header instead of below the list. Limited-tier users keep the counter below the list, while regular users see no counter when the menu is collapsed because their recommended option has no limit. This change is live and makes the usage information easier to find for premium members.

a54b61094c5a8b141e2d1f4dd365e538ffb8529c.text: The command-line tool now shows only the recommended model at startup, letting new users start with one Enter press instead of scanning a list. This applies only when the saved preference matches the recommendation; other cases remain expanded. The warning that MiniMax M3 collects data for training was removed because it is hosted differently now.

9c8af8c79c36649273421ef43e515b2fffe63be3.text: Running the coding tool from your personal home folder used to hide all file suggestions to protect your privacy. It now lists files in nearby folders, but it stops looking deeper after three levels to avoid scanning your entire computer. You will see a message under the file list explaining this limit and suggesting you start the tool from a specific project folder for complete results.

957b9d654a945dcb47e4d91b473f0212e1565ad3.text: The command-line tool no longer crashes when trying to open a web browser. This protects people running the tool in Linux environments without a graphical display, or in Windows Subsystem for Linux when it cannot reach the Windows system. Users will notice the tool stays open and keeps working instead of suddenly stopping.

f0c65d3132424eafe090f368fc5615f2ced05c62.text: The command-line tool now quietly copies important activity records to the company's central monitoring system. This helps the support team diagnose issues faster, but it happens in the background so you will not see any new messages or delays. You can turn this off by setting a specific environment variable to false.

8118a50f77cd572f2b9a82fb5e8525e23aec4d25.text: The command-line menu now shows countdown timers for Premium and Unlimited plans, and displays country names instead of codes. Limited access notices appear below the model list, but hide automatically if the terminal window is too small. These changes are live for all command-line users.

53e9e1ac09bee289c4fe62535ad8eaa07a6f2ff1.text: The login screen now checks if the web address is too long to fit on one line. If it wraps, a warning appears telling you that clicking the link will cut off the code, so you should press the 'c' key to copy the full address instead. This change is active and helps prevent login errors caused by incomplete links.

9d9e3f15ad1e2fd45a3501a73a9ea9d5acc8ed79.text: The web chat assistant can now recommend third-party developer services with setup links. When a user clicks one, the system records that the click came from the web chat instead of the command-line tool. This helps track which product drives traffic. The change is live today.

5f95e26baf6768feb52cc5e67519b4cede3d4a63.text: A new web-only setting for the free tier now blocks anonymous or Tor network users from sending messages, while limiting regular free web users to five one-hour sessions. These limited users can still use specific models like DeepSeek V4 Flash without counting against their session limit. This change is live for web users only and does not affect desktop app users.

f5aebdb4bd86f3c4c97f01039705133a9fd2eb8f.text: The tool that reads web links now checks every step of a link's journey to ensure it never accidentally connects to a private internal network. This protects the system from malicious links that try to redirect the reader to hidden internal addresses. If you try to read a link that redirects to a private network, the tool will stop and show an error instead of fetching the content.

6c85a772586aa5d0ba7760d5ee1cad1723317bf0.text: The chat assistant on the freebuff.com website now uses a faster version of its AI model, which makes replies appear sooner. This change only affects people chatting on that specific website page. The tools used by programmers in their terminals and the website builder still use the original, slightly smarter version of the AI.

ff6f49149b964e3c2f917756c7979cb61ecffe8d.text: The AI assistant now cleans up its working memory when a chat session is interrupted, preventing leftover data from causing issues. It also limits how many assistant templates it keeps in memory at once, stopping the system from slowing down over time. These fixes help keep the assistant running smoothly during long sessions without requiring any action from you.

241cc5bcc2452ac764d35c7d3557bd9490b1a852.text: The command-line tool now recognizes the Enter key correctly when used with a specific type of keyboard setup. Previously, pressing Enter alone was sometimes mistaken for a different command, causing unintended actions. This small internal fix ensures that Enter works as expected for users of that specific setup, with no visible change to the tool's appearance or features.

38401ec1b8df4542b80b71d41256a043e08f29be.text: The free AI assistant now defaults to the newer MiniMax M3 model instead of M2.7. You will see M3 listed as a free option in the model picker. The older M2.7 model is hidden from the list but still works for existing sessions until mid-June.

5d29036496273c2e61ccc2fb490f9c49826cc980.text: The command-line tool now shows the real reason for rate limit errors instead of a generic message. If a provider like Fireworks or OpenRouter blocks a request, the tool displays their specific explanation alongside the standard notice. This helps users understand exactly why a request failed and what to do next.

f34d91198316b40f048582b71a9aa915bac94a52.text: The system that builds the list of available actions for the assistant now allows developers to specify exactly which actions to include, rather than always pulling the entire global list. This change is internal and affects only the developers writing tests or building specific configurations. Customers will not notice any difference in the assistant's behavior today.

e72bcc94a0acd7187855a568de78d5e8cfc49f74.text: The assistant now automatically fixes conversation records before sending them to newer Claude models, which previously rejected requests ending with an assistant message. This affects users routing these models through Amazon Bedrock, preventing failed agent runs that previously produced error files.

409f05fafae7718d0ff9fa5979f74f309b7bc5c0.text: The text tool now recognizes when it is running inside a cloud coding environment or a remote editor where its usual automatic copy method silently fails. Instead of trying to copy text and doing nothing, it immediately tells you to hold the Shift key while dragging your mouse to select text. This helps you successfully copy answers without wondering why the usual button is not working.

370bbb64e5b86de777b8ded4303ad082fcf80b06.text: The web referral system now requires new signups to have a GitHub account at least four months old to count toward rewards. This prevents people from creating fake accounts to game the system. Users who refer eligible friends will see their daily usage limits increase and the 'Powered by Freebuff' watermark removed from their deployments.

6f79426bd3986cb1cd77168c2e80b2ad53862550.text: A small formatting rule was added for places that show subscription access counts. It would list full access, limited access, and unknown access with English-formatted numbers, and show a dash if a count is missing. It is not live today, so no one will notice a change yet.

10144f7ad1bd85fa528642276370444f1862214b.text: A safety step was added to the login screen for test accounts used by the development team. This change prevents the page from breaking by keeping certain server-only details out of the browser. It is active today and ensures the test login button works correctly without causing errors.

360988f0ed5f75d567ab892ee251a9fa0fcde802.text: The assistant now looks up third-party services like databases or email providers in a live catalog instead of relying on memory. This change is active and ensures recommendations are current. When the assistant checks this catalog, the screen displays the action as a clear, bold label starting with 'Services' followed by what it is doing, such as 'Services · Search'.

1dd01919a42648d9da8f473c4f84b3b0b55b8605.text: A small internal cleanup removed the code that used to turn configuration mistakes into friendly, clickable error messages in the command-line chat. This only affects people who run the tool on their own computer. They won't notice anything today, because the tool already has another way to show these errors.

afc8351b5b724273614569816b30691f1fecf536.text: The AI assistant no longer offers a paid, slow deep-research mode. It now only uses a standard web search. This affects users who previously asked the assistant to perform expensive, multi-step research tasks.

0ce5fb0b7d299ff3a646c2785016dd3287928df3.text: The project's public website now forces visitors to choose a specific form (bug, feature, or account issue) instead of writing free text. This helps the team sort requests faster and sends people with simple usage questions to a chat server instead. These new forms and automatic checks are live for the public repository.

df64ef498a3fb6d30d36e94869a65e2fed60f6f5.text: The SDK's AI package was upgraded to a newer version, which now requires a newer runtime environment to function. This change affects developers building with the SDK, who must update their environment to proceed. If they use the older runtime, the SDK will fail to load.

270a776296bc67ae0369762cf91bc6b047ec9f69.text: The system now knows which models are premium and which can handle images. This means users will see a clear badge and daily limit for premium models, and their uploaded photos will actually be understood by the specific models that support them, rather than being ignored.

6f2db456ac3170ab87b7099c362f20f295369fb3.text: The team rebuilt how they check the program's automatic screen-reset safety feature. Instead of starting and stopping the test setup for every single check, they now start them all at once and share a single time limit. This stops slow test computers from reporting false failures and gives clearer error messages if a test times out, helping the developers see real problems faster.

126f792988825047c0b547dcf5f7bfb27ae9000d.text: The system now automatically tags requests sent to external AI providers with a specific name and website. This helps the providers identify where the traffic comes from. Users will not see any change in how the software works.

68b34fa74dd1efa2451b9a4a6df7f5a15ba2a2b3.text: The assistant now only reads project instructions from files named AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, ignoring knowledge.md. New projects automatically create AGENTS.md instead of knowledge.md. Existing knowledge.md files will be ignored.

0b35949fad7bbaf605afbd048ca912c14d4a3173.text: When the assistant finishes planning a new blank cloud project, it now shows a 'Start building' button. This change applies only to users starting blank cloud projects. The assistant will pause and wait for approval before writing any code.

a4837a425cd7f9ac57d590d53a9ef1bc20fa63f6.text: The search tool now includes a version built specifically for newer Windows computers with ARM processors. This means these users can search files faster and more reliably without needing extra software or workarounds.

9ac3cfaccbda1e5eefac4a136587406f1bf5fe83.text: The software now correctly identifies files that are truly inside your project folder, rather than just looking at their names. This prevents the program from accidentally reading or ignoring files that are actually located outside your project. You might notice that file lists are now more accurate and secure.

385a72397d899dcd80b9715f1b86adff24faa644.text: Starting the command-line tool now checks if you have set a spending cap for your wallet. If you have not set one, the tool will stop and ask you to confirm your limit before letting you begin. This only affects people who use the tool's built-in payment system, not those using their own separate keys.

17d6db8ba087352b631923ba3e14852fcbc18b9d.text: A new internal check was added to automatically verify that the command-line tool can update itself correctly on all major computer types. This change is strictly for the engineering team to ensure release stability and does not affect how the software behaves for everyday users.

380909638150bde314b3d4eb96bcd7664fa07529.text: The command-line tool now uses a single routine to shut down, regardless of whether you type the exit command or press the interrupt key combination. This ensures the program always releases its connection and resets your terminal screen correctly, preventing it from appearing broken or stuck after closing.

8e956567928c769287011b3a1b8974d8d646631a.text: The test suite now prepares its own settings and missing files automatically before checking the code. This fixes a problem where tests would silently skip entire sections, making it look like everything passed when it actually didn't. Developers running checks on new copies of the project will now see accurate results instead of false green lights.

2bb0662c5dd481ddb3bb79db171548568e33e9a5.text: The code that checks for updates and installs new versions of the command-line tools was consolidated into a single shared location. This change affects the internal maintenance of the software, ensuring all three tools use the same update mechanism. Customers will not notice any difference in how the tools behave or look.

89ef2b771d74e90e173c03c80e5a0b7e1285932f.text: The command-line tool now labels its service actions with simple, direct phrases like 'Search services' instead of formal brand names. Buttons on screen changed from solid colored blocks to outlined shapes that underline when your mouse hovers over them. The assistant's list of available models updated to show that Kimi and MiniMax M3 can now understand images and text together.

c4a838fedc84d87b1640d62047cc4aa7bff923b4.text: The command-line tool now tries downloading updates up to three times if the connection fails, waits longer for large files, and handles more types of web redirects. This helps users who experience flaky networks or download interruptions. You might notice fewer 'download failed' errors when updating the tool.

07ab1c6445e0e36697f749f10d34eccea254b5e5.text: The system now records activity details for this specific runner service in a uniform format, making it easier to trace events and errors. This update is internal and primarily benefits the operations team by improving how they monitor the service's health and troubleshoot issues. End users will not see any changes in the application interface or performance.

122933fd79cf8b99c6346050f96fc8dc56649141.text: The command-line tool now gets its login web address from a shared list instead of using its own copy. This only affects people who sign in through the terminal. Nothing changes for them today, but it means the terminal and the desktop app will always send users to the exact same website for login.

a6455dbd1cff1467ef80a3c7ce9d364e19756b09.text: The tool now uses a new, more capable assistant model for its most advanced reasoning tasks, replacing the previous one. This change applies only to users on the highest-tier plan, who will see the tool make better choices when solving complex problems. For everyone else, the tool continues to use its standard, less expensive model.

44cbd349993e6f82827d8ca66c2b3dcf6634ce31.text: A new automated reviewer was added specifically for the MiniMax M3 model. This change allows users selecting this model to receive code reviews, a feature previously disabled for it. The update is live and applies only to those using the MiniMax M3 option.

f1a5a202b3505df7216651ab21560dd053faf148.text: The command-line tool now checks your Windows computer's processor speed capability by asking the operating system directly, rather than guessing from the processor's name. This check happens once and is remembered, so the tool starts quickly on later uses. If the tool cannot determine the capability, it assumes the processor is fast enough for this session but will try again next time.

209f11b0fb3bcd73c25e68d691e48144f7cc001d.text: The program now shows one ad instead of a list of ads while you are chatting. This change is live for people using the free version or who have turned on ads. You would see a single ad card appear in the chat window rather than several choices to pick from.

c63b7942c4944f02b89d0326a45adaa3d0c3ff45.text: The freebuff.com chat page now uses a specific AI model that only answers text questions. This model cannot look at files or use other tools, so it acts as a simple conversation partner. Users chatting on the web will see responses generated by this new, restricted setup.

25b2071a417f2e28570f4f40d4cfede17d45a0e7.text: A new background tool now groups response-time data into small ranges so the system can accurately combine hourly numbers into daily averages. This affects the internal dashboard showing how quickly the assistant replies. You will not see any immediate change on your screen, as this is an invisible update to how data is stored and calculated.

2f7f2db929542d200cc6a617dcc3cabd83aaf557.text: The system gained a new backend capability to let the assistant connect to and use outside applications. This feature is currently switched off and does nothing for anyone today. Once turned on, it will allow the assistant to search for, connect to, and run actions in external apps directly from the chat.

e39f9da8bc239a0b8c08ee3014e7ec7c2a287c41.text: The free AI assistant now lets you pick the MiniMax M3 model. This model is marked premium, so choosing it uses your paid allowance instead of the free tier. You will see it listed as 'Frontier' in the model menu.

874c8ec4aabb8c0db77ffe375d5edd248402a83a.text: A new coding assistant is now available for testing. You can select it to generate code, and it uses a different underlying engine than previous options.

28d560182de8500514e34ac4079426b3c965675e.text: The code that lets the assistant talk to different AI services was moved out of the private server area into its own public section. This internal cleanup means the tool you install no longer carries around hidden server-only parts. You will not see any changes in how it works today; it is just a tidier structure for the engineers.

d2ae8a0dc59e09d6a13717590ebdd0fd9e2b3dfa.text: The app's top banner now hides when you scroll past it, and the animation stops when hidden. Long command outputs no longer fill up your computer's memory, keeping only the start and end. These changes are live now.

6200a7bfdbdb111a8b2b94680839ae774b78dc41.text: Internal staff now have a tool to remove specific user accounts from the main database. The tool shows a preview of what will be deleted before doing anything, requiring explicit confirmation to proceed. It only affects the main database; billing and marketing systems remain unchanged.

0e3a2e3a4b1ecfbbd704e53d500087469d665ea9.text: The system now counts how many conversations with the AI are happening at the same time. This helps the internal team see when the service gets busy or slows down. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the app works.

1b5ba7995640155ea933ea7343e3ca8614fbf6b1.text: The command-line tool now recognizes the Enter key on numeric keypads, ensuring it submits messages correctly instead of being ignored. This affects people using a keyboard with a number pad when typing into the chat or selection prompts. Previously, pressing that specific Enter key might have done nothing or inserted a line break unexpectedly; now it behaves like the main Enter key.

6f4dbb428ef40c0f3aaa2d30d97d8f9b51c9d5fa.text: The command-line tool now displays a clear 'Web Search' label and the exact search terms when the assistant looks up information online. Previously, these actions appeared as generic or unreadable text. This change is live immediately for anyone using the command-line interface.

bc108e4bf8cc7d6f36a31989dbb76dd20e9d0d4e.text: The web-research assistant can now read web pages directly instead of running complex technical commands. This change is live and affects anyone using the research feature. Users will notice the assistant gathers information from source pages more smoothly and reliably.

17e14b8a31610135a829565584f8fbc36860041e.text: The AI assistant can now fetch and read content from web links. This feature is active for all users today. You will see a small 'Read URL' line appear in the chat window, showing the specific web address being visited.

d555af2e5b1448463bf81cbb73702e6de7e7003a.text: A new internal tool lets staff download recent AI conversation logs from the company's database. It automatically hides passwords and secret keys in the saved files. This helps the team investigate issues, but regular users will not notice any change.

6c000e2fb5fcd6455833bc4e8ef3b40662e05bcb.text: The program now tracks when you click an ad in the chat or waiting room. This applies to free users. You will see no change in the app, but the company records the click to measure ad performance.

a11f5b9bcc8ef033701e8c20747ebf4f7e70deee.text: The research assistant now uses Google search results instead of a different provider, and can directly download web pages to read them. This is live today. You will notice the assistant provides raw search links and snippets rather than a pre-summarized answer, and may cite specific pages more directly.

cd83f663cb98745c005bd8ef51efcdf67cdf5f15.text: The assistant now understands full file locations, not just shortcuts. This fixes a bug where it failed to show file contents if the path was written out completely. People using the agent to view code will see accurate results without needing to adjust how they ask for files.

a85cb595b5dece0859ec6bb1d05f898d79ad0fdf.text: Internal tools now gather complete chat histories from two specific free trial services into a single file. This helps staff review how these trials work by looking at saved records from the past few months. Nothing changes for people using the service today.

8cca5ab9b098ec1421e51a7c41b5eb13be0d2cda.text: The project guide now includes a full Chinese translation alongside the English version. Chinese-speaking readers can access the same instructions for installing the tool and creating custom tasks without needing to read English. This update is live and simply provides a language option for the existing information.

b1e92cb142e6cb222c6b54d9db58b5c4ac5a0109.text: The homepage now only updates its live usage counters when you actually scroll to see that section. If the section is off-screen or your browser tab is hidden, the numbers freeze. This saves data and battery for visitors who do not view the stats area.

b5460a424824ba881c15a718cdba566112678666.text: The free service now checks a visitor's internet address against a second fraud-reporting company before granting full access. If this new check finds any signs of hidden traffic or data center use, the visitor is restricted to limited access instead. This change is live and affects people trying to use the free version without paying.

f29db9e9ef09c89801ac25e7eaebe384991403b5.text: The world map showing where people use the service now displays accurate country shapes instead of rough outlines. This update is live on the website. Visitors will see a realistic map with dots correctly placed in the middle of each country.

a3dbf723659094910c2cf7d85ec5535dadc3bd98.text: Freebuff now rejects connections from VPNs, proxies, and Tor networks. This affects people using these tools to access the free service. They will see a specific message stating 'VPN or Tor' and their session will end.

6a1803431b6de7e4b6e4519bedfec9e164604a5b.text: A new shortcut lets you switch to a different AI model without typing the long command. You can now type '/model' to end your current session and pick a new model from the list. This change is live now.

14fa5cb720bc6ffa0a47767e93d43d21fb01fb9a.text: The system now keeps a running log of each chat request, saving only the new parts instead of the entire conversation every time. This change helps the support team spot repeated questions and fix slow responses. You won't see any difference in how the app works today.

30c51ac38ce89001a9a39a00416a2d56ad446fce.text: The program now builds Windows versions to work on older computers. This helps people with basic machines run it without errors. You will see this in the next update.

4fb13aebd6a2e8db8ea0f3af3c48be8c74fa0c6f.text: The login system now checks the temporary access key from the command-line tool before using it. If the key is malformed or invalid, the system discards it instead of passing it along, which prevents broken login attempts. This affects only people signing in through the command-line tool; they will see a standard login screen without errors caused by bad keys.

62c807a76b20fde83dc17bad79d7e787a864c538.text: The system now digs through layers of wrapper messages to find the real reason a request failed. This fixes the issue where a retry attempt hid the actual problem, causing the tool to show a generic error instead of the specific cause. Developers using the software will see accurate failure details, like a missing credit or a blocked region, right away.

092de618a0779bc979a7077e49bf77725042e455.text: The free service now checks a second source to confirm whether a user is hiding their location with a VPN or proxy. This helps ordinary people in approved countries keep full access even if the first check mistakenly flags them as suspicious. If the new check fails or confirms a real VPN, the person sees a reduced set of models instead of full access.

af4e0fe1473a8a441a36d071db2cfda4dd30c3b2.text: Free-tier users now see a simple confirmation screen before starting a session, instead of a confusing model selection list. The interface removes internal labels like 'limited' from session counters, so it just says 'sessions' next to your usage count. This change is live today.

2952274587e48f57472f4a9faad67b18d93b91d8.text: The system now skips the step where it records a charge for free-plan requests, since these requests cost nothing anyway. It also reduces the amount of background data sent to monitoring tools for these free requests, keeping only one out of every hundred. Free-plan users should experience faster response times, while paid users remain unaffected.

ec28ae51ea968f910d1f03f1437dfff41fb7d6a4.text: A new public page now shows a live map of where people are using the free service and which AI models they pick. Regular visitors see the map update every fifteen seconds, while banned or expired accounts are hidden from the count. The bottom menu links disappear on this specific page to keep the map clear.

317a5c0532048c69209010f9de87f1f07a740b8e.text: The command-line tool now tells ad networks it is not a web browser when asking for ads. This ensures the ad networks correctly recognize and bill for this traffic. Advertisers will see accurate reporting for command-line users, while the ad experience for those users stays the same.

2506de227fbcba2c132e11a237f66f8e99d4e426.text: Freebuff now offers a restricted DeepSeek option in its model picker. This affects only people choosing that specific model, who will see a separate, smaller daily usage limit instead of the standard allowance. The screens clearly label these as limited sessions so you know which quota you are spending.

201c08b9fa1066d53695d27fa0645bd19abd8216.text: The program now records only one out of every hundred routine activity reports to save space. Normal users see no change, but support staff can set a special switch to capture full details for specific accounts during troubleshooting. This adjustment is active immediately.

efbd0b6f44586275607d449a3052d0d12c8ff41a.text: The system now remembers the location permission check for free users, so it does not need to re-verify their country on every request. This change is internal and live; users will notice no visible difference, but the service will respond slightly faster by skipping repeated location lookups.

ebe848f548bd41e22004128e7960267c059e4693.text: A countdown timer now appears in the waiting room for premium Freebuff sessions, showing how long until your usage limit resets at midnight Pacific time. This helps premium users see exactly when they can start a new session without waiting for the limit to expire.

64b0a93ed00b4dfd435cc8f80083b8d9f201a73b.text: The code search tool now caps memory use when scanning large projects. This prevents crashes when indexing files. Developers will notice the tool stops scanning if it hits size limits, protecting system stability.

5c6068411b13dda14ab547b54853ea8f9839b5cc.text: When a helper tool runs without a main instruction, the screen now shows what it was asked to summarize instead of leaving the space blank. This only affects that specific summarization tool; other helpers look the same. The change is live and visible immediately in the text interface.

bf767d70cac9d83e2918bcde03b419260fb4626f.text: Ads now show the brand name as the headline instead of a generic label. The description text uses the main content, falling back to the subtitle only if needed. This fixes ads that previously displayed incorrect or confusing titles.

f01f29111f35346d3db3a579c82ffc1e4d8af610.text: A new, faster AI option was added to the free tier's model menu. Users selecting this new option will notice quicker responses and lower resource usage compared to the existing 'smartest' model. Additionally, the previous top-tier free model was updated to allow it to ask clarifying questions, making it more interactive.

f1b6d70380846b0af254ec8d85c8241ff545cae4.text: When a command-line login code is used, the system now marks it as consumed rather than erasing it. This allows the service to tell the difference between an expired code and one that has already been used, providing a more specific error message if you try to log in twice with the same code. The change is live for all CLI users.

16137ba62ca6a9b7edb2b431898962c2ef05b8ea.text: The sign-in process now accepts older-style login codes that use dashes instead of dots. This helps people using outdated versions of the command-line tool sign in successfully. If they tried before, they would have seen an error; now, the login will work as expected.

3f698f5a0cd76738416987f6faaad900a70cbef5.text: The text-based app now shows ads from a second ad network when the first one has no ads to display. This only affects free users who see ads while waiting for a response. They will notice a different company's ad appear in the same spot when the main ad source is empty.

a97f891c79334434dad209d7d957a3dfc5abe21c.text: The command-line chat history screen now includes a delete option. Users can remove specific past conversations from their local storage. This feature is live in the current version.

ef6b4ef531ea4711a7407fe672c5f4f5db1e3857.text: The search tool now hides its raw data feed from the command line interface. Instead, it displays a clean summary showing the number of matches found. This change is live and affects anyone using the CLI search feature, making results easier to read without technical clutter.

66648012945c0d1c4002c9b8a370cee1d0735547.text: A small internal update turned on two settings for the AI assistant, letting it track goals and work in different collaboration styles. This affects only the internal team using the assistant, not regular customers. They might notice the assistant following plans more closely or changing how it interacts, but the settings are just enabled and may not be fully active yet.

1a1f7ed3086c3ee50485d777eb0910e9f64fa8ed.text: The command-line tool now automatically picks the right free assistant based on the model you select. Instead of using a single fixed helper, it chooses specific versions for Kimi, DeepSeek, or MiniMax. This ensures the assistant matches your chosen model's capabilities, though the core behavior remains similar for current free users.

5b1551b55d29b3585fe0dacd20a39624d89a42fc.text: The command-line tool now displays a daily usage count on the end-of-session screen. This affects users of the premium free tier. The banner shows how many sessions have been used out of the total allowed, and the border turns amber when the limit is reached.

48caa4cc399c3d7f3522f8d65492c7c007bea9fc.text: The file-handling system now accepts full file addresses if they point inside the current project folder, while still blocking access to files outside it. This update affects the software development kit (SDK) used by applications to interact with the codebase. Users will not see any visible interface changes, but the underlying tool will more reliably locate files when given a complete address.

e58596f99351e5b8fc4639b2fb115c076019a668.text: The system now recognizes two new AI models but keeps them switched off. If a user tries to select either model, the request will be rejected with a message stating they are currently disabled. This change is internal preparation and does not offer new features to anyone today.

df40341c78a885040817d1503f7569c250586f0a.text: The free AI assistant now automatically picks the right reviewer for the specific model it is using, instead of relying on manual settings. This affects people using the free plan with DeepSeek, Kimi, or MiniMax models. You will not see any changes in the interface; the assistant just ensures the correct reviewer is active behind the scenes.

7e3fc2306e2b347b4384a11dac1c9fd9ee173f61.text: The system can now use a new AI model from Moonshot. This is not live for anyone yet because the required connection key is not set up. Once a key is added, users who choose this model will get answers from Moonshot instead of the usual providers.

3dd5916285c3912ebb279fddca5875a5de34dcac.text: The login page now checks the expiration time of temporary access codes more reliably. Previously, if a code had an unexpected format, the page might crash or fail to recognize that the code had expired. Now, the system safely reads the code and correctly shows the 'expired' message when needed. This change is live today and affects anyone trying to log in using these temporary codes.

3afccad624c4f906a74a68fb427af3b43947ec8e.text: The testing system can now run a specific external coding assistant called OpenCode to compare its performance against others. This affects the internal team evaluating different AI tools, not regular users. If they looked, they would see a new option available in their test setup that requires installing the OpenCode software and setting up an API key to work.

264e94a343652ebc6ab665d9f3e7810b107471cd.text: The assistant stopped using predictable labels for its internal actions, switching back to random ones. This change is internal, affecting only how the software tracks tasks behind the scenes. You would not notice any difference in your experience.

8ac94a54affac0eea3470c33444b18393683fa02.text: New accounts now get 500 free credits once when they sign up, instead of getting them every month. Existing users who previously had monthly free credits keep them. The usage screen now says 'Cycle' instead of 'Renews'.

a08c0c90242c4b8ee9b33db2cbd0865a6c1a672b.text: The command-line tool now uses a fixed web address for login links instead of guessing from the current connection. This prevents login errors caused by slight differences in website addresses, such as adding or removing 'www'. The change applies to production environments, where local testing addresses are automatically ignored.

f1af5d0a51e49608ddda053bf92a70b51897aed0.text: Search results now list matches by file with line numbers and a total count. This helps non-programmers scan results faster. The change is live today for SDK users.

495d067c21d83b01b7d3cbd3e820640af3f829db.text: The AI assistant now labels each action it takes with a predictable name instead of a random one. This fixes a glitch where retrying a failed step could confuse the system or duplicate work. You will notice smoother recovery when the assistant has to try a task again.

dc68d3253980fb05661f464748e33fd3d7b541e7.text: The command-line tool now automatically takes over a previous session if the original program stopped running without closing properly. This affects Freebuff CLI users, preventing the need to manually confirm the takeover when restarting quickly. If you see a seat already held by a dead process, the tool will silently resume your session instead of showing a prompt.

881686fe8d94809b7f42b6b88a2ab055f0d19928.text: Freebuff premium session limits now reset every day at midnight Pacific time instead of rolling off after 20 hours. This affects users with premium access who run multiple sessions daily. You will notice the counter for used sessions clears completely at midnight, giving you a fresh set of five sessions each day.

40d8fb340c38df153c7f983458b8ed5cbd72c32d.text: The assistant now clearly marks older chat history as background notes so it stops copying that old style when writing new replies. This affects anyone using long-running agent chats where the assistant reads files or runs commands. You would notice the assistant follows your current instructions better instead of getting confused by past summaries.

5904a9d5b789538679ef7cc195fbdb23ffbbb5a8.text: DeepSeek, Kimi, and GLM now limit free use to 5 sessions or 20 hours, while MiniMax stays unlimited. The tool now shows your remaining time and session count before you join a queue.

9239f01da08d3fa52576091332d67600e7de424c.text: The check that confirms a command-line login was fixed to find the correct session faster and more reliably. This helps people signing in from a terminal. They might notice login screens responding quicker or failing less often.

036ac8dfecd00c04eaef278aa01451a5bae20e6d.text: The command-line tool now downloads a necessary data file separately instead of hiding it inside the main program. This fixes a bug where Windows users experienced crashes because the hidden file was getting corrupted or lost during installation. If you use Windows, the tool should now start up correctly without errors.

d9fd69ae973bef525b620e0b7e119c1722b2b6ef.text: Fixed the text editor's grammar checker so it starts reliably on Windows. Before, the checker's data was stored in a way that the system sometimes dropped during the build, causing startup failures. Now the data is attached as a separate file that the system can always find. You will not notice any change unless you previously saw errors when opening the tool.

88e6e0ea1df2136b01e101ad1400ec6a99c09564.text: The team added a new check to their automatic testing system. This check runs the command-line tool for a few seconds to catch hidden startup problems that older, quicker tests missed. It helps ensure the tool launches reliably for everyone before it is released.

bb658a1142f7c975a92bc0df098c14334f3368c4.text: The command-line tool now bundles its syntax parser differently to prevent a bug that caused the tool to crash or fail to load on Windows computers. This change ensures the tool works correctly for anyone using it on Windows, without requiring any action from you.

1550c8b8a10e07887a59a17c93994e1151a67d91.text: The command-line tool now carries its code-analysis engine inside itself instead of looking for it in a separate file. This stops the tool from crashing when it starts up on Windows. You will notice the tool now opens reliably on Windows instead of failing silently.

c7e9ba8a29b3f460f901969cdcdd6fadf01b89ee.text: The app deleted an old sign-in button for a paid service that was already turned off for most people. This change cleans up the program's inner workings and removes a confusing option. If you looked at the menu, you would notice one fewer item listed.

6f223bf1d7c66c3b444cb4408748480c6d28905f.text: The command-line tool now carries its own language-parsing engine inside the single file you download. This fixes a bug where the tool looked for that engine in a folder from the developer's computer, which doesn't exist on yours. You will notice the tool stops crashing when it tries to understand your code.

d14ae806ccc679972f645f18c4626c742992bc96.text: The system now cleans up messy instructions sent by the assistant's brain before acting on them. It fixes cases where text is wrapped in extra symbols or uses the wrong names for file edits. You will notice fewer failed attempts when the assistant tries to find files or change code.

9b25609a250d7a9bf8b783d0305e212f76f681e8.text: Free Kimi users can now quietly ask Gemini for deeper thinking. This happens automatically when Kimi is selected, so users won't see a new button, but answers may become more thorough.

e781c56c1fd0f019f31795d09fe47b9296ebf740.text: The assistant now shows clickable buttons in the command line interface when it wants you to open a web link. Clicking the button immediately opens that link in your default browser. This feature is active for standard interactive sessions, but it is disabled in fast or free modes.

51359eead23d0c4ffee32cb78a61638ab3fc63f2.text: A new free AI assistant option using DeepSeek V4 Pro is now available for users who have set up their own DeepSeek account key. While this model can perform complex reasoning, its internal thought process is currently hidden from the chat history to ensure stability, meaning you only see the final answers.

744f49cda0f96748aec3e1b875f8c9a01ef009e4.text: The free command-line tool now lists a new powerful option at the top of its model menu. This applies to users on the free plan. When they open the tool, they see 'Gemini 3.1 Pro' as the first choice, marked as the deepest model available once per day.

2fdffcfa789703e0505995fccb30c422c778ab1c.text: The command-line tool now displays plain English summaries when it searches for or lists services. Instead of showing raw technical data, you see simple phrases like 'Searching for payment providers' or 'Listing service categories.' This change is live and affects anyone using the tool to look up services, making the activity easier to follow at a glance.

eb47be392d867a2a8a0235cb993ff4d2af6d6c09.text: People using the free version of this service who hide their location with a VPN or proxy will now be blocked from starting a session or sending messages. If the system's location-checking key is missing, the service fails to start instead of letting everyone in. This rule applies only to free mode, not paid plans.

c4d0d72a10dc26f2e55ce5c2dd709accf0b500af.text: The free coding assistant now uses a different default model. The paid lite version switched to a model that does not retain user data, while the free version uses a model that displays a privacy warning before selection. The interface also hides extra reasoning features for models that cannot use them.

40d0a34ee8bd80033063f06c33855d67d09fdb9a.text: The assistant can now search a directory of third-party services to help you find and connect tools like databases or email providers. This feature is currently hidden behind a setting and does not appear in the interface until enabled.

41a0f4dcb878a8912518a1677857235b3343612e.text: The free version of the coding assistant now uses Kimi K2.6 instead of GLM 5.1 for tasks like editing code and reviewing changes. This switch is live today. Users will notice the assistant's name in the menu has changed, and its responses may differ slightly in style or accuracy due to the new underlying model.

f33c1ebf082f796f6c975627d3cb6b75bb9f980f.text: Freebuff now checks your location and privacy tools before letting you start a session. If it cannot confirm your country or your connection looks hidden, the session is blocked instead of guessing. This affects people trying to use the free service; they will see a rejection if their location is unclear or if they use a VPN or Tor.

25213224df77f64c13bf40df22bf7b2cc4360a93.text: The system now automatically fixes small formatting errors when sending requests to Kimi AI models, ensuring they accept the data. This change affects only those specific models and is live today. Users will not see any visual difference, but the software avoids silent failures when Kimi is used.

a2ded144546c3a4535002cb8ae78cda4dcce08ae.text: The ad banner in the command-line tool now displays the ad's title if its web link is missing, instead of leaving that spot blank. This helps people using the tool understand what the ad is about even when the link is broken. The change is live today.

dffc7e4372e2972a6b191c42e9365ef32a176a71.text: Free users trying to start a GLM 5.1 chat now face a hard limit of five sessions every twenty hours. If they hit this cap, the command-line tool displays a waiting screen showing exactly how many sessions they have used and how long they must wait before starting another one.

a452cabacaf1a0241a39bf657c576840943fba9d.text: The free version now blocks requests when the system cannot confirm the user's location, treating hidden or unknown connections as ineligible. This stops people using privacy tools or those in unsupported regions from accessing the service. If affected, the user sees a specific message saying the location could not be verified, rather than waiting in a queue before being rejected.

b6b99666858e977fb2a300dcf1f8d4c80e018654.text: The free service now tells you exactly why it blocked your connection, showing specific labels like 'VPN' or 'Tor' instead of a vague error. This change applies to the command-line tool and is live today. You would notice the waiting screen displaying the precise reason your location or network was rejected.

3e4179228dddec236914b4fd5e0c7538ecb2da92.text: The waiting room screen now shows ads from Carbon instead of the previous Gravity network. This change is live today for users waiting in the CLI. Users will notice different ad content while waiting, but the ads inside the chat remain unchanged.

8b4f89224820c1cd509317e70450de8042486e3d.text: The internal team changed how the database updates itself during deployments. This affects only the software engineers who manage the database. If they looked, they would see the update tool now checks a specific list to apply changes safely instead of guessing, requiring a one-time setup step for existing systems.

79ce156d76a8b978bdd7425f4b66bff19b6827c6.text: People using the free version of the coding assistant can now choose which computer brain to use while waiting in line. The waiting room shows how many people are ahead of them for each choice, and typing a new command lets them leave their current session to switch.

d77b15357e72be57e8dc063f158ad87368fb7a55.text: The free model picker now shows what time you can use it based on your own location instead of a fixed East Coast schedule. This helps you avoid confusion about whether the service is open right now. The change is live in the command-line tool.

ff675681689666dabad9e8a9172bc40aaa557b99.text: The command-line tool now shows a choice of several ads instead of just one, so people using the free version will see a row of options rather than a single banner. This change also removed the manual button that let you turn off ads in the chat window, meaning you can no longer hide them that way. This update is live today.

57f569e59749eb959251d5293e64f60294a2c64b.text: The system now checks for suspicious free-tier usage every hour and emails a list of suspected bots to the admin. It does not automatically ban anyone; it only flags accounts for human review. Regular users will see no change, but this helps prevent abuse of the free service.

f872c7ae18bc99433babb66eaa22ec7f2a0cf695.text: The command-line tool now identifies your computer by a fixed hardware signature instead of a random number that changes every time. This makes logging in more consistent, so the tool recognizes the same machine across sessions. You will not see any visual changes, but the login process will link to your specific device rather than a temporary identifier.

ec7051080c95a60952a7b243e4c7a89a793c63aa.text: The team set the AI assistant to automatically allow routine file edits and commands within this project's workspace. Only the internal assistant tooling is affected; the customer-facing application remains unchanged. Users will not notice any difference in the product's behavior.

f2386263397b6d6e6d4473c00622d45d3d027ee2.text: The assistant now saves your conversation history even if a technical error stops it mid-task. This prevents your message from being lost or duplicated when the system restarts. The change is live today.

8e39fa2e032c9956dd80ae84cc8f4d1c3420dca5.text: The free AI coding assistant now restricts access to one specific model, making it available only during business hours on weekdays. A new alternative model has been added for continuous use, while older options have been removed. If you try to use the restricted model outside these hours, the system automatically switches you to the always-available option.

c3a379ac7a9ae375387a052e2cb5a2ed48b5cea6.text: The free version of this tool now checks your location before letting you into the waiting room. If you live outside the supported countries, you will see a message saying the service is unavailable in your region instead of waiting in a queue. This applies to the free plan only and is active immediately.

f7bda6243190a9d7853e0dfc16c0c808ac7271de.text: The command-line menu for choosing models now handles keyboard input more reliably. Pressing Enter or Space correctly picks the highlighted option, and arrow keys skip over unavailable choices without getting stuck. If a connection restarts, the menu resets properly so stale errors or stuck states do not appear.

5787c43ba551d59afefddbec4a758a87cfc80cc4.text: Codebuff renamed its 'Free' mode to 'Lite' mode. This change is live today and affects Codebuff users who select this mode. Previously, choosing 'Free' forced advertisements to appear; now, selecting 'Lite' uses the standard paid settings, meaning users can turn off ads. The underlying assistant behavior remains the same, but the label and ad logic have changed.

ab21fbbdc4bac114401e4786199d4a3911af6d45.text: The system now checks if the AI service is running smoothly before letting free-tier users in. If the service is slow or busy, new users wait in a queue instead of experiencing lag. This prevents the system from getting overwhelmed, ensuring that when a user is admitted, they get a faster response.

f7461e3885e81bf95a5058142b2754174f13eb43.text: The command to redeem a referral code has been removed from the text-based assistant. If you try to use the old command, it will no longer work. Existing saved referral states will not be migrated.

ff385b6c6953eb8d617d7f53e1ce76e4dad57f85.text: Staff gained new internal tools to identify and block accounts abusing free access. A safety feature prevents accidental blocking by showing a preview of affected accounts before applying the change. Regular users will not notice any difference today, as these tools are used privately by the operations team.

faa7d7a6e9ebd7897d4497103455f3161c7fc3fe.text: The chat interface now shows a clear button to end a trial session early, replacing a generic stop icon. Clicking it immediately returns you to the waiting room and displays a confirmation message.

7f5b41b7626ba943763be093bc64e920dd6a6956.text: The installer now reuses the existing secure tunnel to the proxy server instead of asking your computer to find the download server's address again. This prevents the update process from failing when your computer cannot resolve the domain directly. Only people using a proxy to install the tool will notice the fix.

8470d9d30ed2c3560e382cce65c03bc155141423.text: The team added a new internal tool to help them investigate if AI usage costs are being calculated twice. This change does not affect regular users and there is nothing visible to see, as it is only for the internal team to use when checking their data.

8a7cf082bdd478b85aa746ebe42879733bb3ecdf.text: A new background check now watches the AI models, alerting admins if errors spike or data goes stale. This tool is live and helps engineers spot outages quickly. Regular users won't see any changes, but the system can now catch bad responses before they reach you.

f231508eb3ebf55810bc726751001b8e306fc6f6.text: A new internal measurement tool was added to track how long an AI service remembers previous conversation parts. This tool is not active for customers and does not change any live features. It helps the team check if memory settings work correctly over time.

512ebc980642295869b91eb7e8415afe83cb451c.text: The system previously added two separate cost figures together for Anthropic requests, causing users to be charged double the actual amount. This fix ensures the system only counts the highest single cost value, preventing duplicate charges. While this correction is now in the code, it did not affect live production data, so no real customers were overcharged.

fa1d71d7675faadfb04596afc792de92d05fc1ab.text: The system now stops free users from using more service than their account allows, preventing them from running up a negative balance. If a free user tries to exceed their limit, the action is blocked immediately. This change is live and affects only accounts without a paid subscription or credit purchases.

13d5f6cb9e9e937400c652728747e50e1f01f2e8.text: A bug prevented the assistant from using certain approved tools, causing them to be incorrectly hidden. This fix ensures these tools are now visible and usable as intended. If you use these specific tools, you will no longer see errors indicating they are unavailable.

9fcd27ae9517496836efbc7244eb02f0c768bc07.text: The assistant now shows the exact data it tried to use when a task fails, instead of hiding or cutting it off. This helps people using the agent tools see why a step broke. The change is active today.

ff89b57040335b83085dbdb299b6133ff2cfd116.text: The free trial now limits you to one active coding session at a time. If you open a second window, the first one stops working and asks you to close the other window and restart. If your session ends while the AI is still answering, a message appears instead of a button so you do not accidentally cancel the work in progress.

72144496dd2dac4bf9da952554b34e69a93783c4.text: Free users now see four selectable advertisements instead of one banner when the system randomly assigns them to the new layout. The text promising rewards for viewing ads has been removed from both the advertisement display and the usage summary. This change is active and affects only free accounts.

0f588b09f03c5086960f61d84df918a3e6303686.text: The team deleted unused test files and an outdated guide meant for internal evaluation tools. This is a small internal cleanup with no visible effect on the software's behavior for everyday users.

868fb291a133d92404b1bc086e483a7823cd053a.text: The team deleted an internal experiment that tested how well the coding assistant could learn from documentation. This change affects only the internal project structure and documentation. Regular users will notice no difference in the assistant's behavior or features today.

3886a0c449d74a23d08ff1e60013f689c18f53ef.text: The team removed three outdated internal planning documents that contained old feature ideas and project timelines. They also moved the guide explaining how login works into the main documentation folder so it is easier to find. This cleanup does not change how the software works or looks for anyone using it.

1579802a544a49757295094a45979ea4e0f16c3a.text: The command-line assistant now unlocks immediately when you stop a running task. Previously, the system held the task open, preventing new requests until the old one fully finished. Now, you can type a new command right away without waiting for the previous response to time out.

88dfbcfa7ef46bd9d4aeb95446ac0e3ec417e959.text: The system now correctly waits until the conversation reaches its full length limit before summarizing or removing older messages, instead of cutting off early. This prevents the assistant from suddenly losing track of recent instructions or tool results during long chats. The fix ensures the AI maintains its full memory capacity before needing to shorten the history.

0df74ef688d9809f4d6e1897f386c3e2e38861dd.text: A new software tool called Expensivebuff is live today as an April Fools joke. It affects anyone who tries to install it, but it does nothing useful; it just shows a fancy logo and a message pointing to the real tools, Codebuff and Freebuff.

db4d3b66234703d944bc7a867be44b83b0236d59.text: Free-tier users now have access to a smarter AI assistant for solving complex problems. This new assistant is available today and is used automatically when difficult tasks are encountered, replacing the previous method that required a separate paid subscription. Users will notice the system handles hard questions more effectively without needing to manually enable anything.

a92b5cf6c09072e0c1e72ed56d9f41922ff0d610.text: The system now records the cost of every message sent through the external AI provider, even if charging the user's account fails. This ensures accurate financial tracking for all users. Previously, a billing error would block the cost record from being saved.

c8bfaa1f66a85810bce9989c8fa8719ca8481b80.text: The system now automatically links a specific instruction file to a shared guide, ensuring the AI assistant reads the correct rules during evaluation tasks. This change applies only to internal testing workflows and does not affect external users. If you looked at the test logs, you would see the assistant consistently loading the shared documentation without manual setup.

3f5910ed11a32b551ef094318694f0d7010f09da.text: A new stop button appears in the command-line interface while the assistant is thinking or writing. Clicking it halts the current response immediately. This feature is live for all users of the command-line tool.

49dbb241650a6c468387d87c21dd4677824a39c5.text: The system now automatically tests AI coding assistants on real tasks and uses the results to rewrite project instructions. If an assistant fails a task, the system drafts new guidelines to fix the gap and keeps only changes that improve performance. This internal process runs in the background to make the assistant smarter without manual documentation updates.

5f271d644e4e896d600fdff14f81b27fe5b84d02.text: The internal testing system now builds practice tasks by deleting a piece of software and asking AI agents to rebuild it. This replaces the old method of using past code changes. It affects only the team checking if the agents can understand and recreate features. Nothing visible to regular users changes today.
