a8119a983e8b19a7e803234bb762b0dc4b01c48b.text: The team reorganized their internal instruction manual by breaking one massive document into several smaller, specific guides. This change affects only the people who write or maintain the software's documentation. They will now find information in separate, easier-to-navigate sections rather than scrolling through a single long file.

5edd8088d621ddf38c76a323de30c93e37f3fc08.text: The AI assistant sometimes asks for lists of items but accidentally sends just one item. This update fixes that mistake by automatically turning single items into lists. This means the assistant will work more reliably without getting stuck on simple errors.

3f47c49de6a9e18c2c045ef8119115eceb591952.text: The setup tool now automatically uses your company's internet filter settings when downloading updates. This helps people who work in offices where strict security blocks direct internet access. If you are in this group, the tool will stop freezing or failing to start, and you no longer need to manually change special settings to make it work.

54f4585e20a1b0c4ece8a8d9197d9697f9df7c36.text: The team cleaned up their internal instruction manual to match how the system works now, adding details about the free version and the testing tool. They also disconnected an old helper program that is no longer used. This is a small internal housekeeping task, so nothing changes for anyone using the software today.

97e7cadd60d76206b8344f53b07d5f30a24e3950.text: The command-line tool no longer tries to open a web browser when running on Linux servers without a screen. This prevents the program from crashing when users click links to buy credits, subscribe, or log in. Affected users will now see the link stay in the terminal instead of the program closing unexpectedly.

4c95226fb382cfcb26fd7b5d09c57377cbfca2d6.text: Some Linux terminals use a different signal for the Enter key than the program expected, causing messages to fail to send. The program now automatically recognizes this alternate signal as Enter if the standard one is missing. Users on these specific terminals will find that pressing Enter works normally again.

cdf440c5e1dc88edc40ee6b4f5de4773b3262b66.text: A new internal report tool was added to track the heaviest users of the free tier. It filters out anyone who also uses paid versions, then lists the top 200 free-only users by message count, email, cost, and last activity over a set period (default 72 hours). It also flags anyone with 50+ messages for review. This is internal-only; no customer-facing changes.

2007a95dcb103c5d503abbef858a5c69af72e12c.text: People who run the tool that improves a coding assistant's instructions now see it learn from past changes more automatically. It can work through old changes one at a time, try several test runs together, and pick up where it stopped if the run is interrupted. It also shortens long notes before writing and stops leftover helper programs when a test takes too long.

1ba9f20469e72bd2b6940227d8811577721861dd.text: The website now records when visitors view the start page, click links, or open help sections. This data helps the team see which parts of the site people use most. Visitors will not notice any visual changes or pop-ups, as this background recording happens automatically without affecting the site's appearance or speed.

fb1bbbe130c7397b115ad5517e1765f12d6f348b.text: The website now remembers which person or page sent a new user to the sign-up link. When that user finishes setting up their account, the system quietly records this source information in its internal database. New users will not see any visual changes, but the company can now accurately track which marketing efforts or individual referrals are successfully bringing people to the service.

dd82cab4cfa6b71e670946fd7a226056e84737ac.text: A bug caused the assistant to forget previous messages if a user stopped a response early. The fix ensures the conversation history is saved before allowing a new message to be sent. This prevents context loss for anyone who interrupts the assistant during a response.

6bca8a1e31d8ac42f4355e0a255970e4d3e6902d.text: The system now records how many milliseconds pass before the first word of an AI reply appears, separate from total reply time. This affects only internal billing and performance tracking; users will not notice any difference in the chat interface. The data is being collected and stored today, but it does not yet change how credits are calculated or how replies are shown.

ea8a3f85557694e0dfe2c37d53bd4840b2ad67a3.text: The system now manages conversation memory more efficiently by separating limits for user inputs and assistant actions, prioritizing recent messages to maintain context relevance. This update affects all users interacting with the agent, resulting in more accurate responses during long conversations without losing track of recent requests. The change is live today.

e1b8a1bf045f51ea8c38f67a3bb2bf5006150444.text: The internal tool that checks how well AI agents handle tasks now talks to AI models directly instead of launching separate programs. It also skips unimportant updates, like version number bumps, to save time and cost. These changes affect only the automated quality checks; users will notice no difference in the main software.

e205b670db0541ddfbc8996ae2f525fafa58cb1a.text: The system now checks how many free chat messages a user sends in a short time. If someone sends too many requests, the service will temporarily block them and ask them to wait before trying again. This affects only users on the free plan and helps prevent automated abuse of the service.

e29a8bbf9b72ab3941c2fa40ce5cf537ef629c5f.text: Release operators can now choose a specific past version of the software to build, rather than only using the latest. This internal tooling change lets them target older updates or specific branches. Regular users will not notice any difference in the final product.

c0d0ea04cec97c6db2e1df022ed57efaa22ce245.text: The team added a new internal tool that tracks how much text the AI model reads and writes, plus how busy it gets. This helps the team plan server capacity and monitor performance. Customers will not see any changes or new features from this update.

3fa2a41c386abbc5a4cbf1b45076ac70cb68450d.text: A new automated check verifies the knowledge file feature works correctly. This internal quality control step runs alongside existing tests for other features. Developers notice no change in app behavior, as this only adds a safety net for future updates.

6a25ed71f39086bc5a602ccda95836735a758390.text: The team added a tool to check if a service saves money by reusing repeated instructions. They also fixed a missing password label that stopped a separate check from running. These tools only help staff measure costs and speed, so customers see no change today.

cb8a36a7e4df9697f164823df2c5f9527e440dc8.text: A new helper can now look at public code projects online. It downloads a temporary copy of a project's files to a separate, safe folder, reads them to answer your questions, and then cleans up. This change is currently in the development stage and not yet available for general use.

a5dffe7095c4de101fb244995422d56488efc270.text: The system now routes requests to dedicated servers instead of a shared pool. This change is live today and affects how the software fetches answers. Regular users will not notice any difference in the interface, but the underlying connection method has switched.

889181a5804829704934025f56da75be65588cf0.text: You can now paste a file path directly into the command-line chat to attach it. The tool shows a small icon and a shortened name for the file, and it waits until the file is fully ready before letting you send your message.

304ebcc5c6ae9afe71d7da416c79dc7ae355c4c9.text: Internal reporting tools now calculate usage statistics more accurately by excluding cached data from total input counts, ensuring metrics align with standard efficiency measures. A new script also allows staff to specifically review cache performance for a particular model over recent hours. These changes affect internal analytics and monitoring, with no visible impact on end-user features.

02ec8206f65656145e2c6e7a4d201323f0a16246.text: The system can now control a web browser to check if websites work correctly. This affects developers who use the tool, as it will automatically open a hidden browser window to test pages and report any errors or broken features. It is ready to use today, provided Chrome is installed on the computer.

499d7efcab4252154770c95067c5a1cb32368b56.text: The company added three written guides explaining how their software is organized, how it reports problems, and how it processes requests. This change is internal documentation and does not affect how the software currently works. Regular users will see no difference, but new employees or external partners reading these guides will better understand the system's structure.

b02ac2e5d465624aba2bd5134f9aed1dc0684002.text: The tool now includes a private way to connect directly to your ChatGPT account for certain tasks, skipping the usual middleman. This feature is currently switched off, so nothing changes for you yet. Once enabled, it will let eligible models run faster and cheaper by talking straight to OpenAI instead of through the service's own servers.

c9768351b870eb8065212af10a5b889b72b2538a.text: Added a test to check how much money the system saves when it remembers long instructions across a ten-message chat. This change is for internal developers only. Regular users will see no difference.

4a4200f89eab492b59b535f1bb9ed0c8305da26e.text: During business hours, requests for a specific AI model now try a dedicated server first. If that server is busy scaling up, the system automatically switches to the standard shared server after a two-minute pause. This change is live and helps maintain service availability for users of that model during peak times.

734d709579253b9ff76e261804262abe28ded7ac.text: The team added a safety check that automatically opens the program and tries to type commands every time they save new code. If the program crashes or stops working, the check fails and warns them before the update goes live. This is an internal quality check, so regular people will not see any new features or changes to the program itself.

3ee603e4c5d23af302e6505d2ead236164edf1de.text: A small internal fix helps the command-line tool build correctly. It affects only the people who compile the tool from source. They would notice fewer build errors, while regular users see no change.

d86a41e78780d812c253791fc73ed3acf2de0e0f.text: Connecting the command-line tool to your ChatGPT account now works automatically. Instead of copying a code from your browser and pasting it back into the terminal, the tool quietly waits for your browser to finish signing in and grabs the key itself. This change is live for anyone using the command-line interface to link their account.

789820e7ef5e012252ad895bb9b25c3ad481ddfc.text: The website's permanent top menu was removed and replaced with a floating menu on the home page. This change is live. Visitors will see the menu fade in over the home page instead of staying fixed at the top of every page.

f689232cfc268ab21eaac235988c85cf986a40f6.text: The software previously had two separate helpers for running terminal commands, one for free users and one for paid users. These have been merged into a single, lightweight helper. This change is active today and simplifies how the system executes basic shell commands, removing the distinction between free and paid tiers for this specific task.

a10cd1daaff1e69d6443e01077f1ba771f8afb1b.text: The free-tier assistant now sends its answers to a different computer service instead of the old one. This switch removes a previous lock that forced the old service, allowing the new one to handle requests. If you use the free plan, you might notice the assistant takes longer to start speaking because the new service gives it extra time to think deeply.

bcc43e4e215493850e86dbffabf5be10c58766df.text: The assistant can now use a dedicated helper to run and monitor command-line tools in a background terminal session. This feature is active for standard plan users. You might notice the assistant handling complex terminal tasks more smoothly, keeping track of session states and reporting results clearly.

47abc4663bdbcf07a7201b136720f8760a1852f7.text: Free-tier users now get the MiniMax M2.5 model from SiliconFlow instead of OpenRouter. This routing is live today, though other providers are temporarily off. You will not notice a visual change, but the service handling your requests has switched.

c68871d3a1a0d94c2af8b33a6e17542f2344a22b.text: The website's underlying software library was updated to a newer, more stable version. The site now displays friendly, branded pages when a visitor tries to access a missing page or when the site encounters a temporary server error, instead of showing a generic technical error screen.

5e4f6082c14a4145927c879088df38f432796901.text: The team added a tool that lets them automatically send the command-line helper to the public software catalog when they are ready to publish it. This only affects the internal release process and requires a special security key to work. Regular users will not notice any change in the application's behavior today.

e5ff7dce443241fe8c79119d00399bca1d6b49f2.text: The system now sends requests for the MiniMax model to CanopyWave instead of Baseten. Internal developers must update their server settings to use the new CanopyWave access key, as the old Baseten key no longer works. Customer experience remains unchanged.

01ef8856c8985577e3f3562a3be1a0e138ea999d.text: The software's underlying display engine was updated to a newer version. This change fixes internal compatibility issues so that text and interactive elements in the command-line interface and web dashboard render correctly without breaking. Users will not notice any visual differences or new features, as this is a background maintenance task to keep the application stable.

189be16225cfa3196773907e41fad7be46f049e4.text: The system now connects directly to the AI provider instead of using a middleman service. This change applies only to paid plans and is active immediately. Users might notice slightly faster responses or more consistent pricing, as the direct connection allows for better control over costs and timing.

208a1782033a7b51bfb9aa784ca1fc1eea778c5e.text: New planning documents were added to define a future tool that helps AI coding assistants understand specific projects. This is strictly an internal design update and does not change how any current software works. Nothing new is available to use yet.

98ffa6c38ece5e15ad14bfa2d018fcfdc9a9b014.text: A new free version of the coding assistant was created by removing paid features and subscription checks from the standard software. This change is not live for general users yet, as it currently only exists as a separate package ready for installation. If installed, the assistant would run without asking for payment or showing credit balances, offering basic AI coding help for free.

c08733b82d4ff63f1214abe238a5535d62c6da00.text: The website's look changed. The brand name is now a picture with a new style, and the browser tab shows a new icon. The main text also changed, removing the claim about 'credits' and adding a new comparison. These updates are live for visitors.

b94e7d2b8279e30a3d824ae3bd29fb3550cad6fe.text: The system now records detailed snapshots of its internal instructions and data when saving information for faster future responses. This helps developers identify why the system might not be reusing saved data correctly. Regular users will not notice any changes, as this is strictly an internal diagnostic tool.

53fc285969ad9e204bfa96d4f93e33e246aaedce.text: A new website for the free coding assistant was added. It gives people an intro page, lets them sign in with the same account used for the existing assistant, and uses that sign-in to let the text-based assistant connect. The change only puts this in place; it is not shown as live yet.

7f1e8004d8c8c86843581b245eecd821aaad634f.text: The software installer now acts as a placeholder, removing the actual coding assistant and background data collection features. Anyone trying to use the tool will see a message stating it is coming soon instead of the working program.

5a57b7b0e3a433e54369592a9387bc0786aba473.text: The evaluation system now uses a version of the assistant that cannot ask clarifying questions. This change applies only to automated tests, not to live users. The assistant will proceed with best guesses instead of pausing for input during these specific checks.

ccbe035eeed0f877262b54c3ef89eae238bf6c35.text: The team created new internal guidelines to help their automated coding assistant verify its own work more effectively. These rules instruct the assistant to check exactly what files it changed and to test commands safely before running them. This change is not live for customers and produces no visible output in the product.

af100a17c0367293ff1f89ad4e992fb09c1eb5fc.text: The team added a hidden switch that records the exact instructions sent to the AI assistant, allowing them to spot why the system sometimes forgets previous context. This is for the engineers only. It does nothing for regular users right now because the switch is currently turned off.

d18df47ac9149474c95f6851ef1eacdb47102536.text: A separate, ad-supported version of the coding assistant now exists. People using this free version will see ads and cannot turn them off, while subscription options are hidden. This is a new, distinct product, not a change to the existing paid tool.

75cfd15b3e81b44411fba88bf35b4f049acf1834.text: The automated tester for the command-line assistant now keeps a single session open and only takes screenshots when the screen actually changes, rather than restarting sessions or capturing overlapping views. This cuts the number of actions the tester takes from 21 to 10 during implementation checks. The change is live for internal testing workflows.

2651c0b945cdb2bea86e2ebe937914aafe81fde3.text: The assistant now sends requests for the MiniMax M2.5 model to a new provider instead of the previous one. This change is live and affects only users selecting that specific model. They might notice slightly different response times or costs, as the new provider has different pricing and longer wait times for complex queries.

4b8bba75d06e4e6391c44a38228dc22ee1ca4609.text: Free plan users no longer get a separate helper for writing code. The main assistant now makes edits itself and calls a new, smaller checker to review the work. This change is live today.

b8dbc9e372c1024fe2544204afa2f653d2a22de5.text: The AI assistant now demands complete file text instead of accepting partial edits with placeholder comments. This change affects all users of the code editing agent. Users will notice the assistant writes entire files, which may increase output length but ensures exact content matching.

e561badadd00e446d412965c34523fc16b410a35.text: The command-line tool now sends your feedback directly to the company's servers instead of just keeping it on your computer. When you submit a rating or comment, the input box temporarily locks while the data uploads, ensuring your message is safely received. This change affects anyone using the tool's feedback feature, making sure your reports actually reach the team for review.

7ea760f09b36d71fd3d7861962cbeb1c146a871e.text: Internal staff can now check if paid plans make money. The tool compares actual usage against costs to show which tiers lose or gain profit. Customers and the app itself will not notice any change.

d6911b070e2fca4b06bb4d6446002f80b0901b5a.text: When you stop an AI response mid-generation, the text that had already arrived now saves to your history instead of vanishing. This fix applies to the tool that runs these AI agents. You would notice that cancelled chats keep the partial answer rather than showing a blank gap.

d778cfd31d9a38a9c36c52ffd6afc76e8644e817.text: The assistant now uses a safer method to edit files, preventing accidental data loss. It also gained new specialized helpers for deep thinking and code review. Users will see a cleaner interface when the assistant processes brief updates, with less visual clutter.

6b1070f762c527e6f79877bd43d54a0f30f727c8.text: The tool that packages this software now fails loudly if it cannot collect all the necessary information files, instead of just showing a warning and continuing. This ensures that anyone using the packaged software receives complete and accurate guidance on how to use it, preventing hidden errors that previously slipped through unnoticed.

11c57cc42a98cd1125768aad0b0baed8e947a8a4.text: The free version of the coding assistant now uses a different underlying engine to make changes to files. This engine was previously named after one provider and has been renamed to reflect its lightweight nature. If you use the free mode, you will notice the assistant relies on this new, faster engine instead of the previous one for editing tasks.

b0b535caa6390e9423727516bdb009508dc9998d.text: A new 'Account' tab was added to the profile page. Signed-in users can now click it to see their email address and a 'Verified' or 'Unverified' badge. This is a small internal change that is live today.

096c4f88b360493a40e18fdd94aebc5d05e61ad1.text: A new internal tool lets staff manually add credits to a specific account. Staff must enter the account details, amount, and reason, then confirm the action. This tool is for staff use only; customers will not see it or use it directly.

699d843343ded107bec26c518ca069e881b2ee11.text: The system no longer tracks a specific payment plan for paying as you go. This change affects internal setup and the database record for each person. No one will see a difference today, because the plan was already gone.

bd60ddac9276ae1a04e46797b412364126f8e514.text: A new button in the internal control panel lets the team start a long-running quality test for the coding assistant without waiting for the nightly schedule. This change is for the internal team only and is live today. Team members will see a new option to launch the test manually and watch it run for up to six hours.

6fc95937c99cd5afd2794e0a27809cbac58ef8cf.text: Removed a hidden web link that handled subscription changes. Since this link was no longer used, deleting it cleaned up the system without changing how the billing page works. Users will not notice any difference.

77ccc55d578796a0ef5a960c972d37396f3103b2.text: The team deleted a help guide that explained how to use their coding assistant for common tasks. This is an internal cleanup, so the assistant itself did not change. If you visited the website, you would just notice that one guide page is gone.

c49789dacbe616b50b764519a6b9e1fba1124c78.text: The team deleted a temporary instruction file used to sort old referral rewards. This cleanup affects only internal records; the actual sorting was already finished in the live system. Regular customers will see no changes, as the rewards are already correctly categorized.

51ae862692a8812e3a488c2e99e7ff465cf51f52.text: The system can now check message length for OpenAI models, instead of only doing it for Anthropic models. This is an internal update, so it does not change what you see in the app.

f3e4216c22135a5d963d01eb1b9bcde68c9994f3.text: A database rule that blocked a specific update was bypassed by splitting the process into two steps. This affects internal referral data, ensuring old recurring grants are correctly labeled and prioritized. The change is live, fixing a potential error during data migration.

0c537d8c58401d1f7556324b6050a649c7557709.text: The payment system now correctly identifies when a billing event comes from an organization account, preventing errors when processing these specific payments. This internal fix ensures that the system can reliably distinguish between personal and organizational transactions, maintaining accurate billing records without requiring any action from users.

0ce28d92c11130c01626a552834fb6f82950b74b.text: The terminal tool now checks your subscription status every minute. If your usage hits the limit, a warning appears, and you can type /subscribe to open the pricing page. The status bar at the bottom also shows when your current access resets.

1147209cdb883e00f1cc2a0779c4fdb941e90eb6.text: The automatic system for updating credit records now fails when trying to assign a new status to old referral rewards. This affects internal operators, who must manually run a separate script after the main update completes. Without this step, the new referral status remains unused, leaving old rewards incorrectly categorized.

415f5a7c7dc0d39a3021bc9a0ea30d5156d3571d.text: Referral rewards changed from small monthly payments to a single, larger payment. New referrals now get 500 credits once, and these credits never expire. Existing users from the old monthly plan keep their current rewards, but the system now treats them differently to ensure their old credits are used first.

f4578bf4f4a245399ea58b440a1a3b30bdcb6d04.text: Developers added safety checks to ensure the AI assistant stops exactly when a user cancels a task, rather than trying alternative methods. This prevents unwanted background activity or unexpected results after a user hits stop. The change is internal, so users will not see any new buttons or text, but the assistant will behave more predictably when cancelled.

7eca73b597318beaafc519ee42999dce041609a0.text: Organization billing is temporarily paused. Members of an organization cannot currently set up new subscriptions, upgrade plans, or buy additional credits, though existing subscriptions can still be canceled. Personal accounts are unaffected and continue to operate normally.

5060a002502a7eeeac76ff122490f241cbaf594c.text: A new internal guide was added explaining how the coding assistant speeds up work by checking many files at once and reviewing its own code. This is for staff to understand product strengths; customers see no change.

d6e7b7ea7418911b23b69894b06833c420876cca.text: The guide for connecting external services moved to the tips section. It now highlights a simple setup file that makes these tools available to all AI assistants automatically. Users looking for integration help will find this easier method first, replacing the previous complex instructions.

ed9b9413bf5867912f4283e6b2e1eb1ada9d16b5.text: The system now handles stopped requests more reliably by using a specific internal signal for cancellations. This change improves how the software distinguishes between user-stopped actions and actual errors. The underlying mechanism is in place, but it does not yet change what you see on your screen.

94a7f9ff1c0c25651633bfc43107387ccfd5fc55.text: A guide page with tips on how to use the assistant was removed because its advice already appeared on other help pages. This affects people reading the online documentation. They will notice one fewer page in the tips section, but the instructions themselves remain available elsewhere.

2303714342ed6476a96c8e2855a5bdaf79d192d8.text: The command-line tool now identifies your computer's unique hardware to prevent creating multiple accounts. It works immediately and updates in the background, affecting only new sign-ups.

ad68b32f3a5e58be70437c75eb3719f3678fa6a5.text: Typing /review in the command-line tool now opens a menu asking what to check, offering choices for recent edits, the current work branch compared to the main branch, or a custom selection. Choosing an option automatically sends that code to the assistant for feedback. This works immediately for anyone using the tool.

3be3cc2d6566d12b7c78b7c50d84f8e17ee62964.text: A new guide explains how to create custom instruction sets for the coding assistant. This helps users define specific workflows, like code review steps or release checklists, that the assistant can load only when needed. The guide details how to organize these instructions in folders and trigger them with simple commands.

986d6a349dc1d95a48794da2396fe718a9c54004.text: The command-line tool now stops trying to refresh activity data after a set number of failures, preventing endless waiting. This affects users running the tool when the service is temporarily down or returning errors. You will see the tool pause and eventually show an error message instead of hanging indefinitely.

7eef4c4bcf2fad1756b3695692c844f23397deba.text: The coding assistant now automatically checks a standard settings file for connections to outside services like Notion or Slack. If you add one of these connections to your project's configuration folder, the assistant picks it up immediately, and it can read your secret login keys directly from your computer's settings instead of requiring them to be written inside the file.

baebc5a012ae1bdee67470879e1c3764e7f5d652.text: New users no longer click through separate setup screens; they scroll down one page to finish getting started. The setup now always uses one standard download command, so the menu for choosing between four different tools is gone. When someone copies the command, the button now flashes a clear 'Copied!' message next to the checkmark so they know it worked.

5802e2b7bdcc4ff1fde7886bf0d390eee994c48b.text: A new command lets people working on remote computers sign in without needing special copy-paste tools. The program now prints the sign-in link as plain text so users can select it with their mouse or keyboard. When the app detects a remote connection, it suggests this command if the normal sign-in screen fails to copy the link.

4b01c207047d44f9acb47b8d4b7e5cafbc8b3fca.text: The system now ensures your text is saved if a request fails before the server processes it. This prevents your message from disappearing during technical errors. You would notice that your typed input remains visible in the chat history even when the assistant cannot respond.

389ccc13f7c34b2bf8d5fdd0580a7575e4dd6bcd.text: The team deleted a long internal log that tracked mistakes and fixes from previous automated coding tasks. This change only affects the developers who maintain the system, not the customers using it. You will not notice any difference in how the software works or looks.

bf9eddaba35d2a608d7600e78e602ed432fcff3f.text: When the tool starts, it now checks your project folder for a saved settings file and applies those rules automatically. This helps people who use a special helper program to manage their project settings. If the helper program is not installed or the file is locked, the tool will show a warning asking you to approve the file first.

a207ad23c2e11b4963b3c78bb4b961eab5e182ca.text: A new 'Strong' subscription plan launches today with three tiers ($100, $200, $500/month). Paying subscribers get their monthly credits first, before any free or ad-based credits are used. If you downgrade your plan, you keep your current credit limits until your next billing date, then switch to the lower tier's limits.

cc4298ee5e138871f9e829f103f77bdc50ff2ce3.text: The company added a new page to their website explaining how they handle your data. It says they don't use your information to train their AI models and only show ads based on your current activity. This information is live now, so you can read these details if you look at their privacy section.

2964be866c3e4b3da1f3d9208ed1e8ee6d476a12.title: Add CLI sponsored capability detection and display acknowledgement
2964be866c3e4b3da1f3d9208ed1e8ee6d476a12.summary: New `sponsored-cli-capability.ts` detects project capabilities (framework, package manager, database boundaries) to route ad requests via `/api/ads` instead of `/api/v1/ads`. `sponsored-project-identity.ts` generates a persistent opaque UUID marker for remote-less Git workspaces, ensuring stable targeting without leaking local paths. `sponsored-proposal-block.tsx` now triggers `acknowledgeSponsoredProposalDisplay` on mount, confirming the offer was actually rendered in the terminal rather than just stored in the transcript. Capability inspection data is included in the ad request body only when a project root is detected.

ab76a003422420b5fc75e3c52c8003ebbf9e3d9c.text: The tool's internal setup was cleaned up to fix a self-referencing loop. This change is strictly for the developers maintaining the code. Regular users will see no difference in how the tool works today.

232f0dddb7dbfb8fb89a438ea7021bdfe535329c.text: The team added a large set of automated checks for the internal AI assistants that help with tasks like editing code, picking files, and reasoning. This work does not change how the software behaves for anyone today, but it helps the team ensure these assistants work reliably as the code changes in the future.

65fb6d39db1b4e441db2014a7557538d1c49c8b3.text: The tool now shows a brief progress summary when you collapse a multi-step editor task. You will see simple text like '2/3 completed' or 'selecting best' instead of a long, messy output stream. This change is live and applies specifically to the editor-multi-prompt task type.

a536f6a827daaf2d25add1d2389f07aaacf2c3fe.text: The automated quality checks now ignore the tests that open a real web browser, so they run faster and more reliably. This internal change affects the software team's testing tools and does not change how the product works for customers.

45df4dfbce44f07701a79a337579475d9a49d48e.text: The team removed unused code fragments that triggered warning messages, and created shared templates for testing fake data. This internal cleanup affects only the developers maintaining the tool. A regular user will notice no change in the application's behavior or appearance.

e025a206c39f203e83d1a6c495d4796c9341aaed.text: The system now checks data shapes before processing requests, replacing loose assumptions with strict rules. This affects internal error handling for payment and chat features. Staff will see clearer logs when bad data arrives, but customers notice no change.

2964be866c3e4b3da1f3d9208ed1e8ee6d476a12.text: The tool now checks your project type and assigns a random private code to folders without online backups to send better ads. It also confirms when an offer actually appears on screen rather than just being saved. These changes are active immediately.

8565c2d0deb416b5b1d8ac874a160b0d2c52c67b.text: The team added a helper to the website's creation process that records every step and detail into a private file. If the website fails to build, this file automatically shows the full error history to the internal team for faster fixing, while hiding repetitive noise from the main screen. This change is live for internal developers and improves how they debug build failures.

3478b8b2654ced86779ac295dbea38fc881ad1e1.text: The team cleaned up the formatting of the internal tools that help them check if the software works. This change does not affect how the program runs or what customers see. It only makes the code easier for the developers to read and maintain.

4215b8a2552107b82d15710d0839adeeaf8f7ff9.text: Developers added automated checks to ensure the 'copy to clipboard' feature works correctly, especially when using remote connections. This change is internal and does not affect how the software behaves for users today. You would not notice any difference, as this only helps the team verify that the existing copy function continues to work reliably.

dc00f93621c2f362b6ce42898478d547ad915abe.text: The team improved the internal tools used to check that the software works correctly. This change affects only the people who build the software, not the people who use it. If they looked, they would see cleaner, more reliable tests that catch errors earlier, but the actual features of the application remain exactly the same.

bb10b2d58731901f13f442a1d7875288169459b0.text: The assistant now uses a different AI model for code editing tasks in 'Lite' mode. This change affects only users who have selected 'Lite' mode. They might notice slightly different responses or processing speeds when asking the assistant to edit code.

abaf6a1f5f527cefccbffbe1290a64ae4d56158c.text: The system can now call two different AI helpers for complex tasks instead of just one. This applies only to accounts with standard or maximum settings. You might see faster answers or different wording on hard questions, though the change is small and internal.

f74b73e042d7d0464901476ba7db59a419999d61.text: Programmers cleaned up how the assistant's settings are written down and made the safety checks stricter when testing commands. This is an internal tidy-up. Regular people will not notice any difference in how the tool works.

88c20d8c1cd5cfd16164b551ea88daea3360cec2.text: The free option in the command-line tool now shows ads and uses a cheaper AI model to save money. If you use this mode, you will see ads and notices that you cannot earn credit rewards for watching them.

a6526e0ba5aa3455b1ca4045b2d268af6cdf3d22.text: The command-line assistant now correctly displays the AI's internal thought process from newer models. Previously, these thoughts were hidden or mixed with the final answer. If you run a task, you will see a collapsible section showing how the AI is reasoning before it acts.

830dba304fb3ad006f48dc4fbdb92f4a43ee1ff5.text: Pressing Ctrl+T in the text-based chat window now hides or shows all background details like thinking steps and tool results at once. This helps users quickly clean up the screen without clicking each section individually. The feature is live today for anyone using this command-line interface.

5938b0ea4263eb3aba69afa997e50c666e945103.text: The command-line tool now changes your terminal window's title to show the text you just sent, prefixed with 'Codebuff: '. This helps you identify which conversation is active when multiple terminal tabs are open. The title automatically clears when you close the tool, and long messages are shortened to fit.

11c14d9693c7f917299bcfe143218701ec49f651.text: The AI assistant gained a new, powerful reasoning mode to help solve difficult problems. This mode is available now for standard and advanced plans, but the assistant is instructed to use it only as a last resort. Users might notice the assistant occasionally taking longer to answer complex questions if it decides to switch to this deeper thinking mode.

02c7a7881109b432b27948add88d805127f1447b.text: The system now ignores billing for simple file-search tools costing less than 5 credits. This prevents unexpected charges for users who connect their own Claude subscription. You will see no change in the interface, but your credit balance will not decrease for these specific background tasks.

c00389f164131f883ab0b8a44003e5b46b59c0f4.text: The command-line tool now remembers exactly where you were when browsing past commands, so switching between normal typing and special modes like feedback no longer shows old text. This fixes a glitch where pressing the up arrow would bring back a message from a previous mode instead of your current draft. The change is active in the latest version.

d752f67c2623da1313c5cf5f2f4bd33c4d8caaea.text: The command-line interface previously hid content when a user resized their terminal window to be narrower than the space needed for multiple columns. Developers fixed this by ensuring the layout always keeps a minimum width for each column, preventing content from collapsing to zero size. This change is live and ensures that information remains visible regardless of how the window is resized.

e8d70e5016ac1950e34efe657bfe86360a5a2cef.text: When you cancel a message mid-response, the assistant now saves whatever it had already written and marks the conversation as interrupted. This prevents the screen from flashing or clearing unexpectedly when you hit stop. The fix applies immediately to anyone using the command-line tool.

76fac870edb54a406f6e2169fe33410dae62b2d6.text: The team updated a shared helper tool used by internal testing scripts to close security gaps. This change does not affect the main product or any customer-facing features. You will not notice any difference in how the software behaves.

accf15783fc7529ae9cf3942c82da8a8830bfb05.text: The team rebuilt the health check that confirms the system is online, making it easier to test for errors. This internal change ensures the check reports success even if it cannot count active agents, preventing false alarms for the operations team. No visible changes for end users.

28b7135a68ba48fa7c1f4c9f39c5b46dcf657e4f.text: The AI assistant stopped rejecting certain external tools because their names contained slashes. The system now translates these names into a format the AI provider accepts before sending them. You will not see a visible change, but requests to use these tools will now succeed instead of failing.

306f8687ad62f943c366f87e6e2033c7332bef61.text: The command-line assistant now shows a small, dimmed label next to commands that have a custom waiting limit, such as '2m timeout'. Commands using the standard 30-second limit remain unchanged. This helps users see how long a command will run before being stopped.

d00903a709a387517c1ce06ba36ac6372c8f6c8c.text: The team cleaned up the written code for the web application by making its spacing and line breaks consistent. This is a small internal change that affects only the developers who maintain the software. A customer or user would not notice anything different when using the website today.

31c6ff78607c4aea4456865d2a9dd28c5dd44608.text: The automated testing system now checks billing calculations in a separate, isolated environment with its own database, while other tests run without one. This change only affects the internal team's testing process and is active immediately. Developers will see faster, more reliable test results for billing features, with failures in one area no longer stopping checks in others.

7177b06ec8ea56cf4a6e9649698f36682efbcbf5.text: The system now makes simultaneous credit spending requests wait their turn instead of crashing and retrying. This change prevents billing errors for individual users and organizations when many requests happen at once. While the safety mechanism is active, new tracking data for monitoring these waits is currently in place but not yet fully utilized.

88d198baf9be9c8c93f3a6627003999f13dc81ed.text: The command-line tool now stops messages from getting mixed up or skipped when you send several at once. If the system gets stuck waiting for a reply, it automatically resets after one minute so you can keep typing. This helps people who use the text interface to talk to the assistant.

614f8ba872fc3e99a949642fc3565cf27ec904a6.text: The system now automatically opens and manages a terminal window for each supported coding assistant, rather than asking the AI to remember to do it. This affects internal tools that launch these assistants. You will see the assistant announce it is starting a session, and the process will fail clearly if the terminal does not open correctly, instead of silently hanging or misbehaving.

6a8af63cf292d48cb9a2b25b0f6f4e271de4a6ed.text: The assistant’s memory-cleaning tool previously failed to start when handling long conversations because of how it was packaged. Developers moved specific settings and rules inside the tool’s main process to fix this. This change is internal; regular users will not notice any difference in behavior or interface.

95a51d89d74b186344a0b8170ae55666a73cfe8a.text: A new guide explains how to connect AI assistants to external tools like Notion or GitHub. This affects only Codebuff users who manually set up these connections. The guide is live, but the connection feature itself is not automatically active for everyone; it requires specific setup steps.

be7a47c3aba6efd68c6a94469ef976b2bf075c1b.text: The code that runs the text-based chat screen was split into smaller, focused pieces to make it easier to update. This is an internal cleanup for the developers who maintain the tool. You will not see any changes in how the chat looks or behaves.

2818f1b149f3c4ff78171c90c70f018d7af53ab5.text: A small internal fix makes the Discord bot more stable when multiple copies run at once. The system now checks the database connection every 30 seconds and stops the bot if it fails five times in a row, preventing duplicate messages. Regular users will not notice any change.

396d0dff0ce1ae452e308763c42339f199e87fc7.text: The system now has a second, stronger version of its file-searching helper that uses a different AI model. This only activates when the 'max' mode is turned on; otherwise, it uses the standard helper. You won't notice any difference unless you specifically enable that mode.

4a88477aab83e69caeceb7e109b377707d815e1d.text: The text-based program's question prompts were reorganized internally for easier maintenance. The final choice in multiple-choice questions, previously labeled 'Other', is now labeled 'Custom'. People using the command-line interface will see the new label when answering questions.

0f4b98503ecce31555b4a32e0f293d39ab4bed3f.text: The software stopped using a complex review system that had several assistants check the same work and pick the best one. It also removed a master assistant that managed other tools for big tasks. This change is internal and not active for regular users today, meaning no one will see a difference in how the software behaves right now.

01c06622102352f6714739724f42933b4e0a4983.text: The text interface now automatically stacks information into a single column when the window is too narrow to fit two side-by-side. This prevents cramped or unreadable layouts in small terminals. The change is live and affects anyone using the command-line tool on a narrow screen.

952cafcea60b275942b7d3b676a7f206432289fd.text: The program now remembers chat settings in one central place, making it easier to manage. It also automatically removes extra blank spaces above text that appears right after a tool or agent finishes its work. Users will notice the chat history looks cleaner and tighter, with fewer awkward gaps between different types of messages.

392655319d5814d42edd8cc06aef380791cadfe6.text: The high-power assistant now uses a panel of specialized inspectors instead of a single reviewer to check its work. This change is active immediately for anyone using the most capable settings. You might notice slightly longer wait times, but the feedback should be more thorough and cover more angles.

ab53db5a63d86b5b55078476d10204f4fd18d3cb.text: Internal cleanup made the tool's memory limits easier to manage. Users see no change today.

58d6c0e7ad61d7c3ba8d057744585e0890655cb3.text: The text styling for messages is now set to be optional rather than required. This internal cleanup ensures that if a specific color scheme is not provided, the system defaults correctly without errors. You will not see any visual changes in the application today.

c6ed3479cbb3d26b18acd3af1544904e8faba7e0.text: The command-line assistant now arranges multiple parallel tasks into a grid layout and adds a status line showing how many are running, failed, or complete. It also adjusts spacing between consecutive tool usage steps based on surrounding content. This affects only those using the command-line interface, who will see a cleaner, more organized view of the assistant's progress.

9495948aaae1dfa6fe453d655f21443e1515ecf2.text: The program's internal display logic was reorganized into separate, specialized parts for different types of information. This change affects the software's maintainability, not its visible features. Users will notice no difference in how the application looks or behaves today.

3a2107e4d0372944191f09aa2bd398224ef0d7b0.text: The command-line interface now displays a visible warning box when a technical problem occurs. This change is live for people using the tool. You will see a red-bordered notice with the error details directly on your screen, keeping you informed without sending the problem to the AI.

abbc9730a4783f84c1fa9c128fd4e1864f1381b9.text: A new rule now helps the command-line tool arrange text columns based on window width. This change is currently just a background helper and does nothing yet because other parts of the tool do not use it.

20e9efa656734873d9199d96b1ba3b17a19582d0.text: Two new building blocks were added to the text-based interface. A layout tool now arranges items in multiple columns when the window is wide enough, and an error handler is set up to show a backup message if a screen fails to load. These parts are in the code but do nothing yet; they wait for other updates to use them.

3f158d6374927f48c756d865153280f5ac0f8f4c.text: The command-line tool now groups similar tasks together more efficiently, reducing visual clutter in the output. This change affects how the tool displays multiple actions in a row, making the log cleaner and easier to read. It is live today.

ed73d8422680785fdd74ad2bbf8c7bd0db804414.text: The terminal chat app now sends your queued messages one by one, waiting for each response to finish before starting the next. This affects people who type several messages quickly while the assistant is busy. You would notice the replies arrive in the exact order you typed them, with no messages getting lost or jumbled together.

253c4754e42312935287f7d0996ea9335394fa10.text: The instructions for testing four different coding assistants were consolidated into a single shared template to remove thousands of lines of duplicate text. This internal cleanup affects only the team maintaining these tools. No visible changes will appear in the software's behavior or interface.

eabf40e54495c612d5a6308fc4f4f4be9ebf08fd.text: The AI assistants used by the internal team can now review code for errors, in addition to testing the command line tools. Previously, these tools only checked if the software ran correctly; now, they can also read code and suggest fixes. This is a small internal update that helps developers catch mistakes early, though it does not change what outside customers see.

85062102870de68eb7871eb8917d67e6e0ad6979.text: In the command-line tool, pressing Ctrl+J now correctly adds a line break in the text box. Before, this key did nothing. This affects people who type multi-line messages in the terminal.

0a378efeb66ac84c6014c50df46a5e923c81f781.text: The code that decides how to display different parts of a conversation, such as thinking steps, tool uses, and agent actions, was cleaned up to use a shared set of rules. This internal change makes the text-based interface easier to maintain for the developers. Users will not see any difference in how the assistant behaves or how the text looks today.

83be8c8402aadb3865406aa15d9a7571a11dc597.text: The internal testing setup now lets automated bots check any full-screen command-line app, not just one. This helps the team verify that interfaces render correctly without manual inspection. It is not live for customers.

9032b27453a861dee6a007ef1d04cbde3a8aa9dc.text: The website now prepares pages for affiliates, pricing, and legal terms in advance, so they load instantly for visitors. Publisher and agent pages update their content every ten minutes, keeping information current without slowing down the site. This internal performance improvement is live today.

88a0c20e49d2b40a3d2eed9eae481241d55ab176.text: The team removed old, unused internal planning notes and fixed broken links in the public help center. This cleanup ensures that when you click on guide sections like 'Customize existing agents' or 'Built-in agents', you land on the correct page instead of an error. The changes are already live.

10f424728d116d125676d97dc1e9df848c01bc50.text: Developers moved the chat window's internal memory and message sorting into separate, tidy boxes to make the code easier to manage. They also added a safety lock for background bots to ensure only one copy runs at a time. You will not notice any difference today; these are behind-the-scenes cleanup tasks.

44e0ce088a75fb8768a03c6447855d81243e7e7f.text: The documentation site now has automated checks that flag typos, awkward phrasing, and leftover placeholder notes before new guides are published. These checks run nightly and also verify that all documentation links and pages load correctly. Writers will notice that poorly formatted or unfinished text gets rejected automatically, keeping the published guides cleaner and more consistent.

2379ebdd7dc0b899dfde10e53aad5d0ee1475536.text: When you paste a long block of text into the chat, it now appears as a separate attachment card above your message, similar to how pasted images work. This affects anyone using the command-line interface and makes it easier to see and manage large pasted text before sending.

5a6348b74a6f86c73f6698bf81502dc5bbdfebf3.text: The nightly check now tests the full website with a temporary database instead of just checking documentation. This affects the internal team, who will see automated tests fail if the site breaks, rather than only catching errors in text files.

8a8f1bf4b2dc63db9287af5c37347c3ab5de358a.text: Search engines now receive hidden labels describing the agents, publishers, and store. This helps them understand what each page is about. Regular visitors see no visual changes.

b15da6fa4c00648fae15b7f32d8ad34708cbbccd.text: Visitors typing the main documentation address now land directly on the quick-start guide. The site no longer opens help pages in a new browser tab.

0ccf198a02188bd380c1a2e571fa25dde374a379.text: Ad buttons in the command line tool now show custom text chosen by advertisers instead of always using the headline. If an ad lacks custom text, it falls back to the headline or 'Learn more'. This change is live today and affects anyone who sees ads in the tool.

4a9f5399ab66052e1793f774e3c50fae738fd4cb.text: The text command line tool now tracks pictures and text files together in one list before sending. This change is internal plumbing that prepares the tool for handling text files alongside images. Today, only images are supported, so the visible behavior remains unchanged for the user.

0e8618beae7340f8c5738483e0c57729269e6573.text: The agent store page now loads basic information first and fetches usage statistics separately. This change affects visitors browsing the store, who should notice the page appearing faster while numbers like run counts populate shortly after.

428186cb3b0d7e93b1e3fa1dc6be1ae6c15eebbd.text: Logging out from the command-line tool now also ends your web browser session. If you use the CLI to sign in and out, your web login will no longer stay active after you log out.

eed20257d2a0c7bd1e6c832bba3408e3259d147e.text: A small internal change added a 'created at' timestamp to user session records. This data is now stored in the database, but no feature uses it yet. Regular users will notice nothing; it is groundwork for future cleanup logic.

b9eb4a78d7ce4a1295a83fb65a3d201e7b6a8521.text: The coding assistant now reads personal instruction files from your main user folder, alongside project-specific ones. This means your preferred coding habits and rules apply automatically to every project you open, rather than needing to set them up each time. The assistant treats these personal files as read-only, so it will follow them but never modify them.

6de489d104eb2a8c5df33254babcbdd8082b6853.text: The website now gives search engines clearer information about what each page is, helping them understand the content better. This change affects how search engines see the homepage, pricing, and affiliate pages. Visitors won't notice any visual changes on the site itself.

7f153b3f0c5abe6ea4067329c8b7c289695ba2c9.text: Clicking buttons in the command-line interface no longer accidentally highlights the text inside them. This small internal cleanup fixes a minor annoyance for people using the tool, making the experience feel smoother.

f043ef6f04e61d61a7fa203fb69d671a68154339.text: The automated testing system now automatically fills in placeholder values for two specific service keys when running checks on a server. This prevents test failures due to missing credentials, but it does not change how the application behaves for actual users.

19fc2d7d12eb4a9df4f71aa489b76a7e9db64550.text: Developers accidentally shipped internal setup files with the software toolkit. These extra files made the toolkit slightly larger and could have caused minor conflicts. Users installing the toolkit today will see a cleaner, smaller package with no change in how it works.

1ad9d6062d128b5250882fff882cec350009cef9.text: A new assistant can open a terminal window to check if the command-line interface displays correctly. It uses special scripts to prevent text from getting lost while typing and saves screenshots for review. This is live now for developers building the interface.

86c38afdba3b611d829db4e2619dbf70f304b910.text: The web server now catches unexpected errors and logs them instead of stopping. This keeps the website running for visitors, who would otherwise see a connection failure message if a single request caused a crash. The fix is active today.

1bb18115cb107d956fa0026d5b9ae840db62b72e.text: The coding assistant now automatically refuses to read secret files like passwords or private keys, protecting your data from accidental exposure. If you ask it to look at a folder, you will see these protected files crossed out and marked as blocked, while safe sample files remain readable. This safety check is active today for anyone using the command line tool.

bc83390be8a7c2995938a7162af2209a82b77017.text: When the AI proposes multiple solutions, they now appear side-by-side in boxes instead of stacked vertically. This helps you compare options quickly without scrolling. The number of boxes per row adjusts automatically to fit your screen size.

0a2247ae002a0eb868ab0a38bedb597749cce5d6.text: Programmers swapped out a shortcut that let the system skip checking if error messages were formatted correctly. This cleanup makes the code stricter and easier to maintain. Users will not notice any difference in how the application behaves or looks.

aa14cd499b507412ae2183857efaf076e008124b.text: The command-line tool now accepts multi-byte characters from East Asian input methods. Previously, typing Chinese, Japanese, or Korean text was blocked because the system only allowed single-character input. This change is live and fixes text entry for these languages.

28e56655182b955afbc04b30e07a97e31ac28efb.text: The system now correctly calculates the size of images sent to the assistant, whether they are uploaded directly or linked via web address. Previously, some images were counted incorrectly, which could have affected usage limits or costs. This fix is live and ensures accurate tracking for all image-based requests.

24d04f4074629d1766bd27fde3f4e62e4fc104ec.text: A new command lets you view a searchable list of your past conversations directly in the terminal. When you select a chat from this list, the program will immediately reload that specific conversation so you can continue where you left off. This feature is active today and works for any user who has saved chat history on their computer.

2c0db067743914f34017ba345f6613ac4d70948a.text: The company moved the standard AI assistants into a shared folder so they can be packaged into the command-line tool. This change affects only the internal team building the software, not customers. Customers will not see any difference in the tool's behavior today.

7541b151819f14294dcb1f61a07acf13772ab145.text: The command-line tool now keeps its background data refresh running smoothly without accidentally restarting it every time the screen updates. This fix helps the tool stay responsive and efficient for people checking their activity. You would notice smoother performance and fewer interruptions when using the tool.

21d528e58eb8198508c6d0df275cccfcef7bd886.text: The system now uses a different, more powerful review tool for its highest-quality mode. This change affects only the code review process for complex tasks, not everyday use. Users might notice slightly better suggestions for fixing errors or improving code structure, but the interface and basic workflow remain the same.

0c321bca7d1954fc485583b706ac234bb750cc42.text: The team removed old, unused code from their internal testing tools. This change affects only the software engineers who maintain these tools. They will notice a cleaner codebase, but no changes to how the software works for end users.

1146a2d326051ac01289ba442e7403ff3c7a019e.text: Deleted old, auto-generated files from the project's storage. This cleanup saves space and prevents confusion, as these files were duplicates of the main source. No one notices any change, as these files were never meant to be seen or used directly.

d117982018b999e2bc02269627b1a86a340f4bd8.text: Deleted 24 old error log files from the test folder. These files recorded failed attempts to start automated checks. The cleanup removes clutter from the project history. No current features change for anyone.

f9864d271e8f84678643282a52af796dc759f60c.text: The terminal now checks if you are actively using it before refreshing your credit balance. If you leave the screen idle, it stops asking the server for updates, preventing connection glitches. You will notice the credit numbers stay stable when you are not typing, and update immediately when you return.

20aaa76bb2a5342c178b3789fe752caa38a69235.text: The command-line tool now uses a standard way to stop tasks when you press the cancel key. This fixes issues where the assistant would keep working even after you tried to stop it. You will see the tool respond more reliably to cancellation commands.

0791333cfed30bcc55af1240090ed5e06d47fbd3.text: A hidden switch now lets the team turn on a special tracking mode to spot why the text-based assistant redraws parts of its screen unnecessarily. Regular users see no change because the switch stays off by default. This helps the team find and fix sluggishness issues without needing to rebuild the software.

57a4cce906474762dd99bec2de2d4763f45cc23b.text: Users with a Claude subscription can now link their account directly to the command-line tool. The process opens a web browser to sign in, then pastes a code back into the terminal to finish. Once connected, the bottom of the screen shows how much usage is left and when the limit resets.

37126c04f583af9a61215363c0d25648e999776c.text: When you run out of credits, the command line tool now shows a special screen instead of the normal typing area. Pressing Enter opens your web browser to buy more credits, and the tool checks your balance every five seconds to see if you can start typing again.

98340cb75d0702cc2595c7854cf89ae6a688c748.text: The internal system for collecting usage statistics was cleaned up. Instead of checking the environment first, the system now connects directly to the analytics service. This change affects only the background reporting mechanism; regular users will not notice any difference in how the software works.

43603d527a501ae9d4a2c02e8adfd19f2d8582b0.text: The system now asks the AI provider for the exact length of the conversation instead of guessing. This change affects agents that run on the Anthropic model. You would notice the agent decides when to summarize old messages more accurately, preventing it from cutting off too early or too late. It is live today but requires a specific account key to work.

a2ce12824d8a873e296bd31e89399fd48d753401.text: The assistant now summarizes long chats into a short recap instead of cutting out old messages. This change affects internal tools and is live today. A reader would notice the assistant keeps the main points of a long conversation without losing track of what was said.

72f3a8e02425af57ec6dbd8d21d7e683e26688c9.text: Two image files were added to the website's public storage area. These images are now available for the site to display, though they are not yet visible to visitors. This is a small internal update that prepares the site for future visual changes.

022a5647165db9116361662682f5cf37bb262932.text: A small internal tool now automatically counts money received between September and December 2025. It separates actual sales from processing fees and refunds to show the final net revenue. This helps the business team see accurate monthly earnings without manually checking the payment dashboard.

1b45d60b9cf8d19c8b38a282e5ebf8df09d38281.text: When an assistant's tool fails a check, the error now appears directly in the chat instead of hiding in the background history. This stops the assistant from getting confused by broken records when deciding what to do next. You will see errors clearly in the conversation rather than in invisible logs.

46b792bd9bd8339b916315562ec5968dbb00d212.text: The team added a tool to view saved recordings of command-line tests. People who run these tests can now replay them, export animations, or send data to AI assistants. This is internal tooling for developers, so regular users will not notice any changes.

4974a0ac14084386cac2c89eaa485117378bb084.text: The website now starts its activity tracker automatically when the server boots up, rather than waiting for a specific page to load. This small internal fix ensures that visitor data is recorded reliably from the very first moment the site is live.

32ed3cd539855c9528c7f60d1257416f86260b78.text: The project's main description page no longer shows an animated picture of the software in action. This affects people reading the project's online home page. They will notice the picture is gone, and the page will load slightly faster.

c269c1cfc765ce0e176612df2263b72579883001.text: The system now sets up its usage tracking tool only when it first needs to send a report, instead of waiting for a separate startup step. This change affects the core service, not end-user features. An observer would notice fewer errors about missing tracking data if the startup sequence was interrupted.

6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.text: A new ad system is live in the text-based tool. It shows rotating ads above the typing area to earn credit balance, but only after the user types a specific command to turn it on.

8042f539c522106d8d639e58a570428e440c407f.text: The assistant now keeps track of your recent file edits and to-do lists when the conversation gets too long. It trims old, bulky data but preserves the most important context from the last thirty interactions. You will notice the assistant stays focused on your current tasks instead of forgetting what it just changed.

025f9ea3de3e383d108eb9fee90cfcc744d54b60.text: The automatic daily checks that verify the assistant's core features are now scheduled for overnight runs instead of happening during every code update. This change affects the internal quality assurance process, meaning developers will see faster feedback on routine code changes while still receiving a full system health report each morning.

8edcd033320d505662b983af3d38e3114fe9ff4a.text: The system now cleans up error messages shown to you when something goes wrong. Instead of dumping confusing technical details, it shows just the main problem. This helps you understand what failed without seeing a wall of code, making the tool easier to use when things break.

33f4f1ee757625a0beb228f8c27292ecb28a5bad.text: The system now automatically retries database tasks that fail due to temporary issues like brief connection drops or conflicts. It adds a random delay between attempts so many tasks don't retry at the exact same time and cause more problems. This change is live and prevents occasional errors from stopping your work.

98e09dcabaff3ff8b117fa4969eb003807818ee7.text: The command-line tool now resets your terminal settings before it closes. This stops the screen from getting messy or broken after you quit the program. You will notice clean text and a normal cursor when the tool exits.

eaab1c00c97488d39d1212c7b8b7036f4ca9088b.text: The command-line tool now only asks you to choose a project if you are running it from your home folder or higher. Previously, it mistakenly showed this prompt even when you were already inside a valid project folder. You will only see the project selection menu when you are truly outside of any project.

7d12c4b1de13b91b3d3233fbad77912dd0adf21e.text: The team cleaned up the testing setup by moving test-only tools out of the main program files. They also fixed a bug that could cause the command-line tool to crash when checking certain types of data, and updated the underlying libraries it relies on. Regular users will not see any new features or changes today; the app just runs on slightly newer, more stable parts.

5ed90fba63526c235aca49db1a3eee6e5da4591b.text: The command-line tool now decides whether to retry a failed login by checking the server's standard reply code instead of its own custom error labels. Users will see the same 'retrying' or 'unreachable' messages, but the tool handles timeouts, rate limits, and server faults more consistently. This internal cleanup affects only the login and message-sending flows in the command-line interface.

46b77ba9352d95676ad63add9be1a82e9098ebbd.text: When starting a new project, the tool now automatically creates a folder for custom AI assistant instructions. It also stops crashing if the assistant's data format is broken, showing a 'not available' note instead. These changes apply immediately to new projects.

d785ad2d1cc547704386b254e06d567c35ad9757.text: A new help command lists keyboard shortcuts for the command-line tool. The tool now shows a project selection screen when you start it outside a code folder. These features are live today.

057da0ff3ce9dd133cdf56c49d9ed0db162833ab.text: The system now automatically reports purchased credit usage to the payment provider for billing purposes. This applies only to active customers with a linked payment account. Users will not see any change in their interface, but their usage data is now accurately tracked for invoicing.

9a06ffce0d6666c7b244ebee6f272b9f45a70bf8.text: The system now automatically suspends accounts that file five payment complaints within two weeks. Affected users can no longer use the AI chat and will see a message telling them to contact support to resolve billing issues. This feature is active and designed to encourage direct resolution rather than bank disputes.

a4f80a52b115799c9bdc515677f0388daba736ae.text: A help page explaining how to undo changes and use version control was deleted from the website. This is a small internal cleanup. Readers will no longer see those specific instructions on the site.

7f1db058a8bc17e8cad49d2b7ea6e1c0a8dc9e13.text: The user records now include a 'banned' flag, defaulting to false. This change is internal and does nothing yet, as no part of the system reads or acts on this flag. You will not notice any difference in how the application behaves.

a769cf4ed37e181a5d9d727c67c7ff433b584c37.text: The copy button for your own messages is now part of the text itself, sitting at the end of your words instead of appearing as a separate line below. This change is live. You would notice the button flows naturally with your message and changes to a checkmark when you copy it.

0ced308f91700a9f6d7f376a08f190cc7bca3e4d.text: The company built a new automated helper for its internal testing team. This helper is set up to never ask humans for input, so it can run evaluation tasks completely on its own without waiting for a reply. This is a small, behind-the-scenes change for the testing tools. Regular customers will not see or notice any difference.

2322b7a1c5f6744d284f7cd524d33e4eec3ffc66.text: The website's internal delivery system was upgraded to match new security rules, changing how it fetches web address parts. This affects only the code structure, not the visible interface. Users will notice no change in how pages load or look.

e8889743c35d14d3e1dce50c5f4e6a4fb5723ee4.text: The tool no longer asks you to fill out a complex setup form. Instead, it creates a simple text document where you can write down how to run tests or other checks. You will notice the setup command now produces this readable guide, which helps the assistant know exactly what steps to take after making changes to your files.

05491fbab4eac3f56281ee813f35728748bb9eee.text: Store pages now show a diagram of which sub-agents an agent can call, visible only when the agent has them. The display works live today. The diagram draws relationships between the main agent and its sub-agents, with fallbacks if drawing fails.

017ae9888f1491d0d8f2eae5c59d16f2688cf46b.text: The software now asks the server for only the specific user details it needs, rather than requesting the entire profile every time. This change affects the application's internal data handling, making profile lookups faster and using less network bandwidth. A user would notice quicker responses when the app loads personal settings, though the visible interface remains unchanged.

da195774d6bbcaef8fd202be64a8c675eb00fbda.text: Visiting an agent's general web address now automatically sends you to its most recent saved version. This helps people who bookmark or share the main link, ensuring they always see the current state without needing to know specific version details.

c905bee12e1bb67dc7d8d5779e871b2e315ec8d8.text: The command-line tool now connects your activity before signing in to your account afterward. This change affects people using the terminal tool, helping the team see the full path from first use to login. You will not see any difference in how the tool works.

d8e58ef8a1ca185fabff999e600f1e3cd4d310cd.text: The copy button for your messages now moves directly next to the text instead of sitting in the timestamp line, and it automatically hides after you click it. This prevents the button from staying highlighted or blocking the view while the message is copied. The change is live for all text messages in the chat interface.

eafae3baf8a8c76c7baf5da8c1f1deda373e37a6.text: The command-line tool now changes wording based on how many questions were asked. Instead of always saying 'You skipped the questions,' it will correctly say 'You skipped the question' if only one was asked, and 'You skipped the questions' if many were asked. This affects only the text shown after skipping prompts or viewing answers, making the grammar match the actual count.

b4dd83faf2eb1c5d5e60489c8387f81d8b3a539a.text: The software's underlying data checking and document processing libraries were updated to newer versions to improve stability and compatibility. This change affects the entire application's internal structure but is not visible to users. You will not notice any immediate difference in how the tool works, as this was a routine maintenance update.

6b4ec78c720a54ba6603924840420f20036fa492.text: The help pages were cleaned up to show current instructions and remove outdated guides. This affects people reading the online documentation. They will see clearer steps for setting up custom tools and a more accurate list of the specific AI models used for different tasks.

af236d6388eb1416df385631d1e23f7f0ca94306.text: The coding assistant now uses a newer, more capable model to help write code. It can also draft changes for review before saving them, allowing you to check the work first. These improvements are active for the highest-tier settings.

c119924adde2adf1c18a026d98240bebd563d2c7.text: A new internal automation mode stops the assistant from asking questions or suggesting next steps. This applies only to a specific evaluation tool, not regular users. Nothing changes for everyday interactions.

4a1ada9b8f349517688429aa120711147b1b7fe4.text: The code that checks if you have enough credits before letting you search the web or documentation was moved to a shared spot. This change is purely for the internal structure of the software and makes it easier for the team to maintain. You will not notice any difference in how the search features work or how they charge you today.

bc4b22cd288f7e377c95386b69528cb760453a5b.text: The team fixed a hidden glitch that could cause database setup tools to lose their connection details. This change affects only internal staff running these tools, who would notice that the tools now find the correct database address every time instead of occasionally failing. It is live now.

96a4cd5c691a14a39fbfe73bf3a1c2c1ebf38c0e.text: The code-editing assistant now drafts changes as clear, separate instructions instead of writing them in plain text. This makes the process more reliable and prevents the assistant from accidentally applying the wrong edits. If you watch the assistant work, you will see it list proposed changes first, then apply the chosen one.

b61898eefd0b58773daa08d6fda070349cc2cb5d.text: The program now reads environment settings through a central filter instead of grabbing raw system data directly. This change is internal and does not affect the program's behavior for end users. Users will notice no difference in the interface or performance. The update helps the software run more reliably across different computers and editors.

ae954b5a7e2e340c5b47c21c7af5f0eaffd3d44b.text: The program now strictly separates where different parts of the application get their settings from. This prevents internal configuration leaks between modules, making the command-line tool more stable and secure for all users.

008d91d863e7bf116e83aaf241e191f2d94628d6.text: The database tools now load connection settings through a shared system instead of a special shortcut. This change only affects internal staff running database commands. The visible difference is that the old instructions for why the shortcut was needed have been deleted.

ae711f9e5b384f72d415333d5c13a5dd558ea0ac.text: The command-line assistant now handles question prompts more consistently, ensuring it automatically moves to the next unanswered question after you reply. Additionally, suggested follow-up actions from previous messages are now disabled and appear as plain text, preventing you from accidentally clicking on old options.

1a2cf0fbe4bde70934185dd2a9319a10ab848d63.text: The command-line chat tool now shows only the last 15 messages by default to prevent slowdowns in long conversations. A new button appears at the top of the chat history, allowing you to click and reveal older messages in batches. This change is live today for anyone using the chat interface.

bc6c3285b51a0a3b9102806c5e632bda264fc4e9.text: The command-line assistant now updates its reply text in small chunks every tenth of a second, instead of refreshing for every single word, to make the screen smoother. It also makes sure that this timer is always stopped when the answer finishes or fails, preventing the program from getting stuck or slowing down over time.

2307e67c59b431d1eea7c06cded952f4eac3c4d9.text: The online help guide renamed its 'Getting Started' section to 'Quick Start' and shortened the wording on several pages to make instructions clearer. This change is live for anyone reading the documentation website. Visitors will notice a simpler sidebar and less cluttered text when learning how to use the tool.
