55668e77242f539867994ee0e9589c7517c02533.text: The assistant no longer runs custom JavaScript code in a protected environment. Users who relied on this feature will see those scripts fail to execute. A minor internal fix ensures the user session list loads correctly.

9f05d5e37cd1d2cb1f08fcb363cd8757202763a5.text: The help guide was tidied up by combining two separate pages into one. Readers looking for examples of how to use the tool will now find them all in a single place instead of jumping between different sections.

a49d960c315177906c541d3a90a7b20997248dce.text: The team added a set of saved examples showing exactly what the AI assistant does when it fails to start a task or tries to use a tool it isn't allowed to access. These files serve as a safety net for internal testing, ensuring the system handles these specific errors gracefully. This change affects only the internal evaluation tools and does not impact the live product or end-user experience.

bcc048163c83d0fd4387a65d618b83d057caa839.text: A new internal command now checks if all parts of the development environment are running correctly. Developers will see a clear list of green checkmarks or red crosses for each service, showing exactly what is active and what is missing. This helps them quickly identify and fix issues without needing to manually inspect each component.

b57c75e9cf2999ad20b2fcf006ae127d321935fb.text: Typing a command that takes no extra words now runs without an error, even if you accidentally type something after it. Pressing Tab in the menu now only fills the text box instead of running the command, so you won't accidentally quit or start a new chat. You can now type '/reset' to start a fresh conversation.

7599418572c1441af7650256cd7f765a9c1fd5ad.text: Internal developers now start and stop the database, web server, and command-line tool using a single unified script instead of separate shell commands. This change does not affect customer-facing features or visible behavior. Engineers will notice a smoother setup process when launching the local development environment, with services automatically cleaning up when the main tool exits.

804b82f7f33e98081bab24a56f5900b97b9306d0.text: We moved several older, unused versions of the AI assistant into a separate storage area to keep the main list of active tools clean. This change only affects the internal setup and does not change how the assistant behaves for anyone using it today. You would not notice any difference in the product.

ea9359be498583c1243a988d5e0f24d75c3c4744.text: Developers cleaned up the code to make it easier for computers to read. This is a small, internal change that does not affect how the website looks or works for you.

67f392b73e9fdf36e30a5dd617111234600aed47.text: The assistant now offers clickable suggestions for your next question instead of forcing you to type them out. This feature is live for standard users but is disabled in the lightweight version of the tool. You will see these options appear as buttons after the assistant finishes its current task.

c70c387429ae44627e8946895102985eeba9625b.text: The staging version of the command-line tool now saves its working files in the same personal folder as the production version, instead of keeping them inside the program's own folder. Testers who install this version will see a warning message confirming they are using the testing release, and the tool will remove its old files cleanly when they uninstall it.

67927deabf1e7c17f14dc4a40e14675ddaa51550.text: The team added a check to ensure the system correctly trims conversation history when it gets too long, specifically testing cases where the total length exceeds the limit. This is an internal safety measure that runs automatically behind the scenes. You will not notice any changes to how the tool works today.

815680200858cf794d4d933963073d133036449f.text: The team added a new set of tougher practice problems to test how well their coding assistant handles complex projects. This helps the assistant learn to manage tasks that require coordinating several steps and tools at once. These changes are only for internal testing and do not affect the software you use today.

13fc2cfee4abcf05831876306a576f0712a2c6f9.text: The software's built-in code reviewer now uses a more capable model for internal tasks. It also received stricter instructions to only provide feedback without trying to perform other actions. This change affects internal engineering tools and is live today, though end-users will not see any differences.

86940e3ca7662f0c32805c5120ee221e1f891fa6.text: When you type a slash command into the chat box, picking it from the menu now runs it immediately instead of just filling in the text. Commands that need extra information will show an error if you try to run them without it, and shortcuts for these commands are now visible in the menu list. This update is live for all people using the command line tool.

bc4fcd1010aebb128c6059d556a1035f7c2e0b75.text: The internal test system now includes tougher challenges for four specific software tools. This change helps the team measure how well their AI assistant handles difficult coding tasks. Regular users will see no difference today.

9b5726e3d5abbd49741ca2d372762ea3d6f573fa.text: The tool that deletes old coding workspaces now checks if a program is still running on a specific network channel and stops it before deleting the workspace. It also rejects names with unexpected symbols to prevent errors. This change affects internal developers managing their local workspaces. The new safety checks are active.

ad5815a052e41a708572f75b0f8e23fb3f334e5c.text: The team deleted old, unused software parts that had been sitting around. This is an internal cleanup for the project's maintainers. Regular people using the command-line tool will notice no difference in how it works today.

cd38d63bce75c5439f033ec51998cad44bcbffe0.text: The system now uses a single, shared method to record usage data, ensuring that information sent from the command-line tool matches the web interface. This change also adds a safety net to catch and log errors during this recording process without crashing the application. These updates are live today and improve the accuracy and reliability of internal usage tracking.

f72d0dd5b11234985d46b0b123d92e3a19403fcc.text: The internal testing tool can now check code fixes across several projects at once instead of one. It automatically finds and re-runs the hardest tasks where the AI assistant previously scored poorly. This change only affects the team running these nightly quality checks; customers will not notice any difference in the product today.

eb64e4dca0d7fb6e502fed42022b45e424628c86.text: Developers who build software using this library can now check its quality with a single command instead of several separate steps. This change only affects the internal tools used to build the library, so customers using the final product will not see any difference.

c56032f0efb738f1db1176c56d141ea141329c41.text: The system now stops automatically sharing pictures with smaller helper programs created by the main assistant. If a helper needs to see a picture, it must explicitly ask for the full conversation history. This change is active and prevents accidental data leaks or clutter.

6808457153458c235fb9ad603598efad7169a0a3.text: The setup for developers running this software locally was simplified. Instead of requiring extra tools to manage secret keys, the system now automatically loads them from a standard local file. New developers will notice a shorter, easier installation process with fewer steps to configure their environment.

8dbf674f3b0ae4511f43298d862b6d39f35a28c0.text: The command-line tool now lets people publish agents using a visual checklist instead of typing commands. Users can see which agents will be shared, check boxes to pick them, and confirm the action, with an option to skip the list if they already know which agents to publish.

03169275bafd4f0e1a8d59e760bd6754af1a012e.text: The code that packages this tool now points to the correct internal files, fixing how it finds type definitions. A new script was added to check these definitions across different setup methods, but it is for the team's use and does not change what the tool does for you today.

a52a4c209234fb70a8bdbc8a3eebffd7ab9dbd88.text: The team added a new folder containing practice scripts and automatic checks for the software that connects to Codebuff. These tools let developers test specific tasks like code review and refactoring, or run examples to see how the connection works. This change is internal only; regular users will not see any difference in the product today.

73e2e27486bcd494c28452c302fe43729555ccaf.text: The AI assistant now counts the fixed instructions and tool manuals as part of its short-term memory limit. This prevents the assistant from crashing or losing recent conversation details when the memory is full. The change is active and improves reliability for long sessions.

e4f52de6c61a65b94a47553497bc4757ed4129ab.text: The streaming view for sub-agents previously displayed text twice due to redundant buffering. This fix removes the duplicate handling so text appears once. This affects anyone viewing sub-agent outputs in the Agent Runtime SDK.

7969fc0fd749ae2267eb95e123836faf47d9a149.text: When publishing tools, the confirmation screen now shows which other tools rely on your selection, letting you include them automatically. Built-in tools are hidden from the list to prevent accidental publishing. This helps you avoid breaking other tools that depend on the ones you are about to publish.

edd9eca23e7811ca00573e211e858edc4aa7f537.text: The system that shortens long chat histories now keeps certain paired messages together. This prevents errors when the history gets too long. Users might see fewer crashes during long conversations.

62f371ab9f8fea40c134bacc74ed3c184f655dc9.text: Typing in the command-line message box got steadier: you can click where you want the cursor to go, and deleting selected text removes exactly that text. This also handles tabbed text and resized windows more accurately, so edits are less likely to land in the wrong place. It affects people who write multi-line messages in the command-line program, and they should see fewer misplaced edits.

9f1a79a6d7d0f1cecaba8752a6e24eb445937f47.text: The command-line tool now checks your terminal's dark or light mode setting before the interface starts. This prevents the tool from missing the response, ensuring the text colors match your terminal preferences automatically. You will see the correct theme applied immediately upon launch, without potential color mismatches or delays.

aea1cc2b5b0e724c255ce1d78154608df8b26933.text: The system now counts image size more accurately when deciding how much conversation history to keep. It also cleans up broken conversation records where a request for an action had no matching result. This prevents errors when the chat gets too long or contains incomplete data. The fix is live for internal agents.

7c8087db46d5abfaf5dfb9640efc89ae25f661fa.text: The tool now tells automation scripts how to type into its command window without losing letters. People who run tests or scripts with a terminal multiplexer will see full text appear instead of random fragments. This update is documentation only and does not change the program itself.

afde2ad4554beaf169454cafe821a670be200bc4.text: The team cleaned up the behind-the-scenes code that handles sending messages in the command-line tool. This internal reorganization makes the software easier to maintain and test, but it does not change how the tool works for you. You will not notice any difference in the interface or features.

a77640d86b6a0a36d02fd56722d9c56ebee86fa0.text: The background system that manages sending messages was reorganized into smaller, clearer parts. This internal cleanup fixes hidden errors and removes duplicate steps, making the message flow more reliable. People using the command-line chat tool might notice fewer unexpected glitches when sending messages, but there are no new features or visual changes.

a759cb9d36b85b618122e8a256b15d405f192a81.text: The team cleaned up old, duplicate files used for testing the coding assistant. Two helper files were moved to the current testing folder, while unused standalone command lines and email reporting scripts were deleted. This is an internal housekeeping task; customers and users will notice no changes in the product.

55d40fae1f7ec759ffa4c4b7a171c7534b2953e4.text: The team reorganized the internal machinery that handles sending messages and displaying responses, breaking a large, complex block into smaller, manageable pieces. This change affects only the software's structure, not its features, so you will not notice any difference in how the program behaves or looks. It is a behind-the-scenes cleanup that helps developers maintain the code more easily.

8f4f6608f9fdb8c08ae534463c5d1d935eff66ea.text: The standard assistant now automatically uses a dedicated editor to make changes. Previously, this required a specific setting. This affects default interactions, making the assistant's editing process more consistent and predictable.

0a44c0a2733540c97459a99ac77c0e684b0d6660.text: The command-line tool now stops waiting for color information after a few seconds if the terminal does not respond. This prevents the application from freezing during startup on systems that do not support these queries. Users will notice the interface appearing faster and without hanging, even if the automatic dark mode detection fails to complete.

cc9334c64de77cce03e96f47dd083d245f3f2ba9.text: The app now checks your computer's theme settings directly when it starts, instead of launching a separate background process to do it. This cleanup removes old, unnecessary code used for that separate process. You will not notice any change in how the app looks or behaves; the update just makes the startup process simpler and more reliable behind the scenes.

b71bb469a43dea417bca0074e86030b73297a566.text: The command-line tool now handles shell commands more cleanly behind the scenes. People using this tool might see a small change in how the screen updates while a command runs, but the main benefit is that the code is simpler and easier to maintain.

92a7fd201b02dc80c3408f37fbecd7a9d2d25462.text: The team cleaned up the code behind the command-line tool by removing old, unused instructions and fixing small mistakes in how it checks for updates. This change affects only the people who build and maintain the tool, not the everyday users. If a maintainer looked at the project, they would see a tidier setup that runs checks without complaining about leftover notes.

387cbcfa0baaef8026e24eb202aeb6e82b14828e.text: The text-based program now accepts pictures, either by typing a command with the file path or pasting from the clipboard. It checks the image size and shows a small preview inside the chat window. This feature is live immediately for anyone using the command-line tool.

db30e8c193515679b6ced7ca24cf99f050a99089.text: The internal testing system can now compare their coding assistant against Anthropic and OpenAI's command-line tools. This change is for the team building the product. They will see the external tools listed as options when running performance checks.

8a3d8338e4d6d3cbb867738a67237e66820dbbf4.text: The command-line tool now shows your terminal commands and their results only in the chat window, rather than sending them to the AI assistant. This change affects people using the terminal interface to run shell commands. You will notice the commands still appear in your history, but the AI will no longer see or reference them in its responses.

de8732e50334a2b2c36715e242966b1cfd39981e.text: The assistant now uses a more reliable method to understand its own actions, replacing a fragile text-reading trick. This fixes a bug where tool results from sub-agents were incorrectly attributed, ensuring the main assistant sees the correct output. Users will notice fewer errors when the assistant spawns sub-agents to handle tasks.

780933c2773c184d84d5bba9e3d500642f7c9bfc.text: When running commands in the terminal, the interface now shows a temporary, dashed-border box for active tasks instead of cluttering the chat history. This prevents the screen from jittering when multiple commands run quickly. Once finished, the results appear neatly in the chat log.

091c6d50b52bdf05cee2bb5910bc5d426d9c30e4.text: A new, faster, and cheaper version of the internal coding assistant was added. This version uses a quicker model and skips some detailed planning and review steps to save time. It is only for internal use and does not change how external customers interact with the service.

10614922a610bd81b6f9491aa50eec0f47a193fa.text: The assistant now uses the same top-tier model for all coding tasks, removing two experimental settings that previously offered different reading styles. This change affects internal testing and does not alter the behavior for general users. No visible difference appears in the standard interface.

2ff04a605d1bc4152b2e674d27b7a1ae8b2cf4a7.text: The command line tool now hides its low credit warning banner for users who have automatic refills turned on. This change applies only to those specific users. They will see the warning disappear unless their account balance hits zero.

515b7693ac6b2f8378ca9df3d5d8bc4de82744e4.text: When you run a command directly in the chat, the tool now displays a temporary placeholder that updates with the actual results once the process finishes. This ensures the assistant accurately sees the command's success or failure status, rather than guessing, while also showing the specific folder where the command ran.

9bfbea1d4e17832f2fed4e58702550e75b34fdcb.text: The assistant now automatically shows a balance warning in the text command line when your credit runs low, instead of waiting for you to ask. It checks your balance every thirty seconds and displays the alert for five minutes before hiding it. This helps you notice when you are about to run out of credits without needing to remember a special command.

56ecce97fc37d6e98ea499132138fc28cf9d4170.text: The assistant's editing mode now forces it to pause and plan its steps before changing any code. This internal update aims to reduce mistakes by ensuring the AI thinks through the task first. Users won't see a new button, but might notice the AI taking a moment to outline its approach before making edits.

d05275532c93db7601d0c45d5740b32db33fd084.text: The program cleaned up how it listens for your keystrokes, combining separate checks into one central system. This is an internal maintenance update, so you will not notice any change in how the chat responds to your typing.

9bcd14928a9295924c79855964f0e6bf45828ee4.text: The system now prepares extra tools in a separate step instead of mixing that work with the main process. This internal cleanup helps the software stay organized but does not change how the assistant behaves or what it can do. Regular users will see no difference.

3e144e64550be90029e056b819564add6e1f6c9b.text: The AI assistant can now pause and show a multiple-choice menu in the command-line interface when it needs more details to build a plan. Users will see a list of options they can select with their keyboard, and the assistant will wait for these answers before continuing its work.

05880abe323b6862e31bc5691a6b42f68cf89cda.text: The command-line tool now uses a single, shared gateway for all website interactions. This change improves how the tool reports errors and handles login sessions. Users will notice clearer messages if a connection fails, but the visible features remain the same.

ea119d20250121da03859f9303b2533c2ae3fbd0.text: The internal system now uses a different AI model to pick the best answer from several drafts when solving complex problems. This affects only the team building the tool, not customers. You would notice nothing, as the change is internal and invisible to users.

170f4ac03f25ef3c2252ed382a85a261e2ec9b00.text: The program moved the rules for showing credit warnings into a separate file. Users of the command-line tool will see no change in how the green, yellow, or red banners appear or when they pop up. This is an internal cleanup to make future updates easier.

90505cc2fddb0cba143ef0524cd598d693a6e012.text: The command-line tool now uses a single shared design for its on-screen banners. This ensures the message text wraps neatly and the close button works consistently regardless of window size. The change is internal, so you will not notice any difference in behavior.

40b0eaac602f290e5127508fe56c6bdcae1b990e.text: The internal AI assistant system added two new configuration profiles using a specific high-performance model. These profiles are currently only used for internal testing and benchmarking, so regular users will not see any changes or have access to these new options today.

c397e4bb6633591bbc0be0ca45900bf89bd1453c.text: The terminal app now has a new command to redeem referral codes or display your shareable link. You can type the command to enter a special mode where the app fetches your details and shows the link, or you can include the code directly with the command to redeem it instantly. This change is live today.

282c13d7bfc774cac3a990c988aa21586a6e3762.text: The command-line tool now checks referral codes for correct format and shows clear error messages if redemption fails or if the referral link cannot be loaded. Entering bash mode requires typing only the exclamation mark, and the default input prompt text is now lowercase.

e2ac3956fd4bbb82821a0b344e7968826d14ead8.text: The internal system that decides what happens when you type a command into the chat window was reorganized into a cleaner list format. This change is purely for the developers, making it easier for them to add new commands or fix bugs later. You will notice no difference in how the application behaves or looks.

4b7158cceb1db887ffbcdf0de8daff9da37ee0bd.text: The command line tool now automatically fixes the format of referral codes you type, so you do not have to worry about capitalization or missing prefixes. It also shows clear error messages if the system cannot load your account details, rather than failing silently. These updates are live for anyone using the command line interface.

8ebd20c4b4f1601b4f4b8e63f40b4dcd7aabcb60.text: The command-line tool now checks how wide your window is to decide how much space to give messages and buttons. Instead of just looking for one specific width, it recognizes four sizes, making the layout adapt better to very narrow or very wide screens.

7d389c79603ffef1b287f51493b37f177be2c7ec.text: The code that displays the buttons and timing information below each response was moved to its own file. This is an internal cleanup that does not change what you see or how the program works.

7028a55d670b1caeee9913d27ac38648c1def091.text: The command-line tool now tries several ways to ask the terminal for its background color, especially when running inside a specific window manager. If the first attempt fails, it immediately tries the next option before giving up. People using that window manager will see the tool match their terminal's dark or light theme more reliably, instead of sometimes showing unreadable text colors.

b3f58f1583db98cf167f1d2bbdfbc14633a78799.text: The command-line tool now uses a stronger artificial intelligence model for its most demanding coding tasks. This change applies only when you select the maximum effort mode. You would notice the assistant producing more reliable solutions for complex problems.

85840c1a181ec17e838f801af87b2b9b01367759.text: The command-line tool now remembers your chosen assistant mode after you close and reopen it. Previously, it always reset to the standard mode every time you started. This applies only to people using the text-based interface on their computer.

983639b668d1cc516831efb9419a9d975d92b17a.text: The system used to keep two separate lists of conversation history, requiring extra memory and copying steps. Now it uses a single list directly, so the AI agent runs faster and uses less memory. This is an internal cleanup with no visible change to how the agent behaves or what it can do.

b3c4c6eb3f506c1a924a0017b5c0c51182b1a08c.text: When you submit a message with a problem, the warning now appears next to that specific message instead of at the top of the screen. This helps you quickly see which message failed and why.

db2ca99cf368616723532902ed6e235764f3b653.text: The assistant's internal setup for launching helper tasks no longer stores its core instructions in a shared background object. Instead, these instructions are passed directly to each helper task when it starts. This is an invisible structural cleanup; users will not notice any change in how the assistant behaves or responds.

a7162eb89147da6766c7f3a6c4a462233712bd0a.text: A copy button was added to the footer of each message. Clicking it copies the full text of the message, including nested parts, to your clipboard. The wait time before the copy action completes was reduced, so the copy happens faster.

7e2ec29d0364ae0695fbedbda96acd28f950c322.text: The internal plumbing for how the assistant's tools report their results was cleaned up to be simpler and more direct. This change affects the software's internal structure, not the assistant's behavior. A reader would notice no difference in how the assistant works today.

08a7817c1c838ec7cdebaf79ca7c965080490573.text: The system now uses standard industry terms for how tools describe their inputs, replacing custom names. This internal cleanup ensures the assistant understands tool requests correctly. Users will notice no change in behavior; the update is purely structural to align with broader software standards.

05d94aa57087efb9bd2d9a9c9eb7f1213f66ee15.text: The command-line tool now adds numbers like #1 and #2 when it shows several identical AI helpers at once. This helps people tell apart duplicate tasks running in parallel. The change is live and affects anyone using the tool's interface.

c0f35bea0a53ef0a7958fb98c7668ad80c21dafa.text: The command-line tool now supports a 'publish' command. This allows users to upload their local agent templates to the central service. If you run this command, your templates are sent to the backend for others to use.

4c9ea8c6a70b5c8f93c498d2bbdab2cd5be618cc.text: The program now checks if your terminal window is active. If you click away, the typing marker stops flashing to save power. This feature stays off until your terminal confirms it supports this check.

bd4783f5a274f641b8397c5dc54f7ec6cf1514d7.text: The internal system that checks code for mistakes now uses a different artificial intelligence model for its most thorough checks. This change affects only the software tools used by the company's own developers. Since this is an internal update, external customers will not notice any difference.

666b406a3a8eb7e05f5a1e266501426ff5e1d65c.text: The tool now automatically waits and tries again when a temporary connection problem stops it from finishing a task. This helps people using the tool directly in their own programs, who will see it recover from brief network hiccups instead of failing immediately. The waiting time grows longer with each attempt to avoid overwhelming the server.

a699bc369f2f25900e4f3af0411d4bf507745b25.text: The team simplified the internal system that picks AI models for coding tasks. They removed support for Google's Gemini model and renamed the high-effort setting to 'max', which now uses OpenAI's GPT-5.1. This is a backend cleanup for the development team; customers will not notice any change in how the product works today.

83a4bfe07f54a7f57b4113d5a721808b10825acf.text: The internal assistant now uses a specific Google model for routine code checks instead of a generic one. This change is live and affects the default review process for internal tooling. Users will see no visible difference, as only the underlying reviewer model changed.

ed6e1d350c8d06b15507c0b82ce54a65bf0a01d2.text: After installing the command-line tool, the setup now shows a short welcome message with steps to start using it. This affects people who install the tool from the command line. They will see the instructions right after the install finishes.

97e8da47b7b1afc60b74c77a65dad1b03cb6f850.text: The command-line interface now keeps its message buttons and text input from flashing or lagging while you type or react to replies. This change affects only people using the terminal tool. You might notice the screen feels smoother and less jittery during long chats.

98f07dd7fb0a63a48e64aa38200065139812ee04.text: The tool now reads the main code directly instead of waiting for a separate build step. This affects the program's own builders. They would see the tool start up faster and without errors caused by outdated code.

14efb668c81fd4179c4c7c316074e0490899497e.text: The internal method for passing tool results between assistant components was simplified. The data structure was flattened, removing an extra wrapper layer and moving the tool identifier to a higher level. This change affects how the system tracks and processes tool outputs, potentially improving efficiency in handling complex agent interactions.

956847a245a4e27dc28944d5383f52f75f040a16.text: The command-line tool now uses a shared system for handling failed requests instead of its own separate method. This change affects everyone using the command-line interface. You will now see a clear message on your screen whenever the tool is automatically trying to resend a request that failed.

5c377ee1a4e4a7d7d2e4e12ee8f5b862fcd1db8e.text: The code editor's backend removed unused Gemini integrations and consolidated GPT-5 into a 'max' mode. This internal cleanup has no visible impact on the user interface today.

6ad51cc53cbb42ea703dec7a8fb785fd94d9f4d3.text: A notice box now appears at the top of the command-line chat window to inform users about a new interface update. This box includes a link to send feedback and instructions for reverting to the previous version. The notice is active immediately and can be closed by clicking a button.

174a50a54c312498a093de80f3ec16c356aef3fa.text: The terminal tool now shows the user's remaining credit balance in a pop-up banner after they run the usage command. This update ensures the balance information appears automatically when the banner opens, rather than requiring a separate manual request. The change is live today and affects anyone using the command-line interface to check their account status.

07c317efa31f9cbb124d001bd1d75765f81015d9.text: The command-line tool now shows clearer, more helpful messages when connection or login problems occur, explaining exactly what went wrong instead of just a generic error. Additionally, the shortcut for deleting text now correctly removes only the visible line on the screen, even if the text wraps around, making it easier to fix mistakes while typing.

adfbddada89a400496438ee1acbad5535695d75a.text: The command-line tool now updates your credit balance display automatically after each task, but only while that balance banner is visible. This keeps the shown number current without making the tool pause to fetch new data. If the update fails, the tool logs the error and continues working normally.

979ee8921cd8ab662050d2321fb6408b9e591d3a.text: The part of the chat screen where you type your message was moved into its own separate piece. This change is for the developers who build the tool, not for you. You will notice no difference in how the chat looks or works today.

aa78173fbc0077512011a1b80bec9b6ddb9f1778.text: The command-line tool now uses a smarter timer system to handle delayed actions. If a timer is set for a specific task, starting a new timer for that same task automatically cancels the old one. This prevents conflicting actions and ensures the tool cleans up properly when closed.

405e44db858954df8326fe7a6fea528a24e364b1.text: The chat window now displays your entire conversation history on the screen at once, instead of hiding older messages to save space. You will no longer see a notice telling you that only the latest messages are visible or that you need to scroll to load more. This applies to anyone using the command-line interface, and the change is live today.

e9d1ea54241dc3e7fbc4bc6f095b629e39adb630.text: The tool's display system was updated to fix a bug where text messages sometimes appeared as blank spaces. This change is live now. Users running the command-line assistant will notice that their messages and responses are consistently visible, rather than occasionally disappearing.

13a08d80e24c9b421d2f26752ba2d6fd68653d11.text: The application's text input now uses a built-in feature for handling pasted text, replacing a custom workaround. This change is internal and improves stability. Users will not notice any difference in how the application behaves.

3d3296b4ea103f3c01c2f2683fb9131c1bd7fe2b.text: The internal editing assistant can now use a new artificial intelligence model to help write code. This change is not active for anyone yet because it requires a specific setting to be turned on. When enabled, the assistant will ask this new model to create code plans instead of using its previous default method.

c07be589486b045d51cf600a1718cbaa589b98cf.text: The team added a new option to use Google's latest AI model for internal coding assistants. This change is not live for customers today; it only applies to specific internal agent configurations. If someone looked at the internal settings, they would see new choices for this model, but the default behavior remains unchanged.

ce8746f8d07699fe23e93474228befa70626b689.text: The command-line tool now includes a separate search program inside its own installer. When you run the tool, it unpacks this search program onto your computer so the assistant can find text in your files. This affects people using the packaged version of the tool, not those running it from source code.

1816b44e4fbfc3c1759cb4fb3289d89be63229c2.text: The tool now keeps its main program inside the folder where you installed it, instead of downloading it separately to your home folder. This means uninstalling the tool automatically deletes the program, leaving no leftover files behind. You would notice a cleaner system after removing the software.

0ec450befdd1e05d7accdeb197863e3ce5b0ff8d.text: The command-line tool now fetches your credit balance from the main website instead of a separate background server. This update is live today. If you run the usage command, you will see a more detailed breakdown of your spending and remaining credits, including any debt or organization-level limits, rather than just a simple total.

9eebdf564d275d8fd08af15dbccf386a11fb4938.text: The team removed a backup option for an internal assistant that was designed to review code. This change is small and affects only the internal tools, not the main product. Customers will not notice any difference because the feature was never active for them.

8e91efe579ef943192965ebf293613d30cea3125.text: The team added a guide explaining how they test their AI coding assistant. This document helps internal staff understand how the assistant is graded on real coding tasks. It does not change how the assistant behaves for regular users today.

349207f275379f7a4070094f7183c47a4cbe8cc0.text: The program's startup process was reorganized internally to separate how it checks for terminal color support from its main launch sequence. This change affects only the software's internal structure and does not alter how it runs or appears to the person using it. You would not notice any difference in the tool's behavior or interface.

63695fd1cb54c891cbf6a049de88203803551ea0.text: The team cleaned up the internal machinery that decides which helper robots work on a task. They removed several experimental options that are no longer needed, simplifying the setup to use only the standard, proven combinations. This change affects only the internal system structure and requires no action from anyone. Nothing visible to the outside world changes.

9aba6179f07afd42472ea2c8568b264599736692.text: The tool now stores the open or closed status of each chat section directly with the message, rather than tracking it in a separate list. This change affects the visual layout of the command-line interface, specifically how much text is visible by default. You will notice that detailed reasoning and agent lists start out hidden to save screen space, while tool usage details remain visible.

60e64003fc6cb8f91ece050371c5f18470cdcb96.text: The system now uses a single, simplified method to choose the best answer from multiple options, removing complex, outdated logic that handled different types of AI models separately. This change affects internal tools used by staff to generate text. Users might notice slightly faster responses or more consistent answers, but the core functionality remains the same.

d1991436ee87e7a50aa5cd1c8955c64e174dbe1d.text: The feedback form for the command-line tool now remembers what you typed even when you switch screens, so you don't lose your draft. The form also offers clear choices like 'Good result' or 'App bug' to help categorize your report. Once you send feedback, the buttons lock to prevent accidental double-submissions.

02673a5a36c56079121349f82cf8ef8292adafdc.text: The terminal tool now lets you rate its answers. You can click a small icon next to any message or type a command to open a box where you pick a category and write a note. This helps the team track what works and what breaks.

5dc3cb8f5d3c297141fdf29dc54d7b791705484c.text: The 'max' performance setting for the coding assistant now uses a different AI model to pick the best code option from several drafts. This change is live for anyone using the 'max' mode, though it does not alter the visible interface or the final code output.

67fc4211757842802ad66af074415327313236a9.text: The system can now talk to OpenAI directly for one specific model when generating multiple answers at once, skipping the usual middleman. This only works if the new direct connection is enabled and the right settings are used. Normal chat features look and work exactly the same.

415d0e7edf82282fe445e5e53a4eb9b400c129f7.text: The software now generates multiple draft answers at once instead of launching separate helper programs for each one. This speeds up the process and reduces the chance of errors for anyone using the editor's 'best-of-n' feature. You would notice the tool showing a message about generating several implementations simultaneously, rather than running them one by one.

bf3c551cdc5273e913222fa3304231bd2edc66d3.text: The tool's creators now have a simple button to automatically package and publish new versions, eliminating manual assembly steps. This internal change does not affect end users, who will continue to install updates normally without noticing any difference.

2bf17736b6335ff9b84f30e0cf4c849cee0561a3.text: The command-line tool now downloads its main program directly to your computer when you install it, rather than including it in the initial package. This change affects anyone installing the tool today. You might notice a slightly longer wait during installation as the file is fetched, but removing the tool will now automatically delete these downloaded files without leaving leftovers behind.

94368ccf248874fa609a0c64672134d6f3eff6b2.text: You can now resume your last conversation instead of starting fresh. When you run the command, the tool automatically loads the previous chat history from your computer. If no history exists, it simply starts a new session without any errors.

0113870be5722e9f1d35500ebd97af8f509a77a6.text: A hidden piece of code that handled typing commands like '/logout' or '/exit' was removed because it was no longer used. This change affects only the internal structure of the application and has no impact on what you see or how you interact with it. You will notice no difference in the app's behavior.

e6fbb859c88a1211185293e12729a369875e7ead.text: The internal coding assistant now has a new configuration that uses a single-pass generation model instead of the previous multi-candidate approach. This change is currently limited to internal testing and evaluation environments. Users will not notice any difference in the standard assistant experience.

3158a6f1ae2d7f078f8cf682a48a83f6c8cab8c2.text: When the AI assistant looks up information in a documentation library, it now shows a simple line indicating which library and topic it is reading. This helps you see what source the assistant is using. You will notice this in the terminal output when the assistant performs a search.

e8e8a05fcb281138c308840f70c28154e8cb3b42.text: The AI assistant now includes a new internal helper that can review complex tasks and make final choices. This helper is only available when using the specific 'max' performance setting. Users choosing this setting might see the assistant pause briefly to consult this helper before giving an answer, potentially leading to more accurate decisions on difficult problems.

0aed1a8c261a72a8b5f60878d41693f4c6b846f2.text: The command-line chat window now has a cleaner bottom bar that shows how long the assistant has been working and a clear button to jump back to the latest messages. You can now pause the queue of waiting messages directly from this bar. The text input field also handles special characters like tabs more reliably, preventing the cursor from jumping to the wrong spot.

fa9ae200a8deda63f5cf9923794dbd56a1c79403.text: A new internal assistant mode now automatically checks its own code edits for errors before finishing. This change is for internal use only and does not affect the standard tools or interfaces that regular users interact with.

99166d1235b91ccda0f08ade523e00c5be5c439d.text: Developers reorganized the internal structure of the command-line interface's message display without changing its appearance or behavior. This internal cleanup makes the code easier to maintain and test for the team. You will notice no difference in how the tool looks or functions.

7e505fbceb0d2c91b30efceb72f8fa23075e3d00.text: The search tools for the web and documentation now use a different provider. Instead of calculating the cost of a search on the user's device, the system now receives the exact cost from the provider's server. Users will not see any changes in how they search, but the billing for these searches is now handled more accurately on the backend.

5aff4e9abb7e273137e9897ed92e08089e85afca.text: Users can now connect their own account to OpenRouter. The system checks for this personal connection and skips charging service credits when it exists. This update is active, allowing people to use their own provider limits instead of shared ones.

56d7380c078b5768aad603721901a06a31c2fbff.text: The system now has two new ways to look up information: one for searching the internet and one for finding documentation for specific software libraries. These tools are not turned on for regular users yet; they are waiting for someone to build a way to actually use them. If you try to use them today, you cannot, because there is no button or setting to trigger them.

2dd14a8796d9eb5e03b00d4d8f713f044fc3f6e9.text: A new internal option lets the assistant generate several different reviews for the same code changes and pick the best one. This affects only the specific new assistant profile. You will not notice this change unless you use that profile, as it replaces a single review with a multi-review selection process.

bde7e88d8f549ae4e56913c25ca9e5b07384692c.text: The text box in the command-line tool now tracks where the cursor sits when long lines wrap across multiple rows. People typing multi-line prompts will see the up and down arrow keys move the cursor to the correct line instead of jumping to the wrong place. This fix is live today.

90e3928e01d3d9600e466ed7c4d8c06492a4f80d.text: The software now allows external tools to control how it checks project history. This change is currently internal and does not affect everyday users or visible features yet.

f98abc6747424c58719df37a51f6b84c20983172.text: Theme detection logic moved into the hook that manages it, consolidating state and detection into one place. This is internal cleanup; no visible behavior changed for the user.

9f957b42e3f0b7bf8a9c2bee7c06ece6c64b34ec.text: The AI assistant now stops working immediately when you cancel a task, preventing it from running tools after you have stopped it. This applies to all users of the software development kit, ensuring that cancelled requests do not consume extra resources or produce unexpected results.

166714289a14e603703e5a97e3eb9e7b5fc299e5.text: Internal tooling updated to route specific review tasks to a new model. This change does not affect external users or products.

a1aefce57da230dee0f784dbc22ad0c7bf3c735f.text: The program now checks its internet connection every ten seconds when it first starts, but automatically slows down to once every ten minutes if the connection stays stable for a long time. If the connection drops, it immediately resets to checking every ten seconds. This change applies to the command-line tool and reduces background network traffic for long-running sessions.

3e90de9474241a1f14dfd9cb1639ab10178b0823.text: A new button design prevents the app from crashing when you click and drag over interactive elements like scroll indicators or mode toggles. This change is live today and ensures the interface stays stable during mouse interactions.

3baf4009a3728d1df7aaa75537148ebee2048f61.text: The program now checks your computer's light or dark appearance setting directly, rather than opening a separate background window to do so. This prevents a brief glitch where the screen colors might flicker or fail to update correctly upon launch. The change is active immediately for all users.

c6b9afa2061bd4a1e20b1640ed273858e0765870.text: A button now appears when scrolling up in the chat, letting you jump back to the newest message with one click. The status line also changed to show how long a task has been running and if the connection is active. These updates are live today for anyone using the command-line chat.

519af8336763e7adef1740f28d0e5442e21bbe9b.text: A new command lets you check your remaining AI credits directly in the tool. You can see how much you have left, plus any bonus amounts and when your limit resets. This feature is active now and available to all logged-in users.

3e8ea0f28e6db2832558a3ccd7aa75929ca6539b.text: The chat interface now redraws less frequently while text is streaming, preventing the screen from flickering or stuttering. This affects anyone using the terminal-based assistant. You would notice smoother updates and less visual noise as the AI writes its response.

267fadde6c1040b10f172801f22c71887f9357ea.text: The internal translation layer between the app and external AI providers was copied into a private folder. This copy adds support for images, structured data, and tool use. Internal developers can now switch AI providers without relying on outside code.

fe344e336954a2f3fb7ec20e5b5f8669b7569448.text: A small internal cleanup fixed a warning in the tool that checks for errors in the code. This change helps the engineering team keep the software healthy but does not change how the product works for anyone else.

2ff2d8eec8ff45929540bff08232b4e4464f8563.text: Developers added a hidden tracking tool to the command-line interface to monitor how often message displays refresh. This change is currently disabled, so users will notice no difference in performance or appearance.

61bec3cb33c0182c25640c2d39b15877a9d7f62b.text: The text-based interface now displays file search results as a single, concise line showing the search pattern and current directory, instead of potentially cluttering the screen with raw data. This change affects anyone using the command-line assistant to find files, making the output easier to read and scan quickly. The feature is live today for users of the command-line tool.

aa16ab568526a0366456d84cfe7d74dfc841e6b0.text: The team renamed an internal helper that assists with editing code to match their standard naming rules. This change affects only the internal tools used by the AI assistant, so there is no visible difference in how the software works or looks for anyone using it.

4b5f5e457dba3f9e2a25d53c69f5b72dcb13e8b1.text: The code that displays the timer counting seconds in the command-line interface was moved into its own separate piece. This stops the entire screen from refreshing every second just to update the time. Users will see a smoother display while waiting for the assistant to think.

946bf225ab7b2e053524aa25771b29338303fb5f.text: The program's inner instructions were rearranged into separate folders without changing how it works. This is an internal cleanup for the people who build the tool. You will not see any difference in how the program runs or responds.

31feeceadd86485c98003c47fe88d70126e4d4c9.text: The software now automatically finds project instruction files, checking for a specific 'knowledge' file first, then an 'agents' file, and finally a 'claude' file. This helps the AI understand the project's context without requiring users to manually point to these files. The change is live and ensures projects using the newer 'agents' standard are recognized correctly.

10a77c9cf193eaa4205656f7aff9ba657d7bc8e2.text: The text-based assistant now hides its internal reasoning steps by default. This keeps the conversation window clean and prevents long analysis notes from pushing the final answer off the screen. You can click the greyed-out summary box to expand and read the full reasoning if you want to see how the answer was reached.

480358465d3d5ec1266aded222aff5c88af41c89.text: The tool now offers a new way to solve difficult problems by generating several possible answers at the same time and picking the best one. This feature is active for users on the default and GPT-5 plans. You will notice it when asking for help with complex tasks, as the assistant may take a moment to compare options before giving you its final response.

dcc0065a1c0ba72393551fd5c6456a307d8fee71.text: Developers reorganized the internal code that draws chat messages in the command-line interface. This change is purely technical and affects only how the software is maintained. Users will notice no difference in appearance or behavior, as the visual output remains exactly the same.

8e9cece8db39ed643d192cde78ced48c799c5b56.text: The command-line interface's internal structure was reorganized to separate the main application frame from the chat window. This change affects the software's underlying code but does not alter visible features, performance, or user behavior. You will not notice any difference when using the tool.

f949ce7dcdca3fbf5acfd0c4b50009fbd789d7bd.text: The command-line chat tool now displays a horizontal line with a bold label when you switch modes or start a new message. This visual break separates different sections of the conversation history, making it easier to see when the tool's behavior changed without needing to remember previous settings.

674e32910ecd258cdbe5a385d3840d4e213ebf8a.text: The computer now remembers what each message looks like so it doesn't have to redraw the whole screen every time a new word arrives. This stops the text from flickering or jumping around while the assistant is typing out a long answer. The change works right now for anyone using the command-line tool.

e986021ad3703043db335b6e60ab5d8c54d0d3fb.text: The text box where you type now measures the exact space available on your screen instead of guessing. This stops your words from wrapping to the next line too early when the window is narrow. The small status button on the right also adjusts its size correctly, leaving the right amount of room for your message.

a9d2c6d98e6eedaad2e8a51a891427487fd486fc.text: The internal assistant now uses a single, faster search tool instead of a heavier duplicate version. This change applies to the background systems that help find relevant files for coding tasks. Users will not notice any visible difference in the interface.

38c345fddae2e93c0411fd400c8b9f1158694321.text: The code behind the chat screen was reorganized into separate, smaller pieces to make it easier to update. This is an internal cleanup, so users will not notice any change in how the tool works or looks.

3a4bb9426497e14f22ec68a982cf95cee262406b.text: The text-based assistant now visually highlights exactly which lines of text it changed in your files. Added lines appear in green, while removed lines show in red, making edits easy to spot. This feature is live today for anyone using the command-line version of the tool.

569aa21fe301a74f85f40a3ccb2076ccdbf45035.text: The command-line tool now displays a bold 'Task Complete' message when an automated task finishes. This helps people see clearly when work is done without reading technical details. The change is live for anyone using the current version of the tool.

291adef5277d360edd064523a5171b088904db0a.text: The command-line assistant now displays a visual checklist when it plans multi-step tasks. People using this tool will see progress bars with checkmarks for finished steps and empty boxes for pending ones, making it easier to track what the assistant is doing.

bddfb8a52d16bf2c1b157382e392a17f8e9af54d.text: The command-line assistant now shows a list of file paths when it reads a folder structure. This change is live for anyone using the command-line tool. You will see a simple line of text listing the paths, without any option to expand or collapse the details.

de236d698f9b83773b4fe50cfb93f0ed1600ff5e.text: The text you type to talk to the assistant now sits inside a drawn box. This helps you see exactly where the message area starts and ends. The box looks the same as other boxes on the screen.

d34e86a543f72eb11f0f9838621009f07726377e.text: The assistant's file search tool now handles custom starting folders correctly. Previously, searching for files within a specific directory could return wrong results or miss files entirely. This fix ensures that when you ask the assistant to look for files in a particular folder, it accurately finds exactly what matches your request. This change is live for all users of the agent runtime.

3c4d47aa33f92d6dbde97c28f2db636c0242cf4f.text: The tool now forces you to explicitly check if an action succeeded before using its result. This affects anyone building applications with this software, as they must update their code to handle potential failures properly. If they don't make this change, their programs might crash when an action fails, instead of showing a clear error message.

0a30509a990ed2c22278282e35da2d4736ec06f9.text: When the assistant reads files, the list of file names now shows the first file on the same line as the action, the next two on separate lines, and any remaining files grouped together on one line. This change affects people using the command-line interface today. You will see a cleaner, more compact view of which files are being accessed, without extra lines for every single file.

22452ae741879dd71b30193efb8585f9f1419bdc.text: The text chat window now speeds up scrolling when you keep scrolling in one direction. This change only affects the command-line version of the app, not the web or desktop versions. You will notice the chat moves faster without needing to scroll as much.

a2aaf401d7a8857b5e12643832b10b438c5e867f.text: The command-line tool's mode selector now expands smoothly when you hover over it, preventing the interface from flickering as the mouse moves in and out. This visual improvement applies to the text-based assistant interface, making the switch between fast, max, and plan modes feel more stable and responsive.

181a942c1336c3e198f43edca9e10af0a0d2c9ac.text: The command-line assistant now shows its actions in a tidier list. The screen looks the same, but the system can display new types of actions without breaking the old ones. This is an internal cleanup, so you will not see any new features yet.

982826a24ba6ed6d3f5ad0b1bc764d9df640dc9e.text: When the command-line tool fails to process a message, it now records the failure details in a clear, standard format instead of a messy dump. This helps support teams read the logs and diagnose issues faster. The tool still behaves the same for you, but the internal record of the problem is now easier to understand.

622efe1d9de19eeababd42d2999e49fe8402869d.text: The software now automatically finds project files if none are provided, instead of assuming the list is empty. This affects developers using the SDK who do not explicitly supply project files; they will notice that the assistant can now see and use project context without extra setup. The fix is live today.

2bb32123f60ddb7e4005bec14aae94e29a6404b3.text: The website's preparation process now checks if it can retrieve the list of AI agents before going live. This helps ensure that the agent store page loads correctly and shows up properly in search results for visitors.

8123b654697ca99500ce7f3f86f90ddde3c5eaaf.text: The command-line tool now saves your recent typed messages to a file on your computer. When you open the tool again, it remembers what you wrote, so you can find and reuse past messages easily. This only applies to the command-line interface, not the web version.

0a6469f29d60e48a1aa18c4a6fc74281273689a4.text: The command menu now finds commands even if you type letters out of order or miss a few, and it highlights the matching parts in color. This helps anyone using the command line interface find what they need faster. You will see these changes immediately when you type a slash command.

90a461c2e715db1aa14e174c1ce7893bd9bb47c1.text: The command-line interface received a visual refresh, introducing rounded buttons for toggling modes and viewing status. The interface now displays agent and tool information in separate, cleaner sections. Users will notice a more polished look with distinct, clickable pills for options like agent mode, replacing the previous box-style indicators.

78f004a6bcef7bc20cec2153b55127a5629fde98.text: The store page now pulls agent information directly from the database instead of asking the site's own internal system for it. This change affects the store page's reliability and speed, specifically by preventing potential errors when the site is being prepared for release. Visitors would notice fewer loading failures or blank spots on the agent listings.

22e79b1075811c2c7819a1d4a55763cc5bee77c5.text: The command-line tool's internal structure was cleaned up to make slash commands and agent modes easier to manage. This change is strictly for developers maintaining the software. Regular users will notice no difference in how the tool behaves or looks.

ed8123417d0efdc798db9c0b825982936b241ea0.text: After the assistant finishes making a plan for a project, two new clickable buttons appear in the command line window. These buttons let you instantly choose how the assistant should build the project, either quickly or with maximum effort, without needing to type any commands. This feature is live today for anyone using the assistant's planning mode.

328e5f2b849e1242af413cc72549754d1caba9ba.text: Programmers moved the code that gathers store data back to its original location, separating it from the page display logic. This internal cleanup affects only the engineering team's workflow and the store's data loading method. Visitors browsing the store will notice no changes to the agents listed or how the page looks.

c4525b44712ca41a7f4033b0e62143368d3e62a4.text: The assistant can now view a map of project folders and files without reading every line of code inside them. This tool limits the view to about four thousand words, dropping the deepest folders first if the list gets too long. The feature is live and helps the assistant understand project structure quickly without getting confused by too much detail.

3e5f667a18687dab45fb0713e3f550d2d907a1cd.text: The tool now recognizes a new command to set up its initial state. This change mostly rearranges internal files, so regular users won't notice any difference in how the tool looks or works today.

35af4be2c9b2244cf105c95a6f98d6fa70e95db0.text: The internal assistant renamed one of its coding helpers to better reflect its job. This change only affects the internal team and does not alter how the software works or what they see.

d965302b24714790de558e0250541d964f2ccd44.text: The tool now checks files without freezing while reading. This applies to the command-line program and testing system. People using those tools would see the screen stay responsive instead of pausing during file scans.

5ddb0fc5ffa9423bb1ffbc77f93ca30b0c0e92fb.text: A new 'plan-only' mode was added to the internal assistant, which stops it from searching files and instead focuses solely on outlining steps. This change is live for internal staff using the specific 'fast' model configuration. Users will notice the assistant provides strategic outlines without attempting to gather file context or execute changes directly.

f1a628329680e646e1a2935eb032d53ebbea8ead.text: The system's internal setup for managing task proposals was cleaned up to remove duplicate instructions. This change affects only the software's internal logic and is live. Users and developers will notice no visible difference in how the assistant behaves or responds.

080f9aa96b9ef948fc728b2ff672e2f06ef960ef.text: The internal coding assistant gained a new model option. When this option is active, the assistant stops using a specific file-lookup helper and removes a particular thinking tag from its instructions. This change is in place but does nothing for regular users yet.

f89e20d18a57f969a42bea09e939d8ed96a976d3.text: The AI assistant now requires a specific signal to stop working, rather than just pausing. This applies only to agents configured with this new rule. If you use such an agent, it will not end its response until it explicitly declares the task finished, preventing it from stopping too early.

118c2379ba39f52f9819c3bdb88abf2c64ed5301.text: The assistant now automatically tries multiple solutions for quick tasks and picks the best one, instead of requiring a separate setup. This internal change makes the system smarter and simpler to use for fast responses.

e1f201cd8af7a5715d954f825612b6eaa46eb3a2.text: The assistant's text search now reads results in a stricter format, fixing crashes on files with unusual names. 80ddeb3b78ea643c7dd930a00fd5a84c50c18e57.text: The command-line chat tool now supports running local agents, displays how long a response takes to stream, and renders markdown text more accurately in the terminal. Users of the CLI will see timing indicators next to messages and cleaner formatting for lists and links.

d71a65c907b832d925e31556da4166a017e5d09e.text: The internal system that generates code suggestions now uses two different AI models to draft potential solutions, instead of relying on just one. An automated judge then evaluates these drafts to pick the best result. This change is live for the internal tooling team and aims to produce higher-quality code suggestions by combining the strengths of different models.

888d9b98c8467caaf5a53bbf9da90537b710ab91.text: The internal team cleaned up the labels and removed duplicate files for the tool that generates multiple code options and picks the best one. This change affects only the internal setup and does not change how the tool behaves. Regular users will not notice any difference.

2529ad939468c6fc9138040858a51345d47a14de.text: A new, quicker way to check code has been added to the internal assistant tooling. This is not active for anyone yet; it is just a new option waiting to be turned on.

e6045ca354143caf0820bbbd035f2a6e1ec4eff3.text: The program now reads its setup instructions from a single, strict source instead of checking each setting individually. This internal cleanup prevents errors from misspelled or missing configuration details. Regular users will not notice any change in how the tool works.

75052a57cb38efdbfaa4ef1a7008bc571c1693a3.text: A new internal assistant mode was created to help it find and read more files when researching. This change is not live for users today.

75ecd3cceb3e27353e7638fc45a129076604b8f5.text: The internal system that tracks user data and usage costs was moved back to a shared location to fix a structural issue. This change is currently in place but does not affect how the application functions for end users today.

673ae6eb753ef1ce2137c5cca9a434c2febe1a9e.text: The program now reads its settings from a single, organized list instead of searching through scattered notes. This change is internal and affects only how the software finds its own configuration. A regular user would notice no difference in behavior or appearance.

314ec8b2f756cd6ca4003b1500289ab4c60e6c27.text: The internal process for publishing software updates was consolidated from two separate systems into one unified workflow. This change is purely administrative and affects only the engineering team's maintenance procedures. External users will notice no difference in the software's behavior or features.

2fce2191f4800b36c2dd3c3d392801d9b30bcbd7.text: The team moved the data storage tools and error reporting helpers into a separate, hidden box. This change is internal and only affects the developers who build the software. A regular person will not notice any difference in how the application works.

06170a5c256b6641cb7305534ade2d1d2a62288d.text: The system now checks agent configurations internally instead of using a shared tool, keeping the validation logic private. This change affects how the platform verifies agent setups behind the scenes. Users will notice no difference in the interface or functionality, as this is a hidden update to how the software organizes its internal checks.

f78605fb0b4af7357f0caa33ed2e61997598d4bf.text: The program's appearance rules were updated to ensure text is consistently formatted across many files. This change affects the internal structure of the command-line tool and its background helpers, but it does not alter how they work or what they do. You will not notice any difference in the tool's behavior or output, as this is purely an internal cleanup for the developers.

11a280be3f2a39b4fc22ce2e965a5e692fbb2238.text: A hidden cost-saving feature for the AI assistant now works correctly when messages are simple text. Previously, the system failed to mark these short messages for caching, causing unnecessary processing fees. Users will see lower API costs, though this fix is currently only active for specific internal testing scripts.

b73182067dbc1e12e451cfe68a116d5fde00e879.text: The system now reads a central list to know which private keys are needed, instead of guessing from code text. This affects internal release and test runs. If a key is missing, the build fails clearly rather than silently skipping it.

07594b7fc745e85de00e5a770d386b1a33c4d789.text: The internal planning assistant now always uses a standard checklist tool, removing old options that toggled this behavior on or off. This affects only the internal 'base2' agents, not external customers. The change simplifies how the assistant breaks down tasks, ensuring consistent step-by-step planning without relying on specific configuration flags.

3a2c574687a93973dc409e2bc24e73548821dced.text: The program reorganized its login screen behind the scenes. This change does not affect how you sign in; you will notice no difference when using the software today.

9e9b23e7ac1a281ad1912d1c07960d4a4884a258.text: A small internal cleanup moved the login step into its own spot. This affects only the command-line tool's login screen. People signing in from a terminal will notice no change; the window still asks you to press Enter to open your browser.

e69082cb5a257484951b8a4f9001d3933472d8da.text: A new background process was added to help the assistant think through tasks more carefully. Before taking action, it now quietly asks two different AI models for potential next steps and compares their ideas. This happens automatically for internal users, meaning responses might take slightly longer but aim to be more accurate.

3b8d54596cb77ac70305951fb8c03549cd220b00.text: The team moved the database access code to a separate internal section. This affects developers working on the server side. They will notice that the shared code no longer includes database tools, making the setup cleaner and easier to manage.

7981212c645f49747a55c7c94e942b2df9b7295d.text: The team moved the rules for checking secret settings back into one main file instead of keeping them in a separate helper file. This is an internal cleanup that does not change how the product works or looks. Nothing new appeared for customers.

dcd79cd82cba676be30221112be9339bb7d2411d.text: A small internal tool update helps developers start their command-line assistant without extra setup steps. If the assistant fails to launch at first, the tool quietly updates a required background component and tries again immediately. This affects only the people building the software, not the customers using the final product.

8450f267d05089ebc24e215e2003a8986d3e03e1.text: When you start the command-line assistant, it now lists available agents in a compact box. You can click the arrow to expand or collapse the list. This keeps your screen tidy at startup.

fc982fd79f84dd0ac4833998c807ed0fff0ead8e.text: The tool stopped using a single central place to read its setup details, like passwords and website addresses. It now reads these details directly from the computer's environment when it needs them. This affects the command-line tool and the server behind it, but you will not see any changes in how the tool works.

4b4381d637361188165ada3105540ee032520149.text: The login screen inside the command-line tool now uses a shared system to decide how to look based on the size of your terminal window. This change is internal and does not alter the visual design or behavior for you today. It ensures that future updates to the login screen will automatically respect these size rules without needing to be rewritten each time.

b01a1c0afbc112e10ba2514f475cb882bd19c679.text: The team added automated tools to help publish the software library, replacing manual steps. They also changed how secret keys are handled to ensure they are cleared in production while allowing them to remain visible during development. This is an internal update for the engineering team and does not change how the product works for customers.

2bc8607144b44f0342871f5137124d47ebd4d133.text: The AI assistant now keeps a visible checklist of its own work steps. People using the command-line tool will see these tasks appear as checkmarks that fill in as the AI finishes each part of a job. This update is active immediately for anyone using the command-line interface.

4005dbdd6d12b10eec8c128e43eb3e7e66ad7d4f.text: The software no longer automatically hides secret connection keys when running outside of testing mode. Instead, the release system now places blank placeholders for these keys before the product is built. This change affects only the production release process and is live today, but users will notice nothing different in their experience.

335496eda9f44762cff28f27e66aee18f07eaafd.text: A new internal AI assistant option now tracks its work steps in a dedicated checklist rather than plain text. This change applies only to a specific fast-mode agent variant used for internal testing and benchmarking. A non-programmer would notice no immediate difference in everyday use, as this is an experimental tool configuration for evaluating performance.

9984487d7cff85d054cb969e1e2b75349057bd9f.text: The search tool now correctly identifies file names that contain hyphens or colons, which previously caused errors in displaying results. This fix applies to all searches performed through the software development kit. Users will notice more accurate search results when looking for code in files with complex names.

3959bf7b5f948219edcc6b32903f7ba5ff9bbcc3.text: The command-line tool now checks your login status automatically instead of manually. This change is for CLI users. You might notice faster responses when logging in or switching accounts, as the tool remembers your status for five minutes.

9e226827a42b370975fde54a1ecf394e5e93c85c.text: The nightly test suite now runs the fast assistant variant with final validation steps disabled to check if skipping the review affects performance. This change applies only to internal automated evaluations, so external customers will not notice any difference in the live product.

e0d6df3ed1ceb4316fe837bb9bd6693f25c5a544.text: Search results are now grouped by file name instead of repeating the file path on every line. This reduces the amount of text sent to the AI assistant, lowering costs and speeding up responses. The change is live in the software development kit.

776aabb75bf7a85f3f1c12b8889fa00c8a438a8e.text: The team reorganized how the system handles requests for user account details to fix internal errors. They also added a safeguard to stop the evaluation tools from crashing if they receive unexpected data formats. This is a behind-the-scenes maintenance update, so customers will not notice any changes to the application's features or performance.

8f6d890f97c0a175dd83c06284794c714b302c9f.text: The system's thinking process now starts fresh with file contents instead of carrying over previous chat history, improving speed and prompt caching. This internal change affects how the AI researches coding tasks, though users won't see direct interface changes today.

c2167451749849219ea711fd55c2327e67980f75.text: The internal coding assistant now uses a two-step process to handle tasks. First, a research agent scans the code to find relevant files, then a separate planning agent uses that information to create a detailed strategy. This change is live today and affects how the assistant prepares to write code, making its planning phase more thorough.

ce5838beffc746f29d2f2bf0de4c4f3a94e0d140.text: The system's method for identifying a user was reorganized internally to follow standard platform rules. This change affects only how the software is built and maintained, not how it functions. No user will notice any difference, as the behavior remains exactly the same.

37316d850d1997c2d84a80ef8a56b2e0b1be07cb.text: A new internal helper mode was added that checks its own work for errors before finishing. This change is only for internal testing and does not affect any live features or external users.

a9da3c1510b478d14fd8521ec25bf8837589d04c.text: The command-line tool no longer hides specific error messages from its tracking service. If that service fails, you will now see its warnings or errors in your terminal instead of them being silently filtered out. This change is live today and only affects people using the command-line interface.

3dcb91e7fcf9a52146e59b4f81ff2207cbf1c5d8.text: The sign-in screen in the command-line chat tool now appears as a panel on top of the chat window instead of taking over the whole display. ef910125a487c7bb1f4af9bf66edd54e011c1d06.text: The assistant's internal plumbing was cleaned up to better handle and hide its own internal commands while it thinks. 9872a589671e7f8e7ac108bb1947ff5ad280e7f0.text: The internal assistant's 'fast' mode now automatically includes safety checks, eliminating a separate, optional validation step. This change affects only the internal team's workflow, making the process more consistent. Users will notice no visible difference, as the underlying behavior remains the same but is now handled by default.

72ac5ceeece0f9f634230cac977a7c635aef9f3e.text: New automated checks verify the command-line tool still works correctly whenever the underlying software library changes. Developers will see these checks run silently in the background, catching broken builds or startup errors before they reach users. This safety net is active immediately for the internal development team.

c3b8d4b4dfd7542eda0fa4be8083d839a55ce90a.text: The team added a new logging tool for their internal testing system. This change affects only the engineers running these tests, not regular users. When they run tests on their own computers, the system now automatically saves a detailed record of its actions to a file, which helps them diagnose issues. This record is not created when tests run in automated environments.

df596975d3847f148250d348fada73ef08f30465.text: The command-line tool now blocks access until you verify your identity through a web browser. This applies to everyone using the tool on their computer.

b28837b59c4e660e1f3643c81e0d0336ccbddaf4.text: The team reorganized internal files to group related assistant configurations together and removed unused ones. This change affects only the developers maintaining the system. Users will notice no difference in how the assistant behaves.

604846184451b01b03c7fcaeab0acf8e869c5ace.text: The tool no longer launches a separate helper program to read its output. This change is internal and affects only the software's own plumbing. Regular users will not notice any difference in behavior or features.

221cb2ec11a00626b71169de7fda5ebe803df7dd.text: The command-line tool no longer displays fake responses or random completion messages when the main service is unavailable. It also stopped logging minor details about system appearance changes, reducing clutter in the background. A new feature for organizing conversation files by date into specific folders has been added but remains inactive.

1c3a5ebec14f47ed14f2b4f689efe2d6cbeab4ac.text: The automated coding assistant can now try several different ways to solve a problem at once and pick the best one, instead of just trying one way. This helps internal developers get better code suggestions, but you will not notice a difference unless you are using this specific internal tool.

e323769925c2d3bf9766a629afcec59219b54378.text: The internal assistant now uses a new setup to better organize its work. It acts as a manager that assigns specific tasks to specialized helpers, such as one that searches the codebase for relevant files. This change is internal and not available to regular users today.

02faa42bd585e2ed567dd8cdb7a1f761febfc97c.text: The system now tags every conversation turn with a unique identifier, allowing support teams to trace exactly which actions occurred during a specific session. This internal update affects how data is recorded and monitored behind the scenes. Regular users will not notice any changes to the interface or performance today.

4e92bc395cc55fd95fb15c8a50a444daf5706bc8.text: The command-line tool now hides background tasks that manage memory, so their internal logs no longer clutter the screen. This change is live and affects anyone using the tool to interact with the AI. You will simply see a cleaner output without those specific technical messages.

This ensures the tool's instructions match the expected format, preventing potential errors when the system tries to use it. Since this is a backend definition update, end users will not notice any immediate change in behavior or appearance.
