e8eef4d62176ab5156b486e6d83d2f72c334f468.text: The team updated their internal quality-testing system to use the same communication pathway as the live product. This ensures that when the system checks for errors, it tests the exact setup customers will experience. This is a backend reliability improvement, so no features, speed, or interface changes are visible to the public.

124fcefd042d4100e46408a1420e80fabb78874c.text: The main assistant can now send two new helpers to find answers: one searches the internet, and the other reads technical guides. This helps the assistant give more accurate advice when you ask about external tools or libraries. You might notice it provides better references or up-to-date information without you needing to paste links yourself.

2cc0ca11dba0871a5942ca10a900f91d78806dfb.text: The internal planning assistant now uses a smarter model for hard tasks. It reads files directly and asks helpers to look up public library guides. Staff might see more detailed plans, though this change only affects internal tools and is not live for customers yet.

9a0d9dde91e6e1e9f77b647b1044da90ecf9de04.text: The system removed broken practice problems from its internal testing library. These problems failed to load correctly, so they were deleted to keep the test results accurate. Only the internal testing team is affected, and no customer-facing features changed.

8d9b622db70eb7529fbf3ef5c456d40717ae4d48.text: The system now has stricter rules for how it reads and writes messages, including text, images, and tool actions. This change is internal groundwork for better data handling but does not alter what you see or do today. You will notice no immediate difference in the app's behavior.

d6c91af4a750ea1fe31cd5be1b235db36ac9d682.text: The system now records the exact cost of every task performed by sub-agents, including those that fail. This allows the main agent to track the total credits used for a complex request. Users will see a more accurate credit deduction on their dashboard, reflecting the true cost of the entire workflow rather than just the final output.

9757c03ed1ba4909a173c2faf0d12868e49a6ea3.text: The website replaced basic browser pop-ups with custom warning boxes for deleting API keys. This change is live and applies to all users managing API keys on their profile pages. Users will notice the warning boxes now match the website's design and show a loading state during deletion.

027e8428279173140bdc3e9fea47749a558c554a.text: The profile page now has a dedicated tab for managing access keys. Old links for keys, usage, and referrals automatically go to the right tab. The wording changed from personal access token to API key.

68bf922740c07889ebec41c5baf8b20276eb4a45.text: The main assistant can now call a new helper for quick questions about code or the internet. Another helper that edits code can also call a web-searching assistant, while the web-searching assistant itself can no longer look at local files. These changes are active now and help the system find answers faster without mixing up their jobs.

f0605b5664fecfd89a9ec8d12a364fd983f7079b.text: The assistant stopped using an extra check that decided whether more project files needed to be looked at. It now always looks for relevant files first, even for short follow-up or command-style requests. The change is live now, but it is internal, so people would not see a new button or message; they might only notice slightly different file choosing behavior.

c695f86e44302c6a1e0f2d23567241b6c845b879.text: The system's internal assistant now splits complex coding tasks into three distinct steps: planning, editing, and reviewing. This replaces a single, all-in-one process with a structured workflow where specialized sub-agents handle each phase. A new deep-reasoning model is also available for the planning stage. These changes are internal and not yet active for end-users.

eae7f3081d5c6ab32780795d8f4ef127ab28d74d.text: The service that ends sign-ins and access keys now handles both browser and command-line logins through one shared path instead of separate ones. A logged-in person on the security page sees browser and command-line sessions on separate tabs, and ending several sessions at once works the same way for either kind.

b705b7fe7d3472c6a391bb2f2b385fa2d1268fce.text: The system now protects login and key pages by blocking requests from other websites. It also changed how it labels sign-in methods, grouping them into browser, command-line, and personal key types. You might see slightly different names for your active sessions on the security page, but your access remains unchanged.

dd30e468c06834f763d571ea1e541e74bf2c4c16.text: The assistant now stops its internal work loop cleanly when it hits its step limit, preventing it from getting stuck waiting for more input. This fix applies to the core agent system, ensuring smoother turn endings for anyone using these automated helpers.

5c24bec1121904e88098db764a25ff597fb953e7.text: The internal assistant team added a new option to use a more powerful reasoning model for planning tasks. This change is internal only, so regular users will not see any difference in the interface today.

552f74d95ca2a9be9a5be74d209437d5961b6fb7.text: The assistant can start helper tasks in a few different ways, and each way used to carry its own copy of the same safety checks. Those checks now live in one shared place, so a task started through any path gets the same permission rules and the same error messages. A new test was added to confirm the permission rules hold. This is an internal tidy-up; nothing visible changes for anyone today.

ef9914ece072339229d796de949244cf5b381d2f.text: The system now builds a map of your project files and their connections right when you start a new session. Before, it waited to figure this out, which slowed down early answers. You will notice faster responses when asking questions about your codebase for the first time.

c2bc8bb0d5595c79cbd8aba647ba40ede710ac4f.text: The evaluation system now supports a second AI assistant. Users of the testing framework can choose which assistant runs the tests. The change also renames internal settings, but this does not affect the final product for regular users.

1369f2367c82b7d9d228b2bcf3651ce999e05db0.text: A new assistant persona named Chloe is now available to help add fun visual touches to software projects. Developers using the command-line tool can now type special words to see animations like falling confetti or scrolling code on their screens. These playful features are live today and are designed to make the coding experience more enjoyable without affecting the core work.

0d765207f7655da140fd151321189db7228110ab.text: A new internal helper now automatically clears out older, less useful conversation details before the assistant responds. This change helps keep responses fast and efficient by preventing the system from getting overwhelmed with too much history. Users won't see any visual changes, but the assistant should handle long chats more smoothly without slowing down.

32031c5c322d983799c40181e0f7450c1f34da31.text: The development team added new automated tests to check how well the AI assistant handles different types of code changes across web, command-line, and desktop platforms. These tests do not affect the software users see or use today. Instead, they help the internal team measure and improve the assistant's performance behind the scenes.

647453e06d65bb13a105495c642cfbe337e6ed40.text: A small internal fix corrected how the system finds specific data descriptions, resolving an error that blocked checks. This affects only the internal tools used by staff to build the software, not the features customers use. Staff will see the error messages disappear when they run their quality checks, while everyday users will notice no changes at all.

b02e0dc13c89be729db385f032d7aa2c9716b15e.text: The main assistant now hides its internal instruction sheet when handing off work to sub-assistants. This prevents sub-assistants from seeing private setup notes meant only for the main assistant. This is an internal change; regular users will not notice any difference.

47b52b66e011bdec337bd279e9beb35d33ff0e83.text: A small internal update lets the team test the rules that decide which helper tools the assistant can use, without running the whole system. This change does not affect what you see or do today.

a3dd658db8918e671462b308acebea0fa7ad771d.text: The team copied a third-party tool used to talk to the AI service into their own internal code to fix how usage costs are calculated. This change is internal and live today. Regular users will not see any difference, but the billing system now correctly tracks spending for AI requests.

dc4ed3ac98a63e8da6104544e6ce162a7060f41c.text: The testing setup for the internal research assistant was rebuilt to prevent automated checks from getting stuck waiting for responses that never arrive. This change affects only the quality assurance process and does not alter how the assistant behaves for end users. You will notice no difference in the product, but the internal tests are now more reliable.

4a6592fd618e1061f9a2c285c0de8d725af04ab0.text: Developers moved a set of internal instructions for how the assistant requests actions into a shared library, making the code cleaner and easier to maintain. This change affects only the software's internal structure; users will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves or what it can do.

60c5963bcfeb53629c083a3d27b096801d61dc4e.text: The tool now uses a single, specific label to identify its access key when sending requests, replacing a mix of different formats. This internal change affects how the command-line tool and server verify identity, but users will see no difference in daily use. It is live today.

97ee03b06fb332b51bbda94fa43c7d8066ef8f42.text: The tool now checks your agent names against the main service when they are not stored locally. This only happens if you are logged in. You might see a brief loading message at startup while it verifies the name.

dcdbad70987dbbed158437edf5945378daa46784.text: A new helper now guides the AI to review code changes and draft commit messages automatically. This tooling change affects developers who use the internal assistant to save time on routine version control tasks. The helper is active today, meaning the assistant can immediately begin suggesting these organized summaries without manual prompting.

7d1f2e244237cc544b5e843e338dc7dfe1104e66.text: The team created a separate, internal folder for the software that powers their AI assistants. This new setup lets them check the code's accuracy on its own, without mixing it up with the main application's rules. It is a small, behind-the-scenes tool for the developers; customers will not see any changes.

138c15f63fda36edbfed7fb7a1cec204ba7468e3.text: The assistant can now accept attachments like images or files and remember previous conversation context. This feature is available for developers building custom tools with the official library. Users will notice richer interactions if the specific application they use has enabled this capability.

0b98c636bc02df17e4290325671290101fc8b210.text: The internal team cleaned up the code that builds the instructions sent to the AI assistant. This change removes duplicate files and moves the logic to a single, central location. Customers will not see any difference in how the assistant behaves today, as this update only improves how the software is organized behind the scenes.

8da355b2536ec849a8f7882e6e8f1685d5f5110f.text: The internal research assistant now uses a different AI model. This change affects only the company's internal tools. Regular users will notice no difference in their experience.

c42281bf67b57f5c7c743bf40c51389d2fd4fa58.text: The assistant can now run commands on your computer directly through the software development kit. Previously, it could not perform this action and would report an error. This affects developers using the SDK to build tools that interact with the codebase. If they look, they will see the assistant execute terminal commands and return the results, instead of failing.

cd9cd6a6b5319406034db4db7032e58ccb439a1a.text: The guide for building specialized AI helpers now shows how to write their instructions in a programming language instead of a simple text format. This lets creators set up complex, step-by-step tasks that react to results, rather than just following a fixed script. The change only affects people who write these custom instructions; it does not change how the AI behaves for everyday users today.

edd38c58d55ce1fdb236bf4f31a5969f705391fb.text: Three new examples show how to set up automated helpers for reviewing code changes, committing updates, and exploring files. These examples are for internal staff building custom workflows, not for general customers. The helpers themselves are not live yet; they serve as templates for future development.

1a557775785ad1c09f91bd4298339db34327e55c.text: The internal instructions for the assistant's automated helpers were updated to match a new standard for how they request actions. This change only affects the behind-the-scenes logic of the software and is not visible to you. The assistant's ability to read files, search the web, or run commands remains exactly the same.

f8aedbbad52d1cf631dec4235a048727dd1d22a9.text: The software removed three pre-made assistant examples and an unused internal setting. It added one blank template file for creating custom assistants. This affects only people who write custom assistants. They will see fewer example files and one new starting point for building their own.

d7a8b17ef8b1cc0a5f2dd7248083ee62b5aabe76.text: The program now builds its assistant profiles from a single shared template instead of copying the same instructions and capabilities into every profile file. This change is internal cleanup for the development team and does not alter how the assistant behaves for you today. You will not notice any difference in responses, speed, or available features.

cc66bae453842ec9a247c477ad02f5701ee998f3.text: The internal system for checking data formats was updated to a newer standard. This change affects how the backend validates incoming requests and defines agent behaviors. Users will not notice any difference in the application's interface or features.

e8a75d0c6b54a8e77eae376869f38c2aa8b7fc17.text: The system's instructions for how automated helpers request tasks were updated to match a newer standard. This change ensures that when the software asks for help finding files or reviewing code, it uses the correct format. The update is live and prevents errors during these automated tasks, though the visible behavior for the user remains the same.

bf9c8d683ccfa2c3c637566de185e420353f9089.text: The team switched back to an older version of the software library that powers the AI assistant's tools. This change fixes how the assistant asks for information, so it can successfully run commands and search files again. You will notice the AI assistant stops crashing or failing when trying to use its built-in tools.

3d8ece358a740c6718282091c53b1d051ecf78dd.text: The files that help you create custom AI assistants were moved to a more central location within the software. This is an internal housekeeping change to make the system more stable. You will not notice any difference in how the tool works today, as the features and examples remain exactly the same.

f973ae976bba995a74979542f236e73f602a2e57.text: When publishing an assistant that uses other assistants, the system now automatically finds the newest version if no specific one is named. This prevents errors when referencing an assistant without a version tag. The change is internal and affects only the assistant publishing process.

ac9fff6cb1c8f512e0cb3565c2abb8f63f85f4b0.text: The team reorganized the sample scripts that help the AI assistant review code and create commits. They removed duplicate examples, renamed the remaining ones to show their difficulty level, and updated the instructions to be clearer. This is an internal cleanup that does not change how the assistant behaves for you today, but it makes the underlying logic easier to maintain.

6fc0452c5f167554ccecad4fb532262c8cc4d898.text: The label used to describe when a specific assistant should be called has been shortened to make it clearer. This change affects people who create or modify their own custom assistants. If you look at the settings for these assistants, you will see the new, simpler name instead of the old one, though the actual behavior of the assistants remains the same.

73da134833ad2e089ad6654266aa3a2f399a1552.text: Programmers added a separate rulebook for the internal versions of the assistant, allowing them to use hidden features like creating sub-goals or spawning background agents. This change affects only the internal tools and does not impact the public assistant. Users will notice no changes in behavior, as this is an internal cleanup to keep the public and private feature lists separate.

d5344c2e9ca9f5578066a53e68ae9ee17a036b92.text: The system removed a hidden feature that let the main assistant instantly start a smaller helper agent to handle a specific sub-task. This cleanup affects only the internal code structure, so users will not notice any change in behavior or appearance.

80b22c7a54f1b774f28e3ea4f109ed5120ce4a22.text: The system switched back to an older, stable validation tool to fix errors, while keeping new features available. This change is live now. Non-programmers will notice fewer crashes or error messages when the AI assistant tries to understand specific instructions or data formats.

7695a102f6c1720f224a9d7a8e1b11448b12d4de.text: The system now keeps its helper instructions in a single, standard folder instead of scattering them across different parts of the software. This change affects people who build or share their own automated helpers. They will see these helpers are easier to find, test, and publish to others, though the core behavior of the assistants themselves hasn't changed.

fe3e591cef9c316211695f4cf7a7f637d6485807.text: The internal labels for defining AI agents were updated to more accurate terms. This change is purely for the developers who build these agents and does not affect how the software behaves for end users. Nothing visible to customers has changed.

940b78477765f959e0aee72c7a109ba1b82126ab.text: The internal assistant that builds other assistants was moved out of the main service code and into its own separate file. This affects only the internal team and changes how the code is organized. Users will notice no difference, as the assistant's capabilities and behavior remain exactly the same.

641cba2e0c6951478f1d34a9de5066bfa07baf3b.text: Renamed internal label for nested helpers to match their actual role. No visible change to current features. This cleanup helps future updates stay consistent.

30c6fe6b64f898b58aa0fe79858a70d373ecad13.title: CLI adds first-tab discount logic to model selector and session API
30c6fe6b64f898b58aa0fe79858a70d373ecad13.summary: CLI model selector and session hooks integrate new `firstTabDiscount` logic via `freebuff-first-tab-discount.ts` and `freebuff-price-selection.ts`. The `freebuff-session-api.ts` adds `x-freebuff-first-tab-discount` header and handles `first_tab_discount_changed` status, while `freebucks.ts` applies account-wide discount quotes to session prices. Scope covers `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, `cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts`, and shared types in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`. Detail: `firstTabQuoteForSession` checks holder instance ID, surface type, and expiry timestamps to dynamically apply or release the discount before purchase.

1a03c37bb1e3db631749b6fcec1dd888e5a7df49.text: The system now checks custom assistant settings through a standard web request instead of a real-time connection. This affects only authenticated users who have created custom assistants. They will see validation errors appear sooner after starting the tool, without needing a live connection to the server.

1b182fcbea278b555d09041f57880dba147187f4.text: The assistant can now hand a specific task to a helper that works inside the current conversation thread. Unlike other helpers that start fresh, this one sees all previous messages and keeps its new findings in the chat history. This helps the assistant delegate work without losing track of the discussion context.

eb2d3ba2ded99f971b20ba32e93cf80fcc985c37.text: The system now uses one shared set of rules to create helper programs, removing duplicate code. Three new example helpers for checking code changes are available for builders to copy, demonstrating simple to complex setups. This is an internal cleanup for the assistant's builder; regular users will see no change in behavior.

121d2628a543f2565607534a6ef1313a72f1dbce.text: The tool for building custom AI agents now carries its own copy of the instructions for setting up agents and choosing actions. This means people creating these agents can install the tool directly and see helpful suggestions for valid settings without needing extra files. The setup instructions are active today, allowing for immediate use in building and publishing new agents.

d774a1190033ba81f120a60be3c9821e52c7588b.text: A feature allowing the main AI assistant to send messages to other AI assistants it created was removed. This change affects only the internal logic of the assistant's task delegation system. Users will notice that the main assistant can no longer communicate with previously spawned sub-assistants to update or redirect them.

ab87eb2287659131d7dcc6e88f70971ab7161251.text: The system renamed a setting that forces the assistant to return data in a strict, pre-defined format. This change affects anyone who manually configured their assistant to use the old name for this setting. If they did, their assistant might fail to start or return errors until they update their configuration to use the new name.

842c13227ee038cd86127c984d9b1e06d59da640.text: A new marketing PDF for The Flex has been added to the public testimonials section. This update is live today and affects visitors to the website. Users will notice this document available for download or viewing in the testimonials area.

117ab40956c9ab02b23ad4d8b937ec63d95b7e6b.text: The system stopped automatically removing a specific company label from agent names. This change affects users who previously relied on that label being hidden to find their custom agents. They may now notice that these agents require the full, unaltered name to be identified correctly.

2a564ae89f287d49c1639bf3038f84292f1028d3.text: The list of helpers an assistant can hire was renamed to 'spawnableAgents' to better describe what it does. This change is live now. If you previously saved a custom setup using the old name, you must manually update it to the new name, or your chosen helpers will not load.

7b74c69b7e9bae928f3a4856871b35ce53c9be3f.text: The software now checks file size and location before reading them, blocking files larger than one megabyte or those outside the project folder. This affects developers using the SDK, ensuring safer file access. They will notice errors if trying to read oversized or external files, but normal small files within the project work as before.

30c6fe6b64f898b58aa0fe79858a70d373ecad13.text: The pricing screen now shows a 'First-tab discount' label when your account qualifies. This offer applies only to the first tab you open for a session. If you switch sessions, the discount releases before the next purchase.

9ffa0d8df053b386eb3457bbae9c37d455ef1905.text: The website now hides the 'refer a friend' banner for accounts older than seven days. New sign-ups still see the banner, but established members no longer see it after their first week.

3191ed4ac57c59d4757a76ad30a2528bb2c7ee49.text: A new tool allows software builders to connect their own applications to Codebuff's AI coding assistant. This change is internal and does not affect current users; it simply provides a way for developers to integrate the assistant into their own systems in the future.

2d55670bb0b79b4ddc3d8fd834329dfcf06a6dfe.text: A new Agent Store page is now live on the website. You can browse published tools, see their creators, and check search or sort options. This helps you find and compare ready-made assistants without writing code.

1e55a7a09e3b4a2387941c0bafd712a2a9350e68.text: The team cleaned up the internal setup for the assistant's tools. They moved a shared setting to a single location to stop the system from repeating the same instruction in multiple places. This change affects only the background structure and has no visible impact on how the assistant works for you.

c35393f6a7ed440d91bdc773b0808a28c4219fa0.text: The system now consistently captures three key details—error name, message, and stack trace—when problems occur. This helps support teams diagnose issues faster without needing to ask for extra information. No visible change for end users, but error reports become more complete and standardized.

6c61620ce9e92107cc1368c32299260afec1c851.text: The assistant now handles file changes through a new, more secure connection method. It automatically creates missing folders and verifies data before saving, preventing errors. This affects developers using the tool to edit code. They will see smoother file updates and unique session IDs.

7b17f6ed1a64395d1a122323932488f7bd0c21cc.text: The software now uses a live connection to receive updates instead of checking for them manually. This change affects developers building applications with the platform's toolkit, though it does not alter the end-user experience. The older method of connecting is marked as obsolete, signaling that it will be removed in future updates.

bd373f80a8158ef1b961df7d31f0721a7ca65b8e.text: The instructions guiding the AI assistant were previously stored as long, unreadable blocks of text. A new internal tool converted these into properly spaced, multi-line formats. This change is live and improves how the assistant reads its own rules, though the visible output to the user remains the same.

6e38dc70e63b946baf6670a2ddb020327e66d3e5.text: The system now attaches a permanent identity tag to every helper tool the assistant calls. This ensures the software always loads the exact, approved version of each tool rather than guessing. You will not see a difference in the interface, but the assistant becomes more reliable by preventing broken or mismatched tools from running.

894cacff0897a61b5df730cbcefcaae4677c9038.text: The team reorganized the internal settings for the AI assistant. This change affects only the internal configuration files and does not alter how the assistant behaves or responds. You will not notice any difference in the assistant's performance or answers.

02d9b66bb03af49cd3065afe48de04a50a7657f9.text: The team set up a new internal tool for connecting to Codebuff's AI services. This tool currently only recognizes login keys but does not actually process any requests. It is not live for anyone yet.

9a98a9628e12ff6a1307e44d61b40004daba75a2.text: People who publish their own AI helpers must now write their account name directly inside the helper's settings file. The option to type this name into the command line is gone. If they forget to add it, the publishing attempt will fail.

96d4ec940f3afb32bfae952aa445e2ef1da0b6b1.text: You can now publish several agents at once instead of one by one. If a mistake happens, you'll see exactly which agents failed and why. This helps people managing many agents save time.

2637bb80b7ac6d1705dcaf06445567cad5a15abf.text: Three sample AI assistants were added to show how to build more complex tools. One reviews code, one writes tests, and one creates documentation. These are examples for builders, so normal users will not see any change in the app today.

9d120f68d2646f2a13a56e363472b375ef11d7cc.text: The system no longer checks if a parent agent's instructions list any child agents that don't actually exist. This internal cleanup fixes a technical error but changes nothing for you. You won't see any difference in how the software behaves or looks.

1c316bcad2efcdbee05d33df22ed000f37001826.text: The team updated the internal settings for all the automated helpers. They moved the name and number that identify who made each helper into one central place, instead of typing them out separately in every single helper. This is just a tidy-up for the people who build the tools. Nothing changes for how the helpers work or what they do today.

881fb5fbfe4559d46b200b3d4e61a7338ced2ea6.text: The system swapped its main assistant for a new, more capable one that can create specialized helpers on the fly. This change is live for everyone. You might notice the assistant handling complex coding tasks more smoothly without you needing to set up separate tools.

ca3a556f4227a0de6fda1901881bb725210d9c76.text: The label for streaming data from the assistant changed from 'object' to 'event' to better describe its behavior. This internal rename affects how the system categorizes data chunks but does not change what users see or how the assistant responds.

64b95a78547e1abc8015aa371bc89af4e516d578.text: The internal team added a new automated reviewer that reads code changes to suggest improvements and find bugs. This change is not live for anyone yet, as it only sets up the rules for this future tool.

6afaedf2780868da8f1e615d1c61b6447edd597a.text: The publisher's page no longer displays a grid of clickable buttons for older versions. Instead, it shows a single line of text highlighting the most recent release. This change is live and reduces visual clutter for anyone viewing a publisher's profile.

859ad7e54b51989ecc9de21310bc696b4f363f20.text: The internal safety checks for the assistant's behavior guides are now fully tested. This is a behind-the-scenes change for the engineering team, so nothing visible to customers today. It ensures the system correctly prioritizes custom guides over saved ones and handles errors properly.

8bb59e8230290449320080bd9ac6b9474da8830d.text: The separate page for creating a new publisher profile is gone. Now, clicking 'Create Publisher Profile' from your organization settings or the user menu takes you directly to the main publishers page to finish the process in one spot. This change is live and simplifies the navigation by removing an extra step.

434a95f4e3ce4356ef0633e6edac259e23aa45fe.text: The system now checks saved assistant templates for errors before using them. If a template is broken, the system skips it and logs the problem instead of crashing. This keeps the assistants working for everyone, even if one saved template is bad.

3102f4b997c556abb4927abb8f962063ed2b521e.text: The software now has a central catalog of assistant profiles, each defining specific behaviors and tools. This change is internal and affects how the system organizes these profiles, not the end-user experience. Users will not notice any immediate difference.

3205731013904f23094a12865f5ef90d9627bfd9.text: Organization owners can now see a list of all the names and versions of the automated helpers their team has created. Clicking a name shows a history of every update made to that helper, including the exact instructions used. This is live for organization admins.

410255d3bae0bcbd08a406fcbb9782f9d246456a.text: The system now builds a private list of available AI roles for each task instead of looking them up from a shared global catalog. This change affects the backend's internal performance and stability. A regular user would notice no difference in the application's behavior, as this is an internal cleanup to prevent errors when the AI tries to use specialized sub-roles.

2662f7293d022e8ac34e3f8d864764ab5a5eec4c.text: The system now identifies each agent configuration by its publisher, its name, and its version together. This prevents two different publishers from accidentally using the same agent name and version. The change is live and ensures each publisher's agents remain distinct from others.

dd600ffc724ef2fde296d49ca596f6bd7b0ebe14.text: The form for creating a new publisher is now broken into three separate screens instead of one long page. When typing an ID, the system checks if it is already taken and shows a green check or red error immediately, rather than waiting until the end. This makes the process clearer and helps prevent errors before submitting.

f49314023bf975ad86703ecb51e01505d994ea66.text: The codebase was automatically reformatted to enforce a single, consistent style for spacing, quotes, and line breaks. This is an internal cleanup for the developers, not a new feature for users. If a developer looked at the code, they would see that the text is now neatly aligned and uniform across hundreds of files, but nothing about how the software actually works has changed.

7e79c46ba0f7f6e3c4d607e71e98154f679615b8.text: The team cleaned up how the computer reads instructions for building the service. This change affects only the developers who write the code. A normal user would notice no difference at all, because the service works exactly the same as before.

5b00580593d2c47f24f40c05b5f72666e3b6dc7a.text: The system now uses its own internal standard for formatting conversations with AI assistants, replacing a third-party one. This change affects how the backend processes requests but is invisible to you. You will not notice any difference in how the application behaves or responds.

9616ee028343f0afa46ce10206604a4dbb2bf11d.text: The system now checks agent templates instantly instead of waiting for a background process to load them. This speeds up the publishing of new agents for users and prevents occasional delays or errors during that step. The change is live and affects anyone publishing or using these custom assistants.

d207ff68dfbf510eba4f15c6cc46e761542d8fe8.text: The page for creating a publisher profile has moved to a new address. Organization admins will now see a dedicated section in their settings to start this process. The form itself is unchanged, still guiding users through three steps to set up a personal or organizational profile.

dbdbac636d7ae581f4c058f33979eb1fcbdceafd.text: People who make and share these tools can now create a public profile on the website to show who they are and what they have built. When someone tries to share a tool, the system gives clear reasons if something is wrong, rather than a vague failure message. This is ready to use right now.

7c98630f058946cec393077942e0d9217d856554.text: The system now stores assistant profiles in a new database table linked to publisher accounts, replacing the old template structure. This change is live in the codebase but does not yet offer a new user-facing feature; it prepares the backend to allow specific publishers to manage and share their custom assistant configurations.

4a70a14b99fb697cf0cd5d3d87abb837c7ae6141.text: The system now includes a specialized assistant named Charles, designed to research deep-sea sardines. Charles uses specific scientific tools to gather data and can break down complex questions into smaller tasks for other assistants. This feature is currently in the background and not yet available for public use.

75420684d805f178a5c0f7e11c47fe5fcf46d9eb.text: Publishers can now be linked to an organization instead of just a single person. This allows teams to manage shared accounts, though the interface might not show this option immediately if the feature is still being rolled out.

2ec998359ef71cd986d5804c00e5fee78967a336.text: The system now automatically creates a list of available tools and their settings whenever a new agent is built. This helps the agent understand exactly which actions it can take and what information each action requires. This change is internal to the setup process and will not be visible to end users.

242dd5da37af12c3be0e1a5b921b5bdd8704ee73.text: The rules describing how the assistant behaves were moved to a shared location, so they are no longer tied only to the server. This is an internal cleanup for the engineering team and does not change how the assistant answers questions or performs tasks.

e25b24b2a4d4c19eed5b79143ac0402cf1a8cf33.text: A small internal cleanup fixes how the assistant tracks its own update steps. Instead of reading a messy text label, the system now handles the number parts separately, which stops it from picking the wrong update when versions get complicated. Regular users will not notice anything different today, but the assistant will reliably use the newest available update in the future.

1f0bac25584d68b774ebefd686e230f6994935ec.text: The system removed two hidden text fields that previously guided how an assistant started its reply. This change affects only the internal setup for building new assistant types, not the assistants themselves. Nothing visible changed for anyone using the product today.

9758acce4176bfc120ebe727e1aa3b3cf929eeb7.text: Added a guide for people building custom AI assistants. It lists allowed tools and models so mistakes show up before running. This is a reference document, not a live feature, so nothing changes for regular users today.

e6c1628bdbfc15462fed7b29f44bb28c4e873fe5.text: The program's internal organization was cleaned up by moving the descriptions of its actions into a shared library. This change is strictly for the development team and does not alter how the software behaves for you. You will not notice any difference in speed, features, or appearance.

060cf727c4c9dcae216f8f887bf820cb28086186.text: The AI assistant now knows which other AI helpers it can call for tasks. This change applies to all agent types, letting them dynamically list available sub-agents instead of having that info hardcoded in their tools. It fixes a technical issue where agents couldn't see each other due to circular dependencies. No visible change to end users today, but it enables more flexible agent coordination.

61db08a8e6fabb1ca7e0b43c2df3e6c5d362e0bd.text: Added digital filing cabinets to store reusable assistant instructions and creator profiles. The system can now hold these records, but the feature is not live yet.

eb753bc25cc19785667584465261ff304d1be965.text: The internal labels for custom assistant templates were renamed to be more descriptive. This change does not affect standard users or the live application. Only people who built their own custom assistants need to update their configuration files to use the new names.

1797faae3610cb0eeb52e971c4c56c8c3a5b9397.text: The assistant now sends structured data alongside regular text during live output, allowing the interface to display richer information like tool usage details. This internal plumbing is complete but requires the user interface to be updated to actually show these new details to you.

0d509da06d767843f74d01b88828b6c01df5cdb5.text: The team added a scheduled check that automatically tests the assistant's accuracy every morning at 9:00 AM UTC. They also allowed ten of these tests to run simultaneously instead of just one, speeding up the feedback loop for internal quality assurance. This is an internal process change, so customers will not notice any difference in the product itself.

ad6627939eca72397fd71d101ead016fb6d72d94.text: The assistant now looks up its instructions for each task separately, rather than using a single shared list for everything. This change is internal and affects only the system's underlying setup. You would not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves or responds today.

fb4a3fa673956b8c5e83855c4107a4bd1b38d04e.text: The system's internal search tool now works as one unified process instead of two separate parts, and it can launch multiple parallel searches to scan codebases more thoroughly. This change is live today. A user asking the assistant to find information across many files might see it gather context faster or more completely, though the underlying mechanics remain invisible.

63d17bdb944e23096a21bf27ad1de36e2e2e758c.text: Developers added a safer tool for replacing parts of the system during automated tests. This ensures the software returns to its original state after testing, preventing one test from accidentally breaking another. Regular users will not notice any changes.

b268e180b5be256164c1f42f74b623a2be7e8701.text: The system now uses a standard structured format for agent responses instead of a custom report method. This change is live today. It affects agents that generate summaries, such as the git committer. Users might notice slightly different formatting in these summaries, but the core functionality remains the same.

12f543cffc41f69df54a321881500e52ab4253a1.text: The AI assistant can now edit its own memory of the conversation. It can add a note to remember important details or erase and replace its entire history to start fresh. This helps the assistant stay on track during long tasks without forgetting what it was doing.

a29a854c99017a698e7c8c673e870465919ec957.text: The tool now ships with a built-in brainstorming assistant that helps generate ideas and explore different perspectives. This new helper is available immediately for anyone using the agent builder. Existing tools for managing code commits and project notes were also updated to use this new, more reliable setup.

7defa45899aaab83853bd9a61504b3badc2f8359.text: Custom AI agents can now follow pre-written, step-by-step instructions instead of just guessing their next move based on prompts. This affects agent creators who write these scripts, letting them control exactly how the AI searches files or processes data. The feature is live, so new agents using this method will work immediately.

8d04c33a5fe3b083a08af02baf11408a378043a3.text: The system now runs custom agent logic in a secure, isolated mini-program, allowing it to accept code provided as plain text rather than just built-in functions. This change is live and affects internal tools, though end-users will see no visual difference; the update simply makes the backend more flexible and safer when processing these specific agent instructions.

0c7e401f9f5a66c8471545377d7077c7a2078105.text: The automatic check for typing errors now also scans the test scripts themselves, rather than skipping them. This change affects only the internal engineering team. Developers will notice that broken test files now trigger warnings, forcing them to keep those scripts accurate.

67de04e383d347076dc197675c3549846bb12642.text: The system now tells its main assistant when to call specific helpers, like asking the 'brainstormer' for creative ideas or the 'knowledge-keeper' to update project notes. This helps the assistant pick the right tool for the job automatically. It is live today and affects how the assistant decides which specialized helper to use.

fd29880e6f8f8d07f16002d301aa6354878cec5c.text: Added a command to let the main assistant hand off tasks to smaller helpers and a switch to turn on detailed activity logs. This affects people using the tool from their computer's command line. If they turn on the logging switch, they will see the helpers' progress appear on their screen in real time and be saved to a file for later checking.

16d12e771a8c781b3fc6ad05bb19ead604b2ad9e.text: The instructions for the AI helpers were moved from a strict text format to a more flexible programming format. This allows the helpers to check their own settings for mistakes before running. Programmers will see the files look different, but the helpers behave the same way today.

0a9d706727c7518decfaf051516b4b4c3123e044.text: The assistant now handles all its tasks through one shared method instead of two separate systems. This internal cleanup affects no visible behavior today because the new path for custom logic is currently blocked by a placeholder error. Staff will notice no change in how the tool responds to user requests.

0995194bd0e08148b005dfd48dfcfaff02af2422.text: The team removed two confusing internal setup files that defined how certain automated helpers behaved. This change affects only the internal tools used by staff, not the software you use. You will notice no difference in how the program works or looks.

5dd32714276f230b86c332ffa34a5a09c244e232.text: The team turned on a safety check that scans test files for mistakes. This check now covers a specific evaluation test that was previously ignored. Internal developers will see errors in that test if they exist, but customers will not notice any change.

e3e403b364549a6ef6a9301f44b8b531f0480fb5.text: The assistant can now run background tasks and share updates between them. Users on the new version might see the helper finish parts of a job without waiting for each step to complete. This feature is currently hidden behind a setting and does nothing until that setting is turned on.

08db44aed164aaed864bc8b391b83b7b07f23915.text: The instructions for setting up custom AI helpers changed from a method of patching existing ones to building them from scratch. This update affects internal documentation users, who will now see guidance on how helpers pass specific directions to each other during tasks.

85179603f1b471b7a414fa3df09b6ddac8f9598c.text: The system changed how it sends instructions to the AI, switching to a mixed text-and-data format to make tool usage more reliable. This affects all automated agent tasks, such as searching code or running commands. Users will not notice a visual change, but agents should now perform these background tasks more consistently without getting stuck.

ff8a3a3182fec78b4c070d595efa07a8e9d21174.text: Support staff can now open a screen that shows a step-by-step picture of what happened during a customer's chat session. This tool helps them see exactly when the system ran a task and what the result was, making it easier to figure out why a conversation went wrong.

236b55735026f8576be5e9243729b501cd47ca67.text: A new help page was added to the website. It shows people who build custom AI helpers exactly which settings they can change, like which brain the helper uses or how it talks. This page is live today, so anyone looking for these specific setup rules can now find them in one place.

83c0bac173fc5dac8df83a1a7809e8860dfd426a.text: The system now uses a standard tool to check the format of instructions given to AI agents. This change makes it easier for developers to create complex agent templates without writing custom code for every new type of instruction. It is live but mostly affects how the software is built rather than what end users see.

b4a95d509ff96b964c2809e742867f056076edf7.text: The internal documentation site can now display visual flowcharts and sequence diagrams to help explain complex processes. Writers can add these diagrams to guide agent customization, and the page layout has been adjusted so wide diagrams fit on smaller screens without breaking the view.

23741261a65e50b975cf7a876cf542bf57ec0c69.text: A new section was added to the help guide explaining how to customize the AI assistants. It covers how to change an existing assistant's behavior or create a new one using simple settings files. This is internal documentation only, so users won't see any changes in the software itself yet.

44d9fc7837de87a7a7b7fb7700a29da7ab52f2f3.text: The system now uses an AI model to identify and retrieve relevant files instead of relying on fixed rules. This improves how the assistant understands project context. The feature is active but currently set to a conservative mode that does not collect full file contents.

87fcf2384eafe3573e1e9364834648f15e4ebd68.text: The assistant's internal system for handling requests was cleaned up to treat all actions uniformly. This change is currently invisible to you; it does not add new features or alter how the assistant responds to your prompts today.

13a1a2ddd2f03b45a2fcbab38bebb96475902f41.text: The system now checks file locations used by custom agents to ensure they stay inside a safe folder. If someone tries to point an agent to a file outside that area, the setup will stop working for that specific agent. This change is live and protects the program from reading unintended files.

9d5cb14ac691fc930b3a0f38680493a348f98607.text: The assistant now loads its custom instructions from a central memory source rather than searching for files on your computer's hard drive. This change prevents errors when those instruction files are missing or stored in unexpected locations. Users who previously saw failures when the system tried to use these custom agents should now see them work correctly.

1fc362b6a7a23cc3872263dc1a88a0757a7f9fc1.text: A new internal helper tool was added to automatically write summaries for code updates. This affects only the software team, not customers. The helper is currently being tested and does not yet work reliably, so no changes are visible in the final product today.

d529db2f4104336c563aab75c217cf016b55da40.text: The assistant can now edit specific text within a file instead of rewriting the whole thing. This change is live for internal users. You would notice more precise edits and fewer accidental overwrites of existing content.

65c432bc959509a143dd2f09a601266ef1731f8a.text: The assistant can now read project files. This feature was previously disabled. Users will see the assistant directly access and display file contents when asked.

cea53e5a106c68ce3a20245020fbfb58be1328d3.text: The coding assistant can now look up official documentation for software libraries during its work. This feature is live for internal testing and helps the assistant find accurate answers without needing external browsing. Users will notice the assistant providing more precise guidance on how to use specific tools or frameworks.

d2fe4f46e112bf9f79fd35ba031fe70166efb744.text: The assistant can now create plans. This is for internal use and is live. If you use the assistant to make a plan, it will save the plan and track updates to knowledge files.

d35987b91ed8bd157c650ffff4512394c650fca7.text: The startup process for the development tool now waits until the main server confirms it is ready before launching the interface. This prevents the tool from starting in a broken state where the interface tries to connect to a server that isn't running yet. The change applies only to internal developers using the local environment, ensuring a smoother start without manual retries.

978abcd00776ef588b41d9e2be44c5f376659813.text: Developers can now safely run two copies of the application at once without them fighting over the same network address. Each copy automatically claims its own unique address, preventing crashes when testing multiple features simultaneously. This is an internal tool for the engineering team and does not change how the application looks or works for customers.

53dc30d932a3f65ce7a28198d6e2bc21ccf0909b.text: A new setting lets you customize how the AI assistant behaves by creating simple text files in a specific folder. This change is live and affects anyone who knows to create these files. If you set it up, the assistant will follow your custom instructions, such as using a different AI model or adding specific rules to its responses, instead of using the default behavior.

7140c172231339f503372d9bbce45094a3ae0423.text: The assistant can now create custom helper roles, like a brainstorming partner, by reading simple instruction files. This lets people add new ways for the assistant to think without changing the core software. The feature is active, so users can ask for these specific helpers to join a conversation.

b275c1a52b7e523d172dfe4fe96066f35bad3782.text: The backend now checks the shape of requests for tools before running them. This update touches the code that handles actions like searching files or running commands. It is an internal cleanup that makes the system more reliable for the engineering team, with no visible change for users.

aa1b41fd45dd6eb6706bda6ccd9a5a3f04f28a7a.text: The system now allows the assistant to save files directly, instead of just suggesting changes. This is an internal backend update, so there is no visible change for you today. It is not live for general use yet.

c05fd779259e5639b1c7ab03beb7da0b7c5df23e.text: The system now checks Google's version of a specific AI model first, then Anthropic's, then Amazon's, when processing requests. This internal routing preference affects only the backend service handling these specific AI tasks. Customers will not see any visible difference, as this is a behind-the-scenes adjustment to improve request consistency.

2ff11c230959e2b2bcc003a223a25934a80827ca.text: The internal rules for how the AI assistant reports its work were standardized. This change affects only the internal systems and is not a visible feature for customers today.

9b31b16ab18e95ee465852912a8f8e612e0e0a64.text: The team removed two files that were meant to set up a testing tool for the backend, but no tests were actually using them. This is an internal cleanup of unused code. Developers will not notice any change in how the application works or behaves.

1b1d47513ef9ed9fa7e565580077d8f9d29633f9.text: The background system that helps the assistant understand coding commands was reorganized to make it easier to update. This is an internal cleanup, so you will not see any changes in how the assistant behaves or responds today.

097d5b66abe48120ca14ff7580d5945f7d095775.text: The team reorganized one busy part of the service into two smaller parts: one for handling actions the assistant requests, and one for preparing file updates. This affects the people who maintain the service, not customers. The change is live now, and users will not notice any difference in behavior.

400f9755ae3ab7aa9d5d11fc17dca2aa413b42b1.text: A new assistant mode for creating custom AI agents was added. It is not live for general use today, as it remains hidden in the background. Only internal system processes can currently access it.

2c1155c49a69577aa2964aee4e854904ff3285fb.text: The system's internal labels for different AI assistants changed from specific brand names to generic job titles. This allows the team to easily swap out the underlying AI models without breaking the application's logic. Users will not notice any immediate difference in how the assistants behave.

90aae81dbea5378d1a84ce40d5b0dda7798d5576.text: The team deleted an internal note describing how to automatically share secret passwords with certain computer commands. This change affects only the internal engineering team. They will see one fewer document in the project folder, with no impact on how the software actually runs.

a7addaf7d9ce6fe2416b953ebcd02e9bfd03fed5.text: The AI assistant can now automatically switch to a backup service to fetch answers if the main provider fails. This change is live for all internal agents using the primary model. Users might notice fewer errors during outages, though the backup service sometimes uses a slightly older version of the model.

5b9b71c236ae63df0ea980f8afb1f58905adfd89.text: The assistant can now follow strict code instructions instead of guessing, making it more reliable for internal tasks. This change is currently hidden behind a switch that is turned off, so normal users will not notice any difference yet.

eeab42f0181892f83d261d1db9dbd374c07f1028.text: The app now hides specific error messages from the internal console when loading terminal components or sending usage data. This change only affects developers and internal tools, not regular users. No visible changes will occur for the average person.

6bd1bce94a1cbcc102aa1d630b4f29404fb89271.text: The system's record-keeping for failed updates was reorganized to handle more types of issues, not just billing ones. This is an internal cleanup that helps the software stay stable. Regular users will not notice any changes in how the product works today.

da73133a25d61bd1bebac97cc84e4d9f56d139eb.text: The release process for the CodeCane app was reorganized. Now, when a developer submits a change marked for CodeCane, a test version is automatically built and shared for early checking. This helps the team try new features sooner without waiting for a full official release.

b4063deba5c1f9345768ae7d4775644bd3762d39.text: The automated system that built and published ready-to-run program files for different computers has been turned off. This affects only the internal process that creates these standalone downloads. People looking for these specific files will no longer find new ones automatically added to the public list.

fa45f1d2216ed59290203a42196afe3f32f0c4a1.text: The Codebuff command-line tool is now packaged as a single standalone file for easier installation and running. The internal setup was reorganized to separate the command-line tool from the server, allowing automated systems to build and release it independently. This is a background change that improves how the tool is delivered and updated, without adding new features for the user.

9729e46d239e367d119ee1a76c7702c767548232.text: The search engine inside the app now finds its helper program correctly in the standalone version. This fixes errors where the app could not look up text in files. Users running the standalone app will see search work reliably without needing to install anything extra.

c001a7c6320bd9578c5c98c1cc80fbee819185ff.text: The list of available assistant templates was moved to a separate file from the template definitions. This is an internal cleanup that helps developers manage the code more easily. Nothing changes for anyone using the software today.

8e43ddbb832c3f82ba86c2fd5ea3233861b0e657.text: The billing system now automatically adjusts the number of paid seats whenever a team member joins or leaves, ensuring the invoice matches the current headcount. This change applies immediately to teams using seat-based plans. Customers will notice that their monthly charges accurately reflect the exact number of active users without needing manual updates.

e64b7691fdaa078c65efdf09e0d54c56f4eae8b8.text: The system now has a built-in profile for a new coding assistant named Buffy, who is designed to be enthusiastic and concise. This change also prepares the backend to track sub-agents, though that specific tracking feature is not yet active for users.

cf9187cabf960dc9d7457161194f2d56e84d58fa.text: The assistant's internal way of naming and tracking its own actions was standardized to match a common industry format. This change is purely technical and affects how the system identifies and processes its tasks. Users will not notice any difference in the assistant's behavior or capabilities.

75e6c77beb02137e71b96ea0df60d8ba7ed005e6.text: The 'manager' feature, which let the AI autonomously oversee complex projects using special tools to pause or stop tasks, has been deleted. This change affects only users who previously relied on that specific high-level automation mode. You will notice these options no longer appear in the interface, and the system now strictly follows the standard single-step assistant behavior.

edcfdeff27d8b493d92cf258fb91f25cb98a6ac5.text: The program now automatically builds ready-to-run versions for different computers when a new version is marked. These versions are placed in a public download area for people who want to use the software without installing extra tools. This change affects only the internal release process and does not alter how the software works for current users.

6039f909d5badf56d3f464c831966286a764b894.text: The admin area now blocks non-admins automatically, so visitors without special access are redirected or denied instead of seeing broken pages. Regular users see only public evaluation results, while admins still view all data. This change is live today.

70fe182b1cb2be918bd0e2afa142c2294b1fdd27.text: A small internal adjustment moved a set of background tools into a standard folder alongside other shared components. This change affects only the team maintaining the software's internal structure. It does not change how the application behaves or looks for anyone using it today.

c4c187769c73e73062c9573a1486dbd5787d7679.text: The internal evaluation runner now caps itself at twenty checks running at once, instead of starting every check at the same time. This affects internal evaluation jobs, not customer-facing tools. Someone watching a large run would see the work queue up in smaller batches, with less chance of the machine slowing down or failing.

df512fead49f7da75f8cf81837b34b7e39ea9cc4.text: The team deleted a large folder of test data and example files that developers used to check the software's internal behavior. This change is internal and does not affect the live application or any customer-facing features. Regular users will notice nothing, as these files were never part of the product they interact with.

1a4ed158f86d613e27df141446b335949495d638.text: Admins can now choose to make specific performance test results public or private. Regular visitors will only see results that have been marked as public. This control is active immediately for authorized staff.

970af3ad42e94e09d6e70f1783316a4ab33a5793.text: Added a new experimental assistant option using a different underlying model. Existing options remain unchanged. Users selecting this new option will see responses generated by the alternative model.

3287b282081f25efe4bb87a438c8108859d0c07e.text: The system now checks code updates simultaneously instead of one by one, speeding up internal tests. This change affects only the testing infrastructure and has no visible impact on end users.

0275ec9804c5514f3ff2beb4f2eb9faed02d7ff8.text: Developers now use a standardized tool to run commands, which automatically checks for and uses a secure configuration manager if available, or falls back to running commands directly if not. This affects the engineering team by simplifying how they start services and run tests, ensuring consistent handling of environment variables without manual setup steps.

f115e675e6f741606cdced358761c2d60b9e0f94.text: Two new assistant settings now offer a choice between faster responses and higher quality reasoning. These options are live for people using the coding helper. The difference appears only in how quickly answers arrive or how detailed the solutions seem.

75183ae0d850204e81d037acb0d05a7a544a3fdf.text: The assistant now always uses a built-in safety limit for its task steps if your custom settings are missing or broken. This prevents the tool from crashing or stopping unexpectedly when it tries to read your configuration. You will see the assistant continue working normally even if your setup file has errors.

40154da3140adb1a3d3901a729d4fd31825fe613.text: The program now checks for invisible formatting codes and zero-width characters before deciding if a line is empty. This prevents the tool from mistakenly collapsing blank lines when it should not. The fix applies to the internal display logic, so the visual output is cleaner.

a5423aef9cac05dd20553c49818748e32620efa2.text: Developers now fetch secret keys from a secure vault instead of copying them into local text files. This change affects the internal engineering team, not the end users of the product. If a developer looked at their setup, they would see that starting the app now requires logging into the vault tool first, and the old instruction file for manual key entry has been removed.

e71a0c76c384f58a533c7df9415092a95a800006.text: The system now tracks the cost and model details for automated code tests. This data is stored but not yet displayed to anyone. Internal teams will use this to review performance, but there is no visible change for regular users today.

76edaada622722b10c9a81e1277ae796a06a3744.text: Internal authentication checks now use one shared rulebook instead of separate copies. This change affects only the company's internal systems and the specific list of staff with admin access. External users will notice nothing, as the visible login experience remains unchanged.

08d9ecfdfbc411d9281fe3a7476b732bc412485b.text: A new automated check was added for the internal team. This check runs a quality test suite only when a developer marks their code submission with a specific tag. The change does not affect customers and is not visible in the product.

6b6e431e66f67bfc112370bfb18a950dfc7f4ca4.text: A new settings panel is live for internal staff to assign specific AI models to individual customer organizations. Regular users will not see this change directly, but their experience may shift if an admin updates their organization's model configuration.

6b06d7c2d22dda3b3b6b3ea9522dc25892387fe8.text: The software's internal organization was cleaned up by separating the code that handles direct command execution from the code that manages background processes. This change affects the system's stability and maintainability, but users will not notice any difference in how the application behaves or functions.

be9cd704489e65d16e3104d8e3959dcf43776d8f.text: Team invitations now use a fixed web address from settings instead of the current page's address. This prevents broken links if the server's internal name differs from the public site. Only admins sending invites see this; the email link works more reliably.

7f28828ae0cf979cb67ac6bf24258b68423d2891.text: The assistant now watches for repetitive cycles where it keeps taking similar actions without making progress. If it detects this, the system automatically pauses the conversation and asks the user how to proceed, preventing the assistant from getting stuck in an endless loop.

6aabac5a3b27729e7bb58fcd22f42d6fbe75afb0.text: The team deleted an outdated internal document that outlined a plan for a new assistant feature. This change affects only the developers who maintain the project's internal notes. Users will not notice any difference, as the document was never part of the live product.

88cc4d16628ef964c963ec43cc6b6b3503ac213e.text: A new internal tool automatically writes weekly update notes by reading recent work logs and summarizing them with AI. This affects only the team managing the software, not the customers using it. If you looked, you would see that the process of manually drafting these weekly summaries is now handled by a script, saving the team time.

6dde6b9b6c63d71a7a11cbd578ac948a35de43bd.text: A new automated check was added to the internal testing area. It starts a sample application and its command-line tool, sends prompts through them, and verifies the full flow works. This only helps the engineering team catch integration problems earlier; customers will not see any change.

da734278793e858621e4ec242f7cc47c6d2af6d0.text: A new internal switch was added that lets developers run automated checks for the main application, shared tools, and server components all at once. This change is for the software team's benefit and does not alter how the product works for customers. Users will not notice any difference.

210b7c44b78d37b414f98d5d8a36ed65a8052783.text: The system now automatically builds and caches a specific testing tool alongside the rest of the software, rather than requiring manual setup. This affects internal developers who run performance checks on the code. They will notice that running these tests is faster and simpler, as the tool is now ready to use immediately after a standard build.

5014af4859bbde92fd438d261f1a1fd362e106f4.text: A new supervisor mode allows the assistant to manage complex, multi-step tasks by running commands, pausing, or stopping processes when needed. This feature is currently in place but only activates when specifically requested through a special command, so it does not affect standard interactions yet.

0422ab89d021af35cd82ac61b3382e427563442a.text: Administrators for approved business accounts can now choose which artificial intelligence model searches their codebase and set limits on how many files it examines. The system checks these settings before running a search; if the configuration is missing or incorrect, it automatically reverts to the standard default settings.

9426dab66658a087315d9ad066c87850a87b75c6.text: The system now automatically checks files for errors immediately after they are changed. If the check finds a problem, the assistant is forced to see the error and try to fix it before continuing. This helps catch mistakes early without needing to ask the assistant to check the work manually.

16dc62f59d5bb5a4150395fe5f0cf7cd4403b3db.text: The system no longer guesses the amount to refill when an organization's balance gets low. Instead, the person setting up the account must type in the exact trigger amount and refill size. If they skip these numbers, the account creation will fail.

71a5dd348de49a75dc8e6d8851dfd82cc295591d.text: A new tool allows engineers to compare how different file-picking models perform against a known correct answer. This helps the team choose the best model for the code assistant. The change is internal and does not affect what current users see.

3af6aacb66eb3ab5ef49661a6bad7562394f88f5.text: The team added a new section to the help website showing recent updates. This area is currently being prepared and is not yet visible to the public. Once finished, readers will see a list of new tools and improvements added over the last three weeks.

c07b0311eeb0e5956971f4e517f4dfddc9cadb64.text: The system stopped using a specific text-generation service. This is an internal cleanup. Regular users see no change in how the assistant behaves.

7c67da92e90a02e3ba79b831a02000b24e604e1b.text: The system now automatically reviews evaluation results to generate plain-English summaries and prioritized lists of problems. This change affects internal engineers running these tests, who will see the analysis printed directly in their console logs. If the review step fails, the main test process continues without interruption.

f6094b46efc0702c2e9effdb80f3195d0c1908a8.text: The internal team added a test suite that checks how well their AI tool handles specific, complex instructions by replaying past code changes. This is a behind-the-scenes quality check for developers; it does not change what the AI does for regular users today.

770ce41fcad5f7ed8dde633ec3ae95b6eb7d908e.text: The backend switched from using a direct connection to the AI provider to a standardized internal tool. This change only affects the hidden systems that grade and relabel AI responses for the internal team. External users will not notice any difference in the app's behavior.

b2abad5b36ea9b7fbf26f3272d0afb631866f9a1.text: An automated daily check that tested the assistant's ability to understand code history was removed. This internal change stops a recurring report from being generated for the engineering team. No customer features or daily software behavior changed.

6913a7ebac0d7da3c464aa06bc09de0d9baa87a5.text: A small internal update moved the assistant’s file-editing requests from a separate connection to one model service into the same shared connection used for other model services. It affects only the server side of the service. It is live in the server side now. Anyone looking would notice no visible difference, just one fewer duplicate way to talk to model services.

3f77b33e6a7c75596e1cc3d0512e80c541ff2678.text: The system now uses a standard format for sending conversation history to AI models, replacing an older custom method. This affects all AI interactions in the background, ensuring prompts are built consistently. Users will not notice any visual changes, as this is an internal cleanup to prevent errors and simplify future updates.

2d55accd2d926586bb9c73324740db2a1231bae9.text: The system now automatically sends an email report containing performance scores and problem summaries after internal testing finishes. This affects only the internal team running these tests. If they check their inbox, they will see the results delivered directly instead of needing to manually inspect the data.

0adc47918fccab0706e1a2b9ddf4b7f6126a2e32.text: The team set up an automatic daily check to test how well their coding assistant handles git tasks. This runs internally every morning and saves the results for the engineers to review. Regular users will not notice any change to the product itself.

427525b708f93cfa71fc8788d46092e8ee7747e4.text: The system stopped using two old, separate tools for talking to Google's AI models, relying instead on a single, modern tool for all AI providers. This is an internal cleanup; regular users will not notice any change in how the product works. It makes the code easier to maintain and ensures all AI features behave consistently.

f227db9b854ccb84a908c2d46dae7b0c5eb0e012.text: The team removed old, unused code that handled streaming responses from specific AI models. This change is internal and affects only the underlying software structure. Regular users will notice no difference in the application's behavior or features.

1ebf8d9b68b11b6e094c42a279daf6cc6d916a0f.text: The internal system that checks code changes can now look at any repository instead of just the one main project. This helps the team test more places. People outside the team will not see a difference.

358d0db78fa82fc0c46511254ba6315755ace647.text: The internal tool that checks how well the code understands changes now processes three tests at the same time instead of one after another. This speeds up the testing process for the team, meaning results are ready sooner. Regular users will not see any difference in the app, as this only affects how the developers measure performance behind the scenes.

122102bb87087439ec17c52fdcb6f3653592f174.text: The daily automated checks now automatically download a copy of the codebase before running tests. This ensures the tests have the necessary files to run against. This is an internal maintenance update, so regular users will not notice any changes.

a5eb09dc80f7f241cc343e69e090224dbd8f5c54.text: The team removed a duplicate internal guide for the npm application package. This cleanup affects only the internal documentation structure. No changes will be visible to end users or external developers.

693635b17ac0bc709ac805ab46be6dbc2543146f.text: The automated checks that verify how the system calculates your remaining credits have been fixed to prevent data from one test accidentally affecting the next. This change is internal and only affects the software engineers who run these checks. You will not notice any difference in how the application works or how your credits are calculated today.

a7c06a2712110372bea2d081c80dda845602e9ec.text: The team added a background tool that lets them review old computer activity logs using a smarter AI model that sees more context. This change only affects internal data scientists and does not impact the daily experience of regular users. The new capability is available for the team to run manually, but it does not automatically apply to live features.

11f760c6a76e7b6e3d6dd8b13ecb1f8ef7cf4d8c.text: The database received a new organizational tool for message completion times. This speeds up the system's ability to find and sort past messages. Users might notice faster loading times when viewing message history, though the change is primarily internal.

ac9a7f7354e3dd3e6e28eb67521b4d340722c6aa.text: Internal tools now let staff see file-picking results and compare them side-by-side. A new admin page shows past attempts, and the system can automatically rank which model chose the best files. This helps the team improve the assistant's file selection, but customers won't see these changes yet.

8af577c6c9d73bcdc8f71a16cb91a4dcbe24c86d.text: The system now organizes its message records differently, grouping them by both the person who sent them and the time they were completed. This internal reorganization allows the software to find a user's finished messages more quickly. You will not notice any visual changes, as this update only improves how data is stored and retrieved behind the scenes.

a566ec2b780dc09c4cded7008af0081931421420.text: The system now safely skips broken file paths instead of crashing when applying changes. This keeps the tool running smoothly when it encounters a mistake. Users will notice fewer sudden interruptions, though the underlying fix is internal.

1b79a6d5380dfdf14a4e6a99cc1a63b5f9ad8b91.text: The assistant now reads its instructions for creating or editing files more reliably, preventing mistakes when the requested changes are complex or nested. This affects all users of the coding assistant. You will notice fewer errors where the assistant fails to write the file correctly or misinterprets your request, and the system now handles these failures gracefully instead of crashing.

b68ef311d4d1f636c5975523293b15ff7a545c47.text: When the system prepares its instructions, it estimates the length of a file list by checking a small sample of files. This update makes that sample always pick the exact same files for the same list, rather than choosing randomly each time. This ensures the length estimate stays consistent and prevents the system from occasionally cutting off the file list unexpectedly.

e2fd961bd1c659ed789bcf6030462ce804e2e40a.text: The command-line tool now hides advanced settings like 'lite' or 'max' from the standard help menu to reduce clutter. Regular users will see a simpler list of basic options. People who know these hidden settings exist can still use them by typing the commands directly.

687e4dbb50a8b1bf82f5dbe8fb29d44140c0b176.text: The website's main button now says 'Get Started' instead of 'Try Free'. Clicking it opens a new step-by-step guide that lets visitors copy installation commands or launch the tool directly in popular coding editors. This update is live on the public site and helps new visitors install the software more easily.

0963ba72ae47c80f897f4c8c270729c0d9dc18e7.text: A new automatic checker was added to the developer tools. This tool scans the code for common mistakes, like using the wrong formatting or referencing files incorrectly. Regular users of the software will not see any changes to the interface or features.

9a4ad025abb84b7082bf8324947873c15ea25c51.text: The system now reads tool commands more reliably, stopping crashes when it receives unclear or broken instructions. This affects anyone using the assistant to edit files or run commands. You will notice fewer interruptions or errors when the assistant tries to perform an action.

91d4333a25cace02ad7b83b188ff28b4c05f9d77.text: The team stopped using a tool that let them run their automated checks on their own computers. Instead, they improved how the online system saves and reuses parts of the project to make these checks faster. This change only affects the developers who maintain the software; regular users will not notice any difference in how the product works.

497d434f8bf4f962710d0b0404f4460fe6404d93.text: The assistant now has a precise editing tool for large files or failed edits. It replaces exact text matches instead of rewriting whole files. This helps users working with big codebases by making edits more reliable and efficient.

a5ebaaba019755369adf2ce7acd08962010cade2.text: The tool that reads XML files now correctly converts special symbols like '&' into their proper characters. Previously, it failed when these symbols appeared at the very start of a data chunk, causing the text to display incorrectly. This fix is live and ensures that any content using these special symbols renders accurately.
