1e5e715fbfb1d537c35ac58d4cdab501b5fd5220.text: The automated testing process now sets up its own environment directly for each task instead of relying on a shared, faulty setup script. This fixes a recent failure where tests could not find necessary configuration files. Internal checks run more reliably today; end users see no difference.

2c1460fdd43768d35ec6d4898ba2243fe7a8428b.text: When the AI reads a file, it now lists up to 25 other files that use code from that file. This helps the AI understand how changes might affect other parts of your project. The feature is live and works automatically for all projects.

5a61a5397e376f1a3e8a62cd0f9ab1012066eaf3.text: Added an internal tool to calculate monthly credit usage for staff. It queries message data to show total credits, user count, and top ten consumers. This is not live for customers.

b2d17e9d5315f24fc2136003a3213616d6fb86b4.text: The internal automated testing system was reorganized to group repeated setup steps into a single reusable block. A setting that tells the system it is running in the automated environment is now set globally at the start, instead of being written to a local configuration file during setup. This is an internal cleanup for the testing infrastructure, so end users will not notice any changes.

e42ccfe65840d616173d0151a2b9917a7e5cb817.text: The automated check that verifies code safety now runs at the same time as the code build, instead of waiting for it to finish first. This speeds up the process for the internal team. They will notice the system reports errors faster and requires less waiting time.

1f43c1b870135fc0ecb44ac13dcb0dcdf9c5dbaf.text: Developers can now test their work on their own computers using the same automated checks the company uses, without needing to send code to the central system first. This saves time by letting them catch errors locally before sharing changes. The change is internal and does not affect customers.

ad147ec5f9339ffaf17daf1f1acca40b87dd987d.text: The team set up a new system to help their computers work together more efficiently. This change is internal and only affects the developers who build the software. They will notice that their tools run faster and use less memory.

17c71f6cd1a840b7e8b7eb26f2282ef90885a5bc.text: The code that saves data to Google's database was moved into its own separate box. This change only affects the internal team, so regular users will see no difference in how the app works.

ff5f5f89dccaaaea3cd2e126a02983444710922a.text: A new system now tracks which parts of the software depend on others, so it only rebuilds pieces when necessary. This speeds up the process of preparing the code for release. The change is internal and does not affect how the product looks or works for end users.

c60fa21bba1531e05cc683abfb8272cae2bc712f.text: The system reverted to an older method for reading assistant responses, fixing issues where instructions to edit files or run commands were misinterpreted. This change is live and affects all users interacting with the coding assistant. If you previously saw failed edits or garbled command outputs, those errors should stop occurring.

6202b3322489c22213ee330a765a775ce8e78633.text: The system now uses a single, consistent method to calculate costs for AI usage. This update fixes errors where anonymous users previously encountered calculation failures, ensuring accurate billing for all accounts. Users will see correct credit deductions without unexpected glitches or errors.

b72ea4bebd2954faa734ef250ea33eaaa5fee143.text: The AI assistant now stops saving its internal activity records to your computer's hard drive when you use the standard online service. This change affects people using the main production version of the software. If you check your computer's files, you will no longer find the debug log files that used to accumulate there.

fb2d1dfca2916877ffe136e6f82f171d831b5726.text: The text explaining the software's settings format was rewritten to look like a standard data file with clear labels and notes. This helps both the AI assistant understand user preferences and the documentation website display them correctly. If you look at the help pages, the settings guide now shows a neat, structured example instead of a messy paragraph.

75e00b83dadca24eafbd038d5231929ab455518a.text: The system now records when people sign up or receive free usage credits. These records send to the analytics service immediately rather than waiting, so the data appears faster. This change is internal and affects only how the company tracks new users and credit grants, not how the product behaves for customers.

02c69f33e90bac403ed0165a7a303ca88d3ff3f5.text: The command-line tool now sends usage reports through its main logging system instead of a separate path. This change is live today for tool users. The only visible effect is that launch reports still arrive, but the internal routing is cleaner.

12424332f7ce042f336c1443112487c5463cd0c2.text: The app now checks if Git is installed on the computer. It sends this yes-or-no answer to internal analytics. Users see no change in the app interface.

2d7d7a990ff33bd90041223f1a955d5b4c987e17.text: The team added a guide for developers who need to test software on Windows. It explains how to access a shared virtual machine and set up the necessary tools. This helps internal developers work on Windows without needing their own computer.

ea533f8d06f0c48e553825c246cc202f920dced6.text: A background checker now starts automatically for the whole project and records any problems it finds in a log file. This affects the internal team that works on the project. They would notice that mistakes can be reported as soon as changes are made, instead of the checker being off.

03cbe0d68e2b22eb3a810c1fb8abb04ed6ba6901.text: The software now sends anonymous usage data to a third-party service to help track how often the tool is launched and how many requests are sent. This change affects all users of the command-line tool and the backend service, but it does not alter the visible features or performance for the user. The data collection is active and requires specific configuration keys to be set in the environment.

9c2c4c5c3d6899dc23a34a8fb9ead53e1c827e80.text: The program now saves its running messages to a file, making it easier for the team to see what happened behind the scenes. New parts were added to the sign-in screen to show a code for the command-line tool, but these parts are not yet visible to anyone using the app today.

b9940e9407b6dd65b151a988c0fd5b6e2a9ebef9.text: This internal update prevents duplicate background tasks by checking if another instance is already active before starting new ones. It also ensures leftover processes are cleaned up when the tool exits unexpectedly. Non-programmers would not notice any visible changes.

c2c62ac86efaf3f89c920c7159e13dd4ae856f94.text: The assistant can now automatically create or update a project settings file when asked to initialize a project. Users can add explanatory notes to their settings file without breaking it, and the assistant will ignore the new optional description field.

b907db6d8af65b13a0871fa4cf04eb63ce3da8e3.text: The website now has a dedicated page for configuration options, which automatically sends you to the relevant section in the documentation. The text describing these options was simplified to be easier for both people and the AI assistant to understand. You will notice this if you visit the new configuration page or if the assistant gives you clearer explanations about your project settings.

a843b8817e843fe1808f0aeeff438fd28e185b5d.text: Admin tools for reviewing user files now require a specific login and are restricted to four named accounts. This change is live and affects only internal staff, meaning anyone else trying to access these review pages will be blocked.

ed236a0bceda603c16863ddda5d7a664ee35b143.text: The tool now automatically starts background tasks, like a web server, when you open a project, provided you have set up a specific configuration file. This affects only people who create that setup file. You will see the tasks launch on their own, and their logs will be hidden to keep the screen clean.

ffd640ed3f0aaaf6f7ff5b5a308e62e4c7d330f4.text: The system can now talk to a specific custom-trained AI model, but this feature is currently switched off and does nothing yet. Once enabled, it will let the assistant send requests to this model and track its usage costs like other models.

99c163f037a9735d9c356e9c2e363dca52e23cd2.text: The software now includes built-in explanations for each setting in the configuration file, describing what each option does and how it should be used. This change helps the development team understand the configuration structure more easily without needing to guess or read the underlying code. It is currently in place but does not yet affect the end-user experience or the software's behavior.

60a75f471aa4a05410ab3d44b15e09560ad01c1e.text: Programmers reorganized the internal command-line tool to make it easier to maintain. They also fixed a small bug so that the system now correctly saves a backup even when no changes are detected, if that option is chosen. This is an internal update, so normal users will not see any changes in how the software behaves.

5246b83c5432b876374e1cf0450c5f6e869f243b.text: The tool no longer hides unrecognized tags in data streams. Instead, it displays them as plain text. People reading the output will now see these unexpected tags instead of nothing.

7f6e2d2aa73926aa1bf8671f77e819316faf0a09.text: An internal tool now lets administrators review and fix how the system chooses which files to show for specific users. This helps improve the accuracy of file suggestions for those users. The fix also corrected a data labeling issue that could have caused the system to miss recent activity.

7fe3167b36cb8dc119d4736b84a649eadc1a022b.text: The system's internal log splitter was moved to its own dedicated module and made more robust. This change affects only backend developers and has no impact on end users.

b9c4a393b92b8814c33c7952356a3d0145ed9a72.text: Users who enable automatic credit refills now get credits instantly when their balance drops below a set limit, without waiting for the bank to confirm the payment. If the card fails, the system stops trying to charge them. This is live for accounts that have turned on the feature.

e9194839f09c07d29defdb1e2d66f2f35bb5e3f5.text: The code that handles undo and redo actions was moved to a separate file to keep the main program organized. This internal cleanup does not change how the software works for you. You will not notice any difference in the features or behavior.

68f85fd4c9cc9441b1cfb768df3f7aa65ab024af.text: The system now breaks large internal data logs into smaller, readable pieces instead of failing to process them. This affects internal tools that rely on these logs for debugging. Users of those tools will see complete, organized log entries rather than truncated or missing information.

c01863b6a8c0af42bab2e1e3e61cb367e548302b.text: The assistant now receives live updates from long-running background tasks. It reports new output since the last check, capped at 5,000 characters per stream, and includes the original command for context. This helps the assistant track progress without waiting for the task to finish.

132778b796b180f9021119dbd0f749076993f323.text: The AI assistant can now show its step-by-step reasoning when using Google's Gemini model, and it stops writing exactly when it finishes its thought. This change is experimental, so most people will not see it yet, but those who do will notice the assistant explaining how it arrived at an answer.

e149d3a326e893650d788669092b77b0fdca2a5b.text: The assistant now supports running tasks in the background. Previously, it had to wait for a command to finish before moving on; now it can start long-running processes and continue working. This allows it to handle tasks like starting servers or running tests without getting stuck.

74c651a6db4b3716ce750abc7a823dd307a2e085.text: The system now quietly records details about how it searches for files during a conversation. This data helps the engineering team improve the assistant's accuracy and speed. Users will not see any change in the interface or behavior, as this is a background logging update.

59567a4df76501aeb4f2605211f209875554ce97.text: The system now lets people pick a custom name for their invitation link, replacing the old fixed list of approved names. When someone uses that link, the system looks up the creator to give them a bonus, instead of checking a static list. The bonus amount for each new sign-up dropped from 500 to 250 points, while the maximum number of people one person can invite rose to 500.

c7f818857794f59f69a714a1c2c0afaa3b28d4f7.text: The tool now supports a new artificial intelligence model and lets people choose which model to use via a command-line option. This affects people who run the tool from their computer's terminal. They will notice they can pick a specific model for tasks, and the system will correctly calculate the cost for this new option.

aeca6290626a96dea7060dcddef7e3461aa5262f.text: A new web page for the Codebuff Hackathon at Mox is now live. It displays the event's date, time, location, and prize tiers for attendees. Visitors to the specific hackathon URL will see these details, but the registration button is currently hidden.

fde2dbec23446274503a18292ca9b8e43f4d0afa.text: The system now locks your personal AI service keys in a secure vault instead of storing them as plain text. This protects your account if the database is ever compromised. You won't see any visual changes, but your private access tokens are now encrypted.

1b0767f9b5193fe1c26fc42e2e1ed981a863ab50.text: This internal change stops the system from confusing two separate login sessions when they run on identical computers. It also removes secret login keys from server logs to reduce security risks. Regular users will not notice any difference in the interface.

894cfcb85b60b8b9fd0edb37d03319389a5bd171.text: The system now automatically searches for relevant documentation when you ask a question. It uses an AI to pick the best match from a library of guides. You would notice answers that include specific, up-to-date instructions from those guides instead of general knowledge.

ceb58b10a8882ac97daad91a16c76253b2104648.text: The system now stores user API keys in a locked vault instead of plain text. This protects account access if the database is breached. Users will not see a change, but their saved keys are now encrypted.

2af716acdbb25762ae53b86c5352ec5e04848fe2.text: The system now cleans invisible text errors from chat messages more reliably before saving them. This affects internal message tracking. You would not notice any visible changes in the app.

f22b4d03a0a972455c39ad9e224a836ac651dc3e.text: The system now directs premium requests to Gemini 2.5 Pro instead of Claude. It tries three different data sources in sequence to ensure a response arrives. This switch happens automatically for users paying for the highest cost mode.

ae194dc9bbd65478c8aed2c99ffbb238a6cbee6a.text: The website's visual design was updated to a high-contrast, bold style with green accents and animated buttons. This change affects all visitors, who will now see a different look and feel on the pricing, referral, and navigation pages. The browser tab icon was also fixed to display correctly.

d7303e3a320dfe599bb499741c829f30c2eb2801.text: A small internal update makes the system read tags more flexibly, allowing extra spaces around the equal sign. This change only affects how the software checks its own parts and does nothing for the public yet.

f6f380735fd0aeab7a8a51079c3187d36fbcec08.text: The team added a rule that automatically sorts the list of tools at the top of every code file into groups and alphabetical order. This change only affects the internal development team and their text editors. Developers will see their files tidy themselves up every time they save, with no action required from them.

083ba34e1b8127271cab8501c442e98772ee098e.text: The Discord bot now runs as a persistent background service instead of waiting for messages to arrive at a web address. This change allows the bot to listen for events like new members joining, rather than just reacting to typed commands. Users will not see a difference in how they use the '/link' command, but the bot is now capable of sending welcome messages automatically.

6baeeab1a6450bcd49bfb45b5356164a89a1442c.text: The system now keeps the five most recent command results in full detail, but simplifies older ones to save space. It also reserves half the available memory for new instructions instead of filling it completely. This change is internal and currently affects how the assistant remembers long conversations.

254095ba25df1931af14d0fc48f39aef06460ad6.text: On phones, the main screen area now adjusts its height to fit content instead of forcing a fixed size. This prevents the interactive code editor demo from being cut off or hidden. The change is live for mobile web visitors.

7013cc6a0c68f7d94e42951b34cc6db0284c07db.text: Website icons and logo loading updated for better visibility and speed. Small spacing tweak added to a call-to-action section. Visitors see clearer browser tab icons and slightly faster logo display.

f33f7ec279296b67b59b9f69f02db55a99716de9.text: The app no longer accepts a specific type of message that previously carried user data, and it now records details when saving files. This internal cleanup has no visible effect for regular users.

454988686e03f8ea672270fc20dc55814ba53a36.text: The service now connects to Discord, letting people link their chat profile to their account using a specific command. This feature is live and works only for slash commands, not general chat messages. Users will see private replies to their commands, while the system checks each request for security and limits usage to five times per minute.

3ea21c0bf5c767ff7bf49eacc27f03ae18ed0e61.text: The system now uses unique tracking numbers for background tasks to ensure results match the correct requests. It also handles errors more clearly when certain features are turned off. Internal reliability improves, but you will not see any visual changes.

3f1365de20974594e130701a2f8ad0e9a14cc010.text: The main welcome screen now shows a full-screen demo that switches views after two seconds instead of four. Document pages use styled arrow buttons for navigation instead of plain text symbols. The demo animation sequence is smoother and cleans up properly when you leave the page. These updates are live today.

e9e6bfa2552ed87cced63694ac7f044c0ff7ee82.text: Developers added a tool to save the text sent to the AI for troubleshooting. It is currently switched off, so nothing happens automatically. If turned on, the system would write these saved texts to a folder on the computer.

4456de5e52c0de58db25dd6050493865b3c6d245.text: The AI assistant now follows stricter rules for keeping code comments accurate when making edits, and it is required to run any new tests it creates to verify they pass. This affects the quality of code suggestions provided by the assistant. You might notice fewer confusing or outdated comments in the suggested code changes and more reliable test results.

be93e9c7a9ad166a3f966d7670e62899912a0d7c.text: The system now cleans up long lists of results from terminal commands to make them easier to read. This change is internal and affects how the AI processes its own tool outputs. You will not see any direct changes in the application interface today.

8807e7c761039f32d9662636b84e3cd83336fa36.text: The main introduction page for this product was rebuilt to load faster and look cleaner. New interactive previews let visitors see how the tool works in a browser, a code editor, and a command line without installing anything. These changes are live now for anyone visiting the website.

ae551e15b0befaf867661627e85e5bb8e2c6650d.text: A new internal tool was added to help the development team track detailed activity logs for the application. This tool automatically records context about ongoing tasks into a specific debug file. It is currently in place for developers to use but does not yet change how the application behaves for regular users.

a1241ac65cad91f81e70464f7c18445e72511a07.text: The system now uses a dedicated tool to handle quick text edits and preserve comments, moving this logic out of the main file processor. This change affects internal code structure, making the editing process more organized and reliable for the AI assistant. Users will not notice any immediate visual changes, as this is an internal improvement to how the software handles file updates.

404c7a37e1937c7e68170eb5ae9823377e24a22e.text: A small internal update makes the file-reading tool add a blank line after each file it reads. This improves the spacing in the text output. Readers will see files separated by a clean gap instead of running together.

4d89fd90e801069dd11296321a667c3c061b1280.text: The testing team added a larger set of standard software problems to their internal quality checks. This change helps developers ensure the AI assistant can solve common coding tasks more reliably. Regular users will not notice any difference today, as this only affects the behind-the-scenes tests used to measure the assistant's performance.

09dcc50f0c0925f20cb6c989762653af1215cae7.text: A new internal tool now automatically counts how many credits paying subscribers have used over the past seven days. Staff can run this to see total usage, a list of the heaviest users, and daily trends. Customers will not notice any changes on their end, as this only helps the team monitor resource consumption.

e8b6afa4c44e491938b76bfcdd87c865aeabfd12.text: The assistant now remembers its core instructions more efficiently, which speeds up responses and reduces costs for everyone. It also limits how many files it can ask to look at in a single step to thirty, preventing it from getting overwhelmed by too much information at once.

ec645def0e60d84b36ae620b6159b65ab5840651.text: When the primary rewrite tool fails to produce a complete file, the system now uses a different AI model that can generate much longer responses. This change affects users who request large code rewrites, ensuring the assistant provides the full file instead of stopping early due to previous length limits. The fix is live.

a3a13cce00f8d4cbe5fcd7b096f420f3a4d0d716.text: The program now saves and restores project snapshots in the background instead of pausing the main window. This stops the interface from freezing while files are being processed. It is ready to use.

0d502c7e7288be983f9f95e1a7200f7d3e7a1c8f.text: The system now sends live credit usage updates directly to clients after each AI message. This affects all users interacting with the assistant. If you look at the interface, you will see your remaining credits update immediately after sending a message, rather than waiting for a separate request.

8585e19830ddf9f824141cb980e20d73a1f52a12.text: The automated safety checks that run when code is saved now actively test the software's behavior instead of just checking its structure. This change affects the internal development process and is live today, but regular users will not notice any difference in how the application works.

3b70e6d56a4ea8c7675e02b1a9ff78f0f0583529.text: The system now automatically tries a different standard name for the main project folder if the first attempt fails. This fixes a setup issue for internal testing tools. Regular users will not notice any change.

2d86909ff04f6c3d79bf105e6115e6ee399e7b9a.text: The assistant now reads more project files at the start of new chats to better understand context. This change affects all users of the internal coding assistant and is live today. You may notice the assistant asks fewer clarifying questions because it has more background information ready.

34743caca48b5ea49a0adc6d8d66baa034df4dc1.text: The main heading on the website's landing page changed from 'Code faster with AI' to 'Upgrade your coding agent', and the text below it now mentions that the tool works in the terminal or editor. This update is live immediately for anyone visiting the site, though it only changes the displayed words and colors without altering how the software actually functions.

bda7d09c830d4d1ea86649fdafff1fc84d4ff379.text: The backend now caps the longest answer from the Sonnet model at 15,000 tokens instead of 40,000, leaving more room for the conversation history. This affects internal Sonnet requests; other models keep their 8,096 token cap. A non-programmer would notice nothing directly, since this is an internal setting change that is live today.

9124f763c550afc4dcb723c93b33cc6cd4cb1140.text: The command-line tool now logs in and out using standard web requests instead of a continuous live connection. This change makes the login process more stable and less likely to fail if the connection drops. You will notice fewer login errors, but the visible steps in the terminal remain the same.

10630e0f5e067bf2525c12ceac195107ca6bdce2.text: The assistant now adds a blank line after the 'Thinking deeply' message, improving text spacing in responses. A new sample project was also added to the internal testing system. This is a small internal formatting fix with no visible change to end users today.

00b34952856356dd00deaf3449c680432a85ff03.text: The internal tooling received a minor update to its release tracking number. This change is administrative and affects only the software's version history. Users will not notice any difference in the application's behavior or appearance.

0579cdcab13ae9aa373130a9429d3fcf6e6cf9a4.text: The assistant now checks if a typed message is a command for the computer itself, rather than a question for the AI. This change is live. If you type a command like 'ls' or 'git status', it runs immediately without the assistant trying to answer it first.

7560af255e825a03c221890bd46c9d9c271e5142.text: The internal system now automatically switches to a different AI provider if the first one fails or times out. This change affects how the backend handles file requests and planning tasks. Users will notice fewer errors or interruptions when the primary AI service is unavailable.

a9f9898592d18ccc113e4156257eff05c4e01d28.text: The assistant now automatically shortens long chat histories to prevent errors when the conversation becomes too large. This internal fix ensures the system stays within its memory capacity by removing older messages while keeping the most recent context. Users won't see a visible change, but the assistant will no longer fail to respond during very long sessions.

f0e8228f1223b9bd2fe7743bd6403bb76ab3389a.text: The assistant now reads large-file editing instructions more reliably by allowing small spacing differences near the end of a block. This fix affects internal tools that process big files, reducing failures when applying changes. Users would notice fewer errors when the assistant edits large files.

bcf9cb8a8fdb47d3878144182788e4c59c5c5a19.text: The system now correctly calculates the cost of using the AI assistant. Internal guides were updated to clarify how usage limits and subscription statuses interact. Users will see accurate billing information.

11d9e80aab463dc74f7ece14f1c7e90f330c30df.text: The help pages now display a detailed side-by-side list comparing the two AI coding tools, making it easier to see how they differ. Additionally, if a subscription upgrade fails because of an unpaid bill, the site shows a specific warning message with a link to pay the invoice instead of a generic error.

1f91f2ea178b06aa306692ce6a76f859b8e945c7.text: The system now uses a faster, cheaper tool to pick which files to read when you ask a question. This change affects internal backend operations and is live today. You might notice slightly quicker responses when asking the assistant to look at your project files, though the actual file selection logic remains largely the same.

7951ebc176382f24ef2511c6ace5aa7d79107e79.text: Internal staff added a tool to measure how often the assistant edits files in the last 24 hours. It scans recent conversation records and counts specific edit markers to generate usage statistics. This change affects only the internal operations team and does not alter how the assistant behaves for end users.

2d126431420f2215e48033847ab6b90fbb58e8a8.text: The assistant can now talk to Google's cloud-based Gemini models through a new, separate connection. This lets it use Gemini for tasks that were previously handled by other services, and it includes special rules for handling images within that specific connection. This change is live and ready to be used.

b79a553e5af77db115cbd740b9712c11e5519174.text: A new loading animation now appears whenever the system is processing a request, replacing inconsistent status text. This affects people using the command-line interface, who will see a spinning symbol with 'Thinking...' instead of static messages. The change is live for those using the terminal tool.

516276fff8cc25ae3416775e22882d6188d62508.text: Developers moved a specific rule for shortening file lists into its own separate section of the code to make it easier to manage. This internal cleanup does not change how the software works for anyone right now, so you will not notice any difference in the results you get.

864595917326240c53d73457c3fbcf724748c311.text: The browser tool now uses the computer's existing Chrome installation instead of downloading a separate copy. This makes the software smaller and faster to install. The tool is restricted to looking at pages; it cannot click buttons or submit forms.

a1b4ad89172ca55f1348017a4d8d39dd3b5cda4a.text: The system now remembers how long previous messages were to avoid re-measuring them repeatedly. This speed-up only applies to messages longer than 100 characters, as shorter ones are faster to measure fresh. Users will notice slightly faster responses when sending long texts, though the improvement is mostly internal.

50c6ad5fbee31d741b783327a0547e32812f951a.text: The internal setup for the command-line tool was reorganized to make it easier to update later. This change does not affect how the tool works or what a person sees on their screen today.

bb02aa5925d19c1d2dd7ddf2b8956ffa5a54e687.text: The assistant can now open web pages, click or type in them, and take pictures of what it sees. Those pictures are added to the conversation, and any chat service that cannot receive pictures has them removed first. This affects people using the assistant’s web-browsing ability; they may see screenshots in replies and fewer failed replies.

480d5741a0687e926e8a97b5ccee533b6dad3d0d.text: Pressing Ctrl+C now stops running tasks immediately, instead of just pausing the assistant's response. This prevents background processes from lingering after you cancel an action. The window to exit the program entirely with a second Ctrl+C press has also been extended from three to five seconds to prevent accidental shutdowns.

c5e75252efbb9d315d2d643f8129097d798bdcfe.text: The team removed three outdated text files that held old notes and plans about how the assistant used to work. This change affects only the internal record-keeping; current users will notice nothing because these files were not part of the active software.

6a47827d9d8c4751aefe4c42e306352b10b62412.text: The assistant now picks which project details to show by ranking them for importance instead of just looking at file names. This change is live and helps the assistant focus on the most relevant code when you ask a question. You might notice slightly faster or more accurate answers on large projects, though the visible behavior stays mostly the same.

84b162580ec88b3547c69a8d9a12db719b78c5a0.text: A small internal tool now checks the last 10,000 messages to see which AI models are used most. It calculates the average cost and length of messages for each model. This helps the team track spending and usage patterns, but customers will not notice any changes.

3be38cadbf028f05ba3e84a6299acc75f85a1636.text: The internal guide describing how the website works was shortened. This only affects the people who read that guide to understand the site's features. They will see a much shorter document with the same basic information, but fewer detailed instructions on how specific visual elements and login steps work.

1e76e4dac70f2d76f74309a5050cdfeee74db946.text: A new internal tool now creates a spreadsheet listing all user email addresses, names, sign-up dates, and subscription status. This affects only staff members who run the tool; regular users see no change. The file saves with the current date and time in its name.

61893b46b9498b063a99cd33325ef541e74eec83.text: A new internal tool helps the business team see how much extra money customers pay when they use more of the service than their plan includes. It checks recent bills for customers on specific paid plans and groups them by how much they spent over their limit. This change is only for staff to understand billing patterns; customers will not notice anything different.

7736bf8c71d2c5a5423312f7ca7527e8c58a083f.text: The online documentation was reorganized into clearer sections, with basic pages under Intro and more detailed pages moved to Advanced. The FAQ now has more questions about what the tool can do and how it handles data, and the getting-started page shows a simpler first command. People reading the docs will notice the new sidebar and find some pages in different places.

34f77ef4ed2a509623586b69f494640e8ddef825.text: A new internal tool now automatically counts how many unique people used the service each day over the past week. This change only affects the team's internal reporting and does not change what customers see or do. Staff can now run this tool to get a quick average of daily active users without manually checking the database.

473544be8885257c683c7ec3ff33551956ac9a17.text: A new internal tool calculates average monthly spending per customer using recent paid billing records. It groups customers by spending ranges and reports totals. This is for internal analysis only; customers and users will notice no changes.

7deebad01fa66f3133bcfb51bb0b8858de07d74a.text: The system now uses a different method to apply file changes, which should be faster. This change is active immediately for all users. You might notice edits appearing more quickly, but the underlying process has changed.

039bf9ca922ea15e5f3b37416477787374bf7c31.text: The project now has an automatic quality check that runs every time code is submitted. It ensures the different parts of the application are built in the correct order and that the web interface has no hidden errors. Developers will see a pass or fail result immediately, preventing broken code from entering the main system.

05e0047e93e5b1604d9473f8fe69e71bb3babb2f.text: A new guide was added to the internal documentation showing how to use the coding assistant for non-coding tasks like writing database queries, generating documentation, or reviewing changes. This helps team members see examples of asking the assistant in plain English to handle these everyday work requests.

541a515f763b1e86d86d008093c8f3c36a7401e2.text: The team moved a small pause function to a more logical location within the shared code library. This internal cleanup affects only the developers who maintain the software. Customers will not notice any changes to how the application works.

842a3c9fe971c84b9a74440c96a10f741ff14816.text: The website now automatically formats code examples written in plain text into styled, copyable blocks. This affects people reading the documentation, who will see consistent colors and a copy button on every snippet. The change is live today.

6573107d01347935aadf697c09bca758bdb5e9ce.text: The website now shows a live, typing demo box on the front page that answers questions about the software. Visitors can type commands to see how it works. The site also added a cookie permission box; analytics data is only collected if the visitor clicks accept.

f68b71753130d7822e19cfc2c1b30632ffcc8a34.text: When a customer changes their subscription plan, they now see a confirmation page that shows their new plan limits instead of a generic success message. This applies to customers modifying their plan through the web app. The change is live today.

9432f8961c0bcaa8d7a21768f833e02d4c7fadac.text: The assistant now checks which command-line tool is active on Windows before running tasks. If it finds the standard Command Prompt instead of PowerShell, it uses that tool directly. This prevents errors when the assistant tries to run commands in environments that do not support PowerShell.

3abfb85ab2fa33ecb2e02d339132beb0b4f78461.text: The program now runs commands in a live shell instead of launching a separate process for each one. This means error messages and normal output appear in the correct order, exactly as they would in a real terminal window. Users will notice cleaner, easier-to-read results when the assistant runs commands, with no jumbled text.

c3285d6f774d056d14008c9b204f0f9fe321e922.text: The tool now lets you start a new project from a pre-made template instead of building from scratch. You type a simple command with the template name, and it downloads the files and sets them up for you. This is available right now for anyone using the tool.

9330c43a06996ca4d64ff92f38d1b661facd6df4.text: The assistant now always uses PowerShell for terminal commands on Windows, ignoring other shell types. This change is live today. Windows users might notice commands running in PowerShell even if they previously used Command Prompt.

aeb348fdcaeca28f3de97d59c3083b2144f69a25.text: The website now has a new help article explaining how to create a special text file in a project folder to store notes about project goals and coding rules. This helps the assistant understand the project better. The article is live today.

017f18a6991ec32e11a7e393b70e282c9bd49f21.text: The assistant now checks which command window you use on Windows before running tasks. If you use the standard command prompt instead of PowerShell, it will open that one. This only affects people using the command-line tool on Windows; web and desktop apps are unchanged.

275ed4dc5f8440c970f6ea2e64b099b22a9164cb.text: A small internal cleanup moved the code that collects your computer's basic details, like its operating system and processor speed, into its own separate spot. This change helps the team keep the system organized and makes it easier to share these details with other parts of the tool. You will not see any difference in how the software works today.

a698cd8441363e0d429b1e191b7295ce9880620c.text: A new internal tool calculates monthly and annual recurring revenue by counting only active, paying subscriptions that are not scheduled to cancel. It ignores variable usage charges to ensure the total reflects fixed subscription fees. This helps finance teams track income accurately but does not change what customers see.

d02430ff07e656278bf8926cafb01b6e4c831e18.text: The code that runs terminal commands was moved to its own file to make it easier to manage. A new helper was added to cut off long command outputs with a clear marker when they exceed a limit. This is an internal cleanup; you will not notice any changes in how the assistant behaves.

4a1c1090ec8373b0f2e1242fab2d79bf473ee973.text: The system stopped using a separate, unused tool for creating documentation files. Instead, it now passes a setting that controls spending limits directly into the main planning process. This is an internal cleanup that helps the AI choose the right files to read while respecting cost rules.

ae3804a62d8269be646f6b94cd9436b94a56492b.text: The system stopped using a special background program to run commands, switching back to a simpler method. People using the command-line tool will notice that error messages now appear in red text on the screen, separate from regular output.

ab8eb3dee6f2248a3e095e2fcd0e240267d2e358.text: The team renamed internal activity labels to follow a consistent format and routed data collection through the company's own website address. This change affects the analytics reports used by the business team, not the website visitors. Users will see no difference on the site, but the data sent to the reporting tool is now more organized and less likely to be blocked by browser privacy settings.

0d8894ca77aef154b2d414afb75c21846988c335.text: Paid subscribers can now upgrade their plan directly in the app without contacting support. The system checks for unpaid bills before allowing a change and updates usage limits immediately. This applies to Pro and Moar Pro users, who will see a new button on their billing page.

79d15dd36fb8d58a489777bc568e4330ec072627.text: The system now sends requests for the advanced planning model through a different service provider instead of directly to the original creator. This change affects users relying on the complex change planning feature, making it live today. They might notice slightly different response times or reliability, as the new provider acts as a middleman for these specific requests.

6a7f6623edd8adaa109fc0a08f77ad85b5d3f01d.text: The website's main page was simplified today. Visitors now see a shorter headline and an automatically playing video instead of the previous multi-section layout with pop-up demos and command snippets. This visual change applies to all visitors viewing the homepage.

65cfd5a0fcd047942bd548117e6700b37a1f0581.text: The app now uses a cheaper AI model when you choose 'Lite' mode. This replaces the previous model for this specific setting. Users selecting 'Lite' might see slightly different answers, but the cost to the service provider is lower.

6290ea41cfa2cd1c46381d5fe38cd3182e9405f2.text: The home page video now includes a second file format to help older browsers play it. This change is live today. Regular visitors will see the same smooth video, with no obvious visual difference.

beb0a7f320489f054fabc167238bb0bce726e643.text: A new story about how a user named Oliver used our tool to build a grant platform was added to the internal website content. This change affects only the team managing the website, as the story is not yet published for the public to see.

0676fd902eaef8c6d6bcc3f00447aa92c784b079.text: The program now keeps the command window open between tasks, letting it remember the current folder and display text in color. Users will see clearer, formatted output from commands like git status, which previously appeared as plain text. The system automatically restarts this window if a command takes too long, ensuring the program does not freeze.

c95d630de7b6227d3f518d884f37df8b8ff987dd.text: Help pages now display detailed explanations about how the software works and which AI models are used. Visitors will see this information as standard articles in the help section, rather than brief answers in a question list.

502c8a171f713aaf91af8ed3ead28e0668af5971.text: The company refreshed its website's front page, pricing page, and help guides to make the text clearer and the layout look better. They also updated the scrolling banner to move slightly faster and changed how images load on the main page. This is a visual and text update for visitors reading about the product, not a change to how the software itself works.

369b8b051db0507ebe41a6534a560ceccfaa8c66.text: The team removed the written help page that listed common connection and permission errors. They also added a new tool to the project's setup files to help automate code tasks. Regular users won't see any change in how the product works, as the new tool is internal and the help page was just deleted without a replacement mentioned.

ca0c95cf0318ef95b381c1d8b11ae04d7628e905.text: A new setting lets you choose between faster, cheaper responses and slower, smarter ones. This applies to all users who have access to the application. You will notice a difference in how quickly the assistant replies and how detailed its answers are based on the option you select.

b2172514822c8405c13432c4393f6620ff737fe8.text: The tool now places changes into a review area instead of automatically saving them to the project history. This affects people using the command line to manage their code with the assistant. They will see their files marked as ready for review, rather than being instantly and permanently recorded.

d591118f115c70fea467813f8f7b134c374153b8.text: The documentation now includes a news section that displays recent updates fetched from an external feed. This change is live and visible to anyone visiting the documentation site, where they will see a list of news items in the sidebar. Additionally, the footer now includes a direct link to the documentation.

78eb505f1c5078acce40199d97be44e615b6d675.text: The tool now lets users choose between 'cheap', 'normal', and 'expensive' modes to balance cost and quality. In cheap mode, the system uses a faster, less capable AI model and ignores non-essential files like tests or configs to save money. This setting is active immediately, allowing users to switch modes via a command-line option.

39e050a949b84a3ea36138b1395939eadd927ad7.text: The team updated a background tool that measures text length for the AI assistant. This change is internal and only affects developers who work on the project. They must now use a new setup command to install dependencies, as the old installation record was removed.

440d6914d76a8fac849413795f68ccbba9626f70.text: The app added a new AI provider option. Users see no change yet because the interface does not offer it. The connection is ready for future use.

3f43ab01953a8cbdde6b426d491904ef631e4fb1.text: The documentation website now displays recent company news articles in the sidebar and footer. Visitors reading the guides will see a 'News' section with links to the latest updates, pulling content automatically from the company's blog. This change is live.

c16ab111a0ff3d9731c3811d694badb5d4a9ee0c.text: The system now records how long it takes for the AI to respond to a request. This change affects internal billing and performance tracking data, not the features customers see. If you looked at the usage logs, you would see a new entry for the response time of each message, though this data is not yet displayed in any user-facing reports.

fbdf1f044cfb39225553aa6fb9ef6979dd190732.text: The website now has a dedicated area for guides and help articles, featuring a sidebar for easy navigation. This update is currently live for visitors, who will see the new documentation section when browsing the site. Separately, the team switched to a different tool for managing the website's code, which speeds up development but does not change what visitors see.

f65adba28db3fa54b0d303b79ce91026b28f437c.text: The site now recognizes when visitors arrive from specific YouTube creator links. Instead of showing a generic homepage, these visitors are automatically directed to a dedicated referral page featuring the creator's name. This change is live and affects only those clicking the new, tracked links.

8151ce2028b89f39a1159fe0f49102ceb2c92046.text: The assistant can now use a new, more powerful model for complex tasks. This change is live today. Users will notice the system can better handle difficult requests by planning them out first, though this might cost more per use.

87b543491dd17629e88ab979f6ced010e6b0e050.text: The company added a hidden marker to the main website to help track where visitors come from. If someone clicks a LinkedIn ad and then visits the site, the system quietly remembers that ad. This helps the marketing team see which ads lead to sales, but visitors will not notice any change.

9137ca0c8cffe43534f1fce215958517349f4c46.text: The system now finds a person's message history much faster. This helps calculate how many tokens they used. People might notice billing reports load quicker.

519f59e3da75e0220722ce9094577d3b11f6afd5.text: The website now uses one shared routine for payment redirects instead of separate copies in different menus. This ensures that when someone clicks 'Upgrade' from the top navigation bar, the system records the source of their visit exactly like it does from the pricing page. Users will not see any visual changes, but internal reports on which ads lead to sales become more accurate.

c485b69b4b1315b0b638e015cb7eb291a7e2624d.text: The system now reports successful subscriptions to LinkedIn only after payment completes, not when checkout begins. This ensures accurate tracking for marketing campaigns. Users see no visual change, but LinkedIn reports will now reflect actual purchases rather than attempted checkouts.

6b20e41107c04b8870bc35225d6371acaeb2289b.text: The assistant now checks if it has finished a task or is stuck in a loop before continuing, rather than stopping after a fixed number of steps. It also enforces using the correct package manager for your project when installing new tools. These updates are live for internal testing.

7d1b3f6252a10308fd6aae37a6e9a158297260fd.text: The website now displays a new recommendation from a founder. This change is live and affects only visitors to the public testimonials page. They will see the new quote and its supporting image alongside existing reviews.

6f27f4d86abf2ba45057e82294ed8f3b753a7746.text: The AI assistant no longer tries to guess if a task is finished or stuck by asking other AI models. It now simply stops working after a fixed number of steps. This change is live and affects all users interacting with the assistant.

35aa8ccddea9fc4b5f340b447a07c4ffd3b2eed3.text: A small internal tool now lets anyone watching the Codebuff Twitch stream type commands into a shared coding window. Viewers see their chat messages appear as text on screen, though the script runs only when someone starts it manually.

40a018d94ff478a6678ecebaed3245b9b3d97178.text: The system now records the exact creation time for each digital fingerprint. This is an internal database update that does not change how the application behaves for anyone today.

8be7449b6eb2832f7ff0ac7ff3d70d09cbd76ebc.text: The landing page now displays a list of common questions about the service. Visitors can click a question to reveal the answer, which covers topics like data storage and supported AI models. This addition is live immediately.

040218df9cf8ad4facc6f386fc53d9a01781eb67.text: The assistant now uses familiar symbols like '<<<<<<< SEARCH' and '>>>>>>> REPLACE' to mark code changes, replacing the previous 'search' and 'replace' tags. This format aligns with standard version control tools, helping the system parse and apply edits more reliably. The change is live and affects how the assistant presents code modifications in its responses.

7fecc6d01a9c82b8b07cb0b1994513c9af0b8f17.text: The software now tracks the specific amount of credits spent during your current active connection. When you close the application or the connection ends, the system displays this exact session usage total. This applies to all active users, providing immediate visibility into how much of their allowance was consumed in that single sitting.

07a24a2fcadc2a4f836f299fb5bdb8b8efd755a9.text: The assistant now uses a second AI model to judge if it is stuck in a loop or if the user's request is finished, rather than just counting messages. This allows it to pause or continue working based on actual progress, making interactions smarter and more efficient. This change affects the internal logic of how the assistant manages conversations and is live for all users.

f670fdb7932f87bef16edeb24cf73db2b5d6077d.text: Monthly fees for the Pro and Pro Plus tiers dropped to $49 and $249, while their included usage allowances were reduced by half to match the new prices. Existing subscribers on the higher rates were automatically switched to the lower prices, and their current usage totals were preserved to prevent billing errors. The updated costs and limits are now displayed on the public pricing page.

7e274e30d3106b8379bfe073e95d045d0adf1a88.text: The website now displays a new customer quote from Stefan Gasser, a company founder, praising how quickly the tool handled a design update. Visitors to the testimonials section will see his photo, name, and a link to his original post alongside existing reviews. This is a small content addition that is live immediately.

07bc5c57d8a158315a50f61e8112658f4751cf58.text: The team updated the instructions for a coding assistant that currently only works with one specific tool. They clarified that a second version is not ready yet, removing old text that promised it was coming soon. This change is internal; customers will not notice any difference in the product today.

8b9d6a0c26752b5619ee9f05bfae867010999bdb.text: Your monthly credit allowance now resets on the calendar date, even if you did not use every credit. Previously, the counter only cleared after you hit the limit. You will see your available credits refresh automatically when the month ends.

b5d976e118da6f39dce3ab47189176b981991272.text: The billing system now charges for actual usage instead of a fixed monthly fee. When you cancel or delete your account, your chat history is automatically removed. You would notice this change on the pricing page, where the cancellation link is now on its own line.

f3375a1a8bd642bea10b8a5b44708e10d9fb89fc.text: The company's website now shows a new review from a design engineer named Omar. He praises the product for completing a complex task in 30 minutes that would normally take hours. Visitors reading the customer stories will see this new entry alongside existing testimonials.

f087bd5656693d637cf464a906611af5b1e75fc0.text: A new customer review from Shardool Patel, a founder and CTO, was added to the website's testimonials section. Visitors to the site will now see this specific quote comparing the service to hiring an engineer for $100 a month, along with his photo and proof of the statement.

9f3905939a7734c5d57e5693ceac0a1e6bbd136a.text: The assistant can no longer look up prediction markets. This internal change removes a feature that fetched live market data. If you tried to ask the assistant about Manifold markets, it would no longer have access to that tool.

c1afad717e45147f90d5bc436067481baaee7a71.text: The website's front page now shows customer quotes in a continuous, moving strip. Visitors to the main page will see these testimonials scroll automatically across the screen, pausing when the mouse hovers over them. This change is live and affects only the public-facing landing page.

a30788b1d677be33608e2c8be3336a4511d02c14.text: Internal cleanup. Moved testimonial text out of main page code. Programmers can now update quotes without touching layout. Visitors see no change.

15e35c14bf1a5b1d7cbc4ee3a7bbbc5d638dd3e0.text: The demo video on the homepage no longer plays directly in the page background. Clicking the video thumbnail now opens a pop-up window that covers the rest of the screen, keeping you focused on watching the video. You can close the pop-up to return to the main page.

8d4806b72aeef12acede91d4f443273c851313ac.text: The website now displays a new customer review from Stephen Grugett, complete with his photo and a verification image. Existing reviews were slightly reworded to use an ampersand instead of a comma between job titles for consistent styling. These updates are live and visible to anyone visiting the testimonials section.

f3fcbc871040f310e55a4afa21ce90c78594c3dc.text: The landing page now shows scrolling rows of customer quotes. Each card includes a photo and a link to a screenshot proving the claim. Visitors can hover to pause the scroll and click to see the evidence.

7906dec3b6cc6fe8901f20be64d91f53dd7dc7e7.text: The internal Python placeholder for the coding assistant was renamed from 'manicode' to 'codebuff'. This change is not live for customers and affects only the internal project structure. No user-facing features or commands changed.

acdc10a9b34eb900af1f7790a360e03f8b4166ae.text: The system now stores file history separately from the main project description, allowing the AI to reuse cached memory when files change. This reduces wait times and costs for users interacting with the AI. The change is live.

6604b7989b06a7bd740d399288d947e70cd1a9fc.text: The app now tracks how many friends each person can invite individually, rather than forcing the same limit on everyone. While everyone starts with five invites, support staff can now grant specific accounts more or fewer without changing the rules for everyone else.

6e292a9504ec4e5d29ec15854e8d1b2f3cb3549f.text: The website now has dedicated pages for its privacy policy and terms of service, accessible via links in the main navigation and bottom menu. Visitors can read these legal documents directly on the site instead of searching for them elsewhere. The home page also updated to let visitors easily copy the installation command with one click.

8e47d113a1f9db946d06668bcf24a5d862996195.text: The system now finds the right spot to apply changes even if the spacing or line breaks look different than expected. This stops errors when updating files where formatting has shifted. Internal tools use this logic to keep edits accurate.

de1b1be8b4adbf10c2464601af2a658d1558639b.text: The website's main page now includes a video player showing a demonstration of the service. The small icon displayed in browser tabs and the logo at the top of the page were updated to match the new branding. These visual changes are live and affect all visitors to the homepage.

535fbc2e860e08b374e529e1f128cb9c3480fc0e.text: Paid subscribers now see their true usage limits and pay fees when they exceed them, instead of being blocked or seeing wrong numbers. The monthly limit for this plan also dropped from 50 million to 10 million credits, so you might hit the cap sooner than expected.

6ab694669541596938b3e537b1e11c0c1baef90f.text: The system now uses a more powerful AI model to finish edits when simple text matching fails. This internal update ensures complex file changes are applied correctly without manual intervention.

9b36eea10a2b242a13c6fc88ddef508a0624fcbc.text: When you run the app on your own computer for testing, it now looks for login details in a separate folder instead of the same place used for the real service. This stops your test account from accidentally overwriting or mixing with your main account. Regular users who do not run the app locally will see no change.

f257801349ff1a8f88a5e39c15887849d0d04de9.text: The website now checks referral limits directly from its main system instead of waiting for you to log in, so anonymous visitors can see if a link works. A new banner appears at the top of pages, sitting above the menu bar to stay clickable. Landing page visuals updated, replacing a globe graphic with animated beams and removing loading delays.

8d675ea7bdec92d5bc572b07f6fc7cc157393dd3.text: The AI assistant now edits code by finding specific lines to change instead of rewriting entire files, which reduces errors when modifying large documents. This update also ensures the system correctly locates its configuration files regardless of how it is launched. These changes are active immediately for internal users interacting with the coding assistant.

18d586d784dc4c6623376cc3f76ed08df8848b2e.text: The website now shows a 'Continue with GitHub' button to visitors who are not logged in. Previously, the 'Referrals' link in the top menu was hidden unless you were already signed in; it is now always visible. Clicking it while logged out reveals a prompt to sign in to get a referral code.

ea33b2602d1ba8b3b3423a203455f67393d23ee6.text: A new page now shows how many credits you have used and when your billing cycle ends. This applies to logged-in users. You can see this information by visiting the usage section in the web interface.

5d7f6c6f547418d57c5d5c81f1a61442518d3ee2.text: The team added tools to clean up messy notes in code files, turning vague placeholders like 'rest of code' into a standard marker. This helps the AI understand exactly which parts of a file are unchanged versus modified. Since these tools are for internal data preparation and not the main app, regular users will not notice any change today.

82b15d5ad5695e1a3a697c4b27d66978ef1d9319.text: The system now correctly sets the date for monthly credit resets when a user upgrades their plan, matching the actual billing cycle instead of guessing. It also started recording the exact creation date for new accounts. Users who upgrade will see their credit reset date align with their next billing date, preventing premature or delayed resets.

23d30e803574b62295d5a2fc559c005f163595ad.text: Users can now invite others to join and earn 500 extra credits per friend, up to five times. Invited friends need to sign up using a special link to trigger the reward. The system also updated how it finds its own web address to ensure login links work correctly.

09b8f1d5bef7c0a6f14c8762231d44747146125e.text: The auto-commit tool now uses an AI assistant to write descriptive commit messages instead of generic text. This affects developers using the command-line tool. They will see meaningful, human-readable summaries of their code changes automatically saved with each commit.

c409707321172e20165a3a6116c0b53ad8c1beec.text: The system now records every AI interaction to calculate precise costs based on text length and model type, adding a 20% markup. This infrastructure is in place but does not yet charge users; it currently only tracks usage data internally.

1376cfaf7769ce0f595c8ff7d0ea4db561e39a28.text: The system now records internal activity details in a standardized, searchable format instead of messy text dumps. This change is live for the engineering team. If they look at the server logs, they will see clear, structured entries that are easier to read and filter by importance level, rather than raw, unorganized output.

603b1250745ae26f6cdf68e8fb64d1d93e4cb220.text: When an AI assistant tries to update a file but only provides the new section without the surrounding code, the system now adds visible markers instead of accidentally deleting the rest of the file. This affects internal users relying on the assistant for code edits, who will see these markers in the proposed changes rather than missing content.

d213792a89fde8df257d192a0c03dcd4afd7ce83.text: The assistant now cuts off very long lists of recent file edits to fit within its memory limits. It also allows a larger list of project files to be included in its view. Users with large or heavily modified projects may see slightly less detail about recent changes but more context about the overall project structure.

7d5989ef8550811be44d7bed834b6f5347e679b6.text: The tool now prepares its initial view of your project in the background instead of waiting for it to finish before showing you the prompt. You will notice the command-line interface appears faster, as you no longer have to wait for slow startup checks to complete before typing. This change applies to the main program interface and is live for the current version.

97a524e86e58a1203a38a17e13cf91bf8e10c892.text: Developers reorganized internal code to fix website errors. This change is entirely behind the scenes and affects only the engineering team's workflow. Regular visitors will notice no difference in the website's appearance or functionality today.

41b405b65610a0b6602197b616c9e653ffdd6e6b.text: When you run out of free uses, the app now sends a clear message about the limit and offers a link to invite friends for more. This applies to people who have not yet reached the maximum number of referrals. The change is live today.

0fbcd881c6a38f09658a71033ea07c5f1c2748a6.text: The system now waits until it has gathered a small block of text before showing it, instead of flashing every tiny piece as it arrives. When the assistant starts working on a file, you immediately see a clear message saying which file is being edited. This makes the response smoother and less choppy, and it is live now.

2f64ead5948cd33b095aaf39edff7eb9de28698e.text: Fixed a bug where saving changes to the very end of a file or files with specific symbols failed. This affects anyone using the patching tool to update code. You would notice that updates now succeed instead of crashing.

92334a746484a4e10f1626df1a0b36e664295bb6.text: The command-line tool no longer supports signing in through your web browser. Developers using this tool must now sign in through the website directly. This change removes the code that handled browser-based login links and session cleanup.

16e9952360cc28c2219d8a130db5581b6c2d076d.text: The command-line tool now generates a temporary security code to link your terminal session to your web browser login. This prevents unauthorized access by ensuring only the device that started the login can complete it. You will see a specific link appear in your terminal that you must click to finish signing in.

8a1b30b651eb64c1d661a51db93cd339e895f109.text: Command line users can now log in securely via browser without sharing passwords. The system creates a temporary, expiring link that verifies your identity once. This change is live and requires specific server settings to work.

cb6b625beb5195bce2988325c81047a4223bbf27.text: The AI assistant received updated instructions on how to search for files and run commands. This helps it understand when to look up code or execute tasks more effectively. The change applies to internal operations and improves the assistant's ability to handle complex requests.

f0ea9490c29d6691ba8bf669a849f2f7322788c8.text: The system now checks if you have used up your daily allowance of AI responses before letting you send a new message. This applies to everyone, from casual visitors to paid subscribers, each with different limits. You will notice that after reaching your specific cap, the service will temporarily stop answering until your allowance resets.

2d267eda1e830442ec31c63f2c1ecafd89bc7669.text: Removed a leftover database setup file from the backend. This internal cleanup affects no one and changes nothing for users or developers.

950bb55122c3a51a3df5b29e2d21a3e20c051552.text: The code that helps the assistant understand programming languages moved into its own separate section. This change makes the main program lighter and faster to update for the developers who build it. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves.

a2e91c18f510cd091d55929f54451a7f9871800f.text: The website's main landing page now displays a spinning 3D globe and animated background beams instead of the previous static layout. This visual update applies only to the public-facing homepage and does not affect the core software functionality. Visitors will notice a more dynamic, modern-looking introduction when they arrive at the site.

d98196190301f2ed83ec0c225b91cae0f4b83acd.text: Added a large sample project structure to internal testing tools to verify that the system correctly identifies and processes files when generating summaries. This change affects only the development team's testing infrastructure and does not alter the product's behavior for end users.

9eef70a6a490319f0a7d38ad9d4a9aefdc1c1d86.text: Developers moved the database setup into a shared spot so every part of the app uses the same rules. This change is for the team building the software, not for people using it. No visible difference for anyone else.

1a7ece065b2da90198d92d34b291f8249a4ac162.text: A new rule now automatically sends every code update to two specific people for review before it can be approved. This affects internal developers, who will see these reviewers appear on their requests without needing to ask them. The update also added a small helper tool to the server's software list to fix a missing piece, which helps the system run correctly.

c587aae615c068ba13fe9290e69628519c378849.text: The service now checks its configuration settings before starting up, stopping the program if any required details are missing. This helps developers catch setup mistakes early, but customers will not notice any difference in how the application behaves.

135d30ff7623de37a897108855894a232e7e4dad.text: The system now correctly reads instructions for updating text files, even when the changes start with removing lines. Previously, these specific updates could fail or apply to the wrong spot. This fix is in place and affects how automated edits are processed internally.

76dfa7f9bf87f34de548b671ec1be25be897ce64.text: The system now finds the correct set of tools to use, ensuring it can perform its tasks properly. This fixes an internal error that could have prevented the AI from completing certain actions. You won't see any new features, but the AI will be more reliable in its day-to-day operations.

1957662225e21cadeedeb264f448951360602776.text: The tool now checks for new versions directly from the public software store and installs them automatically when the program starts. Users will see a brief update message in green text if a newer version is found, rather than just a warning asking them to update manually. This change is active immediately.

3cbefde8c7b78bb988f91f34a80100034bf2d3dc.text: The software now correctly stops reading a list of changes when it reaches the end of a section, instead of skipping lines or reading too far. This affects anyone using the tool to update code files. If you look at the results, you will notice that edits are applied more accurately without missing parts of the text.

9f62f7976a0b44e340a50ec5458112cb4d199167.text: The team added a safety check to ensure the tool correctly updates code when sections are moved around. This is an internal fix for the software's reliability, not a new feature for users. You would not notice any change in how the application works today.

94d47b15dbe328f9fbc8d5a9cc615f38a5387fcc.text: Internal setup improvements added documentation and startup automation for local development. New team members now see clearer instructions and launch the app with one command instead of manual steps. This affects only developers working on the project's code, not end users.

d9881d19056719643cd0b0466eeb4f153f175028.text: A new internal batch processor was added. It can run many small tasks at once, but never more than 20 at the same time, and it keeps the results in order. It is only a building block for future parts of the app, so nothing visible changes today.

7615438e2c03a608ae43b0f591a801fcce0c6c06.text: The tool now finds the right spot to apply edits even if the file text has shifted or looks slightly different. This helps the assistant update files more reliably when the original code has moved around. The change is active today and reduces errors during file modifications.

c6622fefa7dabd0a797510e1c1fb6654b21cd60b.text: The system now automatically creates or updates small guide files when a conversation involves meaningful changes to a project, capturing non-obvious context that might otherwise be lost. This affects people using the coding assistant, who will see these guide files appear in their project folders without having to ask for them.

c11faad368a762482fa6cd50bb9d1658ab05786f.text: A new helper script now automatically launches both parts of the application in separate windows, waiting for the first part to be ready before starting the second. This change only works on Mac computers. Developers setting up their local environment will notice they no longer need to manually start each part in different windows or worry about timing issues.

169a24a087447e04cc889302f8535c7e730a9598.text: The AI assistant now uses special text markers to identify files instead of the built-in tool commands. This change affects the core processing system. Users will not see a difference in the output, but the underlying method for handling file requests has changed.

915f42f128f863efc7d80675193e0ed20ffdc966.text: The tool that scans code files now remembers its setup instead of rebuilding it every time, making the scan faster. It also correctly identifies exported variables in TypeScript, so they show up in the code map. This is an internal performance and accuracy improvement.

34de88ced7e058b1b2b9c7869a6a649994be1525.text: The team added clear instructions for setting up the AI coding assistant, including a template for where to enter secret access keys. They also simplified the process for starting the assistant's two main parts separately. These changes help new team members get the assistant running on their own computers without guessing how to configure it.

bbf6819d104cc6b0a9d35f4b7b934df6402ef550.text: The software's internal label was updated to mark a new release. Two sample projects were added to the testing area to help check the assistant's performance. This change is internal and does not affect any current features or user experience.

d802a8ae32441e522f6c35f2d9c292c92a28d5b1.text: The team replaced an old tool with a new one that automatically increases the version number for both the main application and its server component. They also added a shortcut to test the assistant against a specific sample project. These are internal changes for developers and will not affect what regular users see or do.

a9461c25625621ba785fe8d226cef84808e7c1a8.text: The system can now store user email addresses in a secure database. This is an internal setup change that doesn't affect what customers see or use today.

fff6d38300ea5fd18de41bda42feca55b47a16c7.text: The service now uses a specialized AI model to write code updates, replacing an older, more complicated method. This change affects the core system that generates these updates. Users will likely notice that the AI is better at following instructions to change specific lines of code, especially in larger files.

c7ae728112c6ae83fc2f5f49c91203c25092d701.text: A complete copy of the prediction market website was added to the internal testing area. This copy helps the internal tooling test its ability to read and understand large, complex websites. Customers and the live website see no change.

ee96fe281beb7224909fb3ab0b3a87cd0cb7c7fd.text: The tool now reads code written in Ruby, Go, and PHP to create maps, but it stopped reading code written in Elisp, Elixir, Elm, and OCaml. If you use the dropped languages, the tool will no longer recognize your code structure.

a0572b1406dc1d4d9e8b2fe6b1d90181befe47a0.text: The tool that creates training data for the AI assistant now works on several projects at once instead of just one. It combines information from these different sources into a single shuffled list. This change affects only the internal team building the AI, who will see a more varied dataset ready for use.

c89d785b3f6f9163b1b55b24d2d198bb8a96a325.text: An internal tool now uses a new AI model to turn code changes into training data for a smarter assistant. This helps the team build better software features, but does not change what regular users see or do today.

21d52d137265dd24d44ac81648e97905031c04c8.text: The code that handles file edits was moved to a shared location so the command-line tool and the web app use the same logic. The testing system was also switched to a faster, newer tool. This is an internal cleanup; regular users will not notice any difference in how the software works.

0fa2bf1bc2ec6a37c2fcd6db54d64bfdeaa4799b.text: The team switched to a faster tool for installing and running the software's building blocks. This change only affects the internal tools used to create the product, not the product itself. You would notice no difference in how the software works; it simply makes the setup process quicker for the people who maintain it.

2b08698b2f0fce32c9a3570cfb3d8a760ea48ded.text: The assistant now checks a specific list of folders to skip before scanning your project files. This means it will ignore test data and focus only on your actual code. You might notice the assistant finds relevant files faster and avoids getting confused by temporary or mock files.

a38a3180d7a9e25f1a83f4c3365fddcd90bdd4e6.text: The service now holds back raw file text while it streams responses, so only the file tags and surrounding commentary reach the screen. This affects the internal assistant output path. A reader would notice file contents no longer spilling into the visible reply.

432ee9ff077425f6d079b8c56f8e22710c413c72.text: The team wrote a plan for how the software will handle user logins and payments. Nothing changed for you today; this is just a blueprint for future work.

2e6270d27fa41c8624131a57ae90f25a9c51c50f.text: The program now checks if your installed copy is older than the server's version when you connect. If it is, you see a yellow warning telling you to update. This applies to everyone using the command-line tool today.

66ed712e83dd5455a0196c11ef8b78ee1c8e04f9.text: A new Python version of the AI coding assistant was added to the project files. It is currently a placeholder that prints a message directing users to install the JavaScript version instead. No features are live yet, so users see no change in behavior.

efc5cb41ea406771cacb3a3acdb5cae91fe7f81e.text: The system now tracks AI usage spending per person to prevent excessive costs. This applies to all internal requests made through the main services. Users may notice the system blocks requests if their individual spending limit is reached within a day.

7f031f9931b38b8a8ed67b0739ce455014a82dc9.text: Developers added a test case to verify that the system correctly handles and truncates file contents when the AI generates code changes. This is an internal check to ensure reliability in how updates are streamed to the interface. Regular users will not notice any immediate changes, as this only affects the internal quality assurance process.

be899b33d927028a64cef09a21a1ba9e30cb5252.text: The command-line tool now prints status updates in different colors to make messages easier to scan. This affects people using the tool on their computer's terminal. They will see blue text when moving between file versions, yellow when stopping a response, and green or cyan when loading files.

c4091bc7c28991d8a7f85c28f5a5998885e26ad1.text: The system now fixes mismatched line breaks in files before applying changes, preventing errors when editing text created on Windows. It also switches to a more efficient method for updating large files, saving processing time. This change is live and affects all file edits, resulting in more reliable updates and fewer failed attempts.

8d613fb0a458e56d1fb49cb6068b27c77b9e11c4.text: The system now automatically finds and loads relevant project files before answering, instead of asking the main assistant to search for them. This speeds up responses and reduces errors for internal users. The change is live.

7f1629543df85669e89ad87d7d0d978f06bbe5fb.text: The AI assistant no longer repeats back the user's request before starting its work. This internal update affects how the assistant plans its responses, removing a preliminary step that summarized the question. A reader might notice the assistant skips the initial restatement and jumps straight to reviewing code and brainstorming solutions.

e68c4539c90295fa30bbd970b4c3b662be9bd7e1.text: A small internal adjustment removed an extra blank line at the end of the instructions sent to the AI model.
