This helps the model format its answers correctly without adding unwanted spaces. Regular users will notice no difference, as this only affects how the system prepares data behind the scenes.

92b54a227398657bed70dec701400db26f76f0f5.text: The internal system now separates task lists and problem tracking from high-level ideas and wish lists. This change helps the team keep track of actionable items versus conceptual notes more effectively. Users won't notice any difference, but it makes the internal organization clearer.

d4581ed59329811065c9d3431dc6ef61fa4ea739.text: Developers fixed a test that checks how the system compares file versions. The test now waits longer for the AI to respond and runs alongside other checks instead of blocking them. This internal cleanup helps ensure the code comparison tool works reliably for large files, but customers will not notice any change.

cd5349e25eadd27f76346cd021b6d2160cae5f04.text: The tool that helps the assistant rewrite files received better instructions and examples to show exactly how to keep unchanged text intact. This change affects only the background system that prepares these rewrites. A person would not notice any difference in the app itself.

d2809905e36a4015a9511174f278231dd93fccc4.text: The tool now forces its internal instructions to list exactly which code sections need filling in before writing anything, and to output a clear 'nothing to do' signal if none do. This reduces mistakes where it invents or skips code when updating files. It affects anyone using the file-diff generation feature; they would see fewer incorrect or missing code blocks in results.

8e31d5f27feb75694e2cb28ae6031dac8c82da56.text: This internal fix corrects how the system compares file versions when changes are made on Windows. It ensures the comparison process ignores invisible formatting differences that previously caused errors. The update is live and affects the backend system's accuracy. Users will not notice any direct changes.

33d729465cbb73556b089f0c5501ec4357605772.text: The assistant can now fetch text from a website when asked. It works immediately. If a page fails to load, it will tell you it couldn't get the information.

fe97f7321e301d188dc28144a30295ea016a2de6.text: The command-line tool now quietly creates a unique digital ID based on your computer's hardware parts. This happens automatically when you start the tool, adding no noticeable delay. You will not see any change in the interface, but this ID helps the service recognize your machine.

f1744c6fb4c1c5e1c281acd92756d59a40c9453e.text: The assistant can now look up predictions on Manifold, a site where people bet on future events. If you ask a question about what might happen, like who will win an election, it can search for a matching market and tell you the current odds. This feature is ready to use.

d37dfa943b0da5dda6fe0f9b33eb8e6f0993ec64.text: The service now uses a standard packaging method for easier deployment. The assistant was instructed to skip rewriting files if their contents are already correct. This change is live and reduces unnecessary processing steps.

961453dae185cb06f8ea4b20d52122f7d30cbe8b.text: The system now caps the amount of file text it reads at a set limit. It processes files in priority order and replaces the rest with a marker. This keeps requests from getting too large. Internal only, no visible change for users.

12e25be8a163cb29d77631abc7a6a4ab76ee970f.text: Test files added to check if the system correctly handles complex changes to a single chat file. This is internal work for developers only. Regular users will see no change.

554f7982b3450290329a9a3826bcf8ab5ca1c872.text: The team added clear license labels to the project files. This distinguishes the free, open-source helper tool from the private business software. People looking at the public tool now see it is free to use, while the rest of the project remains closed.

3383120ca5be7ec0dcab06028a1a41a518b54b68.text: A new guide was added to help the AI assistant understand how this specific software project is organized. This internal update does not change what the assistant can do for you today, so you will not notice any difference in your experience.

fc982c8568ae25d4a81d20d465653d8b72cc2069.text: The system now builds file updates by comparing the old and new versions to find exact changes, rather than guessing the whole file. This makes updates more reliable for people using the internal tool. You will not see any difference in the app's appearance.

f8e7677a226835196471a95b36e1b5501fa393de.text: The system now ignores specific test files during its background checks. This change affects only the internal engineering team and does not impact the live service. Developers will notice that automated checks no longer fail because of these test files.

e7f52632973782fea2bf03ea76964af888d84850.text: The program's internal structure was reorganized to separate different tasks, such as handling the chat menu and managing saved conversations. This change affects the software's maintainability and stability but does not alter any visible features or user-facing behavior.

80b9a1ddfa78dd182116dabcfbf1c851628d97c1.text: The team reorganized the project files so the command-line tool can be installed like a standard software package. This change is internal infrastructure work; it prepares the tool for easier distribution but does not add new visible features or change how the tool behaves for current users.

11ccbdb184aab6cb277ee80ccf773aea3f0cc099.text: The software now automatically removes unnecessary background tools and forces the correct settings before sending its updates to the store. This keeps the download smaller and prevents the program from accidentally connecting to test servers instead of live ones. You will not see any visual changes, but the tool will run more reliably.

4ae0090ae9f7110e93090689876343fb1f83ee1b.text: The AI assistant now uses a shorter end-of-message signal, allowing users to stop generation early and provide new instructions instead of waiting for a full response. This change is live and affects anyone using the chat interface. Additionally, unused code was removed to keep the system clean, though users will not notice this cleanup.

b00d1c37492084dec807ea468716e4c9c55c361f.text: The code that handles the assistant's responses was split into two separate files to make it easier to manage. This is an internal cleanup that does not change how the assistant behaves or what it can do for you.

0c7c30edebde240f56733da60cdae23a4f9a6ff1.text: The tool now includes a guide and installation instructions when shared. People using it will see the help text and setup steps directly in the package. This is an internal packaging adjustment.

e7b486a15b295697e22197dd56f26405c827fd92.text: Added a test case to verify the system correctly handles complex indentation changes when updating code. This internal check ensures the tooling accurately compares and applies edits in tricky formatting scenarios. The change is not live for end users; it only affects the development team's confidence in the update mechanism's reliability.

29d41099d146c6cf01e4c86de2f6f7a08e259dc8.text: The team created new sample files to test how the system handles code that already contains many notes. This change is strictly internal for the developers. Customers will not notice any difference, as the software's live behavior remains unchanged.

c0839d542c602e23c2260a2e68fb6b4732c9630e.text: The internal AI assistant now automatically downloads and reads web links saved in its memory notes. This means the assistant can use external documentation directly without the user needing to paste the text. The change is live for the internal tooling.

a528a49ef6a21a7bd4e5990ebb4fb03a5fcda199.text: The application now checks specific folders for shared helpers instead of using a single central list. This internal cleanup ensures the code finds the right tools without confusion. Users will not notice any change in how the software works.

918a7aa4253a876c3a47f6c56395745454283c0c.text: The system now automatically loads its configuration settings when running internal quality checks. This change affects only the team testing the software, not the people using the product. A developer would notice that these checks no longer fail because they can't find the necessary secret keys.

e350c7f460b34059eb4cdd72a9683eb4e6695258.text: Developers added a safety check that makes the AI assistant keep talking until it finishes a long answer, instead of stopping early. This is an internal plumbing change; no visible difference to end-users today.

be19b40c22d27853ff48643096530f0cfeea490f.text: The team added a new system for automatically checking the code behind the service. This helps developers catch mistakes earlier, but it does not change how the product works for regular users. You would not notice any difference in the app.

2edfac49059f0f236e622e58f9ba59f67f9e5d16.text: The system now saves your conversation history to a hidden folder on your computer instead of keeping it in temporary memory. This means your chat logs remain available after you close the program, allowing you to revisit past interactions. These saved files are kept local to your machine and are not shared with the team.

122ee89d87e5519937008129f0e0add084d67079.text: A new internal logging tool was added, but it is currently switched off, so it does not record any activity yet. Separately, a fix prevents the system from processing the same file twice, which stops it from accidentally overwriting parts of your code with placeholder text. This change is live for internal testing.

4e57e9c38ddbb65ddb0564ce4b99c1b2c5331296.text: A new internal document was added to store strategic notes and product ideas for the AI assistant's context. This change affects only the internal team and does not impact external users. The assistant now has access to these specific background details to better understand the project's goals, though no visible features for customers changed.

e35b16b9b2fd62ce6f2305a2e603b07be9a26f4e.text: The assistant's request handling moved to a separate background service. This service listens on the local network and streams responses back to the main interface. The change is internal and does not affect the visible behavior of the tool today.

06e4e19ee1b5c95ea7566e30c5ae0a69345bddc8.text: The team created a shared toolbox for the software, moving duplicate helper functions into one central location. This change affects the developers who maintain the application, not the people who use it. If a developer looked at the project, they would see that different parts of the application now pull these common tools from a single source instead of having their own copies.

2d2e8dd1108a5a2feda2bc02ed593179b79aaf3c.text: The live connection between the app and the server was rebuilt. This change affects the background plumbing that keeps the editor updated in real time. You will not see anything different on your screen.

0d9e257b88312ce91939b721a634a9c1ff1851ef.text: The team moved a specific coding helper into its own separate folder, giving it its own setup files and internal connections. This affects only the developers who use that helper, as it no longer relies on the main project's shared files. They will notice the helper now starts up independently and reads its own configuration, rather than being pulled from the central codebase.

4eb9084f29628018a8f1d25677eb365fc6ff82bd.text: The assistant can now request to view specific files from your project during a conversation, rather than just responding with text. This change is in place but does nothing yet, as the system is not currently configured to send these requests. Once fully active, you would see the assistant explicitly asking to read your code before making edits.

6cd4d481c83bb4d6faae74a0c776ca1556ff0977.text: The assistant now reads special text files named knowledge.md inside project folders to learn about the codebase. It also ignores hidden system folders during this scan. You will notice the assistant gives better answers if you add notes to these files.

8134f2f8f7a358cb93c871c34e16d99ef6b98e5f.text: A small internal update adjusted the expected text for a tooltip in a test file. This change affects only the automated checks, not the live application. Users will not notice any difference in the interface or behavior.

aa91f013a9f0cb8d35f70d8ce5fa0f7f48f785b1.text: A new internal tool lets staff type a plain-language request, like 'create a page showing live bets,' and have an AI assistant write the code changes for them. This affects only the engineering team and requires manual setup to run. Customers will not notice any changes yet, as this is a private utility for building features faster.

bd7d722103b0942a6a51ab1fa30bc4236e2dc4c3.text: The internal coding assistant now receives whole-file instructions instead of specific search-and-replace commands. This change is not visible to end-users, as it only affects how the system processes requests behind the scenes. The assistant remains in development and does not yet impact any live features.

6d8a809148fcc144292078d1af3ab89a7d607005.text: The team created a new guidebook explaining how the computer system that powers the app works behind the scenes. This document is for internal staff to help them understand the setup, fix issues, and plan future improvements. Customers will not see this change or notice any difference in how the app behaves.

fb17d9888659f8054532d4a90a7b8bb5027043e9.text: The system now recognizes a matching program for verified YC companies. If a company collects $1,000, they become eligible for a $1,000 credit. Nothing changes for customers today, as the program is not yet active.

c293aca107f890c0d45d6739e4905bbb80e97aac.text: The system stopped showing extra costs for the 'Flash' model because it now uses a fixed price. This change is live for new connections. If you look at your pricing details, you will no longer see a temporary surcharge badge on that model.

2f90af6aca5f096834b3755d3076f56cc36c5d9b.text: The tool's internal label number increased to mark a new package build. This update only affects how the software is packaged for distribution. Regular users will not notice any changes in behavior or appearance.

217906d84aa2113d8c363debba204695a6e074db.text: When the command-line tool blocks work due to usage limits, it now displays a web address for enabling automatic balance refills. This helps subscribed users resume tasks without manually finding the settings. The change is live and appears immediately on the screen.

286d268c11543e5525d49ce12cd2d707cdd5ecbc.text: The automated testing process now ensures that a live session is properly closed if a check fails midway through. This prevents the system from leaving a long-running session open on the account, which previously happened when a test stopped unexpectedly. These improvements affect only the internal quality assurance team and do not change how customers use the product today.

66ba78e74d208e853547e8331136229c4c1ba045.text: The team reorganized the internal code by splitting one large instruction file into three smaller, specialized files. This change affects only the developers who maintain the software, not the people who use it. No new features were added, and the program's behavior remains exactly the same.

4ff23980eed8bb8c8060150d73829847ba390d48.text: The automated checks that verify the assistant works correctly were updated to use a different test question. This change affects only the internal testing process and does not impact the features or behavior seen by customers.

3cb1fb6862cca34e8ccbba778c11ca697e2a9e05.text: The team added a safety check that runs the website exactly the way the live server does, rather than just in the testing environment. This prevents the site from crashing when real users try to chat with the assistant, a problem that happened recently because the test setup and the live setup were different. Regular users won't see anything new, but this check helps keep the service stable.

2c8541e90dcc9e7641fe7d4ba7c03e1eea64bfa4.text: The account dashboard now uses the phrase 'model spend' instead of 'tokens' for monthly dollar limits to prevent confusion with actual token counts. This change only affects accounts where the operator has enabled dollar visibility; for these users, a new card will display an estimated cost in dollars and cents. If dollar visibility is restricted for an account, the cost card will not appear.

2e67ad0b60df355424e672d6a635b6d5ab2cdad8.text: The team added instructions for a new safety check on the freebuff web builder. This check automatically tests if the app can start and process a chat message using a specific, older version of its underlying engine. It prevents the app from breaking after automatic updates, ensuring that only working versions go live.

abd23ca628058b352e08b9fc4028f775b2c72042.text: The team updated the internal packaging file for the freebuff command-line tool. This is a routine administrative change that affects how the software is bundled for distribution. Non-programmers will not notice any difference in how the tool works or looks.

02082cce25560ae06491ef8c0ef30c6518b5afc7.text: Developers added checks to ensure the command-line tool correctly matches helper tasks to their final results. This is an internal safety measure. Normal users will see no difference in how the software behaves today.

81f78e0c885af9edb97960bf8e8497cf1a45e6a1.text: The system now automatically ignores temporary login files created by an internal automation tool. This prevents accidental exposure of short-lived access keys. No customer-facing behavior changes; the fix applies only to internal repository hygiene.

54ba9b4874e7b588f9f771155853fa42e2218765.text: The free coding assistant's version number increased. This happens automatically when the software updates. Regular users will not notice any difference.

95e3f5f94d99ac80eeac8306d46296208263d5bd.text: A hidden safety setting that controls how many premium sessions a limited account gets was raised from 4 to 5. This change was made because a previous reward system was retired, so the old reduced limit is no longer needed. This setting is currently inactive for most accounts, so you will not notice any difference in your daily usage limits today.

c53b6a752b9954bbd96a70f0d3eafd60c350491f.text: The safety check that verifies the desktop app's automated agent still starts with its required greeting was updated to match how the instructions are now written. This change is internal and affects only the testing team. Customers will notice nothing, as the app's behavior remains exactly the same.

871e0ef0f989d23273c778f4b30eb541c6d0deed.text: The command-line tool's version number changed to the next release. This update is live today. Users will see the new number if they check the tool's version.

a8def7f03d62efcc46ff246bb83a69443036aa27.text: The program removed hidden helper instructions for displaying nested assistant messages. This is a minor internal cleanup. You will not notice any change in how the tool looks or works.

f396f4ef37618acc07c9b6c7e461695e3d357e72.text: The daily limit on how much work accounts using Freebucks can do increased. Instead of stopping after three times the value of their Freebucks, the system now allows four times that amount before hitting the cap. Users paying with Freebucks will see this new, higher limit reflected in the message shown when they run out of daily capacity.

7539eacf2a73bfcbfdb5e37cf88fdcc494361cf5.text: When an ad request fails, the system now records a short piece of the error message returned by the ad provider. This helps support staff identify the specific reason for the failure without guessing. The change is active and affects how errors are logged for ad delivery issues.

54ce330ea151686b4a999b1318617b6c6a069644.text: People using the free plan on the command line now see a countdown to when their daily usage limit resets. This matches what the website and desktop app already show. The countdown only appears when the system provides a current time, so it is live today.

ec6003e6dc37caba65b92c4eca3adb7595eca4e3.text: The coding assistant tool received a routine update. People using this tool will see nothing change, as this update only affects how the tool is packaged for distribution.

d3d99f4c5a6e4bc6fbb83c81ea8b7a63cb53e0b4.text: The internal packaging files for the freebuff command-line tool were updated. This is a small technical change that does not affect how the software works. Users will not notice any difference in the tool's behavior or features.

f1654d2c20dcf2cc75a464b7c6707d1cfeef6711.text: The 'Solar Pro 4' model is now marked as standard instead of experimental. Users selecting this model will no longer see warning labels or restricted access indicators. This change is live immediately.

52fa3fb94d1b2957fdefa82afae8158a0ae19cff.text: A small internal update adjusts the project's file visibility rules. It ensures a template for local settings is shared, while hiding personal editor preferences and tool configurations. Team members will notice fewer irrelevant files in their shared workspace.

20289ffb12000c10fd26cd3735849066e963d1cc.text: The system now records a simple reason when an external ad conversion report is rejected because its click identifier is missing, empty, or malformed. This helps internal teams diagnose why reports fail without storing sensitive user data. No visible change for advertisers or users.

8d21e42dbfa0c7509ffc294601a55f9a95a2cd25.text: The message shown when a single chat response uses too much computing power was shortened. Instead of guessing that an assistant got stuck in a loop, it now simply states that the limit for that specific response was reached. This change affects the text seen by users on the web, desktop, and command-line versions of the app.

5454338099733607d45ae7442117bf2879569637.text: The free version for restricted regions now shows GLM 5.3 Flash as the first option instead of DeepSeek V4 Flash. This fixes a problem where people without earned rewards had the first option locked, causing immediate errors when trying to start. The change is live today.

8fafc97b35aa47a8dcea952690e2a8bf115f2da8.text: Muse Spark now waits fifteen seconds before switching to a backup model, up from ten. This extra time lets the system try other access keys before giving up, so fewer requests get routed to the wrong model. The change is live.

f1ebb9710b9ba26d96f19a1cf8e6fb2e2ae71c8b.text: A new internal logging feature was added to track advertiser operations. This change is currently in place but does not yet affect the user experience or produce visible results. It prepares the system to record basic operation details, such as success or failure, without storing sensitive information.

6222be5e6b2164b7dae9ff261d06be5fc88c2b47.text: The text shown when a sponsored task is offered now only says it runs in a separate workspace, removing the warning that it uses your credits. This affects people using the command-line tool who see these offers. If you look at the screen, the cost notice is gone, but running the task still uses your credits.

13c3ba7d0b36a754116bac24f76957a3eebb9f64.text: We added a new tracking label to the system that records how ads are requested. This helps our internal team connect each ad request to its specific decision process, making it easier to troubleshoot issues. You won't see any changes on your screen, as this is a background update for better data organization.

2a92b62f5263e702f76e3a7c3b9f89b29a046710.text: The released package for the tool was updated to the next edition. People who install or update the tool would notice only that the installed package now says it is the newer edition. The change is small and internal, and it is live today.

bb9e8822ea946d45870d09ff2ad8db35f872bbda.text: This internal update clarifies how the system handles two types of credits: permanent earnings and expiring monthly bonuses. Although both appear as a single total number, the system is documented to spend the expiring bonuses first. This change does not alter user experience or functionality; it simply ensures the underlying logic is clearly defined for developers.

d4bc77782d48297b04fb290ea5fb43ca4dae0d37.text: The version number on the command-line tool was increased to mark a new release. This change affects only the packaging metadata and contains no functional updates. If a user checks the tool's details, they will see the new release number, but the tool will behave exactly as it did before.

477a8a0d84c0b6cd3c5181ef0a6498eec2079321.text: The system now separates the data sent when you start a session from the data sent when another session on your account takes over. This internal cleanup ensures the takeover message correctly displays how many desktop sessions are active. You will not notice any changes to how the app works.

6e53c6db1674d4f343f2392092a6f316fa9644fb.text: The app now uses the access level the server assigned, not the one it guessed locally. This prevents menus from claiming a higher plan than the account actually has. The fix is in place, but nothing uses it yet.

23c15cfd4656c6eb305dfe9e4bbab938ebadbed8.text: We added a private log record for when advertisers check their reports. It tracks the advertiser, the report type, the date range, the number of results, and how long it took. This helps us spot slow or failing report requests, but advertisers will not see any change in the interface.

9ede9a4a53b7798cd504493c12aa75323f7a0225.text: Test runs now ignore live rollout switches from the environment, preventing unrelated failures when flags change. This affects internal quality checks, not customers. You would notice no visible change, as this only stabilizes the underlying verification process.

390944fda9461b1401383ef148dfcd844f8d4427.text: The team added automatic checks to verify how the text cursor moves up and down lines in the command-line tool. These tests confirm the cursor stops correctly at the end of short lines and handles edge cases like moving past the first or last line. This is an internal quality improvement; regular users will see no immediate changes in the app's behavior.

2476a76f4dd8eb14dba89d848e676146c839a7e5.text: A small internal update adds a new tracking label to the system that records ad settlement data. This change affects only the backend reporting tools, not the visible interface for advertisers. Since no active reporting logic currently reads this new label, it does nothing yet.

c179bfcc451be624a8bffc032075ba836a5a967b.text: Added internal checks to ensure usage numbers display cleanly. This prevents long, messy decimal errors from appearing in the app. The fix is not live yet, so no one sees a change today.

26f3b123cc05ef5f25fd8b0fe2adf7fbbdeeb691.text: Internal notes on how free promotional ads work were updated to reflect current rules. This change affects only the developers maintaining the advertising system and does not alter what readers see today. The notes clarify that the safety-net ad is turned off by default and that standard limits still apply to campaigns.

e2b7fe5a4ebe36206150cc194cc297fc0c8bd251.text: The ad system now reports the actual tool used to make a request, instead of always guessing it is a standard web browser. This helps advertisers see accurate traffic data, such as distinguishing automated tools from regular browsing. The change is live today and affects how ad impressions are recorded.

8592ea01be0a05c20e0741bc3b1dfe82c4694e7b.text: A new rule prevents a specific temporary folder from being saved to the central code library. This folder holds sensitive, one-time access keys and private customer lists. Staff members will not see any change in their daily work, but the system now automatically blocks these files from being accidentally shared.

3dd1da66d178a91f9d099d3370564ecb00dde3dc.text: The coding tool's label changed from 0.0.163 to 0.0.164. This is a routine update for people who install the tool themselves. You would notice nothing new, as no features were added.

ae136bca432c7f3c74cb18d6c7fda924de2d8a12.text: The internal release number for the command-line tool was updated. This is a routine administrative change. Users will not notice any difference in how the tool works.

2a958f98f5f8c683057d7419feae9093bea14cfb.text: Small internal update ensures one-off card charges show 'FREEBUFF.COM' on bank statements. Advertisers buying placements see this name next to the main company brand. Subscriptions already display this name, so only temporary charges change.

59cca53dfb5bc9c9c03141f91494646de4a40ce3.text: The system stopped permanently assigning specific ad partners to individual accounts, reverting to random selection per request. This internal cleanup removes old tracking labels from data logs. Regular users see no change, while data teams notice these specific labels disappear from reports.

9c1de51074bf984f2827742fffce78a1e7580203.text: A new rule stops the system from saving exported lists of user email addresses into the shared project archive. This change is internal and only affects how the software stores files. Someone looking at the saved project files would notice these email lists are missing from the archive.

d49020039fb91ec4c15dbfeaf70940853e84f5e8.text: The link that connects your account to GitHub now goes to the main account page instead of the old settings page. This affects only people using the command-line tool who have not yet linked GitHub. They will notice the link takes them to a different page when clicked.

d36ecd09839c43b9c0949a8ad83ea5a171cba6bc.text: The system's internal record-keeping for ad placements was updated to track additional timing and error details. This change is currently invisible to all users and advertisers, as it only prepares the data collection framework for future use.

9c2974837d8b90725ae61ebe6ac5c8c7f29ea493.text: Added tests for the command-line timer display. These verify how the timer shows days, hours, minutes, or 'now'. The app itself remains unchanged.

605ba1edc6365594cf457c25adab324cb801d41c.text: The testing system now forces a specific setting to stay on, preventing real-world configuration changes from breaking internal checks. This affects only the automated quality assurance tools used to verify the software's reliability. Customers will notice no difference, as this fix ensures the tests accurately reflect the product's intended behavior without altering the live application.

7266e1b5944dd0a7094a9cbaa49361d470b67c9e.text: A background check now scans the plans page to ensure every subscription model actually exists in the website's catalog. This prevents the page from silently hiding a plan or showing the wrong model if a name is missing. This is an internal safety check, so it does not change what customers see today.

df7e3aa400c51c34ba5185d01ce1527c892a671f.text: The command-line tool now uses a single shared helper to format countdowns. This change removes a redundant wrapper function. You will notice no difference in the text displayed in usage or limit banners.

1312fa1702921f9df8394bf191da9ef062fba043.text: Small internal fix for Freebuff's own promotional banners. The system now correctly displays the standard logo in these ads. This ensures visual consistency across all campaign types, though the change itself is not directly visible to end users.

23c05c4a5fce1db9301b66529c2dd543d51c1e77.text: The system now tracks the cost of actual ad clicks separately from total billed amounts, which may include manual adjustments. This change ensures that performance metrics like cost-per-click are calculated using only the delivery charges, preventing manual back-bills from distorting the data. This is an internal accounting fix that does not yet affect what customers see in their reports.

646e9fe14848ff98d26448d1c90f42422e3dbe8a.text: A single line in the packaging configuration was updated to mark a new release. This internal change does not affect how the tool works. Users will notice no difference in behavior.

179f317de8d228cc02d32ac4730781a8c0aadbc9.text: The command-line tool's internal label updated to mark the latest release. This change affects only the tool itself, not the service it connects to. You will not notice any difference in how the tool works.

d40c36e4aae67b74e3067d4c23a2c1c3db9bf665.text: The assistant's temporary workspace files are now hidden from the main project history. This prevents duplicate records from appearing if someone accidentally saves them. No visible changes will occur for regular users.

7bb5501109a4dd88daf5e262cb1356b7b815b200.text: A small internal fix corrects how progress bars calculate displayed trust scores. This ensures the interface shows realistic numbers instead of negative or excessively large values when a user's score falls outside expected ranges. Users might notice slightly more accurate progress indicators if their score was previously displaying oddly.

1d9a61e734810b53404ced16489971b33109725e.text: A new AI model is now paid on the website but remains free on desktop and command-line apps. The website only sells this model during specific off-peak hours to control costs, closing access during busy times even for subscribers. This applies to website visitors today; other users see no change.

ed224f5a8768b78f3333974446054d71497e4419.text: The command-line tool's internal release count increased by one. This is a routine packaging update for users who install the tool directly. You will notice no new features or changes in behavior.

4e45c27aa823ee8d4a0abe9d493d85479e030149.text: The system now routes requests through an additional backup service. Free users will see a notice that V4 Pro is temporarily answered by V4 Flash while the main provider recovers. This change is live today.

c5e4bf5459e0119e774dbda81d74d89d580f6c6f.text: The app updated the text shown when you start a free session. It now says that limits on specific AI models are gone, while keeping the note that daily session limits still apply. You will see this new message immediately in the chat interface.

f7d35db5a5e064e98c9f12739e68f1583ced9c5d.text: The free daily limit for the GLM 5.3 Flash model changed from tracking total minutes used to counting how many times you start a session. You can now start this specific model twice a day, regardless of how long each session lasts. In the command line tool, the usage counter now explicitly says 'starts' instead of 'used' for this model, while other models still track partial time.

15ebdcb20344b1faa17ff5345846ba1241d3e664.text: The command-line tool now correctly separates the assistant's private reasoning from its final answer, even when the text arrives in uneven chunks. This fixes a bug where a stray closing marker could cause regular text to be hidden inside the reasoning section. Users will see the answer display normally without missing parts. The change is live today.

b42492330322ad9c82caf4620c05e4ab36d661d4.text: The team changed how the system prepares files for checking new features on Linux computers. It now downloads fresh copies every time instead of reusing old saved copies, because tests showed this is faster for that specific setup. This change only affects internal computer checks and is live today; regular customers will not see any difference in how the product works.

75d33f9429a93c53c7c2f5b5dac73adc3a832d32.text: The release record for the coding tool was updated to match its current published version. This is an internal housekeeping step for the packaging process. Customers will notice no change in how the tool behaves.

a4d50e7363432ab28c574b022a0b2fc76de0ab2a.text: The system now records when ads are seen or clicked, but only saves safe details like location and count. This change is not live yet, so no one sees new reports today. It prepares the foundation for future ad performance tracking.

fbda78872046ff7f2223c83c8093d1d1f9237dca.text: A small internal update prevents accidental sharing of sensitive advertiser details. It stops a specific local file containing real identifiers from being uploaded to the shared code repository. No external changes are visible; this purely improves internal data hygiene.

e3a285c926ba174296495a785ca36ed7ea44aad8.text: A hidden safety check inside the command-line tool now strictly verifies the shape of data passed between its internal parts. This change is invisible to anyone using the tool today. It only helps the builders catch mistakes earlier when they write new features.

ff5d55049a4f9d7a0175b82bbc68a7c75c89e811.text: A model moved from a limited plan to unlimited access, changing which row displays usage counters in the command-line interface. The selection menu now correctly centers the remaining paid models and shows their limits without layout errors. This update is internal maintenance; users will not see any visual differences or new features.

29e42653f8ec332f88173a5a05520ff6f8119655.text: The testing system now checks that the block message for VPN users correctly says to connect directly. This ensures the guidance is clear and helpful. No changes affect live users today.

ee79648a9e2aff11d54250c2dd488709b9fb3626.text: Free users can now use GPT-5.6 Luna three times a day instead of two. This applies to everyone using the free tier. You will notice the extra session and see the updated message on the screen.

50aa984b714af271946c68a2ed80466a01338c4e.text: The tool's internal decision-making for handling arrow keys in menus was simplified. This change affects the program's code structure but does not alter how the software behaves. Users will notice no difference in their experience, as all keyboard navigation functions exactly as before.

116f691de944ce3ef91a7e628964eba0b4e6c10d.text: The free service removed separate daily limits for specific AI models. Now all models share one daily session allowance, except two models that remain completely unlimited. Users will notice they can use certain premium models more often than before.

a23c8b25050c3630473d9be4309c3eaa858cde07.text: The software's internal communication method was updated to use a standard, widely supported technique instead of a newer, less common one. This change ensures the assistant works reliably on a broader range of devices and older systems. Users will not notice any difference in performance or features, but the underlying stability improves.

467ba64dca85ea541f5c3db0d34bbf024ccccf92.text: The ad request form now has a new field for the type of device being used. This change is internal and does nothing yet, so users will not notice any difference.

5acb86de2a75b3c0a36e2ce451723bf1e5dece38.text: The program stopped recording tiny details about every keystroke, command, and internal step you take. This change is live today and mostly affects the company's data storage, saving space and money by cutting out unhelpful noise. You will not see or feel any difference while using the tool.

7e9bd8cdb6cb73fb329d494669361e7226a17ed0.text: The system now removes hidden characters and special codes from ad text to prevent them from disguising banned words or breaking displays. This protects reviewers and readers by ensuring ads show exactly what they claim. The change is live today.

a275174b3e37c2e809245dcc06a74e6406b8d8b2.text: The tool's internal label was updated to mark a new release. This change affects only the packaging metadata and does not alter how the tool works or what it does. Users will not notice any difference in their experience.

b563ba5e6b3bf0de5a76a0d72c354ae3db370210.text: A new security marker was added to let our system recognize when an administrator is acting on behalf of another user. This change only applies to internal server communications and does not affect regular users or visible features. The marker is currently in place but does nothing yet until other parts of the system are updated to read it.

09f62ecb291de42ee67f62602f769b8f37c79bfb.text: The guide for checking software reliability was updated to explain how a specific, unpredictable test failure was bypassed by changing the testing method. This internal update affects only the team maintaining the software, not regular customers. They will notice clearer instructions on why some old testing habits still carry hidden risks.

6f9acbfeb578ed83e026547695d86a172b8011fe.text: The tool's release record was updated to the next published release. This is live for people who install or update the assistant tool. They may see a newer release label, but no new behavior is described.

d777cd21617ccc5dd611a59920a609556e577551.text: The free coding tool now has a new release number. This change affects people who install the tool from the official software catalog. They will see the updated version number appear when checking for new releases.

07685661de57b219d53ab908cf2e2bafcdb3e1eb.text: The ad showcase page now shows updated like and reply counts for two example posts, dated August 21, 2026. Visitors see slightly higher numbers for those specific posts. Repost and view counts remain hidden because they require manual copying from X analytics.

657d06d953134758769d273970853bd370e89c3e.text: Advertising campaigns now charge money again after a free period. Advertisers will see their payment methods charged when their ads run. This change is live today.

5baa7a52d32ba2ed115a659fa28eed38a4414cef.text: A small internal note was added to the cost value for free and standard models. It does not affect customers today or change what they see. Someone reading the setting would now see an explanation that each request's charge is recorded in batches, and that setting a cost to zero would stop that recording for that model group.

115a6a5cc676b1a4969d2045ad34ebb5d8bd00ab.text: The signup form now lets people answer only the questions they want and still save their work. Previously, leaving even one question blank caused the whole submission to fail, so their answers were lost. This change is live and prevents that error.

f7bb825f48d23a5e38f2a43748657d567847cd9a.text: The system now automatically hides temporary investigation notes from being saved to the shared project history. This affects only the internal team members who create these quick, one-off checks. They will notice these files no longer appear in the list of changes to review, keeping the main record cleaner.

b21d5ab27d1d97f850e5b3b673d985093136342e.text: The team updated the software's internal label to mark a new release. This change affects only how the system tracks versions, not what the tool actually does. Users will not notice any difference in behavior or features.

55402897958a0f19676f33abeb1432e63ea53ca7.text: The system now automatically ignores local test files containing real customer names and feedback, plus temporary design notes, preventing them from being saved to the public record. This affects internal quality assurance and design teams. They will notice no visible changes in their tools, but sensitive data is now safer from accidental exposure.

01301385919da16daba8bd458609835c69e31a7e.text: Access to the ad placement reporting tool is now controlled by a specific setting rather than a general switch. Advertisers with admin rights can view the tool, but the data shown remains fake until real financial records are linked up.

04e751a97e5f614d12c8165741fdaaf212197531.text: The testing guide now warns that a passing check does not prove a test never failed, as hidden retries can mask intermittent problems. It explains that the real cause often lies in how the app shares background state across screens, meaning fixing the broken screen usually just moves the problem elsewhere. This is internal documentation for the team; customers will notice no changes.

f9ccbec282a4812b8d2e12af28d75395af286030.text: The team updated an internal safety check so that every version of the desktop assistant's instructions is verified to start with the correct opening line. This prevents future updates from accidentally causing the assistant to fail silently when set to automatic mode. This change affects only the development testing process and has no visible impact on current users.

aaf1843ce840d29bf339feae4644adf3df1e06c9.text: The internal team updated a list of temporary files that should stay out of the main project. This prevents accidental clutter from one-off helper scripts that previously slipped into the official records. Regular users will notice no change, as this only affects how the team organizes their work.

9b9b25e76714ba3cfc7fff9a8b13428164cdc2cf.text: A note inside the system told it to look for the desktop helper in the wrong place. This fix points it to the correct spot so the helper is recognized as official. Desktop users will see fewer incorrect security warnings.

fad014c575a497df9a3169fb2bc516281a081a58.text: A leftover unfinished-work note was removed from a shared list of toolkit settings. This affects only the people who maintain the toolkit. Nothing changes in normal use, and no visible behavior changes today.

bdc6b61fb93d720c2e1dbc084046eec16580336f.text: The number of new chat sessions premium members can start on the web and cloud apps was lowered from six to five. This change is active now. Premium users will notice they have one fewer fresh conversation available in these apps, though command-line tools remain unaffected.

65e0d5161681abdcfe1901f2719c1aff43eacf0a.text: A developer added a small internal note to the software's settings area to remind themselves to review it later. This change does not affect how the program works or what features are available. It is strictly for the team's internal organization and has no impact on the end user.

28220d571736520903c8e75cfd41a8588cd5e1a0.text: The system now automatically tracks restricted models to prevent access errors. A new high-performance model was added to the premium list. Premium subscribers can now use this specific new model.

01ea6aba4c679543e05913a5db8faa49937b13c0.text: The system now recognizes a new service called Luminal for tracking spending. This is a small internal update that adds Luminal to the list of supported providers. You won't see any changes in the app today, as this just prepares the system to track costs from Luminal if it is used later.

d2b9697a48a5b058d6648dbe78561f63a88af7b8.text: The internal label for the coding assistant's command-line tool was updated. This is a routine packaging step that does not change how the tool works or what it can do. You will not notice any difference when using it.

095d6d65a1697d4cb31e0a39df9adeafcf7946c2.text: The 'Beta' label was removed from the Freebuff Desktop product description in the English and Simplified Chinese documentation. This affects internal documentation readers. If they looked at the product table, they would see Freebuff Desktop listed without the 'Beta' qualifier.

9175fd397356dbcfa51334ff19281711e7ade0e9.text: Automated checks for the software toolkit now use a fixed placeholder for a specific connection key. This prevents these internal tests from failing on a developer's computer if that key is missing. No live features or customer-facing behavior changed.

6e27bb24543eadf602931a09a003526915b1509c.text: The team added one standard message for accounts that hit a spending limit. This change is not live today, so no one will see it yet. When it goes live, anyone blocked from using the free service will see the same warning, hiding the specific reason for the block.

7db20c99a59d3ee3b410142d90b0f781f3861cc3.text: The command-line tool's internal release marker advanced to the next sequential step. Only people who install the tool from the official package store are affected. They will notice nothing, as this is just a bookkeeping update to prepare the next build.

204d98237e29a1004f52c2d7d6beac9cfbb9f694.text: Some programs send pictures to AI services. Two small fixes make sure the picture address is recognized even if it's written as plain text, and that it doesn't get accidentally wrapped with two conflicting labels. Anyone sending an image this way would have seen a server error before; now the request goes through. This is live in the update.

2daa1edbfdcc1e2b867db89a6ee29cb5b6ac9c8f.text: A developer removed a test that checked how the system handles an old, delayed response arriving after a new user message. This change affects only the internal quality checks and does not alter how the software behaves for anyone today. No users will notice any difference, as this was a cleanup of the testing code.

fc178cb1ef7c7d06ee0bf55e88a7b6415f2cb291.text: The system removed a temporary workaround that let people skip the setup form for 24 hours if saving failed. This internal cleanup only affects the setup screen's error handling logic. Normal users will not notice any change in how the form works.

8057a82e406417ae68791f4ca8e5e26bb812be03.text: The free web app no longer shrinks or fades any model names in its list. This affects people choosing a model there. The one model that previously looked smaller now appears the same size as the others, but it still shows a note saying it has been replaced.

42f9dcb2036fe5685daf5f73da59512789e1f5c8.text: The command-line tool's version number increased. This affects people who install or update the tool. They see a new version number when checking their installation.

4eab91e6da752b9f8269e52018db5854dd9f0fc2.text: This internal update adds a safety check to the model selection list. It ensures the recommended default model always appears first, preventing the display order from becoming outdated if backend settings change. This change does not affect live user features or interface behavior today.

df226b46771c1d64d1f4fd9f7e11e7996e47cba5.text: The system now recognizes new, high-capacity versions of its AI models for internal record-keeping. This does not change what you see or can select today, as these options are hidden from the standard menu. Support staff and automated tools will use this information to manage specific accounts that have been granted extra capacity.

1fca3e29a75dddac2d4b2fc694f8f13a42b51253.text: The system now identifies your typed questions using internal labels instead of adding invisible text markers to your messages. This change affects only the underlying tools that build prompts for the AI. You will not notice any difference in how the application looks or behaves.

7ef9669a46ffdb16f461c281a67ac52e4d3b9560.text: The testing guide now explains why some checks fail randomly depending on which test runs first, rather than due to actual bugs. This helps the testing team spot and fix hidden issues in the browser simulation setup. No customer-facing features change; this is an internal documentation update.

5f8f4c0129f21df6161929ca0031ce67b2ccd141.text: The command-line tool's internal version label updated from 0.0.143 to 0.0.145. This change affects only the packaging metadata, not the tool's actual behavior. Users installing the latest version will see the new label, but the tool will function exactly as it did before.

9c97c4b81c451b11472f72068b175d485a9512a8.text: A small internal fix ensures that background waiting timers are always cancelled, whether a task finishes normally or times out. This prevents the system from holding onto unused resources, which could otherwise slow down performance over time. Regular users will not see any visible changes to the interface.

58e2564ab07e029b066e81765e85b4be189b303e.text: The tool removed three specific artificial intelligence models from its menu of choices. This change is live now. Users will see these options disappear from the list, and any saved settings using them will need to switch to a supported model.

c1ff21d02571b1a923041ad489802f64a1514bca.text: A new optional data field was added to the pre-join session response to provide account access levels and current limits. This change is internal and currently does nothing, as no client code has been updated to read or display the new field.

d0a5d3f4e4a0caaee723ea2e10499a9c3b64b0fc.text: The software's internal label changed to mark a new release. This is a small administrative update that does not change how the tool works or what it can do. You would notice nothing different when using the program.

9d25b4958aa958f70db200e3cbde351f54538ffd.text: The internal safety check for the desktop assistant's setup instructions was updated to match a recent change in how those instructions are assembled. This is a technical maintenance task for the software's quality assurance system. Users will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves or responds.

c6d10a5bff56b7a83bd09e507bc5adc2a373c8dc.text: The privacy section now includes a clear answer about data collection. It explains that the service is free because it shows ads, and that your files or chats are not collected by this service unless the specific AI model provider does so. This clarification currently applies only when using DeepSeek models.

b615f928ac3c3d888c5e82b21fdd768e8d7e941e.text: The coding tool's release label increased by one step. This only updates the version stamp people see when checking the tool's details. No new features or fixes arrived with this bump.

5db7bafe633f286ebf8cb91d151d557ce8df3db1.text: A background safety check was updated to match a recent name change and to stop checking a specific size limit that no longer applies. These adjustments only affect internal testing tools. Regular users will notice no changes in how the software behaves.

4f80bdb45dcca5ab6c33304482b9699356711a0e.text: The team updated internal notes to explain that a small group of early test users did not accurately represent the whole population. This clarification confirms that a specific detection rule remains in observation mode and will not block or penalize accounts based on that initial sample. No customer-facing features changed.

119af4afe0f2529ce76714ac740c1db1cb8940fc.text: Two hidden test connections to a new AI model were removed from the system. This change only affects internal testing setups and does not impact standard users. Because these connections were never active for the public, no one will notice any difference in the application's behavior.

7ca8fa441715fb750cbaac2bb834a4b544c42313.text: The team updated their testing guide to explain how they now handle slow setup steps in their automated checks. This change affects only the developers who write and run these internal tests. If they looked at the documentation, they would see new rules for giving extra time to tests that create temporary data, preventing false alarms when a computer is busy.

caba427c7fed797dd58e2cd6cc5a22232a5eeaea.text: Muse Spark now always uses high reasoning effort. This setting was present but ignored because the lookup missed web-only models. Users of Muse Spark will see more consistent reasoning depth, and the change is live today.

e39fb73424f48f7861215b6d67b095c21885f9ee.text: The assistant's default thinking level for Muse Spark increased slightly, trading a bit of speed for depth. This applies to all Muse Spark requests. Users might notice responses take about 26% longer, with no visible change in answer quality.

968c6682de8ea3e75d3dbbad2c6591fe28176920.text: A small internal check now waits for a background test to confirm it finished before ending, rather than guessing how long to wait. This prevents false failures during automated checks. Regular users see no difference.

8d95d803aedf841503be0f60718ed8374e492b5c.text: The website now quietly records extra details when a visitor clicks the download button after using the savings calculator. This data includes the specific dollar amount and number of tools they were looking at during that click. Visitors see no change, but the business can now check if showing a bigger savings number actually leads to more downloads.

2bc664c5bd3c5ed730de2a5af880493d2c5d672c.text: The system now separates the usage records for the new desktop assistant from the older version. This change is internal and invisible to you. It lets the team track costs and performance for the new rollout without mixing the data together.

c26a74d54c7b2ff0429b410b0109aa0115f29c6f.text: The promotional message in the command-line interface was shortened to focus on earning bounties and spending daily sessions. The expiration date now appears in a smaller, dimmer font at the end of the line. Only people who see this specific banner will notice the text is less cluttered.

070db75b0429851b103a870004b5029c4cd5700e.text: The assistant now suggests clickable follow-up actions that focus on the desired outcome rather than listing specific steps or file names. This change applies to all conversations with the assistant. Users will notice that suggested next steps are shorter and more clearly state the goal, leaving the assistant free to choose the best method to achieve it.

51994660ab6530ff0764978a8241ed2b80fa1d30.text: A check that makes sure a crashed program can still clean up the screen was made stricter. It now waits longer on Windows and only passes if the exact cleanup message appears, not just any text. This is only an internal test change, so it is not live and users would notice nothing.

787e80a8f1456623d2b0605c9f282165ac72dcb7.text: The team updated the version label for the command-line tool's release package. This change only affects how the software is packaged and distributed, not how it works. Users will notice nothing different in the tool's behavior.

f392d93770b49c7399c49afd550a4d2783c37afd.text: The tool's release label changed from one number to the next. This update is for the software package itself. You would not notice any difference in how the tool works.

6110b0bbfbe668dffcf4d5fe86ce8147293bf73a.text: A specific model's memory limit was removed. If you use that model, it now follows the default limit. You might see shorter chats before a reset.

27caf8248eaf3be6e303a93b58e27529e2008630.text: The assistant now knows how much text the Muse Spark 1.2 model can handle, so it uses that model's full capacity instead of a smaller, default limit. This affects only the internal chat system, not the public interface. A user would notice nothing, as this is a small internal fix to ensure the model works correctly.

175191e4366e34542cfe2d7dfdd9162faf7c2361.text: The public guide no longer lists the custom organization option. This affects people looking for that specific service. They will see it missing from the product list.

1358346295e7e4fcd7b2bd3d4fa93b268518b28d.text: The software now tracks when a bookmark prompt appears and when a user accepts it. This affects people using web or cloud workspaces, but they will not see any change. The tracking is in place but does nothing yet.

52804281c6e03e0c74bbd7eb6b9965d369a5cf15.text: A small internal update allows a specific new AI model to read and remember much longer conversations without cutting off early. This affects only the assistant when using that particular model. You would notice it can handle very long documents or chats in one go, instead of forgetting the beginning.

2368b27e2d8a3b5f98f3e242083ba4a59dc0e0e2.text: The download label for the command-line assistant was updated to the next scheduled release number. This is a small internal packaging step and happens automatically. A person installing the tool would see no change in how it works, only that the version number on the download page is slightly higher.

f831624f857d2174a4f72a594f53e8cdec65e528.text: A small internal fix prevents a specific automated test from timing out when a tool fails to shut down correctly. This change does not affect the software that runs on your computer, but it ensures the test can now catch and report shutdown errors more reliably.

218d2266be52bd7c37ca12f32c07766f8f7c267b.text: The platform's internal list of available free assistants was updated to include two new options: Greg 2 Ultra and Greg 2 Super. This change is currently in place but does nothing yet, as the tools that let you select these assistants have not been updated to show them.

afe8c7918cdd600f464fe453e1c4382eea7061e1.text: The company's main web page now highlights only the free coding assistant. Visitors will no longer see the paid version or its performance claims. This update is live today.

9c3d9f0caebc6cd1ad214b92a7440fd0ff1cf929.text: The coding assistant tool updated its internal label. This only affects the specific program that helps people write code. Regular users will notice no change at all.

a6571b01b1383c6806b1344375d38525846701ac.text: The cloud service is now marked as fully available instead of a test version on the main help pages. A new contact option for large organizations was added, and the system now tracks when someone submits that form to help sort incoming requests by company size.

04d4379f1617e48948e10d522ee2688dd9b84942.text: Fixed a bug where the file browser might hide or show wrong files when projects use nested ignore rules. This affects people viewing project files. You might notice previously hidden files now appear, or vice versa, matching your ignore settings exactly.

c799255a7afc9de583e6fed26712c5a5ec2c48fd.text: New web users now get a smarter default assistant, which helps with complex browser tasks and removes a data-training warning. This applies to new web accounts, not existing ones or desktop users. If the free daily limit for this better assistant runs out, the system automatically switches to a backup model to keep things working.

037b51122b8b627807b9f138f7fffa16b0a6fe65.text: A new tracking signal was added to record when people click the download buttons for the desktop application. This data will help the team see which buttons are most popular and if users are clicking twice because they think the first click didn't work. Nothing changes for you today; this is just a note being made behind the scenes to help improve the site later.

eeb5209f0d72ca408c7decfcbac295cf21d06cea.text: The 'base2-free-fable' assistant now uses the Fable model for its own code reviews, instead of falling back to a cheaper model. This change is live and ensures that the review step matches the main model's capabilities. Users of this specific assistant will notice that the review process now aligns with the session's primary model, preventing mismatches.

e4a3a7abe1a6db3cdb1a3ff7ad5bae9737e48fa3.text: A small internal update adds a 30-minute grace period after a session expires. During this window, the system allows ongoing tasks to finish but blocks new requests, helping it distinguish between active work and closed tabs. This change is currently just a rule added to the code and does not affect what you see or do yet.

7baf11ac08f12726408167fd391367d461a96249.text: The system now separates slow connection checks from quick basic checks. Developers running standard tests will no longer wait for external services. This speeds up daily work without changing what the software actually does for end users.

81bb087616c1eebb0516d8c74562cd6c4cd3cdbf.text: Added 37 specific email domains to the blocklist. New sign-ups using these domains will be rejected. Existing accounts remain unaffected.

a0d5b7f05d51dd5c0638193e6bff94151af278ee.text: Added three email domains to the blocklist to stop fake accounts. This is live now. Regular users will not notice a change.

542451446bb2086182f9a10dfd9dc56cece4c133.text: The chat assistant can now stop a response mid-sentence if the user clicks stop. This small fix connects the stop button to the text stream so it actually works. The change is live today.

4e2403d6d910b7b0f6566d1eba3bfb35d4fb0aaa.text: This update adds a test to ensure the switch-to-Flash notification appears only on the currently selected older model. It prevents the list from repeating the same advice on every row. This change is internal and does not affect the live software behavior.

33d6139537ac60f9e475e9ff4211498fd9f65c73.text: The release package for the coding assistant was updated to a new version. This change affects the software's distribution mechanism. Users will not notice any visual or functional differences, as this is an internal update to the package metadata.

a03e7a8ef057c6b8e9b3c63592e96ab176ea479d.text: The tool's internal label updated to its latest release. This change affects only the software's distribution metadata. Users will notice no difference in behavior.

115d80be38b93542912a3bb3cb0ed85f67f48290.text: The team updated internal guidelines on how test failures are handled. Unit tests now fail immediately if they pass only after a retry, while integration tests just show a warning. This affects the team writing tests, who will see stricter rules in the documentation.

2ae66743c3896cfb8f44812cf9643807c513fd59.text: A new guide explains how to keep tests from interfering with each other on the same computer. It also sets rules for how long checks should wait, ensuring errors point to the right problem. This is internal documentation for the team, so no customers will see any changes.

cc568bb92ddf1d15ac7be8b35e078a80670a6563.text: The assistant now recognizes a specific model can hold far more conversation history than it previously assumed. This change takes effect immediately. People using that model will see the assistant remember more context and avoid rewriting past chats unnecessarily.

66199cc009297b239aa41cf46b945195a7a528a6.text: The free coding assistant tool received a minor routine update today. This change simply marks the new release version for the software package. Users will not notice any difference in how the tool works or looks.

2de7fe6b96aee8b402f989d9b1456d7e4f1259eb.text: The command-line tool was repackaged with a newer release label. It affects people who install or update the tool from its usual place. They would see the newer label in the install listing, but nothing about the tool’s behavior changes. It is live today for that install path.

24c1a306f8c6654c7412241acd117c8074af5831.text: The app’s privacy notice text was shortened by removing specific lists of restricted actions. This change applies to all users of the service. If you read the notice, you will see a simpler summary that mentions ad personalization and AI training limits but no longer details account or location rules.

76d27eac43c54991622be0ff4b8eae09ee27183f.text: The tool's internal label was updated to its newest number. This change affects only the packaging metadata for the command-line tool. Users will not notice any difference in behavior or appearance.

f8a40d8bdea49062791c965233871dac46f9505d.text: The command-line tool's internal version label was updated. This is a routine housekeeping task for the software maintainers. Regular users will notice no changes in how the tool works or appears.

fe2f293cfec04f7effa3601e4719d8d5583b81a2.text: The AI assistant now uses universal file commands on Windows instead of system-specific ones. This prevents errors when managing files, as the old method often corrupted folder paths. Users will notice fewer failed tasks when the assistant tries to move or delete files on Windows.

159673adf8f8dd060344460862f309b21986134f.text: The short descriptions next to three AI models in the selection menu were updated. MiMo 2.5 Pro is now labeled 'Smart & Slow', MiMo 2.5 is 'Balanced', and MiniMax M3 is 'Fastest'. This change is live and affects how these models are described in the app's interface.

b81352e298d504578da3e408754a0274dbcbacd2.text: The team added a new label to track how often the app cleans up old, unused workspace folders on desktop computers. This change does not affect how the app works or what you see on your screen. It simply helps the developers understand when this cleanup happens so they can improve performance later.

2a8c8af1fba063ed768cafb0e9585b8f560a25fe.text: The testing guide now warns that saved test counts go stale, and a real case showed 307 missing tests passed unnoticed. It also added an automatic warning whenever a test only passes after being retried, so flaky checks are flagged instead of hidden. This affects the team maintaining the project's test setup; they would see new caution notes and warning labels on test runs.

4fa56551886ce92ff07d05bc42107ed53ae03a5f.text: Two new tracking labels were added to the desktop application's internal list. These labels are designed to record when a user turns automatic execution on or off, or changes its scope. The change is not live today; the application does not yet send these labels, so no user behavior is currently being recorded.

b15fef86116ef07524649f8b6ffd5027e0bee774.text: The internal label for the command-line assistant updated to mark a new release. This affects people who install the tool, but they will not notice any difference in how it works.

326a33d9c24c462f1640172b775db7a368e84e56.text: The AI assistant now writes shorter, clearer summaries when confirming your cloud plan. Technical details moved to a separate section, so the overview stays simple. This applies to users creating cloud plans and is live today.

860318a19c3c2bd12795963a2e50917ca79e0ba5.text: A guide for the software team now explains how to prevent a specific error where multiple checks running at once fight over the same temporary files. This internal update only affects developers working on the command-line tool locally, as automated systems already avoided the issue. No visible changes appear in the software for regular users.

1499a9d866f9946dca7209a07323b0c4b501c60b.text: The assistant no longer checks for duplicate answers when you retry a failed task. This affects only people using the assistant's external connection to run tasks. If a retry sends the same answer twice, the system might now reject the whole conversation instead of ignoring the extra copy.

cb153c1518104ed5254b2189f9dd5d5794600fef.text: The app now records how busy its main background process is. This helps engineers see if slow tab opening is caused by the app's own computer or the remote server. You will not notice any change yet.

a74c20dc1479774fddf8507f9d9d4ca9e7b6d8f9.text: The team added internal instructions explaining how to deliberately stress-test software to uncover hidden timing bugs. This documentation helps engineers fix rare glitches where tests pass on a quiet computer but fail on a busy one. Regular users will not notice this change, as it only updates the team's internal reference guide.

977abd5ce06611d6fe900d31310c581dfcd95291.text: The instructions for running automated checks were updated to explain how the process was sped up by letting tasks run in parallel. This change affects only the internal team and is not visible to customers. The documentation now warns that certain setup errors can pass unnoticed, so the team must manually verify that all parts of the system are still being checked.

d00f185a4d65a008126a1fbe4e4516fbf003414d.text: The app stopped sending an old, unused report about how ads were placed on the desktop screen. This cleanup happened because the system now places ads differently. You will see no change in how ads appear or work; only the internal tracking data stops collecting this specific, outdated detail.

a6064e62018ea29f9349570ff051500030870c1d.text: The app now knows how to record when you delete a project from your desktop. This small update is live, but it only sets up the tracking system; nothing happens yet until other parts of the app start using it. You won't notice any changes in how the app works.

84b194f1de686f37ab0e471ed617e9aa9ecdb61d.text: The feedback system can now recognize desktop applications as a source. It also has new optional fields to record the app version and operating system. These fields are in place but do nothing yet until the desktop app starts sending this information.

23bcdc85d8b5bee8a0e5c41da85a4fd00a56028e.text: The business now has a way to track when people sign up or start using the service through affiliate links. This change only adds the tracking labels to the system's list; it does not turn on the tracking itself. Nothing will appear in reports or change for anyone until the team connects these labels to the actual user actions.

1614c75f6c19c5cd6ee24e0fab2d21382e012e0c.text: The assistant now uses one universal command style for all computers, replacing the old system that tried to guess which style to use. This prevents a specific error on Windows where the assistant accidentally created undeletable junk files while trying to hide command output. Users will notice fewer failed tasks and less clutter in their folders.

2d0defa35f3f84fc905fcc5fd0d677726ff4d32b.text: A new AI model was added to the list of options available for custom assistants. This change is internal and does not yet appear in the user interface. No visible changes occur for end users today.

9960f1f7021572ab6422137dd38830ec6587af47.text: The planning tool now includes a spot to list which external services need special login keys. This helps the builder know exactly what access to request before starting work. The change is internal and not visible to end users today.

7427361383f2c51d58977ea9a80d8c0daab82016.text: The packaging metadata for the freebuff command-line tool was updated to reflect a new version number. This change affects only the internal label used when installing or checking the tool's version. People using the tool will not notice any difference in behavior or features.

68d2a1c12fcf666d7d4d067a3f00e5953afebd34.text: The assistant now stops after calling one 'thinker' helper for a single request. This applies to all subscription plans. You might notice slightly faster answers because the system avoids asking the same helper twice for no reason. This change is active today.

6238261f2378f06c8e96ce1a0691da31374011e0.text: The internal version number for the command-line tool was incremented to mark a new release package. This is a housekeeping update for the software's packaging system. Nothing changes for the person using the tool; the interface and features remain exactly as they were before.

2da904013fda20a132f41b21f969630331485b9e.text: The coding assistant's internal version number increased. This affects only the tool's metadata. Users would not notice any change in the tool's behavior.

f9e4f6d7dec93b1e1e1ff3f7cb5f4e81966e1ac6.text: The software's internal label was updated to mark a new release. This change is only for people who install the tool directly from the software package repository. They will see the new label appear in their installation list, but the tool's features remain exactly the same.

3dc5a86f835786fcd0a763eb9fd027c58e732ba5.text: The system now has a place to store specific settings for connecting to a new web service. This is an internal setup step. Regular users will see no changes today.

f832b44401fb12895cc2023f6e4daf776f7edd74.text: A small internal update removed an unused text field from the application's background settings. This change does not affect the user interface or any visible features, so users will notice no difference.

95d0fd6d9160780a76fe40fd4f79bb21858f0d91.text: The chat assistant can now show clickable buttons to guide you through setup. This feature is live for chat users. The change also fixes a bug where service recommendations might link to the wrong provider.

658e06ca341886f3236ee04d99506989158b8632.text: The testing setup now includes a placeholder for a new security key. This only helps the internal checks that ensure the software works correctly. Regular users will not notice any difference today.

f306a65c7959b621b722d98e361dedf64a575a88.text: The assistant can now offer follow-up questions without automatically moving the conversation to the next stage. This applies to users who see these suggestions. You would notice the chat pausing for your input instead of proceeding on its own.

0b0023ff8767b3d84e2b2b09dbeb4942bdaeac8f.text: The software's internal release counter increased to mark a new build. This change affects only the packaging system, not the actual features. A regular user would notice nothing different when running the program today.

b3680bc95f78bcedbcb5b13ae1b18a4f4bb2aa8e.text: The minimum window height needed to show the streak bonus graphic was lowered from 52 to 30. This small internal adjustment applies only to the command-line interface. Users with shorter terminal windows will now see the streak bonus visual where it previously remained hidden.

fd7faf65bf78df2e9a52f592853b2ee7e2ead054.text: When the AI edits files, it now reads the entire file before making changes. This fixes errors where edits to lower parts of large files failed because the AI only saw the top section. Normal file viewing for humans remains unchanged.

8b1e3056a8678ddbcd1f18cf505017accb927cfd.text: The assistant's connection to external services was updated to a newer version. The way the system identifies and handles failed requests was simplified to match this update. This is an internal maintenance task. No visible changes to the assistant's behavior.

ace6dfaa46c3c14d6ce640c5146a1110df23d57f.text: The AI assistant's internal instructions were reordered to emphasize working on multiple tasks at once before setting limits on complex thinking steps. This change affects how the assistant plans its work behind the scenes, but you will not notice any immediate difference in its responses or speed today.

ececbb77e5428cdaca12b67e331952f67b7fe267.text: The free coding assistant's installation package received a routine version update. This change affects only the internal packaging metadata, so users will not notice any new features or visible changes in the application.

9db53d4c2136be67ada35d5716835b1bdb6fa07d.text: The desktop app now tags each conversation with a specific label depending on whether it runs locally or in a separate workspace. This helps the system track usage and cache data accurately for these different modes. Older versions of the app still work, but new versions use these distinct labels. Users won't notice a visual change, but the app's internal tracking becomes more precise.

c26e125f40313cb18757411f71954c23c3b1cf5f.text: The small advertisement boxes that appear inside the command-line interface now use two lines of text instead of one. The top line shows the ad title and a clear 'Ad' label, while the bottom line shows the description and the website link. This layout change is live today and makes the ads easier to read, especially when the window is wide enough to show the full link.

1de3f90a35a3cdef2dd3c3cbaee5d8dee637889e.text: The freebuff command-line tool was updated to a new version. This affects only people who install or use the freebuff tool from the command line. They will notice a new version number appears when checking the tool's information, with no change to how the tool works.

b01c3662b93cb30efaf48dd1e2581326fc8a31f4.text: Freebuff Web users outside the supported regions can now create three projects per day, up from one. The daily limit resets at midnight Pacific time. This change is live today.

af893569c95a1986af346b999206f467f2729e53.text: The desktop app now keeps its own private working files in a hidden folder, preventing the shared project folder from getting cluttered with temporary data. This applies to anyone using the desktop version. You will not see any difference in how the app works.

081bdb229790aa903da4ba4462827ba867139ff3.text: The border around the referral banner in the command-line tool changed from a bright primary color to a softer, muted color. This visual update is live for anyone using the tool today. You will notice the banner blends in more with the rest of the interface instead of standing out sharply.
