75c94becef9f223a3266bab4840d4594ae3e8fe8.text: The system now decides where to place the first advertisement separately from the spacing of later ones. This adjustment applies to the command-line tool and shared interfaces. A person using the tool would see the first ad appear after two text blocks, with subsequent ads spaced three blocks apart.

633c256122a18c49ab89171fbcf977a4370c4658.text: The command-line tool now stops sending a default 'chat' label for ads if the caller does not specify one. This affects only ad requests made through the tool. If you inspect the network traffic, the 'surface' field will be absent from the request body when no value is provided, rather than appearing as 'chat'.

185d51ce8b38a5b87b260ff2abd8c5e62afd08e4.text: The release process updated the program's internal label to the latest number. This change is for the software's own tracking system and affects only how the tool identifies itself during installation. A person using the tool would notice nothing different in its behavior or appearance.

6ab789012e6e8f3f43e22246828cb88f0c7a0a80.text: The system now recognizes a paid version of the Tencent HY3 AI model, alongside the existing free version. This is an internal setup step; the paid option is not yet visible or selectable in the interface. Users will notice no change until this model is explicitly added to the menu.

9e48fc62b994946fb6f5412439bc458c0c222904.text: The web assistant's menu now includes a new coding model called KAT Coder Pro V2, which is marked as a premium option. This change is live today. Existing users will also notice that the previously free HY3 model is now premium, with its description updated to indicate it is being tested for performance.

25bcff7a78ced153e5d55e161619e48ffdb74ddb.text: A new tracking label was added to record when visitors copy the setup command on the command-line tool's landing page. This helps measure how many people intend to install the tool based on where they clicked. The change is live today.

05e61796b1e972e04d7ab08ff3ec77fa2d6808ce.text: A small internal fix helps the assistant better measure how much text is in a conversation when using the command-line tool. Before, this measurement often failed for people who did not have a specific setting enabled, forcing the system to use a less accurate guess. Now, the system correctly uses its main method to count text, so the assistant can manage long conversations more precisely.

0fbf0d3b2edb429bb9f489b15af7022062d7e7ec.text: Free-tier users of this specific AI assistant can now choose a new model option. For one of the assistant's background helpers, a setting exists to disable its built-in web search tool, though this setting is not active for you yet.

6e2ec2feb080513c017c65cf5f6aaff9ca564a2e.text: The software toolkit now includes a way to check skill files without saving them to the computer's storage. This helps developers test these files more easily. It does not change how the final product works for regular users.

d0b938bca49fdf28e96d4a4079bcf350946b2f6f.text: The coding assistant's guidelines were merged into a single, shorter list, and an unused setting was deleted. Users on the free plan will see the assistant call itself by the free product's name, while certain modes now prompt it to show its reasoning. The update is live and changes how the assistant phrases its identity and thought process.

4fe98d8c048b271a57a32a41c6e79a114f39cb93.text: The internal label for the free coding tool was updated to its next number. This is a small administrative step that does not change how the tool works or what it can do. People using the tool will not notice any difference in its behavior.

48803a249a48035e7f3c3041d5f704b233720a4c.text: A small fix stops hidden background tasks from messing up the screen on Windows. People using the assistant on Windows who run commands will no longer see random symbols like ^[[I^[[<35;12;7M painted over their interface. This change is live today.

fe1d484e63713352e7fa5bbc033a1171fbed39c7.text: The command-line tool now allows external programs or tests to point chat logs and debug traces to custom storage locations instead of the default project folder. This change affects only tools that interact with the system programmatically; regular users will see no difference in their experience. It is live today for those specific integrations.

04d67d73b9052e63dead5ad1a6cf6bbe76c4cd2e.text: The Kimi AI model has been removed from the list of free options available in the application. If you try to select Kimi from the default free model picker, you will no longer see it as an option. This change is live now and affects all interfaces, including the web, desktop, and command-line tools.

22aa19aade611c31aff555cc55f280c653910fe7.text: The internal address lookup logic was simplified to prevent a specific error. This change is invisible to end users but ensures the software connects to the correct server when hosted remotely.

3966fa98790b1983323c0e71526c781353ab17ea.text: The AI model called Kimi is no longer shown in the list you browse to pick a model. If you had already chosen Kimi in a previous conversation, the app still lets you use it. This change only updates the safety checks to match that behavior and does not affect how the app runs today.

afc82b86ff83681ec1cf4e282c9cf930f7806eac.text: The release label was updated to mark a new version of the coding assistant. This is an internal packaging step that does not change how the tool works or what it can do. You will not notice any difference in your daily use.

fd36250a7af2416544869fa2694916edfd81b6d2.text: A small internal update helps the system check for errors more reliably without needing an extra setup step. This change affects only the automated checks used by the team, not the features available to customers. You would not notice any difference in how the app works.

30819406bcc40a132d363f3ac2bceb285ad06031.text: The program now allows its internal decision-making tools to check if a specific account is connected without looking at the actual account status directly. This helps the program run tests more reliably by letting those tools pretend an account is connected or disconnected. Users will not notice any changes in how the program works today.

e8a95a27ac79ae26a56a5fa8d8e9904471ec4423.text: The system now skips an extra online check for counting text length when using the free version. This removes a small wait time between steps for free users, making responses appear slightly faster. Paid users keep the previous accurate counting method, so their experience does not change.

4ea700cd6ebb12e204b37095f477a2e8fd5955b5.text: The app now has a built-in label to record when desktop users click 'send now' in their message queue. This change only prepares the system to collect that data; the actual tracking is not active yet. Users will not see any difference in the interface today.

bfaad48713d14b4e948a6ad49a2c6f79d6cb250c.text: The system now records when a friend's invite code fails due to strict rules, like the account being too old or the person being banned. It also notes when the new user shares a device with the referrer, which helps identify fraud without blocking legitimate users. This change is live and helps support teams diagnose why an invite didn't work.

f67bb803bda67f875fd14647d3f3458e56e732fb.text: The system now uses a safer method to load custom assistant instructions. This internal update prevents errors when the assistant starts a new task. Users will not see any visual changes or new features from this update.

79127c26ba4d555c14ad85e5f16539447f4a81b8.text: The desktop app now uses one shared label to track all free sessions, instead of a separate label for each model. This change is internal and does nothing yet, as the rest of the system has not been updated to use it.

b5b0f9c223124e9746e9faa8d3d5e96978262dc9.text: The command-line tool's internal label changed to the next number in its sequence. This is a housekeeping step that keeps the software organized and helps track which version is running. People using the tool will not notice any difference in how it works or looks.

e90202304629a44f84287728ac07d150354508a2.text: The Minimax M3 AI model now appears at the top of the free model list. This change affects all free users on the web, desktop, and command line. You will see Minimax M3 as the first option when choosing a free model, replacing DeepSeek V4 Pro.

304f8c16ed581066ab94ad28f4f3d6ab3642865f.text: In free mode, a new 'skip review' setting now stops the assistant from running a separate code-checking step, only performing basic error and test checks instead. This change is live today but only applies when the setting is explicitly turned on. Users will notice the assistant finishing tasks slightly faster, though it may miss deeper logic errors that the skipped step would have caught.

1576d8cceceddde2310b475e1dbe0f0f0add67d5.text: The waiting period for a new GitHub account to qualify for referral rewards is now four months for all products. Previously, some tools required a twelve-month wait. People with accounts between four and twelve months old can now earn rewards immediately.

6937a4a1d869a5d878d178a2c3b57d4ae6f75562.text: The desktop app now records when a conversation's title changes. This adds a new data point for internal reporting but causes no visible change for users.

90210bb6a19dd9ee6bdc4f322668619399caa166.text: The command-line tool now records the user's account tier when sending messages, defaulting to 'unknown' if missing. This applies only to the Freebuff command-line interface. Users will not notice any difference in how the tool works.

3f6c218fcf769874ed0dbdd7ffac50e3294db19e.text: The command-line tool now recognizes a specific 'premium slot taken' response and stops trying to calculate a retry delay for it. This affects CLI users encountering premium slot contention. They might see the tool handle this case more gracefully without invalid delay calculations.

00b24d0ffa5d006b4e9d830de87f5df772cbcc8e.text: The software's internal safety checks were updated to expect the 'lite' assistant to use MiniMax M3 instead of DeepSeek V4 Flash. This is a behind-the-scenes verification change that does not affect how the assistant works for users today. You will not notice any difference.

82827cafd83ff35bc18530e2729ccf86ee4497f4.text: The internal label for the command-line tool was updated to mark a new release. This change is invisible to users; they will not notice any difference in how the tool behaves or looks.

03843a6a7999022e6a7cb133ae6a3d5e8bd851f5.text: The system now enforces two new rules for the referral program: you can only claim credit for people who signed up within the last 30 days, and a single referrer is capped at 100 total referrals. This prevents people from claiming credit for accounts that existed long before they joined or from spamming the system with fake signups. These limits are active now.

fe8de7d67497f25e3d80567e07554ae28a82a6e0.text: The internal label used to track software updates was incremented. This change is invisible to end users and does not add new features or fix bugs. It only affects the automated systems that manage the software's distribution.

d1fb7fdf239e8a306f7d31a19fd4de4fa4ab58e0.text: The chat assistant now suggests three follow-up questions after each response. Users will see clickable cards with short titles and full questions tailored to the conversation, making it easier to continue chatting. This change is live for the Freebuff Chat agent.

6e063e113c757309a151e1c78b52ebca7a12c0e6.text: The system now checks the type of network connection to tell the difference between regular internet providers and anonymous proxy services. This change helps ensure that ordinary people using standard home or work networks are not mistakenly blocked as suspicious. The new logic is currently in place but does not affect any live features yet.

bf6d1e5e2016e11d155092e0e93ad17493db7a12.text: The app's internal version tag increased by one step. This change does not affect how the app looks or works today. It is just a small bookkeeping update for the software's release history.

2cb4fc339e109217ef4fba773241100ee66680f0.text: The program now requires a one-year-old account to qualify for referral rewards, replacing the previous four-month rule for web signups. It also limits the daily bonus sessions earned from qualifying referrals to three per day. These rules are currently just definitions in the system and do not yet affect live behavior.

637bdf14fa0443c9539f6550eeb64ae129fb55c6.text: The command-line tool now quietly records every message a user sends, but only for the Freebuff version. This lets the company count daily active users accurately without guessing from partial data. Users see no change on their screen; the tool just sends a usage signal in the background.

0b97b6efd524e5044a6c7b31e20a7a748326feff.text: The internal tracking number for the free coding assistant tool was updated. This change affects only the software's installation package. You would not notice anything different, as no new features were added.

3c9348e961a86ace862cbc3c379eb2c2cb4fc703.text: Automated checks that run the full product against live services now stay off by default and only run when someone explicitly turns them on and provides a key. This affects the people who run the tests, not the people who use the product. They would notice fewer surprise failures from these checks, and the checks only run live when they choose to.

6e8e17d890d006bf4ee5a2545d18ed9fac02f01e.text: The team added tracking points to measure how people move through the sign-up process after clicking a friend's referral link. This change is internal, so you will not see any difference in how the app looks or works.

feb051debac2365daf253d424385b6c6e57ec64a.text: The team updated the underlying software that runs the application's background processes. This is a small, internal maintenance task. Regular users will not notice any changes to the application's appearance or behavior.

edacbeb3609c311a58aac127c5264255149302df.text: The company updated its legal ownership name to Freebuff in the software's license text. They also cleaned up old name references in internal testing data. Regular users will not see any changes in how the app works, but anyone checking the license file will now see the new company name.

ff16426abdc93feb759df1e90f94539e877a07ca.text: The internal label for the command-line tool was updated to mark a new release. This change is invisible to people using the software, as it only helps the system track which version is installed.

a64b9c03fd75cad359bf64f3c82b1bc7651a2bc4.text: The system now automatically records when a user redeems a referral, completes the process, and the results of periodic checks on pending referrals. This change is for the internal team to track the success of the referral program. Regular users will not notice any difference in their experience.

747abe3c717770a91c955c6e004da6e4154eb159.text: The release label for the coding tool changed. This only affects how the software is packaged and tracked. A person would notice nothing different when using the tool.

de1f1f716ab020ce631b126794f4de1a48daa13f.text: Daily limits for ordinary and higher-quality responses were increased across all referral levels. People who have reached a referral level would notice they can get more responses in a day before hitting the limit. This is a small change and is live today.

cd4e11ce2c5b9b4f3a216ab5c0f02dcfeac333e3.text: The suggestion list in the chat window now appears at the top of the screen instead of near the text input box. These suggestions are hidden if you are viewing a past conversation or if your free trial has ended. This change is live now for people using the command-line tool.

43d2681d423104d649f6809fe00414f57b212420.text: The command-line tool now shows a newer release number. This only updates the label on the program itself. Nothing changes in how it works or what it can do.

ccac201df6fc4a1ab037a5d13c930a49e65459fe.text: Documentation now clarifies that people in restricted regions can still unlock referral tiers, but they only get standard model limits, not premium ones. This change affects only readers of the internal reference guide, not the app's actual behavior. No user-facing features changed today.

25b6dde3bbfade9e2e2423e30c20766f5c73d2b9.text: The team updated the internal release label for their command-line tool. This is a routine packaging step that helps track which version is being distributed. Regular users will not notice any difference or new features.

43301d5fd2bcb9bdf1e0f3fc26a14de115359d84.text: Six new tracking labels were added to help measure how people find and use the service through Reddit ads. This change is internal and does nothing yet; no data will be recorded until the system is updated to actually send these labels. Regular users will see no difference in the app.

f0766573fad36c88ba482c7873e7054124140720.text: The system now checks for an existing attribution label before assigning a new one during tool calls. This prevents previously set labels from being overwritten by default values. The change is live and ensures accurate tracking of where clicks and conversions originate.

7f85312af394fa37a87011970442a28c6c728292.text: The assistant now uses a deeper reasoning step for more situations, including tricky bugs and uncertain approaches, not just the hardest tasks. This change affects full-access models, excluding the fastest tier to keep it responsive. It is live today.

be22023ea98700318566f36138d9cd5c6fe9eddb.text: The automated check that tests how our web research assistant finds answers has been given a slightly larger budget of steps to complete its task. This change only affects the internal quality checks and does not alter how the assistant behaves for you today. You will not notice any difference in the assistant's speed or results.

7f268e15a4c0210e7b041f3cbb2265db15d97167.text: The system now labels traffic strictly by the tool used, ignoring any previous surface data. This means clicks and conversions are attributed directly to the chat or command-line interface. The change is internal and requires no user action.

4999c63158f0f57c511141ac4277be73ca153b19.text: The internal label identifying this specific version of the coding tool was updated. This is a routine administrative change for the packaging system. Users will not notice any difference in how the tool works or looks.

778c6c18965612446c6b4fb568cba5120399fd94.text: The assistant now skips its internal quality-check step when it only answers a question or writes a plan, instead of running the check when there is nothing to review. This affects all subscription tiers. You might notice slightly faster responses for simple questions, as the assistant stops wasting time on unnecessary checks.

937787d54b56ca6ee152ff1bb454214701601916.text: The AI assistant now has access to two new versions of its underlying brain. This affects users who have paid for the highest-tier plan. If you are on that plan, the assistant will automatically use the newest model to answer your questions.

38844c7040fd9dd3eedac0755f87c6bfe6b1f75a.text: The chat assistant can now send a helper to search the live internet for current information. People using the chat interface will see the helper's name change from a nickname to 'Web Researcher' when it is working. This change is live today.

f63541370c2725c95b8e38a776ce4c91402c2f7f.text: The web research tool now forces its assistant to read at least three full source pages before answering, or five for complex questions. It no longer accepts brief search summaries as proof, since those are often outdated. This makes the research slower but more accurate and better cited. The change is live.

f219b409368e128adf95153f694aabf896189c0e.text: The default AI model for new chat sessions has switched from DeepSeek to Kimi. This change affects only users who do not manually select a different model in their settings. Users will notice that new conversations automatically start with Kimi, while existing chats and manual model selections remain unchanged.

e459f2a24426424306293d667cef2ef135ed1cbc.text: The tool now uses a different, more capable thinking model for its most advanced tasks, replacing the previous one. This change is active immediately for users on the highest tier. You might notice slightly better answers for complex problems, but the way you use the tool stays exactly the same.

7715a97463b9c6609c1f9e3a5d32eaf9449fb6dd.text: New free users now automatically see MiniMax M3 selected as their default assistant model instead of Kimi. This change applies immediately to new accounts, while existing users and settings remain unchanged. A new user would notice MiniMax M3 highlighted in their model picker upon first login.

293172345e45adda8b4ab9be0546a1b5614ad09c.text: The command-line tool now shows how much of your session limit you have already spent, instead of how much is left. This matches the wording seen on other screens. The change is live today.

ac888447c1bb269cec8476262a11cf270b02942c.text: The tool's internal release number increased. This is a routine housekeeping update that affects only the packaging metadata. A person using the command-line tool would not notice any change in behavior or appearance.

fe118aa3f6950ee3cc04197a155e65dc87a57339.text: The default AI model for standard requests switched to DeepSeek V4 Pro. This change is live now and affects all users on the web, desktop, and command-line tools. You will notice slightly different responses from the assistant when you do not pick a specific model.

6142b8be692c47b91afbaaced3ad6e433ab47175.text: The command-line tool now shows a clear error message when security software blocks it from starting, instead of crashing with a confusing technical failure. This affects Windows users whose antivirus or Smart App Control prevents the program from launching. They will see a readable warning explaining the block rather than a sudden crash.

323d5e50a72afae4df7bd73a04c94ded077e8d8c.text: The tool's internal release label was updated to mark a new packaging cycle. This change only affects how the software is bundled for distribution. Users will notice no difference in behavior or features.

56b18a1960ad0c308f1b210f01aa7b0fac0b98f0.text: The free coding tool received a routine update. People who use this tool to write code will see a newer version number appear when they check for updates. This change does not add new features or fix bugs; it simply marks a new release of the software.

7754f72e80e57678d648b9170a9bc725d31066a6.text: The waiting screen now explains why only some models appear, focusing on availability rather than restrictions. This wording change affects users on limited access, who see clearer notices about their region or network connection instead of a bold 'Limited mode' warning.

9de3b7019af2014d6245280c7808e2a92afeeed1.text: A test that checked a specific marketing phrase for one AI model was deleted. This is an internal cleanup, so the model's actual behavior and the website text remain unchanged. Nothing new will appear for anyone.

3deed7d21a3488df1deed4440a635321ec6bb445.text: The command-line tool now shows how many free sessions you have left to start, rather than how many you have already used. It also labels your remaining allowance as 'premium sessions' if you are on a limited plan. This change is live and helps you see your available capacity at a glance.

ec6049895f39b81037265dc2dc4ec8ee4577161a.text: A small internal update adjusts the automatic checks that verify how the system describes its gravity index tool. The test now expects a more detailed list of possible actions, such as searching or browsing, instead of a simple name. This change only affects the software's self-testing routine and does not alter what the assistant does or what customers see.

2c743c61f11ee2f2df023ddf95b3268ed4737b07.text: MiniMax M3 now warns that it collects data for training. It also moved up to the second spot in the free model list. This affects the model picker in the app and command line.

0a3669024953392e5c7b6171940113766df9c728.text: When the assistant stops receiving information for five minutes, it now shows a clear message about the connection instead of a confusing technical error. This helps people using the software know to check their internet or firewall settings. The update is live and applies to all agent runs.

a7e0fa38f02a212b5209e1dfcd97f866d9cba34e.text: The description for the MiMo 2.5 Pro model was updated to fix a grammar error in its tagline. This change affects the text shown in the model selection lists across the command line, web, and desktop apps. A reader would notice the tagline now reads 'Smartest & Slow' instead of the previous incorrect version.

87a6812a3ad19cd2f3132214ce5034886777c02d.text: The price tags for several newer AI models have been updated to match current costs. This affects internal cost tracking for requests using those specific models. Users will not notice any changes in the interface, but the recorded expense for each response will now reflect the new rates.

89a10d6afc6fa78b3a7f001542950aae6e48307d.text: The command-line tool now avoids wiping text when you ask for help. Previously, the cleanup step that restores your screen could accidentally erase the help instructions before you read them. This fix applies to the standard help command, ensuring the text remains visible. The change is active in the current release.

4642c507f8c5fe9034ddd46a98554ba964cb16db.text: The assistant now tracks which specific search led to a service recommendation. When it suggests a link to set up a new tool, that link includes hidden data showing who referred it. You will not notice any visual changes, but the service provider will see the referral source when you click the link.

61c1eefd5999cb4bd2d8367929e3016eb6e2d69f.text: Freebuff's free tier no longer offers GLM 5.1 as a model choice. It previously worked only during weekday business hours; now it is removed entirely. Users who had it selected will see it gone from the menu and get routed to another free model automatically.

0491f53a1259429a483e3099e04d576cbb5e5072.text: The assistant now ignores extra helper folders and backup files when looking for new tools. This prevents errors when loading tools from your local computer. Only people using the assistant's software kit will see this change, and it is active today.

2784b64f5e3b68033bc7c17be8184eafb65fb7bf.text: The system now knows the price tags for two new AI assistant models, including a special high-cost tier for the 'pro' version. Internal teams using these new models will see accurate billing calculations instead of errors or default values. This is a small backend update that is live today.

bc2e521ae7126000175fdb40f34658c9a358d7ff.text: Free plan users can now turn off the automatic code-checking step, saving time if they skip reviews. The system now sends complete instructions to the AI without waiting for external files, stopping random connection errors. Pausing a task now works correctly instead of showing a failure message. A new tracking setting exists but does nothing yet.

e438af55d55a845703265971145c837b820313dd.text: Free users connecting through VPNs or proxies can no longer be completely blocked from the service. Instead, they are routed to a cheaper, faster model, while only strict Tor network connections remain fully blocked. This change is currently active and ensures that legitimate users hiding their location can still access the platform, albeit with a different underlying engine.

4c20af5ced7ab262a2098201888f8a73f5383b19.text: When the program fails to start after an update, it now shows the exact reason, like a blocked file or a missing component, instead of a generic error. This helps users troubleshoot startup issues on their own, particularly on Windows where security software often interferes. The change is live and applies to all users of the command-line tool.

ce77a82c508d26c25c88f298f9d65f4ff224125f.text: The assistant's fast mode can now suggest follow-up steps, a feature previously restricted to standard mode. This change is live today. Users in fast mode will notice the assistant offering next steps at the end of a conversation, whereas before it stayed silent.

565af42cfc6575e75f78e03f4ba8ad2609c4f31b.text: The AI assistant now knows the current date. It tells you today is May 21, 2026. This helps it answer questions about time accurately.

f60634199133dea8a0d80c669a57cc7d750525c0.text: The command line tool now follows your computer's proxy settings when connecting to its server. This helps people who need a proxy to reach the internet. If you have a proxy set up, the tool will use it automatically instead of trying to connect directly.

f14fd0cc343ecd2079f46853acc8966fee8a6449.text: The system now records whether a user has full or limited access when they use the free service. This helps the team understand usage patterns without overwhelming their tracking systems. Users will not notice any change in how the assistant behaves.

21bb34cdb3e14f4f8bfd2eea28c3e45691483af5.text: When free users hit their daily session limit, the app now shows a clear message with the exact time until access resets. This replaces a generic button that previously offered no useful information. The change is live and applies only to free accounts.

4423d090bc0971f43a9c24e00c675b163ce61f38.text: The system now allows free search requests to proceed without checking if the user has enough account credit. This change prevents errors for users who previously saw 'insufficient balance' messages when trying to use the free search feature. The fix is live and affects only free search calls; paid features still require credit checks.

ae7713bb730569e0e4cfc464cd0e84ae5a4570c1.text: The waiting room screen now shows the user's detected country code when access is restricted, instead of saying the country is outside available regions. This change is live for all users encountering location-based blocks. The message simply clarifies which country was detected, helping users understand why they see a limited view.

d7915d1a449c1be76381e933b1237998f23e20ec.text: The live stats page now shows fewer words. Descriptive text and raw country codes were removed from the main number and the country list. This is a small visual cleanup. It is live today.

f3d9f45431c96e2327bd28425a86a7bd853be3b4.text: The Windows version of the command-line tool now builds using the standard setup instead of a special compatibility mode. This change affects the automated system that prepares the software for release, not the end-user experience. If you use the Windows tool, you likely won't notice any difference, as the underlying behavior remains the same for most modern computers.

84778f9c96c19f127e53384b91190eb9d0e40c3c.text: A small cleanup inside the command-line tool hides empty error boxes that appear when a background helper fails without producing any output. Only people using this tool will notice the change. Instead of seeing a confusing blank failure panel, they will see nothing, or a normal finished panel if the helper actually did some work.

806e27d82f418a16f9f87c3a3e9d8af62c99d0b4.text: The coding assistant now checks the actual current date every time it starts a conversation, instead of using a date that was saved when the software was built. This means the assistant will always know what today is, helping it give accurate answers about recent events or deadlines. This change is live and affects everyone who uses the assistant.

692b6fa2f3086116b9bf800c806b6963bd46df3b.text: The browser login screen now checks if the link from the command-line tool is empty or expired. Instead of showing a blank page or an error, it displays a clear message telling the person to return to their terminal and restart the tool to get a new link. This affects anyone trying to sign in through the web interface after their initial link has become invalid.

522068a877a8196bc879f2fcd71b4e4d2ccbea38.text: The homepage live stats section now shows fewer words. The explanatory sentence about what the numbers mean is gone, and country codes are no longer displayed under country names. This makes the section look cleaner and less cluttered. The change is live today for all visitors to the homepage.

9d59c700eaa58184656fe03f362b7a04c4aee4c0.text: The command-line tool now adjusts its layout when your terminal window is short. The large decorative logo shrinks to a single line or disappears, and the list of available models gains a scrollbar so you can still reach every option without the screen looking broken. This change is live today and affects anyone using the tool on a small or low-height terminal window.

7dc62c8e1a89fb06800c16072f4db5e169f1ddb4.text: The help page now explains that a restricted version exists for people outside supported countries or using VPNs. This version only allows one basic model and limits usage to five one-hour sessions daily. Visitors reading the FAQ will see clearer distinctions between full and restricted access.

2af416b863e4aab3507c0cb19b141fd839d44871.text: The website's FAQ was updated to clarify that Freebuff is available in all countries, but with two levels of access: full or limited. This helps visitors understand that even if they are outside the supported list of nations or using a VPN, the service still works, just with fewer features.

5380b97cc366aad170b24591ca16269002164dbd.text: A new command shortcut lets people type '/model:' instead of '/mode:' when switching modes in the command-line tool. This change is live today and affects only users of this specific tool. People will notice they can use either word to do the same thing, though most users won't see a visible difference.

47d025ad7973d0b474df5b2f2e83d6459469d17c.text: A small text update in the waiting screen. The separator between 'used' and 'resets' changed from a spaced dot to a comma. This only affects the visual layout for premium users. It is live today.

e43653226f8be2c6f80ddbf0c98bcfa96cde9856.text: A small summary of live activity now appears on the homepage. This information updates once every minute instead of every fifteen seconds, meaning the numbers shown might be slightly older than the real-time totals. This change applies to the public website and affects how quickly the displayed statistics reflect new activity.

cfc3e1ae4f15d4849696cdb1437075ba154a3d0e.text: The number shown on the waiting screen no longer adds extra zeros before it. This affects people using the command-line tool who see their session count. Instead of reading '05 of 10', it now reads '5 of 10'.

7f4d431302996f59c6624a4f9eaf992dc7d413b9.text: The text color of the buttons on the limited access screen changed from a bright brand color to a standard dark color. This makes the words easier to read against the background. The change is live now, but only affects the appearance of those specific buttons.

c3027175a0242057dd0de85ffcc835c9ad75a5e7.text: When you use the free version of this service, you sometimes see a waiting screen. Previously, if your access was restricted, the screen just said your options were reduced. Now, it tells you exactly why, such as saying your location is outside available countries or that a privacy network like a VPN was detected. This change is live and helps you understand why you cannot use all the models.

982f726c537864c08fa1e238ac7eae796286d453.text: We stopped saving the full text of your chats in our long-term records. Now, we only keep basic details like how many messages you sent and which AI model you used. You will not notice any changes to how the chat works, but your private conversations are no longer stored in our internal history logs.

558d1fe9213d28182cede6c95c42da24b4384bb4.text: Small fix for free-tier users of the command-line tool. When returning to the starting screen after a session ends, the tool now keeps track of your current queue position and usage limits instead of wiping them. You will notice the button label changes to 'Back to start' if you are on a limited plan, and the screen will accurately reflect your waiting status.

1796dbd4a28fab935a1eac47ddb0fa9db83fea66.text: The command-line tool now shows a plain message saying it is temporarily busy when rate-limited, instead of confusing technical error codes. This applies to users of the free service. You would notice a clearer message if you hit a limit.

8c189c305a0e72090d8eec4585136627709ce00d.text: Added a hidden switch for internal testing. It lets staff see the restricted version of the free chat tool on their own computers without changing what real users experience. It is not live for customers.

71b82cd473a88c3b984e5369f048ed7d9d7647aa.text: The system now automatically fixes a common formatting mistake when AI assistants try to start new tasks. If an assistant accidentally writes its instructions as a single line of text instead of a structured list, the system converts it into the correct format so the task can begin. This prevents the task from failing due to a minor technical error, making the process smoother for users.

cae558b46d0c0c795fbf2c4644b5bbbfff8b2807.text: The system now estimates message length locally for a specific free AI assistant instead of checking with the provider. This change is live and applies only to that free assistant. Users will not notice any difference, but the service saves time and resources by skipping an extra online check.

cb88ae8074cd9a134d1a6cc2543498652b157004.text: The code that builds the list of free AI models was cleaned up to remove unnecessary steps. This is an internal change, so the list of models, their order, and how you navigate them remain exactly the same.

7d451c872df79982a576bc3a1ac2906762cf1445.text: The system now stops charging for unfinished responses when a user closes their chat window. This applies to a specific fast model and a time limit for other services. Internal error logs also hide message content for limited-access plans.

6383ae8acdef116d44f37f944b28d0f5df4b5397.text: The system now checks if login codes from command-line tools look correct. If a code is malformed, it saves a detailed error note in the background logs instead of failing silently. This helps support staff diagnose why specific login attempts fail. Regular users see no change on their screen.

b94212ab04f5dfc15f13df05c592f633cbe9fab2.text: A small visual fix prevents the ad banner in the command-line tool from stretching vertically when the website address is very long. This change is active now. If you run the tool, the ad box stays a single line tall and the text stays neatly aligned instead of pushing other content down.

7a95a981493400eb1024210de5ea59ab08e9bad7.text: The system now records extra details when a sign-in attempt fails. Support staff can use these notes to see if the problem came from the user's device or the web browser's address. Customers will not see any changes on their screen.

7d59406b7e81d940065af1a346e33a05e61584d4.text: The list of free AI tools now shows a warning next to DeepSeek V4 Flash. This tells people that using this specific tool sends their chats to the company to help improve its future versions. You will see this note if you pick that option in the app.

d885b4bc8b1f30d435472baa2f9126dd647f0cdb.text: The free version of the service now works in France, Italy, Spain, and Portugal. People in these countries can sign up and use the service without paying, just like those in the previously supported regions.

206d2310b08f40f9d840c8a4b7dbf682b597bca2.text: The system now records a short, scrambled code for each login link instead of the full link itself. This helps support staff trace a specific login attempt without exposing the actual secret. The change is live but affects only internal log records, so customers will not notice any difference.

fbdf2f3ecac0bf85fe13a36b6087e65769ab3354.text: When a bash agent finishes its work, the collapsed view now shows a single, shortened line of its result instead of the raw, multi-line output. This change applies only to bash agents that are not currently running. The preview line adapts to the window width, capped at 120 characters, to keep the display readable.

9f96ac1233d28d7111876e14ef5f9682669c2843.text: The free tier assistant gained a new capability to run terminal commands using a specific, cost-effective AI model. This change is active today. Users on the free plan might notice slightly different behavior or speed when the assistant executes commands, though the core functionality remains the same.

00ac6486b7f4a73b04f65ef4eec8fd5066890343.text: The list of free AI models now shows DeepSeek V4 Flash above MiniMax M2.7. People using the free tier will see DeepSeek V4 Flash higher in the menu and in the FAQ text.

e798ad9c6c200fd8a54eaf99e65015dc64af4ee8.text: The assistant no longer accepts one specific AI model for a particular service. If you try to use that model, the system will reject it instead of attempting to process the request. This change is live now and only affects users who selected that specific model option.

37b905688e44841274d2f3af26ae418b8e4b8b9d.text: The system now supports a new chat model for OpenCode Zen users. It costs less per message than the previous option. If you use OpenCode Zen, you can select this model from the menu and see lower usage fees.

9d7e9e4f609d8c4af78b9b11c8943055f969aa86.text: The tool that shows code changes on your terminal screen was previously disabled by a hidden switch, so it displayed nothing. That switch is removed, so the changes are now visible with color highlights. This affects anyone using the command-line interface to review edits.

5cd16cb80591c5258cdcc77501077ddd38de07b4.text: The history screen now uses a compact '[x]' symbol instead of the word 'Delete'. This saves space, allowing longer conversation titles to display clearly without pushing the button off-screen. It also fixes alignment issues when using emojis or special characters in your chat history.

3f192e006104fa3e18ee98879506805d4f0f2ea0.text: A small internal update added a safety check to how the system identifies specific AI models. This prevents errors when unexpected data formats are processed, ensuring the assistant correctly recognizes its supported models. Users will not notice any changes in how the software behaves.

47ae3eb4c94fd1a79d6ec26c490b0f56b799f787.text: The assistant now includes a new free model option. This change is live today. If you use the free plan, you may see this new model available in the list of choices.

cfd4a2c37bc0cd4a2740188a3182a5aa890deca3.text: Internal test fix. A check for unknown user location now runs correctly. No impact on live service or users.

bdd8b09121cea865b3bbb7a8cf71f8b3d54a690e.text: The waiting room screen now shows how many premium sessions you have used today instead of how many are left. This helps you see exactly where you stand against your daily limit. The text stays centered and does not jump around as the numbers update.

9342438a64ebd4276fc73ae80f54727c56b080db.text: The help page now lists available AI models in a simple bulleted format and removed specific daily session limits. The privacy section clarified that your conversations are only shared with third-party AI providers for training if you explicitly pick a model labeled 'Collects data for training'. These text updates are live on the website.

247b4c84619b747079e9b166a2438087fa9ccf40.text: A small internal update stops the command-line tool from showing detailed text changes in the terminal. This affects only people using that specific text-based interface. They will notice that the colored lines showing exactly what changed in files no longer appear, though the rest of the tool's output remains the same.

fdf8d94e5570efa1d48732b81b57608032d9df4e.text: The website's FAQ now lists a new, unlimited-session coding assistant model and clarifies daily limits for existing options. This update is live and visible to all visitors on the help page. Internal maintenance also fixed a background configuration check to prevent build errors.

4987adaefa045c3255aa3ebe3be301b062c639d8.text: The login link sent to your command-line tool now uses a random, single-use ticket instead of your actual security key. This prevents the key from being visible in browser history or server logs. You will notice no difference when logging in, as the system automatically swaps the ticket for your key behind the scenes.

a88ccccad6a67338711b2eab5e57eb0b3f056514.text: Older review tools can now use three specific AI models. This fixes a gap for clients that started before dedicated reviewer IDs existed. Users of these older clients will see reviews run without errors.

b51ad4b60ed674402cdfe528488e453f9929147e.text: The free version of the AI assistant can now use the DeepSeek model alongside MiniMax and GLM. This change applies to the main 'base2-free' mode, so users in that group will see DeepSeek as an available option when interacting with the assistant.

992f3382112e6b710f5d76ee5226430f901aa7de.text: The remaining premium usage count moved from the model list header to the main screen title. Premium users see this number at the top of the waiting screen, turning amber when exhausted. This small interface adjustment makes the limit easier to spot without cluttering the selection list.

c3b019f1668af33082e689fb99254e9a3ce74d8f.text: A previous update that tried to fix how the tool identifies helper agents was removed because it caused the same helper to appear twice on your screen. This change affects the command-line interface, specifically when you use the reviewer agent. You will no longer see duplicate cards for the same helper, though the underlying identification method has reverted to its original behavior.

17f45a497be0e5bc95468c913c2fe0b92db4a9bb.text: The command-line tool now correctly identifies and displays the names of specialized helpers, even when they use underscores instead of hyphens. This fixes a display bug where the wrong name or type might have appeared on screen.

3df6ec9369acfcb1e7cb02288aa307c0940bbbdf.text: When a free chat session ends in the command-line tool, you can now press Enter to start a new session with the same model, or press Esc to choose a different model. The tool also automatically retries with a backup model if the first one is unavailable, preventing the screen from getting stuck. This change is live today for command-line users using the free service.

c11a47350991d7298be950a93d1c2071dbb6ce2b.text: Previously, when the system started a new helper task, the interface would sometimes show the same helper card twice. This happened because the system failed to correctly identify the helper's true name and role during the startup process. The fix ensures the system uses the correct identity from the start, so you will now see only one accurate card for each helper.

1409cf91caa26aca496d30db773169642430a35c.text: The command-line tool now groups AI models by subscription level, placing the usage limit counter at the top of the premium section instead of on each model row. This change affects people using the text-based interface to pick models. They will see a cleaner list with aligned names and fewer repeated labels.

116e456fa93f2d88a754347f5279f0633c3dd877.text: Small fix for command-line login. The system now handles login codes with dots correctly and prevents bouncing between web addresses. People using the command-line tool will see fewer failed logins.

d313c4a1ea19bd8f6fe9f8b2e7ba25d0522cd3c8.text: The text editor view now waits for a file change to finish before showing the before-and-after comparison. This prevents a brief flash of incorrect information when creating new files. Only visible in the command-line interface.

5a613f89b9293bbc9e93f2893301a4b475c8878c.text: The waiting room screen now lets people choose between 'Take over' and 'Exit' using the keyboard instead of just the mouse. Pressing the arrow keys or Tab moves the highlight between the two buttons, and Enter picks the highlighted one. This is live today and affects anyone using the command-line tool when it detects another instance is already running.

884911e73ae7daa3131a1f3640089002400de394.text: Free plan users can now ask the assistant to browse websites for them. This feature is live today across all apps. You will see the assistant can visit pages and gather information without needing a paid subscription.

497dd729d369e5f79ccc4448f522620ebed335b1.text: The test setup now lets the fake tool output be any shape, instead of only text. This affects only the internal test helpers, not the real program. Nothing changes for anyone using the tool today.

53bd37e42721c3c82f38c6e13eeca9ad1f6ef2fa.text: A small internal cleanup removed a broken link from the assistant's instruction list. This link pointed to a guide that no longer exists, so the assistant will stop trying to read a missing file. Only the internal instructions changed; users will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves.

e5a769f1aecce74e5f931b8b7686d435fd3bce7e.text: Previously, the command-line tool hid the final answer from certain AI assistants if they had already used other tools. This fix ensures that the text result appears on screen even when those tools were involved. The update is live now.

19fd493012e249d012cb6ac432019b0b6305b69c.text: The command-line tool no longer displays the words 'Free session' in its status bar. This change affects only people using the command-line version. If you look at the status bar, you will see the remaining time and quota information without the extra label.

c7a858cca6e4e756fd504ebd1e57ab981ff4eecc.text: The assistant now uses shorter labels when summarizing past actions, such as 'inspected files' instead of 'previously inspected files'. This change reduces the amount of text sent to the system, allowing it to remember more of your conversation within its memory limit. You will not see a visible difference in the chat interface, but the assistant may handle longer conversations more efficiently.

c237e011f8bf96dcaedb048c20f4bec2649ad6a1.text: A small change to how the model selection screen displays usage limits for premium accounts. Instead of showing a separate 'used' count for every model, the screen now shows one shared total for all premium models together. The 'unlimited' label was also removed from the MiniMax model description, though it remains available for free use.

30a74b13655cdf54bdb92695b32a79061bab3395.text: The system now hides internal error notes about failed tool calls from the final message list. People reading the agent's output will see a cleaner conversation without these technical warnings, though the underlying errors still occur.

8fa7488daf630728e2d15dc62d3e14b3f3544e07.text: The tab key now works reliably in the model selection list. Previously, tabbing could fail or trigger unintended actions. This fix applies to the command-line interface. Users will notice smoother navigation when switching models.

ed6b40772029fa12c2b2aa696281378a75f40235.text: The text-based tool’s status bar no longer repeats the words Free session. It now shows only the assistant name, when available, and the time left. People using the tool’s status bar will see a shorter line. It is live today.

225ff3c73330ef6e3e8feddd60540221ddf3b765.text: The system now automatically checks that its assistant correctly resumes work from a summarized history instead of copying the summary's format. This change only affects internal quality assurance tests and does not alter how the assistant behaves for you today.

9b64c59cc76e48d59c00491ff539a53a1f2e6b92.text: A small internal fix helps the command-line tool correctly find a specific helper file when running a quick check. This change is live today. It mostly affects developers running these checks; regular users will not notice any difference in how the tool works.

2bb6ffca346d7996349f7df48f315d184562788d.text: Small internal fix. Some older install tools lost a required support file during updates, causing the app to fail. The app now automatically downloads that missing file from the internet on first run. People using those old tools will see a brief message about the download.

11fbf88499efe8ae3efd1f5b4835580e066b498f.text: A small change now helps people who use the free coding assistant on their own computer. If you open a second copy of the program while one is already running, the new copy asks if you want to take control of the session or close down. This stops the new copy from silently kicking out the old one, so you keep your work safe.

c44bdd892aa4070a170df2a76b3dd1f17b9c08b9.text: A small fix helps a text editor load faster on Windows. If the editor cannot find its language rules, it now checks a nearby folder instead of failing. You might notice the editor starting up more reliably without error messages.

1c308ad5aa42aea42643a76b6d4e64e48279bbb6.text: The tool now checks if a required data file is actually readable before using it, instead of trusting a shortcut path that looked correct but failed. This fixes a bug where the feature would crash on some Windows computers. Users who previously saw an error when starting the tool will now see it work.

249bd7f3b2b65513814d63081e8f4fc4adbdccb6.text: The automated checks that run after code updates now show exactly what files the system sees when a text analysis component fails to load. This helps the team find the problem faster by listing the expected file location and what is actually there. Regular users will not notice any change in how the software behaves.

b463207c112fdd3a17ba8a3b2693f83088a63a76.text: The command-line tool now checks its own setup during creation to ensure a specific text-analysis engine is included. If the engine is missing, the build process stops and reports an error instead of creating a broken file. This helps internal release engineers catch packaging mistakes before the tool is distributed to customers.

a3399902180bb42581d2a6eff6229153d3b3d389.text: The command-line tool now finds its text-analysis engine correctly on Windows. Previously, the tool looked in a virtual location instead of the actual folder where the program sits, causing it to fail before starting. Windows users will notice the tool launches without error.

a5d75a28b2b4267967854295d903874554669bd0.text: The command-line tool had a bug on Windows where it failed to load a specific internal component needed for code analysis. The fix ensures this component is correctly packaged within the application's installation file during the build process. Windows users of the tool will now experience fewer startup errors or crashes related to this missing component.

5e57c1f796855869d728591ba4b167d523bcd33c.text: A small internal update added a routine that builds the tool on Windows and runs a brief startup test after every code change. This helps the team catch issues that only appear on Windows, like a recent problem where the tool would start but then fail shortly after. Users will not notice anything directly; this just makes future Windows releases more reliable.

5743114d091cefdc1bda82f2525713d077e6ba42.text: A new optional field lets the release tool build from a chosen past version instead of always the latest. This helps the internal team fix or test specific builds. Normal releases stay unchanged, so most people see nothing.

ba4858b418fe880ea4af7d324806a355ed56c701.text: The program now waits until it is fully running to locate its grammar engine, avoiding a Windows bug where early startup searches failed. This fix ensures the tool can analyze code on Windows without crashing. Users will notice smoother operation when launching the application on Windows.

5e43e630ff377c5e94bd665b5f692c6aa5446abf.text: The command-line tool now hides its code-parsing data inside a locked box instead of leaving it on a shelf. This stops the tool that builds the program for Windows users from accidentally throwing the data away as 'unused.' Regular users won't see a change, but Windows builds are now less likely to fail silently due to this data loss.

2c4b87305949af8fff3128a2d055e243801a2d64.text: A small internal fix ensures a specific testing command works correctly on Windows. If a developer runs this command, the program now checks its core text-processing engine without crashing or ignoring the instruction. Regular users will not notice any change.

adef8ed677d3b8bbf057bae008263a01a245d22b.text: The command-line tool now loads its language-analysis engine directly into memory instead of searching for it on the hard drive. This fixes a bug where Windows users running the compiled version of the tool would see it fail to start. You will not notice any new features, but the tool will now work reliably on your Windows machine.

cb069ac68216580c5dd2fb7e7e24606106126599.text: Internal maintenance updated the safety checks for the command-line tool's startup process. This change only affects the team building the software and does not change how the tool works for anyone else.

74abc489274e376070953134b985d7a893394cea.text: A small internal update fixed the hidden checks that run behind the scenes to make sure the software works correctly. This change does not affect what you see or do in the application today. It simply ensures the system's automated quality checks run without errors.

13805acab332ef9046b6b7681285c5b221755c0b.text: The tool now cleans pasted text to remove invisible formatting codes, preventing display glitches. This update affects anyone using the command-line interface. You would notice only if pasting previously caused visual errors, which are now fixed.

2d282ce3f002e05f6fa23ee3e753dcf71e878f2b.text: The tool used to add a specific sentence to the start of every message it sent to the AI to prove it was allowed to use certain newer models. That extra sentence is now gone, so messages go to the AI exactly as written. This only affects people using a specific sign-in method for the AI, and they will not see any difference in how the tool looks or works.

d4d2c0a14efc1143775dca97336dd6ea21ccb3ae.text: The text interface was downgraded to an older version because the new one caused problems. This affects only people using the command-line tool. They will notice that pasting text into the input box now works correctly again, and the screen display behaves as it did before the upgrade.

83b6eacae7bb294f340070cb93b108c286f5b9e1.text: Freebuff is now available in Liechtenstein, Austria, Singapore, Malta, and Israel. This change is live today. Users in these five countries can now use the free version of the service.

a81339bb43003d5c6f7e97fa18865c42e93b7543.text: A small visual tweak cleans up the model list in the command line waiting room. Previously, the highlighted model's name turned green; now only the border and arrow indicate selection, keeping the text color normal. This applies only to the command line interface and changes no functionality.

8698c9a9a2ae2c01a1619cfeacbc4f38e2e5b815.text: The waiting screen now sets aside a blank space where an advertisement will appear. This stops the text below from suddenly shifting downward when the ad finishes loading. Regular people using the tool will see a smoother, steadier screen while waiting.

70f7a46adf8f52052d3296d9de39e15f79535ad3.text: The command-line tool's display engine received a routine upgrade. The main visible change is that pasting text from other programs now automatically removes hidden formatting codes, preventing them from cluttering the screen. This update is live.

32aa640716e4d7af9ee0b5feac31802250ef2782.text: The Kimi model is now restricted to specific working hours, matching an older model's schedule. This change affects internal systems using that model. If you tried to use Kimi outside those hours, you would get an error message saying the model is unavailable.

2ae871eaca3d57a0d7002b3a0fc77b334a91f44f.text: A small internal update removed a time restriction on one AI model. The assistant can now use this specific model at any time, rather than only during certain hours. No change occurs for other models.

12a85348fc6f4c647e2df06bf06fea631467ed6f.text: When the assistant receives a command written in a slightly broken format, it now tries to fix the mistake instead of failing. If it cannot fix the mistake, the assistant sees the reason for the failure and can try again. This change is live and affects all users of the agent system.

721d1d5c2d85cc0acd878e826b4fd832cd95810a.text: The text menu for choosing an AI model no longer shows how many people are ahead of you in line. This happened because current traffic never fills up the waiting line, so those numbers were just clutter. The menu still shows if a model is closed or if you have used up your limit.

fdadc4602f1fdbda8a076cd0af48714c5c9c4ab3.text: A specific assistant setting no longer offers the option to show visual interface elements. This change affects only users of that particular assistant profile. They will notice that the assistant stops trying to display custom visual layouts or interactive cards.

d727cd453111a7a6c890e0addf6884f095b552a0.text: The waiting room for free accounts now uses a fixed thirty-minute window to let ongoing tasks finish, instead of letting administrators adjust it. This internal cleanup affects only the free-tier system, and customers will not notice any change in how the service behaves.

18cde84c6d5b59255165d0fca707419bd82be4ca.text: A small internal update renamed one AI assistant tool to make its label shorter. This change does not affect how the tool works or what it can do. Regular users will not notice any difference.

40185a3e1bcea3e4c2bc3b4b4c2cd1d9db18f8b7.text: The app simplified how clickable links look in the command line. Instead of staying green or red to show if a link opened successfully, the button now briefly dims for a split second when clicked. This removes clutter and makes the interface cleaner, but you no longer get a permanent color confirmation of whether the link actually opened.

537da7262e41c2b3153deaff46ba434318c2f83f.text: The assistant now labels its helper tasks with underscores instead of hyphens to match what the underlying service expects. This is a small internal cleanup to prevent errors when the system tries to find or run these helpers. You will not see any visual change or new capability in the app.

fdf34b7667ba21a400fdba34045282e9a10e3725.text: The assistant now displays a large, clickable button instead of just a text link when you need to get an API key for a new service. This makes the next step in the setup process easier to find and use. The change is live.

8ebb2284766ba0abd76aa21b0077a4b2bc319ac6.text: The free coding assistant now uses GLM 5.1 instead of Kimi K2.6. This affects new free or lite sessions; existing saved settings remain unchanged. You will see GLM 5.1 listed as the default option in the model picker.

894c58555c70298811bb100eb79190a867c79a13.text: The system now sends requests for a specific chat model to a shared service pool during open hours, instead of a reserved private machine. This switch is live today. People using this model will not notice any difference in how the chat works, as the answer quality remains the same.

ce0dc1e52d1066d1087b9fbc7bd57403bfff2e9c.text: The internal test system now automatically assigns a placeholder key for Canopy Wave services, just like it does for OpenAI and Anthropic. This ensures automated checks run smoothly without requiring manual setup for that specific service. Internal engineers will see fewer errors in test logs, but this has no impact on live products or end users.

8cc765a6f0e563278323a30c4ab4f69bf8d90b0b.text: A small change to the command-line tool for free AI model access. The model list now shows how much of your daily limit you have used and flags models that are full. You can also scroll past unavailable models to see them, though you still cannot join a full queue. This is live today.

362f5d536d5e38b3a744f5c96daba82a0d815412.text: The time limit for using the GLM 5.1 model has been shortened from 20 hours to 12 hours. This means you can still only use it 5 times, but those uses must happen within a 12-hour window instead of a 20-hour one. If you hit the limit, you will have to wait less time for your first use to expire and free up a slot.

08b69435f21d290eebafab30f3bc456f29616697.text: The software now uses one standard format for all ads instead of two different types. This change affects only the free version of the command-line tool and web app. You will not see any visual difference, as the ads still look and behave exactly the same.

fbd3b1e27f7f8ecab654c9e7ca58e5e2557aa928.text: A small internal change helps staff work on the site from their own computers. The system now lets local test requests skip the usual location check, making it faster to try out features without needing extra network tools. Regular customers will not see any difference, and the live website keeps its normal security checks.

14559962af1f8a3de237b44dbaa9c22904093da8.text: The system now matches agent names even if you type underscores instead of hyphens. This helps people who launch helper programs by name, so a request for 'my_helper' finds the 'my-helper' program. It is active now, making name lookups more forgiving.

b8fada28b29c3dca484789f94f35ad43ebc85bbf.text: The free version of this command-line tool now uses Kimi K2.6 instead of GLM 5.1 as its default smart assistant. This change is live and applies to anyone using the free or lite modes. You will see Kimi K2.6 listed as the primary option when you open the model selector, though it still shares the same usage limits and availability hours as the previous model.

e6dbaa57c4631c420cc9490b6751d5d568719e12.text: The text labels in the command line ad banner are now bold instead of dimmed. This affects only the non-domain labels, making them stand out more clearly against the background. The change is live and requires no action from you.

fa3c0324cf252ceff341f9dbc08e52dba3e051d5.text: The ad display logic now checks a backup source if the primary one fails to load an ad. This affects free users and subscribers without active plans. They will see fewer blank spaces where ads usually appear, as the system automatically tries a second provider if the first one has no ads available.

25f8b89c42ac2c35f0d8d4681987dfe169e3280c.text: The limit on how many people can instantly start a free session with the MiniMax model was raised from 200 to 1000. This helps more users access this specific free option at the same time without waiting. You might notice fewer delays when trying to start a chat with this model during busy times. This change is live now.

8cfc4b0c1c15bb82cadba7a997f4383b4bd3ac16.text: The system now recognizes a specific waiting area screen. It uses a different set of ad slots for this screen compared to the main chat view. This change is live and affects only what ads appear while a user is waiting.

08c9f24906e3ca2a5798360242009f7f70f5714c.text: The Terms of Service page now lists Manicode, Inc. as the company that owns the trademarks and copyright, replacing the old name. The 'Last updated' date on that page also changed to April 23, 2026. Anyone reading the legal page sees the corrected company name and current date.

f13eed31aadf22362eae2419ff326f18199b31b6.text: Lite mode now uses standard Fireworks API when custom deployments fail, avoiding errors. This affects internal lite mode requests. Users might notice fewer errors during downtime.

dc84d374a148fa96a6056bf8bccca23e68eca5b9.text: The free daily trial of the Fireworks AI models is now available 9am ET to 5pm PT every day, instead of just Monday through Friday. Users who access these free models on weekends will notice the availability hours label updated and the models working during that window.

49b8b2cfa951743de1affca7625fc4165d9a670c.text: A background check now flags accounts with Chinese-style names or email providers if they also send hundreds of messages in a day. This helps catch groups abusing the free service from outside approved regions, while leaving normal users alone. You would not notice any change unless your account was incorrectly flagged, which requires both the region signal and heavy usage.

f7c7870d8533395e47d9a3ea1216b0036f9c204c.text: The app now remembers your chosen AI model even if it temporarily switches to a backup model when your pick is unavailable. Previously, a single automatic switch could permanently overwrite your preference. Now, your selection is saved only when you manually choose a model, so you keep your preferred option for future sessions.

de32834c77187d82c06aef4462df5c10149f4546.text: The legal text on the Terms of Service page now names the company as Manicode, Inc. instead of Codebuff, Inc. This change is live and affects anyone reading the agreement. Readers will see the new corporate name where the old one appeared, though the service itself remains unchanged.

20dc66e496fe49e4981becbf1c5a5839f1584836.text: Internal testing tools now allow staff to compare costs between two different AI models. The main test script switched to the newer, pricier model to check its specific pricing. This change only affects the engineers running these checks; regular users will notice no difference.

2ce07f2db82e2bbb24f2499cc3bdc767670f3d6c.text: People who signed up for the free trial from a blocked country previously got stuck in the virtual waiting room because the system let them in but the chat service rejected them later. The tool now recognizes this rejection and immediately moves them to a 'country blocked' screen, freeing up their place in line. This helps stop people from typing messages that would never be answered.

8ce2c7174ebedbe8117bf44377c553ceee8be468.text: The system that watches for fake accounts got stricter about what counts as suspicious. It now trusts accounts that have been around for a while or that take breaks, so real people who use the service heavily are less likely to be blocked by mistake. This change is live and affects only the automatic checks, not how you use the service.

4c3be9e5f60b0c89fb7fa8cb42e5d335d949e375.text: The tool now asks which folder to work in before checking if you are logged in or waiting for access. This prevents the folder selection screen from disappearing if the login check fails. It affects people starting the tool outside a project folder.

a33580f1172d15cc5251c499c83675894751aa40.text: The system now measures how long a user stays silent more accurately by counting time before their first message and after their last one within a 24-hour window. This helps distinguish real people who sleep or take breaks from automated bots that run continuously. Only internal safety checks see this change; regular users won't notice any difference in how the app works.

a372554f76118600c0116e7f7d4422c4e8f7e84b.text: The assistant now attempts to fix broken instructions it receives from the AI model before rejecting them. If the instructions are still unreadable, the system displays a specific error message instead of a generic failure. This change affects only the background logic for tool usage and is active immediately.

938191c3f2cdcda8e5f2613ed2f250a2c8b8ee6e.text: The command-line tool for Freebuff no longer falsely shows 'No wait' for every model right after a session ends. Instead, it fetches the real queue lengths in the background and leaves the wait hints blank until those numbers arrive. This only affects people using that tool, and it fixes a small display glitch.

fb2656966ba564e13d588d8ca0a06658d1e5e422.text: The waiting room now shows a permanent 'Account unavailable' message to banned accounts, stopping them from joining the queue. This prevents fake bots from inflating the wait times you see.

76c3d44991d7a4d6424bb1d484b73cb453902454.text: In the Freebuff command-line tool, the suggested follow-up buttons now stop working once a session ends. This prevents you from accidentally clicking on actions that no longer apply.

b234a41d2a82101d48b6df162b29f0896fe3a70a.text: The system now checks for human-like behavior, such as long breaks between messages or using varied tools, to better identify real users and avoid flagging them as bots. This change affects internal moderation processes and is live today. Users won't see any difference, but moderators will get more accurate data when reviewing suspicious accounts.

19bb1512b49bc195eb4ee2a72e73ecf14ca26ba4.text: Requests for the Kimi K2.6 model now go to a different service provider. This switch also updates the cost charged for using that model. The change is live and affects anyone using Kimi K2.6.

2d3a32bd4522b027f88c1460088a2331a540ab22.text: The system now lowers the suspicion score for users who have had their linked account for over a year, and even more for those over three years. This helps long-time users avoid being falsely flagged as bots when they use the service heavily. Regular users will not see any changes, but support staff will be instructed to avoid marking these established accounts as high-risk without other proof.

2e3f02b8ddbf01d0944290ed1180467912f8d048.text: Ending a free session now takes you straight back to the model selection screen instead of automatically putting you back in the waiting queue. This applies to free-tier users who manually end a chat early. You will see the prompt change to 'Ending session and returning to the model picker' and land on the landing page to choose your next model.

0706c98b582684fbc935fa4a36f3575f310b5e6c.text: When a free chat session ends, the program now returns you to the model selection screen instead of automatically putting you back in the waiting line. This affects people using the command-line tool to chat with free models. You will notice that you must manually choose a model and press Enter to start a new session, rather than being silently re-queued.

50f2ade2171191f6369ab907ee04f50cf76f3dfb.text: A small visual update in the command-line tool's model picker moves each model's short description to sit directly next to its name. This change affects the free tier interface, making the list cleaner and more stable. Users will notice descriptions appearing inline rather than in the far-right column, which now only shows wait times.

58e7f306da16d24c097bda7826d08d1444777da7.text: A banned person who was already using a free AI model now loses their spot instantly instead of keeping it until their session time ran out. This means the next person in line can start their session sooner. The change is live today.

212bab08e71dc3d7dec495ba7d7e2600c0ec77e2.text: A new rule lets people join free chat sessions instantly if the specific AI model is not too busy. This affects only users trying to access the free version of two particular models. Instead of waiting in a line, they will start chatting immediately unless the model reaches its maximum allowed number of active users.

6f2d8fa236055ec7e5f93209d3d93f8808c2eb1f.text: When you open the free assistant, it now shows a list of models with live wait counts instead of automatically placing you in line. You choose a model to join, so you know the crowd before committing. This applies to the free tier.

f953ae68f3b5abf9b56cc7d69b56ecd0e9266e25.text: A new version of an AI model was added to the website's settings. This change is small and internal. Regular users will not notice anything different today.

b0d0e55a348de37244c1edb5c8c97017e573c350.text: The assistant no longer uses the minimax-m2.7 model. This internal change stops that specific option from being selected. It is live today.

b3c8862230764bfcb68cdd4001824885c81ee8cb.text: The team added a new AI model to their internal testing script. This change is small and only affects internal tools. No customers or users will notice anything because the script is not part of the public product.

47084a9dee1e018602723f65e34025c41255896d.text: The help pages now list the correct assistant names and roles, replacing old ones with current versions. This update affects only website visitors reading the documentation. You would notice the text accurately describing which specific tools handle different tasks, and a note that older subscription connections are no longer supported.

1d89739afa72e15aba869e50191b1be62a0cb290.text: The model picker in the text-based app now separates looking from choosing. Pressing arrow keys just moves a highlight without changing your place in line; you must press Enter to actually switch models. This prevents accidentally losing your queue spot when tabbing past your current model, while mouse clicks still switch instantly.

72afab04704468996fb3c2eef1150ff28633b78e.text: The model picker now stacks its buttons vertically when the window is too narrow to fit them side-by-side, preventing text from being cut off. This change is live. You will notice the layout adapts to your screen size, and you can use the up and down arrow keys to move between options.

a3087a33f8fffc6f3dbdc169bb6f0c191af8d792.text: The command-line tool's waiting screen now lets people switch between service lines by pressing the Tab or arrow keys instead of typing numbers. The text showing how many people are ahead of you stays the same size as the number counts down, so the buttons no longer jump around. The estimated wait time is also shown in a dimmer color to make the screen less cluttered.

46bf7033c9cdd02a76ffed40eab17c2ee9a3c1d9.text: The waiting room system now tracks how many people are actively using each AI model, rather than just a single total number. This change is internal and does not affect how you use the service, but it lets the support team see exactly which models are busy and which have open spots.

8c694456f59d1ebdf7c410ea979a0a59596156c3.text: The program's internal safety checks now ignore an old 'referral code' label that no longer exists. This is a small, behind-the-scenes cleanup that does not change how the software works for anyone.

a51a9349ec1bcbe51bad6bdacccd11215310bff7.text: The wait time display on the CLI waiting room screen now shows static text instead of an animated shimmer. This affects only the CLI waiting room screen. You would notice the wait time text is no longer moving or sparkling.

b76f9be64e0489961fd31dbb625d9181a9355b1d.text: The tool now shows the list of available models in a clearer, boxed layout, making it easier to read and select options. This change affects anyone using the command-line interface to manage their free tier. You will notice the model selection menu appears above the status details, with each option neatly separated for better visibility.

1242b4e38947578ec285e80ed8d498ad170ecd86.text: The system now uses a specific, older AI model to measure how much text fits in a conversation when using certain other AI models. This change affects how the system calculates message length for some third-party AI tools. Users won't see a direct change, but the system's internal math for measuring text size is slightly different now.

912a3f96607449b4b2915e6addd9b91db2333974.title: Add sponsored delivery client diagnostics
912a3f96607449b4b2915e6addd9b91db2333974.summary: Added `sponsoredDeliveryClientDiagnostics` in `common/src/ads/sponsored-delivery-diagnostics.ts` to report client claims. This function derives execution surface and capability contract version from User-Agent and OS fields. It explicitly never authorizes delivery or execution. The output includes `client_os`, `execution_surface`, `capability_contract`, and `capability_inspection` status.
