6736dfa66d6bf15eb812a131068343af0029f59d.text: This change fixes a bug where browsing chat history would accidentally log you out. It affects anyone using the command-line tool on the free plan. You will now be able to look at your past conversations without having to wait in line to reconnect.

234adfdc33d52adb8e03da558d111ef5755d7630.text: The wait time estimate for free sessions is now 24 seconds per person ahead, down from 60 seconds. This change is live and affects people joining the free queue. If you are fifth in line, you will now see an estimated wait of two minutes instead of five minutes.

20e84ced412bc793ededb64af3c50bca6765fe5b.text: Internal team accounts now skip the waiting room for free sessions. This change prevents automated tests from failing when the waiting room is active. Regular users will not notice any difference, as this only affects specific internal email addresses.

504f80c1ed8afbd7081ff99a1932d9757ff74cdf.text: The website no longer shows the top strip that asked visitors to refer friends. This affects people viewing the site in a browser. They will see a cleaner page with more room for the main content.

dd373b9102d0ec75fe327a1e3b7dcd2b0f654270.text: Five checks for subscription limits now wait 15 seconds before failing. This helps internal tools run more reliably. Regular users will not notice any difference.

9996bc60d46e06a5738df6d568f147ca937513ab.text: The help page example for the 'account suspended' error message was updated to remove specific billing details. This change aligns the documentation with the generic message the system now sends to users. Readers looking at the error guide will see the new, simpler wording instead of the old billing-specific text.

2dee392b72ade5fa5f5da75c8c821c8bc8c2b96c.text: When a suspended account tries to use the chat service, the error message no longer mentions billing issues. Instead, it simply states the account is suspended and asks the user to contact support if unexpected. This is a minor internal text update affecting only suspended users.

2118e41fd1ff01f99c589aaa4be5eb359cbcdf06.text: The system now flags the AI backend as struggling when its slowest responses take longer than half a second, instead of waiting for a full second. This change affects only free users, causing the system to stop new requests earlier when performance dips. Users might notice fewer new sessions starting during busy periods, but those already running will experience less delay.

e0ba3a65c9a4f579af2ffd0f2ed6342ef0513646.text: The waiting room now displays a fixed estimate of one minute per person ahead in line, rather than trying to predict the exact timing of server updates. This change affects users waiting for access to the free service. You will see a simpler, rounder number for your wait time, though the actual wait might still vary if the system is busy or paused.

912a3f96607449b4b2915e6addd9b91db2333974.text: The system now checks what kind of device or app you are using, like a Mac or Windows computer. This information helps the team understand how the software runs on different machines. You will not see any changes in how the app works today because this only collects background details.

1b47ff6b79bfe5516520bd9bc28dee1c2a2c21c2.text: A small internal update adjusts the sample data used to check if the system's workload queue is healthy. It lowers the test queue size to match a stricter threshold set elsewhere. This change only affects the automated checks, so users will notice no difference in how the service behaves.

bf7bf87c62b0dba407d2ee2b03899d2c7ec13677.text: The system now checks the wait time for the slowest 10% of requests instead of the average request before deciding if the AI service is struggling. This change helps stop new free-tier users from joining a busy queue before most people notice slow responses. You would not see any visual changes, but the system reacts earlier to high traffic.

eeffc4f2b7cd78031922b0fd8b22c77f57557e4f.text: The team paused two internal checks that were failing randomly, not because the main software broke, but because the tests themselves were unstable. This change affects only the internal quality assurance process and does not alter how the application behaves for any users. Customers will not notice any difference in service, features, or performance.

3888bda6dbbd4b0dd55364e5781ae9d17b2661b5.text: The system now records the number of people waiting and actively using the free service every few seconds, rather than only when those numbers change. This change is internal and affects only the team monitoring the service, not the end users. Operations staff will see a complete, unbroken graph of demand over time in their dashboard, allowing them to spot traffic spikes instantly.

c0061ed43bee434c65385d84134b8f5dd2b1dd6c.text: The internal health check for the model service used by free sessions now marks it as warning sooner when the typical wait to begin generating text exceeds 0.125 seconds, instead of 0.2 seconds. This is live now. It affects only internal monitoring; a person watching the status would see the warning appear earlier, but no customer-facing behavior changes.

9278d13d86080c3293753ec84c110db59e73deab.text: The system now waits up to 30 minutes for complex AI responses to begin, instead of disconnecting after 10 minutes. This affects anyone using the web interface to ask difficult questions that require deep thinking. If you tried to get an answer and the connection dropped before the text started appearing, it should now stay connected long enough to deliver the response.

528904b505179630fec4697946d63df856a51e4c.text: Two automated checks that watch the assistant edit files and run commands are paused because they kept failing on their own. This change affects only the team's internal quality checks, not the software itself. A customer would notice nothing, as the assistant continues to work exactly as before.

060eb553eefe78c2d477e7363dfda2e3750aceb8.text: The system now flags free AI sessions as 'degraded' if the wait to start generating text exceeds 0.6 seconds instead of 1 second. This change is live for internal monitoring. Users might see slower responses earlier in the process, as the system adjusts load sooner.

87c6e90052b803282e0edd7017a42409e9b36784.text: Fixed a bug where the chat screen would look frozen with a blinking cursor after a free trial ended, even if the AI was still asking a question. Now, the question stays visible so you can answer it, and the 'trial ended' message only appears when no questions are pending. This change is live today.

59640d5c70dd5863abcdf66110b1b7247c66af05.text: The system now marks free AI sessions as busy earlier when they slow down or run low on memory. This applies to free-tier users. They may see wait times or reduced access sooner during high traffic, which helps prevent the service from becoming unresponsive.

4d6e4c343641ea3c6e8789ac8dee87eb5c35233e.text: The automated checks for the assistant's code-editing and terminal-command features now have a longer time limit to finish. This prevents the system from stopping a valid test just because it took longer than the previous ten-minute cap. This is an internal adjustment, so everyday users will not notice any change in how the product works.

d79dc99d54cde0766206015a188840cb46678613.text: The team added a written guide for engineers on how to safely connect their tools to the live product database. This helps staff run checks without accidentally changing real data. The guide is available to read now, but it does not change how the product works for regular users.

79becb7d0014169ea4b07db5f350afbcb8d29669.text: The command-line tool now shows remaining session time in the status bar when idle for free users. People using the free tier will see a countdown like '1h 30m left' or 'expiring…' when time runs low. This helps users track session limits without checking elsewhere. Live today for free tier users.

61914917527ec0b8842fe3a015e34c957b4e3578.text: A small internal update lets a specific test email skip the usual checks that require a paid plan or an old account. This change only affects automated testing tools, not regular customers. People using the service will notice no difference, as this simply makes it easier for the testing system to work without fake purchases.

5c0c0ac2515c4c1ca066fa70a22ddb4d3a4c0edf.text: We removed the waiting period and purchase requirement for using the paid AI assistant. People who signed up recently or haven't bought credits can now use the paid features immediately. You will notice that the assistant works right away after creating an account, without asking you to upgrade first.

07d2d7853bef1571195a1a9b051db169561ba40a.text: Internal engineers updated automated checks for subscription limits to wait longer before marking a test as failed. This fixes random failures when computers were slow, keeping the checks reliable. Customers see no change.

1401668addb1c937cbb5763314294f47f4c8abd1.text: The testing system now waits longer before giving up on checking the free version's features. This change fixes occasional false alarms that said the system was broken when it was just slow. Regular users will not notice any difference, as this only affects how the software checks its own health.

c341c025a0db4f1cf4c9586cee95aac61c126d2d.text: A small internal fix corrected how a code analysis tool counts lines in text files. It previously missed adding one line to the total. This tool is used to build summaries of software projects. The fix ensures these summaries show the correct line count.

553387c77c78e9f73dad13f01aa76605030008f4.text: The assistant now keeps conversation history active for ten minutes instead of five for free-tier users. This change is live. You might notice the AI remembering context slightly longer between messages, though it is invisible during normal chat.

9e0bca43b9da195068a60d936e04e5484f05be61.text: The free version of the assistant can no longer use a specific smart helper for complex tasks. This change is live today. If you are on the free plan, you will notice the assistant stops offering this extra help and may take longer or be less detailed on hard problems.

117cc3de13ecae4863068f4d4870ab01f60d8c25.text: Free accounts can no longer ask the assistant to use expensive AI models. If someone tries, the request fails with a permission error instead of running. This stops unpaid users from using up company money on high-cost models. This change is live today.

9f3f274bf654c394f76472e10eec2f5b683bbf6e.text: The chat assistant now lets people skip the usual checks that require an older account or a paid plan before using the service. This change is live today and applies to anyone sending chat requests. A person who tried to chat before would see a block message; now that block no longer appears for these special requests.

b992bec00d24351d7915f3ffb7ca9cf0c449f546.text: This was a small internal fix for the system's automated quality checks. It corrected how the test data was labeled to ensure the checks run smoothly without errors. No users will notice any change, as this only affects the behind-the-scenes testing tools used by the engineering team.

bd3cface754bc88769a451f1b6f9ee4d2c74fe04.text: Test accounts now have a fixed creation date. This helps internal checks pass. Users see no change.

24c7a015a526af5c874f809a96ea1740a7c9c337.text: New accounts no longer receive a free credit balance when they sign up. Existing accounts keep their current balance. This change is live today.

506c5ab18679267f9ef76a9051f1f4943cf7f0cd.text: A small internal update corrected the fake user data used during automated testing by adding a missing date field. This change affects only the testing environment and will not impact live applications or end users. No visible changes will occur in the product.

c1a63d8422c1b138b8a61e0dc27083b1f6145c4e.text: New accounts must be three days old and have paid money before using the assistant's full features. This stops people from making throwaway accounts to cheat the system. If you just signed up and haven't paid, your requests will be blocked today.

c7e2926787e8a817c260246ce75dfdb89a6c7c0d.text: A small internal billing fix. When an AI response stream cuts off early, the system now waits half a second and asks the provider for the final cost, so users don't get free tokens. This is live now.

63db864d994664afaa6b0b01b5a4a4a08fd14e88.text: The reward for inviting a friend is now zero. Existing records remain, but no new credits will be given to either person. This stops people from signing up repeatedly to get free credits.

c61e5d17a254cc80aac896edc1a7cb3472e41f83.text: A small internal fix corrected a mismatched label in the database's change log. This ensures the system automatically applies the correct database update without manual intervention. Internal tools and services will now sync their data structures reliably, preventing potential errors during automated updates.

c85611b367fb131b85f917fc943799d54363f43d.text: Developers added automated checks to ensure the system correctly finds and loads custom assistant instructions from various folders. This internal quality control does not change how the software behaves for you today. You will not notice any difference in your workflow or results.

fbb215c3b394bb8f70c501c7bbd24017a8bf0ae4.text: A new AI model has been added to the internal testing system. This change only affects the team running long-context tests and does not change what regular users see today. It allows the team to check how this specific model performs with large amounts of text and to track its costs.

0ff352d7420c8d8f9ffacdaea9e6b4568875c06a.text: The assistant now knows which specific AI engine it is using. It tells you this in its internal instructions. This change is live today. You might notice it if you ask the assistant what model it is.

a334a46deccf5e1caa990d649db6a232f453e1d8.text: The team updated the automated scoring tools to use newer, smarter versions of the AI models. They also reduced the number of tests run at the same time to prevent system overload. This is an internal maintenance task, so the results for regular users remain exactly the same.

b702ab96f9e87defdfd18594f0f494e9d284e1f5.text: The free version of the AI assistant now uses a newer, updated brain model for tasks like reading files and checking code. This change is live today for anyone using the free mode. You would not notice any difference in how the assistant works or looks.

d3bc905a3237c8ce84de761f6696803e8a40f840.text: Small wording change: the help pages and homepage now describe the free assistant as using a different chat assistant, and the old name was removed. Readers will also see a lower speed claim and the note that image attachments are not available in the free assistant. The text is live now, but the assistant’s behavior did not change.

6a1ef293a535c2af8503668e8839ca95ccd36009.text: The system now runs twice as many automated tests at the same time. This only affects internal nightly and standard test runs. The tests will finish faster, but no customer-facing features change.

6aa4eb23f3ad33ab5334eb8305474fec2d34772d.text: The system now translates thinking intensity settings into a format Fireworks models understand. Defaulting to medium, it applies only when reasoning is active. This internal plumbing allows those specific models to adjust their effort levels without breaking tool use. No visible changes for end users today.

326f91bb313f53fb16920855c6c9df7b43c325ce.text: Internal test checks for the AI routing system were updated to look for a newer model name instead of an older one. This change only affects the automated quality assurance tools used by the development team. Customers will not notice any difference, as the live service behavior remains unchanged.

af7ab3c768598a761f5b19519be416fdd9c862e0.text: The internal assistant that summarizes long conversations to save space now uses a different AI model. This change is live and affects anyone using the tool, though they will not see a visual difference. The goal is simply to improve how the tool handles and condenses chat history.

23efc014d99ccc747103b54a721bc28a356ce881.text: The AI helpers that write and review code now use the latest version of the main thinking model. This change is live for the paid plan, so the helpers will use the newer model automatically. The free plan keeps using its older, cheaper model, and people who previously set up their own tools can still use the old model if they want to.

f3957c64105e465c713227d0b77cb0f5c42258e3.text: The system can no longer use a specific AI model called MiniMax. People who previously used this model will now be automatically routed to a different one.

a2246d987caf879903aee6cb83886ca00eabef6f.text: A small internal update changed the name of a test tool to match its new setup. This only affects the engineers running automated checks behind the scenes. Customers will see no difference in the app today.

bec1d40804df694a6030c2f9900084e5ef5cfdb6.text: The website now recognizes a new AI model called Kimi K2.5. This change is internal and does not affect what regular visitors see or do.

36f9c1561ecd1d1a70aae3ec3edc914f01cb06d7.text: The free versions of the editing and reviewing assistants now use a different underlying brain, replacing the previous one. These assistants can also take twice as many steps to finish a task before stopping. You might notice slightly different results or that complex tasks run longer without cutting off.

629c552090515dd8e07488eac27309ca9e6c464a.text: The system now counts the extra instructions for tools when calculating usage limits. This ensures accurate billing for Claude models and prevents premature cutoffs for OpenAI and Gemini by applying a specific buffer. Users will see more precise tracking of their conversation length, avoiding unexpected stops during long tasks.

4965185c1a82c6cd29e55d5556c6308ceb2defb6.text: The assistant can now use the MiniMax M2.7 model. This change applies to the web interface and initial agent templates. Users selecting this model will see it available with specific per-token pricing rates.

a69c4f231456107591e85132186ce0c0b82b31d6.text: Pressing Escape on a question form now stops the assistant's response immediately. Previously, the text kept generating after the form was skipped. This small fix is live for CLI users.

ff498d0692371a4a14b0a3e4c3c2d53709ba5968.text: The assistant now checks the format of instructions sent to its helpers. This helps the helpers understand tasks like running commands or searching files without guessing. Nothing changes for you yet; this just makes the internal instructions clearer for the computer.

e001224735a444eeff4190f181c1e8c775d4a0f7.text: The command-running helper now returns the full text output by default, skipping the extra step of asking an AI to summarize it. To get a summary, you must now explicitly ask for it. This change applies to the internal helper tool and does not affect the main chat interface.

176eb0acaa9a773eab604411f2203f6f54953f09.text: The planning feature is now available in the free mode. This affects free users. They will now see the AI create a step-by-step list for tasks requiring three or more steps.

36c7dac32446692336ec0fed4a7d1471fb6030c8.text: The free-tier assistant now only uses its deep-thinking mode for complex problems, skipping it for routine edits. This change is live today. You will likely notice faster responses for simple tasks, while difficult requests still get the same careful planning.

284eea82b096e428c4a24de7fcf47410c8529211.text: The coding assistant now checks the entire project for errors, not just the recent changes, when working on the free plan. It also avoids rewriting whole files for small edits, saving time and preventing accidental data loss. These updates apply immediately to free-tier users.

975b87f312741fc6f9e815ee523b7419b2b2c801.text: When an automated helper rejects a task because the instructions were formatted incorrectly, it now shows the original text it received. This helps staff see exactly what went wrong without guessing, though very long messages are still cut off.

8537ffbb0aa735ab6d711fc652bd11ceb0d076c8.text: The tool now shows the first 100,000 characters of a large file instead of just 1,000. This affects anyone using the file reader in the SDK. They will see much more of the file content before the system stops reading and suggests using other methods to see the rest.

52a75b23037884cbf555f87530e5442d11f62812.text: The system now requires the assistant to explicitly state the exact command it wants to run, separate from the instructions on what to do with the results. This prevents the assistant from failing to execute tasks by sending incomplete requests. Users will notice fewer errors when the assistant tries to run basic commands.

ce142ff1af0292cfac040f7e7cc82402e1424145.text: A small internal adjustment updates the label for a specific testing setup used by staff to check software performance. This change affects only the background evaluation tools and does not impact any features available to customers. Nothing visible to users will change.

eaeec68115cdea97a0c39abb70b8025492bfe3ee.text: A small text update helps the computer understand how to run shell commands correctly. It only affects the automatic task runner. You will not notice any difference.

927f7722099850cff0b359c9f3f7d28be459c95c.text: Free-tier users will see the AI assistant pause to think and plan more often before answering questions. Instead of only thinking deeply for hard problems, it now uses a smarter reasoning mode for most requests to give better answers. This change is live and aims to improve response quality for those on the free plan.

e68a330a70788ea18964be0be64004d86c8be051.text: The system now automatically switches to a backup service if the primary one fails, covering more types of errors than before. This applies to internal operations and ensures requests are not dropped during temporary server hiccups. Users will not notice any visual changes, but reliability for these specific internal processes has improved.

a64c5cc462ef3da1ed159b2a103a9f8e926e790d.text: A small internal change lets the team save a detailed record of an AI's reasoning during certain tests. It only happens when someone deliberately turns on a specific option before starting the test; otherwise, nothing is saved. This helps the team review how the AI solved problems, but customers will not notice any difference.

b45ead77cf75a4f4f2b4c41184295446e9309386.text: The tool now reads the first 1,000 characters of any file larger than 100,000 characters, then stops. Previously, it ignored files bigger than 1 megabyte, so you saw nothing for those files. You will now see a short preview instead of an empty result.

cd1e4e16b21b0742472287db1f86af48b6acc6da.text: A small internal update added a missing payment reference to the testing setup. This affects only the automated tools used by the engineering team, not the live product. Nobody outside the team will notice any change.

d4f08ddeb63417f96c4ba9c7e30fd80e608b52a8.text: A background helper that thinks before answering now works faster and writes shorter notes. This change affects the free version of the tool. You would notice less waiting time and simpler, quicker responses from the assistant.

2df5e04d4e070ae1a75a7fb195654b626c771f7a.text: The assistant can now find and use new instructions that you created during your current conversation. Previously, it only recognized instructions that were ready before the session started. This means if you teach the assistant a new task, it can immediately apply that knowledge without needing to restart the chat.

d6769f7b647e6866397210dda0957bd180ea3b8a.text: The automated helper that runs computer commands now strictly requires a clear instruction alongside the command to ensure it understands the goal. The tool's description also specifies that it uses the Bash system, preventing confusion about which commands work. This small update affects only the helper's internal rules, so no visible changes appear to end users.

759536f390f1616d3e4f73ac9aa8e40c2d40f22c.text: A small internal fix ensures that when you choose to hide the AI's step-by-step thinking, it actually stays hidden. This applies to apps using specific connection settings for the AI service. You would notice fewer unwanted 'thinking' blocks appearing in the chat history.

66318e6a90d7de70353f12eeaf80b2c7058b8652.text: The website's text about how the service stays free now specifies that the ads are text-based. The description of the assistant's features was also updated to list specific tasks like code review and browsing, while adding 'and more' to show the list isn't complete. These are small wording changes on the public homepage.

caf904df1dba70f89294614c03fa39906d09fa90.text: The 'Stop' button in the command-line tool now displays in normal brightness instead of faded gray when not hovered. This change affects anyone using the tool and makes the button easier to read. The update is live.

c89706ad40999ddc78d23a062d26787fd212cbbd.text: The text on the command-line interface button that lets you stop the current action changed from 'Stop' to 'Esc'. This reflects the common convention that the Escape key interrupts execution. If you use the command-line tool, you will see the new label on the button.

ecc1502818ffdeef7c0a8d074f5f02bbb5b51e97.text: The system now checks its internal instruction guide and reference materials before performing tasks. This change affects the automated assistants, ensuring they follow current guidelines rather than relying solely on general knowledge. Internally, tools were also added to track how often these guides are consulted.

ff5f05819b65bdfcbd25b3f67c4ec1dd8130878d.text: The Freebuff homepage now lists nine specialized helpers instead of just three, adding a deep-reasoning tool that uses your ChatGPT subscription. The text describing these features is also slightly lighter in color. This update is live and affects visitors reading the site's feature descriptions.

bb432101d7f49b21528f013bebf610882f5d6afb.text: The command-line tool now recognizes when it crashes due to hardware incompatibilities, such as missing processor features. If the program fails immediately upon launch, it will display a specific error message explaining the likely cause rather than closing silently. This change is active in the current release and helps users troubleshoot startup failures on older or unsupported computers.

bc92e426ed46b2e0e36f445d859859675e559028.text: The system's background instructions are no longer automatically sent to the 'thinker' tool. This tool now relies only on its specific task prompts. It is live today. You might see clearer, more focused answers from this specific tool.

149a328add45abd7bc11cecd4ee0bec3c2d0fdf0.text: A small, internal fix improves the command-line tool's reliability when it crashes. Previously, if the program stopped suddenly, the terminal screen could remain distorted or hidden. Now, the program cleans up after itself, leaving the terminal in a normal, readable state.

571084860ec1996fc025e54911935ff59e722105.text: The command-line interface now arranges its information panels to fit the screen better. Small, collapsed items group together on one line, while large, expanded items take up a full line. This change is live and improves readability for people using the tool.

fa7a9595e40b9274416ac57d46ca2474b7d570a5.text: The system now allows AI agents to use a newer version of the Gemini model. This update affects the internal scoring tools used to evaluate agent performance. Users will not see any immediate changes, as this is a background adjustment to how the system judges quality.

5ca697b1fb19d7a2c270c3cd2266f920b8628f20.text: A small internal update now requires the AI assistant to follow strict formatting rules when using external tools. This change applies only to the Fireworks AI service. Users won't see any visual changes, but the assistant should make fewer errors when trying to perform actions like searching or sending data.

448db9644f4e3a13231905e15d9a9faca0cb7ca7.text: A small internal update improved a tool that tracks free-tier usage. It now shows detailed daily and hourly activity charts for specific user groups. Staff members use this tool to spot trends. Regular users will not notice any changes.

ec3f863b4fc3c158a975971a5633d8f0317636d1.text: When the assistant fails to use a tool, the error message now shows the exact instructions it tried to follow, limited to the first 500 characters. This helps support staff see what went wrong without digging through hidden logs. The change is active for all tool errors.

acef43db12096e373ff788fff9443bf01523b682.text: The command-line tool now runs in its own clean terminal space, hiding your previous screen while active. When you exit, it automatically restores your original view and clears the temporary display. This keeps your terminal history uncluttered during use.

946dd70655b5aca3929477e67877f1d6a3fd7584.text: The automatic checks for the command line tool now wait longer before giving up. This stops the tool from being wrongly marked as broken when the testing system is slow. Only the internal testing team sees this; customers notice nothing.

6bbf8ceebddb2347b03e358dba07c820f7142276.text: The login system can now use a separate set of credentials for the Freebuff service. If these new credentials are provided, the system uses them; otherwise, it continues using the existing Codebuff credentials. This change is not live today because the new credentials have not been configured yet.

ae389387291f5e23faa1e1392195593ea81b49c2.text: A small internal fix ensures the command-line interface displays nested agent information reliably. Previously, the software might have crashed or failed to render certain agent grids if they were empty or too deep. Now, the display logic runs consistently, preventing these visual glitches.

abe4eb8d07ac905d29a84ce6397dce7cef5c7f36.text: The login page now displays a dark green gradient background and frosted glass panels. Sign-in buttons changed to a dark gray style that glows green when hovered. These visual updates are live for all visitors accessing the sign-in screen.

088ce23eb3b6e81ffe376d02ac0ccd6a9a36d7a0.text: The website now automatically sends visitors from one web address to another. This affects only people who click a specific link starting with '/b/'. They will immediately land on the Beluga page without seeing an error.

67c066f27636e4016d3dcea7f0b002c9f1e9a610.text: A tool used by AI assistants to watch terminal screens no longer allows waiting for specific text to appear. Instead, the assistant must now wait for the screen to stop changing for a few seconds before taking the next step. This change is live and may make the assistant slightly slower or less precise when interacting with command-line programs.

71db42d0a57ade0f25939cedd4fab6060e41232f.text: Internal fix. Corrected test clock logic. Simulates 30-minute reset without hitting 5-hour limit early. No user impact.

5e8ed7bfaf21a0a33ad7c498ef064239a3525c81.text: Sign-up records now store which website created the account, marking them as either Freebuff or Codebuff. This data flows to the marketing platform. Users will not see any change.

c1b713e625d91c6c8e60899f4235b4c3b5b71c85.text: The limit on how many free chats you can start in a week has doubled. This change is live today. Regular free users will notice they can send more messages before hitting a pause.

c6128f73521d191ff7f1e60047f6486a5c2918e4.text: Freebuff users now sign in through freebuff.com instead of codebuff.com. This affects only the Freebuff version of the command-line tool. You will notice the web address change when the browser opens to approve your login.

42c96674ee31177b09bc05b4483909a9690a37df.text: The internal tool that tests how well AI agents follow instructions now ignores clutter like auto-generated dependency files and correctly separates setup documents from the agent's actual work. It also keeps a memory of previous document edits to avoid repeating failed suggestions. These fixes are active today for internal staff running the evaluation system.

1c5d74b8b0729556a69dc6f0e8fc1c0ab2a2174c.text: The sign-in button now darkens when the mouse hovers over it. This affects people trying to log in. It gives clearer visual feedback that the button is active.

2d599476c5131484e22f488f306d89526df625e4.text: The command-line tool now lists available actions when you ask for help. Users on the full plan see options to sign in and share their work, while free-mode users only see the sign-in option. This small update makes it easier to find these features without guessing.

9ca55a5f430b82d293a1a8035eed89e612d3cdb2.text: The system now correctly identifies the specific search terms and document titles when summarizing past actions. This fixes a labeling error where the assistant would show generic text instead of the actual request details. The change is live and affects how previous interactions are displayed in the history, making it easier to see exactly what was searched or read.

a8f35eae25cefcebf9ff85cce0fb28e7a668dc9c.text: The command-line tool now checks for a display server using a cleaner method. This affects Linux users running the tool without a graphical interface. You will notice no change, as the tool still skips opening a browser and shows the same warning.

6ca71dc98efecf951cc96f4ac3e0b6aa560cb6f8.text: A small internal fix corrected the location where the automated nightly quality checks look for tests, ensuring they now target the correct directory. This change affects only the internal testing system and does not alter the live product or user experience. No visible difference will occur for end users.

2b9c6ad7c87825fb63acc6ab00954d1bc9524bf9.text: A small change added a new option to the review screen in the command-line tool: 'Changes this conversation'. If someone uses that screen, they can now ask for a review of all edits made during the current chat, rather than only unsaved changes, a broader project comparison, or a custom request. It is available now in the updated tool.

65c4187f2e28a11c50b3c9e143f3362f328861b5.text: The Freebuff 'Get Started' page lost its floating navigation bar containing the logo and GitHub link. The main content shifted up to fill the empty space. Visitors to this specific page will see a cleaner layout without the top menu.

a01949c4e199540a788ea5159ae63fc7c59d6cc2.text: The AI assistant now always suggests three next steps after answering questions, instead of doing so optionally. It also stopped using a time-of-day rule that previously limited which AI model it used. This change is active today and affects anyone using the assistant.

8d0bbfb78f0ffafa963dbf606c63e57af75b31e3.text: The project's underlying software runner was updated to a newer version. This change affects the internal tools used by the development team, not the features available to you. You will not notice any difference in how the application behaves.

f2cfd899c2e71d25f69fdf3e8bdd962a4325d003.text: A small internal update simplifies how the system checks if it should use a special model. Instead of guessing based on the time of day, it now relies on a clear setting to decide. This change affects only the background checks, so customers will not notice any difference in how the service works today.

2e555ff878222bcf498dade93f7cb3df2ab95112.text: The command-line assistant now shows a clickable 'X' button on its sign-in screen instead of just telling you to press Escape. This lets you easily dismiss the screen to return to normal typing if you change your mind or encounter an issue.

7d7138e1f7e4cfca6975491fdd467018717e29ea.text: The project's main guide now lists a free version of the coding assistant that shows ads instead of requiring payment. This helps people who want to try the tool without paying, by giving them clear steps to start using it. The change is live today, so anyone reading the guide can see the new option.

953516b8f05bfc39c35b30a8ec762f68fca0e146.text: A previous workaround allowed custom deployments to start at any time of day. That workaround is now removed, restoring the rule that these deployments can only begin between 10 AM and 8 PM Eastern Time. This change affects only users who set up custom deployments. They will notice that attempts to start a deployment outside those hours are now blocked.

e78d48287319787a3d2a64b144bcc76c67298303.text: The website's 'Get Started' page now looks for a person's name using a clearer label in the web address, instead of a shorter, ambiguous one. This helps the page correctly display 'Name invited you to try Freebuff!' when someone shares a link. The change is live and affects anyone clicking an invitation link.

846076cc9b50bc4917ba2a020b4bf5e9f9aea00c.text: An internal system now points to a new private location for a specific AI model. This change is currently inactive and will not affect any live services or user experiences until a separate switch is enabled. If the switch were turned on, the system would use the new location to process requests for that model.

bc346d5d299af3d1c4c95a05012072c32dcd7807.text: A small internal fix corrected the address used to reach a specific AI model. This ensures that when the system tries to use this model, it connects to the right place. Most users will not notice any change, but the model should now work reliably without connection errors.

4036f839da0e6fb7790a0288b271fabf5dc953d7.text: The system is now configured to route requests to a specific, private server setup instead of the standard public one. This change is active today and affects the underlying model used by the assistant. Non-technical users will not notice any difference in the interface or immediate responses, as this is a small internal adjustment to the infrastructure.

546904add2511685af801fb09866d5c67d229196.text: A small update adds a tip to the command-line help menu, visible only to users on the free plan who have linked their ChatGPT account. This tip suggests a specific order for using available tools: first discuss your project, then make a plan, then build, and finally check your work. Users who have not linked their account will not see this new message.

ad659432d52d69c2172658c9e154c93ebaa96d8e.text: The assistant now accepts results in two different formats, fixing cases where a specific provider's strict rules previously blocked the tool. This affects agents using that provider, ensuring their final outputs are saved correctly without failing validation. If a mistake occurs, the assistant now shows the most helpful error message to guide its own correction.

dae55fdfe7024589b8d7b6b03f71ac798c1b75fb.text: A new safety check was added for free accounts using the chat feature. This check stops users from sending more than one message every second. It is not active yet, as the code was only added and not turned on.

7a2147533f1e73d451545edbd35f7238f180202b.text: Internal checks for the free mode request limits were updated to be more reliable. This change only affects how the system tests its own limits and does not change what users see or experience today.

f6a994b95e61d9b5fe8e3eac9996eb1dd312d35a.text: The service loosened its traffic rules for free-tier users, allowing twice as many requests per second and more per minute. Only free accounts are affected. They might notice fewer 'too many requests' errors if they use the tool heavily.

9a15b34b64bc4e27fc9946b1f122e3c1296089ba.text: The system now tags chat requests to show if they used a free mode. This helps the company track usage patterns. Regular users won't see any change in how the tool works.

78d22242fc0272fc1fffcb7dc8e11c65f62650ae.text: A small internal update now runs each browser session in a separate, temporary window. This stops leftover data from a previous task from affecting the next one. Regular users will not see any change.

305645d86822a91dbc775f595fb8c46c1e938183.text: When you log in, the system now marks whether you use the free or paid version. This helps the company tell the two groups apart in their records. You won't notice any change.

0e542543908c5aac088985127d0d9773675f35e1.text: The program now sets up its activity tracking tool before loading any project-specific settings. This fixes a rare startup crash that could happen if the settings tried to log a message before the tracking tool was ready. Users will not notice a visual change, but the command line tool is less likely to fail unexpectedly.

8d5530d30f22eced4b4121fc93425741f571e3ad.text: Internal reporting tools now show median and maximum requests per client, replacing average-only views. Test scripts send a session identifier so repeated queries reach the same server, improving cache hit rates. Staff will see these extra numbers and stable test results in internal dashboards.

0aa4b4a2b2640bfbe62e7db4bed3ca74bdd50aff.text: The command to connect accounts now works only for users on the Freebuff plan. If you use a different plan, typing that command will no longer do anything. This change is active today.

d5fdfe238f9f7994e68226db45970c9e748cc435.text: An internal test file was updated to include a required session identifier, fixing a build error. This change affects only automated testing tools, not live services. Customers will notice nothing.

3615f8e093a71ed66aab77d729e223d5a43c2aaf.text: The website now always uses the main Fireworks service to generate text, ignoring any special backup routes. This change is live today. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves.

afe8895a33fc3c6d600bee9b1291bd5b1a4f279a.text: The assistant now keeps the full details of file changes in its short-term memory, rather than just a brief summary of the differences. This helps the assistant remember exactly what was modified or proposed during a conversation. The update also stops the assistant from processing certain background tools like the library manager and browser automation.

8b391e482ac25b8c3eb93634e8102c2563d4cc07.text: The automated testing tool now uses a standard public model instead of a private one. This change affects internal quality checks and is live today. Users will notice no difference, as this only updates how the system verifies its own performance behind the scenes.

19a82f970a5661260a917e2506e679d8e440733c.text: The system now tags each request to the AI service with a unique session identifier. This helps the service remember previous context, potentially speeding up responses for active conversations. The change is live and affects all users interacting with the AI.

0c471f89c97d1a59149f15b822325cbc83696486.text: The automated systems that build and test the software were updated to use newer, more secure versions of standard tools. This change affects only the internal infrastructure that prepares the software for release, so customers will not notice any difference in how the application works.

ba2b7f09639dd52b3455bc7d4c6cecbfc6f2865e.text: The command-line tool now shows a specific message when the free service is blocked in your region, rather than a generic error. This affects people using the free version outside supported areas, who will see a clearer notice about availability. The company also added New Zealand to its list of supported countries and updated its speed claims.

97841ca2cf22c0bb84d779fd7f81e0cc8cfba71c.text: The program now looks for a specific text tool only in its own folder, ignoring copies in other places. This prevents the tool from grabbing the wrong files when multiple versions exist. Regular users will see no difference, but the command-line program is less likely to crash or fail to load during startup.

a967c6e936ae8cc5d880b7b03eb46f6db6f2d9bb.text: The build process now searches a wider area to find the terminal interface's core files, specifically looking for uniquely named versions first. This ensures the tool works correctly when installed in complex project setups where files are shared. Users won't notice a difference, as this is an internal fix to prevent potential startup errors.

8ddecbc32ae834589e7c117278110b846ecca378.text: The tool now keeps the session window open after the program finishes. This lets the team read the final screen text for troubleshooting. Only internal tools are affected.

496279d0f4f8f7f026cb0e4a301a8d4b7fc865bf.text: Fixed a bug in the text editor where the cursor position and scrolling were calculated using the wrong data. This change is live. Users typing long text with line wrapping will see the cursor stay on the correct line and the view scroll properly when typing or deleting.

4afe5ddfce9ecbebda62fb155060a29a0eb6cd07.text: The command-line tool now removes invisible formatting codes from pasted text, preventing garbled input when copying from colored terminals. It also improves how text is copied to your system clipboard during remote sessions by using a more reliable method. These changes are live today.

cab81d0e6908fa90f377b3c6bfae2967f3649cab.text: The automated checks now build the program before testing it. This fixes failures where the test could not find the program file. Regular users will not notice any difference.

fa4fa5c6b53f6d2738346cd7687d28fba9a2ea71.text: The automatic publishing process for the Freebuff tool now runs a full system check before releasing a new version. If this check fails, the release is stopped. This change is live today and affects only the internal release process, not the end-user experience.

ac433e6920693a653d3392077d297b490779dbd9.text: The AI interview command now appears before the planning command in the text tool's list. This change is live today. You would notice the interview option listed first when typing a slash command.

0eba219ede87a8c8712489b3a5a5ab190dc19992.text: The text box now catches pasted text even when the window is not focused, such as during file drag-and-drop. This prevents the paste from being lost or split into messy characters in certain terminals. The fix is live, so pasting content into the input field will work reliably without needing to click inside the box first.

436817ae59687e1e192d10213a8facf43ad3c5b2.text: The website's help section was updated to show clearer answers about which AI models are available and how user data is handled. Visitors will now see information about new features like browser automation and a step-by-step guide for complex tasks, along with a promise that future data training will be optional.

9367f31e3f5af6725e18ea8b8aefebdc1cf100e2.text: The startup screen no longer shows a flashing tagline under the logo. This change affects only people using the command-line tool on the free version. They will see a cleaner, static logo instead of the animated text.

8aadbbe8061e7088a6d364ae2198a5616eef1d3b.text: The terminal interface was refreshed to its latest version, fixing minor bugs and improving performance. This update is live for all command-line users, though you may only notice subtle improvements in how the screen updates or handles text.

f994c8d1139555f94ca5ed6ba533862c7ffb03f1.text: The app now hides the animated 'working' symbol inside closed task groups. This stops the cluttered screen when several tasks run at once. You only see the symbol after you click to open that specific group.

a4fa669c020282e34620ce1a4bcd7183c7dec4d5.text: Automated checks for the command-line tool now wait longer for the screen to load and only require visible text instead of specific branding. This change affects the internal testing process and does not alter the tool's behavior for end users.

d2ba4cef9ae65da25bed5bff3f8856a79a51fa9a.text: The automated system stopped running a specific check for restrictions on how the assistant operates. This change affects only the internal testing process, not the software used by customers. No one will notice any difference in the assistant's behavior or features.

5e21d8a169f62b3ca201fa2e2ae2dcdda3906826.text: The system now checks the country tag sent by the web service hosting the site before guessing the country from the internet address. This helps free users in the United States and Canada access the service more reliably, especially if the address lookup is slow or blocked. The change is active immediately for free mode requests.

34e7ba56803e2d7c0117f53603b01d8bb21ee81b.text: The automated testing system now waits for the application's main screen to fully display before running checks. This internal change prevents false failures when the app starts slowly. Developers will notice more reliable test results, but everyday users will see no difference in the application's behavior.

af302c3677798d0e10cb709b70af8983d9a93670.text: The assistant now checks if the web browser Chrome is installed on your computer. If Chrome is missing, the assistant avoids trying to use the browser tool and instead tells you it needs Chrome to proceed. This prevents failed attempts when the browser is not available.

ad37d317e83d0c2102e1e847eb5144f69d12fb2c.text: A small visual update now shows a blinking 'working...' message next to a subagent whenever it is actively processing a task. This affects only the command-line interface and helps you see that the system is busy without checking the code. The change is live today.

bd2276b98669efd76b968fe3fe2253c8a249ca3a.text: The assistant now shows clearer error messages when a request fails. This helps people in unsupported regions understand why their request was blocked. You might see specific error codes or messages instead of generic failures.

70d797f327ad76f34188745720fcfb00c578f068.text: A new command lets the assistant ask questions about a request before writing code. It gathers details through several rounds of conversation and saves them to a plan document. The assistant stops after creating this plan and does not change any files. This feature is available today in the command-line tool.

f2350eca2bd211bd25a64478537f2968b921be9b.text: New Zealand is now on the list of places where people can use the free version of the AI coding tool. This change is live. Users connecting from New Zealand will now be able to access the free features without needing a paid plan, just like users in the US, UK, and Australia.

a0acfcebfe71291893fad20243dc1878b9845fbf.text: A small visual update adds a glowing subtitle under the logo. The word 'free' pulses with light in a wave pattern. This change is already live for the free version of the tool.

8df7b4d10604e41cdd816e0f9055b224a756b710.text: The assistant now reads the server's explanation when a request fails, instead of showing a generic error. This helps users who encounter blocks, like access restrictions, by displaying the specific reason from the server. The change is live in the current tooling.

8d9b6c96fa37ebf843d0576046afb4bffd73abf7.text: The text box now stops leaving empty space where a hidden button would be. This fix applies only to the free version of the tool. You will notice the input area looks slightly tighter, with no gap on the left side.

e70d0892277b28235a2b43ef4f6b0f6fccda03d1.text: The 'plan' command is now hidden from the standard version of the tool, appearing only in the free version. Users of the standard tool will no longer see 'plan' in their list of available commands. This change is live today.

1195b01792da977a0e8634fe269359802855e993.text: The help screen now lists quick tips, including how to reference files or cancel actions. For free-tier users who haven't linked their account, it specifically shows a prompt to connect to unlock advanced planning and review features. This change is live and appears immediately when viewing help.

c6cf9db30789c4c56d264024faa527463bfc864d.text: Freebuff's website now lists the 15 countries where the service is available in its frequently asked questions section. This change is live and helps visitors from the US, Canada, UK, Australia, and 11 European nations immediately see if they can use the product without searching for more information.

d0cc3a429f603da41749352ef1a8e78799b47cb2.text: The service now allows free access from more countries, including the UK, Australia, and several European nations. This change is live and affects people trying to use the basic version of the assistant from these locations. Previously, only users in the US and Canada could use it for free; now, those in the newly added regions can also access it without paying.

799c317d48d98e4090f78ce52078e909aac70242.text: When typing in the chat, the tool now shows and inserts the agent's unique ID instead of its friendly display name. This small internal change affects anyone using the command-line interface to mention agents, making the visible reference text less human-readable.

70da96a9b41ca28173eda9595eecb8da4fb47a52.text: The system now lets the assistant choose a specific server for its answers instead of always using the main one. This setting is ready but does nothing yet. No visible changes occur for anyone today.

b1e00515d7f86dbf24145f7cd8aac084d27e6fb0.text: The wording on the main screen and help pages for the free coding assistant changed to focus on simplicity and speed instead of calling it the strongest. New questions explain that it costs nothing because it shows ads, and that it does not use your code to train the AI. Anyone reading the website or instructions will see these updated descriptions and the new list of supported AI models.

7f62993f7408682aea0ba3b15b6af4b510a2fa95.text: The text shown next to two specific actions in the command menu was updated to name the exact model used for those tasks. This affects only people using that menu. They will now see the specific model version listed instead of a generic name.

ad61a1c83345d5ae36e236ea7eee50e378fad197.text: The tool now shows a text mark instead of a picture when you type commands. This only affects people using the command-line interface to run system tasks. You would see the little indicator next to your typing look slightly different and use more space.

fec627712ea8a9404bf80daa60f0d2d85e87952f.text: The main assistant and its choice-making helper now use a newer version of the GPT model. This only affects the parts of the system that were already set to use GPT, not the ones using Claude. Regular users will not notice any difference, as this is a small internal update to keep the software current.

aadbb4be06d0ed4a0ec75c4d2fec73b57bb412db.text: When you start connecting your account in the command line tool, it now opens the login page automatically and shows a clear message instead of asking you to paste a code. You will see a bordered panel with the link and can press Escape to cancel. This change is live today.

b6f81763204cc7fc69346b0731035c76b92ab44c.text: The instructions for asking the deep-thinking helper for help were changed. It affects the assistant’s request to that helper. If you looked at the request, you would see a much shorter note instead of a long setup message, because the helper already sees the conversation history. The change is in place now.

2013d45f59d629515cc3e90393b8d938223ce755.text: The system's internal directory of which artificial intelligence models handle specific tasks has been updated. It now assigns newer models for complex reasoning and consolidates several quick tasks like file searching and web research to a single, faster model. This change is live immediately and affects how the system routes requests, though users will not see any visible interface changes.

0c9043e39c1ca866b9c65799fa5c494c96815d9c.text: The system now ignores a special private connection for one AI service and uses the standard public connection instead. This switch is active immediately. Internal users will not see any difference, as the service continues to function normally.

37a87f8e75ae11c90fc36e9660235cf4711562af.text: Two previously hidden features are now live. You can use the review command and connect your ChatGPT account.

d212c62159bded47a70d599b740b59d937e10318.text: The free AI coding assistant no longer displays a message stating that ads are required. This change applies only to the Freebuff version of the tool, ensuring the warning does not appear for users of that specific service.

120729c8d54f26de85bef668cc0e5da67a716fc0.text: The ad banner now responds to clicks anywhere on it, not just the buttons. The 'Ad ?' label that shows more info is hidden for free users.

03ffe85e538b3ea5afb8a9f8943aef01c45771c0.text: The code review command now uses a different assistant. People using the free plan will not see this change, as the new assistant is turned off for them. The review results might look slightly different for paid users.

a97a1c6d12bfa1d20ae8c27f2b4d8d3d4a37f12c.text: The system now prepares helper tools before checking if the command-line program works correctly. This change fixes a testing glitch that only appeared when the system automatically checked the code. Developers will notice that these automatic checks pass reliably instead of failing randomly.

3a469f8e39d543e758f96bd149f2cf2922d44b32.text: The landing page headline and description were shortened to remove superlative claims. Visitors see 'the free coding agent' instead of 'The Strongest Free Coding Agent' in browser tabs and search results.

0f77739bef572c0d717fd12abf2d5e75126282e8.text: The chat assistant now sends certain requests to a different service provider behind the scenes. This switch affects only streaming conversations for specific models. You likely will not notice any change in how the assistant behaves or responds.

44084a06cd88c1402dd962c47c1972a118358e00.text: The internal quality-check system now uses a different, free AI assistant to test the code. This change only affects how the team measures performance and does not change anything customers see or use.

cb57c6646303cca800943b0ae9d018e291b93bb6.text: The system now correctly identifies and runs automated checks for specific billing and logout features. This internal fix ensures these tools work as intended, but users will not see any changes in the application itself.

bc4f68a015730597836bc4b56f73d564bc04b8db.text: The free version of the coding assistant now checks where the request comes from and rejects it if the location is outside the United States or Canada. This affects people using the free plan in other countries. If you try to use the free assistant from abroad, you will see a message saying the free option is not available there and you need to upgrade to a paid plan to continue.

26887d8a5a972c250cc792e14e31b0871913f2fa.text: A hidden limit stopped AI assistants from writing very long answers. Removing it lets them finish longer tasks without cutting off early. Most people won't notice anything, unless they've asked for a huge amount of text.

06250cce4548b652a0d978fcd631a3c864e093fc.text: The landing page copy button now shows a green particle burst and glow when clicked. This visual feedback confirms the command copied to the clipboard. No functional change for users.

61dbb26699328e0d2b636c8353ca7ae6060d9787.text: A new 'Install guide' button was added to the Freebuff landing page. Visitors can click it to reveal a simple, four-step set of instructions for getting started, complete with easy-to-copy commands. This helps new users understand exactly how to install and run the software without needing to search for separate documentation.

f092bf89a849e45392c80d88dd5d02d4a0fceb19.text: The system now sends certain live chat requests to a different provider called CanopyWave instead of Fireworks. This switch is active for supported models in the web interface. Users of these specific models will notice no visual change, but their messages are being processed by a different company's infrastructure.

be8555388e2dadcf95b9b51cc2ceed12252acf9e.text: The website's main green color changed from a bright neon shade to a slightly yellower green. This affects visitors to the landing page, who will see the new hue on buttons, text highlights, and background glows. The bottom of the page also lost a small link crediting another company, replacing it with just the copyright notice.

54b1803c12a229de41ae93bf37cbd48fbf4ae781.text: The assistant can now use a specific model provider that was previously turned off. This change affects only users who select that particular model. You will notice the assistant starts working with this model again, while other providers remain disabled.

8b107a0ab89f0bdf9950d4af8db021049885e653.text: The command-line tool now finds its built-in assistants more reliably. Previously, it used a flexible method to look for these files, which sometimes failed if the files were missing during testing. This update switches to a strict, direct lookup. For end users, this means the tool will consistently load its default assistants without the occasional glitch of missing features.

683f6d1c8eb99d8e74da94ce9e56e75f65f85925.text: The system now sends specific requests for a particular artificial intelligence model directly to a different service provider instead of using a middleman. This change affects only users interacting with that specific model. They will notice no difference in the conversation itself, as this is an internal routing adjustment that does not alter the visible output or interface.

8c077776cc855efa89d066e504ded3402611d0a7.text: The setup guide now lists a spot to enter a specific service password. This only helps staff who run the software on their own computers. Regular users will not see any difference.

1390d31043560aa8a653072bab2aeee4e094d7b1.text: The free plan's chat assistant now reaches its chosen model through a middleman service instead of connecting directly. This switch is active today. Users on the free tier will not see any visual changes or notice a difference in how the conversation works.

454dbb9eab7ab3b9a48b93b2d904a0195bc28f89.text: The theme-switching tool was upgraded to match the new website engine. A small code cleanup removed an outdated reference. This keeps the dark and light mode toggle working correctly. Users will notice no visual change, but the site is now stable for future updates.

281a5f52ef9c3a605acea7202a68a9e743d700b2.text: The Freebuff homepage now shows fewer details, removing the list of features and login buttons. Visitors see a simpler page with just the main headline and basic links. This change is live today for anyone visiting the site.

037ae3fe6c825b5f3d851911aad737a1e6455356.text: The website's main page was updated to include a new section highlighting its speed, simplicity, and built-in features. The introductory text was changed to emphasize that users can begin immediately without needing a subscription or any setup. These changes are live and visible to anyone visiting the homepage today.

b872dc945f3985a845747a2981c31200227b4173.text: The file that lets the assistant use a terminal was moved to a different folder. This is an internal cleanup that changes nothing about how the software works or what people see.

aaebab6ba804107ea5fc2277c287fb14d348b7b6.text: The project now sets the React type definitions in one central place instead of repeating the rule in two separate folders. Developers will notice less clutter in the configuration files and fewer chances for conflicting settings.

f29ccc3e1876a5708f2589aaaa6ba667af47ce31.text: Free-plan users now get their AI answers from a new computer service instead of the old one. This switch is live and affects only the free tier. You likely will not notice any change in how the assistant behaves or what it can do.

36aa67ce5bb84e07bceb94d1173995dade9b2f9f.text: The tool now sets up its testing environment in a single step instead of multiple separate actions. This change is live today and affects all users. You would notice slightly faster startup times when the tool begins a new task, with no visible difference in the final results.

ac11f0809762c0c450be227d08607f5a698b5fa9.text: The text display in the command-line tool now automatically removes extra blank lines from the start and end of the assistant's responses. This affects anyone using the tool to view generated text. You will notice cleaner spacing in the output, with no unnecessary empty lines at the beginning or end of the message.

ee5e984f9b354d71352cbca1ef9453fcb1e94ea4.text: The text-based assistant now spaces its replies evenly, removing the uneven gaps between text, images, and tool results. This internal layout fix is live today. You would notice cleaner, more consistent vertical spacing in the conversation history.

7dc3fb96a92c35a2ac7703f2fb11359a12f6e7a9.text: A small visual update was made to the text-based task list. The program now adds a bit more space between the checkbox symbols and the task descriptions. This change makes the list easier to read and is already active.

db37b85cf3e0e64e0beab185886ea30fc43b2dde.text: The tool that shows changes to files now cleans up the edges of the display. If a list of changes had empty spaces at the very top or bottom, those blank lines are gone. This only affects how the list looks on your screen, not the actual work the tool does.

853643090200cdc81d726d5624f823b0c87011dc.text: This change adds a visual effect to a specific text style on the website. When a user hovers their mouse over this text, it fills with a glowing green color instead of remaining as a transparent outline. This effect is live for visitors viewing the page where this text style is used.

17612d804f3826973857304988d4c6cd08a0b322.text: The AI assistant now searches for files directly instead of asking separate helpers to do it. This change affects only the assistant's internal instructions and is live today. A non-programmer would notice no difference in the final answer, just a slightly faster or smoother search process behind the scenes.

a5aa4a5044ac3d47e494cebb025253ff215d43a3.text: The system now records token counts from each assistant request into a saved debug snapshot. This only affects internal cache diagnostics when a special debugging mode is active. Developers running cache comparison scripts will see exact hit rates, but regular users will notice no change.

a6026d1f5fb63b6f0ee4d122e95c05ba6a329e62.text: Free plan users can no longer ask the assistant to suggest edits to files. This restriction applies only to the free tier and does not affect paid users. If you are on the free plan, you will notice that the option to propose changes is missing from the assistant's capabilities.

9fa5e732e6003051c79304b62761a3b2e3253f10.text: A small internal update helps the team figure out why the assistant sometimes forgets previous context. It now groups related sessions together and ignores harmless formatting differences that used to look like errors. This change only affects the internal debugging tool; regular users will not notice any difference.

560f0ace43a7e2bcf5eebbfa7bb838503e411aef.text: The system stopped writing detailed notes about its memory cache while running live. This change affects the background assistant engine and reduces log clutter. Normal users will notice no difference in how the assistant responds.

580d90521384fa40268af32eead85438fd65abf3.text: The assistant can now search files and list folders for all users, removing the previous limit that restricted these features to paid plans. This change is live today. Users on the free tier will notice the assistant can now find and organize files without prompting for an upgrade.

a73857232d3ab61ed1d12790ecac5399f92ac92e.text: The free version of the AI assistant now performs search and file listing tasks directly, rather than delegating them to separate helper programs. This change ensures the assistant processes these requests one at a time, preventing technical conflicts that occurred when multiple helpers tried to work simultaneously. The update is currently live for all free-tier users.

b2c27168a27cc9da6a838be38d1b8c7a5b304718.text: The free version of the command-line tool now has fewer options. Users of this specific free tool can no longer choose a specific assistant type, clear old logs, or start with a pre-typed message. The paid version still has all these options.

ee320c3b975f1f75f073ec2c4d3752c18e3ca04b.text: A small internal fix corrected how the system reports problems when it checks its setup settings. This change is live today. Only developers running the software would see the difference, and only if the setup fails; the error message will now show the correct details instead of being blank.

ed1100f857836154e655880272ece2b2e033d3fb.text: The command that created a knowledge file has been removed from the free version of the tool. If you try to use it, it will no longer appear in the list of available options. This change is live today and affects only people using the free version.

cfb6cbe07b75cbef94ddc92ea79b9c7b5a9d3adc.text: A guide for new team members was updated to list the specific passwords and settings needed to run the software on a personal computer. This helps internal developers avoid common startup errors by clarifying exactly what to change before launching the app. The document is available now, but it only affects people setting up their own work environment.

3c5f2b81ef5375c90a218b0d6e3e65cf58a14229.text: Internal automation for publishing software updates was refreshed to meet current platform rules. This affects only the release process, not the software itself. Users will notice no changes.

417b5ba3a4297703716d4e72791ed38dbadff99d.text: When you open the full view of the assistant's reasoning, the text now keeps its original line breaks instead of squishing everything into one block. This helps you read lists and separate paragraphs more easily. The short preview remains a single line to save space.

a45e5363c132b97909f6a97060e9b53ec65800ba.text: A new shortcut was added to the internal setup menu. It lets the team start a specific tool in a special test mode. This change is for the team only. Customers will not notice anything.

f658c35076ea52904412b671e168fdc382cba0ed.text: We updated the automated building tools to match a new version of the underlying system. This affects how our software is automatically packaged and tested. You won't notice any changes, but it ensures our future updates continue to build correctly.

f90fbb70c5b64cfcee458e25288cefd6c935f149.text: In the special free version of the assistant, commands to switch between different working styles are now hidden from the list of available options. Regular users will not see any change. This adjustment affects only the free-tier interface, keeping the command menu cleaner for that specific group.

a15b697b15ce465ef6b795a5579b534b9ae4a5ac.text: The AI assistant can now correctly read instructions for tools that use a specific advanced layout format. Previously, these instructions appeared blank to the assistant, causing it to ignore the tool's requirements. This fix ensures the assistant understands how to use these tools properly. The change is live today.

af94dfb0e1b78acf86e55af4df5e8717ebdf8a7a.text: The command-line tool now checks only the first word after the command name to decide if you want to publish. This stops the tool from mistakenly starting the publish process if the word 'publish' appears later in the command, such as inside a file name or a setting. This fix is live today for people using the tool to manage releases.

2237ce99e973141912d251e90ea69144dd78e772.text: The assistant now shows the correct error text when it fails to save a file. Before, it showed a blank or broken message instead of the reason for the failure. This only affects people who ask the assistant to write or save files.

c4d97b201a80accb2dde5134ef53f656386fe287.text: The web application now finds a specific database tool through a shared internal folder instead of installing its own copy. This cleanup stops the app from carrying duplicate software files. Users will see no change in how the website works or looks.

9a6cc9d95123a1587958dc38f95415b5b3ca2854.text: The system now shows a clearer message when startup settings are wrong. This helps people fixing broken configurations see exactly what went wrong. The change is active immediately.

a54e61b66c6f64af8e61791d106c8548222a6b3d.text: The system now handles errors in a specific debugging feature more gracefully. If the debugging tool fails to record its data, the main task continues without interruption instead of stopping completely. This change affects only the internal monitoring process and does not alter how the assistant answers questions.

19d1cd67d2075b8e47c0f4889bd4898715ce399e.text: The command-line tool now checks a new setting to see if it should run in a free-only mode. This change is internal plumbing that makes the tool's configuration more consistent. Regular people will not notice any difference in how the tool works today.

27d4960d7467b1464a50fcd89fe28c759356e3de.text: The assistant changed how it names folders for new work sessions. It removed colons from the names because some computer systems reject that symbol, which could have caused errors. Regular users will not notice any difference.

de29db72df8d9fd2823f92a936f99b6bac42a972.text: The download system now checks the file name to pick the right storage shelf. This prevents freebuff files from accidentally grabbing codebuff files. Users downloading freebuff tools will now get the correct file.

b1957203eeb51dba493a545f238baa672aadde9c.text: Two helpers that look through your files now use a newer, lighter AI brain. This applies only when you pick the 'max' setting for finding files. You might see slightly different files get chosen, but the speed and cost should stay about the same.

3c28d5fdb0e7e037023c02e165369fb6828f7d0a.text: The default assistant swapped its internal brain to a new, cheaper, and faster model. This change applies to the built-in helpers that search documents, browse the web, and run commands. You will notice these tasks complete more quickly with no visible difference in how you use them.

b493ab53110787a9c1cc7a02faf624ed4368a8f9.text: The software's list of approved AI assistants was updated to include several new options from major providers. This change is live and applies to all users. You would notice the new choices appearing in the dropdown menu when selecting a model for your tasks.

ed23be94063b44aa0c8e721380a80928ed5d55fb.text: A background helper that guides complex coding tasks now thinks harder before answering. This affects the main planning assistant, making it slower but more thorough. The change is live today.

5d98e790131598e3f38f2b43031e10e4d3a8bf5e.text: The free version of the assistant now always sends requests to one specific company to handle its answers, instead of letting other companies try. This ensures the free model behaves the same way every time and prevents those other companies from collecting your data. If you use the free plan, you will notice more consistent responses from the same underlying service.

618a31581235d86e760779180eee8b476b7662e9.text: The deep agent's work process was streamlined by merging two steps into one, reducing the total number of phases from eight to seven. This change affects users who ask the agent to implement complex features. They will notice the agent now drafts a written plan for the feature and asks clarifying questions in a single combined step, rather than doing these as separate stages.

8a449e81a4a8062056d71cc8c03ee08d19e4520d.text: A small internal fix ensures the comparison table on the knowledge files help page displays correctly. Readers looking at that specific page will now see a neat, readable table instead of broken text lines.

a051d6395f9ebd84f1dcfc5c5c1e4fa534ec5b33.text: A small internal cleanup fixed the visual spacing in a guide about setting personal versus project rules. This change is live today, but readers will not notice any difference because the text on the screen stays exactly the same.

c29bbc207e8ceede2f0b877aab6a76c01f273323.text: The free version now accepts dated names for allowed assistant models, so a permitted model can still work when the model supplier returns a name with a date attached. Only people using the free version are affected. They would notice fewer false blocks when checking which model can be used. The change is live today.

69b64047d85d7aa17986b3d7ec47aa1af35ad0f6.text: The AI assistant now leaves your other open files alone while working, preventing accidental loss of unsaved changes. It also refuses to save short-term task details into its long-term memory, keeping its knowledge base clean. This is active immediately for anyone using the assistant.

f09f86cba11df88d5c46a3f10971c631dc5b5893.text: The assistant now uses a newer, more capable model for complex reasoning and code review tasks, replacing the previous version. This change is live today. Users will not see any visual differences in the interface, but the underlying thinking and review processes may produce slightly different results.

df5a04df20ca02720f3f986a88c04de9b2043965.text: Paying subscribers of the command-line tool no longer see promotional messages or the commands to turn them on. This change is live and applies only to accounts with an active subscription, while free users continue to see the usual ads.

b5cf55edd5737f8dc858fbf424f8ee885aeb06cc.text: The internal system used for testing software performance now uses a different, more capable version of its automated assistant for these checks. This change affects only the internal evaluation tools and not the products used by customers. No customer-facing features or behaviors will change as a result of this update.

f9bfec097638416ef3d1757b7fea3c83ed61b8d2.text: The command to link a personal Claude subscription is now disabled. If you type it, the tool will show a message telling you to subscribe to the service instead. All Claude-specific connection prompts and status displays are hidden from the interface.

be3c2a3d639710f50d2f6daa7573320d02e85ebd.text: The pricing page now shows a small question mark next to each plan. Hovering over it reveals how many credits you get for every dollar spent.

51bf4282d902f44d797956ef786b85d02e9ec640.text: The Discord helper now asks for the main email tied to your GitHub account instead of just any email. If you try to connect your accounts, the helper will show a direct link to the settings page where you can find that specific email address. This helps prevent connection errors caused by using a secondary or old email.

7612d494f6ba94f0641abf30410adbc21a3ffb86.text: A small internal fix stops the system from looking at skill files when it searches for agents. This keeps the two types of instructions separate. Users will not notice any visible change.

f67ecd430e3766470583662754da873a9c14dedd.text: The system now counts a subscriber's monthly credit allotment before checking their balance. Previously, newly issued credits were not recognized until a later step, so a subscriber could be wrongly told they lacked funds. This affects only paid subscribers using the assistant through the web interface.

b7dfc25889af3fcaf6ff17147ea8d5987d252cc4.text: Paid subscribers who had exhausted their extra credit balance were previously blocked from using the assistant, even if their subscription still had available usage. The system now checks subscription status before rejecting requests, allowing these users to continue working. This fix is live today and resolves a minor billing logic error.
