44db78128e3e40441b4b7945e3b1349455870f37.text: Added a translation rule so the system recognizes a new AI model version when accessed via a third-party provider. This affects users routing requests through that provider. They will see the correct model respond instead of an error or wrong version.

6d01d07189ca915f61757a74da8eed6e431c8dc4.text: The $100 plan now gives 20% more usage per session and per week. The $500 plan gives 5% more. The website pricing page was updated to show the new limits. These changes are live today.

9552ba579472f17797bf9350982444258e7618b4.text: The software now has a new way to update existing files, alongside a simpler tool for creating or replacing entire files. This change affects the code editing tools used by the assistant. Users will notice that partial updates to files are now handled more reliably, but the old method of marking unchanged parts of a file with comments no longer works.

de5a6d9cdd7d30b6066ea2b967cd176051dab988.text: The system now uses a single method to estimate message length for all requests, ignoring which specific service was requested. This change is active immediately. People checking usage limits might see slight differences in calculated counts, but no new features or visible buttons changed.

a8dd0f4d5f2ccf7eee5a455bf172127031d8d815.text: The command-line tool now sets up its usage tracking before loading custom agents. This prevents the tool from crashing if an agent tries to log a message during startup. This is a small internal fix; users will not notice any change in how the tool works.

f6607057b83163683840f5ef1f061a905fa77537.text: The quick-start guide was shortened by removing detailed explanations and troubleshooting steps, replacing them with simple links. This affects people reading the help website. They will see less text on the main page and must click links to find the removed details.

427e35f32dd64d15a118db9ac88cf4c93b973d84.text: The table listing models used for main tasks and sub-tasks was broken and unreadable. It now displays correctly with proper rows and columns. This affects only the internal documentation page about model usage.

1226e08dc65010d303b274d2578e471923d4fead.text: The help guide was updated to show users where to find the program's files if they need to delete them to fix problems. Instructions about clearing old data or checking internet errors were removed because they no longer apply. These changes affect only the written help text, not the software itself.

e9cbb031f37a29a3ff75673f8aed0545c75a2d3d.text: The guide for setting up the coding tool was corrected. It previously claimed one command started everything, but that was wrong. Now it explains you must start the website first, then open a separate window for the command line. This helps new helpers avoid errors when trying to run the tool.

14fbb52ffa1149b49cf9293371cc5531ee08dae9.text: Turning on automatic balance top-up now triggers a warning if the current balance is already below the set limit, requiring confirmation to avoid an instant charge. This safety check applies to all accounts using the feature. The default top-up trigger amount also increased from 150 to 500 credits.

e96fc5bc74a277a2c963ca27c994de467656eca8.text: This is a small internal fix for the testing tools used by the software's creators. It ensures the fake data used in tests matches the expected format, preventing errors during development. Customers and end users will not notice any changes, as this only affects how the software is checked for quality behind the scenes.

aed5699db1345178ed99d031a97a57570430aef9.text: The ad banner in the command-line tool now displays the call-to-action text in bold. The website address is also underlined and clickable, matching the button's behavior. This small visual update makes the ad easier to notice and provides a larger area to click.

aa83b05ff418e46a4c508ce209da88b43707f964.text: The team improved how they check if the system correctly saves money by reusing previous work. This change is only for internal quality checks and does not affect how the product works for you.

fd7905763cf8536b21c1d3a990e97cecf58524bb.text: A new button now appears under the plan in the command-line tool. Clicking it starts a build that uses no paid resources, alongside the existing fast and max options. This is live for people using the command-line interface.

3f6de551d04a9dc45132e68878ef980ba0956514.text: The table listing the assistant's four modes on the help page was broken and did not display correctly. This fix ensures the modes, their names, and capabilities appear in a clean, readable grid. The correction is live and affects anyone reading this specific help article.

538f982782ec25624e12fdefff87c429cb96878f.text: A small update improved the appearance of a comparison table on a specific internal documentation page. This change only affects how the table looks for anyone viewing that page, making the features easier to read. No actions are required from users, and the underlying functionality remains unchanged.

419ea9ea24a0d76f129ce34c00b3aed76f41a31d.text: The system now uses a lower score to decide which ads to show. This small internal adjustment means ads might appear less frequently or differently for some people. You likely will not notice any change today.

b222355616dbb009a330d53057729aac8becf671.text: The free version of the command assistant now uses a different underlying model. This change is live and applies only to users on the free plan. You might notice slightly different responses or speed when asking it to run commands, but the overall function remains the same.

310f353fe60e9f05e5292fb22dfd1de8c46f6a0d.text: A small change was made to the pricing page. The headline now says 'Subscribe to use all modes with higher usage limits' and includes a help icon. Hovering over the icon shows a note that these limits apply to five-hour sessions with weekly caps. This affects visitors looking at the subscription options and clarifies what 'higher limits' means.

f538e7ffabb6b0c2bbcc1649706f8cd9f40de76f.text: A small internal cleanup removed extra debug messages that appeared in the command-line tool's log when you pressed Ctrl+U to delete text. This change affects only the technical logs, not the actual typing or deleting behavior. You will not notice any difference in how the tool works, but support engineers will see less clutter if they ever need to check the logs.

da1d2ed9b21ba5bec138c63a84309afdb4788751.text: The tool now lets people who build software with this kit pick exactly where to store their custom skill files. This helps them organize their work better. It is available today for anyone using the latest version of this kit.

47f88beeaab13c5bfff7e652691a9abbe32dea5b.text: The software now lets you point to a specific folder to load special instructions from, rather than using the default location. This change is active, so anyone using the programming toolkit can immediately set up a custom folder for these instructions. If you look at the settings, you will see a new option to specify this folder path.

34d768eb96e9cdc03772e4e2dfed5c9d7c4525d0.text: Internal checks for the command-line assistant were updated to match current behavior. Tests now verify that built-in helpers appear when no custom ones exist, and that empty web-scraping results return blank text instead of a placeholder. This affects only the automated quality checks, so customers will not notice any change in the assistant's features or responses.

841150ec209cce82f55caeade2a4544338a9d2e8.text: The system now passes billing settings to smaller helper tasks. Users on the free plan will see these helpers respect cost limits. This is a small internal fix that is live today.

6fc9d8c2bd75caf2584a33cc37e65e5eac947afc.text: A new code review assistant is now available for free in the basic plan. This change is live today. If you use the free mode, you can now access this specific review tool without paying.

f9f48ae256fd817de10158a33d10bb536eb71ae0.text: The team updated their internal grading system to test a different, free version of the AI assistant instead of the standard one. This change only affects how the team measures performance behind the scenes and is not visible to any customers or users.

ba531540bdad0bb161148debb50a9b23aa6e1bce.text: The system now handles cases where a tool returns no results by sending an empty record instead of crashing. This affects internal message processing and is live today. You would not notice any change in your experience.

13a411578d705e06f6f7487537f54e60bfa13d8f.text: The help pages and guides now say the free plan uses MiniMax M2.5 instead of Grok 4.1 Fast. This affects only people checking the documentation to see which model powers their free tier. They will see the new name listed for the assistant that reviews code and edits files.

74e25483f7660125e88f066816429ecb881fe44b.text: The assistant's instructions were updated to explicitly forbid calling non-existent skills when none are available. This prevents the assistant from trying to use tools that do not exist, reducing errors. The change is live and affects all interactions where no skills are configured.

89baebf19ff27d4b885163ad349612a1c08d45b8.text: The command-line tool gained a new ability to check your computer's specs and operating system details. This change is internal plumbing that sets up the capability, so you will not notice anything different yet.

0e8d8adcfb2f995375dc80ebd5c80821864e4c67.text: When using the command-line tool, the menu that shows suggested options now decides how to display each item individually. Previously, if any single suggestion had a very long description, the entire menu would switch to a less compact two-line format for every item. Now, only items that do not fit on one line will wrap, keeping the rest of the menu neat and easy to scan.

37f5ddf350b79edc494586cbeca21757d11d91c3.text: The system now skips saving tool requests that lack a matching result when an action is stopped early. This prevents errors from confusing the AI provider about unfinished tasks. You will not see any visual changes, but the assistant will be more stable during interruptions.

ff9f6e8944d5a061af8a951291b9c34a5d1c5ab9.text: The text command tool now wraps long text in table cells onto multiple lines instead of cutting it off with three dots. This affects anyone viewing markdown tables in the terminal. They will see full content, even if it makes the table taller.

f4dbe3107e8cdb6cabb4ccfbf949ec634a6dae67.text: The tool now warns that connecting a Claude Pro or Max subscription will stop working on March 1st, citing reports of account bans. People using this specific connection feature will see this warning message appear on their screen. The help guide also updated to recommend switching to the company's own subscription plan instead.

737e8a0c1fe7b13e9cad264c2e4b88be9667d343.text: The assistant now recognizes three new models: Claude Opus 4.6, Kimi K2.5, and GLM 4.7. This update is live for users setting up new agents, allowing them to select these specific options in their configuration files. Existing agents will not automatically switch to these models, but the system will accept them as valid choices.

1ad32d436b2433106ba0549bb663d2de61920e5e.text: We fixed a bug where some automated assistants failed to start correctly when using Amazon Bedrock. This affects internal tools that manage command-line coding agents. The assistants now send setup instructions as user prompts rather than assistant responses, preventing the startup error.

3a503134b62fc72842fc81e9118775ecfc141c6c.text: The text menu in the command-line tool now checks if each suggestion fits on one line individually, rather than forcing all suggestions to use the same layout. This fixes alignment issues where long descriptions would break the menu formatting. The change is active immediately for anyone using the tool.

c961ffad7a8d6ce06e8900082b1529c9861bd7b5.text: A small internal update removes a fixed price label from the data sent to the payment processor when starting a subscription. This change affects only the backend system and is live now. Customers will not notice any difference, as the price and billing details remain unchanged.

46de4ded3f387148406e516df730a7f97de410b1.text: The software now correctly lists every action the assistant takes, instead of sometimes hiding them. This update is currently just a written note in the change log and does not yet affect how the program runs.

240a6d83a7bdb4d644e0e1a3396c85290725d325.text: The internal checks that ensure the command-line tool works correctly have been updated. The automated tests now expect the new 'refer-friends' command instead of the old 'referral' command, matching the recent name change. This is a small internal fix for the software's quality assurance process. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the tool behaves.

e2175c4348d342580d5da89e75d4dfce79568b8e.text: The automated system that releases new software versions no longer needs a specific secret password to upload files to the public store. Instead, it uses a more secure, built-in verification method that confirms its identity automatically. This change only affects the internal release process and is not visible to regular users.

6db3bb59f43f6ad7b28ff85b560b176b8248717b.text: The assistant now strictly pairs every request it makes for a tool with its matching result in the conversation log. This fixes errors when using the Anthropic model. The change is internal, so users will not notice any difference in the interface.

d16dd743087445adaf57103bdd5788486683d9e7.text: Sign-up instructions for new Codebuff users are shorter and cleaner. Confetti emojis and repeated phrases were removed from the bonus credits step. New users will see simpler text when installing the tool.

bb00fb7bc8e3c6cb156e14f0e4b7fd552583cd38.text: In the command-line tool, a small ad banner now has a clickable 'Ad' label that opens an info panel. From that panel, you can choose to hide ads for the current session. This change is live now.

ef6c525a2328e66eee9363b5e1a89d06df76942f.text: The command to invite others now uses a clearer name, though the old shortcut still works. This update lets people see their personal invitation link and copy it with a single click. Users who type the command will notice this new button appear right away.

62fd54667bd81aadcaace15ff17372b51b3869ff.text: The website's credit purchase page now shows fixed dollar amounts to click instead of a box where you typed a custom price. This applies to both individual and organization accounts. Users will see preset options for buying credits and setting up automatic refills, with the default auto-refill amount raised from $5 to $20.

1fa1ede5b2915c94a438455edbcc05f4af9cf392.text: The automated system that sends new software updates to the store switched to a newer version of its underlying engine. This fixes a glitch that was stopping some updates from being published correctly. Developers won't see any change in how the software works, but future releases will now go out without errors.

c5e6ef867a7fa08f4fbed10b840a35d41ce45172.text: The app now recognizes a newer AI model when accessed through a specific third-party service. This fixes a routing error for users who select this model. It is live today.

ee3e0e3cc6e745ab5ceac079827315797956eb65.text: The help pages updated the names of the AI models used to write code. Visitors reading the FAQ or model lists will now see the newer model name instead of the old one. This is a text-only change that does not affect how the software works.

b19028b5468eafc23442f2293c16b224b5c362da.text: Free chat requests now work even when your paid credits or subscription limits are used up. This applies only to specific free models and agents. You will notice these free options stay available, while paid features still block until you get more credits.

63531e11d69aaad066aa74634161ae571a5e89a2.text: The internal helpers that test and edit code now use the newer version of the main assistant model. This change affects only the automated tools that check the software's quality, not the features you use. You will not notice any difference in how the application behaves.

8de679e7a997feac9bb6a84b921cb2a28af4ac34.text: The company updated its website to make its speed claims more precise. Instead of promising tasks finish in one-third the time, it now specifies that complete features do, and highlights a 100-second average improvement. Readers looking at the site will see these narrower, evidence-backed statements replacing the older, broader claims.

96a8378aa63af776c02b36b1be57b10b592b8f47.text: The assistant now checks for and loads specialized instructions before writing code. This change applies to the implementation step of the agent's workflow. You might notice the assistant using more tailored methods for specific tasks, though the underlying process change is minor.

e1d8726dbfaf592e2d5ca2bdc5e02b1886782630.text: The text shown in browser tabs and search results for the pricing page was shortened. Visitors see a simpler title and a description that clarifies subscription options for higher limits. This small update is live now.

63d3a7692d4a3c1f9bc668b4317f37c1c4ac9ef7.text: The command-line tool now shows a clear switch to turn extra credit spending on or off when your subscription limit is reached. Previously, the interface used confusing checkboxes and buttons that didn't match how the system actually worked. You will now see a simple 'Credit spending: enabled' or 'disabled' status with a direct link to change it.

b3a26524d27f2ad674ba50bfdba5237632ad7dae.text: A command-line tool can now change a specific account setting without needing to be logged in through a web browser. This fixes an issue where the tool could not save changes to the 'fallback to a la carte' preference in the live system. Web browser users will not see any difference.

ea14ad4ae4a6f442690cac60e3cb7e4e382a2686.text: When you hit your subscription limit, the text box for typing messages now disappears. Only the warning banner about the limit stays on the screen. This stops both items from showing up at the same time. The change is live today.

75109377ca3c2600aa30493939eef98794842b21.text: A small internal tooling adjustment restores a simpler method for applying database changes in one specific project. This change is live today but affects only the internal development setup, not customer-facing features. Non-programmers would notice no visible difference in the product.

746093347cf3ab3a01ada4aeac298382cf134b3f.text: The text command preview now stretches to fill the available screen width. This affects the command-line interface, where long outputs previously wrapped at a narrower, fixed size. You would notice more of each line visible at once without extra wrapping.

ce23b852c37d3341bb1962973efddb129588ce52.text: The command-line tool now shows the current website address in its help banner instead of an old, fixed link. This ensures users see the correct site if the domain changes. The update is live and affects anyone viewing the tool's usage instructions.

efb9f5d4576330b8d6f3d7a68149e323987df9fa.text: A small internal fix removed an extra punctuation mark from the database's setup instructions. This prevents the system from failing to read its own configuration. Regular users will not notice any change, as this only affects how the internal tools handle data updates behind the scenes.

6ab7d2d0c9ffbe0c67444a76f95286042633179a.text: The service now waits longer for answers from certain advanced models that take time to begin responding. This change is active immediately. Users might notice fewer failed requests when using these specific models.

e4c2bbb3dcaf0c767ed14fd0d41e900709612082.text: When you hit a subscription limit in the command-line tool, you can no longer press Escape or Backspace to dismiss the warning. You must now click the provided options, like buying credits, to proceed. This applies immediately to users who encounter the limit screen.

c564dac5d3681443df760b0752501d8c3de769b5.text: A small internal safety update changed how one team's database updates are applied. Instead of instantly forcing the database to match the latest design, it now follows a step-by-step plan. This protects against accidental data loss during live updates, though regular users will notice no difference.

34c7aaadc5259a9b329e41bcd1910351956cd4a4.text: The command-line tool no longer prints hidden status notes to the screen when its message queue is paused. This change affects only people running the tool in a terminal window. They will see a cleaner display with less unnecessary text cluttering the output.

7f7c6d6b2d01e8af50d71600da3e478db859d3e2.text: The command menu now shows more options at once when the terminal window is tall. This helps people who use the command-line tool on large screens see more commands without scrolling. It is live today.

fc1253a60a0463725587307ebed09941e93115bc.text: The payment system now automatically generates official receipts and asks business buyers in Europe to provide their tax registration numbers during checkout. This applies to anyone purchasing credits or subscriptions. Customers will see a new optional field for their tax ID and will receive an invoice email immediately after paying.

7970c2dee83b155434da93abdaad98ea2f0a0461.text: The command-line sign-in no longer tries to open a web browser by itself. It now shows the sign-in link and tells you to open it yourself. People signing in from a command-line window will notice the browser does not pop up automatically. The change is live now.

7a83297f47d8e25387f7e5bcc56e6d4e6e7e8e56.text: The ad system now checks if the ad provider is working before trying to read its data. If the provider sends a broken or empty response, the system safely shows no ad instead of crashing. This applies only to the internal ad-fetching service.

5fa8a029096d594c513b8ba482e41c67e5d0b26d.text: The setup guide for the website's address has been updated to include the specific port number needed for local testing. This change affects only the internal documentation template, not the live site. Consequently, new users following the guide will see the correct address configuration immediately, while existing installations remain unaffected.

a175054234a1be11eaa0f31276842e32aa2c85ee.text: People using the command-line program can now type a specific shortcut to instantly switch the screen colors between light and dark. The program remembers the current color scheme and flips it to the opposite one, showing a quick confirmation message on the screen. This feature is active immediately.

51f8943c9e8c68f14a91d0b0563872d581de292c.text: The subscription page now works with a direct security key, not just a browser login. This helps command-line tools check your plan status without opening a website. Nothing changes for normal web users; the page looks and acts exactly the same.

fc2d2f13ba01421a10b7c1f3222460759f746ea5.text: The assistant now uses a standard reply format instead of mixed signals when a request is cancelled or completed. This internal cleanup helps other parts of the software understand the result correctly without guessing. You will not notice any change in how the app behaves or looks.

4e10365fd9f9fc1dba7c0ee557306cc1d31d7f12.text: Two options were removed from the menu that lets you choose actions. People who used to select the Opus assistant or the publishing tool no longer see them there. This change is live now and affects only those specific menu choices.

b76866a5955f1c058321a4eaf2fd955a096acb09.text: The text shown to the automated assistant was updated to match the correct names of the actions it should take when suggesting file changes. This small internal fix ensures the assistant can properly request edits without confusion. You will not see any visible difference in the interface, but the assistant's suggestions should now work as intended.

befef2c6bbf198faa2e798f55b4ffe2cfb1c8a68.text: Internal tools that ask the AI for information now recognize when a request gets canceled. Previously, if a request stopped early, the tool would try to read missing data and break. Now, the tool sees the cancellation, logs it, and stops cleanly instead of failing. This is a minor internal reliability fix and doesn't change anything visible to customers.

cb81a65a569238c6ed7ef25877e6156ed8c53da1.text: The system now clearly separates a user's decision to stop a task from an actual software failure. This change is internal groundwork and does not yet alter what users see or experience.

0ec9fa0acfde1fd0235ec3c1adf7e8b1091eaaf5.text: Internal test tools were updated to use a standard format for simulated responses, matching how the main system expects data. This change only affects the automated checks that developers run to verify the software works correctly. Regular users will see no difference, as no features were added or removed.

f9cdd1d365a762fde877ed7b8f186ba85c829dcb.text: The assistant now hides generic network error messages when its background check finds no specific problems. This change prevents confusing alerts from appearing when the check service is temporarily unstable. The update is live and requires no action from the user.

7f9613cdda455a9edda444f35fb5079de51c03c9.text: The automatic system that sends our command-line tool to the public store no longer needs a hidden password to work. This change applies only to the internal release process and does not affect how customers use the tool. You would notice nothing different when installing or updating the software.

1bb1c6853036244ac1d440ccbe3cd1c6d96d6afa.text: When the system hits an error while talking to an AI service, it now saves more details about the failed request in its internal logs. This helps support staff see exactly what went wrong, like the specific web address or data sent, without needing to ask the user for information. Regular users won't see any visible changes in the app, but support teams can diagnose issues faster.

a24ae19af0e80221114f35ffed9b7cbc9e646176.text: Developers updated a small internal check to match how the tool now expects data. This change does not affect live behavior or user experience. You will notice nothing different when using the command-line tool.

4695192b8fd9050c351590b83511098b5ecbd078.text: The limit for pasting long text directly into the command-line tool increased from 1000 to 2000 characters. Text under this new limit stays visible in the chat, while longer text becomes a separate file attachment. This affects only those using the command-line interface, and the change is active now.

37e11effc629201edc6776246bd6318ff94c3232.text: When you cancel a request, the system now stops immediately instead of trying a backup service. This saves time and computing resources that were previously wasted on work you no longer wanted. The change is live today.

b45a8cca698a67999d6c8b35d9ad42cca6e76f99.text: The command-line tool now correctly displays which strategy it chose and why when running multiple prompts. This fixes a bug where the tool failed to find this information because it looked in the wrong place. Users who run multiple prompts will now see the selected strategy and reason in their terminal.

4f45568ffa49272ba10dcc2c4e50f1b1fd531ff6.text: When a helper tool has a very long description, the menu now cuts it off after fifty characters and adds three dots. This prevents the text from spilling over the edge of the window. The change is active and visible in the tool's menu.

61d4975f84aa6c9da41331ec5c4784451a64cc19.text: The command-line tool now finds files and folders more flexibly when you search for them. Instead of requiring an exact match, it recognizes partial names and jumps ahead to find the best results. This helps people working in the terminal quickly locate specific items without typing the full path.

5937834199b395521cd14e84a850d0e204c949af.text: A small internal fix prevents the tool from stopping unexpectedly when it tries to save certain complex log files. This affects people using the development version of the software. They would notice that the tool stays running instead of crashing when it encounters these specific data issues.

0d9a8a2107a299ad81f12dde7a2e9f2b09143f5d.text: A small internal fix restores the assistant's ability to read secret settings from your computer's environment. You would notice this if the assistant previously failed to start tools that required these secrets. The fix works immediately.

02f131b89966bff249f1e1c157234591b028d5cb.text: A small internal rule was updated to allow the command-line tool to read a specific type of configuration file at startup. This fixes a recent issue where automated checks incorrectly blocked the tool from loading these settings. The tool now works as intended without requiring user action.

84f283a51e6ac354b0a8f54ba40aa51229ad8422.text: The help guide now calls the cheapest option 'Free' instead of 'Lite', and lists a different, faster brain for this mode. You switch to this mode by typing a slash command in the chat box, rather than using a special startup code. The guide also explains that the 'Max' mode now uses several reviewers at once, not just one.

0e2633a858d947a582ba57248c1d5272229992b0.text: A small internal update to the documentation site's code display. For anyone viewing these pages, the boxes containing code snippets now look cleaner and more compact. The language name above the code is gone, and the 'copy' button sits neatly on the right side of the code block instead of above it. This change is live for all visitors to the docs.

df0ffb3bb12e8537878061ea497b0ba58c77acd3.text: A small visual fix changes how the command line tool displays actions it does not know how to format specially. Instead of showing all the raw data for these basic actions, the tool now hides the details behind a collapsed view by default. This makes the screen less cluttered and easier to read, while keeping the important, custom-formatted actions visible as they were before.

2a3bf3c9cc9e7041dd804e4bc44a4378d235db42.text: The command-line tool now waits a set amount of time before retrying a failed request, instead of trying again instantly. This prevents the tool from spamming the server when a connection issue persists. You might notice fewer repeated error messages if a background update fails.

585742806f8f389a76da2aff99d032e961f710dd.text: A small internal adjustment was made to a test that checks how the system manages database connections. This change ensures the test accurately reflects the current setup rules for connection time limits. It does not affect live features or user experience; it simply keeps the internal quality checks accurate.

5c129d57b23ad86db8cb9b7aacde501be26a9b4e.text: The assistant's reasoning notes now stay partly visible after a reply, showing a short preview instead of hiding completely. This change applies to the command-line interface, letting you see the first few lines of the assistant's internal thought process without clicking to expand. You will notice the text remains readable until the next message arrives, at which point it collapses again.

ded7d682a8a671d9be16902cc4248528cffcfc62.text: The website stopped making backup copies of every publisher and agent page while the site was being built. This fixes a problem where the building process would take too long and fail. Visitors to these pages now see information that updates every ten minutes instead of waiting for a new site build to see changes.

698b29200760a302869c6687ec3291d4f297bdb7.text: When the AI shows a brief summary of its actions, that text now spreads across the entire width of your screen instead of stopping early. This change helps people using wide monitors or windows see more of the preview without it being cut off. The update is live and requires no extra steps to activate.

f1accc200beda280aa54011c8adfa8cc685d9355.text: A small internal fix ensures the command-line tool correctly identifies which strategy was chosen when multiple options are presented. Previously, the tool guessed by looking at the last item, which failed if other information appeared after the choice. Now, it searches specifically for the selection record. Users will see the correct 'Selected Strategy' label appear reliably.

81e1be31c9ff2782d64d8f52e364e7d30548d8ed.text: The test setup for the file picker was updated to match how the real system reports results. This change is internal and only affects developers maintaining the code. Regular users will see no difference in how the application behaves.

d2ab2877a07a46bf2e58f1342b2c1925dde3bf16.text: The assistant received clearer instructions to stop misusing its team-spawning feature for simple tasks like reading files. This small internal update ensures the assistant picks the correct tool for the job, preventing confusion when it tries to handle basic requests. Regular users will see no visible change today, as this only guides the assistant's internal decision-making.

cc23c66e706d9816db3d96b53b50cf79385fa8f7.text: A small internal cleanup removed a duplicate safety net for unexpected errors in the command-line tool. Because other parts of the system already catch these issues, the tool's behavior stays exactly the same for you. You will not notice any difference in how it runs.

040c7041cf3f5140635b2492e337dacf384de2ee.text: The system now checks requested helper tasks before starting them. If a task doesn't exist, it's skipped instead of causing errors. Users might see clearer messages when some helpers fail to load.

3a07ea51161e323d25c544e19dc49e6fb00bc2eb.text: The system now hides the AI's internal thought process from the final output when a user specifically asks for it to be excluded. This applies only to connections using OpenRouter or Codebuff. Users who requested this setting will no longer see private reasoning notes mixed in with the answer.

aac0817bae2921bcaf1fa91be5e98b906b79260e.text: The code search tool now removes extra quotation marks from filter settings before running a search. This affects people using the search feature to find specific files. They will notice fewer failed searches when typing file names with quotes.

d2d075805ca94adcb02e71fe10ad0ead8f35a163.text: The website now redirects any link starting with '/b/' to the Beluga tracking domain. This affects only people clicking those specific short links. They will land on the same page as before, just with a different address in the browser bar. The change is live but invisible to most users.

9054900a3f68da7de0acb4ae7d2047a95a3d9063.text: The assistant's file search tool reverted a code cleanup that had broken its ability to send instructions to other parts of the system. This change restores the original, slightly repetitive code structure to ensure the tool works correctly again. It is a small, internal fix with no visible impact on how you interact with the assistant today.

9389ab66cd4c47e106b2b4df3bf0d3bace3b0c69.text: The team deleted an old, unused test file that tried to launch browser checks. Internal cleanup only. No customers will notice any change.

3ed910a5818f86c79252356d2f1503902d859b00.text: The website's underlying framework received a small security update. This change protects the site from known vulnerabilities. Visitors will see no difference in appearance or function.

d7b2ad8730aca61f27f58f37995ca05c83e5d68b.text: Developers renamed a specific test file to better match its purpose. The system that runs quick checks still looked for the old name, so it tried to run this detailed test as part of the fast group. They updated the rules to ignore the new name. This keeps the quick checks fast and accurate. No customer-facing features changed.

a651504cd9ede56175ef9ff64e4a6b11e63238da.text: The software now correctly identifies safe file paths that accidentally look like security threats. This small internal fix prevents the tool from blocking legitimate editing attempts in certain folders. Regular users will notice fewer error messages when saving changes to their files.

eb46bbff184fdb9b42ba8a4ed9d640eed47797b7.text: The command-line tool now checks if you are working on a remote computer before copying text. If you are remote, it sends the text directly to your local computer's clipboard. If you are working locally, it uses your computer's built-in copy tools to avoid conflicts with other software. This ensures copy-paste works reliably in both situations.

4b130fd1f9aae88598b93b00845ac841488c8c7a.text: Pressing the shortcut key now always closes open text sections first. The tool only opens them back up if every section was already closed. This change is active for people using the command-line interface.

045a0d335c8787085eaff3833153a946baa0f4f9.text: The code now points to shared settings using direct file paths instead of shortcuts. This change only affects the internal setup for retired AI assistants. Nothing visible changes for current users, and the shortcuts are removed from the project's dependency list.

2d70c9861bcb80e51e86a72457dbf7d88b6b79f5.text: Internal checks that verify the system works correctly were failing because they looked for files in the wrong place and missed a required detail in a test request. This change fixed those checks so they pass again. Only the engineering team sees this; customers notice nothing, as no features changed.

c70f2db602e84f2cf359b3c0afcac5f7c423abfd.text: The software behind the file-browsing assistant was cleaned up to remove repeated instructions and clarify how it handles certain tasks. This internal tidy-up affects only the system's maintenance, so regular users will notice no changes to the assistant's behavior or performance.

c933800c629cf3333831dc106304ec05f130035f.text: The command-line tool now shows clear error messages when required information is missing or when pasting images fails, instead of silently doing nothing. It also prevents crashes when typing commands that reference empty lists of files or agents. This change is live today and affects anyone using the tool in a terminal, making failures easier to understand and reducing unexpected stops.

10c3859d46632fb993e2c9d204f2f9c6f4b7b914.text: The file-saving tool now blocks requests to save files outside the current project folder. This protects against malicious or accidental overwrites of system files. If someone tries to save a file in a restricted location, the tool will stop and show an error instead of writing the file.

1e9795f1daab408d5dd9600641eae8d3c184fd7d.text: The system now spots when a helper tries to launch a tool as if it were a full assistant. Instead of failing with a vague message, it gives a clear warning to use the tool directly. This helps the software correct its own mistakes faster without changing how you see the interface.

162004c22ddcd5d023c411bed40c4335452a2c76.text: The assistant now ignores extra slashes at the end of folder names. Previously, asking it to look at 'src/' would fail, while 'src' worked. This small fix makes folder requests more forgiving. It is live today.

017850d16cb9a501b22498e41f95630281cd8a4e.text: When you click a special link to view a profile, the system now keeps all the extra information in the web address instead of throwing it away. This ensures that tracking details and settings attached to the original link remain active after you are sent to the referral page. The fix is live for anyone using these specific profile links.

f8cd6d97ac46fd462ee1cdb0a8f6520efc811fac.text: Small change, live today. The code-editing assistant now tells the Z.ai model to spend more effort on careful thinking when used in free mode. It also stops asking that model to write visible step-by-step notes before editing. People using that model in free mode may see slower but more considered edits.

896074486d74a53bee12641c7cbd2da90c3cb7f0.text: When the assistant tries to use a helper tool and fails, it now notices the failure and sends a clear message explaining what went wrong. This helps the assistant understand why it couldn't complete the task so it can try a different approach or ask for help, rather than getting stuck.

d3bdeeb451a8021142a2dfe502f833d24ad1a88e.text: Internal testing tools now look in the correct folder for the assistant's instructions. This fixes a path error that would have caused those tests to fail. Regular users will not see any difference, as this change only affects how the software checks its own performance behind the scenes.

93d6bb3d2dad6c28f8555f9a90f24e530c3abf24.text: The website's main headline now lists 'Higher quality output' before the speed comparison. This change affects visitors to the landing page. They will see quality mentioned first, followed by the claim about being faster than the competitor.

629e391b0f39112acb57879f1e961bc40335ede4.text: The assistant now reads partial data faster and searches code more reliably without getting stuck. Past activity lists are limited to the last thirty days. These updates are live but internal, so users will not see new buttons or text.

d2e643f01ffbaf32a36e901de8eeeeb2e8f27b24.text: The command-line tool no longer cuts off long text at a fixed width. People working in wide windows will now see full commands and results on one line instead of a shortened version. This change is live today.

973c9134a66ede21b49b1243e2deb59f92aab594.text: A small internal update fixed a test that checks how the assistant handles user answers in its command-line tool. The test now correctly includes the question number, ensuring the assistant remembers which question each answer belongs to. Regular users will not notice any change, as this only fixes a hidden check used by the software team to keep the tool working correctly.

7c41b100019e7ba2233270eae7edca17d69d1fe5.text: The internal checks that make sure the command-line tool works correctly were updated. This is a small fix for the tool's own testing process and does not change how the tool behaves for you.

eec98f78941dd55bb6a275df98f954c996e99086.text: The team fixed broken rules inside the safety checks that run automatically when developers save their work. This change does not affect how the assistant behaves for regular people. Only the internal development team will notice smoother automated checks.

fc8bc643e8bac0d0dcb97e1b182ddaf0a99b5a09.text: The text about referral rewards now correctly says you get a one-time bonus, not a monthly payment. This affects anyone who sees a referral invitation or checks their billing history. The actual amount of credits you receive has not changed.

3a1a7407db87eb9399a8c6c9d0ec1e07e80be1ac.text: Small text change. When connecting a Claude subscription, the program now shows a note saying Anthropic does not officially support this. People using the tool with a Claude Pro or Max account will see this warning in the setup screens and help pages.

ee1423d89b30317fe03db210e0e99a91facdf551.text: The automatic testing system now runs all checks in one batch instead of one by one. This fixes a glitch where the system falsely reported failure despite tests passing. Internal engineers will see fewer false alarms in the daily build reports.

913ba15a607bd270cc73ca27ed8e745521a99043.text: The help page now lists the assistant's current brain choices. The basic speed option is called 'Free' instead of 'Lite', and it uses a different model for editing text. Regular users will see the new name and updated list of models when they read the documentation.

50dc6cc5ac419d4e4aaef1eb4be622a15f667678.text: A small internal update fixes how the system handles missing cost data from the AI provider. It prevents the program from trying to record a price when none is provided. This change is not yet live for customers and does not affect any visible features.

be4bb8c359e55c7451c27df1647e5df6011f63e4.text: The team added detailed tracking notes to the background program that manages the Discord bot's database connections. This change is internal and does not affect how the bot behaves for regular users. If an engineer looks at the system logs, they will now see precise timestamps and process identifiers for every connection attempt, making it easier to spot timing errors or dropped links.

5b6c1419a54c8f2dde53fc9c3cb2f670fa827e86.text: The program now spaces pictures correctly when you send them without typing any text, fixing a layout glitch in the command-line tool. It also stops showing a temporary 'image attached' message, reducing screen clutter.

8cb6a827a8a3e377340841d9d1dd8eaa08552106.text: The system now records token counts in standard logs instead of sending them to a separate analytics service. This change affects only internal monitoring and debugging. Users will notice no difference in the application's behavior or interface.

20f5e0d7e3b94611e7bfb3b4e3343b4541161aa8.text: Developers improved the automated checks for the command-line tool by making the test data more precise. This is an internal maintenance task to prevent hidden errors. Users will not see any changes in how the tool behaves or looks.

bd070267edc055a452ed73b65ee315c50122284b.text: Checks for the code search tool were updated to handle output limits and timeouts more realistically. These internal adjustments ensure the tool correctly stops and reports errors when searches take too long or produce too much text. Nothing changes for users today.

4daf79edce5959e021eb6ec12228173d82d31c98.text: The application's internal code was cleaned up to remove leftover instructions that were no longer being used. This change affects the software's underlying structure but has no visible impact on the interface or features you interact with today.

67079658628c7649a17b0b669c3736c3c2df7730.text: We removed special instructions that forced the AI assistant to use specific older versions of its underlying components. This fixes a setup issue for the internal team building the software. The change only affects how the software is developed locally; the live service for customers remains unchanged.

977816fea610bf712feeec52af289d8cfd261ff4.text: Small internal fix for the command-line tool's self-checks. It stops the tool from trying to send usage data while tests run, and corrects how it compares file locations on Mac computers. No changes to how the tool works for you.

e3b13bb549cad63cde06c932bab6b9f60450a0ca.text: The system now spends one-time referral bonuses before renewable ad credits. This change affects only users with both types of credits active. You would notice your referral bonus balance depleting faster than your ad credit balance when using the service.

a9f900271908d9a3951b71c2cec947fb4e1a8ec3.text: The tool now sends attached images directly from memory instead of searching the computer for the original file. This fixes a bug where images failed to send if the file location changed during the task. It affects people sending images via the command line, who will see fewer broken attachments.

62bfc2b932a5835c0fd87589df0c7ed95270d79d.text: When the assistant summarizes a long conversation to save space, it now keeps the most recent images you uploaded instead of deleting them. This ensures the assistant can still see and reference those pictures when answering your latest question. The change is active today.

917fbccd9a4ced3c77b20ca144e2f252556275c9.text: The website's automated build process now ignores missing database connections instead of crashing. This affects internal developers testing changes in environments without a live database. They would notice builds completing successfully rather than failing with errors, while normal site visitors see no difference.

c1bf0a413a4381866be9c7a7b66c7f22f912a044.text: A small fix in the command-line tool hides the copy button when a message has no text. This affects people using the command-line interface who see blank or whitespace-only messages. They will no longer see a copy button that does nothing.

58a002be82a21979669f2369ca35ac3c81a508ce.text: The AI assistant now strictly requires all relevant files and background information to be attached when starting a new task. It no longer assumes it can see what was previously discussed or read. This internal clarification helps ensure the assistant has the correct context to work effectively.

3e4406e582fdbde3d55264470fbdb1566ab8deca.text: The command-line tool now hides its promotional messages when the window is too short to display them properly. This applies only to paid accounts; free accounts still see the ads regardless of window size. You will notice a cleaner, uncluttered interface if you use a small terminal window.

c707102f3545a81a8d29c3babaad2c42d6ac4240.text: The program now waits until an image is fully ready before trying to show it, preventing broken or missing previews. This affects people using the command-line tool who attach images, fixing a bug where pictures sometimes failed to display or showed the wrong error message.

7824e45e34da353dcdcc70c4cf54144f4d2d782f.text: The command-line tool now looks for custom agents in your personal home folder, in addition to the current project folder. This lets you set up agents once on your computer and use them across all your projects. If a project has an agent with the same name, the project's version will be used instead of your personal one.

581659ac47ae5409e0f598807b3842d7487eb651.text: The assistant now asks follow-up questions only when the best choice is unclear, and it skips questions when the answer is obvious. This change is already active for people using the base2 assistant. They may notice fewer interruptions and quicker progress on straightforward tasks.

a5c382cba60723c7dfb4344f08b88647597f9b3c.text: The program now shows fewer past conversations when you open the history screen, cutting the list from one thousand to five hundred. It also hides any saved chats that have no messages inside them. You will see a shorter, cleaner list of actual conversations, with no blank entries taking up space.

f8e5c97566f5e2a7b6308e872a6680af67a7a983.text: The command-line tool now checks terminal settings through a single, consistent source. This fixes errors that could prevent clipboard copy and title updates from working correctly. People using the command-line tool will see clipboard and title features work more reliably.

fb0fd39bb4b0c3c78308e015328465970c37c42b.text: The file finder tool can no longer look inside folders to check their contents, only listing them. This restricts its ability to verify files exist or read them. People using this specific agent will see it stop attempting to open or inspect files during its search.

1dfb2cb4e583c9c41350c2306e1bbf9a10b8ce6b.text: The software now automatically creates a unique identifier for assistant actions when a specific provider fails to send one, preventing the process from stopping. This affects internal systems using compatible providers, ensuring smoother operation without visible changes to the end user. The fix is live today.

87f7793bb5a8970d47a8e54e171387551ae1c64a.text: The main assistant now blocks a specific search helper when using the newest model. This stops the system from reloading entire files repeatedly, which wastes time. You will not see any new buttons or menus, but the assistant should finish tasks slightly faster and use less data.

9ac31fc961a4bc7e606903940a41575986e05e3e.text: The AI assistant now keeps a record of the changes it makes to your files. It saves these records in its memory, but only keeps the first part if a change is very large. This helps the assistant remember what it just did, so it can keep working without losing track of your files.

210383f7118a24e3a1116589360867c2ff64113e.text: The assistant now automatically switches to a lighter version of its main helper when the standard one is unavailable. This change is live today. Users might notice the system selecting this backup helper without failing, though the visual difference in the interface is minimal.

c2565033906c4cecd55c4a6686592043c9278430.text: The two AI assistant options now appear higher in the command list inside the command-line tool. People using this tool will see these assistants first when typing a slash command, instead of having to scroll past other items like feedback or publish. This change is live and only affects how the list is ordered, not how the assistants work.

3a4698ee18389356fe27a47f5ecb111b39407018.text: This update lets the system automatically fill in secret keys from your computer's settings when connecting to external tools, so you no longer have to type them directly into the configuration file. If a key is missing, the system leaves the placeholder text as-is instead of breaking the connection. This change is live now and affects anyone who sets up these external tool connections.

4397bbce21cfa5d71613b14afd999451151da269.text: The system now charges zero credits for document and web searches, making them free to use. This change applies to anyone using these specific search features. Users will notice their credit balance no longer decreases when performing these searches.

456cd9e491d89f4f4162d9ded9bd4c7b372ad80f.text: Two background helpers that look up technical information switched to a newer, faster thinking engine. This change is internal and affects only those specific helpers. A person using the research feature might see slightly quicker or sharper answers, but the way they ask questions stays exactly the same.

d85c249c33b9f7060bef187ce95c6ca27c67f3e4.text: Two research assistants are now available for free. This change affects users on the free plan who use these specific tools. If you try them, you can use them without paying or having a subscription.

a31f085d483da7af1cd15b0786989c67e7d75b4f.text: The typing shortcut for the GPT-5 assistant now adds the correct name with spaces and capitals. Previously, it added a confusing string of dashes and lowercase letters. This small fix helps people using the text-based tool to tag the assistant properly.

0ec370051bbc449cc1a5c9e6f27409a39074755e.text: The AI assistant's internal instructions were tightened to make it more likely to search for relevant files before answering. This change is live now. A non-coder would notice the assistant being slightly better at finding the right information to answer a question.

dd9233db8bf1da33155ac59fdb56f2787a42b1df.text: The command-line tool now keeps a short list of ads to display even when it stops fetching new ones after a period of inactivity. This affects people using the tool's ad-supported features. They will continue to see rotating ads instead of the display going blank once the fetch limit is reached.

62aab4646bf93c3a7250f17ab807832f6ec950dd.text: Typing /gpt-5-agent now adds a specific tag to your message instead of running a command. The tag stays in the text box, letting you add more details before sending. This applies to the command-line tool.

707cfbdfd246191b5c2d7fc504c17cdd3ff1d922.text: The main assistant can now launch several helpers at once to search through files and gather information faster. This update only applies to the specific assistant type used for complex tasks, so most people will not see a change. If you use this assistant, you might notice it handles large requests more quickly by splitting the work up.

eb114327c233844252811cb7f72e018741ef385f.text: The login screen now lets people select the web address with their mouse or keyboard to copy it. The tool automatically copies the address to the clipboard when text is selected, and it no longer tries to open the web browser directly. This prevents the login text from becoming garbled or unreadable when the tool runs on servers without a graphical display.

1ad96664363a1ba4ea7428cb82a6234ecf01ba04.text: The deep-thinking helper now has a new name and can edit files. It is available for complex tasks. Users might see it listed as the general agent instead of the thinker.

1aee04f6146e1a59321904e111fb04c6e80d5830.text: The command-line tool now lets users call an Opus agent using a new '/agent:opus' command. It also updates the name of the GPT-5 agent command from '/gpt-5-agent' to '/agent:gpt-5' for consistency. These changes only affect how commands are typed and listed in the tool's menu, not how the agents work.

69aaa1afdea79b06bc74e93f2f8359dda18c92f0.text: The general-purpose helper now checks its own notes before each task step to keep information relevant. It also repeats tasks until finished, rather than stopping early. This change applies only to requests handled by this specific helper, making it slightly more persistent and focused.

2f5d2bb93997374602839e7dbfff2de2b8719926.text: The text explaining what the 'new' command does has been updated to be clearer. Instead of just saying it starts a fresh session, it now explicitly states that it clears the current history and starts a new chat. This change affects the help menu or command list in the application, making the function of the command easier to understand for people using it.

9982f5a561976355256ecea412861e4c9d7db730.text: The main headline and description on the website's home page changed. Visitors now see 'Better agents. Better code.' instead of 'Supercharge Your AI Coding,' and the text below it claims the tool is '100+ seconds faster than Claude Code with higher-quality output.' This change is live and affects anyone visiting the site.

0b7270dbdf852a3793ab1360616c298a9c72dbe1.text: The text editor now uses its built-in tool to automatically tidy up code files instead of a separate plugin. This change only affects the developers working on this specific project. They might notice slight differences in how the code looks after saving, but nothing else changes.

54212111ae03462e4a07daa3346cdd26ae6da731.text: The landing page no longer displays the 'Better and Better Over Time' feature or the competitor comparison chart. Visitors to the homepage will not see these two sections. This change is live.

3dc91a3b5150512e5dd6a50f2dd0b7ece1ffe63e.text: A small internal safety check now asks the database directly whether it still holds a specific lock, instead of just checking if the connection is alive. This check runs every 10 seconds instead of every 30 seconds. If the lock is lost, the system stops the action immediately to prevent errors.

02cb2e5dec72fa2cd02ca6759644f7429f3a6dc4.text: The internal name for the visual indicator shown when the assistant finishes a task was changed to match the system's label. This is a minor cleanup for the software's internal structure. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the application looks or behaves.

e70fc1ca89bf5cd55b9d363c6e664f22f2d77c8b.text: The help guide dropped its list of command shortcuts, leaving only a pointer to the built-in help. Readers will notice fewer options listed in the guide, though the tool itself works exactly as before. This is a small internal cleanup that changes nothing for the software's behavior.

26d1d5313ea418fe17cbba0019e09fda3a4d2238.text: Chinese character input in the command-line interface now works correctly when typing quickly. Previously, rapid keystrokes caused characters to be lost or inserted in the wrong order because the system fell behind. This fix ensures every character appears exactly where typed. The change is live for CLI users.

ad6b2bc5fef693393229939e7dc73b212d15902e.text: The login screen now always shows the web address you need to open, instead of only showing it if the browser failed to start. A new button lets you copy that address to your clipboard with a single click. This helps people logging in from remote servers or other setups where the browser cannot open automatically.

17b2faee10d38e7fa62cff639e53f4301b87efdc.text: A set of old, unused assistant features was moved to a storage area marked as retired. This change only affects the internal organization of the project files and does not alter any user-facing behavior. Customers will not notice any difference in how the software works.

ed0e89912bdc9cf6a9f142aaeca9309a8754f745.text: The command-line tool stopped recording a specific internal note about sub-agent creation in its event logs. This change affects only the tool's logging system and does not alter how the tool functions or resolves tasks. Users will not notice any difference in the tool's behavior or output.

fcf9b5e0e6941dee5525d40ba7b0eb2bbd95d96b.text: The system now uses the correct name for a specific helper tool in advanced mode, ensuring it launches the intended review process. This small internal fix applies only to users operating in the highest capability setting. People won't notice any immediate visual changes, but the background review step will now trigger reliably as designed.

036646e54d2c99d09c563b83e871401975df327e.text: The help screen now organizes keyboard shortcuts and tips into clear sections for easier reading. This layout change is live for anyone using the command-line tool. Users will notice the information is grouped logically rather than appearing as a single block of text.

e309aede7e5bdeea828f731a16fe4c890a376bb9.text: The command-line tool now shows remaining usage quota as a small battery-style bar instead of a number. It affects people who use the tool from a terminal. They will see a visual gauge that stays quiet and gray when capacity is healthy, only turning yellow or red when the limit gets low.

46b2addbb1aaf17bbcd1414c252fc42cd4c8bf53.text: Some retired assistant features were pointing to the wrong internal locations after being moved. This caused them to fail when loading. The fix corrects these pointers so the features can find the data they need. This is an internal maintenance task; customers will not notice any visible changes in the product today.

913a419e099c75154e727ccf433ee5dd84c17633.text: The program now hides internal details from the screen, such as full conversation histories and specific file lists. This change is active immediately for anyone using the command-line tool. You will notice a cleaner display with less text, which also reduces the chance of accidentally showing private information.

96b2d8a6dc65e7718bd3823302841548acb92a46.text: We removed background chatter from the command-line tool so it stops printing extra messages when checking connections, loading ads, or starting new tasks. This affects anyone using the tool directly. You will see a cleaner screen with fewer distracting updates, but the tool's actual behavior remains unchanged.

fd3d3db8705f1aaf3eea54cae6655f2211e78cc6.text: Automated checks that test data safety rules now skip running when the required database is not available. This change affects internal tools and prevents false failure reports. The user will see no difference in the application's behavior.

3b2abb6b97eb8720d420223badeacc444a622467.text: When you type a custom answer into a question, the text box now has a visible border and a scrollbar for long inputs. If you click away by mistake, your typed answer stays saved instead of disappearing. Long answers are also shortened with an ellipsis so they fit neatly on the screen.

9888fb656a1d19118f67a5a82130758e86e419c9.text: The team set up an automated check that spins up a temporary database to verify internal accounting tools work correctly. This change affects only the software engineers, not end-users. You would not see anything different in the product; it just helps the team catch errors before they reach you.

960921026e18e0db354fb614b2d2f8f78fa63b4b.text: The AI assistant no longer sends a detailed log of its answers and the file lists it saw to the company's main database. This change is live now. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the assistant works or what it says.

3860935c805c24b37e13bdcdc6aac874a3270dca.text: People arriving from a referral link now see who invited them and the shared bonus credit amount. The old welcome message was replaced with personalized text explaining the mutual reward. A small background update was also made to the affiliate profile form to keep it running smoothly.

005e8cac511bb7123a56344e16a71a7f5279f33f.text: The command-line tool now automatically records its internal activity messages to a remote monitoring service. This change is active only for production usage, excluding development and testing environments. Users will not see any visible difference in the tool's output, but the company can now better track system health and diagnose issues using these logs.

ca8d393f0a9ec14d2d81239d109d3979ff577c91.text: The team reduced the amount of internal activity records the system saves when you sign in or ask the assistant a question. This change affects only the company's internal technical staff who review those records. You will not notice any difference in the application's performance or features.

ce32bb56eed76e2b336218b6087febc609a9b07a.text: The text terminal now displays five lines of the assistant's reasoning process while it works, instead of three. Once the assistant finishes answering, this text hides behind a small arrow, letting you expand it only if needed. This helps you follow along with longer explanations without cluttering your screen.

34c0e7de63c4b283bb6988ae706f549d0d23bf92.text: On Linux, pressing the Enter key in the command-line tool now correctly submits your message instead of just adding a new line. Previously, the tool treated Enter as a command to create a new line, requiring an extra key combination to send your text. This small fix ensures the standard Enter key behavior works as expected on Linux systems.

56c6c89e0bbe5b442de910c19144193edd842de6.text: Internal test fixtures updated to return advisory lock transaction shape. No user impact. Not live.

55e0209ebf3db68dbf9e46f10055dd4f9cb97bc4.text: When you type a long answer with multiple lines, the collapsed view now shows it as a single line instead of pushing other content down. This affects only people using the interactive prompt and closing the question without expanding it. The text box where you type is also slightly taller, showing more of your answer before scrolling.

9e1ced5fec4155d20a0d5de3a1cd522dda723cef.text: The command-line tool now pastes text into the question box correctly when you drag-and-drop files or use a native paste shortcut. It uses the text sent by that action first, and only checks your computer's clipboard if that text is missing. This stops it from accidentally pasting old clipboard contents.

c3dd4c8e0d50e2b788d2c1ae20912fba60328570.text: The website removed two specific tools that helped manage how often people could use certain features. This change only affects the internal setup of the site, not what visitors see or do. You would not notice any difference in the website's appearance or behavior.

a5cac4bbbc705293539353a70fe0ca0bbb597930.text: The internal helper that checks terminal appearance now clearly states its job is visual testing only. It no longer tries to review code or run standard tests. This affects only the automated checks used by the team, not customers.

9df82f2c07d8d7cfbb84b6ddd213925f2dc0cd14.text: The website added tools to limit how many requests a user can make in a short time, preventing spam. These tools are installed but not yet active, so no one will notice any change in speed or access right now.

546532d217d80b72cd904ab14b4ee2f9824a0ae2.text: The system now counts tokens for non-Claude models by using a default Claude model instead of failing. It adds a 30% safety margin to these counts because different models measure text length differently. This internal fix ensures accurate billing estimates for users requesting token counts on non-Claude models.

6e43d3910d1556f38d39e37c8b83e2bbf4f96740.text: A routine system check was paused to fix a reporting error. This change affects only internal monitoring tools and does not alter how the application works for anyone. You will not notice any difference.

f2f8768f183a4493efa6da16fe64b374ec0b420f.text: The system now stops saving a chat reply once it reaches one million characters, marking the end with a note that the text was cut off. This protects the service from crashing under heavy loads. Regular customers see no change unless they generate unusually long responses.

8298fea956a823265b5aafd2f1e9df8eb5b519a9.text: The help command now appears at the top of the list when you type a slash in the command-line tool. This change affects people using the command-line interface. They will see the help option first in the suggestions menu.

53151c9677656c761e9f0a3117d4f6b45f61c8ac.text: A new help entry explains that people with a paid Claude subscription can link it to this tool. Doing so lets the tool use their existing subscription for some tasks, which saves their separate usage credits. This is a small documentation update and does not change how the software itself works.

18ca79da38544e5a0ea7749d6429dffa69b8cf5f.text: The system stopped maintaining a special, faster way to load agent lists that was no longer being used by any part of the website. This is an internal cleanup that affects only the code's complexity, not its behavior. Users and administrators will notice no difference in how the site works, looks, or loads.

1fd37c57f2de84bfb7df7910b06d9f252b6724cc.text: The help banner now explains pricing, how to buy credits, and how to connect a subscription. It also keeps the message on screen for a full minute instead of thirty seconds. This affects everyone using the command-line tool today.

35b3d4776947057243f70de62a20d766b988f661.text: The system's internal health-check routine now counts available assistants instead of loading their full details. This stops a warning that appeared when the list grew too large for the temporary storage. The change affects only the background monitoring tool; users and the visible interface will notice nothing different.

f5fb361e464098fe551e0b350db6681f2cf83d09.text: We deleted old text about pricing and features from the website's code because it wasn't showing up on the page anyway. This is a small internal cleanup. Visitors to the site will notice no change.

9f4906b6a90d9776bde69a25e7279fa9c60e10bf.text: The automatic tool that shortens long conversations now checks for a small safety gap of one thousand words before cutting anything. This adjustment ensures the system only trims text when the conversation truly exceeds its limit. Regular people will not notice any difference, as this is a small internal check to keep the software running correctly.

1b6379f5e554c8faa0497836fbf8796984ee2c62.text: A small fix to our internal testing setup ensures checks for account balances run reliably. This change affects only the engineers who verify the system. No customers will notice a difference.

6c8bdbb4d5b8554a0cc22cdb85358fb315d7e3c2.text: The automated system that tests software now uses a specific local database instead of one that might have been accidentally set up with sensitive information. This change ensures tests run correctly in a controlled environment. It is live today and affects only the internal testing process.

6ba0df14e0e9a4ee213a8fc10d0ffcdebf91f145.text: The pricing page now shows a new section explaining how to link an existing Claude subscription to save credits. People visiting that page will see a graphic and instructions for connecting their accounts. This is a visual update only; the actual connection feature depends on other tools working correctly.

17830c230a4f6b9ccef2a9ac860b30aa2ce692fc.text: The system's helper tools were updated to close known security gaps. This work happens behind the scenes, so customers will not notice any change in how the product looks or behaves.

44f596450369b5820acfd6c164b8a38a78df8016.text: The automated testing process for billing features now forces a specific database connection setting. This ensures the tests always use the correct internal database, regardless of other system configurations. This change affects only the internal checks that run when developers submit code. Customers will not notice any difference.

9926f45db5808786ce7e7e7f5a652a87dc9ebdc9.text: The system now automatically creates and tracks background work sessions for internal tools, replacing a manual process. Users of these specific internal agents will see the session name appear in the assistant's message, rather than needing to manually start or manage it. This change is live for internal staff using these tools.

442b0290c1ab6a071c3ee5220e19723f5e4be49f.text: The system now saves important instructions from the main planner agent, preventing them from being accidentally deleted when the conversation gets too long. This helps the planner keep track of the overall goal during complex tasks. You will notice the AI stays focused on your original request instead of losing its way mid-task. This update is live today.

07c8edf2d442720b901c628ef1879ba9e0d19a3a.text: The system now records which specific AI model is being used and the exact size of the text sent to it, but only after a successful count. This internal update helps track usage patterns accurately without changing how the tool behaves for anyone today.

2edc81fe91dd34d9a8d86d1f51a514e2a4f78029.text: In the terminal interface, the display no longer passes a shared list of active updates through many parts of the screen. Each part now checks only whether it is currently receiving an update. This affects people using the terminal interface, and they may notice steadier output and fewer unnecessary redraws while assistant tasks are working.

fb890c67d66a6ebe351d627157959cdaba48966c.text: When you press the stop button during a chat, the tool now marks any unfinished background tasks as cancelled. You will see a red symbol next to these stopped tasks, making it clear that they were interrupted and did not finish.

455bdaf609af6bb437c7077cc76ab1f11026df5c.text: The software that packages the command-line tool for distribution was updated to use a newer library for creating archive files. This change removes annoying warning messages that appeared during the packaging process. It does not affect the tool's features or how it runs; it only makes the internal build process cleaner for the team preparing releases.

5792b8402506f1c3b4c5502d704b79ce8b0d22af.text: The assistant now tidies up its memory slightly earlier than before. This small change gives it extra room to think without hitting its limit. You will likely not notice any difference, except that the assistant might summarize a very long conversation a few messages sooner.

3acbf5fec2f171a3ad4a1306ac327dff9a4083dc.text: The command-line interface now hides detailed output from the 'set_output' tool by default. This affects anyone using the CLI to view agent actions. Instead of seeing a cluttered block of text immediately, you will see a collapsed view that you can expand if needed.

99b49c66f7076a3a637649d81ace69a5ac87bed9.text: The tool used to install command-line updates now skips a step where it briefly ran the new program to check if it worked. This fixes a rare error on Windows that blocked updates from finishing, and makes the update process slightly faster. Most people will only notice fewer update failures.

6d30e228aa7f057ffa08e63ef38b39130042fc79.text: The program's internal setup was cleaned up to stop storing duplicate copies of the same helper tools. This change does not affect how the software works or looks to anyone using it. It is a small maintenance fix for the developers who maintain the code.

1676c5b09e27231d61f40e68326ec291ac5c1eff.text: A small internal tool used to update the database structure has been removed. This change affects only the internal setup process and does not impact how the application works for regular users. If you were using this specific internal command, you would find it no longer exists, but standard database updates continue to work as before.

3a8e8925294f18fa14cbd415308f01c1ff1ca3a4.text: Internal tools that help staff write code now use clearer names for their two main jobs: 'work' for building or fixing things, and 'review' for checking code. This change is live but only affects the small group of staff using these internal helpers. You would notice nothing unless you use these specific internal tools.

2020bc7c3d154fd3f8be5e1edd39e517378921ac.text: A tool used by internal engineers to update the database now checks its work before applying changes, preventing a crash that stopped the process. This fix applies only to the internal rendering environment. Engineers running these updates will notice the process completes successfully instead of failing.

1ce2372fe5ddb3fef01c99e60ccc255a83c1fefd.text: The tool that updates the internal database now uses a different method for applying changes. This method is less stable and can sometimes cause the update process to crash unexpectedly. The change only affects the internal team managing the database and does not impact regular users.

01fd3a1357e89fd2d52937003c4663ca77783c34.text: A new command was added to the internal database tools. It uses a different standard tool to check database changes because the usual tool crashes. This helps internal engineers run database updates without errors. It does not change how the product works for customers.

913dc992870658f425f928f263d04565764168fb.text: The tool now looks for a specific, reliable command-line program installed with Git before trying other options. This helps Windows users avoid errors when running commands, especially if their computer's built-in Linux feature is asleep or confused. The change is active now.

b939af8f6d1e89a2896d16ebe0cf8e0919943c6a.text: The help guide for new users was updated to match how the tool actually works. Readers will see clearer instructions on choosing between planning and full execution modes, and simpler steps for setting up a new project.

61fc6ea6bfc70e1118786b4ad40d39255b82c7c1.text: Fixed a bug where rapid typing could cause messages to be sent out of order or dropped. Added a new tool for testing that waits for the assistant to finish typing before sending the next message.

61e2ece6336e56b7c50719637287963a94591a9a.text: The file search helper now uses a faster, smarter version of its underlying brain to find relevant documents. This update helps the system locate files more accurately and prevents it from getting stuck in repetitive loops while searching. You will likely notice slightly quicker responses when asking the assistant to find specific files in your project.

93e36d191e5ae913ffab34acea06bae7e3bd18d9.text: The automatic code reviewer now checks its own logic before giving advice. This small update helps it catch mistakes in the changes you submit. You might see slightly more accurate suggestions, though the reviewer's appearance stays the same.

04cc786be8a45b952f8d235848ffcf4f9e3ad717.text: The AI assistant now checks for errors in the code before reviewing it, rather than doing both at the same time. This applies only when using the advanced 'max' mode. You might notice the assistant takes a bit longer to finish, but it ensures the code is technically sound before asking for a human-like review.

41f44f4862192aed5e18abef99728a67b0c56529.text: The program now requires a specific command-line tool on Windows to run tasks, replacing the older system. If you use Windows and do not have this tool installed, the program will stop and show an error message instead of trying to work. You must install the tool or set its location to use the software.

626cb7cd501ede8e983b11cc8717392d0ffe0b61.text: The help banner now shows how to start a new line in the text box. People using the command-line tool will see two new key combinations listed in the shortcuts guide.
