6fc8bbbcb2f87ec3ba3406e3e6e2218a73bd5fcd.text: The command-line tool now hides the detailed steps of individual code reviewers when they are run together as part of a larger review task. This makes the text output cleaner and easier to read. The change is live today.

153f21c0ce93b7a38c0965fbcdb4f805b4fc8e4d.text: The program removed a noisy status line and a file count from the screen. It also changed the colored bars to softer shades. This gives the file names more room to be read clearly.

2a6aec3f1b54a9d183616be72337540f5cf3f24a.text: The command-line interface no longer displays a summary line counting active, failed, or completed background tasks within the grid view. This affects users running multiple tasks simultaneously. They will notice the removal of this status text at the bottom of the task list.

a30c4db558d52fde3996feef83849945602af5e0.text: The program's internal message display logic was cleaned up to work more efficiently, which helps prevent temporary glitches when messages update quickly. This change is purely behind-the-scenes, so you will not see any new buttons or text, but the chat interface should feel slightly smoother and more stable when the assistant is typing.

40d41aa90dc2bf436ba838cbd8b0461c5e8fbda7.text: In the highest-effort mode, the assistant now consults a different, more thorough review step to check its work. This change is live and affects only those using that specific high-effort setting. You might notice the assistant takes slightly longer to review changes but could catch more subtle issues.

20976b32502f0da1ab7c7d5a494f21e8b694e2f9.text: A folder used to store old, retired experiments was renamed to make it easier to see in standard file views. This change is purely internal and affects only the developers maintaining the project. Anyone using the software today will notice absolutely no difference.

f17e51b7c3f23463f0cfac4f5f0340de36d26c6d.text: The sample list shown when building a new assistant now displays different example setups for planning and reviewing work. This change affects only the internal gallery of examples used to create agents. A non-programmer would notice nothing, as this is a small update to the internal reference materials.

882572d22bf35146c53c73e870a4c19dcb6958de.text: The assistant now remembers the final answers from its specialized sub-workers, such as those who draft code or analyze data. It intentionally skips the results from routine helpers who only search for files or list folders. This keeps the conversation focused on substantive work while reducing clutter from minor lookup tasks.

a93f8c52fb71e8355d3595afcfec0647d6fd2d52.text: When a connection to the service fails or takes too long, the error message now shows exactly which part of the system was trying to communicate and how long it waited. This helps people understand the problem without needing technical knowledge. The change is active and affects all users experiencing these specific connection issues.

ee4243fffcd14b9091a06132807caae6962b0385.text: The text tool now keeps pasted messages up to 1,000 characters directly in the chat instead of turning them into separate files. This affects anyone using the command-line interface. You will notice longer text blocks appearing fully visible in the conversation rather than hidden behind an attachment link.

1506118b849f954ef987c767cd716202fddaa047.text: A small internal update changes how the minimum credit reward for viewing an ad is calculated. Instead of a fixed starting amount, the system now adds a random extra bit to that minimum floor. People earning credits from ads might notice their lowest possible payout varies slightly from one view to the next.

6b2a98d9044c1ca85645d8541f306513a59294bd.text: The system now correctly identifies when a user has exceeded their usage limit or entered invalid credentials for the Claude assistant. Previously, it sometimes missed these specific error signals, leading to incorrect handling. This ensures users receive the proper feedback or automatic pause when these limits are hit.

23332b5a17edeafa295c8845d90ba6a179c10e4d.text: The website's top menu bar no longer shows a link to the Agent Store. This change is live now. People visiting the site will simply see one fewer option in their navigation menu.

97ede16f9f23676151659ad8659acc31b006ca09.text: A small internal fix makes the automation tools more reliable. The tools now clear leftover text and wait a moment between actions to prevent commands from mixing together. They also create unique labels for each session so parallel tasks do not overwrite each other's history. Regular users will not notice any change.

eaadfd2ebfb78e11b037af1e90aec9b09726f447.text: The system now recognizes two additional ways to ask for the Sonnet AI model. This ensures that requests sent through OpenRouter are directed to the correct model. Users won't see any changes, but it helps the software process requests accurately.

b3e504afd2899688e8a5049ca9332a2133d561cd.text: A small internal tool update lets developers paste clipboard content into a testing window as a single block rather than character-by-character. This makes testing attachment features more reliable and adds a retry option for finding the correct testing window. Only internal developers using these specific testing scripts will notice the change.

3af03fe87e2089c2ba3096d0356ee8d8b5479002.text: The program now records when a person clicks a suggested follow-up question in the chat. It saves the length of the question and which option was picked to help improve future suggestions. This happens automatically in the background. A person would not notice any change on their screen.

52c9195bb6690eb8894cf681d1d85ed75f5017f2.text: The system now guarantees a minimum payout of 0.02 credits for each ad view. This change is live for internal testing. If the calculated reward was lower than this minimum, the user still receives 0.02 credits instead of nothing.

2c7bcde4cb24d7266343a781e586fbe47a17bd9f.text: The command-line tool now lets you click only the short suggestion text, not the longer description next to it. This prevents you from accidentally choosing a suggestion when you meant to read the details. The change is active today for anyone using the tool.

ec5fa96b62322090df2731a59f8f6834200bab4b.text: The command-line tool now saves login details without deleting other stored information. Previously, signing in replaced the entire settings file; now it updates just the main login entry. If you look at your local configuration file, you will see your primary account details alongside any other saved profiles, formatted with clear spacing for easier reading.

e1914a11273914c1231cce3e9c601e2a390fddbc.text: The command-line tool stopped printing routine updates about ad banners to the screen. This affects people who use the tool in their terminal. They will see fewer distracting messages appear while the tool runs.

1856ef41b700ca080571d7a991c8bafdf7b0959c.text: A small fix adjusts how credits are calculated when ads are viewed. Previously, the system allowed a tiny fraction of a credit to be granted; now it ensures a minimum of two full credits are awarded per view. Users will see their credit balance increase by at least two points each time they watch an ad.

bee92505bb5ee6828c82b034e39d11aa3e1e0b63.text: The web and documentation research tools now start in a folded state within the command-line interface. This change applies to the tools that gather information from the internet and official guides. Users will notice these specific tools appear minimized at the start, keeping the screen less cluttered.

aded8b49a9e169fa253ad8bae99b655f1d8ed886.text: The store now uses a permanent ID to link each agent to its performance data, replacing a method that relied on the agent's name. This ensures that metrics like usage counts are attached to the correct agent, even if that agent's name changes. The fix is live, so the store displays accurate statistics for all listed agents.

5830a41371f415e37548922dcbfe53ad7c04e124.text: Typing single words like 'help', 'new', or 'exit' into the command line now triggers their actions without needing a slash. This applies to people using the text-based tool. They will notice that simple words work as shortcuts, while longer sentences remain normal chat messages.

624b646319fa2af93d2dd0b7365db47489fe3b99.text: A small internal fix corrected how our ad system reads responses from an external service. The service sends a list of ads, but the system previously expected a single ad, which could cause errors. This change ensures the system correctly picks the first ad from the list. Regular users will not notice any difference in their experience.

6a3e149f939aa8751c92a4c6729dc461d023a865.text: The top menu had invisible layers that accidentally blocked clicks on the Docs, Pricing, GitHub, Agent Store, and Usage links. This small fix removed the blockage, so these links now work normally when clicked. The visual hover effect remains unchanged.

e018647fa7bc63e59f22a1099a0267fc1d3d108b.text: The command-line tool now shows file changes with solid green and red bars that meet in the middle, instead of bars that grow or shrink based on the size of the change. This affects anyone using the tool to review code proposals. You will see the exact number of added and removed lines displayed directly inside the colored bars, making the layout more predictable.

287c179493cd75c1e88a9aecd6d1f8ee30a3e40e.text: The chat program now records detailed notes when a typed message fails to send, showing exactly which part of the process blocked it. This helps support staff diagnose stuck conversations faster. Regular users see no visual changes in the interface, but hidden background safety checks now reset the system if a message fails to process.

21b43d28231b3c8e97a7852037ea24b0574b6d4a.text: The instructions for setting up a new project were updated to match the current software. Instead of typing a long command from outside the program, you now start the program first and then type a short command inside it to create your setup files. This change affects anyone reading the help guides or starting a new project, ensuring they follow the correct steps.

e4e8a22f55e03d98f8691490296f8d6bb1c2c645.text: The website now prepares all documentation pages in advance instead of building them while the reader waits. This affects anyone visiting the help pages. They should see pages appear faster, especially on slow connections.

1bb9f79664696fedfd4b3fd40e6e0cbdb4862270.text: The system now correctly picks the first available ad from the list. This fixes a bug that previously caused ads to fail to load. Visitors on pages with ads will now see them display properly.

4b19be7354005515d072a83cf0b7f023109be47a.text: The website's tool comparison chart was updated. It now shows the assistant's interface as polished and lists its faster response times and built-in review features, while removing claims about specific folder settings. This only affects the public webpage; the actual software behavior remains unchanged.

7995908546f64334e1acb5bdb89b9a63810b4cb4.text: The internal name for the automated testing assistant was shortened to remove the word 'UI'. This change only affects the team members who use the testing tools. They will notice the new name appearing in the help guides and when they call the assistant.

9aa925a46842b21f4939378f22d0e8d5a4b8440c.text: Small internal change. Test scripts now let developers run the finished program version instead of the live-editing version. They can point to a specific file location or use a saved setting. This helps check that the packaged tool works correctly before release.

f4837612792b2fc89e06881c148132e06da070c5.text: A small internal fix makes a background check more reliable. It prevents a temporary failure where the system incorrectly thought a message arrived at the wrong time. Customers will not notice any change.

37bd86e3b484f17066b6d10223f694df268bc8da.text: The list of agents sent to the website now uses a method that handles large data better. Previously, the system tried to store this list in a small memory box, which failed because the list was too big. The list still updates every ten minutes, but the delivery is more reliable. This is a small internal fix, so you will not notice any visual changes.

5f43c1879089db13331ae9f7a0ed2600c17d4ee8.text: The tool now labels your device with a new name during login, replacing an old brand name. This change is live and happens automatically in the background. You will not see the new label, but it helps the service recognize your device correctly.

48828d98ddf7a968703fb8706cf5d60e46bea68c.text: A small internal update ensures ad tracking systems always receive a session identifier. If a session ID is missing, the system now automatically uses the user ID instead. This prevents errors in ad placement tracking for users without an active session.

da73910d42fa47d344cafa9840822922c7675768.text: The command-line tool now allows you to save login settings without a specific user profile attached. This helps the tool work correctly when you are not signed in. You will not notice any visual change, but the tool stops complaining about missing information during logout states.

534e9813c0cc9a2b34aa4fb73ebc2cf878a9fc28.text: The command-line tool now creates its settings folder automatically when you first run it. This stops the tool from crashing on new computers where that folder was missing.

f0eef6be25a0f614dadda4dd0e0485ef3f8c5311.text: A small internal update makes the documentation link jump straight to the quick-start guide instead of stopping at a help page first. This affects only the web documentation entry point and is live today. Visitors will notice the page loads the quick-start guide immediately, skipping the previous intermediate step.

c8ba60fe617f1a2586164bbf60998ae1fbbe31c9.text: A small internal fix makes the system recognize when an agent's setup is missing, instead of treating it as a broken value. This stops a rare type mismatch from confusing the system's logic. Users will not notice any difference in behavior today, as the system already handled this case correctly in practice.

0ae1339c6e2feefdd99e09b9a2a1e6473f7b9dbb.text: The advertising system now collects basic device details like operating system, timezone, and language, along with the user's approximate location from their network address. This update allows ads to be more relevant to the user's specific environment. The change is live and affects users who see ads within the command-line interface.

f51080f878829e318a2b462ba4c040734a35e510.text: The system now asks the ad provider for ads using a new, more precise format, including a specific default value of 0.04 if the provider doesn't specify a payout. This change is live immediately for all users seeing ads, though most won't notice a visual difference, as it primarily ensures accurate tracking of ad revenue.

f8fd02ac2d4e33d0780e9f64b1ff3bd9a20c180f.text: The system now has two fixed time limits recorded for login sessions: one for how long a login lasts and another for how close in time two events must be to count as the same session. This change is internal and does nothing yet because no other part of the system uses these limits today. Regular users will notice no difference in how the application behaves.

206730527e363e1bca216bacd55d5304cd3f5d3e.text: The terminal application now uses the current conversation's unique identifier for ad tracking instead of the general app session. This change is live and ensures ads reset when you start a new chat. You will not see any visual changes, but ad requests will match your active conversation.

5e3264f498daeda08e1f714835bc683f1fd8ce85.text: Search engines now see clearer information about how the documentation and agent pages are organized, which helps them display better results and links. This change is live today for people searching for these pages, though the visual website itself looks exactly the same to regular visitors.

11dbd952bcf4686fd720b4fb417cd0247b4f2b9c.text: The copy button's behavior was reorganized into separate pieces for better testing. This internal cleanup doesn't change how the button works for users, but it makes the code easier to maintain and verify.

43ea122eac6e68bea05bff686c4d6099e2af8072.text: The command line tool now turns on ads for new accounts by default. The option to switch ads on or off is no longer marked as a test version. Existing accounts keep their current settings.

22f963340da5e4dc861ae0e85bb117fa7e1ec1e5.text: The software now checks its internal memory for loaded agents instead of watching what appears on the screen. This change is for developers testing the command-line tool, not for regular users. Nothing visible changes for you today.

2a8e031963a5972dcb1ef8fffb27cd71bdd14fcf.text: The instruction guide for the AI assistant now explains how to limit which files it can see. This helps developers protect secret information, like passwords, by blocking those files or showing only safe examples. The rules only apply when a developer chooses to set them; otherwise, the assistant follows standard project settings automatically.

c7029de47bfc6b8d69f281e78262b226e4bf3c6e.text: The automated checks for the command-line tool now skip waiting periods when testing network retries. This makes the internal verification process finish faster without changing how the tool behaves for end users.

f988d78debb0a98dab289afa81a8239481e3597d.text: Small cleanup. Fixes terminal glitches when exiting the command line tool. Users see the mouse cursor return to normal and text stops garbling after the tool closes.

5d179a62ea85ab8deb4706729b69b6a9eca7d3ad.text: The command-line tool now hides its list of loaded local agents unless you have turned on detailed debugging. Everyday users will see a quieter startup screen with fewer status messages. This change is live today.

363caf8e1860a51c0f4f59f8c3b2b217723e1652.text: A small update to the command-line tool now lets certain automated helpers show their work in real-time, instead of hiding it until the very end. This change ensures that when you run specific text-based agents, you see the full, live output as it happens, rather than just a final summary message appearing all at once.

db3787c4112c1903b4122a030882a3bf7de16745.text: The tool now sends your entire conversation history to the server instead of just the last few messages. The server then decides which parts to use for generating ads. You will not see any changes in your interface, but the system has a more complete view of your chat when creating suggestions.

74616a3668e5a622d6e98737957d79fb61ad9486.text: When signing in through the command-line tool, users may now see a plain web address if their browser fails to open automatically. This helps people on devices where the automatic browser launch doesn't work, allowing them to manually copy the link to complete login.

84afe501fae4f357c8da24a46ee540703bdad6d6.text: In the command-line tool, the main shortcut for browsing past conversations changed its name to /history. The older shortcut /chats still works. People who type either one will see the same list of past conversations.

8f8d69631f510f5e00f0b95e875b7637a42d9b80.text: A small fix in the command-line assistant now shows the full final answer from web research helpers when they return all their messages or an organized result. It affects people using those helpers. They will see the helper’s final answer appear in its result box instead of being missing or replaced by partial text. The fix is live today.

dac685215273c06475caca9eeb14e068e2d0e9fb.text: A small internal fix ensures that when an ad has no title, the system now uses its call-to-action text instead. This prevents blank spaces in ad records. Advertisers might notice that their ads now display the button text if the main title was missing.

b73cf196116be5e193801702359014c9abf7fdf7.text: A small internal update makes the system try up to three times to take payment credits when a search fails on the first attempt. This helps people whose searches sometimes fail due to temporary glitches. If a search still fails after three tries, it shows an error instead of charging credits.

57ee778c1dc43fe76c8cf74948c6ece40f340197.text: The text-based assistant now responds to the Page Up and Page Down keys, letting you scroll back through previous messages or forward to the latest ones. Each press moves the view by most of the screen's height, so you can read older parts of the conversation without losing your place. This small update is live and applies to anyone using the command-line tool.

088b9926045a195d70dbe396641dfdd44e100662.text: The code-editing assistant now runs its usual mistake checks only after larger or less obvious changes, not after every tiny edit. It also saves suggested next steps for the end of its reply. This is a small live behavior change, so you may notice fewer pauses on simple edits and a cleaner ending.

53eca816fa3f666562181383b1c137f78c5b29fd.text: The tool now automatically re-tries sending requests to the database and web services when they temporarily fail due to network issues or server overload. This helps prevent errors for people using the assistant. If a request fails, the system waits a short time before trying again, up to three times.

2156595e43c31fc4c5c8873c0c69f8b9ba75fee8.text: Developers who automate text entry into the command-line tool will now see complete messages appear instead of partial fragments. This fixes a timing issue where fast input was previously cut off. The update is live for these specific automated workflows.

fe0f9da74428dd6f6ab8cdf0333f005332f6d099.text: The tool now looks up environment variables by name at runtime, rather than using a fixed list checked during setup. This affects developers configuring Model Context Protocol servers in the SDK. They will notice that variable references in configuration files resolve correctly even if the names are not known ahead of time.

958c4fea5be1efe9aecae7e88551e51d66015cb3.text: The command-line tool now loads its internal logging system only when debug output is requested, rather than always loading it. This change affects only users who manually enable analytics debugging. They would notice no visible difference in the tool's behavior, but the application starts slightly faster or uses less memory when debugging is off.

da03ad7a6b42e378db51a4acb8836f55d0e26465.text: Developers fixed a startup glitch in the command-line tool that could stop it from loading. Only people running the tool with debug mode turned on will see the effect. Normal use stays exactly the same.

c5de0df8248195257e8d9c953677f428d0e77aab.text: The tool now loads its basic file-handling parts at the start of each session instead of waiting until it needs them. This change speeds up the moment the program begins running. Users will not see any visual differences or new features, as the update only affects internal performance.

b58585a1b493b05414657cc11ec5d7883c46aa03.text: The assistant can now correctly connect to external services using the right security credentials when working in the background. This fixes a bug where these connections failed because the system looked for credentials in the wrong place. You will notice that background tasks involving these external tools now work reliably instead of stopping with an error.

42fda58c17245db40f843a3edddb27d09d6d0a3f.text: A small fix makes the ad banner in the command-line tool show 'Learn more' as the button text if the ad has no title. Without this, the button could appear blank or show broken text. The fix also prevents errors when saving ad records that lack a title or icon.

9d83bb9869fe418a6f49761a11e0f1e3efa33969.text: The program now records anonymous notes about how you use it, like when you open menus or finish tasks, and sends these notes to a reporting service. It also reports when automatic updates fail. You will not see anything change on your screen, and this data collection is active right now.

66270505ffecf8e449f3ba87cdea43b161532819.text: A small change to the command-line tool now freezes the elapsed-time counter in the status bar when the assistant stops to ask the user a question. Before, that timer could disappear, reset, or keep counting while the user was deciding what to answer. Today, the counter stays visible and paused during the question, then continues from where it stopped after the user replies.

7be012258fcb4a33bcabc702f71a45c936b46c55.text: Tables shown in the command-line interface now use decorative lines to create a grid, replacing the previous plain text layout. This visual update affects anyone viewing tables within the tool, making the data easier to read. If the table is too wide for the screen, the software automatically adjusts column sizes and adds an ellipsis to fit the content.

e520374fbcfa06c7757534671a0a9c3657b292ea.text: The command-line tool now displays an extra line of text when you run out of credits. This note explains that even if you have a subscription, you still need to buy credits to use certain other models. The change is live and affects anyone using the command-line interface.

b34f27c30a564364e351e955aeb9631cc8666b4e.text: A small internal update lets the system accept an optional session identifier when processing ad requests. This data is passed along to an external service only if provided, helping to link specific interactions together. Most users will notice no immediate difference, as this is a backend plumbing change for better tracking.

46254878afe23989a846b43e95312b28250ec585.text: When opening the connection screen without being signed in, the login page now launches automatically in your web browser. Previously, you had to manually click a button to start the sign-in process. This small change applies immediately to the desktop command-line tool.

b9faa7c76b61238580b33f2775b2e65401e291d9.text: The command-line tool now automatically recognizes custom assistants created by users. Previously, users had to manually list each custom assistant in the system's base configuration to make it available for use. This change removes that manual step, allowing the tool to see and use any custom assistant stored in the user's local folder without extra setup.

f06fa97aa368fd3c421b6045c3d68f1bc28bf63b.text: The tool now collects extra details about how you use it, such as how long commands take or whether a folder is a project. This data is sent privately to help the team spot slow features, and you will not see any difference in the tool's behavior.

0d38d8e3d5b6bae22fccdd74b7413731d7447c68.text: The command-line tool now sends only the final question and the final answer from your chat history to the advertising service, instead of the last three questions. It also includes a unique session identifier to help track the conversation. This change is live today.

a88f3d09172212d924391e82eadcd75bd8d69eba.text: The list of quick commands shown in the assistant's help menu has been rearranged to put the most useful options first, specifically connecting a subscription and starting a new project. This change is live and affects anyone using the command-line tool, who will now see these primary actions at the top of the list instead of buried among less frequent options like logging out or enabling ads.

2745a2ad758cea1e0e5949d66f770cbca80292b1.text: When the program starts, it quietly checks if your login information is still valid and updates it if needed. This affects only people who use the command-line tool. You won't see anything happen, but your account status will be ready to go immediately when you start using it.

d94c3b4f078ea68664d0d8e2e2bb423ef8d9106d.text: The system now logs when you use a specific login method for the assistant. It records three details: the login attempt, hitting a usage limit, or an authentication failure. This is for internal tracking only, so you will not see any changes in your interface.

07d770778199061f3891325a6f628645b4748a3d.text: A new shortcut lets you type a specific command to instantly open your account's usage page in your web browser. This helps you quickly find and purchase more credits. The command does not get saved in your typing history, keeping the action private.

a436fb59e728ff5c31ced5a91864866579da7104.text: The command-line tool now sends only your last three typed messages to the ad service, ignoring older history and assistant replies. This makes the data sent smaller and more focused. You will not notice any change in how the tool works.

558d2c89186764a8e65d162ef4881a5248a4534b.text: The program now changes the color of your remaining usage percentage in the bottom status bar. If you have 10% or less left, the number turns red, and if you have 25% or less, it turns yellow. Otherwise, it stays gray.

09578671897274d3acb5a20c235b5368e04f2730.text: A note was added to the internal code to record where a specific data format came from. This helps the team track the origin of the tool. Regular users will not notice any change.

69e6936e75c11426c89c6e87aa492fb4707058d9.text: The text shown for the ad control options in the command menu now includes the word 'beta'. This change is live and affects anyone who sees these options in the list. You would notice the label next to the ad enable and disable choices has changed to clearly mark them as experimental.

afd5a5fb26404957351454ae6cfaaa61f34fc2f6.text: Previously, when the web researcher subagent finished its task, the results were missing from the command-line interface. This update ensures that the subagent's output now appears correctly in the terminal, allowing you to see the final text or status of the research without needing to check elsewhere.

9c0b8acb628d9f3699a74960aba0ed8691ba0d1b.text: The AI assistant now skips time-consuming safety checks for edits under ten lines. This applies to internal tools used by staff. People will notice responses appear faster for minor tweaks, while larger changes still undergo full verification.

855741f5fbcd935fe8b0c9b2624f2bf6b1de4585.text: Ad rotation is now simpler: ads only show after you send a message, swap every 60 seconds, and stop after three ads if you stay idle. The server now checks your identity before processing ad requests and records who saw which ad for better tracking. This change is live.

e99971717407dd2a1eea0d0595c99d244cd530b3.text: The system now records the specific error code when an ad request fails. Previously, it hid the failure by reporting a successful status. This change helps internal teams quickly identify and fix ad delivery issues without guessing at the cause.

88a308155a7e7beacd38292b5234e16f3ecbcd22.text: The system now ignores blank text when preparing messages for the AI model. This prevents errors caused by sending empty text fields. The change is internal and live, so users will not notice any difference in their experience.

96591067bade84488cd8127638b44726ac87e11a.text: The internal tool that summarizes conversation history now keeps only 10% of the total context instead of 15%. This means less information is stored for future reference, which may cause the assistant to forget more details from earlier in a long chat.

d477b9c4ec225146614de7953ec1c90eb9cd3ed9.text: The website now checks if an account is suspended before allowing a credit purchase. This applies to users trying to buy extra usage credits through the web interface. Suspended users will see a message saying their account is suspended and directing them to contact support instead of completing the payment.

a1ed1b06034c3724b962164753cf6bb97e905dd9.text: The system now wraps each new message in clear labels before sending it to the ad service. It also checks whether the message already exists to avoid sending duplicates. This small internal fix ensures the ad service sees the correct conversation context without extra or missing text.

500a7b527c8bb22cac539bf045a7caa82fb12016.text: The software now records a timestamp for every message sent to the AI. This change is internal and only affects how the system checks its own accuracy behind the scenes. You will not notice any difference in the app.

026aa43673a847a3dee5f3b752d1800436be8100.text: The software now skips a specific performance test when running on automated servers, because that test requires a real interactive terminal which those servers lack. This change affects only the internal testing process and does not impact the features or performance experienced by end users. You would not notice any difference in how the software behaves.

135181161b75b9b8a65fc48830f607c04d8f5761.text: The system now cleans up extra spaces from text before sending it to the AI for counting, which makes the count more accurate. If a counting request fails, the support team will now see the exact text and settings that caused the error, making it faster to fix. This change is internal and live, so customers will not notice any direct difference in how the product works.

1b7f63b5ab369b2d07964130b6d337bc3e1a5976.text: The system now notices when five minutes have passed since the last message and automatically refreshes its memory of the conversation. This prevents expensive processing fees that occur when the AI provider's temporary memory expires. You will see no visual changes, but the system may run slightly faster or cost less to operate.

8ed3d48f8a1e85adcc5796116ab6237cb1c370b0.text: The command-line tool now checks if the terminal multiplexer can actually start a session, not just if it is installed. This prevents false positives in restricted environments like automated build servers. The change is internal to testing utilities and does not affect end-user features.

9bc6b6279a6d6308b140675fc4e776acb472a322.text: The test system now skips slow checks that require outside services during routine runs. This change is live today and affects only internal developers. They will see the standard check finish faster with fewer confusing errors, but the skipped checks still run when requested.

233b7aa652437e7799f52ad20ddfdb5f2a114b46.text: The system now hides its internal 'thinking' notes before creating summaries of conversations. This prevents those private drafts from appearing in the final recap. This is an internal cleanup, so regular users will not notice any changes.

d556ad7feeb7ae22dd584dbbf92d1fae490ae8c8.text: A small internal fix corrected a check that verifies how the tool handles payment errors. This change does not affect how the tool works for anyone, and you will not notice any difference.

128cb40232f2da78f25fffe7ace79c21a64ae6d3.text: The coding assistant now asks you clarifying questions by default, instead of only doing so in its most advanced mode. This change is active immediately. You will notice it pausing to ask for details about your request before starting work, unless you have specifically turned off that feature.

e99a693aea32b666e23f3b5d31a480106d08b5a7.text: The command-line tool now remembers which agents are currently working, so it stops redrawing the screen every time a small detail changes. This makes the interface feel snappier and less flickery while chatting with multiple agents at once.

5f023636ac8fd147b251e6565adb745ed88b98f5.text: The command-line tool now recognizes a specific network signal indicating that your account has run out of credits. This means the assistant will correctly pause and ask you to add funds when that signal arrives, instead of potentially getting stuck or showing a confusing error. This update is active for all users of the tool.

d86eebfd3bafba52cf5b4c73b8ed4b0a8fef1cae.text: The tooling team fixed a bug where internal activity records were written twice. This small, internal change cleans up the logs. Developers will now see one entry per event instead of duplicates.

bac76a77d3f823a386e81067d463a4aaa9dcf7be.text: A small internal update aligned test data with the billing system's new ad balance category. This change affects only the software's automated checks, not the live service. Users will notice no difference.

151e202d4da7d9ebd388342495b4a3bd4ae934bf.text: A hidden internal check that used to reject oddly formatted ad messages has been removed. This small change only affects the private communication channel between company systems. Regular users will not notice any difference.

7c95ae2da1567bc3b3c089abfdfbdc32682dc45d.text: The system now decides whether to record user activity based directly on the current environment setting rather than a separate configuration check. This change affects all users, but they will not notice any difference in the product itself. It is live today.

67a33a8db3e67c1aa872f9529dc45989b3628de7.text: Developers updated their internal checks to match a new way of starting the analytics system. This change affects only the team's testing tools and does not alter how the product works for you.

4d37107ebcc0605f494429c7ba35071ac554e4de.text: A small internal cleanup fixed the rules for a test that checks how the assistant handles long conversations. This change does not affect the assistant's behavior or any user-facing features, so you would not notice any difference.

e30037ccf61d7fd6c1227087fa99d890f66ff311.text: Pressing the Escape key no longer deletes text you have typed into the chat box. This change helps people who use specific keyboard shortcuts for navigation, preventing them from accidentally losing their message. Now, you must use a different key combination to clear the text.

7a3e53a749133333f6c3aedcb2e70fc81d1f43ee.text: The program now automatically cleans up the screen when it closes, even if it crashes. This prevents garbled text or stuck cursor states from remaining visible in the terminal window after you exit.

ec0c885cfa1098cd8b6c441b3fb44737b7a74e34.text: Developers added hidden notes to the internal system to track when analytics tools start up and if they encounter errors. This change only affects the technical team and does not alter how the application looks or functions for customers. No one outside the engineering group will notice any difference.

08e01629f478039b00048950ecf21ca7abf831ef.text: The program now records its startup details and chat requests in a consistent format. This helps the support team see if tracking tools are connected correctly and logs basic chat activity. Only the team reading these internal records will notice the change; customers see no difference.

874054fee9db3ed1cdc1fa21d529b2f7588e025e.text: The command-line tool now filters out system instructions and internal notes before asking for an ad, sending only the conversation between you and the assistant. This helps the ad service understand the context better to find a relevant match. You might see slightly more relevant ads, or occasionally no ad if the conversation history was mostly internal notes.

326eb6eebd6e018ecb5c12e82fb0cbe3d865914c.text: The assistant now hides its internal reasoning steps unless you use the standard or maximum settings. In the faster, lighter modes, it skips those hidden thoughts and gives you a brief, direct explanation of its actions instead. This change affects only the assistant's behavior and will not be visible in your dashboard or reports.

9bea7bee8d5287bdee1f40071f274db3a66e9bb7.text: The thinking preview in the command-line tool now uses the full available terminal width and joins lines with newlines instead of spaces. This prevents the preview from cutting off text too early or wrapping incorrectly. Users running the tool will see a more accurate three-line preview of the assistant's reasoning.

f18a8857ac5977f5717213c9b3af27a2ca35699e.text: The system now counts every piece of information in a message, not just the main text, when pictures are attached. This internal fix ensures the assistant accurately tracks conversation length, preventing it from cutting off important details too early or too late. Regular users won't see a change, but the assistant will manage long chats with images more reliably.

318ead2df33872679a07d548f4d558d4d528829c.text: When the assistant saves a new task list, it now replies with a simple confirmation instead of repeating every task back. This reduces clutter in the chat history. The change is live and affects how task updates appear in conversations.

131863efb600d81a773a41da157ec1817771914d.text: The AI assistant stopped trimming messages from the middle of its conversation history. This prevents the assistant from getting confused when matching its requests to use tools with the results of those requests. Users might notice fewer errors when the assistant tries to use tools.

27e7b6d754920d27c373c37ed7138c46b2a63848.text: This is a small internal fix for a tool that helps people write software. It changes how the tool checks its own error reports to make sure helpful debugging information is kept instead of thrown away. Regular people using the software will not notice any difference.

55a194bea95574fd13e94cf52d4cfd2e7734bfab.text: When the AI assistant crashes, it now automatically saves the full conversation history and its core instructions to a hidden log. This internal update helps engineers trace the exact cause of errors without needing to reproduce the issue. Regular users will not notice any change in the app's behavior or appearance.

382195146821bd80e40fed2ffba7ba5efcdbe4f4.text: The tool now adjusts the project selection screen when your terminal window is too short to show everything. If you resize your window or use a small screen, the application automatically hides the logo and extra spacing to make room for the list of projects and the input box. This ensures you can always see and select a folder, even if your window is very small.

a995965967df8fdbc1506425313f7cad072c0489.text: The folder list now sorts names alphabetically, and code projects appear in a different color. The highlighted row uses a softer background so the text stays easy to read in both light and dark themes. This is live today for people choosing a project folder in the command-line tool.

d9e302b2e94dc95b45778526b88bc592e38cf8ca.text: When the chat system fails to load a response, it now automatically saves the full conversation text to a private error report. This change helps internal support teams see exactly what was said before the crash. Regular users will not notice any difference in the app interface.

864a1f1e6c44b1841f5ee725c4252b55192780fe.text: The command-line tool now waits only one second for background data to save before closing. If the saving process gets stuck, the tool will still shut down cleanly after that brief pause. This prevents the application from hanging indefinitely when you try to exit, ensuring it always closes properly.

ba20001626733deae4168b84a899b43f5f31c832.text: The command-line tool now resets your terminal screen automatically when you press Ctrl+C to quit. This prevents the display from remaining stuck in a broken state after you leave the project picker or login screens. This small fix is live today.

9b898076ad7ce25534618bfa7a50f6c6827aa4f8.text: When a command-line tool hit an error, it previously erased the hidden conversation context attached to the message. It now keeps that context visible, allowing support staff to see exactly what the tool was doing when it failed. This change is live and helps diagnose issues, though regular users will not see a visual difference in the main chat window.

1c0912ab07069d32ef9bf83302fa44ccf7a5249c.text: The program’s setup instructions were shortened by removing a redundant step, so it now goes straight to the task it used to reach via a shortcut. This affects only how the software is built, not how it works. You will notice nothing, as this is an internal housekeeping change.

201d60896c1ae47d039c0ec9a98b52155ebfeb37.text: Pressing the Tab key in the command-line chat now switches between modes when no file suggestions appear. This change is live today. Previously, Tab inserted a blank space; now it activates the assistant's autonomous mode.

b64dce68089ffb73a86ae204cfd483769030a1cf.text: Buttons in the command-line interface now require a full press-and-release action to work, rather than activating on a simple hover or partial click. This prevents accidental selections when using certain terminal applications. Users will notice fewer unintended button presses when moving their cursor over interface elements.

df5708ec8d1cbeac271e912f58fd6cdda28f39ed.text: A note explaining why the command-line tool builds in production mode was moved to sit next to the correct setting. This fixes a mix-up where the reason for the safety check appeared attached to the wrong option. Developers reading the build script will now see the explanation clearly, but everyday users will notice no change.

41659feb0430aa21b917e73a8e9b2bedcfbd5c50.text: Developers running the command-line tool locally will now start it from the main project folder instead of a subfolder. This change fixes issues where the tool could not find files or settings located at the project root. Regular users of the final product will not notice any difference.

25db595fe9859abdb39da090e44b7e4cbe428e53.text: A small internal fix in the command-line tool now keeps the 'thinking' sections of the AI's response stable when you expand or collapse them. Previously, if new text arrived, these sections might shift position, causing your open or closed state to apply to the wrong block. Now, each section has a unique identity, so your view remains consistent.

e5780608c317ba6bbd3a18c5c5d966d7a3896280.text: A small internal note was added to the code that creates the command-line tool's downloadable files. It explains why the tool must use a specific safe version of its display engine to prevent crashes. Regular users won't see any change, as this only helps developers understand how the tool is built.

680bafa4a2ca4b259404e954b3db541a9e693c70.text: The tool now explains that using the specific agent command ignores any custom setups saved in your project folder. This prevents unexpected changes to how the assistant behaves. People who create their own custom agents will notice updated instructions: they must run the tool normally, without that specific command, to test their new creations.

a0f70e367714a7ca875128b946f1ee81ebd9b619.text: The internal system now reads its setup instructions from a shared list instead of having them hardcoded. This change is live and only affects the automated checks that run behind the scenes. A regular person would notice no visible difference.

a82662b13f70356e4dc381ad40478ee90f5e24d6.text: A small internal fix stops our testing tools from breaking when checking the code. Developers will see smoother automated checks without manual workarounds. This change affects only the team building the software, not the customers using the final product.

9de3cfd7328a6436630d0b2e8758dd87b11ff6fc.text: The automated checks for the editor's 'best-of-n' feature were updated to look for proof of work in two different places instead of just one. This change affects only the internal testing system, not the live product. If someone ran a test today, they would see it pass more reliably because the checker now accepts a wider variety of evidence that the assistant successfully added a new function.

fc563134985b83d2c57b79b6e6b796423eb84d9b.text: The tool that creates the final program now builds it in a streamlined mode that removes internal testing tools. This affects only the people who download the finished program. They will notice nothing, but the program will be slightly smaller and run a bit faster.

391be7121819e81dbfd9849d29a1128d6b82457d.text: The background system that automatically tests the software now uses a newer version of its underlying engine. This change applies only to the internal testing environment and will not affect how the product works for customers.

dc4b67202e6431c98f0a1e0123e042e85a5ca1e6.text: The program now uses one built-in tool to prepare custom assistant instructions instead of juggling two separate tools. This makes the setup lighter and faster for people running the software locally. You will not see any difference in how the assistant answers, only that it might start up a little quicker.

c14d06271ac1eacec8974bb924022e49bcc270f0.text: The system now checks its own rules to ensure that when a specific helper is called, it doesn't automatically get access to other helpers unless those connections are explicitly set up. This prevents unintended interactions between different parts of the assistant. Since this is an internal test to verify existing behavior, you won't notice any change in how the software works today.

53e16e0e54d46b627ddaefc2c06fc7fa3831b2cd.text: The software now automatically uses a backup method to process custom instructions when the main method is unavailable. This fixes a bug where locally stored instructions were ignored in certain packaged versions of the application. Users who rely on these local files will see their instructions work correctly again.

f943f8dcdcacf53ade9e9c59f5cc2f251f26a003.text: The program now starts faster when you name a specific assistant on the command line because it skips the step of loading the full list of available assistants. This speed-up does not apply if you are trying to publish an assistant, ensuring that feature still works as expected. You would notice the program opening more quickly, with no change to how you use it.

7bee7825c743832ab15be6d7fe2a74efd27b7955.text: The usage notification at the bottom of the command line now opens your account page when clicked. A new 'See more' label shows it is a link. This change is live for all command line users.

33e33c5df485c4ee34c0a945a7bcbd263757e64f.text: The program's underlying engine was updated to a newer, more stable version. This change affects the internal setup used to run the tool. You will not notice any difference in how the tool behaves or looks.

bac6b6cb5f0591c3f52b67e53d4da3102737e420.text: A small internal fix makes the assistant's tools load more reliably. It corrects a path error that could make the tools fail to start in some setups. Most people will not notice anything, but the tools are now less likely to break.

c7cc70ffc827b782a8b9b50c068e4606fedefcee.text: The main AI assistant was told to stop manually launching a separate tool that cleans up conversation history. This internal adjustment prevents duplicate tasks, as that cleanup happens automatically. Regular users will not notice any change in the interface or results.

80432f1b4f1ab10ce0575cbd9131422c6eb8c518.text: When a specific assistant is chosen, it can now only create the helpers explicitly listed for that assistant, ignoring any other available tools. This prevents unintended actions by restricting what the assistant is allowed to launch. This change is live.

ebd5edbbb74dae39f5c9a1fc1a855d946486a289.text: The system now checks messages for formatting errors before sending them to the AI. This helps developers find problems faster when the assistant fails to reply. Regular users won't notice any change, but issues will be easier to fix.

b45bf79e8b2ada08ccfad5873fbefd8e8fb9231e.text: The team updated the internal machines that build the software for older Intel-based Mac computers. This ensures the application continues to work correctly on those specific devices. Regular users won't see any changes, as this was a small background maintenance task.

19b5b7a6455bfa5120d548c053f552aa96d89b6a.text: The tool's setup command now runs smoothly without crashing due to hidden text formatting checks. This small internal fix affects only people using the command-line setup tool. They will notice fewer error messages when starting a new project.

2ca472a0cd39b8081ab62966d071c943c469ea14.text: The tool now checks if a specific conversion helper is available before trying to use it. If the helper is missing in certain packaged versions, the tool skips processing custom local scripts but continues to run pre-installed ones. This prevents startup errors for users running the software in compiled executable formats.

9f074c8f750b353560565210fb8562a773951aa1.text: Two internal tests that only work with a specific tool were excluded from the automated checks. This change prevents those tests from causing false errors during the build process. Internal developers will notice cleaner test results.

699c6198a75338e02e129ee74cb2ca8f0fedbd4e.text: The system's internal instructions for its most advanced mode were adjusted to be more direct. It now tells the assistant to implement the entire requested task at once, rather than breaking it down into single steps. This change is live today and applies only to users on the Max plan.

343f9ec46ee9509fb999c8e080c6148ed3a40493.text: The website's documentation pages for the AI assistant's model choices have been updated to ensure their comparison tables display correctly. This affects only the internal web documentation site. Readers looking at the 'What Models' page will now see neatly formatted tables instead of broken text.

51ae4b3182a0298139656c9319fb9d85c6072c90.text: A safety check that stops users from getting banned for too many payment disputes was moved to a new testing system. This internal update only affects the tools developers use to verify the rule works. Regular users will notice no changes, as the actual ban logic remains exactly the same.

811a0abfc1ec6c13cd8ef76013bd7a6928c12e45.text: This small internal update fixes how two automated tests identify their scope, allowing the type-checker to correctly distinguish between global and local variables. It affects only the testing infrastructure, so customers and users will not notice any change in the product's behavior or features. The fix is live today and ensures these specific tests run without compatibility errors.

42f6dc11aa645d63658468bd7d0059435d08ea90.text: The code viewer now ignores duplicate labels that caused hidden errors during updates. This internal fix prevents warnings in the developer console but changes nothing visible to you.

203ba11fc2d9ef5687ad7f61b28c26d22193f472.text: The store page now loads a smaller list of agents for search engines and health checks. Visitors might notice the store loads faster. When you hover over an agent, the browser quietly prepares the next page. This speeds up opening agent details.

ec08abd50cf82fe06e8aeabcd2de8094f20be761.text: The collapsed summary text in the command-line tool is now a clickable button. Previously, only a small part was interactive. Now, clicking anywhere on that summary line will expand the details.

55396b181ba377b0e5aedbf9118569029f6a5005.text: Fixed a bug where diagrams on internal documentation pages could briefly disappear or fail to load correctly due to conflicting naming rules between the server and the browser. This change is live and ensures that all diagrams render smoothly for anyone viewing these internal docs.

a55e9bb7be033f3dbd8868778cbb8a5209452404.text: On mobile, the bar at the bottom of the documentation pages now opens the menu when you tap anywhere on it, not just the small icon. This makes it easier to navigate the site on a phone.

09c2ec040fafdb90a175f154097895e080e0dfce.text: A small internal fix ensures the system correctly counts payment disputes for a specific customer, preventing errors in the account suspension check. This change is live but invisible to users, as it only corrects data retrieval logic behind the scenes. No customer-facing features or messages were altered in a way that changes user experience.

e392b80b1bcfa1947ffd24f5624bb924fa0770af.text: The software now requires every agent link to include its exact version number, rejecting any shortcuts or assumed defaults. This affects internal system stability, ensuring that the visual map of connected agents always displays precise version labels instead of potentially ambiguous names. Users will see clearer, more accurate diagrams when reviewing agent relationships.

ae7c26c81519220602e7916920af8d6f73cf5380.text: A small internal change is live today. The side menu for the documentation no longer shows the headings Learn, Build, and Reference. It now lists the links directly in one simpler menu, with slightly less space between items.

a78e9fb85a9a938121845beefece882a3527f0fc.text: A small internal fix ensures that text inside tables displays correctly, even when it contains special formatting like code snippets. Previously, this formatting broke the table layout, causing text to disappear or appear as raw symbols. Users viewing documentation pages will now see these tables render cleanly without missing content.

e25bb873f43b98638d6adb5e98f9102c22186fa6.text: The expanded task box now removes the extra empty space at the top and bottom. This applies to the command-line tool interface. You will see a tighter, more compact layout with less blank margin around the text.

93fed7acb54103cc815ec637f2fce59ddc608c6c.text: The internal assistant now pauses to write down its reasoning for moderately complex problems. This applies to all standard and high-effort modes, with the highest setting using this step constantly. You might see more detailed planning text before the assistant acts.

39f46e6a389c16d28b5dd59c2348268e2c67b99d.text: The terminal interface now checks if your computer's window can display millions of colors or only a limited set. If you use the default macOS Terminal app, the logo and cursor will automatically switch to simpler, standard colors so they don't look broken or washed out. This change is live today.

75dc6adbd550325abae26c02c5e043db59d9bab4.text: The command-line tool now hides the inner workings of its search and file-listing helpers. Instead of showing every step these small assistants take, the tool collapses their activity into a brief summary line. This makes the text output easier to read by removing clutter, and the change is active immediately.

0c7192b7f8041d52d8d307934b0a35af8448933c.text: The 'Thinking' section in the command-line tool now uses less horizontal space and removes the '• Thinking' label. The collapsed preview text no longer adds empty lines to maintain a fixed height, so the layout appears more compact and cleaner.

d695bf8a37aa4c4c8b5c13d56b347d2d0288d39c.text: The command-line tool now pulls its text colors from a central theme setting instead of having them hardcoded. This means error messages and dimmed text will automatically match your chosen dark or light mode preferences. The change is internal cleanup, so you will only notice better visual consistency if you switch themes.

142aa82d0af8e6072bec419d6dcac60303836915.text: We updated the website's building blocks to ensure they stay at specific, tested versions rather than automatically accepting new updates. This change is internal and affects only the site's stability and maintenance. You will not notice any visual differences or new features; the site will simply continue to function as expected without unexpected changes from automatic updates.

2f68dbcb44c47a3bb0de581b2fc4b52c94875c73.text: The command view now starts folded up when you open the tool. This affects people who use the command line interface. You will see less clutter on the screen until you choose to expand that section.

3e5877af04452de8571ca740dd94d34c0127f73f.text: A small internal update lets a specific tool return the full text of a computer command's result instead of a shortened summary. This affects only the tool's internal setup, so regular users will not notice any change in how things work.

f84768cdf76cefcd313629a3ae7eeb97e051b9f3.text: The underlying software that powers the website was updated to its latest version. This change is internal and invisible to visitors, who will notice no difference in how the site looks or behaves. The update ensures the site continues to work correctly as technology standards evolve.

a3c31fe3eef97c4ca79b6db1427ae5b50e70bb5d.text: The mobile documentation menu now announces itself clearly to screen readers and ignores taps on non-clickable section headers. Code examples in the docs display with correct colors and structure without breaking. These updates are live for anyone reading the online documentation.

a8b27b0b515f609e4a64a2e3e3def342d136df16.text: The system switched back to a simpler method for handling complex editing tasks. It now uses an older, more stable version of the writing model and stops generating an extra, unnecessary draft attempt. This change is live and affects how the tool processes detailed code updates, though the visible output remains largely the same.

1ae077607ebcd74d3be2a464383163ac6e9260de.text: A small internal adjustment was made to how the system reads information from external tools. This change fixes a technical labeling issue so the software can correctly identify the type of data being received. Since this is an internal code correction, the interface and behavior remain exactly the same for you. You will not notice any difference in how the tools work or what they produce.

05edece1025a55155583ebf785527d020ccf7ecc.text: The software now uses a fixed version of a helper library and a newer version of its build tool. This change affects only the internal engineering team, not the people who use the product. No customer will notice any difference.

b661d92a033829829f2e951d64d11ce5ab9f7eaa.text: The text preview for the AI's reasoning steps now displays more cleanly, with the '...' indicator merged directly into the text rather than appearing in a separate column. This small visual fix prevents the layout from shifting or jumping, especially when viewing nested conversations.

becdfc24ad1cdef4db1f1e73d0138ae098d87fc0.text: The program now receives its tracking settings at startup instead of looking them up later. This internal cleanup prevents the tracking system from starting unless the website is running in its live, public environment. Regular visitors will not notice any change.

be87a2d06d2b7f35b5da169bd7aefc4d6da9203f.text: The internal coding assistant now stops writing a closing recap after making changes, because only the changed files are passed along. It also tries the normal editing option first. The change is live, but it is a small internal cleanup, so ordinary users will not notice it.

d9a397e6693692820f72b3ffc33effc80f27cdda.text: A small internal fix corrects how the text-based assistant arranges nested information on the screen. It ensures that when related details are added, they stay in their proper order instead of being shuffled to the end. This change is live and helps prevent confusing or out-of-place text in the command-line interface.

6d5bdef3f6479d606c79e8b0539da7774a272fdb.text: A small internal adjustment restored an older version of the text assistant for the code editor's simple mode. This change affects only the specific text assistant used in the code editor's simple mode. Users will notice a difference in the responses generated by the assistant in that mode.

c95af8ff33cfdb30ca51128342f2fce9340074de.text: The text prompts shown when the assistant asks for a choice were shortened. Extra instructions about using arrow keys to open or close options, or using Escape to skip, were removed. People using the command-line tool will see a simpler list of key instructions, but the way they select an option remains the same.

1ddd94d3131fb162a60154fd08fdf34753f58dae.text: Clicking a suggested follow-up question now sends it immediately, instead of just filling the text box. This change affects users of the command-line chat interface. You will notice the suggestion appears in the chat history right away, while any text you had already typed remains in the input box.

45d06c8428e1e2dc262240d4cea3e1e48c80c88e.text: A small fix to an internal test that checks whether the command-line tool correctly reports an error when a required web address is missing. The test was failing a basic consistency check before this change, even though the behavior it tests was already correct. Nothing visible changes for anyone using the tool today.

5fff2286a0731b3d49e37103aacc010af4a54c5b.text: The text interface stopped adding extra blank space to the left of assistant replies and tool results. This change is live now. Readers will see slightly wider text lines without the double indentation previously applied to nested messages.

8fc366616feebd867e5c469c404b7bb2223f897c.text: The tool that sets up new workspaces now correctly asks for permission to use saved environment settings in the right folder. This fixes an issue where those settings were ignored, causing the workspace to start without necessary configuration. Developers will notice their new workspaces load correctly immediately.

a1cf20b4930cb261ed1152d55236ffa8a9177ca8.text: Clicking a suggested follow-up question now fills the text box instead of sending it immediately. You can edit or review the question before pressing enter. The list also adjusts to fit narrow screens.

84bf61ed7ef12adce11980d82bde80f3c77afce0.text: The tool's visual engine received a routine maintenance update. This affects people using the command-line interface on their computer. They might notice smoother screen drawing, but nothing else changes.

715d336aefb50a08038ad8e61600ef78a49e2722.text: A small copy button now sits next to the time stamp on your own messages in the command-line chat. Clicking it saves the text to your clipboard, so you can paste it elsewhere without manually selecting it.

a769e88e81d9efc26ef8f4567fc0a35723348b03.text: A small internal fix ensures that secret settings, like passwords and database addresses, correctly reach the tools developers use to manage data. This prevents errors when working on new projects in isolated folders. Developers will notice smoother setup and fewer mysterious failures when running database commands.

d60f4be4a11b1da19a0c5dfc2bcbb4b7fd1cb997.text: When a tool asks a question with multiple choices, selecting the custom option now properly deselects any previously chosen answers to prevent conflicts. The visual indicator for the custom option also changes to match the question type, appearing as a checkbox when multiple answers are allowed and a radio button otherwise. This small update applies to the command-line interface and is live.

30856999a66a5eeea585d77aa8651d66e6d89d53.text: A small internal change makes the tool's self-checks more reliable. Instead of temporarily removing a global setting to test for errors, the check now passes that specific setting directly to the part being tested. This prevents the test from accidentally affecting other parts of the tool while running.

487d9b5ada641db3ce0661b0c27bba7b1aea7373.text: The project moved its database tooling to a more central location and updated to the latest versions. This is an internal housekeeping task for the development team. Regular users will not see any changes in the application's behavior or appearance.

efb4ec60987bddaebc096cf506546b4b487c2ec8.text: The program's text instructions for the follow-up suggestion feature were deleted because they were outdated or unnecessary. This is an internal cleanup that changes no visible behavior. You will not notice any difference.

1e59edaedf642587724767fd23812abc1f5da98c.text: The command-line tool now uses an older version of its display library. This change fixes instability introduced by a recent update. It affects only the text interface used in the terminal, not the main application.

66a0ba3d04a5bc1cfa6c2a189303258d0e313351.text: The command-line program now shows file and document lookups with a uniform layout. It also handles sending typed text and skipping question prompts with a single shared routine. The visible result is cleaner text output and more consistent form behavior.

2bb979ff71df8b46a33d306f51f2138ed47ff3e5.text: The command-line tool now speaks directly to you instead of talking about you in the third person. When you skip questions, it says 'You skipped the questions' rather than 'User skipped the questions.' Similarly, it labels your responses as 'Your answers' instead of 'User Answers.' This small wording update makes the interaction feel more natural and personal.

a730d3cbc353019224567e0313077f1d444ef515.text: The automated system that sends out new versions of the software tools now uses the correct command to check the code before publishing. This ensures the release process runs smoothly without errors. The change is already live and affects only the internal release pipeline.

4495f6e886c38895dbb5bb817693a06d49643bb7.text: This is a small internal fix for the testing team. It teaches the automated checks to recognize two specific hidden configuration files as empty placeholders rather than missing items. The software itself remains unchanged, so customers will not notice any difference.

63b9a612692835b63c3e08e91ef8e251fc059dbe.text: We removed two old shortcuts for releasing the software library. The release process now uses a single standard command. This is an internal cleanup for the team that builds the library. Customers will see no change.

e3945fed7a6b0cd294cd5a0bae769838feae2c9d.text: The software now checks if a file exists using a standard method instead of a specialized one. This affects the tool's ability to read project files and apply changes across different computer environments. Users may notice improved stability when the tool scans for existing files, though there is no visible change to the interface.

ed58bd74ecf1901d0f22f956616a6079f57baf37.text: The store's 'Editor's Choice' list now highlights the newer 'base2' assistants instead of the old 'base' ones. This change is live today. Customers browsing the store will see the updated recommendations immediately.

7c90418da5d2db3838bea9bd580ba77dea941db1.text: The gray text color used in the online documentation was made lighter to improve readability against dark backgrounds. This change is live and affects anyone reading these help pages in dark mode. They will notice that body text paragraphs appear slightly brighter and easier to read.

e26fdf1bdbbec7ca5f1928250c43247520484f58.text: When you attach pictures to a message, they previously vanished if you pressed Enter before the assistant finished answering the first message. The tool now keeps those pictures visible in your input box so you don't have to upload them again. This fix is active immediately for all users of the command-line interface.

6378076019964299f2a88220770f254a0f93eef4.text: The text on the help pages now looks easier to read, especially in dark mode. The words appear in a lighter gray, and the space above and below the headings has been reduced. This change affects anyone reading the documentation online and is live today.

195d99303cf451f51a3b55bc4c8e54ac214f2d60.text: The software's internal packaging tool was adjusted to correctly identify shared components as separate parts rather than trying to bundle them all together. This fixes a build error that prevented the toolkit from being created. Developers using the toolkit will not see any changes in how it works, but the team can now successfully build and release it.

d665703accecfcf2b72d2e5a10a3797cec6c52b0.text: The help guide for the coding assistant's different work styles was updated to show a simple table comparing them. Readers now see which AI model each style uses and whether it checks its own work, instead of confusing instructions about old keyboard shortcuts. This makes it easier to pick the right setting for simple fixes or complex projects.

fb28635df30c05560253479bdc0eca8834578deb.text: The help page now states that AI providers do not use your code or chat history for training. It also removed old instructions for starting new projects and moved the open-source information higher up. Visitors reading the FAQ will see these updated answers immediately.

ff2c0cb4afb9c5fc195e64c8601e1dd89f959932.text: This small internal update removes a width limit on the code and diagram boxes in the documentation when viewed on a phone. The boxes now stretch to fit the screen width instead of staying narrow. This affects anyone reading the documentation on a mobile device.

14d9ad5b0cac963b14491bd5fc3d7ea634b07602.text: The team added a guide explaining how to start and stop the computer programs needed for building new features. This helps staff find where to look for setup instructions and how to manage their own work environments without interfering with others. Nothing changes for regular customers, and this update does not affect the live product.

90adb08db264ee8eda935219b117163dc7391e3d.text: The commands used to start, stop, and check the status of background services have been renamed to shorter versions. This change affects internal team members who use these tools to manage their local development environment. They will notice the new, quicker command names when typing these instructions or reading the updated guides.

101c8e6373bf89d48089d1a3415284ca4ca0e6e5.text: A hidden note announcing that a new assistant was created has been removed from the conversation history. This change only affects the internal background processes and is live today. You will not see any difference in the interface or the final answers.

f9c8712d131c51eb2678735a6b5c4573287e30cd.text: A small internal tool update fixes how settings are loaded to prevent old values from interfering with new ones. It also adds a help command to the developer startup script, which now displays usage instructions and log locations when requested. These changes only affect the team's internal development tools and are not visible to regular users.

8f6eccc8d6c7c475f435c2bffe0fbff757dfcd96.text: When you launch the assistant from your computer's command line, you can now type a special code to pick how it behaves. This lets you start it in a quick mode, a deep-thinking mode, or a planning mode right away. If you type more than one code, the last one you typed takes effect.

ff334f0754e4c38e916726d4c5abe1107d32795c.text: The help guide's opening section was renamed to 'Getting Started' to better match its content. Instructions for creating new projects from templates were removed from this guide, as those options are no longer supported here. These updates apply only to the online documentation and do not change how the software functions.

aa2cc38ce520b8ada2de9b10e604f38b4ccd018c.text: The system now labels messages when a helper task starts. This label lets the system remove that specific note from older history to save space. Regular users will not notice any difference.

2e33a27c5b4118b01ad61c6fb66d0344f4ae9acc.text: A small internal change improves how the system warns assistant workers about which tools they can use. It specifically tells workers that tools mentioned earlier might belong to the main assistant, preventing them from trying to use unavailable features and causing errors.

6bd4adab84518b8638e6bedbbf4dddaddb1e402b.text: A small internal fix ensures the system only looks for actual typed instructions when deciding how to respond. This prevents the assistant from reacting to empty or broken messages that lack clear user input. Most people will not notice any change, as this simply makes the background process more reliable.

a1ebbd7f835934b07411fc56b44a5f6b067d59c3.text: The assistant now suggests next steps after finishing a task in the 'lite' mode. Previously, it only did this in the standard mode. If you use 'lite' mode, you will see clickable follow-up ideas appear at the end of the response.

2c50c159687b37f3321892a8e64d2a56fee493f0.text: The assistant now cleans up duplicate instruction messages before processing a conversation, which saves space. It also handles cases where a helper agent has no tools available by giving it a clear message instead of an empty list. These updates are active today and help the system run more smoothly without changing how you interact with it.

8f83669556f66cac14c3fefc3f4fde1d70f6a37f.text: When the assistant tries to use a tool it is not allowed to use, the system now stops the action before showing it. This change affects how the assistant handles restricted tools. You would notice the assistant simply reports the tool is unavailable instead of displaying a failed attempt.

fb495cc7011369f4879cba7a2f713464a66d3351.text: The system now correctly counts the instructions and tool descriptions when deciding how much conversation history to keep, preventing unexpected truncations. This change is live and affects all agents that use tools, ensuring they maintain a consistent understanding of their capabilities and context limits.

5164e122767a5152917146c3ec843735d5686874.text: A small internal fix stops the website builder from trying to package complex code-analysis tools that the website does not use. This prevents the site from failing to build when deployed to a hosting service. Regular visitors will not notice any change, but the site will now update successfully instead of breaking during release.

7553fa892a4883169f33406bd58c70cc07737792.text: The team updated the automated safety checks for the AI assistant's background logic. This work is internal and invisible to you; you will notice no changes in how the assistant behaves or answers questions.

c9855cb2e23f3f6c1294779c24b17f3fce386cbb.text: The system now formally asks for a list of available tools before starting a conversation. This change fixes internal errors that could block the assistant from running. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the software behaves.

86724105737b59ed3925580caf9370c6a88e946c.text: The command-line tool now hides its 'working' or 'thinking' status messages when it is waiting for you to answer a question. This prevents the text from looking like the program is still calculating when it is actually paused for your input.

7de4aea335cc399b8f9bb393471598aea8049ec7.text: The text interface now uses specific colors for links, folders, and image boxes instead of one general blue. This means web links, folder names in lists, and image borders will look distinct from other highlighted text.

1a504a962fb0ba340f0667db6a079e1c143a5451.text: The Codebuff assistant can now talk to other programs more reliably when performing tasks. This update is available today for anyone using the Codebuff SDK. The change is minor and internal, so you likely won't notice a difference unless you previously experienced occasional failures when the assistant tried to execute a command.

66d6c24784a3ad3957c99c778db91e84c80cb0a1.text: Cleaned up internal settings by removing unused data entries and fixing a broken link in the development setup script. This is a small internal maintenance task. Regular users will see no difference; it only helps developers start their local test environment correctly.

d7cba2cc21eed8d693491421d0b8c9cbdba71cfe.text: A new rule now tells the assistant to keep your unsaved work when it saves changes to a file. Previously, it might have deleted your edits if it tried to leave certain files out of a save. This internal safety check is active today and prevents accidental data loss during the saving process.

c83b8ba2fa481d42879f80038b28283cebea37c5.text: The internal judge that picks the best answer from several drafts no longer rushes to choose. It now takes time to compare similar drafts carefully. This affects only the hidden selection step, so no visible change to the final answer appears.

740be5ee61a726eee46178a5b4d99b2a8bf8b17b.text: When a problem happens, the program now saves a full copy of the original error details alongside the summary. This helps support staff see exactly what went wrong without guessing. Regular people will not see any change on their screens.
