370ac2dcb6bf9f412aaa793c2ac78c0ae082b171.text: The assistant now treats a standard request to save changes as permission for safe updates only, never for overwriting shared history. If the system detects a conflict that requires forcing the update, it will stop and ask for specific approval instead of proceeding automatically. This applies to internal automated tasks and prevents accidental loss of other people's work.

644ef70aa27655ee619de61fd5ba8bcb659e0598.text: When the assistant fails, the error message now includes a detailed list of steps it took before failing, labeled as 'Agent run error'. This helps support staff trace exactly where the process broke. Regular users might see a longer, more technical error message instead of a short summary.

f5b277e094f5d3f7809dd90c459f79ad211a344e.text: The system now records more detailed information when it fails to communicate with the AI service. Support staff can see the specific web address, the exact message sent, and the error code returned. This helps them diagnose why a task stopped working without needing to inspect the underlying code.

a36aefb00477f28241ff392f9e6c806bdd40afa1.text: The system now treats brief failures to save activity history as minor warnings instead of urgent errors. This stops automatic alerts from firing when a temporary network glitch causes a save to fail. Staff monitoring the system will see fewer unnecessary alarms.

ed656e08dc31c7ec547e966f286ee4be9668c893.text: Chat scrolling in the Zed editor now moves faster. This update is live and only affects people using that specific editor. Users will notice the text moves more quickly when they scroll through conversations.

77b4dd360c8b5080906b5006bf82aff620f62fb8.text: A small internal change gives clearer explanations when someone is blocked from using admin tools or logging out everywhere. Instead of a generic 'access denied' message, the system now says exactly why, such as 'you are not an admin' or 'this request came from the wrong website.' This helps support staff diagnose problems faster, but normal users will likely not notice any difference.

23192c46e41f062eb3a66c922f200f48a983f906.text: The command-line tool now shows more detailed technical information when an error occurs. If a task fails, the tool displays a clear 'Output error' label and includes a list of the exact steps that led to the problem. This helps users understand why something went wrong instead of just seeing a generic failure message.

01df7deb9ec76b8f9844398bcb4711eda9a254f2.text: The system now records more detailed background notes when a connection to the text generator fails. Support staff can see exactly which account and settings were involved in the error. Regular people will notice no change in how the app works.

b19591a6b5019213b4a36740988f14f8bafc0b3c.text: The 'Thinker' helper agent now uses a more powerful reasoning model and is available by default in the main setup. It produces cleaner, more reliable answers by strictly following a specific format, though this internal formatting change is invisible to the end user.

80fc6e797d22dfb287ea3bd3b2cb2c8e3803a8aa.text: The software stopped blocking certain helper agents from producing structured data if they lacked a specific permission. Builders who create these agents can now set up output formatting without granting that permission, letting the system handle the final formatting step automatically. This change is live today.

617bc23e68c737bcb487f0118ca290bf7de4baf4.text: The text box that shows the assistant's reasoning process now has a wider safety margin on its left side. This change prevents the text from jumping around or wrapping awkwardly when the window is resized or when the assistant's thoughts are indented. It only affects how the text displays on your screen, not what the assistant says.

8738ea71e4b395e86d9ae63d945abefcce4c94c4.text: The assistant now hides its step-by-step reasoning notes from the final answer. This affects the 'best-of-n' thinking process, ensuring only the concise conclusion is shown to the main assistant. You will not see the raw, messy thought process in the final output.

4c7721f34f02a4ad41a357671b21077134aa9790.text: Internal tooling change. Developers running local web app copies now point only the web app to their local port, leaving background tools connected to the live server. No visible change for regular users.

c8be0c250c81ea7c7c1fe30b5e213e8c60d6ffaf.text: The internal scoring check now saves more detail when its automatic reviewer fails. If the reviewer returns an unusable result, the log now includes the full result text, and a separate detail file is created for that task and reviewer. This is live in internal runs. People checking failed scoring runs would see the extra saved detail; normal results look the same.

27d699645a007ce0a5adf684fa685c735f560a59.text: The assistant's background tools switched to a different underlying model for writing code. It now tries fewer parallel attempts by default and caps the maximum number of attempts. This is an internal adjustment that may slightly change how the assistant solves complex coding tasks.

2c4ec02a099d92548a9c199130dc45a39f79c5eb.text: When a digital assistant tries to use a tool and fails, it now reports the error after successfully sharing other tool results. This prevents the assistant from getting confused by mixed-up messages, so it can retry the task more reliably. This is a small internal fix that is live today.

6aa53a0f34027c39730e6fa4d39557451cdbe44e.text: A small internal fix lets the tool accept blank path entries without crashing. It treats empty input as 'the whole project,' matching how file browsing usually works. Only people using the path option in the assistant's file-reading feature would see this, and most wouldn't notice anything different.

9b4c2d6dd03548972bcf7cf540670d63c8193444.text: The assistant now waits until all tool results are finished before adding error messages to its memory. This prevents errors from appearing out of order when the assistant uses external tools. It fixes a rare timing issue for the assistant's internal conversation history. The change is live and affects how the assistant handles mistakes during tool use.

e2f7538f26c9e4863bda7bc0fc95ae6be352f1c3.text: A small internal fix corrected how the system identifies the data source for a specific test run. This change ensures the test runner receives the data in the correct format, preventing potential errors during execution. External users will notice no difference, as this only affects internal testing stability.

35f0bee9b9669b6b45a59e7fdaaefb1264f49482.text: The command-line tool now uses green instead of blue for its main highlights. When viewing code changes, the colors for added and removed lines adjust automatically to match the current light or dark theme, improving visibility. This change is live and affects anyone using the tool's interface.

174c9368a4cf0fb8436e954670c644e7b1990a5e.text: The program now checks your custom assistant instructions only when you start a chat, instead of checking them every time you open the program. This makes the program start faster and prevents it from showing duplicate error messages if your internet connection is briefly unstable.

de2c9c8e7e63c06cd7a03479bd5e55f753978015.text: The startup logo now sweeps a green shine across itself and repeats the motion. The login screen and the main screen share the same animation code, so they look identical. This change is live today for anyone opening the command-line tool.

5bd7d2dea524ea8b7673531bce01c75c1e54d9f1.text: The assistant now uses the same request format for calling one helper as it does for calling many helpers at once. This change is internal, so the user experience remains exactly the same.

91a139f57d7d3ce3db8cec1633b0fd4227742426.text: Internal testing tools now record failures for the code-writing assistant. Engineers see error messages in the console, and detailed logs appear in files only when a special debug setting is turned on. This small change helps the team diagnose problems faster.

6adec6e38daee2d7edc0a67b92a78c5bac5f2b3f.text: The text-based program changed its main highlight color from yellow to green. People using the standard dark or light settings will see this new color in their chat interface. This visual update matches new branding and takes effect immediately.

1fd0a47f2021ecf2c3035541d4ca8cf109c03012.text: This small internal update prepares the automated testing tool to automatically set up the required software environment and verify that the code builds correctly before running checks. It affects only the internal testing process, so you will not notice any changes in the application.

03ebeb98e9df8a00b68d9218aa16b6ab7f7567ed.text: The search tool now checks if hidden folders exist before searching. This stops error messages about missing folders. You will see fewer technical warnings when looking for code.

9406cf9b7f53411bf0ef5fd643a57b6141b69e6b.text: Internal quality checks now use the latest version of the AI model. This change is small and invisible to you. You will not notice any difference in how the software works.

4b2a72de69dde93de80efb62909749bb64db1a83.text: The background software that connects the assistant to the outside world was updated. This change is internal and affects only the system's plumbing, not the user interface. A person using the assistant would notice no difference in how it looks or behaves today.

2553341452476b4e3650aeb8e55b06db53dd3af4.text: When you type the '@' symbol to pick an assistant, you now only see options that fit the specific job you are currently doing, instead of a long list of every possible helper. Any custom helpers you set up yourself still show up no matter what job you are on. This makes the menu cleaner and helps you pick the right tool faster.

f2bfa73c960345a734a5d2609f432e46fca807d8.text: The command-line tool no longer shows a collapsible list of local agents in its header. This change affects users of the command-line interface. Instead of looking for this list, users should type '@' to select an agent. The removal is live today.

03e88c7c3f8dcdda58b5f1e63d1c090589cd0351.text: A small internal fix stops the command-line tool from writing error messages to the screen when a specific background test fails. This change affects only how the software checks itself, not how people use it. You would not notice any difference in your daily work.

92814531a4778a22734fe37783fce92088d9af01.text: The system stopped fixing how it displays partial answers from background tasks, reverting to a method that might show repeated text. This affects users watching these tasks run live. They may notice duplicate words appearing in the output stream until the task finishes.

7e24a0ffe766e2a44fcb5eebc9b376377f5c35e0.text: A minor fix corrects a bug where responses from background helpers appeared twice in the command line tool. Users of the command line interface will now see each helper's message exactly once, instead of duplicated text cluttering the screen. This change is live today.

b6d6602b80c5e71c7ae335968dfa73f8eeec372b.text: The system now translates custom tool instructions into a standard format that can be sent over the network. This fixes an issue where tools defined outside the main application would fail to load correctly. The change is live and ensures that these external tools work as expected without crashing.

fa71be2c8caaef7cf7f2dc7e9958c3375cb40d24.text: The system now displays text responses as they arrive, even when the AI is simultaneously preparing to use a tool. This change affects the internal logic for how assistant messages are stored and retrieved. A reader might notice that text appears more reliably in the chat history, whereas previously some text could be hidden if a tool was being called at the same time.

27b4d7f924a7b1a954d556dbccaded1556675816.text: The automated quality checks for the internal assistant tools now correctly report failures. Previously, the system ignored errors during these checks, allowing broken code to pass review. This change ensures that any future issues in the assistant's core logic are caught immediately before release.

b9f2793b6ebb4362408933309dcaa7de85cdc114.text: The suggestion lists that appear when typing slash commands or file names now react to mouse clicks. Moving the cursor over an option highlights it, and clicking inserts the text directly. This applies to anyone using the command-line interface today.

f27f478adfd54b2168a22a008e2fad73b926618d.text: Internal maintenance improved how temporary activity records are saved during testing. This helps the team see errors immediately instead of waiting. Regular customers will not notice any difference.

678f9061ec3851f825dcad0d291047e6b279d32e.text: The team turned off a specific quality check for the editor's feature that picks the best of several code suggestions. This stops the automated system from reporting a failure while they fix a known bug. Regular users will not notice any change in the application's behavior.

c2ef254e37a476331a3e599595c3c41a2af13f87.text: A background quality check that counted the number of messages was removed because it sometimes failed incorrectly. This change affects only the internal testing process. There will be no visible difference in how the assistant behaves or what users see.

1c720f08851a3ea1d9bbca33df79935e36eb431a.text: Added safety checks to the conversation trimming tool. These checks ensure that when old messages are removed to save space, related action and result pairs stay together so the system doesn't break. This is an internal quality test and does not change how the product behaves for users today.

cf7ff5e4a34be4119018d5d0810e03d026fecf6a.text: The text input box no longer tries to calculate its own width based on old settings. This change is internal cleanup. You will not notice any difference in how the text box looks or behaves.

91fc04d08b2ef28f6dcd579c8fa9e3b916d2d756.text: The assistant now clearly shows examples for creating helper tasks that run commands or search code. This helps the assistant understand exactly what information it must provide when starting these tasks. The change is active today and makes the assistant less likely to fail when launching these specific helpers.

8899146839681cfb82159a5323df150f7c9ad0cc.text: The startup tool now shows a spinning animation while the local server loads, replacing the old silent wait. It also automatically closes background processes and saves detailed logs to a hidden folder when the tool stops. This internal improvement affects only the team members running the development environment.

7b53e571f80bca5dc99cd2eef1d864150528c427.text: The assistant now collects all parts of its text replies instead of just the last one, ensuring complete responses from background helpers. This prevents the assistant from accidentally sending text and tool commands in the wrong order, which previously caused errors. Users running background tasks or file searches will see more reliable, uncut results.

87a98a5374861379cb7165b66d5a90b09527c296.text: The chat tool now checks for a file location before looking for picture data in the clipboard. This ensures that when you drag a screenshot or copy a path, the tool attaches the correct file instead of an old or broken image buffer. The change is live for anyone using the command-line interface.

d3bcf7d35c21f7bad952a609f5530484215e0732.text: A small internal update was made to the library that draws the text-based interface in the command-line tool. This change affects only how the interface is built behind the scenes and does not add new features or change how you interact with the tool. You would not notice any difference in your experience.

899b9c32be24c7ca6614bb65614a660f6a19944d.text: The text interface now uses a single list to define its available modes. This change fixes a risk where a new mode might appear in one menu but not another. Users see no difference today, but future updates will be less likely to break.

859aa304d1c29f80a794a917ba4d2656136acdda.text: Pasting images into the command-line tool now works when you copy a file from your computer's file manager. The tool looks for the file's location instead of relying on old or broken image data. This affects people using Mac or Windows who paste screenshots or photos directly into the chat input.

5cb3cc92bb55b8c47c601ed1e292282fc8672f07.text: The program's automatic check for the mode-switching menu now expects five items instead of four, matching the recent addition of a planning mode. This is an internal fix to keep the software's own tests accurate. Regular users will see no change in how the menu works or looks.

a9dd138609ae7b71e564eb51c95a17799314d731.text: The program now downloads new updates to a separate staging area and runs a quick check to ensure the file is complete and working before replacing the current version. This change affects anyone using the command-line tool to update. If an update fails or is corrupted, the old version remains intact instead of breaking the tool.

343d329ba348c99f7c3fc62fcb01841c08d1f1d9.text: A small update helps people using the command-line tool. When you open the menu to switch between different assistant styles, the one you are currently using is now marked as active. This makes it easier to see which setting is in effect without guessing.

7e8ed53562f22fd7f0f3330266f219fc81e43825.text: The program now waits longer before checking if its command-line tool has finished starting up. This change only affects the automated checks that run behind the scenes, not the actual tool itself. You will not notice any difference in how the application works.

0449bf89d90c35830958e53cb9819fb2d8b715ae.text: The command-line tool now handles pasting text and images directly, rather than relying on the terminal's built-in behavior. This affects the chat, feedback, and question prompts. You might notice pasting works more reliably, especially if you use a terminal that doesn't handle pasting well, and the text will appear exactly where your cursor is.

bbe9f8304767e8ec3175eab531bfe0b465109411.text: The text-based program now switches to its compact view on slightly wider screens. This helps fit more content in smaller windows without hiding information. The change is live today.

f43ff5c72d791bf0063de57f2e6a842616cdac13.text: A new 'LITE' mode was added to the command-line assistant. When you switch to this mode, the assistant uses a lighter model that automatically hands off coding tasks to a specialized editor without extra instructions. This change is live for users of the command-line tool.

2a022ccd9ae24f0630738c6b26c004b7a403c731.text: The tool now saves a small note about its version in a local file instead of asking the program itself. This makes checking for updates faster and smoother. People using the command-line tool will see quicker startup times and fewer delays when the tool checks if a newer version is available.

6012001897b09377dd576b936d5a3a7abf273528.text: When the assistant hits an error, the message now shows which outside service failed and a short snippet of its reply. This helps the support team find the cause faster. Regular users see no change, but errors will be easier to fix.

64e9427805c82393e914edf25027eb33325884b5.text: The chat window now hides the mode switch button when the terminal is too narrow. This prevents the layout from breaking or overlapping text on small screens. If you resize your terminal window to be very short in width, you will simply see the button disappear, and the rest of the chat bar will fit neatly.

e5ba7afcb3474164030258bbf0eab043c7014cc6.text: A small fix ensures the text tool automatically switches back to normal typing mode after successfully adding an image via paste or file path. This prevents the tool from getting stuck in image mode, which would block regular text input. Users will notice the interface returning to standard text entry immediately after adding an image.

60d412d8ab2b9a11095fdfa0a32011380ceba4b4.text: A small internal fix in the command-line tool ensures the keyboard shortcut handler for suggestion menus is always registered, regardless of which input mode is active. This prevents potential glitches where arrow keys or Enter might fail to navigate suggestions in certain feedback or ask-user states. It is live today but affects only rare edge cases, so most users will notice no change.

d7c58203be448e764091f4a1ace649778f31728a.text: The internal testing tool now selects a specific version of the AI assistant instead of a general label, ensuring it always uses the intended model. The team also removed an unused software component and updated the main tool to a newer version. This change affects only the internal evaluation system, and no external users will notice any difference in their experience.

fdc0f6ff77a1d075c58d57cf15cb6d76b41d96a6.text: The chat interface now updates messages instantly as they arrive, instead of waiting to collect them in small batches. This removes a tiny artificial delay, making the text appear on screen more smoothly. This is an internal cleanup; you will not notice any new features or changes to how the chat works.

274190d84e9cac806e7d983d88f830b16f479fdc.text: The command-line tool now lets you change how the assistant works by typing a specific command. You can switch between a standard setting, a maximum capability setting, or a planning mode. The tool will confirm the change on your screen immediately.

d4a26e2750f2a18edc76d9bf3b9c902cd6a32a81.text: The chat screen now hides decorative borders and small buttons when the window is too short. This frees up space so you can see more of the assistant's suggestions and type longer messages without scrolling. The change is live and affects anyone using the command-line tool on a small screen.

001cf58e894f23a2755c163ddc8e0a6c3d7bb2ee.text: Developers cleaned up the internal testing area by removing old, unused labels that described how the assistant should format its answers. This change affects only the team members who run these tests and will not change how the assistant behaves for anyone else. You will not notice any difference in the product, as the assistant's responses remain exactly the same.

286c97c3f69fecbd7b12738df0694e09b37a80b8.text: The command-line tool now starts with its top notification bar hidden. This applies to the tool's default setup, so the banner will not appear when the program launches unless another part of the system explicitly turns it on.

9ae00ce564cf62ba71ec333efd7dc6f3a24ca175.text: The internal evaluation system stopped copying API keys directly into the agent's environment. Instead, the system now automatically selects the correct key for the AI model being tested. This change affects only internal testing tools. Users will notice no difference in the product.

08eeb71ed057de1b8303d34eaa373ab341b7b6ad.text: A hidden check inside the tool's self-test suite was updated to match how it handles streamed text. This change is internal and does not affect the tool's behavior or appearance for anyone.

b26ab6b7434ab25e2bead2ec54f676649603213f.text: The chat tool now checks what you copied before pasting. If you paste text, it appears immediately without a brief flash of a picture placeholder. This fixes a visual glitch for people using the command-line chat.

bbd88d49a0d7a1c51b91fa62c03349132c28eacb.text: Fixed a bug where the command-line interface could leave the keyboard in a broken state after checking the terminal's background color. The program now restores normal keyboard behavior immediately after this check finishes. This prevents issues where typed characters might not appear correctly or shortcuts stop working during startup.

7834671a5b93960ee216da4821e7e9484293d146.text: The internal testing tool now uses the shared access key and a different model. Only staff running these tests will see a change, and they might notice the tool behaving slightly differently or failing if the key is missing. This affects no external customers.

416a550321ba403f602876bcbd4c07ea47900ed5.text: The AI assistant now pauses to reason carefully before choosing or writing code. It also tries fewer parallel attempts by default to save time. Users will notice slightly slower responses but more accurate and thoughtful results.

c163bd75e46e612d8c18d9ab67e874836c8fa574.text: A small internal update improves how chat request failures are recorded. When a specific type of connection error occurs, the system now saves the exact reason behind the failure in its logs. Support staff and engineers will see clearer details when investigating these specific issues, but customers will not notice any changes in the chat experience.

e08f638d4a872d0c9bda1459472ed5f0720223dc.text: The AI now reliably sees commands you run in the terminal, even if you previously had to type them into the chat box. This fixes a gap where the assistant sometimes ignored your recent terminal activity. You will notice the AI giving better answers about your recent work because it actually knows what you just did in the shell.

dfbdff0eec8fc81b0022b0b2f771d7fb7ab39b97.text: Previously, if you tried to start an assistant without giving it any instructions, the system would stop with an error. Now, it treats a missing instruction as an empty request and proceeds normally. This change is already live.

a87657c14662e0ef5c405e8f56d4f79f0f152729.text: The code editor now hides its internal reasoning notes from the screen when using the newer AI model, showing only the final file changes. It also stops the editor from trying to use a specific command that caused messy output. This affects the internal tool's display, making the results cleaner and easier to read without extra clutter.

483ca19b1acc0d765710d6250fdd79ee3f006677.text: A small internal update changes how a nightly test runs. The test now uses a simpler, faster setup and checks fewer tasks at once. This happens automatically in the background, so nobody will notice a change in the app or website.

482e5facf248979f179b53e3cbc7e0dca5b41db5.text: Internal test tools now take login secrets from the computer's environment instead of a special backup name. This affects only the team running these tests. If a tester previously relied on the old backup name, their tests will fail to start until they set the standard environment variable.

d0786316bad375c9ca02e150efda4a5bbfc099c0.text: When you skip a multiple-choice question in the assistant's command-line tool, the message sent to the server no longer contains an empty placeholder for your answer. This small fix prevents a specific data formatting error that could occur when you choose not to answer a prompt.

06fd157fe7987fc9e038696580c3f5d0fa30aa4b.text: The command prompt symbol in the terminal changed color from red to green. This cosmetic update helps users feel more confident that the command is ready to run, rather than signaling an error.

7c4c0f7c4aa7fbd60a9abbc5a8a930896ed9dd4c.text: The internal editor stopped using one specific AI model because that model kept failing to provide required reasoning notes. This change affects only the automated editing tool, not public software. If someone watched the tool work, they would see it switch to a different model instead of the broken one.

ba05886551ad15b488ce6554959fbe7ecb67453e.text: The system now allows setting the AI's 'thinking effort' to 'minimal' or 'none' in addition to the existing high, medium, and low options. This change affects the internal settings for how agents are configured. If you look at the settings, you will see these new options are available to be chosen.

c0a8dfbb7fd0023dc051aec262bdda338815fd73.text: The tool now automatically looks for hidden configuration folders like.github and.claude when searching your project. This helps find important settings and workflow files without needing to change any options. If a folder does not exist, the search simply skips it.

4e41963236dbe8b8b0884fdbb2b00102e70f304b.text: A small internal update fixes a broken test check. It now looks for a real security key stored on the computer, instead of using a fake placeholder number. This change affects only the testing system, not the live product, so customers will not notice any difference.

6343346dabbde8f9d96a1fe1e65ec062e9cc4acb.text: The editor now always allows three specific AI helpers to be used, regardless of your subscription tier. Previously, these helpers were hidden for some plans. You might see slightly different options when asking the editor to write code.

32dc0343d7e0bff59d25cf1a2b9245b5671c0429.text: The 'Other' text field in the command-line prompt now uses the same editing engine as other text boxes. This fixes bugs where typing, deleting, or moving the cursor worked poorly. If you type a custom answer, the text will behave normally.

03827cfd2f388ea2117cd607fac04f8dc6aedc28.text: When the assistant fails to connect, the error message now shows the exact reason from the service provider. Support staff can see this detail to diagnose problems faster. Regular users will not notice a difference in their experience.

ce45b623283bf28c506851791b987a1ef7d24f13.text: A small internal fix prevents the automatic top-up feature from turning off when the payment system experiences temporary connection issues. Customers who have auto top-up enabled will no longer see the feature disable itself due to these brief errors, ensuring their service continues without interruption.

f4ae69009504ff9958e25e76982fc8aad3843aba.text: The instructions for the file-reading feature were shortened. The warning against re-reading files was removed, but the system still automatically alerts the assistant if a file changes. This is an internal cleanup, so nothing visible to you will change today.

7feec3606d35b96b19d004c93867a4c2ab2ec349.text: The system now sends a specific 'session expired' message when your login details are no longer valid, instead of a generic error. This change affects the command-line interface. You will see a clearer prompt asking you to log in again when trying to view your referral link with an expired session.

11a7a0ce795c06b73f27168627aa1b203363dd3e.text: When a person stops a running request in the command-line tool, the program now recognizes this as intentional. It prevents the display of confusing error messages that previously appeared alongside the cancellation notice. This small update makes the stop process feel cleaner and more predictable for users of the text-based interface.

341069192c57970279896134d88fa7b986589a11.text: The command-line tool now shows a fixed link to the referral page instead of fetching a personalized link from the server. Users no longer see loading messages or errors if the data fails to arrive, and the input prompt for entering a code is simpler.

a8f1af16b1fe7fe8d6c9fb3d6839232faea43564.text: The internal format for storing conversation messages changed. Instead of allowing plain text blocks, all messages now use a standardized list structure. This affects developers building custom AI agents, but they will not see any visible changes in their interface or behavior.

5a0568271a9913e329b5138137911df628f72851.text: In the command-line chat, turning off slash suggestions previously blocked the Tab key from completing file paths. A small fix restores that behavior. Only people who have disabled slash suggestions would notice it working again.

791e18173b458b7d12734163484349b0157ee4d4.text: In Max mode, the software stops using one specific AI assistant for writing code and switches to a fixed mix of two other assistants. Users who turn on Max mode will see fewer parallel attempts at solving a problem, dropping from six to five. This change is live today.

8bca30fb396f7d22efecde0b4a23ff770b5b79d0.text: The AI editor now checks five draft options instead of six before picking the best one. This internal adjustment applies only to the automated writing tool and does not change how it works for anyone.

751e74decde37bd796a8b8ce1cdbb993b3aa79aa.text: The system now processes monthly credit updates and bonus grants as a single, unified action instead of separate steps. This prevents technical errors that could previously interrupt the update process. Affected users will experience smoother, more reliable monthly credit resets without visible changes to the interface.

2029e1e9119422e8e2072f925b451ef94c3d7dc6.text: The internal scoring system for evaluating code changes now uses two different AI models instead of three. This change affects only the team members who review these automated scores. They will see slightly different grading results and a shorter wait time for the final score to appear.

6d6554d5d0102a8ecbb6466782719b7634eef9e8.text: The text shown in the command line input box changed. It now says 'enter a coding task or / for commands' instead of 'type a message...'. This helps people using the command line know they can type a coding task or use slash commands.

605f55477bcb6983b0e450b8259e8159d096c257.text: A small internal change to how the system records conversations. It simplifies the process by removing an extra step that previously turned certain actions into formal messages. This change does not affect what you see or how you use the tool today.

0820c1fc4101d0496804bcd3692ecf794aa0c261.text: This change adds hidden debugging notes inside an internal test that checks whether prompt caching saves money. Only the software engineers who run this test will see these notes. It does not affect how the product works for customers today.

b4208070a0713d2fae8fee4854a97aabc4a86fc0.text: A small internal cleanup removed unnecessary instructions from a background process. This fixes a hidden error but does not change how the assistant works. You will notice no difference in your chats.

b3dc2954c2d7a93071f51cb99875d23876e9f028.text: The assistant now records every attempt to use a tool in the conversation history, even if the request was malformed and the tool failed to run. Previously, failed attempts were invisible, leaving gaps in the record. This change is live and ensures the history accurately reflects all actions taken.

ca28cb5bb0d5909cb9edf1c87a346c08c79fcddb.text: This small internal update fixes a technical error in the code that manages how the AI assistant runs tasks. It ensures the system correctly identifies each specific action the assistant takes. You will not see any visual changes, but the assistant is now slightly more stable when processing these steps.

fe406c56163877c198ec15bfd72930b6a58670fb.text: A new helper function was added to the agent runtime to assemble tool sets by filtering and merging definitions. This is an internal code change that does not affect live features or user behavior yet.

dde06ea5cade072e9ea7c619f931079978c7ae3e.text: The internal system that connects the assistant to its text source was simplified. Instead of giving the assistant a tool to get the text, it now receives the text stream directly. This change is invisible to end users and only affects how the software's internal components talk to each other.

2d8c263702920179dd6182c56e08cfe133140f67.text: A new internal guideline now strictly forbids overwriting the main project history. This rule protects the team's shared work from accidental loss. Staff will notice this as a clear warning in their reference materials, ensuring safer collaboration.

de6d712e7cce5198a15fde828e1ee7094c02a19a.text: The system now checks tool inputs using a single, stricter method instead of two different ones. This change affects how custom tools validate data, making the process more consistent. Users will not notice any difference in behavior or appearance today, as this is an internal cleanup.

e3d0b8ee2400ec16e242e5d590582eeb4ca8464b.text: The program's internal checklist for showing account credit information was updated to match a recent change in how the tool organizes its screens. This is an invisible maintenance task for the developers. Users will see no difference in how the command-line tool behaves or displays data.

3c1fed3e2b3910cadb9c2a4ff1ba298136b1661f.text: The program now loads its terminal color detection tool at startup instead of waiting until it is needed. This internal cleanup helps the code stay organized and prevents hidden errors, but it does not change how the program looks or behaves for you today.

2a81534822132ef239dca11a91495cc6341dc9d0.text: The command-line tool now automatically displays a warning when your remaining credits fall below a specific limit, replacing the previous method that required you to manually check this information. This change affects all users of the tool and means you will see an alert message appear without needing to take extra steps to view your balance.

4382642d1725ee9041180281a7dc6e67d9369ea9.text: Pressing Escape now clears special typing modes in the chat if you haven't typed anything yet. This helps you quickly return to normal chatting without needing to delete text first. The change applies to the command-line interface and is live for users today.

51af033b8f28348f0b9361b2e833e93f19350342.text: A minor internal fix corrected how the chat input bar handles its title display. This change ensures the title appears consistently, regardless of whether feedback mode is active. Users might notice the 'Action Required' label no longer flickers or disappears unexpectedly during certain interactions.

509c78f170e4ab48fbb9d61a3968f1b727529cc7.text: Internal test data for the AI agent system was updated to include a missing user identifier. This change fixes a technical error in the testing environment but does not affect how the product works for real users.

bdc676b42c2af84835a0dd1fc4242ffd4589970d.text: The command-line tool now uses a single setting to control whether the usage information banner appears, replacing a separate switch that did the same thing. This internal cleanup affects how the tool decides to show usage data. You will not notice any change in how the tool works.

0fe10c620172c82e64f3659e927721c7acf792b4.text: The system now saves the assistant's requests to use external tools directly into the conversation history, rather than just passing them along temporarily. This ensures the assistant remembers it asked for a specific action during the chat. It is a small internal fix, so you will not notice any changes in how the chat looks or behaves today.

303438b5b7e9dd991d021fd717a174b2ded3eb71.text: When typing long text in the command line, pressing the up or down arrow key now keeps the cursor at the same horizontal position across lines, even if the lines are different lengths. This affects people typing multi-line commands or notes. You will notice the cursor no longer jumps to the start or end of a line when moving vertically.

d0bc9d5a163b7494af38df82fded6eb1d4817255.text: A leftover setting for a feedback button was removed from the chat window code, along with its shortcut key. This change is internal cleanup and does not affect any current features. Users will not notice any difference in how the application behaves.

9be66424bfe2eefc6de4e6079764958a287a5478.text: The mode switch button is back in the command-line chat window. You can click it to change modes, but it will stay hidden if you are currently using the shell command mode. This change is live.

c65563d3538b776cb8d320fde6f4b44bd83194c5.text: The text command tool now shows how long a task took more cleanly. It drops empty parts like '0s' or '0m', so a one-minute wait shows as '1m' instead of '1m 0s'. Users running tasks in the terminal will see these tidier time reports immediately.

c4299636b369b6c46e0e9dfc85b3d59d4c64cd40.text: Fixed a bug where pasting text rapidly into the command line interface could cause the cursor to jump or text to be inserted in the wrong place. This ensures that quick, repeated paste actions are handled correctly by always using the most recent text position. The fix is live and prevents minor glitches when pasting multiple chunks of text quickly.

e0a3ec87d4f12cbf2f35c5f754d65444bc708cce.text: The copy button in the chat interface now shows a brief confirmation when clicked, so you know the text was copied. It also cleans up the copied text by removing any stray cursor symbols that might have been accidentally selected. This change is live and applies to anyone using the command-line chat tool.

54c9838ea7e87ed95d6dbcb051815a11316e8eda.text: The small button used to switch the assistant's behavior modes is now hidden in the text-based chat window. This stops people from accidentally selecting a broken mode. The assistant now only uses its standard settings, and the text input box shifts slightly to fill the empty space.

f5a23a8d422b193bfa0b5a123ea9b267c0bac3be.text: The account details page now includes your personal referral link. You can copy this link to share with others. This update is active immediately for all users.

e93f5b1b9e194a090816baea2196fad26f7bec61.text: The text shown after sending feedback through the command-line tool changed to 'Thanks, your feedback helps! 💖'. This affects only people using the command-line interface to report issues. They will see the new friendly message and heart emoji instead of the previous checkmark.

247519f3f6209f18280177eb6355fa6ada752d6f.text: The command-line tool now checks remaining usage credits after every message, regardless of whether the warning screen was previously open. This ensures credit warnings always show up-to-date numbers. The change is live and affects all CLI users.

8b02bfe097a0390acd55f78bfe176cb51c1b6c53.text: Internal cleanup. The assistant's core engine now receives the user's request as a direct input rather than storing it in a shared background list. This prevents accidental mix-ups between different tasks. Nothing changes for the user; the assistant works exactly as before.

22d03cc31e5073b7ef95c4a08041c5f21eaf52e5.text: The system now passes file-editing progress directly to the tools that need it, instead of storing it in a shared background box. This cleanup ensures that when the AI writes or edits code, it uses the most current information without checking a central hub. Internal maintenance only; no visible changes to how the AI behaves.

e57bbb759a69e22815a4e2acd67fa4f75d9bfffc.text: A small coding error in the command-line tool's message display was fixed. This error previously prevented the tool from working correctly. Users of the command-line interface will now see messages displayed properly without the tool crashing or failing to start.

f49b7de7acbbc543fef82d78b57141b6a2bd2ee4.text: The internal logging system was reorganized to pass information directly to tools rather than storing it in a shared state. This change affects how the AI agent tracks its actions behind the scenes. Users will not notice any difference in the assistant's behavior or output.

732bd015cc29615c2ed8cc002c52d4d5ded40498.text: The text cursor's blinking behavior is now controlled by a central setting instead of being passed down through multiple layers of the interface. This internal cleanup ensures the cursor blinks correctly when the terminal supports focus tracking, without changing any visible features for the user.

2714ea52a5fab5fe2043bb880c68c2806efec3b6.text: The system now passes the streaming connection directly to the assistant's tools instead of storing it in a shared background state. This makes the code cleaner and more reliable. Users will not see any difference in how the assistant works today.

d855034728585356804eb11987de7ab539f2a5c1.text: The part of the assistant that runs its steps now passes the list of smaller goals the assistant is tracking directly to the steps that need it, instead of keeping that list in a general storage area. This is a small internal tidy-up and does not add or change any assistant capability. It is live today, but a person using the assistant would notice no change in behavior, speed, or results.

275c751a17dbc7943e79f39520b0524f5817d427.text: The assistant's internal tools no longer carry a copy of the conversation's current status in their general workspace; instead, they receive it directly when called. This change is invisible to you, as it only tidies up how the software passes information between its own parts.

2c9b78fc4c85ab5f107d24791fe49f68052195be.text: Fixed a spacing error in the command-line chat box. The text input area was reserving extra space on the sides, causing the cursor to jump to a new line too early. The box now uses its full width, so the text wraps at the actual edge.

7ad7b0cb2b698588ba9bee8f8b5f436556f15852.text: The command-line tool now explains why it picked a specific option when comparing several choices. This helps people using the tool understand the reasoning behind automatic decisions. Users will notice a short sentence appearing below the selection status, providing context for the choice made.

b11445494a686bb7e18e5d6881c97e99ef69a243.text: Developers cleaned up how the assistant tracks its own thoughts while it works. This change is internal housekeeping, so the assistant looks and acts exactly the same to you.

fd81c06005017a9dbbfd6d313b3b96790aaeb5c2.text: When the assistant tries several solutions and picks the best one, the status line now names the winning solution instead of just saying it is choosing. This helps people using the command-line tool see which option was selected. It works immediately for completed tasks.

7821b96aa1bc17495f344466cac2100247031474.text: A small internal fix corrected how the terminal app measures width for its visual separators. This resolves a hidden technical error that could have caused display glitches. Regular users will likely see no immediate visual change, but the app is now more stable.

434c216009755013bc1f82684544ceab67a00300.text: The internal editing assistant can now directly modify or create files during its work, instead of just suggesting changes. This affects only the specific 'best-of-n' editor mode used by internal agents. Users will notice the assistant successfully applying edits to files without needing manual intervention for those specific actions.

75c7d459b3feaede4d55b232ab95ca5943a75f8d.text: The command-line tool now displays each of the three AI models separately when they compete to write code, showing their names and whether they are working, finished, or failed. This affects people using the best-of-n feature, who previously saw nothing or generic text. They will now see distinct rows for Sonnet, Gemini, and GPT-5 with clear status indicators.

9b5780c514e8ae5f22c2492a56382a9a2dd8985e.text: This small internal fix improves how the file picker handles data from other programs. If that data arrives broken or incomplete, the tool now stops cleanly and shows a clear error message instead of crashing or behaving unpredictably.

29e43f0d882661811698d1c094e30c964ef79061.text: The system now checks fewer draft options by default when you ask it to pick the best result. This change is live today and affects anyone using the standard 'best-of' feature. You would notice it finishes faster and costs less, while the advanced 'max' setting remains unchanged with more options and a different judge.

f45f5e292263d4cb2e5b23b333337aeba0cc1d5e.text: This small internal fix stops the tool from crashing when it tries to check usage costs or file locations but finds that information missing. Instead of failing, it now uses a safe default, like counting zero cost or using the current folder. This affects the background systems that run automated tests and the chat interface, ensuring they stay stable without changing how you interact with them.

aac77c4b1afb6fbe3a9148bb9fff6c04df877c14.text: The command-line tool now checks for existing helpers using a consistent naming rule, ignoring extra prefixes and version tags. This prevents the same helper from being launched multiple times, which previously caused duplicate windows or repeated actions. The fix is live today.

9340060cb4823034be4c7bc447b086b02b36c429.text: The internal testing tools now pull their instructions from the main assistant system directly, instead of reaching into a specific folder. This only affects how the team runs quality checks behind the scenes. Customers will notice no changes, as this is a small cleanup to make the testing process simpler and more reliable.

177d2a48d6ef03d107678847827501e4f6504bc4.text: The command-line tool now displays a shorter message when it encounters a problem and attempts to connect again. The text changed from 'error, retrying...' to just 'retrying...', and the color effect behind the text remains brighter. This is a small visual update that does not change how the tool works.

3c0215666af80305db88685008dc230311d4d844.text: The assistant now correctly reads token counts for files inside nested folders. Previously, it looked for these counts using the wrong path format, causing mismatches when viewing subdirectories. The system aligns the internal labels with the displayed folder structure. This fix is live and ensures accurate size estimates for nested projects.

51b723a30c360e8f7795d64b625b94c84725d3cb.text: The internal scoring system for code tests now uses three different artificial intelligence models to grade results instead of just one. This change affects only the team running these evaluations. They will notice that the grading process pulls opinions from multiple sources to reduce bias, though the final scores themselves may not change immediately.

e662e8e4e36d83304072585709a47b52da3b339b.text: The assistant now checks the result of a task to see if it failed due to a network issue, rather than waiting for the system to crash. If a network problem occurs, the assistant will automatically try the task again with a short wait between attempts. This change is live and helps the assistant recover from temporary internet hiccups without stopping completely.

6de9da69a18bfada1ba955f506d939dab8eb74cf.text: An internal assistant no longer has an instruction to skip a final summary if it thinks it already summarized earlier. People using that assistant should now see a short summary after it finishes a request, even if it had mentioned the work during the task. It is a small internal change, live now.

166ac30feba3f6206e107390e301e0bd086761f5.text: The command-line tool now hides certain helper agents from the display to reduce clutter. It also simplifies how selection results appear, showing them as brief italic text instead of full boxes. These changes are active and make the output easier to read for people using the tool.

b69057c8c09c4f9070b2ae1bdf1418fcf703adba.text: The assistant now stores tool results in a simpler, cleaner format. This internal fix resolves technical errors in background tests. No visible changes will appear for regular users.

d325ed0b0935aae8fb903cdb2e81be001f9ed6c2.text: Developers updated the automated checks that ensure the agent correctly remembers and shares conversation history. These checks were adjusted to match how the system now stores message text, and one outdated test was removed. This is a small internal cleanup that does not change how the agent behaves for anyone today.

09f9d89ad238a8278e1b9ab156314576ca1decfd.text: The software now automatically tries again when a temporary service issue shows up as a plain error message, rather than only catching certain types of system crashes. This helps people using the AI assistant avoid seeing random failures during busy times. Users will notice fewer unexpected interruptions when their requests fail briefly.

93b2e19a4959d278952ce8a3ef1ea8180fefe656.text: The program stopped refreshing the chat window every time a message grew taller than expected. This change fixes a bug where the screen would flicker or jump during long conversations. Users will notice smoother scrolling and less visual disruption while reading responses.

4ecfb89a072d3e5a63d51fcbf1f4cf950d1ba8d8.text: A new command-line option lets people tell the tool exactly which folder to work in when they start it. If they skip this option, the tool behaves as before and uses the folder they are already in.

7fbded5c31a3638fea28ac089f1241c48ed1bc55.text: The command-line tool now distinguishes between temporary connection problems and invalid credentials. If the internet drops, it pauses the login screen, quietly retries the connection, and displays a 'retrying' message in the status bar. If the key is wrong, it stops trying and shows the login prompt immediately.

c424b54dc846d8ba0002da70feb0ab93ed8c0773.text: The command-line tool now has a hidden system to remember messages that fail to send, so it can try again later. This setup is not active yet, meaning you will not see any automatic retries or error recovery in your chats today. It is a small internal change preparing for future updates.

10b2b46393d1cf59596622e83f72e4feb47a57a9.text: When the command-line tool loses its connection to the service and then reconnects, it now shows a brief 'Reconnected' message. This also refreshes the user's login details to ensure they stay valid. This update is live for anyone using the command-line tool.

fcbc8383397d3d1a39de380ff88e55c69ddcb69f.text: The small 'x' used to dismiss the usage notice now changes color when you move your mouse over it. This visual cue confirms the button is clickable, helping you close the banner without guessing.

226d620de1800ce3c80ac4f71116af77d2c70230.text: When the assistant creates a brand new file, the tool view now labels it 'Create' instead of 'Edit'. It also hides the content preview for these new files. This small display update is live for the command line interface.

be03d6103db9d7026bced827845881361d06214b.text: A small visual fix improves the command-line chat experience. When you send a message, the scrollbar no longer flickers or appears prematurely while the system waits for a response. This makes the interface look cleaner and less distracting during the initial pause.

1785aa064f7ded558ce68a898c980484117d9593.text: The file picker in the command line tool now shows a single dot instead of a filename when the file sits in the top folder. This makes the list cleaner by removing repeated text. The change is live today.

d0479c8e012772a1a45ba2fac7eb2f0eebbf7ad8.text: The command-line tool now correctly sends a starting prompt when the session begins. Previously, a brief delay caused the message to be cancelled before it could be delivered. Users who launch the tool with an initial prompt will see it appear and process as intended.

3deb685d4a5899da4162549765162bd101b5fe1a.text: The file suggestion menu now appears when you type the @ symbol anywhere in your message, not just at the very end. This helps you edit or add file references in the middle of a sentence. You will notice the menu popping up correctly while typing mid-line.

97a7f58f3987f21b3fc93e465865f0df90e48e5d.text: The software now recognizes when a connection to the AI service fails due to network issues, instead of hiding the error. This allows the system to automatically try the request again, improving reliability for developers using the SDK. It is live today but only affects how the tool handles temporary connection drops.

5f9c54bb5e76aacff68ad4fbc86118b2ddade9a3.text: When you install this command-line tool, it now automatically deletes the old version of the program from your computer's settings folder before finishing. This ensures that upgrading to the new version doesn't leave behind broken files that might cause errors. You won't see any visual changes, but the tool will run more reliably after updates.

55510e86599ad4705caec482e646a40847d6de87.text: The web search tool failed to send the required password with its requests, causing searches to fail. This fix passes the password along, so web searches now work. This affects people using the assistant's web search feature. The fix is live today.

6cc81d832ddea9b51f5d5e7dd4fd0fa34d4d5549.text: The command-line tool now fetches your credit balance directly when you open the usage banner, instead of saving a copy in the background first. This internal cleanup makes the data flow simpler for developers. You will notice no change in how the banner looks or behaves.

bfd58abf07ac6b22103638be36ed59a006b7482d.text: The usage banner in the command line tool now changes color based on remaining credits. Green means plenty, yellow means low, and red means very low. This helps users spot credit issues quickly.

f39642630b4f6e9cff6a3767a597070e531c163a.text: The development team paused four automated checks for the command-line tool because they were failing due to software compatibility issues. This change only affects the internal testing process and does not alter the tool's behavior for you. You will notice no changes to the application, as the feature itself remains untouched.

ac81d007830946a2e23a83ea28fb6303f27c2353.text: A small internal update adds an automatic cleanup step to the older version of the software. When someone installs this older package, it now deletes the old program file from their computer before the new installer runs. This prevents the two versions from clashing, ensuring the software starts correctly without manual fixes.

b6bfa99a46154ab82ca7466ac062bd7fab901220.text: A small fix corrected how the text-based assistant arranges timestamps and messages on the screen. Previously, these elements could overlap, making the conversation hard to read. Now, they are stacked neatly in a column, ensuring each part of the message is clearly visible without jumbled text.

47b2c7f18ad4715e38f58bd618f70aaeddf9c46c.text: The internal system that helps AI agents write code now saves the agent's work as organized data instead of a messy block of text. This change affects only the agents used by staff to edit code. Staff will notice the agent's final output is cleaner and easier to read, though the actual code edits remain the same.

6c80db92f0a51c1e4a2878a6b9aab02d46c395b7.text: The chat interface now uses a single, streamlined path to process your message, replacing several separate internal checks that previously decided whether to send your text immediately or add it to a waiting queue. This change affects only the internal structure of the application, so you will notice no difference in how the chat behaves, loads, or responds to your input.

9cf76362033d90140bba5b0b33dc870bc34bda80.text: The internal coding assistant now provides clearer step-by-step examples for complex tasks and strictly forbids running risky commands without explicit permission. This update also requires the assistant to check its work more thoroughly and quickly. These changes affect only the internal team using the assistant and do not impact external customers.

f60c3c11fa1496cdeecd31f4abda58c6a9980b18.text: A small internal fix corrected how the test environment pretends to fetch data. This helps developers keep the code checks passing. Regular users will see no change.

8ae3f5e68ecc24691569cc17196198c800f96343.text: The program's text interface now hides the internal steps for selecting code reviewers and deep thinkers by default. You will see a single line saying 'Generating code reviews' instead of a cluttered list of background processes. This reduces visual noise for anyone running the tool in their terminal.

f422343f49c005ebfc26808204ec5e079b92cbdf.text: The chat tool now waits for the assistant to finish its current task before processing new instructions. If you type while it is working, your message goes into a holding area instead of interrupting the assistant. This prevents the assistant from getting confused by overlapping requests.

c3dfbd80bb523a9a93a5a4ac9c8946d41a5eda9e.text: The code review tool now asks for multiple suggestions directly instead of launching separate helper programs. This change affects internal developers using the review feature. They will notice slightly faster response times and cleaner output, as the system no longer needs to combine separate results.

4fb9eaca81ed1613b553d301e0f4be82dcd977df.text: The code reviewer now uses a stronger, multi-candidate model in max mode, while default mode keeps the standard reviewer. This change is live for internal tooling and affects how post-implementation review is triggered. Users in max mode will see more thorough review steps automatically added to their task plans.

8e1ab6b64c19b96eef585e496c70442a44a5258e.text: The internal coding assistant now automatically asks a second AI to review its work after making changes. This affects the assistant's internal process for standard and advanced tasks, not the end user directly. Users will not notice this change, but the assistant may produce slightly higher-quality code by catching its own mistakes before finishing.

87b54d44dcca1d9e840e713ba3caa7ac98141fa4.text: The command-line tool now quietly records basic usage details when you are signed in. This helps the team understand how people use the tool. You will not see any visible change in the interface.

713fbd3b354aa7527b1ee3a23c05f61244ed6cce.text: The text input area now shows a scroll bar only when there is more content than can fit on the screen. This change fixes a visual glitch where the scroll bar would flicker or appear incorrectly while the assistant was typing. If you are using the command-line tool, you will see a cleaner interface without distracting movement near the edge of the window.

56959415ca1561cd8ab0eea9d35e8771a1c92add.text: The chat assistant now ignores special commands like 'login' or 'feedback' if you type them without a slash at the start. You must type '/login' or '/feedback' to trigger these actions; typing just 'login' will be treated as a regular question. This change is live today.

c9007df924a8d5fa1de6b066d0c74453a370f289.text: The text box for the assistant's replies now hides the thin vertical bar on its right side until you send your first message. Once you send that first message, the bar appears and stays visible for the rest of the conversation.

5bc98c0979bc324368f9ebc6fe7ecb15173a12a2.text: A small internal fix adjusted the order of setup steps in a background test for the command-line tool. This ensures the test reads the correct folder location before running. Only the testing team will notice, as it prevents false failures when checking if local assistant settings load correctly.

3e1289ab723121fab352263453fa17b0d8ade715.text: The command that creates the program's installable file now uses the new name, Codebuff, instead of the old name, Codecane. This affects the build process, not the software's features or behavior. A person downloading the program would see the updated name on the file itself.

4f943907d7c98be5f6f39537c0258d0cf8e9179b.text: When the command-line tool cannot find a project's source-control folder, it previously treated the current location as the project root. Now it reports that no project folder was found, and other parts of the tool handle that missing folder by falling back to the current location. This internal cleanup affects only the command-line tool's path logic and is live today.

a5cab542c9b2183fa1c856bf2d4eba65fb6f4361.text: Previously, the command-line interface hid its main title if it couldn't find any local assistants. Now, it always shows the title and your current folder path, even when the list of assistants is empty. You will see the header immediately upon opening the tool, rather than waiting for assistant data to load.

63e76ba696f1d8be0c6bb6d4d495e4973d387f67.text: The AI assistant now has a stricter rule against changing your files unless you ask for it. This small update applies to the assistant's internal guidelines. You would only notice this if the assistant previously tried to edit your files without permission, which it should now avoid doing.

caad869acf5b7db5bb6bb005ecbf9a3859f96d56.text: A background task that listens for manual refresh commands now starts only when the app launches, not when other parts load. This prevents multiple copies of the listener from running at once. Most people will not notice a difference, but it fixes a rare glitch where refresh commands might have failed.

a0db4b03735c18f6fd7a1b1bd97b8cb76df421d8.text: The tool now accepts a starting folder for finding the project root, instead of always assuming the current working directory. This internal cleanup means the program can look in a specific place if needed, though nothing changes for the user today. You will not notice any difference.

9d30211d7cf3ae0bf4ffb9e4125e64ed6ce30650.text: The command-line tool's name changed from 'codecane' to 'codebuff'. If you use this tool, you will now type 'codebuff' instead of 'codecane' to start it, and its help messages will reflect the new name. This change is live now.

3ef47341d03531bad22cfba2cf4ab3fd870d5190.text: The internal coding assistant now gives specific instructions to one type of AI model to prevent it from making formatting errors when using tools. This affects only developers using that specific model, who will notice fewer crashes when the assistant tries to run code review or spawn other agents.

d68b9ffe1d0038866c338d8141d43bb78018f5e7.text: The command-line tool now waits until the program fully starts up before setting up the clock display. This change is live today and affects all users of the tool. You will not notice any difference in how times appear, but the program may start up slightly faster.

63dfdc008e0e92024c57033143fde2ef237199de.text: The text tool no longer prints hidden debug lines while you read the assistant's thoughts or move the cursor in long messages. This cleanup affects only people using the command-line program. You will see a cleaner screen with less clutter when the program updates.

73838992f9f23e05a45e02b2232ac0c8a86158c4.text: The automated tool that publishes the command-line app was told to look for its files in the wrong folder. This fix points it to the correct location. It is an internal repair; customers will notice nothing because the release process itself was broken, not the software.

8252e43f1dd0e803ad76b6d21e43b9df7f0de5e9.text: The release packaging system now automatically uses the correct name for each new version of the command-line tool, instead of always using the old default name. This affects the internal build process, ensuring the downloaded files match the specific tool being released. There is no visible change for end users.

f6563fe6b59d4cb525a3324100dfe4402074668f.text: The typing box now uses the screen's own layout to place the blinking line, instead of guessing. This fixes the cursor jumping to the wrong spot when you type long, wrapped text. It is live today for anyone using the command-line tool.

a39b4b7f9b4107ec8e86dae5a10ce8f570595cb5.text: When a request asks for multiple answers, the system now stops with a clear error if the reply is malformed instead of guessing or hiding the problem. This applies to internal agent steps, so operators will see a failure message rather than a silent fallback. Single-answer requests remain unchanged.

d916c71ade8be4d24e4e7f23e63803fac126c0eb.text: The release instructions for the command-line coding tool now call the product Codebuff instead of Codecane. They remove the test-version warning and tell people to install the regular version instead of the earlier test version. The updated instructions are live today for anyone reading the release notes. The tool itself works the same; only the written guidance changed.

c20c010458b770b00ca8de619709375b615b94b8.text: A thin vertical line now appears on the right edge of the chat window when messages go off-screen. This helps you see how far up or down you are in the conversation. The change is small and only affects the text-based chat interface.

b2af744ef595e746a92de61afe78bf623988b650.text: The system that prepares test versions of the software now automatically includes necessary helper files in the package sent to testers. Before this, those files were missing, so testers might have found the software incomplete or broken. This change is internal and affects only the people testing the staging version, ensuring they receive a complete copy.

ca74698eef454ab2cb4441701077f4c8608e82f5.text: The command-line tool now uses a shared helper to write timestamps on saved conversation messages, instead of its own date format. This is an internal cleanup that keeps message history records consistent. You will not notice any difference in how the tool works or what it displays.

6fcf6ea7ed8a5a898e7475ae02868f373dcc6b6f.text: The system now handles messy text responses more gracefully. If the assistant sends back a single answer instead of a list, or if the text is slightly broken, the software reads it as one valid reply rather than crashing. This keeps the chat running smoothly for users even when the underlying service sends unexpected formats.

7f4b509b6b5d1bd189a512c0d0d2044d5632eabb.text: The software that automatically publishes the assistant's updates had trouble checking which version was newest. The fix hardcodes the name of the package being checked, ensuring the publisher looks at the correct spot online. This is an internal repair for the release process; users will not notice any changes in the assistant's behavior.

a4870d4e66602bf6eb58c13e8a867330980769b3.text: The release process now targets the correct package folder instead of the old one. This change affects only the internal automation that publishes the software. There is no immediate visible difference for end users.

d6ded0f647fadaab6a78abba7f32bf43313d79cf.text: A small fix stops the search tool from mistakenly blocking valid requests when searching from the current folder. People using the software development kit will no longer see false 'outside project directory' errors during these searches. The change is live today.

d95f52b8c98e0d8003f27da2c79fc194b4e073b9.text: The code that handles your feedback buttons was cleaned up to make it easier for the team to maintain. Nothing changed for you: the thumbs-up and thumbs-down buttons still work exactly the same way.

e699fd335ac4884e7ea85c57f61ba9be6fc0fda0.text: A small internal adjustment doubles the time allowed for a specific automated test to finish. This helps the test runner avoid stopping early when tasks take longer than expected. Only internal evaluation systems are affected; regular users will not notice any change.

40afe229945d4b9b68a1db37dd22f2bdb04a45c5.text: The command-line tool now builds itself using a different underlying engine, matching the one it actually runs on. This is an internal cleanup that doesn't change how the tool behaves for you. You won't notice any difference in speed or features, but the tool is now more consistent with its own setup.

f259c21b669d37722dadda2a01305e7a722c9cf6.text: The thinking tool now automatically selects the best answer from multiple attempts without manually removing the last step. This change affects only the internal logic of the tool and is live. Users will not notice any difference.

b05e8030ada34f1adbf472cd03ba108d9b874cdc.text: The AI assistant now receives sample instructions showing exactly how to format its internal edit requests. This change only affects the specific model being used by the internal development team. No customer will notice any difference in the final product's behavior.

3004a493625bb0fbc0187dd2a0810aa9743517da.text: The command-line tool now identifies your project folder at startup instead of guessing later. This ensures logs and settings save to the correct location, even if you run the tool from a different directory. You might notice fewer errors about missing files or misplaced logs.

b2a139b3367b4cd342ba9b2a60b460f8e98f1376.text: The deep-thinking helper now uses a simpler way to hand off its result, cutting out two extra steps. This change is internal and mostly affects how the system plans complex answers. In the command-line tool, people using max mode will now see a status message reading 'Generating N deep thoughts...' while the helper works.

bde1512b23a3e0d3f849e7f1ba386b32d193ec22.text: A hidden note saying 'Hi!' was added to the command-line tool's startup code. This change affects only the internal structure and has no impact on functionality. Users will not notice any difference.

af0040a76bf0356ba3df336d6da1b08dcb7752fb.text: When the tool creates several versions of code at once, the command-line interface now shows a message saying how many versions it is making. This affects people using the editor's best-of-n feature, giving them a clearer idea of the work being done. The change is live and visible when running this specific task.

2d00a2117b4ee87a0097aa2951aa14b5a9b28828.text: The internal document research assistant now reads files once and replies with a shorter summary. This change affects only the automated agent used by researchers. A user would see the assistant answer faster with less text.

cfc3307af15da7a1c4421c5079cbd303639faa77.text: The command menu now puts the command name and its description on one line when the terminal is wide enough. Short commands fit side-by-side. Long names or narrow screens keep the description on the line below.

0f2eaf2c414270cbb8c83e61e6c9673383dc6aaf.text: The command-line tool now lets you pick a specific saved conversation to resume, rather than always returning to the last one. When you exit, it prints the exact command needed to reopen that particular chat later. This is live for CLI users who manage multiple conversation threads.

daf16ca2ecc600a2a903f2e0a9850aa2f899463f.text: The text box where you type messages can now grow taller to fit your screen, up to half its height. This helps people writing long prompts see more of their text at once without scrolling.

e7b7989e227570a82dcf04c0ade95f9dab958766.text: The system now records the exact instructions and settings given to background helpers. People who review activity logs will see these details in the history of each helper task. This change is live and improves transparency for internal observers.

12bd093e1968d959d33cc228ed5e84186813afd8.text: The command menu in the terminal tool used to show extra words in parentheses next to each option, like 'logout (signout)' or 'exit (quit)'. Those parentheses are gone now, so the menu looks shorter and cleaner. The alternative words still work if you type them; they just no longer clutter the list. This is a small visual tidy-up, not a new feature.

f3d115f270095a094d266b016a3afbd4b2b51422.text: The release tool now checks the main software store directly to find the newest version of the older package, instead of looking at the project's public code page. This change only affects the internal process used to publish updates. No customers or regular users will notice any difference in how the software works.

c0b8ca14393cf63a2919d63ef370dc893a72a5a2.text: The command-line tool now clears its saved login state whenever you sign in or sign out. This prevents the app from accidentally using old login details for the wrong account. You might notice the app behaves normally but handles account switches more reliably.

49aab02e193f67664600a729fa315939dfcc6e4f.text: A bug in the command-line tool made the text input box shrink to a single character wide under certain conditions. This happened because the tool failed to notice when the box's size changed on screen. The fix ensures the box now correctly measures its available space, so typing feels normal again.

950489aee91def0ee271e5f66bb1e15aa3b7b928.text: Developers reverted a small update to their automated checks for the chat and text generation services. The previous update caused these checks to fail randomly by looking for the wrong version of a background tool. This fix restores the correct version so the checks pass again. Regular users will not notice any change.

5f0e9b628a887f061b22e784c3be556852aa6e80.text: The command-line tool now shows the login screen filling the entire terminal window instead of appearing as a small box on top of the chat. This change is live. You would notice the login prompt takes up the whole screen, making it harder to miss.

78f5fcd6c2574813bb4b0a4d659de21d0ca3bf91.text: Small internal change. The tool that prepares a new release now asks the published package catalog for the newest package record, instead of searching a release announcement page for a label. It affects only the release process, so people using the product would not notice anything.

2c8076c8bd7adf07813ed0686e7e1b7514b76c9f.text: When you log out of the command-line tool, it now wipes your stored login details completely instead of leaving a fragment behind. This affects anyone using the tool who logs out and then logs back in. You would notice that the tool no longer remembers old account information, so you start fresh each time you sign in again.

310a76336f906a545e004b7751303704329b7bfc.text: A small internal update tightened the rules for an automated file-search assistant. It now explicitly stops after listing files, preventing it from repeating a search step it already finished. This change is not visible to end users and only affects how the internal tool behaves.

ad9fd7f093114987fae76b180cfe2e862ccec534.text: The command-line login screen now closes when you press Ctrl+C. This change is live and affects only people using the terminal to sign in. You would notice the login prompt disappears immediately instead of getting stuck.

beec8c13a1a01b577732e78de4c02e8cc426e8fd.text: The file-finding assistant now strictly reports locations without launching other tools. This prevents recursive loops during search tasks. Internal staff will see faster, more predictable responses when locating code.

9d173e0096705631b0f27e8544627cffba0c4047.text: The instructions shown to the file-search assistant now tell it to ask for broader descriptions. This helps the assistant find more related files instead of just one. It is a small internal update that improves how the search tool understands requests.

2947b3cc64a7417da3728a98af647e7247ce4b66.text: Agent creators can now specify preferred providers, fallback rules, and price limits for OpenRouter routing. This change is in place but does nothing yet until the agent runtime starts reading these new settings.

7196df259ff67620a2c456e420bbbec92692d74f.text: A small update now cleans up how login links appear in the text-based interface. It removes the 'http://' or 'https://' part from the visible text, making the link shorter and easier to read. The link itself still works exactly the same way when clicked.

486a32de43a44a516729eb482e87a741cad30d4a.text: The software now handles problems quietly instead of stopping completely. If a key is wrong or a task is cancelled, you will see a clear message explaining what happened rather than a crash. This applies to anyone using the automated coding assistant, making it more stable when errors occur.

4e507bf65b8d90ebbd20053dfed5e616ba84f803.text: The team moved the files for the editor's 'best-of-n' feature to a new folder. This is a pure reorganization with no changes to the code itself. It affects only the internal structure of the project and will not be visible to anyone using the software.

10dee2542c0f3ce6f67b573389c4aa11067c282d.text: Small internal tweak. The AI assistant's instructions now require a specialized editor for complex changes, making its code better. You might notice the assistant ending its replies more cleanly, without repeating summaries.

9897a3dd58ae05443a8230e26490a90cfb21c8f2.text: The internal web-browsing tool now performs a single search and returns the raw results directly, skipping the previous step of generating a written report.
