This change affects the automated research assistant's browsing capability. Users would notice the tool returns search links faster, but without a summarized narrative.

2603b90a50e0bb9c8323e685c3933d4120b72ad0.text: When signing in, the browser now shows a simple message telling you to return to your terminal, instead of displaying a large success image. This change applies immediately to anyone logging in. It also stops the system from automatically applying referral codes, so you must enter them manually in the terminal to claim bonus credits.

29aea41011e6fa48048b04ae4e4c893167b1b109.text: A small note left behind by a developer was removed from the text command-line tool's startup code. This change does not affect how the tool works or what you see on your screen. It is purely internal cleanup and has no impact on daily use.

16c5bfa2bb7afad848bad1d614ce15af5d74ab2d.text: A new 'fast mode' for the internal coding assistant was configured to prioritize speed over thoroughness. This mode now uses a specific AI model that skips detailed planning steps and validation checks, instead making changes all at once. This affects only internal tools and will not be visible to external customers.

0191ec4529e34e59920b89b2f195a403ff2b0526.text: The software's internal quality checks were failing because test scripts were missing required instructions for handling collapsed chat sections. Developers fixed these scripts to match the current interface requirements. This change only affects the automated testing process and does not alter how the application behaves for end users.

2f9fcbb89954783baa9f678753b9ce92381fafdb.text: The assistant now checks if the Zed editor is active before trying to read its color settings. It also stops forcing dark mode for users of the Ghostty terminal. This means Ghostty users will see the assistant match their own light or dark preference instead of always being dark.

c7088238ba1e0852431a6280d585515e246e1604.text: The AI assistants that help with editing and planning tasks switched to a newer, more capable version of their underlying brain. This update is active now. Users might notice slightly better answers and fewer mistakes, especially when the assistant needs to use tools or make complex edits.

cf92cb22890b5b99f8e29b7293fd065ddab02d8d.text: The chat display logic was simplified by removing an unnecessary middle layer. This change is internal and does not affect how the chat looks or behaves for the user.

3174c4413b7f2a23aa3184cbe8c6fea27a24ab96.text: The command-line tool now blocks messages that start with a forward slash, unless they are used to set up the initial project. Instead of sending these to the AI assistant, the tool immediately shows a 'Command not found' error. This change is active and prevents unrecognized slash commands from reaching the AI.

ae6b7f01572a5f3cfa0fe6570c47015da81c0c8b.text: The command-line tool now launches directly through its own built-in engine instead of relying on a general system program. This change affects the startup process for anyone running the tool from a terminal. People will notice nothing different in the tool's behavior or appearance, as this is purely an internal cleanup to make the launch process simpler and more reliable.

b447105d2fefc0c74d7ff617170c90c15bac0de9.text: The command-line tool now builds chat messages using a single shared template instead of copying the same rules into five different places. This change is internal cleanup. Users will not notice any difference in the tool's behavior.

e507034c904edc143975fd12492a135c19713b5a.text: A developer added a hidden note inside the startup code of the command-line tool. This note is only visible to people reading the code, not to anyone using the tool. The tool behaves exactly the same as before.

1d5fa92e3c3f06eea801fc7edca8abcb93d29270.text: The tool now automatically hides the long internal reasoning notes after they finish appearing on screen. This keeps the conversation window tidy by removing clutter from previous steps. Users will notice that these detailed explanation blocks collapse themselves without requiring a manual click.

9dd2fdfd32eb1f977e6796e996a993c1c7a732b5.text: Stopping a chat now saves the partial reply in the history. This helps the assistant know what it already said. You might notice it repeats less when you ask again.

5f4d34b2769d81b16d0f701f2a114379dc1f7427.text: The chat window now automatically redraws itself if the text inside grows or shrinks noticeably. This fixes a glitch where the view could get stuck or look broken when a message changed size without being scrolled. The change applies only to the command-line interface and is active immediately.

59628850f6c070bfd42383e35717d22844834d2c.title: Add freebuff-countries constants for free-mode tiering
59628850f6c070bfd42383e35717d22844834d2c.summary: New `common/src/constants/freebuff-countries.ts` defines `FREE_MODE_TIER_ONE_COUNTRIES`, `FREE_MODE_TIER_TWO_COUNTRIES`, and `FREE_MODE_TIER_THREE_COUNTRIES` sets, plus `FREE_MODE_ALLOWED_COUNTRIES` union and `formatCountryCodes` helper. Groups rank by advertiser value per account (measured 2026-09-12); SG and IL exited full access 2026-09-15 due to 8-25% ad fill vs 43-80% baseline, earning ~1/10 US rate. KR remains tier-three by decision despite poor fill. Lives in `common` to avoid server-only geoip/db deps in client bundles; `packages/internal/src/free-mode-country/allowed-countries.ts` re-exports to sync meter and public FAQ copy.

af4eec66d118971ec0b3cecdf2adf08dde566b71.text: Typing the command to leave the program now makes it close completely. Before, it sometimes left the program open or stuck. If you type the exit command, the program should close right away.

53b8b7346749bee218b7eba524694cd1d072b842.text: The command-line tool now separates thoughts from its main assistant versus its sub-assistants. Previously, reasoning from sub-assistants might mix into the main stream; now, only the main assistant's thoughts appear in the primary view, while sub-assistant thoughts go to their specific sections. This makes the output cleaner for CLI users.

8e6faa0b9d53153f9f87387521bfd761a57655bf.text: The dark mode appearance of the text interface was slightly adjusted. The main background changed from pure black to a dark gray, while text lines and borders became lighter. People using the dark theme will see a less harsh background and clearer edges around boxes or sections.

ad99717f547a2dd28cdf6bd4cb6c99271a17bd5f.text: The command-line tool now treats thinking updates as a valid signal to start displaying output, specifically for the main assistant. This small fix ensures the screen reacts correctly when the AI begins its primary reasoning process.

ffe5106290924a533efcaa0a6da7cda824454624.text: The text-based chat window now shows hint text at normal brightness instead of dimming it. The border around the chat no longer changes color when the window is active, and unused background color settings were removed. People using that chat window will see clearer hint text and a steadier border. The change is live.

2b7cc8d044beb0752627cdd7ae585e2be514789c.text: The command-line tool now hides the 'Task Complete' message. This change is live and affects only those using the command-line interface. You will no longer see a bullet point and bold text indicating task completion in the terminal output.

00bc75c53375f3601512779366eba29ac15c81f2.text: The vertical line next to the assistant's responses in the command-line tool is now gray instead of green. This small visual tweak helps distinguish the assistant's text from the user's blue text. The change is live for anyone using the default settings.

d341faaa2c7a0b06664ff9f7aaae57d1009c97c5.text: The website's top menu now stays fixed at the top while you scroll, with a slight blur effect behind it. Links and the logo have smoother hover animations, like a gentle glow or scale-up. This visual update applies to all visitors on the web interface and is live.

4419bc4290dfb8ef6aed8cc7869daf9d3494431d.text: The assistant now shows its thinking process in gray text as it works. This change affects the internal command-line tool used by the team. If they run the tool, they will see the assistant's reasoning appear on the screen before the final answer.

7d78d2f21f026dc755396e89e29753da3c305356.text: The command preview in the terminal now counts wrapped lines based on screen width, not just raw text breaks. This prevents long outputs from overflowing narrow windows. The fix is active today for terminal users viewing command results.

1a5f776fdc01c6f3863e82741646a0909a0a388d.text: The command-line tool now displays build options in a vertical list instead of a horizontal row. This change ensures the choices remain readable on narrow screens and removes the need for the tool to constantly check the window size. Users will see a consistent prompt to select a build option, regardless of their terminal width.

dd76dae19f155430bdab33d4027322a410496399.text: A small fix in the command-line tool stops the suggestion menu from closing when you press the up arrow at the very top of the list. Previously, this action would dismiss the menu unexpectedly. Now, the menu remains open, allowing you to navigate through options without accidentally exiting.

a9788f567596666349e7440f0bc5308844b81974.text: Pressing the stop key during a response now pauses any waiting messages, showing a border to indicate they are queued. The next message you send goes first, and the queue automatically resumes afterward. This applies to command-line chat users.

cdb009caddd9cf86c8e2f9e8be36cebf94ab2431.text: A small internal update fixed how the system's self-checks report costs. This change affects only the testing environment, not the live product. Users will see no difference in behavior or features.

892814b3b51ad549a8965c3045233372216010a5.text: The command-line assistant now sizes its suggestion popup based on your terminal window width, not just the longest text inside it. If you resize your window, the popup adapts. This is a minor visual improvement available immediately.

5ad4ac4b1bb872ca79ba8cda1d8cfcb622e06a1a.text: The command-line tool now automatically folds away the file-search step. People using the terminal assistant will see a tidier screen, with the search details hidden under a clickable heading instead of taking up space.

a54e2c0b461ba6bd84e6b6dbf3f5528da75742a8.text: A tiny fix in the command-line tool's menu now handles the down arrow key when you reach the last option. Before, pressing it might have triggered unwanted default actions; now it simply stops there. This affects anyone navigating the suggestion list, preventing accidental jumps or glitches at the bottom.

59702a8749708d211b2cd2daf5bc3bbfbf80ffdd.text: The tool now checks your terminal's background color to set dark or light mode, ignoring which command shell you use. This fixes mismatched colors for Windows users running the tool in non-PowerShell environments. The change is active today.

7ae3f17d9002681f3dc46d5e2ebc01a85fb1713f.text: The internal research assistant now writes shorter summaries instead of long reports. This change affects only the company's internal tools, so external customers will not see any difference. The assistant simply provides the key facts more quickly, without extra details.

07c152a450251e53dd95775e687532f9de4e4d1c.text: The internal testing system was updated to simulate network responses more reliably, replacing an older method that occasionally failed. This change affects only the software engineers who maintain the code; customers will notice no difference in the application's behavior or performance.

0e972b85f2fe1870103af3097a31dbff4e861be9.text: A small fix changes how text deletion works in the command-line tool. Pressing Ctrl+W now deletes the word before the cursor correctly. Alt+Backspace still works exactly as it did before.

6112546b200896a09c61cb6d13fe012ad1831d11.text: When you run the command-line tool inside a supported code editor, it now automatically copies the editor's current light or dark setting instead of asking your terminal what color scheme it uses. This only affects people using the tool inside those specific editors, and they might notice the interface matches their editor theme instantly without a brief delay or color shift during startup.

47ec5fb424d229f4bb349ce482fe4f5a59f0b681.text: The assistant's internal instructions for asking follow-up questions were clarified. It now labels the default choice as 'CURRENT' instead of 'DEFAULT' and uses clearer formatting. This helps the assistant ask better questions when planning tasks, but it is an internal tweak with no visible change for end-users.

5b00df1c632aa677a9bfbd0f3e5822d949dae85a.text: The command-line tool now counts the credits you spend while chatting in that current window. When you ask for your usage, it shows this running total before the official account balance from the server. This helps you see immediate costs without waiting for the server to update, though it resets when you close the program.

d3831e98e541020175ce5c8e500b0e42e01a6aed.text: The command-line tool now correctly displays error messages when a background task fails to start, instead of showing a blank or misleading success state. Affected users will see a red 'failed' indicator and the specific reason for the failure in the task panel. This change is live today.

818ccf576ed51b2f180f1c592a844bfd08b01576.text: This is a minor internal update to how the software checks its own work. It ensures the tests verify that simple text messages are now formatted as structured lists, matching recent changes to the main system. Regular users will not notice any difference, as this only helps developers confirm the software is working correctly.

cf07ad1d224ec44e02d4f6145d8c4d1705e1237d.text: A small fix to the command-line tool makes the 'thinking' section collapse as soon as reasoning begins, instead of waiting for a specific stream event. Users of the CLI will see the reasoning block fold up immediately, regardless of how the answer is being streamed. This change is live and affects message rendering in the terminal interface.

a5d217f912042fd2f845e8f06d1255fa03ad3c01.text: The team switched back to an older version of a shared helper tool for internal features because the newer version broke automated checks. This change only affects the internal development environment and fixes a broken test. You would not notice any difference in the product.

45e15684d0075eaa744078e21b99c9beed409243.text: The internal helper that builds request metadata now accepts extra provider options and merges them into the codebuff key. This is an SDK plumbing change; end users will notice nothing.

59628850f6c070bfd42383e35717d22844834d2c.text: A single list now holds all countries approved for full free access, so the usage counter and the public help page cannot disagree about who qualifies. This update does not change who is eligible today; it just makes the list easier to manage. If you looked at the help page, you would see the same country list as before.

1cbca347626e2e8f03b187961781f648eb714602.text: This small internal update tidied up the visual style of a script that translates chat messages for the AI system. It removes unnecessary punctuation and aligns text to match current team standards. Programmers and AI staff will notice the code looks cleaner, but the actual translation logic and user experience remain completely unchanged.

d16f6ec50432abc8e5b7dc4d280b7c975ebf1b0a.text: A small internal update fixed how a helper library is loaded. This change has no visible effect on anything today.

a3e71a58bee9aed0b92124e99ddbf8061ce7a1b9.text: The command-line tool now changes the text color of the 'Agent mode' button when you hover over it on a Mac. This fixes a visual glitch where the text looked wrong or unreadable in that state. The change is active now.

1c0c35f9cb1176c2cd2ef65d2a752d146c9b4503.text: The assistant now remembers every part of a conversation, even if a reply was just one or two letters. Before, these short replies were skipped, which could make the assistant forget them. This helps the assistant keep track of very brief answers during a chat.

247e0ea10906dc49d3db10c89cad4f20c90120a0.text: Typing the '@' symbol in the command line now shows a list of files in your current folder, alongside the usual agent options. This lets you quickly pick and insert a file path into your prompt without manually typing it out. The feature is active immediately for anyone using the command line interface.

47e5858bb71893b123e3bef19e6b7fab791f9b5b.text: The command-line tool's startup process was reorganized to allow it to detect your terminal's color theme without loading the full application. This is a hidden internal switch that does not change how you interact with the tool today, but it prepares the system for better theme detection in the future.

332f189caff832d937d0c93841979ffc09b27e66.text: The program now hides a specific startup message when it is checking your computer's screen settings. This prevents cluttered text from appearing during these quick checks. You will not see any changes in how the program works, but the output will look cleaner.

6e752a5a7060b3a294065aef3948380505d8b463.text: Developers cleaned up the internal structure of the command-line tool's chat window. This change does not alter how the interface looks or behaves for you today. It is a small, invisible housekeeping update that makes the underlying code simpler to maintain.

bb254dd891cc2bc69ac23011fd6e8f67a396b5dc.text: The system stopped breaking a single text message into two pieces before sending it to the AI. This change affects the software development kit used to build AI assistants. Users will not notice a difference, but the message now arrives as one complete block, preventing the AI from applying storage rules to only half the text.

d0822688cd878d6e2d8c50c5f752b7d69119bd8a.text: When the command menu is open, pressing the arrow keys now keeps you moving through the list options. Previously, reaching the top or bottom of the list would accidentally scroll your previous commands. This fix ensures the menu stays visible while you navigate suggestions.

4f54abe04d03d3b3793cbad5c1d28d61ba3ef3c7.text: The command-line tool no longer checks your terminal's background color to decide between a light or dark text theme. This change is active now. You might notice the tool uses your computer's general system setting for light or dark mode instead of automatically matching the specific color scheme of the window you are typing in.

1253a11ede478e674b4742e8aead6a1e9d8ed712.text: The command-line tool's built-in help prompt has been disabled. You can no longer type 'help' or 'h' to see a list of available actions. This change is live and affects only those who use the tool via a terminal window.

209b81809c8e3277270343cd139150e6ea9980c0.text: When the command-line program updates itself on Windows, it now tries to move the old program file aside if it cannot delete it because the file is in use. A person updating the program may see a backup file with a date and time left behind, while the update continues. If the old file cannot be deleted or moved, the update stops and reports both problems.

2748b59bb408c5ab8a6b732bceb0a3c2c89dbe66.text: A small internal change makes the automated helper that edits files wait until the helper that reads files has finished. It affects internal automated editing tasks, not outside customers. Someone watching those tasks would see the steps run one after another instead of at the same time, reducing the chance of editing before the needed information is available. It is live.

6791074f2e6a96e6194bda9185e6ac86043b8f59.text: The team switched the computer used to build the Mac version of their tool to a newer model. This change is internal and affects only how the software is made, not how it works. People using the tool on Mac will not notice any difference.

6144999e24b138d5b1c4ff106459daedbd4c1996.text: The team changed which automated test setup runs every night to save money. This is an internal update, so nothing visible to you changes. The system still checks the same code, just using a cheaper method.

23f1843b05a288446643447f84bfb7c93bf7e91c.text: The text editor menu hid commands like 'diff' and 'usage' that do nothing yet. This cleans up the list for people using the command-line tool. You will see fewer options when typing commands, but no working features were removed.

0e3772e4b960dfbeae282fc27f20b663e7b3f03c.text: The instructions for the AI assistant when it runs computer commands were tightened up. It is now explicitly forbidden from using certain commands to edit files and must always include flags that prevent the system from getting stuck waiting for confirmation. This affects the AI's reliability when performing tasks, ensuring it avoids common errors without needing to guess the correct behavior.

fa87d73983c909cfd039bc223e85eb217b2280dc.text: The text shown in the command-line tool's input box now shortens automatically if the window is less than 65 characters wide. This prevents the message from being cut off or wrapping awkwardly. The change is live today and only affects people using a narrow terminal window.

be3bf719cea9eb6056368160455dac26887536c4.text: The instructions for how the AI assistant edits files were simplified. Users will notice the AI now writes out entire files rather than small snippets when making changes, which may use more credits but reduces errors from misunderstood formatting.

5d539472c0038e5019f142b8538a527e89b251b9.text: The command-line tool now checks each piece of chat data to ensure it is the right kind of information before trying to display it. This internal cleanup prevents the program from guessing incorrectly about data formats. Regular users will not see any visual changes, but the tool becomes slightly more stable behind the scenes.

afb3870ca35334872116e92b1f1b0f3ceaa753ea.text: The software now puts a random number in its test instructions to force fresh calculations. This helps developers check costs accurately. Normal users will not notice any difference.

fb21e445221b95fcc9ff72420016282b08ffc1c0.text: The system's hidden instructions were tightened to prevent accidental data loss and improve search accuracy. Users might notice the assistant refusing to run risky commands like saving changes without explicit permission, and search results will now cap at specific limits (250 items for code, 12 for files) to keep responses focused. These safety and clarity adjustments are active immediately.

3f283b469cdf95cb53f9da13fee4fa0f0e8cf2bb.text: The program now waits until it starts running to check your computer's color settings and set up file monitoring, rather than doing it automatically when the code loads. This change affects the command-line tool's startup behavior. You will not notice any difference in how the tool looks or works.

75e0a738128fe57be202cf9b403e42f207e06416.text: In the command-line tool, the elapsed time and completion time now appear on the right side of each message block instead of the left. This small visual change affects anyone using the CLI, making the timing information easier to distinguish from the main content.

bc04de28acb5cb3bbf9180e5929842f84a9046ff.text: The command-line tool now waits until it finishes reading your typed instructions before loading its visual style settings. This change affects only the program's startup sequence. You will not notice any difference in how the tool looks or behaves.

091a2224796cd4bf8b98b7561f666bbde22af57f.text: A small internal fix for the staging release tool. It now gives the version check four seconds to finish instead of one, so it no longer fails early on slow startup. Only staging release automation is affected; end users see nothing.

b4a129b65bdf8777fdb4d314efaa6d31284f8dc9.text: A small fix corrects how text wraps when you press Enter at the very start of a line in the command tool. Before, typing at the beginning could make the text jump or wrap strangely. This is fixed now.

b6eea3716ecb53691384d61f333dc6ce17667df1.text: A developer improved the written explanation inside the program's code about how it finds text positions. This change only affects the people who read and maintain the code, not the software's behavior. Users will not notice any difference when using the tool.

cb7d3aa0f60c0ea94da9b4f1a9898a349744d3fb.text: The assistant's instructions were updated to include a specific example of how to request help from other assistants. This change ensures the system uses the correct method to ask for assistance rather than trying to contact other assistants directly. Users might notice slightly more reliable behavior when the system needs to coordinate with other specialized assistants.

455874924d4ae278e1ea8afc13e5025873ad2e53.text: A small internal update fixed how the software identifies specific knowledge files by adjusting its text-matching rules. This change ensures the system correctly loads these files instead of failing to find them. Users will not see any visual changes, but the underlying data retrieval is now more reliable.

b5a5f6e375c9b0abef4e16a74ccf0e2cc234c397.text: The text box now scrolls to keep the blinking cursor visible while you type a long message. Previously, the view always snapped to the very bottom, hiding the line you were editing. This applies to anyone typing multiple lines in the command-line interface today.

99498b7342b838644ac48dee536b7a57c8273ca4.text: The command-line text box now moves the cursor correctly when pressing up or down arrow keys on long lines that wrap. Previously, the cursor jumped to the wrong spot when text wrapped or contained new lines. This fix is live today and affects anyone typing multi-line text in the tool.

3cfb35fb609c2e9ac0e2c897ca407f4db182905e.text: When you press the down arrow key in the text box, the blinking cursor now moves to the correct character, even if your text wraps to the next line. Before, it often jumped to the wrong spot, especially near the end of a line. This small fix makes typing and editing feel more accurate.

2d79849a40a137eb84bf61e6b7d8e51e972859e8.text: The automated system that checks new code now stops any test that runs longer than one minute. This change applies only to the internal checks that run every time a developer submits work. Developers will see stuck tests fail quickly instead of hanging forever.

8b10157d92388092ef2d4bc4e20589a7bc49808e.text: The automated quality checks now include the developer toolkit package. This change only affects the internal testing process. Developers will notice the toolkit gets checked for errors automatically, but customers see no difference.

888fac9bec031b5d160889fac2d5f3071313237c.text: The system now instructs a specific AI model to always attempt a tool-based action in each response, rather than just replying with text. This change affects internal agents using that model and aims to prevent them from stalling or failing to trigger necessary tasks. It is a small, internal update to the agent's behavior rules.

50e90d8ed74eead0002e97eaeec12b29f0947de0.text: The product already renamed the label for one AI service option and standardized the spelling of a temporary-storage setting. The internal test checks were still looking for the old names, so they would have failed. This updates those checks to match. Nothing a user would notice; it only keeps the internal test suite passing.

5712cb17067e2ae1a07b70d879c7a920ac185ac7.text: When you set your coding editor to automatically match your computer's light or dark mode, the command-line tool now follows that setting instead of guessing. This applies to users of JetBrains and Zed editors who have enabled this automatic theme syncing. You will notice the text in the command-line interface changes appearance to match your system preference without needing manual adjustments.

d4b49a10f72b3943cde3bd016878c1fd850e8415.text: A new check was added to the software's internal testing tools to confirm that reusing previous conversation data lowers costs for the next request. This change is internal and only affects the developers maintaining the system. Users will not notice any immediate difference, as this step ensures the cost-saving feature works correctly behind the scenes.

487c6b962e0ff6e633458cb3e5656315422e2c48.text: Seven internal assistant modes now use the standard thinking setting instead of the quick one. This only affects how these specific background helpers operate, not the main chat experience. You will not see any change in the interface.

3632965d8c5f95cd92596b7df827c31e8fb01d5f.text: The gray hint text in the command-line chat box is now shorter. This affects people using the terminal interface. They will see less visual clutter in the input field.

98b22699c3de87a21a8c6d0907c3a42980e40ec5.text: The internal assistant's instruction manual was updated to include a small space before its sample questions. This helps the assistant format its requests for user choices more neatly. Regular users will not see this change directly, as it only affects how the assistant prepares its messages behind the scenes.

a258347b81604e4f996497ba4f8ca0f511829816.text: Fixed a mismatch that prevented prompt caching from working for the Codebuff assistant. Users of the SDK will now see faster response times and lower costs when reusing conversation context, as the system correctly identifies the service provider.

7d0192f5e45bdc2972b13d8e0ea0df75fd2c2d26.text: A small internal update changed how an automated assistant handles requests. It now decides on its own when to use helper tools, rather than following a rigid step-by-step plan. This affects only the assistant's internal reasoning process. You will not notice any change in the app's behavior or interface today.

914c148586a723bad73aa7b5123e0db034f4dea3.text: The internal assistant stopped forcing a specific editing tool for every code change. It now checks if it has enough information before proceeding, pausing to ask questions if needed. This change affects only the underlying logic for the assistant's decision-making, not the visible interface or user experience.

0d19b1be85e87eafb2ec32c5d731ee09fb3086eb.text: The command-line interface now checks if incoming data actually changes the displayed text before updating the screen. This prevents the view from flickering or redrawing unnecessarily when new information arrives but looks identical to what is already shown. You might notice a smoother, more stable display while the assistant is working.

c295ccc5cf329b479bb39230b11b3a10e9dfdf80.text: A small internal update added a strict instruction to the AI assistant telling it to stop writing out the raw results of its own tool actions, as the system already handles this automatically. The change also reorganized the order of some internal setup steps without affecting how the assistant operates. No one will notice any difference in the assistant's behavior or output.

03bd11c7d7d276931f10e49513dff20319e0e137.text: The command-line tool now shows a 'thinking...' animation while waiting for an answer. Previously, it only showed this if the wait lasted more than one second. This means you will see the animation immediately after sending a request, giving clearer feedback that the tool is working.

f941269ace1a9ecac6f0de8a96938ca50068ae2b.text: The planning step in the command-line assistant now wraps its outline in special tags so the interface can spot it reliably. The buttons to start building that plan moved from the bottom of the screen to sit right under the assistant's message. This affects anyone using the assistant's planning mode in the terminal.

b3dc3e37428c442b82fdc9aa8e1304ed8d259fc9.text: A spelling error in the instructions for an internal coding assistant has been corrected. This change applies only to internal users of the tool. No visible difference will be noticed, as the correction only ensures the assistant follows its guidance to search for files more effectively.

077b984e2c24e294057024b154b7e72f74ee5027.text: The internal assistant named 'base2' now uses the standard processing mode instead of the fast one. This change is live but affects only that specific assistant, so regular users will not notice any difference in their experience.

657f72bd15ce1bc648fffc72988c939288f14a71.text: The text you type into the command-line interface now appears in italics next to a thin colored line. This small visual update helps you distinguish your own messages from the assistant's responses. The change is live immediately.

fce7b21c829808cae74ece664cd88565d64521f9.text: The command-line tool now cleans up the assistant's visible reasoning steps. It removes hidden planning notes from the text and standardizes how the preview is displayed. This makes the output look tidier and prevents internal instructions from appearing as plain text.

66451f5c10be4bf5ef4445575053e7f4be81cc89.text: The command-line tool's standard setting was renamed from 'FAST' to 'DEFAULT'. This change is live today. If you use the tool, you will see the new label on the mode buttons and in the text you type to switch modes.

5777780057dc74a595b0d9d7634c7dfb4504a184.text: The list of files shown when the assistant reads them is now simpler. Instead of a complicated layout that split the file names across multiple lines, all names appear in one single row separated by commas. This change is live and affects how the text looks on your screen, making it cleaner and easier to read.

c4ae9046d992101cf08c8780ffd3cd49d1e9abeb.text: An internal tool that picks the best result from several AI drafts now ignores the model's explanatory text and only applies the actual code changes. This prevents accidental errors if the AI's commentary was mistaken for instructions. The change is live for the internal automation system.

ce635357394cb1f60be837d9ad79c5bc49669d42.text: The assistant now skips creating a step-by-step task list when asked to do simple, single-step requests. This change reduces unnecessary planning overhead for basic questions or minor edits. Users will notice the assistant responds more directly to simple tasks without generating an empty or redundant checklist.

f28057f901036082dd2ff8f8177006cbc5760abc.text: The timer now displays the correct elapsed time immediately upon loading, rather than starting at zero and adjusting a moment later. This change affects anyone viewing the interface during initial load, ensuring the time shown matches the actual duration from the very first second. The update is live today.

b16e005e1b3bd77421ba974aafeb73bb8893ed06.text: A small update improves how you browse command suggestions in the text tool. Previously, arrow keys might jump back to the top or bottom unexpectedly. Now, pressing up or down stops at the first or last option, keeping navigation predictable.

d6111d5d918a09727fdc1734bf302be69d88d531.text: The internal assistant now uses a different, faster model for its 'fast' mode. This change only affects the assistant's behavior when set to 'fast'. You would notice it works slightly differently under the hood, but there is no visible change to the interface.

146adf8a068a1ce7195e80c2e4bfb3c0c3ca2a3c.text: The program now remembers the layout settings for text messages instead of rebuilding them every time the screen refreshes. This small internal fix helps the application run slightly smoother and use less power. Regular people will likely see no visual difference.

f0321ee36eea5dab0eec2c4bc99b5408c0f2a278.text: The assistant now strictly analyzes command results instead of trying to run new commands itself. This internal update prevents it from taking extra actions when reviewing output. Regular users will not notice any immediate changes.

c913ed8c68b019f84669210ee5cf73f7203db1c9.text: The text input area now updates the typing cursor and the text content at the same time, preventing the cursor from jumping outside the visible text when navigating with arrow keys. This change affects anyone typing in the command-line interface and ensures the cursor stays in the correct position during editing.

5b0687dec0c2a62f9337e1c47c5b03f0f1e6093f.text: The instructions guiding the coding assistant were simplified to remove outdated rules and add details about the tool's features. This internal change helps the assistant understand its current capabilities and respond more accurately to user requests. Users will not notice any immediate visual changes, but the assistant may follow instructions more consistently.

1516b58d45de70d316a6ab19e4a0870a6a658d15.text: Typing commands in the text terminal now lets you move the blinking cursor up and down lines within a long message using arrow keys. Previously, arrows always jumped between past commands. This only works when the cursor is not at the very start or end of the text box.

8ee35b48155c024476c8963b4dadd383875c02c4.text: The command-line interface no longer passes a helper package to menu key handlers. This change affects only the internal wiring of the text input box. Users will notice no difference in how the interface looks or behaves.

41b07800279d9b3cd7e6d95caceb91e633167bdf.text: The program now checks text length before placing the cursor. This prevents the blinking line from jumping outside the typed words if the text changes. The fix is active today. It is a small internal adjustment; you might only notice it if the cursor previously appeared in the wrong spot.

0007756071883bcf3c29a5b1688553d3341adea9.text: The code that decides how the chat history is drawn was simplified by removing an unnecessary memory-saving step for the collapse button. This change is internal and does not alter any visible behavior, so users will notice no difference in how the interface looks or responds.

a052fba50746d6bf94672c616798d2bece86b6e4.text: This is a small internal cleanup for the text-based interface. It makes the code that handles clicking to open or close chat messages more efficient. Users will not see any difference, as the feature works exactly the same way.

11055c5b2ae76d97bb98e8cdbe228840919bdd34.text: A small internal adjustment helps the command-line tool display elapsed time more efficiently by keeping the timer data stable. This prevents unnecessary screen updates while the tool is running. You might notice slightly smoother performance when viewing active timers, but the visible functionality remains the same.

400db03e92a8848649af577a846aaf7c148f3134.text: The text-based assistant now removes unnecessary blank lines at the bottom of grouped action results. Regular users will notice a slightly more compact display when these groups end a message.

8eb9652270172c6fbf8d37f3c4026d7d619e4a39.text: The program now remembers which parts of the conversation are open or closed more efficiently. This change happens behind the scenes and is live today. You will not notice any visual difference or new features, but the application may run slightly smoother when clicking to expand or collapse messages.

036b4859567e2ca468d8644d2cbaf8d1fa7d71b6.text: The program now strictly checks key presses against a defined list of valid keys, replacing a previous system that accepted any input. This internal cleanup affects the command-line interface's keyboard handling logic. Users will notice no change in behavior, as this update only improves the underlying code structure.

679d23dc5fcdad5543477f223b21280d6ca45ebb.text: The text tool now forces dark colors when running in the Ghostty terminal. This fixes unreadable text in that specific program. You will see clearer output immediately if you use Ghostty.

0c1b219571909c4932fd6328deec7b88ee754405.text: The program now checks for a preferred color theme in a clearer order: first any setting you changed directly in the terminal, then your editor, then the system, and finally a default. This internal cleanup makes the code easier to maintain but does not change which theme you see. It is live today, so you will notice no difference in how the app looks.

76f9687c51cbf21fb6654f1e21c52c9dfd3d2129.text: When you use the arrow keys to recall previous commands, the suggestion menu now stays hidden so it does not block your view. This small internal change fixes a conflict between two input features. You will notice that pressing up or down reliably shows your history instead of triggering unwanted autocomplete popups.

d67e0b6ead13e3ef7fe0832f83b64d18f7a680c8.text: This is a small internal update to the test setup for the command-line tool. The team added a missing piece of information to a simulated component, ensuring the test environment matches the real software. No visible changes or new features are available to users today.

3b28978c436e50c74fd077f81f9d174468906777.text: The program now uses a safer method to check for specific data fields before reading them, preventing potential crashes. This small internal fix ensures the command-line tool remains stable when processing messages, though users will not see any visible changes in how it looks or behaves.

bc5157ced863b21ffa37b02fcad1e48c8342f034.text: The command-line interface now shows the text you type in bold, with results appearing directly below it. If the results are long, the interface hides most of them and adds a clickable link to expand the view. This makes it easier to read what happened without scrolling through excessive text.

18d6ffd7d8e9762ec350f7ab9a560124ed8db487.text: Small cleanup for people using the command-line chat. When you send a new message, old sections showing background work now close automatically to reduce clutter. If you manually opened a section, it stays open.

a0085a3c128147a52a879fc1ecf718a7282a6134.text: The system now records extra details when a user stops a response early, helping internal teams understand why streams end. This change is live but invisible to customers; only support staff will notice richer logs when investigating cancellations.

aeed81aef003d1668fe467fc4ae47f5745292c01.text: The program now keeps its exit warning and other status messages in one place instead of mixing them together. This cleanup affects only the internal structure of the text tool, not how it works. You will notice no changes in how the program looks or behaves.

a43a7a69148fc5b39586299cab0dc1e8b5ff137d.text: The command-line tool now checks if the AI assistant sends back an empty response before trying to read it. Previously, this caused the tool to crash. Now, it stays open and logs a simple message saying there was no output. This is a small internal fix and is live today.

4e832e9df2f2ed8bfd9f0b1e071fe656f9de575f.text: Pressing the stop key now cleanly halts the assistant's response, marking the text as interrupted instead of leaving it in a broken state. This change primarily affects developers building applications that connect to the service, ensuring their programs receive a stable status update rather than an error when a user stops a request.

8475a8bccf2f7d0b319d0d4405eb0433ac848c40.text: The command-line tool's internal safety checks were tightened to prevent unexpected errors when processing text and tool actions. This change is purely for the software's stability and does not add new features or change how the tool looks or behaves for you.

31b8421b918c662073ba0cfd8a090465c6944856.text: The assistant now correctly handles multiple task lists in a single response. Previously, it might stop working early if it tried to update several lists at once. This small internal fix ensures the assistant only finishes its turn when every task is marked complete.

8c25c4e0597948c76d8db36b53f4d4e17f225767.text: The app now correctly copies the light or dark look from VS Code and Zed when those editors are set to change automatically with the time of day. This fixes a bug where the app would stay dark at noon or light at midnight. It affects people who use these editors and have auto-switching turned on.

7dc922dcf77abcdc873fd44378bab6bfb8345690.text: The build mode selection screen now arranges its buttons side-by-side instead of stacked vertically. The prompt text disappears automatically if the terminal window is too narrow to fit everything. Button colors now match the overall application theme rather than using fixed white text.

52ed28ba9766edc71d2f027357185ccc3cd2b399.text: The internal tool that lists files now has a stricter instruction to include every folder name in the path, specifically noting the common mistake of omitting the 'src' folder. This affects only the automated assistant's internal file-finding process. A person would notice more accurate file paths in the assistant's internal logs, but no visible change to the final answer.

ffe4ccbdfd72127b58e5aed20dc32d2fcb2be84e.text: Pressing the up or down arrow keys to look through previously typed commands now moves the text cursor to the end of the line. This fixes a glitch where the cursor could land in the middle of the text. The change applies to the command-line interface.

72c6c8f8de5e5e816d91ded74abe1b3c77617555.text: A small internal change tightened the instructions for the tool that finds and lists relevant files. It now says to output only the file locations, one after another, with no opening remarks or explanations. People using the internal file finder may see shorter, cleaner results; nothing outside that tool changes.

5a4ed18334dbf0456bbb5e6428e56667206f3751.text: Pressing Ctrl-C now cleanly stops the assistant mid-response. The chat window updates immediately to show '[response interrupted]' instead of freezing or leaving the message incomplete. This change is live for command-line interface users.

98903bec6fbb617384e7dfc9e0c1eb9ac5255df0.text: A small internal update ensures that when an assistant uses a tool, that action is hidden from the chat history if it was marked as private. This change is active now and affects how tool usage is displayed in the interface.

d3730a17be04a5374b39d72e9a80ae519ee3a23a.text: Pressing Escape now cleanly stops the assistant from typing, instead of causing the program to crash or hang. The text will end with a clear note saying the response was interrupted. This applies to the command-line tool today.

2bce10880445870d060d38cb8ecf697097480b68.text: A small internal update stops the assistant from showing its raw search and file-opening steps in its final answer. This affects the tools that edit code and explore files, making their output cleaner and easier to read.

4aef18cc3fa49ed4c38db78add715137ce20f537.text: The command-line tool stops printing detailed internal status messages while you sign in or use chat. These messages were meant for developers to debug the program. Normal users will see a cleaner, quieter terminal window with no change in how the tool works.

7a92255c84bb12116cedcce01d791551450178c5.text: The blinking marker in the command-line text box now sits flush against the letter it is about to replace. This small visual adjustment ensures the marker appears correctly even when typing at the very beginning of a line. The change is live for anyone using the command-line tool to enter multi-line text.

21fe632860e31ca5497fe0ea131e1162e260ae9a.text: The command-line interface now colors short snippets of code differently to make them stand out. Instead of using the standard text color, these snippets appear in bright green or orange, depending on your theme. This small visual update helps you quickly spot technical details in the assistant's replies.

290eaa6a4eaba7f6caf35094ddebe04932a7a6a9.text: The chat window now needs two quick presses of the same stop key to close. If you have typed something, the first press clears it; if the box is empty, the first press shows a warning that disappears after two seconds. A second press within that time actually ends the session. This small update is live today.

761b299c12816ce2a9b58686ccac78b167e3b347.text: A small update lets you split a long message into multiple lines by typing a backslash before pressing Enter. This change is active now and applies to people using the command-line tool. Instead of sending the message, the tool will delete the backslash and move your text to a new line.

bcca78c3594ba2ca964e7ec992f928d9e97e7295.text: The command-line assistant can hide a tool use from the conversation when that tool use is marked not to be shown. People using the command-line assistant would see a shorter transcript when such a hidden tool use happens. The rule is live in the assistant's display, but it only matters for tool uses that request hiding.

8a0e27f107fb54c23a1ed815ee1cc1d3112b2a61.text: The text shown in the command line chat input box changed to guide you on how to start. Instead of a generic prompt, it now tells you to type your coding task or use a slash to see available commands. This helps new users understand how to interact with the tool without guessing.

a711a7583540b23033f83b5523764dd2c0ea41fb.text: The program now shows text edits even when the change details are missing. It also sends error reports to a central log instead of the screen. This keeps the display clean and helps track problems behind the scenes.

d96c8279b4cb496a7023016d4921ef1679aa3aa6.text: When using the command-line tool, you will now see the AI's thinking process displayed in gray text before the final answer appears. This change is live and affects anyone using the tool's print mode, making it easier to follow how the response is being generated.

9a55c28f22dfb904ba25abe6c007982f3e6dea5d.text: A small internal fix corrects how the search tool reads certain commands. Previously, identical words in a command were removed, which accidentally broke the connection between a filter and its pattern (like 'find files ending in.ts'). Now, the tool keeps all parts of the command intact, so these specific searches work correctly.

919d8e7a2332edd48fb0d3cbf90e69f3ba808bb5.text: The command-line tool no longer writes a specific debug message to its internal log when sending messages. This is a small cleanup that reduces noise for developers monitoring logs. Regular users will not notice any difference in the tool's behavior.

2f9ad386ab476a4e9b7bc43a37d47d5e8be99e5a.text: The command-line tool no longer draws tree-like connector lines to show which messages or actions belong together. This is an internal cleanup, so you might notice the text looks slightly less cluttered, but the tool's actual capabilities remain unchanged.

37c9c1dac1d2f4124aeb8b199a2f86d355650aee.text: The terminal program no longer quits instantly when you press the interrupt key combination. Instead, it stays open to let the program finish its cleanup tasks properly. This change is live and applies to anyone using the command-line interface.

784785824d15d26fae0f40c43b0a06bcab44e51e.text: The text command tool cleaned up how it tracks the exit warning message. This internal tidy-up affects only the status line shown at the bottom of the screen. You will see the same 'Press Ctrl+C again to exit' notice, but the program now uses less memory to display it.

585c22ba39a874ac9a437274cc8875f2e1da5898.text: Agents now show their full details by default instead of hiding them until clicked. This change affects only the command-line interface, where users will immediately see expanded information for each agent without needing to manually open them.

df345ddbcb03cc1b7e10855913e205d76dc4291a.text: The command-line interface now displays agent prompts in italics without separate 'Prompt' and 'Response' labels. This visual simplification makes the conversation history cleaner and easier to read for users working directly in the terminal.

b333641ff8b0d0fd63202d8ac7f10a6fe2ff72b8.text: A small adjustment was made to how fast text scrolls in the chat window when using the Zed editor. This change lowers the scrolling speed, making it easier to read long messages without the text moving too quickly. Users of Zed will notice smoother, more controlled scrolling during conversations.

847f968f43424f8b480acb2864cb1fe87a89d7b0.text: The chat interface now hides the agent's name unless you have specifically selected one. This change only affects the visual display in the command-line tool and is live today. You will notice the name disappear from the status line if no agent is active.

014d91c6c14489fa1861747ac8679e353693fd72.text: The label for the file-listing tool changed from 'Read subtree' to 'List deeply'. The display also simplified to show one line instead of a long list. This helps the command-line interface match standard naming rules. Users will see the new label and a cleaner layout immediately.

9d1236be79902dc836b6797e2feaad2589a5b5d7.text: The text interface now uses exact character measurements to align labels with toggle icons, preventing misalignment caused by different character widths. Additionally, agent lists display in a compact mode that removes extra blank lines and reduces vertical spacing. This change is live and makes the tool's output look neater and more organized.

ab11cea0583ddddae98eaa8372fb81275098170d.text: The text input box now consistently applies the correct color style. Previously, the dimmed appearance for placeholder text or specific color settings could sometimes be missing. This small visual fix ensures the text looks right every time you type in the command line interface.

ba8c00dcdcf6d6d2c97e557a16a33b2ccc1566b9.text: The program now displays its small graphic logo on much narrower screens than before. Users who resize their terminal windows to be very thin will see the compact picture instead of just the plain text name.

d0266ee4a01b4e765a74390bf49da765c45f4561.text: The 'Build Fast' and 'Build Max' options in the command-line tool now appear as outlined boxes instead of solid colored blocks. A new prompt, 'Ready to build? Choose your mode:', sits above them. When you move your mouse over an option, its border brightens to white to show it is selected.

57ae36c28b8174a97dde7812300b081ce25de107.text: The tool now shows its menu options instantly when you move your mouse over them. Previously, it waited a short moment before appearing. This makes the interface feel snappier and more responsive.

0b0ad014895f0204c5612bfe89f6a32f66a35a77.text: Typing an exclamation mark before text in the chat now runs that text as a computer command, showing the result in a block below your message. This feature is active immediately for people using the command-line tool.

854079d054d022a272f3ba55974b5acb6b68693f.text: A small internal fix ensures the code search tool correctly handles queries that start with a dash. Previously, such queries might have been misinterpreted as settings rather than search terms. This change makes the search tool more reliable for all users, though you likely won't notice any difference unless you specifically search for text beginning with a dash.

42c340c2c0830bdd269bbe851491652dfe2b7f4f.text: A small internal fix improves the menu that lets you switch how the assistant behaves. The menu now appears instantly when you point at it and disappears quickly when you move away, instead of waiting a noticeable delay. The list of options also stays in a fixed order, so the highlighted choice no longer jumps around.

b423bc61c6f96453c2b60fe4dbd58c8aa80a621d.text: The command-line tool now uses shorter labels for its search and directory-listing actions. It also displays the current working folder in search results and removes extra technical details. Text layout has been adjusted so long lines wrap neatly at word boundaries instead of breaking mid-word.

bcf1184e6c4e3f108f3cd7bf7eefc0d78529532b.text: When you move your mouse over the mode selector in the command line, the option you are hovering over now appears in bold. The borders around the selected option also adjust dynamically to fit the highlighted text. This small visual improvement helps you see exactly which mode is active or about to be selected.

fa06a9fe2aa8d9b4b1b09c3ad88fc78b4014c9f7.text: The command-line tool now displays the assistant's internal thought process in grey text, separate from the final answer. This change affects users of the command-line interface. They will see the AI's reasoning steps appear in a different color as the response streams, making it easier to distinguish between the AI's planning and its actual output.

d658e6d3bffce72c9bd7e0eeab34d79c5a47e1a4.text: The command-line tool's mode switcher now highlights the selected option when you hover over it with your mouse. Previously, the active choice remained visually static, but this update ensures consistent feedback for all options. This small change affects only the visual appearance of the switcher during mouse interaction.

c1de47f91a7067abee48fcce88f29609eaca0134.text: The mode button in the command-line assistant now opens a small menu when clicked, letting you pick FAST, MAX, or PLAN directly instead of just cycling through them. The menu also uses plain text names instead of emojis. This is a minor interface tweak affecting only the command-line tool.

1f8db2ba7a32e708a3317a2d3202d01f36fc41d0.text: Scrolling in the command-line chat interface is now smoother and less sensitive. The system looks at a longer window of time to calculate speed, and the multiplier for the Ghostty terminal was lowered. This affects people using that specific terminal, who will notice the chat history moves more gently when they scroll.

37b97349f8e1d6ea82e87911f14ba25951062d79.text: The menu for switching agent modes now expands when you hover your mouse over it, rather than requiring a click. The layout of the options inside the expanded menu has been updated to display as vertical columns with individual borders, improving visual separation. This change affects the command-line interface and is live.

73fc133bba3cef3489ed499c986ab24b3fe12965.text: Scrolling speed in the chat window was adjusted for specific terminal apps. Users of these tools will notice the list moves faster when scrolling through long conversations. This small tweak is live immediately.

5a8be1a7a1fb4bd5d2509d6fb2a1515b68ff76f3.text: Scrolling in the text-based chat window now moves at a normal speed instead of half speed. This affects people using the chat tool inside specific code editors or standard terminals. When you scroll, the text will move twice as far with each mouse wheel turn compared to before.

e38e3d37e471814f6b4b728099e8d54eb6020aeb.text: A small interface update added a right-aligned status line to the chat screen showing the active assistant mode. It also introduced a brief delay before the mode selection menu opens when hovering, preventing accidental clicks. These changes affect only the command-line interface and are live immediately.

3b2e13ab66a1aab36a742c2528e285910733bd65.text: This update fixes a small glitch in the command-line tool's mode switcher. Clicking the current mode now collapses or expands the menu instantly, rather than waiting for a timer to finish. This makes the interface feel snappier and prevents the menu from briefly showing the wrong state.

7f8f33102e5c03dd36904f7a965535ec8aa259f3.text: A small internal update lets power users adjust how fast text scrolls in the chat window using a special setting. Most people will see no change, as scrolling speed stays the same by default. If you know how to change this setting, you can now make scrolling faster or slower to match your preference.

e954f5f99053c912d7107fd3087e1aa59802c66d.text: The chat window's scrolling speed now always moves at least one line at a time. This prevents the view from getting stuck when scrolling through short messages.

63d75420cad298d212820c1778bf7d4f09fb3aef.text: A small internal fix improves the smoothness of scrolling through long chat logs in the command-line tool. Previously, the speed-up for scrolling was calculated in whole steps, which could cause jerky movement on Mac computers. Now, the tool keeps track of tiny partial steps and adds them up, so the scroll speed changes more gradually and feels natural.

410437bfc210dfe73d11e2901f0cb579e08d1cd8.text: The command-line chat screen now shows less clutter, removing the personalized welcome message and the default agent label. It also displays the full list of active helpers instead of hiding extra items behind a count. This affects anyone using the text-based chat tool, making the initial view cleaner and more complete.

fd73f201245a782db35f3ab05c8ebe5609c25250.text: The command-line chat tool now scrolls differently when you move through messages. It dropped the complex momentum effect that kept scrolling after you stopped moving your mouse, and now only speeds up based on how fast you scroll. This change is active today and affects how quickly the text moves up or down on your screen.

da616d314ee02942d2098ea3582752f64ec84768.text: Chat scrolling now moves at a steady speed instead of speeding up. This change affects everyone using the text-based chat interface. You will notice the scroll feels more predictable and uniform, rather than getting faster the longer you hold the wheel.

43413249f51bf453864381565ef61394e0ddd014.text: Mac users now scroll through chat history at a steady speed instead of a speeding-up one. This stops the screen from flying past the text when you scroll quickly. People using other computers keep the old behavior.

e0d97b8d015a33156113d8d766e1b36eccc6ed6c.text: The command-line chat interface no longer jumps to a specific message when you open or close a section. This small internal cleanup means the screen stays put during these actions, rather than automatically scrolling to keep the selected item near the top.

a4b59dacf055dcc4e1554c15fcd7317b2c77a158.text: The text interface now removes extra vertical lines from the left side of conversation blocks. Only the deepest line marker remains, while older ancestor lines turn into blank space. This small visual cleanup reduces clutter for anyone reading the command-line chat today.

660ec145ac1fecde82d2efdffca1cc83d5ddc0a3.text: The command-line tool now hides the decorative tree lines next to its messages unless you are running a nested task. This small update is live and makes the main text easier to read by removing clutter.

361d2e45cb0845681a4c5b23818f9efce596776a.text: The AI assistant received new internal guidelines to keep its generated code cleaner and simpler. These rules tell it to avoid unnecessary error handling, require all necessary information, and place new features in separate files. This change only affects how the AI plans its work and is not visible to regular users.

8555bf43ac590b20a7657db241d57c280d7282c3.text: The internal instructions for starting a code analysis session were updated to match current standards. This change only affects automated testing scripts and does not alter how the software analyzes code or behaves for end users. No visible changes will occur in the application.

2c43eb9edaf19ff68971df7f3b80673c8324fe93.text: The tool stopped printing a long list of internal setup details when you first open it. This change affects anyone using the command line assistant. You will notice the welcome screen is shorter and cleaner, with no extra technical text cluttering the view.

985a7edea88be2e4a57f41e92eac85ad99521de2.text: The chat interface no longer forces a solid black or white background. Instead, it lets your computer's terminal colors show through. This means the chat window will match the color scheme you already have set up for your screen.

a9395df8485ddc52cd980a9cc46a59dc00d4d62d.text: The text tool no longer checks for Cursor editor to adjust scrolling speed. It now scrolls slower in VS Code and unknown editors. Users of Cursor will notice the tool treats it like a standard editor instead of using its special speed setting.

1533a0da7dddf47d8e389e96789a9bd9985e61d0.text: The tool's file-reading engine switched to a newer, more reliable method for finding project files. This internal cleanup ensures the assistant sees your files correctly without extra processing steps. You will not notice any change in how you interact with the tool.

c458a7c7926924785efd4b35f1b1fa236a3a50d8.text: The command-line tool now shows a cleaner start-up screen by hiding the list of internal settings it used to print. It also shortens the preview of assistant actions, displaying only three items instead of five. These updates apply immediately to anyone using the text-based interface.

152ffd521401cd8b08227eeede5f7066e02d473c.text: The blank space on the left and right sides of the suggestion menu is gone. This change is live now. People using the command line interface will see the menu items sit flush against the edges instead of having a gap.

ce38853421e74583e915c5d7480275ae42e14a16.text: Scrolling speed in the command-line chat has been adjusted for specific applications like Ghostty and VS Code, making it feel smoother and more consistent. If you use these apps, you will notice the text moves at a different, likely faster, pace than before. This change is active now.

07652b39164bd06034983f1e13aedb2c0fb8158d.text: A small cleanup for the command-line tool stopped it from printing extra status messages about checking your login and receiving answers. People using this tool will see a calmer screen with less text scrolling by. Nothing else about how the tool works changed.

aa0d702629ed970d991c64f26e5ba4f349f0daf4.text: Developers working on the code no longer need to set up a real database or fill in every configuration detail just to run basic checks on their own computers. The system now uses safe placeholder values for these tests, while official quality checks still require the strict, real setup.

050f460a48cc6be8db4f5bf6c216bb87088f05cd.text: The command-line tool now shows up to ten suggestions at once instead of five. People using the text interface will see a longer list of options appear without needing to scroll. This is a small visual change and is active today.

0ff14424b901b040bcd950d94c865ce474f005b1.text: A small internal cleanup fixes how the chat tool reports when a menu selection fails. It affects only the command-line chat interface. Users will notice no change in how the tool works.

daaed4019d7b44c9ccef3c878fcb24203f2ff190.text: This internal change removes special shortcuts that allowed the software to run tests without a real database or complete configuration. It affects only the development team's local testing setup, not the live product. Developers will now need to provide real database connections and settings to run tests locally.

5b6b84a99d1b5084203b67e29ae5f658ea5fa2b9.text: The system stopped offering duplicate shortcuts for color settings. Developers now use the single correct location for these settings. Regular users will notice no change.

1746ec3f4fd7645e9dc9338344e58088a65be373.text: The code that draws the dropdown list of suggestions now demands that the caller explicitly state how many items to show, instead of assuming ten. This change only affects the internal structure of the command line tool and does not alter how the menu looks or behaves for you today.

0972d5c1c05e859711d56441de8aa26fd46093dd.text: The coding assistant now checks its work more efficiently by verifying only the specific section it just changed before running broader tests. This internal update helps the tool finish tasks faster and with fewer errors. Users will notice quicker responses when asking the assistant to modify code, though the underlying behavior remains invisible.

04a3759345130a71386a0a27a969f1b07c296808.text: The assistant's internal checklist instructions now emphasize including every applicable task to prevent forgetting items. This small adjustment applies to the task tracking feature. Users might notice the assistant creates more complete lists when planning work.

c6f9d529f6b3abdf86a7c189f803e52b35cab6f6.text: A setting that made one AI assistant think more carefully before answering was turned off. This assistant is used by internal tools to write code plans. It will now think at a standard level, which may make it faster but slightly less thorough.

bd99ce76aa5be86d9e992b23f05f20a0ec1be865.text: The command-line assistant's mode button now cycles through three states: fast, maximum effort, and a new planning mode. When you switch to planning mode, the button turns blue. The assistant will then use a dedicated planning model to outline steps before acting, rather than jumping straight to execution.

ad42fd4105812cf4e320fef6bb37b4403ef598c0.text: The command menu now shows only the exact commands you type, instead of listing every available option. This fix applies to the text-based interface and ensures that when you start typing a specific command, the list filters correctly to match your input. The change is live and improves the accuracy of command suggestions.

c2456e094f56f947238b987e1fd7f0ea17bfbecf.text: A small cleanup fixed the text-based assistant so it no longer shows a sub-agent's instructions twice. People using the command line will notice a less cluttered view when they expand these items. This change is live today.

b648bb7d911ad0715d29c0121fc18dabae8b87c1.text: The chat interface now silently ignores selection commands when no options are available, rather than falsely reporting a successful action. This internal cleanup prevents potential errors in the autocomplete menu. You will not notice any change in how the application behaves.

85bc484bfaf0397fb201e699843a73f3a69f3bf1.text: The system's file search tool now looks directly inside specific folders instead of guessing from a static list. This change applies to internal automated assistants that help find code. If you ask these assistants to find files, they will now search within the exact folders you mention, making the results more accurate and relevant to your request.

ea0e5672c9860afeed32876de87b953e2001b827.text: Automated checks for two internal services failed because they lacked a required logging component. Developers updated the test setups to include this component, resolving the errors. This is an internal maintenance fix; customers and users will see no changes to the application.

61e026159f3a419979f25c86141176258af58b62.text: Programmers cleaned up how the text tool decides what to do when you type a command starting with a slash. The tool now treats this step as routing a prompt rather than just handling slash commands. You won't notice any difference; the tool works exactly as it did before.

c1df8c7639422ed1d9f4d46c2fef006e64fa87cd.text: The command menu now shows clearer hints, like 'exit (quit)' and 'new (reset, clear)', so you know exactly what each option does. Starting a fresh chat is now called 'new', though typing 'reset' or 'clear' still works. This small update affects anyone using the text-based tool, making the options easier to read.

2e6dfaa8a0f25649a775944b1373195da0eddac5.text: A temporary feature that showed internal system details in the command-line chat window has been removed. This change affects users who run the tool locally. They will no longer see a list of hidden configuration settings and web addresses in their chat interface.

d9b729f958badf789386989b4495d686c788f56c.text: The command-line tool now saves your typed command to its history only after the setup process has fully finished. Previously, it saved the command too early, which could sometimes record an incomplete state. This small fix ensures your history accurately reflects what happened during setup.

26a225aedcdd25aa90b5a618a806255e3590e154.text: The command-line chat tool now accepts /clear and /new commands to instantly wipe the current conversation history. This change is active and resets the assistant's memory, allowing you to start a fresh topic without closing the window.

f124c425840c5d9ee9fddbc991e1f376de3c5b37.text: The command-line tool no longer prints a list of system settings when it starts up. This small cleanup affects people using the tool, who will see a shorter welcome message without those extra lines. The change is live.

d56e2c7ac34337e890d0fab14412986da94a4d03.text: A small change makes Tab behave better in the pop-up lists for commands and mentions. Instead of stopping at the end, Tab now moves through the list in a circle, and if only one option matches, Tab picks it. People typing in the chat window may notice fewer stuck key presses.

a57412a744db974df14dcc728e5ae5029a134187.text: A small internal cleanup was made to the software's testing tools. This change has no effect on the application's behavior or what you see while using it. It only helps developers keep their code organized and consistent.

c863b32d9653e8b268cf70477a0e3a358754a8ea.text: We simplified how the system organizes its internal files for checking your account profile. This is a small, behind-the-scenes cleanup that makes the code easier to maintain. You will not see any changes on your screen or notice any difference in how the app works.

7ee10af5c6292c69fe6c2cfc04e5b84cc88e6ec9.text: The system's internal filing method for handling assistant tasks was tidied up. This change affects only the developers maintaining the software. Users will notice no difference in how the application works today.

66b00b05a298ea8200bb3947b3bdf3ccf84b7fc5.text: The system's internal filing method for handling chat messages was updated to match new organizational standards. This change affects only the internal structure and is live today. Users will not notice any difference in performance or features, as the underlying logic remains unchanged.

696e0cb5474c37670a8d2edf5ea5004bccc8091f.text: The AI assistant now runs its step-by-step instructions directly instead of inside a separate, isolated environment. This internal change removes a layer of security isolation for these specific automated tasks. Regular users will notice no difference in how the assistant behaves or what it can do.

4adf0209934e11b8234ccc8cb9cb4ac1397f18c3.text: The system now automatically adds user details like email and Discord ID to activity logs when you use the chat or agent features. This change is live for all users but only affects internal records, not the interface. You will not see any visible difference, but support teams can now trace issues back to specific accounts more easily.

f60cea017f27be06cbfd4e12288c61d6eb024c68.text: The command-line tool now saves conversation history in your personal settings folder instead of the project folder. This change applies to the tool's internal record-keeping. You will not see any difference in how you use the tool, but the saved logs will no longer clutter your project files.

23fce4bc71e65f985c2514766b091e8e03c550b3.text: Programmers moved a small piece of internal code to a new folder to follow standard rules. This change affects only the development team's workflow and organization. Nothing about the product's features or appearance changes for anyone else.

76062241808bf656bbaf44fc48c6fa103d914704.text: When a chat request fails, the system now saves the full text of that request alongside the error message. This change affects internal support staff, not regular users. Staff would notice the added detail when reviewing error reports, helping them see exactly what was sent to the AI provider before the failure occurred.

92c43c83a71391b1a7c012c86e6f6ad283e9402e.text: A new diagnostic command now shows the raw environment variables and computed constants used by the software's internal connection settings. This change is live and affects only people running the command-line tool's environment check. Long values are cut off after 50 characters to keep the output readable.

df7b59628120cabc3ce07e2c2cc62edf5a9486e8.text: The software toolkit now includes a specific blueprint for how the system handles files. This update is internal plumbing for developers building on top of the platform. End users will see no change in behavior or appearance.

66b8f3867533c5bc8a22bd30467770f3eda591b5.text: The team updated the internal instructions for a specific automated assistant to use a standard formatting style. This is a small housekeeping task that does not change how the assistant behaves or what it can do. No one will notice any difference in the service's performance or features.

d480caa1a16550765e58ff21ba3c3d1435e661dd.text: The command-line tool now shows a fixed list of settings instead of guessing from the environment. If a setting's value is longer than 50 characters, it gets cut short with dots. This affects people running the packaged tool, who will see a consistent, readable list of configuration values.

7d7fc6a97ae7101f97f63b9f28d29dd8dd4ed39d.text: The system corrected internal address labels for a specific task assistant after it moved to a new folder. This ensures the assistant can still find the instructions it needs to run. The fix applies only to internal operations, so you will not see any changes in the interface or behavior.

a202fe8bc30d54e7fafad2a1967884bb93aeca52.text: The internal system that generates multiple code solutions now allows operators to manually adjust the number of parallel attempts. Previously, it always ran exactly five attempts. Operators can now choose between one and ten attempts based on task difficulty. This change affects only internal staff using the tooling system and does not impact end users.

3d00284e7b19c3c1cb387e09a8cde04ea2d9fa15.text: The system now automatically sets up the analytics tool when needed, rather than skipping data collection if it wasn't prepared beforehand. This ensures usage statistics are recorded consistently. You will notice more accurate tracking data appearing in your reports, though you won't see any direct changes to the app's interface.

c8b4a8ba4c17a49aa733f77a0092614bff4ed550.text: A small internal update lets the assistant's command runner accept a custom time limit. The default remains 30 seconds, with an option to disable the limit entirely. Non-programmers will notice no immediate change.

c09c49c60611b6ef0dc4d784b2579466d3e7aab7.text: A small internal update clarifies how a specific automated assistant receives instructions. Instead of requiring a direct command, it now explicitly reads context from the ongoing conversation history. This change affects only internal tooling and does not alter user-facing features or behavior.

a1d40af6491908e8b1ff620c92aa66905458a0a7.text: The search tool now shows surrounding text lines alongside each match. Previous limits only counted direct hits, so nearby context lines were ignored when deciding how many results to return. This change is live for anyone using the search feature and makes results easier to read.

1addb355b9dbeac4859d0231e2e262f61789a12e.text: The assistant's internal routing logic was simplified by removing a specific file-searching helper from its toolkit. This change affects only the background systems that decide which tools to use when answering requests. Since this is an internal cleanup, no visible behavior changes for users.

11751cbab44ca3604533167eab638b81617d245d.text: A hidden setup step now restores the project's dependency list to its original state after installation. This change affects only the internal scoring system and prevents it from being confused by minor file updates. Customers and employees will notice no visible difference.

dd918b7f8d5946114c3a55be6e86a8f6c3c24e4a.text: The nightly report email now includes a new section summarizing overall performance trends and key insights. This change affects only internal team members who receive the automated evaluation reports. They will notice this additional summary appended to the end of their existing nightly results.
