f951b57d192cd4618891c28e7d2c0f07904eb66c.text: Internal coding assistants think harder before writing or selecting code. OpenAI model triggers extra effort. Anthropic model unchanged. Assistants take longer to generate answers.

9252a5e521abec47bbfec2727c0e667d6ae13cdf.text: The code search tool now stops after 10 seconds if it gets stuck. Users will see a clear message asking them to narrow their search instead of an endless loading screen. This change is live today.

597070f05ffed5ecc2d27887115ec732146fda98.text: An internal setting now tells the system to use its most careful mode when a specific new model is active. This change applies only to a background tool used by developers, so regular users will not notice any difference in the application.

2d59705ed088acd08024eb653455fb680823c9da.text: The text tool now prints environment settings to the screen when it starts, and it stops treating underscores as italic or bold markers. This affects people using the command-line chat, who will see these settings listed and read underscored words as plain text instead of styled text.

b39871fe018ec4dfa404036a53b964474c663579.text: The instructions for the code search tool no longer suggest a setting that includes hidden files in results. This affects the automated assistant, not human users. The assistant will now stick to standard search rules, ignoring files marked as hidden, matching how the tool actually works today.

b8120de7bf3b353329dc10b9b0c73c55c1552f79.text: The internal coding assistant now signals task completion explicitly rather than relying on a general rule to end its turn. This applies only to the assistant when it uses the newer GPT-5 model. Users might notice the assistant stops responding cleanly when finished, instead of potentially cutting off or adding unnecessary text.

579475bb899ea2315699ec815101fa7833c681d6.text: A tool used by internal release managers sorted software versions incorrectly, placing valid updates in the wrong order. The fix corrects this sorting logic so version lists appear accurate. This change affects only the internal release process and does not alter what external customers see.

4d44be1e03e6ba6e18fa9d2622f2851dddaeec3b.text: The program no longer uses fixed, built-in web addresses for its support and payment features. Instead, it reads these addresses from the current settings when it starts. This change does not affect what you see on your screen today, but it means the tool will always point to the correct web addresses based on the environment it is running in.

8ca27515443e96295bf04038b91f5faa6038edb8.text: People still using the old version of the Codebuff tool will now see a bright warning message every time they start it. This message tells them to install the new version to get the updated interface. The change is live immediately for anyone launching the old tool.

f29bb5032807fceb689ad5eaba1de382382924d0.text: The tool that creates the command-line program now shares its setup details with the parts it builds. This fixes rare errors where the builder could not find the right settings. People building the software will see fewer failed builds, while everyday users will not notice any difference.

f1d505d12316e65c039183eb40ef6a3bbaa3deb8.text: The tool that creates the command-line program now automatically includes the main website address and payment settings when building the package. This ensures the program knows where to send data and how to handle payments without needing extra setup steps. If these settings were missing, the program might fail to connect or process payments correctly.

1ec25c4581e958745551d753f39b311a4b9deeef.text: The tool that packages the command-line program now automatically includes specific public settings from the computer that runs the build. This change affects the people who create the final software file, not the end users. A user would notice nothing different unless the settings were previously missing, in which case the program might now work correctly out of the box.

d16684e78b989f7a2b904db86871b0907098270b.text: The automated process that creates test builds no longer runs under a protected test-environment setting. This is a small internal change for the team that publishes test builds, and it applies to future runs. They may see the test-build process run without the extra checks and restricted access settings that the protected setting supplied; customers will not notice a change.

fe1ba1aa3451b156e5188cb166c2d326f5d867c1.text: A small internal fix helps the development tool find the correct startup program on different computer systems. This change only affects developers who run the tool locally. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the software behaves.

c32392a7eea53f25246c21294fae9f562156e3f6.text: The update process now looks for the main product name instead of the old community version. It also checks the release number more carefully, rejecting any tag that does not follow the strict three-part format. This ensures the software only updates when a valid, correctly formatted release is published. The change affects the internal release tooling and is live.

fc4650a30665ab54c11a6ad9ce30efd590e879c8.text: The automated release process for older software versions was corrected to target the proper older directory instead of the current production one. This internal fix ensures future updates for these legacy versions are packaged and labeled correctly. No immediate visible changes for end-users.

d5be8f5e25c347809b1f87dd9a698b17d3d242a9.text: The test system now reports two average scores: one including all results, and one ignoring runs that scored one point or less. This helps the internal team see typical performance without rare total failures dragging down the number. The change is active and appears in the console output when running the tests.

e7c10938d7d456785ce6e13a8f2c3eefd006030d.text: A small internal update to the AI assistant's high-capacity mode now makes it try several different ways to build new features, then pick the best result. This change affects only those using the advanced assistant mode. You would notice higher-quality code suggestions for complex tasks, while simple fixes remain unchanged.

d3cc5200b205490ee058633a5fbc7cb6529b34e7.text: The system now uses a different label to identify messages coming from automated tools. This change aligns the internal format with standard industry practices. Most users will not notice any difference, as this is an internal adjustment to how the software organizes information.

0cf5f2fd0fc87192cc81fed43cbcdffb39709c4c.text: The internal tool that picks the best code suggestion now uses a newer AI model instead of the previous one. This change affects the automated code-writing assistants used by the engineering team. You would notice slightly different choices in generated code, but the visible workflow remains the same.

5c1ed88897c505c202f355183d8015782e9df60e.text: A hidden setting was adjusted for internal testing tools, causing them to connect to the live service instead of a test environment. This affects only the automated release process, not regular users. Anyone using the tool would notice it behaving like the production version, but no visible changes appear for the general public.

029efd764896cc0c54a6c4a50ed23bffce510542.text: A security check was added to the automated process that prepares test versions of the software. This means the system now requires specific permission before it can move forward with these test builds. This change only affects the internal team responsible for creating these test versions, and it is active immediately.

738788624edf38ab3bdce8c5dc2203e320a56bd1.text: The internal AI assistants that generate and choose code solutions were updated to be smarter. The creating assistant can now pause to briefly reason about complex steps, while the judging assistant gets the original user request and clear ranking rules to pick the best result. These are small, internal adjustments to how the tools work, so there is no visible change for regular users.

78abaad0bb6919008d042580aaef127456719bf8.text: The release tool now checks version labels more strictly. It ignores plain numbers and only processes labels marked for older systems. Internal staff using the publishing tool would see fewer errors when the tool reads a list of available versions.

5f912ba00c65c58d148ba3aba5b5e3b4028cb49c.text: A small internal cleanup made the setup script for the Bun runtime work on more computers. It does not change any visible features, and most people would notice nothing.

21c3c436875d93e37ddf856697eed491f313d566.text: The link pointing to the project's home was corrected in the software's internal description. This is a small, behind-the-scenes fix that does not change how the tool works. People using the software will not notice any difference.

dc08e8bc7f2bf2ec3eae159cbaf3124487b38783.text: The tool that grades AI coding attempts now skips any test where the AI failed completely or got a zero score. This prevents a few bad results from dragging down the average performance numbers for everyone else. The change is live for the internal team running these tests, so their reports will show cleaner, more accurate scores.

ac5ea20c87f129a464330188a3f76cc24b1410b6.text: The assistant now gives each piece of text it generates a unique ID. This helps the system track and organize responses. You will not see any visible changes.

4298f2fa488fbe7807ee74a83b7b422248c41f78.text: Release builds for the CLI, app, and SDK now use a shared setting to automatically pick the right public configuration details. This internal cleanup ensures all three products receive the same correct settings during automated packaging. Users will not notice any immediate changes, as this only standardizes how the software is built behind the scenes.

c36c8d1d728233b01011508bc9cf7ebf78ec0132.text: Small internal change. Test runs for the automated helper now apply the 30-minute time limit to the whole job, including preparing the test project, collecting files, and checking results. Before, the limit only covered the helper’s main task, so setup or checks could keep running past it. Internal users running these tests would see the job stop if the full run takes too long.

bafdc9cb97656953098291f86b53c27fd1d3eaca.text: When you start a new project, the setup tool now writes a limit on how many steps the assistant can take into your settings file. This ensures the assistant stops after a set number of actions instead of running indefinitely. You will see this new line in your configuration file, though it uses a standard default value.

d1135284e8100a3af8d78cc12659d430d38e7ac5.text: The assistant can now display fixed text directly without waiting for a model response. This change is internal and currently dormant, meaning no visible difference exists until specific workflows are updated to use it.

9992d8ab098eacd4ff5a08893c8474114e2de199.text: The system now automatically selects the newest version of an assistant when no specific version is chosen, rather than attempting to fetch a non-existent 'undefined' version. This affects applications that request assistants without specifying a version number. If you use such an application, it will now successfully load the latest available assistant instead of failing to retrieve it.

0ba06cdd22a0e7e26ace49a224490461111e6c13.text: A small internal update stops a hidden instruction from being repeated to the assistants that work on your requests. This cleanup happens automatically behind the scenes. You will not see any change in how the responses look or behave.

153b1f0218ae5d1a20211b9138e36463a7619ef3.text: When the assistant edits a file and some changes work while others fail, it now lists all the problems together instead of just the last one. This helps anyone using the assistant see exactly which edits were rejected and why, preventing confusion about what actually changed.

23e04fb98ad9c2a65bc653d5ae03793690e4f9f6.text: The system now automatically runs basic quality checks after an AI agent finishes a task. This change affects internal testing and is live today. If you looked at the results, you would see that failed type or test checks are now included in the final review notes, helping reviewers spot incomplete work without needing to run the checks themselves.

c008f6b4f7e8a19d42f7412ea6d28ada39bbb990.text: The system now marks its memory break right after the assistant's last reply, rather than after a specific setup message. This helps the assistant remember earlier chats more reliably. It is live today for all conversations.

6865350a9b7493c0effa4d5ad11b47181d166189.text: A tiny, invisible cleanup inside the web app's settings file removed a leftover instruction that was never being used. Because the code already ignored this instruction, nothing changes for anyone. No visible effects.

6160c38b9fd4722a14b473fba5678ea66fb714c8.text: The code-writing assistant now reports back the exact results of its edits, instead of just a vague summary. This change applies only to the internal tool used by the engineering team to generate code suggestions. It is not active for regular users yet, but it allows the system to verify that specific changes were applied correctly before saving them.

691593459fb4286db062ea906c43f353493a125c.text: The software now strictly requires a specific web address configuration to identify its own location, removing older automatic guesses. This change only affects internal development tools and setup scripts, not the live application used by customers. Users will notice no difference in the product's behavior.

7dbbc9519321875aa6f2c6588fc0db4f9976ff10.text: The system now checks the shape and content of agent information received from the server before using it. This prevents broken or unexpected data from causing errors in the assistant's behavior. If the information is invalid, the system quietly ignores it and logs the issue instead of trying to use it. This change is active in the latest software version.

ff643ff7b53ac81b875008a7acd85da592a48bc7.text: Internal cleanup: standardized how the website reads configuration settings. Affects only the site's own machinery; visitors see no change.

5c2a415ead53f971258bcd8476ebd8fa6c3d8ae1.text: The instructions for the internal coding assistants were clarified. The agent that picks the best solution now has clearer rules for reporting its choice, and the research agent is explicitly told it cannot read or change files directly. These are minor internal adjustments to how the tools behave, affecting only the automated coding system.

dd1d8c7857ce3cade456574569c4e6d60790e9da.text: When the assistant looked back through a conversation to place the marker that says an earlier part can be reused, it moved one step too far before checking whether it had reached the start. That could put the marker on the wrong message or try to look past the beginning. The check now happens first, so the marker lands on the correct earlier message. The fix is live.

8a978517c751751f46917fd6f4ae475a8eff23c6.text: Programmers moved the list of settings that control how the app connects to different services so it sits next to the rules that check those settings are valid. This helps the system build the app correctly by seeing each setting used one by one. Users won't notice any difference today because the app behaves exactly the same.

53658287965a4d04997107b939920c1bfe8251fe.text: The system now saves memory more efficiently by marking specific steps in the assistant's thinking process, rather than guessing which parts to save. This change affects all automated agents that use this core messaging tool. Users might notice slightly faster responses or reduced costs for complex tasks, though the update itself is a small, internal fix that is live today.

769c3ffdebbae39e7e6d0ef61fd7e254c0a17477.text: The billing connection moved to a private folder, affecting only internal payment tools. This change does not alter how customers pay or see their invoices.

540c2e6597871bd07df91fb60fb94295ff2bd135.text: A small internal fix corrected how a test finds a payment tool. This helps developers run checks on automatic account top-ups without errors. Regular users will see no change today.

4cf528be260bef14e688d7483e79306398b7385b.text: We updated a background tool that helps us manage how our application stores and retrieves data. This change is internal and does not affect how the application looks or works for you. You will not notice any difference.

5e07e379bdeb1307e191b9c1c3d8bb10861c75c7.text: The assistant now stops automatically when it finishes checking off every item on its task list. Previously, it would wait for a specific command to stop, which sometimes caused it to stall after completing all tasks. This change is live today.

31a5c37a1dd9a7ef1e60647d4a871acaa328ffb0.text: The team switched back to an older version of a database management tool because the new one caused issues. This change is internal and only affects the developers who build the software. Customers will not notice any difference in how the product works.

4140cab495d5f5716cd7df085cbbe087e6fdd053.text: The assistant's gatekeeper now blocks forbidden actions even when the system is busy or preparing a report. This affects anyone using the assistant; without the fix, a blocked action might have run anyway. The gatekeeper now checks every request against the list of allowed actions.

0937bf461415f89e86cb273def271d1c377d0aa0.text: The AI assistant now stops after writing a to-do list, instead of automatically taking another action. This affects all users of the core system. You will notice the assistant pausing to wait for your input after creating a plan, rather than immediately continuing.

405fdb4e065353f9b9c431133989e40229c681f9.text: The AI assistant can now take more steps to finish a task, allowing it to handle longer or more complex requests without stopping early. This change applies to the command-line tool and internal testing systems. You will notice the assistant persists longer on difficult jobs instead of cutting off prematurely.

1d968f141d70cf736dfdcc23afb4a7ba000ea8bf.text: The assistant now saves its memory differently for the alloy2 agent. This small change helps the system remember instructions and the last reply more efficiently, making responses faster or cheaper to generate. Only users interacting with the alloy2 agent will see this difference; other agents keep their old memory settings.

5a4debae16072a00ae66540141bb062737eb1b62.text: Internal team adjusted instructions for the coding assistant. It now focuses on finding files first and explicitly requires checking work after changes. Only internal developers using the tool will notice slightly stricter guidance during task execution.

297b92585db2e31296ef6ab38c845dc8e730bf5f.text: The internal testing system can now download specific helper programs into a temporary folder before running a task. This affects only the automated checks for the Codebuff project, not regular users. If someone looked at the test logs, they would see the system fetching and using these extra tools automatically.

8259dea1273d6153a8ea68e203d5c0c103005e2a.text: Users of the command-line chat tool can now type /exit, /quit, or /q to close the program. This action immediately stops any ongoing responses and clears the screen. The change is active today and offers a simple alternative to using keyboard shortcuts.

1f9ec81e03c61a304a100f1c5710bfc9768ff2c6.text: The release process now always builds from the current main code instead of allowing manual selection of older versions. This prevents accidental publication of outdated or incomplete software updates. Developers managing releases will notice that the option to choose a specific build source is no longer available in the release tools.

631553fec3b98cb5efdca6aed761f547e7e690ce.text: The moving light effect on the login screen's border now sweeps across the entire frame instead of just the bottom edge. This visual cleanup ensures the animation looks smooth and complete while you wait for the login process to finish.

1293bd993c1f1bcb3cf734e674aa568c41fb3840.text: Pressing the stop button in the text-based chat tool now closes the program immediately, removing the previous requirement to press it twice to confirm. Text formatting in chat responses is now plain text, so bold or italic styles no longer appear. This change is live today for users of the command-line interface.

6c955c8fa7400a3e49f70e0b15e7e1bf8ee7a54d.text: A small internal change lets people who run our software release process type in extra instructions when they start a build. This helps them change how the build works without needing a developer to update the system for them. Regular users will not see any difference because this only affects the behind-the-scenes tools our team uses.

34d29421c439314478b2ccd72c43a75efca697a5.text: The automated release process now ensures a software package is fully available for download before the system records the new version number. This change affects internal operations and prevents the release log from showing a version that does not yet exist. It is active today.

3c382a9d57a598839692d3a8f936159be0d5d158.text: The automated system stopped creating special markers for new software versions and downloading related files during releases. This change affects internal release processes and is live today. Users will notice no difference, as this is a minor internal cleanup that removes obsolete steps.

3f22ec37b9abf8976a11b9654ae0e11d6219c47c.text: The software's internal tracking label was updated to mark a new minor release. This change affects only the background system that manages the code, not the features you see or use. You would notice nothing, as this is just a housekeeping update to keep the system organized.

a0e1d569a6715a17f60ff5a4cf1bdb44d590167a.text: The automated system that updates the software's version number for internal releases was switched to a different method to prevent errors. This change affects only the internal build process, so there is no visible difference to anyone using the software.

0b23c08522e35e0f34aed334a23903b166241f32.text: The system now automatically passes necessary security keys to the publishing tool during release, ensuring it can access required services without manual setup. This change affects only the internal release process and is active immediately. A non-programmer would notice no visible difference in the software's features or interface.

80b0d7f5cb9e5b1910d3d51a6986164001987eac.text: The internal file-explorer tool now bundles directory contents into one clean list instead of printing raw chat logs. This change is live for internal users. They would notice shorter, more readable output when checking files.

889a4af5e3b5d248f6935d25fd1ad97617905b6c.text: A small internal fix corrected a missing space in the step used to publish the toolkit. The fix is live today. It affects the team that releases the toolkit, and they would notice the publishing step now runs correctly instead of stopping with an error.

5eee0babc6639e744d3ce7b2318f1c5981c39ef4.text: The production release pipeline now has permission to automatically verify its identity with cloud services. This small internal update allows the automated publishing process to authenticate securely without manual intervention. Internal release engineers will see smoother, more secure deployments for the software development kit.

0469a3f7877565ce3bf6c63863137230a62b5bfc.text: The system now records the exact cost of text generation requests for a specific provider. This internal tracking update does not change visible features or pricing for customers today.

fe92bdacbc7512e47efe755e4518e1efead5d847.text: The internal AI assistant now stops talking immediately after summarizing its work and refuses to create extra example files. This prevents the assistant from repeating itself or generating unwanted documents. The change applies to the assistant's behavior during tasks and is active immediately.

ea626e3586967a305af45e0867cf189acb9fac6b.text: The team updated the internal label for their coding assistant's connection tool. This change affects only the tool itself, not the visible features or how it behaves. Users will notice no difference in the assistant's responses or capabilities.

1493d5f7031faf27fb425ec720b805f40b7c744f.text: When an internal attempt to create a new software package fails, the computer doing that work now opens a temporary remote inspection window for 15 minutes so the release team can look at what went wrong. It applies to future internal release attempts. This affects only the release process, not the finished package. A customer would notice nothing.

7d027b9978d195bb1b197639b2a9c4b1114f4d2b.text: A new shortcut was added to the internal release menu for the software development kit. This change only affects the team members who publish updates, giving them a quicker way to start the process. Customers will not notice any difference, as this is a small internal tooling improvement.

976f74186e3bc976f98a30ea5fbedb9ba26775bd.text: A small internal setting now allows the system to ignore certain checks when running in a specific test environment. This change affects only the testing setup and does not impact regular users or live features.

d13e9fa623ae51bc2ad5fc949224d31273178c71.text: The tool that creates the type definition files for the software development kit now handles this task directly instead of relying on a separate command-line utility. This internal change improves build reliability for developers using the kit. End users will not notice any difference in the application's behavior.

70ee5556c63d09f514ed3114292704b9807cd49e.text: Test configurations can now include environment variables, allowing test keys to be passed directly to the agent. The change also stops forcing colored output in terminal commands, respecting the system's default settings instead. This is a small internal update affecting how tests run; end users will see no immediate changes.

9b97d0dda7a4bf9c70c0496519cb356708a86fe7.text: A small internal fix ensures the software's release process saves version updates to the main record before building the final package. This prevents errors where the built package might miss recent changes. Developers releasing updates will see a smoother, more reliable process, though end users will not notice any difference.

25831ff0488c8a4eab14fe5fcc7183ef8edb6852.text: The system stopped an internal helper from adding fake user messages while cleaning up conversation history. This affects only the automated cleanup process and is live today. Regular users will not see any difference.

e293428d204d5b9e776b088d90bf6bb6fb81d5ea.text: Programmers building custom tools for this assistant can now set specific background settings for the commands those tools run. This lets them pass private details, like passwords or configuration options, directly to the command without changing the computer's global settings. The feature is live in the latest update for anyone using this specific toolkit.

b9c2810da0c0752b43a857ed04412ca1a522e9ed.text: A small internal update improved how the command-line tool checks login details. This change fixes a technical error that could happen when verifying user information during login. Users will not notice any difference in how the tool works, but the login process is now more stable and reliable.

c4b933cad17573856ae8fdc23210a0f639175e1e.text: The build process now includes public environment variables in the output. This affects only developers using the SDK who rely on these specific variables for configuration. They will notice that their environment settings are correctly applied when the SDK is compiled and used.

06ffa6a4e9a40385a3982d0bbca49ce24c357e90.text: The setup tool now correctly identifies which settings are safe to show on the website and which must stay hidden on the server. This change only affects internal developers running the app locally. They will notice that the application loads their specific configuration values properly instead of showing blank fields or errors during startup.

c9c35ea9f51210f82b68841890625deb72a7ff7c.text: The software now automatically hides secret passwords and database addresses from the final version it gives to you, replacing them with blanks. This change is live today and affects anyone using the main tool. You would not notice anything different, as this is an internal safety measure to ensure your private data is never accidentally shared.

a4396df88073029ec1427d8bbbdff0791b21781d.title: Free mode grandfathering constants
a4396df88073029ec1427d8bbbdff0791b21781d.summary: Added FREE_MODE_PLAN_GRANDFATHERED_COUNTRIES to common/src/constants/freebuff-countries.ts. Scopes grandfathering to SG and IL, preserving full-access plan pools for subscribers in countries that left full access on 2026-09-15. Prevents granting full pools to limited-access subscribers in countries that were limited all along.

a4396df88073029ec1427d8bbbdff0791b21781d.text: Singapore and Israel subscribers who bought full-access plans before September 15 keep their full allowances. Subscribers in other regions who always had limited plans do not receive extra access. This internal rule prevents giving full benefits to the wrong group.

d3cb8415d4f5e51b401e1a08187b2f744433cc45.text: The internal assistant now stops adding unsolicited follow-up suggestions or offers to help when reporting command results. This change is live for the internal team. You will notice shorter, more direct responses without extra advice.

7c5a830fbc562d75ad6c797a9cab717830765ac1.text: The assistant's internal instructions now stop listing tools when none are available. This prevents the system from seeing empty or confusing sections about capabilities it does not have. The change applies to all users interacting with the assistant, ensuring clearer responses by removing unnecessary background noise from its memory.

b1d9f0d4f79a0a00b018b8230b41e2cd2b0c472d.text: Internal tools now use simpler names for their helper bots. A setup step that previously hid its errors now shows them in the log. This affects only the team running these tests. You would see cleaner logs and easier-to-read names when running internal checks.

6da99d24210508da809379301201753a8b070d5a.text: A helper tool that finds relevant files now receives clearer instructions to list paths starting from the project root, including a sample output to follow. This change affects only internal tools used by staff. Regular users will not notice any difference, as this is a minor internal adjustment to improve consistency.

f7ffed3713f37613637553e1f4c47e741c23363d.text: The internal assistant now accepts brief bullet points for task summaries and is instructed to continue working until the request is fully satisfied in its maximum-effort mode. This change is live for internal staff using the assistant.

14e4c921d3391bcee7d823be91746dcc6e56b715.text: The command-line tool no longer writes a stray 'asdf' message to its debug log when sending a message. This is an internal cleanup that does not change how the tool behaves for you.

4ba6ef0d829d5a2b3421ca06df034940369865d0.text: A small internal update fixes how the automated testing tool for the coding assistant starts up. It now automatically downloads required background files before running tests. This change only affects the internal testing setup and is live today. Regular users will not notice any difference in the assistant's behavior.

f2c0e412fae5c1f8b8ec9a103ebcde75e5a55dda.text: The code search tool now always includes line numbers in its results, a change necessary for the system to correctly read and display search outputs. This internal fix affects the search feature's reliability, ensuring results are parsed without errors, but it does not change what you see on screen.

21bfc2ffc14919bdbda19440f72908cee57e83ae.text: Internal change to the AI's thinking process. The system now prepares the AI's memory before running multiple tasks at once, ensuring they can share the same context. This makes the AI faster and cheaper for complex questions.

8af8d077a9611738094b23ce30c567a180a5cc0e.text: The system stopped removing a hidden instruction from the message list before counting its length, because that instruction is no longer added there. This internal cleanup prevents the tool from accidentally deleting a real message if the instructions change later. Users will not notice any difference in the assistant's responses today.

77f310f5e4eb270a996b02dda01bac2a1e520bf5.text: The setup instructions now list the specific guide and template files created when starting a new project. People following these steps will see exactly what folders and documents appear after running the setup command. This is a small internal update to the help text.

f8e0282308c20c24f8a88f01c9c1bdf1dadd6d52.text: When an assistant has no extra tools to use, it no longer wastes space in its instructions by listing a blank 'Tools' section. This helps agents that run without plugins or external actions. You would see a slightly shorter, cleaner prompt behind the scenes, but the assistant's behavior stays the same.

1de465822c93327a6615da338c2c8effdf4a6457.text: The tool that searches for text inside files now limits how many results it shows from each file and across all files to prevent overwhelming output. This helps the assistant process information faster and stay within memory limits. The change is active now, but regular users won't see it directly since it only affects how the system gathers data behind the scenes.

e5e30eb18509a80c4bd279f1ef726f7a9962b5ca.text: When you search for code and find nothing, the tool now shows 'No results' instead of a blank space. This small update helps you immediately understand that your search returned no matches, rather than wondering if the system failed.

f05b9bb6ecb95f038f210a3d3a848bb37eca1b37.text: Internal tools now point to the correct assistant settings for testing, so checks run against the right versions. This affects only the team running these tests. A regular user would notice no change.

824924201362ed796c2f4fed6868ddcb0c89a78f.text: The software's internal label was updated to match a new background system. This is a small administrative change. People using the software will see no difference in how it works.

82eb68d7d8908d1b25b20ad01239fdb7f1056f1c.text: The internal assistant now uses a single, specialized search tool to find relevant files instead of launching multiple general searches. This change applies only to the base2 agent configuration and is live today. A reader would notice the assistant gathering context more efficiently, avoiding redundant file lookups and expensive repeated reads.

d0b3c7aa1179cedc7c5903268b27f7cc14aeb26e.text: A new help section explains how to adjust the assistant's speed, cost, and behavior through simple commands. This update helps people who run the tool from a text window understand their choices without guessing. The instructions are visible now in the guide.

d1b7fd02ada4db27165fe63d9c32102c42e47396.text: Internal cleanup of how the assistant identifies available tools. No change to user-facing behavior.

fb5f796ecd4cd7eaf4d258b6827cad92a94a7eea.text: The system now checks if a step has actual instructions before adding a special hidden marker to them. If a step is empty, the marker is skipped. This prevents the AI from receiving confusing blank signals, making its responses slightly cleaner.

5f0d358e8fa59e730c645478890f4ef33fb8520f.text: The system now checks if an assistant has any tools or sub-assistants before adding their descriptions to its instructions. If none exist, those empty sections are skipped, resulting in cleaner, shorter instructions. This internal cleanup helps the assistant process information more efficiently without changing its visible behavior for most users.

5b304a8a02d5f374b0ff1b732d12bd71de8b1b7c.text: The internal communication between the main assistant and its specialized helpers now uses a consistent naming style for data updates. This change is small and happens in the background, so regular users will not notice any difference in how the tool looks or behaves.

ada0e6ba4b39862ee567f88e189f922e68f5a081.text: The text command tool now records a clearer label when noting background events. This helps support staff track issues. Ordinary users see no change in the tool's behavior or output.

11c85e4e1b8ab58f1b8e3cb8846b3987a1e23c41.text: The internal writing assistant now rejects shortcuts that hide mistakes. Programmers will see fewer sloppy drafts. The change is active for the assistant's internal instructions.

5fe62cce84d1124047ce649ecb5bbfcec297d82d.text: Added a troubleshooting guide for Windows users. It explains how to fix common problems like connection errors, command failures, and login issues. This is a documentation update only; no software behavior changed.

008f8dd95ec9f17faf758560b3341d8a0e339728.text: The system now checks if a chat request asks for a live response or includes a specific tracking number before processing it. This ensures the assistant behaves correctly for these requests and records accurate usage data. Internal change; users see no difference.

c1f78c05e1acff6698b19a9a7e3df363894c35e4.text: The login window in the command-line tool is now larger, taking up more of the screen. This change is live today for anyone using the tool to sign in. You would notice the box filling more of your terminal window, with less empty space around the edges.

d03f76120f224e8b93fbeec45c052b76bf8635f5.text: The text-based chat program now asks for confirmation before closing when you press the stop keys. If you press them once, a warning appears and any unsent data finishes uploading; pressing them again within three seconds closes the program. Rapid accidental presses are ignored to prevent crashes.

2e98d744e03a921690fa18ad148ec1e8832202da.text: A new 'clean' command was added to the website project's menu. This command deletes old temporary files created during development. It affects only internal tools and helps keep the workspace tidy. The command is ready to use but does nothing until someone runs it.

1b1aa2e8b54e5a542c1c890cf5b6464c31e2745b.text: A small internal cleanup fixes a duplicate instruction in the login process and stops error logs from failing if extra details are missing. Users will not see any changes to the interface or features.

974f7d91e9343e77bebc2bc2b3283d3a91742cbf.text: After signing in, the chat screen now clears old messages and puts your cursor back in the text box. This fixes glitches where the screen would freeze or show the wrong text width. The change is live for the command-line tool.

5407694c252acfed83864ee7318dddb4f8bef411.text: The text box where you type messages now shrinks to make room for the button that switches between assistant modes. This prevents the button from pushing your typed words off the edge of the screen.

e007c9b18e9eec8c881c0c3b90616bd1b371eb7f.text: A guide was added to internal notes showing how to test command-line interface screens by recording them at set times. This helps developers check that login prompts and loading animations look right before releasing updates. Regular users will not see any change from this note.

8a6461f32fe69fda14f4b16e2f91634c62654d7b.text: The command-line assistant now opens its screen right away instead of waiting for a connection check. If the connection is slow or the login key is bad, the screen stays open and shows an error instead of freezing.

191a634ca10f60e1c8b3ef12e18b154657c715fa.text: The system now tracks and displays the exact cost of each request made through the software development kit. fd5db264d201a2b1b13a23481f72c1153639b0c2.text: The system now finds its code-reading helper by checking exactly where it lives, rather than guessing. If the helper is missing, it stops with a clear warning instead of failing silently. This affects only the internal tools for mapping codebases and will not change how you use the product.

08aae84900d7db2d413a6b470a304213114f0a62.text: The software now finds its own location more reliably when packaged for distribution. This internal fix ensures the tool works correctly across different computer setups. Users will not notice any visual changes, but the application is less likely to fail during startup.

3a420050d14eb712e6931badbaff4c72a511775e.text: The system now sets the cost of each credit to exactly one cent for everyone, ignoring any special pricing that might have existed. This change affects only the internal billing process, so customers will not notice any difference in their checkout experience or account settings. The update is live today, ensuring all credit purchases calculate the total price using this fixed one-cent rate.

7c03da6f383950435336769e74baceae6cb5b0c0.text: The software now allows starting without specifying a folder. If no folder is set, it skips scanning files and uses the current location as a fallback. However, trying to read or write files without a folder set will now show a clear error message instead of failing silently.

dc3afb56b2d763f2560a48ae4069cce0ec96222a.text: The assistant now looks for custom instructions in your personal home folder, not just the project folder. This helps people who set up their own tools to reuse them across different projects. You will only notice this if you have placed your own instruction files in that specific personal folder; otherwise, nothing changes.

61cd0799dff3a72ddb1946f6f1d2917aab0a0e9b.text: When a user cancels a request to the AI assistant, the system now stops processing and reports an error instead of quietly halting. This affects internal monitoring, allowing support teams to see exactly when and why a request was stopped. Users will not notice a difference, but the system's logs will clearly show cancelled actions rather than silent failures.

f732133e0a8af0cc8222051e31c50e2cc46385c9.text: The assistant can now pause while waiting for information to arrive, rather than assuming everything happens instantly. This allows the tool to display responses or handle errors more smoothly without freezing the screen. The change is live today for anyone using the latest version of the connection tool.

758f3c6347a99e60af6fdd986b89c9474e74eab6.text: The rules for asking the assistant to run a command have been tightened. Before, the system could guess how to handle a command if that detail was left out; now, that choice must be stated clearly. This mostly affects how the assistant behaves behind the scenes, so most people will not notice a difference.

3053c4b4b8153c603f22a2cd8f28162c206d4543.text: The system now automatically tries up to three times if a temporary connection error occurs while an agent is responding. This change applies only to agent streams and is live today. Users may notice fewer failed responses during brief network interruptions.

50ae105891eea0851a127e42adf52922422ddd00.text: Two internal research assistants now use a different underlying AI model for their tasks. This change affects only the specific agents used for document and web research, not the general public or other tools. A person interacting with these agents would notice no visual difference, but the text responses might have a slightly different tone or style.

2426408827c5ce5bb9e0a54d3586c4939ccf977b.text: A small internal update improves how the system tracks changes during tests. Previously, it only checked files that were explicitly saved; now it automatically captures all recent work, including new files and unsaved edits. This ensures the system sees the complete picture of what changed without needing manual steps.

5092b1e7ab0ed5fcfbc3fe8b43d4c8e0d96d7717.text: The system now saves the full text of its instructions to an internal log for developers. This change only affects the team building the software, not customers. You will not see anything different in the app.

68cc6bba863ad4c89cca0d107a0af13d673480ac.text: The search box on the agent store page now waits briefly before searching, instead of checking with every keystroke. This reduces unnecessary network requests and prevents the page from slowing down or flickering while typing. The change is live and affects anyone using the agent store search.

9e1b2ce106aba7269fe0c0305dd922069949570c.text: Internal testing checks were updated to match how the system now reports errors when it receives an unrecognized request. This change affects only the software's internal quality assurance process and is not live for customers. Users will not notice any difference in the application's behavior.

d6ef243c976331f43cf81f01788f78446f6fe7bf.text: The list of featured assistants on the store page changed. Three older tools were swapped for three new ones. Visitors looking at the store now see this updated lineup instead of the previous one.

af5450c627d85ee8bbc48281337d72497fa60ec8.text: The naming convention for one specific artificial intelligence assistant was updated to match the official standard. This affects only the internal setup of certain automated research and planning tools. A regular person would notice no change in how these tools work or what they produce, as this was a small internal cleanup task.

597e59d7550eaec92991f537c46bd419f15d850f.text: An internal tool that tests how well the coding assistant works has been updated. The test script no longer tells the assistant to save its changes, which prevents the test from creating unnecessary records. This change only affects the internal testing process and will not be noticed by regular users.

875ca1fb96d29b5ea7af8fa7431dec52421d98ce.text: The highest-level automated assistant now uses a slightly newer version of its underlying reasoning engine. This change affects only internal system configurations and will not be visible to regular users. The assistant itself remains the same, but it may perform marginally better on complex tasks due to the updated engine.

cde6ebb38236816467caa6bfb738dfd2b04faad1.text: The system now checks if a tool name is missing before trying to use it. If the name is invalid, the system reports the error and stops processing that specific request instead of failing silently. This internal fix ensures smoother handling of data streams without changing the user experience.

ce4d79865d668f802cbb6108ecb51ea24094eb2e.text: The system now correctly saves the full text of AI responses to its internal records. Previously, parts of the response were missing from the stored history. This is a small, internal fix that ensures accurate logging for support and debugging.

6f9bb4c9e1eda2bb404b5edfb50567f7a45fb835.text: The system now reads image names written with special codes and converts them into plain text before searching for the file. This helps people who copy file names from technical logs or scripts. They will see the correct image load instead of an error message.

a459d5072eef428cf02c25fa02de540920ddeb42.text: A small fix was made to the written instructions for creating a custom assistant. The example command shown in the guide was corrected to remove an extra symbol that would have caused it to fail. This helps people following the tutorial get their assistant working without hitting an error.

0a0d56fe5f6deb0abb25441da2196a374dd1246a.text: The assistant can now send secret access keys when connecting to external tools. This lets you use private services that require login, instead of only public ones. You will notice this if you try to connect to a protected tool and it works without you having to share the key in the web address.

358b711b30bff9759b631df733db5e27eaf1e56c.text: Internal planning tools now use a different AI model. The complex planner generates fewer parallel drafts. No visible change for users.

6c65de6819f6b14dba70c8a75eefcc7b92506b93.text: A small internal fix corrected a spelling error in the release tool's settings. Previously, the tool ignored a command meant to hide its help text, which could cause errors or show unwanted instructions during automated tasks. This change is live now and ensures the tool runs silently as intended.

bba2125bb19edf0499fd32a8d808c682a46be6ee.text: The assistant's menu of available artificial intelligence brains has been refreshed to include several new options and remove outdated ones. This change is currently in place but does nothing yet, as it only updates the internal list of choices without activating any new features. Users will not notice any immediate difference until these new options are officially turned on.

08d425fcb39702284b08a75e9832c3e99da18afd.text: The system now uses a different engine for the research and review steps. This change applies to the internal assistant. You will notice it responds faster and plans more consistently.

b77fcb25c22bcd14e9d2e16f28e70d2a6086da52.text: The internal tool that helps create custom AI assistants now shares real examples of good setups with them, instead of just describing rules. This helps the tool suggest better starting points for new assistants. People building these tools might see slightly smarter suggestions, but there is no change for everyday users.

d54351ceea1e4234a790c10db86b290f28e3211c.text: The system now automatically enables response caching for all models from OpenAI and Anthropic, rather than requiring a specific entry for each one. This change is live and affects anyone using these providers. Users might notice faster responses and lower costs for repeated or long conversations with these specific models.

ef0502ca017e9e4a07924435b04db75d375ee7cb.text: A small fix in Codebuff’s program stops default settings from replacing saved session details when a session starts. It affects people who use that program with custom session settings. They should now see their chosen session details carry through instead of being overwritten. The fix is live.

d41672194939af5698daaafd6a5aba046b8bbe8d.text: The code editor's language parser now loads rule files correctly when running under a specific JavaScript runtime that previously passed file paths instead of content. This fixes a loading issue for internal developers using that runtime, ensuring syntax highlighting and code analysis work as expected.

e9d593a3928418785a1ca9eef2d1d7807d91ce0b.text: The internal planning tool now creates ten draft plans for a task instead of three. It picks the winner using new checks for completeness and simplicity. Staff using this tool will see it spend more time and computing power to choose a slightly better plan.

f90d544edc648043e312106e70b37161ff11bb20.text: The release number for the toolkit that lets outside programs connect to Codebuff increased by a small amount. This affects people who build tools on top of Codebuff and download its toolkit. They would see a slightly newer version available to install, with no change in how the toolkit works.

3c7a755b150f47bf64c947f062c70ce093a6f20e.text: The team added a new connection tool to the shared software parts. This change is small and internal, so nothing happens yet. You will not notice any difference until the main program starts using this new tool.

2f8cd0b79ba8bd56c167b4bf05eeaea8428948a1.text: A small internal update stops the tool from showing its own help text when asked for it. Instead, it now passes that request to the underlying program it runs. People using the command line tool might see different help information than before.

aab8e78da45bcce60dca96fc8844099e9b2a6c9a.text: Internal checks for the software's building blocks were updated to match new formatting rules. This change affects only the automated tests that verify the software's structure. Regular users will notice nothing, as this does not alter the software's behavior.

43ea37285bc949353ca37b1490a8f0773dc6ac5d.text: The assistant now uses a newer, more capable version of its underlying text-generation service. It also received clearer instructions on how to properly end a conversation turn, preventing it from stopping while still waiting for search results. These updates are live and apply to all users interacting with the assistant.

cf5fa9ce2a6ce5a84d81a85e252f75f3ad5fd80a.text: The instructions for connecting to the AI service were simplified to make them easier to read. Extra text used for debugging was removed, and the steps for handling errors were made clearer. This update only affects the written guide, so the actual behavior of the software remains unchanged.

55dbd5b724660edb3ae2089c091d318bb8aade5f.text: Internal test files were updated to match new rules for how the AI assistant stores information. This change affects only the development team's quality checks. Customers will not notice any difference, as the software's behavior remains unchanged.

8ec81740a15d8d26e36294d859936ecbc8d0bdc9.text: A developer added a required setting to a test file to fix a type-check error. This change affects only the internal test suite and does not impact any live features. Users will notice no difference.

3fbf6fbab9c3d5ff80e3644e90d58a269a4e1852.text: A small internal update improved how the software defines data structures for text-based information. This change helps developers write more consistent code but does not affect how the application looks or behaves for you. You will not notice any difference in your experience.

17d52d9f1ddef72f79f223695292607f7c05f89c.text: The software now reports failures with a specific error message instead of returning nothing. This affects programs that use this tool to automate coding tasks. Users of these programs will see clearer explanations when a task fails, rather than just a blank or silent stop.

6ec38f475fdf58a64ec30ab716f13fa972a49123.text: A tiny internal cleanup fixed a glitch where the system might reject valid custom actions if their names clashed with built-in ones. Only the specific custom actions you create are affected. You will notice nothing; the system just handles name conflicts more smoothly now.

6738315292b23625abf3ef87f6b502b85f27213c.text: The Agent Store page now loads its data directly, removing a placeholder screen that previously appeared while waiting. This change affects anyone visiting the store, and they will no longer see a brief loading animation before the agent listings appear. It is an internal adjustment intended to fix a potential double-loading issue.

db7219b6aaa0393878700d422abdc9921fc4d956.text: A small internal fix adjusts the website's top banner to fit better on mobile screens. It removes a rigid size limit that previously cut off content on smaller devices, allowing the text and layout to expand naturally. Visitors on phones will see the headline and main buttons display fully without awkward gaps or clipped edges.

a57a6e9232d5fa9fdfc595eeba4679364aa8600e.text: The software toolkit now sends a smaller, simpler file package to developers. This change removes hidden background files that helped programmers trace errors back to their original code. Developers will notice the download size is smaller, but they will lose the ability to easily jump from an error message directly to the specific line of code that caused it.

b63f3373cf2e1bd926511d53c065af014c1f3b8d.text: When a software task fails, the system now sends back a detailed report of what went wrong instead of an empty response. This change helps automated tools better understand and handle errors during execution.

232bdd1042bdbe3d4a9984634cbfc81d889ce924.text: The login step now uses a standard method to open your web browser, replacing an older technique that sometimes failed on certain computers. This change is internal and affects only the command-line tool used for authentication. You would notice this if your browser previously did not open automatically when you tried to sign in.

e19f097a032f8b691751589bec7f348684af5683.text: The website's top menu now waits until it confirms your login status before showing account options. This prevents a brief visual glitch where the menu might flicker or show the wrong buttons for a split second. The change is live and affects anyone viewing the site.

4a3511f1d7e763642926e8362f0b66b329970393.text: The onboarding screen now shows clearer instructions for redeeming a referral code. Instead of just announcing the code, it guides new users through the next steps to claim their bonus credits. This text update is live and helps users understand how to use their referral.

9a081a74e4684c0770c984e63b80dc103d47b11e.text: The system now automatically grants certain foundational tools permission to launch any other tool, skipping the usual security checks. This change is live and affects internal operations, allowing these specific tools to start new tasks without needing extra configuration. Users will not see any visual changes in the interface.

93ae8bc2a945091b9121a29cb5a7f86f6281f325.text: The tool now arranges loaded agent names into multiple columns instead of a single long line. This change affects internal developers running the command in a terminal. They will see a more compact, grid-like list that uses less vertical space.

0a303c15bb5b3805ff12f94d1b858cfa5e00117c.text: Two internal pages (profile and new publisher) previously failed to load correctly due to a technical conflict. Developers added a placeholder screen that displays while the page data loads, preventing errors and ensuring smooth access. This change is live now and affects anyone visiting those specific pages.

57fe4878aeb00ff3c9a09fa7fc920efce81c0ad9.text: The software toolkit for building apps now shares more information with the people using it. This helps those builders write better code, but regular users will see no difference.

348327c308dbf8213b90930567fa01e6a2e43504.text: A small internal update adds an option to the command-line tool so a person can start a task already aimed at a specific helper by name, instead of typing the mention by hand. The main assistant now also knows to look up a helper's details when its name appears in a message. It works today for anyone using the command-line tool.

c3782ed681722b82b1f051de41f61503a1b88090.text: Internal fix. Missing version data caused assistant records to fail checks. Corrected data inclusion. No visible change for end users.

50195d8e16652bc4a47f7fe98d7734a4cb443ea7.text: The agent store now counts how many times each agent ran in the past seven days. Previously, the weekly usage number showed the total lifetime runs instead. Publishers and store visitors now see accurate weekly activity alongside weekly spending.

cc127b8d4a3b7a2a184e64603b505d023d4c9fe8.text: The system now keeps a record when a helper tool fails during a task. This change is internal and small. Users will not notice any difference in the interface or results.

a6578ab91bc012766c77409f5ade42c6b9e19cbe.text: A small internal cleanup removed a routine status message from the system's activity log. This change affects only the technical support team, who use these logs to troubleshoot issues. Customers will not see any difference, as the removed message was never displayed to them.

c302ee664192f47477ef81dc8cbd3b97566466d4.text: A small internal update improves how the system handles errors during automated code checks. It now captures failure details and stops gracefully when a response is missing, instead of crashing unexpectedly. This change affects only the internal evaluation tools and is not visible to end users today.

937f3aef56c009ecdd48ae68593c83c2cd76b6b3.text: The top menu bar now shows a grey placeholder shape instead of empty space while checking if you are logged in. Once the check finishes, the placeholder instantly swaps for your user profile or the login button. This prevents the menu bar from jumping around or flashing blank during page load.

36d2e3111661b2dcc14e70621317665a184c7a91.text: The website's agent store cards now use simpler visual effects when you hover over them. This change affects anyone browsing the store, making the cards react slightly faster and more smoothly to your mouse. It is live today.

f936c23a7f2949d88caa1ceec39618baa046c89c.text: A small internal update removes temporary tracking messages that were printing detailed information about how the system processes streaming data. This change affects only the backend infrastructure and does not alter how the service works for anyone. You would notice no difference in the product, but engineers will see less cluttered logs when monitoring the system.

e8b77f4dd8a78030e4eb7d5e899c9bdba9b5e557.text: A small internal fix now automatically copies a required settings file when developers create a new workspace. This prevents errors where the system fails to find its configuration. If the original file is missing, the setup process displays a warning telling the developer to create it.

7144de66ec0b48661cefdf6f12d6cebd2fb927dd.text: The software toolkit's label changed from an older version to a newer one. This update is purely administrative and does not alter how the toolkit behaves or what it can do. Programmers using this toolkit will see the new label appear in their project files, but they will not notice any difference in how their applications run or respond.

4839d9d8c7ff22ecb76d21160ec650ea5e7833b1.text: A small internal fix corrected how a test checks for a missing message number. It now expects the database to return an empty value, matching what it actually does. This change affects only the automated checks and has no impact on what you see or do in the app.

200ee742891daf817accd2e169856c6138347812.text: The software now accepts newer, small updates to its connection tool automatically. This helps people building with the tool keep their connections working without manual steps. No visible change for end users.

75db11d044131e8b21a6a2a79cb055195bb8c4b2.text: The agent store page now loads faster by skipping fancy animations on long lists. Hover effects use simple CSS transitions instead of heavy animation libraries. Data is prepared once when loaded, so scrolling and sorting feel smoother. This is a small internal performance tweak; you might notice slightly snappier interactions on the store page.

b23bc94258b930de94dd1cd24e13486fcb57942c.text: The agent list on the store page now loads more smoothly by only drawing the cards you can see, which helps especially on phones and tablets. To stop the list from jumping around, all cards were given a fixed minimum height, and the version number, tags, and copy button were removed or hidden from the mobile view. This change is live and applies to everyone browsing the agent store.

ee5733dc8b0bc3939eb82202bc411ce352182bab.text: The internal testing system now uses a different AI model to guide its evaluations. This change affects only the automated checks developers run to measure performance. Regular users will see no difference in the product.

30f6fec087d67ef5eefb8a98394652cdf9ed4351.text: The software toolkit stopped using an old, duplicate set of instructions for finding its internal guides. This cleanup affects only the toolkit's own setup files, not the apps built with it. Nothing changes for anyone using the toolkit today.

099efeb6465994fec9d67eaa1c8ee466f19b70e3.text: The system now hands over the chat message's unique ID immediately when the AI finishes speaking, rather than passing it separately in the background. This internal cleanup prevents rare errors where the ID might be missed. Users will not see any difference, as this is a minor stability fix for the backend.

f4acf8077f22e390c9b79fe20a2af5a08ca995ed.text: Housekeeping for the Codebuff software toolkit. Cleaned up duplicate settings and fixed a path so the toolkit builds correctly. Moved a build script into a folder. Removed a redundant publish step. No visible change for end users.

ec1acfbea24e178c1f0d43dbbc566fbb238bcd95.text: The library now bundles its instructions into one file for smoother setup. Programmers will see cleaner, less confusing guidance when building their apps.

6cc189012b7e1f789d1ab4205c64d60b5306b00a.text: Small internal cleanup to a test tool. Two lines changed to fix a build error. No customer features added. Nothing visible to anyone outside the team.

bb309a8ff1a036914857adcf5c94370cf8b5a9ee.text: A small internal fix corrects how the system tracks when a specific command should run for an entire session rather than just one part of it. This change is not live for users today and requires no action; it ensures the backend logic accurately associates the command with the correct execution context.

9e00a78856a5a9a4bde9a03049007a6522123e59.text: The internal agent directory now prepares its main views in advance so they load faster and show more items at once. This change is live today and affects anyone browsing the store, making the page appear more quickly without a loading spinner.

d3815aa253ea421df8ee8266f46d40413189591c.text: The software toolkit gained a new component to handle real-time connections. This affects only the developers who build applications using this toolkit. They will see the toolkit automatically download this extra component when they update it, but they won't notice any difference in how their applications behave.

cb19c32e8d6f251b8b7983c72748ff62ce652c2f.text: The website's list of agents now measures each row slightly smaller and prepares more rows off-screen. This helps the page scroll more smoothly when you browse the full list of agents. The change is live and affects anyone viewing the store page.

aa88ea714c5165826eddf572167f53bcdfa3602a.text: The link in the help guide for finding reusable assistants was broken. It now points to the correct store page. Visitors clicking that link will reach the right place instead of an error.

14a59f3b5ea40df605caf705c07df4d73c9a158a.text: A slow helper tool for searching large projects was turned off to save time. This change only affects internal researchers using a specific assistant. They will no longer see results from this particular search method, though other ways to find information remain available.

55161deda604127fbe680c50a68752b690bfc023.text: The system stopped requiring three unused service keys. Setup lists and validation rules now ignore these entries. Internal developers setting up the environment will see fewer required fields to fill out.

2f91aae1c0d4abd07dc3334de68afc47388dfbab.text: The system now tracks each agent's activity by a unique session ID instead of a shared name. This prevents leftover data from one session leaking into another if the same agent is used twice. Users won't see any direct change, but background processes are safer and more reliable.

2e933cf93a18c26f4475cc448db5fa89ae5f7c05.text: The internal system now reads data in a format that includes extra labels, and adds a detailed record of each step. This change affects only the company's own engineers, who use the new records to find problems. Regular customers will not notice any difference in how the product works.

a69f1398a49bd7c3dba880a9d6b53e60dce4eedd.text: A small internal fix corrects how the software describes custom actions, allowing them to be created without errors. This affects only those building their own tools for the assistant. They would notice that their tool definitions now work properly instead of failing to start.

15c52b7c0e02a4e4352b5d648e406723e04b18a0.text: A small internal fix stops the system from waiting forever when the AI provider fails. This change is live today. Non-programmers would notice no visible difference, as the fix prevents a background process from hanging during rare errors.

9d9f09f6a8d0bdb0b2b7ce2c694bc428f7fbb958.text: A small internal tidy-up. The team gathered the names of actions tracked for statistics (like clicking a button or signing in) into one shared list, replacing scattered duplicates across the website. Visitors and users will notice no change; the website looks and works exactly the same. This just ensures the data collected about how people use the site is consistent and accurate for the team.

c488469718d6bf1526551860c0807ba27313780d.text: The guide for new helpers now lists setup steps as a clean, indented list instead of lettered paragraphs. This affects only people reading the instructions to start the tool in different folders. They will see the commands easier to follow, but the tool itself works exactly the same.

87944dbecf2845a66c751e488f50c8a29bff8ddf.text: The tool now uses the agent name directly instead of hiding it inside the text box. This fixes an internal handling issue. Users will see no change in how the tool works or looks.

491f154e344ed2e787764e2808156cb39e36ab79.text: The sample setup guide for internal developers now shows 'dev' instead of 'development' for the environment name. This ensures the instructions match the actual values the system expects. New team members copying this file will get the correct label immediately.

87f11bddc0736d4d7a54d1d0a1c71b472d99223a.text: The assistant now waits for custom tools to finish before moving on. This affects apps using the software toolkit. A user might notice fewer errors when a tool takes time to complete.

716de248d94d2856229009d742d92c29f21f7a66.text: Developers who build custom tools for the AI assistant must now use a new name for the action that runs their code. This change aligns the system with a common industry standard. If a developer does not update their code, their custom tool will stop working.

df7f77aa8708fc48f5c262c19777a74b1c60be54.text: The assistant now hides database warning messages when working on a computer in test mode. This change helps people building the software see a cleaner screen while checking agent settings. It does not affect the live service that customers use today.

69a28634eed528e1c4376de0b753e0d65eca5e81.text: The assistant now requires a follow-up action after creating a new sub-task, rather than pausing. This prevents the chat from stalling during complex requests. Users will see fewer instances where the assistant stops working without explanation.

cb59f9fd1886bbb81b61c577689a4b6ec18d2c5e.text: The setup guide now explains how new team members can manually add testing credits to their own accounts without needing a payment system. It also updates two internal connection addresses to match current server locations. This only helps people setting up their work computers, and they will see clearer instructions when trying to log in or test the tool.

3b8cfa8ce3c2b96b51ae824a9c3d14f4582bbec2.text: The system now allows custom tools to finish their task immediately, without waiting for a background process. Builders of these tools can write simpler, faster code for basic actions. If they use this update, their tools will respond instantly instead of showing a loading delay.

b71e164eba828984235a1655cc03d2be0311680c.text: The system previously checked every custom tool against strict built-in rules, causing errors when those tools were used. It now skips that check for custom tools, allowing them to run without failing. This fix is live and affects anyone using custom tools.

6eeaf68db34acc80d3f93704856e06f08da09cf3.text: The server no longer cuts off parts of the conversation history when sending it to the assistant. This internal change helps the assistant remember details from earlier in the chat that it might have previously forgotten.

dcb913abd286e9b2dc50711d66a38de16158926c.text: The website now remembers the list of agents for one minute instead of rebuilding it from scratch every time someone asks. This change helps the company's servers run faster and more reliably. Regular visitors will not notice any difference, except that the list might be up to one minute out of date.

df2d7681d5c46e125f01f00bedf6f73d6f64316b.text: A small internal update changed the default helper used for automated software tests. Instead of using the standard version, it now picks a lighter, simpler version by default. This affects only the team running these tests. Users will see no difference in the product itself.

951be1fa1b9038cb1704e9290c5b40bf9e6d8071.text: The team updated their internal publishing tool to use a different script for checking releases before they go live. This is a maintenance task for the developers who release the software. Customers will not notice any changes in how the product works.

aeb93d09c7bc4d57a4995f657a91203bcfbd8c3a.text: The assistant now correctly understands simple folder instructions when running commands. Previously, it failed if you did not specify the exact location. This fix is live today.

0b95a09804e81283740e2f7155acd09955f5de5a.text: The tool for building custom commands was simplified. This helps developers write code more easily, but the assistant's behavior stays the same. You will not notice any difference.

e8da05d461a83d2f61e4f7aea5dd6136a1a08826.text: The instructions for using the software tools were updated. The link to get your account key now goes to a simpler web address. Extra notes explain how the system reports progress and how to build custom helpers. This is a small documentation fix for people setting up the tools.

760ee27aff29334d9388e88537ef646d1720c7b4.text: The library now ships only one file format, dropping the newer standard format. Developers building on this SDK will see installation errors if their project expects the newer format. This change is live in the latest release.

c2837def5728f8e4a82058424ca1f7a5ca0bf4cc.text: A small internal update removed a specific helper tool from the project's default setup. This change affects only new projects created with this template. Existing projects and current users will notice no difference.

09627a59071c8cb535f1437ff20876369e7556ce.text: Broken links in the help guides have been repaired. Readers looking for specific answers will now reach the correct page instead of seeing an error. This is a small internal fix and is live.

b170d52ff00b8a43e52b387e0adfb13b1fe5766b.text: The system stopped repeating text it already received from the app. This internal cleanup removes duplicate instructions when sending messages. You will not notice any change in how the app behaves or looks.

a0110d19af5cfccb07011e1fa9ccb4fc50f5f0aa.text: The team switched the tool that sends the software library out to the world, changing how it runs behind the scenes. This only affects the engineers who publish the library, not the people who use it. You will see no difference in the library's features or behavior.

06439eff34a19ee2d658e6cd5153f7146cbb8d11.text: The list of recommended AI helpers on the website's store page has been updated. The 'reviewer' and 'codebase-commands-explorer' options were replaced with 'planner' and 'rampup-teacher-agent'. Visitors to the store page will now see these new suggestions instead of the previous ones.

ca55ac53b557cd590534ac0be7be6c1868dd6d1a.text: The internal tests that check the assistant's responses were broken because they expected plain text but the system now sends structured messages. Developers updated these test checks to match the new format. This change does not affect how the assistant behaves for end users today.

200e55c179b2b5d38b30cef143064762fff4275c.text: Internal plumbing update. The backend now labels AI responses as 'text', 'reasoning', or 'error' before passing them along. Users will not notice any change.

d95ae9e26ad6795da108db2ffb6c2a696f386158.text: Before the assistant's response appeared on screen, a spinning loading icon stayed visible, creating a brief visual glitch. The loading icon now stops exactly when the text begins to stream in. This is a small internal fix affecting how the app handles streaming responses.

f7d4075fd903d0ee921844674552a0a9462477a2.text: The command-line tool now adds a short text label listing the filename when you attach a picture. This ensures the AI assistant knows exactly which file you sent, rather than just seeing an unmarked image. You will see these labels appear in the chat history alongside your uploaded pictures.

70ac9d82264ea73ca2e8df0881570637229dc774.text: A small internal fix ensures that when you include a picture in a message, the system correctly finds the file location. Previously, certain file names containing slashes were mistaken for user tags, causing the image to fail loading. This change is live and prevents these errors for anyone sending messages with attached images.

02150d4eeee407e8db14b476e53d1cb0ac9a8e37.text: We cleaned up the internal setup for our data-handling assistants by removing an unused version label and updating the ownership tag to Brandon. This is a minor housekeeping task that affects only our internal engineering team; customers and regular users will not notice any changes.

b682d913025ea387539f62a1a58c134d648a60d9.text: You can now manually add or remove specific helper tools from the main assistant's list. This change is active and affects anyone who uses the project configuration to customize which tasks the assistant can perform.

60200e78e66fe7747ddc96ecab99dbf3d29e9cbd.text: The online store for AI assistants now loads its list of products instantly, without the previous sliding and fading effects. This change affects anyone browsing the store, making the page feel snappier and less sluggish. The cards still lift slightly when you hover your mouse over them, but the entrance animation is gone.

2f42d22f25517d68fc0ff26001798856bd1143c7.text: The copy button on the agent store page now includes the publisher's name and the specific version number in the command it generates. This prevents errors when different publishers offer agents with the same name, ensuring the correct agent runs. The change is live and affects only the text copied to the clipboard.

6b1d63c5b788db9167f88c1b4e9e074a512bca3e.text: The image uploader now ignores file paths with spaces unless wrapped in quotes. This prevents accidental detection of regular text as an image location. Affected internal users must quote such paths to upload them.

376bf7e2cc49a8d817b90674e817a8ca88f110e9.text: A small internal change updated the loading message shown while the assistant works. Instead of saying 'Reading through files...', it now says 'Processing results...'. This only affects what text appears on the screen during that step.

8d6c0e63332f891b799c10800e5c7a92f07a5a15.text: The Agent Store page now loads more smoothly. The 'Publishers' button slides in gently instead of fading, and the 'Editors' Choice' section fades in as one block to stop the page from jumping around. This change is live and affects anyone browsing the store.

8c471757d2bd4d71df718d490f75c77d711700f6.text: The system now records the raw reply data after saving the conversation history in its internal logs. This reordering only affects how support staff review the logs, not how the assistant behaves. Users will notice no change.

8155a97484de68f4a92bc384a29567f5a0c5356d.text: The server now sends the count of past conversation messages when a chat session begins. This is an internal plumbing update. Regular users will not see any difference in the interface.

5ec3534506916a4466e6d5937085d5b7ef7f3aa2.text: A small internal cleanup changed how the system prepares past conversation history before sending it to the AI. Previously, the system forced a specific setting to 'off' for every past message; now it simply uses the setting that is already attached to each message. This change affects only the background logic for internal agents. No visible behavior changes for end users.
