30e74b20042a3e3af86fe1e357656c66e3110abf.text: A new, shorter list of project files is now available for internal use. This list limits the file count to 2,500 items, whereas the standard list allows 20,000. Nothing changes for users today because no feature uses this shorter list yet.

6cbd91b1dfc04e0946944d193098e0fc3811b3ed.text: A small internal fix ensures that the final piece of an AI's response is saved when the test run ends. This affects only the automated testing system, not live products. If you looked at the test results, you would see complete logs instead of potentially missing the last few words.

04dd986dc53bcf7d7272e962694bd9e32b3b7eae.text: A small internal update adjusts how the AI coding tool describes its data to other software, without changing what it actually does. This affects only the underlying library used by the tool, so you will see no difference in the interface or behavior.

19b18574929a9c3ac181bdcb5cece86ed488be46.text: The app now shows a loading indicator that says 'Reading through files...' while it processes information. This change only happens when a specific user action is active, so most people won't see it yet. It is a small internal update to help users know the system is working.

92ef47a31b12f1e75c0831c192b8d50d03d164ca.text: A small packaging change makes the library create its description files beside the installed code, for both common ways of installing it. People using the library may notice their tools can find its details more reliably. It is live today and does not change visible behavior.

e05b79eafc7f4e5b5d8a7cbfcbd2879473103364.text: Setup instructions for the local development environment were corrected to point to the right database names and server address. This helps new team members connect their computers to the system without errors. The live application for regular users remains unchanged.

f2ba232efe0a72760cdeebd88dcb7d93ac639c47.text: A small update added a chart to the project's main description page. This chart shows how many people have favorited the project over time. Visitors will see this visual growth tracker when they read the page.

0203027d0bb0d5b765435e6ca59913e420c1a9d4.text: Search and sort controls moved above the agent list. This affects internal agent store users. They now see filters before browsing results.

5e883532deefef112874f946493469ec9c566c2b.text: A small fix corrected how example text appears in a guide for creating custom AI assistants. Readers following the steps now see clear, readable instructions without stray symbols cluttering the display.

a0ff417fce5cc87cd4843bc6b684db30030033c9.text: A small cleanup fixed a formatting error in the guide for creating your first agent. Readers following the guide will now see the instructions clearly without stray symbols breaking the layout. This update affects only the help documentation and does not change how the software works.

f51b44d3c12b7736e6cdc78331d037a0f1ae32b4.text: The guide for building your first agent now suggests a helper tool but advises trying manually first. This is a small text change in the documentation. Readers will see this tip when following the steps.

a08f9cff13abcca298c078ce541259645fa0317a.text: The store page now shows a different assistant as one of the top picks, replacing an older option. This change is live and affects anyone browsing the store page, who will see the updated list of featured tools.

d573159865734d54fae97bcbadf0ee816a61c366.text: The system now keeps a saved copy of the agent list for one minute before checking for new updates. This affects anyone viewing the agent store. They might see the same list for up to a minute after changes are made, rather than seeing updates instantly.

2f49439aa1b9c0e7a7f0986a3e7cf6b4d6672242.text: Small internal update. Publisher icons and names on agent detail and store pages now link to their profile pages. Hovering dims them to show they are clickable. Live today.

b0091ce2c3d28284800c6d702f9fc9aa48a7730c.text: The team changed the tool that downloads software parts for this project. This affects only the people building the app, not the customers using it. They might notice faster download times when starting the project.

a899c94590d8b9d2d7072a93ae9aaa5ebab6fa0c.text: The text-editing tool now handles files saved in two different formats. This fixes a rare bug where replacing text could fail on files from certain computers. Internal tooling only; no visible change for end users.

440d1327dfc9a3b86ca9cc99ca3543b50e427267.text: The system now stops saving copies of agent performance data, ensuring the dashboard always shows the most recent numbers. This affects anyone checking agent stats, so they will see updates appear immediately rather than waiting for a refresh.

2afe981bc91f71749098c1a87aedfedd899a7819.text: The assistant no longer stops working when it produces a result that doesn't fit the expected format. Instead of crashing, it now receives a specific error message telling it the format was wrong and to try again. This change is internal and affects how the assistant handles its own errors.

3ea428b88171417329ad66277f1fa7661c3ae6ba.text: The system now records the individual pieces of text an AI sends, not just the final combined message. This helps internal staff see exactly how responses were built when checking for errors. Regular users will not see any difference.

84398517afd68ed360d5db31fd0afe65be2b4ea0.text: Fixed a bug where making multiple changes to the same file in quick succession could fail or ignore edits. The system now correctly processes these changes one after another instead of getting stuck waiting for unrelated tasks. This ensures the assistant reliably updates files during complex editing sessions.

fa2a6d7fe15d1513b99b7d92999eb578d3d90de0.text: The code assistant now shows its final answer in a clear, organized format on the user's screen. Additionally, the assistant's internal process for scanning a project has been sped up by checking different parts of the code at the same time. These changes are live immediately for all users of the command-line tool.

bcfa26df1b0bc6a768025b8f3f1d7396eace9709.text: The release staging tool now stops printing a stream of raw data to its logs whenever it checks for a new package version. This cleanup affects only the internal team running the staging pipeline. They will notice the log output becomes quieter and easier to read, without any change to the software's actual behavior.

b20b07f85f95950d5980853f6e9d7521290145d4.text: Developers removed tests for a loading animation that no longer exists. This internal cleanup fixes a build error but changes nothing for regular users.

4eda42c86b810924982a351f06ac801ec3ef6171.text: A short guide now includes a video and explains how to connect different helper tools. People learning to use the software will see clearer instructions for combining tools from the library with their own. This change is live today and affects only the documentation page.

5775c775c4a4f53adff96886b0aea617f388fa26.text: The search tool now shows up to thirty matches by default instead of three. People using the tool will see more results and a note if some matches were hidden. This change is live for current searches.

480de71d81c0c71e0abacf87a62501d6190962b3.text: A small internal change adjusted the limit for how many automated quality checks can run at the same time during our nightly tests. This setting was temporarily lowered and is now back to its previous level, allowing the tests to finish faster. Because this only affects our internal testing schedule, you will not notice any difference in how the product works.

1a2d26f2c94bded264acc966d296d79ece223844.text: When you ask the assistant to read files for the first time, it no longer automatically includes background knowledge files. This prevents duplicate information from appearing in the results. The change affects internal file processing logic and is live now.

25d1a63defbf9158bff0ba26f57f4631bc520dec.text: The 'last used' timestamp is now hidden from the Agent Store page. The label 'Weekly spent' changed to 'Weekly spend'. This is a minor visual cleanup affecting only people viewing that page.

7d689bcbef4dcf858d042d1eef17b4ae1637beb9.text: The internal release tool now records extra details about its data checks. This affects only the engineering team managing software updates, not the final product or its users. Staff running the tool will see these new notes in their system logs, while everyone else notices nothing.

be57454b44726626352e06a2b6873b3783514cc5.text: The system stopped automatically sending background project notes when checking for file changes. This internal cleanup affects how the assistant tracks file updates behind the scenes. No visible changes to the user interface or assistant behavior.

26f4657033a26a318fa34b8f0ebd9a8f1260d50a.text: A small internal update hid the 'Download' button on agent detail pages. This button previously appeared but did not function when clicked. Users visiting these pages will no longer see the button, preventing confusion.

5f63472e4658c30ae98bfbf4fa31ae5bf9b6981b.text: This small internal change moved the loading dots shown while text is streaming into one shared loading-dots routine. That routine can now remember whether it was showing dots with text or dots alone, so the display resumes correctly when another task prints a header line. People using the command-line assistant may see steadier loading dots while a response is streaming; it is live today.

bcedb34354a69d3183827e79c1a816bd58cf0e10.text: The system now wipes the entire three-dot 'thinking' animation from the screen when it finishes, instead of leaving faint ghost dots behind. It also stops the animation loop before clearing the text to prevent a glitch where the dots freeze on screen. This is a small internal cleanup that makes the interface look tidier while waiting for a response.

0ed809f2206bb8a837e0305cabfae89d7fe85c7b.text: The system now saves the correct identifier for a specific assistant template when starting a task. Previously, it saved a general category label instead. This is a small internal fix. Normal users will not see any change in their daily experience.

a96ca03f570f26957f6e9da4a6a399485e3e96d4.text: The system now stops immediately if a requested text edit targets a non-existent file, rather than attempting the edit and failing later. This change affects internal processes that modify documents, ensuring that missing files are flagged with a clear error message prompting the creation of a new file. Users will not notice any visual differences, as this is an internal stability fix.

8646f5d7a111384bf2786fb050d4b8b4d60fc884.text: Labels on the agent store page changed to show 'Weekly spent' and 'Weekly runs' instead of just 'Weekly' and 'Runs'. The green badge now says 'Updated' instead of 'New'. This helps people see exactly what the numbers mean.

905c18bf93f3c1e6cdcf640ad68b176b708075a3.text: The publisher page now shows the complete list of agents instead of stopping at 50. This applies to internal users viewing publisher details. If a publisher has more than 50 agents, all of them appear in the grouping view.

c168a9fbde4c22ff48801f596a5786ddae074282.text: The agent store now shows usage stats for each version of an agent, not just the total for all versions combined. This helps users see how much a specific version of an agent has been used. The change is live and affects the agent detail pages.

7255f468e7e731ff8f736088c7e9c4259abc4c75.text: The Agent Store page now shows a new button in its header. Signed-in users see 'Create Publisher' if they have none, or 'My Publishers' to view existing ones. This change is internal and minor.

9d2ff93d42c26d0295ca59e5bf5dd9d92c6415d6.text: A small internal fix corrects how spending data is counted for automated assistants. Previously, if an assistant had multiple updates, the system incorrectly applied the same cost figures to every version. Now, it checks only the newest version, so weekly and total spending reports are accurate.

3f04e5b07d0ed57e4f81ba3dbe4390e61c4bb3d8.text: The system now checks message types more quickly and accurately. It also allows file updates to skip listing which files reference them. This is an internal cleanup; you will not notice any changes.

330b28f48bcfb5b6c632d7723775000850546f6e.text: A new section appears at the top of the Agent Store page, highlighting six specific tools as 'Editor's Choice' with gold stars and borders. This applies to anyone browsing the store. The highlighting is currently fixed to these six tools and does not change based on user activity or popularity.

2d49059d7d6deb57b5b0789d0d412f4b5c10dda8.text: The agent marketplace now shows a green 'New' label on cards for tools added within the last 24 hours. This helps you spot fresh options alongside existing 'Editor's Choice' badges. The change is active today.

621caab47b023609cbb1cbc8f03cf86714d6bc50.text: The system's internal blueprint for handling tool results was cleaned up to fix minor errors. This change affects how the assistant prepares data for display, ensuring it matches expected formats. Users will not notice any difference today, as this is a small background maintenance task.

394a20a27d65f54cb1b6eb79a08e44a149e84cd5.text: The Agent Store link is now live in the website menu. When you click it, the search and filter options appear below the list of agents rather than above them.

b0e00faf4f414930f30b12bbe226e4987dabeecb.text: The file search feature now prioritizes results where the search term appears at the beginning of a folder or file name. People using the command-line tool will see more relevant files listed first when searching. The help text also updated to clarify that the '@' symbol works for finding files, not just selecting agents.

167a90885971be3d7ce1943f1d6d4c6fd4dfdd8e.text: The tool that opens web pages for the assistant stopped saving login details and preferences between sessions. This internal cleanup affects only the assistant's own browsing activity. A person would notice nothing, as the assistant already starts each web task fresh.

fc42ff3e264645abf7cccec56e3d1fdcd7503091.text: The assistant's profile list now includes a version number. This internal change affects only the data sent to the app. Users will not see any immediate difference.

48d92c2aac5956d616b4ddc82270b7fe0539fe98.text: Bold text in the app now uses the standard text color instead of yellow. This is a small internal visual update affecting how messages appear on screen. Users will notice that bold words no longer stand out by color, only by weight.

72f530b67942e103a670ba032070bf1556f2eb64.text: A small internal change makes the list of assistants group each assistant by its owner and name, adding together its usage counts and costs across all updates. It also hides assistants that are not publicly published. The list is live today, so someone viewing it will see fewer entries, without an update label, with totals covering the whole assistant history rather than separate updates.

2d7bd9933357dab3148c7fbdbae66d66ccfa6705.text: The software now tells its code-review assistant to skip checking tiny updates because the wait time isn't worth it. This affects anyone using the assistant to check their work. You might notice fewer review requests for small edits, saving a few seconds.

792bc54e45f1da9fe265950d8ca81091eec409a4.text: A small internal fix cleaned up a background process that was leaking memory and causing warning messages. It also fixed a glitch where leftover dots stayed on the screen after loading finished. You might notice fewer warning messages and a tidier screen while using the app.

0838f4fb0a134e922b8691fe6f7da9f92b5b4f6d.text: The overnight quality-check process now runs fewer checks at once, so each batch takes longer to finish. The maximum waiting time for these checks was raised to allow for this slower pace. This internal change affects only the automated testing system and requires no action from staff or customers.

51a9cf6ec831309e6e5938a2f807978886029983.text: A small fix to the name suggestion feature when typing @. It affects people who mention names containing spaces. They will now see suggestions that match the full name after @, instead of only the last word.

0efad5d39dd06945d05cf060285246ae2133bc7c.text: The command-line tool now suggests file names when you type an at-symbol. This helps people using the text interface find and attach specific files faster. It is live today.

96863c321b7a9372ac5092113ed85989138c9d54.text: The assistant’s list of internal settings was cleaned up by removing six unused modes and simplifying the names of two active ones. This is a minor internal tidy-up that makes the system’s configuration list shorter and clearer. People using the assistant will not notice any difference in how it works or answers today.

8be5fbd73d12fb50c27b9425aefee45a7bcae44d.text: Wrote out instructions for AI helpers and user guides, then fixed spelling errors in them. This affects people reading the instructions or guides, not the software's actions. They would notice correct words like 'ability' instead of 'abiltity' in the text.

c32293cd44f11a690888b98370da25754305f351.text: The tool now skips fetching web pages listed inside its own setup file. This stops it from pulling in unwanted links when preparing project information. You would notice nothing, as this is a small internal fix.

c8b9d6f0c31158e22e143f44f8c538c7ed80464c.text: The command-line tool now shows a loading spinner faster, after just a fraction of a second instead of waiting a full second. It also keeps line breaks and indented text intact, so code snippets and lists look correct instead of squashed together. Additionally, the tool avoids crashing when it encounters missing or empty data while displaying information.

e2239c70237ed1e925c48d01e3f3209b5ea95463.text: The internal agent store now calculates weekly spending and unique user counts directly from live activity data. People viewing the store will notice that the default list order changes to show the most expensive agents from the last seven days first, and each card displays a new weekly usage summary.

dd11ea1898423928a22abd37b8a15fcd793b0521.text: The automated checks for the assistant's text-streaming feature were updated to match the current delivery method. This internal change ensures the safety net accurately verifies that messages and separators reach the screen, preventing false alarms during future updates.

dd049fdd7dadc0ca752c0355f5a73040171a110c.text: A small internal update ensures the assistant keeps a fully separate copy of its memory during automated tasks. This prevents accidental mix-ups where one task could wrongly change another's history. You likely won't notice anything directly, but it makes the system more reliable behind the scenes.

c9fda9fcc946fa948ecee730213f9296d66dbe95.text: The assistant now remembers files it found or changed, not just files it opened. This helps it keep track of your work better. The change is live and affects how the assistant understands your project context.

bf89ed5263bd37f73130630bdc6a410636bd159a.text: The team updated the automated checks that monitor how the assistant displays its progress when handling complex tasks. This internal maintenance ensures the system correctly reports when a task starts and finishes, matching recent changes to how information is streamed to the screen. You will not notice any difference in the assistant's behavior or performance today.

743f1d9eded33ab4cfc8c4490ad0666e9feda8fd.text: The system now always attempts to fill in blank spots in messages sent to the AI, even if no specific text is provided for those spots. Previously, it would skip these blanks entirely if the information was missing, potentially leaving confusing placeholder text visible. This ensures that empty fields are cleanly removed or left blank, preventing broken or messy messages from reaching the AI.

e42a4ab995a2e11ada6e24f7aa0fa6ba71f5a0a2.text: The assistant's internal instructions now use generic placeholders instead of specific tool names and formats. This helps the assistant avoid confusing real tools with fake ones when deciding how to act. Users will not notice any visible change, as this only adjusts how the system thinks behind the scenes.

42c21943893bbd62254ebc3682ca43daec04438f.text: The internal instructions for the chat assistant were shortened to remove repetitive warnings about tracking file changes and formatting requests. This helps the assistant follow rules more consistently when answering questions or editing files. The change is already active.

c27f169ca051f678a11de3039c8c1689d3ed62ac.text: The tool now measures the visible length of text lines more accurately to prevent them from wrapping awkwardly at the edges of the terminal window. It also ensures that internal cleanup processes only remove their own specific resize handlers, leaving other system functions untouched. These changes are live for internal users and result in cleaner, more stable text display during long sessions.

cd14fb30dda157962368080bdddfa8f88148e3d9.text: A small internal fix prevents the word 'undefined' from appearing in text displays like headings, lists, and code blocks. This ensures that if data is missing for these sections, they appear blank rather than showing error text. The change affects how text is formatted on screen, making the output cleaner and more professional.

046deb32c5f71317c3b57fc656e0864c174b99cd.text: The assistant no longer reads your personal computer startup settings, such as command line preferences. This small internal update reduces the amount of private information sent to the AI. You will not notice any difference in how the tool works.

eb5af8d7675aabbfb5941c8843db7b9f02bdf01b.text: The instructions for connecting the assistant to your own software now point to the correct tool. People who follow the guide to set up the assistant will no longer get an error about a missing package. This fix is live in the current documentation.

fbb18db7bde110275b486bb366b7f3dc260063f1.text: The website's top menu and bottom section now include a button that takes visitors to the project's code page on GitHub. This change is live today. People browsing the site will see a new GitHub icon and link they can click to view the source code.

bd3d070e1ba70c5dc57c5960882a1472c4c545a4.text: The guide now explains how to set up custom helpers for the coding assistant. This helps people who want to build their own tools or reuse existing ones. You will see clearer instructions on how to start this process.

ceb0a75a57367452510e51e058a5c74fe9c67b28.text: The public description of the AI assistant's testing process was updated to state that it evaluates performance on over 175 coding tasks, correcting a previous claim of over 200. This change affects anyone reading the project's main documentation page. Readers will see the accurate task count listed in the comparison section.

28af8887e283cc0f6ac818aa84b9e9d692e5a227.text: The written instructions for using the software were updated to show simpler ways to start tasks. People reading the online help will see fewer steps required to point the tool at a specific folder, making the guides easier to follow.

33d08de5b081f7d6ea1ed68f492a23a697207c44.text: The automated code review assistant was renamed and switched to a smarter model that searches deeper into the project's files. It now automatically finds related files and checks them from multiple angles before giving feedback. This internal tool change is live and improves the quality of automated reviews without requiring any action from the team.

a8168d89d8bcf02009eb65dc34fc99f45ddd8210.text: Choosing an assistant from the menu no longer switches the active conversation. Instead, it adds the assistant's name to the message box. This prevents the current chat history from being cleared unexpectedly.

c99899bb5db495c24994ba35b8bd79f9cf6b0688.text: The system stopped checking if an AI assistant was allowed to use specific tools before running them. This means assistants can now access any available tool, even if their settings previously restricted them. This change is live and affects how internal assistants execute tasks.

ec9b8a5dd57caba9ced3a53ac0473ed585f3ad66.text: Small internal fix to the documentation pages. On phones, tapping a section title to copy its link now shows a confirmation badge for three seconds, up from 1.5 seconds. Also, section titles with code snippets now wrap correctly on small screens instead of breaking the layout.

320b7ab6e8ba097f77606819c9cf59591835ed91.text: The internal planning assistant now uses a faster, more accurate model and can search through more files to understand the project context. It also follows the user's direct instructions more closely than its own initial plan. This change affects only internal agents and is live today.

163f1494a641f585c09c89c029aa6b930250a7a0.text: The instruction guide for building custom coding assistants was updated to show how to create a specific helper with its own name and personality. This helps people who are setting up their own tools to see exactly how to define these helpers. The change is just for the documentation, so it does not affect how the software currently works.

d79f7619c012ca1e54ad3e7d2261745942bfa906.text: The system now protects background task notes from being deleted when conversation history gets too long. This internal fix ensures that temporary helper agents keep their instructions, so they don't lose track of what they are supposed to be doing. Users won't see any immediate visual changes, but background tasks should run more reliably without forgetting their original goals.

08575fd718d278870b48f29ff93d46aefa483e73.text: A small internal safety adjustment was made to the automated system that checks code changes. This system now stops processing just before reaching its maximum capacity, leaving a five percent buffer. The change prevents the checker from failing due to running out of space. This affects only the internal testing process and is live today.

c38edb41f7993dba1831b85a550dbc0e55043e43.text: The AI assistant now skips saving tool results to the chat history when a specific setting is off. This keeps the conversation log cleaner and shorter. Regular users won't notice any change.

ed79f0b30210b762433b14e31960833a8af70509.text: A new line was added to the command's built-in help text. It shows how to generate sample agent files directly from the command line. This affects only the command-line tool itself. Users will see this extra example when they ask for help.

150007805900c05738188ccf169b33ff8045376c.text: The tool can now use a new AI model. Users who pick this model in their settings will see it as an option. The guide for building custom workflows moved key steps to the top so people find them faster.

573e46f9daef1ff68b684087db2e5aa80acb2386.text: The system now correctly recognizes specific short names for certain AI models, enabling them to save memory during long conversations. This change affects only users who select these specific models via those short names. If you use one of these models, you might notice slightly faster responses or lower costs, though the difference is small and internal.

5938d3024297c1ca6fec3c017885e10857dd2f4f.text: The internal system that checks the quality of code suggestions now uses a different service to access its AI models. This change helps avoid limits on how many times the system can ask for answers. Only the team running these quality checks will notice anything, and the results for regular users should stay the same.

3e422877010f0bf12f1098f08189797d6a560b43.text: The system now sends a clear signal when a specific document-generation task begins. This small internal update helps the interface correctly identify the start of the process, ensuring the agent's status is accurately tracked.

c926f0cbf3b7491a6f1e344aad805cab3786150e.text: The guide for building software assistants now shows a simpler example of analyzing text feelings instead of images. People reading the instructions will see a clearer way to connect the assistant to online data, replacing the previous picture-focused demonstration. This update is live in the documentation today.

097d63eaa87ccd502b8143b3fe12dc894556af39.text: The team updated the internal label for their coding assistant toolkit. This is a routine housekeeping step with no new features or fixes. Developers using the toolkit will see a slightly newer version number, but the tool's behavior remains exactly the same.

406dd98ffa42f4e0b3c3aeac34cb7840729aa091.text: The internal assistant now checks if a file exists before trying to read it, preventing errors from missing paths. It also switched to a different reasoning model for read-only tasks. These updates affect only the internal automation tools and are not visible to end users.

8ec216cfd8cc953adc0823987de24f31d55c74c3.text: A duplicate key for the Google AI service was removed from the internal setup. This change only affects the system's configuration files and does not impact the live service. Nothing will look or behave differently for anyone.

b9b229a6072d4d76b3df18935c42a937e1fa9fb0.text: The assistant now routes its requests for Google's Gemini models through a third-party service instead of contacting Google directly. This internal switch affects how the system processes text rewriting, file searching, and documentation lookups. You will likely not notice any change in speed or quality, as the underlying model remains the same.

6901c9c4d143b58847b876c126898f002cf2e4d8.text: The system now only copies files to the second location when specific template files change, ignoring other updates. This stops unnecessary background tasks from running on unrelated changes. The fix is active immediately and only affects internal automation, with no visible change for end users.

874971b99ff9342c809180788dfb9ff437f6b431.text: The instructions for using the tool were corrected to match its current setup. People reading the guide might have been confused by old terms for custom agents. Now, the guide accurately describes how to set up these agents.

7b82ec78d5763176acf743e51f04e13948b2d1aa.text: The code assistant now recognizes Windows computers and adjusts how it saves project changes. Previously, it used a method that only worked on Apple or Linux systems, causing errors for Windows users. Now, it writes the save command in a way Windows understands. This fix is live and prevents failed save attempts for Windows users.

f52ed20ac0b03ee49d866201607dc47f4c0499bd.text: The guide for building with this tool now shows how to watch progress updates from the very first step, rather than waiting for a later step. People reading the instructions will see the same simple example twice, making it easier to copy and paste. This is a small update to the written instructions only.

1bbf85f918f98463ef92034643164341ff9ba5c1.text: The automated tool that copies specific template files to a separate public repository was previously paused for debugging. This update removes the debugging mode and restores the automatic copying process using the correct access key. Users will not notice any immediate changes, as this is an internal maintenance fix to ensure the public template library stays up to date.

511534018dec7b7ae2bc3c5889cde63e375c4a0d.text: A small internal fix cleans up the text interface. When a person pastes multiple lines at once, the system now hides the repeating command symbols that used to clutter the screen. The normal symbols reappear automatically once the pasting stops. This change is live today.

c5670183c50cd176a211fa3b5791a987351e7f24.text: The internal testing tool now displays the specific task description and a clickable link to the code changes after completing an evaluation. This helps the internal team reviewing test results quickly identify which changes were tested and where to find them. The setup process also hides routine progress messages to reduce clutter in the logs.

fe49e6f8c4af3655f2676b7dd28421d97664083a.text: Deleted old, unused instructions that told the AI assistant how to behave and which tools to use. This is internal cleanup. Nothing changes for anyone today, and no one will notice anything.

0859093d95719d2f3c312ee718ac55c32ffdca10.text: The end-of-session message is now sent by the service the tool talks to, not printed by the command-line tool itself. If someone uses the tool in its output mode, the final message with the cost and which assistant was used still appears, but it arrives through the live connection. It is a small internal change and is live today.

995d5e269e196d96295ae6020db178718f5b63f5.text: A small internal safety fix for the tool that copies files between systems. It stops the copier from keeping a login key it does not need, and uses a different name when it posts updates. Normal users will notice nothing.

5cce7867142f30163d3fdb4e6f2a70f422119d8a.text: A small internal update reactivated a temporary remote access tool within the automated deployment process to help engineers investigate blocking issues. This change affects only the internal operations team, not external customers. Engineers would notice the automated system now allows interactive troubleshooting sessions during specific deployment steps, with a fifteen-minute safety limit.

a3a0eed769e93b41a159c422b2aea6797ceb5dbb.text: A small internal security fix removed a line from a background process that was accidentally printing the first few characters of a secret access key into system logs. This change does not affect how the software works for anyone. If you looked at the logs, you would simply see that the partial key is no longer displayed.

19bad4ba30660ac3413b24ac750f9e12789732da.text: The internal editing assistant can now take up to 25 actions before it must summarize, instead of 20. When it reaches that limit, it now collects the file changes it actually made from clearer records, so the summary should list successful edits more reliably. This is a small internal change, live in the editor.

a7ac818af6f9aa81ebece365873a822421f10e6e.text: The system now checks for a missing access key before trying to copy files to a shared storage area. The old method for using that key was corrected to match the storage area's requirements. A tool that let staff inspect a broken process was removed. These updates apply to the automated copying process, so staff will notice fewer confusing errors.

02344853f4f34e9dde1a248d9550cc16a147ef0b.text: The automated process that copied internal templates to a separate storage location has been paused. This change affects only the background system and fixes a blockage that prevented the website from updating. You will not notice any difference in the website's appearance or features.

26a93a855408c78025e1ef53df7e3bda586fe022.text: The automatic process that copies files to a separate location was failing because it was trying to send them to the wrong address. This fix corrects the destination, allowing the copies to succeed. Since this is an internal maintenance task, it does not change what you see in the main product.

034b52f03bfbaf7cdaf0b292c6088cd5d296ee03.text: An automated system that copies files to a separate location was updated to use a different security key. This internal fix ensures the copying process continues to work correctly. Regular users will not see any changes or notice any difference in their experience.

a9ca04b8a0da3dc5646552969c1b57709e3fa505.text: The automated process that copies files to a separate location now runs whenever any changes are made to the main project, rather than only when specific folders change. If this copying process fails, a temporary remote access window opens for the team to investigate the error. This internal tooling update affects only the maintenance team and is active immediately.

2952abb9dde8e89d899676a39e41e44145536af4.text: An internal automation tool now points to the correct folder for starter files. This fixes a broken link that prevented these files from being copied to a separate location. Regular users will not see any change on their screens.

78eab1e5b244f70a2238aada4ba8cb4fe4553641.text: The 'Lite' mode assistant now skips its built-in quality check step and uses a faster, simpler way to process requests. This change affects anyone using the Lite mode, making responses quicker but potentially less detailed or rigorous than before.

093de5b9e128dd35b8eaf616e7bdf184c0c1b562.text: This is a small internal maintenance change. An automatic copy step now shows the first ten characters of its private access value in the log instead of only saying whether the value exists. It also signs in to the copy destination in the expected way. People who watch these internal copy runs may see a short visible prefix of the private access value, and the change is live for the next run.

7cc677c2a299a34f680f541d5d94fc34e534e6d4.text: The scoring system for AI coding tests was updated to judge solutions only against the provided instructions. This prevents the system from marking down correct answers that lack extra features like tests or docs, which the AI was never asked to create. Internal evaluators will see fairer, more accurate scores for the AI's performance.

2d0bc7154793daea53cb4b79828b72e047072b22.text: A small internal fix ensures the agent selection menu now shows every available agent, not just a limited subset. This affects people using the command-line tool to manage agents. They will see a complete list of options when opening the menu.

1eef5bf54585e7ff8deeb5403b902fb1a6fcc3c7.text: The command menu now accepts 'agnet' and 'agnets' as shortcuts for managing agent templates. This small internal update helps people who mistype the command name. Users of the command-line interface will notice fewer errors when they accidentally use these alternate spellings.

738047948da8bafa663ee8dd22e2e59b133ab679.text: The internal system that grades automated coding tasks no longer scores how fast or efficient the code was. This change only affects the internal reports sent to the team who builds the tool. If they look at the email summaries, the 'Efficiency' score and 'Cost per Point' metric are gone, leaving only quality and completion scores.

73ba6801279b8482b646f55d0a0846323981057c.text: The tool now points to the correct location for its instruction manual. This affects people building software with this tool. They will see fewer errors about missing information when they use it.

375ac3d8a8093a24b304b474797c00d9d89fe3c0.text: A small internal layout fix corrected spacing in code example boxes on the documentation site. Readers viewing these examples will no longer see an unnecessary horizontal scrollbar on some screen sizes.

9e19fbf894b5f10371930ea53d5c7639c857589c.text: A tiny invisible mark was added to the end of the instruction guide that appears when you first set up the assistant. This change ensures the file follows standard computer rules for text files. You will not notice any difference in how the guide looks or reads.

8e2cecaf295f155d6c5ec1894dc757be51a460c8.text: The team's release rehearsal process now includes an automatic build check before simulating a software update. This change affects only the internal publishing workflow and is active today. Non-technical users will not notice any difference in the product itself.

9364db9653d1210879f1f7dc508b8be3bd734548.text: Small internal update. The test judge now checks if the work is fully done, including tests and docs. Only internal evaluators see this.

05f7587f6a80520989c64fe28c8910a77783005e.text: A small internal cleanup removed a helper tool used to make words singular or plural in developer debug messages. The debug output now simply says 'files' regardless of the number. This change affects only internal development logs and has no impact on how the software behaves for anyone else.

796a2a5971b0c45e630360f1e0f69eb34bdf3332.text: The tool's internal label was updated to match its latest release. This change affects only the software library used by developers building on this platform. Nothing visible changes for end users, as this is a minor administrative update to the codebase.

bd29c2bed79f3b2476277f51e4e5778fef4e0b3e.text: The instructions for connecting to the AI service now wrap the sample code in a dedicated startup block. This ensures the examples run correctly in more standard environments without needing extra configuration. The change affects only the documentation text, not the service itself.

fd01d8267659545f5826743424545c7610ca2a23.text: The version number for the Codebuff software toolkit was increased. This change does not affect how the toolkit works or what it can do. No users will notice any difference in behavior.

18a48d5e1a06d51a3825c5e3d9d6a745686e1446.text: The documentation page for setting up AI helpers now displays the starting command inside a neat, boxed card with a rocket icon, replacing a plain text block. This visual update applies only to the internal documentation site and is live today. Readers will notice the command looks like a distinct, polished button or card rather than raw text.

2ca05c66a2592ffc8ff059f3ac5040dc66923bf2.text: The automatic scoring system now sees the total dollar cost of each test run alongside timing data. This helps the system judge if a task was done efficiently. Internal reviewers might notice cost figures included in evaluation reports.

43ec3102480107f0f837840bafe08c699eca1fd1.text: The app now hides its internal connection error messages from the browser console unless detailed logging is turned on. This affects anyone using the service, cleaning up the developer view without changing what normal users see on screen.

de15d859394629a94bb7c44e107776bb94122867.text: Docs pages now color-code command and code examples to make them easier to read. This small visual change is live on the website. Visitors will notice the text looks clearer and more organized.

c32a36384842682ad1d7ef25f2d1e62b8e60b765.text: A small internal correction fixed where the toolkit looks for the result format used by custom tools. It affects people who use custom tools through the toolkit. They will not notice a new feature; the toolkit simply loads that part more reliably. It is live.

ecad4a3decacc57e3f282a29ebb95c7e300a55da.text: The automated email sent to internal reviewers after code tests now lists the exact dollar cost and time spent for each test run. This change is active immediately. Recipients will see new lines in the email subject and body showing average cost per run, total budget used, and a detailed breakdown of expenses for each test group.

77b060911448e40458034948f955dd521353dc99.text: A background setting for the assistant's model list was corrected to match the actual list used by the system. This internal fix ensures the software accurately recognizes which models are available. Users will not notice any visual changes or new features from this update.

02996cd58b1a38df836194073a3f9dbe9bf5ac08.text: The analytics tool now records the correct completion status for terminal commands. Previously, the system failed to capture this specific result data. This internal fix ensures accurate reporting on command outcomes. End users will notice no visible difference.

3d8f7b75f56b6c5d4630fe9807b52bb2830fe6dc.text: The internal system that checks how well AI coding assistants perform now tracks the money and time each test takes. This change affects only the employees running these quality checks. If they look at the results, they will see average cost and duration numbers added to their reports, alongside the existing quality scores.

4ce916cb53ff52e8e5744ae41e72f03ee56e408a.text: The software's internal quality checks no longer expect a fixed limit of twelve steps for the assistant. Instead, they now automatically match whatever limit the system actually uses. This change only affects the testing process and is not a feature available to end users.

234f95f91a19ccacd0567ecd1b3647cba28f2d2b.text: The limit on how many actions the assistant can take in one task now uses a single shared setting instead of two separate numbers. This affects the background testing system and the assistant's main connection point. You will not see any change in how the assistant behaves, as this is an internal cleanup.

5ab58c3f0247fba60a2a89e3eb2fe4d3a8fff883.text: The system stopped writing small, repetitive notes about cost calculations into its internal records. This change affects only the hidden logs that support staff read, not the main program. A person looking at the system's output will see fewer cluttered entries, making it easier to find important information.

c5338b079aa0319f21dc0fa68f8f7c4003ec3d4b.text: The system now sends the assistant's final answer as a single, standard package instead of a loose pile of separate parts. This change is internal plumbing that ensures the answer displays correctly across all apps. You will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves or speaks today.

048bf594aca2b45cea30481bbadd2fdcf1455da0.text: The limit on how many times the assistant can act before stopping is now consistently set to 25 everywhere. Previously, different parts of the system used conflicting limits of 12 or 40, causing unpredictable behavior. If you run the assistant, it will now reliably stop after 25 actions unless you manually change the setting.

875deb4b45b35556f32c131b989a028e77f36fd7.text: The system now records who created six specific thinking assistants. This internal update does not change how the assistants work. Users see no difference.

ef53dba9eb42f6f2a6d30bf39716bb2c5ae31c9e.text: A small internal update crossed out old login details for a shared computer in the team's notes. This affects only staff members who might have tried to use those specific accounts to access the machine. They will now see the old passwords marked as invalid, with a note confirming that access via those details no longer works.

940603121fe01781a65343348e9a187dc69c7603.text: The system now correctly identifies where to find the rules for checking new assistant setups. This small internal fix ensures the software can properly load these validation rules when creating or editing agents. No visible changes for end users, but it prevents potential errors in the background.

ae5c7311d4cad4e9f4ae4ac8d92ef8ee82cbb2b4.text: The system now avoids sending specific 'stop' instructions when using the grok-code-fast model, preventing it from rejecting the request. This small internal fix affects only this specific model. Users will not see any changes in the interface, but the model will now respond correctly instead of failing.

f1ca0081d2611880668eafe846e91e9f96a1b28f.text: When someone stops a task that requires their input, the system now reports the result as an empty list instead of an empty text string. This small internal fix helps other parts of the software handle the cancellation correctly. You won't see any visual changes, but the system is less likely to get confused by the interruption.

7ed7df84f61b9005335e70c0832624136e40fb7d.text: Secret login details for internal company accounts were deleted from a public guide. This protects company data from unauthorized access. Regular users will not notice any changes to the software.

abb844f031249653287d333e3bdd455c4aca35ce.text: Internal automation steps previously skipped safety checks on tool inputs; now they enforce them. This affects only backend internal tool execution. Non-programmers will notice nothing, as the change only tightens validation for automated internal processes.

b133712e7c3c310c96fb3228a82bdc71a2983774.text: A small update lets people who build tools with this service see the final answer an AI agent produces, instead of just knowing the task finished. It also makes specifying a project folder optional and allows adding extra background details when starting a task. These changes are live now for developers using the library.

7fd14d1556b60aa5488858b150a8428c0355afd9.text: The internal tool that tracks monthly spending now displays names and email addresses for the top ten users, instead of just anonymous numbers. This helps staff identify heavy users quickly. The change is live and affects only the reports viewed by internal teams.

6ca447150510855e9b41813a4da1f13b3ea608a7.text: The system now accepts any format of conversation history instead of checking if each message has specific labels and text. This prevents errors when setting messages, allowing the assistant to receive varied inputs without blocking. Users might notice fewer interruptions when the assistant tries to update its memory or context.

e00a1e06009e7eb2f7f418a9296140633d181869.text: Internal tool steps now skip a strict format check, allowing raw data to pass directly. This affects automated background processes, not people typing prompts. You will notice nothing.

33e23801370cb00e7d4dbb58e875492087b73b78.text: The license for the developer toolkit changed from a restrictive private status to a permissive open-source one. This affects people who build software using this specific toolkit. They can now legally copy, modify, and distribute the toolkit's code without needing special permission from the original creators.

5aca4d9c7c0c1802ddc96ad312f0b44e6cd9e219.text: The automated nightly testing process now runs more tasks at the same time. This makes the tests finish faster. The change is internal and live today. You will not see any difference in the app.

11ddecd052ee57018e7fc77b93f704732caab76f.text: A duplicate message was removed from the internal system logs. This cleanup affects only the support team reading those logs. They will see one less repeated line when tracking user input.

d9ff4b06d44698241aea455e6ba097906ef9aa9e.text: A small internal fix corrected how the system checks if a background task started successfully. Previously, successful tasks were mistakenly shown as failures in the console output. This change ensures the display now accurately reflects whether a task is running or not.

d853317e31570975cdd20ae4112be189ace1a1bc.text: A small internal update lets staff choose which assistant model to test. Previously, the testing tool always used a fixed, default model. Now, testers can specify a different model when they run evaluations. This change is not visible to regular customers.

ae7bedbbd480b89e8ce8e152c5328766b5d09e82.text: The command-line tool now treats a logout attempt with an expired or invalid token as a success, rather than showing a scary error message. This affects anyone using the tool who tries to log out twice or after their session has already ended. They will no longer see confusing failure alerts, just a quiet confirmation that they are logged out.

fdd3f221a877cdc55a321cdd7829f2a2d217e2a6.text: The automatic overnight quality checks now have more time before they are stopped. This is active now and affects only the internal team that runs those checks. They may see fewer overnight checks ending early when a run needs extra time.

5aed73e0eec402149ee94c56ec5c47fffa660d20.text: The version label for the Codebuff software toolkit increased. This change does not alter how the toolkit works or what it does. Users will not notice any difference in behavior.

1177729cc42b278ee64bfd68f73d0ab5cc3fd62a.text: A small internal cleanup removed an extra note that printed the full converted message content while the assistant was preparing messages. It affects people who watch the program’s internal activity, not normal users. The change is live today, and they would notice fewer cluttered records in the running output.

cd5eb8dbf2a3758f4f676093c2db1f2f76014f5b.text: The system's internal checks were updated to expect extra separator messages when a sub-agent replies. This is a small, internal maintenance task that ensures the software's own testing remains accurate. Users will not see any change in how the assistant behaves or how messages appear.

abd66bda3d2e0248408b51d66e441f99f7869239.text: A small internal update made a ready-made usage-tracking tool available to the shared building blocks of the app. No one will notice anything today. It only prepares the app for later changes.

da474825cb8e031deb16d2d81ac46b9c4281d0ec.text: Internal testing tools now record errors instead of stopping when a tool call fails. This change affects only the team running automated tests, so regular users will not notice any difference in the product's behavior.

de2d2380c074572ed332d5cb81ee7d2b69c90496.text: When a file update fails, the system now records the error details more clearly for the support team. This internal cleanup helps engineers diagnose issues faster. Users will not notice any change in how the software behaves.

d2192cf8639ebcecf8d3e68a0a6b548cdba7f469.text: When a request to change a file fails because the computer cannot find the exact spot to make the edit, the system now reports the failure as a regular message instead of stopping the entire process. This keeps the assistant running smoothly so it can try again or explain the problem, rather than crashing.

1d7bf55bcc427808e96678fbbab73ab3087ec01d.text: The team added a small, invisible note to the system's internal diary whenever someone types a message. This change only affects the engineers who look at the server logs to troubleshoot issues. Regular people using the software will not notice any difference, as the actual behavior of the application remains completely unchanged.

1f4061f2d40dc0cb129feb4b0f2e084df4a051d6.text: Small internal fix. Developers running several project copies at once now reliably use their specific settings, like custom ports, instead of getting overridden by older saved values. You would notice fewer conflicts when starting the software locally.

9742a0a8dccd1d750dbb8fad1d1647be43409cc3.text: The system now shows live updates for any single assistant task, not just specific ones. It adds clear start and end labels to these updates. This helps people track progress without seeing cluttered or missing information. The change is live.

9f4f26545c911b5dcb860eb774cbfac43f1fa61f.text: A small fix corrected a misspelled web address used by the software to find its main server. This affects the tool's ability to connect to the correct online service. If the address was wrong, the tool might fail to start or communicate properly.

0efeedbe8c1cb6f2aca0c99effc40a0d0b9c9889.text: The code evaluation system now starts a fresh connection for each test run instead of reusing the same one. This internal change ensures every test gets a clean setup and closes its connection afterward. Non-developers will not notice any difference.

a9ff22ff4fe1c03e32c3bcb5475bf0b508641381.text: A small internal fix corrected how a file finds another file. This stops a background check from failing. Regular users will see nothing different.

3ab02d5c226224e860018e1fa2b27d78eec69a85.text: A small internal fix corrected how the testing system identifies specific background actions. Previously, these actions were mistakenly recorded as if they were real user requests. Now, they are properly hidden from the test reports. This change affects only the internal quality checks and does not alter the experience for end users.

a77c87dba037907d63c95bc2c098367fa65601f9.text: The team swapped their own hand-written comparison tools for a standard library that already handles this work. This cleanup affects only how the system internally checks data settings, not how the assistant behaves. Nothing changes for anyone using the software today.

bc7aab720aeae87e38ce76e5b50b05d3d849a17a.text: A small internal update standardizes how a specific AI thinking tool identifies its source. Another change adjusts a hidden setting for experimental cost modes. Users will not notice any difference.

0c135314b791f927b4e2a3e55a0e9d12a815a341.text: A small internal cleanup removed a fake helper that was no longer being used by the testing system. This change does not affect how the application works or what regular users see. It simply makes the internal test setup cleaner and easier to maintain.

98f4e7b93c14e93d9259202c583942543e63c662.text: The assistant's editor mode now handles up to twenty steps instead of fifteen, allowing it to finish more complex tasks before stopping. When the assistant reaches its limit, it will now provide a plain text summary of its progress rather than using a specific output format. This internal change is live today and affects users interacting with the Base2 agent configuration.

d310a1da69393a91e18c009964025c4cc54700ed.text: The assistant now stops adding explanatory notes inside code files unless you specifically ask for them. It also cuts out chatty updates while it searches for information, delivering only the final answer without summaries or follow-up questions. These changes apply to the built-in tools used by the assistant, not to your own code or projects.

0a565ba2fd828697f63a1666d4336967a2fb3d19.text: The system now decides whether to store conversation data for faster reuse at the exact moment it prepares the message for the AI, rather than checking later. This ensures the reuse feature activates correctly only when the specific AI model supports it. You might notice slightly faster responses when continuing long conversations with compatible models.

3f1dc4edc04175607be6144602133fe45182c03d.text: The limit on how many actions an AI agent can take during a single task was raised from 25 to 40. This change is live now. Users might notice that complex tasks are less likely to stop early due to hitting the action limit, allowing the agent to complete more steps.

d378eecee8ec9136a58f5371624ea8c51a70984e.text: This small internal update cleans up the test logs by hiding long technical details from the screen. It affects only the engineers running these tests. They will see a shorter, clearer summary instead of a cluttered output, but the test results and behavior remain exactly the same.

9c17f38817bbadd8830df8289915003fce9b8081.text: A small internal update removed an old safety check from the system's testing tools. This check used to force file changes to happen one at a time to prevent conflicts, but it is no longer needed. Regular users will not notice any difference, as this change only affects how the software is tested behind the scenes.

e4b82f2d61967aa88a2658d6672e40d3f96a0d01.text: The system now hides internal step details when saving test results. This prevents large, unnecessary data from cluttering the output logs. Only internal tools are affected; no customer-facing changes.

b18932b4b7c3d1e2b66fa0ceac9c382ece0bd330.text: The text box inside the pop-up window that asks for confirmation now automatically empties itself when the window closes. This change ensures the box is always clean when opened again, regardless of how the window was dismissed. It is an internal cleanup that fixes a rare case where leftover text might have remained visible.

c563016ebe857b18e8b013cd94480b0d886d263c.text: The system now places its temporary memory marker only on the very last piece of text in a conversation, rather than tagging the entire message. This helps the AI service save costs and speed up responses by caching just the right amount of information. Most people will not notice any difference, but the AI might respond slightly faster or more cheaply.

2a4a206c48d09a29bf24d0f9a20faefcb7e97f19.text: A small internal correction fixed a broken link between two shared parts of the software. This change affects the underlying code structure rather than visible features. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the software behaves or looks.

13e5f01636d1faf4e9a9cd2f62f469b1ab0fb924.text: The internal assistant now stops writing long, repetitive wrap-up paragraphs after finishing a task, keeping responses brief unless a single sentence is needed. It also skips preliminary research steps for simple requests, going straight to editing files. These changes apply only to the internal automated coding assistant, so external users will not see any difference.

2e6102cc872545c0d074083a07500383beeef66d.text: The system now automatically stops any single code-checking task that runs longer than thirty minutes. This change affects only the internal tools used to test software updates, not regular customers. If a test gets stuck, it will now fail and free up space for other tests instead of blocking the entire queue forever.

b1c932d3ae4a39eef370a42f26af09a0cced29c0.text: The assistant's instructions for launching multiple helpers were updated to clarify that they run at the same time and separately. If you need one helper to finish before another starts, you must now launch them one by one. This is a minor internal wording change that helps the assistant avoid making mistakes when coordinating several tasks.

3656683d7651195e4cc1864e405d32b7ac19d1cd.text: Developers corrected how the system labels its internal message records, ensuring it uses the standard format. This is a minor technical fix for the code's structure. Users will not notice any changes.

653c32d27e6381fca316eb93fb06bf392342b0a6.text: The system now cleans up login records more carefully when you sign out. It ensures that old access keys are fully removed and any related device tracking data is reset. You will not see a visible change, but your account security is maintained more reliably during logout.

ed219d95f7545ae4d8625d0ea5e45d91cf3f63ab.text: The coding assistant's connection tool now lets people get their access pass directly from the website and add their own helper commands. This update is live for anyone using the assistant's external connection features. People will see new options to grab their access key and add custom tools.

ae64084bdbcd643a79633f8cfa8d055be46fcac6.text: The test system now asks the AI model directly for its next instruction, instead of routing that request through an internal connection tool. This is a small internal cleanup for the team running automated code checks. Regular users will see no difference in the product.

466a687e9c749e65862c670f434c21391a9e382c.text: When a tool takes too long to respond, the system now reports the delay as a message instead of crashing. This keeps the assistant running smoothly for internal users. You would notice fewer unexpected stops when tools are slow.

c28e7b1820d0657418acc4f285ea6d80b2edc8a8.text: Two small internal changes. The research helper can now read files directly, but remains read-only and will not offer code changes. The editing helper now only reports changes that actually succeeded, hiding failed attempts from the final summary.

43c739b354b8e516e4486cf2558a7c3c8a0f0762.text: The instructions for using the Codebuff service changed. Instead of installing a separate login tool, you now create an account on the website and copy a secret key. You must paste this key into your program settings to connect. This affects anyone setting up the service for the first time today.

70eef53debcc406accb01d6b24f70df38fa264b7.text: The system now limits the text it saves from user inputs to the first 100 characters. This reduces clutter in internal records, making it easier for support staff to read. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the application works.

f6731aa54fd5f414e9c9d148276feebb65bf232e.text: The document-reading tool now grabs twice as much text by default, pulling 20,000 tokens instead of 10,000. This change is live today. Users will notice the assistant retrieves and processes significantly longer documents without needing to manually adjust settings.

6032016de28fabc85399c603fd51e1bfc8ff129a.text: The system now tracks spending for each assistant separately instead of mixing everything into one total. People who use multiple assistants at once will see individual credit costs listed next to each assistant's name in the command-line interface.

88e41fc12e11640490384eec7417c1f97588e79d.text: The internal system that checks how well the assistant works now ignores a specific background step where it updates its own memory. This change keeps the test results cleaner by removing clutter from the final report. It only affects the tools used by the team to measure performance, so regular users will see no difference in how the assistant behaves.

57f0d403bc1b0ef1e365250d45cce469d1853bb1.text: Two internal helper tools, the 'scout' and the 'planner', now use a different artificial intelligence model to do their work. This change swaps out the previous Google models for an OpenAI model. Users will not see any visual changes, but the background reasoning for these specific tasks is handled by a new provider.

48bced48506177dfe8170f46a138fdc18811097c.text: A small internal fix stopped random errors when checking the automatic credit top-up feature. The tests now properly simulate the logging system, preventing false failures. Customers will not notice any change, as this only helps developers keep the feature reliable.

e3b8150c100550555473d49f6bb6a2e8a284fa54.text: The system now checks if an assistant is allowed to use a specific tool before trying to run it. If the tool is missing, the system stops and records a clear error message instead of failing quietly. This helps support staff find problems faster, but customers will not see any changes.

bba8333cc83d2193e71d39cbe23fad873e5f70b9.text: A small internal update changes how the AI editor reports its status when it runs out of steps. Instead of writing a free-form summary, it now fills out a standard form. This helps the system capture progress data reliably, though regular users won't see a visual change.

ccb934efb2f26f8c1f85e0baa24cc52d21294136.text: The internal testing system now automatically uses your existing login credentials if a specific test key is missing. This only affects the private tools developers use to check the assistant's performance, not the main product. You will notice no changes in the app itself.

e3b921fb1f45cee450366c1857f317c4aa700367.text: The system now runs a setup step to download required files before testing a specific project. This helps internal tests run smoothly, but customers will not see any difference.

3940bc5bf3da0fce00aec33aa5dcbac74ee4a769.text: A small internal update changed how the main assistant handles complex tasks. It now trusts its helper programs to plan and do the work instead of checking every detail itself. It also stops after ten steps to give a quick summary, preventing endless loops.

02b675499b82ee25ee56883fba8f11c0e23317f6.text: The internal search assistant switched to a faster, lighter brain to answer questions more quickly. This change helps the system find information without making any edits to the actual files. It is live today for the internal team, though the speed boost is subtle and mostly felt as quicker responses.

87c3cc7a100f195cf54de5f8299843acc86049d4.text: The internal code-editing assistant now knows it should only handle small or medium tasks alone, or follow a detailed plan for larger ones. It also stops talking immediately after reporting its work, preventing unnecessary extra summaries. This is a small internal adjustment to how the tool behaves, affecting only the automated editing process.

45903e821e643794b1b06143aad1e97636d8df00.text: The internal assistant now asks all necessary questions at the start to avoid repeating work, and it uses a specific tool to report changes instead of just writing a final message. This affects internal users of the coding assistant. They would notice fewer redundant steps and clearer, structured summaries of what was modified.

1df6ce209f2c5387d3e0fda01c81aa7c2dc296b8.text: The profile security page now filters out long-lived access keys before showing the list of active sessions, so only browser and command-line logins appear. This change is live for all users viewing their security settings.

f67bfb8e16211d8aa1ff308ad50cf1d031a3c53d.text: The AI assistant now skips unnecessary thinking steps when it updates its internal notes, plans, or outputs. This change makes the assistant respond faster and use fewer resources while working on tasks. It affects all users interacting with the assistant, though they won't see a visual change, just quicker replies.

0094be01347708db547e416e30d97909d0cfe9fd.text: Added a translation layer between internal chat history and external AI services. Currently a direct pass-through with no visible change. Future formatting updates will apply automatically without breaking existing connections.

5b71cc05c54a3e992f6280aca02f9af35af0b838.text: The evaluation system now properly stops all background tests when a user cancels them. Previously, pressing the stop button might leave some tests running in the background, wasting computer resources. Now, all tests stop immediately when you cancel, and the system cleans up properly.

5197a531b9409439ad93600a00e89158be331ae6.text: The system now uses a single, standard method to check if a person is logged in before letting them manage their access keys, replacing older, separate checks for web browsers and command-line tools. This change is internal and affects only the security logic behind the scenes; users will not notice any difference in how the feature works, as the login requirements remain the same.

83db70c36f9187592256af5cd7782e2b7d758c51.text: The side menu on the documentation pages now stays in place slightly later when scrolling, and its position shifts up a bit. Tables on the profile pages for API keys, referrals, and security now have rounded corners and can be scrolled sideways if they are too wide. The bottom of the website now shows community links on more pages.

921a9dd7cedb6e3960e0634ccfed1392bfe65202.text: The system now uses a cheaper, simpler tool to check if terminal commands are safe. This change affects the background process that reviews commands before execution. Users will not see any visual changes, but the system may process these safety checks at a lower cost.

630fab418b2ab2b8c5f5e30702ff71321f4bb30a.text: A small internal change fixes how the documentation and profile pages look on phones. The navigation menu now stays pinned to the bottom of the screen, and wide blocks of text can be scrolled sideways without pushing the rest of the page off-screen. The sidebar on the documentation pages now stays in view only after scrolling past the top header.

2b90ca3ebfd5ac5e18391024c3a9728b1351185c.text: A small internal cleanup removed a duplicate security check from the session deletion process. This change affects only the system's backend and requires no action from you. You will notice no difference in how the application works.

53c29980b8ba74855d7e0261996f51aebe900f7f.text: The server now waits thirty minutes before forcing a stop when told to shut down. This change affects internal systems, not customers. No one will notice any difference in how the software works.

ece4c4eeccde7d28b329a9b1e4cbf98bb03c4e01.text: The internal system that helps the main assistant manage other helper programs no longer forces a strict step-by-step routine. Instead, it lets the main assistant decide when to use planners, editors, or reviewers based on what the task actually needs. This change is live today and affects how the assistant organizes complex requests behind the scenes.

b821dbafc27aa028944e94613927765c31d1e50c.text: The internal planning assistant now routes requests to the correct model instead of an outdated one. It also requires a planning step for complex tasks before editing begins. This change affects only the internal coding tools and is active immediately.

1b4978feea857b27c5598daf0233612b35cfbaa7.text: The assistant stopped writing extra internal notes while it looks for files, reads files, saves a result, and prepares search instructions. This affects the team that watches the assistant’s activity, not customers. They will see fewer repeated records in the activity log, while the assistant’s actions and results stay the same. The change is live.

bd85fa06b5d6adc6457dfcf033579f8d2e51d477.text: A small internal fix ensures the system correctly stops running a sequence of tasks once the AI finishes its part. This prevents unnecessary or incomplete steps from executing afterward. Internal tooling is affected; regular users will not notice any change.

901ca6899cbc872fa49a34441ff149cd456d88a8.text: The internal review assistant now spends less time thinking before giving feedback. This change makes reviews faster but may result in less detailed suggestions. The adjustment is live and affects how the automated review tool processes requests.

0c809f7c46ee2979c87f1042e4cb3163c2493ba9.text: A small internal correction fixed how the system identifies specific types of login sessions. It now correctly marks sessions that have a unique device identifier and a long expiration date as 'cli' sessions. This change is live but affects only how these sessions are categorized in the background, so users will not notice any difference in their experience.

0ff0cf5a75037625ba733bd9066d586fe6fd5364.text: The system now counts words more accurately when text includes unusual symbols. This internal adjustment prevents errors during processing. Staff will see smoother performance, with no visible changes to the interface.

b359e568dff8dcb23b90b1488b191576da8825e7.text: The system now accepts mixed text and images in chat messages instead of only plain text. This applies to the underlying structure for AI agents. It is internal plumbing and has no visible effect on the interface today.

20174678342a313b374697d6b9fa2d706fefb35b.text: A small note was added to the code that controls how the system runs tasks. This change was made only to test if the software updates correctly. It does not change how the system works or what it does.

1e1c59120f7f451fea7d048e4687cfbb9c317c93.text: The team fixed a hidden error in the automatic checks that test how the assistant creates sub-tasks. This change only affects the internal testing system and does not change how the assistant behaves for anyone.

ce6025467273f41d5cddf171d9fd287dca57fcd1.text: The internal planning assistant now always uses a specific high-effort thinking model instead of guessing which one to use. This change affects only the behind-the-scenes coding assistant, not regular users. Nothing visible will change for customers today.

4afa6da12eb885834b4ce6a4b4a951da09253784.text: A small internal update ensures that when a program step fails, the error message is now recorded in the assistant's conversation history. This change helps internal tools debug issues by providing more context, but it does not affect what customers see or how the assistant behaves.

aaa5ff99477225fbd40e8e6324ad3ab559396213.text: A small internal fix corrected a hidden error in the web interface's text animation. This change does not alter how the page looks or feels for visitors. It only ensures the code follows strict formatting rules.

572a6be6c629b26e453415738c14a1aed3798ef4.text: This small internal update fixes how a helper tool shares its progress with the main assistant. Previously, the helper's status updates were ignored, causing the main assistant to miss real-time feedback. Now, the helper correctly passes its status updates directly to the main assistant, ensuring the workflow stays synchronized.

ced6aa30219243e2304681e623d3134977354137.text: Internal cleanup. Test checks tightened to match exact error message formats. Developers see stricter validation in automated tests. No user-facing changes.

aa1d37418a39f6e98eb01aee009c4b79062841dc.text: Internal tooling now automatically tidies up code formatting and import order only when files actually change, avoiding unnecessary rewrites. This affects developers' local workflow by making their code-checking tools more precise and less noisy, though end users will notice no difference.

f79f1b75132acd589995ecf7adf2a44901453491.text: A small internal fix stops the system from crashing when it launches a helper task without extra settings. Before this, missing settings caused errors; now they are treated as empty. This helps the background assistant run more reliably.

4a977e1da6526fee1fbec27c7adbf6b03a6a85c7.text: A minor internal update added a record of how many steps are finished before a task begins. This change affects only the system's backend logs, not the visible interface. No user will notice any difference in how the software behaves.

49132b99b0c133860cea38b62c4bafe6a0d676e3.text: A small internal fix adjusts how the system handles replacing text when multiple matches are allowed. Previously, it ignored specific formatting rules during these operations, causing errors in the backend. This change ensures the system correctly processes these replacements, though regular users will not notice any difference.

05fa4aa455136cec4d95383868f095d8f9bd247e.text: The system now records fewer routine details in its internal activity logs. This change affects only the technical staff who monitor these logs, not the end users. Staff will notice cleaner log files with less repetitive noise, making it easier to spot important issues.

466c455d78fea41a66873789406f843560bbe4d4.text: The tool now listens for server errors during prompts. Previously, these errors caused the system to wait indefinitely. Now, it stops waiting and reports the problem immediately. This affects anyone using the software development kit.

498c89b1a43c97cbf97df366d5ee615e50383f1c.text: A small internal cleanup fixed a broken label in the documentation for the text generation settings. This affects only the written instructions for a specific AI model provider, not the software itself. No one will notice a change in how the product works.

65a8db449db3809e03ada37ec516914e545f762b.text: A small internal fix stops the system from accidentally deleting your instructions when it cleans up old messages. If you use the feature that runs a helper task inside your main chat, you will no longer see your original request disappear or leftover temporary notes clutter the conversation.

bc04df62c7aaf1201e61e5588044f22eef564b2e.text: The system now records more detail when it runs a specific internal task. Support staff can see the full set of instructions used, not just a reference number. This helps them diagnose issues faster. No changes to how the software works for end users.

c59351ec41cab33bcb4535910d6be3bf3cd01f2a.text: The software now finds its internal parts using a simpler naming rule. This fixes a hidden glitch that could stop the tool from loading in some setups. You will not notice any new features, but the tool will run more reliably.

00ed17e9cd503aaa66cc502fc402c3c502902968.text: The AI assistant now refuses to edit a file if the text it wants to change appears more than once. This prevents accidental overwrites of the wrong section. If this happens, the assistant will ask for a longer, unique piece of text to target the specific spot.

7acf918dcddb0a623710ba35082eca31ca0ac68f.text: The assistant now uses a safe default setting when starting a specific background task, preventing potential errors if no custom instructions are provided. This change affects only the internal system's reliability, not the features or performance you see. You would not notice any difference in how the assistant responds or behaves.

6106bf7416a58fc36e2e2180ebdb86dd9658540a.text: The tool stopped working because it looked for a type definition file in the wrong format. Developers fixed the file extension so the tool can read it correctly. This update is live and ensures the software builds without errors.
