2c0e585b275840a69052df127bce5defc5ebf18f.text: A tool for adding custom actions to the assistant now requires a written description. The default behavior also changed so that using a custom action now stops the assistant's current step, whereas before it continued. Developers building integrations must update their code to match these new rules.

c5c546abac213b43b02a44e6488a8116e04b26d6.text: The software now automatically includes specific search-pattern files when it prepares its code for release. This affects the tooling used to understand code structure. Users will notice fewer errors when the tool tries to read these patterns, as the necessary files are now guaranteed to be present.

3842eba2a9c4cf5c59779d475c9d182b92d7fa08.text: A small packaging fix makes sure the tool's map files are included when the software is downloaded. This affects people building apps with the toolkit. They would notice that the code reader now works correctly out of the box.

686e581799bbadecea340e54e102ca2837c812b5.text: The system now checks if an assistant is allowed to start another assistant by looking at the specific version required, rather than just matching the name. This means an assistant can successfully start a newer version of a helper that its configuration allows, instead of failing because the names were not an exact match. This is a small internal fix and is live today.

d9bdc235bfc28d405c9051f360e5889ff2c31402.text: The internal assistant now defaults to launching separate helper tasks instead of running them inside the main conversation thread. This prevents the chat history from becoming cluttered with background processing details. Only internal staff using the agent tools will notice slightly cleaner conversation logs.

48dbd251d56a5b9e1a5a225d472fc1490cf7de66.text: A small internal correction was made to the rules that check if the system's dynamic agent templates are built correctly. This ensures the software can properly recognize and use a wider variety of tool names during its internal checks. Developers will see fewer error messages when verifying the code, but regular users will not notice any difference in how the application works.

f07e8f30470ae9041baebdcbe1ae3ccf7ce964cc.text: This update adds written instructions explaining how to ask the assistant to spend more time thinking before answering. It affects people who build their own custom assistants. If they look at the guide, they will see new examples showing how to set thinking effort to low, medium, or high.

3010303cb12101d62bdce70ed5c34520780a74ad.text: The assistant now hides its internal thought process when a specific setting is turned on. This is a small internal update. Most people will not notice any change unless they are using the assistant with that setting enabled, in which case the step-by-step reasoning will no longer appear.

d09d4774246ba3f251b78c7f13a40a984753381e.text: The system no longer demands reasoning settings for every agent template. This helps internal builders avoid errors when creating templates without those specific options. Nothing changes for end-users today.

7133b2f649a9e3311b571632646c6f2e3a93793b.text: When the assistant tries to create a helper worker, it now checks the request against a list of allowed workers by breaking the name into its parts. This means the assistant can find a match even if the request leaves out the creator or the version, instead of requiring the full name to match exactly. The change is internal and affects how the assistant finds workers to help with tasks.

f2a7d15f5ca801f2139496acfe7800dd7c51c926.text: The code editor library stopped checking for a required helper program when starting up. This change affects developers using the library to build tools. They will notice that the library loads faster and no longer fails immediately if the helper program is missing from their computer.

abc2602ba7df9873f05f1b6ab88caf02f7af5a88.text: The software team updated the label on the toolkit that lets other programs connect to Codebuff. This is a routine housekeeping step with no new features or fixes. Nothing changes for anyone using the service today.

a914f537d153bc0c7967231c2e911515022a5daa.text: The system previously had a fixed limit on how much text it could process at once. This update allows the limit to be adjusted, rather than staying stuck at the previous amount. This change is internal and does not affect how the software looks or works for people using it today.

acc61e3c1e835d7b8cccecc9206b82610f86b195.text: The system now matches saved assistant profiles using their unique internal identifier instead of the name typed by the user. This prevents loading an old or incorrect profile if a name was reused or changed. The fix applies to all published assistants and is live now.

91a9d936f55f85cdf8d5ee357fae8a78b9baa364.text: The documentation sidebar now has soft edges at the top and bottom that appear only when you scroll past the first or last item. A thin, custom scrollbar replaces the default browser bar. This visual polish applies to the documentation navigation on the live site.

8ebf7637f295f2dc14d8bb2d9b10b1e847410674.text: The software's internal label was updated to a newer number. This change does not alter how the tool works or what it does. Users will see no difference in performance or features.

19bd7164da35526b4cfcc1117edad79e4c2f54d1.text: The system now checks the data sent to custom tools against a strict rulebook before passing it along. This ensures the tool only sees the exact information it expects, ignoring extra internal details. Developers building these tools will notice their code receives cleaner, validated data, preventing errors from unexpected inputs.

582891870f26b9fc499527a009946fea0134a78c.text: A small internal update fixes how the navigation menu on the documentation website behaves when you scroll. The menu now stays perfectly aligned on the left side of the screen without shifting or hiding behind other elements. This only affects the web documentation pages and improves the visual consistency while reading.

4c4b2ec64c3e14e1143e5372e719f7949e1d2abe.text: The toolkit now allows the AI assistant to use custom functions defined by the user, such as reading images or performing specific calculations. This update includes clear examples in the guide showing how to set up these functions. The feature is available immediately for anyone using the latest version of the toolkit.

b132de6aa8ab904338a5cc3479ec30d9dd1e1e9b.text: Agent templates gained a field to control how much internal thinking the AI performs. This setting is now live and replaces previous fixed defaults for specific models. Users building agents can notice changes in response depth or cost when they adjust this setting.

c3980e0c4d91cd62081f361d57730807f994ee25.text: The internal guide now explains that main assistants should manage workflow steps, while specialized reviewers only check specific details. This helps people designing assistants avoid copying human job titles and instead focus on controlling information flow. It is a documentation update for internal builders, so regular users will not notice any changes.

448c29417a9d25d287d1e27c28247c7e33e9b8a0.text: The documentation website now updates its text to better explain the differences between the two AI coding tools. When someone clicks a section title, the page smoothly scrolls to that spot and the web address changes to link directly to it. This is live for anyone reading the help guides.

a2265d31bda94aa882d816dd4560a3c13a165405.text: A small internal fix restores correct communication with the agent validation service. This change is live and ensures that when agents are checked, their details are sent properly for verification. Internal staff verifying agent configurations will see the process work as expected without errors.

756f7f0d55ed5907cba2f201026efc2d4a9d84c0.text: A small internal update makes the documentation easier to read by automatically shortening very long lists of settings. If a list is longer than 25 lines, it now hides the extra text behind a 'Show full schema' button. Readers can click this button to see the complete information or click 'Show less' to return to the short view.

f4ad445c3bf782b024d0def158181c0ac492f1fa.text: The internal check that verifies the assistant's logic now uses the same setup as the local development tools. This change only affects the team's workflow and is not live for customers. You would not see any difference in the app.

03d3b0b2a559d13fa06550416fde331e5ea7e242.text: The team adjusted a background setting for five separate parts of the internal system to fix a minor warning message. This change affects only the software infrastructure, meaning no external customers or users will notice any difference in how the product looks or behaves.

d0101564a997051fe25cbc8600a5359912f8e58e.text: Internal guides for setting up AI helpers got a cleanup. The team fixed broken layout tables and deleted old, confusing advice about how to organize tasks. This change affects only the people reading these setup guides; they will see cleaner, less repetitive instructions.

9050e5a178333d1a3b2a39a9d675223c90981c31.text: The AI assistant previously forgot how many steps it was allowed to take, resetting its limit to zero every time it ran. This fix ensures the assistant remembers its step limit, allowing it to complete tasks without stopping prematurely. This change is live and affects anyone using the software development kit to build AI applications.

a7967b63be343ae69f6464c2f5c27f038ef97a16.text: The tool now automatically finds and uses specific knowledge files when setting up a new session, if the user hasn't manually specified which files to use. This means developers building with this software don't need to write extra code to locate these files, as the system handles it for them. If a user has already chosen specific files, their selection remains unchanged.

a892fb6c7929c2032d066c164c2fa4164bb162ed.text: The web app now checks code against a newer standard, allowing it to use modern browser features directly. This change only affects the development process, not the live website. Regular users will not notice any difference, as the app looks and works exactly the same.

0ed7999b5a74286322fb3a42554d848752671a0a.text: Internal tweak to assistant guidance for GPT-5 model. Discourages stopping work too early. Affects AI behavior only. No user-facing change today.

74d8596771e6c2b379adfa53f09a02eed0efbc27.text: A new folder for internal assistant tools was registered in the project's master list. This lets developers build and check those tools separately without breaking other parts of the system. No changes affect customers today.

be3205147ce0ee22439c930c3d0f9c5de54f691e.text: The heavy benchmark tests that check the assistant's coding skills are now paused. This prevents them from running automatically during local checks, saving time and resources. No change to the assistant's behavior or performance for end-users.

b42476c552d0ea10ff3bb036699a3ae64df01929.text: The internal code reviewer now runs automatic checks on new files before writing its feedback. This ensures the reviewer's comments include the results of those checks, rather than analyzing the code first. This change is live for the internal agent system.

4880892de0b267bd0f50271e280591f09984c903.text: A small internal update changed how the system checks agent setups. Instead of pushing data to the server, it now asks for a check using a different standard method. Most people will not notice this change, but it helps the system communicate more reliably with some network setups.

13b1f3ae04f848402bdbd5f455cb205acebcdeaa.text: A test helper now passes a required list of agent templates that was previously missing. This keeps internal checks accurate. No customer-facing behavior changes.

53531399f18cd7b498f3d385fb42a4380d6c9f6a.text: The assistant's internal rulebook was cleaned up by removing unused instructions. This change affects only the system's underlying logic and does not alter how the assistant behaves for anyone. You will not notice any difference in the responses or features.

ebb53ada6c7b34aa51da776c3c6eae118664469e.text: A routine check was added to ensure the system correctly rejects requests missing required security credentials. This change affects internal testing processes and does not alter how the application behaves for end users today. You would notice no difference in the software's performance or features.

fe9143b324e5fad508bd34f3ffe90b460f2f1f17.text: The internal tool that automatically checks code submissions now uses a different artificial intelligence to perform its reviews. This small change affects only the automated inspection process and does not change any features available to customers. No one outside the engineering team will notice a difference.

ff19ac180a2da63800d5f9e67d4ae9f057d6b474.text: The internal label for the speed setting on open-source AI models changed from 'fast' to 'nitro' to match the provider's official names. This update applies to the base, coder, researcher, and other specialized assistants. Users will not notice any difference in performance or behavior, as this is a minor administrative fix to keep the system's internal references accurate.

bdf1081a9f5ff13601e2fcf313c96dcd27a3f8ca.text: The command-line tool now hides the list of available helpers when you already specify which one to use. This reduces clutter in automated scripts and makes test results more consistent. The change is internal and affects only startup output when a specific helper is targeted.

978879f488e5800a3e67f1c2a141380b6286e4c7.text: The tool now offers a specific action to end its live link with the service. Developers using this tool can manually shut down the connection when finished. This change is available immediately.

9a56b300d710e61c802980a1a15ed12203c275c2.text: The team removed a hidden debug message that only appeared for internal developers when the command-line tool finished running. Regular users never saw this text, so nothing changes for them. This cleanup makes the tool's exit messages less cluttered for the people who build it.

7cea76074a4473b16074489b3b80deaa070cc84e.text: The assistant now ignores missing shell configuration files instead of logging errors. This change is internal and live today. Users would notice cleaner logs, but functionality remains the same.

d700210b1282dc119a2469349100b7cfb26cd0ae.text: The internal tool that reviews code changes now uses a different artificial intelligence model to perform its analysis. This change affects only the automated review process and does not alter how the software behaves for end users. There is no visible difference in the application interface or user experience.

8e8d6485f4f9bcd307bba2cf037fdea1ab14a6d4.text: The tool now checks for a valid account key before verifying a selected assistant, rejecting requests without it. It also waits for the server to confirm the assistant's identity before showing its name on startup. This prevents the wrong name from appearing briefly if the assistant is still being checked.

8b09d700502c1b692bcdeafd046bba97f0757bb0.text: The system now finds the correct folder for its activity records, even if it cannot locate the current conversation's folder. This prevents the app from crashing when trying to save these records. The fix applies to internal tools, and users will not see any changes in the product.

693a21ec0120f19a241802a414d3c13a81e7b665.text: The internal coding assistant now gives longer, clearer answers when using the newest model, instead of forcing extremely short replies. This only affects that specific model choice. Users will see more detailed explanations for complex tasks rather than over-compressed text. The change is active now.

004ecf718a16aea9ebd2ca177cd99e4061a97861.text: The tool now checks if an agent exists only when you run it from the command line, not when starting the main application. This is an internal cleanup that affects nothing for regular users. If you use the command line tool to validate an agent name, it will still work exactly as before.

79cc1cfe5b9cdf5db5a9f49ba012cd10539753d7.text: The tool now generates field descriptions from what the assistant expects to receive, not from what it sends back. This affects people who read prompt examples, tool field lists, or docs showing what can be filled in. They may notice required fields, optional fields, and descriptions that match what should be provided.

7ca496720a86798e47ac97391284482cb35eee08.text: The system no longer requires a specific limit on how many steps an assistant can take before it must stop. This fixes an issue where documentation pages failed to load. Users will notice that these pages now display correctly.

84de5cf460c31cc670af2441a88d1d704aa944f0.text: A small internal fix stops the system from wrongly showing zero cost for certain AI model uses. It also updates the model name to match the cost tracker exactly. No user-facing changes are visible today.

62bdb9babd895935bd3b63d9b7d8f12da24d63e7.text: The internal assistant builder now has a specific set of instructions telling it to perform just one focused task at a time before stopping. This change is currently in the codebase but does not affect the live service yet. When it becomes active, the assistant will stop trying to do too many things at once, making its responses more predictable and less likely to get stuck.

3dfff48c660ed06f9df4e6be6a18568fb8d67d5e.text: The system now checks for assistant instructions and shows them or validates them in one step, rather than two. This internal cleanup removes redundant code. Users will notice no change in behavior or appearance.

e4c99325184057d07038fb437b7f6b532c3a317a.text: The internal tool that helps find the right files now uses a different, faster AI service. This change is small and affects only the background processing, so regular users will not notice any difference in how the software looks or feels.

c885525f6fd05c1d823b2a3e274964056e207794.text: The internal system now shows more detailed error messages when a background helper fails to load. This helps the support team diagnose issues faster, but regular users will not see any change.

689cc1afc07632f7588727b64f4f401768460bc6.text: The automated check for broken code now prints failed tests directly in the log, replacing the old method of saving separate result files. This change affects internal team members reviewing these checks. They will see a simple list of errors in the main log instead of a detailed report tab.

71429006be3d972011b91a692dcfe36926bce975.text: The team removed a temporary feature that automatically posted detailed test results to the project dashboard. This change affects only the internal software developers who check the automated quality reports. They will now see the standard, simpler test output instead of the extra summary details, reverting to the previous way of checking the code's health.

e9569cf002ee1c265a64d3cbcbed2429e8953122.text: The assistant's automatic stop limit for completing tasks increased from 12 to 25 steps. This applies to all agents by default. Users will notice the assistant can now take more actions before stopping to ask for help or reporting a failure.

98a82572d05247e530ee2fcbf39e2372850e14e7.text: The automated quality checks now use a standard reporting format instead of custom text searches. This internal update means test failures are listed clearly and precisely in the check results page. It affects only the team monitoring these automated checks.

48dadcf386fa907ebf26914d856842eb7a1b96ea.text: Small internal change. New helper agents now start blind by default, meaning they cannot see the conversation history unless explicitly told to. You will notice no difference in the app interface, but the assistant will no longer assume a spawned agent knows what you just said.

2434be1fd79aa61611a1e5e7a24510e57ccf4115.text: The team fixed a timing issue in their internal test checks for the agent list. Previously, the test tools set up fake data too early, causing occasional failures. Now, the fake data is set up at the correct moment, making the tests reliable. This change is internal and only affects the stability of the development checks, with no visible difference for end users.

c24b77fa176cb519b9fcfdaf5d6fb6d99752419e.text: The limit on how many steps an assistant can take before stopping now comes from one shared setting instead of being written separately in four places. This change only affects internal code, so nothing about how the product works or looks changes today. It just means future updates to that limit will apply everywhere at once.

2c6225ce333f471171a50a17850822b763433913.text: A small internal update added a new option for the system to include extra advice alongside error messages when publishing fails. This change affects how the software reports problems behind the scenes but does not yet display any new information to you. You will not notice any difference today, as this is just a preparation step for future improvements.

53cce531c371524cef89c89e62bc207d885dfb27.text: The internal rules for describing custom helpers were updated to correctly list available tools. This ensures the system accurately recognizes which tools a helper can use. The change is purely for internal code organization and does not affect how the software currently works for anyone.

76f7a396e7f904908030318923ab10bc2bcd452b.text: A small internal check was corrected to match how the system actually handles conversation history by default. This ensures automated tests pass. Normal users will notice no change, as this only affects the software's internal verification process.

5650e1ff92df689348224e76247ae01df4915980.text: A small internal fix corrects how the system labels automated actions taken by the AI. Previously, the system incorrectly marked these actions as coming from the human user, but now it properly attributes them to the AI itself. This change also ensures the text of these actions is sent to the display stream, so people watching the process can see the AI's steps in real time.

19a4324e22da0c79a32e3925496f2b2591b71c56.text: A hidden setting inside the AI assistant's configuration was renamed to better explain its purpose. This change only affects how the system internally labels the reason for activating specific assistant modes. Users will not notice any difference in performance or features.

c442299be0f3a40c9e7d0dff567d0430e355cb1e.text: Removed broken code that checked tool names. The system now uses built-in rules to verify these names automatically. This internal fix stops errors when creating custom assistants. No visible changes for end users.

89c2a27a5a8c0cfa9c8df4112076bf819c35e9d4.text: A small internal cleanup removed a leftover note from the code that told the system to do something it was no longer doing. This change affects only the internal setup of the software and does not alter how the application works for anyone. You would notice nothing different when using the app.

eab3a00a52bf5373b9600f58e57c2b774d8d3484.text: This small internal update changes what information the system records when it processes a request. Engineers will now see key details like the model used and timing at the very beginning of the log, while bulky, less useful data was removed from the end.

f999cc7982e9c76bb18ffdea19bb443a5015d10e.text: The system now checks agent settings before starting a task. If a setting is wrong, it stops and shows the specific error message immediately. This affects people using the internal tooling and prevents tasks from failing later with confusing results.

b244cd26fc7fb4b1c602b0d6a54c965360dcbfee.text: The names used inside the assistant’s built-in instruction sets were made consistent. This is a small cleanup for people who maintain those instruction sets. It is already in place, and nothing about how the assistant behaves should change.

185ebc43ab70ebc7bba66b74b18b40aff38e1c3f.text: The system's internal instructions for handling live chat connections were simplified to make them shorter and easier to manage. This change only affects the code structure behind the scenes, not how the software behaves. Users will not notice any difference in speed, features, or stability.

f4bc2996958d258318bf16cf39404a39e17329bf.text: The system now checks for errors in the agent's setup instructions before sending a warning message. Previously, it always sent a warning, even when the instructions were correct. This change stops unnecessary error notifications from appearing when the agent is configured properly.

327256f8d622d94b391613b5d072a70204ec2b71.text: The system now checks local assistant templates for errors immediately upon startup, rather than waiting until after a connection is established. This internal improvement ensures that any configuration mistakes are caught and reported earlier in the process. There is no visible change to the user interface or functionality.

fc2b860783adfcbf9602dad57a3b17e5b0678b2b.text: The assistant now stops its turn when it only thinks about the problem instead of taking action. This prevents endless loops where the AI keeps analyzing without doing anything. If you use the assistant, you will see it pause and wait for your next instruction rather than continuing to process silently.

283720666a6716c7a30d90a3f6fdaf1fee189ad5.text: A small internal update fixes how commands appear on screen. Some automated systems previously hid the text under the command itself. Now, two blank lines are inserted before the command displays. This ensures the instruction remains clearly visible for anyone running the tool.

4f626984c985df0a5bad27a0d9e0b57fbde5847b.text: The internal check for agent settings no longer requires a login. The tool now sends a list of settings instead of a labeled group. This change is internal and affects only the validation step. Users will not notice any difference in the interface.

45acd256d19c3abe4da1903a3a552626eef96021.text: The program now uses a standard way to report when a specific request fails, instead of building error messages manually each time. This affects the command-line tool, ensuring it correctly displays failures like running out of credits. You would notice the same error messages, but the system handles them more reliably behind the scenes.

130669184edf23a672b78e3e0ef8dff3bcd3a136.text: The list of recommended AI models for agents was refreshed. Newer options like GPT-5 and Claude Opus 4.1 were added, while older models like GPT-4o were removed. This change is live. Users configuring agents will see the updated selection in the model picker.

2dcd8cb052847b0112fe1d6dc90baa5016accbe9.text: The automated checks that verify the assistant's output feature were updated to use a fixed, simple test setup instead of relying on the live system's configuration. This change is internal and only affects the software testing process. Customers will not notice any difference in the product's behavior or performance.

6e860fe9de2082c1a2dccc56460c22d0a764480e.text: A small internal update improved how the command-line tool displays its activity. When the system starts a new sub-task, you now see a clear header, the specific agent's name, and the instruction it received, followed by a loading spinner. This change is live today and makes the process easier to follow.

943dd6d4f5df714265c84fc84f23be9db18bf00f.text: The internal label for the instructions that define how an AI assistant behaves has been updated from 'config' to 'definition' for better clarity. This change affects only the underlying tools that build the assistant's logic, not the end-user experience. You will not see any visible changes in the application, as this is a minor internal cleanup to keep the system organized.

d9c305afc5545636b8ae82a9fc7d739adc056ca4.text: The assistant's command tool now accepts requests without specifying how long to wait or whether to run in the background. It falls back to standard defaults automatically. This affects the assistant's reliability when issuing simple commands. You would notice fewer errors when the assistant tries to run basic tasks.

781b6c96b6a45e87f21847b3138f5aa77213d2df.text: A small internal update makes the tool automatically tidy up the layout of its generated instructions every time it creates them. This change affects only the internal setup process and does not alter how the software behaves for anyone else. You would not notice any difference in the final product.

a862a7631739428591169521b08a2e54eb18b6fd.text: Programmers will now see helpful explanations when they hover their mouse over the options for the assistant's tools. These notes, like how to choose a number for a goal or what kind of browser action to take, were previously hidden. This change affects only the people building the software, and it does not change how the assistant behaves for regular users.

bd848cbe4d1af2ece2b1a98bfa44af3d65232d7d.text: The automated nightly quality checks now run three tests at a time instead of ten. This prevents the system from timing out when the checks are busy. You will not notice any difference in the product, but the reports will be more reliable.

6a5d3f500f7cacec9f7226c8b13aa3613bd015de.text: A small internal fix corrects how the system decides when to keep or delete temporary messages during a conversation. This ensures that certain messages are retained only when appropriate, rather than being deleted too early or kept too long. Users might not notice any difference, as this is a behind-the-scenes correction to the message management logic.

0fe1f1dd28233a1278b309984f3a6b9cbd18b10a.text: The tool that packages the software for distribution now works more simply. It used to rearrange files during packaging; it now packages them directly from their original location. This change affects only the internal packaging process, so there is no visible difference for people using the software.

218b5bb68b6c3be40500e6773e52cc3910dca472.text: A small internal fix stops old, temporary notes from cluttering the chat history. This helps the assistant keep track of the current conversation without getting confused by leftover data. You will not notice a visual change, but the assistant should stay focused on your latest request.

03c28acba1bacead04d5643552fa1b90b46b9330.text: The team updated the version number of their software toolkit. This change is internal and does not affect how the software works. Developers using this toolkit will see the new version label, but no features changed.

256e3c826cab1e5a39f408f052fc5e39aef399ec.text: The internal toolkit used by AI coding assistants received a routine version update. This change is invisible to end-users and requires no action from them. It only affects the software libraries developers install to build or integrate with the platform.

587078819d21ebc9d0f3f5718469f41ba980258b.text: The standard assistant mode now uses a different underlying model, while the lighter version switches to the model the standard mode previously used. The assistant also no longer requires a specific hidden signal to finish a task, relying instead on completing all steps naturally. This internal adjustment affects default behavior for users who do not manually select a specific mode.

d6f286a4e3c3bedf8f67ecd4613d19db2796ebdf.text: The tool now lets you give instructions for several assistant personalities at once instead of just one. Programmers using this tool need to adjust how they list these personalities. The change is live, but only affects those who set up custom assistants.

ecb2ad86f26dfde8611f3df04cfea9ecd7736c0d.text: The software now uses the same internal logic for two different file-editing tasks. This affects developers building applications with this toolkit. They will notice that their custom handling for one task now automatically applies to the other, reducing the need to write duplicate code.

8ed8d337f45cc8aeb9bf0d93b42344cf6409896c.text: The program's error reporting logic was moved from a shared background component to the main application interface. This internal cleanup affects only the code structure, not the visible features. A person looking at the screen would notice no difference, as the program still displays the same error messages and stops in the same way if a connection fails.

4c24c3d44e0b871f4f75d25edecc36f5f8059593.text: The software stopped listening for extra background data about how much work it did. This cleanup affects only the tools that connect to the assistant, not the everyday chat interface. You will not notice any change in how the assistant answers or looks.

dfdb3a8a3392881ded3efe5637677cdc36bdca47.text: Programs that use Codebuff can now pass their access key directly when starting the client. This makes setup simpler for developers building custom tools. The change is live.

e96e48e9f4c433cd888490e04f19dc9c9f7ba73a.text: The assistant now saves its memory after each step, letting you continue a conversation or restart if it stops working. This helps developers building tools that use the assistant. You will not notice any change in how the assistant behaves.

739992a3a86434ecdb09aa84c4097a1e3449e50c.text: The tool that helps you connect your code to an AI assistant changed the name of the setting used to send your project's files. This new name is clearer, but it means anyone currently using the old name must update their setup to keep working. The change also includes detailed instructions explaining how to use the assistant, so users can find help without looking at the code.

ed517e9d60056abf497af15bdf5c0f9770d66801.text: The default assistant model changed from one provider to another. This affects new internal agent setups. Users will not see any change in the interface or options.

db63b5f74ff8ea0a4423a578177c64cff74b64d3.text: The guide for connecting to the service now shows how to add a step that catches and reports problems when a message fails to send. This helps people building their own tools see how to handle errors, but it does not change how the service behaves for everyday users.

3af903105725886254d5a6db2aaf9510a4b46666.text: The software now checks for necessary background tools using Windows-compatible methods and prevents duplicate connection attempts to ensure stable communication. It also blocks file editing requests that try to access locations outside the permitted folder, stopping potential security breaches. These improvements help the assistant work reliably on Windows computers and keep file changes safe.

d67fc734bb61c965a12dfa1531fb737b5fe67e4c.text: The system now uses a single, central label to identify the specific AI model used for the default assistant, rather than typing the name directly in multiple places. This change is internal and affects only the software's maintenance structure. No visible changes will appear for users or administrators.

cef67de6ebd051fa47c08f0ba60e17b5ce6fcea4.text: The system now includes a tool for connecting to AI services. This is a small internal setup step. Regular users will not notice any change.

f1146062c7c1a0639055be5c4029fcfa27e9bddd.text: The 'Agent Store' link is hidden from the website's top menu and mobile dropdown. This change affects all visitors, who will no longer see that specific navigation option. The rest of the site remains unchanged.

9812b9865e81d387f83bca8972d39f0c7a53811c.text: When you start the assistant in a conversation window and pick a specific helper by name, the screen now shows which helper you chose right after the welcome message. This helps people who use the command-line tool remember which assistant they are talking to. It is live today for people who pick a helper when they start the program.

cc12e138692a984c4bc908a1ce1845a37ef8abd0.text: The software now lets people building on this platform choose which specific alerts they want to receive, rather than requiring them to set up a response for every single event. This affects the tools used by those developers to connect their apps to the service. If they look at the setup, they will see that they can now ignore certain notifications without breaking the connection.

aa6d5ba9ac074fe76f7cba4c875e6ca9fa8d1a43.text: The system swapped the brains of two helper bots: the research bot now uses a faster model, while the thinking bot uses a stronger reasoning model. Programmers also cleaned up how the system describes its tools, removing old labels and simplifying the text. Regular users will not notice any visual changes, as this is internal housekeeping to make the bots smarter and faster.

46ea9eb5635acaa15255b77420c4e8b89931f061.text: A small internal cleanup was made to the software that connects the service to your computer. This change removes unused, temporary instructions from the code that handles these connections. You will not notice any difference in how the software works, as this update has no visible effect on its performance or features.

73bf4a3584ba7e5a4ef5df05163390abb2032e0f.text: The assistant now stops adding extra helpers when you pick a specific one, so your chosen setup stays exactly as you configured it. This fixes a bug where the assistant ignored your choice and used its default list instead. You would notice this if you previously saw the assistant using helpers you did not ask for.

343d7841cc1159d658bb8c2bd204d56b3848b58a.text: We simplified the instructions for our internal AI helpers. We removed repetitive text prompts and strict formatting rules that were no longer needed. This change is only for our internal team and does not affect how the product works for you.

63a113df6b6604e45ed0ea4731e62df896ea2088.text: The tool now loads its setup files only once when starting, rather than checking them multiple times. This internal cleanup affects the command-line version of the app. You will not notice any change in behavior or speed.

f3d89de2a35340111154033a4bab036490904565.text: The system now checks agent names using the short label first, then applies the full address, preventing mismatches. It also skips loading extra local agents if a specific one is requested, speeding up startup. Users might notice slightly faster initial launch times when selecting specific agents.

76cd22a649c0739b4c7d22097f191382d9771365.text: The system now automatically trims the middle of very long conversations when sending them to the AI, keeping the start and end intact. This affects all requests routed through the OpenRouter service. Users will notice more stable responses in lengthy chats, as the AI is less likely to get confused by too much context.

a9ac1c4375bec000469115abdd72bb4b90e06663.text: Two checks that verify a tool can look up documentation sometimes fail randomly. Developers paused these checks to stop false alarms. The documentation tool itself still works normally for everyone.

be46935411f83652527754ff8dd39713f6dfb7f6.text: The team added automated checks to ensure the AI assistant correctly processes step-by-step instructions and knows when to stop. These checks verify that the assistant makes only one call to the model when given a specific step, and no calls when it finishes. This is an internal quality improvement, so users will not see any immediate changes.

c05cc909d0b6427286daa5622135a086cfb7cf99.text: The company lowered the extra charge added to AI message costs from 30% to 5.5%. This change affects the internal billing calculations for the backend service. Users will not notice any immediate difference in the interface, but the cost tracking system now applies a much smaller markup on each message.

c30879321093563c4b43bbb5f121323ce12bb704.text: The tool now checks your access key automatically every time you ask it to do something, instead of waiting for you to manually start a session first. This affects only the software built on top of this tool, not regular people using the app. You would not notice any difference in how the tool works, but the way it handles security behind the scenes is simpler and less prone to errors.

3c1b2b086848c2d4ffbaf4442545f54be1727fa4.text: The command-line tool now accepts a secret key saved in the computer's environment variables to authorize print mode, instead of requiring a prior login. Users who set this key can run print commands without logging in, while others still see the standard login prompt. This change is live today.

f6bcb4ef5b599144e3d956a8690f2a5a26bc0480.text: The rules for checking custom instructions are now handled by the main system instead of the local program. This means the local program will no longer reject custom instructions based on its own strict formatting rules. If there is an error, the system will provide a clearer message that includes the name of the specific instruction set.

fddfb181b3a65de0b44bcccf214b962ac228916e.text: A small internal fix corrected where the system saves its list of available assistant tools. This change ensures the list is stored in the right folder so other parts of the program can find it. Developers will notice the list is now formatted on a single line instead of multiple lines, but there is no visible change for regular users.

dcf97aec60eba6d59bc9c1fed9e354426aba1ff5.text: A small internal fix changed the list used when preparing the downloadable software bundle for release. The bundle now includes the folders that hold the ready-to-use parts, rather than relying on loose matching rules. This affects anyone who installs a future bundle, not anyone already using an older one. They would not notice anything except the bundle is less likely to miss needed parts.

94e3b0c38f1e25cb8eff0890400ffdd0ce93f2bf.text: The system now checks if an assistant is set up to create sub-tasks or return structured data without having the required tools enabled. This prevents a specific type of configuration error where the assistant would fail to start because of mismatched settings. The validation is active immediately for anyone creating or editing these assistant templates.

485bea43a8e879f9baeb76a501d311138e5819cb.text: The system now delivers search results and file contents as simple text instead of wrapped in a data container. This change applies to the internal logic that builds automated agents, making it easier for them to process information directly. Since this is an internal structural update, users will not notice any visible changes in the application's behavior.

0148b8f7a7cce8f7bfeb7e02f2281fb053e248f7.text: The system's internal search tool was told to be much briefer when listing files. This change affects how the tool reports its findings, resulting in shorter, less wordy summaries. Users will see less clutter in the search results, focusing only on the most relevant information.

59edf2216b0c8b3f1209b1f22345d11cb491c797.text: The internal test suite failed to locate a specific data type definition due to an incorrect file path reference. This change corrects the path so the testing tool can find the required information. Non-programmers will notice no change in the application's behavior, as this fix only resolves an internal error during automated checks.

3cebe0678b504046eb5a7d85650400e5a78f8794.text: The software no longer allows users to pass a security key directly when starting a session. Instead, it strictly requires the key to be stored in the system's background settings. This change affects anyone using the tool, and they will notice an error message if they try to provide the key manually or if the background setting is missing.

cdd2732feb413f5349b2793f739418b81643e26d.text: An internal name for a specific AI assistant profile was shortened to remove a version number. This change affects only the software's internal labeling system, not its visible features or behavior. A non-programmer would notice no difference in how the assistant works or appears.

1def93b5a3ebe3aa0d55ee3ba4f4508c004392e1.text: The system now correctly finds the list of agent types it needs, fixing a broken link in its internal map. This prevents errors when the software builds or runs tests. Regular users will not notice any change in the app's behavior, as this is a behind-the-scenes fix for developers.

53f1a6ced6c797b7892183aefea9c197d806b383.text: The AI assistant's underlying engine was swapped for a newer version. The startup message claiming the assistant uses the previous engine was deleted. People who use the assistant will see it run on the updated engine, with no change to how they interact with it.

d44ef2aadf36cdee2acc6f6eb8f77e9a5a01f4ad.text: A small internal fix prevents a specific text marker in a developer's instruction guide from being misread as a command. This only affects the tool's internal documentation, not the chat experience. You will notice no change.

772fb6736f8b613bb5a5f2cff480336b26a3220b.text: The software now checks for a saved access code before asking you to sign in. This helps automated systems run without a human entering credentials. You will not see a new button or menu, but the sign-in screen may skip if the code is already set.

5f8870d7261d3e0a42b499f5c52611770ab2a654.text: Developers fixed an internal rule so that the assistant can no longer accidentally ask for a file search without providing the search terms. This prevents the assistant from getting stuck or failing when it tries to find files but forgets to say what to look for. You might notice the assistant handling file searches more reliably.

d0e77491636ca5e0183ecf1f8f1c3580bacb8a7c.text: The internal research assistant now sends search requests with the correct label for the text to search. This fixes a mismatch where the assistant was using a word the search tool did not expect. The change is live and affects the automated research feature. Users will notice searches work as intended without needing to do anything differently.

8b4782c66064526f3ff5f82aae8c8929ded7ea3d.text: The lightweight assistant mode now uses a different underlying AI model. This internal adjustment affects only the basic agent template. Users will not see any immediate difference in the interface.

49d43ad4489917dd30d71a10d88f829ac9d90f2d.text: The internal system now reports AI connection failures immediately, instead of hiding them in production. This change affects the team monitoring the service, who will see error messages appear where they previously did not. It is active now.

cb67c9918f45e21abf10f92a106c691ae9086bad.text: The tool for building this software now uses a different method to check data shapes. This helps people who install the software get the right checks without needing extra setup. Most people won't notice any change.

f4018046b52024b6ed2cfee6490a386ced1dbc39.text: A small internal update changed the name of a specific data type used in background testing. This rename ensures the test code matches the current system definitions. Regular users will not notice any difference, and the application's behavior remains exactly the same.

725b2b04129f4ed21cd85c8418f2d05f2699e30e.text: The team paused a background check that tests how the software creates helper bots. This change is internal and does not affect the live product. Users will see no difference, as this only alters the safety tests developers run before releasing new features.

e4304f0610695fca33e934ace145d997ecb1ddfb.text: A small internal fix stops a test tool from crashing when an assistant skips a step. This affects only the team checking the software's quality, not the people using the final product.

31524dd2ffe0d4987c964b7d785081ce4d5afaf2.text: The automatic system that checks how well the assistant performs now runs up to 100 tests at once, instead of just 10. This change speeds up the process for the internal team who monitors quality. Regular users won't notice any difference today, but the team will see results faster.

1638023eef33dd1e87ff9c4f1571f66e060b801d.text: A small internal adjustment limits how many automated quality checks run at the same time. This change prevents the system from getting overwhelmed or hitting service limits. You will not notice any difference in your experience.

98ac67e34a64b23585f31ca07cd74afa2d4f07bc.text: The system now checks the shape of instructions sent to the assistant before they are used. This change affects internal tool definitions, ensuring that outdated or incorrect examples are caught early. Users will not notice any difference in the assistant's behavior today.

27272da6d21cab1375cfd7b5ff31a7c6d2f13af4.text: The system now shows the internal judge exactly which tools the assistant used, instead of just its final answer. This prevents the judge from mistakenly marking a task as finished when no actual file changes were made. Since this affects only the internal grading process, regular users will see no visible change.

4934f12749986fd4767c3ddad91e151ac2d851c2.text: The system stopped automatically marking certain internal setup steps as skipped. This affects only the tools that build new agent templates. Nothing changes for regular users, as this is a minor internal cleanup.

0044ee481f88e5f33ccde6a3d81413644d471545.text: The assistant now knows to format multi-line text instructions correctly for Windows computers. This prevents errors when creating records that need several lines of explanation. Only people using Windows will see this difference in how the assistant builds these messages.

69e985100095577f03f64e32462eda928a5b5b12.text: The software's internal labels for two file-handling helpers changed their format to match a standard style. This is a small, behind-the-scenes cleanup for the program's structure. You will not notice any difference in how the software works or looks.

e756fd3d88d54df8ca3e5ea9e07c6da455462d0f.text: The system's internal search helpers now follow strict, pre-defined checklists for finding files and web information, rather than deciding steps on their own. This is a small, behind-the-scenes update that does not affect what you see or do today.

ac3eab66b6c015a00474ab4c9b5b10d2457b0f07.text: A small update improved the instructions for a tool that edits text. It now shows how to correctly handle lines with spaces or tabs at the start. This change only affects the guide, not the tool's performance.

9e04d20f836041f6c884094f69f6c3ed300525b7.text: A small internal correction tightens the rules for how the assistant requests tools. This change affects only the system's underlying structure and does not alter any visible behavior for users today.

18c6dc71deb8b178a046d0dc2cc3519094ebd5fb.text: The system now uses a single, shared reference to identify the file explorer assistant, rather than repeating its name in multiple places. This prevents internal errors if the assistant's name ever changes. No users will notice any difference, as this is a small internal cleanup.

81bf172a7a092b9f8f23cbb16c3c0bb358bf46a1.text: Developers cleaned up the safety checks inside the test area for the assistant's agent registry. This change affects only the internal testing tools, not the live product. A non-programmer would notice nothing, as the assistant's behavior remains exactly the same.

50ae9e895614e56a52e0d0ced7f906aed772f43e.text: The software now automatically uses a faster, lighter version of the artificial intelligence when you select the 'Lite' mode. This change is live and affects anyone using that specific setting. You will likely notice the system responds more quickly or efficiently, without needing to change any settings yourself.

ffc7b7d5eff47b4575e8f6a2c85155504c373787.text: The command-line tool for managing custom assistants no longer offers an 'Edit Agents' option. This change affects only users of the command-line interface. They will notice the menu option is gone, and the tool now uses a direct creation process instead of a chat-based one.

851284e3c574f5f4f61264b329b2ba7d230b0fda.text: A small internal fix improves the command-line tool's agent menu. It now waits for the agent information to load before showing the menu when you type '@'. This prevents the menu from appearing blank or incomplete if the data isn't ready yet.

b83e6d1c5d5899528fc2cd4e01db6b1af930507b.text: An internal assistant persona named Charles now focuses on tuna instead of sardines. This change only affects how the assistant describes its own expertise and research topics. Users interacting with Charles would notice he discusses tuna behavior and conservation rather than sardines, but the underlying capabilities remain identical.

ece31b407f89f68ecb8b30bd1f5c6b2e8c38308d.text: A missing instruction was added to the internal tool that helps staff create or modify AI assistant templates. This fixes a broken feature, allowing the system to now properly set up the necessary folders and copy template files when a user asks to build or edit an agent. Staff members using this internal tool will see the creation process complete successfully instead of failing.

c4dc5d0473febb6d35718cfd66a6a51d65ecf28d.text: The internal tool that helps staff create new AI assistants now requires less information to start. Instead of asking for a detailed list of settings, it only needs a simple description of what the assistant should do. This change is not visible to customers and only affects how staff build these tools.

df2f2a8040b7751091a8e3040f0ec99fa7e097d1.text: The internal name for the tool that creates new custom assistants was changed to match other similar tools. This is a small cleanup inside the program. Regular users will not see any difference, but developers using the command line will now see the new name when creating agents.

98d7fdcc7c3e742db22596b70712dfc747597d9a.text: The command-line app now suggests and accepts commands typed with a leading slash even when those commands were previously hidden because they had no menu text, including help and usage. It also accepts alternate names, such as h for help or signin for login. People using the app will see fewer missed suggestions and fewer unknown command messages; the fix is live today.

e5faeba512eac048bb1c87d21798262a5342e445.text: The system now rejects agent setups that include an empty or invalid input form definition, instead of silently ignoring the mistake. This affects people creating custom agents who accidentally left the input requirements blank or malformed. They will see a clear error message pointing to the specific file and field that needs fixing.

061bb95cd6de361b5b374ab07c811a1e6f49453f.text: Internal tests now use the official list of assistant names instead of hand-typed labels. A hidden mismatch between two naming styles was fixed during this update. This change affects only the quality checks developers run, so customers will notice nothing and there is no live feature impact.

e9162fbe8f71f75ae9158b80a87370ec035f8289.text: The system now correctly turns words ending in 'f' into plurals like 'roofs' instead of 'rooves'. It also makes labels for money and people look cleaner by using lowercase letters. You will see these small text fixes on the billing and usage pages.

03001d7e21f8e7ad13ba01a5e0d290fa5282efd7.text: Publishing agents from command-line tools previously failed due to a login check that only accepted browser sessions. The system now also accepts a direct access key included with the request. Command-line users can now publish agents successfully without being logged into a web browser.

8a13db603118abb3ff149c90e632db543548a0eb.text: The review assistant now loads correctly because a missing link in its setup was restored. This small internal fix ensures the tool is available to team members today, with no visible changes to the interface.

26dcb4d0824f6f614e1a3c71b3adb051b0dd4a1a.text: When publishing a new assistant template, the system now sends your login key inside the message itself rather than as a hidden label on the envelope. This internal fix ensures the server correctly recognizes you without changing how you interact with the tool. You will not notice any difference in behavior or results.

32e9eaced0261c508a6633c9520e33c843c90288.text: A small internal fix changes how an agent's publisher is credited on their detail page. Instead of showing a unique number, the page now displays the publisher's actual name. This makes attribution clearer for organizations and publishers reviewing these pages.

14b097934387989e9a4817ec58ed27d5328a4ca4.text: The agent detail page now shows the complete name of the tool alongside a button to copy it to your clipboard. Previously, only a partial name was visible. This small internal update helps you identify and share the exact tool you are viewing without needing to reconstruct its full name manually.

428d4a2077143f3dd8bbc36d824fc8f3f3c84876.text: The program’s internal review helper was reorganized so its instructions and settings are clearer. It was set to use only the new request, not the earlier conversation, and to follow a shorter checklist. This is a small internal tidy-up, and no one using the program will notice a change.

8be0ee4da114042c498c476f9636e2bd19ce0561.text: The system's internal blueprint for recording tool results was updated to match the actual data being generated. This is a minor technical cleanup that does not change any visible features or user experience today.

3d810733f24820330c90e528a36c949fce46bb32.text: The system now protects essential instructions from being deleted when a conversation gets too long. While older chat history might be removed to save space, the core rules and current tasks stay intact. This update is active now and ensures the assistant keeps its bearings during long sessions.

cafe220ad4f83aa24c5829b4cc9cb7353ebf4ee6.text: The publishing tool now lets people choose which publisher profile to use instead of always picking the most recently updated one. If you publish agents from a command line, you can now add a specific publisher name to the command. This change is live today for that command line tool.

9113967080b38198f9593ea40eeb98e8cae7997a.text: A small internal fix ensures profile pictures save correctly when creating a publisher account. Previously, the image data failed to reach the database. Now, selecting a photo immediately embeds it in the submission, so the avatar appears reliably without extra steps.

97c88e135c82741c1d3935b2b1708ecb470d9223.text: The system now automatically adds specific instruction blocks to the main prompt if they are missing. This ensures the assistant always receives the necessary context for using tools and identifying other agents. The change is internal and live, requiring no action from users.

b97e8c1d7690a052b1d1d3035ee58ef5f8686273.text: A minor internal cleanup removed a specific instruction from how the system prepares messages for its automated assistant. This change affects only the backend logic and ensures the message format strictly matches current standards. No visible features or user interactions change today, as this was a behind-the-scenes alignment with existing rules.

7873f8311694903fc425caf3cc04cfae57fc1fc4.text: The system stopped adding a redundant copy of the error explanation to messages shown when an agent fails validation. Since the detailed explanation was already part of the main message, this change removes the duplicate text. No user-facing behavior changes, as the error message content remains the same.

bf5e301c79b4133c9ec854ab295d20c80b16fc29.text: The system now counts each assistant once, ignoring extra versions. The screen stops showing total counts in the headings, but labels each assistant correctly as singular or plural. This is a small internal fix, live today.

9c5d2d175e9dec606c18996cffd1f4858360b23f.text: The tool now reloads custom instructions automatically when files change, instead of requiring a restart. This helps people who build custom assistants, as edits take effect immediately during testing.

fd549691e1225ea3bc1950707b849b0660aef58a.text: The system now requires people building custom assistant templates to clearly state when they want structured data output. If a template defines a specific data format but doesn't explicitly ask for JSON output, the system will reject it instead of guessing. This affects template creators who previously relied on the system to automatically choose JSON mode for them.

2646a8f0111a6be37bda72472e595afb8da3b1dd.text: The system now places its blueprint files in a separate folder. This change affects only the internal tools that generate new agent templates. The blueprint files themselves remain unchanged, so the agents will look and function exactly the same.

71c4ce12f25622b9d168de56a3d08a2a57cbbc63.text: Developers deleted a leftover rule for checking version numbers that nothing was using. This cleanup only affects the internal tools, not the live product. A regular user will not notice any change.

6f5aee81b4c78d66bcf85944861dc0598de7254b.text: The form for setting up an AI assistant no longer forces you to fill in a specific instruction box. This helps people building assistants, as they can now leave that box empty if it is not needed. The change is live, but most users will not notice a difference in how the assistants behave.

6e9f603bbf62aa250c6665f099a26cca423c257d.text: The code that runs the assistant's tasks was cleaned up to remove unnecessary parts and fix formatting. This change affects only the internal structure of the software, making it slightly more efficient. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves or responds.

4910cdaee920ba5099266043301c7e6e67819379.text: The internal assistant now automatically launches specific helper tools whenever a user types their name with an '@' symbol. This affects only the backend logic for these assistants. Users will notice that typing '@HelperName' in a chat message reliably triggers that specific helper to start working, instead of the assistant ignoring the request.

8f909aeaecb926b608bc3896a07231f5b864a9ca.text: The AI assistant now automatically receives a list of available tools, even if its base instructions forget to mention them. This internal update ensures the assistant knows what actions it can take. You will not see any visual changes, but the assistant may behave more consistently when using features.

73849f7511c1b59e7586ab39650efb47c94102c4.text: The agent builder tool now includes a list of available actions when creating new agents. This change helps the system understand what capabilities can be added to custom agents. It is an internal improvement and will not be visible to end users.

842c56b34bdd131145c280d8d410ecab658571e6.text: A small internal update adds a helper tool that checks the project's code for leftover instructions that are no longer used. This only affects the team building the software and does not change anything for people who use the app. Today, the tool is installed but not yet active, so it does nothing until the team turns it on.

43075290fbe734dd5b7cdcc5dda1b1fb9d70b9e6.text: The publishing tool now checks your saved login details directly from your computer, rather than waiting for a full system startup. This speeds up the process for anyone publishing content, though you might not notice a difference unless the tool previously failed to start.

aa1411205856175ee44107e466698d6d05977cea.text: A rule now blocks publishing a new version of an assistant if its number is the same as or older than the current live version. Instead of quietly ignoring the mistake, the system now stops and shows an error message. This change is already active and prevents accidental updates that would not actually change anything.

5c7a3cf95f6bc2a60703d872d3492fe833edc650.text: The assistant now reads its instructions directly from the agent's settings instead of searching for separate text files. This affects only internal tools that load agent definitions, and it makes the process faster by skipping unnecessary file searches. A non-programmer would notice no change in behavior, as the same instructions still appear.

81841a49cb41c0dfb6d5cef978e1e78681db165b.text: The command to share a custom assistant changed from a special switch to a simple word. Instead of typing a dash before the action, you now type the action first. This fixes a bug where the tool mistook your request for the command itself.

5359944010043c475dd37e61bb50dc22480f81b7.text: A small internal update adjusts how code is automatically cleaned and sorted when saved. Developers will see unused code lines removed and lists formatted with extra commas, making files neater. This change affects only the team building the software and does not impact customers.

ffee261accfd719fa2ea10622016ce4737a638db.text: A small internal update removes a strict rule that required a specific setup instruction for automated assistants. Now, if that instruction is missing, the system uses a blank default instead of stopping with an error. This change is live and allows assistants to run without that specific setup instruction.

2772a1fd21ba7e1aad075cbd9923db46dec2f153.text: The assistant stops repeating a message when it adds a note to the chat. This fixes a bug where the text appeared twice. The change is internal and already live. You will notice the duplicate line is gone.

db27f2647832129d0e6c2a9aa47e371c75d64f2c.text: The application stopped loading extra, unused data about agent names and types. This cleanup slightly reduced the app's size. Internal developers and the automated code checker will notice the change, but regular users will see no difference in how the app works.

bc27a99489882495b913da830826f93e08301a17.text: A small database fix makes a required label mandatory for a specific type of content, preventing it from being saved without one. This change applies to local development environments and does not affect live services. You will not notice any difference in the application's behavior.

63a8f31fe5e2afceeb45b0beee81fd2ec0b6ec74.text: The team fixed how the automatic quality checker handles timing. The system now reliably records how long each test took, even if the follow-up analysis fails. It also stops waiting after ten minutes if the analysis gets stuck on large data. This is an internal fix, so regular users will not see any visual changes.

7d744484d7507c720877f3377ac9ba2bbc200611.text: The database update process now ignores specific system performance logs, preventing errors that previously blocked changes. This internal fix ensures smoother maintenance for the underlying data storage. Additionally, rules for naming internal assistants were tightened to require lowercase letters and hyphens, though this does not yet change how they function.

c41bd0e3af2042bfd300dea21f9fc932ca6371d1.text: The automated checker now stops if either the code check or the website build fails, rather than hiding the error. This ensures broken web updates are caught before release. Internal tooling only; no customer impact.

2ff18647c9c01186a50d7ef25b3c2f5c7552e650.text: The system now requires agent names to use only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. This applies to shared tools used across the command line, web, and desktop applications. People creating or loading agents will see errors if they use uppercase letters in the name.

b1579e6b3fbdea2a0039b75d256e622b25886fe0.text: The system stopped automatically summoning a documentation assistant when other tools found new information. This is an internal adjustment that does not change how the main assistant behaves for you. You will not notice any difference in your interactions.

1681877c218b562d775639c734c010d5f05f3d96.text: A small internal cleanup simplified the instructions for the automated tool that saves code changes. The text explaining when to use this tool was moved to a clearer spot and duplicate notes were removed. This does not change how the tool works or what it produces.

909d1f15331a82f841b7694064545c493862a9a2.text: The internal file used to define assistant behavior was renamed from 'template' to 'config' to better reflect its purpose. This change affects developers who create or modify these assistants, requiring them to update their references to the new name. Users will not notice any difference in how the software functions.

aa60399b6484e377d98b1019aeeb71cddb35a9f7.text: The tool that helps users create custom AI assistants now recommends leaving out unnecessary details to keep setups simple. It also stops saving the full history of past chats by default, so each new request starts fresh unless the user specifically turns history on. This affects people building these assistants, making their creations less likely to get confused by old, irrelevant information.

4af568e3b32db5534f947b63c2757ecdadd51dc7.text: A small internal update changes how two automated checks run at the same time. If one check finds an error, the system now stops immediately and reports the failure, rather than waiting for both to finish. This helps developers catch broken code faster.

72a02114a2e6eb2217d3fc8708f929d3add4be03.text: The rules for building custom AI assistants now accept extra details in the instructions. This fixes internal checks that were failing. Nothing changes for you today; this just makes sure the system can read your custom assistant setups correctly later.

d21d710cf42b82018cf932cf5e1f198fffbbfda9.text: The assistant's internal guidebook for choosing AI models and sub-agents now shows helpful suggestions when typing names, while still allowing custom entries. This change affects only how the system validates these choices during configuration, not how the assistant behaves once running. Users will not notice any difference in the assistant's responses or performance.

7527c0a7c324cab08cd2bdfcf50ad1f36c7185d2.text: The system now checks that assistant templates use the correct setup for handling multiple steps, preventing errors when an assistant tries to run a task. It also tidies up how optional information is listed in the template's instructions. This is an internal fix for developers building assistants, so regular users will not notice any changes today.

a4b0ea11e13a93f5e7b551abb1707fc9ee1c3002.text: The AI assistant stopped using a special note that told other AI helpers when to call it. This cleanup is live. People building custom AI helpers will notice the assistant no longer reads that old instruction field.

74192bdfeee65d5aa1b80b1a6aa04ffb8729d975.text: The tool now prints a final summary line when it runs in the special quiet mode for scripts. This summary shows the total cost of the task and, if a specific helper was used, its name. Normal interactive use is unchanged, and the summary only appears if that quiet mode is turned on.

d622228ad6f7ed2f513ea29a275fb0320e11ce4b.text: The rules for creating custom AI agents were tightened to match the main system's requirements, ensuring all parts fit together correctly. This affects developers building new agents, who must now follow stricter formatting for tools and instructions. Regular users won't notice any changes today, as this is an internal cleanup to prevent errors when new agent features are eventually released.

89c06b888049cf9b4ccc2f9aea55a94be65c1983.text: The software stopped rejecting certain custom agent setups that were actually valid. This helps developers building AI agents. They would notice their agent configurations work without triggering false errors.

7b80473853699462c74086a14d9469dfe74ad33b.text: The guidebook for creating custom AI assistants was updated to clarify how to label them and define their behavior. This change helps people who build these assistants choose the right settings for how the AI responds, such as giving just the final answer or showing all its steps. Nothing changes for regular users today; it only improves the instructions for those making new assistants.

7508b2be3b88e55e57c075a834b372d30079dc27.text: The system now records a private note whenever it automatically finishes a command for the assistant. This helps internal teams understand how often the assistant needs help completing tasks. No changes appear in the interface.

276e16b060b9f993e6241f7324832c854f91e369.text: The coding assistant now checks your project's settings file for specific instructions on which core engine and helper tools to use. If you list these names in the file, the assistant uses them instead of its standard automatic choices. This feature is active today, but you will only notice a difference if you manually edit the settings to include these new options.

418e37a511f2212b05f77068a7df9729319842ad.text: The system now waits for a specific tool signal before finishing a response, instead of guessing based on any text. This prevents the assistant from adding unwanted extra words to regular messages. The change is internal and live today, so you might notice fewer strange endings in replies.

b63965d158c74af7166ecdf38ae280c47558b59b.text: The assistant now finds custom helper programs in any folder inside the project's agent directory, instead of only looking in one specific subfolder. This helps people who organize their helper files into different groups or nested folders. They will notice the assistant successfully loads helpers from these new locations without needing to move files to a single folder.

d39fb2a7a256b86714f97ecfc5a88bba683ff648.text: The system now records the correct parent link when creating a sub-agent. This ensures internal debug logs show the accurate hierarchy. Only internal staff reviewing logs will notice the fix.

5a490631f975f1acd63a1dd8fea179f5d515a6f1.text: The software now quietly records when someone switches to the simple text-only view. This is an internal note for the company's data team, so regular people will not see any change in how the tool looks or works.

9a47fef1efdc3b960a1938a606fccacabf2e1448.text: The login tool now opens your web browser correctly on Linux computers. Before, it tried to use a command that often fails on Linux, so the browser window would not appear when you signed in. This fix works right away for anyone using Linux, but you will only notice it if the browser failed to open previously.

f029917387d400e18035491552fbf2449e34dcfb.text: The internal instructions used by the assistant were shortened to match a recent update. This change only affects the test environment and does not impact live features or user experience.

fe4420b9faf6ca73d3d00520acede7cde693c444.text: The release tool now supports a quiet mode that hides animated progress bars and prints plain text results instead. This helps internal teams read output easily when running the tool in automated systems. The change is live today but only affects those who choose to use this specific option.

17342cca0ae01585529c47a6a5cdd7e4adc7eb45.text: A small internal tool that sets up separate workspaces for developers now reuses an existing workspace name instead of stopping with an error. This change only affects the team building the software and will not be visible to customers.

086f05fb5d74098333fcde044dcf86cf49c9ff30.text: This small update improves the list of AI models and helper agents available for configuration. It keeps the list of known options for suggestions while still allowing the use of any other valid model or agent name. Users setting up custom assistants will see better guidance when typing names, but the actual behavior of running assistants remains unchanged.

cf24c26cbd54d0e4138c558ff490c24fd25212f4.text: A small internal update now records the individual pieces of text an AI assistant sends, rather than only saving the final combined message. This change does not affect any visible features or user experience, as it is purely for internal monitoring and debugging purposes.

5796127d324536093f8d647aeede391bb6f2da72.text: The rules for creating custom AI assistants were simplified into a single set. The main instruction prompt is now optional, allowing creators to instead add specific guidance that appears after every user message. This change affects only those building new assistants, and the updated instructions are ready for use.

a16c4ec41998c38d0a50345fccee257214794b2e.text: The assistant now includes a specific example for writing multi-line commit messages directly in the terminal. This helps the AI avoid errors when saving work with detailed notes. The change applies to the background instructions for the coding tool, so it affects how the assistant formats these messages.

7dcd6127d2ca696ada8c442ec76aaf4577035dcb.text: A small internal fix corrects how the tool reads commands when launched as a standalone program. It ignores an extra system path that previously confused the input. People using the compiled version will now see their typed commands process correctly.

7e53db23132ab7e71689b5d4471ccf720748744b.text: The software's safety checks for live text updates were retrained to match how data actually arrives. This internal fix ensures the system correctly identifies when text is complete versus still loading. Regular users will not see any changes today.

793bc101117052c056761dfbc0fd7cf4429171b1.text: The assistant now shows tool details more accurately during live responses. Previously, overlapping data chunks could cause the same parameter to appear twice on screen. This fix ensures each detail is displayed only once, keeping the output clean.

ce83fa99ea83aa3537f20acb5aae221e72e45976.text: When the system fails to read a search request, it now records a detailed error report instead of a vague note. This helps support staff diagnose why a request broke. The fix is live today.

664de46c08e361b11c97a6cfedf7a32a01475c71.text: The system now stops guessing a tool's name from incomplete data, preventing it from overwriting correct information with empty values. This internal fix ensures the assistant uses the right tool when processing complex requests. Users will not see a visual change, but the assistant becomes more reliable when handling streaming text.

da847de456d3be35922ca04d316cd8358084d0bf.text: A small internal fix corrects how the assistant handles incomplete text during streaming. When a partial message ends with a number, the system no longer adds a false closing mark. This prevents errors when displaying answers that include numerical data.

5e852c3246d88793c6b7bb3813885aacd72fe417.text: A small internal safety check was added to the text streaming system. It stops the software from trying to combine new text with an old message if the old message is missing from the start of the new one. This prevents the system from showing broken or incorrect text fragments, though most users will not notice this change because it only triggers when something goes wrong.

72283cb3ad34bc140e2ad843981065e080184a60.text: A small internal fix corrected how a test finds its fake database. This change affects only the developers running tests, not customers. No visible behavior changes for end users.

f511ffec5e7000266f63637f6091a3007e582722.text: The system now uses a simpler signal to decide when an assistant's turn is finished, replacing a list of variations with one fixed marker. It also quietly records when the assistant sends a tool request with broken or unknown formatting, helping the team spot errors. Regular users will not see any change today; this is a small internal cleanup.

eee79edfa37fb1bb1b6ca90cad62fd631448e4b5.text: The software's internal label for handling assistant tasks was updated from a singular to a plural name. This change affects only the backend code and is already active. No users will notice any difference, as the assistant's behavior and features remain exactly the same.

ad1083ef61768cc5b7204ddbf6496fce47284f3a.text: The system now records detailed notes when checking code updates.
