Previously, if a check failed silently, no record was made; now, failures are logged with specific reasons. This helps internal engineers spot and fix problems faster by seeing exactly what went wrong during automated tests.

3e16287740f1557c405ec048a27f206e6e024e1e.text: Shortened internal labels for tool definitions to reduce token usage. This affects only shared core constants. Consumers must use new names; no migration logic. No visible change for non-programmers.

cc5711b84ba75c7380bd25d3caa330dae051142f.text: The assistant no longer records empty messages when you cancel a response without typing anything. This keeps the conversation history clean. You will not see any visual change, as the cleanup happens in the background.

ec444cc309a3733d9fbbba6c0337cbbf34cf31d1.text: The system now cleans up text you type before sending it to the AI. This prevents confusing errors if your message contains special symbols. You will not notice any visual change, but the AI will handle your requests more reliably.

e062af6483335d394a1c2be8a91b4599ccc1c3e2.text: The automated testing system now downloads required tools separately for each test instead of waiting for one shared setup step. Developers will see tests start faster and run more reliably, as they no longer depend on a single point of failure for the initial setup.

ca78bc86d1640981548e39bae60064a23c34e184.text: A small internal cleanup removed a leftover test message from a template used to create a brainstorming assistant. It affects only internal assistant-building tooling. No customer would notice a change today.

827ff59b4b6669d0e8eb5371b47a8a9117715325.text: Developers changed how the system keeps track of information, removing an extra layer of packaging. This is a minor internal cleanup. Regular users will not notice any changes to the software's behavior or features.

9180f967b49b755f230017ac2132da3e6c7bbc2f.text: Fixed the website's internal label for its content library so it points to the correct folder. This stops the site from breaking when building from a clean state. Only internal site builders notice; visitors see no change.

66c78557eea2c8558160e5ab4e935c5cc6b60382.text: Developers updated internal safety checks for a list of supported models. This change does not affect how the software behaves or what users see. It is purely a behind-the-scenes cleanup to prevent future errors.

891b001d3d53cc6a2126eb394646eb83b7bf6e6b.text: The automated system that checks code for errors no longer looks at a specific folder of generated website content. This stops the checks from failing when that content is missing or broken. The change is internal and affects only the team's automated testing process, not the live website.

8a25fb4611c05256e2193ff79c9413a02c311290.text: The automated system that checks the website's code for errors was previously failing because it lacked a specific placeholder file. This fix ensures the placeholder contains the correct data structure, allowing the checks to pass. This change is internal and affects only the development team's workflow, with no visible impact on end users.

8ed339c1d7699ff209dc33c1e12dec59eec7b03f.text: The team updated the automated delivery system that moves files between computers during software checks. This change only affects the internal testing process. Customers will not notice any difference in how the software works.

0bad4769d0cd38a4ed0e0a8876adb49e78f21ce1.text: The automated checks that run every time a change is submitted now happen at the same time instead of one after another. This makes the entire checking process finish faster. Developers will notice their changes are reviewed and ready to merge sooner, while the actual software remains unchanged.

62ad75f8e85230ea5a1da560992088ccfefb3e5e.text: The startup tool now checks for broken installation files. If the tool fails to load, it automatically deletes the damaged file and downloads a fresh copy. This stops the 'unknown error' crash that happened when the previous download was interrupted.

bf47687a2f5b7d5d3ebd9654c84dd6cfc2635ac8.text: The system now skips saving the assistant's reply if the text is completely blank. This prevents empty entries from cluttering the conversation history.

439503d77504035e2ea8d25c66ad6f823ceeec76.text: Small internal change. The timeline view in the admin tool no longer cuts off long event details after the first thousand characters. Anyone reviewing a trace will now see the complete text in the scrollable box instead of a shortened snippet ending with a truncation notice.

aaa25aa7b24c5e242be4f228b30342df56d3a699.text: The system now shares one copy of its tools with other checks instead of each one rebuilding them. This makes the checks start faster. Only the team running the checks will notice the speed-up.

a17bd25564db357988d60a0d237cd9f78965e725.text: The system now builds the conversation summary only when the agent actually starts working. This stops the software from doing extra work if it stops early. You will not notice any difference.

6f93b768db05fb9d083095d985b3f2c71c6330fe.text: Internal tools now let developers name a new workspace with a slash, like 'feature/login'. This change is live for the team's scripts. Regular users will notice nothing.

def525e231d81e806379a00bd1bcab9d0b355cc1.text: The system now strictly checks if a model is known before allowing cache control. If the model is not recognized, it defaults to no cache control. This affects all models that are not in the list of known models. Users will notice that unrecognized models no longer have cache control enabled.

2f5589814f6e96270288d13fa4d68150c8168ffc.text: The system now saves temporary login details for a short time instead of asking the server every time you start a task. This makes the tool launch about seven times faster. The saved details automatically expire after fifteen minutes or if the project settings change, so the system stays secure.

2cff88d16544598e296e6fcae972f6cba7e2b09c.text: The team updated the automatic checks that verify how much AI usage gets recorded for billing. These checks now run using a different testing tool to match the rest of the project's setup. Nothing changes for anyone using the product today; the system still tracks usage exactly as before. This was a small internal cleanup to keep the code running smoothly.

e7cb3d09fc3c812260954b2f81a66e6d69aa5a3d.text: The system now checks test files for errors, which it previously skipped. This change is for internal code quality and helps developers catch mistakes early. Users will not notice any difference in the product.

6959c02278f1642cd72694ffdb80e2a0c6faad41.text: A small internal fix now finds the project's main folder using version control history, rather than relying on where you happen to be standing. This stops a helper script from accidentally leaving you in the wrong folder after it finishes its work. The change is live today for anyone running this specific helper script.

68652f26a1bd45f7c131446ef1502231b7d11d62.text: The software no longer checks for mistakes in the names of AI models used for automatic tasks. This change removes a test that verified the system would reject unknown model names. Since the system now accepts all available models, this check was no longer needed. No visible changes will occur for users.

dc3464289d810a13a28c83a8819cc271ba7d7fef.text: The assistant stopped cutting off old conversation history when it marked a task step as finished. It now keeps more of the chat context before trimming it to fit the size limit. This is an internal cleanup. You would not notice any difference in how it works.

95a48c9ea91d41af4131419ed361f2c4c750032c.text: The system now checks the safety of its own internal test instructions, which it previously ignored. This helps catch small errors before they affect the main program. No visible changes will occur for users.

ee8e6301311b44ef7cb96b26520e91491d70627e.text: A small internal update makes the developer tools start faster and show less clutter. It stops the tool from checking for updates and hides extra messages during startup. Developers will notice a cleaner command line and slightly quicker launch times when working on their computers.

a13b3c9856e6d29b405dfadd13b653a238209633.text: The system now creates the conversation summary right before sending it to new helper tasks, rather than earlier in the process. This is an internal cleanup that ensures the summary always uses the most recent messages. Users will not notice any difference.

e6ded262964744c92e4326959417d7736f3701bf.text: The label for an agent's job description was changed from 'description' to 'purpose' to make its role clearer. This internal rename affects how the system reads and displays agent capabilities. Existing saved configurations using the old label will stop working until they are updated to use the new one.

0e41172996f3dd2745000897a3c458628fac06e2.text: The team turned on automatic checks for the code that tests the system's inner workings. This affects only the internal tools used by the staff, not the customers. No one will see any change in how the product behaves.

508f60b39f1be9bc9378731c213ef28bb877542b.text: A small internal update teaches the main assistant to contact an existing helper for similar tasks instead of starting a new one. This change affects the assistant's internal decision-making process. Users will likely not notice any visible difference, though the system may become slightly more efficient by avoiding duplicate work.

ad42541ac1c3f1411509997cf39d2b3b4b1b2dcb.text: The assistant stopped repeating a fixed reminder to create helper tools during tasks. This internal cleanup affects the underlying instructions sent to the assistant. Users will not notice any visible change in the interface or responses.

f0a62f722271bc4b4c88ecad14e52763a6d613e1.text: Internal testing guidelines now require a specific mocking method to prevent tests from interfering with each other. This change affects only developers writing automated tests. No user-facing features changed; the update is live for the internal team.

169cfe8a9f32a7b2bde473a27ebe649ac2b83eec.text: Internal software now rejects old configuration files that try to replace standard assistant behaviors. Teams using these specific setup files will see an error message until they update the settings. This change is not visible to general customers.

91ff102e9aadb77aa7816450ee5fcb75796a5f05.text: The command-line tool now displays the correct summary text when listing built-in agents. This fixes a minor internal bug where the wrong data field was being read. Users of the command-line interface will see accurate descriptions instead of generic placeholders.

44b7f2568a6baa967756a741becc676cd3fe029c.text: A small internal switch was turned on. Background tasks now keep running even if the main chat stops. This change is live but invisible to most people.

e920a2f1fe10f912bb442ac482bf8667e79a2f27.text: The system now recognizes built-in tools by their simple names, ignoring the default company label. This change is internal cleanup for how names are checked; users will not notice any difference in how the tools work or appear.

c8e6db866b61d942679a726e78ec4e9a92a35cd0.text: The team turned the automated end-to-end checks back on after pausing them. These checks verify that the different parts of the system work together correctly. This is an internal quality control measure, so customers will not see any visible change in the app.

e707c836ad521ed123cdde4bdef3ed4013f2e367.text: The system now correctly handles situations where an assistant's role hasn't been assigned yet, instead of forcing a placeholder label. This fixes an internal logic error that could cause confusion when starting new tasks. No visible change for users today, but it prevents potential glitches in task routing.

5e1975004572293ca62e0cf83def9374a05bc5aa.text: The command-line tool now automatically finds custom helper programs you create in your project's special folder. If you add a text file describing a helper, it will appear in the tool's menu and suggest itself when you type its name. This change is active immediately for anyone using the tool in a project with that folder.

8d7bb32e78128440de4ac3d4818e2ea45519aeb7.text: The search tool now looks for conversation history in a new, separate storage area. This internal cleanup ensures the tool finds the right data without crashing if the history is missing. Regular users will not see any changes, but the system is more stable behind the scenes.

7f421fb293897e10ee8363f69dac6b658b18bbc0.text: Internal cleanup. The assistant's tools now get session details handed to them directly, rather than digging through a shared state box. Users notice nothing.

929d9ff13003b9dbefd44bae79afcf9d0fd8a51f.text: The assistant now finds custom instruction files in the folders you specify, rather than looking only in a single fixed location. This change is internal and affects users who set up their own agent templates. You would notice your custom templates working correctly without needing to move files into a specific hidden folder.

0d4efa922e06c107e1615fa818735ab714d80b75.text: The system now waits for a list of available helper tools to fully load before trying to use them, preventing errors where the tools appeared missing. This change affects internal operations and is live today. Users might notice fewer random failures when starting specific tasks, though there is no visible change to the interface.

7114c75f4aeac61ebbc1dee2fb1aca7b5cfce46e.text: A small internal fix makes the development tool start in the right folder automatically. Only engineers running the software locally are affected, so regular users see no change. Without this fix, the tool might look for files in the wrong place.

1877ed40d79229fd20aa8003bfe0d11e94c1e61d.text: The assistant now records extra details about its internal actions at a lower visibility level, making the main activity log cleaner. Only support staff or developers who open the hidden debug logs will see these new entries. Regular users will notice no change in how the assistant behaves or responds.

7edf8ee1bf22b0138a09bde499dc49c0ed5049da.text: The program's menu now shows a slash symbol as an option to list available commands. The startup message tells people to type slash-help instead of just help. The decorative logo at the start no longer has extra empty space on its left side. This is a small internal fix for the command-line interface.

5c0008ddf0c253f0384c3d7b1494ff9ee681fe6e.text: The system no longer copies the full list of available AI helpers into every base profile. This internal cleanup reduces redundant data storage. Users will not notice any difference in behavior.

d30469f4ee37b3e2cb2dbbece02b52cd4da25f61.text: This small internal fix restores custom helper tools to the main assistant's available list. Previously, these custom tools were missing, so the assistant could not use them. Now, if you have created custom helpers, they will appear and work again as intended.

87cbb266baeb3d24eebce49268d6b5c8aae8e979.text: A small internal change removes a message that appeared when the release tool used your saved access key. Only people who run the release tool see this, and nothing about how the tool works changes. The message no longer prints to the screen.

4716e11693dab3c390eec1579cd6a2f3c9e048f9.text: The system now clears old settings every time it prepares custom assistants, forcing it to reload them fresh instead of keeping stale data. This fixes a bug where changes to assistant rules might not appear correctly. The update is live and affects anyone using custom assistants, ensuring they always see the most current version.

9c18f8cba27f161e20ea2b80e4960dd9b947f44c.text: The command-line tool now accepts two new options to pick a specific assistant and provide extra instructions. This lets users skip the automatic selection process and choose exactly which helper to use. The feature is active today for anyone using the command-line interface.

f6a1aa2d6ace11d33266da263d675a80b28a0751.text: Internal documentation pages now show a clickable link icon beside every section title, not just the main headings. Copying the link takes you directly to that specific section, and the page scrolls to the right spot. This only affects how our internal guides look and behave.

2dce0a73862dce97ed26ca7a5ddeb47dff205c7d.text: The tool now needs a specific label when you tell it which folder to work in, instead of just guessing based on the folder name being first. This is a small internal change for people who run the tool from scripts or command lines. If you have old scripts that just put the folder name right after the tool command, they will stop working until you add the new label.

cff210788c5a35ba898b8d583393e3e7f50b662a.text: The system now cuts off older conversation history slightly earlier to stay within memory limits. This internal adjustment helps prevent errors when processing long chats. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the assistant responds.

b9dbb87a896aeabcc0b59aa2446f3fc4cc520fe9.text: The documentation tool now keeps the original spacing of code examples intact. Previously, the system automatically removed leading blank spaces, which made nested code look flat and hard to read. This fix ensures that code snippets in the guides display with their proper indentation, making them easier to follow.

41d2e750bafe7bf3dc5869a989eaad5032615397.text: The command-line tool now offers a one-shot mode. Instead of staying open for back-and-forth chatting, it answers a single request and immediately closes. This lets people set up automated scripts that ask the tool a question and get the answer without needing to type anything or stay logged in interactively.

87a7b4bd082d74f59360a69b053cfb38d664d942.text: An internal text-generation tool previously forced its output into rigid five-word sentences. Developers removed this strict rule while keeping a general instruction to stay brief. This change is already live but affects only how the system drafts its internal thoughts, so regular users will notice no immediate difference in the final product.

0fd278629c2cc763462e29d5a1af9bb3e5d53588.text: The system now checks if a custom AI agent name is correct before using it. If you type a name incorrectly, the software will stop and show you the exact list of valid names to choose from. This small update helps prevent configuration errors by ensuring names match the official format.

4dac0f67281001587cadf3aa951c7808bad70468.text: The documentation pages now display the correct information for agent templates instead of showing a generic placeholder. This change is live and fixes a visual error for anyone reading the guide.

5161f204cd81fcbc5ba71d8d07f506f6691012b7.text: Developers working on several versions of the same project at once can now run them simultaneously without clashing. Previously, starting multiple copies would cause errors because they all tried to use the same network addresses. Now, each copy automatically gets its own unique address, allowing parallel work without interference.

23de9f55734aef7a9120500e36d0c7d4d7f62746.text: The guide now labels the option for building assistants with custom code as unavailable. This affects people reading the documentation. They see a note that the feature is still being built, rather than an instruction to use it today.

c62f4dc9fafde11f44f2ec090cc5883724b8f1a1.text: The system now uses one shared rule to check which helper agents can be launched. This stops different parts of the program from giving conflicting error messages when an agent name is wrong. The change is internal and affects no visible features today.

c5d753dbc1ccd8b870ef9ebb1091a9ea2ed3ff78.text: The cleanup tool now checks git records instead of folder presence before removal. Missing worktrees trigger a warning, not a failure. This stops automated cleanup from crashing when a worktree is already detached.

b25257700ce48db3c78efbf0dac893ea5940609a.text: The system now checks that any tools assigned to a custom assistant are actually available in the library. If you try to add a tool that doesn't exist, the setup will fail and list the valid options instead of saving the error. This prevents broken assistants from being created.

a2c4d6e1367a1c5e9c15064daca7df9bee181db5.text: A small internal fix stops the system from rejecting valid agent configurations. Users who define custom agents will no longer see false error messages when using them.

21fff52c5c358d9a345f1650a662f63868684bc1.text: The system now checks all custom assistant profiles together before verifying their connections, preventing errors when a profile references another defined later. This affects developers creating these profiles, who will no longer see false warnings about missing connections during setup.

c27f5e78ddbbafb0477a917402d9f52a95566101.text: The internal tools that check code style now use a newer method to load their settings. This change is for the software team building the website, not for regular visitors. People using the website will notice nothing.

698d5a7dcd7fef0a4c035b5f31b8de956b6d9618.text: The internal helper now waits to receive its file search results before starting its deep analysis. This stops it from thinking about incomplete information. The change affects only the internal tooling and is live today.

eea6396c234082bf661564b58677f02bb8119823.text: The assistant now displays a single combined name instead of separate name and title fields. The system also stops showing any label for unrecognized helper types, hiding them completely rather than displaying a generic fallback. This affects how helper agent names appear in tool call outputs.

18a7d79e130256e56788be6703e58d37fea3393f.text: Internal testing scripts now check for the correct label on assistant templates. This change only affects how developers verify the system works. Regular users will not see any difference in the app's behavior.

6120f46401805d692b37253c0c25a1f5642429c3.text: The system stopped writing routine status updates about loading assistant templates to its internal logs. This only affects the team reading those logs during startup, not the people using the software. They will see fewer lines of text in the log files, with no change to how the assistants actually work.

35408cd3842bbf4bad167c04540d583dfb557fe2.text: A small internal cleanup renamed a specific label inside the system's agent profiles from 'type' to 'id'. This change affects the underlying data structure used to identify different assistant modes. Regular users will notice no difference, as the agents continue to function exactly as before.

df51fc0e1225fbef80597abe27c5eaa64314c31a.text: The system now puts the word 'Start' or 'End' at the beginning of its internal notes about agent actions, rather than at the end. It also hides the prompt preview if no prompt exists, preventing confusing 'undefined' text from appearing. This is a small internal cleanup for the support team reading the logs; normal users will not notice any change.

1199aa0919bd7f397b2fea70ce02cb3446efd4df.text: The system now prints fewer routine status messages when it starts up and connects to data services. This change affects the internal logs that developers read, not the features used by regular people. If you looked at the logs, you would see a cleaner list with only important errors or warnings, while the actual performance and functionality of the application remain exactly the same.

c374050938e47559d792aad3d2275f0ef4a1b456.text: The system now finds prompt files using shorter paths relative to the current folder or project root, instead of requiring full absolute paths. It also accepts agent names without the mandatory 'CodebuffAI/' prefix, making template configuration more flexible. This change is live and simplifies how developers write and reference dynamic agent templates.

3879fc1debf18baf2a8e1d959e2041b4296b2bef.text: A small internal update improves how the command-line tool handles specific instructions. If a user types a command that requires a slash (like '/reset') but forgets the slash, the tool now sends it to the server instead of trying to run it locally. This prevents accidental errors for internal tools users. The change is live for the command-line interface.

389cd3d7c211f0dba961dfc35b7aa87c3459653b.text: The system's planning and thinking steps now use a different AI model. This switch changes how costs are calculated, with prices doubling for large tasks. Users might see slightly different results or billing for these specific steps.

c7a6f84e1289be28e0cabfaa9ebdf8794ef56daa.text: A small internal update adds a switch to control whether message history includes special memory tags for the AI. This helps the system save costs by skipping these tags when they are not needed. Nothing changes for regular users right now, as this setting is only used by internal tools.

e66dc736378804bdc8127aa28ba797ffa231817c.text: A small internal cleanup updated how the system labels text blocks for AI prompts. This change only affects the backend code and has no visible impact on users today.

7706aeaf01f13d3f8e1ea5e920a0fb082009f9fc.text: A small internal fix stops the AI assistant from showing the same thinking text twice when it explains its reasoning. This affects only the internal chat service; regular users will not notice any visible change.

fb06f629bfcb85e0d6cd534bb051b5f883c3113d.text: The internal startup shortcut now passes extra instructions directly to the main tool, replacing several rigid preset buttons. This helps developers who run the software locally. They will notice fewer menu options, needing to type flags manually instead of picking a preset.

d19b63ec1b9ea8af210ea98a33e2d26948755b09.text: A small internal fix added a cleanup command for developers. It removes old, broken cache files that caused the code checker to get stuck in an endless loop. This change is live for the team but invisible to regular users.

b4d6d0fbaa14e33456d21cdd608258cfb5f47258.text: The internal cleanup tool now wipes all installed software libraries and rebuilds them from scratch. This affects only the team's local development machines. They will notice the cleanup step takes longer to run.

635180e80ec364723d5e85f585f6c41a6c4ef5f2.text: The app now turns on text colors for history and comparison views right after the command starts, instead of tacking the setting onto the end. This ensures the colors appear correctly when someone asks to see changes in specific files. The fix is active now for people using the app's built-in terminal to view their work.

08939022d786bba4e62950f78f41af20c8970592.text: The team added a shortcut to start the local testing environment with one command instead of two. This helps developers work faster by managing the background processes automatically. Only internal engineers will notice this change, as it does not affect the live product.

81f52d5248fd5d7e4690ec9ccfb906c1227b33b9.text: The internal coding assistant now automatically tidies up the layout of text files it creates or edits. This change affects only the assistant's behavior, not the final software product. If a person watched the assistant work, they would see it adjust spacing and line breaks in code files without being asked.

a85766f499aec1bd3697d456c96579cc96144f0b.text: The file-finding assistant now only searches for file names, instead of reading or searching inside code. This makes it faster but less detailed when picking files. The change applies to internal tools and is live today.

ecdf54f5bf58360fb1a7c76c743efdaad2d1aed0.text: A small internal fix stopped the AI assistant from getting stuck in a loop while processing tasks. Users of the agent step feature will no longer experience hangs when the assistant starts its response. This change is live today.

a281199d73d0091ac7696975b6faf1d67b3c6ed3.text: The code review assistant now uses a fixed version of its underlying AI model instead of a generic label. This change is internal and does not affect how the assistant behaves for anyone today.

d16619e75699a919e04e25ff33668dda06aa3767.text: A small, behind-the-scenes update improved how the assistant waits for one task to finish before starting the next. This ensures actions like searching code or running commands happen in the correct order without errors. You won't see any visual changes or new features, but the assistant's internal processes are now more reliable and consistent.

dcf1248b453754e2d0e17116fa2e14f09c82d9e8.text: The assistant now loads its available agent names at startup instead of on-demand. This means the command-line interface can immediately display friendly titles for all agents, including dynamically added ones, rather than falling back to generic identifiers. The change is live and improves how agent names appear in the tool's output.

97312a3108d8be1a0a5f58ce2148bc78eece9abb.text: The system no longer sends certain requests to Amazon's service. This internal routing change affects only how the company's tools handle specific tasks behind the scenes. Users will not notice any difference in speed or results.

496fb51030a09714dde7fc021fcb2eb32a55652f.text: The system's rule for checking custom assistant settings changed. Before, it looked for a nested box labeled 'override' containing the details. Now, the details sit at the top level, and 'override' is just a simple yes/no switch. This is an internal cleanup. No visible change for end-users today.

b2995afb32b7e6eb3c3ddb85200c3278b0118fa1.text: The system now relies on the review step to manually trigger code checks, rather than running them automatically every time files change. This internal change means reviewers must explicitly request validation for code updates. You would not notice any difference in your experience, as this only affects how the internal tools coordinate tasks.

8d3cb7b2c0e4fbd3e9ddb28cdbb162055ad6b434.text: The app’s main account connection now has clearer rules for when it can be treated as ready and when it might be missing. Several places now use that connection once instead of asking for it again. It is an internal cleanup, so no customer would notice anything today.

3e8496cb93ccd1c19a4d7d9b518b13cc5dcc76c7.text: The system stopped keeping two copies of the rules for which files to show the assistant, so it now uses only one central set. This cleanup is internal and affects only the background code that helps the assistant read project files. Users will not notice any difference in behavior, as the change only removes redundant instructions that were already ignored.

774035a626c9551e53042fd4d693a77e1cca6eae.text: The AI assistant now sees a brief reminder of its available tools and helpers at each step of a task, rather than just at the start. This internal adjustment helps the assistant stay focused on the right actions during longer conversations. Users will not see any visible changes, but the assistant may respond slightly more accurately to complex requests.

400b8c3a90390f3fb0404cd254eb867059860c70.text: The markup added to the price of every message sent to the assistant increased from 25% to 30%. This change is live and affects the internal cost tracking for all messages. Non-programmers will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves.

85f076b0a56c344769a76071988df65757d9e09c.text: The internal system that tests how well the AI assistant works on code tasks has been switched to use a standard version of the assistant. This change affects only the automated testing tools, not the product used by customers. Nothing visible will change for end users.

64625567ead79bd99b0320bf96702decfc454488.text: A small internal check was removed. It used to verify how the assistant decides whether to look at more files during a conversation. This affects only the team maintaining the assistant, not customers, and no one would notice a change in behavior.

00ffb9f582ba344870e4fa0cdb418270c9394153.text: The system now handles cases where the service provider does not send back a specific cost number for certain AI models. Previously, missing this data could cause the chat request to fail entirely. This fix ensures the conversation continues normally even if that pricing detail is absent.

616a6df5509f7bf65462b273e0c2ecfe9771e6da.text: The software now requests specific, dated versions of AI models instead of generic labels. This ensures the AI behaves consistently, even if the provider updates their default models. This change is live, but users will not notice any difference in the interface or output.

83921bb4aa7711926563fdc50b85a910e6321c88.text: The service updated its internal connection address to use the standard version of an external AI tool. This change affects only the background systems and is live today. End users will not notice any difference in how the product works.

eb66058492309a7b7172c327206e8e632c636fdf.text: The system now uses different companies to run the Sonnet 4 AI model. If the first two companies are busy or fail, it will not automatically try the third company, Amazon. This small change affects only requests using that specific model. You might see errors or delays if the first two companies have problems, instead of the system quietly switching to Amazon.

5d13344a278455400336c430deb5863c334c223a.text: The system gained a hidden internal tool that creates new AI assistant templates. Regular users will see no change, as this tool operates silently in the background to help build other features.

e0abb539ab48d1673b1f51ac5c9694a7f44ef916.text: The program now automatically chooses your computer's preferred command-line tool, specifically looking for 'zsh' before defaulting to 'bash'. This affects people using Mac or Linux computers who have 'zsh' installed. They will see their terminal window open with their usual 'zsh' setup instead of the standard 'bash' environment.

2f68d11fae988a63fb9174e2eb9c962bb35024c1.text: The system now automatically selects the best available server for the Opus 4 model, matching the setup used for Sonnet 4. This change affects requests using Opus 4, ensuring they route through preferred providers like Google and Anthropic first. Internal users may notice slightly more consistent performance or reduced errors when using this specific model.

7d0a6181c33f2a931e5875bebca10720367bdacd.text: A small internal update makes the browser startup failure message include the underlying error text. Only the person who reads the logs will notice. It does not change how the browser works.

68d3ca003fa1c1a182ad2c44b8b1dbc5bd66c7c1.text: Agent names and titles in internal logs are now bold. Only internal tools display this change. No user-facing impact.

0ecd9ff224a67a92a743b5a786f877c7ba3b8171.text: The system now treats certain failed attempts to stop a user's active session as minor notes rather than serious errors. This change affects only internal engineers reviewing system logs, as the user experience remains unchanged. Engineers will notice fewer false alarms when sessions end naturally or race conditions occur.

4ce94161073ce64fa52f963f037d048e2c0cb27b.text: The assistant now checks instructions for its helper tools against specific rules instead of just confirming they exist. This helps the system spot missing or badly formatted details before starting a task. You might notice clearer error messages if a request is incomplete, but the overall experience stays the same.

1ccc95cc29936ac8318f0a0355e71f8363d88fc0.text: The system now continues to run normally if the background tracking tool fails to start, instead of crashing. Additionally, when a user tries to use a referral code they have already used, the error message they receive is now more accurate.

e319cc9f1ba1c764bbd3b4184a4daafc159b4a3b.text: A small internal fix prevents a rare error when checking live inputs. The system now safely handles missing data instead of crashing. Users will not notice any change, as this fixes a background issue.

c79fb12ffd52c1b21523dd1cb034348adc246fac.text: A small internal fix ensures that when a user stops a running command in the terminal, the process halts cleanly and the loading indicator disappears. The status messages shown while the assistant works were also updated to be more specific, changing from generic 'Thinking' labels to 'Processing results' or 'Fixing' during certain steps.

7f44ae43e17e9fc90c2437036f79653b1a06f858.text: The software now only works with three specific command-line tools: bash, zsh, and cmd.exe. If you use a different tool like PowerShell or Fish, the app will no longer load your custom settings or aliases for it. This change is live and affects anyone using those unsupported tools.

debe21652898b9c67b12812635c192421e055193.text: Typing the @ symbol in the command tool no longer opens the agent menu if the text was pasted. The tool waits a fraction of a second to see if the input arrived too quickly to be typing. This prevents the menu from appearing when pasting text that starts with @.

de0adfaa42b7001c354a9f12849e6c8787dc252d.text: Two experimental helper options were marked as hidden, so they no longer appear in the text menu. This change is active today. If you open the menu, you will see fewer choices than before, with only the standard options remaining.

6c5cd50eb5b2c5cde021aed5e114ed8ed2c6ec1b.text: When a user starts the tool for the first time, it now automatically sets up a configuration file and launches any background tasks defined in that file. If the configuration file already exists, the tool skips the setup and simply notifies the user. This change is live and ensures the tool is ready to work immediately after the initial setup command is run.

cbee75b9d33c371389dd28cf6fcd85ab4696ad08.text: The app now records a separate, more detailed note each time a one-off terminal command finishes running, instead of lumping it in with other activity. This change affects only the internal data collection and will not change how the software looks or behaves for you today.

e885170f4baafbd3be8a299f909fa65cb043f801.text: The app now records a hidden note every time it restarts its command window after a crash or reset. This small change helps the team understand how often that recovery happens. You will notice nothing new, as the note stays invisible and does not change how the app looks or works.

83b0aa5ff659f58a986bf335f79886a5af734025.text: The team moved the description of how the assistant calls its tools to a more organized spot in the internal system. This cleanup helps the software stay tidy but changes nothing for the people using the app today. You will not notice any difference in how the assistant works or responds.

23b42d371db181d709c37c0a39731d191fc78bdb.text: The internal planning assistant now gives shorter, less confident advice. Instead of step-by-step instructions, it lists key points using brief phrases. This change affects only the automated reasoning process behind the scenes and is live today.

5f0216df5b0f3c942990d614ed9a4fd25e4f9cec.text: The AI assistant now has a new 'deep thinking' mode for complex tasks. It only activates after the assistant has first scanned your files, ensuring it has enough context before tackling hard problems. This update is live for all users of the backend assistant templates.

ce2997f5f619c41bfe765bdd5eff650c1221f4d8.text: The staging release process now builds the app using the production environment flag. This affects the test version of the software, not the live public site. People using the test version might see features or data configured for the production setting, even though they are on a staging site.

5f915cbfccf773c50dcaae7f07252cb05150d748.text: The tool previously flagged a connection problem whenever a 60-second timer expired, even if the connection had actually recovered during that time. It now double-checks the real connection status before raising an alert. This internal fix reduces false alarms in the system logs.

77d7fc13548eabc20be1ddfe496b8dcc1b3dba2c.text: Internal testing tools now run checks directly without first loading secret credentials. This speeds up automated quality checks for the team. No customer-facing features change.

dc1b2c1148180d86a198b46e02695549dffc8c15.text: A small internal fix corrects the progress indicators in the command-line tool. Previously, the 'Loading Files...' and 'Saving...' messages could overlap with the 'Thinking...' message. Now, each message stops before the next one starts, so the status updates appear in the correct order without visual glitches.

8be2bbb661ec127dc2574ff6bc279fd40404169d.text: The team removed a specific connection to Amazon's AI service from the server's list of allowed tools. This change affects only the internal system setup, not the features you see. You will not notice any difference in how the application behaves.

5bf96c300de80eb1ef3bd998e094caa2c4fcb332.text: Developers updated how their internal test tools find shared settings, matching a new naming rule. This change affects only the team writing checks for the billing system. Customers and the live billing service will notice no difference, as the actual payment logic remains unchanged.

e9c80a6fe5c9d7f30a11523403a1131f3bb1d220.text: The system now allows a single person to run multiple assistant tasks at the same time without them stopping each other. Previously, starting a new task would cancel the previous one. Now, each task stays active independently until it finishes or is manually stopped. This change is internal and will not be visible to end users.

03fe8206bde10c0562e10a522addbc4d7fc46f5d.text: The build process now accepts custom settings to control which environment the app targets. This change is live and affects the team managing software releases. They can now adjust these targets without editing the core build code.

a69bc4e3c8d448ca21eeabc6ae396dd86d326113.text: A small internal update fixed a broken link in the automated release process. Previously, the system failed to record the correct new version number when publishing updates. Now, the release notes will accurately display the version being distributed.

9cec44f1b6c37819695f699ae2dbea98bf695163.text: The internal tooling team updated the software's release counter to keep track of the latest version. This change does not add new features or fix bugs. No one outside the team will notice any difference in how the software behaves.

6797adce93a659d4f297f1e825d39144ccfbb524.text: Added a new Google AI key to the internal settings list. Only affects internal tools. Nothing changes for regular users yet.

2e66dcc86ca5aa1bb15e1f4ffa7d945edccbfb2c.text: The team updated the internal label for a specific software tool to match a new release cycle. This change is purely administrative and does not alter how the tool functions or what it can do. No one outside the engineering team will notice any difference, as there are no visible updates or new features.

cae5c5a1fd07cc04556965404ef14914d154ee82.text: The safety checks that spot when someone is frustrated with the app are now all stored in one place instead of two separate spots. This is an internal cleanup for the team maintaining the software. Regular people using the app will not see any difference.

8380bf79f11b441193ec517f25828a51c00ae9cd.text: The tool that publishes the production app now checks for new changes before saving its update. This prevents the release process from failing if someone else updated the main list at the same time. It also stops adding extra credit lines to the release notes. Internal only.

bdaa4f573db1c8497738f98fc46fc9638f7fd5ba.text: The automated process for releasing the staging version of the tool was fixed to prevent it from failing. This change affects the internal team who manages these releases, ensuring that only one release attempt happens at a time to avoid conflicts. The public-facing software is not affected, and no visible changes will appear for end users.

9aa62e6fc2e7bbd7c23dfb2683e7148104dc39bc.text: The release process for the production app was reorganized to prevent mistakes. Staff can no longer type any version number; they must pick a standard option like a small fix, a new feature, or a major update. This makes the automatic versioning more reliable and consistent.

0414ada5ace4f7643bca8f637b2f95d76e9b840e.text: The test checking for repeated cancellations now points to the correct source for its data labels. This is an internal fix; regular users will notice no changes.

b8c97893092cb3f84e402605f5a251bdc9d69d57.text: The website now shows that free credits cover a few hours of work, not a full day. This change affects visitors viewing the pricing page. They will see a shorter time estimate next to the credit amount.

3237af0f56fa929e72b7e167200b0b147065f699.text: A short note was added to the internal instructions for the AI coding assistant. It tells the assistant to follow the main system's rules for using tools, rather than the older rules found in this specific file. This is an internal cleanup to prevent confusion for the assistant. There is no change to how the software works for regular users.

17c6428faea219ee83e0ae6df5f827947fd6f4fe.text: The table comparing AI models got clearer. Model icons look sharper and have more space. A new reasoning model now shows its proper name instead of a code. These changes appear immediately on the website.

82f003f63cd3aa047d21b52dfa4e217f63e00658.text: A small internal fix corrected how a testing tool finds its settings. This ensures the tool can properly load its configuration data. Regular users will not notice any changes.

92b3b3a5ff8e8910a101a21676719d3bdb186383.text: The evaluation dashboard now shows an average turns metric, provider logos, and friendly model names. Non-technical reviewers comparing AI models will see cleaner, easier-to-read results. This change is live today.

e57ce1f53d19292bce98742f4cf4e9ae126de40b.text: The app now loads its terminal tool only when needed, preventing crashes if the tool is missing or unsupported. This affects internal users running the app. They will notice the app starts reliably even if the terminal component fails to load.

d083cff15fc40d13c7e6c3e4d7e2170c8698605a.text: Small internal fix for the billing system. It stops the service from getting confused when the same credit request arrives twice at the same time. If you paid for credits, you now reliably get them, even if the system tried to give them to you twice.

c1d532c6f8f9e4700de685a185841538982693ca.text: This small internal change fixes a broken safety check in the code. The check now correctly measures waiting time for connection problems. Users will not notice anything different.

60e272f574e6f7175ae85a97934f13da57f22559.text: The setup guide for our internal team was simplified. New members now verify their access permissions manually and skip a separate build step, making the process faster and less prone to errors.

1232858ff022388ff4512d9afdc3ed9355f7638b.text: The app now puts its search helper into the same folder it already uses for settings, instead of a fixed spot that some computers reject. This affects people running the tool on their own machines. They might notice fewer random failures when the app tries to find files.

61ca242ce408f41d09797ebba92e865d5a6cd6ff.text: The team swapped the brain powering a specific internal test tool to a faster, cheaper option. This change only affects how the company measures the tool's accuracy behind the scenes. Regular users will notice no difference in the app's behavior or features.

6d11303a006de71433f2ca2b745f4fc9a30e8dd9.text: The setup guide for the password manager tool was updated to use numbers instead of letters for its sub-steps. This affects only internal team members who need to configure their local environment. They would notice the list format looks more consistent and easier to follow.

11f4ea2be931e7b97512cdc1b4492488b43d6bb5.text: The system now cleans up temporary connections after checking your progress. This stops old links from piling up and slowing things down over time. You will not notice any visual changes, but the tool should run more smoothly during long sessions.

8ee68ac2626b70c448b989f087e0528f259ef1fd.title: Add foundation-backend-desktop mode and storage intent angle
8ee68ac2626b70c448b989f087e0528f259ef1fd.summary: New `foundation-backend-desktop` mode and `storage` intent angle added to Supabase ads. `sponsored-capability.ts` defines `hasCommittedAuthBoundary` and `hasCommittedStorageBoundary` as optional booleans, treating missing values on older clients as unknown, never provider-open. `supabase-format-experiment.ts` introduces `SUPABASE_BACKEND_FOUNDATION_VERSION` and `supabaseFoundationDeliveryVersion` to route backend-desktop traffic. `SUPABASE_FORMAT_BACKEND_FOUNDATION_PAIR` consolidates database, auth, and storage under one procedure and budget.

0b6573799be418d6a3b484d3a804bd6d4ceaed55.text: The release tool now prints a direct link to the specific build job it just started, instead of a generic page. This helps internal staff track progress immediately. If the link cannot be found, it falls back to the general list. The change is live for the release script.

86e1d94b91de38f7ecca0cf6a00227041586645b.text: The release tool stopped trying to print a direct link to the specific release progress page. Instead, it now provides a general link to the main actions dashboard. This affects internal release operators. They will notice the tool prints a generic monitoring link rather than a specific status page link.

df45175bae82d4e037863f76c0b41eb887cce029.text: We stopped the system from recording routine details every time a user signs in or connects to a live chat. This is an internal cleanup to reduce clutter in the technical records. Customers will not notice any change in how the product works or looks.

1c6183b12a7c1cfb8082014c4a7388e3b858f58d.text: A small internal fix corrected how a specific part of the application finds its logging tool. This resolves technical errors for the package, ensuring the software builds correctly. End-users will not see any changes in the app's features or appearance.

74f862240de8082d65de13657ebbce64f417518e.text: A small internal update ensures that the tool's executable file is automatically deleted from your computer's configuration folder when you remove the software. This change applies to all users who uninstall the program. You would only notice this if you manually checked your system folders, as it prevents leftover files from cluttering your device.

00b0464d1e5bdd1c3878e80d5ef437d47607c833.text: The release tool now checks the installed program's version without freezing, and if that check fails or times out, it automatically downloads a fresh copy. Before downloading, it deletes any existing program file to prevent corruption. This internal fix ensures the tool recovers from broken installations instead of getting stuck.

b2b3aaa23e889cff8ee71ca19b84cce0686ed8dc.text: A small internal update ensures the database viewing tool now loads necessary setup details before starting. This change affects only the person running the tool directly on their own computer. They would notice no difference in how the tool looks or works, as this fix simply aligns it with other database commands.

c027e956959f160bd402b2f4f53525684b3a71af.text: The tool that checks for new versions now asks the public release page instead of the private data service. This stops the check from failing when too many requests are sent in a short time. Only internal staff running the release process will notice, as the tool no longer skips version checks due to limits.

3a774075882c5ef899ea5c7d2f22f042a5cfe521.text: The release tool now uses a standard message channel to report when it cannot check for new versions due to usage limits. This change affects only the internal team members who run the tool. They will see the warning message appear correctly in their output, even if the tool's display settings are not fully active.

6ad625158f885c1b71f08d85e09af0b251bd0ed3.text: The release tool now shows a brief 'Request timeout' message when a download takes too long. Detailed internet troubleshooting advice only appears if a required program fails to download. Internal tooling change. No user-facing impact.

435945b5b0aaa397d68c6640aca3a6e71253a9c9.text: The assistant's terminal now switches to a simpler command runner if its preferred terminal tool fails to load. This helps people whose computers cannot run the advanced tool, letting them still see command output. Nothing changes for people whose computers already work normally.

85ddb95a1fe7571d1f8d7ce2ec487d03d914ca29.text: The software now hides connection errors from a background tracking service. If that service fails, the error message no longer appears in the command line output. This change is live and affects only the text displayed during use.

20dcc6293f261bd06981d359e60546744e996610.text: The command-line tool now tracks how long it waits for a response. If the spinning indicator remains active for sixty seconds without stopping, the tool records this as a potential hang. This happens automatically in the background. You will not see any visual changes or alerts, but the data helps the team understand when the tool seems stuck.

fe06b462903daa6168304889fbcbb20b4048c5e5.text: The command-line tool now prints a hidden list of lingering connections when it shuts down, but only during development. Regular users see no change, as this extra detail stays invisible outside the internal testing environment.

c2d6adcb343dd8f939311cc7da0b76bf29e6db30.text: The app now allows a larger amount of data to be stored temporarily when saving project states. This prevents the saving process from stopping unexpectedly if the project contains many files. The change is active immediately and requires no action from you.

5123f79a82386fcd6ca8efae0a37a195e413dcec.text: The app now hides more types of background errors from the analytics service from appearing in the developer's console. This change affects only internal developers who inspect the console while using the app. They will see a cleaner console with fewer irrelevant error messages when the analytics service encounters problems.

4e3e8200cd129ec8dfe12d711fdeba3f4fc006da.text: The system's automated safety checks were updated to verify that the research tool is correctly disabled when the assistant is in read-only mode. This change ensures the code matches the intended behavior, preventing accidental access to research features during restricted operations. No users will notice any difference in the assistant's behavior today.

6ed878c5dd69e33bc73de7685041095eadec1ca9.text: The internal labels for the assistant's instructions were renamed to match their actual text values. This change only affects the assistant's configuration files and has no visible impact on users.

7b5459d51edc76f4a51e4d459a178a332ee668b9.text: A small internal change makes view-only assistants stricter. When someone uses the assistant in view-only mode, it can no longer run research or create a plan. They would notice those actions disappear or be refused, while normal answering still works.

a5b2752eb82cd7b4474b4983077adddd5ab00e0b.text: We renamed internal labels for parts of the assistant's instruction templates to make them easier to read. This change affects only the backend code and does not alter how the assistant behaves. You will not notice any difference in your experience.

ab5e6a57326209d71b9002a0e5b9745d811bf7f3.text: A small internal update ensures the assistant always uses the correct current location when generating prompts. This change prevents the system from relying on potentially outdated location information provided by other parts of the software. The update is live and improves reliability, though users will not notice any visible changes in the interface.

8c04479d0caecd8aa5812727bd1cadf50105912e.text: Fixed a bug where the system forgot to tell the AI assistant it was in 'view only' mode. This affects internal testing or specific 'read-only' agent scenarios. Without this fix, the assistant might have thought it was allowed to change files even when it was supposed to only look at them.

f8f58ec037f484a0a5384574eae6fc0ad900d9ab.text: Internal renaming of data fields to match standard library expectations. Affects backend tool definitions. No user-visible change.

69458a874a9b7c3eff67230f67a642e3abec0526.text: The system now uses a fixed list of labels for filling in details within the AI's instructions, replacing flexible text tags that could be mistyped. This change is internal to the software's construction process. Users will see no difference in how the AI behaves or responds.

beaf6f94b3b2db8a62053df80b11b82a4ecfdea0.text: Labels for the AI assistants changed from generic names to model-specific names. This affects only the internal naming system, not how the assistants behave or what they can do. Nothing visible to end users has changed; the assistants still work the same way.

eb2ac674792a936a452b6c47421377c77305333f.text: A new shortcut was added to the internal system to help standardize how instructions are formatted for AI agents. This change is currently in place but does nothing yet, as no other part of the system uses it. It will not affect any visible behavior or features at this time.

207152a623b63fa174750ef851d43bbca9fb0b9c.text: A small internal setup change now automatically supplies secret settings whenever tests run. Programmers will notice fewer failed checks caused by missing environment variables.

354a3463a809a8e900ff1546905f709928113ff9.text: The internal setup for one AI assistant model was simplified to remove duplicate instructions about its available tools. This change is purely for the software's internal organization and does not affect how the assistant behaves or what it can do for you.

68860ccd6a481f9ab06194546f95648dfd194bb3.text: A small internal fix corrected how the system labels a folder's location during automated checks. This change does nothing for regular users and is not live today.

5903e989582d7d2867a98b6d83e486af72c8e755.text: A small internal check was corrected to ensure the assistant properly counts down its remaining steps. This fix only affects the software's internal testing process. Users will notice no changes to the assistant's behavior.

c3b5a8116e599533e82169570bdd41a80090e74a.text: The label showing the initial folder location was updated to be clearer. This change only affects how the status information appears on the command line. It does not change how the software works or behaves.

9a2c50ecef123fa892f16647fc653ab27056ac77.text: The system now records which specific assistant model was in use when an error occurs. This change affects internal support staff who investigate problems. They will see the model name next to the error message in their logs, making it easier to identify which model caused the issue. It is live today.

7573845dff6f240690ee1ca5520c437749553b8e.text: The AI assistant now uses a single countdown clock to decide when to stop acting on its own, replacing an older, unused counter. This internal cleanup ensures the limit of twelve steps is applied consistently without redundant tracking. You will not notice any change in how the assistant behaves.

ebefaef283560321a2112374229ed3ac84f6aa75.text: A note about pricing was deleted from a webpage comparing two AI coding tools. The page no longer claims that one tool offers pay-as-you-go pricing for occasional users. This change affects only visitors reading that specific comparison page on the company's website.

d51122bc6283ab2e8626aa3c4941114502bb2581.text: The assistant now tracks your current folder location in a single, central place instead of separate spots. This internal cleanup ensures it knows where you are working, especially after running commands that change directories. You won't notice any new features, but the assistant should handle file paths more reliably.

03bbd82e9081359b0b0d3a27b7c923a15027756a.text: The help page for the assistant now tells people how to check if they have the newest version, and what to do if it gets stuck updating. It also changed the fix for failed installs to point to the right folder instead of using a risky shortcut. This is live now.

69fffe8f6b530e155e645d0bfd9c931f24294498.text: The system stopped telling the assistant to treat its own past replies as errors to be fixed. This change is internal and live now. You will notice no difference in the chat interface.

29fe45e5bc81dd36fae50d786fdb476225b51471.text: The system now checks the list of available actions more strictly to prevent errors. This internal fix helps developers catch mistakes early, but regular users will not notice any change in how the software behaves.

25737320854a10c0e05284c05d711f3c133d8611.text: The system now makes short labels by combining the current time and a random value with ordinary number math, instead of a slower big-number method. This is already live, but it only affects the part that creates those labels. The labels still look and work the same, so people using the app will not notice a change.

1c584685b8d0df69908061aea316c1a766ed8b2f.text: The tool now checks if starting or closing takes longer than five or ten seconds, respectively. These checks are live, so the system can flag unusually slow launches or exits.

588e20211f58ae72afe95da52e254881bed967cf.text: The evaluation process now runs against the live production environment instead of a local test server, and it sends fewer requests at once to prevent overload. This change affects only the internal testing team and does not impact regular users or customer-facing features. It is active today.

df2b439018be96faa7142d9a7cd3b706cc079288.text: A small internal adjustment improves the visual consistency of loading indicators in the command-line tool. Previously, the system automatically added dots to status messages, which could result in double dots if a message already included them. Now, the dots are manually specified in the text, ensuring that status updates like 'Thinking' correctly display as 'Thinking...' without duplication.

aac5b2350146850b8962175c788b529f22ce966a.text: The software's internal quality checks were updated to match how it currently handles text formatting. This is a minor maintenance task for the development team and does not change how the application works. Users will not notice any difference in features, speed, or appearance.

87eb5eb7a63480b24bbd7f947b43ea4810175046.text: The internal research assistant now stops after ten questions and reports problems as plain text instead of crashing. This small change affects backend staff running the tool. They would see the assistant finish cleanly even if a question fails, rather than stopping entirely.

8364c1755c3e8f79e43aa9e99c5cfc08144406b1.text: The system now creates shorter, unique reference numbers for messages and records. These new numbers are safer to use in web links and are much less likely to accidentally duplicate. Regular users will not see any difference, but the underlying data management is more reliable.

c07d48726435795bf1fa8d2c432fb6293514a308.text: The system now waits for the terminal to finish loading your personal settings before running any new commands. This prevents errors where a command fails because it cannot find a tool or setting defined in your configuration files. The fix applies to the internal terminal interface and is live today.

4d9e40f7c092b0135e56b8171b1b265500bd9fed.text: The backup system stopped creating duplicate snapshots for projects containing nested folders. This fixes cluttered history for internal users. You will see fewer repeated save points when restoring previous versions.

4d433c8d0d500bf95a5c5753c6f08fac12b791be.text: The assistant no longer stops itself when it thinks it is repeating the same step over and over. This change affects internal tools only. A non-programmer would notice nothing different, as the safety net for stuck loops is gone.

b6fd8c63140a17abf9b53e0f06b42c86fc0fee66.text: The system now stops the research assistant after a set number of steps, preventing it from running indefinitely. This change is live immediately for all research tasks. A user might notice that complex queries occasionally return partial results or stop earlier than expected if the limit is reached.

4f0bacb0c98336fac86fa041ce9c6959aeeb05bd.text: The tool now decides on its own which key presses count as 'frustrated typing,' ignoring special keys but counting repeated normal keys or Control-C. This internal cleanup does not change how the program looks or acts for the user today, but makes the detection logic easier to adjust later.

132bf926a3c2470e980eb5ce46eeab6dd706e400.text: The system now checks if a test repository download finishes correctly before moving on. If the download fails, it stops and shows a clear error message instead of running tests on empty files. This helps internal developers find broken tests faster, but does not change anything for customers.

5b0bc2ee0c6750a08a79eade0d96ec883d7c1dc4.text: The assistant can now perform actions behind the scenes when displaying tool results, rather than only showing text. This internal update helps the system run tasks without adding extra visible text to the chat. There is no immediate change to what you see or do.

841b80ab4b870a94374df2dc2e14c6f9102347d1.text: The research status indicator now animates instead of showing static text. The background system also cleaned up invisible spacing characters in its internal communication. These are small, live internal adjustments.

db5d4f0c2380c1f7611e751b59ca245bfbd7acd2.text: The tool now checks if Git is installed before trying to use it. If Git is missing, it returns empty results instead of crashing. This helps people running the software on computers without Git installed. They will see the tool continue working normally, just without Git-specific information.

83880a24d1c3cac370970d5462d2df3b639421e2.text: This small internal update improves how the system reports errors from the AI assistant during testing. When a problem occurs, developers now see the original error message attached to a new one, rather than just a generic summary. This change only affects non-production environments, so customers will not notice any difference in the live service.

a25a238939b4c0fe11835c0a3c59e8cf187002c6.text: The loading indicator now shows specific actions like 'Saving' or 'Using browser' instead of always saying 'Thinking'. This applies to the command-line tool. Users will see clearer status messages while the tool works.

b8ceddac690afbc228b27371a86e248341a91e40.text: When saving progress, the screen now shows a 'Loading' message while waiting for the system to be ready, then switches to 'Saving' once the actual work starts. This small visual change helps people understand what the computer is doing during the wait. It affects anyone using the checkpoint save feature.

a3673d4fd91b47f3b7608ca5ac280213e0619fd9.text: The system now handles private code repository access more securely during test setup. This internal tooling improvement ensures tests run reliably in automated environments. Developers will notice fewer setup failures when working with private repositories.

abc62735a6c1356953de5dc78deb7bb0a394fd7b.text: Previously, the app sometimes created two separate folders for a single chat session because different parts of the system guessed different names at slightly different times. This fix ensures all parts agree on the folder name before saving any files. Users might have noticed duplicate or empty chat folders in their project data; this prevents that from happening.

fa845457b7f7ee385a2742e9514707aea22d876b.text: The system now hides extra text about how many tests it runs at once. This change affects only internal checks, not regular users. You will not see any difference in your experience.

2aa6b5383deb1e349339a045cf706e9c7fd3ff79.text: The system now records complete terminal output when commands fail, instead of only saving cleaned-up results. This helps internal support teams see exactly what happened during errors. No customer-facing change yet; only visible in internal logs.

fdcdf800aad9c6dffb6e1c35e61ffa8eb87c2ee7.text: Internal cleanup. Removed redundant setup steps from six project configs. No user-facing changes. No one notices anything.

1807375bb53c78d2a9eb6c1134ebf0ee1058d28f.text: A small internal fix ensures that when the system runs background tests, it correctly passes along the specific settings needed for the AI model to work properly. This resolves an issue caused by a previous update where the test runner was missing these instructions. No changes are visible to users; the system simply operates more reliably behind the scenes.

7d08f24b7939469a6bb9807a009b11e887bee60a.text: A small internal adjustment ensures the evaluation system waits for its setup tools to finish loading before starting. This change affects only the automated checks that run in the background. You will not notice any difference in how the application looks or feels.

9da3544686236b416ac81189fc7db12c5a165403.text: A small internal fix makes the system check if a folder is actually a valid repository before reusing it. If the folder exists but is broken, the system deletes it and starts fresh. This prevents errors when running tests, so the system works more reliably.

7cbac9a2d89aa8b248701d95de168616cb50c26b.text: The tool used for testing internal code now always looks for the testing server at a fixed local address. It ignores any custom address settings. This only affects the automated tests running on a developer's own machine and ensures they connect to the correct local service.

1f3755c0c96867ce04ebd78d17c16f61052cc7d2.text: A small internal update lets the evaluation tool run directly without needing to compile its helper code first. This change affects only the internal team running these tests. They will notice that starting a test run is faster because it skips the extra preparation step.

6c31588bc5e211b48a3a96148febfa2bfd5237c8.text: The automated testing system now uses clearer instructions to decide when to run checks. This small update ensures the system correctly skips tests when not needed, preventing confusing errors. It is live today and affects how the internal quality checks start or stop.

bcd24d28ecd1f45921ad9f729c7cbf458b5590a1.text: A small internal fix ensures a specific tool is fully ready before other tasks try to use it. This prevents occasional errors when developers run local commands or build parts of the app. Regular users will not notice any difference in the application itself.

ae93fb9037b77824d4f83612a95332ecd9808060.text: This small internal fix ensures the evaluation system finds its data files correctly, no matter where the script is started from. It affects only the team running these internal tests. They will notice fewer errors when launching the test suite from different folders.

3feed691233fe92ca9c52ed90ce0ee8ee9f2d0ba.text: The evaluation system now lets testers choose specific AI models instead of relying on default settings. It also records new performance details like average speed and code quality for each test. This change is internal to the testing tools, so regular users will not notice any difference in their experience.

47e63753ac5af6cc5cd5ee6019db93c2341299cf.text: The system now backs up folders containing separate projects before saving changes, ensuring nested projects are preserved correctly. This internal fix affects only the automated backup process, not visible features. Users will not notice any difference in the interface.

7f4759152d3d6155ab17a1e6aef97fa839f11efb.text: The system now runs fewer evaluation tasks at once, cutting the maximum number from twenty to ten. This change applies to internal tests and will not affect regular users. Staff might see evaluations take slightly longer to finish.

97c512708414a56938ebbe864642895fdbd2246b.text: A small internal fix makes the automated system that checks commit messages handle special characters correctly. This affects only the internal testing process and prevents errors when messages contain certain symbols. You would not notice any change in your daily work.

a150b4e20295d8f907ba8d42f155d5c673decfcd.text: The backup system now ignores folders that look like saved work but lack the hidden marker identifying them as separate projects. This prevents the process from crashing when it encounters these empty markers. Staff running backups will see smoother completion without error alerts for these specific folders.

61268ac205708796f1b4f18854e1300bc3aec722.text: Internal tooling now prints the outcome of each single evaluation run to the console. This change only affects the automated testing scripts used by the development team, not the main product. Engineers will see the final result logged immediately after a test finishes, making it easier to spot issues without digging through files.

5bc5336e85d1d696c5ad4cef471144dde8d91046.text: The system now stores test files in a single folder instead of nested subfolders. This change affects only internal testing tools and is live today. A non-programmer would notice no difference in the product's behavior.

ac79e41ed0b901cae39368732e5b81fff7238729.text: A small internal adjustment was made to the system that runs automated checks. The check now waits two seconds before finishing to ensure all background tasks complete properly. This change only affects the internal tools used by the development team and will not be noticed by regular users.

d376339de7eb134ec935207ad6aa19b2868f9d8a.text: A small internal update now adds the specific repository name to the start of each evaluation log entry. This change affects only the internal team monitoring these automated checks, helping them distinguish which project is being tested when multiple checks run at the same time. The update is live today but does not change any visible features for external users.

5f1ed18014f89acdedf814cf55b5b51da417f550.text: The automated testing system now stops evaluation runs after six hours. This change affects only internal developers who trigger these specific tests. They will notice that long-running evaluations are forcibly ended if they exceed the time limit, preventing stuck processes.

28470c3a9e8357389394996924268aed29a67730.text: Small internal fix. The system now passes large data via a temporary file instead of a long command line, preventing crashes when data exceeds OS limits. Internal evaluation runs only; no user-visible change.

df27c6b9e9aef7642b9eda8e0bf51b528f74ac9f.text: A small internal update improves how the system records failures during automated checks. If a check fails, the error details are now printed more clearly and completely. This change helps the internal team diagnose problems faster, but it has no visible impact for regular users.

d94df780116b6156f0a7b77744a009d7b905d6b8.text: The system now reports task progress instantly as each item finishes, rather than waiting until the entire batch is complete. This change affects only internal monitoring tools used by staff. People watching these tools will see updates appear sooner, though the final results remain the same.

45ccb2377f64a4ca6a029156117dd0f8eb46a462.text: A small internal update ensures the database starts automatically before the web interface launches. This prevents errors when developers begin working on the web app.

cf98ac954a3a21f6fb791b77cf3bde6fd0770b41.text: The system now checks code updates for multiple projects at once instead of waiting for each one to finish. This cuts the total wait time in half, so the automatic quality reports appear much faster.

43ca5a4369d2c74e7dcb209b0cab1db2cecdfff6.text: The system now accepts a wider range of backend address formats during setup. This helps internal deployments use non-standard server locations. You will not see any change in the app interface.

c54707e4cb86937db504b0d826f53eea9f804b10.text: A small internal cleanup stops the testing tool from saving incomplete results to disk after every single check. This change only affects the automated evaluation runs, so regular users will see no difference in their experience.

950cd5b9b5e7ee83e66fb9e5869eaaf0c185bb27.text: A small internal update removed a broken link in the project's setup instructions. This change only affects the underlying system configuration and will not be visible to users. No features were added or removed, and the application will continue to work exactly as it did before.

d725527ba6f5b22819ba432096aec4fd9b2cddb9.text: A small internal fix is live today. When the assistant hit an error while sending a reply, the error could appear as a meaningless placeholder instead of useful details. The fix turns those errors into readable text, so test systems show what went wrong.

11e80bd9328da522db4e8cc400514c22a75e3d4a.text: The assistant now uses Sonnet for standard tasks instead of Gemini 2.5 Pro. Gemini 2.5 Pro is still available but only for experimental features. This change is live and affects how the assistant responds during normal use.

da92ba9d348e354fa12c8b2bd24d530b80ab0356.text: A small internal build setting is live today. It tells the project to use an older helper that prepares the app's files for running, after a newer helper caused the build checks to fail. People using the app would notice no visible change; the affected group is the internal build process.

e489a748c481fd8b8ceb5058f18569b352f6cb49.text: A small internal fix corrects the order of steps used to package a specific application. It ensures that the application's internal links point to the right places after all files are gathered. This affects only the application's packaging process and has no visible change for end-users.

18f6326560ecc0e2ad9f6488a4a3ed7666fed0ec.text: The website now loads faster by fixing how it handles settings and ensuring admin pages show fresh data. Admins will notice the organization export page updates instantly without needing a refresh. This change is live today.

04a2166f8b5c70a58a0466038bcd58ea7978c4e7.text: Internal systems now check if the location of the main server is set. If it is missing, the application will stop working. This prevents errors for the team building the app.

4408b769103ee2e3aa047eb0b7536a7ee198c638.text: The startup script now deletes leftover files from previous builds before launching the new version. This prevents the app from running outdated code during the transition to a new system. Internal developers will notice the app starts correctly without needing to manually clear old files.

d38f9086cbe320727643780ba29111952f098661.text: The startup process for internal web and Discord services was simplified to run directly, removing an unnecessary middleman step. This affects only the internal team, who will now experience faster service launches without extra configuration checks.

754532c99e33cdd53f0bd03a821801d75d8f3635.text: The file-editing assistant now accepts a short description of your goal along with the code changes. This helps the system understand context to make edits more accurately. You might notice clearer summaries when reviewing proposed file updates.

f7d34f17c69f0bb8e2aa5e69238a0d3a689906c1.text: The system now records errors that occur while the AI assistant is generating a response. This helps the internal team identify and fix issues more quickly. Regular users will not notice any difference, though the assistant may behave more reliably as these errors are resolved.
