05394e89a84b9932395cba16a38eb702afef1198.text: The database update command now checks if a specific secure key manager is installed. If present, it uses it to fetch credentials; otherwise, it runs directly. This ensures database migrations work consistently across different developer environments.

a43570ec04636f7a38125ca46b18939316455c86.text: The system now tracks the price of two AI models more accurately. The standard model is cheaper, while a new, more powerful version is more expensive. This change only affects internal cost reports and is live immediately.

c5dd22f472223c5d2350c99c64094b5c323a6345.text: The internal testing system for code tasks was switched back to standard cost settings. This change affects only the team running these evaluations. They will see the tests use normal resource limits instead of experimental ones.

f662f6b5e19599bd4cd3d6de0b9c4adadad06a03.text: The assistant now checks for repetitive loops before applying file changes. This prevents users from seeing edit confirmations followed by a request for direction. The fix ensures the stop signal appears first, keeping the interface clear.

2b543527d01642e2324fed04cadf4a46d17e674f.text: The team added helper tools to the project's setup list so the system's code checker stops complaining during the automated build. They also created a shortcut command to wipe out old, temporary files. These changes are internal housekeeping. Regular users will not see or notice any difference.

8990d2ea0de5d84de0fc91ea0857b743a45edd20.text: A small internal fix updated a setup script to handle hidden messages better across different computer systems. This ensures the database tool runs reliably for developers working in varied environments. Users will not notice any change in the application.

0348b5a9490bec7f2bc5a156e3663ceabeb3a26c.text: A small internal update makes starting the Discord connection easier for developers by automatically finding the right settings. If the secure settings tool is missing on a computer, the system now skips it and runs the connection directly, preventing errors. This change helps developers run the service smoothly without needing to manually check if specific tools are installed.

f32e6b0581ce13c8182457cf05795c17fd0e4da9.text: Internal scoring tool now checks only top 2 file choices instead of 3. It compares AI model picks against a reference answer to see if the best matches align. This helps tune models to be more precise about their top recommendations. The change affects only internal quality checks and does not impact live user features.

19ca4cb6372db69115d8ea599697dc06ab2a23c1.text: The tool that packages this software now finds the right settings automatically instead of relying on a fixed list. This change affects the release process for the command-line app. Regular users will not notice anything, as this fixes internal packaging errors for future updates.

471b9d3f1713c130974280eb79b85d938e7e4ded.text: The assistant can now use two new AI models. This change is just preparation and does nothing yet.

d51f479a1a409ac7291317650365fafbab6a97a4.text: The system now hides the AI's internal reasoning steps from the live output stream. Users of the AI assistant will see only the final answer, not the intermediate thought process. This change is active immediately for the backend service.

a353ad008ce4a61ca8c343ba237f74e33a682389.text: A small internal change makes the file-editing program always add a clear note when it removes something, even a single line, instead of just leaving it out. This affects internal use of the program when it proposes file changes, not ordinary end users. It is active today, and someone reviewing a proposed change would see the removal stated directly.

347deaaf718b8a84bd948c15c626ba291f04242b.text: The system now recognizes two new, more advanced AI models. When selected, these models use a different communication channel and receive specific instructions to stop thinking and start acting as soon as they know what to do. This change is live and allows users who choose these specific models to experience faster responses without unnecessary delays.

9007dc17e64b15a73ec007cf443d64ccba17b765.text: A small internal update fixed how several evaluation tools find their shared resources and automatically set up secure credentials before running. This affects the team's ability to reliably test new features, as the tools now work without manual configuration steps.

cf84049767d3fda35d5b3d7416cfd4390fd79f9b.text: The system now quietly records when a specific type of knowledge file is updated. This is an internal tracking change, so you will not see any new features or visual changes.

e1c1810bac639e58c4caa195d25b153d13d8ded8.text: The system now checks four different parts of your project's history simultaneously instead of waiting for each one to finish before starting the next. This makes the tool respond faster when you ask for context about your files. If one check fails, the others still work, so you get partial information instead of an error.

5079f20cd56303de5154809924493bfcdcb3934c.text: Small live fix. The file list no longer hides folders named env or ENV by default. It still hides the usual hidden settings files. If your project has a real folder called env or ENV, you will now see it in listings and searches.

f79be5425d9a5ce31fb22344a89898b659191a56.text: The tool now correctly shows a file as deleted if it is missing, instead of failing. Internal teams will see accurate change lists for removed files.

1444b463df73811cd59c1c6ff942cd38f3abfae9.text: The system now records the time taken for each conversation step. This change helps the support team track performance internally. Regular users will not notice any difference in their experience.

8fe7e9d8bb38a461a6967cde1c76e62870c81b02.text: The system now limits how much extra reasoning time it spends on certain tasks. This change applies to the internal assistant tools, not the public app. If you looked at the logs, you would see the assistant stops thinking after a set amount of effort instead of using no limit.

9fe1f80112ceb1e4772a7141c6c8f961c0ad4f26.text: A small internal change made the daily checks use the experimental model setting instead of the normal setting. This lets those checks try a newer model. Someone watching the checks would see them use the newer model; no customer-facing behavior changes.

cf7c3ece3945401c9f0aca127e6700fdf1a11b35.text: A small internal safety check now prevents the tool from treating your entire personal computer folder as a project workspace. If you accidentally start the assistant from your main home directory, it will correctly recognize that no specific project is open, rather than trying to manage files across your whole system. This change is active immediately.

d2d9f3ae6eb94c0ae789e285535a8e1d4698ada2.text: The AI assistant now uses a different underlying model for standard and high-performance tasks, replacing the previous default. This change applies to all users interacting with the assistant in these modes. Users will not see a visual change, but the assistant's responses will be generated by a different system.

c1439b43948499b7c377ab1712ed237f9cb6d100.text: The command-line tool now checks the operating system before opening a web browser for login. Windows users can log in without manually clicking the link. This fix is live today.

f6dccab6eadefa9a1223163aff1797d26eb7dd68.text: The program's internal file-checking tools were moved to a shared location to prevent duplicate code. This change affects only the developers maintaining the software. Regular users will notice no difference in how the program operates or appears.

f914e147af1d6985f3b3c9c2ae6b217cd46d522d.text: The assistant now stops automatically running safety checks after every edit. It waits for the project owner to define specific verification steps instead. This change is live for internal users.

bd613eb21be70ac2ad1882719942c4869b09a4fe.text: The assistant now updates its internal notes more often. The previous rule required learning something truly rare before saving it. This change removes that strict limit. It affects the assistant's behavior during conversations. You might see it remember small details more frequently.

542f1be338598c4f9e9944009c47afd6687d87fd.text: The backup tool now saves your work before checking for special folders inside your project. This prevents the tool from accidentally missing recent changes. You might notice that your files are consistently saved in the background without needing manual retries.

d28a2899ada8f0c8ad9a6d2d8f9341d2f01c1a1c.text: The assistant now correctly recognizes local file paths starting with a slash, treating them as files instead of web addresses. This prevents errors when trying to open documents or images stored directly on your computer. The fix is live and applies automatically when the assistant processes local file locations.

99ea9ed3b2b10f6e83fc5a4fde2ce271deedba1d.text: The system now handles empty project folders without crashing. This internal fix prevents errors during data collection. Users will not notice any change.

8c6ad54c0c633e22d707982c3321fdfbf9c19885.text: The assistant's internal instructions now require it to give very short answers. This change is active immediately for all interactions with the assistant. You will notice the assistant stops using polite filler phrases like 'Sure thing!' and answers with just the necessary words or a single sentence.

cf3435fdb7832d01428b9fe3737a55ef83b08b6b.text: The system now stops trying to save your work if the required backup tool is missing. It also ignores hidden project folders inside your main folder so it doesn't get confused. You might see a clear message saying backups are unavailable instead of the system silently failing.

840a5cfe8fbf6b384ab10c98f641809f1f2da2ea.text: The system stopped trying to record who changed an organization's settings. This internal fix matches the current database layout, which no longer has a spot for that name. Regular users will not see any difference in how the settings work or look.

885c07499a942aac2ec0e1ce6454777b4ec3b549.text: The assistant can now create or update planning documents while in a read-only questioning mode, rather than being restricted to only answering questions. This change affects internal users who rely on the assistant for structured guidance during discussions. If they ask for a plan in this mode, the assistant will now generate or overwrite the plan file instead of refusing the request.

2dc51dd01d317d65ef0d5ca9f56899e2f564535d.text: The automatic quality check now looks at the shared building blocks a program uses, not just the program itself. This change affects the internal tools developers use to find mistakes before releasing updates. Nothing changes for regular people using the product today, but it helps catch errors that might otherwise slip through.

14732e57b7cc6cd92104180ded4a7c59b681f8c7.text: A small internal fix ensures the assistant correctly stops writing when it finishes a task. This prevents the system from continuing to generate text after it has already provided the final answer. Users may notice fewer instances of the assistant rambling on after completing a request.

6d5132fe0079da1f755de28cc142653355ed8070.text: The web address for the company management page was shortened from 'organizations' to 'orgs'. This is an internal cleanup, so the page looks and works exactly the same as before.

7ca58ba30216393e548245c276a8d3a082e97c58.text: The application now uses the official, stable version of a background tool that manages terminal connections, replacing a temporary test version. This change affects internal systems and does not alter how the product works for you. You will not notice any difference in performance or features.

d7069b26853983bbee4578bb3090b86af616c75b.text: The app no longer prints a warning message when it runs in a folder that isn't a project repository. This cleanup affects internal logs, so regular users won't see any change. It reduces clutter for developers monitoring the system.

4c6e211fd43468d6947146a0da1dfa93e66796ba.text: The system now waits for a file backup to finish before running commands that change files. This prevents the tool from acting on old data while a save is still happening. You might notice fewer errors if you run commands very quickly after a save.

5210e6206bf4f4f6d757ca6d993accc1e101811d.text: The AI assistant's internal guide for writing detailed project plans was updated. It can now revise existing plans by overwriting them and use the planning feature more than once in a single conversation, but only in 'ask' mode. This change applies immediately to the assistant's behavior, though it is an internal adjustment that users will not see directly in the interface.

b3635743890db81079ecc68fca3e23b4022dad6a.text: The coding assistant now stops after one attempt to fix a problem instead of trying repeatedly. This change is live today. You would notice the assistant ending its response sooner, rather than continuing to adjust the code.

47b7d8a51e19698b51793676075fca9c1c76f70f.text: The team removed an unnecessary preparation step for internal testing tools, allowing them to run directly without a waiting period. This change affects only the developers who maintain these quality checks. Outside users will not notice any difference in the application's behavior.

c07f2a21bfa2a51d9491920a940f4fd78c14a8ef.text: The program now cleans up terminal text more accurately, removing hidden formatting codes that previously caused display glitches. This ensures that when the tool runs commands in the background, it correctly detects when a task is finished rather than getting stuck or misreading the output. The change is live and improves stability for anyone using the terminal integration features.

919feca0c9dd5b71552e9315a3c5478d2a0d4a64.text: A small internal cleanup tells the evaluation checks to ignore files created automatically when the evaluation code is built. It affects only the internal evaluation tools. Someone using the product would notice nothing.

a3887a96ef09b27e692e55398c651355db10ed71.text: The system now uses one specific method to guess which files a user wants, replacing an older test mode. This change is live and affects how the assistant finds files during a conversation. The user will not notice a change, but the assistant may guess files differently.

3831d39f0f1ac516d3ba805372f427c356c2d67a.text: A small internal update fixed a broken setup for the team's testing environment. The tooling now includes a specific component needed to launch the home automation software during tests. This change affects only the internal evaluation system and is live today. No customer-facing features were altered.

7474488918ec1d9d750f2151b69cdc6b1e88a43e.text: The internal tooling that helps developers work with the codebase has been cleaned up. Two automatic checks that used to run separately, one for testing code and one for checking code types, now run together as a single step. Additionally, a small piece of internal tracking for terminal commands was removed, which simplifies how the system handles command outputs.

38ba1be288146175bb1e7036bfb3f6408b555022.text: A small internal cleanup simplified how the team runs their evaluation tests by removing an unnecessary compilation step, letting them run the scripts directly. It also loosened a strict technical rule in the code that checks terminal connections. This change is purely for the internal development team; customers will not notice any difference in the product.

481268890ead7e6df216c6c78649b97d8eaf1108.text: A small internal cleanup makes the email-sending tool read its instructions directly from the source files instead of waiting for a separate setup step. This change affects only the team running automated tests, not regular users. Nobody outside the team would notice any difference in the software's behavior.

178ff024821759fd4218f34b9462517b7d377be2.text: The system dropped an old, experimental version of the AI assistant. This cleanup ensures the software only uses the current, stable model. Regular users won't notice any difference in how the assistant behaves or responds.

05eb927283b72ed9ac1b0f034715b58970d9b3d4.text: The team updated internal settings so the testing tool now correctly connects to the main assistant code. This change affects only the internal evaluation system, not the live product. External users will not notice any difference.

16a8781a854b5d1b966146de52dc82635bebf871.text: A small internal update ensures that old, leftover files are deleted before new versions are created. This prevents a mix of old and new data from causing errors during the testing process. Only the team building these tests will notice this change, and it does not affect the final product.

76fe25777121d9df5ced907e9696eca783c97050.text: A small internal update fixed how a test tool finds the terminal command. This change only affects the automated testing setup for developers. Regular users will not notice any difference, as the feature itself remains unchanged.

00a4791b7bbed21b7958d230fe0f5033ca3fe658.text: A small internal update lets the testing system recognize new connections to outside services. This change only helps the testing tools work correctly. Regular users will not see any difference or new features yet.

6da7097649cd6490bf022cfd3967bde498a85929.text: Team invitations now pull the recipient's name from the central user list instead of relying on the sender's input. If the name is missing or unreadable, the email defaults to a polite 'there' greeting. This ensures all new, bulk, and resent invitations use accurate names without requiring manual entry by the inviter.

b079c0e919038c49325b03e4692d910c76c06fe2.text: A small internal update fixed a broken link between the testing system and the Codebuff assistant. This change only affects the automated tests that check how the assistant works. Normal users will not notice any difference, as this was just a repair for the internal tools used by the team.

fbb448901329d98ab192434ec5661ae847f5c7a8.text: The internal system now recognizes a new testing area, allowing automated checks to run correctly. This is a small technical fix for the engineering team, so customers will not notice any changes.

c7e10fa6b013a444577cb2dba89b561bbc42f9e0.text: A small internal fix corrected a broken link in the code that runs automatic quality checks. This ensures the checks can properly start their simulated environment. Only the internal testing team will notice, as the system now reliably runs these background evaluations.

c0f7206f5367022aec340a19cf411925241f5c02.text: The internal system that tests how well AI agents write code was updated to accept instructions in a new, standard format. This change fixes technical errors that could have prevented these automated tests from running correctly. It affects only the internal tools used by the development team to evaluate AI performance, and no changes will be visible to external users.

faddc8bd73f9615b5b097660ea5e2d921bbc6b52.text: The layout of the invitation page has been adjusted to remove excessive vertical spacing, ensuring the content fits naturally on the screen. In the team management area, clicking 'Cancel' on an invitation now opens a custom confirmation window instead of the browser's default alert. These visual and interaction improvements are live for administrators managing team invitations.

4314b9b04c81603d346c22ece0a495e522136c73.text: The software's connection to the AI assistant now uses a strict, unchangeable link to a specific version of the AI service. This prevents the AI service from automatically updating to a new version without permission. Internal systems will always use the exact same AI version, ensuring stable and predictable behavior for everyone using the tool.

92a9d9ffc967b74c6da37d418990ac7e2b3f6018.text: The system now uses a newer version of the AI model for generating responses. This update applies to all users of the service. You might notice slightly different or improved answers, but there is no visible change to the interface.

f6c7068c3e36a2803c699018a8ac13a98eb17e27.text: The internal team removed a failed experiment designed to fix broken text messages sent by an AI model. This is a cleanup task for developers and does not change how the software works for you. You will not notice any difference.

05b7ab118676ea5d660e8cee1f6d9ffa434db87b.text: The tool now checks if you are already in the correct project folder before switching. If the folder has not changed, it stops clearing the temporary work history and skips the message about the switch. This small fix prevents the tool from wiping your progress when you repeat the same command.

121f21767f0e319102ded87d84d9c772133a7d36.text: The system stopped writing routine notes to its internal log every time it checked a user's or company's account balance to see if it needed to add more funds. Engineers will see fewer repetitive entries in the server's activity record, making it easier to spot actual problems.

6e293d16cb835cbf5d8d01c24090826b9752cdf7.text: A hidden tool that saved a copy of every command run in the app's built-in terminal to a file was removed. This change is internal and affects only the software's maintenance, not its visible behavior. You would notice nothing different when using the application.

304f2f3392465a401ec0cfd4ed09617ad623ac1c.text: The app now shows the AI's step-by-step thinking process in a separate block before giving the final answer. This change is active for internal testing. You will see the model's reasoning appear in a distinct section, helping you understand how it reached its conclusion.

3776415c358351a43aa76982e12fd39ca28c7a79.text: The program now records your typed question and clears previous file-change logs before starting the AI response, rather than after. This ensures the system tracks file edits exactly once per conversation turn. Internal staff will notice no visual changes, but the underlying data logging is more reliable.

a6f1cafd2ffe93167338a3b7512b8cb05fe4d835.text: The program stopped writing error messages to its log when you save your work for the first time. This change affects only the internal record-keeping for the command-line tool. You would notice cleaner logs, with fewer false alarms appearing when there is no prior save to check against.

8328215807fd545487b12ec415ded2afdceb3920.text: The testing team removed an old check that expected a specific warning message when a tool command ended abruptly. This change does not affect the software's actual behavior or what users see; it only ensures the internal quality checks match how the system currently works.

797d3010f3528cefed363168f0981ac76a1a6af6.text: The build process no longer wipes out old files before creating new ones. Internal developers will notice the software builds faster, though they may need to clear old files manually if the system behaves strangely.

ff94f9b459190ac8962fe83774f0e0fdd67b4d1c.text: The system now checks three internal sections for basic errors every time code changes. This happens automatically in the background. Developers will see errors sooner, but regular users will notice nothing.

1ff848fc63f3ee45f56592a856b410f600544afa.text: The assistant's description of the 'file change hooks' setting now correctly shows it as optional. This only affects the text the assistant reads to understand configuration, not how the assistant behaves. Users will not notice any change in how the tool works.

489ef82e6834cd8f830f72df2c3092415b6b990f.text: New projects started with the command-line tool now include a blank section for file-change actions. This affects only people who run the setup command to create a fresh project. They will see an empty list in the default settings file, but nothing happens automatically until they add instructions there.

e6a47725bfa7cdf648bd6683802382696c79b34c.text: Billing system now records failures when checking automatic top-up eligibility. Internal change only; no customer-facing behavior impact. Support staff can see error details in logs.

9828b304ee7e2f2ecf81d719fa48e6340835ed65.text: Internal billing setup screens now show a field for discount codes, letting the team test subscription flows without charging real cards. This change is not live for regular customers.

143623d373dd5e0f6e42638cd3d21b98edc048f0.text: The AI assistant no longer automatically runs a full safety check on the code after every edit. This internal change means the assistant will only perform these checks if you specifically ask for them or if the project has custom rules set up to trigger them. You might notice the assistant finishing its response faster, but it will rely on you to request verification when needed.

780ac80ca3a0dae5b1eb0bff6874c03aa8837e08.text: The instructions for a small, fast helper that applies code changes were tightened to prevent confusion. This helper now strictly expects a specific placeholder phrase for unchanged sections and must not receive extra guidance on how to apply edits. This internal update ensures the helper correctly understands which parts of the code to change, preventing errors in applying edits.

44c427d4ae7ec6898a37ff4a106d4e26db7c4414.text: The internal tool that runs automatic checks now hides the lines that say a test passed or was skipped, leaving only the important results. This change affects the development team's automated report, which will look shorter and cleaner. It is active now, so the team will see less clutter when they run these checks.

9addae7a5cdff64a2d5cedd9cb11f4cd9f4c2fad.text: Added internal checks for configuration rules. This ensures the system correctly handles project settings and backup files. Developers will notice more reliable error detection when testing these rules.

d4329f12325cc6be7e1acca7136dad5109f4728c.text: The build tool now automatically deletes old output files before creating new ones. This ensures that every time a developer builds the application, they are not accidentally using leftover files from previous attempts. Developers will notice that the application behaves consistently, even if they forget to manually clear old data first.

1a11d023861aafcfb59e659582919ade23c7b3bc.text: The system no longer shows a warning message when it automatically finishes a task that was left open. This is an internal cleanup for the team's logs. Regular people will not notice any difference in how the system works.

609a06c6ced4ea40f2a0218260008dde32837f45.text: The instructions for a helper tool that edits code were simplified to help a smaller, faster computer model understand them better. This change affects internal operations and is already live. Users won't notice any difference, as it only makes the system's internal communication clearer and more efficient.

a3b028d976a689de8d51f855df29cf7aeda271ae.text: The system now removes hidden color codes from command results before saving them. This prevents the automated assistant from getting confused by unreadable symbols. You will not see any changes, but the assistant will understand command outputs more accurately.

1ad01db32c48fa48d3e7d7ca647720787d886f57.text: The system's instructions for asking permission to run commands were updated to explicitly forbid a specific format, using a branch deletion as an example. This internal change affects automated tests only. Users will not notice any difference.

2972b73cabb2fec16e7fe93dceef6e1e8abed691.text: Internal tooling now runs quick checks on three specific program sections when files change, replacing slower full-file scans. This helps catch basic errors faster during development. Nothing changes for external users.

b22b4f316ad87b710f53ef58bbd5d034da3ca006.text: The assistant now refuses to edit files or run commands when set to 'ask' mode. It only answers questions or makes plans. This applies to everyone using that mode. The refusal happens instantly, so no changes are made to your system.

6feaf6ed6e79c832e43abae1e26a1cfb6376a433.text: A background helper now receives the correct folder address before saving or restoring project snapshots. This internal fix prevents files from being saved to the wrong place during automated backups. Regular users will not see any visible change in the app interface.

7075ddbb9d540293df8c3b8ca479b4543a2e5f57.text: The software now secretly records a copy of everything typed into the terminal, but only when running on a developer's own computer. Regular users will not see this, and it does nothing on the live website. This is a temporary helper for the engineering team to track down glitches.

bc19f676ad3ea7db58df4f59f929fcb624b4aeb6.text: The program now correctly stops an action if a background task fails after changing files, even if it produces some output. Previously, it only checked if there was any output at all, missing failures. This ensures the system knows when something went wrong and can react appropriately. This fix is live today.

1b5e2cce43aab4ddff937d61cddb8944e50d1452.text: The system now correctly marks when it fails to understand instructions from a tool. This is a small internal fix for the software team. Regular users will not notice any change in their experience.

6563095b22da191d83d89515ac45f5598f31f03a.text: A small internal update adds a switch to control how special symbols are translated when reading documents. This affects only the background tool that handles this data, not the visible interface. If someone looked at the code, they would see that the system can now choose to keep symbols exactly as written instead of automatically changing them, though this option is not turned on by default.

7dc06c38a8daa17713d51230f8eeced8a262ab88.text: A small internal update to the AI assistant's connection with the Relace service. The system no longer forces the service to return answers in a specific structured format. This change is invisible to users and only affects how the software processes data behind the scenes.

69d5ba4f7ad91db2b67f24252a471e8cc19c6316.text: The system now correctly reads instructions from an AI service. Previously, it failed to extract these instructions, causing tasks to stop working. This internal fix ensures the service reliably processes requests.

85c97f507637ec01a548916fd2a3e47b86233919.text: The AI assistant now has a built-in limit on how many steps it can take to finish a task, defaulting to 12. This prevents it from getting stuck in endless loops or using too many resources. The setting is ready to use, but you won't see any difference in the interface yet unless you specifically configure this limit in your settings.

367086a1ab85ef4c3ca72bf0be83bb5c22f6a233.text: The system now strictly requires the AI to provide answers in a specific, organized format when processing certain requests. This internal adjustment helps prevent errors or misunderstandings when the software tries to read the AI's response. End users will not see any changes on their screens, as this works behind the scenes to keep the service running smoothly.

c9f4956589e405226e8ac8348351d6b719c8ea3b.text: The assistant now displays the exact command it wants to run inside a clear text box when asking for permission, rather than showing confusing technical details. This helps non-technical users understand exactly what action is being requested, such as deleting a specific file or branch. The change is live and applies to all permission prompts.

5946f6b14f13e7c089384ffff938b4456f72317b.text: Internal fix for Relace API response format serialization. Tool formatter now converts output schema to a JSON string before passing it to response_format. Max tokens reduced from 32k to 8192. Added messageId to error logging context. Small change, 6 lines added, 2 removed in one file. Not a user-facing feature.

6ace47b07474690a0056b8b379dd0587c1687011.text: Internal AI assistant now allows up to 20 steps per task, up from 5. This lets it handle more complex operations without stopping early. Only affects internal tooling; no visible change for end users.

24d66d6db0c8d74fbdcf88bcea417bbf93114853.text: A small internal update changed how past conversation messages are labeled before being saved for training, ensuring they are marked correctly even when combined. It also increased the number of recent conversations pulled for this process from one hundred to three thousand. This only affects the team's data collection; customers will not notice any difference.

338b7c42f56bf4dba3c8c90aa5f9247cbfe9de8f.text: The command-line tool now records detailed failure notes when saving chat history, restoring checkpoints, or adding API keys. Internal support staff can review these logs to diagnose issues. End users see no change in the tool's behavior.

88983de123c2aa22493f343f05ed6a664347e253.text: The system now correctly removes old tool results when cleaning up message history, ensuring the main prompt stays accurate. This internal fix affects how the AI assistant processes past interactions with external tools. Users will not notice any visible changes in the interface, but the assistant's responses may become more consistent and contextually appropriate over time.

f3c42362f96444b3153bf6bdf1ae785e73fc45c3.text: The internal system now records detailed error reports when background tasks fail, such as closing a browser or saving chat history. This change affects only the support team and does not alter how the software behaves for you. You will notice no difference, as this purely improves how the company tracks technical issues behind the scenes.

a411ce217fa50108b872b7c95cf6881a9695566d.text: The application previously crashed if it tried to record an error but the tracking system was not ready. Now, it simply skips the recording step and continues working. This small internal fix prevents unexpected shutdowns for people using the app, though they will not see any visible change in the interface.

e19de57f2d7d6f57085046a66540bcc7320031bd.text: A small internal update now tags each request to a third-party service with a unique message number. This change helps the service match requests to specific conversations for better tracking. Users and developers will not notice any difference in the application's behavior.

2a9def687faa80ab7b729e648395a401b42eaedb.text: The internal system that talks to the AI models now takes all its instructions in one combined package instead of two separate lists. This change only affects the background code that processes requests and does not change how the AI behaves or what the customer sees.

4a709cbdf0a65f791c4ef7951039217b7b2a6a11.text: For internal chat features using Google's Gemini model, the system now skips its optional 'deep thinking' mode. This stops the assistant from spending extra time on hidden reasoning steps before replying. Users will see slightly faster responses, with no visible change to the interface or other models.

9d0d843a287db028f99589085911cace793ca4fb.text: A new rule stops the AI from talking too many times in a row without you speaking first. If it hits this limit, you will now see a clear message explaining that its turn ended automatically and that you can adjust the limit in your settings. Previously, it would just stop talking without telling you why.

c00cc73df21c34d993e75a369726f3b9c7b7f9ba.text: Internal tooling now only sends automatic error reports to the analytics service when running in the live production environment. Developers working on local or test versions will see fewer irrelevant error notifications. This change is active today and affects only the internal analytics tracking setup.

a02d1b0667af38977e7bc8beedfad27653ce109f.text: The system now marks conversation summaries as internal background information rather than treating them as direct messages from the user. This is a minor internal cleanup. You will not notice any change in how the assistant responds or behaves.

55cafbbe6486fa6a3fc021757d015a105db06462.text: The assistant now stops after a set number of replies to prevent endless loops. The default limit is twelve steps, but project owners can change this in their settings file. If you see the assistant cut off early, it hit this safety limit.

f699f18b7773043c9535dffbbdb6f17e22e9e85d.text: A small internal adjustment restricts a text cleanup feature to run only on developers' local machines. This change prevents the cleanup process from accidentally activating on the main system when it encounters difficult-to-read text. Regular users will not notice any difference in their experience.

e58d6325e565f9efa8fd15b33ba3b9d66b531919.text: The tool now pulls the configuration file name from a single source instead of repeating it in multiple places. This change affects only internal maintenance and ensures that if the file name ever changes, startup messages and status checks update automatically. A reader would notice nothing different today.

3914be3730cd7b9669f62806128c6d85280525e8.text: The automated check that verifies the chat history structure was updated to find messages by content rather than fixed positions. This change only affects the internal testing suite and does not alter how the software behaves for end users.

5dfd3878ccf2d93e3856305cb581eae53ba565c7.text: A new switch lets people ask the assistant for advice or a plan without letting it change their files. This helps people who want to think through a problem first before making edits. The switch works right now if you turn it on when you start the program.

fe8b008bd79e7f9436e2e2accf13d3077bfe7aef.text: A small internal switch was turned off to stop the system from collecting entire files for training purposes. This change affects only the background data-gathering process and is active today. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the software works.

84b7ece47249ee80fa993ed025f7a4e1961c7ad6.text: The list of options shown in the chat menu is now ordered by importance instead of alphabetically. This means the 'init' option appears first, followed by 'login', while 'compact', 'export', and 'ask' are grouped near 'reset'. This change is live today for anyone using the interactive command menu.

fe0a0113126efb40ae5e2e23a77f4a378a7105ee.text: When the assistant's response is messy or unreadable, it now automatically tries to clean it up before showing it to you. This fix is currently limited to internal testing environments, so regular users will not see this improvement yet.

21581fcb49ab41635d1dc59b1c9453eab0f1c149.text: The team added new settings for training an internal file-picking tool. They also changed the tool to expect a specific visual stop marker, which is currently only active for one small test group. No customer will notice any change today.

2bdbdcb8e73ffa8b2b79349b22fbaf7d2d0e4f9c.text: A new 'compact' command now summarizes long chat histories to save space. This change is live today for internal users. You will notice the assistant forgets older details after you type the command, keeping only the summary.

b47a049c6b8178d360f9696bef04a921b2013d25.text: A small internal script that calculates monthly usage now defaults to the current month instead of a fixed past date. This affects only staff running the tool manually. If they run it without specifying a date, it automatically processes the current month's data rather than April 2025.

9276e9a4ad680ef832bf93f5b6f19c7c06378273.text: A small internal fix makes the admin view more reliable when reading recent AI interactions. If a message arrives in a new format, the tool now checks for alternative text fields instead of showing 'Unknown query'. Internal staff reviewing these records will see the correct prompt text appear where it previously might have failed.

3e91db4f5c60edad5fe3b25ed48f9bf827ca226a.text: A new command now saves a plain-text summary of your chat to a file. People using the tool will see a new document appear in their project folder containing key decisions and changes. This works immediately when the command is used.

47e976b76377e5c7496529c281817ec650d5a23d.text: The system now only reminds the assistant to check its own work when you send a new message, not during every background step. This stops the assistant from repeating the same check endlessly and getting stuck in a loop. You will notice the assistant responds more reliably without hanging or repeating itself.

5c065d17d6fab07f0bb40e7856be2a240476f402.text: The system rearranged its internal instructions to save memory and processing power. This change affects only the background operations of the assistant and does not alter how it responds to your questions. You will not notice any difference in the assistant's behavior or output.

c78cbbdbeaaa5768fa3485bc411ffdb1548cb0aa.text: The help page no longer lists options to switch between cheaper or higher-quality responses, because those settings no longer exist. It now tells readers to type a slash to see available commands. This change affects only people reading the help page; the software itself works the same.

f10c01859ad10f35fe05d145b89f2447079634b2.text: Two new file-selection assistants were added to the internal admin dashboard. This change only affects internal staff, who can now choose these new models to test how the system picks relevant files. Regular customers will not see any difference.

a15a34f2e48067613114f82155512b98b0e6aaec.text: The file selection screen now lets people scroll through long lists of files without accidentally triggering the browser's back button. Previously, any horizontal movement blocked scrolling; now, only strong swipes or two-finger gestures stop the page from going back. This is a small internal fix for staff using the admin tools.

b93b155edeb5f0e7d7a8d244804722db0bf073df.text: The system now remembers background information for the entire conversation instead of just the current step. It also places the results of its research directly before its instructions. This ensures the assistant uses fresh data and context consistently while working.

28d9dfd2a1df083a2ef0716beba110a8c8d52593.text: This small internal update helps the software's internal checks work better by clearly defining what data certain actions produce. It affects only the team building the app, not the people using it. You will not notice any changes in how the app works or looks.

7eec7198bbfbc34afaff675141501d4884496511.text: The assistant now avoids repeating information it has already shared in the current conversation. This applies to all users chatting with the service. You might notice slightly shorter responses when the assistant continues a topic it has already explained.

ff240b4f7b1485aae3af7bbf22f29f5b2bfd7551.text: A small internal update changes how the system handles batch relabeling tasks for admin tools. Previously, if one item failed, the entire process would stop; now, it continues through the rest. This affects only internal administrators, so normal users will not notice any change.

a9794796ca383c226fd2bae4301f45b44a0b89f6.text: The system now uses a separate tool to decide when to remove temporary notes from the conversation. This change is internal and invisible to you. It ensures the assistant's temporary instructions are handled consistently, but you will notice no difference in how the chat works.

10e774b85abd195925bb21c4a251e8e88bb17284.text: The command-line tool now closes its network connection when you exit. This prevents the connection from lingering in the background after you are done. You will not notice any visual difference, but the tool cleans up its connections more reliably.

5214caf0b52faf568ca998880cf8c11c7b87201e.text: Developers renamed a data label to ensure chat history keeps its expiration settings. This fixes a bug where old messages might not disappear when they should. End users likely won't see any immediate visual changes, but the system now handles message cleanup more reliably.

3e82d5794506e66ce963b4077067120904a863cc.text: A small internal update added a tool that picks the two best file matches for the assistant to use and another tool that re-checks old decisions with more information. These tools only help the team build better training data for the assistant's file-picking skills. Regular users will see no change today, as these are behind-the-scenes scripts for the engineers.

1e2e3fe3c2fbd0d297f48434252822317c80c597.text: The team added a new version of the AI that helps pick files. This update is only for internal staff, so regular users won't notice any changes. It is not live for the public yet.

130b01934f43422f0c68a465ba6f2817f0391770.text: Internal tuning adjusted the instructions guiding the assistant's self-correction logic. This change is not live for users today and requires no action. It has no visible impact on current functionality.

c62ad83322fd7b856408a90a250e4edcc1cc321e.text: The team swapped out the old tools for a new one that helps the computer pick the right files to show you. This change is for internal testing only, so regular users won't see anything different yet. They also slowed down the testing process to make sure the system doesn't get overwhelmed.

f11c9008f98b1366c2ca0f785f4b5a8996666138.text: This small internal update stops the admin file picker page from accidentally going backward when scrolling sideways through wide tables. It affects only staff using that specific admin tool. They will notice that swiping or scrolling horizontally no longer exits the page unexpectedly.

deafd88df6958e257ac11126429d6a464222ef39.text: The build process for the npm-app package no longer clears its cache before starting. This speeds up the build by reusing existing results when possible. The change is internal and live, affecting only how the app is assembled, not its final behavior.

4d128a44264f41894df3dcfe5ed6af6f084c0d03.text: Internal tooling updated to double the batch size for processing data traces from one thousand to two thousand, while documenting a new AI model training run that uses a stronger teacher model with additional context. This change affects only internal developers and does not impact external customers or live features.

342e583e980eea2ffdbc1c6de830ba44fcdfc939.text: The assistant now shows the complete updated text after changing a file. This helps the assistant verify the change without guessing, though it sends more data each time.

55420032c4e09974d175a09cde27a312706a224f.text: The internal tool that checks the assistant's performance now shows complete problem descriptions and all suggested fixes in its reports. Previously, these details were cut off after a short limit. This change affects only the team reviewing these reports, not the assistant itself.

01c30feb446875e2a283e9a40192e4baabb05216.text: The system now marks temporary instructions, like file-reading requests, with an expiration label. When building the conversation history, the system checks these labels and drops expired instructions. This prevents short-lived system notes from cluttering the long-term memory, keeping the assistant focused on the actual user request.

44fd6081ffb8bd9df6c0c32e6410044520303e8e.text: The assistant now stops talking immediately after using the code search tool. This prevents it from adding unnecessary extra text to the answer. This small internal update is live today.

f1e4db44c82a3c0893a1e56b6332ac5cbc41a859.text: Internal test messages now record costs in system logs without charging real accounts or saving to the database. This only affects automated test runs, so regular users see no change.

95feb5d7ad41bf58bcdd508dea45ce944a37c9af.text: The command-line tool now clears its saved list of project files when you type the reset command, forcing it to re-read the folder contents. This affects only people using the tool's command-line interface. If you reset a session, the tool will now correctly see files added or removed since you last started it, instead of possibly using an outdated list.

d608ab04c68fe3409f1f388e7d6fa90563d2378c.text: The system now removes hidden memory markers from all previous messages in a conversation, not just the last one. This change applies to internal message handling. Users will not notice any difference in how the assistant responds.

cc66c81328613121e61b5171b45c0d9f175572df.text: A small internal update turned on a hidden setting that lets the system track how long a message stays active, marking it as either part of an agent's step or a user's prompt. This change is not live for anyone yet because no other part of the system reads this new information. You would not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves.

a14639a460caa65ad66586f4e55cc816ba01b1cb.text: The project dropped a library that defined how chat messages are structured. This change affects the internal message format for the AI assistant. Users will not notice any difference in the app's behavior or appearance.

5d7f0c9ccd09064db68f2f7dfcc46a5c33ca5ea1.text: A tiny, invisible line of text was added to the program's startup file. It does absolutely nothing and has no effect on how the software works. Nothing will change for anyone using the tool.

48061fb16e514eb0ea98d1c5f012464eff178b94.text: A small internal safety check was added to the automated testing system. It briefly launches a specific application component to ensure it doesn't immediately fail. This change is live today but invisible to end users; it only helps the development team catch startup errors earlier.

014e363c52c4bf4150f9f9caf230b41aaa7dd62b.text: The automated system that checks if the software starts up now waits ten seconds instead of half a second before deciding if it worked. It also hides the startup messages to keep the report clean. This change only affects the internal tools used by the engineering team, so customers will not notice any difference in the product.

e36d2a6e60a5c879d93f5b5de716e910238e80d3.text: A new 'ask' mode now prevents the AI assistant from changing files or running commands, restricting it to read-only answers and planning. This affects users who select this specific mode, and they will notice the assistant only provides suggestions without executing actions.

2ceccf9438d104d90be9cbe51ee823675b287cb0.text: The shared library now includes the AI toolkit it needs to work. This fixes a hidden error that could stop the app from starting or building correctly. It affects the whole product's core, but not your specific features or data. The fix is live and ensures smoother operation.

3faf57ca33b068da56647fb4e19b908f3c0b28f1.text: Removed an automated check that verified if the application starts correctly. Developers will notice this specific test no longer runs during software updates. Users will see no difference in how the application works.

2269b526f252ee2e429c69ae0208ae3a4c115bd2.text: The system now saves test results in files named after the specific project being checked, rather than using a generic name. This helps internal staff tell apart results from different projects when they review the files. The change is live for internal testing tools.

7df30906209e3765762c20e0dc8ab72a194fd185.text: The team moved internal files that create email reports about how well the assistant performs. This change only affects how the team organizes their work, so nobody outside the team will notice any difference.

c0930b244b3fd2aa5374be479d58f6664f0de971.text: A small internal fix improves how the system checks if a specific startup script fails immediately. It now verifies if the program is still alive after a brief wait, rather than guessing based on timeout errors. This change is live today and affects only automated checks, not end-users.

be8d7c8d3ff26a55ca8b6b3dda22caf7bd554693.text: The command-line tool now lets people type cost mode names like 'lite' or 'normal' directly, without needing a slash in front. This affects only people using this specific internal tool. They would notice that typing just the word works the same as typing the slash plus the word.

dc2d86731ec6a8d30de2afe678eb5e54f6cf57dc.text: The system now packages personal details correctly before sending them to the email service. This fixes a formatting error that previously prevented custom information from appearing in transactional emails. Users receiving these automated messages will see their specific data display as intended.

64b83645b97f0a2ede87d1256898f3d9e7c389d0.text: The internal system now automatically handles cases where no main instruction is given, rather than requiring a blank placeholder. This change affects only the underlying code structure and does not alter how the assistant behaves for end-users. You would notice no difference in the chat experience.

c68a23236e2d2f25c4091f3938b4fcc70a4e2150.text: The system now uses a single, simpler method to send text to the AI, replacing older, separate connections. This change affects only the internal plumbing of how requests are processed. Users will not see any difference in the interface or how the assistant behaves.

4e73dfd334684dfd3f5388691669be1da1a8f891.text: The system now uses a single, unified rulebook to define the structure of core messages, replacing separate manual definitions. This internal cleanup ensures consistency in how message data is understood and processed behind the scenes. Users will not notice any visible changes or new features from this update.

b15faabe12b4c900fab6a0cf0574290ccf60a83c.text: The website now sends visitor activity data directly to the analytics service, instead of routing it through an internal relay. This change affects how the site records page views and errors. If you monitor traffic, you may notice data appearing faster or more reliably than before.

973904e9252deba01c18eaafb46f417fb4b483c1.text: The system now recognizes a special 'expiration' tag on certain chat messages, allowing it to keep or discard them based on whether the conversation is currently active or finished. This is an internal plumbing change; ordinary users will see no difference in how the assistant behaves today.

db002767ec6ce88575552e82a32af197bb82fd32.text: A small internal cleanup moved a data-formatting step out of the thinking-stream handler and into the code that calls it. This affects the backend system that generates deep-thinking responses, but no user-facing behavior changed. If you looked at the logs, you would see the same output as before, just produced by a simpler, more focused component.

750eb9f3c2a2cc5a4842a185671db416b7663101.text: A small internal update changed how the system checks permissions when copying code repositories. It now automatically uses saved access keys for GitHub projects, regardless of where the copy happens. This affects only the internal testing tools, so external users will not notice any changes.

2d2b94cb3a19628b0f83212ef0ddb1b6bcc7b4e3.text: A small internal update to the chat system. It changes how the system prepares messages before sending them to the AI, making the process more efficient and standardized. Users will not see any difference in how the chat works or looks.

c9cde42591f5468a327e8063ff6fb96d898e812c.text: The search tool now includes a strict rule preventing the assistant from stopping immediately after looking for code. This ensures the assistant reads and processes the search results before responding to you. You might notice fewer instances where the assistant stops mid-task without providing an answer based on its search.

2f0921c2ddaeb0246b78c44900e8a41d1e3de045.text: The system now quietly records background failures instead of stopping the entire process when the external tracking service has a problem. This change applies to all users who interact with the application's core features. You would not notice any difference in how the application behaves, as it continues to function normally even if the tracking service is temporarily unavailable.

120d9ffac77b2a64c06a02eab9c8cfb05ed7c258.text: The assistant's 'Lite' mode now uses a standard version of its underlying technology instead of a slower, more deliberate one. This affects only people using the Lite setting, meaning they will see answers appear faster but potentially with less detailed reasoning.

945aaa0fa65003c5231712f30deba214885b2601.text: The app no longer crashes when it tries to record activity in test environments lacking analytics setup. It now ignores the missing setup outside production, while keeping the crash for production errors. This internal fix prevents false alarms for the team running tests.

8c0c174acfbc096426407fb7968eed7e0c21fc2c.text: This internal fix improves how the system logs into private code storage during automated tests. It prevents the process from getting stuck waiting for a password prompt and ensures the correct security key is used. Engineers will notice fewer failed test runs when checking code updates.

ff000064d63484c4b3b05293bb8621923d597b09.text: Internal cleanup removed duplicate helper code for sending data to the AI model. Programmers now use a single standard method for these requests. No visible changes to the application's features or behavior.

15b3737d741546f6844e1038b334b00456fb01f6.text: The website now sends usage data directly to the analytics service instead of through an internal relay. This change affects the package manager website and restores previous tracking behavior. Visitors will notice no visible difference, but the service receives data through the original connection path again.

eafbb9af9a67a5ac02c1443a60eb594608ff2175.text: Internal testing tools now recognize a second automated service. This ensures private code repositories can be downloaded correctly during scheduled checks. No visible changes for regular users.

6a9d9e9e002983b8cf2be0a282b2c4abc05c5592.text: The command-line tool now recognizes a new 'experimental' mode. Users who switch to this mode will see a purple message confirming the change. This feature is live immediately for anyone using the tool.

3c7fbc0482ba4fe0308cc0c20c348523a4a0baf6.text: The internal tool that tests code changes now processes each test one after the other, instead of running three at the same time. This applies only to the internal evaluation system, so regular users will not notice any difference in the product.

e597c115d38c5d07f159a513be38ea576686c2a9.text: The system now copies only the project's history records instead of every single file when setting up a test environment. This change affects internal testing processes by reducing the amount of data moved, which helps prevent setup delays. A non-programmer would notice nothing, as this is an internal optimization to make automated checks run faster and more reliably.

b4ea0d85c61d75efd99001660aee39c96eaf5e72.text: The limit on how long the assistant's answers can be was increased. This change is already active. Internal staff testing the system will see that the assistant can now produce much longer responses without cutting off early.

aba1891449b97c273e3890de33ba9488ba62643b.text: A small internal update clarifies that the computer system, not the assistant, provides tool results. This prevents the assistant from guessing or making up outcomes when using tools. The change is live now.

6f40fb3f1c8e1d3df70d17bda44e4014d946335b.text: The system now automatically includes a new internal testing folder in its setup process. This change affects only the development team and happens behind the scenes. No customers or end users will notice any difference in how the software works.

2315a113c6c7f2450a809b06a43868d2eaf82426.text: The daily check now fetches the full history of the code repository and clones it directly from the remote server using secure access, instead of copying local files. This change ensures the system sees all past updates and works reliably in the automated environment. It is active today for the internal team running these checks, but customers will not notice any difference.

dade11c3a2372adb78a7889bf30f31ea550340b9.text: A hidden note that recorded web addresses during library searches was deleted. This internal cleanup affects only the system's backend, so no one will notice any change in the application's behavior.

1c073efa0d43c0130e7bca488376843075853dd1.text: The automated testing system now copies the project's history directly from the existing workspace instead of downloading it from the remote server. This internal change prevents authentication errors during test runs. Users will not notice any difference, as this only affects how the background evaluation tools prepare their data.

b86305adba4a1d4035c51f8852f222ed05dfdb75.text: Internal maintenance updated the file-transfer step in the daily code-checking routine. This affects only the automated system, not the product. No visible change for users.

0a077ef91968600ad55f6e41961144506dfbbe65.text: The automated system that checks code quality now uses a saved password to download the project files. This stops the process from getting stuck waiting for a human to type in login details. The change is live and affects only the internal testing tools.

32af0d70169f9358b79d351038931fc0fc4c5438.text: The system now uses the correct password format when downloading a private code repository for evaluation tasks. This fixes an issue where the download would fail or ask for a password interactively. Internal automation teams running these evaluations will see the process complete without hanging on authentication prompts.

9246661c66d3c8c44a359d68828b60b7d6bfbf95.text: The script that re-grades old assistant responses now grabs them in small batches instead of stopping after twenty. This lets it process up to a thousand items in one run, but it only changes how the internal tool works; customers see no difference.

b92928268176a1a4dde5f0cf6e448cfecf783cbf.text: The automated system that saves test reports was switched to a new method because the old one stopped working in early 2025. This change affects the internal team running these tests. They will notice that reports upload and download much faster, preventing delays in checking test results.

bc20e13eb270ea1f445fa226483a639111046d85.text: The system that grades AI coding attempts now automatically shortens its instructions if the task is too complex to fit within the model's memory limit. This change is internal and affects only the automated quality checks. A regular user would notice nothing, as this only ensures the grading process completes successfully instead of failing when faced with very large code changes.

50a0cad6548f68c6d3f8f766dc745cd83f0e24b8.text: The internal testing system now stops waiting if a coding task takes too long, cutting off after five or thirty minutes. It also records crashes that previously caused silent failures. Developers running these automated checks will see clearer error messages and results that finish on time, rather than hanging indefinitely.

2e04e27f018162dd626784f75da68b6948f2b7ba.text: The system now combines multiple instruction blocks into a single text block before sending them to the AI. This internal change ensures the AI receives a unified set of guidelines rather than separate pieces. No visible changes will occur for end users.

645460ce970644bb12946c65fa8142b6267370ee.text: The system now saves progress after each step of a long test run instead of waiting until the end. If a test crashes or times out, earlier results are kept instead of being lost. This internal change affects only the testing tool and is live today.

18feb799f943e6f1e43a94ba321e765fb6038531.text: Typing the @ symbol now suggests matching file names and known terms. This helps people using the command line tool find things faster. The feature is live today.

1621707d9f8c9334e7b546e4d0847aaa06fb93d0.text: The system now sends the cost estimate to the user's screen before saving the message details to the database. This small internal change reduces the wait time for the cost to appear. Users will see the price update slightly faster after sending a message.

1122f6c13ddc2d8545a7b94ef77fb58cf6e3a81d.text: The system now holds back a partial web address code if a message cuts off right after the start symbol, rather than guessing it is finished. This prevents broken text from appearing when data arrives in small pieces. The fix applies to the background text reader and is live today.

a07bfc55a360a2c5f3dd9fcf5f0becbe626d4745.text: The system now respects a setting that tells the AI to stop generating text when it sees specific words. This fix ensures that if this setting was already configured, the AI will actually follow it instead of ignoring it. The change is live and affects internal operations, but most users will not notice a difference unless they were previously using this specific stop-word feature.

cf6fa144e64f39c43b53f920e44410cf97bd2b47.text: A small internal change makes the command-line assistant show at most 20 suggestions when someone starts typing an @-mention. It also stops adding the @ symbol to each suggested name, because the @ is already in the place being typed. People using that command-line assistant may see a shorter, cleaner suggestion list, and it is live now.

85727445a1bf904311456cdffcee0be52cc2d0a4.text: Typing a short command now switches the assistant between three modes that change how much effort it spends answering. The prompt at the bottom of the screen shows which mode is active unless you are using the standard one. This update is live for people using the command-line tool.

2b0ead0f2f861631ae69c42436af9a3bc38b6249.text: Developers updated internal safety checks for the AI assistant's responses. This ensures the system's automatic tests run reliably without accidentally calling the real AI service. No changes affect how the product looks or works for you today.

467cc64c2eee2eca3e02235782aead3a1a873749.text: The system now correctly marks specific messages for temporary storage, allowing it to reuse previously processed data instead of recalculating it every time. This change is internal and live today, meaning users will not see a new button or feature. However, if you monitor usage metrics, you might notice lower costs or faster responses for long conversations due to this efficiency improvement.

faae0b7c9d92d8ddff2b4019e8a25fee4a8c76ae.text: Internal test setup corrected. A helper now supplies the missing mock for a specific AI stream. Another mock changed from a stream to a single response. This fixes test failures. No user-facing behavior changed.

f5754d1fac5f26e3e5dc789bdf265e9557e5da4d.text: A safety check was added to the file upload process. If a file is missing, the system now skips it instead of stopping. This prevents crashes when preparing training data.

5467138a5fdab77c57ae9acfab23e2587eb6feb9.text: This small internal update lets the AI assistant recognize 'temporary' instructions from our service providers. The assistant now applies these instructions to user, assistant, and tool messages. Users won't see any changes yet, as this only prepares the system for future provider updates.

cc7ea4b18f5495fce53018a51ca9663ac8b1fa29.text: The system now uses a single, shared connection method for all major artificial intelligence providers, replacing four separate, provider-specific connections. This change affects only the internal server code that processes your requests. You will not notice any difference in how the assistant responds, as this is an internal cleanup to make the system easier to maintain and update.

51e607e54327e47b7872c039f86094d5db0a0fe5.text: Internal check for credit balance calculation. Fixed test setup so checks run correctly. Added test case for offsetting positive balance against debt. No user-facing change; system behavior unchanged.

90e7765fc0aaf504c18a697dfe060bb4bc3df1da.text: Charles Lien is now a required reviewer for all code changes, alongside Brandon and Jahooma. This internal update ensures his approval is needed before any new software goes live. Regular users will notice no changes to the product itself.

d09143aeacc7ea61ec5ae41cb91c7992ab3f0bdd.text: The assistant now offers a reset command that wipes the current chat history and restarts the session fresh. This change is internal and not yet available to regular users.

dd1fc083a17a228fdc1e11b5f964d6a1ce1b7a42.text: The system now automatically corrects hidden line spacing marks when preparing text updates. This ensures that edits apply cleanly without breaking due to mismatched formatting between different computers. Internal tools handling these text patches will function more reliably, though regular users will not notice any visible difference.

e84dad64cc9b873a87de5631d51e4770aaa176a8.text: The tool now automatically sends error reports to the service team when something goes wrong on your computer. If you see a failure message, the team receives details about what happened without you needing to report it manually.

f554e4f6875aa970c5e3eb2d9f841bafd2cb7934.text: The system now accepts a wider variety of message formats from the chat history. This ensures that images and text sent by users are correctly processed, while ignoring internal tool data that belongs elsewhere. The change is live and helps the assistant understand conversations more reliably without dropping information.

360c1ad77fa0fa29e26e6fbadd2d9148dde26360.text: A hidden rule that previously filtered out certain internal instructions during message processing has been removed. This ensures the system treats all past messages consistently, which helps the underlying AI model cache data more effectively. Regular users will not notice any change in how the assistant responds, as this is purely an internal stability improvement.

30b6bffa7528557ff91b30ab2160a133eaec35bd.text: The coding assistant now requires explicit notes when removing code to ensure the background tool applies changes correctly. This internal update improves accuracy for the assistant's file editing feature. Users will notice fewer errors when the assistant deletes sections of code.

817c4fc03608956cc5e8aef17b320aa710c435b8.text: The application now quietly collects basic statistics about your project folder, such as its age and number of files, when you start working. This data helps the team understand how the tool is used, but it does not change any features or visible behavior for you.

c30832c674a1eebe071d6d8de47afd23ba8c6a8a.text: A small internal update ensures the main AI assistant always signals when it has finished a response, matching how the lighter version already works. This helps the system know when to stop processing and display the final answer to you. You might notice fewer cases where the assistant leaves a response hanging or tries to continue unnecessarily.

7fc0330976e1fc68818be66994fbb527a18a96ed.text: The build process now clears out old files before creating new ones. This affects the team who builds the software. They would notice that outdated files no longer linger in the output folder, ensuring every new version is fresh.

74dfac8401e2a598f738eac46c67ee9e76a70fa9.text: The AI assistant now strictly requires explicit user permission before running scripts or saving changes to the project history. This prevents accidental errors or broken live systems. Users will notice the assistant asking for confirmation before performing these specific actions.

ad6d724e9c34fe830d06749854a0c21f308e8b9b.text: The software now checks folder locations more accurately on Windows computers. This prevents the program from mistakenly thinking files on a different drive are inside the current project. Most people will not notice any change.

7808329c547b03e6efb0693309b2336480f2cbec.text: A tiny internal fix repaired the code search tool. Previously, a missing space caused searches to fail. Now, searches run correctly again.

538bad74e285b51cec47d602d5d48fcf4211b429.text: A small internal update clarifies how the assistant handles special symbols in its instructions. This prevents the system from accidentally misreading text that looks like a command. Regular users will not notice any change in behavior.

27ffd5a802b2f9f178863bbc9b15b54f9685056a.text: The system now handles broken special character codes in data more safely, treating them as plain text instead of guessing. This affects all users of the service. You would not notice a change unless you had data with these errors, which previously might have displayed incorrectly.

bbae1e98e4b9762b4893b5ecf2e097aad1228f8d.text: Developers reorganized how the command-line tool shares its text-input display with the main program. This internal cleanup prevents a technical conflict where two parts tried to control the same screen element. Users will not notice any change in how the tool works or looks.

a788e33dff020e23d7d022419340d16b329d25bb.text: A small internal test was updated to check how the system handles extra labels on data tags. This change affects only the automated checks and does not alter the software's behavior for anyone. No users or developers will notice any difference in the application.

1daa8a155d91ec8bf8816832f898822decb2c924.text: The code search tool now keeps quote marks in search terms instead of deleting them. This means searching for exact phrases with quotes works correctly. The change is live and affects anyone using the code search feature.

e8b4277364f163d0b8fa172d74ebe71f48021b33.text: The system previously logged a failure report whenever its usage data upload failed. However, attempting to log that specific failure could itself fail, causing an endless loop of error reports. The change stops the system from generating these recursive failure logs. Users will not notice any difference in the app's performance or features.

f07ddb1b39622cbbcb46a4e8a73b66e2759434a3.text: The startup message shown when running the tool from the wrong folder was updated to clarify that it is an AI pair programmer. It now explicitly displays the current folder location and instructs the user to navigate to their specific project directory before launching. This internal wording change helps users understand why the tool stopped and what step to take next.

b37a5ce3861e2626194c55921680c7cdf43a5061.text: The AI assistant's brain got a small update. This change is live today. You might notice slightly better answers or faster thinking, but nothing looks different.

6e704acbf06f1a8757c62304f3b02e493be15bd2.text: The team added a new, stronger option to their internal quality-checking tool, which reviews how well the AI assistant understood code changes. This update is live for the internal staff who run these reviews, meaning they can now automatically test against both the standard and the new high-capacity model. Regular users will not see any immediate changes in the app itself.

79dc159133c2af0ac84ebd7e8ef619bb920791c5.text: The system now uses a newer, faster engine to find and replace text in large files. This change affects only the internal processing of these specific file operations. You will not see any difference in the interface, but the task may complete more quickly.

fe649402a09aacff407e90cf2819de61de8ca371.text: A small internal shortcut was added so the team can start the app in a lighter mode while building it. It is available today only to the people using that shortcut during development. Customers and normal users will not notice any change, and the app behaves the same as before.

3bc799fc01407634259af6f3746b4250865d9c53.text: The system now handles messy data more carefully. If it finds a new piece of information while reading an existing one, it keeps the original data intact instead of stopping early. This prevents losing text when the input is formatted incorrectly.

af80b63047e5f9927938b7054b51edfb2389d319.text: The AI assistant can now write longer responses and edit multiple parts of a file in one go. It also no longer forces a specific ending command, allowing more natural task completion. These improvements are live for all users of the coding tool.

efb016beae9069917fa236ac21558a565b26c927.text: The internal command-line tool now ignores pasted text when checking for menu triggers. This prevents a slash menu from appearing if a slash is pasted as part of a larger string. Only typing a slash as the first character activates the menu.

9ba698a4bd4852081e2ad21f0037c552883c71a5.text: The system now waits longer for the AI to respond when searching documentation, reducing failed requests. It also limits the amount of information sent to the AI to keep responses focused. Internal staff using the documentation search tool may see fewer timeouts.

d49578e20a008503231d0a4059153313745f1e79.text: The assistant's search for help now checks against a much larger, up-to-date library of technical guides instead of a small, fixed list. This means when a user asks how to use a specific piece of software, the assistant is more likely to find the correct, current instructions. The change is live and improves the accuracy of answers for software-related questions.

863afde43257d6028fabd3cf3a4124933d8321ba.text: The system now tells the AI assistant to fix computer errors, not just its own mistakes. It also gives clearer instructions on when to stop talking. If a command fails, the error message is now more specific and helpful.

44471279fd03b59ed9f9d68bf571efa2640dd975.text: The system's internal check for how it reports errors was updated to match a recent change in its warning messages. This is a small, behind-the-scenes fix that ensures the software's self-tests pass correctly. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the system behaves or what messages they see.

3ba6c2937062ebfb4438460d59570ad62e93ac7d.text: Developers updated the automated checks that verify the assistant's core instructions. This ensures the system correctly identifies when a user is speaking versus when the assistant is responding. The change is internal, so users will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves.

a68ccdf37c1bdcccbab922fa291f74df62033acc.text: The system now processes files up to four times larger using its main tool, skipping a temporary workaround. This change is live. Users with very large files will see edits apply normally without needing a special backup process.

398d348899bdc2d782b4d61504f1f8c62c043658.text: The app now records which menu options you choose and notes when you type a command it does not recognize. This change is live and affects you by helping the team understand how people use the tool, though you will not see any difference in the interface.

3695d0edfe0ebfe54ab989d9ee380184e9c16dad.text: The command menu now lists options alphabetically with brief descriptions. Typing an unknown command shows a clear error message instead of failing silently. The login command no longer requires a slash prefix. This update is live in the current version.

d15a58924a5dba81dd334f226a1b15ec6f8a2331.text: A small internal update lets admins choose how many items to process at once, instead of being stuck with a fixed number of ten. It also fixes a counting error so the system accurately tracks successful updates, even when multiple changes happen for a single item. Only internal admins using the relabel tool will notice these improvements in their workflow.

7bc711d065c89f75f32eb37b7b633a00b247bc2d.text: The system now uses a standard built-in tool for processing data streams instead of a separate add-on. This change is internal and does not affect how the software works or looks for you. You will not notice any difference in performance or features.
