0cff8f16b32c99da988a2e24cbc3aa3c2f382921.text: The program stopped adding hidden formatting to empty spaces when printing information about its work. People using the command-line tool might see cleaner text displays, though the change is internal and minor.

2b9b266402806c96d9421e1a73f8599431bcfaa8.text: The command-line tool now properly closes its hidden background terminal when you quit. This stops leftover sessions from lingering after you exit. You might see a 'Codebuff out!' message and notice cleaner shutdowns.

005a3621451b792942a26a091e28474f88cd5ba1.text: The tool that prepares the app for sharing now automatically removes a specific internal helper file from the final package, as it is already included inside the main code. This affects only the internal build process, not the end user. You would notice no change in the app's behavior, as this simply ensures the shared files are clean and correctly structured.

8941387a11a8a9c35377a8c67f997a1f9fea9cdd.text: The assistant can now search for files by describing what it is looking for, instead of needing exact names. This helps when it needs to find code or documents but does not know where they are stored. The change is live today.

ed5afb37835eb4580a6b8e2614f7a75beeb0f3a1.text: Internal logging messages were updated to combine text and data into single strings. This change affects only the system's internal record-keeping, not user-facing features. Customers will not notice any difference in how the product works or looks.

e23fe979916c4fc7f85866ff7be5abac68e26bd0.text: The backend build process now compiles code incrementally, meaning it only rebuilds parts that have changed. This change affects the internal development workflow for the backend team. Developers will notice faster build times when making small changes to the code.

80dc207c45d2fb589f7bed4af95b91485331166c.text: The team improved the internal checks that scan all parts of the software for errors. This ensures each piece is built in the right order before being checked, preventing false alarms or missed issues. Developers will notice a smoother process when verifying the software's health, though the final product for users remains unchanged.

29ae90b5d539f0f2faa6e7915f32e6a222350825.text: The system now reads its connection details directly from a file instead of guessing where to look. It also requires a specific project name to be set up beforehand, or it will refuse to start. This internal fix affects only the software's background data processing, so regular users will not notice any change in how the application behaves.

bcb487462ab02d9d1d225633e0b67204a844d30e.text: The system now records a small note in its internal logs when it loads the password key needed to connect to the data warehouse. This change only affects the engineers who read those logs to fix connection problems, so regular users will notice no difference in how the app behaves.

515e4a46586ce7c252fa000b7f51aa7e19cc862e.text: A small internal update improved the help guide for fixing installation errors. It replaced specific, personal file locations in the examples with generic placeholders. This ensures the instructions are easier to follow for anyone trying to resolve a stuck installation, without needing to adjust the paths for their own computer setup.

bdc0533c84261e279105318642ecf28b46e25746.text: The server now waits for its data warehouse connection to finish setting up before starting. This prevents early requests from failing because the system wasn't ready. If the connection fails, the server logs the error but keeps running. This internal fix improves stability for everyone using the service.

d67e0f0c30f1a656b9be68f6db3364807385234f.text: The system now checks for a specific security file before connecting to the data warehouse. If the file is missing, the connection fails immediately with a clear error. This helps internal staff fix setup issues faster, but customers will not notice any change.

cce7b2ae97c1476e011ea0ae7e5e92386266836f.text: The system stopped checking if it is healthy and paused sending data to a storage service. This internal change means monitoring tools will see the service as unavailable, and new usage data will not be saved.

ec6c336bab7052b2185e928ae8eb8f50088a300e.text: The system now checks if a specific digital key file is present when starting up. If the file is missing or unreadable, it records a clear note about the problem. This helps internal support staff quickly identify why Google services might fail to connect, though regular users will see no change.

492164d69262c88b895a81ced8d2900968df5ff0.text: This small internal change makes the system print the location of its Google Cloud access key to the log whenever it starts up. This helps the engineering team confirm the key is found correctly, but regular users will not notice any difference in the app's behavior.

db8db034f2571ffcf4d91ef9f65e415503900753.text: A small internal safety update stops the system's usage tracking from breaking other features. If the tracking service fails, the system now logs the error and keeps working normally. This change is live and affects how the system handles background tracking errors.

07ea8f3351c27afa7f413552bd50047f9a716c50.text: The system now automatically creates a specific folder for saving local activity records if it is missing. This helps developers who run the software on their own computers, preventing errors that stop them from seeing detailed logs. Nothing changes for regular users or when the software runs on servers.

45d9b1c862b085b50c4dc3526e1256a433b4825a.text: The system now checks that its data connection is ready before trying to use it, preventing crashes when the connection is missing. This fixes a technical issue that stopped the software from building correctly. Regular users will not notice any change in how the application works today.

8508ba29b8a82bffde06f65f1f3a8ed3e5dc3f67.text: A new help page explains how to fix a specific installation error where the software fails to update because old temporary files are blocking the way. Users who try to install the tool and see a 'directory not empty' message can now follow these instructions to clear the blockage and finish the setup. This guide is live on the support website.

35d41c75dd13b3a967a7b64c477e2459215c9dcd.text: The system now records detailed notes when it starts up and connects to the data storage service. If this connection fails, the error messages will show more specific information about what went wrong. This helps the support team diagnose startup issues faster, but you will not see any changes in the application interface.

ca30129b7369a7599d625d4ec5d6e82f3d76ab87.text: During automated testing, the software now skips saving local log files. This keeps the test reports cleaner and prevents unnecessary clutter. The change is active immediately for the testing system.

39cca8c00af9dcb717cab367a282c2c154c6f6af.text: The logging system now skips saving detailed records to local files during automated checks. This change affects only the internal testing environment and is live today. A non-programmer would notice no difference, as this reduces unnecessary computer work during automated tests.

7306a994e9eafdfa2744becedb3fe69a4f19e987.text: The system now records where a sudden crash happened inside the background service. This helps support staff pinpoint the exact cause faster when investigating errors. Regular users will not see any difference in how the application behaves.

d0d019a273ae5e2ee9cf7e93908ad4411c19fc09.text: The software now stops sending usage data to the tracking service when running in a test environment. This change affects only the internal testing tools, not the live product. A tester would notice fewer unnecessary data points being recorded during development checks.

b744cf35cc4609312ff942060ad1b495ab5aba78.text: Small internal fix to the affiliate page. Affiliates now see a simpler referral link that uses their username instead of a longer link that also included a separate referral code. If that referral code was missing, the page no longer shows a warning asking them to contact support.

8e42c3fa37cdb1dde61648e6137e84a4fc56dfa8.text: The internal system that records activity logs now only rebuilds its recording setup when the storage location changes, instead of checking other project details. This cleanup affects only the software's internal record-keeping and is live today. Regular users will notice no visible change, as the log files continue to save in the same places.

b8af53a675d71698dff6fc85693b8607f7ba9bc5.text: The command-line tool now properly cleans up its internal error handlers before shutting down when you press Ctrl+C or close the terminal. This prevents the tool from hanging or showing confusing errors during exit. The change is internal and already live; you might just notice a smoother, faster shutdown.

a27d41d36fd56f795f32ea53cfc3048108a90ce4.text: A small internal update clarified when the assistant should stop talking and wait for a human to type. Previously, it might have paused while waiting for a computer tool to finish. This change helps the assistant distinguish between waiting for a person and waiting for a machine, making its responses smoother for everyone using the tool.

616a92ba4ae03b37711bcffd8598afdb5bd956ca.text: The command-line tool now cleans up its text output by removing extra blank lines. When the assistant sends a response, any run of three or more empty lines is squeezed down to two. This stops the terminal from looking messy with large gaps between paragraphs.

9e4d024da55ede70a8f3bbbd2fe9e70b14462772.text: When a user stops a response, the system now saves the exact text received up to that point, rather than a cleaned-up version. This affects only internal data logging and does not change what the user sees on screen. The change is live but has no visible impact for end users.

7e21afde61095f67b4f93e3e7371453502f2663a.text: The app now checks which environment it is running in to decide where to save activity logs. This fix ensures that in production, logs are written to the correct location instead of a default one. Internal teams will notice that debugging information is now reliably available in the right place, though end users see no change.

7797300f605e61c21d0440226892445a47175218.text: The app now sends user activity data through its own secure channel instead of a direct third-party link, and it only records this data when you are using the live production site. If you are testing the app locally or on a preview link, your actions will no longer be tracked in the analytics reports.

802e0cea25fb42dfb9aed1b2e623a777611f18f8.text: The name of the AI assistant now appears with a capital C in all text prompts and automatic project backups. This change ensures the brand name looks consistent and professional wherever it appears on the screen or in the history. It does not change how the tool works or what it can do.

19c46db5a3bfa04d77dfcb2989cbd1ad603f2b0d.text: The app now ignores its internal activity notes when running on the live website. This stops the system from trying to write those notes to a file that might not exist, preventing potential errors. You will not see any change in how the app works or looks.

223f241eb2a1302ea52025df6e0f397d0e232445.text: The system's internal logging tool was updated to better handle switching between different workspaces. This fix ensures that error and activity logs are correctly saved to the right folder when you change projects, preventing lost or mixed-up log data. It is a minor internal improvement that helps keep your local development records accurate.

7c1cd15419bfa5218a5da87b755a1aaa9f5a682a.text: A logging tool was added to the internal app settings. It is not active yet and has no effect on anyone today.

8a8e4e5d08355332f1a001818c59c57e06a53b3f.text: The program now records more detailed notes about background tasks, tracking their start, end, and leftover instances instead of just their beginning. It also ensures these notes are fully saved before the program closes, preventing data loss. This is an internal improvement for the development team to better understand how the tool behaves, so regular users will not notice any changes.

778bfb18cbd7e593d8395d4f0452625731d4820c.text: The app now looks for shared parts of the code in the correct folder. This fixes a background error where the app couldn't find the analytics and logging tools. The app works as before, but the internal structure is now correct.

19be4bb7b62962bef60e9a335c3877487c7c4c0d.text: The app now closes background tasks more cleanly on Windows, stopping related helper programs instead of just the main one. This internal fix prevents leftover processes from slowing down your computer when you stop the app. You won't see a new button or menu, but the app will leave fewer invisible programs running in the background.

5e19586d1ab609bc0033e47008c475fbf9ac1f1a.text: The text describing how error messages are handled was corrected to clarify that they are saved alongside standard output if no separate file is specified. This change only updates internal documentation records and does not alter how the software actually runs or stores files today.

1e88e73993752e785e0cd6ed5881d5ab6aeff0bf.text: The tool now records a brief note when you successfully log in. This happens automatically in the background for anyone using the command-line interface. You will not see any change on your screen, but the company can now count how many people sign in.

d0297b1de8804e50fcb565fd9effc512af3ade6f.text: The app now creates its log folder before saving records. This stops the tool from crashing when it tries to write to a missing folder. Users will not see any difference, but the tool runs more reliably.

000bd9f527893b93a620870ddf0682eb6ab77ba9.text: The application now adds a unique reference number to every message sent from the computer to the service. This helps support staff match specific requests with system logs when troubleshooting errors. Regular users will not notice any visual changes or differences in how the program behaves.

bb3d358fe494ddc3dbf30fe781a34d5c9707a205.text: Internal test checks updated to match current settings. No customer impact. Invisible.

803e039b6702465eaec7bdcf630f527fe83c139c.text: The startup screen no longer shows a unique number for each running process. This small change affects only the text log seen during development. A developer will see a slightly cleaner list with just names and commands.

77dfbd74de9c70bc00042cc5e78237877e00b791.text: A small internal cleanup makes the command-line tool handle a cancelled response correctly, ensuring the prompt returns to you properly. Only people using the command-line version are affected, and they might notice the text input behaves more predictably when stopping a response.

999ee4f1e3e546b4749b01be7e7321441abb1893.text: A small internal update added a new startup option to the command-line tool. People using this tool can now run it with a special flag to automatically start the setup process. This change is live for users who add that flag when launching the program.

2f82f187c4b2b473f505c91419c67342ecd06281.text: The assistant now follows stricter rules when setting up background tasks. It will only add specific log locations and working directories if those details are actually needed, avoiding cluttered or incorrect setup files. This change is live and ensures new projects start with cleaner, more accurate configurations.

1bbf9532f7e7f31b9aec00978b6e43340e7ee80d.text: Small internal fix for the assistant's file creation display. When the assistant creates a new file, the summary now correctly shows the total number of lines written instead of a partial count. Existing file updates remain unchanged.

4c693bd6efb85134755b3c451e6324a7cd51c655.text: The public help page previously stated that a specific fast AI model was used to locate relevant project files. That claim has been removed, though the model remains in use for other quick tasks. Readers visiting the site will see the updated text immediately, but the underlying software behavior is unchanged.

3c567fbc6da4246be4c3cd94d6eb7c8501075fa3.text: The system now automatically sends error messages to the same log file as standard output, if no separate error log was specified. This prevents error messages from getting lost or appearing in unexpected places. Only internal system logs are affected; end users will not see any change.

6e6070edc398eff93684924144c3794266fe4fea.text: The file finder now always uses a specialized AI model instead of switching based on your settings. This means results will consistently reflect the capabilities of this specific model. The change is live for all users accessing the file search feature.

9f8c0cce87df10772390f220584334ebe7e89f23.text: The system now picks only the newest rating for each task, stopping duplicate examples from training the AI. It also grabs more data at once and skips overly long records. These updates are for the internal data collection team and do not affect daily users.

9a1f34db9bd2c00a7410e4ee572a41f3b60cb881.text: A new AI model was added to the file-finding system, but it only works for accounts using the experimental cost setting. Regular users will notice no changes. The team added tracking labels to see which model handles each request and set its price, but the feature is not live for everyone.

812cb8c1d2608eb2a367d90e162cd8d31e5efb71.text: The AI now wraps its internal instructions in a specific label. This helps the computer separate background rules from user questions. It is a small internal update. Users will not notice any change.

82baf196ace3e86f173eb57e0de8f07a00c0e433.text: The program now automatically sends error messages to the same log file as regular messages, unless told otherwise. This change affects how the system records startup issues. People will notice less clutter in their configuration files and a simpler, unified way to view both normal output and errors.

0f59d8b251cd5a8c4fdc8ef5d6bf6cae62b54f77.text: The text you see when the tool starts up has been cleaned up. The product name is now capitalized correctly, and confusing labels about which background tasks are running have been updated to be more accurate. Additionally, the tool now hides some repetitive status messages when stopping tasks, making the display less cluttered.

c1b94ae0c196207adcafe89014ee39d8d1acf740.text: When someone asks the assistant to look at a website, the text from that page is now attached as a separate note instead of being pasted directly into the chat message. This keeps the conversation cleaner and helps the assistant understand where the information came from. The change is live for all users.

f131589598d2cf2afafbe08cc7059b6401942b6c.text: The internal tool now displays a count of added and deleted lines when it creates or updates files. This affects only developers using the command-line interface, who will see numbers like (+5, -2) next to file names in their console output. The change is minor and does not alter how files are processed, only how the results are reported.

cfc0936f7c332b64960713c4926a8a8c3f2ce0ee.text: The tool's startup menu now includes an option to automatically set up your project settings. You will see the name 'codebuff' written in all lowercase letters instead of capitalizing the first letter. This change is live immediately and applies to anyone opening the tool.

13ac3e2bf59d4298c3319884e98ac10682c88e97.text: The AI assistant was told to stop using short cuts when creating brand new files. Before, it might have saved space by leaving out parts of a new file, but now it must write the whole thing out. This change is live and ensures new files are complete rather than just empty shells.

c2aa5a31540d63ff75742afd0e7ffacbbd4003d8.text: The assistant stopped saving a duplicate record when a user starts a new project. This fixes a bug where the same event was logged twice for fresh folders. Users will see cleaner history in their project logs.

2d481063a4f98716a1dd383878818b8fbb152661.text: The experimental mode now uses a new AI model to help with coding tasks. Only people who turn on this experimental setting will see the change. This makes the experimental option more powerful than the basic option.

a59eb8799ca9dcfd8d1a89439e7c125417e44464.text: A small internal update fixes how the system displays the assistant's reasoning steps when using a specific new model. This ensures the text appears on a separate line, making it easier to read. The change applies only to users testing experimental or high-cost modes.

aa47ceb8544353b8178662323e94db768d27fe29.text: The assistant's internal reasoning process now enforces stricter brevity, especially when the next step is obvious. This change applies to the hidden thought generation logic used by the system. Users will not see any interface changes, but the assistant may respond slightly faster by avoiding unnecessary deliberation in simple cases.

170734af27ebee319e1db40ff10302e2ac4d9a53.text: A small internal update added a specific instruction for one AI model to ensure it properly finishes its written commands. This affects only the backend's communication with that specific model, preventing it from sending incomplete requests. Regular users will not notice any changes, as this is a background fix to improve reliability.

fb5808311a44ad0bcd320b6aedcb96fbb4ec5621.text: The assistant's 'Lite' mode now uses a different, more capable AI model. This change is active immediately for anyone using Lite mode, though the system's internal cost tracking was also updated to ensure billing remains accurate for this new model.

87cb434d8399f9de0a4d3a549a37d229697006dc.text: The help pages for the coding assistant now list the correct AI models used for its economy and premium settings. This update only affects readers checking the documentation, not the software's behavior. People will notice the text describing which models handle simple versus complex tasks has changed.

62b53d39e63cf6bacd03840a124dedec307fb865.text: The system now uses a single, consistent setting to identify which environment it runs in, replacing previous inconsistent labels. This affects internal operations like logging and database connections, ensuring they behave correctly across all services. Users will not notice any change in the application's features or performance.

c062d0d02a3dd39428f470dab47c7cb080898f1d.text: A small internal cleanup made the automated checks for background tasks simpler. Developers now verify the full text output of these tasks against a saved reference image, rather than checking each line separately. This change affects only the testing code and is not visible to end users.

11fc25a9bec9271d36cf766784d435e6eeea0164.text: A small internal update stopped the admin file list from sorting entries alphabetically. Only staff using the admin dashboard will see this change. The file list now shows items in the order the system originally provided them, rather than in alphabetical order.

8368751eadd40e5d083abcb67fe8d915005b423b.text: The command-line tool now looks directly at your computer's folders to suggest file names when you press the tab key. This fixes broken suggestions for internal tools, making it easier to find files without typing full paths. The change is live for the command-line interface.

df4132024acde861056cede0f156f52ecf79b718.text: The login page now checks for expired access codes on the company's servers instead of inside the web browser. This change affects people signing in to the command line tool. If a code has expired, the page will show a clearer message asking them to restart the tool in their terminal and providing a support email address. This is a small internal update and is live today.

3558b7a0601943015cd6076d3af876a0f6ea4ea6.text: Internal backend update. Added a control to limit how much 'thinking' the AI does, and renamed a function for clarity. No user-facing changes. Not live.

88cd9c7070d987c9ec6b239fe03d10c5a9501fa5.text: Local logs now go to a debug folder instead of cluttering the main project area. This change is internal and affects developers working on the code locally. They will notice log files are organized in a specific folder and won't accidentally share them with the team.

3502c13ca329b1df069bc552c62b113f0cce5662.text: The AI assistant's internal rulebook was shortened by removing repeated instructions and old notes about tracking work progress. This change affects only the assistant's behavior, not the software itself. Users will see no difference, but the assistant now follows a cleaner set of directions, which helps prevent it from getting confused or repeating itself unnecessarily.

621176216624c9d6a65ecc6a7fbe1a4db66ddcd8.text: This is a small internal cleanup of how the app reports long-running commands. It now sends a simpler status message, leaving out empty output sections instead of wrapping them in an extra layer. The change is live today, so people who see these command reports would notice shorter, cleaner updates.

43ede3cedf244282db007ba5c0b5d1619366aa95.text: When the command-line tool is stopped, it now cleans up its helper tasks before exiting. This prevents leftover processes from running in the background. Users will not see a change, but their computer stays tidier after closing the tool.

dfb6dcceaf7eab595f4a660efbf0032c46e0bd91.text: When the tool shuts down, it now kills all related helper tasks together instead of just the main one. This stops leftover tasks from running in the background after you close the tool. You might notice fewer stuck tasks or faster cleanup when exiting.

fffe46da7dcb1526f248a3a6d48ce3b66abc9548.text: A small internal update added a tool that checks the account balance and usage limits for the external service providing AI responses. This change does not affect the visible app or end users today; it only helps internal staff monitor service status if they manually trigger it.

ed9d99e02360dcdcf0006cb9553399815cf137fc.text: The application now cleans up leftover background processes while it loads, rather than waiting for this task to finish first. This speeds up the startup time for the command-line tool. You will notice the program opens faster without any change to how you use it.

097f53f35c0c4e5784d898ecce9cb9d3fc984a9d.text: The tool no longer prints a 'Starting Codebuff CLI...' message when it begins. This change affects people using the command-line version of the software. They will see a cleaner screen with less unnecessary text.

35439a6f3d7516558d9fe733baa8b5d2619c86e1.text: The system's internal memory for tracking one-time messages was reorganized to prepare for a new configuration prompt. This change is not live today; the new prompt state exists but does nothing yet. Users will not notice any difference.

dd7fee1b4c0b329726c934cbc68da6845e6fa874.text: A hidden message that used to appear in the background when the system refreshed its connection has been removed. This change affects only internal tools and does not alter any visible features. Users will not notice any difference.

32afb049ea62e113f2a917f82ef35c34daf716e4.text: After updating the app, it now automatically stops any old helper programs left running in the background. This prevents those outdated helpers from interfering with the new version. You will not see any visual changes, but the update process will be cleaner and less likely to cause glitches.

68ed740c94d260ec66109afabaeb789d43d12282.text: The cleanup tool now finishes its first message with a blank line instead of waiting until the end. This fixes the visual glitch where the final line of the cleanup log was missing a newline. This change is live today.

09ca2079e19c8c19059b4d9b17105d44e24915c0.text: Long command outputs now cut off in the middle instead of just the end, keeping both the start and finish visible. This helps people see important results that might otherwise be hidden at the bottom of a long list. The change is active immediately.

475defeec44c951ccae49628378caeab89a60f3e.text: The startup screen no longer shows a 'Starting development processes' message if every background task is switched off. This change only affects internal developers running the app locally. They will see a cleaner console output when they have disabled all startup tasks.

145218cea047ea5fe5fcf5a50a7469fc1c378209.text: The system now limits monthly free credit grants to 2,000 for users who had a previous free grant. This temporary safeguard applies only to accounts with expired free grants, excluding those created during data migration. Affected users will see their monthly credit allowance capped at 2,000 instead of their prior amount until May 22nd.

fe61fbce45249eaa4d5315f08f5dbbd8a5f9bf7f.text: The system now removes hidden color codes from background task logs to keep them clean. This change is not live yet because the cleaning function is currently a placeholder that fails if used. Internal staff will see no visible difference until the logic is finished.

37f4ad341aa7a1e20a9033a61e34a9916a30f694.text: A small internal fix corrected a background error in the admin access check. This change is live today. Staff members using the admin area might see fewer system errors, but the visible experience remains unchanged.

5c754409e6fed7a72529da0291bd97702e75f8f4.text: Previously, the system's search for unreviewed records could accidentally mix data from different accounts. This update restricts the search to the specific account being viewed, ensuring the list only contains relevant items. This change is live and prevents the wrong information from appearing in the review queue.

6e7f07c2a2bc2880dae86ac05e287a09eaf4de52.text: The app now removes hidden formatting codes from terminal output. This change affects the Homebridge npm app's terminal display. Users will see cleaner text without stray color codes or symbols.

16cb8af62a63963dfe7c3c79d06622d08fa8e192.text: A small internal fix improves how the experimental 'deep thinking' mode handles responses. It ensures the system correctly collects the full answer and cuts off output if it accidentally triggers a tool or ends unexpectedly. Users in experimental mode might see fewer broken or truncated messages during long thinking sessions.

fa8524ab00b723913e68a0a103e3904d17dacd89.text: The assistant now waits until the moment you see a new prompt to check if it needs to reconnect to the server, rather than doing it earlier during cleanup. This prevents a brief glitch where the connection could drop before you were ready to type. The change is live and applies to everyone using the command-line tool.

59de873218d28f4d606584fdafd97c840a072e88.text: The program now waits to confirm a background task has fully stopped before clearing its status marker. This prevents stale markers from remaining if a task hangs or closes slowly. Internal reliability improvement; no visible change to current users.

8569968c83cf953a5130ab0df262b99c558f96e5.text: The system now recognizes a specific, smaller AI model when operating in a simplified mode. Previously, selecting this model would cause an error. If you use this simplified mode and choose that particular model, it will now work correctly instead of failing.

cda988485ad9cb9c48b4b484e004b137d19298c2.text: The system now allows the 'max' setting to use a deeper reasoning step, which was previously only available in the experimental setting. This change is active immediately for anyone using the 'max' mode. The assistant may take slightly longer to respond but will show its step-by-step thinking process before answering.

a3b80a5561c434ee5be99b3fac408860c8fe63e4.text: The tool now saves the text output of its background tasks to separate files instead of only showing it on screen. This helps people who run these tasks see what happened, even if the task fails or finishes quickly. The change is active today, but only affects tasks specifically set up to record their output.

6b0e30c9d0759d496936a7daa18479d9c72a587d.text: The AI assistant can now read your project's settings file to understand how you want it to behave. This change makes the assistant aware of custom configurations, such as specific instructions or preferences, allowing it to follow them more closely during conversations.

592741068507116c31948dfd0fb06da9e32000e8.text: A small internal update lets developers mark specific background tasks as off in their setup file. Instead of deleting a task's details to stop it from running, they can just flip a switch. This change is active now for anyone using the development tool.

d2beef4a39af1fdac8a0318d73c62d8e95d32c55.text: A small internal fix corrects which AI model the experimental setting uses. The experimental mode now uses the standard Sonnet model, as intended, instead of a different model it mistakenly selected. This affects only users who turn on experimental mode. They will notice the AI behaves as it did before the mistake, with no visible change to the interface.

f9664212fcdfe36fcede07c3b543772583438337.text: The app stopped checking your saved service credentials when it starts up. This change is internal and temporary, so most people will not notice any difference in how the software behaves.

bfbd79994c52af7d9811ffe2d546a12e8ae72235.text: An internal tool that creates a list of user emails no longer includes a column showing if an account has an active subscription. Only staff who use this export script will notice the change. The resulting spreadsheet now contains just email, name, and sign-up date.

cb69155f5191841058235c85b82d54eb092bed6a.text: The internal tool's startup message now shows a new note in the command help text. This affects only the internal tool's command help text. The change is minor and internal.

06d6e237cb6134133634191ed689908e80ae6b3a.text: Engineers added the model name to internal activity logs. This change affects only the internal record-keeping system, not the software interface. Users will notice no difference in how the application looks or behaves.

e4cdaf0567a9271d5eeb210ce02728e5e6dc8354.text: The automatic testing system now re-runs checks up to five times if they fail, with a ten-minute limit per attempt. This internal change helps the team avoid false alarms from unstable tests. Only the engineering team notices this as fewer unnecessary failure alerts.

065af55655ad8faac986403b4261caf1a0629754.text: The program now has a new rule for how it formats internal requests to its tools. This is a small, behind-the-scenes adjustment that does nothing yet, as no other part of the software uses it. Regular people will not notice any difference in how the app looks or works.

e671365ca0378641c32c0f96ccd2d38badb1f9d4.text: The assistant previously refused to launch local web projects, even when asked. It now obeys such requests. Users who ask for this will see the assistant start the server instead of giving instructions.

23606a7601c6c3348786002f643c770bd8dea489.text: The assistant now has a clear rule to answer questions directly instead of trying to edit code when asked. This applies to internal tools and helps users get simple answers faster. The change is active now.

2268a794c24d0dc6735c2e2caf615e4bb074dbe5.text: The software's internal quality checks were updated to use standard formatting tools instead of manual ones, and the expected results in these checks were adjusted to match the new output. This is a small maintenance task for the development team to ensure the system's self-tests run correctly. Regular users will not notice any changes in how the software behaves.

1d551b74b3e551f2837a5ee173709e75e47b5b16.text: The assistant now finds project guide files regardless of capitalization. Before, a file named 'CLAUDE.md' was ignored if the system expected 'claude.md'. This helps people who use uppercase names in their folders. The assistant will now read those guides correctly.

b4d0321e07c62ef59fff27ba9365887a3c9cf3a6.text: The system now builds its internal instruction templates using a shared rulebook instead of hand-written text. This ensures commands like file reading and goal tracking are formatted consistently every time. The change is live, but only affects how the assistant constructs its own prompts behind the scenes.

6b7e9c51f08a2a1354883a3575e5ea713cb6ee36.text: The system now asks connected apps to disconnect before shutting down, preventing sudden interruptions during updates. Users might notice smoother transitions when the service restarts, as active tasks are less likely to cut off abruptly. This change is live today.

ffff62bf5e82a229d3b1341026b95c771cfd049f.text: A small internal update helps the system better understand instructions. When someone asks the assistant to check code using a specific tool, the system now correctly recognizes this as a request rather than a command to run immediately. This change is live and improves how the assistant interprets such requests.

8d6e147ca2aa8a616f742396b0a6e045b8a54275.text: A program now cleans up leftover helper tasks when it starts. This affects people using the command-line tool. They will see fewer stuck processes and clearer startup messages.

627ee082b926cbfc1fdb1b1ae945d04696b053a6.text: The program now starts checking for its own updates immediately when launched, instead of waiting for other setup tasks to finish first. This small internal change helps the tool become ready to use faster, especially on projects with complex startup configurations. Users may notice a slightly quicker response time when opening the application.

492bd7bf6f64f163eb2461d9d659cdf3315eaf2a.text: The command-line tool now prints a green confirmation message when it automatically adds more credits to your balance. This helps you see exactly how many credits were added right after a request finishes. This small internal update is live for anyone using the tool today.

8964327c04bf88ccfd3e52e99b2a20cf0b623cd2.text: The billing system now combines a user's unused credit with any money they owe to calculate a single net balance. This change is live. On the usage page, users with both credit and debt will see a 'Total' figure that reflects the settled amount, shown in red if the net result is negative.

682496045a36df798e2348d6566e094dbbe2d53e.text: The program now shows tool activity in light gray text instead of white text on a black background. This helps people using terminal themes where black backgrounds clash with their settings. The change applies to the list of files read and the paths of files edited. It is live today.

3b7842883aa9aa4b606101b2b4313063c688b410.text: The program now refuses to save files that are marked as hidden or ignored in your project settings. If it tries to write to one of these protected files, it will stop and tell you the file was ignored instead of changing it. This applies to anyone using the file-writing tool.

8038bdd21c9049fcb8881712c9b9f8dcd1504508.text: A small internal fix corrected how a background process manager finds its terminal tools during build. This ensures the development environment starts up correctly without module resolution errors. Developers using the npm-app will notice smoother startup behavior.

f66dcc735bcda39156d836c9c84dd3eb1b2f2a20.text: The pricing page now displays a helpful note explaining that 500 credits typically cover a day of intense coding. This change also adjusts the layout to ensure the information is centered and easy to read on all devices. These updates are live and affect anyone viewing the pricing information.

57177db953b48e2bebfee1d898f3b684336ed238.text: New accounts now receive free usage credits that expire automatically at the regular monthly reset time. Previously, these initial credits could last forever, allowing new users to avoid paying for extended periods. This fix applies to new signups starting today, ensuring their free allowance follows the standard expiration schedule.

f9fbcd66fad41bea3bfd8c2a184b5b4d6889222d.text: The system's internal record-keeping now accepts a new format for chat logs, preventing errors when saving data. This change is invisible to customers; it only helps the computer store information correctly behind the scenes.

dd3c922664f258943a251edff35798f64f82ba50.text: A tiny internal adjustment was made to how our system connects with a specific cloud service for custom AI models. This change only affects the code's internal labeling, ensuring our tools accept the connection without errors. It does not change how the AI works, what it can do, or what you see on your screen.

37578fe5b7e169da7d8f3f9f3a27a047d03bdff9.text: The system now sends very large file edits to a specialized long-context service in the background. This affects requests for files that are too big for the standard process but still under a specific size limit. Users might see slightly better handling of these large edits, though the main workflow remains unchanged.

c4ab57a230b98c90bc6b414d3e0d5759e4b4f83d.text: The text reader now checks if a '<' symbol is actually the start of a command or just part of the sentence. Before, any '<' caused display errors, even if it was just text like 'less than'. This fix ensures that only valid commands trigger formatting, preventing broken layouts for everyone using the assistant.

52253c178284a2f41d8c021636ef72b86d89a121.text: Internal code cleanup to fix a dependency issue in the web app. No user-facing features or visible changes.

6a05623253923036450c0c161b878cc4dc274d20.text: The system now gives up waiting after five seconds if it cannot quickly check your saved access keys. This prevents the app from hanging indefinitely if the local connection is blocked. Regular users see no change, but developers testing the app locally will now see a clear error message if a conflict on port 3000 stops the check.

e6a34a32810809bece68aa2d2f4948eac1728204.text: A small internal tool that updates payment subscriptions now remembers handled customers by their payment account reference directly, instead of adding a fixed prefix before that reference. The change also tidied how the tool writes some status messages. It is internal maintenance only, so no customer should notice a difference.

2db8ab0f1f31fe680cb74c738ba4618c2079ede3.text: The assistant now has clearer instructions to finish all requested tasks before stopping its current turn. This internal update aims to prevent the tool from cutting off responses prematurely during multi-step processes. You might notice fewer instances where the assistant stops working before fully completing your request.

0f2b48b729bd41d4f3ca072ef16ab2450acc3080.text: The test for the text reader was updated to match how it actually handles line breaks inside tags. This change is internal and only affects developers running the test suite. Regular users will not notice any difference in the app's behavior.

56453d3e917573d9e3f876898e6c1e63908cbfb3.text: The system now counts saved data separately from new data when measuring usage. This internal accounting fix means usage reports are more accurate for the team. Regular users will not notice any change in the service.

3492f067bf495271b05efc95f019c21a79358370.text: The assistant's ability to find specific library documentation was restored after connecting to updated service addresses. Internal tools that search for code examples now function correctly again. This is a minor backend fix with no visible changes for end-users.

b448dbd6dc50182f57ef128cfe812c3bd40ba6ce.text: The assistant now signals its own end-of-turn, ensuring it stops talking or waiting for you at the right moment. This internal cleanup affects how the system manages conversation flow, though you won't see a visible change in the text it produces. It is live today as a minor stability fix.

702ec61bae61c34a111ccd6e29f9a33a041bb82b.text: The command-line tool now recognizes '/help' as a valid way to open the help menu, matching the style used by many other chat interfaces. This change is live and affects anyone using the tool. Users will notice they can type '/help' instead of just 'help' or 'h' to see the menu.

660192fdacff4afd3c2a623e4842531990ac03e4.text: The name of the person who referred you to this service is no longer a clickable link that opens your email program. Instead, it is just plain text. This small change applies to everyone who sees the referrals page, which is live now.

8e3cd39731c3b05487f31ff8cdb7ad89c6cf2d18.text: The reward for successfully referring a new person was reduced from 500 to 250 points. This change is live and affects anyone who invites friends to join the service. A user would notice that their referral bonus is now half the size it was yesterday.

0981cbf98aab05c6dd1fff27279fb5d1bd525d6f.text: The AI assistant's instructions for signaling when it is done talking were simplified. This change applies uniformly to all models, removing a previous condition that treated one specific model differently. Users will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves.

a3fe403d34fa4d76ba0961bb74f14cdbe92b6e41.text: Small internal fix. The system now blocks image uploads for two specific AI models, matching rules already set for a third. Users picking these models will see a clear rejection message instead of a confusing technical error if they try to send a picture.

c6434887277061959deedd47604d65d78b6176cd.text: The tool now checks if you are starting it from your main computer folder. If you are, it shows simple steps to pick a project instead of giving confusing errors. This helps people who are just starting to use the software.

b9a5da20235889ac2aeb5c7e9900c784594e1673.text: When you stop the assistant mid-reply, the system now records the partial text as a note from you, labeled 'Received output', instead of pretending the assistant finished the message. This keeps the conversation history accurate for the internal agent logic. You will not see any visible difference in the chat window.

a55a6d5f83a3fa1eae52a2a4604d077f8eeec0fb.text: The internal command-line tool now lets people manually save a snapshot of their work, even if no files have changed. Previously, the tool skipped saving if it saw no updates; now, an explicit command forces a save. This helps users track their progress during long sessions where they are thinking or typing without modifying code.

c683317d851c3081aa173f237081a1a09eead58a.text: The AI assistant's internal name for the tool that checks browser errors changed from 'browser action' to 'browser logs' to better describe its job. This is a small, invisible update for regular users. You will not see any changes in the interface or how you interact with the assistant.

81e4c5b655665872eba00da2e04eaeaae3d37627.text: The tool now avoids creating backup files when run directly from a user's home folder. This prevents clutter and potential errors in that specific location. People using the tool from their main directory will see fewer unexpected hidden files appear.

f2a76411487f328117048b0d4f61dc185f59941f.text: The assistant now follows a strict checklist before saving code changes, ensuring every update includes a standard credit line. This affects internal users who ask the tool to record their work. They will see more consistent summaries and automatic attribution in their saved history.

8330bae36895631f1304fc6a9f1a76544d8952cb.text: The instructions on the referral page now tell people to first move to their project folder before starting the tool. This helps new users avoid errors if they start from the wrong place. The change is live and only affects what is shown on that specific webpage.

82155f758be1037060fc3e513fb91e2bbec69a4f.text: When a new visitor opens a referral link but hasn't signed in yet, the site now quietly saves the code in their browser. This means if they refresh the page or click away before logging in, the referral credit isn't lost. The change applies only to new visitors using referral links and is live immediately.

faf7dc7431ec61a3216b47bdd073984870bad1e6.text: The terminal now correctly handles typing 'cd' with full file paths or the shortcut '~'. Previously, it only worked for simple folder names relative to the current location. This small internal fix prevents errors when navigating directories.

fa7e7bcf3b80ee78a2fdba4cf2f736914ddd0a71.text: The assistant can now use two new OpenAI models: o3 and o4-mini. This affects people who pick models in the command line tool. They will see these two options in the model list. The change is live today.

ac1ff026ad92929d401c9821b4f5ed3203ec9143.text: The title of the 'Best Practices' guide was updated to 'Codebuff Best Practices' to match the navigation menu. This change affects how the guide appears in the website's sidebar and header. Readers will see the more specific title when they browse the tips section, ensuring consistency between the menu and the page content.

98c359de87a1f4c30a5bed0a440eb85fa1ce2af3.text: The system now has clearer examples of what counts as a command versus regular speech. This helps it ignore accidental triggers when you type normal sentences. The change is internal and already active.

e8c8234508d08ace059d25a52d767d9f51fead51.text: The assistant was told to stop talking sooner when it gives a short answer. This applies only to the specific model used internally. Regular users will not notice a difference.

f9feef47a9aa22cfe899d5b705eee5e2adc3926b.text: A small internal fix stops the tool from remembering the wrong folder location when you switch projects. This prevents the tool from mixing up saved history between different folders. You might notice fewer errors when moving between project directories.

ebf8103ea303805eb97fd7c1afa09dbfdcae2559.text: The system now checks if a requested AI model is actually available before trying to use it. If someone asks for an unsupported model, the system stops the request immediately and shows an error listing the valid options. This prevents confusing failures later in the process.

775f66ad3b7313c43d63c38b392fd17cff856890.text: The internal system now recognizes the newer AI model version and applies the same pricing rules used for the previous version. This update ensures that usage costs for this specific model are tracked accurately. Since this change is internal, no customers will notice any difference in the product's behavior or interface.

5274ebc2a99d52319396c6213a4678118cd005f0.text: The app now blocks its file list when opened at the main user folder, stopping it from seeing private files there. This affects the main and web tools. People will notice the list stays empty instead of showing up to 1000 files.

dc5bfd0da3fc8b9dd049fd9e9bca6a3a2107b1d1.text: The internal assistant can now save new reference notes even if none exist yet, provided it is not the first message in a conversation. This change applies only to the assistant's background logic and is live today. Users will not notice any difference.

425676d520c1042d399a919b44b787c563d65a4c.text: The team deleted a set of internal checks that verified how the system breaks down large pieces of data for logging. This change affects only the developers maintaining the logging tool and is not visible to regular users. No new features were added, and nothing in the product's behavior changed for customers.

c025a7b51e6566c548c85616f7135c7a3ce688d3.text: The app now blocks saving automatic backups if you are working in your main personal folder. This protects your entire computer from accidental changes. You will see a warning instead of a backup being created.

a56079cfa56d0b6dc5ee7b9a51e288e501f75db1.text: The AI assistant's internal memory was updated to track how many times it has replied in a row without a new prompt from the user. This change ensures the assistant pauses and asks for guidance after too many consecutive responses, preventing it from rambling on indefinitely. The behavior remains the same as before, but the system now uses a simpler way to count these replies.

4886cec452d9cc08f5ee5a481ad47871efa645b0.text: When the assistant runs commands in the background, it now keeps track of each command's original request ID instead of merging them together. This helps the system correctly match results back to the specific commands that were asked for. The change is internal and does not affect how the assistant looks or behaves to the user.

b154c52e1781895a6edb887004b9af01bf5e4bff.text: We disabled two automated checks that were taking too long to run. This change only affects the internal testing process, not the software you use. You will notice no difference in the application's behavior or features.

127613a4956730779e13b49791c39a1eeef2fc7a.text: A small internal fix corrected how the system recognizes certain built-in testing tools. This change only affects the code used to check other code, not the final product. Users will notice nothing, as the software's visible behavior remains unchanged.

d08272cd612503e01bad0a8d8a1426390be54a53.text: The instructions given to the AI assistant were simplified to plain text, removing complex formatting rules. This internal change aims to fix occasional errors where the assistant ignored user requests or displayed text incorrectly. Users might notice the assistant follows specific commands more reliably.

a5057f5991af09804645b38ed2ec44339375b39c.text: The assistant now checks on long-running background tasks after every action it takes, not just when you send a new message. This keeps the status of these tasks up to date in real time. The change is live and affects internal processes.

fdd8132d50b598b7531f127d5aeca78ccafb0e28.text: The internal search tool for documentation now applies stricter rules when choosing keywords, ensuring it only picks terms directly related to the specific guide being looked up. This change affects the backend system that retrieves help articles. Users might notice slightly more accurate search results with less irrelevant noise, though the visible interface remains unchanged.

cc65c7a3c53c54602fcef62e9dba933a034c95b3.text: This internal update fixes how automated checks simulate data streams for the AI assistant's main prompt. It replaces complex, outdated simulation methods with simpler ones. Since this only affects the testing environment, customers and users will not notice any changes in the live product.

186aa68c16ef589274f609c1873311ebc255e728.text: A small internal change was made to the testing tools used by the software team. This adjustment prevents a technical warning from appearing when the system checks the code for errors. Regular users will not notice any difference, as this only affects the internal quality checks for the test suite.

a5aa2af8f37961c5d5375b88b64fe88f22962fe7.text: A new shortcut was added to the internal website's address list. If someone types the short web address ending in '/vibe', they will be automatically sent to a specific referral page for a coding tool. This change is active now and only affects people who know to use that specific short link.

e6d9990b88cc6b604af5b6fe08ea1056123565e7.text: When a background process produces too many error messages, the system now keeps the newest ones instead of the oldest. This helps people see the most recent problems first, making it easier to spot what is going wrong right now.

73c28e89e02dedfca7546682f8fae519dc21ac0d.text: The AI assistant can now secretly open web pages to check for errors, without showing a visual window. This helps the assistant debug code more efficiently by reading hidden logs. Users will not see a browser pop up, but the assistant might respond faster to coding issues.

968af547bb4e66152ab80c3d0c07b5209dfbded8.text: The reward for inviting a friend doubled from 250 to 500 credits. This change is live today. Anyone who shares their referral link will now see twice the bonus balance added after a new user signs up.

62b05acf9f9cf6d90d4abb0f837e1377987c2e43.text: The command-line tool now reports stopped background tasks before showing the final summary and exit message. This internal cleanup ensures shutdown logs appear in a logical order. Users will see 'Killed process' notices earlier in the output sequence when closing the tool.

4a82b75160973eb5a773413995e008d3fa6444a4.text: The app now has a new setting that lets you pick the absolute newest, most powerful artificial intelligence model for coding help. This model is still being tested, so it might act strangely or fail sometimes. You only get this if you specifically choose the new option; the normal high-quality setting now uses a different, safer model.

260093037778f6d99c17b7064bc177a6a4817bef.text: The system now skips a special step that breaks large text messages into smaller pieces when running on a local computer. This change only affects the internal logging tool, not the main product features. Developers running the software on their own machines will see raw, unsplit messages in their console, while the live service continues to process logs normally.

56ab198ea52e28db5c0b4f22e7db16ccd2cd1e5e.text: The system now reserves a few characters for punctuation when breaking up large internal messages. This prevents those messages from being cut off if they are exactly the maximum allowed size. This is a small internal fix that affects how support teams see logs, not what you see.

dc65613d159180225b42160b448ab102c3d3c11e.text: The system now splits large internal logs into smaller, safer pieces to prevent errors when recording events. This change affects only the backend team's monitoring tools and does not impact customer-facing features. You will notice nothing as a user; this ensures the internal record-keeping remains accurate and stable.

47797595b7874c359f8fe0967ddf293e21299ce2.text: Developers removed two temporary notes from a system tool that helps split large text messages into smaller pieces. This change is internal and does not affect how the software works for anyone outside the engineering team. Regular users will not notice any difference.

8fc97a62296b489f996b2c36eb3714f8efc4c8c5.text: The system now keeps a larger amount of background information when saving internal activity records. This change affects only the engineering team's monitoring tools and happens automatically in the background. Regular users will not see any difference, but engineers will have more complete data when investigating issues.

8bd79ed84c6021d429eeb34bd9e4ea196e962657.text: The system now reserves more space for extra details before saving large logs. This change is live and affects only the internal logging process. Staff would notice no visible difference, as the system simply handles large information chunks slightly differently to prevent errors.

8a760c9361c7486fd1d37518cf6a23987f7a5c7d.text: The command-line tool no longer accepts two specific model flags, simplifying how you choose between budget and high-quality modes. The help menu now lists project templates before examples and explains how to use an exclamation mark to unignore files. This change is live and affects anyone using the tool's command-line interface.

b59b93cc5415e7b299c9848c2c7d4e1946719199.text: The assistant's personality was adjusted to be calmer. It now avoids excessive excitement and forced cheerfulness, using a more natural, friendly tone instead. This change is live for all users.

2215183fd2c618ca1ea990e8ea29d83cf644d464.text: The undo feature now correctly restores the list of actions the assistant previously took, ensuring it remembers what it did before. This internal fix prevents the assistant from losing context when you revert to a previous state. You will not notice any visual changes, but the assistant will behave more consistently after an undo.

24da962235ece29c99c9730d825d436ad187a2d0.text: The instructions given to the AI assistant were slightly shortened by removing a specific example of incorrect file-writing syntax. This change is internal and affects how the assistant interprets its own rules, but users will not notice any difference in behavior or output.

3f35d98849c0cd31d310e377c891d30ca41033f7.text: The system's method for handling file requests was updated to use a more robust format. This change affects only the internal processing of file data, not the visible interface. Users will notice improved reliability when the system processes files with complex characters or line breaks, reducing the chance of errors.

5c872dacbe6ab3a18ad665a447dc2e688b304b8b.text: The assistant now checks its own instructions for mistakes before trying to act on them. If it finds a broken instruction, it reports the error instead of crashing. This keeps the conversation running smoothly when the assistant gets confused, though you might see a brief error message instead of the action completing.

ae3212816638584c7964a09743fbe79a392acf68.text: The system now wraps user text in quotes before sending it to the AI, preventing the AI from confusing the user's words with its own instructions. This internal safety update affects how the assistant interprets requests, making it less likely to misunderstand complex text. Users will not notice any visible change, as this is a behind-the-scenes adjustment to improve reliability.

8530b2ba3ca97bf6f621b3c0dbde2a271339cd8a.text: The help page now points to the correct location for the safety setup tool. This affects people who want to run the assistant in a protected environment. They will notice the link takes them to the right page instead of an error.

ce0623e2b73f3a8732c7d0644468cba3fbe1a3bf.text: The AI assistant's internal instructions were tightened to require a specific format when it asks to use tools. This prevents the system from crashing due to poorly formatted requests. Users might notice fewer failed attempts when the assistant tries to perform actions like reading files or running commands.

25022813ff557c458d638f78fce60549a696d6e9.text: The assistant's internal instructions were tightened to ensure it formats requests for computer actions correctly, preventing errors when it tries to edit files or run commands. This change is active now. You might notice fewer failed attempts to complete tasks, though the assistant's helpful and enthusiastic tone remains the same.

e053ff3f6459b021b89a072c2cfa33cc3e2fa47e.text: A small internal update now strictly limits the AI assistant to a specific set of approved actions. Previously, if the assistant tried to use an action outside this list, it could cause confusing display errors for the user. This change prevents those glitches by ensuring the assistant only attempts actions it is officially allowed to perform.

72ad881ebfb1ff0e97ef12627183014f14e30b9f.text: The system now tries fewer backup options when a specific text generator is unavailable, making responses arrive slightly faster. This change is active immediately and affects how quickly the assistant recovers from service interruptions. Users might notice shorter wait times during rare outages, but the actual answers remain the same.

7fa2f34c2d5c93bf654ee6cf573a029943156805.text: The system now automatically breaks down very large internal records into smaller pieces so they can be saved. This affects internal support staff who look at these records. They will see long data entries split across multiple lines instead of being cut off or missing.

8985862e597817d73737c756a71927e50df87a21.text: The system now ignores instructions to edit files that appear in your messages. It only accepts these commands from the assistant itself. This prevents the software from trying to change files when you merely paste code snippets or text into the chat.

dc031beaedfd476f7e0d00fd00200dcc3bc1122c.text: A small internal fix improved how the system records problems when it talks to a specific text generator. Support staff will now see the exact error details and the correct name of the service, instead of a vague, wrong message.

0a0e09c432c0b1f0eaee15fbd6ca62858015eca1.text: The system now tries the direct Google connection for the preview model before using the third-party service. This affects internal requests using that specific preview model. You would only notice this if you looked at the internal logs, where the error messages now show the direct Google connection as the first attempt for the preview model.

f381f57e68a242a353feedd5dffd444066c58afc.text: The AI assistant received clearer instructions on how to format its responses when changing files. This internal update aims to make the assistant more consistent in applying edits, reducing the chance of formatting errors when it updates code.

65dc85d48e6b059bcc14ec17f298ca50edf2f980.text: The referral page now shows the actual credit amount for each person instead of a fixed number. This affects users who have referred others. They will see the specific credits earned from each referral update automatically based on real data.

cefd642960b736ed0799a58188960ec19bcd51e9.text: The command-line tool no longer asks you to paste a Google AI key when you run it in 'max' mode. This change only affects people using that specific mode. You will notice that the yellow text block asking for the key has disappeared, and the tool starts working immediately without that interruption.

a00ff2818ca9386935333a9d33525c488a6ba6ab.text: The April 2025 Hackathon event page now shows the correct date and time, lists the three judges, and highlights the free dinner and credits. Visitors to this specific event page will see updated details and a new judges section. This change is live.

032e10876f009524f01fb693ce9f27a9d140a27e.text: The system now picks which service answers your questions in a simpler order, skipping steps that used your personal login details. If a primary service fails, it automatically switches to a backup without asking you to re-enter passwords. This change is live today.

bf69696e0f8b19dc50032099c1b1f113a992f6ed.text: A small internal update fixed a typo in the instructions that tell the AI assistant how to handle system commands. The assistant is now clearly told not to run version control commands without explicit permission, preventing accidental changes to project files. This change is live and improves safety for anyone using the assistant to manage code.

1cbc08e7eaafe9095b0a216a6d3fbdd73ef292ba.text: Small internal fix for the command-line tool. Previously, unexpected errors could make the program stop working without warning. Now, the program shows the error and keeps running so you can continue working.

fd74605d71216ccf102d9d46a47487eec69c9eb5.text: When the system switches to a backup AI service because the first one stops mid-answer, it now remembers the words already shown instead of starting over. This keeps the conversation context intact for the final backup model. The fix is active for internal requests using specific experimental and preview models.

54a429841fcb251aba97cfb5406a54f88f426390.text: The system now tells its helper to automatically agree to safe actions when using command-line tools. This stops tasks from getting stuck waiting for a human to type 'yes'. It affects only the internal helpers that run these commands, so regular users won't see any difference.

1cc019b921c42b3ca53252da284e0083f3c856f4.text: The team stopped a specific background check that verifies how the assistant ends its responses. This check was failing randomly, so it was paused to keep the system stable. Customers will not notice any difference in the assistant's behavior.

0d29aa3c0f170c037d1361797a01dbb65934830b.text: A small internal update added a warning to the assistant's instructions, telling it to stop using a specific formatting style that causes errors. This affects the automated editing tool, helping it avoid mistakes when modifying files. Users will likely notice fewer failed edit attempts when asking the assistant to change code or text.

c1205d24205ed2a2d46d047cc5097a7c11c3ad93.text: A small internal fix ensures the last line of text no longer disappears when a task finishes without returning results. This affects internal console output, making the final message display correctly with proper spacing. Users will see complete, readable text at the end of responses instead of truncated lines.

64c6a2013c52f196e42446853e569d8b46bb13ed.text: The system now recognizes when a user's personal Gemini password is incorrect, showing a clear warning instead of failing silently. It also adjusts credit charges, ensuring users are only billed for platform overhead when using their own password, not full service costs. This change is live and affects users who have connected their own Gemini credentials.

c41a74e13876be3326142e6bc1fa60515066ad27.text: When the app tries to use one AI service and fails, it automatically switches to a backup service. You will see a brief notification on your screen letting you know this switch happened. This ensures your request still gets processed even if the primary service is unavailable.

2b20c41c8caf11b91e3a9db6c1e0e4497c908837.text: The system now automatically shortens long conversation histories before asking for file recommendations. This prevents errors when requests are too large for the service to process. Users might notice fewer failed attempts when searching for files in very long chats.

1f561a4c640de3af4907585b5782985657b8fe89.text: The system now forces its internal assistant to run one command at a time. It must wait for the first command to finish before starting the next. This prevents overlapping tasks and keeps the process orderly.

21a9235fb756a9868f482c6b3dc98bf653ba5332.text: The command-line tool now checks pasted API keys more carefully. If you paste a valid key, it accepts it; if you paste something that starts like a key but has the wrong length or format, it warns you instead of trying to use it. This helps prevent mistakes when adding keys. The change is internal and affects only people using the command-line tool.

d452b52b7e26006237d0091dae5d465e53deece6.text: If you connect your own account for this service, the system now tries to use your connection first before falling back to other options. It also correctly calculates the price for longer conversations, ensuring that the first part of the text is cheaper than the rest. This change is live now.

9f1f23959d962776a202355db2f6f2e2ac44d241.text: The help guide for new users now includes clearer steps for fixing installation problems. People setting up the tool will see a new checklist that starts with verifying their basic computer setup, followed by the previous advice on fixing permission errors. This update is live on the help website.

336178888ea7b62b16044caa0fadcabd34911663.text: The system now uses Google's official software tools to talk to its AI models, replacing a custom-built method. This change affects how the backend processes requests, making the code cleaner and more reliable for developers. Users won't notice any difference in how the AI behaves or responds, as this is an internal maintenance update.

d16dc3de0a0bd7e716dde06b243cd3b69de81adb.text: The assistant now correctly handles commands containing the ampersand symbol. Previously, a specific text format for this symbol caused some terminal instructions to fail. This internal fix ensures that requests to run commands with this symbol work as intended. Users will not see a visible change, but the assistant will be more reliable when executing these specific tasks.

5ef9c11bf56fb8dc330e5c756ac65e587e219a8c.text: The sign-in button now checks the current web address before sending you to the next page. If you are on the login screen with a special code, it sends you to the setup page instead of the home page. This helps new users land in the right place after signing in.

74352a7abbddf4ace7a80d21ad4bd373561e1761.text: The sign-in system now handles two different login methods separately. If a command-line tool sends a code, the system directs the user to a setup page instead of the main site. This change is active for internal users and ensures the correct page loads after signing in.

929fa1954a73f3cce70c64cb8dd08e463c2d5472.text: A small internal change added a note to the system's private log every time someone checks their list of access keys. This helps the support team track who is looking at their keys. Regular users will see no change in the app's behavior or appearance.

1b900b1bf625bc3267901f2e95644b10ed3a469a.text: The internal assistant now correctly writes command symbols, stopping it from turning '&' into broken text like '&'. It also reminds the assistant that changing folders only affects one command, not the next. This is a small, live fix for internal tools; regular users will see smoother automated tasks.

0e378ecb4fff72500e96ebbc69ea4214247031cb.text: A hidden piece of data, specifically the start date of your billing period, was removed from the system's internal quota check. This cleanup affects only the background processes that verify your credit usage, so you will notice no changes in how the application displays your remaining credits or billing dates.

6e951a730e2a7acc6c8a2329f23727451c411e80.text: The command-line tool no longer displays a playing card emoji at the end of its welcome message. This small visual change affects only users of that specific tool, who will see plain text instead of the icon when they start it.

b9ca62bd9bc1906a4339801efa2fff35726383cb.text: Small internal fix. The file browser now correctly reads ignore lists placed inside subfolders, so files marked to be hidden there stay hidden. Without this, those rules were ignored, showing extra files that should be excluded.

908706b65c46689f8a4a55ddf412d9cb70919521.text: A minor update, live today, makes the command-line tool wait for its connection to fully load before saving a new API key. Users adding a key will now see a loading spinner while the tool prepares. This prevents errors caused by trying to save the key before the tool was ready.

a205282c954f2ca2ae047908e299d9e1c825aee0.text: The internal instructions for the AI assistant were updated to strictly forbid it from adding extra formatting symbols around its commands. This ensures the system can correctly read and execute tasks like saving files without errors. Users will notice fewer failures when asking the assistant to perform actions.

1a72b48e2b0ff4b6fd2e9ebe1e1074258139a3a9.text: The internal tool's welcome message now ends with a joker emoji. This small visual tweak affects staff using the command-line interface. They will simply see a card symbol at the end of the greeting.

6c04ddd7f853b6b4f0b34655d3c132e2ccef7bcb.text: The command-line tool now displays a warning message immediately when a user hits their monthly usage limit or exceeds their quota. This ensures users are notified of their status without needing to manually check their account settings.

e556eff04f4d707cf39f024447cb713a7bdadfae.text: Paid subscribers now see their credit reset date based on their actual billing cycle from Stripe, not a fixed monthly guess. This fixes inaccurate reset dates for anyone whose billing period doesn't start on the first of the month. The change is live for active paid accounts.

85d3d6ddf10ac1cd963b30839b1bee382c6d4fd9.text: The internal billing report now checks every paying customer instead of stopping after the first hundred. It also separates regular subscribers from those who exceeded their usage limits, ensuring average overage costs reflect only the affected accounts. Staff running the report will see accurate totals and a clearer breakdown of who is incurring extra charges.

360e748770224a069eb6622b9bf8e907e5862582.text: Internal check tightened to ensure conversation history remains correctly ordered. Programmers only. No visible changes for end users.

7c6a3873c1eacd433d116334df6071b06b4a7d63.text: The program's memory for recent tasks now uses a simpler built-in method to remember and drop old items. This internal cleanup means the system manages its own memory more efficiently without extra tools. You will notice no change in how you use the software, as this is a behind-the-scenes improvement.

c32f38e54c6fb7b66ff820ab5f49dc055a2da1c9.text: A small, internal update to the automated checks that verify the assistant's core instructions. This change fixes formatting and data handling rules within the test code itself. It does not affect how the assistant behaves, what features are available, or what users see today.

7c1d32a9f89af5d53a27952e563ff9296e54205d.text: Internal cleanup only. Renamed one helper function to clarify its purpose. No user-facing changes. Nothing to notice.

24fade14d192a9fec4519c32dc97be7a73228e4b.text: Small internal fix for the command-line tool. Pasting text no longer accidentally runs a command immediately. Users will see pasted text stay on screen until they press Enter.

b89142e4054b2ef112559c95d8245acd2097b72d.text: The system now bundles user details into a specific section of its internal notes when tracking activity. Support staff will see these details grouped together rather than scattered throughout the notes. This change is active but only helps staff investigate issues; regular users will not notice any difference.

ea0ebdfd45a2e313e1346a6b957dd6709681fe94.text: Programmers fixed a small error in their internal safety checks that stopped the tests from running correctly. This change does not affect the app's behavior or what customers see. It only helps the development team keep their code clean and reliable.

184039842a6b2fdfd491ad3f32d67424f19b9c36.text: The system stopped writing routine messages to its internal record when it disconnects inactive sessions or encounters minor checks during cleanup. This change affects only the technical logs viewed by the operations team, not the features used by customers. Engineers will see fewer repetitive entries in the system's history, making it easier to spot actual problems.

7194441fa69e3c64b590e664fc0b913c6b3dbbab.text: Programmers using a specific code editor now have a setting updated to automatically fix certain style mistakes every time they save a file. This change affects only the internal development team's local setup. You would notice nothing, as this tooling adjustment helps maintain code consistency behind the scenes.

bb46f041631b662febe4be3ae09c93e151e15649.text: When the main system fails to rewrite a file, the backup now uses a different AI model that wraps answers in code blocks. The system automatically strips these blocks before saving. This only affects internal reliability during errors, so users see no visible change.

9077874c7bd33bc48035090e458182045b3d7337.text: The program now stores the reason why file-saving is turned off as plain text instead of a complex error object. This fixes a bug where the program would crash when trying to read the last saved file while saving was disabled. The command-line tool now shows a clear message about why saving is off, rather than breaking.

ae65f86e78660e76628f4b441e046fbababcc189.text: The system now safely handles missing or unreadable files during creation, preventing crashes when it tries to read a file that doesn't exist. This affects anyone using the file creation feature. If a file is missing, the system will skip it gracefully instead of failing.

a3c2420addf103825f58187ff477c7aaf415b899.text: The safety filter that stops dangerous computer commands was updated to check the first word of a command instead of the whole text. This prevents false alarms on safe words that start with 'yes', like 'yesterday', while still blocking the actual 'yes' command. The change is active now and applies to internal tools.
