0eb3abf36efb50b013298c896cde7f23805ad854.text: The system now finds the right instructions for handling file results. This internal fix ensures the assistant correctly processes information from files. Users will not notice any immediate changes, as this corrects a background error.

6e97eb90e4b3b9fa9368efc51ef7c77af6143f26.text: Developers fixed a hidden issue in their internal quality checks. Previously, fake data used during testing could accidentally leak into other tests, causing false alarms. This cleanup ensures tests run independently. No customer-facing features changed, so users will notice no difference in the product.

d0edf14d10e19dfefb1e8f8e2cba605493cfb806.text: The system now correctly identifies which files have already been loaded when preparing a response. Previously, a technical error caused it to misjudge whether a file was ready for use. This internal fix ensures the assistant accurately tracks available file information, though the change is small and affects only the underlying logic.

957f50c280ba823d04fad59c08122a6b8acfc61c.text: The assistant now stops after 20 consecutive replies to prevent endless loops. This applies to the core chat system. Users will notice the assistant pausing and asking for input if it talks too much without hearing back.

9fdad5633eb69054c86960f49e32cb82d9631af1.text: A new help section was added to the online instructions for installing the software. It tells people what to do if their computer blocks the installation because it needs permission. This change is live now and helps new users fix setup problems on their own.

f39b1d6f04fd27f94f95f0c4181ce2fc523a05c4.text: The team simplified how the software checks its own safety nets. Instead of manually swapping and restoring fake data during tests, the system now handles this automatically. This change is internal to the development process and affects no one outside the engineering team. Users will notice nothing, as this does not change how the app works or looks.

2876575615ed9aa91c8df4bfdcdc5b9ce9633d04.text: The system now labels file-sharing instructions more clearly to avoid confusion. This internal cleanup affects how the assistant reads project files. You will not notice any change in behavior.

c82696f7121ad9cf25d1a60564d5937bb886bf42.text: Developers silenced the automatic status messages that appear while running internal checks for the main assistant prompt. This change affects only the testing environment and will not change how the software behaves for anyone outside the development team. No visible difference for end users.

896aa1b61626f7b18c1b7bab5e4b0991bb9b4dad.text: The tool that decides which files to hide from the assistant was updated to handle path names correctly on its own. Previously, the system had to manually remove a leading slash from ignore lists, a step now deleted because the new version does it automatically. This change is live and ensures that files listed in ignore settings are hidden exactly as intended.

33b2e10c844c7e25e234ffee3c380cc67fade0ad.text: The assistant no longer tells you which files it has already read. This is a small internal cleanup. You will not notice any change in how the assistant works.

a72b42b796dcbe23dc6c2cf30d8170716df14769.text: A small internal fix corrected how the system records which files it successfully read. This improves the accuracy of the logs that help the support team understand file access issues. Regular users will not notice any change in their experience.

329031e75f4e2133392a91230287585461952b70.text: When a new member joins the Discord server and gets the verified role, the system now records their username in its internal log. This helps staff trace who was added during debugging. Regular members will not see any difference, as this change only affects internal records.

060a630a5c78235f73f227ec9bcc0133c5aaa47f.text: The AI assistant's internal instructions for handling project notes were clarified. It now more accurately identifies when to update these notes based on user feedback and explicitly states which details to omit. This change affects how the assistant manages its own knowledge base and is live today.

05bc43e718f37af5141e80fb8bb56d7f22def5ed.text: This internal update connects signed-in user details to the analytics tool. It uses the email address to link data across different services, while keeping the internal account number as a secondary reference. Customers will not see any changes on the website.

34726d285b632fcf26051267f34879732cfcf109.text: The Discord bot now uses the platform's official setting to hide its responses. This means messages like account linking confirmations or error warnings are visible only to the person who triggered them, not to everyone in the channel. This change is live.

32458bca8729c98d3585808918afd113f106a47d.text: The AI assistant now stops repeating itself when a task is finished, especially after running a command. It also shares results more directly instead of asking for the same file again. This fix is currently in the code but has been reverted, so it is not live for anyone yet.

e95547801c583a4233d60240f0c797a57fd66888.text: The system now knows which group label to apply to verified accounts, but the actual labeling step is not yet active. This internal setup change affects no one today. Users will see no difference until the next update connects this label to the verification process.

7922b9b45c3d6dbc0efcc5509353392ccdb16cd7.text: The assistant now reports exact reasons when it cannot read a file, such as missing, ignored, or too large, instead of just failing silently. This helps the assistant understand why a request failed and choose the next step. You will notice more accurate responses when asking about files that cannot be opened.

840c30c49390890c07d6a53877dbafd098158b23.text: The system now stores a specific Discord role identifier as text rather than a number. This prevents the software from accidentally altering the digits of this long ID, which could happen with numeric storage. Only the internal verification step for Discord interactions is affected. This change is live and requires no action from users.

825f3c07c5f942cb1395d6c02a0be27e04ed8ccb.text: The Discord bot now automatically sends a private message to new members in the welcome channel, instructing them to use the /link command to connect their accounts. Additionally, the account linking process was updated to prevent errors if an email or Discord account is already connected to a different profile. These changes are live and affect only new members joining the Discord server.

c7b243c61fcc0f765d37586a5fe744cbf6c71ed1.text: When you ask the assistant to read a file it already has, it now shows that file again. Previously, it skipped re-showing files it already knew about, causing it to forget they were available. This helps the assistant keep track of what you asked for, even if it had seen the file before.

edef5e00209aa5a2d7b9481da9790232d6154ce2.text: A small internal update now tracks how much data the AI model uses during live conversations. This change affects only the system's internal reporting, not what customers see or how the assistant behaves. No visible difference will appear to users.

c7591186338e34ae81780518f88d0f6abd057496.text: The assistant stopped using a special shortcut to end conversations after running computer commands. Instead, it now relies on a standard instruction to know when a task is finished. This change affects how the internal tool decides to stop, but regular users will not notice any difference in chat responses.

a6655b63d3863d1e3c2800853a0e5b26144160ce.text: The system stopped recording detailed internal notes about how it processes information. This change only affects the hidden logs that engineers use to track system performance, not the actual features or speed of the application. You will not notice any difference in how the software behaves or looks.

e977634108b72c1eff8bc68e07db8bfded59eeb5.text: A recent update that changed how the AI assistant handles task completion and file results was reversed because it caused errors. The assistant now returns to its previous behavior, meaning it will correctly finish tasks and show file contents as it did before the failed update. This change is live and affects all internal users of the assistant.

94a86e1476a5c8fddc37794dd9fe484687dc4ca6.text: A quality check for the rewrite feature now allows a slightly larger change before it reports a problem. This only affects internal checks, not the product itself. A customer would notice nothing.

531e3bbdf9d49fed8e7c5d9ee0abc65038cb86e7.text: The assistant now notices when you manually change a file it previously created or read. Instead of overwriting your edits with its own old version, it treats your changes as new instructions for future updates. This is a small, internal improvement that helps the assistant keep up with your work in progress.

6149275ecdf5c64575ecfe4c495d658ab94a17e9.text: The assistant now checks if you have asked it to look at specific files before searching for them. If you haven't mentioned any files, it skips that search step to save time and effort. This change is live today and helps the assistant respond more efficiently to simple questions.

1353fca7fa528a93f5518a4761ac856ac44936be.text: The main headline on the website changed from 'Codeflow' to 'AI Coding', and the text below it now reads 'Simple. Fast. Powerful.' instead of describing technical stack knowledge. This update is live immediately for anyone visiting the homepage, making the first impression simpler and less jargon-heavy.

6fde2cbd3467f24217ab8640a5795756ec808925.text: The help pages now clearly list which artificial intelligence tools handle different tasks, such as writing code or finding files. This update affects people reading the online documentation. They will see a new question and answer explaining the specific tools used to power the service.

570831eff513a245158889574f6021a585dd6993.text: The cost tracking system now adds a 30% markup to AI usage fees, up from 20%. This change is live and affects internal financial reports. No customer-facing features or prices changed.

8dbf4f061611d6890e2f3ad3b5a12ccd2bc99880.text: The system now asks a specialized tool to identify which files are most relevant to your request. If this tool fails or times out, the system safely falls back to its original method of selecting files. This internal improvement helps ensure the assistant focuses on the right information without causing errors.

65cec2d69e90bd0b25e6657d312310527f69bc04.text: Developers cleaned up how the system marks the last message for temporary storage. This internal tidy-up ensures the system handles messages consistently without changing how the assistant behaves. Users will notice nothing different.

06c65a9acde8f942931df3c4ee85ff9209dd2444.text: A short note inside the system's internal instructions was corrected to remove an incomplete sentence about text limits. This change affects only the internal documentation for developers, not the live service. Customers and users will not notice any difference in how the software works.

fca2d740496f13e80bc48a46e9415258d68f9415.text: The system now places your core instructions at the very beginning of the message sent to the AI, rather than the end. This ensures the AI prioritizes these rules even if the conversation history gets too long and older parts are cut. You will not see any visual change, but the AI should follow your initial setup and constraints more consistently.

017c24c785fc424fd44da9348ae74da9ec97696a.text: The command line tool now automatically re-enters your previous text into the input box when you use the undo or redo commands. This saves you from having to retype or copy-paste the original request after reversing a change. The update is live and applies to all users of the command line interface.

bd51b864ff7db8ed47bad306b99c012f0434930e.text: The help guides now use simpler names for the AI models to match current branding. A new section explains how to fix common setup errors if the tool fails to start. These updates are live on the website.

1857561a2c060c839ccf1b76dd07d9f47cc902c4.text: A small internal adjustment changed how the system treats the 'which' and 'where' commands. These commands are no longer grouped with other multi-word instructions, so the system handles them differently when checking terminal inputs. This change is live but affects only the underlying logic, not the visible interface.

5fb0f5407f8ac0f706f8808ce282355b0d529516.text: The system now uses a cheaper tool to rewrite text. This tool works as fast as the old one but makes fewer mistakes. Internal operations cost less. Regular users see no visible change.

a670ce167ad29c50e1567d0a24489f2fe91471d9.text: The heading text on the website's customer review section changed from 'See them raving' to 'Watch them rave'. This affects visitors reading the homepage, where they now see a slightly more active phrase above the video testimonials. The change is live and purely visual.

92bbfc1519ef829bf72ef2cf1c4d3ba8be2dce6f.text: The terminal display for the assistant mode no longer prints an empty line before showing the command. This removes a small visual gap, making the output slightly tighter. It affects users viewing command executions in the assistant interface.

b4cfc60a624a82c7e4b53b134fb523b467c0755b.text: The app now hides connection error messages in the developer console when sending data fails. This change affects the background system that keeps the app connected to the server. Regular users will not notice any difference, as the system automatically tries to reconnect.

5dc9e20b7174e8410c56f1ee4aafb7b82581010b.text: A small internal update speeds up how developers launch the app on their own machines. It skips rebuilding shared background components if they haven't changed, starting the app faster. This affects only the team running the software locally, not the live product.

94c6a1f3431f0ad539c432bad5a4d747da3adf6a.text: The software now uses a newer version of the main artificial intelligence engine for all its features. This update applies everywhere the engine is used, such as when rewriting text or generating content. You might notice slightly different responses or improved accuracy in these areas, though the change itself is minor and requires no action from you.

f2964699fe0a27c33aa00d9c5ef313b113dfea2f.text: The system stopped using an extra step to re-add comments to code edits. This change makes the process faster and simpler. Users will not notice a difference in the final code, but the system works more efficiently.

e097b3f55689b7a7712e2408242c355237eacf01.text: The system now keeps the original line breaks when saving file edits. This prevents mismatched formatting that could cause errors during updates. Only internal file processing is affected.

ac61a3dcb6d91484a6c784e623921c7f660732cb.text: The command-line tool now uses a standard library to read instructions, replacing custom code that previously required a specific hidden flag to run correctly. This change affects internal developers running the tool locally. They would notice the tool automatically generates clearer help messages and version information when asked, and it no longer fails due to missing internal flags.

71ac9b657e2e5006b0cfb6592cd215eb06e6921d.text: The assistant now limits its view of a project's change history to the five most recent updates. This prevents the system from being overwhelmed by excessive text when it checks the history. You will notice this change immediately when the assistant reviews recent activity, as it will no longer display the full list of all past updates.

de61584048a43d6ffd1a153de63b4adef04fb5a2.text: The system now sends tool results to the AI assistant in the correct order, before your next message. This ensures the assistant sees the most recent information first. Internal logic change only; no visible impact for users.

307ad70ab086e54912205100a22a3942805600a5.text: The assistant can now record an initial note when it first creates a task step. This aligns the creation process with the update process, allowing for a complete history from the very beginning. The change is currently in place but does not alter visible behavior until the assistant chooses to use this new option.

a17bd88894ce4de861b23db36b08f46c0788adbd.text: The app now catches and records errors when it tries to send a command over its live connection, instead of letting those errors go unnoticed. This change affects the command-line tool, ensuring that failed actions are logged for debugging rather than silently ignored. Users will not see any visual difference, but support teams will find it easier to diagnose connection issues.

c70a7bd007480d503affbbdc6648917752cd48de.text: The internal instructions for the assistant were slightly adjusted to clarify its behavior regarding file and version control tasks. The assistant now follows a rule to perform these actions only when explicitly requested, but it is instructed not to refuse such requests from the user. This change applies only to the internal guidance system and is live today.

1c0db17a18120507fe9a679429276efe3b4b466e.text: The system now stops and tells you to update if it cannot send your request, instead of trying to continue silently. If the connection drops, unfinished tasks are marked as done rather than failing, allowing the app to recover smoothly. This change is live and affects anyone using the real-time chat interface.

7775aa33d0f6879497aff01816d1fbf3dc8713ff.text: The system now reads more background files when a user sends a single, initial message. This helps the assistant understand the request better from the start. The change applies only to the first message in a conversation and is already active.

4eee2dd5a47c061ac2cfa13ec1d705d133d793d3.text: The assistant now displays the actual text of files it reads, instead of hiding this information. This small internal update means you will see the file contents in the output when the tool finishes reading, rather than just a blank space or a loading state.

91b3aed1da4af4e61c9793ac3a8ef3e315ea66dd.text: The system now checks if a user's connection is still active before sending cost updates, preventing errors when the connection has already closed. This internal fix affects backend stability and logging, so regular users will not notice any visible changes in their interface.

cb26ddc3796a646656e02e5e13caa3cc7d45f049.text: The program stopped showing a loading animation twice when it was waiting for a response. This is a small internal cleanup. You might notice the waiting indicator behaves more consistently, but nothing else changes.

b241d9279c541e2eb7a4eb0b867561c20f43fe04.text: A small internal fix ensures the system correctly uses its primary method for saving work snapshots, only switching to a backup method if the first one fails. This improves reliability for users creating checkpoints. You likely won't notice any immediate difference, but snapshots will be saved more consistently.

f32b6ff3ed8db914de1187c2b4b44635c8f893a1.text: A leftover debugging note was deleted from the checkpoint restoration system. This internal cleanup removes unnecessary noise from the logs. The change is live today but invisible to users.

8df0d11f7528869f7a9b936b5c25e4ea67104dae.text: The assistant's internal logic for deciding when to ask for file access was adjusted. Previously, it might skip requesting files if a tool had just been used; now, it only skips this step if no new instruction was provided. This change is live and affects how the assistant manages context, ensuring it doesn't unnecessarily withhold file access based on recent tool usage.

459ea4195ed3508bd72e694c5372b5cb47996a4d.text: The tool now lets you move back and forward through your saved work states using simple commands. This helps people who accidentally undo too much and want to get their previous work back. You can now type a redo command to step forward again.

9fb5b4a08247ddbd73c7dcca05d8aed36a7589ed.text: The website now gets its news updates from a cleaner data source instead of an older format. This internal fix makes the feed more reliable and prevents errors if the source changes slightly. Readers will not notice any visual difference, as the articles appear exactly as before.

7d80bfcfaf40b60a3321533e365e2d23497f6526.text: A small internal fix stops a loading animation from spinning while the assistant performs background tasks. This change is live now. You might notice the progress indicator pauses briefly during certain operations, making the interface feel slightly less busy.

82cb8bbaede30bf2e00ef695a7f64c07aa0d69e8.text: A new safety check stops the assistant from running three specific commands that could restart or freeze the computer. This applies to internal users today. They would notice these commands are blocked before the system even tries to approve them.

105df9c10b72a55a483d0a6f5a7252545cfd23eb.text: The assistant now automatically creates a written outline when asked to build a new feature or reorganize existing code. Previously, it only did this if you specifically used the word 'plan.' You will see this change immediately when starting a new project or cleaning up old code.

a94529d60072531f3172605b9d6ca329aa125a52.text: The software now hides technical status messages from its internal background process when saving changes. This keeps the main conversation clean and prevents confusing text from appearing in the assistant's response. The change is active immediately and affects how checkpoint saves are displayed to you.

a07fa2b893936873e96cf80160da83b1458f930c.text: When you switch to a different folder, the assistant now forgets the temporary snapshots it saved from the previous folder. This prevents it from accidentally using old information from the wrong place. You won't see a visual change, but it keeps your work accurate when moving between projects.

9e9be1917697c97278d5b2362e12fe697e759c68.text: The program now clears the text cursor before checking if you pressed Enter without typing anything. This prevents a confusing visual glitch where the cursor would stay on the previous line when the empty input was rejected. The change is live and affects anyone using the command-line tool.

d300f180a0152ba44abedcf405fd895c0a4f5826.text: The system now handles edits to the same file one by one instead of all at once. This prevents errors where multiple changes clash and corrupt the file. It is an internal fix, so you will not see any visual changes, but the tool will be more reliable when updating code.

64dde186e5ca7b4e0ff2401f2af7cf14961199a8.text: A small internal update ensures that text files created by the system always use the same line spacing format, regardless of the computer they are made on. This change happens automatically in the background and does not affect how you see or use the application. You will not notice any difference, but it helps prevent minor formatting errors when saving files.

e6bdcf4ae10c7ec740fa7126cbfdc44d592bd02b.text: The tool now saves a backup of your work only when you use specific commands like undo, restore, or send a message, instead of after every single action. This prevents unnecessary clutter and clears old backups when you log in again. You will see a simple text confirmation instead of a colored message when a backup is created.

fd9fb1d8e2d9590db8bfe8da8bdd87101d9df2ab.text: The command-line tool now clears leftover text from the screen before showing the next prompt. This prevents old, half-typed commands from appearing when you finish a task or press a key combination. It affects anyone using the text-based interface, making the screen look cleaner and less confusing.

a5e8e0b1b94ecc896a8ee912a80991bea27c76ac.text: The command-line tool now updates the displayed folder path when you navigate to a different directory. This affects internal users of the tool. They will see the correct current folder name in the prompt after moving directories.

5396f20c74fb3efde805856b2ae2f1b2bbcc8f8b.text: The system now applies file updates more carefully, ensuring edits fit smoothly into existing text without adding confusing markers. It also skips extra processing steps unless specific conditions are met, making updates faster. Users will notice cleaner file changes and quicker responses when editing documents.

a0ac982ba134446924f9fd30fbdf91a826e8150a.text: The command-line tool now stops automatically typing 'checkpoint [number]' into the prompt when restoring a previous state. This prevents clutter when a restore action itself created the checkpoint being restored. The fix applies to the internal command-line interface and is live.

40521de35528c488d39557a4ef9e774351831a81.text: A small fix helps the system handle rare invisible characters that sometimes sneak into saved messages. This prevents occasional errors when recording usage data. Most people will not notice any difference unless they previously saw a message fail to save.

09425b4ead90942452204181dd3d67679347c665.text: The greeting message now displays a clover emoji instead of a pie. This visual update applies to the text shown when the program starts. Users will see the new symbol appear next to the welcome question.

7348c640bb9308878bd4ffd9085529e98f307ac7.text: The system now tells you exactly why it cannot save your work, rather than just saying it is disabled. Today, you will see a message about the project being too large if you try to undo changes, but future problems will show their specific causes.

9b7e25c267e23cc232b323f6004d1b2018dc9c95.text: The system now skips creating a backup if nothing has changed, preventing unnecessary clutter. This internal fix ensures that storage is only used when actual modifications occur. You will not notice any visible changes in your interface.

d6357823470aa9c365a19bdee374d4410646356b.text: The internal assistant now reads more project files before making changes and finishes all planned steps instead of stopping early. This affects internal staff using the tool. They will notice fewer incomplete tasks and better context awareness in the assistant's output. The change is live.

c1d96037d902848e46d7b1be21b283389e6fb72d.text: The system now skips an unnecessary step when saving your work, making the process slightly faster and more reliable. This change affects internal operations, so you will not notice any immediate difference in the application's behavior.

193d18c027e53bf15765ab673db01e66f2b52aab.text: A small internal fix is live. If someone ran a command that printed nothing, the command window could stay stuck waiting. Now it correctly checks all the output it has collected before deciding the command is done, so the window becomes ready again.

0a2adb636c9c14cb40d6f8b26ffc83d17fb8f978.text: The system now displays a color-coded summary of code changes during internal testing. Green lines indicate new additions, red lines show removals, and cyan lines mark section breaks. This update only affects internal tools and does not change what customers see in the main applications.

2ea746abe49347978c1a31d8956bf2f73bcde972.text: A small internal update changed the assistant’s instructions for its deep thinking step. It now tells the assistant to begin with very short thinking notes, each five words or fewer, and it removed an old example and a repeated condition. Someone using the assistant to plan a task may see a shorter, more focused opening to its reasoning. The change is already in place.

116e23c2a5a3aea16627c3d43d420daa05383f5c.text: A small internal fix ensures that when a user cancels an ongoing request, the system still records the usage data correctly. It also prevents the system from processing unrelated responses by checking the request ID earlier. Users will not notice any visible changes in the interface, but the underlying data tracking for cancelled actions is now more accurate.

b4f522ef10553fcd59f63f000089fb8d02c745cf.text: The assistant now uses proper comment markers to signal skipped code when editing files, instead of bare ellipses. This internal cleanup ensures the system correctly identifies and removes these placeholders before applying changes. You will notice no visible difference in the output, as this prevents accidental code corruption during edits.

f91c7f4911e4ade7152333ea11effa84c8b073bd.text: The system fixed a broken link between two internal parts of the application. This change ensures that the feature for saving and restoring project states works correctly. Users will not see any visual changes, but the application will no longer fail when trying to load these saved states.

cedba23a052dd10e0e19fd0f5b47196058dcf7f2.text: The system no longer stops working when it encounters a malformed document with missing closing tags. Instead of showing an error message, it simply skips the broken part and continues processing the rest of the file. This change applies to the underlying document reader, affecting how the application handles imperfect data sources.

b326939d5dfc96ed494f512ac658b599419558c8.text: The internal software that connects the system to the AI assistant was updated to a newer version. This change is small and happens behind the scenes, so regular users will not notice any difference in how the application looks or behaves.

21d3f66edd767c5f133c3588a7cad3d54a1db71c.text: The program now closes the connection to the server immediately after you run a command in the terminal. This stops the interface from freezing while waiting for extra billing information that never arrives. You will notice the screen updates right away instead of hanging.

ce9cdad782114777416dec58fec2c630e10c63cb.text: A small internal update opened a door for the testing team to check the system's file-saving features. This change does not affect what you see or do in the app today. It only helps the team ensure that the automatic saving tools work correctly behind the scenes.

e85fe3406786b7454267a242f53f135e123320cc.text: The system now blocks access to saved history lists and details if the project exceeds a size limit. Users of large projects will see a red warning message instead of their previous snapshots. This change is active immediately.

506a760c80c202983ffb04369b60357e0794277d.text: The internal evaluation system now displays the text prompt in blue before running it. This change affects only the tools used by the team to test the software. Team members will see the prompt printed on their screen during these tests.

e2b522b7208e4b6c6c3edd96f207458b77ef1340.text: A minor internal adjustment stopped the software from automatically gathering specific background processing files during its final assembly stage. This change affects the tools used by the development team to prepare the application for release. You would not notice any difference in how the application looks or behaves, as this step was part of the behind-the-scenes packaging process.

bab2c967f0275c15aab8f0dfb476946ded10622b.text: Internal staff who use the assistant will see clearer guidance on how to ask it to manage tasks and edit files. The assistant now knows exactly which instructions are for it versus which are for the user, and examples use generic placeholders instead of specific file paths. This is a minor internal update that improves how the assistant understands requests.

dee1d9d695f79ccd242c5c4ff41c689d55617980.text: The welcome message now says 'today' and adds a pie emoji. This only affects the internal menu screen. The text is live immediately.

96f5c6445925ccc27f73748b4a84071f761b5408.text: The tool now checks if your project files have changed before saving a backup. If nothing changed, it skips the save to save time and space. You might notice fewer backup messages when you make no edits.

9d5722474c27c94d9313d9e1cc988eea6cb2e8b9.text: The app now stops calculating credit usage until a request finishes, preventing errors if multiple actions happen at once. This small internal fix ensures the credit count shown to you remains accurate.

b3f32169ae9264c8ccbe6bd9a83f3a08ce89851c.text: When the assistant fails to generate any text, the system now silently stops the conversation instead of falsely claiming it will continue. This prevents the assistant from making up responses when it has nothing to say. This is a small, internal fix affecting all interactions where the assistant returns an empty result.

2115c454a75d328426b5f55ab4c506158f1fb038.text: The program's internal file-reading helper moved to a new folder and got a shorter name. This is a small housekeeping change for the development team. Regular users will see no difference in how the app works.

e9639036290d93a64a5175e97fe64ba9a33128e9.text: Programmers cleaned up how the app stores its undo history, making the code easier to maintain. They also fixed a small check that verifies if a specific background tool is installed, making it work more reliably on some computers. This change affects only the internal structure and does not change how the app looks or behaves for anyone using it.

b49ef8c09b8a8caf7ce6260663feb99bc9309b75.text: A small internal fix makes the screen-clearing command work correctly in the terminal. Users who type this command will now see the screen wipe clean as expected, instead of nothing happening.

ec76265ba536b400093d8604cf490320bf93f134.text: The tool now checks if it can undo a change before trying. If undoing is not possible, it shows a clear message instead of crashing. This helps people using the command-line version who work on large projects or have no saved steps to revert.

611b9448bf98d8633cc052c38cb854d9b619a4d0.text: The assistant now only asks clarifying questions when a request is truly unclear and blocks progress, instead of stopping for any minor ambiguity. This change affects internal prompt logic and is live today. You might notice fewer interruptions when asking for work that has slight uncertainties but is generally understandable.

d8d5a78690544df7d7938e15051b2424dd7697ba.text: When the assistant fails to answer, it now sends a clear stop signal instead of leaving the chat waiting forever. This stops the screen from getting stuck after a backend error.

c968bf257b1ed8227b8d2786a74328603baa89ce.text: The assistant now stops asking clarifying questions if you tell it not to. Instead of waiting for answers, it picks the most likely interpretation and starts working immediately. This change is live for all internal users.

88ec7b61f05a05eecfeabac08947cb84dae352cb.text: The app now draws task lists with less empty space between lines. This affects people using the internal tool, who will see a cleaner layout for new and updated tasks.

3e2d18332a103aace9036d8923d1a2ad3aaee44b.text: The app switched back to an older version of the main AI assistant for everyday tasks. This change affects how the assistant handles very long requests, limiting the amount of text it can process at once. You might notice the assistant stops mid-sentence or fails to answer if you ask for extremely detailed or lengthy outputs.

53f26c8f9b9b944cc021da415b66e021ea1ece55.text: A new safety check was added to the file editing tool. If the first AI model returns an incomplete or messy edit, the system now automatically tries a second, more reliable model to fix it. This happens silently in the background, so users will just see a completed edit instead of a broken one.

2393f9729496218177d700f1e3d32bccee607071.text: The tool now stops saving project snapshots if the folder contains more than 10,000 files to prevent slowdowns. Large projects will no longer show checkpoint numbers in the command line prompt or display a confirmation message after saving, while smaller projects remain unaffected.

0cbf99e28ed75d9c0eecb31c6319d33ff19870d3.text: The tool now prepares its backup system in the background instead of making you wait when starting up. This speeds up the initial launch for everyone using the command line interface. You might notice the program opens slightly faster, with no change to how you save or restore your work.

2032de0401b67206e72b694b335701d590255017.text: The tool now saves and restores only the specific files you are working on, instead of scanning your entire project folder. This change improves performance and prevents accidental errors in large projects. You will not notice any immediate difference in how the tool works, but it will run faster and more reliably when handling many files.

c572c558d4584221037e713d11d7326e25eac068.text: The software now uses its built-in internet access tools instead of separate helper programs. This change only affects people running the software on their own computers, as it requires a newer version of the underlying platform. They might notice faster startup times or fewer installation errors, but the software's visible behavior remains identical.

e059a365a97c2c83494f003220a5bff01981b69b.text: The internal assistant now follows stricter rules when it encounters unclear instructions. Instead of guessing, it must ask three specific numbered questions to resolve the ambiguity before proceeding. This change applies only to the internal system's guidance logic, so external users will not see any immediate difference in their experience.

94e958b02fbd94d469effe3f9e162e05b0923025.text: The backup system now checks if a standard file-tracking tool is installed on your computer and uses it when available. If that tool is missing, it automatically falls back to a built-in alternative. This change is internal and affects how backups are saved and restored, but you will not see a difference in the interface.

6957d13cde567601b629dfd248805c8e55c6a575.text: The checkpoint system now checks file status before starting the saving work, skipping files that do not need changes. This is an internal cleanup for the core system, so it affects no one directly. If you looked, you would see the same checkpoint saving as before, just with slightly less wasted effort behind the scenes.

d7f34b1299c747691f12a7fb61bad2590eef3837.text: The system now correctly identifies which files have changed, ensuring it only saves the actual updates instead of ignoring them or saving everything every time. This internal fix prevents unnecessary data duplication and keeps the project's history clean. You will not notice any immediate changes, as this improves how the tool manages your work in the background.

9576da521188efd8acda60f8f23249cd4ea07b08.text: The monthly allowance for free accounts dropped from 1,000 to 500 credits. This change is live now. Free users will hit their usage limit sooner than before.

8bfded24eee0b8ed1b429b1e4f24a035671f3f6f.text: A small internal housekeeping change added a rule to the project's ignore list. This rule stops the system from saving a specific type of temporary index file into the main record. Programmers won't see a difference in how the software works, but they will notice fewer cluttered files when they review changes.

c232fa69ae6915eceb5eb51f2068289a73b577e4.text: A background tool for connecting to external services was removed from the main list of required software. This change affects only the internal setup of the application. Regular users will notice no difference, as the tool was no longer being used.

4e3aa180766ffa110e797589ec6fdc67120a3180.text: When the AI takes too long to write a plan, the system now stops waiting after a few minutes and tries again without asking for deep thinking. This prevents the tool from hanging indefinitely on slow requests. Normal users might notice slightly faster responses when the AI struggles, though the change is mostly internal safety.

f89235c667f73c57879eb7f11bb9ddc554ac7621.text: The assistant now stops writing automatic plans for difficult tasks. It only creates a plan when you explicitly ask for one. This change applies to internal tools and is live now.

5030044b940e33aa84b5e510ba01846c09f16fb2.text: The system now accepts edit instructions that lack a final blank line. Previously, missing that line caused the change to fail silently. This internal fix applies to all code editing tasks. You will notice fewer failed updates when the assistant edits files.

6bdbe7cc634f42bdf373b6b989981a5ed92dbc19.text: The assistant no longer stops working after six steps. It now keeps going until the task is finished or you tell it to stop. This change affects internal tools and is live today.

b30e9adbe737fae97ff0543c45e8bca53405d4ee.text: The assistant now spends less time planning its answer, saving cost and speed. This applies to all requests. You might see slightly simpler plans, but usually no visible difference.

882b2ece9292ce528ac86e9a07933c8851c75e38.text: A small internal fix improves how the system recognizes failed commands in Linux environments. Previously, the system missed errors when the failed command name was enclosed in quotes, leading to incorrect handling. This update ensures those specific error messages are now properly detected.

548294cc51ff8fded56487e1f26dea5dd964decf.text: The login screen for the internal command-line tool now shows a single 'Press ENTER' prompt instead of a long instruction with a link. The web address only appears if the browser fails to open automatically after pressing the key. This small change affects only people using that specific internal tool.

9e69b7cbaab90ee30f6162a6874268c780c972f3.text: The system now allows the text assistant to write longer replies when using its most capable model, while keeping shorter limits for other models. This small internal adjustment means the assistant can handle more complex or lengthy requests without cutting off its answer prematurely.

5fe5052faa014781fa8c3ec5e71b856e0807b9d7.text: The system now allows more attempts to finish a long response before stopping. It also checks if a response has actual text before trying to continue; if the response is blank or just spaces, it stops trying to continue. This helps ensure that long or empty answers are handled more reliably without getting stuck.

5c737b023f7f8de544b08688650ebd2935b45afc.text: A small internal update lets people using the command-line tool run system commands by typing an exclamation mark before the command, like "!ls". This replaces the older method of typing "/run" first. The change is live today and only affects those using the command-line interface, not the web or mobile apps.

327451aba62289d4477402b928c639976a9de307.text: The command-line tool now checks if you have a paid subscription before displaying a 'usage limit exceeded' warning. This means paying customers will no longer see this message, even if they go over their limit. The fix is live for users running the updated version of the tool.

2abae689244d1ca1268143bc4f1113c7e7ff9314.text: The system now stops waiting for extra data once a response is complete. This prevents a long pause before the next step begins. You will notice the assistant moves faster after it finishes speaking.

4685a02af64bf05c8ec4ab4e55cafadbc77d6b7e.text: The system now matches file requests to responses using a unique request ID, ignoring the file names in the response. This prevents the system from mixing up requests if multiple people ask for files at the same time. This change is live and affects how the assistant retrieves files, ensuring it gets the correct content for the right request.

71cd514a6bf55bfd952227c413b70af32d0b2b87.text: The setup guide for running the software on your own computer now lists three separate commands instead of one automatic script. You must open three windows and type one command in each, with the second step requiring a specific background service to be installed. This change is live in the guide but does not affect the software's behavior.

bdb7458a47eb23c5756827ab0b60724ef678ad7f.text: The software now displays a blue warning message when a user's monthly usage reaches its limit. This notice tells the user to upgrade their plan and provides a direct link to the pricing page. The change affects all users who hit their usage cap, making it clear how to continue using the service.

39fdaef5146797690e94d31d91d689d043586b7a.text: The AI assistant was given new instructions to avoid creating empty files using basic system commands. Instead, it must use its specific file-writing tool to generate new files with content. This is an internal update affecting how the AI behaves when asked to create files.

9008c4d39db3d0ebcf75bd8c6722ef50a5ea176c.text: The default version of the mid-tier AI model was updated to the latest release. This change applies to all users of the application. You would notice the assistant using a newer, potentially smarter model without any changes to your settings.

14a9f09003f8dffae273f44210b285f08e2204ab.text: The limit for processing large documents has been raised. This change is live now. If you upload a file that is bigger than the old limit but smaller than the new one, it will now be handled normally instead of triggering a fallback error.

764fc5c039fef63f34a8a17cd5b996d76001b4a2.text: The assistant's limit for how much text it can generate in one response was increased. This affects internal systems using the Claude service. Users might notice longer, more complete answers without the assistant stopping early.

94955aa10e7943431bcc0d69dc97f2a8e00b4939.text: The website's main page now displays the exact command needed to install the tool, replacing a generic button. Visitors can click a copy icon to place the command on their clipboard, and the surrounding text and spacing were adjusted to fit this new layout. This change is live today.

f0fbce126c1c63b0e2aaa83c3d763e4979267a01.text: The help pages were updated to list the newer, smarter AI model used for coding tasks. This change affects only the website's documentation, so nothing in the actual software behaves differently today.

27859dbc15c578992c5d5467da16768643511400.text: The internal system now adds a specific tag to the start of its responses. This tag tells the assistant to skip re-reading certain files in the next step, saving time. This is a small background fix for the team building the tool, so regular users will not see any visible change or notice a difference.

d39b95b614a7379d6bc1132117d05359fe3a3190.text: The sign-in process now checks a unique code to ensure only the correct login attempt succeeds, preventing mismatched or stale attempts from going through. This internal cleanup improves security for people using the command-line tool, but you will not see any visual changes in the app.

3fb4a9afc114cd3304f791c5c38413897a8ecacd.text: The service that applies suggested code edits now connects to a new address. This internal update fixes routing for the code application feature. Users will not notice any changes.

4ffb037d93470a988ea46da3a8c584ce267f9d2a.text: The system now uses a different AI model for planning complex code changes, specifically one that can 'think' longer before answering. This is an internal change that affects how the tool prepares to edit your code, but you will not see any visual difference or new buttons.

02261d21f962896ced32422b26d0a11047499ab3.text: The system now attaches a unique reference number to every file request and its matching reply. This helps the software correctly match responses to the right requests, especially when many files are being fetched at once. Regular users will not notice any visual change, but the file loading process becomes more reliable and less prone to mix-ups.

9d0f409a24799ca79d762b467c9c76164b1554a2.text: A small internal update fixes a typo in the instructions given to the AI assistant, ensuring it correctly identifies file locations when making edits. The update also clarifies security rules, explicitly telling the assistant to treat files outside the current project folder as read-only. This helps prevent accidental changes to system files or other projects.

b50498d1fbab70b90d64ac90b129defe4be4e7bf.text: The AI assistant now asks two or three follow-up questions to confirm what you want before starting work, rather than just giving a brief summary of its plan. This helps catch misunderstandings early, especially for non-technical users who might not spot errors in a summary. The change is live today.

1e13e67b1811c1710a91de58aca0a7523583baa5.text: The system now asks a different service for help applying code changes. This new service is faster. Users will not see any change in the interface.

ef4e8ece4482dde9ad6378626b73590f97347ed6.text: The command-line tool now blocks a new sign-in attempt if someone is already logged in, forcing them to sign out first. This prevents the software from automatically kicking out an active session during a login, so switching accounts requires a deliberate step. This change is live and affects anyone using the command-line interface.

12d5f25d0111002f64df3eb156d444611bf53964.text: The AI assistant's deep thinking feature now uses your most recent message directly, rather than trying to generate its own instructions. This internal update ensures the AI focuses on exactly what you just asked for. You might notice slightly more accurate results when asking for complex changes, but there are no visible interface changes.

77b6e0be4e1d2db45fd1b929799567eef24e3665.text: Previously, the system would show leftover text if a message ended without a closing signal. Now, it hides that text and properly ends the message. This affects internal tools and ensures cleaner output.

cec67e5dbc17bdd9cbc4366ad6bb8450794458ab.text: The system now automatically saves chat history with the Gemini assistant, even if it previously skipped saving due to missing identifiers. This ensures that past conversations remain accessible for internal review and continuity.

7533053de393b8c4404cfebc14e77098a6238f06.text: The assistant's instructions were updated to clarify that web scraping returns simplified text. This change affects only the internal guidance for the tool, not the tool itself. You would not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves.

2db8a6e8e13c959209fc60c8d2836510489d4a70.text: The AI assistant can no longer type text into web forms or click buttons. It can only view pages, scroll, and take screenshots to help fix design issues or errors. This change applies immediately to anyone using the assistant to work on a website.

bc0ed49b14838d3547f300bfc915583ba3a54843.text: The assistant now limits its use of the command-line tool, preferring to display commands as text instead of running them. It strictly forbids installing software packages or editing files via the terminal, reserving those actions for safer methods. This change applies to all users interacting with the coding assistant.

f5f53a911b5b8799f8d31b0663d0520bed7e3bab.text: The system previously rejected new text files if they contained incomplete editing instructions. It now accepts these files, allowing the assistant to save partial drafts instead of stopping the process. This change is live for internal tools and removes an error message that appeared when creating unfinished documents.

10860243e7e5e9a8ae76abeb4881fba8d0040bae.text: The assistant now asks for your approval before installing new software components, unless you are working in a small, new project. It also lists both Mac/Linux and Windows commands for moving or deleting files. You will see a pop-up asking permission before the assistant tries to add packages to your project.

66cde57607533bd581f6a3812f4366da5fbd608b.text: A small internal fix corrected how the system saves the full text of a response while it is being generated, ensuring the complete message is stored properly instead of being lost. This change affects only the background service that handles AI conversations and is live today. End users will not notice any difference, as the visible responses remain the same.

0f817e0f7f1c77d213eac09ecf310f3c85ca26f3.text: The help guide describing which artificial intelligence tools the system uses was updated to match current settings. Readers looking at the documentation will see that the file-finding and deep-thinking steps now use different tools, and that the cost-saving mode now uses a cheaper editing tool than before. This is a small internal update and does not change how the software works.

70879af86afc2f3102abe28bf7e129f4da1abfa8.text: The system now sends its requests to the Google AI service through a separate tracking company. This change is internal and affects only the company's own staff. No customer will notice any difference in how the product works.

6669d9c32c1fbef0c97133ced12918192559d3a8.text: The assistant now reads more background files when it starts with very little information. This helps it understand requests better by gathering more context automatically. Users will notice fewer missed details when asking complex questions from a blank slate.

92a6fce7754249f14b90d44ba1abc67826681b26.text: The system now stops waiting if the text generation service takes too long, giving up after 30 seconds for fast models and 200 seconds for others. This prevents the internal tool from hanging indefinitely when the service is slow. It is active immediately for the backend team.

81808634a99bc94ba34d26708f5fdad100e0bc77.text: The system now uses a backup service to rewrite code files if the main service fails. This change is live. You would notice fewer errors when the primary service is down, as the system automatically tries a different method to complete your request.

396be03305477f51b63cb82c3276205c888f1ffc.text: The assistant renamed its internal 'planning' button to 'think deeply' to better describe its function. This change affects how the assistant decides whether to write out a step-by-step plan or make changes directly. Users will not notice any visible difference in the interface, but the assistant may choose between these two actions more accurately based on recent conversation context.

2b89eaf3032fbe4402ffdaab010e77bb66af42e2.text: The system now remembers only the last 1000 text measurements instead of 5000. This saves memory. Staff might see slightly slower speed if they check the same long texts repeatedly, but usually no one notices.

b182a9488e677e052869ec65e18e12195dbd2138.text: A small internal fix stopped the program from adding extra text to commands sent to Windows computers. This extra text caused errors on Windows because it used the wrong language for that system. Windows users who run commands through the terminal should now see the commands work without those errors, while Mac and Linux users see no change.

8768274d32f7b4809798f29d59f2e62d713e9ca6.text: The system now automatically switches to a backup AI model if the primary one fails to identify relevant files during planning. This change affects internal planning processes, ensuring reliability without user intervention. Users will not notice any difference unless the primary model experiences an outage, at which point the backup seamlessly takes over.

82302959c27344c2e8e96498412977ae623fef83.text: The internal assistant now follows a stricter rule to delete old, unused code and add missing links after making changes. This affects the automated coding tool, not end users. You would not notice any change in your daily work.

3b40ec8dc13a9f2a431de8c1646a3220ba18f8a7.text: A small internal update cleaned up how the software's parts are labeled and checked for errors. This change affects only the team building the application, not the people using it. Regular users will notice no difference.

ea6f908232f1e252fa8a46a3535651ee8eceb46f.text: A small internal change removed one instruction from the assistant’s guidance. It affects only the assistant’s behavior, not a customer feature. If someone looked at that guidance, they would see it no longer tells the assistant to consider running helper commands or to warn about effects that cannot be undone. The change is live today.

0694f950f64c8ec6d86790444db73d20804667c8.text: The system now records the number of tokens used for saving and reading cached data when interacting with the AI assistant. This ensures that internal billing and cost tracking are accurate. Regular users will not notice any changes in the application's behavior or interface.

55af42d53d0de581bbcb5456c5804379fecb5cd9.text: The help page now says that typing two spaces in a row creates a new line. This affects people reading the instructions for the terminal area. They will see a new tip explaining how to write multi-line prompts.

25f40133635d3022b5d581ea2a5420dbbdae0078.text: The help guide now includes a new section on how to give the coding assistant extra background by pasting web links or adding them to a specific file. This means the assistant can automatically read those online pages to understand your project better. This is a small update to the written instructions, so no new buttons or features appeared in the software itself.

8cbdc73347e85d668d33b7ff5b3499f292624563.text: The team reorganized the code that connects to the AI services to make it cleaner and more consistent. This internal cleanup affects only the developers maintaining the system; customers will notice no changes in the application's behavior.

c6f640b3b82e52cf9e9483c3f4e8784277a271d1.text: The website slightly widened the space reserved for the main video on the homepage. This is a small internal visual adjustment that is live today. A visitor would barely notice, except the video now fits its box a bit more snugly.

93b68969ecc063e461b8a9625a1a3c72ed1b7372.text: The online help pages now show clearer menus and easier-to-read text boxes. Visitors will notice the page looks tidier, and the button to copy code examples works better for people using keyboards or screen readers. This update is active now.

bcac47d1913b1d6e361e0336c8b77d962f1609a9.text: The system now gives the AI different instructions for listing files depending on whether it is searching or editing code. This internal update helps the AI understand that the file list might be outdated during editing tasks. Users will not see any visual changes, but the AI may make fewer mistakes when working with new files.

e2f1b4bdc73fddeafd3c9863c5cbf451805df367.text: The homepage video player now keeps its shape exactly, so it no longer jumps or shifts position as the page loads. This change affects the main landing page for all visitors. You will notice the video stays fixed in its box instead of moving around, making the page look steadier.

6027349d0085a934a6355db88872264da52a4a48.text: The system now ignores empty or broken file links instead of marking them with special text labels. This keeps the AI's planning notes cleaner by automatically skipping files that are too large or failed to load. Users will not see any visible change, but the assistant may make slightly better decisions when choosing which files to read.

4dc4b2495dc8de7815333dd1c0fe5250f726fbc6.text: The assistant now automatically takes a picture of the web page after visiting it, so it can see what loaded instead of just guessing. It also shows a spinning circle while working on web tasks to indicate progress. These changes affect anyone using the browser tool, making its actions more reliable and visible.

776b4284c2efaec40b4b0716b8199f67a50c3239.text: The tool's internal planning engine now uses a different AI model to select relevant files. It can also process larger amounts of text during this step. This change is live for internal operations, but users will not see any visual differences in the interface.

8640d37bda0e87cd0f486964d44622cd61462d68.text: The assistant can now show you a command to run yourself instead of running it for you. This applies when a command is too long to run safely or when you just need the text. You will see the command in a copyable box.

fdd41f4a93a9b5cafd3f4df7e6bb16701a79563f.text: The planning tool now uses the same file-editing process as the main assistant, removing a duplicate version. This change is internal and affects how the system handles complex planning requests. No visible difference for end-users.

c6c8f1edfa697fe0bbcf87b13e6b76f6a41f84d9.text: The system now waits for all incoming data to finish arriving before it stops processing, rather than stopping early once a completion signal is received. This change is internal and affects the backend logic that handles assistant responses. A non-programmer would not notice any visible difference in the interface, but the system is less likely to cut off long responses prematurely.

402caa5317de72e99b6c5d46b981da66b3caecc8.text: A small internal fix stops the loading animation from flickering off and on while text streams into the terminal. This affects only people running the command-line tool. They will see a smoother visual experience, with the spinner staying steady or disappearing cleanly once the text finishes printing, rather than restarting repeatedly.

4374a203a950e2a34bda96f526466b4a6296ed0c.text: The AI assistant now stops talking immediately after successfully running a command and finishing a task, instead of waiting for further instructions. This change affects internal tools and is already active. A person might notice the assistant gives shorter, more direct responses without unnecessary pauses.

62928301ba1f53a4470c0ea84e9d250f58429662.text: The AI assistant now chooses more carefully whether to open new files when answering requests. Previously, it was told to guess 'yes' if unsure, so it often opened extra files unnecessarily. This change removes that bias, making the assistant skip opening files when it already has enough information. Internal tooling adjustment; no visible change for end users.

1713f2f42d4bcda6dc812844f4c096409206e6eb.text: The assistant now checks for better answers instead of just new questions. This internal update means it is more likely to look up extra information when needed. The change is live, but users will only notice slightly more thorough responses.

b3ac409ed586259c2d576691baeb1235055941df.text: The assistant now follows stricter rules to avoid making unwanted changes to files when you only ask for explanations or reviews. Instead of automatically trying to improve your code, it will simply summarize its actions or answer your questions. This update is live and affects all conversations, making the assistant more predictable and less likely to edit files without permission.

2bb9bff2a728b4e55598108634696ea8704ed805.text: The system now gives stricter instructions to the AI assistant when it tries to edit large files. This helps the assistant find the exact spot to change by avoiding mistakes with spaces and quote marks. Internal staff might see fewer failed edit attempts, though the change is minor and does not affect how the software looks or works for outside customers.

ff2c47c2c6e1666504b78554c33399555befe2f9.text: The system now records a fixed cost for every request made to the code-editing assistant. Previously, these requests were logged without any cost data. This change affects internal billing records for this specific service, ensuring accurate tracking of usage expenses.

1540281574940d0588fe14e9a41c5eda43ab2ba3.text: A small internal update prevents the system from accidentally including specific 'knowledge' files in its random selection of examples. This ensures the AI assistant receives a cleaner set of context, avoiding confusion or repetition. Users might notice slightly more relevant examples being used, though the change is subtle and mostly affects how the system prepares information behind the scenes.

b74bdd12b707706762d3fc523efc4ae3ea45af57.text: The system now uses a different, cheaper AI model to automatically fix failed file edits, replacing the previous method that switched models based on cost settings. This internal backend change affects the reliability of automated code updates, though end users will not see any immediate visual changes in the interface.

f4c4c51543faf23224585686cb4a6436e451f764.text: The system now asks a different, more reliable service for help when looking for files. If that first service fails, it tries a standard backup, and only uses a final alternative if both fail. This change is live today and helps ensure file requests succeed without the user needing to retry.

0a63280ece8d0607d41cf98bbfec901e432d812e.text: The small spinning animation that appeared while the system worked on a task has been removed. Internal tools no longer show this visual cue. The underlying processing speed and results remain unchanged.

8a44dd81d72202066687a33e09bf23b58c87e7ac.text: The system now switches to a backup assistant if the first one fails to read files. This internal reliability fix is live for everyone. You would only notice it during a rare outage, where the process continues instead of stopping. Test files are no longer hidden from the search.

593fac4cd7025d938086a69315aff780815cf17d.text: The system now tries a faster search service first when finding files, only switching to a slower backup if the first one fails. This change is live and affects internal file-finding operations. A user might notice slightly quicker results when searching for files.

97d0c0e85151118dd07d01ab7babac07ce16f72f.text: The website no longer shows the small box asking you to accept or decline cookies when you first visit. The step that used to decide whether to display it was disabled. Visitors will not see that pop-up. This is a small internal change and is active now.

d95d6054d95c7fca3206b03275858f7394437aee.text: The team removed a separate helper program that used to clear a specific network slot before starting the backend. Now, the system uses built-in computer commands to free that slot automatically. Developers starting the backend locally might see slightly faster setup times, though the daily experience looks exactly the same.

491594474c6bdedb64040e1656e687b7586a5b03.text: The system's internal method for creating unique identifiers for messages was consolidated into a shared utility. This change is purely for code organization and does not affect how the application looks or behaves for users. You will notice no difference in message delivery or appearance.

2ca353455a6a76e88fd67336af97e4b96b222a68.text: The system now uses a new, cheaper artificial intelligence model to find relevant files for your requests. This change is active today. You might notice slightly faster responses when the system searches for files to edit.

caf14641c6d23645bdc31ad7a74a7f61da41f253.text: The system now checks if it needs to look at more files by asking a different, faster AI model first. If that model fails, it automatically switches to a backup model to ensure the request still gets processed. This internal update improves reliability and speed, so users might notice the assistant responding slightly faster without any change to how they interact with it.

1948b7c48205a73c5fb27e6a2136f72b161877e0.text: The assistant now strongly prefers to replace only specific parts of a file rather than rewriting the whole thing. This makes its edits shorter and clearer. You might notice it asks for less confirmation or makes smaller, more precise changes when updating text.

02ea49d99afda03ad99d5a9206fbbf34dcecae3b.text: The AI assistant received clearer instructions on how to control web browsers, requiring it to use a specific text format for commands. This internal update ensures the assistant stops trying to use incorrect formats when navigating or typing on pages. The change is live immediately for all internal agent operations.

4dd2635751db0e307420be6b741cadeff72ca549.text: The system now automatically detects when an AI assistant forgets to mark the unchanged parts of a file during an edit, triggering a quick correction that re-adds the missing context. This ensures edits are accurate and complete, preventing broken files. The fix is active immediately for all internal backend processing.

4cd218eb007183350c84760e9077cff2e34b296e.text: The system now uses a shorter, faster label to track each editing request. This change is internal and affects only the service's own bookkeeping. A customer would notice nothing.

bd0104d370f19b44533cfa87868c40f5d8739ba8.text: A small internal fix corrected a rare glitch where file-editing messages could get invalid ID numbers. This only affects the backend system that processes those edits. Regular users will not notice any change in the app's appearance or behavior.

bc3e00b4d36f645ab6596594973dd37892f54fad.text: The AI assistant now saves memory updates by rewriting the entire note instead of using a specific search-and-replace method. This change is internal and live, affecting how the system stores information behind the scenes. You will not notice any difference in your daily use.

296fb315222e37ee7371b9d72d30b2b91ae48237.text: A small internal fix ensures the planning step correctly receives the original user request. This prevents a technical error that could have caused the assistant to fail when processing file updates. No visible changes for users; the system now handles the request data more reliably behind the scenes.

128d19903a01ee58337e23e0a6f6fc5a0ff318d0.text: The AI assistant now applies file edits instantly and can self-correct if an edit fails, rather than waiting for user confirmation. It also stops mentioning internal system instructions in its responses to keep conversations cleaner. These changes affect the AI's editing workflow and output style.

824a97c16f7ad7b181d6c2ce7e4e771eedc9162a.text: The system now attaches a unique tracking number and the user's original text to requests sent to the code-editing service. This change is live but only helps the internal team track and debug issues. Normal users will not see any difference.

2eeafb528346e4bd3a89b210b6a7652727dcacdb.text: The assistant's internal instructions were tweaked to stop it from repeatedly asking for a new plan after finishing work. This small backend fix prevents the AI from getting stuck in a loop during complex tasks. Users will notice fewer instances where the assistant stalls or repeats itself unnecessarily.

e059aaa20a4005fd799df4277357452b7d61ff66.text: The help guide for fixing connection problems is shorter. It now tells people to just check their internet, then log out and back in, instead of running a separate status check first. The guide also notes that while paid members get answered first, everyone else should expect a reply within a week.

07bf5aa64eae87a42088c706854e16d468379bb2.text: The internal tool now automatically captures a picture of the web page whenever it opens a new site. Staff using this tool will see the image appear without needing to ask for it separately. A small visual update also made the top banner on the web interface shorter and the text larger.

e7d7d25cc8e1bb270a8d46316b6c6ee967182cd2.text: The assistant now strictly requires you to manually start any local web servers before it can inspect them. It also received clearer instructions on how to format its internal requests to the browser tools. This change applies immediately to all internal users.

0c7cbe8e92e59caf330c937d089b0c73aa0008ad.text: The system now limits the amount of text it reads when planning changes to prevent errors. Broken or overly large files are ignored, and the total text size is capped at 140,000 units. This change is live and helps the assistant focus on relevant code without getting stuck on unreadable parts.

310c04f72b9540cf7ba4712207207c7a875f0e07.text: The tool now gives clear error messages instead of crashing when browser commands are formatted incorrectly. This internal fix helps the system recover smoothly from bad instructions, though end users will not see any direct change.

697619cc9c67d01e53fb768d202f52f6466cfd7d.text: The AI assistant can now see your project's folder structure again. This helps it understand where files are located to answer questions more accurately. The amount of folder information shown is limited to save space, with stricter limits for lighter plans. This update is live for all users.

5eab73b6f997945b3b8a8bb060a5fc1e34958fa5.text: A small internal safety check was added to prevent errors when the system tries to read a missing or empty file location. This change does not add new features or change how the application looks or behaves for anyone. It simply ensures that if a broken link is encountered, the system handles it gracefully instead of crashing.

9e21191a3b09258068cc151f1a3ef1f8944a06aa.text: The troubleshooting guide moved from the general help section to the advanced section. Readers looking for this guide in the main help area will not find it there anymore. This change is live today.

08a4e3eb7255aec4c3d6a6e054708e7890cd758b.text: The system now automatically adds the correct web address prefix when it is missing. This prevents errors when the assistant tries to visit a website that was listed without the full address. You will notice fewer failed attempts to load web pages.

5583b8a276f342d7fc3d9ac200e52ca7a5f897c9.text: The blue top banner now looks correct on mobile phones. Previously, the text and icon could get squished or cut off on smaller screens. Now, the layout adjusts automatically so the message stays readable and properly spaced on any device.

e4895637047fb9f8dcb6b78e8caf8ed578f4100b.text: A small internal update changes how the web browsing tool reacts when a page action fails. Previously, the tool tried to recover by restarting the browser automatically. Now, it stops immediately and reports the error. This affects the automated browsing features, making failures more visible rather than attempting silent recovery.

60bf2430b1376d6a41ce65b65068580e9b361510.text: The AI assistant stopped receiving a list of the project's files in its background instructions. This internal change saves processing space and reduces costs for the engineering team. Users will not notice any difference in how the assistant works.

6f966d91be4cdc45dacb1bff6d82a8c25c022f28.text: The system now checks the speed of trimming long file lists more strictly, flagging anything taking over 100 milliseconds instead of 300. This change is internal and live, helping developers spot performance issues earlier. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves.

db4428789d250fcc5306448278c76cd6c840d597.text: A safety switch was added to the system that trims large lists of files to fit within a size limit. This prevents the software from getting stuck in a loop if it cannot make progress. The change is internal and affects only the backend team's monitoring, so customers will not notice any difference.

c489f830d43b132f01281dd53e0ab72b8f6f3702.text: The system now guesses how many files to remove from a large list to fit a size limit, instead of checking each file one by one. This speeds up the process for internal tools handling big projects. Users won't notice a difference, but the software works faster behind the scenes.

b5c52c7eb19a457c5f45b98c9c9c70a105955b8c.text: The system now stops sending duplicate status messages to the browser when it checks if a user is logged in. This change is live and affects how the login screen appears during startup. A person might see fewer confusing pop-ups or loading indicators before the login page fully opens.

3ca6b55ace5ede8cf3f1a41e5015703262facf2d.text: The system now records how long it takes to prepare instructions for two different assistant modes. This change is internal and affects only the engineering team's monitoring tools. Regular users will not notice any difference in their experience or the assistant's behavior.

4368a1be6570f488ca878e48b010b24e9145d0ef.text: Internal change: the planning tool now reads the entire conversation history before answering new requests. Previously, it only saw the latest instruction. This helps it understand context in long chats.

9ede9cd45c61f6a1eb816f77cb2cce008aec2574.text: The software now skips creating an extra, unnecessary folder when it finishes building the app. This internal cleanup affects only the development process, not the features you see or use. You will notice no change in how the app behaves or looks.

bc997875003b3b3b68eb16f8b0cf7b71ca97f91d.text: The assistant now updates its internal memory files without writing explanations about why it made those changes. This applies only when the assistant learns new information that cannot be found by reading the code alone. Users will see cleaner responses because the assistant stops adding unnecessary notes about its file updates.

c1a6261cf3828b9ede5029cb129403035755c4af.text: Fixed a typo in the tool's command name. Only affects new installs. No visible change for existing users.

e509ba2aca5614762173531ddb6cdc06a8811d25.text: This small internal update speeds up how the system decides which file details to keep when space runs tight. It changes the pruning method from removing one item at a time to removing groups of low-priority items all at once. You will not notice any difference in your work, but the system may respond slightly faster when handling large amounts of data.

49c035e7ff9f11a5874099b6391ff2156a17408c.text: The AI now shows a clearer picture of your project files when the list is too long. Instead of suddenly hiding everything, it gradually removes less important details like file sizes or deep folders to fit the space. This helps the AI understand your code structure better, so it can give you more accurate help.

444163bb826361a61851ee8a3ad30109d98c0ca4.text: A small internal fix stops commands that produce no visible output from getting stuck. Previously, silent tasks would hang the system until a timeout occurred. Now, the system always confirms completion or failure immediately after the task finishes.

a754368804d5909f4b9b52fafbbe3c5c26228d83.text: The assistant now reserves a fixed amount of space in its memory for viewing project files, rather than calculating it dynamically. This allows it to see more files at once in standard mode, while reducing the space available for search results. The change is active immediately for all internal agent interactions.

66ee89f3bf9e919512c71bfd9c77c523556375b6.text: The system now counts text for the Anthropic model less optimistically, applying a safety margin to prevent messages from becoming too long and failing. It also trims empty folders from the file list sent to the assistant to save space. These changes affect users interacting with the Anthropic-based assistant, making it more reliable when handling large projects.

0c5ab268c64244b8fb2f0566438ed23461136b32.text: The team updated the internal setup so that small utility tools now check their work against the latest version of the main system. This affects only the tools used by the team, not the product you see. You will notice no change, but the team can now catch errors in these helper tools earlier.

9cf3bfbcac4396e5329c43788753a9ad73f98f26.text: The team updated the internal tool that connects the system to the AI service. This change is small and happens behind the scenes, so customers will not notice any difference in how the product works. It ensures the system uses the latest version of the AI connection for better stability.

107cb74b7a12f53e82ef48b7ff94a83f2a15bae1.text: The command-line tool now reminds you to type 'undo' to revert changes, alongside the existing 'diff' prompt. This affects only internal command-line users. They will see the updated completion message immediately after a request finishes.

eb5d673adb9d351e45298296a763562714171376.text: The system now stops generating text immediately after asking another program to do a task, rather than waiting for the task to finish.
