This change applies to the internal assistant tools and saves processing time. A person watching the logs would see the assistant's response end cleanly at the point of delegation, with no extra commentary or wasted tokens following the request.

051c20c7cb2a698c7ae81ab6bb539b8440308006.text: The system's method for sending text updates from the AI models to the application changed. This small internal update prevents the connection from closing too early while data is still arriving. Users will not notice any difference, as the visible behavior remains exactly the same.

b0d70e9344fccd4622e0394b2cacbb63f28e63d8.text: The website's cookie warning box is now narrower, and the top banner is slightly shorter. These visual adjustments affect all visitors, making the page look tidier on smaller screens.

54bb40a1c63b9cdf52197e89290141ffd441de0b.text: The search system now stops printing internal data to the console. This change affects the backend server and is live. If you look at the server logs, you will no longer see extra clutter from the search process.

5e9ae33025fefa1f49a0080f8325e2eb22c67e73.text: The tool now downloads text files directly from GitHub instead of using a middleman service. This change affects the internal web scraper and makes reading raw text links faster and more reliable. You would not notice this change directly, as it happens silently in the background.

d239ea8241ac4466117233c7a83692154e11fee9.text: The assistant now applies suggested changes directly to files instead of only listing them. Users will see edits happen automatically without needing to confirm each step. This update is live for internal testing.

c8664912289388e1b560b64150fa34691f4f6f03.text: A small internal update makes the command-line tool's auto-complete feature ignore capitalization. When typing a command, pressing the tab key now suggests matches even if the typed text doesn't match the case of the available options. This affects anyone using the tool's interactive command line.

7744bdfb31ecec854ee534f08a61c9efa3dddee8.text: The assistant's internal settings now allow adjusting how much thinking power it uses for different tasks. By default, it uses a moderate level, but the planning step specifically forces a high level to ensure accuracy. This is an internal update, so regular users will not notice any changes in how the service behaves.

cceae9af9f1c1ba4dedda9e5c9c4eb9f52db34af.text: The system now automatically hides its own temporary working notes from the shared project history. This change affects only the internal team managing the software. They will see that these hidden notes no longer appear in the list of files being saved or shared, keeping the project record cleaner.

c760ba147d16ef6b1f3eeb258be8c2c1b32dc445.text: The referrals page had a display glitch that could cause the text and layout to look broken or shift unexpectedly after loading. This fix cleans up the page structure to prevent that mismatch. It affects anyone viewing their referral link and history, ensuring the page renders correctly every time.

a2ca0e6854a7f0277aebb2349edef399684dc49d.text: The system now strictly requires blank lines between specific markers when processing code updates. This affects the internal tool that reads AI-generated changes. If the format is slightly off, the tool will reject it instead of guessing, preventing broken updates from reaching the final result.

e44611848fbe485b38121225957841582e0f3fff.text: The three informational cards on the pricing page were updated to look correct in both light and dark modes. Previously, these cards had a fixed dark background that made them hard to read on a light screen. Now, they adapt to your theme, have more breathing room, and gently lift with a shadow when you hover over them. This is a small visual polish that is live today.

88cf03f9da7b2def88a04a55f0a38c5f8118912a.text: The tool that calculates monthly revenue now includes customers whose payments failed but whose subscriptions remain open. Previously, these overdue accounts were ignored, causing the reported total to look lower than reality. This correction applies only to internal financial reports and does not change what customers see.

d5bd30c076875dd76f7b58a21c0470f3d5bcdee9.text: The space reserved for background instructions when generating search responses was doubled. This affects the system's ability to fit all necessary context into a single request. The change is live now and prevents errors when the background details are too long.

7eee186cefc703e803978090a4db20e025ca825c.text: When you ask the tool to start a new project, it now puts the files in the exact folder you named instead of the current one. If that folder does not exist yet, the tool creates it for you. You will also see messages on the screen telling you what the tool is doing, such as downloading files or setting up history, so you know the process is working.

db699f21fa45574829ffb3f33bbadd1e9b5d6606.text: The website now sends visitors from a short link to the community chat. This helps people join the group without needing to memorize a long, complicated web address. The change is live and affects anyone clicking the specific short link.

977781bef1944811126532fcce0e1466917d193d.text: A small internal change stops the system from blocking a new command if a previous one is still running. Instead of showing an error, it now resets the session to let the new command proceed. Regular users will not see any difference.

9a8d233f9d196c46a2a08800bd6189cb69e57e27.text: The internal assistant now uses a more precise search tool to find every place a renamed code element is used, ensuring no references are missed. It also automatically saves planning and design discussions into structured text files. These changes affect only the internal operations of the coding assistant and have no visible impact on end users.

d7aef9b715aaeade4eb8eefb2440d42902ba6835.text: A small internal fix stops the command-line tool from turning two spaces into a new line when pasting text. This affects only people using the tool in their terminal. They will notice pasted text stays on one line instead of breaking unexpectedly.

6bd57ae3a33672c64efd35999acf71854863c8ee.text: The system now correctly uses your chosen performance setting when preparing file requests. This fixes a caching issue for users selecting the maximum performance mode. You will notice faster responses in that mode.

8439268878175b5567899e1fcac22e4ed520037a.text: The program's command runner was reorganized internally to handle two different execution methods separately. This change affects only the software's internal structure, not its visible behavior. Users will notice no difference, as the commands still run, display output, and time out exactly as before.

5e5220c6dffa13ae7d95ffd94a43619e9b01530a.text: Pressing the stop key now instantly erases any leftover text you had typed into the command line. This prevents old, unfinished words from sticking around and appearing in your view. The fix is active today.

ef186f3b409f355dbb77ea735512328b5800af7e.text: The assistant switched its internal planning tool to a cheaper, faster model. This change is live now. You will notice planning steps finish quicker and cost less, while the assistant now uses this planning tool for all complex requests instead of only high-budget accounts.

27245ad41e46a001880f7d7b06fbdcf1fff1d472.text: The assistant now strictly refuses to send changes to the main project repository without your direct approval, preventing accidental site breaks. It also stops trying to start long-running servers itself, asking you to run them manually instead. This update is active today for all users interacting with the assistant.

83a09ad6b4de35a8bbb483183d90a4b88ceb8b2c.text: A small internal fix ensures the text cursor stays visible in the command-line tool. Previously, the cursor could disappear if the program stopped unexpectedly, leaving a blank space where you type. Now, the tool automatically brings the cursor back when it closes or is interrupted, so you can always see where you are typing.

d28b3d5117c3e80bd5007c13033a2edfc1081858.text: The tool now checks for errors when deciding if a file is hidden. If it cannot read the rules, it marks that specific file as failed instead of stopping the whole task. This change is live and affects anyone using the file scanning feature.

469ff525a232701bf55e36a2cce6174500cfba54.text: The system now searches for less obvious files even in its cheaper, faster mode, matching how it works in the standard mode. This change is live. Users in the cheaper mode might see slightly more accurate file suggestions without any noticeable difference in speed or cost.

e1a0031a517a37010bc8638bd002d61499c559fb.text: When creating a new project, the tool now automatically enters the project folder and starts the assistant, instead of just printing instructions for the user to do it manually. This affects anyone using the project creation command. They will notice the process continues immediately without needing to type extra commands.

85ecb13c084669f3761230d6bf70e9b1459bd66e.text: The command-line tool now shows its version number when asked. People using the tool can type a specific command to see which version they have installed. This update is live immediately for anyone using the tool.

3be2d5e260318c6283a0f4ca94e73d15d7a14776.text: The command-line tool now requires you to log in before you can type any commands. The temporary login code stays valid for one hour instead of five minutes. You will see the welcome message and project warnings only after you are signed in.

7647f19829affd7dd786eb8e665bad501c034bd2.text: The assistant now looks for personal notes in your home folder and reads them to better understand your preferences. These notes are strictly read-only, so the assistant can use them for context but cannot change or delete them. This update is live for anyone who has placed such files in their home directory.

1a070f6016b016b407870b0869f2243ef024ad44.text: A small internal update makes the command-line tool treat two consecutive spaces as a line break. This affects only people typing directly into that tool. They will see the text jump to a new line when they hit the spacebar twice.

1a7bc28151c8ef7ccb58e9741b68fd1f69cc8686.text: The assistant now knows to ask before installing new software pieces. This stops it from accidentally changing your project files without permission. You will notice this if you ask the assistant to add a feature that needs new tools; it will check with you first.

2a62e8508b74c8bb9fd33f63ee0d23fc234ca4e4.text: The internal tool no longer forces color settings off for terminal commands, relying on the system's default behavior instead. This affects the internal development environment, not the end product. Users would notice no change, as this is a minor internal adjustment to how the tool communicates with the terminal.

fea0adfa4b3a7a9380f3c4d8226242d47d4bb086.text: The lightweight assistant now uses a reasoning-focused AI model instead of a standard chat model. This change is live and affects users who select the lightweight option. They may notice the assistant takes slightly longer to respond but provides more logical answers to complex questions, though it now costs more per message.

f627e2530a620022fb721b9d6f0be34357189220.text: The AI assistant stopped adding extra blank lines between its messages. This small internal fix makes the text look tidier. People using the chat will see cleaner formatting without unnecessary gaps.

bb7a30ef9cea709728f973a3a9042fa064f8a5ec.text: The internal guide for checking software errors was corrected to point to the right tool. This helps developers avoid running the wrong command during quality checks. Outside users will not notice any change.

fc4c81c5f3a695cf6ce2c4560759f6ff7768c41c.text: The setup guide now requires building three parts of the system in a specific order before installing the rest. It also lists the exact configuration details needed for the app to run on a local machine. This only affects internal staff trying to set up their work computers. New users will see extra steps in the instructions.

b361e9fe6f8e32245a7c08f0284e2f75eb82bbfb.text: The assistant now automatically wraps text searches in quotation marks, removing the need for users to manually add them. This change applies to internal guidance for the code search tool. Users will notice the assistant no longer requires manual quoting for search patterns, though it may still need specific characters like dashes or periods to be marked with backslashes.

7043e237da9c08540c354264c1ccaf0e1814272f.text: The command to start the highest quality mode changed its name. People using the old name can still use it, but new instructions tell them to use the new name. The mode now uses a deeper thinking model for hard problems.

fe766691f1530ba4575701b060baf516fbba6c8e.text: The terminal no longer automatically shares certain hidden settings from the background system. This affects only internal staff using the command line interface. They might notice PowerShell modules or automated build tools behave differently if they relied on these automatic connections.

7001a8a4f4662ef982f45b3232f66d973be151aa.text: The assistant received a new instruction to be more careful when running tasks on your computer. It will now only use this feature when necessary and will avoid actions that could permanently change files. This update is live today and helps prevent accidental mistakes.

0193b3a0d465ba1adf4ed441230b342e9ce781fb.text: A small internal fix ensures that when the system changes its working directory, it correctly remembers the new location. Previously, it kept using the old location for subsequent steps, causing errors in finding files. This change is live and prevents the system from failing to locate files after moving folders.

5044119481cc47730f8f3f99f85675aff2043fc4.text: The assistant stopped guessing when you are giving it a command to run if your request has an apostrophe. This change is active now. You will notice it if you try to run a command like 'echo "hello"' without a special prefix; the assistant will just answer your question instead of trying to run the command.

c3fa982685f2b2cf8d9117c1074bf488fb1cf199.text: The highest usage tier is now called 'max' instead of 'pro', and the plan display name changed from 'Pro Max' to 'Pro Plus'. This affects anyone using the command-line tool with the old flag. If they try to start with the old 'pro' setting, the tool will show a warning and stop working, forcing them to restart with the new 'max' setting.

10e5042a46f8a5369982b00658fa1d39fdea0643.text: A small internal change makes the system wait a fixed time for a slow response from a specific AI service. If that wait expires, it tries again a few times, but only for timeouts, not other errors. This is live today. Staff using that service might see fewer long waits or stuck requests.

f455c371952754aa6399023a9e599d0e6b2dfd86.text: Pressing the tab key while typing a command now fills in shared letters if multiple options start the same way. This helps people using the text-based tool type faster without guessing full words. The change is live.

e47cfaa4d0d93073fecdbe019fae9a8a87edc43c.text: Small internal fix for billing. When customers downgrade their plan, their new lower usage limit now applies immediately instead of keeping the old higher limit. Customers who downgraded previously might have noticed they could still use more than their new plan allowed.

d9361f97059416156af3b2b2706f8c0ba49ae077.text: The internal cost calculation for a specific AI model was corrected to match current market rates. This change affects only the billing system's accuracy for internal tracking, not the user-facing price. Users will not notice any difference in service or cost.

506c48b036eaf6147d393735610cf963d92889fa.text: This small internal update fixes how referral credits appear on billing statements. People who received credits for referring others will now see a clear description for those credits on their invoices, instead of the credit showing up with no explanation.

b44f1d9a895a0797a3df472e2617707c2f0b7081.text: Fixed a glitch on Windows where the first command typed into the terminal window failed to run. The system now ignores the initial text marker that appeared before the command. This small internal fix ensures that the very first action works correctly, matching the behavior on other computers.

baba7b8b0a573668dbc63cccdfce33348204b2f4.text: Active paid subscribers now see a 'Manage Billing' button in their profile menu instead of a disabled message. Clicking it takes them directly to the payment provider's website to update their card or cancel, with their email already filled in. This change is live immediately for all paying customers.

d91ef3f135dd1cca6dcda7b8dc7f98f097c5edf0.text: The AI assistant now measures the size of your project's file list in words instead of characters before deciding whether to include it. If the list is too long, it gets cut off to save space and money. This change is live for internal use and helps the system handle large projects more efficiently without losing track of the most important files.

3e66e5307621f23e926f16efde9dcc61f0482756.text: A small internal check was added to help the team catch errors in helper tools before they are used. This change affects only the people who build and maintain these tools. Users will not notice any difference in how the product works.

c42c1d8fc932b4b33f75238ccdcf68b11539c902.text: The system now uses a smarter, faster model to decide which files to open when you ask a question. It ignores extra background details to make this choice quicker and more accurate. You might notice slightly faster responses when the assistant figures out what information it needs to read.

e5e8438d6a64ffec26f9af957516d14bbf060a23.text: The automated checking system now verifies each part of the application separately, rather than checking the whole thing at once. This internal change makes the checks faster and more consistent for the team. Nothing visible to end users will change.

36927f7bdb7ac9fba3b030e4983e3211baddabb2.text: The internal billing report now distinguishes between new and existing customers by checking their first payment date. It calculates average spending only for long-term users and lists individual accounts paying over $49. This change affects only the internal team reviewing financial data, with no visible impact on customers.

beb7c4ab2ec83b7d54ebed31d8c542f291857aaa.text: The tool now saves a backup of your files before making changes. This happens only if you set the tool to 'stage' mode. You will not notice any visual changes, but your work is safer if the tool makes a mistake.

b37633c1c9c60972bc76d853f4c9675e772f34a7.text: The assistant now has a 30-second limit for any single command it runs, so it will stop trying to start servers or other long tasks. It also requires your explicit permission before installing major software or creating new environments. These rules are live today and apply to all internal tool usage.

377d549540468ab0aa8fdabd38b2db573e87a628.text: When a connection drops and then comes back, the program now automatically stops any spinning loading icons and puts the cursor back where you can type again. Before, it might have just printed a message but left the screen frozen in a waiting state. This helps people using the command-line tool avoid getting stuck after a network blip.

a7f8c0182cbbedd3a18e79f9809c8544ede315a7.text: The app now starts its internal command window without loading your personal computer settings first. This small internal update prevents potential conflicts when the app runs tasks. You will likely see no visible change in your daily use.

92608f821299aba1dba330d57c1b0dfb3fcfaebe.text: Anonymous users now have a daily limit of 250 credits instead of 500. This change is live and applies to anyone using the service without signing in. If you are an anonymous user, you will run out of free credits after half as many requests as before.

5d25488cfc53270b3a014df054637b3fd4dbec5e.text: The internal tool now stages every modified file when you ask it to, not just the ones it already applied. This affects the tool's automatic file-saving behavior. You might see more files marked as ready to commit than before.

c9918c0786a1baf82d4c82542d90d27ac9da10df.text: The internal tool now loads your personal settings when starting a new terminal session, so commands behave like they do in your own shell. Windows displays were also simplified to a plain path marker to help the system recognize when a command finishes. This change is active immediately for internal use but produces no visible difference for external customers.

013a51e080edf3d610661982eac933a5ea0ad8f3.text: The system now correctly finds the project folder when running terminal commands. This fixes an internal error that could stop commands from working during setup. Regular users will not notice any change in how the app looks or behaves.

caad2a8f527d86af19df2b4268cfeb8ca0b94d24.text: Staff fixed two mistakes in the written instructions that tell the assistant how to safely run computer commands. The text now shows a correct example for running tests and spells 'globally' right. This is a small internal cleanup, so nothing changes for anyone using the product.

6546a77b438f1d8a268a4f2f767a213d05f27e6a.text: The internal code search tool now shows the first three matching lines directly in the console instead of just a total count. This helps developers see immediate context for search results without opening files. The full list remains available to the system, but the visible preview is capped at three lines followed by an ellipsis if more exist.

917bbde1858dc6cc6c07edbd59d9e256fdb8d1da.text: The automatic stop timer for running tasks has been extended from ten seconds to thirty seconds. This small internal adjustment helps longer processes finish without being cut off early. You will notice fewer interruptions when using the terminal feature.

3609a538a5f3139cf9a405b48e71d1114fec3566.text: The system's helper for running terminal commands was updated to a newer, experimental version. This affects only the internal command-line tooling. You would not notice any change in the main application's behavior.

854143b9093caeabb5a147fc7eb953493663a586.text: The command-line tool now correctly checks if any edits were actually made before trying to save them to the project history. Previously, it looked at the total list of proposed changes, which could cause errors if no changes were applied. This small internal fix ensures the tool only attempts to save files when there are real updates to record.

dd07bc673668d98facdf9bee7a38d26be7721cf1.text: The assistant now automatically skips two specific types of large configuration files when scanning a project. This change is live and affects anyone using the assistant on projects that include these files. You would notice the assistant responding faster and more accurately because it no longer wastes time reading irrelevant technical details.

90dff3f523d2680cd232c19d685fa41b9682f8e5.text: A small internal fix makes the invisible text box used for typing on the terminal screen completely invisible and inactive to touch. This stops the hidden box from blocking the screen or causing layout issues on mobile devices. Phone and tablet users will now experience smoother scrolling without accidental taps or frozen views.

91537f0d53f45b8dc993fedfff319536140140b5.text: The app now waits to show the first word until it receives actual text, ignoring any blank or empty messages sent during the connection setup. This small internal fix prevents the interface from briefly displaying a loading state before the real answer appears.

fd04248ef741ac72d79bbb72f3dd6cb272530289.text: A small internal fix corrected the address where the system looks for its building blocks. This ensures the tool finds the right definitions instead of missing them. Developers will notice fewer errors when checking the code.

f58f0944e0bb45f70bdeb6e159c3dcd7344704a2.text: The company's main website page now loads faster and looks slightly cleaner in light mode. Visitors will see the background animations run more smoothly and text boxes have standard borders instead of faint shadows. This change is live today and affects anyone visiting the homepage.

f1590167d684f272710b2b2e319ef7239b74c069.text: The tool now stops printing the final command line once it detects the system is ready for input. This prevents the same text from appearing twice on the screen. The change applies internally and fixes a minor visual glitch for people using the terminal feature.

520d15a41012ac00a4f389d2d1918ccf3562b01a.text: A small internal fix stops the assistant's 'Thinking' spinner from breaking the text display on Windows computers. The tool now checks if it is talking to a live terminal; if not, it just prints new lines instead of trying to erase them. Windows users running the command-line tool should see cleaner output without scrambled or overlapping text.

bca20eb7c06a149a3c55cfcd224198bfa36408d0.text: The automated system that checks for errors now generates necessary data structures before running its checks. This ensures the error detection process works correctly without failing due to missing information. This is an internal maintenance update that improves reliability for the development team.

f27dc96467a6e1a6504927fb60566d2a485f89f7.text: The app now loads your computer's standard startup settings when opening its command window, ensuring text displays correctly and the window adjusts when resized. This affects internal tools users who rely on custom configurations. You will see the command prompt respect your usual environment settings and adapt properly when you change the window size.

aad41fd2f1e8d948f67a628587f24eb08403e95e.text: A small internal update changed how the website checks its code before saving. Instead of just checking for typing errors, the system now tries to fully create the final website files. This catches more problems automatically. Regular visitors will not notice any difference.

fc33b81842c741f0d9b56486ec3d7fc03014e812.text: The system now waits longer for DeepSeek to answer and tries again if it fails. This applies to all requests using that service. If DeepSeek is slow or unavailable, the system will keep trying instead of stopping immediately.

fb2faab94efb1ec18f203297d019e4c73636254a.text: A small internal update ensures the map of the codebase is built before other parts of the system. This change affects only the automated checks that run when developers submit work. No customer or user will notice any difference in the software itself.

bf037ad3bcd486ce96317be0407b5cdd62af91bd.text: The automatic check for one internal tool now only verifies code types, skipping the full build. This change affects only the development team's workflow. A non-programmer would notice nothing.

9fa91417f7faa69ef8e8c15074ee69351306ff92.text: The planning feature now uses the full version of the reasoning model instead of the preview. This model thinks harder but takes longer to answer, so the process waits for the complete response rather than showing text as it arrives. This change is live and affects anyone using the complex planning tool.

d40adfe6b20aae6ed0e9e0dc2ed17a6724f3178e.text: The system now detects when a file has been partially edited, even if the user used different capitalization or added extra spaces in their notes. This helps the assistant understand that only part of the code changed, rather than assuming the whole file was rewritten. This small fix is live and works automatically in the background.

74e1a7a47a16bbb67a72e9e384b2ee7fc9ea75fa.text: The setup instructions on the website now show the full word 'install' instead of the short letter 'i' in the command line text. This change is live. People following the guide will see clearer text, but the command still does the exact same thing.

c8eb5b645d899998c0deb7db264acc286f2014a1.text: Mobile users of the interactive demo now see the conversation box stay in view while typing, instead of the whole page jumping around. The system also quietly records details about each demo request, like the device type and message history, for internal tracking. These changes are live and mostly invisible to the average visitor.

0b41bb2890916f8ac878d1011c069ff1c4d9d06c.text: A company profile page now names the business as StartMatch and adds a link to its website. The file was also renamed to match a standard format. This is a small internal cleanup. Visitors reading that specific page will see the company name and a clickable link.

c9b8dfc97959583230cdce6950a22860304cb6d3.text: A small internal update improves how the system recognizes certain error messages from the computer's command line. Specifically, it now identifies a particular type of syntax error as a sign that a command was not found or invalid. This change affects only the internal tooling and does not alter the visible interface for end users.

cc68afa80e8fe010cafd9db3ebeed53a062c934b.text: The tool that reads and maps code got a routine update to its underlying engine. This change is internal and affects only the software's ability to understand programming languages. A person would not notice any difference in how the application looks or behaves.

5fc2da2850390542054c9ab1b7df38227491cfcb.text: A minor internal adjustment prevents a specific background component from printing error messages to the console when it starts up. This affects the command-line interface tool handlers. Users will notice a cleaner output with fewer unnecessary warnings if the optional component fails to load.

b1245b24ac1c146fa17c1da0bfbad818f8ee1e75.text: The website now includes two new settings for tracking visitor activity. This change only helps the website's builders set up their systems correctly. Normal visitors will not notice any difference.

9b2430b0c456a1509bc516c2b38a6449c8feefb0.text: A small internal cleanup changed how the system stores plan names and fixed a text display bug. If a name was shown with extra capitals, like 'PRO', it now appears as 'Pro'. Most people will not notice anything.

0b397f5d019402242c5449c891b088a0862ef381.text: The team updated the underlying setup for the Bun runtime to use its official type definitions. This change is internal and affects only the developers working on the codebase. No visible features or user-facing behaviors changed.

8da363766af2704b229ce6108ea70cdf0f675bc1.text: The label for the highest-tier subscription plan changed from Moar Pro to Pro Max. This update affects how the plan name appears in the user interface for customers on that specific tier. You would see the new name displayed wherever the plan is listed or selected.

3d5418aff18ef33dfef1abdfcc778fb852e09b47.text: The page shown after confirming a plan change stopped loading because it tried to use plan details before they arrived. This crash affected only people completing a subscription upgrade or change on the website. The fix ensures the page waits for the correct plan information, so it now loads successfully.

315986b546823cc85c2c621df8b159d923bb6177.text: The system now hides a technical warning message when it starts up, preventing it from cluttering the internal logs. It also updated how it recognizes a specific error in German software, making it easier to identify when a command cannot be found. This is a small internal fix that does not change how the application behaves for end users.

b3d5eaab4e0c94e8a8296df4865f63d2b989e86b.text: The tool now checks fewer conditions before automatically saving previous file changes when staging is enabled. This internal cleanup ensures the process triggers correctly based on current activity, without changing how the tool behaves for you.

48702972af6b73864b19f9eee0c095e208b84c84.text: The AI assistant now strictly limits its file reading to folders inside the current project. If it tries to access a file outside this project, it will stop and report that the file is unavailable. This internal safety rule prevents the assistant from accidentally reading unrelated system files.

8c81f3aa4e37a2cb5dd1547c2b18e039ef512b19.text: The AI assistant now checks if it skipped parts of a file by leaving a 'rest of the code' note. If it did, the system forces a rewrite to include the full text. This prevents saving files with missing content.

c77783dc1a17c67ec0a9a146dd070e0dbcec5d46.text: A small internal fix corrects the pricing page button for logged-out visitors. Previously, anonymous users saw a 'Downgrade' option. Now, they see 'Get Started' and are sent to the package page, matching the experience for free accounts.

d35d51e295dfede403c0df56a48b5039d045db31.text: The app's terminal feature now checks if a specific advanced tool is available. If it is missing, the app automatically switches to a simpler built-in method to run commands. This internal change prevents the app from crashing on certain computers where the advanced tool fails to install.

99d576e61c043c7a94ab28bed7e116e699311e0c.text: The assistant's internal instructions were updated to strictly forbid using placeholder comments when rewriting files. This change ensures the system always applies precise, targeted edits rather than risking accidental data loss from truncated instructions. The update is active immediately for the backend agent.

38aeb1c921aa31c27514693c07df77e715c2827b.text: The software renamed an internal folder to fix a glitch that prevented it from working correctly. This change is invisible to customers and does not affect how the product looks or behaves.

e71a809870d31cd002ccb4cca70a60e646aedcfb.text: Logged-out visitors now see a blue 'Upgrade' button on the pricing page. Clicking it sends them to the login screen. This fixes a blank or missing button state for anonymous users.

d3f2357b21c36b29846d3bc35ac92bc9c3cc49c2.text: A small internal fix makes the search tool work correctly when looking for text containing symbols like pipes or quotation marks. This change affects the assistant's ability to find code, ensuring it no longer fails on these specific patterns. Users will notice the tool now also displays the total number of matches found at the end of a search.

3fa4bc3605360ab0fe373c0b5d8c383aa4cb0d84.text: The system now automatically reads web links found in internal knowledge files and adds their content to the assistant's memory. This change is live and affects internal knowledge bases. You would notice the assistant answering questions using information from those linked web pages without needing to manually copy-paste the text.

e73fbb33f6392a6c3bf10bf29201761c337cb3f4.text: The system now recognizes specific German error messages from Windows commands. This affects users running commands in a German language setting. If a command fails, the system correctly identifies the failure instead of missing the error.

16ff9a300de5251929aaf5a429704d4eca67f7bb.text: When a paid subscription ends because of a failed payment or immediate cancellation, the system now automatically drops the account to the free tier right away. This ensures that users with expired or canceled plans no longer retain access to paid features. If you cancel but choose to keep service until the billing period ends, your paid access remains active until that date passes.

2043ab4a67b6cd5f4ed1819b90a8c263516b14e4.text: The tool now recognizes plain Windows command lines like 'C:\...>' as valid prompts. This helps the assistant understand when a command finishes on Windows systems using standard Command Prompt. No visible change for users; just smoother internal command handling.

378b851f01a1bd8f4a8ac4e83f2e31d8d65d2508.text: For pro plan customers, the system now uses a smarter AI model to fix errors when updating files. This change is live today. Customers will see fewer failed file updates, but there are no new settings or buttons to use.

78fe64f1ceb0a50579950e56468c172881395321.text: Fixed a bug in the demo terminal where fast typing caused display errors. Improved security checks for the demo's data source to accept slightly different web addresses. These are small, internal fixes. You likely will not notice any visual changes.

673bb02bba2b4e4e1886a17a0facb9cfb19e797b.text: A small internal fix helps the system recognize when a command fails on German-language computers. Previously, these errors were missed because the message was in German. Now, the system correctly identifies the failure. This change is live and affects anyone using the tool with a German system setting.

ee30ecb6f13737dc8dbfae749174dffefd7f31f7.text: This small internal update adds navigation links to the bottom of documentation pages. Readers browsing these pages will now see arrows pointing to the previous or next section, making it easier to move through the guide without using the side menu.

6a3165ecbf753be2ffc95b333e6b0520b47bdd45.text: The limit for free, unlogged users dropped from 500 to 250 credits. This change is live now. If you use the service without signing in, you will run out of free credits twice as fast.

6f539a6136f42ed8db0e420e471ee07f380ca725.text: The system now recognizes a specific German error message that appears when a command is not found. This improves how the tool handles errors for German-speaking users. You would notice fewer confusing failures when using the terminal in German.

0cb901cdd22d5e3ab65784b92843a5ef07a8f67a.text: The system now uses a cheaper AI model to fix text errors when you choose the budget-friendly mode. This helps reduce costs for internal operations. You won't see any changes, but the system might take slightly longer to correct mistakes.

b1b052c78616d75d58f67dd82eb8d6b25c253ff0.text: The command line tool now suggests possible file paths or variable names when you press the tab key while typing. This helps people who use the internal command line interface type commands faster and with fewer mistakes. The change is live today.

890b5912499975c4ea7f615e6a74dddd5241c641.text: The system now checks whether a file actually exists before describing it. This prevents the assistant from claiming it read a file that was never there. The change is live.

8b70e9059a23d07ab8233568dabbb5de21f24ddd.text: The help pages now open links to outside guides in a new tab instead of replacing the current page. This applies to readers using the documentation site. No other visible changes occurred.

f50573107e2ef2f3f222cb0c45ef8a0c05e2900f.text: The software switched back to an older version of its reasoning model because the newest one isn't available through the current service provider. This change is live today. It affects the system's planning tasks. You might notice slightly different responses or reasoning quality, but the interface remains the same.

a42ced07e08c3226a8584e9f6972afd158b6409a.text: A cost-saving setting now limits how much project information the assistant can process at once. This change applies to internal tools and reduces the amount of file data included in responses. The assistant will simply include less context from project files when this mode is active.

ea07c1a5ac11e6650f7b1b2dd17d46d7f730652a.text: The navigation links on the website's top menu now sit on the far right side, leaving more empty space near the logo on the left. This small visual change affects all visitors who view the site on a desktop or laptop. You will notice the links are pushed away from the logo, making the header look less cluttered.

25bf18c95dc060332e914ac83a8cba130aa81966.text: A small internal fix hides the 'refer a friend' banner from people who are not signed in. Previously, visitors saw a message about earning credits, but they could not actually claim them without an account. Now, that banner only appears for logged-in users, so visitors see a cleaner page without a confusing offer they cannot use.

7d63183f5701c34d55ed2671dbca5120c0b1259e.text: The internal label for this software release increased by one number. This update is live today. People who use the tool would notice no change in how it works, as this was only a routine version update.

b5f8015e91062d3fb747cbe6e0775c61dc981176.text: The AI assistant now waits longer before stopping to ask for your next step. It will complete up to six tasks on its own, instead of stopping after three. This helps the assistant finish longer jobs without constant interruptions.

2be5ae7a6594f5cd817dba1ecf97199e599fe81a.text: The system now checks if you have saved custom notes and if this is not your first message. If both are true, it reminds the assistant to consider updating those notes with new, useful information after answering. This helps the assistant keep your saved context current without cluttering the start of a conversation.

3cdf87242f07ca2829e21b9d7ef6b6eafdea23cb.text: The internal system updated its method for counting text pieces to better match a specific AI model's requirements. This change affects the backend service that processes messages, ensuring accurate size calculations for the new model. Users will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves or responds.

ca216648702c2cce0358fe9baca28e0122c38b21.text: The internal system that searches for project files now has stricter instructions to look beyond obvious matches. It specifically checks for documentation, examples, and related tests when planning a change. This helps the assistant find the right context faster, though the improvement is small and happens behind the scenes.

7b75881543bc0af917b79daa032c27848ac84b62.text: The system now retries failed requests to the AI assistant with increasing delays, improving reliability for internal users. Placeholder fields for cloud service credentials were added to a template file but do nothing until filled in. This is a minor internal maintenance update.

d527e4775bb4d882fb072b1e7f2938a1cfb48029.text: When the assistant is set to run without stopping for approval, it no longer receives a rule to make only tiny changes and wait for permission. This lets it finish larger tasks in one go. The change is live for that specific mode.

a605eb68cacd92404eb936c1f6d3f193ed458efe.text: The system now checks if a file still exists before trying to save it. This stops errors when files are removed during work. Users will see smoother updates without failure messages.

b3d2a104156df34952fbf27576e79dda625769ca.text: A small internal update now checks file names before including them in the assistant's search list, rejecting any with spaces or special symbols. It also added a rule telling the AI to ignore previous user commands when picking files. This change is live but invisible to you; it just helps the tool find the right files more accurately.

c03c11d7b0be9bb8a98ec3eb544c575fee88f3fa.text: When the assistant proposes a multi-step plan, it now automatically continues working through all the steps instead of stopping to ask permission. This change is already active and helps ensure complex tasks are fully completed without needing manual prompts to resume.

18d5e003dee7ea5b7933c08cd58ab5f429b2c405.text: The AI assistant now automatically runs safety checks after finishing a task, but only for specific internal projects that have defined verification steps. This change is live and ensures the assistant verifies its own work for those particular teams. You would notice fewer errors in the final output for these projects.

43aa27fdfc1d3345b4131cb6d610d196672b0cdc.text: A blank line was added to the Oliver case study to separate the description of past tool failures from the success of Codebuff. This affects readers of the case study. They will notice the text is easier to read because the comparison is now split into two distinct paragraphs.

4075972ed32841af532cdd8a572bd2b67e4cb005.text: The usage page now hides the overage fee details if a user's plan does not have a set rate, such as a free account. This prevents the page from showing broken text or errors for those users, ensuring they only see billing information relevant to their specific plan.

dd3012203660f7eb2d79cabe28a9245c56f006a2.text: The system now identifies new files more directly, removing an unnecessary step in its internal process. This change affects only how the software handles data behind the scenes. Users will notice no difference in performance or functionality.

70f42362b0771f5ca0130285f72a4b9270236ad6.text: The billing system now checks which plan you have before calculating extra fees for using more credits than allowed. Pro users will see their overage cost increase to 99 cents per 100 credits, while Pro Plus users stay at 90 cents. This change is live and ensures customers are charged the correct rate for their specific subscription.

4b737984c62adeefece6a6e70d32d349ca94154e.text: The system stopped adding an invisible end marker to the final message text. This change is internal and affects only how the backend stores the conversation history. Users will not see any difference in the messages displayed on screen.

1ffa07da0d957e4a9059e5de94d1b71b4a59f0da.text: A small internal fix prevents a partial template file from appearing as a separate page in the website's documentation. This stops the website from trying to build that fragment as a standalone document. Readers will not notice any change, as the broken or duplicate page simply no longer appears.

de59cd8a129423f999301e25c50e987f241d8baa.text: The assistant can now search for specific text patterns across all project files. This helps developers quickly find where code is defined or used. The results are limited to prevent overwhelming the system, and the feature is active immediately for internal use.

c19645815c47cbab0acc37544e20a74b0ce4193e.text: The command-line tool now stops staging old changes if no new changes are found. This prevents unnecessary actions when the system is idle. The change is live and affects internal users of the tool.

aefb207e1738a672e5eeffb2086838226be2f7a3.text: For paid accounts, the system now checks your actual subscription details to set usage limits and extra charges, rather than using fixed numbers. This means your usage page will accurately reflect your current plan's limits. The change is live.

8ba905bca1fbdde31bd7335204efc5a38ac44093.text: The written story about how one customer used the tool was rearranged to be easier to read. Headings were added to split the text into clear sections, and repetitive details were cut out. Readers looking at this specific story will notice a cleaner layout that focuses more directly on the problem solved and the results.

1681e199385ce89a1d33766a2354d82f471572e2.text: The assistant now skips searching for new files when you send a follow-up message or just say hello. This stops it from wasting time reading files that do not help answer your question. You might see it respond slightly faster in these cases.

37eecb174d98099780d0becc53758c30e768b2fa.text: When someone creates an account, the system now sends their name and email to a marketing tool. This happens automatically in the background for new signups. The person signing up won't notice any change on the website, but they will likely receive a welcome email from the marketing service shortly after.

a7294e394d936ec3782b9c4445ef9f63c66489df.text: When a payment is processed for an account with referral credits, the system now adds a clear note to the invoice stating that a referral bonus was applied. This change affects customers who have accumulated referral credits and are making a purchase. If they look at their invoice, they will see a specific line explaining that their referral bonus reduced the total cost.

37fa4c785cf3fcbd46be0456614c951464d2edc7.text: Referral credits are now applied to a customer's bill before it is finalized, rather than after payment. This affects customers with active referral credits, who will see their final invoice amount reduced by the exact credit value on the statement. The change is live today for new invoices.

24d7ad7fc30c6dbf98d51d0c7835d78858be2d9e.text: The tool now saves earlier edits before applying new ones, fixing a timing glitch where changes could be missed. This only affects users who enable the automatic saving option. They might see a message confirming previous edits were saved before the new ones appear.

e6d16d0bfec019acef0ac4b8deeff1f3c44cf154.text: The AI assistant now checks if the user is on Windows. If so, it adds a note to its instructions to use Windows commands like 'dir' instead of 'ls'. This only affects the assistant's internal instructions, not the user's view.

56063ff50d80541ea0d50110670ac0f676b04c1f.text: Pressing Ctrl+Z now quits the command-line tool instead of pausing it. This change is live and affects anyone using the tool directly.

4afd0074a494a5135098f5231c4ce1977847999c.text: The website's case study for Benjamin Bryant was updated to remove a confusing phrase. It now clearly states that his work time dropped to minutes, rather than vaguely saying 'minutes, if not hours'. This small text correction is live and affects only readers viewing that specific page.

eff9c6be11845e708e20788406ffffd3273b0dd9.text: The spacing between the side menu and the main text on desktop was adjusted to keep the page layout aligned. This small internal fix ensures the guide pages look correct on larger screens without shifting content unexpectedly.

99e74e93b4adf5f45b132df8c66fdbac2c8e2fd1.text: A small wording fix was made to a public case study page. The text previously claimed that implementation time dropped to 'two minutes', which contradicted the surrounding context. It now says 'minutes', making the statement logically consistent. Visitors to that specific page will see the corrected sentence, but nothing else changes.

21d748c48c3edc8a2e677db6bd6df477033e8463.text: Website pages for help and pricing now fit better on small phone screens, preventing text from sticking out past the edge. Visitors can also find a link to the help pages in the top menu, and the bottom of the page hides on help pages to save space.

1e3e7fd9a68962ae2944ee3187f9cf43e3638146.text: The command-line tool now checks the computer's underlying software before running. If that software is older than a specific version from several years ago, the tool will stop and show an error message. This prevents the tool from crashing later during use.

53a1670cfe1d31ed6b3a3acb51d3f35dc3646c66.text: The website's story about a specific investor was updated to fix small mistakes. The headline now uses simpler words, and the text consistently calls the person 'Ben' instead of switching between names. Readers visiting this page will see cleaner, more polished writing, but the facts of the story remain the same.

03e91522f6de843ecbddeffd88285bfd390e003a.text: A small internal change is live today. In modes other than the lowest-cost mode, the assistant now makes fewer separate requests for files at the same time, and each remaining request asks for more files. If someone looked, they would see fewer file-collection steps and larger file lists in the remaining steps.

ac5d79136aa688830f28c0c60793bbe95f9f0263.text: The website's recommendation section was updated to feature a new quote from Dennis Beatty praising the company's daily use of the product. Visitors reading this specific testimonial will now see the new text and a link to a more recent post instead of the previous one.

055e1a087350e0593bb66cfac9bab8ab20eb6219.text: The names for the two cost-saving and cost-increasing options have changed. Instead of 'cheap' and 'expensive', they are now called 'lite' and 'pro'. If you use the command-line tool, you must now type --lite or --pro to select these modes; the old flags will no longer work.

af2dd8415506131f5a49ae8ffade5e1329a0fb0f.text: The case study about Benjamin Bryant was rewritten for clarity. People who visit that page will see a new title, a smoother description of his work, and one subject label instead of several. It is a small wording update, and the new text is live on the website.

1048f59905bbf7a35925abdeacbc9662d789d4e7.text: The command-line tool now shows a colored banner at startup to indicate if 'Lite' or 'Pro' mode is active. This replaces the previous method of hiding the mode inside the welcome message. Only people using the tool's command-line interface will see this change; the web interface is unaffected.

a2c879fce06b41a71b823495cbf5d0cb951150d5.text: The website text about one investor's experience was shortened to remove extra details. This change is live. A visitor reading that page will see a simpler, quicker story without the removed background information.

46118f636c46b7c6d3b34b3d990ad255f2b5adff.text: The website's scrolling testimonials now display in smaller, tighter boxes with adjusted text casing and reordered entries. Visitors to the homepage see these compact quotes as they scroll. This visual change is live.

4edac09cee1a84f5e58581036a43730c8e831469.text: The app now explains how to pick between cheaper, faster answers and higher quality ones when you start it. This helps new users understand the cost options without guessing. You would see these tips in the startup menu and the online help pages.

68cb82724cc5370312951fb27bbbb2c1c46f3182.text: The AI assistant now automatically sees your computer's operating system, shell, and hardware specs when helping with code. This helps it give commands that work on your specific machine instead of guessing. You will notice the assistant stops suggesting wrong commands for your setup.

cf23c145ce70cdcd245e025304dafa020b7d7e04.text: The command-line tool now uses simple switches to choose model quality instead of typing a specific value. People using this internal tool will notice that they can now type '--cheap' or '--expensive' directly, rather than '--mode cheap' or '--mode expensive'. This makes the tool easier to use and reduces errors from typing the wrong mode name.

6e7ad99c5c21dba05812a65e0dab9619dcaca601.text: A small internal safety fix was added to the system that processes your requests. Previously, if a specific check for unlimited processing failed, the whole request would crash. Now, if that check fails, the system assumes unlimited processing is not allowed and continues normally, so you are less likely to see a complete error message.

eeadaab84c6ba21b057e3e0d207b3dc32cccfd37.text: The website now ignores capital letters when searching for a sponsee's profile. If you type a name with capital letters, the site still finds the correct page. This small update works immediately.

62a0134a4aa2d77f3231ecca7ae1aaf18114c15c.text: The service now records background errors in its logs instead of stopping when they appear. This keeps the system running for internal staff. They would notice only a new entry in the logs, with no visible change to the interface.

bd517f15859805bdb577eb1a2068f5db5d46bb63.text: The system now adjusts how many files it requests from the codebase based on the selected cost and quality mode. Users in expensive mode see six files requested, cheap mode requests seven, and normal mode requests five. Additionally, cheap mode skips generating example prompts to save resources. These changes are live and affect how the assistant gathers context for its responses.

3b2183eb92065c9623fafbeada3fb116f8c63646.text: The update tool now recognizes when the assistant is installed via a common Mac software manager, treating it like a standard installation. This helps users who installed the tool through that manager, ensuring updates work correctly. If you use that specific installation method, the tool will now update smoothly without errors. This fix is active immediately.

b1067ad47bd356da68c45eb832479355a0a76bf3.text: The code now labels its three spending settings as 'cheap', 'normal', and 'expensive' with a clearer name, preventing confusion with other settings. This internal cleanup affects only the system's own bookkeeping. You will not notice any change in how the tool works or how much it costs you today.

3b31538d9feac271f582483bb3cf72f3fb23a47a.text: The assistant now asks for explicit permission before running tasks that permanently change data or affect live systems. This small safety update applies to all users. You would notice the assistant pausing to request approval before executing such actions.

0b8ab09f123b442516dbe547673eb0496958edec.text: The AI assistant stopped requiring Git commands for moving or deleting files, switching to standard system commands instead. This internal change affects how the assistant performs file refactoring tasks. Users will see no visible difference, as the assistant handles these actions the same way, but the underlying instructions guiding its behavior have been simplified.

a4b4d850b4d24a966aadbb0cbfa93eb0024dc79a.text: The team cleaned up internal setup files by removing duplicate database tools from separate project folders and keeping just one copy in the shared folder. This change affects only the engineers who build the app and will not change how the product works for you today.

98bcb3a09187603ef2381eb9f5c9a37cbf246554.text: The system now asks the AI to think about whether to save new knowledge without writing down its thought process. If no new knowledge is needed, it explicitly states 'No knowledge file changes needed' instead of staying silent. This helps the system reliably decide when to update its memory, affecting how accurately it remembers important details from conversations.

086c126431333da97c6243501da4e4abb0def26d.text: The system now treats dollar signs in new text as regular characters instead of special commands. This prevents errors when editing files that contain dollar signs. Users will see fewer failed attempts to update text with dollar signs.

cd15427d4df3eba8f62457c54eb83144ddd51320.text: The internal system now uses a different, cheaper AI model to decide if it needs to read more files to answer a request. This change is live and affects how the backend processes requests. A user would not notice any visual difference, but the system might make slightly different decisions about which files to read.

4fb51045a01c64697eba586648de4b624000fefc.text: The system now includes project notes directly in its instructions rather than generating them separately during chat. This internal adjustment means the assistant may reference existing project context more consistently when answering questions.

7150842f1f9d5e1e61cef3168d394d501e2ff518.text: The software team deleted several old, unused shortcuts from the internal settings for the server. This cleanup does not change how the application works or looks for anyone. It simply removes clutter that no longer serves a purpose.

e92b346971a2e04f5525674d2348b07b291b3513.text: The system now requires a very strong reason before saving new information to its memory files. This internal change reduces clutter by ensuring only highly relevant, non-obvious details are recorded. You will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves or responds.

d3a6c538d61969e08d092563304caf31a451461a.text: Closing the program now requires pressing the interrupt key twice within three seconds to prevent accidental exits. The first press shows a warning message, and the second press closes the program. This change affects people using the text-based version of the software.

a34ba22f1b0c1706fd7989330ac0ff52108e14d6.text: The search feature stops saving temporary copies of its instructions when working on just one file. This internal update affects only the background system. You will not notice any changes.

4e699130e92374eb633fac2c40623e07079ff557.text: The system now checks for an active subscription using the actual subscription record instead of the payment tier label. This prevents the account from incorrectly showing as active during cancellation or downgrade events.

f72b036ddb7d80a82f8bda8c1ff95baeb8e2a7a4.text: The startup process no longer waits for a confirmation from the server before continuing. This prevents the application from freezing if that confirmation is delayed or missing. You might notice the app opens slightly faster, especially if network conditions are poor.

92c08115233436487f5e0c757584e36e585e3b3e.text: The usage page now shows the exact overage price from the billing system instead of guessing based on the plan. This affects paid subscribers who go over their monthly limit. They will see the correct cost per unit in their dashboard and command line warnings.

5ec8008e3f2dc755ccbe0c20a8f5726dd780eb62.text: The system no longer sends a fake request to the AI every time a new session starts. This stops a small, unnecessary background task that ran before any real work began. Regular users will not notice any difference in speed or results.

50abb8014679fde7dc7a28b430a3ee58407365aa.text: The system now marks blocked connections and usage limit hits as warnings instead of errors. This change affects internal support tools, making routine blocks easier to spot among critical failures. Users will see no difference in how the service works.

bd9eebfe97d8cca4befa261b1273103c61023748.text: The AI assistant can now read specific files directly instead of searching for them first. This change is internal and affects the assistant's behavior when you ask about code you already know the name of. You might notice the assistant answers questions about known files slightly faster and more accurately.

2e7608915470d28ef8d2536a86e8f989e144ee8e.text: The program stopped recording a log of every communication with the payment service. This is a small cleanup that does not change how payments work. You would see fewer messages on the internal screens used by the support team, but nothing else looks different.

b5fb776d443920e4599793053740e78b2aedc92c.text: The system now fetches web pages through a third-party service that cleans up the text before saving it. This change is live for the internal tooling that handles web scraping. Instead of receiving the raw website code, the system gets a simplified version, which may make the stored text easier to read.

b948c09a26677459a8d19276fe7d9de812dda5dd.text: When the assistant searches for files, it now sends a short summary of the request instead of the entire response to check for updates. This helps the system accurately determine which files have changed without getting confused by extra text. The change is active now but only affects internal search processes.

ad3166ef0dcd02f0400e70725d4c15421e9b3888.text: The software reverted a recent update to its login system, returning to an older, more stable version of the underlying tool. This change affects the core authentication process for the application. Users might notice improved reliability or a fix for a specific issue that occurred after the previous update was installed.

de1deda5fcc4f75b0a204420af8d4e2b456ffad0.text: The system now uses a simpler, consistent method to find relevant files for the AI assistant, removing complex, variable logic based on request order. This internal change affects how quickly and accurately the assistant retrieves context, potentially making responses slightly more predictable, though users won't notice a direct change in behavior or interface.

f878fa88123182167052cb74de2219258f481500.text: The daily usage limits for anonymous visitors and free accounts were reduced to 500 and 1,000 actions respectively. This change is live now. Affected users will notice they can perform fewer tasks before hitting the cap compared to previous days.

5aab0b5ee5902370cefb69d340f6cb2b3dd1bbb7.text: The application refreshed its background connections to the database. This update happens automatically and fixes minor internal issues. You will not notice any changes in how the application looks or behaves.

b6989659f72b2ed4413dee950d65349d9b285aa9.text: A small update added 'install' to a list of commands that the AI assistant ignores. This means if you type 'install' into the terminal, the assistant won't try to process or intercept it, allowing the command to run directly on your computer as normal.

71ff7075391839932d1a0d6a1f67b08f1735527e.text: The team updated the tool that helps the website talk to its storage system. This keeps the site running smoothly and fixes small issues behind the scenes. You will not notice any changes in how the site looks or works.

5514885ebd100eb0e72038ff28c838e8292d9afe.text: A small internal fix ensures the site's top banner loads reliably for visitors arriving via specific links. Previously, this banner could cause errors for these visitors, but now it displays correctly without interruption.

3635d45bfa58833e890c17e39ea0356fe20abfb2.text: We removed unnecessary instructions from the code that builds the website's main frame. This change is internal and only affects how the site is built. Users will not notice any difference, but the website may load slightly faster due to cleaner code.

775edca1c2cdbb94c609647669c4396352731a8f.text: The referral page now shows a person's real name instead of their username when someone uses a valid referral code. This affects people viewing referral links. It is live today and is a small internal fix.

3f7dbde8192229ec2652690ed021d648bb446b51.text: The website now displays a new customer quote from Dexter Horthy. Readers will see his photo, title, and statement about using the service six days a week. A broken link on an existing testimonial was also fixed.

7a5ea0107fbda2f103b168d84e3fe66226a75c4e.text: The enterprise pricing page now states that custom credit limits require a minimum of three team members. This text update affects only enterprise plan viewers. Visitors see the added requirement next to the credit limit feature.

ef308a3c78412bbd507e9887fd1667b574eaed7c.text: After signing in, the app now checks remaining credits right away. People who use the tool after logging in will see their current balance immediately. A temporary warning message during this check was disabled.

25d4a8e48e68260979c0602f009c58de0537c73f.text: Developers added internal safety checks to ensure text formatting rules work correctly. These tests verify that extra decorative symbols are removed from copied code snippets. No visible changes will occur for users.

87cc3bdea5ceaab4fc2c5da6cce3032ac7da21e6.text: The internal assistant no longer stops working just because it hit a fixed step limit. If it needs more steps to finish a task, it now keeps going automatically. This change is internal, so customers will not see any new buttons or screens.

2393cf1d3365ad1d84271aaf7f854be2e6af0e9f.text: The software now automatically skips temporary system files and hidden configuration folders when scanning project directories. This prevents the tool from wasting time processing unnecessary data. The change is active and runs quietly in the background without altering visible results.

be867f7cc267dac46c3901eda5875596d8304fa3.text: The assistant's internal instructions were adjusted to ensure the software correctly identifies which parts of the conversation should be saved for quick access later. This is a minor technical cleanup that does not change how the assistant responds or behaves. Users will not notice any difference in the service.

5b94e8f906453756aa040429716834383a4d93d1.text: The default preview image shown when the site is shared on social media was replaced with a smaller version. This change is live now. Visitors might notice slightly faster loading of these preview images, but the visual content remains largely the same.

a340fce4c6b6402295c0a3cbd45f16ed425c4402.text: The team added an automated check to ensure the system can correctly apply multiple changes to a single file at once. This is an internal quality control measure and does not change any features for end users. You would not notice any difference in how the application behaves.

01e2d7e1acc1a0c22f92063232afdfa6708878fa.text: The system now checks file paths to ensure they point inside the project folder, rejecting any that try to escape or use full computer addresses. This change is live for the internal tooling. If a file request was previously ignored because of a bad path, it might now be handled correctly or rejected more clearly, preventing silent errors when the assistant tries to read or edit files.

c4bf385ecf319f2a9da8b77ebb8f9779d05df37f.text: The assistant now avoids starting background tasks that run indefinitely, such as web servers. This applies to all internal agent sessions. Users might notice fewer stuck conversations where the assistant waits forever for a command to finish.

5f66481bc140904bb2b7f8133fd371ecc1983cb2.text: The AI assistant now receives a clear message when no files are selected for context, preventing it from guessing or hallucinating missing data. This small update ensures the tool understands the current state is empty, leading to more accurate responses when starting new tasks without file attachments.

0b9b8fd1a297f41f85a9a65c0ae3246190d34f57.text: The pricing page now sends visitor data to a new, correct marketing campaign. This change is live and affects only visitors who clicked a specific LinkedIn ad. The company sees more accurate ad performance data, but visitors see no visual difference.

697f570e52aa3b07a5b8d6987a1913c23ce7c3c1.text: After paying, customers now land on a page that confirms their new credit limit instead of the pricing page. This small fix ensures paid users immediately see their updated usage allowance.

f21fac01d4c9831c4e968b03e7282b08415c3253.text: The website now records which marketing campaign led to a payment by keeping that source label on the page shown after checkout. This helps the internal team see which ads work, but customers will not notice any change in how they pay or what they see.

732906174af2edd05627bf13c4b9ea43b7a56b67.text: The website stopped sending visitor details to LinkedIn when someone clicks the upgrade button. This affects only people who arrived via LinkedIn ads. They will not see any difference on the site, but LinkedIn will no longer record these specific clicks as conversions.

43ed770f045a64d251db3d3c9319bb1d937c7f38.text: A small tracking snippet was added to the bottom of the website. This tool helps the marketing team measure how many people arrive from LinkedIn ads. Visitors see no change on the screen, and the data collection only activates if the marketing team fills in a specific account ID in the background settings.

b175b35b1b9a671dc20bcd4817ca721bb2fba917.text: The payment system now keeps tracking details from LinkedIn ads when a user completes a purchase. This ensures the company can accurately measure which ads led to sales. Users won't see any difference on the website, but the business gets better data on ad performance.

7ed1ff4eafe0b4d2989120f08f663f77da6616e7.text: The system now tags visitors coming from LinkedIn ads with a standard label so marketing can count them correctly. It also directs buyers to a specific thank-you page after they pay. This is a small internal cleanup, so the customer experience stays the same.

c24ba8efe2c06ba215111e206c351f49a5129293.text: The system now removes extra blank spaces from the end of its replies before saving them. This affects the internal history that helps the assistant remember the conversation. A person would not notice any visual difference, but the assistant avoids getting confused by invisible leftover spaces.

ec0f0960ae0e556b39166323f9965f11c3b58d7e.text: When visitors click pricing links, their visit is now recorded for marketing analytics only if they arrived via a specific LinkedIn ad. This small internal update removes a tracking code from the web address, so visitors see a cleaner URL, while ensuring the ad campaign's effectiveness is accurately measured.

6a576126c7f8988ea1cab4927ec78bc55740d91c.text: The system now automatically removes decorative formatting wrappers from the text returned by the AI assistant. This ensures that when the assistant rewrites a file, the result is clean code without extra symbols. This internal fix is live and improves reliability, though you will not see a new button or visual change.

6314fa1ed7c3df329d94e0685d9894e9bb73a2f0.text: A small internal rule was added to the assistant's instructions. It prevents the assistant from accidentally running a tool when it is simply describing what tools are available. This change is live today and improves reliability for all conversations.

cb97eb063b233b3e46290c91d4b05fbe64b6242a.text: The system now checks if any files are actually relevant to a request before trying to read them. If no files are found, it skips adding blank or confusing text to the message sent to the AI. This keeps the AI's instructions clean and prevents it from getting confused by empty information. Users might notice slightly better responses when asking questions that don't involve specific files.

b380c24195f43b3a6cc9e8819cae75f6ed8d4cb4.text: The command-line tool now shows the number of credits used for a request, but only if that request cost more than one credit. This helps users see the cost of larger tasks, while hiding the message for trivial requests that cost one credit or less.

ad7784faa1da0e75ead84ada8b6809e0116c0a2e.text: The text-based logo shown when opening the internal command-line tool was updated to reflect the new brand name. This change affects only the visual display at startup. Users will see 'Codebuff' instead of 'Manicode' in the colorful block-letter graphic, but all underlying functions remain exactly the same.

f85464740b55160de057dcd39b8c6aa512be4d07.text: The system now skips checking the technical descriptions of external tools to avoid false errors. This change is internal and affects only the backend service. Users will notice no difference in how the application works.

bf51ae2f197d6b22892722ae73c176e9f1740d91.text: The assistant now stops searching for extra files to read after it finishes a task, like running a command. This prevents it from using outdated information in its next step. This is an internal fix for the AI's memory system. You will not see any visible changes.

1aaf38e06dc8e559f842ebd7cd28034b6db24ce5.text: A new quote from Dennis Beatty was added to the website's testimonials section. This change is currently live and appears on the public site. Visitors scrolling through the reviews will now see his praise for the terminal-based coding tool alongside other customer feedback.

5e74c44b22a766a6d7fb72f43f2fab042ed90b2d.text: The assistant now shows a cleaner list of files it is reading. Instead of a long, messy line, it displays a short bulleted list for the first few files and groups the rest together. This small change only affects how the text looks on the screen; the actual work of finding and reading the files happens exactly the same way.

6ac89cc4c5269bcdf2c51ed4b142e2f180fd0675.text: The assistant now ignores the word 'break' when it appears in a list of commands it is supposed to skip. This is a small internal adjustment that ensures certain actions are handled correctly without stopping the process unexpectedly. There is no visible change for you today; this simply helps the system understand instructions more accurately behind the scenes.

43dfad61c5c5f6b528c6ec9499014cea069ef82d.text: The system's internal instructions were clarified to explicitly forbid using absolute file paths, requiring only paths relative to the project root. This change affects the backend logic that guides the AI assistant's file retrieval process. Users will not notice any immediate difference, as this is a minor internal adjustment to improve accuracy and prevent errors.

fefd759f6be743da29d8bd9d89bc578c6c96cad4.text: The instructions for setting up the coding assistant were rewritten to be clearer. New users will see simpler steps for installing the tool and better tips for fixing permission errors. The feature list now highlights that the assistant can edit multiple files and run tests automatically. This is an internal documentation update, so the software itself did not change.

42c28d63b9490ba5f63f5b1f616e7b8fd090d50d.text: The system now automatically sends credit usage data to the billing provider for paying customers. This happens in the background after a message is saved, so the user will not see any delay or change in the chat interface. The billing provider uses this data to track how many credits have been used for the current billing period.

26092ae9a09c3e9e0f587f3ab06c17da484a208a.text: The file reader now understands full folder addresses. It converts them to simple names before checking rules. This stops errors when someone asks for a file using a complete address.

c9371008d553ea874e6929ca416ae24f7f6e6e4f.text: The assistant now ignores the 'where' command when running tasks, matching how it already ignores 'which' and 'who'. This prevents errors when the assistant tries to locate files using that specific command. The change is active immediately.

dc707c40a6af0680e0464e97c6c7a59e9e0c33b6.text: The system now more accurately detects when a user asks for a task to continue until completion, rather than misinterpreting simple requests like 'try again.' This prevents the assistant from incorrectly assuming it should keep working indefinitely. The change is live and applies to all conversations.

046534f3a22f24c03f03efbe5a65976900efcc49.text: The system now cleans up the internal notes it uses to decide if a task is finished, removing leftover formatting symbols. It also sends these decision notes directly to the screen so people can see exactly why the assistant stopped or continued. This change is live for internal tools and makes the assistant's reasoning clearer during long tasks.

2c55be5648921d8bc2b0803a95969e3ab4941e70.text: The assistant now checks if a task is fully finished before stopping. If work remains, it receives specific notes on what to do next instead of a generic prompt. This small internal update helps the assistant keep working until the request is completely satisfied.

3250b8c1712f68ac2ae74ae1cec1a2cf9237178f.text: The AI assistant now follows clearer rules for checking its own work. It must first look for specific instructions on how to verify changes before running any tests, and it skips these checks only for very small, confident edits. This internal update improves the assistant's reliability without changing what you see on screen.

cca3ced75e6f2223a2a173f5d75bf74ea48c99cd.text: A small internal update helps support staff see more detail when checking why a task might have been skipped. This change affects only the hidden logs that engineers read to solve problems. Regular users will not notice any difference.

fbf01f1f57948f9d4ab0fbf313b878b0d7b08ea4.text: The system now automatically removes blank sections from the instructions it receives when a list of files is empty. This small internal fix ensures the assistant gets cleaner data without confusing empty spaces. Users will not see any visible changes on their screen, as this improves how the underlying tool processes information behind the scenes.

91988bf6a74263671795cca88d37661d256f1847.text: The coding assistant no longer automatically runs error checks after making small changes. It now only performs these checks if a specific project file explicitly asks for them. This makes the assistant faster and less noisy for routine edits, while still allowing thorough verification when needed.

43e03e58db80c99614d63ea0dc1971258af72603.text: The system stopped removing a special end-of-message marker and filtering out empty text blocks during conversation processing.
