This internal cleanup change affects how raw responses are handled before display, though users will likely notice no visible difference in chat output.

66006c3871aec152096f4f48fa655af7b3d66ab2.text: The assistant now asks for supporting files, like test scripts and settings, separately from the main code to make sure it sees the full picture before making changes. It also forces a check after edits to confirm nothing broke, unless the change is tiny. This is an internal update that improves how the assistant handles complex tasks, but you won't see a new button or screen.

e5f85d760ee77cd7cfeb10a2489c36ae3746ae96.text: The checkout page now shows two separate charges: a fixed monthly fee for the basic service and a second line for extra usage beyond the included amount. This change requires a new setup key to be added to the system's hidden configuration files. Until that key is added, the checkout page will fail to load.

37b631589d5a5ccb928d9f0409f998cb352f08a4.text: A small internal fix ensures the system stops checking Twitch messages as soon as it finds one it can use. This prevents the tool from wasting time reprocessing old or duplicate notes. You will not notice any changes in the app, but the background assistant will handle incoming messages more efficiently.

67dc1947f10464791cd5cfd8f5ff6f81f88cf1fe.text: The pricing page now clearly states that the free plan does not allow extra usage beyond its limit, while paid plans explicitly list their overage rates. It also updated the estimate for a busy hour of work to a flat 500 credits instead of a range. These changes are live and affect anyone viewing the subscription options.

640ba7053b1769172a2c81bc5a4e61c6d199914f.text: The system now skips saving updates for files that contain placeholder text instead of real changes. This prevents accidental overwrites or errors when a file hasn't actually been modified. Users won't see this directly, but it stops the system from trying to save empty or fake updates.

09348fe3cd58008666ef4263b4a53dc1607245bf.text: If the website failed to load your referral code or details, the page would previously crash when you tried to go back. Now, it displays a friendly error card instead. This small internal fix applies to all logged-in users on the referral pages and is live today.

846073e11af5a585d774bca1a3c19e05b4738828.text: The pricing page now lists 'Pre-buy credits' as a feature for the custom tier. This is a text-only update that affects anyone viewing that specific plan's details. They will see the new line item describing the ability to purchase credits in advance.

8908de22dfeacdba150a8d59632233bfc1f733a2.text: The picture that automatically appears when someone shares a link was replaced with a clearer version. This change is live now. Anyone sharing the link will see a sharper preview image, though nothing else about the page changes.

dfe8b52458c5aabadb0a4f4b72070b5dba409e1d.text: The system now reads change instructions even when they lack a final blank line. This fixes a small internal bug in how updates are processed. Users may see fewer failed updates if the system previously struggled with these specific instructions.

3806bde8ed7f61bc6a883e71389ee1b0f4d56e06.text: The Twitch chat listener now checks for commands every 15 seconds instead of every 60 seconds. It only acts on messages starting with a greater-than symbol. Viewers typing commands in the stream chat will see the bot respond much faster.

497e275e19f1831cf5ef9c8761ec3de9e7d5cbeb.text: Internal instructions for the AI assistant were updated to require a specific verification step after every code change. This affects only the internal team and the assistant's behavior, not the end-user experience. No visible changes will occur for current users.

0f517782fec99400b1314809cdeed2c69482aba7.text: The assistant now skips searching through messy, temporary files created by Python programs, such as cache folders and virtual environments. This change is live immediately for anyone using the tool to analyze Python projects. Users will notice the assistant responds faster and avoids getting confused by irrelevant technical clutter when answering questions about their code.

e33f588367b6276f2875377d232c39d6a19a00ee.text: The team fixed a small internal setup issue in the live chat server. This change only affects the program's internal structure and does not alter how messages are sent or received. Regular users will notice no difference in speed, features, or reliability.

21ee88b1ac1218481753ee1128c5c696262f3c5c.text: The system now keeps blank lines at the top and bottom of code edits when applying them. This fixes rare cases where an edit failed because the system trimmed spaces it needed to find the exact spot in the file. The change is live for internal file editing.

63de78d54dc6a38f5f9cdbe85e9a497b21a65a30.text: The assistant's ability to recognize and execute typed commands has been refined to reduce false positives and catch more errors. This change is live today. Users may notice the assistant is slightly more accurate when interpreting short command-like phrases and will receive clearer feedback if a command fails.

03eea8e272e4d0801cc8b073520d6450f844deab.text: The image shown when the website is shared on social media has been updated. This change is live now. People who share a link to the site will see the new picture in their posts, but nothing else on the website changes.

fb6fdb5a187b1f6a275891fb52ee500752293a59.text: The assistant now remembers all the edits it makes during a task, not just the final ones. This means the summary you see at the end of a request will show every change, even those made while the assistant was using its tools.

4dc401072f493d4382d4dd4e2ef16a3704e43545.text: The AI assistant now checks its own work by running safety tests after making changes. If those tests fail, the assistant fixes the errors before finishing. This update is internal and live today, so users may see fewer broken results.

ae02bac00074bbaa7c79f2b30f2a96df08a4a0a7.text: The assistant now stops reading command results after ten thousand characters. This prevents the system from wasting resources on extremely long outputs. Users will notice that very lengthy command results are cut short and marked as truncated.

48495e6d349bce9ca157754a142057a0df415c5c.text: A small internal fix stops the system from trying to use an extra step when creating file changes. This step was causing errors, so it was turned off. You will not see any difference in the final result, but the process is now stable.

b537be76793649924a221925df4d883c24d4ec36.text: The small gift box picture next to the 'refer a friend' message at the top of the page is now hidden on phones. This gives the text more room to read clearly on small screens. The picture still shows up on computers.

32813dc7f27196da7dffc6595e489c1d44cb3a67.text: The assistant now rewrites a file entirely if it accidentally leaves behind its internal editing instructions. This prevents the final document from showing messy, leftover markup. The fix applies automatically when such errors occur, so you will see cleaner output.

adc5fe5a106b2a1103a77bfa05fd8746c5e60820.text: The AI assistant can now write twice as much text in a single response. This change is live for internal systems. Staff using the tool will see longer answers before the system cuts off the message.

6156588518166800a73786c8a3cb58f5b7099066.text: The pricing page now forces all plan cards to have a uniform header height and aligns their content evenly. This small visual fix ensures the price and feature lists line up neatly across all four tiers, removing the jagged appearance caused by differing text lengths.

eee8d487422f09b3cba1d221008952862d923d26.text: The pricing page now displays four plan options side-by-side instead of three. For the Pro Plus plan, the price for extra credits dropped from $0.95 to $0.90 per 100, but it no longer includes a personal account manager or custom software connections. This change is live today.

ace7e6a4f1fc2ca19e4bfaf9ebe711a3226b0918.text: A new 'Pro Plus' plan now appears on the pricing page for $500 per month. This plan includes 55,000 credits, priority support, and a dedicated account manager. Instead of a direct buy button, customers must click 'Contact Sales' to sign up.

129ec1deb8773872b1b517ed185f193b0f3cbae8.text: The gift icon in the referral banner is now larger on mobile screens. This makes the icon easier to see when the text wraps to multiple lines. The change applies to all mobile users viewing the banner.

027d0e963ef82bf0831d72b4686b28a65450f6f9.text: The program now gives clearer instructions when an update is needed. Instead of just saying an update is required, it tells you the exact command to type to fix the problem. This helps people who use the tool know exactly what to do next.

a8ed9b01a4b3e0e8d6fe78d3454c7b30c757fc90.text: The pricing page now lists a 'Team' plan at $99/month plus usage instead of a custom 'Enterprise' option. The Free plan label is shorter, and the top-tier plan button now opens an email to support rather than a sales form. Support text promises access to both email and Discord, not just one. These changes are live for everyone visiting the pricing page today.

7217444eefb125db1e27e9bb2c870058b4e9cd12.text: A 'News' link was added to the website's top and bottom menus, pointing to an external news page. The bottom menu was also made more compact by reducing its height and text size. Visitors to the homepage will see the new link and notice the smaller footer, but no functionality changed.

d0367fdc6b85d6477c1a7d3b8dbd5acbffc1566d.text: A small internal change tells the note-writing assistant to keep existing knowledge when updating a file. It affects people who rely on automatically maintained knowledge notes. If they compare an updated note with an older one, they should see new information added rather than old information disappearing.

69fd0e1a55ce069874dbffb155652662af586c35.text: The website's help section now shows only one answer at a time. Clicking a new question automatically closes the previous one, keeping the page tidy. This change is live and affects anyone viewing the site.

4429fe5b49d617b1ce922f915e0d9c71c8e259f8.text: The system now removes extra formatting symbols that sometimes appear around file text, ensuring files are saved cleanly without unwanted decorations. This internal fix affects how rewritten files are processed behind the scenes. Users will not notice any visual change, but saved files will no longer contain stray symbols at the beginning or end.

f565d6738b61d650acc5adda4143780e03f0c314.text: The internal tool that records lessons from code changes now requires a much higher standard before writing anything down. It will only save information if it is broadly useful and cannot be guessed from the code itself. This reduces clutter in the team's notes, making it easier to find genuinely helpful context.

e5ab17ce596a729cbf493a2b5bc31c3b0272a2d5.text: The help guide was updated to explain how the assistant handles your project's context files. It now clarifies that the assistant will never create a new context file if one is missing, but it will automatically update existing ones. This change only affects the text in the help section and does not change how the assistant behaves.

55f715ecef90771744be1918df1edb18c31b36ed.text: Internal cleanup renamed a leftover 'Manicode' label to 'Codebuff' in the backend server's status message. This is a small, non-functional change that aligns old naming with the current brand. No user-facing features or behaviors changed.

72eca15260568914ae982b8496e70b236f034245.text: The team added new internal checks to ensure the tool correctly handles file edits that remove entire sections or leave them blank. This change affects only the software's testing process and does not alter how the application works for anyone. You will notice no difference in the product.

bf3e3979338128284676dbc17e8a39c9c2dc758c.text: The assistant now checks if you want it to keep working without stopping after a few steps. If you say yes, it skips the normal pause and keeps going. This change is live and applies to all internal chats.

d4e6b4852e4e6edd5489dfe378c2b1d43a0b5bc1.text: The system stopped saving full instructions for the search tool in its internal records to keep logs clean. Only developers reading these technical logs would notice less clutter. The feature itself works exactly the same for everyone.

b7a9877b2311466d90c85fb9e759477ed7e45166.text: A small internal housekeeping change. When a developer uses an AI coding assistant to work on the project, that assistant creates temporary files to keep track of its own settings and history. The project is now told to automatically ignore those temporary files so they never accidentally get saved into the shared codebase. Nothing visible changes for anyone outside the development team.

38e712ea42aa0fc6423ae59e49431d19cc57b69e.text: A small internal update adds a startup message to a test version of the API server. This change only affects developers running the mock project locally. They will see a rocket emoji and text appear in their console when the server starts, confirming it is initializing. This feature is not live for general users.

f7b709cdf6a572c576b559f6de33581711713221.text: The help page text now clearly explains which AI tools are used and how chat history is saved. Small wording tweaks fix grammar and make the answers easier to read. This update is live for anyone visiting the help section.

70b081956b9b41a76b49af35e29d3fe0c2226166.text: The assistant now says 'Reading additional files' instead of 'Reading the following files' when it checks new documents. This update fixes a glitch where the list of files shown could be wrong or empty. The change is active for internal staff using the backend system.

bed66e77fbce2642b9586d28017b0cc9e65423f2.text: Small internal update to the help page. Links now look plain until you hover, showing an underline. Some answers changed to guide people to the help command.

932205a6fe86d93ac12502bae9e1435518e48ed4.text: The assistant now checks only newly added files for updates, ignoring those it already knew about. This internal adjustment affects how the system builds its context list, ensuring it does not redundantly re-read existing files. There is no visible change for the end user; the assistant simply processes file information more efficiently behind the scenes.

e10cc509557fa80cce701c3879e05100b660a2ed.text: The support contact listed in the setup guide changed from the old company name to the new one. This only affects people who copy that guide to start a fresh installation. They will see the new email address in their instructions.

a509a507ed7c12dc97c0f88b5e3329da795f898c.text: The referral banner now states that the credit bonus is awarded per month, not as a one-time reward. This clarifies for people using the web interface that the benefit is recurring. The change is live and affects only the text displayed in the banner.

65d4068daf78f248f98a532fb84d6589fb5a6bcc.text: Visitors typing the old web address are now instantly sent to the correct new site without any loading delay or visual glitch. Previously, the browser had to load a page and then move the user, which sometimes caused a brief flash or warning. This correction is live and ensures a smoother transition for anyone using the outdated link.

87511b7f2a9d3851292c3c8f4c07eef68801a7a8.text: The internal step that prepares generated file text no longer removes the extra lines that sometimes appear around that text. It now uses the text as it comes, assuming those extra lines are already gone. The change is live; if those extra lines ever remained, they would now appear in the final file.

3e48ea292cee05fa9dba0ea9918a6595a698be57.text: The assistant's internal name changed from Manicode to Codebuff. This update affects only the text labels inside the software, such as welcome messages and documentation, with no change to how the tool actually works. If you look closely at the assistant's responses or help pages, you will now see the new name, but your ability to use the features remains exactly the same.

a4474e2319f10b239ca7eb77d3c3951bf776bebb.text: The website now displays Shardool Patel's job title as 'Founder & CTO' instead of 'Founder, CTO'. This change affects only the text shown on his specific testimonial card. Visitors will see the updated punctuation if they look at that section.

a2db8442c2c5681ec52f68db50fdbfbe6ae772c7.text: The homepage text describing the tool was shortened. Visitors now see a cleaner sentence that removes repeated words and a specific mention of how they type instructions. This change is live.

895c960f43599afb5d94d40394d195afcf484601.text: The assistant now checks for a special list of files you want it to ignore. If you create this list, those files will be left out of the information sent to the AI. This helps keep your private or irrelevant documents hidden from the assistant.

35ae9a125fe5c06ccf5c5ba48278d93b9d97785c.text: A small internal update ensures that visitors typing the old website address are automatically sent to the current main site. This affects only people using the outdated link; they will see the correct page without noticing the switch. The change is live now.

54a0a6383bea6eb29ea54463dcfb86114f3f7731.text: When the assistant lists extra information it wants to save, it now uses a clear sentence instead of hidden computer markers. This small internal update makes the output easier to read for anyone watching the assistant's responses.

ceeb0875f009cb76f56d48c86a60b758531f188d.text: The main page text was updated to explain that you can edit code and run commands using natural language, rather than just saying it is faster. This change is live and applies to everyone visiting the homepage. You will notice the new wording immediately when you look at the subtitle under the main title.

00e2b84f8dee82e7e2ca7040dd61d6e0cc62be38.text: A small internal fix corrected the email address listed in the instructions for sending feedback. Anyone reading those instructions will now see the correct contact address instead of an old or incorrect one. This change is live immediately.

53c1d8efd300d6bd90abb2faa10ba8fb327e9304.text: This internal update fixes technical setup issues for developers using Windows, ensuring their tools find necessary files correctly. It also updates the project's name and organization labels. Regular users will not see any changes or notice anything different.

03e4a0e7c07570061e5f645e0d26ba6a7f2dec73.text: The website's description of its features changed to be more specific. Visitors will now see headlines about understanding entire projects and working directly in the command line, rather than vague claims about editing multiple files. This is a visual update only; the software's actual abilities did not change.

915ccbd3ffcae904caf1d4e80e08dd9090af99a7.text: The pricing page now labels the free plan specifically for signed-in users. It also clarifies that one hour of heavy work uses 500 to 1000 credits. Visitors see this updated text immediately.

1367890292c8ed494196706ac6dd0e5b0872d06b.text: The text suggested for copying on the referral redemption page was updated to match the current product name. People using this page will now see the correct command instead of the old one.

42c471aa23438ba9b24ef93ccad939e15823dd54.text: The assistant now shows any knowledge updates it finds directly in its reply. This helps people who ask the assistant to look up information, as they can see exactly what was added or changed without checking a separate list. The change is live today.

f76a0a674d943feae9d7ede7805bf532b60ce4e7.text: The free trial credit limits were lowered. Anonymous users now get 750 credits instead of 1,000, and free registered users get 1,500 instead of 2,500. Paid users are unaffected. This change is live.

c1575f66a59c713f50c78b558ab8f52d8043dfb9.text: Customer testimonials on the main page now show a small round profile photo next to the person's name. This applies to the three featured quotes from Sarah, Michael, and Alex. Visitors will see these faces alongside the text today.

e26fcadca4ed9e5c89a5e1e2fe88c708d8ceaf57.text: Fixed broken website code that caused the site to fail loading. This affects anyone trying to visit the homepage. You would now see the page load correctly, including a note explaining that old reviews mentioning the previous brand name refer to the same product.

24ffbc551c15b8370fae243054251787e876ce0e.text: The description of the tool on the referral page was updated to clarify that it is a command-line tool. The new text compares the tool to a talented junior engineer who understands the code structure. This change affects visitors to the referral page, who will now see this more specific explanation instead of the previous general description.

a913dd5159bedd88adfe1dfcc3aaebaf0e488150.text: The website's main page now shows a different video when you click 'Watch a Demo' and uses slightly clearer wording. The page where you claim referral rewards was also redesigned to look cleaner and easier to read. These updates are live immediately for anyone visiting the site.

fe2f1af665f8f3b5ba7451a05754d720c6e13a16.text: The assistant now remembers the latest version of any file you edit, even if you hadn't opened it before. This fixes a bug where it ignored recent changes to unread files. You might notice the assistant giving more accurate answers about your code without needing to open every file first.

9fcb8e63f86abfef961566aa7e3b74a402ec44de.text: The help guide for the AI coding assistant was updated to reflect its new name, Codebuff. It now warns that the tool can automatically run computer commands while working, and lists a new email address for feedback. This is a small internal change; only people reading the guide will notice the updated instructions.

f86d9a6e05a6e4eb5cd7fa04a20a6837795aaf50.text: The tool now calls itself Codebuff instead of Manicode. This change affects people who use the command-line version to write code. If you look at the welcome messages, help text, or update instructions, you will see the new name. The old name no longer appears in the interface.

7f4a1ffd11ddda89e09f98e9d9c22019a308df3a.text: The company changed its name from Manicode to Codebuff. This update fixed the text on the main website, privacy policy, and terms of service pages to show the new name and correct web address. If you visit these pages, you will see 'Codebuff' instead of 'Manicode' everywhere, including the contact email and the button that copies the installation command.

7b26863a97693a9aa27f5d6bf59bca8a3279a310.text: The software's name changed from Manicode to Codebuff everywhere people see it. Visitors to the website and readers of the instructions will now see the new name, and anyone installing the tool must use the new command. The homepage also describes the main benefit as editing multiple files at once instead of just understanding code.

34cf7983623180c9e0045365263ebef11b7736c4.text: The system now uses a different AI model to process file updates, which speeds up the work. This change is internal and affects how the backend handles requests, but users will not see a visible difference in the interface.

e2e028fae06563f943db0b587224c5383c307da1.text: The link to the referral form now points to the new company web address. This affects people who open the referrals page and click the referral form. The change is live today, and they may see a slightly different web address, but the form itself works the same way.

748d8771e89c39953132547896e55c346d710a17.text: The AI assistant now introduces itself as Buffy instead of Mani. This is a minor internal branding change that does not alter how the assistant works or what it can do. You will only notice the new name when the assistant starts a conversation or references its own identity.

c431be6326ebdbecaf9b36efd4da59624377128c.text: The AI assistant now uses special commands when moving or deleting files to ensure these changes are properly recorded in the project's history. This small update affects the assistant's internal instructions and is active immediately. You might notice slightly more accurate file management during code refactoring tasks, though the visible behavior remains largely unchanged.

ca14c85607d18e1ad0018681c673836aa5e0ce90.text: The setup process now works on Windows computers. Developers using Windows can start the database without errors. Regular users see no change.

38709b23e80cdb95ef6ea6230e7db77d9cda8079.text: When the system fails to update a file, it now uses a different, cheaper AI model to fix it. This is an internal change, so users will not notice any difference.

86db77ee28f24762aa0a73040d65eac10a4203b5.text: A small internal update clarified how the system identifies which files to retrieve for a user's request. This change is live and affects the accuracy of the assistant's file selection. Users might notice slightly more relevant files being pulled into context, reducing confusion in the assistant's responses.

b11b9f06bc3a36da563f30984dff8e957fa2c978.text: The system now strictly instructs its AI assistant to write out an entire file when making changes, rather than just showing a small section. This affects internal users who rely on the assistant to update code files. If the assistant previously skipped parts of a file during an edit, it will now provide the complete, updated version.

21fdc209a42dc4541d73ee63d00ea515b19c8ca5.text: The command-line tool changed its name from manicode to codebuff. This is live now. Existing installations keep the old name and do not update automatically. New installations use the new name.

3c666803289ed5ed7cb9b58c0e8ac6500c783507.text: The website's tab icon has been refreshed to match the new logo. This visual update applies to all visitors. You will notice the new symbol appearing in your browser tab and bookmarks immediately.

3247e65412974a410f3d2681145e8bb7b3f10f7d.text: The 'Request limit increase' link now automatically fills in your email address when you click it. This change affects signed-in users who want to raise their referral limits. You will notice the email field is already populated, so you do not need to type it manually.

c4f1d8ec13d142b549a693c0adb3da11e4bbd525.text: The AI assistant now receives project files in a clearer format, so it can tell the most recent version of a document apart from older drafts. This reduces the chance of the assistant using outdated information when helping with a task. The change is live and applies to all conversations where multiple versions of the same file are present.

61978dc9e65d5549e0458e9aa2e5d2df4bf9951a.text: A small internal fix prevents the system from crashing when it tries to read a file that doesn't exist. This makes the assistant's responses more stable for everyone using the service.

b59a8ab8c6bdd0625e2088c8ccc199a7b541dcd5.text: The page where you invite others to sign up has updated wording and a moved link. The phrase 'Send this link' now reads 'Share this link', and the option to request extra invites moved from the top of the page to sit next to your current invite count. This is a small internal change that is live now.

114f246f470db549078f90abcb5f13fb97b8236f.text: The software's name changed from Manicode to Codebuff. This update is live and affects anyone visiting the website or reading its instructions. People will now see the new name everywhere, including the login page, help documents, and the commands used to install the tool on their computers.

c530833adc99de98bf2ff74b263145f33b35d9f8.text: The software that connects the application to its database was updated to a newer version across all parts of the system. This is an internal maintenance task, so there are no visible changes for users. The update ensures that different sections of the application use the same database connection tools, which helps prevent technical issues.

d0245347b3f5052039ffc6f8151c3f99212ec7bd.text: The system now strictly ignores file requests that use absolute paths, only accepting paths relative to the project root. This prevents errors when the tool tries to locate files. No visible change for users, but internal file lookups are more reliable.

557b21047f102e2923b51d2d3210518493a75844.text: The system now filters out empty file records before generating reports. This prevents errors when a file's content is missing or null. Users will not notice any visible changes, as this is an internal fix to improve stability.

e2c83ec90996cfda4d35246b2dc750aaec4057e9.text: The assistant now checks if requested files are inside the project folder and not hidden by ignore rules. If a file is outside the project or hidden, it returns a status marker instead of the file content. This protects against accidental or malicious attempts to read files outside the intended workspace.

c3593160eb31595ec0645c71cfa7895aba96f1d5.text: The system now uses a smaller, faster AI model to handle simple background tasks like preparing file requests and starting sessions. This switch makes those specific actions cheaper and quicker, though it costs slightly more per step than the previous tiny model. Users will notice no visible change in the final results, only a minor shift in the underlying cost accounting.

640a2011fe541a7b002611f82a384a91997a259c.text: The system now checks file paths before loading them to block requests that try to access folders outside the project. This prevents the assistant from crashing when given bad file addresses. Users will not see any change unless a previous error has stopped the assistant from working.

4555b46bb32251dae58cc4b889ce7640dd4dfbaf.text: The assistant now stops trying to track very large edits to a single file. If you change more than 8,000 characters at once, it will skip saving the details of that specific edit to keep messages manageable. This is a small internal adjustment to prevent performance issues during massive file rewrites.

d4c10cd1008c16f441222947fccdedcf7c2ac7f3.text: A small internal fix updates how referral rewards work. When someone successfully uses a referral code, the system now also removes the 'quota exceeded' block that might have been stopping them. This means people who were locked out because they ran out of credits can get back in right after earning a referral bonus.

627588ec121c731dab388632e09f78d8e9499574.text: The assistant now catches more types of command failures on Linux computers, matching the existing checks for Mac and Windows. This internal fix ensures the tool reports errors accurately regardless of the operating system. No visible change for end-users; error handling just became more reliable.

5abea6033162cfc7885d2d14e2dc94fbc97333e9.text: The assistant now correctly marks the end of file edits it creates. This small fix helps the system read the assistant's instructions properly. People using the tool to generate code files may see fewer errors.

c36de5f1a6d3fbce0773ba8602d26f0ea42a8635.text: The system now handles errors during knowledge file creation gracefully, logging issues instead of crashing. This change is internal and affects how the backend processes data, ensuring stability. Users will not notice any direct changes, as it improves reliability behind the scenes.

1326b4c6b1afaaba15273e5053137ec83049eaa8.text: The update tool now recognizes a specific way of installing software that it previously missed. This fix applies only to people using that installation method. They will now be able to update the tool successfully without seeing errors.

03f9e4b86210df1e98b0c3fb33fa0245ffcaab15.text: When a paying customer cancels their subscription, the system now recognizes the cancellation immediately, rather than waiting for the billing period to end. This change ensures the pricing page displays the correct renewal status and links for these customers. The update is live and affects only users who have actively cancelled their subscription.

ab177ae5ce5dbea15830c399b3611434a037a5f7.text: The cost for extra credits on the Pro plan increased from $0.90 to $0.95 per 100 credits. This change only affects the text shown on the public pricing page, not the actual billing system. Visitors will see the higher price when checking Pro plan details, but their actual charges remain unchanged until the billing system is updated.

09990fbfc577df08a4bc0861dbf9d31f3016735f.text: A small internal fix adjusts the bottom section of the pricing cards to stretch across the full width of the card. This change affects anyone viewing the pricing page. Visitors would notice that the buttons and text at the bottom of the pricing cards now align consistently with the rest of the card, rather than potentially appearing narrower or misaligned.

d1951f6fbc907fc35c25de9ece5056f25a2af2aa.text: The pricing page text now says a busy hour costs 500-1000 credits, replacing the old note about multi-hour sessions. This helps people plan budgets more accurately for heavy work. The change is live on the website.

146e09dd961e67875aae7396c526a17de639f321.text: The internal system stopped sending a specific speed limit instruction to its text-generating services. This applies only to the backend servers, not the user-facing app. You would notice nothing, as this is a small internal adjustment to how the servers talk to each other.

d8c9d999966f2921fd78bb495bbc37b25ae61729.text: Added tests for parsing code changes with unusual spacing. This ensures the tool accurately handles complex edits. No user-visible changes occurred.

b25566f45187d9a8415a76a3b19343f1c3ee8808.text: A small internal security update is live today. It prevents other websites from hiding our pages inside invisible frames, which stops a trick where people click on fake buttons that actually control our site. Users will not notice any change.

40be20c1a00bb2a2fc8134efacc594cebee87985.text: The update tool now checks how the assistant was installed to choose the right refresh command. This affects people who keep the tool inside a specific project folder rather than on their whole computer. They will see the update succeed instead of failing or changing the wrong copy.

d7f2d6ac64b8ec4c6fb4bdfe621697e07aecf5f0.text: The tool stopped fetching live web content from links found in knowledge notes. Users see only the text written in the note, not the website's current information. This change is active now.

021ff879220086cff042045d1106497a67e403ee.text: A small, internal change makes the command-line tool more forgiving of typing errors. It now ignores accidental spaces around typed commands and recognizes several shortened or misspelled versions of the word 'diff'. People using this tool will find it easier to see code changes without needing to type the exact command.

a807e38ba995ea368f26450df77562a85120aaf4.text: A small internal fix ensures that when the assistant creates a new file, it removes the extra lines used to mark code blocks in chat messages. This prevents those visual markers from being saved as actual text inside the file. Only the backend was changed, so the user interface remains the same, but files created by the assistant will now be cleaner.

50ca3f3ec7049f4cb081c369a7e8cdd36bd63e3f.text: People who have already paid for the higher tier will now see a 'cancel subscription' link on the pricing page. This link takes them directly to the payment provider's page to manage or stop their billing. The change is live for existing subscribers.

24c16b3a2476eacf23a71b3a290d0a4305387027.text: The update tool now correctly identifies which method to use when refreshing the software. Users will see a clearer message stating the specific tool being used for the update, followed by a shorter goodbye note upon completion. This is a minor internal fix that improves clarity without changing core functionality.

91139688c0e564d65a3d2258e5fe764085eb0e0c.text: The internal rulebook for the AI assistant was updated to require it to automatically check its own work for mistakes every time it makes a change. This ensures the assistant catches and fixes errors before presenting the final result to you. You might notice the assistant taking slightly longer to respond as it performs these checks, but the output will be more reliable.

57836c9ef17bf5436ea134b20014e5d357a4ba4e.text: The website's invitation banner and referral page now explicitly state the exact number of monthly credits both the inviter and the invited friend receive. The instructions on the referral page were also split into clearer sentences. This small text update is live immediately for anyone viewing these pages.

4dbefaa92d5935b8a805c0cb0cbafb904f541e91.text: The system previously waited briefly before sending a completion signal to your browser when a request failed, which sometimes caused the signal to be lost. This wait has been removed, so the completion signal is sent immediately. This internal fix ensures your browser correctly recognizes when a failed request has finished.

15f637a7185d2fb1c783715a175dcc83380d9b94.text: The system was updated to recognize the word 'look' as a command to ignore. This small internal change affects how the software handles that specific word in terminal inputs. If you type 'look' into a command line within the application, it will now be skipped instead of being processed as an instruction.

8389f1d1d064aa676d5d455714e291d1b012a534.text: A small internal update stops the AI assistant from permanently changing the project's starting location when it runs a navigation command. Only when you explicitly type a navigation command will the project's location actually move. You might notice the assistant staying in the original folder instead of moving into a subfolder after it tries to navigate there on its own.

8ca14540dc0c0a9f1a71a17f4bf08693e2b33308.text: The pricing page now correctly lists 'Custom integrations' only for the highest 'Custom' plan, not the standard tier. The 'Dedicated AI model' feature was removed from the Custom plan's list. This is a small internal text correction to match what each plan actually includes. Visitors to the pricing page will see this updated feature list.

505bf6edac0718d665628739101396a887fb6858.text: The assistant now correctly saves conversation history when it uses tools or prepares responses. Previously, these specific interactions were not recorded. This fix is live today for internal systems.

0c078bfdc22034cdc837719fc5f0f12cf585613e.text: Wording on the welcome screen, menu, and referral page now states that both the person sharing the link and the new user earn monthly bonus credits. The free credit limit and current usage count are shown exactly. Upgrade and referral prompts appear in green instead of yellow.

74fddbca36640c7007e6709ca39735bb52cf8e60.text: The command-line tool now remembers your specific device identifier instead of creating a new one each time you log in. This change affects only users who have previously authenticated with the tool. You would notice no visible difference, but the tool now handles your login session more consistently behind the scenes.

2f1b213d1a4583a370275a663b30caa7aba29c74.text: A small internal update fixes how the system creates new files when it receives partial instructions instead of full text. Previously, these instructions were ignored for new files, causing incomplete results. Now, the system correctly assembles the file content from those parts, ensuring new files appear with the intended text immediately.

9cd16ae0354363557c893960f676c2a03430b7ca.text: The main landing page text was updated to include the word 'faster' when describing how the tool edits code. This change applies to both mobile and desktop views. Visitors will see slightly different wording on the homepage, but the tool's actual speed or function remains unchanged.

5703126c1bcbb0de93b2ea9912b926d32ffa919b.text: The app now waits up to 30 seconds for a response from the server, instead of giving up after 10 seconds. This affects people using the live connection feature. If the server is slow to reply, the app will stay connected longer before trying to reconnect.

1f271671867dfba845970b18e6471adce4dc42ba.text: A small update fixed issues that prevented the website from building correctly. The support email address is now available for use across the site, and a typo in the referral limit message was corrected. Users will notice the referral page now displays the correct punctuation when they have reached their limit.

7a1efe5fcb6853b8b262c9ecddbf496d3d22272c.text: The application's default smart assistant engine was switched to a newer, more capable version released in October. This change is live immediately for all users interacting with the main chat interface. While the underlying technology improved, the visual interface and available features remain exactly the same.

d61954b5d65b66d860e35250dbe04ce786749da1.text: Freebuff now ignores the words 'please' and 'apply' if they appear as terminal commands. This prevents the system from trying to run them, which likely stops errors. The change is live for all users.

45869d40206f66ec7512d4a77c2c3ed5dbd2e0f8.text: The system now checks your login token directly against the database when you redeem a referral code, rather than using a general session check. This change is live today and affects anyone trying to use a referral code. You will not notice any difference in how the feature works, but the underlying verification method has changed.

1c50f5ee498e22fd579aebfe163af3bc497963b2.text: The system now waits only a short, calculated time for alternative code suggestions to arrive, rather than waiting for all of them. If a suggestion is too slow, the system ignores it and proceeds with the ones that finished on time. This change affects the internal generation process and is live today.

afa2739e2016b111b317f344820982ecb4850eb5.text: A small badge linking to the company's Product Hunt launch page was added to the main website. This change is live now. Visitors will see the new badge appear in the center of the homepage, and its colors will automatically match whether the site is in light or dark mode.

270a8f9b7f645a0209233fb4c19ed0b6bf94d6af.text: This small internal fix corrects how the tool handles missing commands. When a user types a command that does not exist, the tool now shows the standard error message directly. Previously, the tool might have incorrectly sent the request to the AI assistant instead of displaying the error.

9bd24bac82d19576e43dadf2f76cbd5053e9c85e.text: The AI assistant was told to stop guessing which version of a tool to use when adding new features. Instead, it now automatically fetches the newest available version, ensuring the software stays up-to-date and compatible.

95e461430a3db11de81d449e3326a017bec19889.text: The login page text was shortened to 'Login' and 'Continue to sign in to the Manicode CLI'. A playful note about phishing was removed. The button now correctly displays 'GitHub' with a capital H.

33f0e7ca14083cd03c663bd5d8c5fe3e919a2e7f.text: The landing page was updated to remove the old product name and highlight that you can edit code and run commands using plain language. The installation command was moved to the top of the page for easier access, while the bottom button now directs you to a free trial. These changes are live and apply to all visitors.

2a697a73f4f35675cc9ef569aa90414b862f6846.text: Developers renamed a hidden setting to clarify it skips both logging and history saving, and organized training data scripts into a shared folder. This internal cleanup affects only the engineering team's workflow; users will notice no changes in the application's behavior.

811d56ee00eb9a481adbe24e7cd2e514f4a81c47.text: The system now uses a newer version of the AI model to help create code updates for internal tools. This change is live today. It is a small internal update, so regular users will not notice any difference in how the software works.

84e14ee58ea24229f57dca4790018e5ab5c4df8c.text: The homepage layout was adjusted to remove extra space under the main title and fix the line breaks in the startup description. This is a minor visual tweak for website visitors, making the text appear more compact and aligned. No functionality changed, and the update is live on the site.

4ceead5ccce3f7a14182ea1ba0cb03894d15d676.text: The assistant now clearly separates code it wants to change from code it just wants to show you. If it shows code in a standard block, nothing changes in your files; if it uses a special edit format, the change happens immediately. This prevents accidental edits when the assistant is just explaining or displaying code snippets.

9e0ba44869f5e9a4e617bf207697154bd68a3105.text: A small internal fix prevents a background setup step from blocking the main connection if it fails. This affects the initial loading phase of the application. If the background setup encounters an error, the application now logs the issue and continues loading the interface instead of stopping or showing an error screen.

fc03f28466cca75c0c96f57614f36fafa4e505ab.text: The internal system that decides how to update files now accepts a small local edit if it simply believes that is the intent, rather than requiring strong certainty. This change affects only the automated code generation process and is live today. A non-programmer would notice nothing, as this is an internal logic adjustment.

fff10829091d6eb31ec593b2e4e293f37b2e549f.text: After signing in, people now see a line about earning monthly credits for inviting friends. The startup menu also shows updated examples for building features and integrations. This is a small internal text change, live today.

6ee165addf06f13c322b693b531062c554bbe1e0.text: A small internal update changed the wording of the referral message shown in the command line tool. People who use this tool will now see the exact number of credits they earn per month for each friend who signs up, instead of a vague promise of 'more credits'.

11f6aed905d7e5640b03567d78e83e5669a40b32.text: The homepage now displays the official Y Combinator logo instead of just text. Visitors will see this new image, and the description of the tool now consistently uses the name 'Manicode'.

99fa7895e91da94dbd8c8171655f7252ef526b8f.text: The system now ignores internal data when saving conversation records. Staff reviewing support logs will no longer see clutter from background processes. This helps them find actual customer messages faster. The update is live.

77a1ee5ba552df96ac94cf69ede92c2f391f0e4c.text: The system now uses a single, specific account for its AI service instead of randomly switching between two. This change is live immediately and applies to all internal requests. Non-programmers will notice no direct difference in the interface, but the service will consistently use the updated account to handle more traffic.

022c717dea34c02b76b59227b08cdfe557339712.text: A hidden setting that forced a specific tool version was removed from the project configuration. This change fixes a conflict that was confusing an internal assistant. The adjustment applies only to the main project file and is live now.

fb3e26bdf23087b7bb3f017afb39134eca8d6233.text: The cost for extra usage beyond the monthly limit on the Pro plan increased from fifty cents to ninety cents for every hundred additional units. This change is live now. Only Pro subscribers will see this higher rate when they exceed their included allowance.

bcdfbf51858dea9839d99351f65c8ca9d98a68e2.text: The 'Community support' text on the Free plan pricing page is now a clickable link that takes visitors directly to the Discord server. This change affects potential customers viewing the free tier, making it easier for them to join the community for help without needing to search for the link separately.

25ebdc54239630ac0679ccb4d869b548c5e738a6.text: The picture shown when a website link is shared on social media has been updated. This small change ensures that the correct image appears in preview cards instead of an old one. People sharing the link will now see the newer graphic.

7d89b9143ecec8630eace9a02717e51cb64c8dfd.text: This small website change updated the bottom of the page. Visitors will no longer see the robot-coded tagline, and the link to the community chat now reads as an invitation to join the Discord server instead of a vague keep-in-touch prompt. It affects anyone who opens the site and scrolls to the bottom, and it is live today.

ac1d046cb508d1f697e5a02fc531049e35221618.text: The assistant now correctly identifies which files were previously edited, even when the content format varies. This fix ensures that when you ask to update a file, the system accurately recognizes it as a file you have already worked on. This is a small internal improvement, live today, and will make file updates more reliable for users who have edited files before.

fa94e8e486ba0e884c2b5ca3eb68df3171e2eac4.text: The pricing page was updated to clarify that 500 credits roughly equal a multi-hour work session. Pro plan users now see the overage cost stated simply as '$0.90 per 100 credits afterwards'. The visual layout of the plan cards was adjusted so they all have the same height, and the community support link now opens in a new browser tab.

8a2a55ce7b6b178352de769a3a641668b4f5508c.text: A small internal update now saves detailed activity notes to a file instead of only showing them on the screen. This helps the technical team track issues when working outside the live public environment. Regular users will notice no changes.

67dea5d21a532a655a9a03ae58cc61d0a005f448.text: The system now limits how much text it reads from websites to 75,000 characters. If a page is longer, it cuts off the excess and adds a note saying the content was too long. This helps keep responses fast and prevents errors from overly large web pages.

8cac781f8e04012d8ff94c72780091fb30107fb6.text: The text on the internal referrals page was updated to explicitly mention the monthly credit bonus for referring a friend, replacing a generic instruction. This change is live today and only affects internal staff viewing the referrals page. Staff will notice the new, more specific wording.

f34dfb314852af30b6bd2a368395cbf6a2f4b405.text: The code that keeps track of your chat history was cleaned up by deleting features that are not actually used. Since saving chats to your computer is currently turned off, this change only tidies up the internal notes for developers. You will not notice any difference in how the chat works today.

41498026ec398fd7742e26025ab10d7abddcaa4c.text: The team added a test to check that the tool can correctly update website style files. This is for internal quality assurance only. Customers will not notice any changes.

e1ce9db7f53491e135c1ee0e7cf9f1984d814579.text: The system now better recognizes when the AI assistant intends to update only a small part of a document, rather than rewriting the whole thing. This prevents accidental deletion of unchanged content during edits. The improvement applies immediately to all document editing tasks.

3c7f9217997a70f48266ae36f3fb79c6658f1987.text: The system now uses one fixed phrase to mark code that stays the same, instead of guessing based on different comment styles for each programming language. This cleanup makes the tooling more reliable for developers, but people using the assistant will not see any difference.

f28de674005b83cd5a5b2979b50e14b53ca3ba8f.text: The system now recognizes a specific way developers mark code sections as 'unchanged' or 'rest of code' within visual user interface files. This ensures those sections are correctly replaced with the actual existing code when the tool generates updates. No visible change for end-users; it improves internal accuracy for developers using the tool.

bd64b7f177bb7e92d08d2183619e53ee1d189001.text: When you hit your daily message limit, the program now shows a red error message telling you to check your usage, instead of a confusing blank screen or a separate notification. This affects all users running out of messages and ensures the input prompt returns immediately so you can type again without restarting.

ea7d2dd260f854f9ec70a090890f850f805c0bf2.text: The system now automatically skips any conversation records that are too long when preparing data for internal use. This change affects only the background data preparation process and does not alter how the service works for customers. You would not notice any difference in the app's behavior or performance.

e9b21c2d37f054932d7b8b7fb4233efacb221417.text: This small internal update removes a safety check that normally verifies connections, but only when running on a developer's own computer. Regular customers and the live website are completely unaffected by this change. Developers might notice slightly faster testing times on their local machines, but no visible changes will appear to anyone else.

952fa8c84387446b85044aef5815af31befb9783.text: A small text update fixed how a referral success message appears, removing extra symbols that made it look broken. It also clarified that you must log in to get a unique referral code. These changes affect the website's onboarding and referral pages, making the instructions clearer and the messages look correct.

1e26d2d9c56e11c8fa6902adccc8cda0b772e68c.text: This small update makes the system wait longer before giving up on a background connection, and it now hides the clutter of thousands of internal software files from the project view. It also sets a stricter limit on the size of files it will process. You will likely notice fewer connection errors and a cleaner, faster list of files when working on your project.

67b14536ed4e738d021b9da9b6719f42472f8172.text: A small internal update stops people from swapping referral bonuses back and forth with someone who already referred them. Anyone trying this now sees a block message instead of getting credit.

e94190c145566fc78ccf053a062bf0750ac4ed0e.text: We fixed spelling and punctuation mistakes in the error messages that appear when someone tries to use a referral code incorrectly. This affects anyone seeing a warning about using a code twice, using their own code, or referring themselves. The messages now read correctly with proper spacing and periods.

f69e63694f1c3e7f92a77ed5167cafe70a2323b2.text: The system now randomly picks between two separate access passes when asking the assistant for help. This change is for internal staff and happens automatically in the background. People will not see anything different, but the system can handle more requests without hitting limits on a single pass.

1e3f61cf86eeb9adb06b66fc27c2afa0a4ae48f6.text: The system now assigns the same service account to the same user every time, instead of switching randomly. This helps the service handle traffic limits more smoothly for users who talk to the AI assistant.

48b17912a5de555d39ba6fc8177fc74ece88ec05.text: A second backup key for the AI service was added to the setup template. This affects only internal developers who configure the system manually. They will now see two places to enter an AI service key instead of one. The feature is not active yet and does nothing until the system logic is updated to use it.

9b75e22adeb88a77be9113ce1cd4e1fec32702d3.text: The app now uses the correct Windows command to find where the tool is installed. This fixes a bug where the app could not locate the tool on Windows computers. Windows users will see the app work correctly without errors.

21a7ba6d0c84d43b01f95994d8d40f9bf93d18bc.text: A small internal tool update improves how file changes appear on screen. Added lines now start with a plus sign, and automatic commit messages no longer show in green text. This helps people reading the tool's output tell new content apart more easily.

f78d41250eb5835e52d8a1e49853a16bca7b03c1.text: The system now creates three different drafts of each requested change and picks the best one. This happens behind the scenes, so the final update appears cleaner and more accurate. The feature is live today.

24a7b3028414b7cc67dffcc4a68874caa7ea3aa1.text: A small safety update protects the computer from freezing when the assistant scans your project. It now ignores any single file larger than five megabytes, skipping it instead of trying to load it into memory. You might notice that the assistant stops reading huge files like large images or videos during its analysis.

3422538d1f19bd3fbc4d6c823b4ab3acb1920caf.text: The system now copies its internal tracking data before writing logs. This prevents one log entry from accidentally showing information meant for another. Internal developers are the only ones who see these logs, and they will notice cleaner, more accurate records when troubleshooting.

ab0e6d1c2572ce6ab30f1531b31e145e2b60f4eb.text: The warning message shown when you use most of your monthly credits was rephrased for clarity. It now says 'over X%' instead of 'X+%'. This change is live and affects anyone running the command-line tool.

4f70425b5129db047161a98a35db550581dec9ed.text: The tool that shows file changes now lists paths in plain text instead of green. This affects the internal command line view. If you look at a change report, the file names will appear black with a dash before them.

01dcb7699252d1ae09fd248d324a83c49b0e1a1d.text: A small internal fix corrected how the software finds the right place to apply changes to files. If the starting point was missing or pointed before the current position, the system now ignores that bad hint instead of trying to use it. This prevents rare errors when updating file contents.

5a4af4e5028e95612781da33abcec1a537c55d09.text: The command-line tool now automatically saves any pending work before adding new changes to the list. This prevents a common error where old edits get mixed with new ones. You will see a message confirming that the previous work was saved automatically.

97ab43be2b6a93b084c2d3f97c7a519102056f5e.text: The system no longer saves chat data to the external provider's servers. This change affects internal backend operations. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the assistant works.

9e51d6d8c9c52eeb4ddf69ee0aef6fc9ab9a47c6.text: The tool now checks for staged changes before attempting to commit, preventing errors when there is nothing to save. It also cleans up the text output, moving line breaks to make the messages easier to read. This affects anyone using the command-line interface to automatically save their work.

c95395cbd1421a001dc8a2d639723a4451313926.text: The system now checks account limits on the test server, not just the main one. Developers working on their own computers can still use the service without limits. Regular users will not notice any changes.

5dcf2c6bc9477fdacc7ce43bd9ec6e727d591db5.text: The pricing page for the Pro plan now lists 10,000 monthly credits and adds a line explaining that extra credits cost $0.50 per 100. This text update is live for anyone viewing the Pro pricing page. No billing rules changed, so actual charges remain the same.

0ca813ae18ce0f5c031b2086a1483c5e06902aff.text: The pricing page now checks if a person is signed in before letting them start a purchase. If they are not signed in, the page sends them to the login screen instead of trying to buy the plan. This applies to anyone trying to upgrade to the Pro plan today.

907f0c597b3bb9542a04638fa30f6078f82d6e57.text: Internal security limits for real-time data connections are now disabled when the system runs in a testing setup, but remain active in the live service. This change affects only the testing environment, allowing developers to test connections without hitting speed restrictions. The live service behavior remains unchanged.

3ad8161f54f606085223f3683c182a726e40d7c2.text: The tool now recognizes more ways the update command was installed. This helps people who installed it in non-standard locations. They will see the update command work correctly instead of failing to find the right method.

004944622f0c376786eb2ff4caee6ad10696e404.text: The tool now recognizes 'keep' as a marker for existing code in comments, alongside 'rest' and 'unchanged'. Previously, using 'keep' might have caused the system to misinterpret the instruction. This ensures that when you tell the assistant to keep parts of your code, it correctly preserves them instead of trying to replace them.

1a2b21b7958fb4db49eb50322c5a909fff47b8b0.text: The system's internal record-keeping format was adjusted to make entries easier to read. Instead of using codes, it now writes out the severity level in plain words and uses a standard date format. This change is live but only affects how staff view technical logs; regular users will not notice any difference.

a91bdaf622ea5f8f00cc8557ff18dd1d1a4057e9.text: A small internal tool update lets the assistant automatically save all recent edits before starting new work. This affects only developers using the command-line version of the software. They would notice a green message confirming that previous changes are staged, ensuring the tool tracks edits correctly.

d5755643aec3760a38c22012acd48cea9924de97.text: The system now recognizes text placeholders even when the final three dots are missing. It automatically adds the missing dots to ensure the format is correct. This change applies to code comments in many common programming languages. If you look at a comment like '//... existing code', it will now be cleaned up to look like '//... existing code...'.

7d6c953a5942f1daf7b5beab1d6ce14467650914.text: The command-line tool now accepts a new command to display the exact changes the assistant made to your files in its last reply. This helps you verify edits before accepting them. The tool also instructs the assistant to double-check that it has seen the current file content before attempting any edits.

f40d27414760f00ae5731c7b390ae6a14fbaf3c0.text: The command-line tool now checks usage limits after every task completion. This prevents the system from asking for the same data twice, speeding up the process. You will see a warning if you hit your monthly limit.

ebf36d4bceac3e6d79e707a93d7e4b351dba2156.text: The computer now records messages about its internal work in a cleaner, more consistent way. This helps the team understand how much information the assistant processes at once. Regular users will notice no difference, as this is a small background tidy-up.

b87b4ec631f69c7930ae5bf220e458be5f880133.text: The system's internal record-keeping was cleaned up. Instead of scattering separate notes about its file-searching process, it now bundles them into one organized entry. This helps the support team track exactly how the system made its decisions. Nothing changes for the end user.

fe7d4c67ed9a26f06c17b637c782a60eb0aae895.text: The system now automatically cleans up messy notes left by AI assistants in code files, ensuring they look standard. This change is live for all code generation tasks. Users will notice fewer errors or formatting issues when the AI suggests changes to their files.

a9b4dafb599fa3a076a9ad4961c0d604172d04e4.text: A small internal update lets the command-line tool accept a starting question. When a person types their request right after the folder name, the tool reads it immediately instead of waiting for them to type it in later. This saves a step for people using the tool from the command line.

724fd998785430febc6f24a7b1decbd24a9d462d.text: The assistant stopped repeating older updates when sending live responses to your screen. This prevents information from appearing twice during a conversation. You might see slightly cleaner text output, but no new features or visible changes if you weren't noticing the repetition before.

c959d4b4ca2ddbc22e9324b7234e65a1c3190de0.text: The system now uses a simpler, built-in method to record which environment settings it is using when it starts up. This change is internal and invisible to users. It prevents the startup process from getting tangled with other tools, ensuring the system loads correctly.

9ba7a7b550434c4407f6eefafb53347dba53cf37.text: The system now collects web page text before saving your message, instead of after. This ensures the assistant reads the original links you typed, ignoring any later edits to the chat history. You will see web content attached to your prompt as soon as you hit send, rather than appearing in the saved record.

b3c4509650d8eeb93e9d35843febb2cb46eed4c7.text: A small internal tweak increased the temporary memory limit for processing text streams. This helps the system handle slightly larger pieces of information without interruption. Regular users will not notice any difference.

7fbf7670167134f3fea31af8fb19a5ed98acd5df.text: The assistant now checks if a file already exists before saving it. If the file is new, it displays 'Creating' instead of 'Editing'. This small internal change helps non-technical users understand whether the assistant is adding a new document or updating an existing one.

de75f4e6a81dbb638c89ae575e8afec8f2f37d5a.text: The system now checks a digital fingerprint when you first connect, creating a record if one is missing. This prevents unauthorized access attempts from bypassing usage limits. If the check fails, you will see a specific error message instead of a silent disconnect. This protection is active immediately for all new connections.

d331ada8e2cebedc02a80dce4c97070bf60ba802.text: The service now records a serious error and stops immediately when an unexpected crash happens. It is live in the internal service. The added one-second cleanup and forced-stop step is in place, but it likely does not happen because the service also tells itself to stop right away. Someone looking at the logs would see the error just before the service ends.

37e52b627435c37225417f54e78b3b03afd3c912.text: A small internal update removed a security check from the very first step of connecting the app to the server. This stops the connection from getting blocked or delayed before it starts. Users won't see any changes, but the app now connects more reliably.

311c427fce7296d68921d2f47107ec1855e122ff.text: The program's text-based help menu was cleaned up to remove clutter and confusing symbols. The greeting now simply says 'Welcome back' without an emoji, and the list of actions is split into clear categories for examples and commands. This is a minor internal change that makes the initial screen easier to read.

511d68cee61c813e39b673c71b67da324ad9afed.text: The system now holds less text in memory before processing it. This change is only for demonstration purposes and does not affect the live service. No user will notice a difference.

c5c62f922dad7f963ecad0de4fab769c1f3bbd58.text: A small internal update fixed the button used to send a specific software component to the public store. The old method pointed to the wrong folder and tool, causing the release to fail. Now, the process correctly targets the right location and uses the standard publisher, ensuring this component can be shared without errors.

0cf519228ac6c030e31d3a0537f3830a0af0710d.text: The menu text updated to show 'Refactor a component into multiple components' instead of 'Refactor a large file into smaller files'. This change aligns the suggested prompts with component-based refactoring patterns. The menu now displays the new example, making it easier for users to understand how to use the tool for component refactoring.

a889ebf02c82ddb0a0ad88839b56503c9d048196.text: The assistant now reads your personal command-line setup files. It uses these to understand your specific computer habits and preferences. You will notice it giving more personalized advice for your system.

982cb5a21e70e009d775d118c37cf1862f728b39.text: Fixed a hidden error in the database's blueprint for setting automatic expiration dates. This ensures future records correctly calculate their one-month validity window without failing. Regular users will see no difference today, as this only corrects internal setup data for upcoming changes.

35884b7b561c34e2784872abdabdff17f4540cfe.text: The system now checks if a project already has specific background information files before trying to create new ones. If those files are missing, the system skips the creation step entirely. This prevents unnecessary actions on projects that don't use that feature.

c1a6afbe729a1dc133b8979f2f995775ff79241a.text: The system now keeps a copy of the answers it generates on the service provider's servers. This change applies to the internal backend and does not affect what end users see or do today.

be23e161a7b41337d25b2fac5314d461036fda05.text: A small internal fix stops the system from adding a hidden list of file changes to the end of its response. This prevents errors that occurred when the assistant made edits, affecting only the internal processing of those specific responses. Users will not notice any visible difference in the text they receive.

d423ddda29da8d609f43bfa616b9c3677ab9069d.text: The website now sends people straight to the free tool instead of asking for an email first. Visitors will see a 'Try Manicode for free' button on the main page and a 'Keep in touch' link at the bottom. The top menu links for Features, Pricing, and Docs are currently hidden.

e02cb2c8cdf9734275e22935905d8396afe0a2b6.text: The tool now uses the folder you are currently in as its single source for reading and writing files, rather than tracking two separate locations. If you ask the tool to run a command that changes folders, it will print a green message telling you the new location. This is a small internal cleanup that ensures terminal commands and file operations always look in the same place.

ae02ee8ff41b5f74cf4bb7fbb6375c0fd6a899a7.text: The system now reliably displays a 'Please wait' message when applying file changes, moving this notification from the user interface to the server logic. This ensures users see the status update regardless of how the interface handles incoming data. The change also adds a 'Complete!' confirmation after files are updated and displays three startup messages when the tool initializes.

a61a6eb25a2dd6f238acb75f5d729ef61eb4efc9.text: The assistant no longer saves or reorganizes your work history on its own. It now requires your direct permission before making these changes. You will notice a prompt asking for approval before any such action occurs.

3d17d0bf8290054e72b266dbd5fc684f8ab67e3b.text: The assistant now understands the '/run' command to execute terminal instructions, making it easier to distinguish between requests for help and actual commands. This change affects people using the command-line interface, who will see the new option listed in the help menu. It is live today.

750792c767609146a22c1f40c9ce6f33a61213ea.text: Removed three greeting messages from the tool's startup screen. The tool now goes straight to the first prompt instead of showing 'Manicode initialized successfully' and 'Ready to assist you with your coding tasks'. This change only affects the internal tool, not external users.

7882259039863d3e678a72bf45a534f421b2d9ae.text: The system now only treats short phrases as computer commands if they have three words or fewer. This stops the assistant from accidentally running commands when you type simple questions. The change is active immediately.

02bdf194609c3974a27ea19a265700bece9163e2.text: The assistant now recognizes 'add' and 'hey' as non-commands, so it won't try to run them as system instructions. It also skips command processing if your message contains the word 'error '. This prevents accidental execution of short phrases that look like commands but are just normal conversation.

9e9123c9c35a23cdcbc35cebfcad617df69a9d00.text: The assistant now ignores long, less important documents when building its memory for a conversation. This applies only to files ranked below the top five and larger than about five thousand words. Users will see fewer errors where the assistant fails to answer because it ran out of space.

52011e941a82a3c3cfe0b0b5709b6c0e48276b3e.text: A test was added to check that the system correctly handles a specific file structure when generating updates. This affects only the internal quality checks and does not change how the tool works for anyone today. If you looked at the testing setup, you would see a new scenario marked to run first, ensuring this particular case is caught before others.

af42ba6fddd1964b1355b73d830828792fdd6c07.text: A small internal fix corrected a test that checks how the assistant handles file updates. The test now explicitly verifies that it receives a valid result before checking the content, preventing a potential error that could make the test fail unexpectedly. This change affects only the internal testing process and has no visible impact on the assistant's behavior or user experience.

487692dc90b49b2eaa365b8d35a77f81252825df.text: The tool that writes project summaries now shares its background instructions with the search feature. This allows the system to remember common parts of the instructions, reducing processing time and cost. Developers will not see any change in the summaries, but the service runs more efficiently.

1dd3fa95a71f8fa2156f1e8cc507049acfdbec35.text: The assistant now skips tiny, unreadable copies of website files when scanning your project. You will see a cleaner list of your own documents and scripts. This change is live today.

7015281c3cd27267275e3ad8c3ba9f8619e93a3d.text: The system stopped recording brief messages every time a connection opens or closes. This affects only internal staff who read server logs. They will see a much cleaner log view, with no change to how the service actually works.

062d3bbb0093d619576b2a8444c91454e8b4999b.text: The instructions on the software's information page now list the correct email address for sending feedback. This only affects people who read that page to contact the developer. If they send an email to the old address, it will bounce; the new address will reach the right person.

a23ac9df33c00f92cf5bc50b4212fa160ccc5ed6.text: The build process for the internal application now checks for missing configuration settings before finishing. If required connection details are absent, the build stops and reports an error instead of creating a broken package. This change affects only internal developers and takes effect immediately.

1e75915c45f7a0704bef650b2697ec3a206e4467.text: The assistant now sees a list of the last 20 files you recently opened in your project. This helps it understand your current context better without you needing to mention which files you are working on. The list is generated from your computer's record of when files were last accessed.

8e247ecaa0a0d587f313eab5cc6ab53be3a18dec.text: The automatic version check for the coding assistant now runs only on live servers. This small internal update stops the check from triggering on local development machines. Developers will notice fewer unnecessary background processes and potential errors during local testing.

44db2b765f106bae76c677ff4d6b2ee2335b01dd.text: The program's help menu now lists new ways to ask for help, like fixing broken code or organizing large files. It also shows the correct email address for sending feedback. This change is live and only affects the text you see when you ask for help.

30c758cd8e1ae29522bd0c069ed428fa54c42586.text: The program now shows a friendlier greeting with a waving hand emoji when it recognizes the person using it. If it does not recognize the person, it simply asks what they would like to do without the greeting. This small change affects how the program looks when it starts, making the experience slightly more personal for known users.

1919ba5957042d59a9b187b293fa11be882fee94.text: This small internal update changes how the system displays troubleshooting information on the screen. It now adds a specific label before these messages, making them easier to spot and separate from other activity. This only helps the team who maintain the software and does not change what regular people see or use.

b8948ba46d8e1b1a846112cfff0bf2f3eaf54b14.text: The update checker now asks the package manager directly for the latest version instead of reading the website. This makes the check faster and more reliable. If the direct question fails, it still falls back to reading the website. This is a small internal fix.

f3a40a02a39f2b5b86ded617043916b38cc645be.text: A small internal update refined how the assistant decides when to save new instructions for itself. It now prioritizes fixing misunderstandings over just clarifying code, and ensures existing notes are preserved during updates. This change is active today and helps the assistant better meet specific user expectations without losing previous context.

e7bf5dedf3b0ded8a502e30b5b8cb18be6d7776e.text: The software now correctly looks for its secret configuration files in a secure, hidden folder when running on a specific cloud platform, rather than checking the wrong location. This fix ensures that the application can start up properly and find its necessary settings without errors. The change is live immediately for anyone using that cloud service, preventing startup failures.

4cf5b36e27ee4e7b13e94506e4fa7df37439e244.text: The software's internal version label was updated from 1.0.69 to 1.0.70. This is a minor administrative change affecting only the package's metadata. Users will not notice any difference in behavior, features, or performance.

bf5126fbe07a44ac5e3c2e36f15d750fee80ef7c.text: The program now looks in the correct folder for secret keys when running on the Render hosting service. Previously, it checked the wrong location, which could cause the system to fail to start or load settings. This internal fix ensures the service runs correctly on that specific platform without changing how you use it.

0741ec583056162f9a64d7ff0393fe58058b21ab.text: A small internal fix improved how the system reads special markers in streaming text. This ensures the system doesn't get confused by repeated markers, preventing potential parsing errors. No visible changes for users, but the background process is more reliable.

7c6ef69a37cbf607682679ed7c19ce0ff33997cd.text: The assistant now keeps the raw text of its answer separate from the text shown on screen. This ensures that when it edits a file, the user sees a clean 'Editing file' message instead of confusing technical code. This is an internal improvement for the chat interface.

2c6f16d0f484eee151bbfed00d77dd3be3f4d9fc.text: The program now hides the detailed technical error report when the automatic update fails. Regular users see a simple failure message instead of a confusing block of code. This change is live but only affects the internal update process.

bbe93e4bd866ffdd12913862a5445943d85e2a74.text: A small internal check was added to ensure the system correctly identifies and records changes in text streams. This affects only the software's internal quality control processes. Users and non-technical staff will notice no changes, as this update purely verifies that the underlying logic functions as expected without altering any visible features.

ec0d7df5d6f1192b300c268f77b768b62ab00e0e.text: The program now hides the text '[END]' while streaming responses to the terminal, though it keeps it in the saved history. It also adjusts blank lines around prompts, exit messages, and file change logs to make the text layout look cleaner. This change is live for anyone using the command-line tool.
