b0034f122ec20d275ca0207ffca811bacedca698.text: The update tool now checks the actual location of the command-line program to decide how to install new versions, rather than guessing based on the background system running it. This internal fix ensures the tool correctly identifies whether to use npm, yarn, pnpm, or bun. Users will not see any visual changes, but the update process is now more reliable.

1574228876c81d067cf4e025f5fd02b99625a2cb.text: The internal version label for the backend service and the assistant application was updated to match the latest release. This is a routine bookkeeping step that affects only the software's own identification records. End users will not notice any functional changes or differences in behavior from this update.

c78cc674b21fda605af3dbd890e00063ceb539dd.text: The system now records which software versions are running when checking for updates. This helps support teams spot mismatches faster. Regular users won't notice anything different.

f19d717189cacb8acc4eebf229fff8d919acb5e2.text: The app now stops looking for files after finding ten thousand in a folder, or one thousand if it is scanning your main home folder. This prevents the assistant from freezing or taking too long on very large projects. You would notice the file list appears quickly and reliably, though it might not show every single file if you have more than the limit.

e74bee41117c1e9d96b2e3a5959b4a8165daa902.text: The system now explicitly tells the assistant to look for files to edit or read when deciding if more information is needed. It also shows 'None' instead of a blank space when no files are currently open. This internal adjustment helps the assistant make better choices about which files to access.

405898a1bd09a0c4bb0e07e5e63c378a4060fdaa.text: The text prompt shown in the command-line tool now includes a colon at the end. This visual change helps clarify where to type a response. It affects only the appearance of the input area, with no change to how the tool functions.

8463c9b1b24463cf01d4f77e78bce6b593ed850d.text: The system stopped printing error messages when cleaning up old connections. Support staff will see fewer log entries.

ebd94d1f47e0f60716c7870b127c7553b465281d.text: The tool now checks if it can update itself safely before trying. If it finds a new version but cannot handle the update automatically, it shows a warning asking you to update manually instead of failing silently. If it updates successfully, it closes immediately so you know to restart it. This change is internal and affects how the tool behaves when a new version is available.

2a27f72e60fa1fb141926d64667971fd2041eb54.text: The tool that writes project notes now sees the whole folder layout, not just changed files. This helps it spot when a new note is truly needed. Only internal note generation changes; no visible effect for end users.

b501a194b9dae0624a74d492bb41b8b0c6bcfba0.text: The internal assistant now updates existing knowledge notes instead of creating new ones for changes. This keeps information consolidated and prevents duplicate files. The change is live for the system's internal knowledge management process.

75faaa098288028603dd2a95f6fb936723b23408.text: The AI assistant's name changed from Manny to Mani in all internal guides and website text. This affects the company's internal branding and the public-facing description of the tool. Visitors to the website will now see the new name in the introductory text and feature descriptions.

bb8fa45142b5f64ec57ffbe039e7c3ba8733b37b.text: The change fixes how the system finds its database files, resolving a local setup error for developers. It also removes a leftover button code for the theme switcher. These are small, internal housekeeping tasks that do not affect how the application looks or behaves for regular users.

3ad9add1f9e9f4f48f69b4840e3f2c7300195b7d.text: The assistant now skips its automatic file-reading step when the previous action already involved using a tool. This small internal change affects only the backend prompt logic. Users will likely notice nothing, but the system avoids redundant steps, potentially saving a slight amount of time.

ea56afa4c417a71e869102be3a06de00ec4a9e9c.text: The system now checks if a file's content has changed before saving it. If the new content is identical to the old content, the system skips the update step entirely. This prevents unnecessary work for the background process, though the end user will not notice any visible difference in the application's behavior.

5c3735a2c5cc07a9968b5d85e591a9234dc30258.text: Internal tools now give clearer rules to the assistant for editing files, focusing on brevity and accurate context. The assistant also checks if a requested change already exists in the file and tells the user if so, avoiding unnecessary edits. This change is live for internal operations.

175ac5e4ea10ed0acf5e2d68099168da37f7528c.text: The rules guiding the AI assistant were simplified to remove confusing distinctions about how it stores project notes. This change is live and affects how the assistant interprets instructions, but users will not notice any visible difference in the interface or output.

3c7bb3d4dff0d30b995ac492f75842a618bedc16.text: The command-line assistant now prints a green, underlined 'Manicode' label before each response. This small visual change helps users quickly identify which text comes from the assistant. It is live for anyone using the tool today.

36c00fe204598485ad7c19f632fdc30de44fea55.text: The assistant previously sent an empty list of file details to the chat stream when no new files were needed, causing a blank line in the response. Now, it skips sending that empty message entirely. Users will see cleaner chat responses without stray blank lines.

01b7a9284017f06caf57bcd391bc11722ec36e40.text: A small internal setting was adjusted to limit how many background file checks the system runs for certain non-assistant interactions. This reduces the total number of times the system looks for context information. Users will not notice any change in the interface or response speed.

99d56e0dda49a39054bff4fede7488f097bad9cb.text: Developers fixed an internal error that was blocking the software from being built. This change affects only the technical team's ability to compile the application, not the features available to customers. A user would notice nothing different.

ed65d7975f641fe3555db03b8c6daa517876a5b0.text: The website's top navigation bar now sits correctly without extra spacing or overlapping elements. This visual cleanup affects anyone viewing the site's main page. You would notice the menu logo and links align properly against the black background, with no flickering or misplacement.

fa0f1455114d1b0b8fc4733c036b40504403125e.text: A small internal cleanup removed the special helper tool and setup instructions required for starting the backend program. This affects only the team members who run the code on their own computers. They will notice the program starts without needing to launch that extra helper first.

0f585dfefd153fba545d3b0715fbf722d95a998c.text: The app now always checks the installed version against the correct reference file, instead of only doing so in specific setups. The update reminder message changed from green to yellow. This internal fix ensures the version check works consistently for all local installations.

05dfcc10dc24307b66ac25a68583104de975a91b.text: The system's internal communication tool had a technical mismatch in how it tracked waiting times, which could have caused connection issues. This fix ensures the tool correctly manages timeouts for sending messages and checking if the connection is alive. No visible changes for you, as this was a behind-the-scenes correction to keep the connection stable.

86f82192302d02d8b750c27b59f4c576f1c7304c.text: The build process now sets a different environment flag for the final application package. This internal adjustment ensures the software reads its configuration correctly without conflicting with standard system settings. Customers will not notice any difference in the application's behavior or appearance.

461c31d4eb7e7e0cfde1fa5c3d6b5bb6f263c854.text: The team turned off a strict code-checking rule for the website's navigation bar. This change only affects the tools developers use to write the code, so it will not change what customers see or do on the site.

3d2c0dd251f5323cae50c6a0e65403169de218dc.text: Added error handling to prevent server crashes when the AI file check fails. If an error occurs, it now logs the issue and defaults to assuming new files are needed, allowing the process to continue without stopping. This small internal fix ensures stability for all users of the request processing pipeline.

6d92b457cfff31df35ca996775618d0d88248015.text: The website's top navigation bar now appears on all pages, not just the homepage. This change standardizes the look of the menu and logo across the site. Visitors will see the same navigation experience wherever they go on the site.

25b24d859173d122b99bb79c09982f9463f40d90.text: The system now checks if existing files are enough before searching for new ones. This saves time and resources when no new information is needed. Internal tooling only; no visible change for end-users.

76934587f33ced5b3f877ca425a59f75ff54116b.text: The assistant now demands stronger proof that a piece of project context is truly non-obvious before it saves a new note about it. It also prefers saving these notes for broad sections of the project rather than for single files. This keeps the assistant's memory cleaner and focused only on genuinely surprising details.

8ef404f7828bc7ce6d1e927f3953bd5cf490fd11.text: The internal logic for applying file changes was cleaned up to improve reliability. This is a background maintenance task for developers. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the application behaves.

79334019ff6a5000395bbdb1a5f5596dac98ce20.text: The internal system now uses a newer, more accurate brain to write code updates. This tooling swap is live today and affects only the backend team. They might notice slightly different suggestions when the system drafts fixes.

7892ae54c08423ec2c4c1c0e19f7056138d0459d.text: A small fix now prevents the app from crashing when an automated edit tries to delete a line that does not exist in the file. This affects the core system that applies changes to code, making it more stable when it encounters mismatched or hallucinated edits. Users will not see a new feature, but they may experience fewer unexpected errors or freezes during file updates.

8152a30a735673952b411fb9951bd727a4b90599.text: The assistant now lists its own changes to your files at the end of its reply, so you can see exactly what it modified without checking the files yourself. To prevent overwhelming responses, the system automatically replaces extremely long descriptions of your own manual edits with a placeholder note. This update is live for all users of the command-line tool.

596552d28cd8b1286c64955972d5ba6cefa1467c.text: When the list of files is too long to fit in the AI's memory, the system now shows just the main folder instead of getting confused or stopping. This is an internal safety measure that keeps the assistant working smoothly under tight limits. Users will not see any change, but the system is more reliable when handling large projects.

504c3ce42b4001e0060d854c3d6807b75171f06f.text: Internal change. Stops automatic style checks from blocking website code saves. Affects website developers only. No user-visible effect.

cf93047761b47fe5053f4ca63ec8522ddc15eb01.text: The tool that makes examples for the AI now remembers its work if it stops early. It can pick up where it left off instead of starting over. It also looks at more projects and files, but runs fewer at once. This is an internal change, so you won't see anything different.

a9a2b7dbdc9a560ce4e4e4d6ea432ca32fd72dca.text: The assistant's internal version label increased by one step in two separate places. This is a minor housekeeping update for the team. Regular people will not notice any change in how the assistant behaves or looks.

2600b6a51d8c45da537f42241e0978bf0bf4260e.text: The assistant now remembers the list of files in your project between messages instead of reading them from scratch every time. This change makes responses appear faster and reduces the cost of processing long conversations. You will notice the assistant feels more responsive when discussing code, though the actual answers remain the same.

01a6efbf4a81d533df15129e27e54d3e6991cfa8.text: The tool that gathers examples for training the AI now skips files that are too large or look like they were made by a computer. It also uses more examples overall but processes them more slowly to avoid errors. This change is internal and affects only the team building the AI, not the people who use it.

6983ecf60e43e3716f196e278067b77de84b2caa.text: When the assistant saves a new file, it now automatically creates any missing folders in the path. Previously, saving a file into a brand-new folder would fail. This change is live and prevents errors when the assistant writes files to new locations.

b95f7a01b4b08be2401cc2442d4e5746c197ebb8.text: When you edit files yourself between messages, the assistant now sees exactly what you changed. This stops it from accidentally overwriting your work with old versions. The fix is live for the command-line tool.

c3a6bfd24c93e02fcda7828c282b8a4ece8c9c49.text: A small internal fix prevents the assistant from saving file changes if you stopped it before it finished. This applies to people using the chat interface to edit code. You would notice fewer unwanted edits appearing in your files after hitting stop.

f15370c008abddafff867814d4b18b9c774dd3aa.text: The AI assistant now stops after three tool calls without new input. This prevents endless loops and requires user feedback to continue. Small internal safety guard.

7ec5babbc99e1493543bca1f189c7b34ebc94eb9.text: The assistant now prepares its memory of newly added files immediately after they are loaded, rather than waiting until the end of the task. This internal optimization ensures the system has the correct context available sooner for subsequent steps. No visible interface changes or new features are introduced for end-users.

d8e2e520d17be9d59672da347039667622e06c90.text: The app's help guide now includes a fix for permission errors that happen when installing it. This helps people who get stuck during setup by telling them to use a special tool to manage their computer's software. You would only notice this if you looked at the help page after an installation failed.

4277bb6ba248b95a4afb0bcbdf0ddcbd3904af0b.text: The tool now ignores blank lines when matching text, so updates apply correctly even if spacing differs. This affects anyone using the automated patch feature. They will notice fewer failed updates.

87740f70af36f31019f86a277552379e39b05bad.text: The system now uses two different sets of instructions depending on whether it is searching for files or writing code. To save space, it skips showing the full list of files to the coding part if that list is very long. This internal update helps the tool run faster and cheaper for everyone.

15db2d570cc59ac20c67b0e74bb6b6b13406752b.text: Small internal adjustment. The command-line assistant now attaches the note about files you edited since its last reply to the message you send, instead of hiding it in background instructions. It is live for command-line assistant users. If they looked, they would see the edit note in the conversation, which helps keep their manual edits visible to the assistant.

6847f8e06b1c1a43b06d9fbaff652e64fcfc9ab4.text: The software now includes necessary data files for analyzing code structure in its final packaged form. This fixes an issue where the tool might fail to recognize programming languages correctly after installation. You would notice this if the assistant previously struggled to understand specific code files, but it now works as expected.

3a539e522a7f148413c00a624c98d92beae57632.text: A small internal tool now automatically saves and records version number changes in the project history immediately after updating them. This affects only the team members who prepare software releases. They will notice that the tool completes the saving step for them, so they no longer need to manually record the change.

5965ee9b8ce9d5e259dfcaac8811d44b2b97a9ea.text: The app now loads language tools only when needed, rather than all at once. This makes the program start up faster. You will notice a quicker initial load time when opening the app.

92e3be3aa98dc53a4d94f787f1e2cda59cb899d9.text: The program now uses a different, lighter tool to color its text. You will see the same colored messages when connecting or updating, but the program starts slightly faster and uses less memory. This change is already live.

f9ddb198eedc1aa7dc9c30142de4a887285bfaa7.text: The command-line tool now shows status messages like 'Undo', 'Thinking', and 'Exiting' in green text. The assistant's replies appear in bold black text instead of blue. This small visual update applies immediately to anyone using the tool.

e6703e5c5f03cc8ec462f24435f6a556d052612f.text: The tool now reads C, C++, C#, Java, and Rust files to build project maps. Programmers using these languages get accurate file summaries. This works immediately.

40c4900cd1ef6078e2c6d4740ff31ad0a7a644f3.text: The text stream in the command-line interface no longer appears in bold. This is a small visual adjustment that affects anyone using the tool to view responses.

2b6ba0522ae4bd01b8578d8f1938450d8af0a043.text: The setup guide's help section now links directly to instructions for fixing common installation errors. This small update makes it easier for new users to find the right steps for their computer.

526541c50b1103ad92b33ca991a1b827d18956ec.text: The internal version number for the assistant's backend was updated to match the latest release. A line of code that was no longer being used was removed to keep the system tidy. This is an administrative change for the engineering team; customers will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves.

4414f83055f0970cabdace6ef093de9587aef6ca.text: The system can now read Java files to understand their structure. This helps the assistant answer questions about code written in that language. You would notice this if you asked the assistant to explain or find specific parts of a Java project, as it can now see the relationships between different pieces of that code.

337f5d8c049f383cc9a52013789e0ba5712f3656.text: The internal tool now uses a simpler method to color its terminal output, switching from blue to green for command prompts and completion messages. This change affects only the internal command interface, not the end-user experience or functionality. Users will notice a minor visual difference in the color of the command text displayed during terminal operations.

18f0083112519bee19f3dced0a13adc4f5416a19.text: The instructions for the AI coding assistant were updated to be clearer. The text now says the tool helps generate better code and explains that you must start it from inside your project folder. This is a small internal documentation change, so nothing about how the software works has changed for users.

6b7ee257fb17dc1a6f92be8bfd7c2d2408dd71d3.text: The tool that maps out how code connects to itself can now read projects written in the Rust programming language. This helps the assistant understand and search through Rust codebases more effectively. Regular users will notice better answers when asking questions about Rust projects, though this improvement is not active for everyone yet.

46332752838fdbc146595ff39c1d1354332a9645.text: The search tool learned to recognize Rust implementation blocks. If you look up a Rust type, its methods now appear in the list.

d6f12897fdfa5c4182151bd2afa38b0731ba6480.text: The system now automatically hides a specific set of temporary test folders from its main storage area. This keeps the central repository clean and organized for the internal team. The change is live today, so anyone checking the storage list will see fewer cluttered items.

d859e4810be56d2c57db8d549304a249d60f160d.text: The assistant now always puts code changes in a special format. This stops it from showing raw code in chat. Small internal fix.

2291f88b15dbeef9fc45726e84326295790f669c.text: The system now ignores more specific words at the start of a request and stops trying to run any request that has four or more words. This change is active now. Users will notice the assistant refusing to execute certain phrases as computer commands, treating them as regular text instead.

1d5ff54ec05689765212bf379e7258f8a51b9fc9.text: The tool now rates code pieces based on how deep they sit in folders, their length, and how often they are used, rather than just listing them. This helps the system understand which parts of a project matter most. The update is currently in the background and does not change how the tool works for you yet.

0b3b4355e24223ca2766f2a0ae5a717f3e8b4ea1.text: When the assistant asks a question, the system now requests fewer files to speed up the process. This internal adjustment reduces the number of file requests made during assistant-initiated queries. Users will not notice any visible changes.

366778fb4c6efd6bbdcdcb07fde79f1fb46698f4.text: A small internal fix helps the system read update instructions more accurately when those instructions have varying lengths at the start. This change is live today. You would not notice any difference in your own work, as this only affects how the system processes background data.

77f61ef3bb526e99c4f5427f0a830a4a24d7a8fa.text: The AI assistant now uses a smaller budget for the project map and file lists, and it draws that map with simple spaces instead of wider tabs to save room. It also stops writing extra diagnostic files to the project folder. This affects the tool itself, not the files it edits.

3d2509aa497840cfdcc79f1e41e927cc0d2da8c0.text: The assistant now applies requested code edits even when the file's surrounding text looks slightly different from what it expected. This prevents failed updates when the assistant guesses the wrong location. Users will notice fewer errors when the tool tries to change a file.

19d4290319603d8cb4608d224b243907637423dc.text: The app now skips checking the instructions inside third-party tools to save time. This makes the software build faster and prevents errors caused by mismatched instructions from other companies. The change is live and helps the whole system run more smoothly.

ca0767a691bcd246be6d06fee0a7a7c5ed22e061.text: The code reader now correctly identifies names in JavaScript and Python files. It ignores standard setup names like 'init' and 'call' to reduce noise. It also handles larger files without crashing. This improves how the tool maps out code structure, though it is an internal fix with no visible interface changes.

98218308adbf621288c469b1d1c369c2eeb3d851.text: The internal version number for the software components was updated to mark a new release. This change is purely administrative for the development team and has no visible impact on end-users. There are no new features, bug fixes, or interface changes associated with this specific update.

e65d9700e20a1005aa25b1b5e5708ec8d368ce2d.text: An internal tool that prepares training examples now skips files marked as automatically generated. It also processes fewer files each run and includes one more sample project. People who use the tool would see smaller, cleaner example sets; customers would not notice it.

f67ca0d994dd62b87cca3ef6ed484b626d348dfe.text: A new switch lets the system skip a middleman service and talk directly to the AI provider. This is only used by an internal tool that creates training data, so regular users will not notice any change.

633f39f939a33ae126addd07689ff1b8ad104903.text: The tool that builds training data for the AI assistant now cleans up hidden carriage return characters from text files. This prevents the assistant from learning bad formatting habits when reading code written on different computer systems. This is a small internal fix and only affects the data preparation process.

81121b36247a0b2fac42ab769815e13acb871f9d.text: The internal tool that creates training examples for the AI assistant now processes significantly more files and has switched to a simpler method for generating these examples. It also skips any files where the assistant fails to produce a description, ensuring cleaner data. This change affects only the internal dataset generation process and is not visible to end-users.

f33d602ee496897e47d452a7d9cc72a7eee55f60.text: The written instructions for the AI coding tool were rewritten to be clearer. The new text explains that the tool is for experienced engineers working on large projects and lists the steps to start using it in simple numbered points. This affects anyone reading the help guide, though the tool itself works exactly the same as before.

398708a6162e4123f40b85d991bddac93c5dedec.text: The team updated the help text for their AI coding tool, clarifying that it is designed for editing large projects directly from the command line. This change affects people reading the online instructions, offering a more precise description of the tool's intended use. Nothing functional changed, so current users will not notice any difference in how the software works.

4dfcaab8c0e5a0741974bc1d1a3dec0c29d0e3e1.text: A tool that prepares training examples for an AI model now also saves them in a specific chat-style format. This change is for internal use only and helps the team teach the AI to write code updates by showing it questions and answers. It also reduces the number of examples processed at once to make the tool run faster and use less memory.

204541c94317189c62b94080e75d188ba1840262.text: The assistant now lists more of your project's files in its instructions, but only up to a strict size limit. If the list gets too long, it automatically cuts off the least important files to save space. This helps the assistant understand your project better without getting overwhelmed by too much information at once.

05911ef13af14afffdf853692add368681458928.text: A small internal tool update lets the assistant learn from many more kinds of files, not just one specific language. It now checks larger batches of past changes and ignores tiny edits to keep the training data useful. This affects only the team building the AI's skills; regular users see no immediate change.

17204f201230ce24266355c1fbbb9f07bd65c121.text: The system now waits twice as long for answers from the AI service before giving up. This helps people who ask complex questions or expect long responses, as they are less likely to see a timeout error.

d4930b71d53ee015fe53634d66c4a6ead5380f0c.text: The internal tooling received a routine version update. This change does not affect any features, performance, or user experience. Nothing will look different to anyone.

0ccf19a06d0003bc841730dcaee2ad1d8f752200.text: The program now uses the line numbers written in the patch instructions to find where to apply changes, instead of searching from the last known position. This makes applying changes to files more accurate and reliable. Users will notice fewer errors when the system tries to update or edit code files.

b0dba61a8f106062474ffda74b8b3956aed7b56a.text: The command-line tool stopped automatically saving all your recent file edits into the version history before sending a message. This change affects only people using that specific tool. They will notice that their files are no longer marked as staged for a commit, leaving them to decide what to save.

216017404bcabd4cba4933fdbba011c83fd8c99d.text: The public description of the AI coding assistant was rewritten to highlight benefits for experienced engineers, and a spelling error was fixed. Instructions for reversing changes were updated to tell people to type 'undo' or 'redo' instead of using specific keyboard shortcuts. These text updates are live now, but the added testing shortcut is internal and invisible to users.

c9b9c0d971e42663662d5721237eb8e76a9d173f.text: The system now reviews the full conversation before applying changes to code. This prevents accidental deletions when the AI updates a file, ensuring it only changes what was asked for. The fix is active, making the editing process safer.

bdfe6c3ba161fec4c4350609bd917988ad2f558a.text: The tool now updates its map of your project files whenever you switch folders. This fixes a problem where the assistant might list old files after you moved to a new directory. It is a small internal change that makes the tool more reliable for engineers working across different folders.

4f9313ee46b29fde5a76d87f2d707ed5cedd935d.text: The system now correctly saves text from uploaded files into the final message sent to the AI assistant. This fix ensures that when you attach a document, its content is actually included in the conversation, rather than being ignored. The change is internal and live, improving how the assistant reads your attachments.

a16795258bd8b4260c7a92db4756b5cc472cd835.text: The team updated the internal release labels for the developer tools. This is a small bookkeeping change that does not affect the features or performance of the tools. You will not notice any difference.

07f411856def360a640c6395035c570aa90e68f0.text: The system now recognizes 'file' as a command it should ignore, alongside 'what' and 'which'. This helps prevent the assistant from trying to run these specific commands in the terminal. Only internal tools are affected, and users will not notice any change in behavior.

69336f58aa6e5072e8031b0857784fdec186edba.text: The command tool now skips running more common commands, including date, history, man, top, touch, who, and yes. This affects people using the command tool. They may notice those commands are treated as plain text instead of being run. The change is live now.

73ee33db17b72f3d87846c2f01e91836006fb8ce.text: The system now allows setting a limit on how much text the AI can generate in a single response, defaulting to a specific length if no limit is given. This change affects the backend's communication with the AI service. Users will not notice any immediate difference unless the new limit is actively used, as the default behavior remains unchanged.

03b881ed98315908cfb83e453e779d7cc956e321.text: The AI assistant stopped writing its internal reasoning steps before acting. This change affects all internal users of the tool. People will notice the assistant answers faster and shows less explanation about how it decided to make a change.

afc40f9bf6ffad4673482b8a7e8067eecbca2a62.text: The assistant now reads your project's recent history to understand what changed. This helps it answer questions about the current state of your work. You will not see a new button or setting, but the assistant will give more accurate answers about recent updates.

59daf6ff6ec0f41343cb551c44e45483054b3654.text: The system now correctly recognizes when a command fails on Windows due to being uninstalled or missing, matching how it already works on other computers. This affects internal tools running on Windows. A user would notice fewer confusing errors when trying to run a command that doesn't exist on their machine.

8e6b19452a41a34a6fe31ef9071107e6a5153bc6.text: The software's internal label was updated to mark a new release. This change applies only to the engineering team managing the code, not to people using the app. No visible features or behaviors changed for anyone else.

196e3b3450191b23765922abe86fbe661347a123.text: The team corrected how a background service finds its helper files. This internal fix ensures the service loads correctly, but nothing changes for the reader.

96b46ce6bfd87ea6a5f210a46b75da81bac52580.text: The assistant now shows the project's file structure using numbers to indicate how deep each folder is, instead of using spaces. This makes the list more compact and easier for the assistant to process. You might notice the file list looks slightly different, with numbers appearing before the names of files and folders.

0c7b020b87db6a1db630f7c09e51dcfa16f97f2e.text: The assistant now automatically reads your unsaved and staged changes in your project folder to better understand your current work. This helps it give answers that match the code you are actively editing. If the folder is not a project or the system cannot read the changes, the assistant simply ignores this step and works as before.

eb383b425230f5cabfe0f05cfc5693170962f99e.text: The internal tool that picks relevant project files now ignores any AI response containing spaces, preventing random commentary from breaking the file list. This change is live for internal users, ensuring they receive clean file paths instead of mixed text.

5647c2b851a47d8c5b33a9e3a5e73c6fc84992b3.text: The software's internal release counter increased by one. This is an administrative update for the engineering team to track versions. No new features or fixes are included, so customers will not notice any difference in how the tool works.

24a9ca34782ccdf03a164e870e646dbe93c09e43.text: The team moved the automated checks that verify the software works into a separate folder, away from the main program files. This change is internal, so no one will notice a difference in how the product behaves or looks.

ed8ad07551bb886153f0bac365f9efc818d10131.text: The system now asks for relevant project files in parallel batches instead of one at a time. This change is internal and affects how quickly the assistant gathers context. No user-visible behavior changes today.

d665e076fc232bfff32ff2b22d506795c183c7c1.text: The system now accepts a simple list of file names instead of requiring specific formatting tags. It also allows up to 10 files per request, up from 6. This internal adjustment improves how the assistant retrieves code context, making it slightly more flexible and comprehensive for developers.

f34f16a80654dbedc03e428bcef6bc40a4784d8e.text: A small internal fix corrected a broken link in a tool and shortened a wait time during deployment. The tool now finds the correct file list. The deployment process now waits ten seconds instead of a minute for the server to be ready. This affects internal engineers and speeds up their workflow.

8adbaf5a764d911a8b7d24d04d7f66e18ee9b2ae.text: The internal labels for the server and the assistant tool were updated to reflect the latest release. This change does not alter any features or behavior. Users will notice no difference.

10d3a623fc5bbda24c1d5c3690e0ee618eecf4c2.text: The assistant now treats a typed command with bad grammar as a missing tool, rather than showing a raw error. This applies to commands run by the assistant, not direct user inputs. People will see a cleaner fallback message instead of a technical error text.

039cc2fcaadaf98344b28f8608686639e5e6040a.text: The backend system now has a new rule for filtering out specific file paths. This change is internal and affects only the backend services. Users will not notice any difference yet, as the filtering logic is not actively used.

da8f45af149c6bbd6357dc8af4234c48de8b6635.text: A small internal fix clarified instructions for the assistant's file-reading feature. The instructions now explicitly state the assistant can only select from files that already exist, not create new ones. This change is live today and prevents the assistant from attempting to write files using the reading tool.

a8ce7118e3609a6b2c921e01183ecd8f453e425c.text: The AI assistant now follows stricter instructions to keep existing code comments and logic intact during edits. This change applies to internal tasks and is live immediately. A non-programmer would notice the assistant makes fewer unnecessary changes to the underlying software structure.

0c6ae21abfdd36c42508d92756d45a58e933fb17.text: The system now uses a standard, up-to-date method to measure text length. This change ensures the internal calculations remain accurate as the underlying service evolves. You will not notice any difference in how the tool behaves.

b72d9ee5c9ad777dc88f86be71f1de7da4007e40.text: The program now skips test files when building its server image, making the final package smaller and cleaner. It also added a helper tool to the shared parts, but nothing uses it yet. No visible changes for anyone today.

436a91c968214639b664c1b8c64d5571e725f506.text: The assistant now checks if a folder change command worked before saving the new location. If the command fails, it keeps the old location instead of getting confused. This prevents the assistant from looking for files in the wrong place after a failed attempt. This is a small internal fix available immediately.

658d323a4edd196f253471fffb843a5c7bab2fb9.text: The app now quietly prepares its memory for your project files before you ask a question, making the first answer faster. It also forces the file-picker to output only a strict list of paths, stopping it from adding confusing extra text. This is live for all users.

a057530b64f7268510ee4586f7342ddcac8aceb2.text: A small internal update makes the text-based tool easier to read by coloring the current folder name green and the assistant's replies blue. It also stops the tool from running shell commands when a question starts with 'what' or 'which', sending those to the assistant instead. Only people using this specific internal command-line tool will notice the color change and the new question handling.

b54a1daaab12901b9e8afd8575f6956bc78fc960.text: The assistant now remembers which folder it is in when running commands. Previously, every command started from the main project folder, so typing 'cd' to change folders had no effect on the next command. Now, if the assistant moves into a subfolder, the next command runs from that new location, and the command prompt shows the current folder name.

11da2ea162e545230221a28e9c527695d60c3737.text: A small internal update tells the system's file picker to skip certain reference documents. This prevents duplicate copies of those documents from being sent to the AI. Users will not notice any visual change, but the system may process requests slightly faster by ignoring redundant files.

e2af5e4b0d1eff03c534faae67b1db0eea65e128.text: The system now better understands long file paths when deciding which project files to share with the AI assistant. This internal adjustment helps the assistant find the correct files more reliably, especially in complex projects. Since this is a backend improvement, you will not see any immediate visual changes, but the assistant may make fewer errors when referencing specific files.

3f031b1990ef9473706fb968f3c9e1397735b906.text: The assistant now uses a smarter model to find files related to a request that aren't immediately obvious, improving search accuracy. It also checks if a file exists before trying to delete it during a reset, preventing errors if the file is already gone. These changes affect how the tool selects and manages files for everyone.

7f7e1e5d9d1ed21d35e4e813b482de26c4e583b3.text: A new safety check now confirms the system correctly identifies the specific comment and the user's permission level before removing it. This internal tooling update ensures the software follows strict rules for data handling. The change is live for the testing team, who will see the new confirmation steps in their reports.

b16069fba90733892204c961141be294766caeb4.text: The internal version label for the main server and the command-line tool was updated from 46 to 47. This is a minor housekeeping change for the engineering team. Users will not notice any difference in how the software behaves.

e4ee9f0732b9fa01dbcc9184c2b62262bfa0386f.text: The system now checks if it can write code correctly when it lacks extra background information. This internal test verifies the assistant creates the right files and avoids errors without hints. No customers see this change.

91c4a4a6ae820ffd9c693535eacaefe572734054.text: The internal test setup for the Manifold project was updated to remove a caching option and enable a mapping feature. This change fixes a build failure in the test environment. It only affects the internal testing process, so there will be no visible change for users.

7d2290025bada11b496290bcf90babe3ec7b1823.text: The system now loads its text-measuring tool once when starting up, instead of loading and unloading it every time it counts words. This change is internal and invisible to regular users, but it makes the background process slightly faster and more efficient when handling many files.

6a3f42b71e8280b52b1ea4136d60a4e65437e943.text: The internal deployment tool now deletes old software copies before installing a new one and labels each copy with its creation time. This change affects only the automated setup for internal servers, not the service itself. Anyone watching the deployment logs would see the cleanup step and the new time-based labels replacing the generic 'latest' tag.

9adc2e0f03a1ca6fad5812a8653e055dca4dd716.text: The system now runs multiple internal quality checks simultaneously instead of one after another. This change affects only the team maintaining the software, not everyday users. They will see results faster and get a clearer breakdown of which specific checks passed or failed.

17d000f69b76d9b2bfbe75205acca743d8fae3e4.text: The storage space for the computer running the backend services doubled from 10GB to 20GB. This prevents the system from running out of space for logs, which could cause errors or downtime. No visible changes will appear to the end user, but the service becomes more reliable.

5afb342c276e4fada0e837eff2f4a59c38fa7657.text: The testing system now grades internal checks like a quiz, counting how many pass versus fail instead of stopping at the first error. This change is for the internal team and does not affect customer-facing features. Developers will see a final score ratio in their test logs, helping them track overall progress even when some individual checks fail.

ab99d9e25b99b3786d97592159cfb1378f5be4d2.text: The command line now shows the project name before the prompt and runs any typed command immediately. This change affects internal tooling users. They will see the folder name in the prompt and notice commands execute without waiting for the assistant.

5814fa1bb7ef48aacf2421365ef3febb7e19ba20.text: The internal testing tool now gives partial credit for projects that compile with minor errors, instead of only awarding points for perfect success. This change is for the team evaluating automated coding assistants and does not affect the end product. If they looked, they would see the scoring reports become more detailed, showing exactly how close a project came to working.

5f88470bb786e7c810b5346462a0e0afe6203f9b.text: The service now stops waiting if the external AI provider takes longer than one minute to respond. This prevents the system from hanging indefinitely when the provider is slow or unresponsive. Users will notice the request fails quickly with an error instead of spinning forever.

29ac523f8c9684c05c3a16d258e710e903fe3860.text: The system now stops trying to continue a task after ten attempts instead of twenty. If the assistant fails to finish a step, it will show an error message rather than an empty response. This change is live and applies to all internal stream processing.

75e525e8d9fe924b794327fc0b2815c4f4d54019.text: A safety limit was added to the internal assistant process. If it tries to complete a task more than twenty times without success, it will now stop instead of running forever. This is a small internal safeguard; regular users won't notice any change in how the assistant works.

6278ff4309ddfdf4559ca9cac2333e5195531a52.text: The team updated the internal version number of the software. This is a minor housekeeping task that does not change how the program works. Users will not notice any difference.

2f5ba66fcd23a18efe394cdde082b68ca30d76be.text: The description of the software was updated to be more accurate. It no longer claims to be a super-intelligent, human-like system, but simply calls itself an AI assistant. This change affects only the text people read when learning about the tool, not how the tool actually works. You would notice this if you looked at the introduction page, where the wording is now more honest and modest.

b44b574b9613a88a19bdaba500c3ada3a5f48c61.text: A small internal update changed how the backend software is packaged for release. Instead of using a generic label that gets overwritten, the system now assigns a unique date-and-time stamp to each version. This helps the team track exactly which version is running, but customers will not notice any difference in how the service works.

a6a7e8373a4d63e88b6949d8c0e50f8dabf5a3dd.text: The system now remembers the background instructions it uses to find relevant files, so it does not have to read them from scratch every time. This makes the file selection step faster and cheaper to run. Regular users will not notice any change in how the app looks or behaves.

e3d7ecf5e945857fb978c162c08d9bee1c45b3b0.text: The system stopped showing error messages when a routine connection check fails. This keeps the technical logs clean without affecting how the service works for you.

0a074a6fe9e7ed40a972f9828d57a0594f7b48ca.text: The system's tool for measuring text length was updated to a more stable version. This internal fix ensures the service remains available, though regular users will not see any visible changes.

93a9f340acb4c805d80af606144cbf1ba310a7b8.text: A background task that removes old connections now survives a single error. Previously, one mistake stopped the cleanup permanently. This affects internal systems, not the visible user interface.

5de755f789383c905878a4067098aa72333c2954.text: The team added a new shortcut to start the application using a specific configuration. 138b6523ea8bba873b18ae504146131a97839737.text: A small internal fix corrected a step that prepares the application for release. It ensures a required part of the code is ready before the main build starts, and it uses a compatible version of a library that colors text in the terminal. This change affects only the software's internal build process and will not be visible to end users.

129e703b4190c531c880480151dacc95a72bc406.text: This small internal update teaches the project's safety checker about a specific set of tools. It fixes a gap where the checker might have wrongly flagged valid code as broken. Developers will notice fewer false alarms when reviewing changes, but users see no difference.

c224d5cf9b5d417b71f517c3b1cfbe0a07867b14.text: The team fixed a small internal error in the tool that prepares the app for download. Before the fix, the tool sometimes failed to clean up temporary files after publishing a new version. This change ensures the cleanup happens correctly every time, keeping the app's files tidy for future updates.

d11936f407a1f2e2a00efd8826f46d99d83b7cb5.text: When the connection to the service fails, the tool now stops spinning its loading indicator and resets its state before showing a retry message. This prevents the interface from appearing stuck or frozen while waiting for a response that will never arrive.

4eceb0e0dce596c3a3f0e89263a724ba5589d3a8.text: The program now shuts down instantly when stopped manually. Staff running the service will see it close cleanly instead of hanging. This is a small internal adjustment with no visible effect on customers.

e45f260c04c55d5d0c55050c0f1a1f46c3082251.text: The system now records the original text of new files before processing them. This small internal update helps engineers diagnose issues with how code changes are generated. Regular users will not notice any difference.

b4f4a1c8e883bcb00978eb7b3d77d7cd7072e72e.text: The AI assistant now checks if it has all the necessary files before answering. If it thinks it has enough information, it must double-check and actively ask for any missing files instead of just assuming it can proceed. This helps the assistant avoid guessing when it lacks the full context of a project.

f977ea9080d8aafbeef118619502b9a6d875fc5f.text: The assistant's internal instructions now tell it to ask for missing files before it starts describing the code it already has. This applies to all users of the AI coding tool. You might notice the AI asks for more context earlier in the conversation, rather than after giving an initial summary.

c86b10d05f2666442089a002166eade9ad99c578.text: The internal release number increased. This change affects only the software's version tracking. Users will not notice any difference in how the application works.

74bd3f565bffd3e804fb7ee04373547b4aa6f25a.text: The system now waits a tiny bit longer to decide if you are pasting text or just typing quickly. This helps it catch paste actions that were previously missed due to slow typing speed. The change is active immediately for the command-line tool.

9972f7a121ed80148afe4ee4b1f62b38a4c0309c.text: The server now includes a configuration file in its final build, ensuring it has the correct settings when running. A version check was also fixed to stop looking for files in the wrong place during development, preventing errors. This is a small internal update; regular users will not notice any changes.

2a1da4dab3ae9b1e1794cbb7aca3416a0505dc10.text: A small internal fix ensures the system correctly records the first change to a file. Previously, if no prior version existed, the update was ignored, causing the undo function to fail for new files. This change is live and prevents errors when undoing initial edits.

077c204682065b3c083ef7fcbc9ccffff05b7b79.text: The internal safety filter for AI responses was turned off. This affects only the backend system that handles requests. The visible result is that AI answers are no longer automatically blocked if they contain sensitive or unsafe topics.

e735ec85762098d81964e4a5071854052bd8f702.text: The version number for the internal backend and the command-line tool was increased to mark a new release. This is a small housekeeping change for the team. Users will not notice any difference in how the software behaves.

beaa17a54105cca01fc8ed4e2fc727b0be689d25.text: The service now accepts the main instructions as either a single block of text or as multiple separate parts. This fixes a mismatch with the external assistant provider's rules. Nothing changes for normal use; the assistant behaves the same. The update is live.

fa4da0ab3aad385caa2d0eb0be36422cfc82e4b3.text: A small internal fix corrected the undo button in chat so it can now revert to the very first saved version of files. This affects the chat tool's history navigation, ensuring users can step back to the beginning of their work. The change is live.

28f5b49ec01651f15db22fa86dd52daa97dab378.text: The app now shows one clear message when it cannot reach the server, then confirms when it reconnects, instead of repeating errors. The startup screen also waits until the connection is ready before showing the folder warning. This applies to everyone using the command line tool.

88a37c539f708e91b08c99a7d39f7d2503ee6cbb.text: The assistant now remembers the overall layout of your project files and its background knowledge notes for the entire conversation, instead of re-reading them every time you ask a question. This internal optimization speeds up responses slightly. You would only notice this if you compared the time it takes for the first reply versus later replies in the same chat session.

af6e99710b317e7db155e12408286afde3766f63.text: The command-line tool now opens instantly instead of waiting for background setup to finish. This change affects people using the internal text-based interface. They will notice the prompt appears immediately, though the tool still waits for setup to complete before processing the first message.

2348663a7319595360bf355b7ba77d8229560f7c.text: The AI assistant now follows a new rule to make only the smallest necessary code changes and stop to ask for more instructions. This internal adjustment aims to prevent the assistant from making unwanted extra edits during tasks. a0c552072f3588c4501e4bb04da2220e50c5c9c6.text: The instructions given to the AI assistant were reorganized into separate sections for better clarity. This is an internal maintenance task that does not change how the assistant behaves or what it can do. Users will notice no difference in the assistant's responses or features.

0cbe3ff3d039b022031b83c7d9d3e2612f1f2697.text: The server's underlying engine was swapped for a faster one. This is an internal change that makes the system run more efficiently. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the application looks or behaves.

e4b3d766dde242dbd34af5e40a801ab729f36d22.text: The assistant now checks if it has enough information before starting work and stops after two failed attempts to try a different approach. This small internal update helps prevent it from guessing incorrectly or getting stuck in a loop, making its responses more reliable and less frustrating for you.

708bb5499554d3681ca34b5060d86e135548783d.text: The tool now saves a snapshot of your project files before it starts working. This helps it track exactly what changed. You won't see anything different, but the system has a clearer record of your work.

8164ee2ad970632ed612f141d883459eccc435eb.text: The AI assistant now checks its own memory more carefully before starting work. It will ask for missing information if it realizes it doesn't have everything needed to complete a task, but only for files that actually exist in the project. This change is already live and helps prevent the assistant from guessing or working with incomplete data.

f5e02504a5ae732101c476b65df9296a621b3a75.text: The program now checks the correct folder before saving your edits, fixing an issue where it might have missed files if you started it from the wrong location. This is a small internal update for people using the command-line tool. You will not see a new button or menu, but your changes will now save reliably every time.

4ebc99deffebb8dca59db124002dba9b291b192d.text: Small internal fix for the code assistant. When it fails to read a file, it now keeps the old version and logs the error instead of crashing the whole request. Users might see a blank line after the loading spinner stops, and clearer instructions in the menu.

f7806cf07b5919933ec7d4f4f7407473438e1ad8.text: The assistant's undo and redo buttons now show simpler text like 'Undo last change' instead of 'Undoing last change'. This small update affects people using the command-line tool, making the messages clearer when they reverse or repeat edits.

53c28f871e6643f80f80f86c923f11708a9bb11c.text: The system now saves the static background information sent to the AI, such as project structure and general rules, so it does not need to resend this large block every time. This change applies internally to the backend service and is live. Users will not see any visual difference, but the AI may respond slightly faster because it skips reading the same basic instructions repeatedly.

f7124b68c843c913e947df945560e0d71f5d03f2.text: The app's internal release number was updated to keep track of this version. This change is for the development team only. Regular users will not see any difference.

55e6b53c51e231dca63340cf3be5dc31b9364fd3.text: The instructions guiding the coding assistant were reorganized to clarify how it accesses project files and uses tools. This internal change affects the assistant's behavior but is not visible to the user.

f654b710fc71f37dee91fa334b1b9f4825cc10c5.text: Pressing the Escape key now stops the text being written. It no longer opens a menu if nothing is being written. This change is live for people using the command line tool.

b17a5633b4ca701fb88f08aa3e5161f465118fd2.text: The tool now ignores self-explanatory notes like 'Add this import' when creating code changes. This makes the final output cleaner and easier to read for anyone checking the updates. The change is active now.

58e20dff5dd4e25b668878cf8f85f86f69c5147e.text: Small internal fix for command-line tool. Undo/redo messages now appear only after action succeeds. Failed attempts show 'No more undo/redo' instead of silence.

b6b56b35a163ec66ca4687a7be5773f7ed0f95ee.text: The assistant was told not to use shell commands to create or edit files. It must use the normal file-editing method instead. This is a small internal rule change, live today, and it mainly affects how the assistant behaves behind the scenes.

00d7919b9aa249263d7d19d38dd97a66e8306784.text: The application no longer automatically creates a storage folder for chats when it starts up. This internal change affects the system's setup process, not the features available to people using the software. Users will notice no difference in how the app works or looks.

63532e78aaf889034e87f463a4861813b6f9265d.text: Internal housekeeping updated the version label for the assistant's core components. This change does not affect how the software works. Users will see no difference in performance or features.

fa63a68f0819a8de5fd4f034b958334306b4cffe.text: The AI assistant now saves and applies file updates immediately after each step, instead of waiting until the end of its reply. This helps the assistant keep track of the latest file versions during complex tasks. a75a11152a6ca1105754c8bbe3c4ecd2f7550f95.text: The text shown when the software is outdated was shortened. It now just says a new version exists, instead of showing the exact version numbers you currently have. This change is live and affects anyone who sees the update notice.

71bfc86adbea6aece98931154253b4d8d9ae72cd.text: The internal labels for the core system and the user-facing tool were updated. This change is live but has no visible effect on how the software works or looks. It serves only to mark the current state of the product.

63f191756da1bbfed0c21c5546ff80c16f206b7e.text: The team set a specific control to ensure the AI assistant gives consistent answers instead of varying its responses. This affects the internal tool's reliability. A person might notice the assistant repeating the same output for the same input.

e660eed1ee376323f25735b4fc80471cbbadd5bb.text: The system now passes the AI's original explanation along with the code changes when generating file updates. This prevents the AI from accidentally deleting unchanged sections of your code that it forgot to mark as existing. You should notice fewer errors where parts of your files disappear during an edit.

91edc1f008ecfcbe1061646034c880943a6c4d8f.text: A new test case was added to check that the system correctly handles missing action lines. This change is internal and does not affect any features or user experience. No users will notice any difference.

24ca807698520e29f4e6d0d7144f61d044355942.text: The text-based assistant now uses typed words for undo, redo, and help instead of special key combinations. People using it will see the opening message tell them to type help, and the menu lists the new words. After undoing or redoing, it says it is undoing or redoing the last change. The change is live now and is small.

3ede4b9ef73b2c63626b319a74a88d03ada958a7.text: The system switched to a different artificial intelligence model for generating code changes. This update is live and affects all internal users creating code edits. You might notice slightly different wording or structure in the suggested changes, but the overall process remains the same.

729dd03a1d1948e6c16c90919d7c6101c4a710d0.text: The system now keeps a record of files it previously identified as relevant, ensuring they are not accidentally dropped during updates. This internal fix helps the assistant maintain context across conversations without losing track of important documents. Users will notice more consistent responses when discussing multiple files, as the system remembers earlier references.

4b216929255223d16c52bb9a09c5de3abde4f172.text: The internal instructions for the AI assistant were clarified to specify that a separate component applies the edits, requiring shorter, explicit change requests. This helps the assistant avoid overwriting user changes or deleting unchanged code. This is an internal adjustment; users will not notice immediate changes.

3f8b579382b457dc4522d73da9a3062b3ae2b57e.text: The AI assistant now has an instruction to keep your manual changes intact when it edits files. This helps prevent the tool from accidentally overwriting work you did while it was thinking. 583aa0626abe520f57608b3665c0bda83a710d9a.text: A test added to verify the system correctly removes error-handling code from comment deletion. This is internal work for the team building the tool. It does not change how the app behaves for anyone using it today.

6a7aa5141c1e2529077307bb6937ca11a345c1e7.text: The internal build number for the assistant was updated. This is a housekeeping change that does not alter how the software works. Users will not notice any difference in their experience.

10c9d37b5107b50b193dafc8841732a7f80b95bc.text: The assistant now automatically reads web links included in your last message and uses that information to answer questions, similar to how it previously handled links found in project notes. This change applies to all users interacting with the tool and ensures that relevant online documentation or resources are considered without requiring manual input.

cab368ef9a62857a642b1b7e766f74add8537ea2.text: The internal label for the current version of the AI assistant was updated from the previous number to the next one. This change affects only the software's internal tracking system and does not alter how the assistant works. Users will not notice any difference in the assistant's behavior or features.

d9775dd20e37da9c948ceea5c1f21ae9fc8bd60d.text: The system now tags internal file-editing tasks with the specific user's ID. This change applies to the backend and does not affect the user interface. No visible change will occur for end users.

ea9015aa9c22aaa0cbeda2c446d77b0e602ab871.text: The system now uses a newer, faster, and cheaper AI model to find relevant files for requests. The previous two-step search process was simplified to use only this single model. This change affects how file requests are processed internally, but users will not notice any difference in the results.

e31b5f853ccb43e43a5ae3e97d329f6d50a16d2c.text: The assistant no longer loads all project files into memory at once. It now only fetches specific files when it needs to read or change them. This saves space and prevents the assistant from getting confused by too much information.

646e41095783f6ce01346f6487f71bb383e4eb54.text: The AI assistant now checks its confidence in a plan before choosing it, ensuring it asks for clarification if unsure. It also receives strict instructions to make minimal code changes and avoid breaking existing features. These internal rules are active immediately for all interactions.

25f3fe76ee7af4776c620e81e0ad087162b02d68.text: Small internal update. The system now checks AI conversations for security risks before processing them. Users might see blocked messages if they try to trick the AI into doing something unsafe. This feature is live today.

3b4ed03fcecaa75b207956fa60fdcf07a1080b53.text: A small internal fix improves how the command-line tool handles pasted text. Previously, multi-line pastes could trigger separate responses for each line. Now, pasted content is buffered together, so the tool processes it as a single input.

716ba48f0206c4bdc92ec1351fa15908f31e71b6.text: The system now tags each request to the AI with a unique identifier derived from the user's device fingerprint. This allows the AI service to track usage and apply limits per user. A user would not notice any change in how the application behaves or responds.

a291dca7a8c9eccdccdda944f6439faa76daf28f.text: The system's internal connection to the AI service was updated to a newer standard. This is a small, behind-the-scenes maintenance task that keeps the software compatible with future updates. Regular users will not notice any changes in how the application looks or behaves.

2ace24ce4c4783985274f508bf22919ad944b92b.text: The internal tool now automatically creates missing folders before saving files. This prevents errors when the tool tries to write to a location that does not yet exist. Users will notice fewer failures when the system applies changes to new or nested file structures.

167fc49d8e6fe45e8e551b8b950f29b33df949c8.text: The internal tool that creates file edits now uses a stronger AI model. This change is already active. Users may notice slightly better results when the system suggests changes to their code.

5cb4611c2d42ad79e951a9d5d1193db5b3984176.text: The internal tooling got a tiny update that only changed its label. The program's behavior stayed exactly the same. You would not notice any difference in how it works.

ce4c9e3658175fcf90ceaddf43aad3bf7d353b43.text: The text command tool now ignores pasted text that arrives in a fast burst. This stops accidental commands from running when someone pastes a block of text. The change is live and affects anyone using the tool.

94adf5fb064359dfcd5360ef9831e90ae8f72e43.text: The team updated the internal tracking number for the assistant software. This change only affects how the system manages its own records and does not alter any features or behaviors. You will not notice any difference in how the assistant works.

85f06cb54f1c0a96577a7a9e373232de627c9e35.text: The AI assistant now makes sure to save notes when a user corrects it, helping it remember mistakes for next time. The command-line tool also fixes a bug where pasting text would sometimes fail to register as a paste. These are small internal updates that are live today.

834fd560811b8e2954481970a12f0942eb16bf05.text: The AI assistant now asks for more clarification when it is unsure about what you want. If its confidence level is lower than before, it will stop to check with you instead of guessing. This affects all chat sessions and makes the assistant more cautious.

0c9caf592f2d2af87ebbe17a8e991727243d4540.text: The internal address the system uses to talk to its AI service changed to match a company rebrand. This is a small backend update. People using the app would not notice any difference.

ad123adb0ab8edb8d9f7689aa03b113e39c2b702.text: The tool's menu now appears once when a specific button is pressed, rather than staying on screen and blocking other actions. It displays the menu title in random bright colors and clears the previous line instead of the whole screen. This change is internal and affects how the tool looks and behaves during use.

108cb92c1d9876cba6293e6b671d5bd479b94d4a.text: The internal assistant now checks how unsure it is about a request instead of how confident it is. 18e7005f8467e2e9652f0edac600762e3256d6be.text: The menu logo now uses geometric shapes with three random colors instead of block letters. The assistant's internal instructions for asking for clarification were simplified. These are small, internal adjustments.

ab6adec5f86225152d1b5c80c92de8006cd37c86.text: The assistant now moves to the project's main folder before running any command. 3463b5ab00159dde8d12775cc64a2356893561d8.text: A small internal change fixes a formatting rule for a temporary file created during the software build process. Only the automated build system sees this file, so customers and developers will not notice any difference in the final product.

726f29a193eb5ca6df7007d3d517fc72d74284c8.text: The assistant now gives clearer updates when running commands, especially if a command takes too long. Instead of just saying 'timed out', it explains the wait and shows any partial results. This helps people understand what happened without guessing.

1e55853080386c44abb26ef55ae1b910b8964ae2.text: The assistant's internal instructions now tell it to ask for more file information if it needs it, then restart its planning process. cf59adfa96aba3cd3c0ae2571ccbc79343836bfc.text: The assistant now correctly identifies which folder is the current project. adea156802b0c3e9e498ccf2b0c35974de9ded72.text: The internal team updated the release number for the AI coding assistant tool to mark a new version. This is a small administrative change that does not add features or fix bugs. Regular users will not notice any difference in how the tool works.

182fa2dff468b2b9d55179d1e254387aa48e372d.text: The internal tooling received a routine update to its tracking label. This change affects only the underlying software package used by the system. No visible behavior changed for the end user.

fdad7a3cea8e9baeee33c821eff94d189828fd19.text: The assistant now stops running a computer instruction after ten seconds and shows any results it gathered up to that point. 53789205f380cc3dd994ee70c5e6a9a3e06add65.text: The AI assistant now rates its certainty (0-100) before editing files. If it is less than 90% sure it understands your request, it stops and asks you to clarify instead of guessing. This prevents unwanted changes when your instructions are vague.

5d6d472a7e58d375b97a722abf7f384cd8c7d9fa.text: The command-line tool now shows a spinning animation instead of three dots while waiting for a response. This animation stops as soon as the first part of the reply arrives, so you know the assistant has started thinking. Additionally, when the assistant runs a command, the tool now prints the completion status code to the screen.

380ebf372cdeac37b0fc2365c8de5a18a92e063b.text: The project's internal labels now consistently mark the code as unlicensed, replacing mixed or missing notes. This standardizes how the software describes its ownership rights in its configuration files. It is an internal cleanup with no visible effect on how the application runs.

8e4bcab16c46c3b4cd9c7ae98149ec5b246c79e7.text: The AI assistant now recognizes that general advice or contradictions, not just mistakes, are worth remembering. It saves these notes to its memory file after finishing its work, rather than before. This helps the assistant learn from feedback more consistently.

26a6f8d6373c4c7e9816805ba5b400239dee5058.text: A small internal update teaches the coding assistant to respect existing program logic and avoid removing safety checks or adding unnecessary features. This helps people who use the assistant to edit software by preventing it from accidentally breaking working code. You would notice the assistant making fewer unwanted changes to files.

4a4d25764b97290ec02cb877105331a7cc4cbd51.text: This small internal change is live in the tool and affects people who run it from the wrong folder. It also clears leftover text when the tool closes.

d5a852d0725232b4806fb5088796160a67fee30f.text: The internal release marker for the assistant was updated. This change affects only the deployment tracking system. No users will notice any difference in the assistant's behavior.

dfb7ed8fcc5250ebfd7887b6b4a58cfe0590dfd6.text: A small internal fix corrected how the system reads blank spaces at the very beginning and end of text instructions. The change is active now and improves the reliability of automated file updates.

5815032be151d6d273eed2303699edcf0fd323e0.text: The system now automatically removes extra blank lines at the start of generated files. This prevents messy formatting that could confuse other tools. 083a060ca9f4544cdcfedf34350a93bb157adff4.text: The assistant now skips searching for project files when you type a command instead of a question. This saves time and avoids showing irrelevant file lists in the chat window. The change is active immediately.

83aabe570d1c4e1401398e6d96b6f4c91c14c20d.text: Developers added safety checks to ensure the system correctly updates communication rules. f347eed4ada633148087b31daf567c613ea90470.text: The system now handles errors more gracefully, preventing crashes when issues occur during file requests or API calls. 8e18438d05f682b2793fbae585d9a7ba65741d36.text: The internal instructions the assistant uses to find relevant files were reorganized to prevent specific system text from leaking into its analysis. 99e137ae93ee9ece6a9a7c1ebf0838d8bfd2990a.text: The system now sends whole-file updates instead of small search-and-replace snippets. This affects people using the command-line tool, making edits more reliable for large or complex files. 9a9c514a858218e6e04ff162318bc213d57b4fae.text: The assistant now receives the most relevant project files automatically, rather than having to ask for them before making changes. a8aa186e55a1cbadd10fbfcea5f1166157a4d2ec.text: The software now sends requests to its two artificial intelligence services through a third-party monitoring company. 82beff8938c9dbed81038959bd7de58482a08bb6.text: The system now wraps conversation text in quotes and escape codes when sending it to the assistant. 2ee70575b64e03eb88061d1ef403c7cbf994a3e4.text: Every request you send to the assistant now carries a unique label, and the server attaches this label to all replies. The app checks this label to ensure it displays responses for the correct question, preventing confusion if multiple requests overlap. This change is active in the current version.

a685d7755e69a75bfdd4a411b9acf3e65619e22b.text: The software's internal label was updated to mark a new minor release. This affects the tool's distribution package. Users will not notice any change in behavior.

afba5af63c25c8835945eda70a9117ef9951d24d.text: The assistant now remembers which documents it has already been shown. It stops asking to see the same pages over and over again. This makes it faster and less likely to get stuck in a loop. The change is live and helps anyone using the internal tool.

26a934456ed7a4b4a5223013cf7e69eccbad0ac6.text: The system now reads a different label in the text describing file changes to find the correct file name. This fixes a bug where changes were applied to the wrong file or failed completely. The fix is live and requires no action from you.

105b6250c6a7b540cf610c381240e86f015a16db.text: The assistant now tells you which files it is reading. It also shows your project folders directly, without the extra top-level folder name. This makes the list of files easier to read.

64a25d71569463067303f06c0c93c72572fbd965.text: The AI assistant now receives lists of files sorted with the most important ones first. This helps the assistant focus on the most relevant information when answering questions. It is an internal change that is live today, so users might notice slightly better answers.

63d4625c2cbd17c41a4301659b7ce819b304bc76.text: The system now asks two different AI models for file suggestions at the same time: one picks the most important files, and the other casts a wider net. It combines these lists to remove duplicates. This helps the assistant find the right context more reliably, though the change is internal and not directly visible to you.

b87028262f6a5d870126ea483302cb85d5b93c02.text: The internal guide describing how the system works was updated to match the current setup. This is for the team maintaining the software, not for customers. People using the product will see no changes.

1b712e5f1c642eb5fa98d1df6cb3b10f16f2915d.text: The assistant now selects relevant project files automatically using natural language instead of requiring explicit paths. 5c4b02d9a49aba52f1c0e129ea77b3889d493ffb.text: The tool now shows the list of loaded files in green text instead of blue, matching the color of the label above it. c91e9d666a74a8101af3ff71ad67d7a82e626684.text: A small internal fix corrected how a background service finds shared file tools. This prevents errors when the service builds or runs. Regular users will not see any change.

f3243f024b2d10f2a8bc9dd6f95f3796f2ab9a8d.text: The assistant now picks up to 25 files to read, ignoring repeats and folders it should skip. This makes its answers about your code more focused. The change is live.

d07c29de932ab6022db9d3d52dd58dc0d9a36796.text: The internal label for the assistant tool was updated to mark a new release. This change affects only the software's version tracking and has no impact on how the tool works. Users will notice no difference in performance or features.

b5c0bfe715e5039f527623630959910a2157dbe2.text: This internal change updates the written guides that explain how the software works. It does not alter the software itself. d286f873e19f46d4629469c6e6fffb4323631881.text: The assistant now receives its core instructions about handling web links and saving notes through a permanent, behind-the-scenes channel rather than alongside each individual message. This internal cleanup ensures these rules are always applied consistently. Regular users will notice no difference in how the tool behaves or responds.

a3ff180f323ba45d7623c73bfac233a3f600785f.text: The AI assistant now checks for other places that use a renamed item before changing it, preventing broken links. It is also restricted from touching files outside the current project folder. These internal safety rules apply to all conversations immediately.

c8ca3f1b922450a98f239013efb57c43fd3f53da.text: Developers moved a small piece of code that formats folder lists into a shared spot to keep things tidy. This change is internal and affects only the code structure. Users will notice no difference in how the software works.

fb58235d16d47825439bb7840573652c19a00dd7.text: The assistant was told to read more background files before starting work. This applies to internal staff using the tool.
