f47b3f976467d6e7a7d74d2d194227a5b7dcae38.text: The internal tool received a routine update to its version number. This change does not affect how the software works or what users see. It is simply a bookkeeping step to keep track of releases.

939542dbe591e65ea5849cf29d7a1a30d3e45e28.text: The startup screen now lists the folder the assistant can access and explains what it can do. The tips section was rewritten to be clearer about how to help the assistant improve. This change is live and affects anyone using the tool.

182f4530e763cd4d5ea1b868f7c8ff55ec28cc0b.text: Internal update to the assistant's tooling package. No new features or fixes added. The change is not live for users and has no visible impact on the assistant's behavior.

9bc2e51edb889c1c9a57b7707167e70258caedf3.text: Previously, when a command produced any error message, the system discarded the normal output and showed only the error. Now, both the normal output and any error messages are shown together. This helps the assistant see complete results from commands, even when those commands report warnings or issues alongside their main output.

df3047298098a06e9306328fa09300d35bc4eb6c.text: The instructions for the coding assistant were reorganized to be clearer. The tool now automatically works on your current folder unless you tell it to use a different one. You can also undo or redo file changes using keyboard shortcuts.

a65dcd02b1a8753aeb1cf44d6e1b59c2a34a1360.text: The program stops showing error messages when it cannot open certain folders or files while building a project view. This change is internal and live today. A person watching the screen will see a cleaner list without red warning text about missing access.

4933c6335fc244e12e3dd1413c24c827fd711a79.text: The assistant now runs typed commands and shows only the result, skipping extra explanations unless asked. This affects internal testing, where users will see cleaner output from command executions.

579eaa90e04ca60a8be12a4077e20cd7cff902f8.text: The app stopped trying to guess the folder location if the system failed to find it automatically. Instead, it now immediately reports an error when the current location is unknown. This internal cleanup means users will see a clear failure message rather than a warning followed by a potentially incorrect action.

967d8a04f1cf376de26634a4683dc4d413818672.text: The app's internal version number was updated. This change is for the team's tracking only. Normal users will not notice any difference.

96b27cb268419a95ff3074414bce203ebb798f69.text: The command-line tool now displays a help message when requested and explicitly states which folder it will access upon startup. It also ignores typed text while a menu is open to prevent errors. These updates apply to internal tooling and are live for anyone using the command-line interface.

6f6bf64e518a6b2c1b7919035e1d0fa48c3101b4.text: The assistant now finds its project folder even if the folder it started in was deleted. This affects people running the tool from a missing directory. They would see a warning message instead of a crash.

1d31f52b488c5509c6ec43b6ae891313cfc8080d.text: The command-line tool now prevents duplicate prompts from appearing and ignores new input while processing a previous request. This stops the interface from getting confused or showing the same question twice. Only people using the command-line version will notice this cleaner, more responsive behavior.

f5b545f4051816951d89c3d7deedda256de3ad04.text: The file list feature now correctly reads ignore rules that start with a slash. Previously, these rules were broken, causing the assistant to show files it should have hidden. This fix applies to internal project file browsing. It is live today.

b72978018a8365e59b50ed7910ee47f07c35c29c.text: The tool now requires you to type the folder path where your work is located when starting it, instead of asking you to choose a folder after it opens. This affects internal users launching the command-line tool. If you start the tool without providing a folder path, it will default to the current location you are in, rather than pausing to ask.

31f7de7cac01d96dead9146ddd61f9d54ac0916f.text: The deployment system now updates the server directly instead of deleting and rebuilding it from scratch. This change speeds up software releases for the backend team by preserving existing server settings and avoiding the wait time associated with full setup.

b0747decef0e9c53413e9cf4b09190456b996f87.text: The assistant now receives the project's file list as a nested folder structure instead of a single flat list. This helps it better understand which files belong to which folders. You might notice it references file paths more accurately when discussing your code.

a72118747f09a2e07a0ad93c289360752fb8b968.text: The internal tooling package updated its version number. This change affects only the build system and has no visible impact on the user interface or application behavior.

aff53c7551c70dcad00d744b35a9902b95c069d2.text: This small internal update reorganizes how the system records the size of requests sent to the AI. 1f86dbbdd6e16a41222551540eb99bf60e5382b1.text: The assistant now knows the exact folder where your project lives. 46be127346fb972fea119f4fe244051d423b585e.text: The service now connects to a different web address for real-time updates. This change is live and applies to the main application environment. Users will not notice any difference in behavior, speed, or features.

f958197f5e506f58dd43054cfe8668f691e89cdc.text: A small internal update ensures a final line break is added to a specific configuration file during the build process. 33ffa777d15bae95e4aaeabfdeb2533708cdab88.text: A small internal update now records the size of text sent to the AI assistant. This change is for developers to help them monitor performance. Regular users will not see any difference or notice this activity.

d0954571c6b2760060e03f1fee816a23fff1b208.text: The software's internal cleanup rules were adjusted to ignore specific temporary files created by the backend service during testing. 59ae997b11f54f1c34c578778feed1b4c7ac01a2.text: The AI assistant now uses a specific search tool to find all places where a piece of code is used before changing its name or type. This prevents broken links in the code when updates happen. It is live today for users working on their own projects.

5c80a84f990f119a51db1f172827e751735f635c.text: The internal instructions for the AI assistant now clarify that it only saves file changes after it finishes writing its entire response. 682e9fe5268e2eb2892d214c6cf4dfe22235f1e3.text: The internal tooling team updated the version label for the command-line assistant package. This is a metadata-only change with no functional updates. Users will not notice any difference in behavior.

b315e16373a3a4de337c60dd025dd6c3dae6c9f4.text: The team updated their internal record to show that keyboard and editing problems on Windows computers are now fixed. 4ae09f01e7101d41e80049d3a3124268d40df2cc.text: The chat tool stopped saving conversations as files on the computer. This change is internal and minor, so people using the chat will not notice any difference in how it works.

24667acf4343433cba3279e8a8235efd0df83c7b.text: The assistant can now run commands on your computer, such as searching for text or checking file status. 5a1168bae1ff1b897b96323f72fe2cb1cd1cae9d.text: The command line tool no longer shows an extra blank prompt line when it finishes a task. This small cleanup affects people using the terminal interface. They will see a slightly cleaner screen with less visual noise.

b50f3e0787f1faf744fc8a879bd0dd9470643d50.text: The software's internal label was updated to mark a new release. This change affects the team managing the application's distribution. A non-programmer would notice nothing, as this is a routine administrative step.

cf60580e175b2db88db0bc2818b8ea16fbdba792.text: The assistant now finds project files by reading the project's own ignore lists instead of checking a fixed set of folder names. baf505b980bb3e0e3c5d316a82b97e0bb170f8f2.text: The assistant's internal label was updated to match the latest release. This change is for internal tracking and affects only the software's own identification. You will not notice any difference in how the assistant works or behaves today.

efd99c7795a40dc705ea225946d8e2efd1e9fd92.text: The team recorded specific bugs found during a Windows test, including issues with the backspace key, left arrow, copy commands, and failed edits. c12ece9730cc02fb05a607840526fa595b0433c3.text: The tool now recognizes that Windows files use a different invisible break between lines than Mac or Linux files. e788290a856521ec286135becbe706f8ae01dedd.text: The AI assistant's internal instructions were updated to encourage it to brainstorm multiple solutions before acting, rather than just planning the first idea that comes to mind. 112c961f63b83290118b293bbb8a05e0fb1316c0.text: The text commands 'undo' and 'redo' now work in the terminal, and the keyboard shortcuts for going back and forward changed from Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y to Ctrl+U/Ctrl+R. 2f3f472c6863b430222380e62ef807d6f8d142f4.text: The tool's internal connection to the server was renamed to make its purpose clearer to the team. This change does not affect how the software works or looks for anyone using it. Nothing visible will change.

b0511da7882199f5cacbbd0b37380c3fe33dde85.text: The AI coding assistant now saves chat history and reads project files from the folder where you run the command, rather than the folder where the tool was installed. 7ec8dddba2b6139649c21b314ea6c24c062cb47e.text: The startup menu's text was updated to show the correct keys for closing the app and undoing changes. This affects people using the command-line assistant. They will see clearer instructions on the screen.

d8e0e8bda4483fb8973248c4589cc7f3ab2d63f2.text: When you save a web link in your project's notes, the assistant now automatically reads that page and adds its contents to your notes. 5e81bc14db8a67c436efd3daf760b76f7fb31b37.text: The internal team removed a leftover instruction that told the AI assistant to look for a shared tool that it never actually used. 4d25562637e4f7a3ab075a45705211bb33a7e90c.text: The system now checks for a 'production' setting to decide how to connect. Right now, it uses an unsecured connection for this mode, which is a temporary internal configuration choice. No visible change for end users yet.

02565d598fcc0b55c1ac1769c8807d9fdc7d6c20.text: The internal setup for running the service on Google Cloud was automated to handle building, uploading, and starting the server with necessary security rules. f2dbd7a08cd0a43be5d10aa3a45ec34f8504400a.text: The application's default network address changed to port 4242. 35b93639aaa0860381c7b3f2c3ba39bee6170b8d.text: The tool that calculates file changes no longer reads the conversation history. This keeps the result focused on the actual code updates. It is live now. You will not see a change in the output.

72591c6b937cf3872d2e2162a041fedadb2e3965.text: The command-line tool now checks if the AI actually proposed file edits before displaying the 'Generating file changes' message. a68ca54ce698b982ea9fc51d829501e1ed954c10.text: A fix ensures that AI responses are always saved, even if the user stops the generation early. This prevents a bug where the chat history would become disorganized or incomplete after an interruption. The change applies to the command-line tool and is live immediately.

bf2c0599c4ad19c2859bca142536c5b8f8187e71.text: The build process for the Manicode tool was updated to include a shared library and copy necessary files into the final package. This internal change ensures the tool compiles correctly and includes all required components, though it is not a visible feature for end users yet.

6efe8eaafa786edb594157b9bb413f90093b2426.text: A small internal fix stops the command-line tool from erasing a half-typed message when you press the up or down arrow keys to look through past commands. 033bd3caba7038d2fde5ba62b7a1e3554c5dccac.text: The startup screen now shows a static graphic and usage tips instead of an interactive chat list. 5b3e9d0875c0b9501bb7a38993cb70c999308f3c.text: The assistant no longer automatically downloads web pages linked in its memory files. This ensures users receive immediate feedback on failures and are not misled by false success indicators.

f4d70bdcc4276869ebffbfe0dd36d4839a93305b.text: The command-line tool now displays typed characters instantly instead of redrawing the entire line each time. cabb0ebd15ee2b4ec5e01b4af15e1c2be2f3dde2.text: The chat interface now correctly handles multi-line text input. 6840865ee112e14b4b38f78a9de774bc20187aad.title: Onboarding adds web clilogin surface values

Unknown missing forged input defaults `web`, older form sends none, forged value blocks segment pollution. Scope Shared/Core `common/src/constants/freebuff-onboarding.ts` only, `web` dashboard dialog, `cli_login` CLI Desktop browser landing sharing auth code redemption.

a659222a118d5923e8a49c83f036c3faeab55fd8.title: Onboarding referral shuffles options, retires Reddit GitHub Copilot
a659222a118d5923e8a49c83f036c3faeab55fd8.summary: Referral question gains `shuffleOptions: true` with other pinned last and drops `reddit` and `github`, `role` drops `pm` and `non_technical`, `subscriptions` drops `copilot`, because first-chip position bias handed advantage to whichever channel listed first and dropped channels honestly read as `OTHER_OPTION_ID`. Change lives in Shared/Core via `common/src/constants/freebuff-onboarding.ts` in `FREEBUFF_ONBOARDING_QUESTIONS` plus `ONBOARDING_LEGACY_OPTION_IDS` and new tally helpers. Retired ids remap under current rules with `data_ml` to `professional_dev` and `discord`, `blog_news`, `reddit`, `github`, `designer`, `pm`, `non_technical`, `copilot` to `OTHER_OPTION_ID`, `ONBOARDING_TALLY_VERSION` bumps to 3 to trigger full rebuild on mismatch, and `applyOnboardingAnswersToTally` folds legacy ids in place with `sign` -1 for resubmission while `emptyOnboardingTally` seeds every current option at zero.

6edaba95110f54cfee58529bbb0cfe1e19d95f5d.title: gpt-5.6-luna BYOK fix, OpenRouter attribution via transform
6edaba95110f54cfee58529bbb0cfe1e19d95f5d.summary: BYOK `gpt-5.6-luna`, OpenRouter `openai/` bodies rewritten pre-serialization via `transformRequestBody` in `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel` using `byokRequestTransform`; direct Luna swaps `max_tokens` to `max_completion_tokens`, strips `stop`, forces `reasoning_effort: none` with tools; OpenRouter injects `user`, `safety_identifier` from SHA-256 provider credential fingerprint. Live probes showed OpenAI rejecting both fields independently; Luna Chat Completions rejects function tools at default reasoning effort, Responses API required with reasoning plus tools; anonymous OpenRouter OpenAI traffic inherits shared policy block. Ships in `sdk/src/impl/byok-request.ts`, `packages/llm-providers/src/openai-compatible/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts`, `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts`; endpoint match uses actual completion URL including custom-saved connections; fingerprint attributes provider credential without Freebuff account, domain-separated hash, key never enters body, SDK handles stop markers locally.

d9857812d3dab70010a4ae80c0f94bf3a971ee32.text: Team updated internal practice samples checking language reading. Samples now use reusable greeting holders, waiting tasks, list handling. Outside work stays same today.

e28b6ff48b312fa18d1e10ff49c992c05b6c4190.text: Internal checks that total spending across multi-step assistant work now demand exact totals. Only internal testing uses them. Nothing in the live product changed.

cf44fb86bf6833e3405dc1ba2c24e9164c5469e3.text: Engineers gave a new name to an internal check for new files. Only the engineering team sees it. It works exactly as before. Live now.

6840865ee112e14b4b38f78a9de774bc20187aad.text: The team added a way to label new-user questionnaire answers by where they were given: the box inside the main website, or the browser page that finishes a sign-in started from the text-based tool or the desktop app. If an older form sends no location, or a fake location is sent in, it is counted as coming from the main website so it cannot create a false group. The labels are written down but not used anywhere yet, so anyone filling out the form sees no difference.

6edaba95110f54cfee58529bbb0cfe1e19d95f5d.text: If you plug in your own OpenAI key to use the Luna model, your requests now go through instead of being turned down. The assistant quietly rewrites those requests to match what Luna demands, leaving out stop phrases it handles itself and switching off deeper thinking when it needs to use tools. If you plug in your own OpenRouter key to reach OpenAI models, the assistant now adds an anonymous tag made only from your key, so your traffic counts as yours and not as one blocked shared stream.

0cbff57aed44d5a012b9dbb93912884ba1be0ccc.text: If you open the list where you pick a free model, the fast DeepSeek option for coding and tool work has a new name without a date in it, but it still does the same job without using your daily sessions. If you use the limited version of the service and look at choices that cost extra, each of those rows now shows its own short note that the price drops with a paid plan. You can see both the new name and those notes today.

f8ed82aaaa4ed3c5776a04b6c7423b894b294f74.text: People using the free version in the typing-command tool and the desktop app now see Ox Alpha in the list of models, and it is live. People with limited free access outside supported areas, who previously had only one free model to pick, now have two to choose from with the same daily amount. Ox Alpha is marked experimental because it may give unreliable answers, but it can look at very large amounts of text at once without using extra free time.

88e05db4b26f8e58eca99dbae7cf8ef26f22d0a5.text: The team put in place the measuring system for a full-screen sponsor message that pauses desktop chat and takes over the screen, separate from the small text cards that sit inside the conversation. It records when that interruption appears, how the person gets out of it — clicking the close cross, pressing a continue button after reading, or hitting the keyboard key — and how long the message was up before any tap, so a tap made as the card popped under the mouse can be told apart from a deliberate one. It also marks the different looks an ad can have and puts people into fixed test groups that would see either the current mix or fewer small cards plus a larger style. None of this runs yet, so a person using desktop chat today would see no difference.

a659222a118d5923e8a49c83f036c3faeab55fd8.text: People filling out the welcome questions now see the "how did you hear about us" answers in a different order each time the form opens, with "Somewhere else" always staying last. The form no longer offers Reddit and GitHub on that list, Designer or PM and Non-technical on the role list, or GitHub Copilot on the tools list, and any old picks for those now count as "something else." The system recounts past answers under the new lists so the counts staff see match the choices people see now.

8ee68ac2626b70c448b989f087e0528f259ef1fd.text: People who work in the desktop program and see offers for database help now fall under a new combined offer that also covers login and file storage in one approval and one shared budget. They can now see messages about file storage too, not just database and login, and the program keeps separate notes on whether login and file storage are already set up. The new checks are live, but older copies of the program do not send the new setup notes, so the system treats those as unknown and never assumes they are open to an outside provider.

3de218cfbec42f26a76cf460205d0a5727735c10.text: If you have sponsored suggestions turned on in the command-line tool, a bad network check no longer makes the suggestion card disappear. The card stays visible but its accept and menu buttons are switched off, with a note that it could not be refreshed. It only disappears when the service successfully replies that there is no offer.

09fa12bf061ab808dd43735fc2de7beb5288e441.text: When an assistant gets stuck in a loop on one request and burns far more than a single reply should use, the tool now stops that reply at once. Before, it kept trying again for about fourteen seconds and then told the person to wait a moment because of too many requests. Now the person sees a message right away saying that reply went wrong but the chat is fine and sending a new message will continue from a fresh start.

0f33961336a021a0fe9943aa72144fec1183c3ab.text: The system that tracks sponsored work now has three new labels ready: one for when someone turns down a sponsored suggestion, one for when the paid work saves its result, and one for when it ends with nothing to save. They are for advertisers who pay when work is saved, and they will one day let those advertisers tell rejected offers from unseen ones and saved work from failed work, without a failed mark returning money by itself. The labels are defined but unused, so reports show nothing new today.

a852b83bdfb6dbc2fdc996eb33eecc2e1fbb2489.text: The record saved each time ads finish loading now also notes how likely that opportunity was to be kept for long-term review, why it was kept, and which secret version made its anonymous user tag, not the tag itself. Staff who tend the ad dashboards and the yield count will see those extra details, while the old duplicate number stays for a while so existing charts keep working. Only the randomly picked entries fairly stand in for all opportunities, and a secret change now shows up at once instead of looking months later like an unexplained break in per-person totals.

b6775f5c3e83b041816b59b2c2bb6dcadadf9f91.text: Advertisers building in-chat ads see previews of how their wording looks at three text widths: the narrowest width that still shows their website address, plus two wider widths people actually use. The extremely narrow preview almost nobody runs is gone, and the widest preview now stops short enough to fit inside its box without sideways scrolling. Ads that do appear on a real super-narrow screen still keep the same short title limit.

4ff67e17e1d2980de3411ac0f573e20160b845d8.text: People who get work offers paid for by a sponsor in the desktop program see each offer on a small card. That card now knows when a job is still in progress or still owes a result, so it does not show Start again by mistake and keeps watching until the finish is clear. Jobs that do the work in a separate side folder can now record and hand over what they made, instead of failing when they tried to save.

bd4a417e32556ffb2004437274d0cdd893ad3907.text: For businesses that pay to show sponsored work suggestions, the team wrote down the full path from showing the card to someone pressing Accept to the work being drafted and added and the connection to the business being set up to the person later creating an account and using the business's tool. Only pressing Accept can ever create a charge, billed just like a tap on a regular ad, while every later step is only tracked to help price future campaigns. The outside business can only report back the last two steps, creating an account and using the tool, and cannot report steps like the work being added that the system sees on its own. The shared list is now in place for the different parts of the system to use, but by itself it changes nothing you would see or pay today.

f4fca07fcd3d2a041699d3c1216bb216d2dae2ec.text: Engineers wrote down a new lowest charge of 50 cents for a single ad click after its price is lowered for the country it came from. It is for advertisers who pay a higher normal price, such as $4.50, so those discounted clicks cannot bill below 50 cents. The number is only saved for now and does nothing yet.

57c010db236b4b5ffba7030cb4eff4bb50a4a333.text: If you pay for a plan, picking a model from the list now shows a quiet line underneath with your plan name and how much you have used today, over the last five days, and for the month. If you have hit a limit, it also names the limit that stopped you and when it clears, except the five-day one which has no single reset time. The same wording is used on the website and desktop app, and the list was fixed so that blocked message is no longer cut off.

a49b46d62f39fd4cf45e3ba02499b8aefbca0d24.text: People who run the assistant in a text window and run out of free turns now see a short message on the waiting screen that tells them how to get more time, with a link to the plans page. People who pay keep at least seven dollars of daily use, or three dollars on limited accounts, even in places where free use stops at one dollar, so a paid plan no longer gets trapped under a free cap. The Pro plan is for sale again. The website and the desktop program now both flash a warning once someone has used about four-fifths of their allowance.

6891efd69b17644d4cc43382efd3a757e25507a1.text: Engineers fixed the test comparing ads we sell ourselves with ads from outside networks so one person now stays on the same side each time an ad could show instead of flipping back and forth, which allows a fair per-person comparison. Each time an ad could show now gets one tracking number made on the server that follows it even when no ad shows, and the completed-request record now also keeps which decision rules ran, which side the person was on, and how many ad campaigns qualified and why the rest were left out. It is active now in the shared code, but it is internal measurement work, so someone in that test would just see normal ads with no visible difference day to day.

2cf1163dc72fd40df1b7d56a4ed94d668116dc47.text: For publishers who show Imprezia ads, the safety time limit now stays on until the full ad reply has arrived, so a slow or stuck reply cannot leave the ad spot waiting forever. When a publisher's account has not been switched on for that ad product, the internal records now plainly say no ads will fill until Imprezia switches the account on, instead of recording a general failure. It is live now and is a small behind-the-scenes fix.

4a41787b377f56263a296bc5a8458ad2707aafae.text: People waiting on the free start screen in the command line tool see ads from the company itself in the intended order, with no repeats even if the view loads twice. The tool now reports back when one of those ads was shown, trying up to three times if the connection fails, while ads from other companies still use the old counting. This is live now.

9a9f7dd95b7843187a4048b1b950b3539ab8fd5c.text: Advertisers writing a short text ad get a preview that shows exactly how their words will be cut and wrapped when the ad appears inside the assistant's text display at small, medium, and larger sizes, because both sides now use the same fitting rules. Anyone shown one of those ads will only see a working link when the advertiser entered a normal web address; other link types show with no place to go. The new lists that define ad spots, how views and clicks are counted, and how prepaid money works are stored but switched off, so they do nothing yet.

5c0c933cea38831e8f3c2a1042c1852363445159.text: Engineers wrote new rules for ads that are being deliberately wound down: the daily money can drop a lot on the first day and then ease toward its end point, and each day's share drips out as the day passes on a West Coast clock, with an hour's worth ready at midnight so early visitors still see something. A person watching one of those winding-down ads would see spending fall fast then linger, and late-day visitors would still find ads instead of finding the pot empty because morning visitors took it all. The rules are written down but nothing follows them yet, so nothing looks different today.

8953a389fa9deb1c8cb479d483b24327a2c38cb7.text: Staff who look at delivery totals will now see clicks on tracked outside links listed under a proper name instead of a blank. Advertisers choosing where their ads appear will not see that link as something they can buy — it stays out of that list on purpose. The setup that decides who should get the company's own ads now uses one shared rounding step in both checks, and the request records now write the word none when someone was deliberately left out, so an empty spot means data is missing.

ed27ce1cf3e461105e209dcd13d8e5e22219331f.text: Advertisers who send sale reports directly from their own servers have a new background count for those reports. Staff checking operations would see only broad facts like whether a report was accepted, why it was turned down, what kind of sale and traffic it claimed, whether payment settled, and the amount charged and time it took. It leaves secret sign-in details and individual click and event codes out, and full detail stays in the main database. The counting rules are in place now but do nothing until the reporting path starts using them.

ec01bf10020d29d13062f0218f3176e5a0e3f4b0.text: Advertisers whose ads stop because money ran out got two new saved explanations behind the scenes. One says the ad hit its limit for the day and will start again at midnight Pacific time, and suggests raising the daily limit. The other says the ad spent all of its total money, and suggests raising the total. The wording is in place but nothing shows it yet, so there is no visible change for now.

35dc6d079403192cc19e9552f4a951fa9776f707.text: Assistants can pick up extra abilities saved inside a project and also saved in a computer's personal folder. The second search now stays off unless explicitly allowed, so work running on a shared server no longer picks up abilities left in that server's personal folder instead of the project's own. A team running a project online will now see only the abilities stored with that project, while someone working on their own computer can still allow the personal folder.

2afc2b2dfac9a0bcb48e18ccc0c1f720f6f2e6a7.text: If you use Luna, it stopped working completely on August 16th because the usual supplier blocked every request from this account as a policy violation. It now still prefers that usual supplier but can switch to four other low-cost suppliers when it has to, and it still refuses any backup that would cost about ten times more. You will also now see the supplier's real refusal reason instead of a misleading message telling you to check your internet after repeated tries.

d0c7b069051a45044d107598a2ce98ef80d63100.text: On August 16 the outside company that powers the default answers on the free website raised its prices and started charging double during morning busy hours. If you open that free website you still get answers from the same place, and your daily share still counts the same way, so you would notice nothing. Staff only rewrote the hidden notes next to the setting to warn that the old money-saving reason for that choice is now backwards and needs a new decision.

fe7b8fad52fa2ea67a8d2cbb86638e7e0cbb7cf8.text: People on Windows with older processors that could not run the fast standard version used to crash in a loop, and now the opener spots a death in the first ten seconds as a processor mismatch and retries with a slower version made for older chips. If that slower version also fails, they get a plain note that the program stopped while starting, with advice about the older-computer version and the last error text the program printed. That saved text is cleaned so it cannot scramble the screen, and the opener no longer checks for updates after the program has already quit.

79d6a9de6e44b00e4d484725b74991122ae257ab.text: If you use the assistant by typing commands in its normal or light setting, including when you pick a free model, your requests now run on a rebuilt inner system. It is live now. The extra-careful setting and the planning setting still run on the old system, and the team cannot switch you back from afar — it would take another update you install.

c200e2d4f1c2dbc77bdd889971d83fb755fb0f53.text: The team pulled the scattered checks that watch the main production database into one shared set with fixed alarm levels. It now raises a warning when the database is halfway to needing its internal counter reset, when one connection has held old data open for about a million transactions, when a search index build has been stuck for 30 minutes, or when a single heavy query is using as much power as the whole system normally uses. This is internal work for the staff who keep the database running, who will see consistent warnings and will get a clear error instead of a false all-clear if the checking account lacks permission to see activity across the system.

35eec19e84f06cc0bfef213d204165ac1e9867a4.text: People using the free DeepSeek allowance pay double between 1 and 4 in the morning and again between 6 and 10 in the morning by the world clock. The price counter and the spending guard now use the same clock, so someone who bumps into the lower temporary cap in those hours gets a message saying the cut lifts in hours, when full use returns in local time, and that the cut keeps the day's allowance from burning twice as fast. That shared clock and message are in place today.

da1f340a36ff033086086da3fe1411e796af2bc3.text: The team made one shared scale for how hard the assistant thinks before it answers, so the desktop app and the main service mean the same thing by each step. A model can offer a choice from that scale, but the top step can never go past what that model already does today, so you can only turn thinking down, never up. If your saved level moves with you to a model that allows less, it drops to the strongest level that new model allows. Nothing looks different on most models yet because the choice stays hidden unless it is turned on, and leaving it in the middle keeps behavior exactly as it is today.

2d6439de4640f2f4642e07c1f8decad1cdb00812.text: People who only get the smaller set of models because of where they appear to be see a short line right under the model list saying those other models aren't available in their country yet. The team moved that sentence to one shared place so the typed version and the desktop version always show the exact same words, but the words themselves did not change. People who get the full set of models see no extra line at all.

660747443d071feffcc7ccb584ac2977e631e0dc.text: For people signing into the desktop app using a short code, the team prepared a new marker for when that sign-in fails on the person's own computer. It matters because the central system still thinks the sign-in started well when the computer cannot reach it, security software gets in the way, the computer clock is wrong, or the person abandons the code. The marker is set to be kept every time, but nothing writes it yet, so someone checking why sign-ins fail would see nothing new today.

accfa422f66916c360186c12c240d9279acaf396.text: The assistant's end-of-turn suggestions now use one shared wording rule and it is live. Anyone who is offered next steps after a task will see short ideas that name the outcome, like adding tests, without spelling out files or steps, and each one names its target because it opens without context. The assistant can also now suggest checks it runs itself, like trying the login flow and fixing what breaks.

09e160095a84086726021f1c614790d8558f8ca5.text: Workers laid small internal groundwork for telling two prove-you-are-human checks apart at sign-up. One check scores you silently in the background and the other asks you to tick a box, and they can run together. When it goes live, a person stopped because the Google check never loaded would see a note naming the blocked address and pointing at a browser add-on or filter to switch off, instead of a generic try-again note, and support could tell from the records which company's check failed. The settings and wordings are in place now but change nothing you can see yet.

68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.text: People using the company's own web research helper for free were being mistaken for outsiders and given answers from a smaller backup system. The check looked for a hand-written list of special abilities and missed that this helper only uses web search and page reading, so it now counts everything the company built except a short list of common abilities that outside apps also use. Those helper users, plus people using the desktop auto-run helper that was also mistaken, get the normal free answers again, and free requests that truly come from outside apps are now always sent to the backup system.

8553a9efe9d42dc01079c1f7a63907ea55ec77d0.text: The crew that puts together the typed-command helper refreshed the kit that draws its screens and added a safety check around the extra machine-specific pieces. If that setup is interrupted, mismatched, or two setups collide, it now stops early or brings back the last finished copy instead of leaving a broken one. The work is in use for that crew today, and people who just run the helper notice nothing different.

5d8bc0232add269427599ffd4f928ee6a4786f52.text: People with full access who unlocked the extra model through referrals can now keep it selected in the command-line picker while they still have weekly uses left, instead of being bounced back to the first listed model on a refresh or retry. The tool now stores referral details separately for full and limited access, so when the server reports no referral the old invite display clears instead of sticking around. The extra referral-only choice is never saved as the startup default, so the next launch returns to the person's usual saved model.

851f10f5262ed0de613c360e7724ff58e450f0ad.text: Fixed a small bug in the model picker for people with limited access who earned bonus time with the extra model by completing bounties. Before, tapping the banner to use those earned sessions looked like it worked, then the screen quietly switched you back to the suggested model even though you still had time left. Now your pick stays put while you still have time left.

7005d45cc1116a842069903738371fc3c64f2c92.text: People who ask the assistant to look at files from the typed-command tool get more steady protection for files that hold real passwords and keys. Those secret files stay blocked even when their names use Windows tricks like extra spaces or dots at the end or an extra colon part, while sample files that show the format with no real secrets still open unless the project's own skip list blocks them. A single bad line in a skip list no longer erases the good lines around it, so listings stay complete. It is live now.

76020951df33514036c99751ccb03abd92b47274.text: The team added a behind-the-scenes helper that tidies the name tag an app sends with each request into a short label that is safe to count. It follows a mistaken block of 659 accounts that trusted a tag the app picks for itself, and gives staff who look for unofficial apps a second clue that is also easy to fake, so it can only suggest, not prove. It is built but not hooked up to block or allow anything yet, so nothing looks different today; when staff later look at counts they will see only the first word of that tag in lower case, with extra details and addresses dropped and overlong junk grouped together as unknown.

b2a5e5362384591ac9d67ae57216ea088c5cc01d.text: People who see the message asking them to invite friends for free use now see one more line underneath. It offers free time on the new model for doing small tasks instead, and spells out the web address to visit because the screen they are on cannot open it for them. The line shows up whether they have free time already or not, and time earned this way can be used from anywhere.

d62db1eebd81b366812817ac479860ba7ab066e9.text: The write-up that comes with the free tool now lists the exact helpers you can pick from instead of speaking in general terms, and it names which fast helper is picked for you at the start. It also tells people outside the fully supported countries that they get two helpers and six one-hour tries a day, and that extra time with another helper can be earned. Nothing in the tool itself changed; the updated words are live now for anyone reading that page.

ae8c38c6a145ee540ec48aea9027714917d9da36.text: Engineers added an automatic safety check for the screen where people pick a free model inside the terminal tool. For someone with full free access who earned the bonus model from referrals, it verifies that every shown choice — both the regular list and the separate referral banner — will actually work when picked, after the bonus choice on the desktop app recently showed up but was rejected as invalid. The screen looks the same today, it just can no longer slip through with a visible option that fails when selected.

65f20efb85fbaa7d2ec42f484fbbf9b39c57f751.text: People with full access on the website now see an extra premium assistant choice in the picker, labeled for one chat a day. You get that one chat each West Coast day on top of your normal allowance, so using it does not eat into your other chats. It is live now, but people in limited-access areas cannot see or pick it.

d248ecc5ad5aafd3b80a52ed21c4244e0aa849d6.text: People who add skills from skills.sh can now open them instead of having them fail over the extra publisher notes tucked inside. If a skill's written summary runs too long, it now shows cut short and the skill still works. It is working today.

ff0629f1f1b73fec52d0107117f3c27cc46c389f.text: Services that run the assistant over and over on the same project files can now map those files once and hand that map back in on each later run instead of rebuilding it every time. The shortcut only applies when those same files are supplied with the run, and it is ignored without them. It is live today as a small behind-the-scenes speedup, with no new button or setting to see.

f5526661a4291076b5784de328a4ddb405831935.text: Since July 29, people with full access who unlock the special model by inviting friends get a fresh allowance every day on California time instead of once a week. Staying active day after day adds one extra session a day for each full week in a row, up to four extra for a four-week run, and the extra disappears as soon as the run breaks. The invite box now talks about sessions left today and when they refill, instead of this week's sessions.

c9bdd9c7b58e05b498d296cf64fcaaa3db54890d.text: It helps outside programs that feed the assistant answers from commands run between questions. If one of those programs sends the same answer twice after a failed attempt, the assistant now quietly skips the duplicate and keeps only new answers. That stops one retry from breaking that conversation for every turn after it, while answers that are still waiting still get added.

1402b75d5bd6d305c9bb326da1e9fb0c60a4b35e.text: People who run the assistant in its standard or high-power settings now get answers from a newer model, including the helpers that write, review and think through code. There is nothing new to click — the same settings just run on the updated model. The team also stored that model choice in one shared spot so the next update applies everywhere at once.

c8e487a6246813b34d1f8a6942bef69352c80bc4.text: For people starting a blank cloud project with full access, the planning chat now runs on a smarter helper while the actual build still runs on the older helper so the move from planning to building keeps working. The planning chat is live now and stops after 12 back-and-forth messages for each project, but someone with a finished plan can still press start building. People in limited regions keep using the one helper they are allowed for both steps, and a plan no longer gets stuck just because the helper cannot point to an exact lookup for an outside service that needs a password or key.

d6ec35acf28349f0742cb015e2400f5d07d83eb0.text: People using the free version of the tool you run by typing commands now get more reliable starting and quitting. The team gathered the cleanup steps in one place, so quitting tries to hand back your free spot and a crash during startup fixes the screen before showing the error. A check for a free spot now gives up after 20 seconds instead of leaving the starting message stuck.

4aa3d4c337e0d6424a23184465fdd0d98b1d387f.text: The part that looks at unsaved work in a project used to try to read all of it, and if those changes were enormous it would run out of memory and crash. It now stops reading after about ten million letters, stops that check, and keeps the first part, which is all the assistant actually uses. Only people with very large changed files would have hit the crash, and for them it keeps working instead of failing, and the fix is live now.

5b05edcad1c49dbfae18bb40a3a8026b8b5673c6.text: For people with full access who have used the tool every day for seven days or more, the free extra turn with the special model now refills every Monday as long as they keep using it daily. If they miss a day, that extra turn disappears right away. The short bonus note under the days-in-a-row count only mentions the model perk when it can actually be used.

aa75163a8f27b8cfc8af9d2ce07ba5f3253fdce0.text: People opening the help pages or picking a model in the command tool see new privacy answers now in effect July 23. The answers say typed prompts and messages, including pasted text, may be checked to tailor ads, and input is kept to develop and improve AI systems only when the picked model or feature says it may use data for training, with a short May use data for AI training tag on those choices. Behind the scenes the tag and the decision to keep records now come from the same setting, so editing the wording cannot accidentally change what is kept.

6741ac4a35ff3d5b290540a363ae19c6c5c485cf.text: For people who try the free version after tapping a Reddit ad, first use and repeat use after 1 day, 7 days, and 24 days are now sent to Reddit as single shared reports, no matter whether it happened in the downloaded tool, on the website, in chat, or in the hosted version. A repeat-use report only goes out if the person opens it on that exact day; coming back late no longer triggers a late report. Email addresses are now tidied before they are scrambled and sent, so dots and extra tags after a plus sign no longer stop a match, and the individual ad-click marker is no longer sent at all. Old labels for past charts still work, so someone checking ad results today would see cleaner matching and no late catch-up counts.

e8c2211146a5a3fd3718e8dee4825c4757e60986.text: The team added three internal names to count what happens to background helpers in the desktop program when it quits, when it cleans up after a crash at start, and when it resumes interrupted work. It is meant for people who use the desktop program, but you would see nothing different because the names are in place and do nothing yet.

4e24162fc7e8d8a5ebc827b26c3afc48c6ed057f.text: When a chat gets so long that the assistant has to forget old parts, it now counts what you said and what it said separately. Many long answers no longer push out your earlier questions, and many of your questions no longer push out its earlier answers. The very last message always stays, even if it alone is too large to fit.

3d1a8e68f275183a92cfbb5100a2528bd5ce4c79.text: People who run the assistant in a terminal window get a safety net for hard crashes. The program now launches a small backup that sits aside and puts the screen, cursor, mouse, pasting, and typing back to normal if the main program is killed suddenly and cannot tidy up itself. After a force-quit or crash they see a usable terminal again instead of a blank screen, missing cursor, or keys that type the wrong symbols.

7f4effcaa955faf0576cdffb799998fd36733bbe.text: People who check their daily streak on the opening screen can see it now: the row of dots fills for a week, then adds a small plus sign when the run goes past seven days. If the window gets very narrow, the streak drops to its own line below the heading so words and dots do not crowd together. The invite line underneath also reads more simply and no longer names a limit on friends.

66b39f9ac99af7faa8b610590717bdfa5daeb7f1.text: If you chat with the assistant in the terminal, its behind-the-scenes debug notes now save only a short summary — which helper answered, how long your message was, and how many past messages there were — instead of saving your whole conversation and attachments each time. That keeps those notes tiny and stops them from growing to gigabytes and eating your disk space. The tool also now quietly deletes debug notes bigger than 10 megabytes from chats you have not opened in two weeks, while leaving your actual saved chats untouched. If you need full detail for troubleshooting, you can switch on a separate detailed record.

ad5e77cb4eae7ef2f6a183e84e915704819fea2a.text: People who use the coding tool without a subscription see ads in the chat and in the waiting room. If the first ad company has no ad to show, the main system now tries a second company and then a third company that had been left out. It is live now, so those people should see fewer empty spots where an ad should be.

ae4bfa7060da887ef37210aa0d5c33adad14963d.text: People waiting for a free turn who have come back days in a row now see that run written as "2 day streak" with seven dots that fill in through the week and start over after day seven, while people with no run see no line at all. People who invite friends to keep using the most powerful free model now see how many successful invites they have toward the limit, and the box changes its wording and button once weekly turns run out.

a4b9f8de17a56af3e9a90753bcdfe9858f9a3a4d.text: One shared backstage rule now decides which helper brain may run in the typing tool, the desktop program, and on the website, and it lets website-only trial brains share the same work areas while the typing tool keeps showing its old short pick list. Three free choices joined that backstage list, and a new private tag lets the website's own computers say which person's work to open. Regular browsers cannot use that tag to open someone else's work, and the tag and rule sit written down but do nothing yet, so someone looking would see no difference today.

9e59dcc4f5df63719dff99e9e4ec1db6abcb1fbb.text: If you choose a model or answer the waiting-screen prompt on certain Linux setups, pressing Enter on the number pad now confirms your choice; before, the highlight moved but Enter did nothing and the menu looked frozen. If a file read or past output was cut in the middle of an emoji and left a broken half-character in the past conversation, the tool now swaps that broken piece for a safe placeholder before sending, so one bad character no longer blocks every later answer. Both fixes are live now.

4d7555cb6f9415176119010fabe5c27f13d8243b.text: It is live now for the free allowance in the coding tool and in website chat. Only the automatic reasoning helper in those two places may use the powerful paid Gemini model, which you cannot pick yourself, so nothing else can quietly run up time on it. A dated copy of a model name now counts as the same model, so it still uses up the daily limit and cannot slip past the block.

9468967ece2e1fcecf85d2f09903b4ec5fd97702.text: The team tidied up the instructions it gives its automatic coding helper. It removed three separate instruction sheets, including longer review and troubleshooting notes, and left one short instruction to look over the whole piece of work with fresh eyes and find a simpler, cleaner way to do it. Only staff inside the team who use that helper are affected, and they will see the single instruction where the three old ones used to be. It is active now.

6b27aeb79704c214f07456c7198eb0c01f684d65.text: People who type commands to have the assistant search through code are affected. When that searching helper's work is folded shut, it now shows a short total saying how many searches ran and how many matches were found. Most of the work just moves the counting into one shared place so the number stays consistent. It is live today.

dbdd64cd923cf4fa16a3cf73050c57b273b2c0c3.text: People who choose DeepSeek for answers and include a picture or file with their question are affected. The system now removes the picture or file before asking DeepSeek and leaves a short note in its place saying it was left out because DeepSeek cannot take that kind of input. Written text still goes through, so the answer is based on words alone.

31cf16f7e26bd33459b002c33bc55747baf8b2ca.text: The team renamed two internal labels the editing assistant uses when it swaps exact text in a file, spelling out the piece to find and the piece to put in its place. The work still covers people asking the assistant in the command tool to rewrite files, including clearing text away and repeating a swap in several spots. Those people see no difference in daily use — edits and previews behave the same — and the new wording is live now.

dd383810b20d07df3a1cd71f9be94d9fb173512a.text: People using the free version now get their harder requests planned by a helper that starts fresh each time and only looks at the question plus the specific files it is handed. The main assistant must hand over those files with each request because the helper can no longer see the rest of the chat. It is live now and looks the same from the outside, and it keeps running costs down behind the scenes.

894a5b618d53a24c2af1bb8db82fb17bb3494dbd.text: When a long job gets so long that the assistant squeezes older messages into a short recap, that recap now warns it that shorthand notes are history only and it must still take real actions. People with those squeezed chats would notice the assistant keeps actually doing the work after the squeeze instead of just typing lines like Read files: as plain text. The action notes also list directly without a Tools: label in front, and this is live.

80dc53ab3110fbd9c09ce2fa2e90453e4013893a.text: People who choose the extra-thorough file search now get help from a single dedicated finder instead of two smaller ones. It pulls together up to 20 relevant files with a short summary for each, where the normal search still stops at 12. It is live now, so that deeper search shows a longer list.

94809a3c60388d1c7f5a95708bb118a7967338d8.text: Freebuff put up a new Get Started page on its website for people installing it for the first time, and it is live now. The page spots what kind of computer the visitor uses and shows the install instruction to copy, alongside pictures for VS Code, Cursor, IntelliJ and the terminal. When someone opens the page through an invite link, the top of the page names the friend who invited them.

22fd5ee0dee41fc394c50853ba1146c5b41ceea9.text: If you use the helper inside the terminal and need more usage, you now type /subscribe. It opens a simple page that only shows the subscribe buttons, instead of the full pricing page or the usage tab in your account. Typing the old /buy-credits still takes you to that same new page, and the help hints and out-of-credit warnings point there too.

15d4c1857812f92171a6bd18590d29ac326492d8.text: People who talk to the assistant from the command line can now type /plan followed by an idea and get a step-by-step build plan after the assistant looks through the project. In the free setup that planning help only works after connecting a ChatGPT account. Asking for a plan or a custom check of the code also looks tidier now, with the typing box showing a small plan or review label instead of a separate input box.

1ac0923d47a048c8e0030e8f5cb25a901b2e9fb7.text: Someone setting up payment for their organization now has the payment helper loaded as soon as that setup page opens, rather than only when they press to continue. Pressing to continue now sends them straight to checkout without a pause to fetch that helper. The other edits only tidy up automated tests and add explanatory notes, so they change nothing visible. It is live today.

27a1225a727911ef4aff187402652ae400435967.text: The team added a new automatic checker for internal work that opens Google's Gemini assistant, types test commands into it, and reports back whether it behaved correctly. It sits alongside the existing checkers for other assistants and keeps saved copies of what was on screen during each test. Only the internal testing crew sees it, and it is ready to use now.

e32b581101f3fec2bbd000bd15aa0bbde2a77c51.text: People who ask for several work proposals in the typed tool now get a clearer message when a card has no edited files yet. The card says generating... while it is still working, no changes if it finished without edits, and failed or cancelled if it stopped early. The old generic waiting message is gone, and the new labels are live now.

c1d136969c18ef32ecf0f4344f4f50bd7dae232c.text: People who run the assistant from a text window can now save reusable instruction sheets that the assistant pulls in only when the job calls for them. Each saved sheet also shows up as its own short typed command you can run directly. It comes with two examples that look at work you have not saved yet, one to tidy and simplify it and one to check it for mistakes.

b9c092fdbe928382fd8f37fe37866ddbe2a6f7ed.text: People who talk to the assistant in the terminal window now see multiple helpers working at the same time placed side by side instead of stacked. The columns drop to one when the window is narrow, and a mistake in what someone typed shows as a short warning strip inside their own message. Most of the work was behind-the-scenes tidying, and it is live now.

954d9565fd3c0c0a4c907dcd4210d4995637e0e8.text: People who talk to the assistant by typing keep the text they already typed when a pop-up question appears and they answer it or skip it. Typing an @ name right after a word with an apostrophe, like don't, now brings up the name list, and results from computer commands keep spaces at the start of lines so trees and tables stay lined up. It is live now.

cdbf0ac186158369f2a0a744f25ce56b78f4bd70.text: Workers moved the tiny reader that turns the assistant's labeled action notes into neat fields into one shared place that works in a web browser, so there is no second copy to keep. Staff who open the staff-only page that replays past assistant work see details like what to click and how long to wait come through steadily, and the checks around logging out and logging back in with the typed tool run more steadily. It is live now, and as housekeeping the automatic tests no longer run on two separate parts.

9ff89c4b30b689fa83204343720511eda0b2ae6e.text: People who hold prepaid credit now have any overspend recorded on their last active batch, even when that batch shows zero left. The billing store also digs through layered failure notes to spot a short-term database problem and tries the job again instead of quitting. Both behaviors work today, and the only sign is accurate owed amounts and fewer interrupted saves.

ba9dc9b36ea82fdfdd28d57e5a11e0247658aa2b.text: People who answer the assistant's questions in the typed-command window now see them all together in one list. Each question can be opened to pick an answer and closed again, instead of stepping through one screen at a time and then reviewing everything on a last screen. Once the last question is answered, the answers go through on their own.

a61071b5cda4641493bb22d6fa4f4382765163d0.text: When the assistant asks you to pick an answer inside the terminal, the row you are on now lights up with a solid background and bold text. A hint line underneath tells you to use up and down to move, left and right to open and close, Enter to pick, and Escape to skip. Waving the mouse over the list no longer moves that highlight by accident, and you can see it today.

c7e5ac5c9632319d3cba4aebe761309f32c656b0.text: People who run the assistant from a command window get corrected login handling, live now. If you swap the secret key you log in with, the tool checks the new key and shows the new name and email instead of holding onto the old account. It now keeps only a scrambled fingerprint of the key for that check, and it pulls a saved key from the shared settings reader the rest of the tool uses.

99bb1e61a149a143d39b030770c2d8af2bda629d.text: The tool you run by typing commands now carries its built-in helpers inside itself. It used to look for them as separate files on the computer each time it started. Someone who downloads and runs that tool will see the same helpers as before, only now they cannot go missing.

9a112b81ee00de1ca0b1a37baca1fd690857420d.text: People who talk to the assistant by typing in a black command window can now type /bash or ! to stay in a mode where everything typed runs directly on their computer, or start a line with ! to run just that one line that way. While in that mode the typing box looks different and hides the normal mode switch. It is live now, and pressing Escape clears the line or leaves that mode.

f194a6ef6209225032bae93d1e2ed9dc22de5318.text: The most powerful editing helper now handles tricky work by trying a few different plans at once and keeping the best result. It only runs for larger edits, where one plan might reuse saved work and another might keep the edit as small as possible. It is live now, but it is behind-the-scenes work with nothing new to see or click.

c84b6395e68969d2ebfb3208b9545e5863d4b364.text: The command tool and the website now send their background usage notes through the same shared step. Test copies used by the team send nothing, and the command tool holds early notes until it knows who is signed in, then sends them together. It is live now, and people using those tools will see no outward difference.

ceae0abf396aea5f2e5e76df7dfd68ad992f1308.text: People who chat through the command-line tool now see the assistant's private step-by-step thoughts in their own separate section instead of mixed into the answer with visible markers. It holds back half-arrived markers until the whole marker shows up, so stray characters don't flash on screen while words appear, and the thinking section closes cleanly when the thinking ends. It is live now.

9fdebef076cb48328a0f9c9a11f584f8055fcfda.text: If you chat with the assistant by typing in the text window, the typing box now has three setups instead of two. Normal typing works as before, running a computer command still shows a ! and hides the pop-up suggestions and the mode button, and a new referral setup shows a ◎ mark in a warning color with a referral notice above the box. Pressing backspace at the very start of the line now drops you back to normal typing from either special setup.

1df0789330bbb5b37778fc7427c7a9d00d04bcc1.text: If you use the assistant from a typed command window and ask how much you have used, you now get a yellow-outlined box above where you type instead of a line mixed in with the chat. It shows what you spent in this session, what you have left, and when free credits renew, and the text reshapes to fit narrow windows. The box goes away on its own after a minute, or you can close it yourself.

6c564150707150f8c838ff312c839dffdbc13b6b.text: Workers set up a common way to tell a bad login apart from a cut connection or a busy service, with a rule to try a failed chat message up to three times while waiting longer each time from one second to eight seconds. The parts sit ready but nothing follows them yet, so someone typing in the company's text tool who loses connection would see no difference today.

fd4c93b3bfb2e431317665fc6cb87aab12607158.text: The command-line tool now figures out which command program started it and only asks about colors when the terminal window can answer, so it no longer freezes in windows that stay silent. People who run it inside PowerShell on Windows will see light or dark text that matches PowerShell's own background color instead of the general Windows setting.

8952cbcc915f0cc3d0f70839b57f1aaa25344e60.text: Behind the scenes, the team added an automatic way to put out updates for the older edition of the coding helper. It matters only for people who deliberately install that older edition. Those people now get a separate install choice that picks the right download for their Mac, Windows, or Linux computer, and if the saved program fails to run or the download was cut off halfway, it throws the broken file away and fetches a fresh copy.

155ad8212eb92a904c328576c5868bcf81d8bbbb.text: The starter pages that new helpers are copied from lost their built-in safety checks for things like text, numbers, lists, and file contents. The pages still describe what those things should look like, but they no longer check them while running and no longer need an extra checking tool. It is live today, so anyone making a new helper from those starter pages gets the shorter version.

9ada540db1aacc997d1ddadd035e472ff92c638f.text: The most thorough internal helper now always uses the newer stronger model and the team retired the separate test copy that did the same job. Staff who choose that thorough option get the stronger answers automatically with nothing extra to pick. It is live now, and that helper can no longer start a small side job inside its own answer.

a7d0c59f9544e21786009224776572e99b86bead.text: The team standardized how the terminal assistant writes its behind-the-scenes diary so every part records details the same way. Anyone who opens those troubleshooting notes will see error explanations and extra details spread across separate lines instead of jumbled together. It is live now and does not change what the assistant does, only how its notes look.

a25fb6d74829e92aca5c6f1c6715d0495dd6ae8d.text: The internal coding helper dropped its middle-speed setting, so the versions that used it now run on the quick setting and two spare versions were removed. When it edits code it no longer calls in a separate helper to review the writing or another to run checks for errors; it just finishes and asks its supervisor to double-check. Anyone looking at internal test runs now will see shorter jobs with no automatic review or check step.

fdd062321c48cef702d2cbe04a635f597f994f4c.text: The assistant you run by typing in a terminal window now asks that window what text and background colors it uses and picks matching light or dark colors for its own display. That helps people whose terminal can answer the question, including those working inside Zed, and it replaces an old rule that always used dark colors in one terminal. When opened, the menus show light colors on a light background and dark colors on a dark one, and the sign-in box uses a slightly adjusted shade to fit in. It is live now.

fb08bf54f6dd19d6ea8727fe6da1fca4faf3aa98.text: Internal work put in place a new coordinator for hard coding jobs. It first sends a helper to study the task and pull together useful files, then wipes the chat down to just that research before starting edits, and the helper must now always return its thinking, key facts, and file list in the same three-part form. An older editing helper was renamed with no change to its work. People outside the team notice nothing; only staff testing the helper would see cleaner, more predictable research to start from.

b5676a455ce66a06314c0fcdb60608a69b6c8f3d.text: The team rewrote the behind-the-scenes cleaner that removes hidden tool instructions from the assistant's answer as it types out. It only matters for people watching that live typing, from the main answer or from background helpers, and only when the screen is actually showing it. It is live now, and those watchers see no difference — normal words still appear right away while the hidden instructions stay hidden.

58b1334d6359b8685011bf063a677132bd80010c.text: The team moved the work for outside chat requests into its own separate place so each part can be checked on its own, and added separate tallies for when a request arrives, when the secret key is wrong, when details are missing, when an account runs out of credit, when the answer starts sending back, and when it fails. It is live now and affects only outside tools that talk through that chat connection. Those tools act the same as before, so a person watching would see no difference except the team can now tell exactly where requests stop.

3827ca8068cbbf8e9617771fb87c2aad118cf0d9.text: Someone who sets up an automated helper can now give that helper connections to outside tool libraries, either by running a program on the same computer or by linking to an address on the web. Normally the helper can use everything those libraries offer, but the person setting it up can limit it to specific items by writing the library name, then a slash, then the tool name, so library names themselves cannot contain a slash. When the helper starts a step, it asks those libraries what they can do and adds their answers to its own list of available actions.

de8997f72f16d19ca4777f92a437418d4e13c860.text: People who use the assistant inside a terminal window now get a proper chat display. Someone opening it would see a box for typing messages over several lines, answers shown with clear formatting, and separate lines of work listed on their own. Helper jobs started by the main assistant now stay grouped underneath it so their updates do not get mixed up, and all of this works today.

5f818783ccab888062b1eb7844c09409d94d235d.text: The assistant now hands the parts that read, find, and edit files a way to ask for file contents each time they run, instead of letting them grab files on their own. When many files come in at once, it adds a missing final line break before using the text. The cleanup runs behind the scenes today, so a person watching normal work would see no difference.

6cb0d214c2573ba320cd6c7560ed76b5d193e9bf.text: People who open the store page that lists all assistants will get smoother scrolling when the list is long. The page now draws only the rows on screen instead of everything at once, and shows one, two, or three across depending on how wide the screen is. Short lists look the same as before; the speed-up only starts once there are more than six rows.

ca45080a3851f24c32b1dd46f90f0bfe88953620.text: The team deleted old internal testing tools that automatically built a sample app and checked proposed fixes against long lists of past problems from outside projects. Only the internal team is affected. Anyone looking through the project files today will see those old checks are gone, with just over a thousand lines removed.

c06f476a31525cc3320c0b1a24108623d72dee22.text: The record-keeping that writes down what each answer cost now tries up to three times, waiting a little longer after each miss, and stops with a failure if it still cannot save it. Automatic refills still count each credit as one cent. It is live now and is an internal fix, so someone looking at charges sees the same price and simply finds the cost entry present instead of missing.

6fb0494b34834fad98b268ce430968f4c42f5985.text: The team threw away an old way of writing down conversations and now keeps everything in one shared style, so it no longer has to translate between two styles behind the scenes. Only staff who maintain the service feel it, and it is live now. A person using the assistant would notice nothing different in answers or speed; the work just makes the inside tidier.

1ada6a5e7e9e376dbc88aefefdd09eb4c1f13404.text: People who build assistants with the building kit can now add their own extra actions for the assistant to use. Those actions now appear in the instructions the assistant reads, alongside the built-in ones. When the assistant tries to use one while working, the system runs it and checks that the details it sent are shaped correctly.

7c2cb2b0bdf6644394975a621161b7434a7ad7d3.text: The team swapped out a messy internal setup for the automatic checks that run after an edit, and it is live now. When everything passes, the people who watch those checks now see one short success line instead of a long list. When something fails, they still see the full details to help fix it.

584bcc4789235699a30cc12d7dc9fb116854e467.text: The team added an internal helper for very hard questions. It splits a question into four angles and checks each angle in three different styles — one deep, one balanced, and one creative — then merges everything into one fuller answer. It is live for internal work today, so only staff using the internal tools would notice longer, multi-sided answers on complex topics. The separate tool that builds new helpers also dropped its long step-by-step directions and now uses shorter built-in defaults.

c75a1f2e2a6788f8446606eb76b184240799e7e0.text: If a friend sends you their invite link and you are signed out, you now see a sign-in button for GitHub that saves their invite so you still get linked to them after you create an account. If you open your own invite link while signed in, the page does not offer you a button to claim your own bonus. If you are signed in and open your account menu at the top, you will find a new Refer Friends choice that opens your referrals section. All of this is live.

39fe906737675184504341cc8944ff08505797d9.text: A new helper team was added that runs only on free, openly shared models. It is for people who want to avoid paid models and run things cheaply or on their own machines. Someone who picks it will meet Buffy as the lead helper, who hands work to smaller helpers that write code, find the right files, look things up on the web, and check the work.

f64d2087ca0c709d15abdfcebdebb20e57e13fb0.text: People who ask the builder to make a custom helper now get a ready-to-edit starter for their own helper saved in the main folder, while the example review helpers are saved in separate folders below. The example review helpers now run on a different model and call a different file-searching helper when they need extra context. It is live today.

b9be8087852566eebb4f957a163e292428599b14.text: People who start a helper by typing a short name in the typing-command tool get help: if the name is not saved on their own computer and does not already have an owner name with a slash, the tool now looks it up in the shared default collection instead of failing. If sharing a helper fails, the tool now shows a short failure line, then the details, then a separate hint on how to fix it. When browsing the list of past helper runs, pressing q now steps back just as the escape key does. Those touches are live now.

ef15e7858ec99e23e936839f8bcb220101667bed.text: The assistant now reaches Claude only through one outside middleman instead of trying a direct line first and using the middleman only as backup. The team cut out the direct line and the extra switching code. For people whose requests get answered by Claude, answers look the same as before, and the new path is already live.

77ed9c98ca9647885e2623ef13430e6ade412bf4.text: The team that builds the product reshaped the automatic build and check steps that run on each proposed update into a build step followed by tests. Those longer assistant quality checks now run one at a time and are allowed much more time to finish. It is already in use, and only the build team would see the difference when they look at a run.

fd9f50be684550f2b3fbcfa836b96452fa2eb901.text: People who make their own assistants will see the teaching samples renamed to simple numbers instead of specific jobs like code reviewer. The setup for an assistant no longer offers separate spots for background details, when to call it in, and step-by-step directions. A new builder assistant is live today and drafts those descriptions from a short request.

4f44503c013b7a94ff1a6e6467767916a8e70b0b.text: Organization managers making a publisher profile now use a separate creation page that walks through ownership, basic facts, then profile details. The main publishers page shows only the list of existing profiles, and the create button in organization settings opens the separate page with that organization already selected. The Publishers choice is gone from the personal account menu, and organization settings now also shows billing and seat use at the top. It is live now.

4cb06d0fd7555769708e20cfe6d06e19b5b3c846.text: The check that reads assistant names listing the maker and the helper, with an optional release label, moved to one shared spot so every part of the service reads them the same way, and it is live today. It is mostly behind the scenes. People whose assistants start other assistants would notice that a short name without a maker is now read for its helper and release parts instead of rejected outright, while assistants pulled from storage still need the full maker and helper form.

16923279ae32387da295cc3c5b23b8813379b09a.text: People who run the project on their own laptops no longer have to add an extra step to load secret passwords before starting, testing, or working with stored data. The usual start and test actions now fetch those secrets automatically only when needed and otherwise run as normal. It is in use now, and fresh setup asks for a one-time helper install to make it work.

202feaac7b6dd5ffe35f8729a3d9b1eaa7facccf.text: People who talk to the assistant by typing commands now have quiet frustration tracking running in the background. It sends a silent report to the team if someone mashes keys five times in one second, repeats the same request three times in thirty seconds, quits within ten seconds of an error, or sits stuck waiting for over a minute. Nothing looks different on screen; it only helps spot painful moments.

d2eddcb6a9a9369239a4a5cf928f1716e4b5a4f3.text: The team created one shared place for talking to outside services, starting with the emails that send team invites and internal test reports. Those messages now go out through the email company's own sending tool, which also reports back clearly when sending fails. Anyone receiving an invite will see the same email as before, and this cleanup is live and mainly makes future work easier for the team.

668035297dccf48b348d35b23ec1fb68661d6851.text: When someone asks the assistant a question or asks for a work plan, it now sends out several helpers at the same time to gather facts first. Each helper can only look and cannot change anything, and it keeps looking until it says it is finished, up to ten tries. The answer or plan that comes back is built from what those helpers found, and this is how it works today.

663ba6dc6110c21286c3f0c2de6893729e5323d9.text: Team members working on a shared project can now have that work billed to the team. If they open a project the team covers, the amount-used display can show the team's balance, and it shows their own personal balance if that team check fails. This is live.

e981392bdbddda96419fd5168ddf806ca16b28d5.text: People who run the assistant by typing in a text window now see tidier spacing, with never more than one empty line in a row in answers and error messages. The cleanup is live today, except it pauses while waiting for typing, and it still misses gaps where hidden color formatting sits between the empty lines.

1b50daa17311dc7c04d314fa4e1180db472f1065.text: Engineers reorganized the behind-the-scenes list that describes what the assistant can do, separating the descriptions from the work that carries them out. It affects only the staff who look after the assistant, who now get a firm stop if a progress step for a complex request is saved with a blank name.
