From the outside nothing looks different, and the reorganization is live today.

f49acb7d1549800c1a73424b8600eccb51894aa7.text: People with a monthly credit allowance get their refill checked when they sign in or open the usage screen, so a refill that is due goes through right away. If two actions try to spend credits at the same instant, one waits for the other, so the same balance cannot be spent twice and a monthly refill cannot be handed out twice. That safeguard is live now, and when a refill lands today the typed command shows the full date and time.

d100b687b82eff62836f87e7f3b2b3bf049539ee.text: The editing helper now decides a file is too big by adding the size of the old text and the new requested edit together, and it lets slightly bigger files keep using the normal method. Only people asking for changes in very long files would notice the switch to extra-careful handling happening at a slightly different point. The team also added a link to another internal piece that does nothing visible yet, and both are live today.

36b930f637bf4d39a76afa4168b6599bd3d3572f.text: The help area now includes a page for fixing problems. Someone using Codebuff who opens it will see where past chats are saved on their own computer so they can share them when asking for help, plus what to check first when the connection fails, like internet access and sign-in. The questions page next to it also got a short cleanup to say more plainly that only parts of chats are kept to fix bugs.

892afc07c227187bb69953d291875bd56e3b3bb4.text: The helper that clicks and types in a web page for you now saves a picture of the page right before it acts and right after, but only when the page is already open. People asking for that browser work with the main helper get up to two pictures with each step and can see what changed. If a picture fails to save, the work still finishes.

a05cfb6fe95189eae4071effa32404356c159d61.text: People opening the homepage now see a white background with black text by default, with the wording adjusted to stay readable, and can switch to a dark background using a button in the top bar next to the sign-in control instead of a floating button in the bottom corner. The line at the very bottom of the page no longer floats over content and now credits the Manicode team with a link to manicode.ai. It is live on the site today.

996ccc5a44c36603479e0c9e51952148f7e46493.text: Behind the scenes, the system now stamps every internal record from a chat message with that sender's device identifier, login credential, and tracking number for that message. Staff who review those records will see the three details attached automatically, making it easier to follow what happened in one conversation. It is active now, and people using the product will see no difference.

af4c1ae2a9c6c51b83636a9a8cdb2c647f2061a6.text: The assistant was mistaking notes from its own lookups for a new message from you, which threw off its count of replies since your last request. The team fixed the counting so it now finds your last real typed message. If you ask it to do work that needs running commands on your computer, it now sticks correctly to the three-try limit, and the small behind-the-scenes fix is live now.

de7f68d523d5b79acadd2e592f2e95d3b4f6c12d.text: Workers put in place a new behind-the-scenes reader that can open work written in many common computer languages and list the named building blocks inside. Nothing uses those lists yet, so people using the product see no difference. They also added one extra private log line that saves what a file looked like before a suggested fix was drafted.

ee0663dbef0086abfcdbabc749210904cf8dc92c.text: The team tidied how upgrade payments remember where buyers came from. Buyers who arrive from a LinkedIn ad now keep that ad marker saved in their browser, and after paying they go to a new thank-you address that fills in their receipt number on its own. That thank-you page is in place but still blank, so it shows nothing yet.

1a0cb9c328cdeba83a093af35e3751910662ac21.text: The team added an internal test for how the coding helper builds updated files. The helper writes a short draft that leaves markers where old text stays the same, then a smaller faster helper fills those spots back in and lines up old and new text by peeking a few lines ahead. The work sits behind the scenes and changes nothing visible yet, and the team's notes warn that peeking too far ahead slows the work and makes matches worse.

f50c11cd424aa5fa7d072d06cbcb7380dfac2d84.text: The file-editing helper got an internal tidy-up that is live now. It now has to label each separate edit A, B, and so on, and write down what nearby lines it will use and how far each line is pushed in. If the spacing is still slightly off, it tries again with extra push-in added, so a person having a file rewritten sees fewer misses from bad spacing and step-by-step notes grouped by letter.

2190b8d08c3d40aabf14682199e64cdbe8dbe628.text: The small crew who sends new versions live changed how they wrap up that work. The wrapped bundle now uses the name of the computer that will run it instead of one fixed name, and it leaves out bulky leftover files and temporary fix-it notes so it stays light. It also makes a second copy stamped with the exact date and time it was put together, but that stamped copy is prepared only and is not sent out yet.

99c8777e213d27579525e378d569d3e430d7b1e6.text: The live ad system kept using a test key, so it blocked every ad and wrote a loud error for each block, making over a million lines a day that hid real problems. It now writes that loud error once when it starts and records later blocks quietly. Staff who check the error logs will see real problems again instead of the same warning on repeat, and the fix is live now.

4b3edc7eee72aa55a274b36f9281093957978009.text: The team gave the built-in helper that edits code from typed instructions the name Manny. People who use Manicode will see that name in the request box and in the notes about which files were changed. Manny will also skip opening a file again if it just looked at it, and the new wording is live.

e6578a9d7b4b1c9b7b82f7d175ec1782913ce13e.text: The program now keeps the sign that its answer is done in one shared place so all its parts look for the same finish. Someone asking it to write or change code will see fewer failed attempts, because it only opens files from its project list and no longer tries to open a file that does not exist yet before creating it. It is live today.

210f7ac71cdb6b0f59662b85b4b86cdf0ef5e723.text: The lowest price charged for a single ad click in countries where clicks rarely lead to purchases fell from 50 cents to 10 cents, and that lower minimum is active now. Advertisers running cheaper ads priced around 50 cents will see clicks from those countries get sold and billed instead of going unsold. Advertisers with higher-priced ads still pay more than 10 cents, with the price rising with expected purchases.

062743b69a890d6f0e6efba5b3806cd8f6cad036.text: People picking an assistant brain in the command-line tool now see '· Images' after every short description in the list. Even plain-text choices show it, because a pasted screenshot gets turned into a written description for them before they answer. It is a small label fix so a choice does not look like it cannot take a screenshot when it can.

0be72bef521398a74121b5719210a8c5c2e1abfb.text: Nothing in the finished tool changes. The team fixed an internal rehearsal that checks the tool closes quickly after the starter program that launched it is killed. Someone watching that rehearsal will now see a clear explanation when the close is too slow, instead of the check simply running out of time with no details because the computer was slow to warm up.

e1129d9e5842529779d9d8098b3d0b0efe715045.text: A shared date rule now counts a day from midnight world time when deciding if someone came back after 1, 7, or 24 days and reporting that comeback to Reddit. It closes a gap where counting by California time could lose a comeback for good because the two clocks start a new day at different hours. The rule is in place but nothing uses it yet, so anyone checking Reddit results for those returning visitors sees no difference today.

ed764c4f8db46d834c0b0f04883fee15b35c4c55.text: Engineers fixed a small behind-the-scenes startup check, with nothing new for people using the tool. On test computers running Windows, the tool sometimes prepared its screen but did not show its welcome words before time ran out, so the check marked a good start as broken. Now the check counts that screen preparation as proof the tool started, so someone watching those Windows results sees fewer mistaken failures, while real later startup problems still fail.

d8395764bbe0f063c5f616efa7ca997c238aff8e.text: Someone picking a model whose name begins with opencode followed by a slash used to get turned away with a message that those models were disabled. That block is gone, so the same pick now goes through and returns an answer. It works today and matters only for those opencode-named choices.

9e34f2500899c235232c0aab3b39452f9963b387.text: People who log in to the typing tool by opening a link in a browser now get an address that shows a short random stand-in instead of the real login details. The website swaps that stand-in for the real details privately and then throws it away, so each link works only once. The login steps feel the same, and old links still stop working after an hour. It works this way now.

d8e01e3216f2c9976b43ad30fad7f90308f32d70.text: It is live today and only touches mistaken requests where the assistant sends plain text instead of a structured set of details. The assistant now gets back a plainer note that says whether its text could not be read because it was broken, or was readable but still the wrong shape, and asks it to send the full details again with punctuation handled correctly. It is a small internal wording fix, so you would only notice it if you looked closely at the reason given for one of those failed attempts.

baaa1bb3570337a95a6fdc526ef83963dd67bde6.text: It is a small cleanup that affects people who build their own tools on top of the assistant. The assistant now skips instructions saved in the old general knowledge file, so anything written only there gets ignored unless it also lives in one of the other instruction files. The team lists it as upcoming, so it does not run yet.

2974f323e3997b744e9210484e13afe6a2b69787.text: A small internal safety check is now active for the team that builds the tool you operate by typing. It does not change the tool itself. The startup test used to pass as long as no known error appeared, and now it passes only if the tool actually shows a normal opening screen like the login prompt, the waiting-room message, or the main header, so a silent freeze or a brand-new error now makes the test fail and show what the tool printed.

61ebc7842f5ed64de0431a0a74a94c99ef4903e9.text: The assistant now saves its private thinking with its answers so it can see that thinking again on the next turn. When it thinks in several short bursts, those bursts join into one note. It is on now for longer back-and-forth chats, and someone checking the saved conversation would see that thinking note where before there was none.

d0b522ba55ee7857e935292f29ecffe9fccb4355.text: The planning, editing, and reviewing helpers that rely on one specific model now always run through the same outside computer service instead of switching between services. The switch is live now and helps that service remember recent work, so those helpers less often lose track and have to re-read everything. Nothing looks different on screen; it is a small behind-the-scenes fix, and helpers using other models work exactly as before.

43afde76e2a2f2d85fb5a1d72361df54fab988ae.text: Fixed a small internal timing problem for people who turn on the extra record that shows what was sent when the system checks its saved answers. That record used to show up while the answer was still coming in piece by piece. Now it shows up after the full answer has arrived, so it reflects the finished request, and the fix is live.

f3083517a4d8a9e600ca5cf3854e2a2577f3ad16.text: No one using the product sees a difference. The team simplified the hidden automatic checks that open the typing tool to confirm its help message, version message, and error for a bad command still show up. It is active in testing now, and someone watching those checks would see the same results, just with each check waiting to finish before the next starts.

18283ca63e9608056a4b7fa4fce9c0b1ebf9ecca.text: The assistant that builds websites no longer looks through the underlying work itself. When it renames a shared part, anyone following along will now see it hand that search to a separate searching helper to find every other place that still uses the old name, and that helper now gets stricter instructions with examples for how it must be asked. It is a small internal switch and it is working today.

0242d2d8a6e36b9bb9fc39a8a744aff446df5366.text: When someone uses up credits they bought, the billing system now attaches its own one-time tracking number to the record it sends to the company that processes payments, creating one when none was passed along. It is live now. It is a small internal tidy-up — if someone looked at those payment records, every use would show a tracking number, but the credit balance itself works the same.

c9a72f15599f448ed43719b0e9b4029bc1776138.text: Behind the scenes, the team removed the 10 in the morning to 8 at night Eastern limit for trying its reserved servers. It is live now and is a small internal plumbing fix, so overnight and early-morning work now takes the same first path as daytime work. Someone checking an overnight request would see it go to those reserved servers instead of skipping them.

8f5254f7269d7dabb514d76c63f7eca69169a77d.text: One building helper got a small internal tweak. Its instructions now say to bring in extra how-to notes only when they might help with the job, and to leave alone any notes it already brought in earlier in the talk. It is live now, so people working with that helper would see it skip notes it already has instead of fetching them again.

59d88d23d299030c7f9dc5af8cb47c79c3e98c26.text: The thorough helper for large building jobs now follows a strict eight-step checklist instead of loose guidance. People who ask it to build something complex will notice it researches first, asks several rounds of clarifying questions, writes down what it will build and how, then keeps rechecking and testing the work until it passes and saves notes on what it learned.

f845d424d49d74b5c3664eeedd402cea4b09bac0.text: The assistant version used only for evaluation runs now skips its final lessons write-up. It still plans, builds and checks its work, but it stops after testing and does not save notes about what it learned. Someone reviewing an evaluation run today would see it finish a step early with no lessons note left behind.

54c1386d5622b034b8a26ec4280e9cddf87bd27c.text: The team locked the small marketing site to the older set of display building blocks the rest of the project already uses, and pointed the main site, billing work, and helper scripts at the same copy of the database tools so automatic checks agree. It is live today and only matters behind the scenes. If you set your referral name on the partners page, the save button still locks and shows it is working while it saves.

e2d1e227bce8efc8b39a011a6d32040293be0f62.text: The helper used to quit when it sent only silent thinking with no answer and no action. Now it keeps going in that exact case instead of stopping. It is a small internal fix and it is live, so a person who saw that quiet early stop would now see the helper carry on.

db4d9fd47ecbcf0c9e8c20f1195d3a717950af92.text: People who control the assistant by typing while logged in to a distant computer can now copy text to the computer sitting in front of them. The tool first asks the window you type in to save the text, and if that fails it uses that computer's own copy helper as before. It works today, except very long selections still go through the old way only.

66d02a7ddb897fec57232e58e92d65efb1ddb8a4.text: The system that makes sure only one copy of the Discord bot runs at a time misread replies from the database and sometimes lost its link, so the bot could fail to start. Engineers fixed how those replies are read, kept the link open, and stopped overlapping safety checks from raising false alarms. It is a small internal repair that is live now, and teammates who use the Discord bot will just see it start and stay online as expected.

a2b8c129128542a80a72b660be508873d199c53b.text: People who share their assistants using the typed command tool are affected by a small behind-the-scenes tidy-up. The success checkmark with the list of names, and the failure notice with the error and helpful hint, now go through the tool's normal display system so they match other messages. The words and colors look the same, and it is live now.

fef63081a41aae1ff84c058596dd97c80f9a1d71.text: Nothing changes for people who use the tool by typing commands today; this was a small fix to internal checks only. The checks now expect more than one instant attempt when the network connection fails, instead of expecting just one. Someone watching a failed-connection check would see several attempts recorded before the error is shown.

f029fe416ce90be9af4e32b173412e8b36a34d20.text: The setup instructions for the helper that reviews new work from several angles at once now show two example lists instead of one. People who set up those reviews will see one list that asks for ways to simplify and reuse work, and another that splits the check between what shows on screen and what runs behind it. It is a small internal wording update that is live today.

f45a870de64fdcf94b7c81fca177faa4cf8cf34d.text: The automatic helper that checks recent work now has firmer instructions to only write suggestions and never change anything itself. For people who get the expanded review that looks at the work from three to five different angles at once, the helper now clears away extra back-and-forth first so each angle sticks to the original work. It is live now, and it is a small behind-the-scenes fix, so those reviews just stay read-only and stay on topic.

3b94768dd3dc50c99953bed604d70a84131451ef.text: The team updated the instructions for the internal helper that drafts plans from requests. Anyone asking that helper for a plan may now get several rounds of follow-up questions until the request is clear, focused on the important choices and skipping obvious answers or details that are easy to change later. It is a small internal tweak and is live now.

e28fbc6dea6867b8174f5f79b5403567b33fba4c.text: During very long conversations, the assistant used to hold onto every repeated copy of its standing instructions. Now it keeps only the most recent copy and throws away the older ones before it shortens large past results. Someone watching a long conversation would see nothing new, just less repeated clutter carried forward, and it is working now.

544c715d25319753d2828fb288fc474c531dd947.text: People who start the helper from a smaller folder inside their work now stay in that smaller folder instead of automatically jumping to the top. A notice appears at the very top of the screen explaining that and offers a link to switch to the top folder. It is live now and only shows when the starting folder and the top folder are different.

0113a78e3c2200437ef8b60e79d1b7ba1af8989c.text: People who use the two helpers that talk to Notion get safer handling of their private key. Those helpers no longer store the real key in their setup and now pull it from a separate private file on the same computer when they start. Anyone who opened the setup would see a pointer to that private file instead of the real key, and if the key is missing there that helper does not start.

6e4aa872d7d57efc68a738139497c0b8fc46f17a.text: Nothing for people outside the team changes here. The team refreshed the automatic helpers that grab the latest work, remember reused pieces, and run tests, and brought its internal guide up to date to match. The version made for older Apple computers with Intel chips is now assembled on a different Apple computer. The new setup is already in use, and if you watched, you would just see the usual test and release steps finishing as normal.

bf65fbf5987a232e17b137c759b2fa05896af174.text: People who run the assistant in more than one window at a time no longer lose past entries from one window when they type in another. The assistant now keeps lines that start with an exclamation mark in the list you get by pressing the up arrow. Their typing box also clears right after they send such a line.

2dea1fa6086fdf5f3cd63e75019e388a7bfed451.text: The team updated the instructions for its internal helper, and the new wording is live now. The helper now asks through its built-in question feature when there is an important decision to make or it gets stuck, after first looking for background on its own. This is a small internal tweak, so someone using that helper would notice clearer questions instead of a general pause for help.

d3b4b34c177bf28f8f82d02e3afc8c3a06cf6f48.text: People who run the assistant in a terminal window will find the mode switch no longer pops open when the mouse passes over it unless they are actively typing in that window, so it does not flip by accident after clicking away. The folder name shown at the top is now a dimmer gray. Both are live now.

91060649741d99fd1441980999feee963757a83d.text: If you chat with the assistant in the command window, the short follow-up ideas it shows after an answer now remember which ones you tapped. A tapped idea stays marked as used even if you scroll away and come back to it. The list also sits in a tidy lined-up column and lights up as you move across it.

eab9fde59dc664d510cc806e19ad273592b7e0b1.text: The help pages were fixed to show the right way to turn on the planning option that talks through work without changing any files. People reading the guides to plan first will now see that it only works by typing a command once the assistant is already running, not by adding extra words when starting it. The comparison list now shows how to turn on each option and the links for learning more point to the right place. The corrected pages are live today.

33a6741d49fa451cda5b90755833124051e6e83c.text: Anyone checking the help site now sees clearer explanations of how the helper works. The page about the underlying systems now lists which one does the main coordinating work and which ones handle editing, searching files, running commands and other jobs, and the questions page notes that instruction notes written for other tools will also be read, with one set used per folder. The guide to the fast, thorough, and planning-only settings moved into the getting-started area, and the community chat links across the site now use the same short address.

e5b83fdee5888c8f1ae6350f39dc58c17b045fe2.text: A small internal fix affects team members who set up separate test workspaces. The setup process now points helper tools in those workspaces at the test website running on the same computer instead of the live site. It is active now, so anyone running the toolkit's full checks in a workspace will see them use the local site and will need to start that site first.

45a9b9e36ff194bcfbb27cd2cf026a3de12156ea.text: The team paused four automatic checks that make sure the assistant actually uses background notes and files from a project when it answers, because those checks kept failing unreliably. The pause is already in place for internal testing only. Anyone watching those test results will see the four checks listed as skipped instead of passing or failing.

fcead726bfadac72b13f6c3e357125eb9e54f5db.text: Engineers repaired the automatic checks that confirm new work still works after recent changes to how new jobs are recorded. It affects only the team building the product, and nothing you can see or use changed today. Someone watching those checks would now see the sign-in, sign-out, and job-tracking checks pass instead of fail.

d649e3ba3c0fb84e173ba336e3163abc553fddd1.text: The team tidied the hidden list that builds the typed commands for switching how the assistant acts. People who type in the typing tool to switch styles will notice nothing, the same typed switches still work and leave the same switched confirmation note. The tidy-up is live today.

545e1a2ce3e6f1ab00ad481fe027025c2204312d.text: The internal editing helper that writes several versions and picks the best one got a small cleanup. It now throws away extra instruction prompts before starting, always uses the same kind of writer for up to ten tries, and pastes in the full winning version instead of cutting it down to edits only. It is live now and only affects internal work, so someone checking a result would see the complete chosen text applied.

1ce04fbe5c2eb965bf9e7bb22486bbd0899b8448.text: The setup guides for people preparing to help build the product now tell them to use one step that starts everything at once. They no longer need to open three separate windows and start each piece by hand, though the guides still list that manual way for those who want closer control. Nothing in the product itself changed, only the written instructions, and the new wording is live now.

0a76f50db2648f18dde1520fb121562bd038ca31.text: The builders cleaned up how the program asks where it is running, so live use, testing, early work, and automatic checks on build machines are all defined once in one shared place. Those checks still do the same jobs — deciding when to send usage reports, where to write notes about what happened on the computer, and whether saved history goes to the live store or the test store. Nothing looks different from the outside, and the cleanup is already in use.

6e517df5e97c2e6f5ce4d6ed3a2c42b3a1679c19.text: Anyone typing a long prompt that wraps onto extra lines in the command-line box gets steadier keys. Home and End now stop at the start and end of the line you see on screen instead of the whole wrapped block, up and down arrows hold the same sideways spot better, and deleting a whole line with its shortcut no longer messes up the history of edits. It works now.

780173c123743abd3e02d175a4ba0c0ef6c20860.text: Behind the scenes, the helper that writes code now makes four practice attempts instead of three before choosing one, and six instead of five when doing more thorough work. It was also told not to repeat its wrap-up and to just finish if it already gave a summary. It is live now and is a small internal adjustment, so a person asking for a code change would simply see less repeated text at the end.

0662ac17643877ad192255f1b517e8f382e51fc2.text: The team cleaned up hidden extra work inside the typing box in the command-line tool. It affects people who type long messages that wrap onto several lines and move up and down between those lines. They would notice nothing new — typing and moving still behave the same. The cleanup is in the tool today.

75c574de3ba8ad07f64d3f5447ef157c33d29b15.text: The helper keeps a private to-do list while it works. It used to stop right away when it checked off the last item, but now checking off items never stops it on its own — it keeps going until it says it is finished or has nothing left to do. The fix is live and very small, so someone watching would just see the helper take one extra beat after finishing its list instead of stopping early.

961949cda2cda5761de94254f9626205ce2a507d.text: The search helper now shows clearer written hints. Those hints guide the helper when it looks through files for a project. A person checking those hints would see examples for sticking to certain file endings, leaving out test files, and including files that are normally skipped, and those words are live now but searches themselves run the same as before.

de61ea8a1e87e0d3eac64149fc73f72b22a9800b.text: The team added a short pause to the automatic release builder that lets the staff member who started the build log in remotely and look around the build computer. The pause lasts up to 15 minutes and shows up right after the program is built and before the final check, on every release build including the Windows one, even when the build fails. It is a small internal repair aid that is active now, so people outside the release team see no difference.

33d27b8fc4e7f8c5a73860288ad364de49e0d0f9.text: A small internal tweak is live now. The automatic grader that scores test work runs three separate grades at the same time, averages the numbers, and keeps the written comments from the middle score. Staff who check those results will see an average score plus a note listing the three separate numbers, and one failed grade no longer ruins the result unless all three fail.

1d78d8a12d6d39196c329f94a9db7bb2ae551f47.text: A small internal adjustment is live today. In its normal setting, the lead assistant must now hand editing work to a second assistant that tries several versions and keeps the best one. In its fast setting, it skips that handoff and does the work itself, so there are fewer intermediate steps to wait through.

98c597943c9ba218c4c03c4117330eddf99a591a.text: People who talk to the assistant in a terminal window now get a small fix to how answers show up while they are being written. The tool stopped trying to guess when a new piece of text overlapped text already on screen and now simply adds each new piece to the end. You would notice replies growing smoothly as they arrive, with no skipped or repeated words.

826cd02a168a7cc23c07b97c1ec3dae0c0363952.text: It is small internal work on the automated steps staff use to build and publish the add-on for live use. Live packages now point at the live service and mark themselves as live, and the step that stamps a new release number tidies loose edits first so it does not get stuck. Failed packages no longer open a temporary remote login for inspection, and the new setup is in use today.

b78d7b42f852086c0796e93268bf276d7e1a882b.text: Behind the scenes, the assistant now puts a simple label on three kinds of internal notes — its step reminder, the person's actual request, and extra handling instructions — instead of telling the system directly how long to keep each one. People who build assistants on this setup decide for themselves what to do with each label, and the system now keeps the latest note with each label plus the very last note handy for the next step. Blank instruction text is now left out entirely, and all of this runs live today.

81b1faa006e98bd4e0599edefd96a9296e783f8a.text: The assistant you control by typing cleaned up the way nine of its behind-the-scenes jobs report back, such as searching code, finding files, listing a folder, reading files, running a command, swapping words, saving a file, and keeping a to-do list. When one of those jobs gets started with no details filled in, it now returns an empty result box instead of returning nothing. People who type commands to the assistant see no difference on screen, and the cleanup is already in place.

41f86aafad9366829ce6e2a3030b85cbbd72c715.text: Someone added a small internal note for the team behind the automated coding helper. It warns that the helper freezes when the tool that tracks saved work stops to ask a question, so steps like combining saved work, picking which edits to keep, or cleaning up extra files must be run in a separate window where a person can answer. Anyone opening the internal handbook today will see that warning, the list, and how to open the window.

e8c2de98a92d4fa210e73dfc0b8729303b063a99.text: The team tidied up how mistakes get recorded behind the scenes. It only matters for staff who open the internal error records. Those records now always show the same three details — what kind of problem it was, what message it gave, and where it happened — even when the problem arrives as plain text. A new standard way to label work as passed or failed was also put in place, but nothing uses it yet so it does nothing today.

39bfc0cc2dd3a8f910d2f1a1fcc5681ebb8e8e4e.text: Nothing customers can use has changed today; this work is only on an internal test example. A person running the example now gets back a short answer with a labeled greeting in a fixed box instead of free text, made by a different outside model. The example also holds the addresses for that outside service but leaves them turned off.

9c1fee05c60c77404eee91a41a4bfaf40931b5c9.text: The team deleted an extra safety check that made sure the helper files for reading computer code were present and not empty. Someone running the internal tests will now see only the practical check that actually tries reading code, without the earlier list confirming each helper file one by one. Nothing in the finished product looks different today.

403f68a87ecff3329fca3a528a2d567c6500de17.text: Staff who test coding helpers with an internal comparison tool got a small fix that is already in use. The tool now writes its comparison report after every test, even when only one helper ran, bases that report on the exact instructions the helper received, and handles problems in that report step more safely. Reviewers looking at the saved test logs will now see a report for single-helper tests where they previously saw none.

33412ddc2e939a5f3cc6bb63f92b0071ccf67e91.text: People who make their own extra tools for the assistant are affected. The building checks now insist that a tool's settings and the information handed to it are a set of named values, not a single word or number, so a wrong setup gets caught while the tool is being put together. It is live now, but it is a small behind-the-scenes fix and does not change how finished tools behave.

0ecce5c9e4d62760508c0f1312725cbd51607f7e.text: The building guide for people making their own helpers got a small cleanup, and it is live now. Anyone opening it sees examples that start one exact saved helper, show a mood-reading helper using a different fast model, and spell out which outside data lookup that helper may use, with running updates printed as plain readable text. Nothing in how the helpers actually work changed.

a1720e179d12622aab9f09cd3122a1c381436e8d.text: Fixed a small internal bug in the helper that edits files. It now keeps a running list of every successful save as it works, instead of only looking back at the end. Staff using that helper will now see the full list of changed files, even on long jobs where earlier work used to go missing. It is live.

71441bd51e14d4d3dd85dbf4335497b014e0d9a4.text: Workers cleaned up how the waiting sign works while an answer prints out. For people who run the assistant in a text window, the sign now returns after each finished line, and if a helper job stops without any words, the sign shows Thinking again. It is live now, and it is a small behind-the-scenes tidy-up.

55179df4a53f2a542640b2bf05f3a109fe5cc02a.text: Engineers made a small internal fix that is live now. It affects only staff who maintain the automated helpers. If one of them opened the setup, they would see two titles and short job descriptions typed out directly: one for Superagent explaining it can start several code-editing helpers to finish a task, and one for Buffy the Lite Base Agent explaining it runs the full answer.

7a7eaf0575af04a13d266d08a2b79827fc2a4060.text: Builders who make their own automated helpers get a corrected instruction for the check that runs between steps. That check now gets the result of the last action as a list of detailed parts instead of a single piece of text. The correction is in place but nothing looks or acts different yet.

1916381de95ca756c6fae9d46583c4fd75b9a4d0.text: The team added two missing labels when setting up its behind-the-scenes helpers. The helper that tries new ideas is now marked as experimental, and the helper that works through tasks step by step is now marked as normal. It is live today but it is a small internal fix, so a person checking the product would see no difference.

cd831b628e9adc60d03b577c5e9d86a998ce3c39.text: If the assistant runs one helper job with a very long name, the notes that mark when that job starts and finishes no longer fail. The assistant now shows the full name with no dashes on the sides when the name is too long to fit. It was a small internal repair and it is live.

6e7401cf6d5da75b46dd1c87bad082f7698c0504.text: People trying to work with an old or bad login now get the same message when checking if a project is covered, looking at past use, or signing out. The message says they may have been signed out on the website and need to sign in again. It is live now. Someone checking past use with no login at all still gets the old general failure note.

1606d967be0aa15b2803ca89e38bf2ad0935233e.text: The writing helper inside the automatic plan-write-check team now runs on a different model, and the lead helper now tells the team to make a plan first, then write, then check and rewrite if needed. The tool now saves answers from two other models so it can reuse them. It is live today and small and internal, so someone using that team would just see it follow the plan, then write, then check steps.

1a1affad6eebbc262b25acf84fd0c595bee03648.text: A small internal update to the test coding helper is active now. Staff trying it will see shorter, more direct replies that stick closely to existing patterns, with the lead helper only handing out work instead of writing fixes itself and asking for everything it needs in one go. The helper that makes edits can now ask two separate look-up helpers for aid, one for the public web and one for written guides, and it always sees a short list of recent file edits.

76a16fb5e9be7d60ed8ae7a599594f30df481d43.text: The master list of models the assistant can pick from now includes one more chat option, but nothing in this update actually uses it yet so there is nothing new to see from that part. The guidance for the slow helper that searches through code and the web to write a full plan and answer hard questions was softened. Someone bringing a complicated job that needs careful thought may now get that detailed planning step a bit more often.

755448ffd8131e6c0c7892583473715014d94fc7.text: Someone made a small internal tweak to the hidden instructions for assistants that run on the newest model. Those assistants now keep working through several steps on their own — reading files, searching, and starting extra help — and only hand work back when done or stuck. Someone inside the company using one of those assistants would notice fewer check-in stops and a shorter explanation that handing back means asking for feedback. It is live now.

62182905e81dde741de93c24aeb40f94a4fbe710.text: The main work-splitting helper now keeps only two jobs — calling smaller helpers and finishing — and it must call any helper a person names with an at-sign. People using that set-up would notice the plan-making helper now offers to look things up online and answer any question, not just coding jobs, and the code-writing helper says it can change files and run commands and may ignore a bad plan. These new instructions are live now, and it is a small internal tidy-up.

ae5c76de5c0de3d28d2886fb3804774c815fcaf7.text: The helper that writes out the list of tools for new setups now makes its folder first instead of failing when the folder is missing, and it saves that list alongside the starter files. A web search no longer has to say how thorough to be; leaving it blank gives quick results. It is live today and only matters to people keeping that tool list up to date.

39bf72e5293133330a4b99fc875af740266ef0ed.text: The team added a small behind-the-scenes helper to the automatic verification that runs when new work is submitted. It is active now and only matters to teammates who review those runs. If they open a run they will now see a neat list of exactly which quick checks and which longer live-system checks passed or failed, and a broken list will itself mark the run as failed.

31bb570f2bd80ee28e9abeee1294558c53859c18.text: People who build and share their own assistants can now leave the starting instructions blank and sharing will still go through, with the blank treated as empty text. They pick which assistant to share by its set name or shown name. It works today.

324f2f307281f37980899a815ae7d867c5d38c64.text: The outside building kit now shows a shorter, cleaned-up list of jobs custom helpers can do. It hides inside-only jobs like starting helpers in the background, pulling up browser records, and making formal step-by-step plans. People who build with that kit only see everyday jobs like finding and editing files, running commands, and searching the web, and the cleanup is live now.

7944c91097bb73c5914dc7a89ef69352f1b9a31b.text: People building with the add-on kit to run the helper no longer need to include a list of replacement tools when they set it up. If they leave that list out, the helper now assumes there are none and starts normally. It works today, and it is a small cleanup.

ad4c92bb4c335733ebe986d35ba8bc2e29b4bced.text: The guide for letting outside software talk to Codebuff now shows new steps, and those steps are live today. Only people building with that outside-software kit need it. The guide tells them to sign in through the main Codebuff tool instead of pasting in a secret key by hand, and it walks through a much longer example for opening the link, sending a request, and getting back progress, cost, and answer updates.

ec897ec0cc858627130f9cefb0611a7040c5f084.text: For people who build the assistant into their own software, asking it to do work no longer requires listening for step-by-step progress — they can skip that and just wait for the final answer. If the live link to the service breaks, that problem now shows up in the normal place for errors instead of disappearing quietly. A behind-the-scenes fix keeps file edits working, and all of it is live now.

fe3776e76cf1aad51cf24c7981007d1b3996d1a3.text: People who build their own assistants now get a refreshed short list of suggested models to run them on. The short list now favors the latest OpenAI releases and adds suggestions from Qwen, DeepSeek and others, while older OpenAI and Claude suggestions no longer appear, though builders can still type in any model they want. Builders can also name any helper for an assistant to call on, rather than picking only from five fixed helpers.

67f372f023d3ae06a562b5367f20dd55aa169ea7.text: The team made a small internal cleanup and it is live now. It affects the staff who keep the company's own helpers, who will no longer see error warnings about an extra way to hand back a final answer because the main helpers no longer offer it. The brainstorming helper can now bring in other helpers, and the helper that writes save notes for code now hands back plain writing.

a447f95766f235935ce322c14e524b8cbe24b51c.text: People who build their own assistants now find the complete list of jobs their assistant can do at the very top of the setup text, spaced out cleanly. The list itself stayed the same, it only moved to make it easier to spot. It is live now and is a small behind-the-scenes tidy-up.

e28dd1d7e1d77283c7e6b5c9d0c88c0a5e14ef2f.text: Builders who run Codebuff from inside their own software must now always give a written request when asking for a single answer; sending only extra settings no longer works, and the old way of packing the request inside a separate holder no longer works. A builder who leaves the written request out now gets an error that says a written request is required. It is live now.

9ed2ed7bb5d876e51add2e2a94b369ab7232f959.text: Someone tidied the internal workshop where helper assistants are defined, moving the shared rule sheets into their own drawer and pointing four helpers to the new spot. The tidy-up is live today. Builders can now leave out the repeated note that used to be required at every step, and the idea helper no longer shows its cheat sheet telling other helpers when to call it.

8c24d94b8692b456791ddb07a72b2f1a3c8f7911.text: The automatic checks that run when a team member saves a change now use the copy of the checking tool stored with the project instead of the copy installed on each computer. It touches only the people building the product, in three separate work areas. A teammate watching would see fewer false failures when the two copies act differently, and it works that way today.

0ef68b547c97738f22114ec4203474481896cdbe.text: The team tidied up how the assistant's built-in abilities are stored behind the scenes, filing each one under its own name instead of keeping them in one long list. It affects only the people who maintain that machinery and is in use now. If you watched the assistant work, you would see no difference — it still reads, edits, searches, and runs the same jobs as before.

e2714f8c2430a5ac228a7608b32fbc042ca435bf.text: The automatic check for a new version now waits 20 seconds instead of 10 before giving up. People getting the program through that check with a slow connection get more time, and if it still fails they see a message telling them to check their internet connection and try again. It works today and is a small behind-the-scenes fix.

e133a602b602a3d8024e4330429ce623df4eeb9d.text: When the helper stops mid-answer because something broke, the people who keep it running now get a full readable note about what broke instead of a blank one. Chats sent through one outside answering service now also ask that service to hold recent messages for a short time to respond quicker, matching what was already done for the other service. It is live now and is a small behind-the-scenes fix, so someone using the helper would see no difference in normal use.

526019e6e147a73b3757f7f33682d1d5990d7b53.text: A small internal safety fix is live now. If the main way of running commands fails on someone's computer, the tool now uses a simpler backup way instead of stopping. Only people on computers where the main way fails are affected, and they will just see the tool keep working.

33185154b2617f737880d811644a7519bb249063.text: This is a small internal cleanup and it is live now. People who maintain the assistant's built-in instructions can now pull a person's latest typed message straight from the chat history. If they looked, they would see that message show up cleanly where asked, and the old workaround that tried to unpack the starting instructions for the main request and a list of relevant files is gone.

86965a85fbc64343fcdfb7aea4b1cf161fabeb85.text: The assistant now sticks only to its preferred sources for certain models and will not automatically switch to a backup source if they are busy. People getting answers from those models will notice nothing in normal use, but will get no answer instead of one quietly coming from elsewhere when the preferred sources are down. It is a small behind-the-scenes fix and is live now.

cedfe34b881aed3644851cf55fdabfa29b6ba164.text: An internal tidy-up is live now for the team that builds the product. The long automatic checks still run in full only when the save note includes the word buffbench in square brackets. On all other saves the check now shows up and marks itself as passed right away instead of staying hidden.

bd5503188e6c85e04e2936af3eadbcd43fcf42ea.text: People who turned on the experimental option for picking files now get suggestions from a newly trained helper. It looks at past conversation a little differently, treating the assistant's earlier replies as background notes from the person so it matches how it was taught. You would see no new button, just possibly different file picks when that option is on. A second trained copy was also saved for internal testing and does nothing in the product yet.

cdc96f36a56704cd70d63e8aa7b28c10aa23cbe8.text: People who build their own helpers and choose which model powers each one can now type in any name from the outside library and the helper will try to run with it instead of stopping with an error. Unfamiliar names run without the shortcut that reuses earlier instructions to save time, and failure reports now keep the service's full reply. It works today, and a warning shown when a helper reaches for a tool it should not use now stays linked to that helper's actual attempt.

60f1404da95fc5c107dc9f0001a1120ca198d4dd.text: The team folded three separate automatic checks on submitted code into a single check that runs the mistake scan and the website assembly at the same time. It is live now and affects only coworkers who submit code. When they look at a submission they will see one combined result instead of three separate ones, and the separate step that assembled the extra app no longer runs.

e5d8d416efb390e971990a46d12fd5d2227fceac.text: Engineers added two extra instructions to the helper that cleans up the assistant's answers behind the scenes. It now remembers to keep long file contents in place and never makes up extra details it was not given. It is live today as a small internal fix, so someone watching closely would just see fewer missing or invented bits when the assistant writes a file.

e1a0281bc4129afbfdbf103a22481c40abab0a00.text: Someone using the assistant in its questions-only setting is affected. The assistant now gets a reminder on each step not to write files or run commands on the computer, because those actions are turned off in that setting. The block was already there, so the visible difference is the assistant attempts those actions less and just answers. It is live now, and it is a small internal fix.

67ff237180cb905fc6e7962fe013d7993a793c8c.text: Commands run behind the scenes used to freeze and never finish because the tool looked for the wrong finish marker in the messy command text. It now looks for the location marker at the start and a different finish marker at the end, so it can tell when work is done and hand back the results and the ending folder. The fix is live and internal, so people working on the product will see fewer stuck commands and will see trial runs and correctness checks reported separately when files change.

3e9d4b721994f767a1db3998df9158571c8e6218.text: A staff-only tool that gathers past work to improve how files get picked got a small tidy-up. Only team members who run that gathering will see a difference: it hooks up its data store by itself, takes a shorter typed word for live runs, and drops results in a renamed folder. It is active now.

6441cc7e8b117833035bdcf4d5956dfc01d62f32.text: The team made a small behind-the-scenes cleanup that is live now. It affects only the private notes the assistant writes to itself before acting. If someone opened those notes, they would no longer see pieces of the coming fix spelled out there or a full plan written out in advance, so the notes look shorter.

52ced87cc0559e20f25596bb2c1451d8326ae6a9.text: Behind the scenes, the step that passes answers from outside helpers back to the assistant now looks in two places for the number that links an answer to its request, instead of only one. Staff keeping the assistant running would notice fewer stopped conversations where an answer arrived in the second shape and could not be matched. It is live today.

5d20d722a70f1bc76d0715100dd3f7239280ded3.text: The coding helper got a small internal tweak to how it double-checks its work. It now only tries to run a project check on its own when the project's saved notes tell it exactly what check to run; if those notes list no check, it simply pauses and waits for the built-in results instead. It is live now, and someone watching closely would see fewer stray check attempts on projects without instructions.

82fe2020dcb20becda30267c3c5339ed6e7df806.text: The team made a small fix to the automatic checks that run when new work is submitted. The checks now step inside each part's folder before running its tests instead of listing the test files from the outside. Staff watching those runs will see the same pass-or-fail result, just started from a different spot. It is active now and touches only internal work.

4253f0ee60da409114f99cc7fc7ee070dde19027.text: Engineers cleaned up the hidden check that decides whether typed words can run directly as a computer command, like git pull, or are just chat, like hi. It now asks one smart helper instead of asking two at once, and still gives up after 30 seconds if there is no answer. People using the product see no difference, and the cleaned-up check is live.

c5bd510c980c3d6d357df91ed909bca8568b4df9.text: Someone who starts Codebuff from their home folder or a folder above it sees a short welcome note telling them to move into a project folder and start again, then the program stops. It now shows that note even when the home folder sits inside the folder where it was started, not only when started from the home folder itself or the very top folder. The team also tidied the wording a little, and it is live today as a small fix.

324585540c95b54eef3a326d5779fbeda0f4e10c.text: The automatic checker that assembles the product now pulls in its private settings earlier, before assembly begins, and it sticks exactly to the approved list of outside parts when setting up. This only affects the in-house team that builds and tests the product, and it is already running today. If they watched it work, they would see the private settings file ready before assembly instead of showing up later.

35138891ec5298e376333c6656ee7eabf35f02ff.text: When the assistant pulls in outside help pages to answer a question, it now reuses the tracking number from that question instead of making a new one. It affects staff who check internal records to trace what happened. If they looked, they would see the help-page lookup and the final answer share one number, so the two steps link together. It is a small internal fix and it is live today.

7c6d8ede48ab90462888cda96218d9af4879db81.text: Fixed a small behind-the-scenes mistake in how the assistant puts together its next step, and it is live now. It affects only chats running in the experimental mode that handles costs. Those chats keep past messages correctly and get full directions for using tools, instead of losing history or getting a blank or broken direction.

98614e3a708ecb0bc1ed6aa3d1ca329670f7036e.text: The system now tries to set up a folder for notes to help fix problems wherever it runs, except during automatic checks, instead of only on staff laptops. Staff who open the files on a live computer will now find that folder there too. It is live now, and it is a small internal tidy-up with no visible difference in the product.

1d2fb9167fecb76bd03aeb6be033a2246f1f0a70.text: The part of the product that runs on company computers now answers the automatic check that asks if it is running with a healthy signal instead of an error. It also keeps running even if it cannot connect to the storage for usage numbers, and it no longer prints secret login details into its internal records. It is live now for the staff who run the service and for staff testing on their own machines, and it changes nothing else.

9ad0b6817630de0a6b7e597fd9b6198dfe69a81d.text: The assistant that helps with projects now reads tip sheets saved under two names instead of one. Teams who already kept tips under the second name will notice the assistant follows them with no extra setup, like running a safety check after an edit when the notes ask for it. It is a small internal improvement and it works today.

bdb31790678fca58776d4c0f0235ba39160664d4.text: Team members who run the system on their own laptops for testing now have detailed log files saved correctly, while other test and live setups no longer save those extra files. It also makes sure the storage folder is created from the file location instead of using the wrong value and failing. It is live today and is a small internal fix.

e1bb9c9b4e42cb5e97ee69391a2c3d701c423423.text: Engineers refreshed the saved description of start-up settings. People who set up programs to run automatically when a project opens would see two added lines for where to save normal output and error output, plus shorter wording for the on/off switch. That update only corrects an internal record, so it puts the wording in place and does nothing else yet.

bae6577e52869979f91cb276fbe2f7faa1ae5d1c.text: If you close the tool while it still has extra tasks running in the back, it now tells you what it shut down. You see your credit use first, then a yellow line naming each task it stopped and a red warning if one could not be stopped, right before the final goodbye. It is a small internal tidy-up and is live now.

653f0c599b744af3f5e206d63cd95268c2f44d29.text: Behind the scenes the service fixed the wording it uses to tell models where to end an answer. For normal answers it now sends that cut-off phrase to every model except o3 and o4 mini, and for long answers that need a second request to finish it sends it only to o3 and o4 mini. People asking those two models for long answers that run in pieces will see the answers end in the right place, and the fix is live.

dfb5716bf6a147f31157182f6aa2eb1d0ed4cafb.text: The part of the system that reads the assistant's action requests now keeps everything as plain text with extra spaces trimmed off. It used to turn numbers like 5000, words like true and false, and paired position limits into special values on the spot. It is a small internal cleanup that is live now, and nothing looks different in the product.

2a0b3726e7ff6a8aa45a857d1a6cf1ddfe78d7aa.text: Engineers took out a recent attempt to send people to a smarter spot after they sign in and went back to the simpler behavior. People who sign in from the login page with a one-time code will no longer land straight on the setup page with that code carried over. It is live now, and it is a small internal step back while the team keeps debugging the flow.

d6c53eb3197e539f7d3a7ea8537b6380803f7c60.text: A small behind-the-scenes fix affects people who store private codes for outside services through the helper program on their computer. The helper now sends proof you are signed in along with each store and check, and the website looks that proof up itself instead of asking the sign-in helper to do it, and it now waits for the stored list to finish loading before moving on. If you looked you would see the same screens as before, with nothing new to click, and it is live now.

2ade59eedf3a1ddf3d8a02d31ccb4d8d1b3b04a0.text: A small behind-the-scenes fix changed how the helper program that lists saved keys proves who it is. It used to tuck the sign-in proof inside what it sent, and now it stamps it on the outside for the key service to check. It is live now for people who pull their keys through that helper, and the key service turns away an ask missing that stamp for not being signed in.

f3f6d8319b554023b6bf98bea46b94992dfab588.text: Engineers made a small behind-the-scenes tweak to how the assistant decides whether to open additional files. It affects someone already chatting with the assistant, who will see it pull in fresh material after a switch to a new topic or a mention of a new part by name, and see it hold off after just saying hello or asking it to run something simple like installing packages. The new wording is live today.

467de2de8ea96333e5618c8e084c3663ce844100.text: The assistant got a small tweak to its hidden instructions for handling unclear orders. If you give a command that could be read in more than one way, it will now stop and ask at least one question to pin down what you meant, unless you told it not to ask questions. It is live now, and you would notice it no longer has to put multiple questions in a numbered list.

3b14eb62d7ff07249716d3d0b56d47acc4d70613.text: The assistant that edits files got a small internal update to its instructions. People who ask it to make an edit will see it ask a follow-up question only when different readings of the request would lead to very different results. When it makes the edit, it leaves their original notes in the file exactly as written, line by line, and that behavior is live now.

091eb2b4c595a9e1213cb7a3da2fa61c9c35d53a.text: Fixed a small internal mistake in how the assistant handles long work. When no part of the job was marked finished yet, it kept the whole conversation even when it got too long. Now it shortens that early history the same way it does later on, and the fix is live.

c5c151ef64d26c0ebff8641e2c5dd8fd692aa645.text: The helper that shortens a long chat before sending it on no longer sets aside the last question and anything after it as must-keep. It now starts empty and keeps as many of the newest messages as fit, dropping the oldest first. It is live now, and it is a small internal cleanup, so a person with a long chat would see no difference in everyday use.

db5076fef7fe4d056544d1fe80ce722266a15f7f.text: It is a small internal safety tweak to the assistant's instructions for doing work on your computer, and it is active now. If you let the assistant do work for you, it must ask your permission before sending your saved work to a shared place or running extra programs that change things or have lasting effects. You would notice it pausing to ask more often and warning that jobs running longer than 30 seconds will be stopped.

f008686b5ffc15440d464376d1b08b1a98f98f23.text: A small behind-the-scenes fix to the command box built into the app. It now stamps the end of each finished command with a secret marker instead of guessing from the shape of the text, so it no longer mistakes a program's own output for a finished command. Every computer gets the marker, with Mac and Linux loading the normal startup settings first, and it is live now, so someone running a command would simply see the finish spotted more reliably.

35cfba10d6e1cfe94f7669dcc5b11a9713b64934.text: Behind the scenes the helper now measures how long the back-and-forth has become before loading the map of project files. People getting coding help in very long chats keep getting answers instead of hitting a failure, but the helper looks at fewer files as the chat grows, with a slightly smaller starting allowance in both the cheaper setting and the regular setting. It is live now and is a small reliability fix.

4853758b7a91f6e226b73b7d571e3efa273581df.text: People using the pro option got a small behind-the-scenes tweak to how the assistant works. The assistant now writes out a full step-by-step plan first only for very tangled jobs that span many different parts, and even then only rarely. Someone on that option would notice the assistant skipping the upfront plan more often and just starting the work, and it is live today.

470ac84747b03409b6f2611bf9283f20bdf4bfa1.text: People who first ask for a step-by-step plan and then ask the assistant to do the work no longer automatically let it keep working on its own through many steps. The assistant now has to pass the same approval check as any other request, so those people may see it stop and ask to go on where it used to just keep going. It is a small behind-the-scenes fix and it is live now.

bec6f9e4270093a25d10f7897116369abbcc0c76.text: Someone tidied the hidden instructions that tell the building helper how to run commands. It is a small internal cleanup that is live now for people who have the helper do work inside their project. Those people would notice the helper is told more firmly to obey its safety list, still makes file changes with its editing step instead of with a command, and now understands that no output can still mean success, like when a check finds no problems.

907eb5a4c6a7e902f3684cfa3b5e09438ca0ba55.text: If the service that writes answers briefly loses its connection while working, it now tries again up to three times and waits a little longer between each try. People waiting for an answer would see fewer cut-off failures during those short connection drops, and it is working now. Other kinds of failures still stop right away and show a shorter message without the extra word Error at the front, along with an address to contact for help.

922bd5565bc52bf44f0ead6df57c776630daeb22.text: People who steer the helper by typing and run low on credits now get one steady warning and can keep typing right away instead of getting stuck. Those who are signed in see a single note pointing to the pricing page and a friend-invite link for extra monthly credits, while those who are signed out are told to log in for more credits. Typing konami, codebuffy, or the letter run for the old game cheat clears the screen and plays a large animated spelling of codebuffy that grows or shrinks to fit the window. It is live now.

46234ad15d8366899aebf7099af3e77ae17f746a.text: The team fixed one word on the help page. If you open the answer about the instruction notes that tell the assistant how to work, it now says the assistant typically will not start a new note on its own, but it will update notes you already have. You can see the new wording on the site today.

2a74626af7b974735c402b81d47c6556bbe688dd.text: People building the product updated the internal description of the assistant's background instructions so it can note that part of those instructions should be kept briefly for reuse, and deleted a leftover note about request limits that nothing used. That clears an error flag that said the description was wrong. It is in place now but does nothing visible, so no one outside the build team is affected.

69167eee20eeaf7b0f8eaa1707d188d9cb4eb21f.text: The assistant that edits code used to be told to always double-check its work by running the computer's own checks. Now that check is small and optional — it looks at the project's saved instructions first and only runs a check if those instructions ask for it. The warning not to launch something that keeps running, because you would be stuck waiting for it to finish, was kept but moved to a clearer spot. It is live now, so someone asking for a code change would notice fewer automatic checks after small edits.

bb0b6f8596654c2b1e0a2d349f6427a6238d0764.text: When the writing helper tries to change a file but cannot find the exact lines to replace, it now receives a clearer layout of the wanted edit plus the earlier reasoning behind it before rewriting the whole file. That matters only for people making file edits where that first placement fails. They would notice the rewrite sticks to the wanted edit and leaves other text and notes untouched. It is live and is a small internal tidy-up.

f495d4509a07cb41354593acedd1cef9216e4ade.text: The part of Codebuff that updates it missed people on Windows who installed it once for the whole computer with a helper that stores and switches between versions of its engine. It now reads Windows locations the same way as other computers, so it recognizes that whole-computer setup and refreshes the right copy. The repair is live and small.

41a7988a22d8f5ffe87e36db62da2dc7963c6819.text: The team made a small internal tweak to the hidden instructions for the helper that rewrites files. The helper must now write out the full replacement and cannot leave a short note saying the rest is unchanged. It is live now, so anyone who asks the helper to replace a whole file will get back the complete new version.

19487b28dbc9089e4cbd33a68ce86777b8682dee.text: Behind the scenes, the assistant now also looks for a few similar pieces of existing work to copy from when it answers a coding request. It skips the general notes pages because those are already added every time. It is live now, so someone asking for new code would see answers that follow the patterns already used in their work.

c7c8077b288702857e9e6248b9eeceb06c90d776.text: The writing helper now has stricter rules to put all edits for one file in one package instead of splitting them up. If the helper produces an edit where nothing actually changed, it now stops and records that nothing changed instead of pushing an empty save through. It is active now, and it is an internal tidy-up. Someone watching the helper work would see fewer broken-up edits and no empty saves.

859ac32a5fd2380b563ec5787fc1f9a90d2838b2.text: A small behind-the-scenes fix changed how the system checks invites. People asking for their personal invite link who have not yet hit the allowed number now receive the correct link instead of an error saying they are not in the system. People who have hit the allowed number still see a message saying they have reached their usage limit. It is live now.

3d1a187e92fa77daf5b14912902ad5fd5c951ff0.text: Behind the scenes, the helper that rewrites files now marks its proposed changes with a clearer edit label instead of a general file label, so those instructions cannot be mixed up with other mentions of files. It is an internal cleanup that is live now, and anyone asking for an edit will notice no difference in how the work gets done.

edebdcd2b2a8209e47de4d799d1dc895039d99a8.text: The program now picks where to load its passwords and keys by asking if it is running on Render. That matters only for installs on Render that use a name other than local, which used to look in the locked system folder and fail. The fix is live now and is behind the scenes, so those installs simply start up using the settings file kept beside the program.

7d1470ef751884910c4d1a8c32d40577343b3955.text: The tool that applies file edits now first asks a quick yes-or-no check for leftover shortcut notes like "existing code stays here." If none are present, it writes out the edit directly instead of asking for a full rewrite. It is live and internal, so anyone asking for a file update that is already fully written would just see the result come back a little faster.

1033372807349c8e71c8a5fea54d12a2e7760580.text: Engineers fixed a small internal problem with how the assistant asks for work like editing a file, and the fix is live now. Staff watching it run will see the editing note now starts with a dash and ends with dots, and the note that a command finished now leaves a blank line below it. The assistant also stops waiting for more words as soon as its request is complete.

6421d5838fa8fd42595093a1a083ede9e6874add.text: A small behind-the-scenes tweak gave the work assistant clearer directions for asking for files. It must now give the full address starting at the top of the project, even when it spots a short address used inside a lower folder. It is active now, so anyone watching the assistant work should see it ask for the right place instead of getting confused by short addresses.

4a256323e5415622215fb4aa78dab851bfefd801.text: Engineers made a tiny behind-the-scenes fix to how answers that include files are put together. It only matters when the helper sends back files as part of its reply. A person asking for those files still sees the same files, but the helper now adds their text to the full reply right after it starts their separate work, and the fix is live.

538005e79df18e371aaf34755dfe2be9704083fd.text: Engineers have now locked most of the outside parts used to assemble the product to exact copies and moved several of them to newer copies. It affects only the team doing that assembly work internally. If you watched, you would see the same parts picked every time instead of slightly different ones slipping in.

7722459eb1ed718ae76ec7d2d2484459a13eedf0.text: The helper that writes code used to get a reminder to hunt for missing work files even right after it had just collected them at the start. The helper now skips that reminder when it just collected files. It is a small internal cleanup and is live now, and a person checking the hidden instructions would see the reminder missing in that just-collected case and present at other times.

b95c04e5e2171588c98c8f3fb8f5d14251d0aead.text: The system now waits to set up its link to the outside writing service until it actually needs to ask something, instead of setting it up at start-up. It is live now and is a small internal tidy-up that affects only staff who start the service without its secret password in place. Those staff would see the service start up fine and only run into a problem later when it tries to get an answer.

37ae6a49f281f6033ddfef12c54fb2ef5a859b7c.text: The team marked a new internal release and added two reminders to its private idea list. Nobody outside the team sees any difference, and the helper acts the same today. Someone reading that list would see new lines suggesting the helper show only the small edited piece instead of rewriting everything, and ask the person first when it is unsure.

fc1d61f2fe380d69c7f58013b793a9d1f15ccc7a.text: People who talk to Manicode by typing see a tidier start screen. The lines for exiting, stopping, stepping back, and getting help now sit under one heading with a dash in front of each. The tips underneath now tell them to ask Manicode to write down facts about their project and to add to those notes when it makes a mistake. It is live today, and it is a small cleanup.

1dbb42756316f806d1067fb14b43b3ecd57dccab.text: Engineers cleaned up how the assistant you talk to by typing handles stopped answers. For people who use that typing tool, stopping a reply early no longer brings up the 'Generating file changes. Please wait...' note by mistake and no longer saves that stopped reply twice. It is live now and is a small internal fix.

8f965d94fe3cc86e60ec0305657274091e8ef9fb.text: The team fixed how the assistant shortens the location of each file in a project so the short name stays right no matter how the computer writes slashes. Cleaning up old finished work no longer fails when a little tracking note is already missing, and the team added a shortcut that opens a direct line into the main computer running the service. They are small behind-the-scenes fixes for only the people who build and run the assistant, and they are live now.

508d5810e2018a14c94d1c386da2c55429c5bb8e.text: People who use the assistant by typing commands got a small tidy-up that is live now. The starter question now ends with a period instead of parentheses and appears again every time you step out of the menu, after the screen clears. The tool also waits until it has connected before it lets you type, and it no longer prints a leftover list of files on your computer when it starts.

f23277e9a0fdc0988a4d8b4559acb3bb131972ce.text: People who use the text-based version of the assistant get file updates later than before. Files no longer change while the answer is still appearing, even when the assistant pauses to look something up. Once the answer finishes, the screen says it is making the file updates, then lists each file created or updated.

48ad7f372029c76ef633a3fcb148a1601d110352.text: The team updated its shared instruction notes for the assistant. Someone on the team reading those notes would now see a new part explaining that the assistant keeps learning notes in different folders and updates them on its own for teammates to check, plus a new reminder to explain tricky work clearly, and a to-do list that now asks for a better way to show text changes instead of fixing rare errors. The new wording is in place now, but it only changes the notes, not what anyone outside the team sees.

ca5f91dc4d362b9e1936d21121f9711545343daf.text: The team fixed the packing for the helper part of Manicode that runs on company computers so it starts up instead of failing to find its own pieces. Anyone putting that helper up now gets the same fixed internet address on the same size and kind of company computer that matches how it was packed. The editing tool now also picks the live helper automatically, and only talks to a test copy on a person's own computer during testing. It is live now.

c21fabe374e86cdcca1dad300951054a989389c0.text: Staff made a small internal cleanup to the name shown for the downloadable coding helper and removed extra words at the end that marked it as old. It is live now and the helper itself works exactly the same. A person checking the listing now sees only the plain name with nothing extra attached.

6a2e93e1a002a3682492aebb7bc43743771cd483.text: The team added a small internal rule telling the coding assistant to finish every finished answer with a set signal word that means it is done, and it is active now. It only affects the team's own testing. If they looked at a full answer they would see that extra signal word at the very end, and the assistant can now edit an old learning note instead of only adding new ones.

5fd3d84cf5204db3f6b4448086f22aa00225c9f1.text: The team tightened the hidden instructions for the internal coding helper so it stops getting stuck opening the same files over and over while it researches a task. It must now check what it already opened, make a plan for what else it needs, and write a short summary before it changes anything. The team also removed the old shortcut that let it skip opening a file before a change because it had just seen it, so it always opens a fresh copy first. It is a small internal fix that is live, so staff using the helper would notice fewer stalls and one extra fresh open right before an edit.

cc5b0e70c3f3f370e8df9fa7b15bb414a674f9b7.text: A small internal tidy-up affects only team members who dig into early failures. The team now keeps its troubleshooting notes when the main program starts instead of wiping them, and those notes list file names and the number of messages sent instead of pasting full contents. The tool no longer skips a file it already saw, so it handles a repeated file again, and it prints a short note when it leaves a file alone. It is live today.

50a33327c3305300e5094147244c7bd990cc229b.title: Supabase setup invitation capability bumps to schema version 2
50a33327c3305300e5094147244c7bd990cc229b.summary: `supabaseSetupInvitationCapabilitySchema` in `common/src/ads/supabase-setup-invitation.ts` bumps `schemaVersion` from `1` to `2`, renaming the inferred type from `SupabaseSetupInvitationCapabilityV1` to `SupabaseSetupInvitationCapabilityV2`. Version 2 recognizes existing third-party provider packages, so version 1's incomplete provider evidence is no longer accepted for serving new invitations. Scope is Shared/Core via `common/src/ads/supabase-setup-invitation.ts`, which remains a read-only Desktop facts check that proves neither a committed checkout nor a runnable paid task.

50a33327c3305300e5094147244c7bd990cc229b.text: The desktop program tightened the behind-the-scenes check that decides who gets offered help setting up Supabase. It now recognizes outside helper tools already installed, and old incomplete checks can no longer open a new offer. It is active for new offers, so a person who only passed the old check will simply not see the setup message.

57740be2e72a0a17ea154ebf41bec32f7a7816d1.text: Advertisers who only allow their ads on pages with a certain meaning are affected, and the new handling is live. When the rule is faulty, when there is not enough private viewer information to check it, or when the page does not match, they see only a general note that the page setting held the ad back, without seeing the viewer information or whether it matched. Internal records also now save eleven extra details about profile checks, which advertisers never see.

502a0060842d7b99b090d8a19756e14230c60699.title: {{advertiserClickId}} adds command-scoped CLI attribution
