502a0060842d7b99b090d8a19756e14230c60699.summary: common/src/ads/sponsored-procedure-inputs.ts adds `ADVERTISER_CLICK_ID_PLACEHOLDER` (`{{advertiserClickId}}`) and `advertiserClickIdFromLink()`, extending `sponsoredProcedureRuntimeInputsSection()` to emit an `advertiserClickId` section when the procedure opts in alongside `{{advertiserLink}}`. It reuses the same advertiser link's opaque `bfcid` for command-scoped CLI attribution with shape validation only, since the server supplies the link and the postback verifies its HMAC. Scope is Shared/Core in that single file via its `isSignedConversionToken` import from `./sponsored-proposal-cta`. Extraction requires `https:` with exactly one `bfcid` value passing `isSignedConversionToken` and a 512-char limit matching the postback's `BFCID_MAX_CHARS` contract without an internal-package dependency, with missing attribution rendering unavailable so the model skips the dependent command instead of falling back to an unattributed conversion.

502a0060842d7b99b090d8a19756e14230c60699.text: Only sponsored task templates that ask for it are affected. Those templates can now request the tracking code hidden inside the advertiser web address, separate from the full address itself. When they do, the run shows an extra line with that exact code plus rules to use it only for that one approved advertiser step and never save, share or print it, and if the address is missing or fails basic safety checks the run shows it as unavailable and skips that step instead of running it untracked.

ea08076516aa21e440150902f9290c71b0336b98.title: SubscriptionCostReport adds forecast and coverage fields
ea08076516aa21e440150902f9290c71b0336b98.summary: `SubscriptionCostReport` in `common/src/types/subscription-costs.ts` gains five optional fields: `forecastMethod`, `allowanceForecastStatus`, `allowanceForecastReason`, `coverageStatus`, and `latestCoveredHour`. The existing USD forecast remains an `uncapped_daily_run_rate` extrapolation until retained admission-to-provider-cost grain supports an allowance-constrained estimate, with the separate Freebucks-allowance-constrained estimate marked `unavailable` for `missing_funding_cost_basis`. Scoped to Shared/Core via `common/src/types/subscription-costs.ts`, `coverageStatus` (`current`/`missing`/`stale`) stays independent from `status` so a `collecting` report can still be current, while `latestCoveredHour` holds the newest attested hour or null.

ea08076516aa21e440150902f9290c71b0336b98.text: Engineers added extra labels to the cost summary that tracks paid subscriptions, to note how the dollar forecast was made and how fresh the hourly totals are. The forecast still just stretches the daily spending pace forward, and the version that would respect free allowances stays marked unavailable. The labels are in place but do nothing yet, so anyone checking paid-subscription costs today sees no change.

ed27ce1cf3e461105e209dcd13d8e5e22219331f.title: Axiom log adds external conversion postback event
ed27ce1cf3e461105e209dcd13d8e5e22219331f.summary: Added `ADS_EXTERNAL_CONVERSION_POSTBACK_EVENT` (`ads.external_conversion_postback`) in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`, wired through `getAxiomOnlyLogEvent` via `sanitizeAllowlistedFields` and added to the `AxiomOnlyLogEvent` union. The event is deliberately limited to a small, content-free operational census so partner credentials and opaque click/event identifiers never leave the request handler, keeping the postback stream safe to aggregate while the database owns attribution drill-down. Scope is Shared/Core in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`, allowing only `outcome`, `rejection_reason`, `event_type`, `traffic_class`, `primary_allocation_cohort` and `settlement_status` as strings plus `charged_cents` and `duration_ms` as numbers.

23c15cfd4656c6eb305dfe9e4bbab938ebadbed8.title: Axiom only log adds advertiser reporting read event
23c15cfd4656c6eb305dfe9e4bbab938ebadbed8.summary: Added `ADS_ADVERTISER_REPORTING_READ_EVENT` (`ads.advertiser_reporting_read`) in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`, with a new `ADS_ADVERTISER_REPORTING_READ_FIELDS` schema enforced via `sanitizeAllowlistedFields` in `getAxiomOnlyLogEvent`. The handler adds the event to the `AxiomOnlyLogEvent` union and returns sanitized `data` on exact name match, preserving the file's allowlist-only logging pattern for ads telemetry. Scope is Shared/Core in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`; logged fields are `advertiser_id`, `key_id` and `endpoint` as strings, `range_days`, `rows` and `duration_ms` as numbers, plus `outcome` as string.

1f35b8067456bba14e902e3018e6c41545b2a64e.title: Imprezia fetch completed event adds bounded Axiom logging
1f35b8067456bba14e902e3018e6c41545b2a64e.summary: Adds `ADS_IMPREZIA_FETCH_COMPLETED_EVENT` (`ads.imprezia_fetch_completed`) with `sanitizeImpreziaFetchCompletedFields` enforcing allowlisted `outcome`, `selection_reason`, `experiment_arm`, `surface`, `ad_count`, `duration_ms`, `test_mode`, and `failure_class` fields. The event records browser-side Imprezia decisions while deliberately reporting only bounded serving dimensions, so request/content/creative identifiers, URLs, and raw provider errors never enter Axiom. Scope is Shared/Core via `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` plus `.gitignore` now excluding `docs/specs/` for Linear-tracked plans; sanitization restricts outcomes to `fill`/`no_fill`/`timeout`/`provider_error`/`not_configured`/`not_eligible`, surfaces to `freebuff_web_chat`/`chat_assistant`, and caps duration at 60,000ms.

69fffe8f6b530e155e645d0bfd9c931f24294498.title: Main prompt removes previous assistant correction instruction
69fffe8f6b530e155e645d0bfd9c931f24294498.summary: Removed the self-correction instruction that framed prior assistant messages as from a less intelligent assistant from `mainPrompt` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, with `expireMessages` history now passed through without `castAssistantMessage` mapping. The change is scoped to backend prompt construction, commenting out the `hasAssistantMessage`-gated `user` instruction with `timeToLive: 'userPrompt'`. The `castAssistantMessage` import was removed while `expireMessages(messageHistory, 'userPrompt' | 'agentStep')` selection is preserved.

7b65652ad9decd202054622a7fbe267cc7c11201.title: Ads fetch logging adds request geo tier and decision outbox status
7b65652ad9decd202054622a7fbe267cc7c11201.summary: `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS` in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` gains `request_geo_tier`, `decision_outbox_status`, and `decision_outbox_sample_rate_ppm`. `request_geo_tier` logs the viewer tier (`tier1`, `tier2`, `unknown`) on every request while `first_party_inventory_geo_tier` keeps its gated routing-policy meaning, preserving the inventory-versus-configuration distinction for sizing a geo ramp, and `decision_outbox_status` (`scheduled | saturated | cooling_down | schedule_failed | disabled | not_sampled`) makes a stopped producer visible as a status change rather than absent rows. Scoped to Shared/Core Axiom-only logging in that single file, with `decision_outbox_sample_rate_ppm` reporting the rate that actually applied — certainty on the >=2-admitted override and zero on unwritten opportunities.

57740be2e72a0a17ea154ebf41bec32f7a7816d1.title: Advertiser redaction v3 adds semantic codes and profile lift logging
57740be2e72a0a17ea154ebf41bec32f7a7816d1.summary: `ADVERTISER_REASON_REDACTION_VERSION` bumps to `advertiser_reason_redaction_2026_09_v3` in `common/src/constants/advertiser-reason-redaction.ts`, adding `semantic_requirement_invalid`, `semantic_evidence_unavailable`, and `semantic_mismatch` to `ADVERTISER_OPERATOR_REASON_CODES` mapped through `ADVERTISER_VISIBLE_REASONS` to `{ kind: 'generalize', reason: 'context_filtered' }`, plus eleven `profile_lift_*` entries in `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS` in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`. The advertiser owns the rule but viewer evidence and whether it matched remain request-private, so all semantic refusal states share the existing bounded context projection and never serialize an input reason directly. Scope is Shared/Core across those two common files; the logging detail adds typed fields including `profile_lift_arm_probability_ppm` as `number`, `profile_lift_serving_assignment_applied` as `boolean`, and experiment, epoch, assignment, mode, config digest, and followup/maturity timestamps.

00ffb9f582ba344870e4fa0cdb418270c9394153.title: Upstream inference cost accepts null for Anthropic responses
00ffb9f582ba344870e4fa0cdb418270c9394153.summary: The OpenRouter chat completion response schema now allows `upstream_inference_cost` inside `cost_details` to be null or missing via `z.number().nullish()` in `packages/internal/src/openrouter-ai-sdk/openrouter-chat-language-model.ts`. This handles Anthropic responses that return a nullish inference cost, avoiding strict-number validation rejection. The outer `cost_details` was already `.nullish()` and sibling `cost` remains `.optional()`, so only the inner field widens.

9960f1f7021572ab6422137dd38830ec6587af47.title: Cloud plan ready adds required integrations list
9960f1f7021572ab6422137dd38830ec6587af47.summary: The `cloud-plan-ready` input in `common/src/tools/params/tool/cloud-plan-ready.ts` adds `required_integrations`, an array of `{slug, name}` objects for every selected Gravity service that returned required API keys or environment variables. The change is scoped to Shared/Core in that single params file, implemented with `zod` `min(1)` string validators for the exact recommendation `slug` and user-facing `name`. `[]` is reserved for plans needing no credential-bearing external service, and the native tool example now passes `required_integrations: [{slug: 'resend', name: 'Resend'}]` with the React/Vite/Supabase/Resend stack.

9f3905939a7734c5d57e5693ceac0a1e6bbd136a.title: Remove Manifold markets search tool and API client
9f3905939a7734c5d57e5693ceac0a1e6bbd136a.summary: Removed the Manifold markets search tool, deleting `npm-app/src/manifold-api.ts` with `searchManifoldMarkets` and dropping `handleSearchManifoldMarkets` and the `search_manifold_markets` entry from `toolHandlers` in `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts`. The client used `axios` against `https://api.manifold.markets/v0/search-markets` for `BINARY` contracts with default `limit` 5, mapping `id`, `question`, `probability`, and `url`. Scope is confined to `npm-app` tool handling in `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts`, where success previously returned JSON-stringified markets and failures returned a `<manifold_search_error>` wrapper, both now removed.

f1744c6fb4c1c5e1c281acd92756d59a40c9453e.title: Search Manifold Markets tool adds prediction market forecasts
f1744c6fb4c1c5e1c281acd92756d59a40c9453e.summary: Agent gains `search_manifold_markets` for future-event questions like presidential elections, returning Yes/No markets with probabilities to interpret as forecasts. It is defined in `backend/src/tools.ts` with `query` and `limit` inputs, handled in `manicode/src/tool-handlers.ts` by `handleSearchManifoldMarkets`, and implemented in new `manicode/src/manifold-api.ts`. The implementation queries `https://api.manifold.markets/v0/search-markets` with `contractType: BINARY`, defaults `limit` to 5, and returns `id`, `question`, `probability`, `url` as JSON, wrapping failures in `<manifold_search_error>`.

4c9007c7eaa0c04135f1be020c5209621d5aa716.text: You won't see anything different. If you use the website chat or the free web project assistants, the system now attaches your own scrambled ID so sign-ups and payments count for you instead of all being lumped together under one shared account.

df4b9aa599930aa2b2b9b2bd283089261c4d445d.text: You see no difference when a sponsored ad appears in web chat or the computer app. Your device now quietly notifies the advertiser's own counting service that the ad showed, because the same notice sent from company computers gets thrown out as fake and the advertiser would never count it. If you use the text-only terminal version this does not affect you, and the team also records what the advertiser sent so they can tell 'they sent nothing' from 'we dropped it'.

ed27ce1cf3e461105e209dcd13d8e5e22219331f.text: You won't notice anything yet. If you advertise with us and send word back when someone buys or signs up, we put in place a new behind-the-scenes count of those reports. It records only whether the report worked, why it failed, what kind it was, and the charge and time it took, and it keeps your passwords and private tracking details out of that count.

161b864dd4f665957ded8250837935b5f8612cfc.text: You won't notice anything different yet — this is behind-the-scenes groundwork. The team gathered all the rules for sponsored work offers into one shared place, including safety checks that block a bad advertiser link or logo before you ever see it, so the website and the text-based version show exactly the same thing. If you are offered sponsored work, its progress will use the same familiar words as your normal tasks, and when it finishes you will see clearly that its work is saved and waiting for you to decide whether to share it.

10c51ede09cee9de5090c0aa49d4d200a6e9a065.text: If you use the desktop app on a Mac or Linux computer, you will see nothing different yet. The groundwork is now in place for two background rules: one keeps checking for a paid offer for the conversation you have open even after you go quiet, but stops if you hide the window or switch away, and another can note why paid work with Supabase is not ready when your project has nothing saved yet.

7b65652ad9decd202054622a7fbe267cc7c11201.text: You won't notice anything different, as this is internal record-keeping only. Behind the scenes, every ad request now notes which broad location group you were in, even when location rules are switched off, so a future rollout can be sized from earlier traffic. It also notes what happened when the system tried to file away its ad choice for later review — saved, too busy, pausing, failed, turned off, or skipped — and the chance that actually applied, which reads as certain when at least two ads qualified and zero when nothing was filed.

1f35b8067456bba14e902e3018e6c41545b2a64e.text: You won't see anything different yet — this plumbing is in place but does nothing you can notice. Behind the scenes it prepares a short, safety-limited note when the chat tries to fetch an ad, keeping only simple facts like whether an ad showed, why, which chat spot it was for, how many appeared, and how long it took up to a minute. It leaves out page addresses, ad and request details, and full error messages so those private details never get stored there.

57740be2e72a0a17ea154ebf41bec32f7a7816d1.text: If you run ads, you now get less detail when your ad is held back by a rule about wording or meaning. You only see a general note that it was filtered for context, because the details checked in that request and whether they matched stay private. Behind the scenes the system also saves extra notes when it fetches ads to track a test, which changes nothing you see.

9f3905939a7734c5d57e5693ceac0a1e6bbd136a.text: You will no longer get live predictions from public bets on future events inside the assistant. It used to pull up to five yes-or-no questions with their current chances and links, and that lookup is now gone.

0c39f78ab53aa4ff4957ec4ea87c1e91e7373053.text: If you are the one account blocked after challenging a payment, you now see an 'Overloaded' message when you try to chat. The service shows that message on purpose to hide the block. It is a small internal block that is live now and touches no other accounts.

23c15cfd4656c6eb305dfe9e4bbab938ebadbed8.text: You won't see anything different. If you run ads and open your performance reports, the system has a new private internal note ready to capture which account checked, which report was opened, how many days you asked for, how many rows came back, how long it took, and whether it worked. It is small behind-the-scenes record-keeping and does nothing you can see.

9960f1f7021572ab6422137dd38830ec6587af47.text: You won't see anything different yet. If you have an app built for you, its finished building plan now has a place to name each outside service that needs a secret key to work, like Resend for sending email, and that place stays empty if no secret is needed. The place is set up but nothing uses it yet, so this is small behind-the-scenes work.

f5e983617b6b009dbe5b9977c689f63dbcc69167.text: If you are the one blocked account that kept disputing charges, your chat requests now fail with a message saying the service is overloaded. The system rejects you on purpose but shows the busy message to hide the block. It is live now and affects only you, no one else.

f1744c6fb4c1c5e1c281acd92756d59a40c9453e.text: If you ask about a future event like who will win the next presidential election, you now get an answer grounded in live crowd odds. The assistant looks up matching yes-or-no questions on a public prediction site, usually up to five at a time. You see each question with its current chance and a link you can open to check it.

00ffb9f582ba344870e4fa0cdb418270c9394153.text: You won't notice anything different. If you use Claude answers, they now keep working even when the reply leaves the underlying running cost blank. It's a small internal fix and it's live now, so those replies no longer get thrown out for missing that number.

69fffe8f6b530e155e645d0bfd9c931f24294498.text: You won't see anything different on your screen — it's a small behind-the-scenes tweak. When you keep chatting, the assistant no longer gets a hidden note telling it its earlier answers came from a less intelligent helper that it should double-check and quietly fix.

c8694a01c6c6efb7a4bd3faee3ebbe50ac627a45.text: If you open a friend's invite link while you're logged out, you still keep the invite after you sign in. The site remembers it in your browser while you log in and applies it automatically once you're in, whether you sign in from the home page or the login page.

0848e5169e83b1cc9d6b335d7f518e42a54d4fa6.text: If you ask the assistant to save your work, you will now need to give separate permission before it shares that work with others. Its behind-the-scenes instructions were tightened to keep saving and sharing as two separate approvals, so a save request no longer counts as approval to upload. It's a small internal safety tweak and it's live now.

bb37a001c0175bbf146f0523b2ad0c724a7a2c3e.text: You won't see anything new — it's a small behind-the-scenes tweak that's live now. When you ask the assistant to edit something, it should leave your existing words and notes alone and send only the changed bit. It does that by including a few nearby lines for location and using a stricter shape for its edit requests so fewer edits fail or wipe things out.

b25cd0e15f031f492bb4523ec6895aafacc6ffef.text: If you tell the assistant it did something wrong, it will try to remember your correction for next time. Its built-in instructions now tell it to write down a short rule for itself once it understands what you meant. It's a small behind-the-scenes tweak.

381def1ba350b81d8f1e5ab5af18c69b3e66dfb6.title: Supabase setup invitation adds v3 capability and v2 card
381def1ba350b81d8f1e5ab5af18c69b3e66dfb6.summary: `common/src/ads/supabase-setup-invitation.ts` renames existing schemas to `supabaseSetupInvitationCapabilityV2Schema` and `supabaseSetupInvitationV1Schema` and adds `supabaseSetupInvitationCapabilityV3Schema`, `supabaseSetupInvitationV2Schema`, and `supabaseInvitationInspectionReasonSchema`, with unions accepting v2/v3 capabilities and v1/v2 invitations. This keeps outstanding v2 capabilities and v1 cards valid while new Desktop clients send v3 capabilities and render v2 discovery cards. Scope is Shared/Core via `common/src/ads/supabase-setup-invitation.ts`. V3 is a broad discovery capability with `workspaceId`, `desktop_macos`/`desktop_linux` unchecked execution, `compatibility_check_required`, and `missing`/`present`/`unknown` provider evidence, while V2 cards carry `invitationId`, `angle`, `surface`, and `expiresAt`.

381def1ba350b81d8f1e5ab5af18c69b3e66dfb6.text: If you use the desktop app on a Mac or Linux computer, you may see a suggestion to set up database help, login help, or file storage help. When your app asks for that suggestion it now only says you have a work area on that computer, whether each piece looks missing or present, and that a compatibility check is still needed, without sending file locations or error details. The new suggestion names which help it is for and when it runs out, tapping it starts nothing paid, and older suggestions still work, so the groundwork is in place but you may not see it yet.

da165be855e3ab42d7ee67881a23710c0617542c.title: Subscription cost snapshot preserves last known report
da165be855e3ab42d7ee67881a23710c0617542c.summary: Added `SubscriptionCostSnapshot` in `common/src/types/subscription-costs.ts` to return the last known `SubscriptionCostReport` independently from the subscriber-list scan. It exists so an interrupted collector never erases useful data, keeping `costs` alongside `savedAt` and `nextRefreshAt`. Scoped to Shared/Core in that one type file, it tracks `snapshotStatus` as `fresh`|`stale`|`empty` and `refreshStatus` as `idle`|`running`|`cooldown`|`failed`|`unavailable` with nullable costs and timestamps.

da165be855e3ab42d7ee67881a23710c0617542c.text: You won't see anything different yet. It is small internal groundwork that is in place and does nothing yet, but it will allow the last saved subscription cost summary to stay on screen even if a new count is interrupted, along with whether that saved copy is fresh or old and whether an update is running or waiting.

cad79f08e6293749c664db735a10c1cce98c40e1.title: Testing docs add credential free Cloud Agent smoke test
cad79f08e6293749c664db735a10c1cce98c40e1.summary: docs/testing.md adds instructions for running a credential-free smoke test in checkouts or Cloud Agents that lack Infisical access. The workflow bypasses the repo .bin/bun wrapper, which exits with code 1 when .env.local is missing, by invoking the pinned Bun 1.3.14 binary directly before .envrc modifies PATH. Targeted at @codebuff/internal, the run executes src/ad-targeting/__tests__/iso-3166-alpha2.test.ts without requiring bun install, leveraging bunfig.toml to preload sdk/test/setup-env.ts for three passing tests.

cad79f08e6293749c664db735a10c1cce98c40e1.text: If you use an automated cloud assistant or work in an environment without access to the team's private security vault, you can now run a small internal test to confirm the workspace functions without needing those credentials. The internal testing guide is live today with instructions for launching a single isolated test that bypasses the normal security checks and avoids downloading extra software packages. If you look at the documentation, you will see a new walkthrough showing how to start this test directly and confirm it passes.

4ba40c22c6481732936643698562bfcc1b874d51.title: CLI streak bonus lines display Freebucks daily rewards
4ba40c22c6481732936643698562bfcc1b874d51.summary: The CLI landing screen now displays daily Freebucks streak rewards (`+<N> Freebucks every day`) via a new optional `freebucksDailyBonus` field in `FreebuffStreakResponse`. This makes the streak line server-decided for accounts on the Freebucks meter so advertised perks match what the ledger credits rather than promising session units or GLM bonuses the gate will not honor. Spanning `cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx`, `cli/src/utils/freebuff-streak-line.ts`, and `common/src/util/freebuff-streak-line.ts`, unmetered accounts and older servers returning null or undefined fall back to standard bonus session copy.

4ba40c22c6481732936643698562bfcc1b874d51.text: If your account earns Freebucks, the terminal's welcome screen now shows the exact amount of Freebucks you receive each day for keeping up your streak. Instead of advertising bonus sessions that your account cannot use, the screen displays the daily credits you actually unlock once you hit a seven-day streak. The app now checks this reward directly with the server so the displayed perk always matches what is deposited into your wallet.

0a94252116dc9319f6db81f5abb25f50a5a8f6c7.title: Recent limited country block reason adds account notice
0a94252116dc9319f6db81f5abb25f50a5a8f6c7.summary: The `FreebuffCountryBlockReason` union in common gains a `recent_limited_country` variant, and the restricted-capacity notice plus the model availability notice now explain that state. It is set by the access floor in `access-cache.ts` when the request's own network passes but the account was seen from a not-allowed country within the access-floor window — never by an IP lookup — so the account keeps that country's limits. Touches `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, `common/src/util/freebuff-model-availability.ts`, and `common/src/constants/freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts`; the other reasons (anonymized or unknown country, missing client IP) fall through unchanged. Updated copy tells users who have moved to verify their country at freebuff.com/account?tab=country.

0a94252116dc9319f6db81f5abb25f50a5a8f6c7.text: Some people keep reduced limits on their account even when the connection they're using today looks fine, because their account was recently seen coming from a country where some models aren't available, so those limits stay for a while. If that's you, the messages you see about which models you can use and the one about reduced capacity now explain that and point you to verify your country on your account page if you've moved. The country limits themselves were already applied elsewhere; what's new is the wording that tells you why.

d6c8cb0a140c8b3ece3730206176a37a74172b20.title: BMP and TIFF images transcoded to PNG or refused for vision providers
d6c8cb0a140c8b3ece3730206176a37a74172b20.summary: BMP and TIFF images are no longer sent to vision providers as-is: the CLI transcodes them to PNG via Jimp in `cli/src/utils/image-handler.ts`, while the SDK read-files tool refuses them in `sdk/src/tools/read-files.ts` with a conversion hint. Both formats are recognized as images but no provider decodes them, and sending one causes a 400 unsupported-image error for that turn and every later turn because history is replayed. The new `PROVIDER_IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES` set and `isProviderSupportedImageMediaType` helper in `common/src/constants/images.ts` restrict inline provider media types to PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP; if Jimp cannot read the BMP/TIFF, the CLI returns 'Unsupported image format... Convert it to PNG or JPEG and try again', and the SDK error suggests converting with `magick` to a temp PNG.

d6c8cb0a140c8b3ece3730206176a37a74172b20.text: If you use the command-line assistant, attaching a bitmap or TIFF image now quietly converts it to a PNG first, so the model can see it instead of the whole reply failing. If you use the separate file-reading tool, those same image types are refused with a suggestion to convert them yourself, for example by running an image converter in the terminal. That is because the image services only accept a few common picture formats, and sending one they reject would break not just that reply but every later reply in the same chat. It is live now.

2a92180a36c023f405081b2ff39b4be06887ea0c.title: Freebuff CLI release manifest bumped to 0.0.176
2a92180a36c023f405081b2ff39b4be06887ea0c.summary: The `version` field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` moves from `0.0.175` to `0.0.176`, with no accompanying dependency, source, or lockfile changes in this commit. The edit touches only the release manifest's top-level version key, so the diff carries a release pointer rather than a behavior change. Scope is limited to that single file under the CLI release directory; the `name`, `description`, and `bin` entries are unchanged, so the published `freebuff` binary mapping stays as-is.

2a92180a36c023f405081b2ff39b4be06887ea0c.text: The label for the next release of the freebuff assistant's downloadable tool moved forward one step. Nothing about how freebuff works, what it can do, how it is installed, or what you see when you use it changed. If you use freebuff, you would notice nothing different today; this is small release bookkeeping that adds no feature or fix by itself.

bd9237b1808e650373ecd6303080a5f3c29e1071.text: As of September 3, full-access users no longer see Gemini 3.8 Flash in the model picker: it was withdrawn hours after launching that same day because it was slow and still failed about a quarter of the time even after a fix. Because it was also the most expensive option per message, it came off the picker rather than stay in front of everyone while it's evaluated. The app still recognizes the model for people who already have it installed, but no new sessions can start with it.

92c4f5ef87df3e074a688d0c635c551b51d46b37.text: The free model picker's Muse Spark entry now offers the model's previous edition instead of its newest one, across the web app, desktop app, and command-line tool: Meta stopped serving the newest edition — every request for it failed — while the older edition answered every test. If you had saved the newer edition as your model, you're automatically switched to the older one the next time you open the app, and conversations already in progress keep running as they were. The listing itself reads the same as before: Meta's coding model with a very large memory, shared by every free user, which may quietly answer with a different, faster model when the shared pool is busy rather than making you wait. The swap is already live.

d9ecc85e1636aa3b8fc950f42de71c3ec8da7250.text: Since September 4, 2026, people using the free version of the coding assistant in the command-line tool or the desktop app can pick Muse Spark 1.3 — Meta's coding model with a very large memory — from the model list, where before it only worked on the web. Because every free user shares the same pool of requests for this model, it can get crowded: when that happens your request queues and a backup model answers instead of making you wait. An automatic code reviewer for this model was also set up as a safety net, but nothing calls on it yet.

0cbff57aed44d5a012b9dbb93912884ba1be0ccc.text: In the free model picker, DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31 now appears as DeepSeek V4.1 Flash — same slot, same fast-coding description, still unlimited at full access. The old date in the name was only there because the model updates itself silently and the date warned returning users it had changed; the vendor now puts the version in the name, so the picker shows that instead. If you're on limited access — outside supported regions or on a VPN — every row that costs you extra, not just the one you've already picked, now shows a short note that a $5 plan cuts the price and multiplies your usage sevenfold, and the service now decides who sees that note and what it says rather than the app working it out on its own. All of this is live today, and the catalog also now marks the model as

9501bb0a55ec3bbbd225e477130c427534dc3f11.text: If you use the free model picker, there's a new option: Solar Pro 4, available for a limited time as a trial. It works with text only — it can't take images the way some other picks can — but it can handle much longer conversations at once. It's live today, and anything you send to it isn't kept on file by the company providing it. It costs more to run than the current default, so the trial may not stick around.

4ac1fd1d59197d7f28602ac38da5d4c46e0277a3.text: If you use the free model picker, you can now choose Gemini 3.8 Flash — it went live on September 3 on the website, the desktop app, and the command-line tool at the same time. It can take in very long documents and is the only model on the list that can listen to audio, though it also reads images, video, and PDFs, and it costs the most per message of any model listed. Behind the scenes it got its own reviewer running on the same model, because without one, sessions using it would get cut off partway through. It's also routed through a cheaper, faster path than the default one.

26f374dc2bc2abd17e24eabe0c254e426e49d350.text: Muse Spark 1.3 has replaced Muse Spark 1.2 in the free model picker on the web app, desktop app, and command-line tool, as of September 13; the newer model had briefly stopped working and was pulled earlier in the month, and it is back now that it is fixed. If you had picked the older model, the app switches your saved choice to the newer one automatically the next time you open it. Chats already in progress and copies of the app already installed keep using the older model. The price and limits are the same — it is shared by everyone, so at busy times it may queue and answer with a different model — and the newer one is described as better at coding tasks.

654a906e6758ffe17974dae829d35423dcd827b3.text: An older edition of Meta's Muse Spark coding model is back on the free plan's list of models, replacing the newer one that had taken its spot. If you had picked the older model, you're back on it, and the automatic switch that steered people from the older one to the newer one no longer happens. Nothing else about it changed: it still shares one usage limit with everyone, so at busy times it can queue and answer with a different model instead of making you wait, which is why it deliberately sits last on the list. The swap is live now across the app, its docs, and the command-line tool.

8d7a935e56beac4db2faa5f2421e2af0f1c6a905.text: Ox Alpha, the experimental model that was free to use and cost no sessions, disappeared from the free model picker on August 27 because the company providing it stopped offering it for free — it is no longer available at any price. If you were using it, you'll need to pick something else; MiMo 2.5 is now the only free model that costs no session at all. Sessions already underway when the change landed were allowed to run their full hour instead of being cut off partway with an error.

68b487b1f0fc0e9fd42f83503efa2533890ff411.text: The free model picker's deepest-reasoning option is now GLM 5.3 Flash, replacing DeepSeek V4 Pro, which has been retired. If you pick it, you can use it for only 2 sessions a day, where the old model had no separate limit — a temporary cap while the team measures what the model costs at scale. The change is live now in the assistant's desktop, web, and terminal apps, and the new model is routed through a middleman service that only uses cheaper providers so it can stay free to offer.

477475a9e9f4723ccff8403fd2b739bf68b87c42.text: If you have full access, you will now see an updated model labeled DeepSeek V4 Pro 08/13 in your model picker, replacing the older preview version. This release provides deeper reasoning for complex tasks and lets you adjust its thinking effort across three levels—low, high, or maximum—instead of being restricted to only the top two. It also expands the model's memory to handle significantly longer conversations, while continuing to draw from your daily premium allowance.

28663a3cb73ad6b81408aa9cf131a8edf1f1f5ba.text: If you use the command-line assistant, typing /export now saves your entire conversation to a file — a readable document by default, or a raw data file if you prefer — with no size cap, and it refuses to overwrite a file that already exists; until now that command only copied to the clipboard, which cut off long chats. Separately, if you step away from a chat for up to an hour, the assistant now keeps your full history: before, after half an hour of inactivity it would shrink the conversation down to a summary and drop details, which felt like it forgot everything over a coffee break. A related fix also stops an empty reply from wiping the conversation entirely. Both changes are live now.

9d2ffeb174143be273cd3257275edcf79094c33f.text: If you use the free version of this coding assistant, its model picker now offers five more AI models at no charge — new ones from DeepSeek, GPT, MiniMax and MiMo — and two of them can also take images as input. The terminal and desktop apps now start with a fast DeepSeek model by default, while the web, cloud and chat versions start with the new GPT model. The product's English and Chinese introduction pages were rewritten to match: they now describe everything under the Freebuff name as five free products supported by text ads, with no subscription, credits, or personal access keys needed. The new lineup and defaults are live today.

175ea48e5f9acebbb528cd76425d4f268f0d947c.text: Freebuff command-line users can now connect their own artificial intelligence accounts directly instead of routing requests through Freebuff. Activating your own provider skips the usual sign-in step and removes all advertisements from your chat screen. Switching between providers automatically clears your current conversation to prevent formatting conflicts between different services, while keeping your private keys out of your saved command history.

f8ed82aaaa4ed3c5776a04b6c7423b894b294f74.text: You can now select a new model called Ox Alpha from the free menu in both the desktop and command-line apps. It is open to all free users, including those connecting from limited-access regions or through a VPN, and can handle exceptionally long conversations without using up your daily session allowance. Because this model is experimental and can be unpredictable, the system also pairs it with its own dedicated reviewer behind the scenes to keep tasks from crashing midway through.

73b3e16cdc03da2402d2a3eed7e3bbec76b073f1.text: If you use the free mode, you can now type /reasoning (or the shortcuts /effort or /think) to control how hard the AI thinks before answering: type it alone to see the current level, or add a level like low, high, or max, and it takes effect on your very next message with no restart needed. Typing 'default', 'auto', or 'reset' hands the choice back to the model's usual setting, and the model picker now shows each model's thinking level, marking the ones you chose yourself with a star. The level you pick is a request attached to each message you send, and the server has the final say if it ends up running a different model than the one you selected. This command only exists in the free mode; the regular tool doesn't offer it.

c8ad1e274f4ab909d17fd050698c542d99ec3b63.text: When choosing a model on the free tier, you will now see DeepSeek Pro instead of an older, dated preview version. Aligning the menu with recent server updates prevents your requests from falling back to a paused model and failing when traffic is heavy. Depending on whether your account has full or limited access, the screen also displays tailored notes explaining model availability and daily session limits.

cbdf5030d0238565dfe2852e8eacc93bfc803b82.text: Free users can no longer choose MiniMax M3, which has been removed from the free model menu due to high operating costs. As of August 20, 2026, you cannot start new conversations with this model, and the app will let you know it is unavailable. If you were already in the middle of an active chat using it, that conversation will finish normally rather than abruptly freezing or cutting you off.

3dc7ec2306d94243ab2ba83ab457b59bcd4713c1.text: If you type messages while the assistant is still answering an earlier one, you can now manage that waiting line directly: typing /queue (or pressing Ctrl+Q) swaps the typing box for a full-screen list where you can rewrite, reorder, or delete any message still waiting its turn. The panel closes itself once the line empties, and if a message leaves the line to start running while you're editing it, the panel tells you instead of silently pretending your change went through. There's deliberately no /q shortcut for it, because that already quits the whole program.

98e174e577d764b45973ff8a4091cb3b3d6196d8.text: If you use the Freebuff command-line tool, typing /dashboard — or /usage, /stats, or /streak — now opens a web page showing your usage, daily streak, and account activity. Freebuff had removed its old usage display, so this gives you a way to answer "how much have I used?" again. On machines where no browser can open automatically, the web address is printed instead so you can still get there. Codebuff users are unaffected and keep their existing credits-based usage display.

0a94252116dc9319f6db81f5abb25f50a5a8f6c7.text: If your account was recently used from a country where some models aren't available, you'll now see a message explaining that those limits stay with the account for a while, even when your current connection is fine. The check is based on where the account was used recently, not the network it's connecting from right now, so the old country's limits don't lift just by switching networks. Both the reduced-capacity warning and the model-availability message now say this and point anyone who has moved to confirm their country on their account page. This is in effect now.

d6c8cb0a140c8b3ece3730206176a37a74172b20.text: If you gave the assistant a picture in BMP or TIFF format, it used to fail with an 'unsupported image' error — and because the picture stayed in the conversation history, that error kept blocking every later message in the same chat. Now the assistant automatically converts BMP and TIFF pictures to PNG before sending them, so they simply work. If a particular picture can't be converted, you get a clear message telling you to convert it to PNG or JPEG yourself, instead of a conversation that's stuck.

ce02985fc2dae21a5d6635d933952781273e3b33.text: Typing /copy (also /copy-chat or /export) in the chat now puts the whole conversation — your messages, the assistant's replies and reasoning, and the results of any commands it ran — onto your clipboard as formatted text, ready to paste anywhere. It works today for anyone using the command-line chat. One catch: if you're working on a remote machine, the clipboard can only carry about 22 KB of text, so very long chats get trimmed — the largest command outputs are replaced with short notes saying they were left out — while a local session always copies everything.

381def1ba350b81d8f1e5ab5af18c69b3e66dfb6.text: Desktop users on Mac or Linux can now be shown the sponsored Supabase setup offer even when the app has done far less checking of their project — it only reports that a project is open, without proving it examined the project's files, code history, or security sandbox. The offer card itself now says which part of Supabase it's pitching (database, sign-in, or file storage), which platform it runs on, and when it expires. Offers already sent in the older format keep working, so nothing outstanding breaks. This is live now, but actually starting the setup still waits on a separate compatibility check.

cc2e698cf6c70dfad256e440be039d256a163222.text: The command that linked a ChatGPT account to the assistant is gone, so you can no longer connect one. If you had linked an account, the planning and review commands no longer send their deep-thinking step to GPT through your ChatGPT subscription — they now run entirely on the model you have selected. Free-plan users also stop being offered a 'think harder' helper that previously could fail for them with an access error. This is live now.

502a0060842d7b99b090d8a19756e14230c60699.text: When the assistant runs a sponsored task that includes an advertiser's command, it can now be handed a short tracking code pulled from the advertiser's link, so the advertiser can tell that any resulting sale came from that run. The code only gets handed over if the link is secure and the tracking code inside passes a basic format and length check; if it's missing or fails, the assistant skips that command and explains tracking wasn't available, instead of running it untracked. The assistant is also told to pass the code only to that one command and never save it to a file, commit, or share it elsewhere. This is live now, but it only changes anything for sponsored tasks that specifically ask for the tracking code — everything else runs exactly as before.

dc18d1a2063a92cc1939648a0280c0847a662c73.text: You can now type a new command in the assistant's chat that prints a health report — how long the app has been open, how much memory and computing power it's using, and the ID numbers of any terminal tasks it's currently running — with the actual command text and account settings deliberately left out so the report is safe to paste into a bug report. On Windows, when the app closes a command window it opened, it now force-shuts down every background task that window started, not just the window itself, so tasks no longer get stranded running after you quit. The small animation at the top of the chat also now plays only while your cursor is in the input box, and that on-or-off state carries over between chats instead of resetting.

4ba40c22c6481732936643698562bfcc1b874d51.text: If your account earns daily Freebucks, the command-line welcome screen now displays the exact Freebucks credit you receive each day for keeping a seven-day or longer streak. The screen checks your account directly with the server to show these wallet rewards, ensuring it matches what you are actually credited instead of promising extra sessions your account cannot use. Accounts that do not use the Freebucks meter will continue to see their standard daily bonus sessions instead.

50a33327c3305300e5094147244c7bd990cc229b.text: When the app decides whether to offer you an invitation to set up Supabase, it now demands stronger proof before sending one: it must recognize the third-party provider packages already present in your project, and the older, incomplete evidence it used to accept no longer qualifies. If your project only shows those older signs, you may stop getting new setup invitations that you would have received before. The stricter check is live now and applies only to these setup invitations; nothing else about your project or setup changes.

57740be2e72a0a17ea154ebf41bec32f7a7816d1.text: Advertisers whose ads can be held back by a rule about what you is reading will now see only a generic 'context filtered' explanation when an ad is turned down for three new reasons: the rule itself was invalid, the system couldn't check you's context, or the context didn't match. you's actual reading context and whether it matched stay private — the advertiser never sees them, just the generic label. Behind the scenes, ad-serving records gained eleven extra fields for an internal 'profile lift' test — which test group an ad landed in, how likely that assignment was, and the test's follow-up and wrap-up dates — so analysts can measure the results later. Those extra fields only record data; nothing about which ads appear changes because of them.

a4396df88073029ec1427d8bbbdff0791b21781d.text: Subscribers in Singapore and Israel who bought full-access plans keep the full allowances they paid for, even though both countries dropped to limited access on September 15, 2026. The keep-your-plan rule now covers exactly those two countries and no others, so the roughly 550 subscribers in countries that were always limited don't get a free upgrade — they keep the limited plans they bought. If you subscribed in Singapore or Israel before the switch, your allowance stays as it was; if you're in a country that never had full access, nothing changes for you.

a659222a118d5923e8a49c83f036c3faeab55fd8.text: When you sign up, the 'how did you hear about us' question now shows its choices in a random order each time the form loads, with 'Somewhere else' always last, because the first-listed choice was winning picks on position alone. The survey also dropped five choices: Reddit and GitHub from that question, 'Designer or PM' and 'Non-technical' from the role question, and GitHub Copilot from the tools question. Anyone who picked one of those in the past now counts as 'Somewhere else' or 'Something else' in the results, and the running tallies were rebuilt under the new rules so the results bars match the shorter list. These changes are live for new sign-ups today; the recount happens behind the scenes.

8ee68ac2626b70c448b989f087e0528f259ef1fd.text: Desktop app users may now see sponsored backend tool recommendations expand to cover file storage alongside existing database and user login suggestions. These backend capabilities are now combined into a single unified campaign and budget instead of being handled through separate promotions. To prevent misplaced offers, older versions of the app that cannot report whether you already have storage or login setups in place are treated as unknown rather than assuming you need a new provider.

6edaba95110f54cfee58529bbb0cfe1e19d95f5d.text: If you plug in your own OpenAI key and pick the luna model, requests that used to get rejected now go through: the app renames one setting to the form OpenAI accepts, drops another it refuses while handling those stopping instructions itself, and switches off the model's extended thinking whenever tools are in play. If you use OpenRouter with your own key for OpenAI models, each request now carries a unique tag computed from your key — it marks the traffic as yours without ever sending the key itself, so you no longer share the block that hits unidentified traffic. Only people bringing their own keys are affected; nothing changes on the built-in plan. The fix is live now.

6840865ee112e14b4b38f78a9de774bc20187aad.text: If you finish the new-user questionnaire after signing in from the command-line tool or the desktop app, you do it on a browser landing page, and this change sets up the ability to tell those submissions apart from ones filled out in the dashboard's pop-up form — two paths that look identical on that page today. It defines exactly two labels and a rule that anything missing or made-up counts as the dashboard version, so a tampered submission can't show up as a fake category. Nothing records the label yet, so you wouldn't notice anything today; it's groundwork for grouping sign-ups by where they came from.

10c51ede09cee9de5090c0aa49d4d200a6e9a065.text: Desktop app users on macOS and Linux can now receive relevant offers while keeping an active conversation open, even if you have temporarily stopped typing. The app pauses these background checks the moment you hide the window or switch threads. Behind the scenes, rules are also now in place to check whether your workspace is properly set up to connect a database provider, though this foundation currently only notes what is missing rather than launching any setup steps.

59628850f6c070bfd42383e35717d22844834d2c.text: People using the free tier in Singapore and Israel lost full access on September 15 and dropped to the limited tier, because ads rarely actually get shown to users there — each account in those countries earns about a tenth of what a United States account does. The service now keeps one shared list of which countries get the full free tier, ranked by how much advertisers pay per user: the United States alone in the top group, then Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and much of Northern Europe, then much of Western Europe — South Korea stays in the full-access group by decision even though its ads perform as poorly as Singapore's. You'd notice the public help page now spells out exactly which countries get full access, and it and the usage meter read from that same list so they can't

912a3f96607449b4b2915e6addd9b91db2333974.text: You won't notice anything: the app can now write down what each copy of it claims about itself — which operating system it's running on, whether it's the desktop app or the command-line tool, and which set of sponsored-content rules it says it supports. These records only report the app's own claims; they never decide whether a sponsored message actually gets shown, and nothing reads them yet. Sponsored messages work exactly as before, so this is invisible groundwork for the people running the ads system.

30c6fe6b64f898b58aa0fe79858a70d373ecad13.text: If you use the command-line tool, the model picker now shows a 'First-tab discount' label and lower prices whenever the tab you're in is the first one active on your account — the listed prices already include the savings. The discount is held by one tab at a time: if you switch to a different tab, the old one gives up the discount before your next purchase, and it also ends when it expires. Before each purchase the tool checks with the service that the discount still applies, so the price you confirm is the price you pay.

2964be866c3e4b3da1f3d9208ed1e8ee6d476a12.text: If you use the CLI and see sponsored offers in your terminal, the offers you're shown can now be matched to your actual project: whenever you're working inside a project folder, the tool quietly inspects what you're building — its framework, package tools, and database — and includes that description when it asks which offer to show. The ad system also now learns the moment an offer actually appears on your screen, not just when it's saved in your chat history, so it can tell an offer you saw from one you never noticed. Each project also gets a random ID that reveals nothing about your machine or folder names, so offers can be aimed at your workspace consistently without leaking where your files live. All of this is active now.

4b2b9ba193f215d52fdda833622d4929ab3b2be8.text: When the AI agent reads large files, those fresh results no longer get cut off before it can use them. The system that shrinks old conversation history to save space used to be able to trim the very results the agent had just gathered but not yet looked at, which could make it lose the thread of the task it was working on. Now that process always protects the newest exchange — the results the agent hasn't read yet — and counts the fixed setup text, like instructions, tool descriptions, and images, toward the space limit, so only genuinely old history gets summarized. This matters most when you connect your own AI account, where the space limit is tighter.

8ae0c9c1da31404dd515238cb4e196c13c2872fc.text: If you're running an assistant session on a GLM model and it gets stuck writing out the exact same to-do list over and over without doing any real work, the session now catches it instead of letting it quietly burn through all its attempts. After three identical repeats, the assistant gets a warning to stop repeating the list and either take a real action or explain what's blocking it. If it still repeats the same list a sixth time, the assistant's turn is stopped and you're told the model got stuck, with a suggestion to try a different model or reasoning level. Only identical, completed lists count as looping, so a changed list, a different action, or a message from you resets the count, and the model admitting it's stuck in its own words doesn't count as progress.

02e98eb553ef6474710195bcf76d8659282ce708.text: If you restart a session in the command-line tool and start fresh, the new conversation now saves to its own separate place instead of overwriting the record of the conversation you just had. Each fresh session gets its own saved history, the same way starting a brand-new chat already did. It's a small fix, live now, that matters mainly if you go back and reread old conversations.

385a99b3d9437720f257e7edf99fc5570dfe8fa1.text: If you're among the people who can be shown the Supabase promotional offer, a separate pilot is being set up for its database-focused version where everyone gets the same new assistant-style format, instead of the ongoing test's random split between two formats. The update adds a second label for those pilot offers and a rule that still honors offers already reserved under the older label, so turning the pilot on or off won't void existing reservations or force anyone to re-sort the ongoing test's results. Pilot results are kept out of the randomized test's report entirely. The label and rule are in place now; nothing changes for anyone until the pilot actually starts serving offers.

1217a53754489ef6be6257b36a25fcd8d4edb110.text: If you resume a conversation after your own key for an outside AI service was removed or changed, the app now tells you to pick another provider or a built-in model to continue, instead of telling you to start a brand-new task. Apps built on these tools can also carry an existing conversation over to a different provider, but only when you picked that provider yourself — a provider failing on its own never moves your chat. The new wording is live now; the transfer itself only happens in apps that explicitly allow it, and once a conversation moves it stays locked to the new provider.

b0ec8028c8fa97b1e285eb8739988689b8520e7d.text: When you type "/" in the command-line tool, the list of matching commands that appears works exactly as before — this is behind-the-scenes tidying, not a new feature. The code that decides which commands match what you typed had two nearly identical copies, one for command names that start with your text and one for names that merely contain it; those copies were merged into a single shared routine, and the matching logic was opened up so automated tests can exercise it directly. Anyone using the command-line suggestions notices no difference; the change just makes the matching easier to maintain and test.

990e923559d61a9fd04f94fc5f330ae24f0c8f97.text: If you're on the free daily Freebucks allowance, your refill now happens at midnight in your own timezone instead of always at midnight Pacific time. The app tells the service which timezone you're in with every request, so moving or traveling updates your schedule without a restart; the first switch away from Pacific time may bring your refill earlier, while later moves keep your current schedule and can delay the next refill. You'd notice the small print under the model picker now describes 'your reset timezone' rather than Pacific time, and once your refill time passes, the display shows 'Updating balance…' instead of a countdown until the service confirms the new balance. This is live now.

44616e1e8cbc975b693b136b98b301ccc157d7d1.text: The Solar Pro 4 limited-time trial now costs 10 instead of 5, as of 3:46 AM UTC on September 14, 2026. Anyone buying that trial pays double what it cost the day before, while the 'Limited-time trial' label stays exactly the same. The new price was scheduled in advance: the app checks the current time against a list of planned price changes and shows whichever one applies, so the increase switched on by itself at the appointed minute with no new release needed.

4897491493104492eafbdca91dfd2ccda3c00020.text: When you start a practice coding session with this tool, you can now hand it a few extra settings—like an API key or a folder path—without those secrets getting written down where the assistant can see them or saved in the session history. The tool copies those settings into their own locked-down file in a temporary folder, then quietly reads them in at startup so the secret stays hidden from the project directory and the command log. If you look, you’d notice the session folder has an extra subfolder that appears and disappears with each session, holding only your sensitive settings with strict permissions, and the session cleanup routine now removes that folder along with the main workspace. This is live today whenever someone starts a session using the new options in the project’s

a8d0c1a83f4dc3677069dec06aca8a2aa3bdfb20.text: If you ask for Solar Pro 4 through the service, it now counts against your regular usage instead of running free. Your account pays the standard rate for that model starting at 5 a.m. UTC on September 13, 2026, and the system begins billing each time it deploys the change. The model's pricing on the OpenRouter option reflects Upstage's ongoing 90% discount, so the displayed cost is already low, but you are no longer getting it for zero tokens.

51e6c7bcf02623bda9cd8faa187aad7ffeaad37e.text: The cost numbers that get shown for paying subscribers are now defined in one shared place, so every report uses the same labels for what counts as subscription-paid, what is Freebuff-paid, what can't be traced to a funding source, and what the next 30 days are expected to cost. Any part of the system that displays or calculates these costs for a single paying subscriber, a subscription tier, or the whole list will now pull from the same set of fields, including a flag that turns red when any cost in the period can't be tied to who paid for it. The structure is ready for use today, but the reporting screens that would show these numbers are still being built.

aa93519f568da1f67f76245d2f2c9e8724ad9ebb.text: You can now set a custom price (in cents) that someone pays to accept a sponsored compute offer, instead of it always being 200 cents. The price is controlled by a new environment variable; if that variable is missing the price stays at 200 cents, and if the value provided is missing, zero, negative, or not a clean whole number, the system stops accepting the offer entirely rather than guessing. Today the feature is live: any deployment that sets the variable gets the custom price, and any deployment that leaves it unset still gets the original 200-cent fee.

a7ea9ca1fdbf59aea2aedd91b557f4416f19695b.text: Starting around September 2026, the software that records certain ad-related activity (specifically, a type labeled as a Gravity Showcase experiment) will now check incoming data much more carefully before storing it. Instead of keeping any data that arrives—even malformed or incomplete data—it will now reject and discard any data that does not strictly match the expected format, ensuring only valid, well-structured records enter the restricted storage branch. You would not notice this change directly unless you were inspecting the stored records or relied on previously accepted-but-malformed entries, which will now be dropped.

72627b4a8b54f0f2fb08b872d0ad770891b87e24.text: Your billing view for paid subscribers now shows two separate things: a fresh tally of the actual hours covered so far (including any hours from an incomplete UTC day) and a cleaner, complete-days-only span used to project your 30-day forecast. If you look at your subscription cost report today, you may notice an observed-hours number and start/end markers for the full-day range that backs the forecast, sitting alongside the existing collected-days count. This only adjusts how the cost report is structured, so any system reading it will start receiving these new fields when available.

a784cf2d81b03b3074f794fb5acdcfcb18ef35fd.text: You are in a 50/50 split for how you're asked to pay for the Freebuff house subscription: half of eligible users see a monthly price and half see a yearly price. Your assignment is locked to your account, so you keep the same billing option every time you visit, across all sessions and servers. The experiment uses today's date in its identity, so anyone moved into the other half from now on gets a fresh, consistent assignment. No other experiments or offers affect which price you see.

5f024bab305902dc778d74b92756ae6c96cb42f4.text: When an advertiser on the postpaid plan saves their payment card for the first time, they now get a $200 starting credit line instead of $100 before any ads actually run. This higher starting limit only kicks in after the system confirms the card can be charged, so advertisers can't spend money they haven't yet been verified for. Additionally, the rules that increase credit limits later now use a fixed $100 minimum step that no longer changes if the default limit changes. These adjustments are already live today in the billing system.

0e7e3934db90c7866404ed431039233bc6f1a628.text: If you run the command-line tool very early in its startup or during automated tests, it sometimes couldn't find your project's main folder and would crash instead of continuing. It now quietly treats that missing folder as unknown and keeps going, so short scripts and test runs that never set a project location won't break. You'd notice this only if you saw the tool fail at startup before; now it just skips that step.

dedd70d5414f7b9b98050623b74a4fa850669e1b.text: When you ask the assistant to look at files in your project, any image files (like PNGs or JPGs) are now shown to the assistant as actual pictures instead of garbled text. Previously, reading an image produced a mess of replacement characters, so the assistant couldn't describe or understand it. Your coding environment needs to support this new image-reading feature for it to work; if it doesn't, images fall back to the old text-read behavior. Large images that exceed the size limit are skipped, and the assistant tells you it needs to make them smaller using terminal commands.

ebc17a50dc3d760f6d6eb023df4abc508e1dbd9f.text: Subscribers can now be billed once per year instead of only once per month. When you go to upgrade or change your plan, you'll see a new yearly price option appear (for example, $75 for the Starter tier) alongside the existing monthly price, and that yearly checkout will only be offered if the system's payment settings are fully configured for it. The system now also tracks whether your plan renews monthly or yearly, when your current paid period ends, and whether your subscription came through the standard payment processor or a special access grant - information that helps the app show your correct renewal date and plan details.

1fe7bfe3bb89a5f39ce493861f57c861565e81ed.text: When the assistant can't start a new session because the service is at full capacity, the refusal message now includes the exact bucket and limit that blocked it, instead of leaving you to guess. This only affects the client that reports capacity refusals; older servers still send the previous message without these details, and clients are expected to treat the new fields as optional rather than assume a limit. The change is already in place.

bf468de5940335611a1669118edb2540e6618f6e.text: Your hosted desktop session will now stay open for up to 15 minutes of inactivity before the system reclaims it, up from 10 minutes. If you start an action like an end or refund request on a pinned desktop tab, it now stays tied to that specific tab instead of resetting, so retries won't launch duplicate actions. This applies only to desktop session slot management.

6bfe1fe6644c350a1d13259cd4141c316e57e1ac.text: When purchased Desktop sessions are temporarily on hold from the server side, Freebuff can now tell the difference between that pause and the model being broken. Newer Desktop builds will display a message saying purchased sessions are paused and the model itself is fine, while older builds will show a scoped availability label that prevents users from thinking the model is down. Only the Desktop multi-session path handles this flag; Web and CLI clients ignore it but still render updated availability hours.

f48d871ed62bc99da5c8486f58e5847750fcb2fd.text: When you open the chat helper that thinks through answers before showing them, it now runs on a different AI provider that uses a stronger, more careful reasoning mode. The switch happened in the agent that powers Chat deliberation (id still thinker-gemini), which moved from the previous AI to GPT-5.6 Luna with extra-high reasoning, and the system's configuration was widened to accept this and a couple higher effort levels. The result for you is that the assistant child spawned during chat now uses the new model with more deliberate thinking, and the change is recorded as live today, replacing the prior configuration.

2570b57ebdbf98f703cd9515379d76615eb48e4a.text: Free subscriptions are what give you more usage during busy times, like late at night or early in the morning. The assistant can now show a new picture and shorter text that explains why it's worth upgrading to a paid subscription. Both the banner above where you type your message and the full-screen pop-up after completing a task now share the same advertisement, so you see consistent pricing and messaging regardless of where you encounter it. The new artwork features a cozy late-night workspace with a laptop displaying the actual app interface.

4cb83e770ab4290df3813b4526fcd55978f5a323.text: Sponsored runs on Linux now mount an empty tmpfs over the linked worktree's common dir and rebind existing entries read-only, keeping `packed-refs` hidden and `packed-refs.lock` in the tmpfs to allow git commits without rewriting the ref table. The CLI `sponsored-proposal-api.ts` now maps upstream machine codes like `funded_accept_required` to human-readable sentences instead of displaying the raw enum. `sdk/src/run.ts` fixes the `OverrideToolHandlers` type by excluding `read_files` from the mapped half, resolving an unsatisfiable intersection that previously forced callers to cast to `never`. `common/src/ads/supabase-format-experiment.ts` introduces a `SupabaseFormatPair` registry to centralize campaign IDs and procedure hashes, preventing drift across serving paths.

c8894546fb126b852322d188c60fd21efc9a0faa.text: The Freebuff Desktop app now gets a clearer message when an old version can't resume a purchased hour: instead of being told the model is unavailable, you're told your app version needs updating and that doing so won't charge you again. This only affects the Desktop multi-session path, for binaries old enough to lack a purchase-rotation mechanism; newer clients and web users see the existing availability labels unchanged. The server sets the new flag and, for supported clients, surfaces the updated wording, while older binaries continue rendering the generic label (worded so it doesn't blame the model). It's live today for any Desktop binary new enough to read the flag.

af898dcad679dbbd27389aef8a674cee31d58d43.text: If you've been running tasks using the hosted (platform-provided) inference, you can now switch to your own provider keys exactly once during a resumed run, and after that switch the system will keep using your keys. You can no longer revert from your own provider keys back to hosted inference, and the system will not silently change your credentials while resuming a task that already uses your keys. This rule is live today in the SDK: a transition from hosted to your own provider is allowed once, while any mismatch in keys or provider on a resumed run is blocked.

4aa36c7b25c32bdc0605e5abfc8529e306dc4dd7.text: If you use the app on an iPhone, you'll start seeing inline ads appear at three specific spots: right after the assistant's reply in a chat, right after your message in a coding conversation, and right after the assistant's reply in a coding conversation. These iOS ads use their own tracking setup and stay separate from the ads you see on the web. This is live today for iPhone users.

b816aed976efe357204d4878122710062c89ec89.text: When you're trying to start a paid AI session on desktop, the system can now tell you three specific things: the session claim it reserved for you got released (so you should generate a new one), the session is currently in use, or there's no capacity left. If you see any of these messages, the assistant will wait for you to take the next step rather than retrying automatically. The system also exposes which instance IDs belong to your ongoing purchase and whether parts of your desktop purchase have been refunded, so the session picker can show you an accurate picture before letting you proceed.

5f45bd81450eb50ba253ec315e067f798771d98a.text: If you're using the Solar Pro 4 pay-as-you-go model, its price has dropped to 0 Freebucks. Starting September 9, 2026 at 15:49 UTC, anyone who reaches that point in their bill will see that model listed as free. The older prices before that moment are still kept in the system for bookkeeping, so past bills aren't rewritten. Even if you aren't actively refreshing the app, your screen will pick up the new price automatically because the pricing plan travels with the quote the server sends.

e9ebac6cb68071c635ef41d4d6807073a57b513c.text: When you use the platform, the ad-delivery system now passes your real IP address through to its partner so that off-site targeting and measurement treat it as a single, trusted user address rather than the raw chain of forwarding addresses. This only applies to the shared core ad-request utility, and the header is only added when a clean IP is actually available, so nothing changes when one can't be determined.

abd1eed4ab8de4111232935a21962b5a03ff5a33.text: If you use the CLI tool and hit the on-screen landing page that shows available models, pressing any key to dismiss the one-time Freebucks introduction card no longer also starts a paid session using the highlighted model. The introduction card now captures keyboard input on its own so the same keypress can't be read by both the card and the model picker. Also, rows for models you can't currently afford now show a paywall message and plans link when you press Enter on them instead of doing nothing.

cc9069e251e8fedd5784c688ce78ccfecd76815f.text: When you accept a sponsored proposal, the assistant can now see a separate advertiser call-to-action (your campaign landing link) without it being baked into the consent-covered procedure text, so the signed agreement stays untouched. You'll notice an extra line of sanitized text below the proposal showing the advertiser name and verified https link when settlement has minted one, and the run will pass that link to the sponsored agent only if the procedure explicitly asks for it using a placeholder. Nothing changes unless you work with an accepted sponsored proposal that declares that placeholder, and the feature is live today for those cases.

df46a33ebe7178f9f9a56740f859e846215f982d.text: When you ask the assistant to use its Solar Pro 4 model (from Upstage), it now connects to Upstage's standard route instead of the special zero-data-retention endpoint Upstage had set up. This switch is for Upstage's own debugging purposes and is already live. Your data still isn't used for training, but the connection now goes through a path that allows provider-side debugging logs, so Upstage can see more detail if something goes wrong. You won't notice a visual change, but the underlying link to the model provider has shifted.

17106e2e4b02aee3ffa07db72fad3327df43b1b2.text: If you're a free-tier user ending your session early, you now get clearer credit tracking: the tool shows you exactly how much of your unspent balance was refunded to your wallet, and it does this by keeping your session slot reserved during the refund process until the system confirms it's settled. This prevents race conditions where multiple cleanup steps (manual exit, app unmounting, or timeout) could cancel and double-refund your credit. You'll notice a new message on the landing screen telling you when your refund is pending, plus a final confirmation once it lands in your wallet with the exact amount returned. This applies to all freebuff session users, with no plan-based restrictions.

6e661ec6984d33a02c3a592348b160d68dacfee3.text: The text next to the link that sends you to the 'Earn Freebucks' page now reads 'Earn Freebucks · engage with a promoted post' on every client (CLI, Desktop, and browser), instead of the old 'Earn Trust · level up for more daily sessions' which referenced a currency that no longer pays out. Your assistant moved the wording and the web address for that page into a dedicated spot so the instructions wouldn't get deleted along with the old 'Trust' and 'Levels' system that was retired on 2026-09-07, and the page still loads at the same place it always did.

3e63daca691768e95055f250f95cdf1404b251ad.text: When you use the free assistant, you no longer see a monthly spending limit shown in the header or a hard daily cut-off that would stop you mid-session. The system now gently slows you down within a session instead of refusing requests, so prompts keep going rather than getting blocked once a daily money cap is hit. Older error messages around daily spend ceilings are kept only for compatibility with older servers; live servers now use this softer pacing. The change is live today for free users and affects how usage is managed during a single session.

4972f1e7a75e6c7f2421c55040c0746c9e5d97da.text: If you were on the free usage meter and had Freebucks left, you stopped getting told you’d used up all of today’s free usage just for being in an elevated country or trust level — those ceilings no longer apply to you, so your remaining balance works like it should again. The abuse prevention checks still block the same accounts they always did. This is live today.

253ee6c497c3d67371a7cddabfeacaebb19e308a.text: When Solar Pro 4 is offered for free, using it no longer eats into your daily spending limit, so it won't lock you out of other models on the same day. The system now calculates exactly when a model is priced at zero from its official price schedule and exempts that time range from your daily budget, closing the exemption the moment the price returns to a paid rate. You will notice the difference if you use Solar Pro 4 on a day it is free: you will not be blocked from other paid models later that same day, starting from September 5, 2026.

872fc2305848cdcdd0e5d4199e211b9f82831fe1.text: If an ad fails to reach someone in a given country, the system now tells the advertiser whether their own country rule blocked you or whether the ad simply couldn't be placed at all. Advertisers see these two reasons directly because they already wrote and own those country rules. You wouldn't notice this unless you're an advertiser reviewing why your ads didn't show in a specific country, and even then it only matters when an ad is actually blocked in a region you targeted.

04578916f453fcab40ef1d5dac060e94ab126108.text: When you open the list of AI models to pick from in the command-line tool, models that cost extra during busy times now show a small 'Peak pricing' badge right on their row, with a tooltip that tells you the surcharge amount and when the extra charge ends, all in your own time zone. Models on peak pricing no longer show the server's separate text notice because the badge now carries that information instead. This is live now and affects anyone choosing a model through the CLI model selector.

e8a3c7930b8024d099e2c2abf75ff582798a73c9.text: People with a full (paid) account can now spend their premium allowance on the GPT-5.6 Luna model through the web interface, the command-line tool, and the desktop app, just as they already could with the other premium models. Previously, the system treated Luna as if it were locked behind the limited-tier plan everywhere, which would have kept it out of reach for full-access users on some platforms. The change keeps Luna plan-locked for limited-tier accounts (who still cannot open it), while letting full-access accounts use it normally on every surface that serves premium models. This was recorded as a minor adjustment to the catalog constants and is live today.

02ec3583806e4bf811825a7f7bc3a1082c4583d3.text: When a Freebuff Pro subscriber hits a sponsored break in their chat, they now see a full-screen visual card built around a hero image instead of the inline text floor. The break's picture comes from a newly added hero asset (freebuff-pro-hero-1600x1000.png) uploaded behind a token rather than from a static file path, and the copy is keyed by placement so it can never be confused with the regular inline ad.
