28d0514641dc8804ec29db0727c13bb9f2bc2ca1.text: If you have a paid subscription that gives you extra sessions, those extra sessions now add on top of your free daily allotment instead of replacing it. For example, if you start with 5 free sessions and your subscription grants 4 more, you now get 9 total to use in a day, and the free ones are used up first. This also means the usage numbers shown to administrators and special accounts now match the combined totals everyone else sees, so the numbers in your settings panel and the usage picker at the top of the screen will always agree. This change went live on 2026-08-26.

cb53f476e75fa8151b31fc9ae263d0aa59281d5d.text: When a subscriber cancels, they will now be asked to pick a reason from a short, fixed list instead of typing whatever they want. The list is checked by the system, so the reason cannot be something the software does not recognize. At the same time, the cancel flow now shows that the special beta price they signed up for is three times the regular price and will not be held if they come back later. These two pieces are both live in today's product update.

9043277365c41dd3d8c20f4d192b64d879823dce.text: When you go to leave a comment on a sponsored post, the suggestion card no longer offers pre-written comment options. Instead it now shows you rules to follow — write it yourself, make it original, say something specific, keep it short and in clear English — alongside the advertiser's own guidance for that post. The goal is to keep the thread from filling up with identical copy-pasted replies that look bot-generated. If you looked, you'd see a short checklist of dos and don'ts replacing the old multiple-choice comment suggestions.

b11ec75a04ede2ef903e89bbe41fb5080514e102.text: If you use the free trial sessions included with your subscription, you can now see exactly how many of today's free sessions you've used and how many you get total, right on your account screen. This only shows up for paying subscribers who get a free daily session pool—it stays blank on older servers that don't know about this feature, and stays zero if your account is exempt from limits. You don't need to change any settings for this; it just starts showing up whenever your service provider updates to the latest version that includes this field.

10218ba5aa9794a3327524cc1922daa9f3e39ce1.text: When you open the model picker, time-restricted models now tell you the next window they'll be available in your own timezone (e.g. 'Open 3:00 AM – 5:00 PM'), so you can plan around the restriction instead of just seeing 'unavailable'. Models marked 'off_peak_only' (like Flash) are genuinely shut at peak hours for everyone, while 'deployment_hours' models show their open window in local time. The system now distinguishes between 'this model is closed right now' versus 'this plan is paused', and paid-subscription-only models are gated so a free account cannot start them at all — though no Pro-only models are active yet, since the intended rows haven't shipped. If a free account tries to start a subscription-only model, the response now carries a flag that tells the app to show an upgrade

ec01bf10020d29d13062f0218f3176e5a0e3f4b0.text: When you buy ads, your campaign can stop showing for a few reasons — like running out of money for the whole campaign, or hitting the daily spending limit set for today. The system now clearly tells you which one happened: if you hit today's limit, it says your campaign will resume at midnight (Pacific Time); if your total budget is gone, it says the budget is spent and the only fix is to add more money. You'd notice this on your campaign dashboard when the status or tooltip updates to show these new spend-related reasons instead of a generic pause message.

9f0de8454bcac2ea8898d1f6592c488da4942f7b.text: Imprezia ads now hide the advertiser name that used to appear next to them. When you see an Imprezia ad, you'll no longer see a destination label, because Imprezia's system doesn't include recognizable advertiser domains. The ad still opens the same link when clicked, so the destination URL hasn't changed, only the display name beside it.

72f1310353bddeacfee88d760a6193527ff69dd2.text: Starting today, the small daily limit that held back the fancier AI model on the Starter and Pro plans has been removed, so you can now use that model for the full number of daily answers your plan allows instead of only a portion. If you were on one of those plans and noticed a message telling you parts of your day were restricted to a simpler model, that warning no longer appears in your app because it no longer matches what you can actually do. The company left a behind-the-scenes setting in place rather than deleting it, which means they can quietly bring the old limit back later with a quick switch if they ever need to.

907cda721501e4f656b82ef0bf61e19af07926ef.text: The subscription panel now stays on screen instead of blinking out when you switch from the main interface to the plan picker, and it no longer disappears when the session transitions to ended. While the assistant fetches the latest usage data in the background, your active plan and rate-limit details are kept in memory and reused so the panel doesn't reset to blank.

54790e3a6614fea67d6dabd01fd367fabb684dc8.text: When you use the assistant in a software project, it now quietly records a small, safe summary of your repository — like how many files it has and roughly how active it is — instead of sending sensitive details such as branch names or file paths. This summary is stripped down to only aggregate numbers and counts, with a strict allowlist preventing any raw patch content, code changes, or identifying names from being transmitted. The feature is live today and applies to all SDK users whose projects generate telemetry, ensuring repository scale metrics are captured without risking source code or private repository information leaking into analytics.

4a41787b377f56263a296bc5a8458ad2707aafae.text: When the assistant waits to be started on the free landing screen, it now asks for ads in a specific, stable order and refuses to show the same ad slot twice. The first-party (built-in) ad network gets a more reliable way to confirm you actually saw an ad, retrying quietly up to three times before giving up, while external ad networks keep their older tracking method. If you looked, you'd notice ads appear in the same order each visit and that duplicate ad cards are gone. This is live today for the freebuff landing screen.

cb3ea78eda6ea14b43bc1624d0e854fdd9a898d0.text: If you promote a GitHub repository through this advertising system, you no longer have to write a comment to go with it. Instead, you simply star the repository, and to verify that you actually did it, you send in a screenshot of your star rather than a link. Links can't prove a star happened, but a screenshot of the starred page can, so the system now expects one for GitHub specifically. This only affects promotions on GitHub.

7a65d914646cc0f2883efcbc94971198e8064c16.text: When you try to use a model that is closed during DeepSeek's peak pricing hours, you are now told the correct time it comes back instead of a generic staffing-hours message. Previously, models marked as off-peak-only would incorrectly tell you they were unavailable during our own support hours, even though they actually reopen after DeepSeek's peak window ends. You now see a clear local-time message like 'again at 7:00 PM' instead of a confusing range mixing two time zones. This fix is live today for anyone using free-tier or public-API sessions that hit these model restrictions.

8238d829cad6ce2b95694de923e6e58c9a240e5d.text: Your subscription plan now has a monthly spending cap in addition to its session limit, so the platform can track how much real-world provider cost you're generating alongside how many conversations you start. When you get close to or hit that dollar ceiling within a billing cycle, your plan will stop new sessions just like it does today when you run out of monthly conversations, and you'll see a clear message that the spend limit for the period is reached rather than an ambiguous block. The change applies to every tier and is already wired into both the pricing definitions and the usage tracking that powers the paywall, so it lives in the product experience now rather than waiting on a future release.

dc2947f208c695a64f1781053d8afe1a3968a40a.text: When an OpenRouter-powered assistant encounters an error in the middle of generating a streaming reply (instead of before any text is sent), the system now preserves the specific reason the provider gave for the failure, rather than collapsing it into a vague 'Agent run error' message. The streaming error chunk is now converted into a full structured error object that carries the provider's own explanation, so applications and developers relying on these streaming responses can see exactly what went wrong — matching the detailed information already available from non-streaming failed responses. This behavior is live today and affects anyone using OpenRouter through this provider layer, since the change updates how mid-stream errors are reconstructed and surfaced to clients.

a733b317c1e05ace5fe868e3d4f52d300dbd018c.text: If you use the free GLM 5.2 assistant through a referral link, you are now capped at earning just one session per day, no matter how many friends you invite. The referral banner will stop showing promises of extra daily sessions once you hit that single-session limit. This replaces a period starting July 30 where referrals granted unlimited daily sessions, which lets people with many referrals turn that into a lot of free time on the assistant each day.

ed41bbe6cce57a22a3d03f3a69848063615c385c.text: The documentation that describes one label used across the shared app platform has been corrected, so it no longer misleads readers about what that label actually represents. If you were reading how the platform is identified when requests are sent to Imprezia, you would now see it described as the platform family, with the product source noted separately, matching what the system expects. This is a documentation-only change and is in place now.

ed27ce1cf3e461105e209dcd13d8e5e22219331f.text: When a advertising partner sends a notice that an ad led to a sale or signup, the system now records a small operational summary of that notice. Only broad status fields like whether the conversion was accepted or rejected, what kind of ad it was, and the final payout amount are kept, while partner login details and tracking IDs stay on the server for privacy and attribution detail. This summary is safe to aggregate and review across campaigns without exposing sensitive data.

81dc44a30b2de783596bce9e6c8192a674be6a23.text: The system that tracks how money flows through the platform now records two additional settings: which billing approach an advertiser's purchases use, and whether that advertiser can receive payments from external partners. These two settings are logged alongside existing configuration details whenever the system captures the state of an advertiser's account, so reports can later distinguish accounts running on a company-managed billing model from those that allow outside settlement, and accounts that are permitted to receive money from external sources from those that are not. If you reviewed the logged data today, you would see these two new pieces of information appear as part of each account record, even though nothing in the product experience changes for users yet, and all

8d2fe1d276001824281f633df332852e67e82564.text: Starting August 24, accounts signed up with five specific temporary email providers—gmaoiil.com, duojumbo.com, duojumbo.online, itesun.com, and geusil.com—are now refused at sign-up, so people using those inboxes cannot create new accounts. The system decides to block them not because most accounts get banned, but because a high share of each domain's accounts (22% to 52%) hit hidden traps set to catch automated sign-ups, compared to Gmail (0%) and Outlook (5%). Two similar domains, gieemel.com and bekri.site, were deliberately left out because too few of their accounts triggered those traps. This is live now for everyone signing up.

8953a389fa9deb1c8cb479d483b24327a2c38cb7.text: You might have noticed that clicks on special tracked links could previously show up in reports with a blank or missing label. The system now assigns those clicks a consistent, readable name so they are no longer logged as undefined. Separately, the percentage that decides which users see first-party ads is now converted to a shared, high-precision scale used by both ad delivery and campaign selection, preventing small rounding differences from sending a user to two different ad sources. The logging system now separately records the exact cohort a user was chosen for, the cohort that actually served the ad, and whether that allocation was deliberately invalid, so control groups can be distinguished from missing data. This is live today across all surfaces that label placements.

0b60b7df7979a111f67629386bd2a64f36885060.text: When the assistant starts up, it used to read your entire repository's raw change log at once, which could be so large it crashed with an out-of-memory error. It now reads a brief, structured summary instead: the branch name, how many files and people have worked on it, and at most the first 25 changed files. Old saved sessions that still store the raw text still work because those old fields were kept as an option. If you were watching the assistant get ready to help and it previously froze or failed on very large projects (more than a few thousand changed files or multi-gigabyte diffs), it should now start without crashing.

8bf398cd72689f7ca4bea6eb14ad7a7b162763ee.text: If you're on the full-access plan (not the free limited tier), the DeepSeek V4 Flash model is now unlimited again — it won't count against your shared daily quota the way it did after August 18. You won't see any pop-up about hitting a per-model cap for Flash, and new conversations will still default to it; if your daily pool runs out, the system falls back to the standard free model automatically. The change is live today, but it only affects the full-access plan — people on the free limited tier still only get MiMo and are not impacted.

1bbdc9e90d4becb32401d13293d9cbd7c9a5841c.text: If you sign up or log in using an email address ending in @imprezia.ai, or the specific test email jahooma@gmail.com, you will now always see Imprezia ads by default instead of being randomly placed in the experiment group. This only affects the people on that email list—everyone else still gets sorted the same random way as before. The assignment is stable, so once you are in, your experience won't flip around between sessions. Nothing changes for anyone who does not use one of those addresses.

836022e5e8a479b8330a80261070e80b636da639.text: In Freebuff Desktop, you can normally run up to three tabs of the cheaper, unlimited models at once, but only one tab of the expensive ones at a time. A pricing change on August 18 accidentally made that rule follow the wrong list, so when a new model was added to the quota list, the default model suddenly became limited to a single tab and about a thousand people per day saw a "Another tab is using the hosted model" message on the very model they were told to use. The two lists now stay separate, so adding a model to the billable quota no longer caps how many tabs can run. A side note in the code admits that models which are both metered and multi-tab cannot be safely allowed yet, so that combination stays blocked until a separate safety check is upgraded. The fix is live today.

061b2465fb339069a9a7b09081c6125a5919a574.text: Starting today, GPT-5.6 Luna is the default model when you use the full mode picker, replacing DeepSeek V4 Flash as the preselected option. If you use the free tier during peak hours, DeepSeek V4 Flash and DeepSeek V4 Pro will now pause availability, pushing you to alternate models until demand eases. Subscription tiers can now schedule a future downgrade at renewal, showing you the lower tier you'll drop to without immediately cutting off your current access. You can read about the new default and the peak-hour pause rules in the updated README files for both English and Chinese locales.

01b15151126e71919675bb0ab8972e1720377b12.text: When you open the app or start a new chat for free, you no longer land on the DeepSeek V4 Flash assistant by default. From Thursday onward, the assistant named Luna is now the one that's selected for you automatically, and Flash is only available during off-peak hours. If you tried to use Flash during peak times, you'd previously be redirected to the Pro assistant, but now you're redirected to Luna instead, because Pro no longer costs less than Flash during those hours. This change happened today, so if you opened a new chat right now, Luna would be your default assistant.

989208414f3649ca01ab3b87500917770ddcf204.text: When an ad fails to load the first time, the system now records whether that failure was later recovered—essentially tracking missed opportunities that still got fixed—without storing any details about which advertiser or creative was involved. This matters to you if you work with ad performance tracking today: logs will now include a clear label showing if the preceding ad attempt filled, did not fill, or failed, letting recovery happen visibly. The change is live today, adding one new field to the logging system so recovery can be measured while keeping sensitive campaign data private.

d9e94b083c24c9e1fa9655b0e55f5cdfc6506865.text: If you were using the assistant called Luna, you could only talk to it three times per day before it stopped responding, even if you still had plenty of your normal daily chat time left. That limit is gone: Luna now pulls from your regular daily allowance, the same pool Pro and Flash draw from, so a given chunk of time lasts longer than it used to. You might have noticed before that Luna felt more expensive per conversation than it should have; the system now charges it at a cheaper rate, which is why the extra cap is no longer needed. The team kept an empty placeholder in the settings so they can quickly bring a cap back if costs change later, but for now Luna runs without a daily ceiling.

1a069f10a6dcb5116116520f285a565bc7e658ac.text: You can now turn on test ads from Imprezia while real ads are running in production by simply requesting it — the assistant used to also check a separate email list of approved testers, and that list is gone. If you were on that tester list, you no longer get any special treatment; the old allowlist that the ad partner managed through an environment variable has been deleted, so only the new explicit request flag matters. The behavior is live today: anyone who asks for sandbox creatives by name gets them in production, and the old email-based approval no longer exists.

2b718cc3be65d5704cf71390e398c989c1641b84.text: The placement and measurement of ads was updated to track newer diagnostic data and to recognize two additional ad slots that were previously hidden from live inventory, which means ads in those spots will now count toward availability reporting instead of being treated as if they never existed. First-party ad routing, which lets ads come directly from the publisher instead of through third parties, is now set to stay off by default until an operator intentionally turns it on, so it will not accidentally pull demand away from paid networks. Reporting on cost-per-click metrics now surfaces billable clicks and average cost-per-click for the primary view, while legacy conversion labels remain accessible to the system but are deliberately hidden from that click-focused dashboard. These changes

79ca37b5008dc6dfe804a8b7bb002be7d4435abf.text: The assistant now shows a time-until-reset counter that can display days (for example, 4d 7h) and explicitly handles terminal command output before falling back to generic formatting. Developers also cleaned up how blocks of conversation are searched and updated by replacing nested if-else chains with simpler early returns and continue statements, which is behind-the-scenes housekeeping that does not change what the assistant does for the reader today.

4fa5ea05a929de13ec11d3f1a4549953efa6c09b.text: If you place an ad with us now, the system will first check our own ad inventory for a match before sending your request out to paid third-party networks. Roughly 10% of signed-in users are in the group that gets our own ads shown first, and the rest may still see our ads as a backup option instead of a blank space. The ad text and links from advertisers are now automatically stripped of hidden codes that could mess up terminal displays or redirect visitors to unsafe locations, and the control panel for tracking where ads appear is live with real performance data rather than placeholder numbers. This is active today for the advertisers and users on the eligible cohorts.

4140a604bcff8120f0e60c1cd20258bdbb9e6cd0.text: If you have an account that is exempt from the daily usage limit, the model picker no longer shows a counter that read "0 of 4 used" alongside your "unlimited" status, which was misleading. Instead, the counter is hidden entirely until you build up usage. The display now relies strictly on data the server sends, and the documentation for a related flag was clarified to note its name is historical but kept so installed clients continue working.

695d4d15676d9937d172ccf87909013085942be1.text: If you're on a subscription that includes DeepSeek models and you use it over the weekend, you will now always get the cheaper off-peak rate, no matter what time it is. During the week, DeepSeek still charges the higher peak price only in the morning hours, from 5pm to 3am Pacific time. If you look at your rate plan details, the note about DeepSeek availability during peak hours now reads 'weekday peak hours' instead of just 'peak hours', reflecting that weekends are never restricted.

41eb6446627cc703eeb8323efaf1e6477204a06d.text: If you are one of Imprezia's house-ad partners and you want to see their internal promotional creatives (the "Developers. Earn money with your AI app." banner) while working in a live production environment, your email now needs to be added to a special list before those ads will show. Previously the system only checked whether a developer was running in a test mode, which meant anyone with a sandbox key could see the house ads during development; now an additional gate requires both a matching email on that list and an explicit session flag, so a stray link or an old bookmark alone will no longer accidentally surface a house ad to real traffic. The list lives in an environment variable the partner controls, so adding someone does not require a new code release, and if that variable is

95e94c20aecc773fd13da69de9eebff40f6436bb.text: When you start a new conversation and a sponsored slot comes up, roughly one in ten signed-in users will now consistently see an ad from Imprezia in that slot across the web app, CLI, and desktop — the assignment is stable so your experience matches whether you're chatting in the browser or the CLI. Unauthenticated users (not signed in) are deliberately kept in the control group so they don't dilute the test, and they see no ad there at all. If Imprezia returns no ad, nothing shows; if it does, you see it once for that turn, and the advertiser is only billed when your browser signals the ad was actually viewable, not just loaded.

923de567621991a2f4d90fe7bcfcf4fd016a24ca.text: The system now records extra details when it tries to load ads, like which ad provider was asked for, how many ads it got back, how long it took, and which device or app you are using. Those details are saved in the internal operations logs (not in product analytics) and are kept only if they match a strict, known format, so unexpected or extra fields are dropped. This only applies to that one ad-loading event and is already live today, so engineers monitoring system operations can see more about how ad requests are behaving without leaking other information.

990ae116fee764e1daf72f0fda57880cf3d369b7.text: If you use V4 Pro today, you are no longer cut off after one prompt per day, and you will not be pushed into another model during peak hours when this used to be paused. Your prompts now draw from the same shared pool of high-quality models as Flash, which costs the same rate, instead of being limited because it was once the most expensive option. If you see the notice that says which models pause at peak hours, the text for that notice now matches the actual limit table, and a check prevents them from drifting apart again. The team can re-add the old daily limit if Pro stops being the cheapest premium choice. All of it is live now.

5a504c380ad0497547ff88e63624d6101795cc92.text: The assistant model called DeepSeek V4 Pro is now available all the time instead of only during off-hours. Previously, it would shut down during busy daytime hours to save on server costs, but now it stays open because the company switched to a cheaper provider that charges the same rate all day. If you use this model, you no longer get blocked out during the middle of the day. The change also removed the automatic switch to a backup model during those hours, since the backup is no longer needed.

ac2a035d604166a86390a7272dd56b60efd8a556.text: As of August 22, the free assistant switched its default model from the deep-reasoning DeepSeek V4 Pro to the faster DeepSeek V4 Flash, so when you open it you now get Flash unless you pick another model. During your area's busy hours (roughly 5 PM to 3 AM Pacific), Pro is paused and limited to one session a day, while Flash stays open all day as the cheaper option that keeps the premium pool active. If you looked now, you would see Flash listed at the top of the model picker and Pro moved lower with a note that it is closed at peak times.

b2efafdc0d4a0bf860ea5dd9581c8d754a664087.text: A new AI model option is being set up specifically for Novita's server, which acts like Codex (a coding assistant) but is a different model from the existing Luna one, so they're kept separate to prevent mix-ups. This new option gets its own dedicated slot among the free tools, but is restricted to a select group and won't appear for standard free access. Users who have special access can now use a model that supports about 372,000 tokens of text input — much less than Luna's own capacity, but matching what the server actually offers.

84c46ec290a6e544a29a30189b87a2fa1fa4ec90.text: The $60 Pro subscription is no longer available when you sign up. The system that handles checkout now only offers the $25 Plus and free Starter plans, so even though the Pro price still exists in the payment system, no one can pick it during checkout without a code change first. If you browse subscription options today, you will only see Plus and Starter; the Pro tier has been removed from the list you can choose. This is in effect now.

098dd053d11a6338dae3f4abd62996a0c18982aa.text: When you use the command-line tool to check which AI assistant is working on a task, it now figures out the friendly name (like 'Opus' or 'GPT-5') using a simple list instead of a long chain of if-else checks. This only affects how names are displayed in the terminal, not which assistants you can use. If you glanced at the output, nothing would look different today, but the change keeps the naming logic tidy behind the scenes.

0b697402591b23688e8fff0b8861d7b427190e2e.text: When an ad shows up in the command-line assistant's interface, it now displays the ad's main headline (title) as its own bold line, instead of only using it as a backup label. You'd notice ads with their own call-to-action buttons no longer lose their headlines — previously, those headlines disappeared entirely. The ad's disclosure ('Ad') and other layout elements adjust automatically, and missing fields default gracefully so malformed ad data won't crash the display. This affects anyone running first-party placements campaigns through the CLI landing screen, and it's live today.

2a3c3c791364d4f39c2c61d80162909cd199cd29.text: Starting today, the service offers three new paid subscription tiers — Starter, Plus, and Pro — each giving you a shared monthly allowance of sessions to spend across premium AI models like DeepSeek V4 Pro and GPT-5.6 Luna, with the more expensive models drawing from the same pooled allowance rather than being unlocked separately. Kimi K3 Eco is deliberately excluded from pricing because it's currently bait for automated traffic, not real user conversations. If you're a developer or customer, you'd see new plan options and a paywall that reflects these tiers, with Stripe checkout prices kept private on the server side.

7895583a6c3216d4a977080028483c8b65fc9d3d.text: Ads now reset every day at midnight Pacific Time instead of at some other moment, so your daily spending and placement limits all turn over together. This only matters if you run or see ads in the system, and you would notice that your budget and stats roll over at the same clock hour that the product's other daily limits already do. The change went live today and is ready for advertisers and the payment system to use.

9a9f7dd95b7843187a4048b1b950b3539ab8fd5c.text: Ads placed inside the chat will now look exactly the same whether you see them in the terminal app or in the web preview that advertisers use to check how their copy will display. The code that decides how an ad's text is squeezed into 20, 48, or 60 character-wide columns was moved out of the chat app into a shared library so both surfaces use one and only one set of rules. If you run the chat in a narrow terminal, an ad with a web link still won't show that link unless the URL actually starts with http:// or https://, so junk like javascript: links get blocked instead of rendered as a clickable card. A new placements setup is also in place defining fixed preview widths, activation windows, and prepaid balance rules, though the first-party ad rail it supports is explicitly still unbuilt

ed706ca47d476c9a68e7302b22b3c615dd522dd1.text: As of August 21, 2026, the CLI's model picker now defaults to DeepSeek V4 Pro instead of V4 Flash. If you use the full-access mode, V4 Pro is now your starting point — it's the cheapest premium model available all day. V4 Flash, which was previously the default, now pauses during busy hours and automatically routes your requests to V4 Pro to avoid slowdowns. Meanwhile, GPT-5.6 Luna's daily session limit doubled from one to two. The list order in the picker is now the only way the system suggests which model to use — the old 'recommended' badges and upgrade prompts are gone.

aefe67a7bd41d1b8cce4e53d39f9e22677aaf630.text: You may have noticed that the assistant picker on the CLI sometimes hid rows like V4 Pro depending on what time of day it loaded, because some tiers are temporarily unavailable during DeepSeek's peak-cost window (00:00-10:00 UTC). The picker now accepts a "pin clock" input so automated runs (like CI tests) can freeze the displayed time to a specific moment, and when that input is set the clock stops ticking entirely instead of drifting back to real time — meaning the list of visible options stays consistent no matter when the check runs. This only affects automated/CLI-driven sessions that pass the pin value; in normal use the picker keeps reading the real clock so tiers reopen naturally without restarting. The change is live today in the CLI build.

3f3cb3851705ca43846d8a13c2c12a7ebfe94a38.text: When you ask for your daily free allowance of compute tokens, the system used to check the time of day and, if DeepSeek was in its most expensive pricing window, hand you a smaller cap instead of your usual limit — with a message promising your full allowance would return in a few hours. That time-based ceiling logic has been removed entirely: the clock that decided when your limit should shrink is gone, so your daily allowance no longer changes based on when you happen to be using it. Right now, your allowance is the same no matter what time it is, and the admin dashboard no longer needs to explain any temporary, peak-window reductions to you.

b9ace3f9b2782eb321dd299ec9972689f3e08daa.text: The small banner about updated privacy terms that sat at the bottom of marketing pages has disappeared a few days early, because the date that turns it off was moved up to August 20. At the same time, the page that showcases advertising examples now pulls its sample posts and reported costs directly into the page instead of loading them through an external embed, so they stay the same width and height as the rest of the content. You would see these example posts render cleanly without shifting the layout, although some engagement numbers like reposts and views are left blank because they can't be pulled in automatically.

592d93f5d9e627a00fa4db4e1d1e8ca7662421a0.text: If you look at the featured ad posts on the site now, you'll see real numbers for how many times each was reposted and viewed instead of blank spaces. The team manually typed in those counts straight from the post pages, since there's no automated way to pull them, and made sure to record the full numbers rather than shortened display versions. The post showing a deleted Bolt competitor now displays 498 reposts and 48,300 views, while the one about Bolt's $700M wipeout shows 436 reposts and 16,800 views, and those posts already gained access to these metrics as of August 21, 2026.

9d0e435b3802e4b6b833c1ed349d604e5b804f0d.text: If you use the assistant in your web browser or on the cloud version, you can now tap into Ox Alpha, a brand-new anonymous coding model that's free while its makers test it. It's not available on the desktop app or via the command line right now, by design. If you looked, you'd see it's locked to that one model and has a hard stop so the service can't accidentally start charging you if the host raises the price later. It's live today for browser and cloud users only.

ffed5e29d2c86da974e22ca462675bb334d3212c.text: When the assistant tries to create a folder on Windows machines that use cloud-based file storage, the folder sometimes appears a few moments late, causing the creation to fail and interrupt your work. The assistant now waits briefly and checks again if the folder exists before giving up, so file-saving operations that previously errored out now complete successfully. You won't see any new buttons or options, but actions like editing or creating files in nested folders should stop failing unexpectedly on those Windows setups.

9311890b70d198454df8e25b72df2d064854dc48.text: When you look at the model picker in the app, you will now see a note saying, for example, 'Returns at 10:00 AM local time' next to any model that is currently unavailable due to its peak pricing window, instead of just having the row greyed out with no explanation. This only applies to models like DeepSeek V4 Pro that have specific hours when they cost more; models that are closed for other reasons, like staffing hours, still show the existing label. The change is live today.

105640d21d124ff1dd6a7ccd7df06fffb9a5c34f.text: When an agent (an AI assistant) recommends a service like Supabase or Stripe, it can now create your account and give you the login credentials directly in the conversation, rather than sending you to a signup page. This only happens after the agent asks you first and you explicitly agree — it requires your permission and the ID from the earlier search. If it works, the account is set up on the spot and the agent receives the credentials to hand back to you immediately.

6c1591f8a5caf4b189e75bea718139d506c0b121.text: Starting today, the assistant switched its main helper model to DeepSeek V4 Flash for faster responses, and MiniMax M3 is once again available without counting against your premium usage limits. The two costliest models, DeepSeek V4 Pro and GPT-5.6 Luna, are now capped at one conversation per day (V4 Pro only during off-peak hours) because their providers raised prices beyond what the free service can absorb. If you looked, you'd see these caps and the "temporary" note in the model list and CLI release notes, along with the switch of the default model to DeepSeek V4 Flash.

1e69baf9bf0ba91e9f693f1a6942e2b92c880783.text: When you tell the assistant to open a file on Windows using a path that looks like /c/projects/notes.txt (the way Git Bash writes paths), the assistant now correctly converts it to the standard Windows form like C:\projects\notes.txt before trying to find the file, so it stops getting lost on Windows. This only affects Windows users working through Git Bash paths; everyone else sees no difference. If you watched the code, you would see the conversion relying on a tool that ships with Git for Windows and skipping conversion for paths that already look native. This is live today.

b378f994a87f43adea2fa4fed651663f2b89b08e.text: If you create an ad campaign right now, you won't be charged on your card—billing stays paused so campaigns can run free for testing. Any campaign you start is automatically capped to end within 7 days, even if you try to set a later end date, so free delivery doesn't run forever. This is live today: the payment step is skipped for you, and your campaign's end date is clamped to a week out from today.

b4e5713b824dff395fcf7112cfc5ccae94429984.text: Advertisers you've already approved can now publish new campaigns without a staff member manually reviewing each one first. The campaigns simply go live as soon as they're submitted. Your existing staff review tools still work: the dashboard at /web/admin/advertisers now shows every live campaign for spot-checking rather than holding them in a queue, and you can flip a setting to turn the manual review queue back on later, at which point any new campaigns will be held for approval as before while the ones already running stay exactly as they are.

08a8371fb064793ba00624c528e8738489aea268.text: If you send messages, each one now costs exactly one unit of trust, no matter which version of the assistant you use. Previously, basic and most common models cost nothing per message, while the most advanced limited models cost two units, and the middle tiers cost one — so your trust score changed at unpredictable speeds depending on which model answered you. Now the rate is flat: since one engagement earns fifty, it reliably covers fifty messages. The different model groups still exist as labeled categories, but they no longer change how much you lose per message. This is live today for everyone whose messages draw from these trust balances.

7b1bde13e85e50fb7f0ca7675ebf8c29788ec464.text: If you open the model picker in the CLI's Premium section, each model row now shows its own usage count from the correct quota pool instead of one shared count for the whole section. Before this fix (live today, 2026-08-19), the Premium section read the first available quota and assumed every model in that section shared it, so when DeepSeek gained a second daily pool alongside the premium pool, some rows displayed stale or mismatched numbers next to already-spent limits. The picker now groups usage by pool and labels each row inline when it draws from a stricter pool than the section header, while servers that don't send pool info keep working unchanged.

2e3e3f6691f3de16b7b0b5ddcb1612c553a382de.text: When you use the standard assistant, it now costs nothing against your Trust score, so the everyday messages you send won't push your balance into the red. Trust is now only charged for the scarce model tiers like GLM and the limited premium waves, and a balance can never drop below zero, so you'll never see a negative Trust score next to your name. If you currently have a negative balance, it will show as zero the moment you load the product again, with no waiting period. This change is live today.

24de8d9513fd0584a4a18a73f3d3ca5e7e54a1bf.text: When you type a website address like "x.com/my-post" into the product without including the "https://" part, it was being rejected silently — pressing Submit did nothing and no error explained why. The system now automatically adds "https://" to addresses you type without that prefix, so your website is recognized correctly. You'll notice that pasting a scheme-less URL (like "reddit.com/r/all") now works instead of failing quietly. Existing addresses that already include a scheme (like "javascript:alert(1)") are deliberately left untouched and still blocked, ensuring only the missing-prefix problem is forgiven, not malicious input disguised as a normal address.

b5111f885a8e3b737cffff102f353444ea860ada.text: The advertiser landing page now shows real posts from @victorxheng that were boosted, along with honest view-count ranges (typically 10,000 to 50,000 views per post) for each one. You can see actual results the system produced instead of vague promises, and every number shown either comes straight from the database or is something the operators verified themselves. Posts that never ran through the system are silently dropped, so nothing on the page can be a fabricated claim.

8c034b5f9242c0bb48b8021f96eeb2e159096d16.text: When you run an ad and need to prove you actually engaged with the post (liked, reshared, and commented), the system now refuses the link to the post itself and asks for the link to your specific comment instead. This fixes a glitch where copying the promoted post's own URL on LinkedIn used to pass the check, even though the same link was correctly rejected on X and Reddit, making verification inconsistent across platforms. The confirmation message you sign now also spells out that you must have liked, reshared, and commented yourself, rather than the old generic statement. If you look, you will notice the error message now tells you to open your comment's menu and copy its link rather than the post link, and this is live and applies to all ad submissions going through the verification

ba0e40bacf53a1ffa8dfcf0db6ab7b0da43b139a.text: FreeBuff's ads now send the same browser identity to the ad server when they show an ad as when they bid on it. Previously, the browser looked modern during the auction but then sent an outdated-looking 'Freebuff-CLI' label at the moment the ad impression was recorded, which ad networks like Gravity flagged as suspicious bot activity on their bot-filtering screen. The built-in Chrome version label was also corrected from a 2024 value to match the current browser, stopping the appearance that a two-year-old browser was visiting the site. This is now in effect whenever an ad impression is tracked.

7dcb4fb1e09cbd72bb0d86409739ff616bc6d472.text: Starting today, any single account you use here can run at most two project workspaces at the same time, and you can start at most five new web projects per day across all regions. The daily-project limit used to be ten and only counted new projects in certain regions, but the regions now measure it everywhere, so if you hit five new web projects in one day you will need to wait until the next day before starting more. The two-at-once workspace limit was set to match the highest amount any individual account was actually seen using on August 19, 2026, so it does not slow down anyone who was already working that day and only keeps that number from growing. If you are one of the small number of accounts that regularly ran more than two workspaces at once, you will now hit a hard stop when

e73d39fff1ab55bc2c2615d60efd7129afa5c7fc.text: When you click the referral banner inside the tool, it now opens the Earn page on the Trust feed, which pays out within a minute, instead of the old referral-status tab that only pays after someone signs up and sticks around. The wording that points you at the Earn page is now pulled from one shared location so the CLI, desktop, and web versions say the same thing: "Earn Trust for more sessions." If you watch the banner, you'll notice the link label is shorter because it has to share a row with a quota summary, but it still tells you it leads to the Trust engagement feed where rewards drop quickly.

187b1e916c06bd3ab87208ac647577fb4b9f6b03.text: If you run an ad campaign, you now pay a fixed daily subscription rather than being billed for each individual engagement. Your $10/day rate still buys you up to 20 engagements, but the cost no longer depends on whether those engagements actually happen—you pay the daily rate regardless, and that same number sets your delivery cap. This is live today for advertisers using the flat daily pricing model.

1470aa4e189c2d0347843109e5ec86dbab395402.text: The database health checks now run even when the database user lacks full admin privileges. Instead of silently skipping the checks when a special permission is missing, the system now reports how many database sessions and slow queries it cannot see, alongside the ones it can. Database administrators running the tool with a restricted account will see alerts continue to fire (they were dark for a month before), and the alerts now expose invisible work rather than hiding it by reading 'all clear' from an empty list. This is live today in the shared core monitoring tool.

7129d45870e6486850aca5729015b555653ca7d1.text: Starting today, you can earn extra free sessions by engaging with promoted posts — each like, comment, or repost from a real developer account adds to your earned capacity. The free daily sessions you start with dropped slightly (premium users from five to four, limited-access users from six to three), but the new earned levels let you climb back up to seven. Advertisers can now buy daily campaigns at a flat rate (starting at ten engagements per day, priced in five-dollar steps up to a self-serve ceiling), with each engagement costing fifty cents. Everything is live now, including the ability to turn off the new earned-level system entirely if needed.

35dc6d079403192cc19e9552f4a951fa9776f707.text: When an assistant running on a shared server looks for a reusable skill, it now only searches the project's own folders unless explicitly allowed to search the server's home directory. You'd notice this if a server-hosted assistant previously picked up a skill stored in the server's general settings instead of the one shipped with the repo you're working in; from now on, the repo's copy takes precedence unless the server is configured to allow the home lookup. The flag is off by default, so nothing changes unless someone turns it on.

5f72959fab4202f5b667112c914282bcc195fb9b.text: When you ask the assistant how much room it has left before hitting its thinking limit, that number is now calculated instantly on your machine instead of being fetched from a remote server, so each step no longer waits a few seconds on a network round-trip before deciding what to forget. The exact wording your custom helpers use to describe themselves is now parsed in one shared place, which stops a crash that otherwise happens when those helpers are loaded in a serverless environment like AWS Lambda or Convex. If you're running inside a hosted or automated tool that embeds Codebuff's core (not the desktop app), your personal helper files stored at home no longer leak in, and the desktop app explicitly opts back into showing them. Live today.

cef358330ebed218abe3c1d8df88a8d4bb8315db.text: When a model leaves the free tier, the system used to accidentally try to charge your account for using it, even though you're supposed to use it for free. Now, the assistant correctly recognizes these substituted models and lets free-tier users keep using them without hitting the paywall. This only affects requests where the server swaps in the limited tier's default model, and it's already live for free-mode agents under the codebuff publisher.

89832d9b3ade452149cf8e9658bd4537107fc5e7.text: If you're on the limited plan, your usage cap will no longer get extra-tight during the three peak hours each day when rates usually double. That reduction was meant to offset those doubled prices, but the limited plan doesn't include any of those higher-priced models anymore, so tightening the cap there just squeezed you for no reason. Your hourly spending room now stays the same whether it's peak time or not.

8da51dc0eaecae13822690e91ea90a9038bd9dc6.text: The free version of the tool no longer uses the DeepSeek V4 Flash model for limited (free) access. Because that model was paused due to a price change upstream, MiMo 2.5 is now the default model you see when you use the free tier. The change affects what model loads when you start the tool without a paid plan, and you would notice the landing screen still shows the free session limits but the model label now points to MiMo 2.5 instead of Flash. Full (paid) access still uses Flash as its planner and fallback model.

d0c7b069051a45044d107598a2ce98ef80d63100.text: The AI provider DeepSeek raised its prices on August 16, 2026, and the system's help-center software still points new visitors to that now-more-expensive option as the default. Nothing has flipped for you yet, but a warning is now written into the system for whoever decides later whether a cheaper alternative should replace it. If you looked, you'd see the cost notes next to the default setting have been rewritten to show it used to be cheaper than its rival and now costs more.

d20038cb58001e360bbcfb30960817b202e8993a.text: When you look at your monthly spending dashboard, costs are now filed under two separate columns instead of one: the company that built the model (like OpenAI for a model served through OpenRouter), and the company that actually sent you the bill (OpenRouter in that case). Rows written before this update appear as a single visible "(unattributed)" group that disappears on its own as it ages out, rather than being silently guessed. If you drill in, you'll see that high-traffic mixed-vendor models no longer get mislabeled, because the system stopped trusting the model name and now records exactly who computed each cost when it happened.

35eec19e84f06cc0bfef213d204165ac1e9867a4.text: If you use DeepSeek during its high-demand hours (early morning and morning in Universal Time, specifically 1am-4am and 6am-10am UTC), your free allowance of service gets temporarily reduced, and now the system will clearly tell you that this is only temporary and show you exactly when your normal amount comes back — instead of making you wait until the next day. The reason your allowance is lower right now is that the provider charges double rates during these busy periods, so your free credits stretch further if they limit peak-time usage; this is now calculated from one consistent set of rules so the price you pay and the limit your account sees always match. This applies to you whenever you hit a limit during those specific hours, and the messaging now explains that your full allowance

c200e2d4f1c2dbc77bdd889971d83fb755fb0f53.text: The system that watches the company's main databases now uses a single, shared set of rules to decide when an alert should fire, instead of having different scripts each make up their own thresholds. If you manage one of these databases, you would notice alerts now trigger at consistent, documented levels: when the database gets close to needing a transaction-ID cleanup (50% of its capacity), when a running query snapshot has hung around too long (1 million transactions behind), when an index build has been stuck for at least 30 minutes, or when a single query is consuming as much database workload as the entire fleet (4 busy-backend equivalents). A new probe also ensures the monitoring account itself has the right permissions to see these signals, so the system won't silently report 'all

695a52ed5a16bd3c3482682e2f84b29ac47c5190.text: If you are on the restricted-risk plan (including people in restricted countries or on restricted Desktop tabs) and you start a single-session reclaim or send a new prompt, you now hit a second hard stop at twice your daily limit, on top of the existing fresh-admission gate. The first gate still only blocks brand-new external sessions from starting, so a session already in progress is never cut off, but restricted accounts can no longer spend their way to twice the daily allowance on one active session before the Pacific-midnight reset. Measured on 2026-08-13 against a one-dollar baseline, the worst restricted country reached 12.6x ($6.32) before this second cap, so the hard backstop now kicks in at the 2x level instead. If you are an internal account you are exempt before callers tally

2fa82f2e26c68a2e750dcdd3515855e661d05577.text: You would now see rollup jobs (like ad-revenue and freebuff-spend) and dashboards consistently compute time windows for UTC days, reducing the risk of rows being dropped or double-counted. The duplicated logic for shifting, filtering, and defining these time windows has been extracted into a shared utility, ensuring all tools use identical math for half-open timestamp ranges. This prevents off-by-one and precision issues where Postgres microsecond-level timestamps could misalign near day boundaries. Live today across the affected shared core utilities.

6c49e12dc09c72d510ee13940ea543ef19b418e5.text: When you leave a free Desktop tab idle, it can now automatically pick the next step instead of stopping with an "Out of credits" error. This only affects free-mode Desktop users on Auto: their tab's idle assistant was previously routed through paid paths and got blocked, so it produced no next action for most free users. Behind the scenes, the idle decider is now recognized as a free root agent, tied to that tab's own model (not a single fixed one) so it no longer 403s on `session_model_mismatch`, and it has its own brief prompt that tells the model it only chooses inputs and never edits files or runs commands. The fix is in place and live today, per the developer comments, which note auto-run simply never produced a next step for the entire free-mode population before this.

eb2eb5ec4b15f2b31cee2ff7c6870aef398526aa.text: The system no longer lets operators redirect certain analytics traffic to custom server addresses they chose themselves; traffic of this kind now always goes to the standard destination the system picks by default. This affects teams that run the software who had previously pointed this traffic at their own alternate endpoints. If you looked right now, you would see that the option to set those alternate addresses has disappeared from the configuration, so any such redirection you set up will be ignored.

2afc2b2dfac9a0bcb48e18ccc0c1f720f6f2e6a7.text: When you ask the assistant to use the Luna model, the system no longer hard-locks to one specific provider endpoint and instead tries OpenAI first, then falls back to cheaper alternatives if OpenAI refuses the request, while still enforcing a strict price ceiling to prevent unexpectedly expensive routing. This means you, as a user, may have previously seen complete failures with no explanation when OpenAI blocked the request; now those requests can succeed via the fallback endpoints, and if any endpoint returns an error chunk mid-stream, the system will properly detect it instead of silently treating it as a dropped network connection.

2d370c194f127b56a4273462587f7589a557b834.text: When you ask the assistant to do several things at once that involve photos or images, your app used to freeze up while it waited for all the answers to come back. Now the program keeps those photos in line instead of letting them spill out between the separate answers, which is what was tripping up the validation and getting threads stuck when your conversation history was replayed. You don't tap any new button or setting for it: the next time a multi-step request with images gets answered, it simply completes instead of locking up.

ae35b542f1b2cc0e6e455ef9effa1cdb9ad4c818.text: If you are an ordinary developer in Singapore, your daily free allowance just went up from $0.50 to $5, so you are no longer refused mid-day for a price that was meant for abusive traffic. The refusal rate that triggered the change was 22.9% of Singapore's active users, and most of them carried no abuse signal; the developer team traced the actual abuse to a set of throwaway email domains and blocked those by name instead. You would notice the difference the next time you use the service: a request that would have been denied a day after this change is now allowed through, while the handful of flagged disposable email providers are the ones getting turned away.

f97ca5511b01eba2552e9be7d7332194f5118ca3.text: If you sign up using a Proton, Tutanota, Apple Hide My Email, DuckDuckGo, or Firefox Relay address, the system still recognizes it as a privacy-focused mailbox but will no longer treat it as a sign you're creating multiple accounts to bypass limits. This took effect on 2026-08-14, after an operator decision. You wouldn't see any visible difference in your account, but if your signup was previously held back or flagged because the system thought your email was a disposable alias, it now passes through normally.

6eb9bf8e4038d432a370d0186b0d124fe912fabe.text: When you save your progress, the system now quietly removes any tool requests that were started but never finished before writing them to disk. This only affects people resuming a saved session: you won't see half-finished tool calls anymore, and the program won't crash on restart trying to load an incomplete message. From your perspective it just means saves are a little smoother and resumes are a little safer.

09e160095a84086726021f1c614790d8558f8ca5.text: If you sign up for an account and it gets blocked, you might now see a message that names Google's reCAPTCHA specifically instead of a generic verification failure, so you can quickly check whether a browser extension or network filter is blocking it. The system now reads new settings that let it use both invisible and click-box versions of Google's reCAPTCHA alongside its existing Turnstile verification, and it keeps reCAPTCHA errors separate from Turnstile errors in its logs for faster troubleshooting. These changes apply to anyone signing up for an account today.

5db7a544be7c5ec414b833a4cb295fa8511b1b8c.text: Accounts on small usage limits (roughly under $50) can now be stopped mid-session if they try to spend far past their cap, instead of only being blocked from starting a new session. Before this, a low-limit account could blow past its limit and keep running an active session; now there's a hard cutoff that applies only to the smallest ceilings. The change also adds a new status for privacy checks that were deliberately not run (because the provider was turned off or out of credits), which gets reported as unverified egress instead of a normal failure. This is live today.

7c219be7ef6d60e088fcfa9fcd566a798153d57b.text: If your account gets restricted because of a VPN, a blocked country, a suspicious email domain, or unverified traffic, the system used to show you a generic 'capacity limited' message. Now it shows a clearer message that tells you the specific categories of reasons it might have been flagged for, including a note that turning off your VPN may fix it. Accounts flagged for other reasons, like using third-party tools or having low trust signals, still see the original generic message by design, since those are not meant to be spelled out. This is live today for the affected accounts.

192cb715a3ae26a1deee15731d0ddd86560fe262.text: Desktop sign-in now records both the moment you start signing in and the moment you finish, so the team can tell how many people are actually trying to sign in rather than only counting those who succeed. Before this, a redesigned first-run screen could look successful even if sign-in itself broke for most people, because only the completion was tracked. Now you—as someone signing in on desktop—produce one extra analytics event at the start, and the company sees an accurate sign-in conversion rate. This is live today.

cef314aab409b9198cc4f5665e4a52da528c4eb4.text: When you see a special invitation to track your referrals in the command-line tool, clicking that link now takes you straight to your referral status page instead of the general earn page. The button next to it also says 'Open referral status' instead of 'Open GLM 5.2 dashboard' so it matches where you actually land. This only affects people using the command-line version of the tool.

0029f0a29f01837307120b1212694ffaa2899474.text: When you start a new session using a VPN, proxy, Tor, or residential-proxy exit, the system now treats it the same as a request from a restricted country. Your first fresh session can still begin and spend up to $0.50, but after that you won't be able to start another fresh session until the daily reset rolls around at Pacific midnight. If you're using Apple iCloud Private Relay or a regular hosting provider, nothing changes for you. This behavior is already active today.

ad5d3005fb7f08e572e6fe8323303b26497795e1.text: If you use the desktop app, the system now quietly records two new background events: when a group of messages gets tucked away automatically after they're no longer active, and when a new message couldn't be delivered because of a conflict and that issue is noticed or resolved. These notes are only logged when something actually changes or a batch of items is moved (rather than constantly repeated), so your activity history stays clean without extra noise. It's already live today, but you won't see a new button or message - it just helps the people who maintain the app understand how messages are behaving behind the scenes.

871d75810e6732f65067d4bd6faec927c529332d.text: If you use the free version of the service, you are no longer limited to a flat $50 of usage per day. Instead, your daily limit depends on where you are, the type of email address you used to sign up, whether you are using a third-party app to access the service, and your account's trust level. For most users, the new limit is $15 per day, but it can be as low as $5 for limited-tier accounts, $1 for users in certain countries like Singapore and China, and even less for accounts flagged for suspicious behavior like using disposable email addresses. The lowest applicable limit wins, so if you fit multiple restricted categories, your allowance is reduced to the smallest of those. This change is already live and affects anyone who signs up for or continues using the free tier today.

43db7ec34405a23491b376662bf243226a136619.text: The system stopped running its automated checks that watched how long certain backend database lookups took and whether they suddenly got slower. This monitoring, which had been tuned against real production traffic after a recent shift to a faster private network path, was removed as part of cleaning up shared utilities. If you relied on those cost/regression alerts, they will no longer fire. This is live today; the removal applies to all traffic handled by the core web service.

190ac96c3428bfbd1ea3ffbdeaf77659f088a902.text: When you copy a long conversation to your clipboard in a remote session, the assistant now shrinks the text to fit instead of failing or silently skipping. If your selection changes while a previous copy is still running, the older copy is stopped immediately so it can't finish later and paste stale content. When the clipboard tool you're using gets stuck waiting on a broken display, the process is forcefully killed so the interface stays responsive. This applies to remote sessions and is live today.

80bc9c895dd73f9996ae18af67432e9ae1b09181.text: When you're chatting with an AI agent and it asks to use a tool, sometimes that tool call never gets answered before the conversation moves on to a new topic or a new message from you. Previously, the system would keep waiting for an answer that never comes, which could break the conversation permanently. Now, the system automatically drops those unanswered tool calls before handing the conversation history to the AI model, so leftover questions from earlier turns don't poison future replies. You'd notice this as fewer confusing errors or broken responses when an agent's tool call gets interrupted — it just moves on cleanly instead of getting stuck. This is live today across the agent runtime and shared message utilities.

603b0d994dece07838c774cb022529dee7a28f1d.text: When you tab through the referral banner in the command-line dashboard, the focused button now shows up in the app's accent color and bold instead of a leading arrow, and a fixed two-column gap keeps the label from bumping into the adjacent "Copy invite link" control. The streak row that counts your daily usage days also switched back from bullet and middle-dot marks to solid and hollow circles, so a full day and a partial day stay visually distinct at a glance. You'll notice this today whenever you open the referral banner or check your usage streak in the CLI.

a801ecf452f6262853055d6aafb484bf3a74ec3c.text: The label shown next to GPT-5.6 Luna in the model picker changed from 'Balanced' to 'Strong all-around', so you'll now see Luna described that way when choosing a model. Developers made this change in the shared settings file that powers the picker, updating the short description that appears on Luna's row. Luna remains a general-purpose premium option, and the row's existing badges (such as Images) are still what differentiate it from other all-around models. The change is live today wherever that shared settings file is used.

c0e5740f4ee47c3c7dd3fe6f890b2fc5b26b34d7.text: When you include an image in a message to the AI assistant, you can now paste either a direct web link to the picture or small inline image bytes, and the system will correctly turn it into the format the assistant expects when going through the compatibility layer. Before, sending image data this way could fail to convert properly on the new AI SDK 7 path, so the assistant wouldn't see your image; now it handles both URL links and raw image data, including a new shorthand for image file types. If you looked, you'd notice images you attach are reliably passed along instead of being dropped or misread.

c7ddc18ceedc4938f6df6f859c14e98de8ad0562.text: When you open the model picker to choose which assistant powers your chat, the premium recommended model now appears at the top of the list instead of the basic one. The picker used to show the fast-but-limited basic model first, then the deeper-reasoning premium model second; the project flipped its recommended default to the premium model on August 12, but the on-screen order never caught up until now. If you look, the first two rows in the picker have swapped places across the app, the command-line help text, and both the English and Chinese readmes, and the explanatory comment in the model list now documents that order matches that intended default-plus-fallback ranking.

d9ee7bfc3e52b9156522bc86250fc7376f9fe955.text: When you open the model picker now, the assistant that was already selected for you is the stronger one instead of the speedier one. The picker still offers both, but it will quietly switch to the speedier unlimited option if the recommended model's paid daily pool runs out, so the highlighted choice you can always click is no longer greyed out. The labels on the two models were changed to make the pairing obvious: the recommended one now calls itself the smartest, and the fast fallback calls itself smart and fast. The written guidance and the in-app hints match that ordering today.

a0a9a4c80ae8b8aba38b449aa29ad9e214633c43.text: Free users on the new "-max" model tiers (DeepSeek V4 Pro Max, DeepSeek V4 Flash Max, and GPT-5.6 Luna Max) can now run as top-level assistants instead of failing with an invalid agent error. These extended-context versions are provisioned per account rather than selected from a menu, so they won't appear in picker lists or quota displays. If you have access to one of these -max tiers, you can start a conversation with it directly; if you don't, nothing changes for you.

0d865059f023cea0d49fd9dce302ed1762f196c8.text: You will no longer get stuck on the sign-up questions page if the system fails to save your answers. Because the questions are required and can't be skipped, a broken save used to trap you in an endless loop on that screen. Now the system lets you past the page only after a save attempt has actually failed, and that temporary pass expires in a day. The form now also tells you to pick an option for any question you leave blank. This is live now and only affects sign-up flows.

bab9f2907dff6c3f090b3ba645f64c91e95e997e.text: You'll now see a new question in the signup survey asking which online services you follow for updates, and you can pick more than one answer. The list of places to choose from was also reshuffled: Instagram and TikTok are grouped under one label, Discord and newsletters were removed for now, and picking any choice that's marked 'exclusive' will automatically clear your other picks for that question. Behind the scenes, any old answers you or others gave in the past are quietly redirected to the new matching option so your past responses don't get lost or count as something different.

79d6a9de6e44b00e4d484725b74991122ae257ab.text: When you run the assistant on the free tier from a terminal, the default and 'lite' modes now use the newer base3 engine instead of the older base2 one. If you are a free-tier CLI user picking any of the standard models, your sessions will run on base3 roots starting today. This routing change is baked into the shipped CLI release, so there is no toggle for it; rolling back requires a new CLI release since the CLI has no remote kill switch like the web or cloud versions do.

e43fdc88870d851ec92b669dbba00bd5ffe17d0d.text: When a Web, Cloud, or Chat request to the assistant hits its rate limit these days, it now falls back to DeepSeek V4 Pro instead of GPT-5.6 Luna, and that's the same model those new conversations start on anyway, so the rerouted turn behaves like a normal one rather than reaching for something different. Your daily quota and access don't move: Pro sits in the same shared premium pool as the original request, and any image you send in that rerouted turn is still read because the system converts it into a written description for Pro, which only handles text. The documentation tables have been updated to reflect Pro as the default for Web, Cloud, and Chat, and Luna as the image-capable alternative. In practice you'll notice nothing about your access or limits, but if you ever land on a

fe30ebff1d8856788874e037cf2b741f95b6ead3.text: If your account was created on or after the onboarding cut-over date and you haven't finished filling out the post-signup questionnaire, running the assistant in free mode now stops with a clear message telling you to open the web app and complete setup — it no longer shows a countdown timer that resets and retries. Accounts created before the cut-over, or with no creation date on record, are permanently exempt and never see this block. The message is terminal: waiting does not clear it, and you actually have to answer the questions to continue.

b07e38d987cc4aa41a1c0fea1a2502a462f0f50f.text: People signing up for the free assistant no longer hit a hard stop if they skip or ignore the short setup survey — the signup flow can't be blocked by it anymore, and the survey is shown as a friendly one-time redirect with a Skip option instead. If you're using the free tool today, nothing looks different at first: you'll still see the quick survey appear once in your browser when you sign in, but closing it won't lock you out of using the product. Behind the scenes, the system no longer treats an unanswered survey as an error that cancels your session — it just keeps going, whether you answered, skipped, or never saw it. This applies to anyone using the free version, new and existing users alike.

4da4570dc9d90c75467c5d5541882cd919481bf0.text: Freebuff Web visitors using the platform today can now have their sessions recorded for behavior analysis, if the site operator chooses to enable it. The site owner activates this by providing a public key and an ingestion address that tells the recording tool where to send the data, and these settings only apply when configured. For most visitors nothing changes, because the feature stays off unless the key is present, and developers working locally can continue without it. This capability is live now for deployments that opt in.

364433c460916d2de22bf35956dfa0f9f5e8edff.text: When you start a task and pick how much thinking power the assistant should use, the list of strength levels now includes a new lowest option called 'minimal'. This only changes what you see in the picker: if you choose 'minimal', the assistant runs at the weakest reasoning setting the model actually supports. The underlying code already picks an appropriate default on its own, so nothing else changes unless you explicitly select the new option.

a5b6b0cf4ef9fbf7f6cf529e803601f243cd1b0f.text: If you're a Freebuff Web or Cloud user outside the main regions on the limited plan, you can now start 10 new projects per day instead of 3 or 5 — and failed project setups no longer count against that limit. The system still only lets one of your projects run an agent at the same time, so starting a second project while another is active will pause the oldest one; this stays at one until web support for multiple sessions is finished. You won't see these numbers, but you'll notice you're less likely to be blocked from making a project after a few early setup hiccups, and you'll still get a heads-up before a long-running project hands control over to a newer one.

84f4ca34cd7481a4d5bc577ebf5d7343b385650a.text: If you use the command-line tool, the text that shows up inside the highlighted call-to-action buttons (like the "Open dashboard" button) now stays consistent no matter which color theme you pick, instead of occasionally getting hard to read. The referral/promo banner also stops rearranging itself when you tab through it with your keyboard: the buttons keep a fixed width so the rest of the row doesn't jump around, and the model-pick and referral/dashboard buttons no longer overlap on narrower screens. You would notice this by the buttons behaving predictably while navigating with the keyboard and the text being clearly readable in both light and dark themes.

3a66664e54bc6ebb3dcc9dd073e45769a85d045f.text: If you download and run the assistant's standalone tool on a Linux computer that uses the musl system library (a slimmer, less common setup than the standard glibc), the tool now correctly pulls in the matching musl-native packages instead of failing mid-installation. The developer notes the musl build carries the same os/cpu pairing as its glibc sibling, and the package name simply gains a '-musl' suffix, so one target now resolves both library flavors cleanly. The fix is live for Linux musl users today, and they'll notice installation succeeds where it previously aborted with a missing-module error.

44212cc2816aedc01e2239edb193a18909727871.text: When the assistant hits a problem talking to its AI provider, you used to see a message asking you to buy credits. Now, if you are using the free version and the provider is simply out of capacity, you see a short note saying Freebuff needs to refill its provider usage and that you are not being charged. The assistant detects the provider's out-of-quota wording and shows that shared message instead of sending you to the credit purchase screen. This is live today for free users when a provider like OpenRouter or CrofAI runs out of budget.

c235ded0aec8696b8af0e9fbb9e7fe1529e8bf1f.text: When you're chatting in the CLI, the small preview of your queued messages now acts like a button: clicking it opens the full queue panel so you can edit, reorder, or delete those messages. The developers also adjusted the hint text so it only shows a 'click to expand' prompt when the preview is wide enough to display it without crowding the text. This is live today for anyone using the CLI chat interface.

90ca26c0745bcbbcd40ea7ac385c031977d328cc.text: Requests to the API are now scanned for signs that they came through a specific kind of third-party Cloudflare Worker that pools and resells free access. The platform only treats this as proof when Cloudflare itself has confirmed the request passed through its network, and it automatically logs enough detail for a reviewer to investigate any automated action, so internal tools and paid traffic are unaffected.

00e5fa83a7e86d744e826cef0021ee41b4ccce17.text: Developers building tools on top of the assistant SDK can now receive two new real-time notifications: one every time the assistant talks to the model (so they can track costs and usage per agent), and one whenever the system needs to trim the conversation history to stay within size limits. These notifications are delivered through two new optional callbacks, `onUsage` and `onCompaction`, which apps can plug into when starting a run. The compaction alert specifically fires for the main agent and includes what forced the trim and how big the limit was, and it is designed so the alert never slows down the trimming itself.

44177dad55f47ee36c17c8c98b60c95202fa9ab1.text: When you hit a free account's concurrent-tab limit, your chat tab now shows the same clear rejection message as every other surface, instead of a slightly different one that could get out of sync. The matching logic that recognizes those rejections lives in one shared place and only treats codes the CLI can actually recover from — the fatal session-loss codes and the transient ones, not Desktop's tab-only cap. Today, if you're over your concurrent-tab budget, you'll see the standard rejection notice, and a race during admission no longer produces a confusing or polluted error. The underlying rejection codes keep their waiting-room names so nothing already deployed breaks.

b9810f1556b1ad235441f5bea1278b948d119973.text: When someone tries to sign up but is blocked, the login page can now show a specific, friendly explanation tailored to the exact reason for the refusal instead of a generic error. Messages like turning off a VPN or waiting until tomorrow are now ready for the five most common refusal scenarios. The text and rules live in a shared part of the app so login pages can read them without loading heavy backend code into the browser. This is live today for new signups that hit one of the five named refusal conditions.

a6f9f6f9f36afe33900b80d4df2d61d646a8460f.text: If an AI answer gets cut off before the system receives the final usage numbers from the provider, a new safety check now fires an 'onUsageIncomplete' callback so cost and token tracking no longer silently drops that session, and the provider usage is reported exactly once. Anyone using the SDK or agent runtime to track usage and costs will now see an explicit notification instead of missing data when a stream ends unexpectedly. Developers who registered the existing usage callbacks will not see any extra duplicate reports, since the new callback only runs when the expected final usage receipt never arrives.
