ed223e710e22a010882d619831743d1c66d4ce9c.text: You may have noticed the app getting cut off or erroring out partway through a long response — especially if you're using it through a desktop or SDK integration, where network hiccups or runtime quirks (like Bun or certain Node setups) could cause the stream of words to drop suddenly instead of ending cleanly. Now, instead of crashing or losing what was already generated, the system detects that kind of interruption, treats it like a temporary network blip, saves whatever partial output you got so far, and quietly restarts from that point — so your conversation keeps going without you losing context or seeing a hard failure. This only affects scenarios where the response comes as a live stream of text and the connection gets severed mid-sentence; it doesn't change how finished answers are

4aa3d4c337e0d6424a23184465fdd0d98b1d387f.text: When the assistant checks your project's code changes, git can sometimes return gigabytes of output from huge files, which used to crash the tool with an out of memory error. Now it stops collecting that output after 10 million characters, kills the git command, and keeps whatever it gathered before the limit so you still see your changes summarized. The assistant logs when this truncation happens, and you would only notice if you were debugging because the final summary it builds still works fine. This fix is live in the software development kit today.

21e20ab6257f3141ddca47ec45624e70688a4bc1.text: When a Desktop user with multiple tabs open is blocked from starting a new session because they have too many tabs open at once, the system will no longer distinguish this specific reason from a daily or weekly usage limit. Instead of telling you "close a tab" versus "you've hit your daily limit," the rejection message now omits the specific cause. This affects Desktop users who run concurrent tabs and is already live today; you'd only notice if you were previously seeing the "close a tab" guidance and now see a more generic rate-limited message.

aff0092445df1aceda16b73f9435f9121831fa44.text: When the assistant holds a very long back-and-forth with you, it tries to save the whole conversation every few seconds into a file named chat-messages.json. If that pile of text gets too big or tangled, the save used to fail over and over, spamming error logs and silently dropping the record of your chat. Now the assistant quietly trims the worst offenders, writes a tiny side note about each chat so your list of past chats still loads, and only complains about a full disk or a weird error once every five minutes instead of every five seconds. If you ever open the folder where your chats are stored, you'll see an extra small file beside each conversation and far fewer scary red error lines piling up.

d6ec35acf28349f0742cb015e2400f5d07d83eb0.text: When you exit the CLI (via Ctrl+C, /exit, or SIGINT), the assistant now reliably releases your Freebuff slot and restores your terminal before reporting any fatal error. This happens synchronously and best-effort, skipping the normal React unmount so cleanup completes even if the interface is mid-render. You'd notice the difference if the process was about to hang: a session API request that would otherwise pin the 'Starting…' spinner for up to 300 seconds now times out after 20 seconds, allowing the exit handler to take over.

6a8bd574f8f06b5f519397bf8b066709ab784545.text: If you use the free AI chat service, you can now choose to run the DeepSeek 2.1 assistant model through a partner marketplace (OpenRouter) instead of only through its original home. This is a testing-only option that shows up as 'DeepSeek 2.1 (DeepSeek)' in the advanced settings, and it uses your existing free allocation the same way as the other models. For now you won't see any difference unless you know where to look for it, since it's still being evaluated before any wider release.

19ef71044ca314d9713b6f291ef272abbcc58724.text: The system stopped checking a setting that used to tell web containers where to run (a list of addresses you could give it). If you relied on that setting to point containers at a specific place, you would no longer get a clear error when it is missing, and you should move any such configuration elsewhere, since it is no longer part of the shared environment checks. It is live today.

de58a616b9b0ca15d0fba59c68fe8b7e19ef2fb5.text: If the assistant stops making visible progress for a while during a task, the system now quietly records a 'turn stalled' event. This only adds a monitoring signal; it does not interrupt or cancel the task, so nothing you see changes. The developer comment notes this helps distinguish a long-silent tool call that later recovers from a true hang when reviewing completed turns.

7f0aadcf9dac5265474b698062f1d51776223fd8.text: If you configure the assistant to run inside its browser-based workspace, you can now point it at more than one backup location for where the code lives; just list them as a web address, another web address, separated by a comma, and the first one you put is the one it trusts most. Each address you list still has to look like a real web link or the system will reject the setting. This only affects the shared rules that all browser workspaces follow.

c11ed01ddcbcb4bb5477850724e03e3bce8441e5.text: If you're on the verified YC founders plan (the 'god-mode' tier), the assistant can now run a new experimental model called DeepSeek 2.1 from DeepSeek, accessed directly through their OpenAI-compatible API instead of going through a middleman. You'd spot it as a new option labeled 'DeepSeek 2.1 / Direct via DeepSeek' that's hidden from the regular model picker and clearly marked as experimental. It's already live for that group today — not a public rollout — and it's the kind of behind-the-scenes plumbing that lets the team test a direct connection before deciding whether to open it up more widely.

21d02b63f7a0e4b97b0e825243a70231d24de6fc.text: The assistant can now use a new version of the GLM model that talks directly to the CrofAI provider instead of going through Fireworks. This route is only available to internal testers using god-mode access, not to regular users. If you looked, you'd see the model labeled as "GLM 5.2 (Crof)" marked as experimental, with a direct "Direct via CrofAI" connection instead of the normal referral path. This is live today for the internal testing group, isolated from the standard public model selection.

74ee22bd83306ec1e06b515b52e03e43a31b41cd.text: Starting today, Freebuff gives you six one-hour sessions per day instead of five, whether you are on the premium tier or using limited mode from outside the full-access countries. Both the daily allowance for paid (full-access) users and the daily allowance for restricted (limited/VPN) users went up by one, and the help text you see in the app and in the installation guide now matches. If you rely on referral bonuses on top of the base allowance, your new ceiling also rises, since each referral still adds one session up to a cap of three extra. You will see this right away the next time you open the app and look at your remaining sessions.

6741ac4a35ff3d5b290540a363ae19c6c5c485cf.text: Reddit now records specific retention milestones — one day, seven days, and twenty-four days — using precise calendar-day counting instead of the previous "newly crossed" logic, and the event names have been simplified to generic versions like FirstPrompt and Retention1d replacing surface-specific ones like FirstPromptCli, while email addresses used for user identification get their plus-tags and extra dots stripped before hashing to improve matching accuracy, but one field (click_id) is no longer included in the data sent to Reddit's servers.

31731d4b275ad637ad19e9531442b3f5acaa8d7f.text: When the AI assistant gets cut off mid-response or hits an output limit, it now records a cleaner, safer telemetry event so engineers can see exactly what kind of interruption happened and the most recent recovery attempt. The logging now only keeps the specific fields it expects (text values get trimmed to 200 characters, unexpected fields are dropped), and the lookup that matches interruption types uses a secure map so a stray tag like 'constructor' can't accidentally trigger a match through the code's hidden inheritance chain. This is live today across the agent runtime and SDK streaming paths, so interruption tracking works for any subscriber hitting these stream-cut sites now.

8785289028f63c9a6d0f34de8380e3de400c1f3c.text: When you open the service on a computer, the free daily quota of top-tier model sessions is now shown as a live countdown that matches what the server actually allows (including extra sessions you earned from streaks or referrals), rather than a fixed guess. The previously free MiniMax M3 model has moved into the paid-tier pool, so it now draws from that shared daily bucket instead of being unlimited. If you run out of those premium sessions while a session is ending, the screen automatically offers to continue you on the always-free DeepSeek V4 Flash instead of leaving you stuck on a model the server would reject. The model picker counter is visible even when collapsed, and a fresh daily reset time is shown based on Pacific time, so you can see when your allowance refreshes.

ff901fe20bad843eac69657fe3f446d4285af737.text: When the assistant is in the middle of answering you and the connection drops, or it runs out of space while thinking and never gives an answer, the CLI used to just stop and your turn ended incomplete. It will now silently try again for you instead, showing a small 'retrying' note, and it will keep retrying up to three times before giving up. The change affects anyone using the command-line interface today and only triggers on these specific drop-and-die moments, not on ordinary tool errors.

908988675e48fa01e64a50b5f9ac2410d06900dd.text: As you chat, helper tools that trim down your conversation (like one named context-pruner) used to sometimes leave behind leftover labels in your chat window until you got the next message back; now the app hides those tools completely, both while you're typing and when it reloads past conversations, so you won't see their names or stray tags cluttering your view. The change is live today for the CLI app and only affects what you can see during a chat session.

4b03dcbd2a7791366306ab976dba52fd9659b6d6.text: Starting today, when you send your very first message, the system can report that event to Gravity's ad-measurement service so your first-message conversions are tracked for attribution. If your browser provided Gravity pixel data, it gets sanitized and sent over, with any oversized fields cut off to protect reliability. The conversion is only recorded if Gravity accepts it on the spot—any other outcome throws an error and leaves retry handling to the calling code. The five supported surfaces are cli, desktop, web, cloud, and chat.

9262d077baa57360516b372dae789cd193f7a15a.text: If you use certain full-access models through a web browser, you'll now be limited to 6 new conversations per day, the same timezone and daily reset window used for other account limits. The command-line version of the software still lets you start as many conversations as you want, so this cap only affects browser-based use. This took effect on 2026-07-17 as part of a set of shared changes across the software.

6501764d584c609c88de49fbb649c5b5f055c3d9.text: When the assistant briefly pauses to trim away old conversation history behind the scenes, that internal step no longer floods your view with a chunk of plain-text summary. You still see a clear marker that the pause started and finished, so the interface can explain why nothing appeared to be happening. This only affects what you see during that pruning pause; all other assistant actions remain exactly as before.

35474f6bf77e51e4dbcf3773cbb0ebf5c30d6fe7.text: The CLI now stops whatever it's doing more smoothly when you switch chats or sign out. Instead of a blunt "abort everything" command, it uses a new approach that gracefully pauses and discards queued work based on the reason (like a user interrupt or logout). You would notice that switching to a new chat or resuming a previous one no longer risks overwriting the wrong transcript, and signing out cleanly halts any in-flight work before flushing analytics. This is live today and affects the CLI experience directly.

92ff02610686d5d9fc79060254e0ba759de87c76.text: When you open the Freebuff coding assistant in a terminal, the welcome screen now rearranges itself depending on how much vertical space your terminal window has. On smaller screens, it hides the decorative streak bonus message and the ASCII logo to prevent the model picker from getting cramped or spilling onto extra rows, while keeping the streak indicator's spot reserved so it still appears once a streak is active. The change is live today for anyone using Freebuff in a terminal, particularly those with shorter windows. Separately, the Kimi K2.7 Code model's brief description tagline was updated to now also say 'Best for coding & Slow', which you would notice next to that model's name in the list.

b6199c08ae729268fb8e37886fe7608ee7c7c17c.text: The assistant's free-session welcome screen now tells you whether your next batch of free sessions renews today or this week, instead of always saying 'today.' When you run low, it shows how many of your free sessions came from your base allowance versus referral sign-ups versus an active streak, so it's clearer why your total limit is what it is. This matters if your account resets on a weekly schedule rather than a daily one.

e78563f1e523d46e46a3234eeb84bb3e77cb9b4b.text: When you navigate between your chat history and the main chat in the CLI, the conversation now stays exactly where you left it instead of restarting or reloading. The program now keeps track of your chat session separately from the conversation itself, so moving around doesn't wipe out what was happening. Also, if you open a chat with a pre-typed message, it will only send once and won't accidentally resend if the chat reloads for any reason.

94f0f052111d7430d1cc973c9653333d045e5f6d.text: Right now, when you chat with the MiMo 2.5 Pro assistant on this platform, it will no longer try to look at images you upload. The developers discovered that this specific version of MiMo only works with text, so sending pictures to it was causing errors; they flipped a setting so pictures are simply not sent anymore. The list of assistants that can see images is now built straight from the same place the assistant definitions live, which means any assistant newly added or removed will automatically be included or excluded from image-handling without requiring a manual update. Finally, there’s a new helper function that returns an unknown answer for assistants the system hasn’t verified yet; until they confirm whether a brand-new or paid assistant accepts images, those assistants will

6655cc5ad6e660c64cbca9251ef019eecf59dde9.text: When you're running a conversation and the chat window gets removed from the screen — like when a gate or transition temporarily unmounts it — the program used to forget that the assistant was still working in the background. That made the status bar flip back to idle even though the conversation was still going. Now the app keeps a separate, shared record of which conversation is actually running, so your screen shows that the assistant is still thinking and you can still cancel it, instead of acting like everything already finished.

4ccefe89dc731502797440fa56faa60e1417f9eb.text: When you're chatting with the assistant and pick a model, the app now checks whether that model is one of the officially supported ones in a faster, simpler spot behind the scenes, without looping back through the old model-setup code that sometimes got stuck in a circular import. You won't see this change yourself, but it means the part of the app that decides which models you can use and how they behave is now a bit more reliable and easier for the team to maintain, especially for the referral and billing flows. It's live today as part of this update.

16931ade9e64c9e5a453642da335cf4b08ed6093.text: If you use more than one Freebuff session at the same time, the app can now show you exactly when each session started and when it ends. The change adds the model name and two timestamps to the session information, so multi-session clients display the active window instead of a flat status. No one sees a difference today unless their client already asks for that detail.

ea226cb387463c614ad636bf2fa368cca721099c.text: When you ask an assistant to look up documentation on a library like Next.js or MongoDB, it now pulls from an updated documentation service (API v2) and is more careful about how much text it pulls at once. The amount of text it can bring back by default has been cut from 20,000 to 10,000 words, and if you ask for a really tiny amount (under 10,000) it no longer secretly boosts it back up to 10,000. The assistant is also stricter about what you have to provide: empty or vague search terms are now rejected, and numbers like how much text to return must be positive whole amounts. If you look at the results you'll see shorter, more precise excerpts that are less likely to cut off in the middle of a word, and the system will no longer quietly ignore what you typed if it's sloppy.

1328a3f288ed36e8ee37a3aac1b8ca1efff52cd6.text: The app now keeps two stable model names (DeepSeek V4 Flash and MiniMax M3) in a separate, dependency-free file so that browser code can safely import them without pulling in server-only configuration. If you look at the code, those identifiers appear once in the new file and are re-exported from the original module for backward compatibility. The change is in place today and does not alter which models are selectable; it only fixes a build-time type error in the desktop renderer that occurred when those IDs were defined alongside server-side model config. The effect you would notice is that the waiting-room model selector continues to work with the same two options, and the desktop build no longer fails to type-check on import.

e8c2211146a5a3fd3718e8dee4825c4757e60986.text: The desktop app is adding new tracking signals to monitor what happens to its background helper processes during shutdown and startup. Specifically, it now records when interrupted work sessions get cleanly stopped at quit time, when leftover processes from a previous crashed session get cleaned up at launch, and when interrupted turns are automatically resumed by the recovery system. These are silent telemetry events that report back to the development team so they can measure how often users encounter stuck background processes in the field. The tracking infrastructure is now in place alongside existing desktop analytics.

1b952b35d6dac171d48c8e0fd7daf70c873a40b5.text: The app now records a one-time event each time it runs to report which command-line tool (codex) it manages to locate, or the reason it couldn't find one. This event is always sent without sampling, so it happens for everyone using the packaged desktop app. You wouldn't see this directly, but it helps the developers know whether the app is successfully finding codex installations on users' machines, especially when they can't see the usual startup messages in the terminal. This is live today and actively being tracked.

ef2019f26ece398825b6dbe8451e9b5aec3be563.text: If you start a new free session in the app, you might now see a message saying you've hit today's spending cap, instead of the usual rate-limit message. This only affects brand-new sessions: any session you already started, or a reconnect to one you're in the middle of, keeps working. Behind the scenes, the app now recognizes a second kind of cap (a daily provider budget) and treats it the same way as the old per-user limit when it blocks a new session.

c931d187e9c094739c6acc86ec1c583dc9319d51.text: When a trusted service account runs an assistant on your behalf through the SDK, it can now pass along your specific user identity so the run is counted against your account instead of the service account's. You would only notice this if you are already running assistants via a trusted service account and inspect the run headers or attribution — an extra identifier is sent and the SDK prefers your requested identity over the authenticated one. Ordinary API keys are unchanged: this delegation is available only to trusted service accounts, as the code comments state, so your access and billing attribution are unaffected unless you are in that trusted-service flow.

ed5c777e9ea95739a4f2484a600d096304e6a3e3.text: A behind-the-scenes note in the code that describes how streak rewards work has been reworded for clarity. The change does not alter any actual behavior — users and systems still see the same thing today. You would not notice any difference in how rewards are given; only someone reading the code would see the clearer wording.

5b05edcad1c49dbfae18bb40a3a8026b8b5673c6.text: Starting today, the weekly AI session bonus for your referral streak now activates automatically each Monday Pacific time and turns off immediately if your streak breaks. Previously, you only got a new bonus session once every 7 days on exact milestone dates. Now, if you've been active for at least 7 consecutive days, you'll see your weekly bonus refill every Monday as long as that 7-day streak stays unbroken. This affects users on the full-access plan who maintain a qualifying referral streak, and you'll notice the bonus counting resets at the start of each Pacific week rather than landing on specific milestone days.

191fd58e6fbdcd4f428da59d556490c152d2361f.text: When the assistant trims down a long chat to fit a size limit, it now quietly records how much it cut and why, sending those numbers only to its internal monitoring system and skipping the general analytics pipeline. If you watch system logs, you'd see a new stream of trimming reports that include counts like dropped message entries and cache gaps, but these won't show up in any product analytics dashboards. This keeps infrastructure metrics separate from user-behavior tracking, so only operators see the extra detail.

10fb028c168f112636f95dc76cc992a67819940e.text: When you ask the assistant to read several files at once, it now stops at a combined size limit — the total returned text can't exceed about 20,000 words or 100,000 characters, whichever comes first. Previously each file got its own cap, so requesting a handful of large files could easily return far more than the system could process comfortably. If you request more than the new shared budget allows, the tool trims whole files from the end of the list and skips any duplicate file paths, so you get the smallest set that still fits. This keeps responses reliable and fast, especially with repetitive or Unicode-heavy content, and it's live now.

d24c97e0aa12993c710b9495edbe6315550f9910.text: The assistant now uses the same fake browser address book-wide when it asks ad providers for relevant ads, instead of each native app (like the CLI) making up its own. This means if you run the assistant on a Mac, you'll send a consistent desktop Chrome browser identity to ad networks, just like everyone else on a Mac does, rather than sending a technical runtime label like "Bun/version" that ad networks might flag as a bot. The shared browser identity is already in place today across native clients, and it picks the right operating system variant automatically, falling back to a Linux-style identity if your platform isn't specifically mapped.

4e24162fc7e8d8a5ebc827b26c3afc48c6ed057f.text: When a long-running chat hits the token limit, the assistant trims the conversation history to make room, but now it does the trimming in two separate boxes: one for what you typed and one for all the assistant/tool replies. Previously, filling up one box would spill over and start deleting entries from the other; today, exhausting your message budget won't drop the assistant's replies, and overflowing the assistant's budget won't erase your prompts. The most recent message is also explicitly kept even if it alone exceeds its box's limit, replacing the old blank-summary fallback, so the last thing you said or the assistant answered is never silently lost.

a793b16ecd43ca8d61e002222b2c9f8f8614880b.text: The GLM referral banner (the card that promotes referral bonuses and account linking) now scrolls together with the list of models inside the model selector's scrollbox. You'll notice that when you arrow through the model picker with your keyboard, the referral banner's copy and Open buttons are now part of the same navigation flow instead of being handled by a separate focus system. The referral banner only renders inside the selector when there's space available, and on short terminals a single scrollbar controls both the models and the referral card. Additionally, when a referral is present, the landing screen no longer promotes the full ASCII logo, keeping vertical space for the scrollable menu.

7dbf452bebddc6dd0ea8d46809d425a182a44753.text: If you're a Freebuff Web user in a limited region who picks models from the free panel, the "KAT Coder Pro V2" coding-test option is gone from your list today. It was a premium, experimental model that has since been deprecated upstream, so the developers removed it from the shared pool of models your region uses; every other model on the free panel remains geographically restricted as before. The accompanying code comments reference a July 9 incident where trial runs of this model failed to spawn, explaining why it's being pulled entirely rather than just hidden for some users.

9ef7e7f28943c8ab971309b595bafd08d00d7b3a.text: When the program downloads itself to your computer, it can now connect through the kind of intermediary server offices often use to filter web traffic, and if that download gets interrupted, it picks up where it left off instead of starting over or keeping a broken file. If a downloaded package turns out to be incomplete or unreadable, the program treats it as corrupted and downloads it fresh rather than trying to resume what wasn't fully there. People running the installer behind restrictive network setups will get the proxy support right away, while anyone whose download fails partway through will notice the installer no longer leaves a half-written file behind.

ae87d9cee86c3c4665a0447b4c8cef653c739b76.text: When you chat with the assistant and a response streams in, small banner ads used to be fetched in one big batch of eight before your reply. Now the system first collects a smaller, capped pool of four unique ads, only showing them once they've fully loaded, and then quietly cycles through that same stable set to fill each available ad slot—so you still get ads woven between your reply sections, just without waiting on a large upfront load. The ad slots now turn on or off based on how many response sections you have (every two sections earns one non-trailing slot), and the team added two new usage stats that record when an inline ad slot became eligible and when a previously built ad pool got reused. This is live today: the desktop client now reads these helpers from the shared package, so

739b605e24c6307c71c81c8323b3f38563a76ec1.text: The lightweight helper assistants in your toolkit are now powered by Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite instead of the earlier preview version. If you use an agent that runs quick file lookups, web research, terminal commands, or browser tasks, it is now calling up the stable release rather than the trial build, which should make those small jobs a bit more reliable day to day. The same model is also now the recommended default for the budget-friendly agents, so both free and low-cost workflows get the steadier version.

464115e810f97affdcebc6f7e5485d3664c6956c.text: Starting July 11, 2026, when you switch chats in the CLI (using commands like /new or /resume), any in-progress conversation with the assistant is immediately stopped before the switch happens. This prevents the previous conversation from accidentally saving its notes or progress into the new chat's folder, which used to overwrite parts of the new conversation. You'd notice this because interrupted conversations no longer leave behind confusing or corrupted text in your new chats.

4beca76c6485fa3c57a3716650a0eecd996044b4.text: If you sign up for signup credits using a Google account instead of a GitHub account, you will not receive the one-time free credit grant of 500 credits, because signup credits are now limited to GitHub-first users whose account is older than four calendar months. When you look at the signup flow, you will notice that Google-first signups simply do not qualify for the signup credit, while GitHub accounts under four months old also do not qualify, though this rule is now in place and ready to be enforced.

47ef2af4ac5eb7f77c5ae2be02f77801fabf9490.text: You are using the Freebuff CLI (the command-line tool that runs DeepSeek in your terminal) and it sometimes shows small ads inline as you read responses. The developers added quiet, behind-the-scenes measurement that records when an inline ad slot is available for a response and only when that response runs short of ads and has to reuse its small pool of four ads. This data is sampled, meaning only a fraction of eligible slots are counted, and it is designed so it can never slow down or break ad fetching. As a result, when you sit in a long conversation with Freebuff CLI and your reply needs more ad slots, you might see a fifth ad pulled from a reused pool, and the tool is now watching that behavior to understand how long responses get. This is live today for Freebuff CLI users and

879cc9e68d329f65c252f1f1473f5d0b37dccd15.text: When an AI model uses certain reasoning services, it can sometimes send back empty thinking blocks that accidentally end its turn early. The system now cleans up these leftover thinking markers in one consistent place, so the assistant treats them as internal scratch work and keeps going instead of stopping. This is a behind-the-scenes code cleanup with no visible effect on how the assistant behaves; it only makes the handling of these markers more reliable for developers building on top of it.

2f0296cf9937bb0bc0256849868e81c193f0f472.text: When you chat with the free CLI, ads now load only as needed for spots the renderer actually needs, instead of fetching a fixed batch of eight ads up front for every prompt. As a result, longer answers reuse a smaller pool of four ads (repeated as needed) rather than always pulling a fresh eight, so there are fewer unused ad requests. The rotating banner ad above the input stays on its own placement for reporting, while inline response ads use the new CLI-Chat-Inline placement. This is live today for free CLI users.

c4c5dcd66aaa42cd023a0ad0c146feacf180ebc9.text: If you keep using this tool every day for a week (7-day streak) and continue through the next day, you now get one extra session added to your daily session count every single day, instead of only receiving a bonus once per week when your streak hit a multiple of seven. The weekly bonus of one GLM 5.2 session for people with full access still only arrives on the exact 7th, 14th, 21st day, etc. You are most likely to notice this because the wording in your app will switch from "each week you keep it up" to "every day you keep it up" once your streak reaches 7 days. This change is live today.

8e3f104307089d0da674ad22011f2114b5bcf71d.text: If you're using the SDK on a Windows computer and the program launches a terminal window (for example, when it tries to run something in the background), it now quietly tells a helper named MSYS to turn off a modern display mode called ConPTY. That mode was causing Git Bash (a common terminal tool) to pop up a visible window even when the program asked for it to stay hidden, so this change keeps your screen from flashing that window and also makes sure any other settings you already configured for that helper are still kept intact. The change is live today and applies automatically whenever the program starts a shell command on Windows.

bc264d00cf190d86d2953e9937afc68c3b371446.text: If you start a free trial run in your browser, the assistant can now use three more helper tools (hy3, hy3-atlas, and kat-coder-pro-v2) without the system blocking it, fixing the failures that happened on July 9. The model picker in the browser can also now show you the real-time count of how many free sessions you have left by requesting zero-usage quota snapshots, so the "N of M sessions" labels are accurate without making your CLI response heavier.

1d64a9f44880ccf58e335af1efb24a93ec923831.text: When you switch away from or back to the CLI's terminal window, other keystrokes or pasted text sometimes got mistaken for focus changes, causing the screen to flicker or go dim at the wrong time. The program now looks for the exact focus codes (ESC [ I for focus gained, ESC [ O for focus lost) and only acts on them, ignoring unrelated bytes that happen to share the same chunk. It also remembers the last focus state it acted on, so a terminal that repeats the same focus message won't trigger repeated screen updates. This fix is live today in the CLI for anyone running it on a terminal that supports focus reporting.

e1ce92184215843f83e268d758011594a4a0c8a5.text: You know that frustrating moment when you're deep in a long back-and-forth with the assistant and it suddenly freezes mid-response while it "saves a checkpoint"? That freeze happened because the system was painstakingly copying your entire session — every message, every step — just to snapshot it, which is slow on big sessions. Now it only copies the essential parts using a much faster method, cutting that wait from a quarter of a second down to a few milliseconds, so the pause you felt is gone or nearly imperceptible. It's live today whenever you run a long session that hits its 5-second checkpoint save.

33192e18252182b6f101ffe9191d2da5fb230c57.text: You can once again pick Kimi K2.7 Code as a model inside Freebuff's free tier. Developers had hidden it after the older version (Kimi K2.6) stalled on its first token, but the new K2.7 Code version is served by a pinned provider that avoids those stalls, so it reappeared in the list of free models and the docs now describe it as best for coding. If you open the free model picker or ask an agent to review your code with Kimi, the assistant will now use Kimi K2.7 Code instead of the previous version.

758fdbfedc1bd8c31dee38e5fdf17ae71b7cb67c.text: When you use the command-line tool for a long conversation, it periodically saves your chat so you don't lose it. That save used to happen on the same thread that shows your messages and takes your keystrokes, so during long chats the screen would freeze for a moment every few seconds while the entire chat was written to disk. Now those periodic saves happen in the background, so the tool keeps responding to your typing without stalling, and the final save when the chat ends still runs the safe older way to guarantee nothing is lost.

4afa065433a1f7c99574755052324ab24fc7bd1c.text: You can now choose a new AI model called HY3 from the model menu when using the assistant in a web browser. The developers added HY3 and a related version (HY3 Atlas) to the list of models visible on web-only surfaces, but left them out of the shared lists used by the desktop and command-line apps, so they show up only on the web side for now during a quiet, staged rollout.

d0de3f5b1cbd70534b9d6c36f0dfc9c77ae8f92b.text: When you open the model picker, three of the paid models now show a TEST badge so you know they're still being tested and might act unpredictably. The same picker also gained a new event that records when a logged-out visitor on the /cloud page clicks a 'Continue with GitHub' or 'Connect your repo' button, letting the team measure how often people intend to sign up. This tracking is already wired up and will fire today; the TEST badge is also live as soon as the picker is shown to anyone with access to those models.

bd3b19ed76cf17a16e45df2e329ee5e84b7b6883.text: When you run a terminal command through the assistant, it now always launches the command in its own separate process group instead of only doing so on non-Windows systems. This means that on Windows, the command no longer attaches to the same console as the terminal you're using, preventing background programs (like cmd, pause, or choice) from stealing keyboard and mouse input meant for the assistant's interface and printing garbled escape sequences over the display. If you look at the terminal while running such commands, the interface should no longer show stray text or become unresponsive when the command times out or is cancelled.

0deed0f9ae60e3d338e71d7077fe4180e21277f4.text: When the command-line tool starts a hidden background process that resets your terminal window on Windows, it no longer hides its instructions inside a secret scrambled code that some security scanners flag as suspicious. Instead it now sends those instructions as readable text, so if you ever peeked at the running process you'd see plain words instead of a long string of random-looking characters. As part of that, the tool also makes sure it won't accidentally leave behind a stale cleanup file when the background process fails to start. This is live today for anyone using the command-line tool on Windows.

d049aa594eaa6ffe79276ee9358921814f6e3077.text: You're building an AI assistant that can spawn helper sub-agents. The system now lets you launch those helpers inline (during a turn) instead of only at setup time, using new inline or programmatic spawn paths. If you tried to configure a template with spawnableAgents but no 'spawn_agents' tool, it previously failed validation; it now accepts 'spawn_agent_inline' or a handleSteps generator as valid alternatives. This is live today for templates that define spawnable agents, and the clearer error message tells you exactly which spawning option to add.

a4b9f8de17a56af3e9a90753bcdfe9858f9a3a4d.text: When you use Freebuff through a web browser or cloud service, a new safety check now makes sure you're only connected to the specific session models you're allowed to access, so you can't accidentally end up in someone else's workspace. Three new AI assistants (HY3, HY3 Atlas, and Kat Coder Pro V2) are now available for selection in your free desktop and agent lists. Behind the scenes, a secure, invisible header is added for the website's internal communication that prevents regular users or browsers from posing as someone else to peek into private sessions, and this protection is only used by the Codebuff API when it's acting on behalf of the Freebuff Web service.

0a6df5765585fe3da17d92272fbce28be74bc127.text: When you're chatting with the assistant and you're on the free plan, small ads now appear in between the answer blocks as the assistant writes them, instead of just one static ad below the whole conversation. The ad that rotates above your typing box stays where it is and works separately, but now the system picks fresh ads for each message you send based on what you asked. You'd notice ads showing up at different spots within the assistant's response as it streams, and how many appear grows with how long the answer is. This is live now for free users and subscribers without a paid account.

f0d966458519ffa59de0fbce27fad27f0ac7a047.text: The separate worker that ran your agent tasks (like generating code or reasoning) outside of the main app has been removed. For you as a user, there's no change: your agents still run normally through the Convex platform, and nothing is broken today. If you looked under the hood, you'd see one whole folder called 'freebuff/runner' has been deleted — it contained a standalone service that used to claim queued jobs and stream results back over HTTP. That service is gone, but its on/off switch still exists in the configuration; it's just unused now.

e40725574901bc9196b956db9113351627654769.text: The free assistant that helps you write code now uses only the newer MiniMax M3 model instead of the older M2.7 variant. If you use the free or lite mode, you are seeing the updated MiniMax M3 model being used automatically, and the older M2.7 model support has been completely removed from the system. The change is live today for all free and lite users, and behind the scenes it removes outdated model configurations and a separate reviewer agent that was built specifically for the old model.

f7828c2c4b5a55de46b00f0484ed047e091d0964.text: If you send a Freebuff, Codex, or Claude Code request, it no longer runs on Convex's built-in compute. Instead it is picked up by a dedicated, always-on worker that was just added as a separate package. That worker needs your deployment and service-account keys to be running before the new code path turns on by default, otherwise your requests queue up for ten minutes and then get cleaned out with nothing processing them. From your perspective the request still arrives the same way, but the assistant's response now streams back through the worker rather than through Convex's temporary action process.

c59bde7fe2f90f0e25b0ce36a1d8856ec8ccfa5f.text: Ads now appear inside your chat, spaced between completed answers rather than all in one banner at the bottom. If you are a free user or on the freebuff plan, you will see a single ad slot drop right after the assistant finishes answering (for example, after your first answer, then every few answers after) instead of a rotating banner. The change is live today for CLI "waiting room" ad viewers and inline "cli_chat" ad viewers, using the same placement API the server expects. The terminal watchdog that restores your screen now also runs on Windows via PowerShell.

778ce13d412dcf87de7eec8b2732d27aa9c35c3a.text: The way the software counts how much text and images fit into a single conversation turn with the AI has gotten more accurate. When you chat with the assistant, it now estimates the token cost of your messages—especially any screenshots or images you attach—using a flat per-image charge and a small overhead per message, instead of guessing based on the raw text length of the image data. This means the system will make better decisions about when your message history is getting too long and needs to be trimmed, and it won't overcount the size of images you send. The change is live today in the agent runtime that powers the assistant's step-by-step reasoning.

2a0165cd6654c96138ebf48279da6271d3edb8d9.text: If you use the agent runtime, the assistant can now correctly send certain input schemas to Anthropic models that previously failed because a required field was missing, null, or empty. The system now treats those invalid values as if they were absent and automatically adds the required field, preventing API errors during schema conversion. This fix is live today and applies whenever the runtime converts input schemas for Anthropic-compatible models.

5ab9f24e10c3cafc301fe1eb3838c0c54008806f.text: When the assistant asks the token-counting service how many words are in your tools, it now sends the tool definitions with a clean JSON-Schema description, avoiding a previous format that included technical clutter that inflated the count and made a few tool types fail entirely. This makes the token counts that the system uses to manage the length of your conversation noticeably more accurate and keeps the agent runtime from breaking mid-task when those tools are involved.

dc8f236d73ec651b392b4dbb09a8826258f12666.text: When you use the free assistant for the first time, whether through the command-line tool, the website, or the chat interface, the system now quietly tells Reddit's advertising tools about that conversion, but only if the company has set up its paid-advertising access token and only sends over anonymized data like a hashed email - no personal details. For command-line users specifically, the assistant also tracks whether you come back after one day, one week, or twenty-four days, sending those retention milestones to Reddit as well, and each milestone notification happens at most once per user. None of these notifications block your experience or cause errors - if the advertising setup isn't configured, the system simply skips recording the event, and nothing breaks if a network hiccup

10ec4e5ad003a6c5bd72ba98ad322469581d3d69.text: Tools like the assistant's file reader, directory browser, and code search can now look at any file or folder on your computer, not just the ones inside your main project folder. If you point one of these tools at a location outside the project, checks that normally hide private files (like your app's secret settings) are automatically skipped for that location only. This is already live, so anything that already asked for an outside path will suddenly work instead of being blocked.

bd166f455bc3bee08e35e0cc212e4da6fbbe4f15.text: If your internet connection hiccups for just a moment during a conversation with the assistant (like a dropped call that reconnects), the request now automatically retries instead of failing completely. This applies to anyone running agent steps or using the SDK's run function, which now recognize these specific 'socket closed' or 'connection refused' errors and treat them as temporary, triggering the built-in retry logic that was previously ignoring them. You would notice fewer failures and shorter interruption messages guiding you to check your network, as the system now handles these brief connection blips silently in the background.

f8b3b17b3ed642b2fb5d7bea14d33db9aa340651.text: The terminal app renamed its internal code labels for the screen you see while waiting around before free usage starts, but the thing you actually experience didn't change. When your free session ends and you're kicked back to pick a new model, this screen now appears with the same buttons and ads as before, because it's still the same place where multiple ads are shown in a row to keep the space filled. The system still tells the ad server it's showing the old name in the request so placements don't break, and nothing about how or when ads load or how long the streak countdown shows changed.

7f595c4c0634c855c18f0cfb325c173392e3bd61.text: The CLI tool no longer shows 'You are in the waiting room' or 'You are next in line' messages when starting up. Instead, if your free session is still initializing during a brief race condition, it now simply says 'Your free session is still being set up. Try again in a moment.' and automatically retries. This affects anyone running the CLI who might have encountered those old waiting-room messages, which were removed from both the startup checks and the testing helpers. The underlying behavior of admitting sessions immediately remains the same; only the user-facing text changed.

3d1a8e68f275183a92cfbb5100a2528bd5ce4c79.text: When you run the command-line tool and something crashes hard enough that the program can't clean up after itself (like losing power), your terminal could be left in a broken state where things like your mouse and keyboard behave strangely. Now, a separate helper process watches in the background and, if the main program dies unexpectedly, it automatically sends reset commands to fix your terminal settings, including newer keyboard shortcut modes. If the program shuts down normally, it stops the helper first so it won't interfere, and the escape sequences that fix your terminal are now stored in one shared place so they stay consistent across different parts of the system.

cee618d4b5a9d00053d9955262595b276fd7ea1e.text: When your free session runs out, the assistant used to keep trying to send your queued messages to a server that would just reject them. Now those messages pause and wait instead of getting rejected one by one. They automatically start sending again as soon as your session becomes active again, so you don’t lose anything you queued up before the session ended.

030a4c60e51b5da6ad04a6ac3e3470a7ce53b874.text: Web visitors now land on the chat page and may see a different style of advertisement being tested alongside the chat interface. The system quietly records when the ad experiment is shown and when an ad is actually displayed, tagging each record with which version a visitor saw, so the team can later compare whether visitors notice and click the ads. No on-screen appearance, message, button, or layout changes are visible to visitors today; only the behind-the-scenes counting was added.

f65992d39adda73162606b55c07b364ca8afa181.text: You are a user running the assistant from a command-line terminal. When the terminal tries to connect to your account session and the server is slow or unresponsive, the "Starting..." spinner on the landing screen would hang for a long time with no way to recover. Now the terminal stops waiting after 20 seconds, logs the issue internally, and automatically tries connecting again on a shorter retry schedule, so the spinner no longer gets stuck indefinitely while it waits for a response.

8151087175d6205542190ed092126bdd19ae4130.text: When a Freebuff session ends unexpectedly — for example, the server reclaims your slot between the moment your message is pulled from the queue and the moment it begins actually running — your prompt is now placed back at the front of the queue instead of being silently dropped as if it had been sent. If the rejected message had not yet produced any streamed output (meaning the prompt was consumed but never processed), you now see a plain inline error explaining the prompt was dropped, rather than the chat simply appearing to hang or look sent. If the run had already begun producing content, you still get the quieter banner-style notice. Additionally, when the system holds queued messages because the Freebuff session is gone, it logs that transition exactly once instead of repeating the

671c093077dc5cd74ab2b1892c7c134d84c8fbd8.text: When you open your past chats in the CLI, it now loads faster because it reads a small summary file instead of the full chat transcript. Your complete conversation history is no longer cut off at 100 messages, so long chats are kept in full. You won't see any visual changes, but your oldest messages won't get silently dropped anymore.

4f5a72d6b85c9521b28248e359c11719cf6d55c4.text: Logging across the platform is now unified: services emit logs through a single shared helper that formats and size-limits log data, so queries behave consistently whether a log came from the long-running sink or from Convex. Log payloads are capped in size to prevent runaway data from inflating ingest costs, and circular references no longer crash logging. The `MESSAGE_SENT` analytics event documentation was clarified to include 'cloud' as a valid surface and to list all emission points (cli, chat stream, desktop module, and the Convex send mutation). Live today for codebuff's internal logging pipeline.

77cfee986c1b3e6fd7fffc5b37bb7c4028a30446.text: When you use the assistant's tools (searching code, reading a web page, or running a terminal command), you can now press Ctrl+C or otherwise interrupt the task, and it will stop immediately instead of running to completion. The interruption works across the whole chain of processes, including any program those tools start, so nothing is left running in the background after you cancel. If you looked, you would see tool calls return a short message saying the run was aborted, and on Linux or macOS those commands are started in their own group so the cancellation reliably ends them and their child processes, with a 1.5-second grace period before a hard kill.

85ccc41bab5e0ee15d2cd97f2230055f4f2984b2.text: When you use the desktop version of the assistant on the free-limited plan, opening a second session tab now closes the first one automatically instead of letting both run — the same one-tab rule that already applied to paid models now applies to every model for limited-plan users. If a limited-plan user tries to open a second tab while one is already active, they'll see a clear message telling them to close a tab (rather than being told they've hit a daily limit), because the system can now distinguish a concurrent-tab block from a usage-quota block. This behavior is enforced through a single shared rule used by the server, so the desktop client and the server stay in sync about who can have which tab open at any given time.

effaebabd70b475f18cd90481cc6cbc88c5ff9e3.text: When you type a message to the assistant in the terminal and the program crashes or your terminal closes before it finishes, your message and any partial work the assistant had done will no longer be lost. Behind the scenes, the system now saves your conversation to your computer the moment you hit send, and keeps updating that saved copy as the assistant works and thinks out loud. When you restart, the conversation reappears exactly where it left off, with a small note explaining that the assistant was interrupted before it could finish.

b10e9ab1644601375492fa771f2acd2088b27429.text: When the assistant thinks out loud and then makes a tool call (like using a calculator or looking something up), those two parts used to be sent as separate messages, which caused newer models like DeepSeek to reject the request because the reasoning and the action were split. Now, the system sticks the reasoning and the tool call onto the same message so the model sees them together, like writing your thought process directly above the step you take. If you use a DeepSeek reasoning model, conversations that involve tool use should stop failing during validation. This fix is live today for anyone using the OpenAI-compatible chat converter.

a07d73d1f0bdd5f9c47d64423d3837d59bcb2309.text: When the Codebuff helper library runs on a cloud server instead of your own computer, it now figures out which online service to talk to at the moment it needs to, rather than being permanently pointed at a test address baked in when the program was assembled. This stops cloud-hosted tools from trying to contact an address that only works on a developer's laptop. If a deployment sets its own address, that one is used; otherwise it falls back to the built-in one.

d304465cf1503c0d27dc79e6ffaf252657fe922c.text: Desktop app users who see sponsored ads in their conversation will now have those ad views and clicks recorded. The app now tracks when an ad appears on screen and when you tap it, sending that information through the analytics system. This lets the team measure how often people see and interact with ads shown right inside the transcript.

e6af6ff08ba0ed02b362aae22b208e554fd5f74a.text: When you build a custom assistant workflow that runs special logic steps, the system now keeps that live step-function in memory next to the version it converts to text. This stops crashes where the text-only copy referenced code that wasn't available after being bundled and minified, which previously caused confusing 'ReferenceError' messages during in-process execution. Nothing changed for assistants saved to databases or disk, since the live function is automatically excluded during serialization.

b88380a4c48c5a1dfe12d788f62d794c5df7db57.text: When you save a chat, it's now written the safe way (write to a temp file, then swap it in), so a crash mid-save can no longer leave you with a half-written conversation. If the chat file does show up broken, it will now appear in your history list as unreadable, so it won't silently disappear, and you can still delete it; selecting it just shows a status message instead of trying to open it. Starting a new chat or running /clear now also rotates to a fresh chat id, preventing the new conversation from overwriting the previous one's directory. These changes are live today.

55f61ffc60b73ecdfb31f8d649e85e4ff3086c0b.text: When you open the app and see the screen where you pick which model to use, a small 'invite friends' message now appears for people on the limited plan. Instead of offering weekly GLM reward sessions (which is what full-plan people see), the limited-plan version quietly tells you that referring friends earns you one extra free session per day, and shows how many you have earned so far. The app already checks your plan type to decide which version to show, so the banner no longer gets squeezed or overlaps other text when the limited-plan version appears.

b4989d0c77187ca908ff2417b1dfd4e68be25818.text: Your terminal can now keep the referral banner and its bordered buttons from getting squished into the text above when the window is short. The fix tells the landing layout to hold its height so the copy button and the "Use GLM 5.2" card stay spaced out instead of overlapping the lines next to them. You would see the banner sit cleanly under the status line instead of its border bleeding into the row above. This is live today for the full-tier landing screen.

0eb5e08fac20277f02c9f486b6176610e73431da.text: Starting today, free-level Web users outside the main regions can only create one new project per day. The limit resets at midnight Pacific time, so if you hit it, wait until the next day to start another project. This is a temporary cap meant to manage demand, and it only applies to the limited-tier Web users, not paid or full-access accounts.

c7df706d4a2306da3d645b3d5091a718f0b057bc.text: When you've kept up a 7-day streak (a full week), a short note now appears under the streak counter in the waiting room, telling you that you earn a recurring reward each week you keep the streak going — one extra session, and if you have full access, one GLM session too. The note only shows up once a week is reached and disappears below that, so it doesn't clutter the screen for shorter streaks. It's live today for anyone on the CLI landing screen with a 7+ day streak, and it accurately tracks whether the GLM part is actually available (the extra GLM session only appears if the program is fully enabled, so the note never promises something that can't be used).

a60a6abccdfcbbe6d3a72c17ed86dbc03810876a.text: When you're typing a slash command and several matches pop up, pressing Tab now drops the highlighted command straight into your input so you can keep typing (like adding extra parameters for a skill) instead of cycling through the options — you now use the arrow keys to move between suggestions, and Enter to pick one and send it. If you use Freebuff every day and keep a streak going, hitting a 7-day milestone (7, 14, 21 days, and so on) now automatically grants you one extra session in your main pool — full-access subscribers get a premium session plus a weekly GLM 5.2 session, while limited-access subscribers just get the daily limited session — and these bonuses are available today, with a single on/off switch and a separate switch to toggle just the GLM perk if the providers want to

92a719efa08071eb2c6f0eb67079416304201adb.text: If you use the desktop app, your activity now shows up in the company's usage reports alongside web and mobile users. Previously, only about 1 in 100 desktop app actions were being recorded to save computing resources. Now, every time you launch the app, log in, start a new conversation, open a project, or switch models, that action is fully tracked rather than randomly sampled out. This ensures the analytics team can actually see how people are using the desktop app, since only a small number of people use it compared to the website.

15c9fe6c7e7bff8436ca2e3f48cb699de7d56c55.text: When you use Freebuff Desktop in multi-session mode, you can now only run one premium model at a time per account — like DeepSeek V4 Pro or MiniMax M3 — but you can still open as many tabs as you want of the free models like DeepSeek V4 Flash. If you try to start a second premium session, the system will stop you and tell the desktop app to switch you to a free model or close the tab. This only affects the desktop app; web and command-line users, who already get one session at a time, are unchanged. The change is live today for anyone using Freebuff Desktop's multi-session mode.

454dcd2c72790576154d4ed6cc68d96bf47dad96.text: The assistant can now accept new instructions mid-conversation without stopping, so a program running the assistant can feed it fresh input while it's still working and have it respond to that input in the very next step instead of waiting until the current task finishes. If you were watching, you'd see the conversation continue seamlessly with your new question appended as a normal user message, rather than the assistant halting and restarting. This is available to hosts that pass in the new steering option when starting a run.

9e61e4b90860c77829c87b675c5a7f002276ef9d.text: The assistant now handles it when one of its outside tools (like a database helper or document reader) quietly fails to start. Instead of stopping everything and showing a confusing message, it will tell you which tool had the problem and why — showing the real reason it couldn't connect rather than just saying the connection closed. You can keep working with your other tools while it figures out what went wrong with the one that failed.

8a96d48d79d02c951416f047ba4d2b269407b584.text: When you use the CLI version of CodeBuff and keep it open, it now quietly records one analytics event for each minute you're actively working, so the team can see how long real sessions last. The timer starts only once the interactive screen has actually loaded (so quick commands like login or smoke tests don't count), and it stops the instant the program begins shutting down. If you happened to watch the logs, you'd notice a new 'product_active_minute' event appearing roughly every minute while you type, with a 'cli' label attached, and you'd also see it deliberately missing from the mirrored log output so it doesn't clutter those traces.

425e9cb485d05a34b93c2abdf22a8e980fc2effb.text: When you start a new chat, the system generates a title for it, and now it records how that title was created. Every attempt to make a title is tracked with details like whether it succeeded or failed, what tool made it, how long it took, and how long the title ended up being. If you looked at the analytics dashboard, you'd see a new category of data showing how often titles are being generated automatically versus when they fail or come back empty, along with timing information for each try.

5824dc1d4e6d9948220ac83e68c0254f775f08c7.text: When you open the assistant in a fresh terminal, the automated checks that confirm it started correctly now look for a broader set of on-screen prompts (like 'Start coding for free' or 'Pick a model to start') instead of relying solely on the ASCII logo, so the check works reliably across different terminal setups used in continuous integration. The change is live today in the end-to-end test utilities used by developers building the free-tier session flow.

ca8ddb859a773965c2058c74e401c818650f92d9.text: When you open the command-line assistant and pick a model to chat with, you now go straight into the conversation instead of sitting in a virtual waiting room with a countdown timer. The tool no longer puts you in line or shows a 'you're queued' screen, so choosing a model always starts something fresh rather than switching places in an existing queue. If you're someone who was used to seeing a wait estimate before chatting, you won't see that anymore; the tool simply moves from the model picker direct to active chat. The developers note this is live now for people using the command-line version.

c0d984a61fa18c7fdb06b8132b63d3134abf5816.text: If you use the CodeBuff assistant in the terminal and click over to the GLM referral banner, that banner will now stick around after your session ends or while you are in the queue, instead of vanishing during the brief moment the app returns to the landing screen. The app now remembers the last referral it showed you and re-displays it on the landing view until a fresh, clean response comes back, so the banner no longer blinks out during the join end, and return-to-landing transition. The 'sessions left' text in that same banner also got a color fix so it reads correctly against the green button, and the streak line in the waiting room now stays visually full once you hit a seven-day streak rather than resetting its look.

ae4bfa7060da887ef37210aa0d5c33adad14963d.text: If you open the app today, the landing screen now shows your daily-use streak as a row of seven dots, like "2 day streak" followed by filled and empty circles that visually count how far you are into the current week, and the row stays blank until you have at least one day so it doesn't pop in unexpectedly; the referral banner for the new powerful model now shows your referral count against a fixed weekly limit, like "3/5", instead of an open-ended call to refer more friends. The change is live for you if you're someone who lands on that screen or sees the referral banner, and it only affects how your progress and referral status are displayed, not your actual access or rewards.

7f4effcaa955faf0576cdffb799998fd36733bbe.text: If you use the assistant in a terminal window that's narrower than about 50 characters, the daily streak counter now moves below the heading instead of squeezing against it. When your streak goes past seven days, a plus sign appears after the row of dots so you can tell the run is still growing. The referral message on the landing screen no longer mentions a fixed friend cap, so the wording stays accurate whether or not that limit changes later.

b3c3decd0afb7d08f0ab70a80070a316c1547bab.text: When you load a skill by name, your assistant now always grabs the latest copy it finds on your computer instead of relying on a version it remembered when your session started. This means if you just installed or updated a skill (for example by running a command in your terminal), that new version is used right away rather than the old one it had cached. You would not see anything different unless you had updated a skill during the current session, in which case the changes show up immediately instead of on your next session.

ec42536f50943a38138d63621738bf4a4e5bfa8f.text: The referral invite you see in the program is now a real, clickable button that copies your personal sign-up link instead of plain text, and when someone uses it they land on a page that greets them by your name. The invite line now appears right after your streak indicator in the waiting room. Only full paying subscribers see this banner at all; if you're on a limited plan, it stays hidden because referrals aren't a perk for that tier yet.

dd3e1e6aa9ef1bd11f446bb4cca0ceaf1ac3e89b.text: The assistant can now click the 'Copy Invite Link' button without its border looking squished or cut off when the text line around it gets narrow. The number showing how many friends you've invited also wraps neatly onto the next line instead of getting pushed off-screen. These fixes are live today.

979954f98423e67c331525052c100358fa1f97a4.text: When you sign in to the assistant through your terminal, the system now quietly records where you dropped off. If login never finishes or something goes wrong, those specific failure points are tracked so the makers can see which entryway (the pop-up sign-in window versus typing a command) loses more people. You won't see anything new on your screen today, but this data helps explain why some people never complete the sign-in process.

eebd6089f2b07ee217e4367ccdf074effed29364.text: When you open the model picker in the CLI and arrow down through the list of models, you can now keep pressing down to reach the referral banner's buttons (Copy Invite Link and Use GLM) that appear below the model list, and pressing up from those buttons takes you back into the model list — the two areas now share keyboard focus so navigation flows seamlessly between them. A shared focus store keeps track of which control is highlighted, so the banner's matching button lights up when you arrow into it, and the copy-to-clipboard logic was rewritten into a reusable hook so the banner's copy button can trigger the same 'copied!' behavior when activated by keyboard. This is live today for CLI users, no feature flag needed.

3e442f817a080ee0f2ac2ecd86193db9e2c7349f.text: When you use the CodeBuff CLI tool, it now assigns you the same anonymous tracking ID every time you launch it before you log in, instead of creating a brand-new ID with each launch. This means all your pre-login activity (like opening the app multiple times) gets grouped together under one identity, rather than appearing as separate individual sessions that look like people dropping off before logging in. The system then properly records your login when you sign in through the web flow or when your existing session is restored automatically, so your pre-login and post-login activity is correctly linked to your actual account. If you're a developer looking at the analytics, you'll now see the complete user journey from first launch through login as one continuous activity instead of

4d7555cb6f9415176119010fabe5c27f13d8243b.text: If you use the free assistant on the website or in the terminal, you can no longer accidentally ask it to run the paid Gemini Pro model behind the scenes. The only pieces of the assistant that are allowed to talk to that expensive model are the two small 'thinker' helpers, one on the web and one in the terminal. The system now also recognizes dated versions of the model name (like 'gemini-3.1-pro-preview-20260219') as the same premium model, so someone can't trick it into using the paid one by appending a date. If you looked, you'd see the assistant quietly blocking any other part of itself from spending your free quota on Gemini Pro.

4c9007c7eaa0c04135f1be020c5209621d5aa716.text: If you use a product like Freebuff Web or Freebuff Chat (which run shared accounts instead of individual logins), your actions used to get lumped together under one shared account for tracking purposes. Now, the system sends your unique user identifier alongside those requests so your conversions and payouts are credited to you specifically. The server hashes your identifier before sending it to Gravity, keeping it private. This affects anyone using shared service account surfaces today.

750dc9aaa60a81d5716bfe47380a859dd7159720.text: When you use /plan or /review, it now runs on the model you have selected instead of forcing you to connect a ChatGPT account first. If you have connected ChatGPT via /connect, those commands still delegate the deep-thinking step to the GPT model as they used to; otherwise your selected model handles the work directly. The prompts that /plan and /review send are chosen automatically based on whether you have ChatGPT connected, so you do not see a 'connect required' message anymore. The tips shown in the help banner now suggest trying the full '/interview then /plan then implement' workflow regardless of whether you have connected ChatGPT.

692bf102f5e653d85d43fc32883c4d8366c537ef.text: If you install or update the free coding assistant Freebuff, its help documentation now lives in one central place instead of being spread across multiple files — the main guide points you to the single source, and the other files just link to it. The model information is also refreshed to show which AI engines are available in full mode (DeepSeek V4 Pro, MiMo 2.5 Pro, Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek V4 Flash, MiMo 2.5, and MiniMax M3) versus limited mode (DeepSeek V4 Flash and MiMo 2.5), and the release notes now clarify that Freebuff is supported by text ads and that labeled models may be used for training data.

95a1156a6015112ed1b82cb897df77395b0fd5b0.text: When you open the model picker in the CLI and land on the recommended model, you'll now see a right-aligned "Press Enter ↵" label on that highlighted row, making it obvious that pressing Enter will select it. The developers only put that label on the recommended row and folded its width into the layout calculation, so longer rows like DeepSeek Pro's warning text don't push every button wider than necessary — the buttons only grow if the recommended row plus its cue is actually the longest line. The cue only appears when there's enough space after the details text, keeping the list readable and the focused row clearly actionable.

1bac5606860ccd893adeb9188103fde0d2bb93f6.text: If you use the free assistant, a new model is now available to you, but only as a thank-you gift for getting friends to sign up: each friend you refer earns you one hour of access to this newer model each week. You'll see a small banner on the waiting screen that tells you whether you've unlocked it yet and, if you have, how many hours you still have left this week, along with a button to copy your personal referral link to share with friends. The regular model picker no longer shows this option at all, because it's meant to be earned through referrals rather than chosen directly.

538768ba9aaf73180427a125c12e05edf67fbbd6.text: If you open the model picker on the premium side of the CLI today, the daily reset countdown now appears even when you haven't used any of your allotment yet. The counter shows the full-access tier from the start instead of hiding until you've spent at least one session, and the timer still falls back to the next Pacific-day boundary when the server hasn't sent a reset time yet. You'll see the label change from a plain muted tone to amber once the pool hits zero, matching how the premium rows themselves grey out.

2e94bb23cc19832c25dad3b04883f71a44fdd998.text: If you use the assistant and have run out of your daily premium tries, the countdown showing when your tries reset now appears right inside the premium section of the model picker, instead of below it. People on the regular free tier still see the small counter below the model list — but only if they've already used some tries — because there's no premium section for it to live inside. The counter disappears entirely while everything is collapsed and you haven't used any tries yet, since there's nothing to wait for when your allowance is still full.

59f2ba13cee05f37282e74d3738adfe15633ef31.text: The test that checks if the program starts up properly now tries three times instead of giving up after one failure. This helps because sometimes the test server has a temporary hiccup where the program doesn't start fast enough, and retrying usually fixes it. If the test detects a real problem (like a crash), it still fails right away without retrying, so actual bugs are caught just as quickly. The change only affects the automated tests that run on the build system, not your experience using the program.

b9439256f51364c82f6d6a551a213ae995a8813c.text: When you open the CLI and the model picker is collapsed on a terminal at least 26 rows tall, the full ASCII logo now appears above the waiting room instead of the compact text logo. The picker reports its collapsed/expanded state to the screen, and useLayoutEffect ensures the logo decision settles before paint so there's no flicker on first load or when toggling. You'd just notice that the bigger logo shows up in the freed-up space when the model list is tucked away.

a4f5d94ecbd0e09f41c432abf7115b65eb498f3e.text: When you start the app before signing in, the CLI now privately notes key events like launching the app and completing setup, sending them to the diagnostic logs so the team can see the full path from download to login. These notes travel anonymously and are matched together using a session ID, so pre-login actions link up with your activity after you sign in. Diagnostic copies skip over frequent automatic background events (like screen recording data) to keep the logs focused, and anonymous submissions are capped at a small rate to prevent overload. The feature is active today as part of the CLI.

a54b61094c5a8b141e2d1f4dd365e538ffb8529c.text: When you open the model picker in the command-line tool today, it now starts collapsed to show just the recommended model first, so a new user can press Enter once and immediately start coding without scanning through multiple options. The full list of models remains accessible via a 'see all models' toggle, which stays keyboard-navigable and keeps the same product/availability grouping as before. Returning users whose saved preference matches the recommendation also see the collapsed view, while anyone whose preference differs gets the expanded list so their chosen model is visible and focused. Separately, MiniMax M3 has lost its 'Collects data for training' warning and has been removed from the list of models whose conversations are stored in free mode, because Fireworks hosting prevents

d38aa87d8f52653a6efbd545aba736173cf07a89.text: When the assistant uses its thinking helper (the 'thinker-gemini' agent) and streams out reasoning chunks, those chunks now carry a stable agent ID instead of a run-specific ID. This means anyone building on the SDK can now correctly tell which subagent produced which reasoning — especially when matching against subagent_start events — instead of trying to map it through a temporary runId. You'd notice this if you were consuming the stream and had previously seen agentId values that didn't match the ones from subagent lifecycle events.

a94090ee7b615e9cb447b239791b4a5fb1dde283.text: If you use the Lite mode (the faster, paid tier), your conversations now run on MiniMax M3 instead of DeepSeek V4 Flash; the assistant simply talks to a different model behind the scenes, so you might notice subtly different answer styles but not a change in how you open the app. The change is live today for Lite users, while Free mode stays on the existing MiniMax model and people using the model picker can still pick whatever variant they want.

bf245a37e473e354eca1d24fc06a78c14059dde6.text: If you've never talked to the code assistant before and you're using the free version, you'll now see a row of clickable starter questions — like 'Explain this codebase' — right in the chat window when it's empty and idle. These questions disappear forever once you type or click any prompt, and they only show up when no menu or pop-up is open so they don't get in the way. Hovering over a short question reveals the full prompt text in a preview, as long as there's room for it, so you can see exactly what you're sending before you click.

f0c65d3132424eafe090f368fc5615f2ced05c62.text: If the CLI crashes or spits out an error while you're using it, that diagnostic information now silently copies itself to the developer's logging server in the background. The data is batched and sent in small chunks (up to 500 records at a time, each message capped at 4,000 characters, with a total size limit) and it only happens automatically when you're not in a development, testing, or continuous-integration environment. If anything goes wrong while shipping those logs, or if the program isn't authenticated yet, it simply holds onto the data or drops it on the floor rather than letting your session break.

8118a50f77cd572f2b9a82fb5e8525e23aec4d25.text: When you open the list of assistant models in the command-line tool, the headers for Premium and Unlimited tiers now show how many free sessions you have left and when they reset, instead of just a plain label. The notice telling you that some models aren't available in your country, along with your usage streak, now appears below the model list rather than above it.
