If your terminal window is short (under 22 rows), that notice is hidden to keep the model picker readable. Country names like 'BR' are shown as 'Brazil' when possible, falling back to the code if the name can't be looked up.

957b9d654a945dcb47e4d91b473f0212e1565ad3.text: When you ask the program to open a webpage on a Windows-connected Linux setup or on a computer without a visible desktop, the program used to crash and stop working entirely. It now checks first whether the helper it needs is actually available, and if it isn't, it quietly skips the open attempt instead of failing. This keeps the program running so you can keep using it instead of being kicked out.

370bbb64e5b86de777b8ded4303ad082fcf80b06.text: When you sign up for Freebuff through a friend's referral link on the web, your friend now earns a higher reward only if your GitHub account is at least 4 months old at the time you join. Younger accounts can still sign up, but the referring friend won't get credit for them. Each additional qualified referral raises the referrer's tier in a four-step ladder (1, 3, or 7 qualified referrals), increasing their daily usage limits and eventually removing the 'Powered by Freebuff' watermark from their deployed projects. A new cap of 20 attributed web signups per referrer keeps this from being abused, and the first tier unlocking watermark removal requires just one qualified referral.

9d9e3f15ad1e2fd45a3501a73a9ea9d5acc8ed79.text: The web chat assistant on freebuff.com/chat can now recommend third-party developer tools and services directly, something it couldn't do before. When it suggests a tool, the system now tracks that recommendation as coming from the chat product specifically, rather than lumping it in with traffic from the command-line product. To someone using the chat, this means they'll see tailored suggestions for other developer services appear in their conversation, formatted with clear links for getting started. This is live today for chat users.

9c8af8c79c36649273421ef43e515b2fffe63be3.text: Starting today, when you use the assistant from your home folder (or a folder above it), the file list that pops up when you type @ only looks a few folders deep instead of searching your whole computer, so mentioning a file like docs/notes.md still works but deeply buried files won't appear. A short hint line now shows up at the bottom of that file list telling you it's only showing the top few levels and that opening a real project folder gives you the full list. This prevents the assistant from accidentally scanning every file on your disk when your project root is your home directory.

ff6f49149b964e3c2f917756c7979cb61ecffe8d.text: Today's update fixes a behind-the-scenes memory issue that could slow down or destabilize the agent runtime used by the freebuff chat server and other long-lived processes. Sometimes when a chat session was interrupted or errored out, the system forgot to clean up the internal state (the generator object, flags, and proposed file content) for that run, causing it to linger in memory indefinitely. The fix now ensures that cleanup happens every time a run's loop exits—including on aborts and errors, not just on normal completion. Additionally, the agent cache that stores large prompt templates has been capped at 200 entries with FIFO eviction, preventing unbounded memory growth in long-running sessions. These changes are internal stability improvements with no direct user-facing behavior

5f95e26baf6768feb52cc5e67519b4cede3d4a63.text: The web app now blocks people connecting through Tor or other anonymous networks from running agents server-side, while still letting them open the app; the assistant simply refuses each request it receives. Web users on the limited plan get a fresh, Convex-enforced session pool of five sessions lasting one hour, separate from the existing pool on the desktop version, and two specific models (DeepSeek V4 Flash and MiMo 2.5) now run without consuming those limited sessions even if you're in a geo-restricted region. If you're on the limited web plan, you can only pick from a restricted list of models, and any older or premium model you might have had saved locally gets quietly swapped back to a default, unlimited model.

6c85a772586aa5d0ba7760d5ee1cad1723317bf0.text: If you open the chat on freebuff.com/chat, your conversation now gets answered by a slightly faster version of the same AI assistant, while the command-line tool and the web page builder that Freebuff provides still use the original, full-powered assistant. Developers made this switch only for the website chat by pointing that one chat at a hosting service that delivers replies more quickly, even though that service is a small step down in how capable the assistant seems. The command-line and builder tools were intentionally left out of the faster version, so their behavior is unchanged.

66b39f9ac99af7faa8b610590717bdfa5daeb7f1.text: When you run the CLI, the main log file (log.jsonl) no longer stores the entire conversation with the model; instead it records only a brief summary, like how long the message was and how many previous messages existed. A new log file (trace.jsonl) is written only when you set the CODEBUFF_TRACE environment variable to 1 in production (it is recorded automatically while testing on your computer), and it stores the full back-and-forth of each conversation. The application also waits until after you start it before scanning for old log files larger than 10 megabytes that were last touched 14 or more days ago, deleting those oversized debug files in the background while leaving recent logs and the actual chat history untouched.

f5aebdb4bd86f3c4c97f01039705133a9fd2eb8f.text: When you ask the tool to read a web page, it now checks every link it's about to follow to make sure it's not secretly pointing at a private or internal address instead of a legitimate public site. Previously, a malicious page could use a chain of redirects to trick the tool into reaching internal-only addresses; now each redirect hop is validated, and addresses like 127.0.0.1 or localhost are always blocked. If a URL is rejected for these security reasons, you'll see an error message indicating the fetch was denied rather than returning any page content.

53e9e1ac09bee289c4fe62535ad8eaa07a6f2ff1.text: When you log in near the CLI, the long web address it shows you can sometimes wrap onto two lines because your terminal window is narrow. If you click that wrapped address, only the first line gets used, so the login fails because the address is cut off. Now a warning appears under the address telling you to press 'c' to copy the full link instead. It's live today and only affects anyone using the login prompt in a terminal that's too narrow to show the whole address on one line.

e72bcc94a0acd7187855a568de78d5e8cfc49f74.text: If you use a newer Claude assistant (such as Claude 4.6 or Fable) through certain providers like Amazon Bedrock, conversations that were about to continue from a previous assistant reply would fail with an error saying assistant messages aren't allowed as a starting point. The runtime now rewrites those conversations so they begin with a user message instead, letting the assistant generate its next response. Older Claude versions and other providers keep working exactly as before. Failed test-run dumps that were cluttering the project's evaluation folder are also now ignored automatically.

5d29036496273c2e61ccc2fb490f9c49826cc980.text: When the assistant talks to other AI services behind the scenes and gets told 'slow down, you're hitting me too fast,' the app now shows both its friendly warning and the specific reason the other service gave, such as 'you ran out of capacity.' You'll see phrases like 'free mode rate limited (Request rate is too high)' instead of just 'too many requests.' This only applies to people who hit rate limits; subscribers and paying users aren't affected.

241cc5bcc2452ac764d35c7d3557bd9490b1a852.text: When you press Enter in the CLI's new interactive input on a Kitty-protocol terminal, it now reliably inserts a new line instead of being mistaken for Alt+Enter, which had been adding unwanted paragraph breaks. The terminal sends Enter as a special encoded sequence, and the input handler now recognizes that encoding format directly rather than running it through legacy Alt+Enter detection, so plain Enter, Shift+Enter, and Alt+Enter each behave as expected on these keyboards.

38401ec1b8df4542b80b71d41256a043e08f29be.text: When you open the free model picker, the assistant no longer offers MiniMax M2.7 and now offers MiniMax M3 instead; M2.7 is kept only so older clients keep working until roughly June 16, and MiniMax M3 is no longer treated as a premium option. If you look at the picker, you'll see MiniMax M3 listed under the free choices and MiniMax M2.7 missing from the list.

409f05fafae7718d0ff9fa5979f74f309b7bc5c0.text: When you copy from a message while working inside a GitHub Codespaces or remote VS Code terminal, the app now detects when that terminal will silently swallow the copy command instead of actually copying. Previously, some messages were hidden in that situation, so you could end up with nothing in your clipboard and no explanation; now the guidance to drag-and-select text (or click the copy icon) is always shown, even when the app is told to keep quiet. This only affects you if your terminal lives in a browser-based or remote environment, and you would notice it as a reliable hint instead of a silent failure.

f34d91198316b40f048582b71a9aa915bac94a52.text: When the system generates its list of available tools for use, it now accepts an optional explicit list of tools to include, rather than always using the full published set. This lets developers running tests or specific workflows compile tool definitions for just the tools they need without altering the main shared list. The change is live in the shared code today. If you look, you'd see the generation step now takes a parameter that defaults to the usual full list, and a new structured entry holds each tool name and its parameter definition separately from the global constants.

270a776296bc67ae0369762cf91bc6b047ec9f69.text: If you use the assistant and pick a model marked as premium, you'll now see a "Premium" badge and a per-day usage limit, because the app now tracks which models are premium and enforces that limit. If you upload an image and the model you chose accepts image input, the app finally forwards the actual image to the model instead of dropping it or pasting it as text. Both of these behaviors are live today for everyone who can already select those models.

89ef2b771d74e90e173c03c80e5a0b7e1285932f.text: The action buttons you tap in the CLI now read as plain verbs like 'Search services' instead of 'Services · Verb', so each action looks like a single readable phrase. Buttons switched from solid blocks of color to unfilled accent-colored outlines, and they now underline and dim when you interact with them. Kimi and M3 added to the list of models that can read images, so image-based prompts now route to them where multimodal support is supported.

360988f0ed5f75d567ab892ee251a9fa0fcde802.text: The assistant now has a new tool to look up third-party services instead of guessing from memory, so when you ask about a database, payment provider, or other external service it will use this catalog to find the right recommendation. The text shown in the command line for these lookups has been simplified to read like a clear menu item, such as 'Services · search' or 'Services · browse.' This is live today for anyone using the assistant.

9e59dcc4f5df63719dff99e9e4ec1db6abcb1fbb.text: When you press Enter to pick a model or confirm something in the terminal app, it now works correctly even on some Linux setups and keyboards where Enter sends a slightly different signal — previously the menu could look stuck even though you hit the key. At the same time, the app now automatically cleans up stray broken characters (the kind left behind when text is accidentally chopped in half mid-emoji) inside your conversation before sending it to the AI, so a single corrupted character can no longer make the whole conversation fail on the AI provider's side. Both fixes are live today.

1dd01919a42648d9da8f473c4f84b3b0b55b8605.text: The assistant used to tidy up validation error messages before showing them to you in the CLI chat, wrapping long paths into neat clickable links like “.agents/myproject/file.ts”. That cleanup code has been deleted, so any tool that relied on it to pre-format errors is now missing. If you run the CLI today, you won’t see the polished path links anymore when validation errors appear in your chat session.

358336a18e557894e7bbdd623c43e34f1bc54f6f.text: A small software package that powers the assistant's command-line tool had its version number bumped from one release to the next. This is a routine behind-the-scenes update that doesn't add new features or change how the tool works — it just keeps the version tracking current. You wouldn't notice anything different when using the tool; this kind of change is housekeeping for the software's release process.

385a72397d899dcd80b9715f1b86adff24faa644.text: When you start a paid-assistant session in the CLI, you now get asked to confirm your wallet's spending limit before any models load — this is the new 'consent_required' gate that locks the session until you opt in. The tool now sends your approved spending cap to the admission endpoint and refuses to proceed (throwing a clear 'unsupported' error) if a server predates the feature. You'd notice it as a one-time consent prompt at session start; after you accept, your available Freebucks balance and model picker behave exactly as before.

6f79426bd3986cb1cd77168c2e80b2ad53862550.text: If you look at a summary of how many subscribers have each kind of access tier (full, limited, or not yet sorted), the numbers will now appear as properly formatted counts (like 1,234 instead of 1234), and any tier with no data will show a dash instead of blank space. This only affects the internal tools staff use to inspect subscriber tier breakdowns, not anything you would see as a customer today.

10144f7ad1bd85fa528642276370444f1862214b.text: When developers run the app on their own computers to test it, a 'guest login' button appears that lets them sign in without real credentials. That button and the underlying login system previously each defined their own name for the same login method, so they could fall out of sync and stop recognizing each other. The shared name now lives in a spot that the login page can safely read without accidentally pulling in server-only code that would break the page before it even loads. If you looked, you would just see the guest login continue to work the same way it always has on a developer's machine; the difference is invisible to anyone not building the app.

0ce5fb0b7d299ff3a646c2785016dd3287928df3.text: When you go to report a problem or request a feature, you'll now see simple fill-in-the-blank forms instead of a blank page. This helps organize feedback so the team can respond faster. The automated system that checks code changes is also doing a better job spotting unclear titles, which keeps the project cleaner.

df64ef498a3fb6d30d36e94869a65e2fed60f6f5.text: The tools that power your AI assistant now run on a newer version of the underlying AI system and require a more recent version of the Node.js runtime (version 22 or higher), meaning you will need to update your development environment to continue using the latest features and improvements. Additionally, the way certain data types are handled has been updated to allow for undefined values, which makes the system more flexible when processing information from different AI providers. If you rely on the older Node.js version or have custom code expecting the old data structure, you will need to adjust it to match the new requirements.

68b34fa74dd1efa2451b9a4a6df7f5a15ba2a2b3.text: The assistant no longer reads a file called knowledge.md for project instructions. It now looks only at AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, with AGENTS.md taking priority. If you rely on knowledge.md to guide the assistant's behavior in a project, that file is ignored now; you need to rename or recreate your instructions in one of the supported files. This is live today for anyone running the updated CLI.

afc8351b5b724273614569816b30691f1fecf536.text: If you ask the web-research assistant to dig in deep for a thorough, cited answer to a hard question, that request now simply won't run. The assistant has stopped using the deep-research service entirely and instead runs every question through a single standard web-search engine, so any setting in the question that asks for extra effort or a research style is ignored. People using the deep-research feature today will notice their questions come back faster but less comprehensive, with no charge for the previously paid step. This rolled out with the September 2, 2026 agent runtime updates.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: The program you use to talk to the assistant from your computer just got a small, behind-the-scenes update to its version numbers — like changing a label on a package before shipping it. Nothing about what it can do changed, and if you looked at it, the only thing you'd notice is a slightly different release number. This update is live today for anyone who downloads or updates the tool.

a4837a425cd7f9ac57d590d53a9ef1bc20fa63f6.text: If you run software on a Windows PC with an ARM-based processor (like the new Snapdragon-powered laptops), the tool it uses to quickly search through your files now runs natively instead of needing translation. The program also swapped in an updated version of that search tool across every supported system type. Behind the scenes, the way the software picks the right version for your computer got simpler and more reliable by replacing a long series of if-then checks with a straightforward lookup table.

17d6db8ba087352b631923ba3e14852fcbc18b9d.text: The assistant can now automatically check and apply updates to itself on your computer. It simulates downloading and installing new versions across different operating systems (like Windows, Mac, Linux, and various chip types) to make sure the update process works correctly. A small test script was added to verify this works, and the software's internal version number was bumped from 0.0.136 to 0.0.137.

25b2071a417f2e28570f4f40d4cfede17d45a0e7.text: The system can now keep a running tally of how long it takes to start generating a reply, measured per hour and per assistant model. Instead of trying to average individual response times (which breaks down at scale), it sorts each measurement into a series of labeled buckets that grow in size the longer the wait gets, then adds up how many fell into each bucket. Anyone looking at the performance dashboard will now see response-speed numbers that combine correctly across many hours or many different models at once, instead of figures that jump around when you try to add them together. The trade-off is baked into today's data, so tweaking how the buckets work later would require redoing the stored history.

8e956567928c769287011b3a1b8974d8d646631a.text: When you run tests from inside one of the project's subfolders, bun now automatically loads the right environment and build files before running them. Previously, those subfolder test runs quietly died with confusing 'unhandled error' messages and skipped entire groups of tests, making it look like everything passed while hundreds of tests never actually ran. This only affects developers running tests directly; the automated test system was already loading these files correctly.

126f792988825047c0b547dcf5f7bfb27ae9000d.text: If you use the assistant through OpenRouter, it now sends a small set of identifying information with every request that points back to Freebuff as the source and marks the request as coming from a command-line or cloud-based agent. This means OpenRouter can correctly attribute usage and enforce any product limits that depend on where the request originated. The change is in place today in the shared core files, so any CLI or cloud integration pulling requests through OpenRouter will carry these identifiers automatically.

6f2db456ac3170ab87b7099c362f20f295369fb3.text: The automated checker that makes sure the terminal watchdog works correctly has been reorganized so all the test pieces start up at the same time in one shared setup step, rather than each test starting its own piece individually. This is only a test-suite change, meaning nothing in the actual product is different—it affects the internal quality checks, not what you see when you use it. If you looked at the test results, you might notice the overall test run is more reliable on slower computers, especially Windows machines, because the built-in timer for waiting on everything to get ready was given more room to complete.

0b35949fad7bbaf605afbd048ca912c14d4a3173.text: When you're setting up a new blank Freebuff Cloud project, the assistant now knows exactly when your plan is fully thought out and ready for your final sign-off. After the assistant explains your options, answers your questions, and checks any third-party services, it can present a clear summary of what will be built, and a 'Start building' button appears on your screen. Until you click that button, nothing gets built - the assistant pauses and waits for you to approve the plan first. This works for anyone creating a blank project in Freebuff Cloud who wants to review before committing.

380909638150bde314b3d4eb96bcd7664fa07529.text: When you close the assistant, it now shuts down the same way whether you press Ctrl+C, type /exit, or click quit. Before, each of those could leave your terminal in a weird state or forget to save your usage data, so quitting was a little unreliable. Behind the scenes, the launcher now stamps the parent process ID on the child process so crash reports can trace where a failure came from, and a small reporter was added to print fatal errors even if the screen hasn't finished drawing yet. If you watch closely while it exits, you may notice the terminal resets more cleanly and your session analytics get flushed consistently.

9ac3cfaccbda1e5eefac4a136587406f1bf5fe83.text: When the assistant figures out which files belong to your project, it now correctly recognizes files even when their exact folder names contain dots or special characters that previously confused it. Instead of just glancing at the file name, it now checks the file's true location on your hard drive, so files sitting just outside your project folder won't be mistakenly included or skipped. This applies to anyone using tools that scan a project's files, like when listing what's in a folder or deciding which files to process.

2bb0662c5dd481ddb3bb79db171548568e33e9a5.text: When you install Codebuff, Codecane, or Freebuff from the command line today, the installation instructions that run your tool now come from one shared location instead of being copied separately into each product. The developers consolidated the download-and-setup steps so that future updates to how these tools install only need to happen in one place, which should make the setup behavior consistent across all three products going forward.

d2ae8a0dc59e09d6a13717590ebdd0fd9e2b3dfa.text: The animated logo and shimmer effect that appears at the top of the chat screen were moved into a single, reusable component, and that animation can now be turned off programmatically instead of always running. For you, that means the header can be hidden as you scroll up through the conversation, freeing up vertical space in the terminal for your actual chat. Behind the scenes, a new memory buffer was added for long-running commands so that if a command floods the screen with output, the assistant keeps only the start and the end of that output instead of every line, which keeps the terminal responsive even during very noisy tasks.

c8464c6866193ec4780e23b225ab06252eee2ffc.text: Older versions of the free coding agent that were released before July 2026 send along a model identifier no longer used today. That identifier is now explicitly named and published in the tool, so the system can recognize and handle it instead of treating it as an unknown request. If you looked at the version history you would see the free tool move to 0.0.121 and the main tool to 1.0.684, with this named retired model ID included as part of that release.

07ab1c6445e0e36697f749f10d34eccea254b5e5.text: The freebuff runner now records its work in a structured, searchable log instead of scattering plain text messages across files. If you looked at the logs, you'd see consistent records with labels like the runner's ID and the run it belonged to, and they can ship to a central logging system when configured. Existing environment variables were documented so operators know which keys are needed to turn on remote logging. Nothing changes for you right now unless you're the one configuring and watching those logs; the new logging setup is live in the code, waiting for the matching server keys.

122933fd79cf8b99c6346050f96fc8dc56649141.text: When you sign in to the assistant from the command line, the app now reads the Freebuff sign-in address from a single shared location instead of having its own copy of the URL written directly in the code. This only affects command-line sign-ins; the address you get sent to is still the same Freebuff website it always was. Nothing about how you sign in changes, but the behind-the-scenes lookup is now shared with the desktop app so the two can't drift apart.

f1a5a202b3505df7216651ab21560dd053faf148.text: When you run the app on Windows, it now double-checks whether your specific processor supports newer, faster math instructions by asking Windows directly. It remembers the result on your computer so it doesn't have to check every time, making launches quicker after the first check. If something blocks the check, it proceeds assuming your processor is capable and lets the app fall back gracefully if it turns out to be wrong.

44cbd349993e6f82827d8ca66c2b3dcf6634ce31.text: The free Buffy MiniMax M3 assistant can now review your code instead of just running it. Previously, this version had a special flag that turned off code review, but that flag was removed so the assistant now automatically checks your work for problems. If you use this model in free mode, you’ll see it offering quality checks alongside its responses.

209f11b0fb3bcd73c25e68d691e48144f7cc001d.text: When you chat in the Freebuffer waiting room, you will now see only the single top-sponsored banner ad instead of the full set, and the chat view collapses any extra ad slots that used to stack. Under the hood the program that paints that banner was split into two: one part handles the waiting-room view you see today (keeping its existing height and padding), and the other handles the single banner shown mid-conversation, so the two screens no longer share the same code. Everything you see looks the same as before, but the pieces behind the screen were rearranged to make that one difference.

874c8ec4aabb8c0db77ffe375d5edd248402a83a.text: The Buffy agent that helps build apps in the playground now has a new option powered by Kimi's latest coding model (Kimi K2.7 Code), which is better tuned for writing code. If you're picking which helper to use, you'll see this one alongside the existing DeepSeek model. Behind the scenes, the tool list that picks Kimi as the default for free users was also cleaned up to use this new setup, and the official scoring test for these helpers was switched to measure this new model instead. It's live right now.

a6455dbd1cff1467ef80a3c7ce9d364e19756b09.text: The assistant's top-tier helper tools now use a newer, faster model (Claude Fable 5) instead of the previous one (Opus 4.7), while the main assistant model (Opus 4.7) is upgraded to version 4.8 for standard tasks. If you use the high-end features, you'll experience slightly smarter and faster problem-solving during complex coding tasks. The changes are in the system that manages how the assistant helps with writing code, reviewing changes, and picking the best solution among multiple options. These updates are live today for subscribers using the maximum-tier features.

e39f9da8bc239a0b8c08ee3014e7ec7c2a287c41.text: You can now pick a new paid-tier model called MiniMax M3 from the free orchestrator menu, and it will route your request through MiniMax's official API instead of the older m2.7 endpoint. The system treats it as a distinct, premium option alongside the other free agent choices, so it shows up as 'Buffy the MiniMax M3 Free Orchestrator' when you're selecting which assistant handles your task. This is live today for anyone who can already choose from the free orchestrator list.

ad5e77cb4eae7ef2f6a183e84e915704819fea2a.text: When you see an ad in the app, the system used to decide which ad network to try first and which to fall back on right from your device. Now that fallback order is controlled entirely by the server, which tries Gravity first, then ZeroClick, and finally Carbon if the earlier ones can't fill the request. You won't see this change on screen, but you may notice more ads loading successfully because the server can coordinate across all three ad networks instead of your device giving up after two tries.

b5460a424824ba881c15a718cdba566112678666.text: Starting today, the system that decides who can use the free plan from certain countries now checks one more service before granting full access. When your IP address looks like it might be hiding your location (such as through a VPN, Tor, or proxy), the system now asks both Spur and Scamalytics whether that traffic looks safe. If either service can't give a clear, clean response, or if it flags your connection as suspicious, you’ll be placed in a limited-access waiting room instead. A clean result from both services is now required to skip the queue entirely, so residential proxies and Tor usage are more likely to be blocked outright.

2f7f2db929542d200cc6a617dcc3cabd83aaf557.text: The assistant now has the plumbing to connect to external apps like Notion or GitHub through a service called Composio, but the ability is turned off for now. Four new tools for managing connections, running actions across apps, searching available apps, and checking app details have been added to the system, but they sit behind a switch that is currently off, so nothing happens yet. If you looked, you'd see the assistant can already talk to those apps in theory, but you cannot actually use the new features today.

6200a7bfdbdb111a8b2b94680839ae774b78dc41.text: A developer can now run a behind-the-scenes tool that finds and removes a single person's data from the internal database using their email address or ID. The removal does nothing unless the developer explicitly turns on a confirmation flag, and even then the tool shows a plan of what would be deleted first instead of destroying anything immediately. By design the cleanup only touches the internal database, so payments, analytics, and email systems are intentionally left alone, and deleting the person's organizations requires an extra opt-in flag, otherwise the tool refuses to proceed if you still owns any organizations.

0e3a2e3a4b1ecfbbd704e53d500087469d665ea9.text: Your assistant can now quietly keep count of how many conversations are happening at the same time on each server. When you send a message, a counter ticks up, and when the reply finishes (or fails), it ticks back down, writing a brief note that includes which machine handled it, which conversation, and how long it took. If you run these servers yourself, you'll see a new kind of line in your logs roughly once every 20 requests, giving you a running tally of live traffic without flooding your system with data.

9468967ece2e1fcecf85d2f09903b4ec5fd97702.text: The assistant was given a new way to check its work: instead of three separate review habits it used to follow, it now does one focused pass to spot places where a change could be made simpler or cleaner. This only affects how the assistant itself evaluates and improves changes behind the scenes, so you wouldn't see a new button or different output. If you looked at the project's instructions today, you'd find the old review steps gone and replaced by a single step telling the assistant to rethink changes with fresh eyes.

28d560182de8500514e34ac4079426b3c965675e.text: The SDK kit that outside developers use to talk to the AI no longer secretly leans on the company's private server-only code. The pieces that connect to OpenAI-style and OpenRouter AI endpoints were moved out of the hidden, server-restricted toolbox into a separate, publicly shared toolbox that the SDK is allowed to open. If you are an external developer pulling the Codebuff SDK into your own app, your project now depends on a clean, shareable package instead of tripping over internal plumbing; nothing about what the AI calls changes today, but the connection path is now safe for you to touch.

a11f5b9bcc8ef033701e8c20747ebf4f7e70deee.text: The web-search tool now pulls results from Serber instead of Linkup, so when an agent searches the web it gets Google-style search results (titles, links, snippets, answer boxes, related questions) rather than the old Linkup format. To set up the search, you now provide a Serber API key instead of a Linkup key, and the example config file and schema have been updated to match. The research agent can also open those result pages directly using a terminal command, which lets it read full articles, not just the short snippets the search returns.

1b5ba7995640155ea933ea7343e3ca8614fbf6b1.text: When you press Enter on the numpad (the number pad on the right side of many keyboards), the command-line chat now treats it the same as the regular Enter key, so your message sends instead of doing nothing or inserting a line break unexpectedly. Also, the input bar now ignores accidental printable-character keypresses that used to slip through when special keys overlapped, making the chat input smoother to use. If you use the command-line interface today and type with a full keyboard, presses of the numpad Enter will work like a normal Enter, and stray characters won't interrupt your typing.

6f4dbb428ef40c0f3aaa2d30d97d8f9b51c9d5fa.text: When you ask the assistant to search the web from the chat command line, the search request now shows up as a small labeled card that prints the exact question you asked, instead of showing up as raw technical input. The terminal interface now has a dedicated display component mapped to the web search action, so each search is presented in a readable, consistent format. This behavior is live today for anyone running the assistant from the command line and triggering a web search tool call.

17e14b8a31610135a829565584f8fbc36860041e.text: When you talk with the agent named base2, it can now fetch and show you the contents of a web page just by giving it a link, instead of being unable to reach outside sources. If you watched the agent working, you would see it list the URL it grabbed in its usual compact display card, the same style it uses for reading local files. This ability is turned on for everyone using base2 right away, with no special setting or extra key needed.

14fa5cb720bc6ffa0a47767e93d43d21fb01fb9a.text: The CLI now records a detailed, step-by-step log of each conversation it has with an AI model and stores it in a database. This means developers can later look back at exactly what was sent and received at each point, including which parts were reused from a fast cache versus freshly generated. Each conversation is grouped under a unique ID so related steps can be connected together. The logging only captures data when the app sends these new trace records, so you would only notice it if the application was updated to use this new tracing feature.

092de618a0779bc979a7077e49bf77725042e455.text: Free-tier users in supported countries who were incorrectly blocked by a VPN flag will now get full access when a second check confirms their IP address is safe. If that second check can't decide, they fall back to limited access instead of being fully locked out. The change also records the reasoning behind each access decision so the waiting-room screen can explain why you see the reduced model set without re-checking your location.

a3dbf723659094910c2cf7d85ec5535dadc3bd98.text: If you try to use the service from a VPN, proxy, or Tor connection, your request will now be rejected outright instead of being processed through the normal queue. When this happens, the tool you work in will show a message naming the specific kind of traffic it found, such as 'VPN' or 'Tor,' rather than a vague note about anonymous networks. People already in the middle of a session over one of these connections will be kicked off with an error saying the feature is unavailable. This is because the backend now treats these privacy tools as an automatic disqualification, allowing only direct, clearly identified internet connections to access the free mode.

d555af2e5b1448463bf81cbb73702e6de7e7003a.text: A new internal tool now gathers recent chat conversations from the company's data warehouse and saves them as readable JSON files you can inspect locally, with secrets like API keys and tokens automatically hidden in previews. Engineers can ask it to pull the last few sessions from the past 24 hours, or fetch one specific session by its ID, and it pieces together full conversations from partial message updates stored across multiple records. The script lands at.context/recent-chat-completion-traces by default and writes a matching index file, and it already works today when run by an engineer with the right BigQuery access.

6a1803431b6de7e4b6e4519bedfec9e164604a5b.text: When you're done with a free chat session and want to pick a different model to switch to, you can now type /model instead of /end-session. Both commands take you to the same place — the screen where you choose your next model before rejoining the line. If you look closely, the list of slash commands also drops the extra note about the "waiting room." This is live today for anyone using the free tier from the command line.

30c51ac38ce89001a9a39a00416a2d56ad446fce.text: "When the assistant builds its Windows app for you, it now asks a slightly different version of the builder to do the job—one that plays nicer with more kinds of Windows computers, especially older ones. You probably won't see anything different when you download or install the app, but this switch means the finished app is put together using a setup that's already downloaded and ready to go, making the whole build process a bit smoother behind the scenes. This only affects how the app is packaged for Windows right now and doesn't change what the app actually does once you're using it."}.

a85cb595b5dece0859ec6bb1d05f898d79ad0fdf.text: Developers added a new internal script that pulls together complete, multi-turn chat conversations from DeepSeek's free tier (both the Pro and Flash versions) into saved trace files. It groups the conversations by a unique session ID and picks the most detailed version of each chat to reconstruct the full back-and-forth history, then writes them out as JSON files or a single combined file. This is a behind-the-scenes tool for the team to inspect and analyze how real free-tier sessions look today, not anything end users would see in the product itself.

cd83f663cb98745c005bd8ef51efcdf67cdf5f15.text: When you ask the assistant to read a file, you can now give it the full path to that file instead of only a shortened path, as long as the file lives within your project. Previously, if you pasted the complete path, the assistant sometimes came back empty-handed even though it had opened the file, because of a mismatch in how the two sides named the file. With the fix, the assistant now matches the file it just read to the one you asked for, so it returns the content instead of reporting it as missing. This behavior is live today for anyone using the assistant's file-reading feature.

8cca5ab9b098ec1421e51a7c41b5eb13be0d2cda.text: The project's main guide now has a link to a full Chinese translation, so Chinese-speaking users can read setup and usage instructions in their language. Anyone opening the English guide sees a language switcher linking to the translated version, which covers the same installation steps, commands, and agent-building guide as the English original.

f29db9e9ef09c89801ac25e7eaebe384991403b5.text: When you open the live map on the website, you now see properly shaped countries drawn from real geographic data instead of rough hand-drawn outlines. Each country marker is placed at its true center point, pulled from an official country database, and the whole map uses a balanced projection that keeps landmasses looking correctly sized. You can tell because coastlines, borders, and marker positions look accurate rather than sketchy.

4fb13aebd6a2e8db8ea0f3af3c48be8c74fa0c6f.text: If you try to log in with a login code that doesn't match the expected format, the system will now refuse to accept it instead of passing it along to the next step. This affects anyone using the web login flow, especially when coming in from a command-line tool. The code that checks these login codes has been moved into one shared place so it's easier to maintain, and the login buttons and redirect logic now use that single set of rules. You would notice this when attempting to sign in with a malformed or tampered login token: instead of seeing a confusing error later, the invalid code is rejected up front.

62c807a76b20fde83dc17bad79d7e787a864c538.text: When something goes wrong during an AI-powered coding session, you now get a clearer message about what happened and why. The system can now dig through layers of wrapped errors from the AI provider to pull out the real status code and message, so failures that were previously reported as generic or confusing now show their true cause. If you've ever seen a vague failure when the AI service hit an issue behind the scenes, that message should now explain the actual problem, like a rate limit or authentication issue, instead of hiding it.

bc108e4bf8cc7d6f36a31989dbb76dd20e9d0d4e.text: When the research assistant tries to look up information online, it can now grab the full text of a webpage directly instead of using a separate command-line tool to fetch it. This makes web research faster and smoother for anyone who asks the assistant to gather information from specific web pages. You would notice this if you watched the assistant working because it would simply read webpage contents without first running a manual fetching step.

61bbbed7acda7e26413a443b17854e6dfdd359d9.text: The CLI tools you interact with have been updated so that automated testing now drives a new set of AI helpers (MiMo Pro agents) instead of the old ones. If you open the command-line workspace, the previous helper profiles—like the ones named after Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini—will no longer appear, and the new helper behaviors will run in their place. Today, anyone running the CLI under release 1.0.680 will see the old helper definitions gone and the new assistant agents active instead.

c63b7942c4944f02b89d0326a45adaa3d0c3ff45.text: The freebuff.com/chat assistant is now defined as a simple, no-tools chatbot that takes a single text prompt and gives back the last message. Visitors to that chat page will notice a basic conversational assistant running the default model, with no ability to use plugins or spawn helper agents yet those features are explicitly planned for a later update. This foundation is live today, even though it currently does nothing beyond responding to plain questions.

c4a838fedc84d87b1640d62047cc4aa7bff923b4.text: When this app tries to download its own update over the internet, it used to give up at the first sign of trouble — a temporarily busy server, a short network blip, or a redirect to a different download location would all cause the download to fail outright. Now the download process will automatically retry a few times if the server is temporarily overloaded or the connection drops, and it handles a wider variety of redirect responses from the server without breaking. If you watch the download progress and it previously stopped with no explanation, you'll now see it pause briefly and then resume instead of failing completely. The underlying download machinery was also reorganized to make future updates more reliable, but that's behind the scenes — what you'd notice is just that updates

6c000e2fb5fcd6455833bc4e8ef3b40662e05bcb.text: When you click on a sponsored ad inside the command-line assistant (either in the main chat or the waiting room splash), the app now records that click before opening the link, letting the team measure which ads get clicked and how often. Your login token is sent along silently, and if anything goes wrong the click still opens normally with no error shown to you. The change is live today for free users and subscribers who haven't paid for an ad-free plan.

2506de227fbcba2c132e11a237f66f8e99d4e426.text: When you open the Freebuff model picker in the CLI, you may now see a third quota group labeled 'limited sessions' alongside the existing premium and unlimited sections; users who previously were blocked outright because they are in a disallowed country or are using an anonymized network are instead routed to a restricted DeepSeek Flash path with a capped daily session count, and the session-ended banner and waiting room update their wording to say 'limited' or 'premium' depending on which tier your session was granted. The database now records each session's access tier so the UI can render the correct labels and quotas, effective with this release.

317a5c0532048c69209010f9de87f1f07a740b8e.text: When you run the application from the command line, it now tells advertising networks that it's a command-line tool instead of pretending to be a web browser. As a result, the ad system can correctly recognize your command-line activity for ad targeting and billing. If you looked, you would see the command-line requests carrying a custom identification header and those headers flowing through to the ad services.

b1e92cb142e6cb222c6b54d9db58b5c4ac5a0109.text: When you scroll to the live stats section near the bottom of the freebuff homepage, a richer summary now loads in: a small world map with highlighted countries, a running total of live users, top models, and the last-updated timestamp. The page no longer pings the server for those numbers every minute whether you're looking at them or not—it waits until you've scrolled within roughly 240 pixels of the section, and stops again if you switch tabs or blur the window; if a refresh fumbles, yesterday's numbers stay on screen instead of vanishing. This is live today for every visitor to the homepage, and the older, lighter counter that used to sit in that spot has been taken out. Behind the scenes, the code that fetches and formats those statistics was copied out of the detailed live-stats page.

efbd0b6f44586275607d449a3052d0d12c8ff41a.text: When you make a free-mode request, the assistant now remembers the country-access decision instead of re-checking your IP location every time. That decision (allowed or blocked), your country code, and any IP privacy signals get saved in a new cache table that also stores when the entry was checked and when it expires. If the database is slow or down, the system still falls back to the direct country/privacy check so free-mode availability never depends on cache health. Cache writes are best-effort, so the direct result is still treated as authoritative for your current request.

af4e0fe1473a8a441a36d071db2cfda4dd30c3b2.text: When you're on the free limited plan and open the assistant's landing screen in the terminal app, you now see a simple confirm screen instead of a list of model options. The screen shows the single model you get, a note about data collection, your session count (e.g. '0 of 5 sessions used · resets in 8h 21m'), and a button to start a session that grays out once you've hit your daily limit. The wording also dropped the internal 'limited' label from session counters so they just say 'sessions', which reads more naturally next to the count and reset timer.

201c08b9fa1066d53695d27fa0645bd19abd8216.text: If you do anything that generates a lot of activity—like running many tools in a row or typing long messages—the app now records only about 1% of those events by default instead of logging every single one, which means your usage data is summarized and sent in a much smaller form. The CLI now respects new sampling and telemetry flags, and there are two new environment variables ("CODEBUFF_FULL_TELEMETRY" to turn off sampling for debugging, and "CODEBUFF_FULL_TELEMETRY_IDS" to target specific users) documented in the environment variables guide. This change is live today and reduces the amount of data the app sends about your actions, unless you opt in to full telemetry for troubleshooting.

ebe848f548bd41e22004128e7960267c059e4693.text: When you're sitting in the Freebuff waiting room, you'll now see a live countdown showing exactly how long until your next batch of premium tries resets. The app watches the clock on its own and updates the timer as you wait, so you can tell whether to wait a few minutes or come back later. Once the reset time rolls around (either the server's stated time or midnight Pacific time), the waiting room automatically refreshes its information without needing you to do anything.

2952274587e48f57472f4a9faad67b18d93b91d8.text: When you use the free AI assistant, it used to pause and check country rules again on every message you sent. Now, because you already passed those checks when you first joined the queue, it skips the repeated checks and talks to your billing record more lightly, so free conversations flow faster. The change also logs and reports far less often on free traffic, which stops the system from getting overwhelmed when lots of free users chat at once. You would not see new options or text on your screen, but free responses that were coming back slowly should feel snappier, especially when many people are using the service.

bf767d70cac9d83e2918bcde03b419260fb4626f.text: When a sponsored ad from ZeroClick appears, it now leads with the brand's name at the top and shows the product description or subtitle as the supporting text underneath, instead of mixing those details around as it did before. You'd notice that ads now display the company name first, making them easier to recognize at a glance. This fix corrects the previous logic that sometimes showed the wrong text in either the headline or the body of the ad.

6b27aeb79704c214f07456c7198eb0c01f684d65.text: When you run several code searches in one assistant session, the collapsed summary line now shows a single combined count like '3 searches · 12 results' instead of listing each query separately. This affects anyone who triggers multiple searches through the code-searcher assistant, because the summary text is generated in one place and both the search results display and the branch overview now read from that shared helper. If you watched the side panel while a code-searcher agent was working, you would see its collapsed preview update to that combined total rather than a longer stack of individual result counts. The change is live today.

f01f29111f35346d3db3a579c82ffc1e4d8af610.text: You now have a new free AI model to pick from when running the assistant: DeepSeek V4 Flash, labeled as the 'Most efficient' option. When you open the model picker, alongside the existing DeepSeek V4 Pro choice, you'll see DeepSeek V4 Flash listed as available to everyone, and the tool will automatically assign it as the main agent and the code-reviewer agent for that model. The older DeepSeek V4 Pro free agent no longer asks for permission before making changes, removing that extra confirmation step that some might have expected.

64b0a93ed00b4dfd435cc8f80083b8d9f201a73b.text: When you open a very large project, the assistant used to try reading and analyzing every single file at once into its memory, which could crash your computer or your chat session. Now it quietly stops itself after it has collected about 10,000 files or roughly half a gigabyte of content total, and it skips any individual file larger than about a megabyte before it even tries to read it. If you watch closely while opening a big project today, you may notice it finishes scanning sooner than before, and it no longer freezes or disconnects your chat on repositories that previously overwhelmed it.

ec28ae51ea968f910d1f03f1437dfff41fb7d6a4.text: When you visit the new Live page on the Freebuff dashboard, you'll see a real-time map showing which countries are currently using the service and which models they're running, with the data refreshing every 15 seconds. The page pulls live data about active user sessions, excluding anyone whose session has expired or been banned, and displays it on a stylized world map with country markers and model breakdowns. The site footer automatically disappears on this page, and the feature is available to all Freebuff visitors starting today.

7e3fc2306e2b347b4384a11dac1c9fd9ee173f61.text: The assistant can now use a new AI model called Moonshot Kimi, which is now offered alongside the existing model options when someone asks for it. A new setting (MOONSHOT_API_KEY) has been added that is required to use this new model, and it is automatically set to a test value in the company's automated testing systems. When you request the Moonshot Kimi model, the software checks for it first before looking at other available models, ensuring it gets picked correctly.

5c6068411b13dda14ab547b54853ea8f9839b5cc.text: When a basher agent runs, the terminal preview now shows its summary prompt instead of leaving it blank. Developers see the basher task text displayed directly in the collapsed view, making it easier to identify what each agent is doing at a glance.

ef6b4ef531ea4711a7407fe672c5f4f5db1e3857.text: When you ask the tool to search through your code, it now hides the raw, jumbled technical details of what it found and only shows you a clean summary line like "Found 7 matches" instead of dumping the full internal results data into your terminal. Behind the scenes, the search agent now sends an empty message field when reporting results, and the display component reads the match-count header to figure out how many hits there were. The documentation also adds step-by-step tmux commands so testers can capture and replay a terminal session to verify the cleaner output.

3f698f5a0cd76738416987f6faaad900a70cbef5.text: When an ad doesn't load from the primary ad network, the command-line interface and web tools will now try a second ad provider instead of leaving a blank space. Free-tier users and visitors to the waiting room screen are the ones who'll see this backup ad; if the preferred ad isn't available, a ZeroClick ad is shown and tracked directly by the browser without going through the server. The developers added a new API key setting and told the system to keep these backup ads only for the current session so they don't get cached or reused later.

48caa4cc399c3d7f3522f8d65492c7c007bea9fc.text: The SDK's file-handling tools can now accept either relative or absolute file paths as long as the file lives inside your project folder, instead of rejecting any path that doesn't start from the project root. Absolute paths that point outside your project still get blocked, preserving the existing safety check. Developers using the SDK tools internally will notice they can pass paths like `/home/user/project/src/code.ts` or `src/code.ts` interchangeably without errors. The change is already active in the current SDK version.

f1b6d70380846b0af254ec8d85c8241ff545cae4.text: If you sign in to the CLI and then try to use the same login token a second time, you will now see a clear error telling you the token was already used, instead of the system silently deleting it and treating it like it never existed. The system now keeps a record of used tokens, marked as consumed, so it can tell the difference between a token that was never valid and one that was already claimed. This affects anyone who logs in through the CLI and tries to reuse the same browser-based verification step.

df40341c78a885040817d1503f7569c250586f0a.text: You no longer manually pick which assistant reviews your code when using the free version—the system now automatically chooses the right reviewer AI based on which main AI you selected. Behind the scenes, instead of typing a specific reviewer name into your setup (like telling a librarian exactly which shelf to check), the orchestrator now looks up the matching expert for whatever AI model you picked, falling back to the default "lite" reviewer if your model doesn't have a specialized one assigned yet.

16137ba62ca6a9b7edb2b431898962c2ef05b8ea.text: When signing in with an older command-line version of the tool, the login code it sends no longer causes a sign-in failure. The system now recognizes the legacy two-part code format (using hyphens instead of dots) and correctly reads the three pieces of information from it. If you use the latest version, nothing changes; if you use an older command-line client, you can now log in successfully again.

5b1551b55d29b3585fe0dacd20a39624d89a42fc.text: After a free premium session ends, the goodbye screen now tells you how many of your daily premium sessions you've used, like "2 of 3 premium sessions used today," instead of just saying the session ended. This number updates live while you wait in line and when your session finishes, and if you've used all your daily allowances, the screen border turns amber to signal you've hit the cap. The count can show fractions (for example, 1.3 if a session ran long) but always matches the daily limit shown alongside it. This is live today for anyone using the free tier of premium models, and you'll notice it both in the waiting room while your turn is coming up and on the final banner once your session is done.

e58596f99351e5b8fc4639b2fb115c076019a668.text: If you ask the assistant to use the new model options 'minimax-m2.7' or 'kimi-k2.6', it will refuse and return an error saying those models are currently disabled, even if you have an API key for them in your settings file. The system has been taught about these models so it recognizes them, but the actual connection to talk to that provider is blocked behind a switch, so nothing actually works yet for users on any plan.

66648012945c0d1c4002c9b8a370cee1d0735547.text: You can now ask the assistant to work toward a specific goal and set it to a more collaborative mode where it checks in with you. This is an internal configuration change that turns on two new capabilities in the system. Nothing breaks, and you'd see this if you used those modes.

3afccad624c4f906a74a68fb427af3b43947ec8e.text: If you run BuffBench evaluations against coding agents, you can now point it at OpenCode CLI using the identifier external:opencode. The suite spawns OpenCode with a default model of opencode/kimi-k2.6, overridable by your OPENCODE_MODEL environment variable, and uses JSON output plus your OPENCODE_API_KEY to authenticate. The supported external agent list, docs install steps, and a fallback error message now all accept opencode.

a97f891c79334434dad209d7d957a3dfc5abe21c.text: When you open your chat history in the command-line version of the assistant, each past conversation now has a delete option right next to it, so you can remove individual conversations without digging into folders. Pressing that delete button erases that conversation's saved files from your computer and immediately updates the list so the deleted entry disappears. The change only applies to the command-line tool, and the system checks the conversation name before deleting to prevent deleting files outside the conversations folder. This is available starting with version 1.0.670 of the command-line tool.

1a1f7ed3086c3ee50485d777eb0910e9f64fa8ed.text: When you ask the free Codebuff assistant to review or work on your code, it now picks the version of its helper tools that matches the specific AI model you selected at that moment—for example, if you choose the DeepSeek-powered free assistant, the code review helper is the DeepSeek-tuned reviewer, and if you pick the Kimi-powered one, you get the Kimi-tuned reviewer. The default free option still uses the fast MiniMax model and its matching reviewer unless you specifically switch models. This means the helper that gives you feedback on your code can now be tailored to the same AI that is driving the session, instead of using one generic helper for everyone.

a08c0c90242c4b8ee9b33db2cbd0865a6c1a672b.text: When you log into the command-line version of the app on a new computer, the website will now always send you back to the correct main address, instead of sometimes bouncing you to a slightly wrong version of it during the OAuth login step. The system now reads the official app address from a configured setting first, and only falls back to the address it saw in your request or a hardcoded default if that setting is missing. This fix is already live today and applies to both the free and paid versions of the web app.

264e94a343652ebc6ab665d9f3e7810b107471cd.text: The assistant used to give each tool call a predictable name based on what tools had already been used, which helped keep things stable and repeatable. This change removes that predictable naming system and goes back to generating random identifiers for each tool call instead. You would notice this in the background processing of the assistant's actions, where tool calls are now tracked with random IDs rather than structured ones, making the internal tracking less consistent but simpler.

3dd5916285c3912ebb279fddca5875a5de34dcac.text: When you sign into the web app using an auth code, the login page now reads the expiry time from that code more carefully instead of cutting it out by hand. If you paste an auth code that has an unexpected format or missing pieces, you will no longer get a crash or a misleading 'expired' message; the page will simply tell you the code has expired only when it actually has. This fix is live today in both the freebuff web and main web login flows.

dc68d3253980fb05661f464748e33fd3d7b541e7.text: When you use Freebuff and start a new session, the CLI will now automatically take over a previous session if it belonged to your own process that has since died, instead of asking you to confirm. It does this by leaving a small record on disk with the process ID of the current session owner; before you're asked to take over, it checks whether that process is still alive, and if it's a zombie (dead), it silently completes the takeover itself. This only applies to your local Freebuff sessions; if the stale session belonged to another running process or another account, it still asks you first. Live today for Freebuff users.

8ac94a54affac0eea3470c33444b18393683fa02.text: When you sign up for a new account, you now get 500 credits once at registration instead of receiving 500 credits every month. If you already had an account and were getting monthly credits, you keep getting them the same way you were—the system checks your past credits to decide your monthly amount. If you look at the app, the labels that used to say 'Monthly Free' have been changed to just 'Free' or 'Cycle', and the counter that shows your renewal will now say 'Cycle' instead of 'Renews'. This change is live as of May 6, 2026.

dbdd64cd923cf4fa16a3cf73050c57b273b2c0c3.text: When you chat with the DeepSeek model through this system, any images or files you attach will now be quietly replaced with a short text note saying they were left out, rather than causing the request to fail. The system also now correctly translates the model's 'thinking' responses instead of mislabeling them, and bills you based on a single shared price list for all DeepSeek models. If you look at the chat, you won't see broken image placeholders or confusing pricing errors anymore.

495d067c21d83b01b7d3cbd3e820640af3f829db.text: When the assistant asks itself to use a tool (like a calculator or a web search) during a conversation, it now gives that tool call a predictable, traceable label instead of a random one. This means if the same request happens again or gets replayed, the assistant can reliably match the tool it called with the answer it got back, making retries and re-parsing smoother. You wouldn't see this directly, but you'd notice fewer mix-ups when the assistant repeats or revisits a step that involved using a tool. The change is live today for everyone using the agent runtime.

881686fe8d94809b7f42b6b88a2ab055f0d19928.text: If you use the premium Freebuff sessions, your limit of 5 now resets at midnight Pacific Time each day instead of counting the last 20 hours. For example, your five sessions at 11:59 AM will refresh at midnight Pacific, and any new ones start fresh at 12 AM. The CLI waiting-room screen reflects this change, showing how many sessions you have "today" rather than "in the last 20 hours.".

f1af5d0a51e49608ddda053bf92a70b51897aed0.text: When the assistant searches your codebase, the results now open with a count of how many matches were found, and matches are listed grouped by file with clear line numbers. You will see a line like "Found 3 matches" at the top, followed by each file's name, then its matching lines indented and numbered. If the results would be very long, the assistant now truncates the final readable text rather than the raw stream, so the summary header and file grouping stay intact instead of being cut off.

31cf16f7e26bd33459b002c33bc55747baf8b2ca.text: When you ask an AI assistant to swap one piece of text for another in a file, it now uses "oldString" to name the part to find and "newString" to name the replacement part, rather than the shorter "old" and "new". This change is already live today and affects anyone using the file-editing tools built into this system, because some tools and programming languages reserved "old" and "new" for their own use, which could cause mix-ups. If you looked at how these edit tools are described, you'd see those renamed labels in the examples and menus, but you wouldn't notice any difference in what actually gets done to your files.

5904a9d5b789538679ef7cc195fbdb23ffbbb5a8.text: When you open the model picker in the CLI and hover over DeepSeek, Kimi, or GLM, you'll now see a live counter like '3 of 5 sessions used' instead of just the model name. That cap—five paid sessions per 20-hour window—now applies identically across those three models, while MiniMax stays unlimited. The change is live today: the database migration (0050) and backend snapshot query already back the CLI's usage display, so the 'N of M' line updates in real time as the 20-hour window rolls. If you're on a free or pay-as-you-go plan, nothing about your access changed.

bb658a1142f7c975a92bc0df098c14334f3368c4.text: Today the built application can load its tree-sitter grammar without crashing on Windows. Previously the binary shipped with a large grammar file that Bun's Windows build silently dropped, so the feature was missing at runtime. Now that grammar is split into hundreds of tiny text fragments and stitched back together in memory, and the build verifies those fragments before shipping the binary. As a result Windows users no longer hit a silent crash when the feature starts up.

40d8fb340c38df153c7f983458b8ed5cbd72c32d.text: When the assistant runs low on memory, it now wraps past conversation history in a clearly labeled memory block and prefixes tool logs with 'Previously' so it doesn't mistake summaries for live dialogue. A disclaimer instructs it to ignore historical memory for formatting and continue from the live user message. If pruning happens before responding, the latest user prompt stays as a real message; if mid-turn, it's embedded in the memory block with a synthetic continuation. The final messages array is built as summary first, then instructions, then either the live prompt or continuation. Live today.

d9fd69ae973bef525b620e0b7e119c1722b2b6ef.text: When the assistant runs in a compiled binary form (not just a regular command), it previously broke specifically on Windows computers because the tree-sitter parsing code was being incorrectly dropped during compilation. Now, the binary includes a verification step that will fail the build early if the parsing code doesn't make it in properly. You would notice this if you're a developer trying to compile the binary - instead of getting a broken executable that crashes on Windows, the build will stop and show an error before shipping a broken product.

036ac8dfecd00c04eaef278aa01451a5bae20e6d.text: When you install or update the assistant on Windows, the package now includes an extra file called tree-sitter.wasm sitting right next to the main program. That file is what lets the built-in code analyzer understand programming languages, and before this fix it would sometimes go missing during installation on Windows, causing the analyzer to crash. Now the installer explicitly copies that file next to the program during setup, so the analyzer has what it needs at startup whether you're running the official release or a local test build.

9239f01da08d3fa52576091332d67600e7de424c.text: When you sign in to the service on the command line, the tool now checks your login status using a simpler, more reliable method instead of a complicated database lookup that could slow things down or give incorrect results. This makes the sign-in polling process work correctly during the OAuth flow, so you won't get stuck waiting or seeing errors while the system confirms your session. The change is live today and directly affects anyone using the CLI to authenticate.

88e6e0ea1df2136b01e101ad1400ec6a99c09564.text: Starting today, the CLI tool now runs for five seconds during automated testing to catch crashes that happen after it begins, not just during its first immediate check. When you launch the tool, some failures (like problems loading the tree-sitter parser) only appear after a short delay, so the old quick version-check would miss them. The test now watches for error messages like "Fatal error during startup" or "Cannot find module" and will fail the build if any appear, meaning broken builds get caught before reaching you.

c4d0d72a10dc26f2e55ce5c2dd709accf0b500af.text: When you start a free coding assistant session, it will now run on a model called DeepSeek V4 Pro instead of the previous default. If you explicitly ask for the lighter 'lite' mode, that picks a different model called Kimi. The picker screen you use to choose a model will show an extra line of caution next to any model that collects data, so you can spot it before confirming. These defaults are live now for anyone starting a new free or lite session.

6f223bf1d7c66c3b444cb4408748480c6d28905f.text: When you run the Codebuff command on your computer, it previously failed to start because a required file (tree-sitter's WASM engine) couldn't be found on your machine, as explained by the developers' own comments. This update now bundles that file directly into the program you download, so it travels with the software and is always available. The system also checks a specific location first before falling back to standard search methods, preventing the error described in the technical summary. This fix is live today for users running the compiled CLI version 1.0.648, as noted in the version bump listed in the evidence.

c7e9ba8a29b3f460f901969cdcdd6fadf01b89ee.text: The /connect:claude command and its OAuth setup flow were removed from the CLI, so you can no longer link your Claude account through this tool. This only affects people who were using the Freebuff build, where the feature had already been disabled, and you will now see a message telling you to use /subscribe for usage instead. The login screens, authentication utilities, and related banner displays for Claude OAuth have all been deleted, along with the code that would have guided you through the connection process.

2fdffcfa789703e0505995fccb30c422c778ab1c.text: When you use the assistant and it looks up information in the service catalog, the result now appears as a short, context-aware one-line summary instead of a blank or generic entry. This applies specifically to catalog actions like searching, browsing, listing categories, viewing a service, or reporting an integration. The new display logic is now wired into the command-line interface, so anyone interacting with these catalog tools will see clearer, self-describing output right away.

9b25609a250d7a9bf8b783d0305e212f76f681e8.text: When you use the free Kimi model in the CLI, the assistant can now optionally bring in a Gemini-based thinker to help with deeper reasoning, but only for that specific model combination. The developers' own notes confirm this lets a Kimi freebuff root spawn Gemini Pro for deeper thinking, and the interface hides Gemini Pro from the model picker while keeping it available behind the scenes for this sub-agent role. A comment also forces a session row check even when the waiting room is globally disabled, so this applies to trusted session state for these subagent/model combinations today.

1550c8b8a10e07887a59a17c93994e1151a67d91.text: When you start the CLI, it no longer crashes on Windows because the file it needs to read (tree-sitter.wasm) is now built directly into the program instead of being read from disk. Previously, the program looked for the file on your hard drive, but on Windows it couldn't find embedded files at their special internal paths, causing silent failures. The change also updated the startup test to wait a bit longer and check for errors that appeared after the window was already open, preventing similar crashes from slipping through testing. This is live today and affects anyone using the CLI binary, especially on Windows.

d14ae806ccc679972f645f18c4626c742992bc96.text: When the assistant asks to search files, replace text, or run code actions, some AI models accidentally mangle the message so badly it arrives broken: the arguments come jumbled, double-encoded, or with slightly wrong names like "old_str" instead of "old". Today, the assistant quietly fixes those broken messages behind the scenes, re-parsing the garbled text up to three times and mapping the wrong names back to the right ones before deciding what you actually asked for. You'd notice fewer times the assistant refuses a command or fails mid-task complaining it couldn't understand you.

51359eead23d0c4ffee32cb78a61638ab3fc63f2.text: A new free AI assistant named 'Buffy the DeepSeek V4 Free Orchestrator' is now available for users who can provide a DeepSeek API key. When you use this assistant, it uses the DeepSeek V4 Pro model to help you run an agent that can perform tasks on your computer, like running evals or managing software. The assistant will not save the model's private reasoning steps in the conversation history unless you turn on a special flag, and it uses an extended timeout for the longer wait times that deep-thinking models can need.

41a0f4dcb878a8912518a1677857235b3343612e.text: The free coding helper that kicks in when you don't pick a premium model has swapped brains today - it now runs on Kimi K2.6 instead of the old GLM 5.1. If you're using the editor or code reviewer in light/free mode, or the base agent when you don't choose a paid model, you're now talking to Kimi K2.6. The model picker in the command-line menu shows Kimi 2.6 as your default free option alongside the existing Gemini 3.1 Pro, and the system that decides which model backs which agent has dropped references to the older Kimi K2.5 and GLM names. This is live now - anyone running the CLI or using the free-tier agents gets Kimi 2.6 automatically.

744f49cda0f96748aec3e1b875f8c9a01ef009e4.text: The free assistant now lets you pick Google's new Gemini 3.1 Pro model when talking to it through the command-line tool. Gemini 3.1 Pro appears first at the top of the model list, while the previous default (GLM 5.1) moved down one spot. The system automatically updated its internal lists everywhere the old model name was hardcoded, so the new model is available in all the same actions the old one was, plus the assistant now records when one chat came from another for better tracking.

25213224df77f64c13bf40df22bf7b2cc4360a93.text: If you use the service through a provider that routes to Kimi models (the ones labeled with a moonshotai prefix), those models expect slightly different data than other providers accept. Requests sent to those models now automatically get the extra fields attached that Kimi requires; other models keep receiving their normal data. From your perspective, conversations that rely on those specific models no longer get rejected for missing those fields.

40d0a34ee8bd80033063f06c33855d67d09fdb9a.text: If you are chatting with an agent, it can now look up third-party services (like email, payments, databases) by searching or browsing categories, and the results include a button to connect your credentials. The agent also tracks these actions for analytics, and a new internal tool type was added so the agent can describe what it is doing to keep your conversation context tidy.

e781c56c1fd0f019f31795d09fe47b9296ebf740.text: When you run the assistant in the Codebuff terminal, it can now show you a clickable button right in the terminal window. If you click that button, your computer opens the linked web page in your regular web browser, just as if you had clicked a link in an email. The assistant can choose a blue 'primary' button for important actions or a simpler 'secondary' style for less important ones, and the button matches whether your terminal is light or dark. This only works in the standard (non-rushed) mode today.

f33c1ebf082f796f6c975627d3cb6b75bb9f980f.text: If you try to start a free session, the system now does a stricter check on your country and IP address before letting you in. If it can’t figure out where you’re connecting from or if privacy-protection tools like VPNs or Tor are detected, it blocks you by default instead of guessing. The system remembers the result of this check (without storing your actual IP address) so it can be reviewed later, and it records a specific reason for any block. This affects anyone trying to start a free session through the waiting room.

b6b99666858e977fb2a300dcf1f8d4c80e018654.text: When a user tries to use the service but is blocked by a waiting room screen due to their IP address being detected as coming through a VPN, Tor network, or proxy, the screen will now show the specific reason instead of a generic "unknown location" error message. The system now extracts precise information about which privacy tool or network is causing the block (like "VPN" or "Tor") and displays that directly to the user.
