If you looked today, you would see V4 Pro as the saved-pick row in the Premium section, anchored by its quota chip, with Luna remaining the recommended hero row above it.

75d33f9429a93c53c7c2f5b5dac73adc3a832d32.text: The coding assistant's release identifier was updated from one minor version to the next, like changing a product's internal batch number. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping to keep release tracking consistent; you won't see any new behavior or features when using the assistant. The change only touched a single configuration file that records which version of the tool ships to users today.

99c8777e213d27579525e378d569d3e430d7b1e6.text: You'll notice far fewer error messages cluttering your logs from one specific sandbox configuration, but if a sandbox key is still set in production, you'll still see one clear error explaining the problem before it quiets down to debug-only logging. The system now remembers it has already told you about this misconfiguration for the current process, so instead of repeating the same warning millions of times a day, it says it once loudly and then mutes itself. This change was deployed on 2026-08-25 and directly affects teams running production services with sandbox API keys configured.

115a6a5cc676b1a4969d2045ad34ebb5d8bd00ab.text: When someone fills out the onboarding questionnaire but leaves a few questions unanswered, the app now saves the answers they did provide instead of throwing an error and losing everything. Previously, any skipped question caused the entire submission to be rejected with a 400 error, forcing the person to start over. Now, only a completely blank form (with no answers at all) is refused, while partial answers are accepted and recorded. The change also includes a note explaining that skipping questions is treated as a user choice, not a technical mistake.

467ba64dca85ea541f5c3db0d34bbf024ccccf92.text: The assistant's ad system can now receive a label telling it where a request is coming from, such as a phone, a web page, or a desktop program. When someone asks the assistant for an ad on their behalf, this new label is passed along so the ad system knows the context of the request. This is now in place, so the assistant can use this label to make better ad decisions when it has access to it.

e3a285c926ba174296495a785ca36ed7ea44aad8.text: The CLI's internal event handling now uses stricter type checking instead of loose typing. This prevents unsafe type assertions and improves type inference for developers using the hook. It's a behind-the-scenes developer experience improvement with no impact on end-user functionality. The change is already live in the codebase.

7e9bd8cdb6cb73fb329d494669361e7226a17ed0.text: Ads served through the platform now have stricter cleaning applied to the text they show, so characters that are invisible or could trick a reviewer into approving something that actually looks different are removed before the ad goes live. If you review or approve ad copy, the version you see is now closer to what viewers will actually see, because the cleaning also catches more types of hidden or control characters that used to slip through. The change is part of the core ad-safety handling and applies to ad creative text processing on the shared/common code path. It is live now.

116f691de944ce3ef91a7e628964eba0b4e6c10d.text: The free assistant service no longer keeps separate daily usage limits for each model. Previously, some of the smarter AI models (like V4 Pro and GPT-5.6 Luna) had their own strict caps, like only one or two uses per day, separate from your normal usage. Now, those models draw from the same shared daily pool that other models already used, so you can use them more flexibly as long as you have daily sessions left. The documentation across the main guide and the Chinese version was updated to reflect this change, which appears to be live now.

ee79648a9e2aff11d54250c2dd488709b9fb3626.text: People using GPT-5.6 Luna can now run 3 sessions per day instead of 2. If you use that model, you will notice you can start one more session each day before hitting the limit. The system that tracks these limits and the message that tells you about it were both updated to reflect the new number, and the change is already live.

5acb86de2a75b3c0a36e2ce451723bf1e5dece38.text: The CLI app is sending fewer analytics events to reduce noise and cost. Specifically, it stopped tracking when you finish typing a message, stopped sending log data to PostHog (it still goes to Axiom for debugging), and now handles ad reuse through a simpler logging path. You won't notice any change in how the app works—this is behind-the-scenes cleanup that lowers the volume of data being collected and where it's stored.

a23c8b25050c3630473d9be4309c3eaa858cde07.text: When an assistant handles streaming output from a model, it needs to wait for that stream to end before finishing up. The mechanism that tracks whether the stream is done was switched to a more widely supported form of waiting, so it works on runtimes that don’t include the very newest JavaScript features. If you looked closely, you’d see the stream-ending logic now uses the basic waiting construct that all JavaScript environments understand instead of the newer convenience helper. The result for you is no change in behavior—just broader compatibility under the hood.

50aa984b714af271946c68a2ed80466a01338c4e.text: Arrow keys now move you through the command suggestions and mention lists one at a time, unless you were already paging through your previous commands with arrow keys. In that case, the arrow keys skip the suggestions and go straight to scrolling through your command history as before. The list still pops up at the top or bottom so you know you've hit the end, but the code now handles it with simpler checks instead of nested ones.

01301385919da16daba8bd458609835c69e31a7e.text: Only people who can sign in with the right admin setting can still see the placements tool—the old on/off switch for the console page is gone, and access is now decided purely by that admin setting. The page still shows made-up sample data instead of real numbers, and that hasn’t changed.

09f62ecb291de42ee67f62602f769b8f37c79bfb.text: The team rewrote the instructions developers follow when something in the app acts unpredictably during automated testing, to reflect that one particular unpredictable test has been brought back online after switching it to a newer way of running those checks. If you were reading those instructions, you would now see the team openly note that the fix is based on a guess not yet proven, that eleven other tests still use the older method, and that the original tracking ticket stays open until the test runs cleanly through several automated runs. No user-facing behavior changes; this only affects how the test is executed behind the scenes.

28220d571736520903c8e75cfd41a8588cd5e1a0.text: You might have noticed a new model option, named gpt-5.6-luna-es, now showing up as a premium choice. This is available today for paying subscribers, who see it offered in the usual premium spot. On the backend, the system now watches two related places for the 'god-only' models (such as kimi k3 eco) and keeps them hidden from non-god visitors instead of manually duplicating a list. One note: kimi k3 eco remains excluded from the subscription catalog because, as a bait model hit mostly by automated traffic, its measured cost does not reflect real usage, and it is not priced for individual subscribers today. Comments throughout the code were also clarified to reference the array used for that exclusion.

a275174b3e37c2e809245dcc06a74e6406b8d8b2.text: The release version of the coding assistant's command-line tool was bumped from 0.0.152 to 0.0.153 by the maintainers. This is a routine version number update with no changes to how the tool works, so you wouldn't notice any difference in its behavior or capabilities. It only affects people who install or update the tool from the official command-line package source.

6f9acbfeb578ed83e026547695d86a172b8011fe.text: The free coding assistant's release number quietly ticked up to the next build, which is the kind of small bump that happens whenever a new batch of changes is packaged together. If you use the tool from the command line, you may be prompted to update to pick up that latest mix of fixes and additions. That's it — no single feature announced itself; it's the usual behind-the-scenes refresh that keeps the tool current.

b21d5ab27d1d97f850e5b3b673d985093136342e.text: The coding assistant's desktop app quietly moved to a new internal version number, which you would see only if you check the installed program's about box; your daily work, commands, and features stay the same. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping that sets up tomorrow's improvements and keeps the installer working smoothly, not a feature you can use today. If you reinstall or update the program, the change takes effect automatically and you won't notice anything different while using it.

07685661de57b219d53ab908cf2e2bafcdb3e1eb.text: If you look at the showcase tweets on the page, their like and reply counts now show numbers from August 21, 2026, instead of the older August 2026 date. The two tweets displayed had their counters ticked up slightly (for example, one went from 857 likes to 871), and the date stamp shown alongside the numbers moved forward by one day. The repost and view figures are still blank because the website cannot pull them from X without a special login key, so they stay hidden until someone types them in by hand from X's own analytics page.

b563ba5e6b3bf0de5a76a0d72c354ae3db370210.text: When you use the Freebuff Web or Cloud proxy to act on behalf of someone with admin or god-level permissions, the system now sets an internal 'x-freebuff-privileged-user' flag to '1' after verifying those elevated roles server-side. This flag travels silently behind the scenes and is only trusted when the request comes from the Freebuff Web service account, meaning any attempt by other callers to forge it is safely ignored. Nothing noticeable changes for end users today beyond slightly more reliable privilege checks during admin-gated operations; the new flag is in place and already live as of August 21, 2026.

55402897958a0f19676f33abeb1432e63ea53ca7.text: The assistant added two items to a behind-the-scenes config file so they never get saved into the project's shared version history. One is a file of real feedback from users that includes their Discord and GitHub names, which shouldn't be exposed publicly. The other is a folder of temporary design-tooling files that people were accidentally committing. You would notice nothing in the app itself, but these files and folders will now stay on each person's computer instead of being shared with everyone else.

04e751a97e5f614d12c8165741fdaaf212197531.text: You may have noticed a test in the documentation guides that keeps failing unpredictably for no clear reason. This update adds a note explaining that such flaky failures are hard to pin down because re-running tests sometimes hides the original error. It also clarifies that the root cause may lie in shared code used across many test files, so fixing one file does not guarantee the problem goes away. If you check the test history carefully, you might see earlier attempts that failed before later ones passed.

5baa7a52d32ba2ed115a659fa28eed38a4414cef.text: The system now keeps clearer written notes inside its own rulebook about how the standard free assistant models (like DeepSeek Flash and MiMo) record usage charges. These notes clarify that because each prompt does count toward a cost, the recording is collected and saved in batches instead of one-by-one, and that setting any model's cost to zero removes it from this recording step entirely. This is housekeeping for the shared rulebook that all products read, so there's nothing users would see differently today.

657d06d953134758769d273970853bd370e89c3e.text: Campaign billing has been turned back on, so campaigns will now be charged through Stripe again after the free-campaign window ended. If you looked at it now, you'd see campaigns being billed again, and the system still uses a single rule to ensure no campaign serving is bypassed. This change is live today.

d777cd21617ccc5dd611a59920a609556e577551.text: The free coding assistant tool just got a fresh, numbered release so package managers and update checks can pull the latest copy without confusion. Nothing in the program changed besides that version label, so there's nothing new to try or see if you already have it installed.

fad014c575a497df9a3169fb2bc516281a081a58.text: A developer removed a leftover placeholder note that sat unused inside the assistant's settings file. It does not change how the assistant works today; you would notice nothing different in your chats. Only people reading the source code would see it is gone, and the cleanup simply makes that code easier to follow.

f9ccbec282a4812b8d2e12af28d75395af286030.text: When you launch Freebuff Desktop in Auto mode, the assistant quietly decides each step using a built-in opening line. That decision prompt now lives in a shared location that holds both the live version and any alternate wordings being tested against it, and a safety check was moved to scan every one of those wordings instead of just the main file. If a tested version ever drops the required opening line, the check will catch it before the assistant ships, because a missing line would otherwise silently stall every tab in Auto mode. Nothing you use changed yet — this keeps the next prompt update from breaking Auto mode.

f7bb825f48d23a5e38f2a43748657d567847cd9a.text: The team added a rule to the project's ignore list so that any temporary scratch files created in the scripts folder (named starting with _tmp-) won't accidentally get saved as part of the official code. This only affects people working on the project's code, not anyone using the tools it produces. You'd notice this if you looked at the ignore settings file, where the new line appears alongside similar rules for other throwaway files.

aaf1843ce840d29bf339feae4644adf3df1e06c9.text: The system now automatically ignores any temporary helper scripts that get created in the root folder, so they won't accidentally be included in the codebase. If you were to look closely, you'd notice this prevents throwaway files from being saved alongside the main project files. This change affects anyone contributing to the project's code, even those in subdirectories. It's live today, so the protection is already in place.

01ea6aba4c679543e05913a5db8faa49937b13c0.text: The system that keeps track of where your account's usage spending comes from now recognizes 'Luminal' as one of its supported billing sources. If you looked at how your spending activity is organized behind the scenes, you'd see Luminal listed alongside other providers like DeepSeek and OpenAI where it was previously missing. This change is already live and just adds a label so Luminal spending is properly identified, rather than being treated as an unknown source. It affects how your expenses are categorized, not what services you can access.

65e0d5161681abdcfe1901f2719c1aff43eacf0a.text: A developer left themselves a single blank reminder note inside the SDK's central settings file, adding two empty lines marked with just the word 'todo'. This note is private shorthand for the team and changes nothing about how the SDK behaves, so you will not see any new features, settings, or limits when using it. The reminder sits in the SDK source code only, where it does nothing until someone acts on it later.

d2b9697a48a5b058d6648dbe78561f63a88af7b8.text: If you use the free coding agent called freebuff and have the command-line version installed on your computer, you received a new small version of the software. The version number went up by one tiny step, like turning page 149 to page 150 in a manual. You would only notice this if you specifically check what version you are running; otherwise, nothing looks or acts different today.

bdc6b61fb93d720c2e1dbc084046eec16580336f.text: Premium subscribers now get 5 fresh assistant sessions instead of 6 before hitting the same hard limit on Web and Cloud. The limit still does not apply in the desktop command-line tool, where sessions remain unrestricted. This cap is enforced today on the subscription surfaces that count usage, so paying subscribers will feel the reduction the next time they start a new conversation.

9b9b25e76714ba3cfc7fff9a8b13428164cdc2cf.text: The background system that watches over your Freebuff Desktop coding assistant had its paperwork corrected, so it no longer mistakes the assistant for a third-party app. The internal tracking that flags suspicious activity used to point to an old file path that no longer matched the real one, causing every one of the assistant's 2,904 daily requests from 41 users to be wrongly flagged as foreign. With the path updated to match the actual file, the system now correctly recognizes the assistant as belonging to Freebuff, stopping those false alarms. You won't see this directly, but it means the assistant is less likely to be incorrectly restricted or challenged during use starting today.

6e27bb24543eadf602931a09a003526915b1509c.text: When an account reaches its usage limit, it now sees the same single message regardless of why it was restricted — so you can't tell from the wording whether the limit was triggered by location, domain, or tool behavior. The notice is a pre-written string that lives in a shared constants file, ready to be shown by the error screens and command-line prompts that gate free usage. Nothing about who is restricted or how much you can use changes, but the explanation shown when you hit the cap becomes identical for every restricted account. It is live today as the shared notice, and will start appearing in the existing free-mode error messages and command responses that already check your usage ceiling.

9175fd397356dbcfa51334ff19281711e7ade0e9.text: The software tests now use a fixed fake key for one part of the system instead of relying on whatever key happened to be set in the developer's computer environment. This means test results are consistent regardless of which machine runs them. You wouldn't notice anything when using the software. This change only affects testing code.

095d6d65a1697d4cb31e0a39df9adeafcf7946c2.text: If you browse to the project's documentation in either English or Chinese, you'll notice the word "Beta" no longer appears next to the Freebuff Desktop product listing. The product is still described the same way (running parallel agents locally), and the download link works just as before. This is purely a label change in the written guides; nothing about the software itself has changed, so existing users won't see any difference in behavior.

c6d10a5bff56b7a83bd09e507bc5adc2a373c8dc.text: Freebuff has added a short FAQ entry explaining its data collection habits. If you use or read Freebuff's data-use notice, you will now see an extra question that answers whether your activity traces or files are gathered while using the service. The wording clarifies that Freebuff is ad-supported and only retains your traces or uploads when a model provider (such as DeepSeek models) dictates it, keeping the public-facing explanation consistent with how the service actually handles data.

9c97c4b81c451b11472f72068b175d485a9512a8.text: When you ask the assistant to do something with a time limit, the system now properly cleans up the timer whether the task finishes on time or runs out of time, so leftover timers from failed or timed-out requests no longer pile up unseen in the background. Previously, only successful completions cleared the timer, leaving the system holding onto timers from every timeout, which could gradually slow things down over a long session. You won't directly notice this unless you were experiencing gradually degraded performance from many timed-out requests, but going forward those stale timers are cleaned up automatically on both success and timeout. This is a behind-the-scenes reliability fix rolling out today across the core assistant experience.

8057a82e406417ae68791f4ca8e5e26bb812be03.text: The model list you see on the website no longer hides any assistants at the bottom — the MiniMax M3 option now appears at full strength instead of looking faded or secondary. When it was the only muted entry left and the cheaper Pro option returned, the faded styling next to the normal rows looked broken rather than intentionally quieter, so the team stopped muting it but left its notice that a newer model is recommended. If you open the picker today, M3 shows up as a regular choice with its upgrade suggestion intact rather than looking deliberately dimmed.

1fca3e29a75dddac2d4b2fc694f8f13a42b51253.text: The way the system tracks which messages come from you has been simplified. Instead of wrapping your messages in special XML tags and then looking for those tags later, the system now relies on a plain label attached to your messages. This means there's less invisible formatting in your conversations, and the code that finds your last message does it by checking that label directly rather than searching through wrapped text. This is live today and affects how agent-based conversations handle user input behind the scenes.

2daa1edbfdcc1e2b867db89a6ee29cb5b6ac9c8f.text: The team removed a small check that used to verify one specific edge case about how tool results behave around conversation boundaries. Nothing about the live product changes—you won’t notice any difference in how things work today—this just trims an unused scenario from the internal test suite that guards the assistant’s message-handling logic. The code that actually runs for users is untouched; this is purely behind-the-scenes cleanup of a test that was no longer needed.

7db20c99a59d3ee3b410142d90b0f781f3861cc3.text: A new version of the free coding assistant's command-line tool was prepared for release. If you download or update the tool from a terminal, you'll now be getting this slightly newer build, which mainly just bumps an internal version label so the release system has a fresh package to hand out. For everyone else, nothing you do with the assistant itself changes today.

fc178cb1ef7c7d06ee0bf55e88a7b6415f2cb291.text: The onboarding flow used to have a safety net for when our servers failed to save your answers, but we've removed that escape hatch. If something goes wrong while saving your onboarding responses now, you may get stuck completing the form rather than being able to bypass it temporarily. This cleanup simplified the code, but it also means a broken save is no longer quietly worked around behind the scenes. The change is live today.

df226b46771c1d64d1f4fd9f7e11e7996e47cba5.text: The system added internal catalog entries for the extended-context flavors of DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash and GPT-5.6 Luna so that provisioning and support tooling can recognize and display them by name. These rows are intentionally kept out of the public model picker and billing quota lists, since the extended tiers are provisioned per account rather than chosen by users. If you looked, you would see new named variants alongside the existing model definitions, with no change to which assistants end users can select.

42f9dcb2036fe5685daf5f73da59512789e1f5c8.text: Behind the scenes, the helper tool quietly increased its own internal version number from one tiny step to the next, like a robot counting up its own age. This affects no one directly: it's merely a label that helps the builder team tell different print runs of the app apart, so what you see and how it behaves stays exactly the same. You would not notice anything different if you looked, because nothing you use actually changed.

7ef9669a46ffdb16f461c281a67ac52e4d3b9560.text: Intermittent React rendering test failures across approximately twenty unrelated component tests (Tab.rename, ContextBar.menu, AccountMenu.menu, AgentPicker.menu, QuotaBadge) occurred when an earlier test file left a fake "requestAnimationFrame" function on the shared test environment that never actually triggered callbacks. The documentation now records why this happened: the shared DOM setup tool captures which browser functions exist the first time it runs and reuses that list for every test, so a leftover stub from one test file caused five subsequent files to hang waiting for animation frames that never fired. To prevent recurrence, the fix requires properly removing any fake browser functions during test cleanup rather than just blanking them, and always obtaining the shared DOM

4eab91e6da752b9f8269e52018db5854dd9f0fc2.text: You, as a user, can now rest easy knowing that the list of recommended AI models shown to you will stay in the right order even if the company later changes which model is set as the default. The engineering team added a behind-the-scenes checklist (a test) that automatically checks if the first model in the list is still the one meant to be the default, and the second is still the designated runner-up. If it ever isn’t, the system will flag it before it goes live, preventing the list you see from accidentally showing the wrong order.

204d98237e29a1004f52c2d7d6beac9cfbb9f694.text: When you send an image to the assistant alongside your message, the system now handles image addresses correctly no matter how they are written. Previously, if your image came from a plain web link or an already-embedded image string, the system would wrap it again, producing something the assistant's provider rejected as broken. The system now checks whether an image is already ready to use and leaves it alone, so image messages that used to fail should now go through cleanly. This is live today for anyone sending images to compatible assistants.

c1ff21d02571b1a923041ad489802f64a1514bca.text: The account's Access Level and the limits it currently selects. The account's standing, including Access Level and selected limits, is now returned only on the pre-join response that renders a picker, so a client can explain the numbers next to the models they apply to. Clients should render the standing field only when it is present, since it is absent when the feature is off.

b615f928ac3c3d888c5e82b21fdd768e8d7e941e.text: The package version for the freebuff command line tool has been updated. This is a routine release that increments the version number to track ongoing development. There are no new features or changes to functionality, so nothing will behave differently for you. This change is live today as part of the regular release cycle.

5f8f4c0129f21df6161929ca0031ce67b2ccd141.text: The free coding assistant got a new version number, moving from version 0.0.143 to 0.0.145, but nothing else changed about how it works. You would not see or experience any difference when using it today. This is behind-the-scenes updating, like refreshing a name tag while keeping the same badge holder.

d0a5d3f4e4a0caaee723ea2e10499a9c3b64b0fc.text: The software quietly updated its own version label from 0.0.145 to 0.0.146, a routine step used when packaging a release for distribution. This only affects the release packaging process and doesn't change any features or behavior for users. If you checked the project's configuration files directly, you'd see this version number change, but otherwise nothing noticeable happens from this update.

9d25b4958aa958f70db200e3cbde351f54538ffd.text: You wouldn't notice anything different when using the desktop assistant. The developers fixed a behind-the-scenes test that checks how the assistant's instructions are put together, making sure it looks at the new way those instructions are combined rather than the old way. This is just maintenance work to keep the testing system accurate.

c26a74d54c7b2ff0429b410b0109aa0115f29c6f.text: If you run the CLI tool, the small referral banner at the top now shows a shorter message: it reads 'earn a bounty, spend up to {number} a day' instead of the longer 'up to {number} sessions a day'. The part telling you when the offer ends moved to a muted, parenthetical line right after the main text, so the active-promo line is easier to scan.

119af4afe0f2529ce76714ac740c1db1cb8940fc.text: Today the experimental DeepSeek DeepSeek 2.1 assistant was taken off the free list that only a select group of users could access. If you were one of the few people who could summon that assistant alongside the other 'god-mode' models, you will no longer see it as an option; the remaining god-mode assistants, like Kimi K3 Eco, are still available. The change only removed the existing entries and did not add anything new.

5db7bafe633f286ebf8cb91d151d557ce8df3db1.text: The automated test suite that checks the assistant system now refers to a helper agent by its new name. Where tests previously checked for responses tagged with the old helper name, they now look for the replacement tag instead. You would not notice this unless you read the tests themselves, because nothing about the assistant's behavior changed. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping to keep the tests accurate.

7ca8fa441715fb750cbaac2bb834a4b544c42313.text: Your automated tests used to give each step — including database setup — the same 5-second timeout, so when the test machine slowed down, the setup step itself would fail and blame a random test that had nothing to do with the failure. Now, setup steps that build real test databases get a separate, longer time limit, and when a test run flakes out (passes on retry), CI captures the name of the failing test instead of burying it in thousands of lines of log output, so you can quickly see which test actually stalled instead of guessing from a wall of text.

58e2564ab07e029b066e81765e85b4be189b303e.text: If you create a custom agent, the starter template no longer offers the Grok models as a choice and has switched its default assistant to a different one. The list of assistant models the system recognizes no longer includes the three Grok options, so they cannot be selected or used anymore. You would see this when setting up a new agent, since the example agent now runs on the replacement model out of the box. This is live today.

baaa1bb3570337a95a6fdc526ef83963dd67bde6.text: The software used to look for a file named knowledge.md first when gathering project instructions, but it now skips that file and only collects AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md instead. If you relied on knowledge.md being picked up automatically, it will no longer be read; place your instructions in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. The wording in the on-screen instructions also changed to refer to labeled blocks of text rather than mentioning knowledge.md specifically.

caba427c7fed797dd58e2cd6cc5a22232a5eeaea.text: You are now guaranteed to get the same, high-quality reasoning from Muse Spark every time you use it, instead of that behaviour being left to chance. Previously, the system had decided how deeply the model should think on your request, but a lookup glitch meant that decision could silently fall away for web-based users. The developers pinned that reasoning depth to 'high' explicitly and fixed the lookup so it now checks the full catalog of available models, ensuring the setting actually reaches every Muse Spark request you make.

e1129d9e5842529779d9d8098b3d0b0efe715045.text: If you run ads or track how people return to your app, your system used to guess 'did we already count today?' using your local clock, which can drift behind the global day. Now it decides that moment using a single, consistent UTC day boundary, so a late-hour Pacific user no longer slips through the cracks and loses their retention milestone. The new helper is a standalone utility that other code is instructed not to rebuild, and anything checking 'have we done this today?' is pointed at it. It is live today and only affects the day-boundary check; nothing else changes for you.

968c6682de8ea3e75d3dbbad2c6591fe28176920.text: When the terminal broker smoke test runs a PowerShell script to check console availability, that script now writes a small 'done' file on disk only after it has actually finished its check and flushed its output, instead of the test just waiting a fixed quarter-second. The test now waits until that 'done' file appears before deciding whether the script leaked a console, which prevents it from aborting too early on slow or busy Windows machines where PowerShell hasn't finished starting up. If you watched the test's exchange directory, you'd see a new file named 'console-reader-verdict' appear after the script completes, and the test would reliably wait for it before proceeding.

e39fb73424f48f7861215b6d67b095c21885f9ee.text: If you send a question to the Muse Spark helper, it will now spend more time thinking before it answers. The extra thinking time is modest — roughly a quarter again longer to wait for a reply — and it only adds about 8% more internal reasoning, so most turns will feel slightly slower with a little more careful digging behind the scenes. The team also opened up the setting that controls how deeply any given model is allowed to think, so one model's extra level of effort doesn't force that same extra level onto every other model. These adjustments are live today in the core system that routes requests; nothing on your screen changes, just how much silent work happens before a reply shows up.

4f80bdb45dcca5ab6c33304482b9699356711a0e.text: The internal notes that explain why a certain flagging rule for outside automation tools were only rewritten, not the rule itself. The rule still flags accounts that connect using root assistants without tools, and it still stays in report-only mode rather than blocking anything. If you looked at the code comments, you'd find a clearer warning that an early hand-sample of 18 users isn't proof the signal should be enforced, since the larger 30-day backtest shows 90% of flagged accounts still do real agentic work. This only affects how the logic and comments read internally today.

2bc664c5bd3c5ed730de2a5af880493d2c5d672c.text: The desktop assistant now tracks two separate sets of usage numbers for free users: one for the older version (still called 'freebuff-desktop-thread') and one for the newer version, which gets a 'v3' tag appended to its name. This affects free desktop users who are gradually being moved to the new version, letting the product team compare how the old and new versions spend compute and run sessions side by side. If you looked at the internal billing database today, you would see usage records split into two clearly labeled buckets instead of being blended together, making the base2-to-base3 rollout measureable.

787e80a8f1456623d2b0605c9f282165ac72dcb7.text: The version number on the packaged assistant tool was increased by one small step, from its previous label to a new one, and nothing else in the underlying behavior changed. This only affects how the packaged tool is identified when it is downloaded or installed. If you were looking at the version information, you would see the number go up by one; otherwise, you would not notice any difference in how it works.

070db75b0429851b103a870004b5029c4cd5700e.text: When you click a suggested followup prompt, it now sends a short, outcome-focused question instead of a long, step-by-step instruction. The assistant's suggestions are shaped by clearer guidance that favors naming the goal over listing files or chores. Because the rule is shared across chat and deep research agents, you get consistent, goal-oriented prompts wherever you click a suggestion.

1358346295e7e4fcd7b2bd3d4fa93b268518b28d.text: When you open the app for the first time in a browser, you'll now see a small pop-up asking you to save a bookmark before you can continue working. The app records whether you see that pop-up and whether you click the bookmark button, so the team can count how many people close the tab instead of continuing. That count is the key number they're watching, since the pop-up doesn't have any other way to skip it. The change is live today for anyone opening the app in a web or cloud workspace.

0be72bef521398a74121b5719210a8c5c2e1abfb.text: The developers split a single testing deadline into two separate timers: one for letting the program boot up (now 15 seconds) and another for how long it should stay alive after its companion program is killed (now 6 seconds). This fixes a problem where a slow startup on a crowded testing machine would eat into the time the program was allowed to keep running, making real bugs invisible under a generic timeout. Only the testing setup changed—no feature you can touch was affected, and nothing new is live today for you to use.

f392d93770b49c7399c49afd550a4d2783c37afd.text: The free coding agent you run from your terminal got a new small release. It bumps the program's version label from the previous one to 0.0.141, which is the number shown when you ask the tool what version is installed. If you already had the latest version, you probably won't notice anything functionally different today, but anyone installing or updating will get the freshly labeled package.

6110b0bbfbe668dffcf4d5fe86ce8147293bf73a.text: If you use an AI agent that was previously told it had a one-million-token memory limit for a specific older Meta model (muse-spark-1.2-contributor), that special setting has been deleted. The agent will now fall back to the standard, shorter token budget it uses for everything else, so any behavior or output quality that depended on that larger memory limit for that model is gone. In practice, this only affects users still relying on that particular older model configuration; most people won't see any difference.

52804281c6e03e0c74bbd7eb6b9965d369a5cf15.text: As of August 5, 2026, the Muse Spark 1.2 contributor model can now process much longer conversations—up to a million words—instead of being cut off early. This mainly affects power users who rely on Muse Spark 1.2 contributor for extended tasks, like writers or researchers working on large documents. Previously, the system was treating the model as if it had a much smaller memory, limiting it to only around 52,000 words worth of context, which meant long discussions or complex prompts would get truncated. Now, the model's full memory capacity is recognized and used.

27caf8248eaf3be6e303a93b58e27529e2008630.text: If you use the chat assistant and pick the new Muse Spark 1.2-contributor model, it now correctly understands very long conversations instead of getting cut off early. Previously this model was treated like one with a much smaller memory, so it would stop paying attention well before your chat reached a million messages; now the assistant knows that model can hold about a million words at once and will use that full space instead of a tiny default limit.

2368b27e2d8a3b5f98f3e242083ba4a59dc0e0e2.text: A new version of your coding assistant’s package got released today, bumping the version number up by two tiny steps. You wouldn’t notice anything different in how the tool works right now, since this change only updates a label behind the scenes that tracks which version is current. If you peek at the tool’s version info, you’ll see the updated number, but day-to-day use stays exactly the same.

a6571b01b1383c6806b1344375d38525846701ac.text: If you've been waiting for Freebuff Cloud to leave beta, it has: the 'Beta' label is gone in the project tables, and a new Freebuff Enterprise row now links to the enterprise sales page for organizations wanting custom deployments. Submitting the /enterprise contact form now fires a tracking event that records the company size and whether the sender is an AI lab, so inbound leads can be sorted automatically. These changes are visible today on freebuff.com/cloud and /enterprise, and the new event is already live in the analytics stream — not a placeholder.

afe8c7918cdd600f464fe453e1c4382eea7061e1.text: The project's main guide page now pushes the free, ad-supported tool to the front and stops leading with the paid product, dropping the old branding, comparison picture, and performance numbers that used to sit right at the top. You would have seen the free tool named first with a new web address (freebuff.com) and the paid product's screenshots and stats gone if you opened the project's front page today. This only changes words and pictures on the public-facing read-me; nothing about how either tool actually works changed.

9c3d9f0caebc6cd1ad214b92a7440fd0ff1cf929.text: The team released a new version of their coding assistant tool to package distributors so the latest build is now what gets installed when someone installs it fresh today. You would only notice this if you were reinstalling the tool from scratch; existing copies you already downloaded or built keep working exactly as before, since this just labels the new batch of the same software.

c799255a7afc9de583e6fed26712c5a5ec2c48fd.text: When someone signs up for the web or cloud version of the tool today, the preselected assistant is now a newer, higher-quality model called Luna instead of the previous default. Existing users who already picked their own model, or anyone using the desktop or command-line version, are not affected and stay on the old default. If you opened the web app for the first time on or after August 4, 2026, and the Luna model ran out of its shared daily usage limit, the picker would automatically switch you to the fallback model so your request still goes through instead of failing.

218d2266be52bd7c37ca12f32c07766f8f7c267b.text: The software now recognizes two new free AI assistants you can pick from when using the service at no cost. When you browse the list of free options, you'll see two additional models from the Greg 2 family (one labeled 'Ultra' and one labeled 'Super') alongside the existing free choices. The system was told to expect these new assistants and how they map to their model names, so they're ready for you to select today.

7baf11ac08f12726408167fd391367d461a96249.text: When developers run the project's test suite, it now only runs everyday unit tests and skips longer-running integration tests by default. Those integration tests are filtered into separate commands, so a developer choosing to run the full test suite would notice that certain tests no longer run unless they explicitly select the integration test option. This makes routine testing faster and keeps different kinds of tests organized. The change is live today and affects how tests are grouped across several parts of the project.

037b51122b8b627807b9f138f7fffa16b0a6fe65.text: When you click a download button for the desktop app — whether you're on the homepage, browsing products, or visiting the dedicated desktop page — the site now records that click and which spot it came from, along with your operating system. If you double-click quickly because you're unsure the download started, the site counts the extra click as a retry rather than a fresh attempt, giving the team a clearer read on how well the download buttons are working. The change is in place and live today.

04d4379f1617e48948e10d522ee2688dd9b84942.text: The assistant's file browser was incorrectly hiding files and folders when there were multiple ignore rules stacked in different directories. If you opened a project and some files that should have been visible were missing, that was the bug. The fix rewrites how nested ignore rules are combined so that each directory's rules are applied independently, and the results are layered together instead of mashed into one path-rewrite. The change is live today, so a project with nested.gitignore or.codebuffignore files now shows the correct contents.

eeb5209f0d72ca408c7decfcbac295cf21d06cea.text: When you start a new assistant session tagged as a Fable-based session, its built-in code checker now runs Fable instead of automatically falling back to a cheaper DeepSeek model. The system now blocks the assistant from launching sub-checkers that use a different model than your session, so a Fable-bound session can no longer silently route its review to a lower-cost provider. If you looked at this in practice, you would see that every Fable session gets reviewed by Fable only, and the old "fall back to DeepSeek if unsure" behavior no longer happens. This change is live today and affects any session configured to use Fable.

542451446bb2086182f9a10dfd9dc56cece4c133.text: When you ask the assistant a question and it starts answering you a little bit at a time, you now have the ability to stop that response mid-stream instead of waiting for it to finish. This is handy if you asked something by accident, changed your mind, or the assistant is taking too long to respond. Behind the scenes, the system that sends your question to the AI now listens for a 'stop' signal, so your request can be cleanly cancelled while it's still working.

81bb087616c1eebb0516d8c74562cd6c4cd3cdbf.text: If you try to sign up using a throwaway email address, the service will now turn away 37 more domains that are known for spam. These aren’t big providers like Gmail or Outlook, but newer domains that were minted in single-day bursts and have a very high chance of being banned. The list was built from real data: each domain either had at least 20 accounts already registered, with at least 75% of those accounts already banned. So if you use a disposable email from one of the new entries like gmaiko.com or gmito.my.id, your signup will be rejected, and you’ll have to use a different email address.

e4a3a7abe1a6db3cdb1a3ff7ad5bae9737e48fa3.text: After a session expires, there's now a 30-minute buffer period where active tasks can finish but new ones won't start. This prevents your work from being cut off if you're still using the app when your session ends, while stopping new work from starting once that window closes. You'd notice this if your session expired but you could still finish typing a response before the app fully logged you out. This change is live today.

a0d5b7f05d51dd5c0638193e6bff94151af278ee.text: The assistant now blocks sign-ups from three email-address providers that were used in a coordinated attempt to run 48 free accounts at once. Anyone trying to register with an address ending in l0veyou.com, pumpkinai.space, or pumpkinai.it.com will be turned away at sign-up, so the service rejects new accounts that rely on throwaway or disguised email addresses (like gmail.l0veyou.com) instead of a real one. This rollout went out on 2026-08-02 live today.

2ae66743c3896cfb8f44812cf9643807c513fd59.text: If a test relies on a process running on your machine rather than something isolated, two copies of it can interfere with each other by trying to manage the same global set of processes. To prevent this, an atomic directory-creation lock is now used to ensure only one such test runs at a time. Additionally, test files now explicitly declare how long they expect to take, and polling helpers are checked to give up before that deadline. This change is live today and affects how tests behave on shared or heavily loaded machines by making failures more attributable and preventing unattributed unhandled errors from masking the real issue.

115d80be38b93542912a3bb3cb0ed85f67f48290.text: When a test in the main code-checking system fails and then passes on a retry, the system treats it differently now. For the core unit checks (the fast ones that test specific pieces of logic), a pass only on the second or third try now fails the whole submission, because analysis showed retries never actually helped these — they just hide real problems. For the slower integration checks (the ones that test multiple parts together, like database connections), a retry rescue still works but leaves a warning note for people to investigate. Right now, if you see a test pass only after retrying in the unit category, you should know it's flaky and needs fixing.

a03e7a8ef057c6b8e9b3c63592e96ab176ea479d.text: The version number for the freebuff assistant was bumped up by one small step, from 0.0.134 to 0.0.135. This is the kind of thing that happens with each routine release, like a car getting a new paint job between models. Nothing visible changed for users — no new buttons, no altered behavior, no performance tweaks. It is a behind-the-scenes label update that developers use to track builds, not something you would notice or act on.

cc568bb92ddf1d15ac7be8b35e078a80670a6563.text: You may have noticed the assistant sometimes cut off conversations that still had plenty of room left, summarizing or losing earlier messages even when it didn’t need to. Behind the scenes, the system now recognizes that the assistant’s Luna model can hold about 1,000,000 words of conversation in a single session instead of the much smaller default, so it stops rewriting your history prematurely and keeps the prompt cache intact. This applies to users routed to the Luna model through the supported provider network, and the change is live today.

4e2403d6d910b7b0f6566d1eba3bfb35d4fb0aaa.text: When you're using an older model that has been replaced by a newer, faster one (like DeepSeek V4 Flash), you'll now see a gentle reminder on the screen telling you the new model is better, but only if that specific older model is the one you're currently looking at. If you switch to viewing a different older model that's also been replaced, you won't see multiple reminders cluttering up the list—just one on the model you're focused on. And if you're already using the recommended new model, you won't see any reminder at all, since there's nothing for you to switch to. This change is live today and only affects what you see in the model selection screen when browsing available models.

2de7fe6b96aee8b402f989d9b1456d7e4f1259eb.text: A small housekeeping update was published for the assistant's release package, nudging the version number up by one notch. This is the kind of change you might notice only if you were watching the build numbers roll by; otherwise, it behaves exactly like the previous version. Nothing new became available or stopped working for anyone today.

66199cc009297b239aa41cf46b945195a7a528a6.text: The free assistant tool quietly moved to a new minor version, so anyone opening the program gets the latest small adjustments and bug fixes that come with it. Nothing flashy changes on screen for you, but the launcher you double-click is now the updated 0.0.131 build instead of the previous 0.0.130.

76d27eac43c54991622be0ff4b8eae09ee27183f.text: The release version for the coding assistant's installer was bumped from the previous number to the next step in its sequence, so the downloadable package now identifies itself with the latest version label. If you grabbed the installer today, it would report the new version number; the program's actual behavior and features remain exactly as they were in the prior release. This is routine packaging maintenance that only updates the version metadata used during installation.

159673adf8f8dd060344460862f309b21986134f.text: You'll now see shorter, simpler labels for three of the AI assistants when you pick them in the model menu on the Web, desktop, and CLI apps: MiMo 2.5 Pro says 'Smart & Slow', MiMo 2.5 says 'Balanced', and MiniMax M3 says 'Fastest'. These are just text tweaks — the names on the menu are friendlier, but the assistants themselves haven't changed.

b15fef86116ef07524649f8b6ffd5027e0bee774.text: Today the program that installs the coding helper got a fresh version number, so anyone downloading it from the official installer gets the latest packaged copy. This is behind-the-scenes bookkeeping for distribution and does not change how the helper behaves once it's running on your computer. You won't notice anything different unless you're checking download sources, and the change is live now for people installing today.

f8a40d8bdea49062791c965233871dac46f9505d.text: Users running the free coding assistant from their terminal saw the program's version number tick up from 0.0.129 to 0.0.130, a routine increment that simply marks a new release with no new capabilities or bugs fixed. If you happened to check the version printed by the program, that's the only thing that looks different today.

8d95d803aedf841503be0f60718ed8374e492b5c.text: When you click the savings calculator on the homepage, a new tracking event is now recorded in addition to the existing download tracking, capturing the specific savings amount, per-seat pricing, seat count, selected tools, and total tool count at the moment of your click. This allows the analytics system to measure which computed savings values correlate with higher conversion rates by grouping visitors based on the savings figure they were shown before deciding to download. The change is live today and applies to all homepage visitors who interact with the savings calculator call-to-action.

51994660ab6530ff0764978a8241ed2b80fa1d30.text: When the terminal watchdog tool kills a frozen program with the strongest shutdown signal, the test now waits until the program writes its exact recovery password text to the terminal before declaring victory, rather than stopping as soon as anything appears. Previously the test would accept any output, so it could pass even if the recovery text never showed up fully. The waiting period now matches your operating system: Windows gets up to 45 seconds because it takes longer to wake up and write, while Mac and Linux get 15 seconds, and the overall test timeout grew to two minutes to reduce false failures under heavy load. This only affects how the software is tested before release, so you will not notice it in daily use, but it makes the automated checks more dependable, especially on

33d6139537ac60f9e475e9ff4211498fd9f65c73.text: The version number for the release package was bumped from 0.0.135 to 0.0.136. This affects whoever consumes or builds from that release package, since the published package now carries the new version. If you looked, you'd see the version string in the release manifest changed and nothing else did. It is live today as part of the release build.

f831624f857d2174a4f72a594f53e8cdec65e528.text: When the CLI's package launcher disappears during a test, the test now waits for the process to fully exit and gives it a short window to finish sending any remaining output before declaring success or failure. This only affects the test infrastructure that verifies the CLI exits cleanly when its launcher vanishes, preventing the test from hanging and throwing away the fixture's exit code and diagnostic messages. A surviving CLI still causes the test to fail rather than pass, and the fix is live in the test suite today.

062743b69a890d6f0e6efba5b3806cd8f6cad036.text: When you open the assistant picker, every model now shows an 'Images' badge next to its name, including text-only models that previously didn't. This reflects that even text-only models can analyze screenshots you paste, using a server-side vision service to read the image first. If you looked, you'd see the badge consistently in both the compact and full model list views. This is live today for anyone using the CLI model selector.

175191e4366e34542cfe2d7dfdd9162faf7c2361.text: If you look at the main project page that describes what Freebuff offers, the row advertising Freebuff Enterprise has been removed. The Enterprise offering is no longer listed alongside the Web, Cloud, and Chat products. Today, the public documentation only mentions three products.

b81352e298d504578da3e408754a0274dbcbacd2.text: When you stop using a temporary, separate copy of your project (called a "desktop worktree"), the program can now quietly record that reclamation as a new internal telemetry event. This only adds a new analytics label to an existing list, so you won't see a button or notification; it's a behind-the-scenes tracking addition that prepares the product team to monitor how often reclaimed worktrees are cleaned up in the future.

1499a9d866f9946dca7209a07323b0c4b501c60b.text: When you run something on the assistant's behalf, it used to quietly throw away any repeated command feedback before adding it to the ongoing record, to avoid confusing the AI provider. That duplicate-checking step has been removed, so repeated feedback now gets passed through directly. It only affects the internal agent runtime, and you wouldn't see anything change just by looking, unless you were watching how extra tool results get recorded after a retry.

fe2f293cfec04f7effa3601e4719d8d5583b81a2.text: When you ask the assistant to run a command on a Windows machine, it now uses the same bash-style commands everywhere instead of switching to Windows-native commands like 'dir' or 'copy'. This means file paths on Windows won't get corrupted (for example, 'C:\Users\me' won't become 'C:Usersme') because bash will treat backslashes as escape characters. This change is already live today whenever the assistant interacts with the system prompt on any operating system.

977abd5ce06611d6fe900d31310c581dfcd95291.text: The project added a guide explaining how its automated checks run faster by splitting one big pre-check step into separate typechecking and web-building jobs that now run in parallel, roughly cutting the total time from eleven minutes to under six. The guide also notes which slow tasks are unavoidable setup costs (like waiting for dependency caches) rather than the actual tests, and records a few silent-failure traps in the tooling that can make a fast-feeling build still miss checking new code or run against an outdated software-development kit if a future job isn't configured to either rebuild or explicitly reuse the pre-built one.

860318a19c3c2bd12795963a2e50917ca79e0ba5.text: If you run a certain group of tests side by side on your computer, they sometimes trip over each other and fail for no clear reason, even though each test passes when run alone. The problem happened because those tests were all trying to write their temporary files to the same shared folders on disk, so when two tests ran at the same time, they would overwrite or delete each other's data. The fix gives each test run its own private folder to work in, so they no longer collide, meaning those flaky failures should disappear when you run tests locally.

24c1a306f8c6654c7412241acd117c8074af5831.text: If you see the policy notice on Freebuff, the short summary you were shown just got shorter. The longer list of specific restrictions like account limits, automated use, direct endpoint access, and location spoofing is gone, and the message now only mentions ad personalization, AI training, and a general update to usage rules. This is a minor tweak to shared text that appears across the whole product, so you’ll notice it the next time a policy notice pops up.

4fa56551886ce92ff07d05bc42107ed53ae03a5f.text: When you turn the automatic-start setting on or off in the desktop app, that action is now recorded as an anonymous usage event, as is any change to whether that setting applies just to you or to everyone who uses the computer. These new tracking entries are defined today but are not yet wired up to send data, so nothing is being collected yet; the code that reads them and reports the events still needs to be added. The change only affects the desktop app and leaves the web and command-line experiences untouched.

2a8c8af1fba063ed768cafb0e9585b8f560a25fe.text: The change is live today for teams running the automated test suite that guards against silent test loss. If you maintain such a suite, you'll now see a "Flaky suite" warning appear on the run page whenever a test that failed on its first attempt passes when retried (the system still retries automatically, but no longer does so in silence), and you'll see a "Suite ran no tests" warning when a configured job selects no test files at all (for example a job pointing at a directory that doesn't exist yet). These warnings replace a previously green-without-reason status, so the concrete thing you notice is a yellow annotation calling out flakiness or empty runs instead of a clean green pass that hid the problem.

a74c20dc1479774fddf8507f9d9d4ca9e7b6d8f9.text: When tests pass on a quiet computer but fail on a busy one, the problem is not the machine — it is the test hiding a real bug that load only exposes. A new troubleshooting guide explains how to reproduce those conditions on purpose by running tests many times at once while fake CPU work competes for resources, then lists the three most common hidden defects to look for: two runs talking over each other through a fixed connection point, waits that guess at timing instead of listening for the real signal, and background work from one test leaking into another. When you read it, the difference is concrete: a single test that looks fine on its own will start failing in groups, and the output will name exactly which assertions broke and under what load.

326a33d9c24c462f1640172b775db7a368e84e56.text: When you ask for a product plan, the assistant now produces one short, user-facing sentence instead of a longer paragraph. Technical details stay out of that headline and live in a separate build_prompt, so the plan overview stays clean and the implementation guidance stays detailed. This is live today whenever the plan is generated through the affected entry point.

cb153c1518104ed5254b2189f9dd5d5794600fef.text: When you open a new tab or use any feature in the app, that action travels through one central pathway inside the software. New monitoring was added so the team can now see whether that pathway is getting backed up — which helps explain why some people noticed tab opening felt slow. You won't see this directly, but it lets the developers figure out if the app is slowing down because of its own internal traffic or because something else is waiting. The tracking is now in place, so the next time someone reports slowness, the logs can check whether this central pathway was overloaded.

d00f185a4d65a008126a1fbe4e4516fbf003414d.text: Desktop users will no longer generate a specific analytics signal when the ad pool is reused, because that ad-delivery method was retired in favor of inline ads capped by a message count. Nothing else visible changes for users — the assistant still serves ads the same way on the desktop surface; this just stops collecting one obsolete telemetry stamp. The command-line version of this signal keeps firing unchanged.

2d0defa35f3f84fc905fcc5fd0d677726ff4d32b.text: You can now pick the new Claude Opus 5 model when configuring an AI agent in the system. If you were setting up an agent and the model list stopped at Claude Opus 4.7, you will now see Claude Opus 5 as an additional option. The same new model was also added to the list used to translate between the system's internal model names and the ones provided by the external model service. This is a small addition behind the scenes, so if you never build or edit agent definitions yourself, you will not notice anything change.

7427361383f2c51d58977ea9a80d8c0daab82016.text: The assistant's downloadable package received a new catalog number so stores and update systems can tell they are fetching the latest build; this is purely a label change with no effect on how the assistant works. If you reinstalled or updated today, you'd get the same features and performance as before, just tagged with the newer version metadata.

a6064e62018ea29f9349570ff051500030870c1d.text: When you remove a project from the desktop app, the program now records that action as a distinct analytics event, so the team can see how often and when projects get deleted. You won't see any new popup or menu item yourself; this simply adds the 'desktop.project_removed' tracking label to the shared list of things the app already monitors. The change is live today and applies to all desktop users, enabling the team to track project removals just like they already track project openings and thread creations.

1614c75f6c19c5cd6ee24e0fab2d21382e012e0c.text: The assistant now runs every command through the same bash tool on all operating systems, including Windows, instead of using Windows' own Command Prompt. If you use Windows, any command that redirects output to 'nul' (the Windows trick for discarding text) gets automatically swapped to '/dev/null' (the bash equivalent) before it runs, which stops the assistant from accidentally creating a useless file literally named 'nul' on your computer. If you looked at the instructions the assistant shows before running a command, you'd see the Windows-specific examples are gone and only bash-style commands remain. This behavior is live today.

95d0fd6d9160780a76fe40fd4f79bb21858f0d91.text: When you ask Freebuff Chat for help picking a service, the assistant can now drop an interactive button right into the reply, and that button can open setup links that the Gravity recommendation tool already tracked. If you're wiring up a cloud plan, the required-integration step now asks for Gravity's search identifier instead of the service name, so your setup links stay correct. Behind the scenes, the tool that validates those buttons got moved to a shared library so the web, CLI, and agent versions all check the same rule.

84b194f1de686f37ab0e471ed617e9aa9ecdb61d.text: The feedback system now accepts reports that come from the desktop version of the software. When someone using the desktop app submits feedback, that report will include the app's version number and the operating system it's running on, so the team can tell which version is being used. This does not change anything for web, command-line, or developer-tool users—only the desktop client is affected. This is live with the change, since the desktop client can start sending that desktop source and the two new details right away.

9960f1f7021572ab6422137dd38830ec6587af47.text: When you ask the assistant to put together a cloud project plan, it now has to spell out every outside service that needs an API key or login credential before the project can actually run. So instead of just saying "here is a React and Supabase app," the plan will now explicitly list services like Resend (for email) and what account you need to set up. This only affects the planning step you see in the assistant flow today; the new requirement list is already live when you ask for a cloud-ready plan.

3dc5a86f835786fcd0a763eb9fd027c58e732ba5.text: The app can now be told how to talk to a WebContainer-based runtime, a technology that lets code run inside your browser. Two new optional settings were added to the shared configuration: one for an API key that authorizes the connection, and one for the web address where the runtime lives. Because these are optional and no other code in this change reads them yet, the feature is in place but does nothing until a later update wires it up.

f832b44401fb12895cc2023f6e4daf776f7edd74.text: The app no longer passes along a secret key used to run code inside isolated containers directly in your browser. If you looked at the configuration that loads up when the app starts in a web page, that key field and its matching setup line have been removed, so any browser-based sandbox that depended on reading that specific key will no longer find it there. Who is affected today narrowed to teams actively relying on that browser-based sandbox path, since the shared startup configuration no longer exposes that key.

23bcdc85d8b5bee8a0e5c41da85a4fd00a56028e.text: The product now records two new analytics events when someone signs up or activates through an affiliate link, so the tracking system can tell which users came from affiliate recommendations versus other sources. If you looked at the analytics dashboard, you would see new funnel steps labeled affiliate signup and affiliate activation appearing alongside the existing acquisition events. This change is in place now, but it only adds the ability to capture these events, so you would not notice anything different until the affiliate program starts sending users through tracked links and the team begins reporting on the new data.

6238261f2378f06c8e96ce1a0691da31374011e0.text: The packaged copy of the assistant you get from the command line quietly moved from build 0.0.126 to 0.0.127, so anyone pulling a fresh install picks up this slightly newer bundle. Nothing behaves differently once it is running; it is just behind-the-scenes label housekeeping on the release package. If you reinstall now, you are on 0.0.127, but you will not notice any new features or changes in how it works.

2da904013fda20a132f41b21f969630331485b9e.text: The coding assistant you use got a routine version-number bump for its package release, moving from the old version string to the next one in line. If you install or update to this version today, nothing looks or behaves differently in the app—it just carries the updated number that developers see when they bundle and ship the tool to people. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping: the kind of quiet maintenance that happens so your installed copy matches what the makers put on their download list, with no new capability turned on for anyone yet.

68d2a1c12fcf666d7d4d067a3f00e5953afebd34.text: A helper mode within the assistant now starts at most one deep-reasoning sub-agent per question you ask. Previously it could spin up several of these sub-agents at once; now it stops itself after the first one, which should keep responses a bit more focused. The change applies to everyone using that assistant mode today.

ace6dfaa46c3c14d6ce640c5146a1110df23d57f.text: Your coding helper just got slightly better at deciding when to ask for a second opinion. The instruction that told it how many sidekicks to call in was moved to a new spot in its internal checklist, right after the note reminding it to keep prompts short. It now sees that limit in one more place it plans its next steps from, and dropped it from a separate spot it used mid-task. Nothing about how many it can actually call was changed, just where the rule sits in the list. Live now.

b3680bc95f78bcedbcb5b13ae1b18a4f4bb2aa8e.text: If you use the command-line version of the app, you'll now see the freebuff streak streak bonus visual element appear earlier (at 30 lines minimum height instead of 52). This only affects how things look in the terminal and is a minor adjustment to the rendering threshold.

8b1e3056a8678ddbcd1f18cf505017accb927cfd.text: The team quietly swapped out a piece of the assistant's language-handling software for a newer version of the same tool, replacing some of its custom error-handling code with the newer tool's built-in version. If you looked at the surface, nothing about how the assistant responds today would feel different, but behind the scenes it is now relying on the newer library's way of translating error responses instead of its own. This is the kind of maintenance you only notice when it goes wrong, not when it goes right.

0b0023ff8767b3d84e2b2b09dbeb4942bdaeac8f.text: The assistant's public release received a new internal build number, going from the previous version to the next one, with no new features, fixes, or behavior changes for anyone using it. This is routine housekeeping that developers do when preparing software for distribution, so you won't notice any difference in how the assistant works before or after this change. Nothing you experienced has changed because of this.

658e06ca341886f3236ee04d99506989158b8632.text: The software team's internal testing setup now includes a new secret code for connecting to Gravity's payment system, alongside the existing codes it already had. This only affects the developers building and testing the command-line tool; if you're using the tool today, you won't see any difference. The new code is a placeholder, so the software still works exactly as it did before.

f9e4f6d7dec93b1e1e1ff3f7cb5f4e81966e1ac6.text: A small software package that powers part of the assistant's command-line tool quietly rolled to a new release number, bumping from one version to the next with no new features or fixes. This change only touches the packaging files that track the version number, so it doesn't change how the tool behaves. You wouldn't notice anything different, but the behind-the-scenes build system will now reference the updated version when developers compile the tool.

f306a65c7959b621b722d98e361dedf64a575a88.text: When you are using the assistant and it offers you suggested prompts to continue the conversation, the assistant will no longer automatically jump to the next step after showing those suggestions. This affects anyone using the assistant runtime who triggers the suggested prompts feature, and you would notice that after picking a suggested prompt, the conversation waits for your next input instead of moving forward on its own.

0fbf0d3b2edb429bb9f489b15af7022062d7e7ec.text: The assistant can now be told to skip its 'gravity index' tool and the reminder it keeps about using that tool, via a new yes/no setting added to how it is configured. One specific free model, identified as GLM V52, was also added to the list of models you can pick at no cost, so it now appears alongside the other free options when you choose a model. These changes are in place now: the tool is conditionally available depending on the new setting, and the new model is selectable today for anyone using the free tier. If you looked at the menu of free models, you would see the GLM V52 entry where it was missing before; and if the assistant is run with the new setting turned on, it simply won't have the gravity_index tool or its built-in reminder about it at all.

1de3f90a35a3cdef2dd3c3cbaee5d8dee637889e.text: The assistant's downloadable program had its version number updated from one minor number to the next. Anyone who installs or updates the assistant tool will now receive the new release number. If you look at the version information shown by the tool, you would see the updated number where the previous one used to appear.

fd7faf65bf78df2e9a52f592853b2ee7e2ead054.text: When you ask the assistant to edit part of a very large file, it used to read only a shortened preview of that file before making the change. Now it reads the entire file when doing those edits, so it can find and modify the exact spot you pointed to even if it sits deep in a long document. The default behavior of only reading a short preview is unchanged for normal reading tasks.

6e2ec2feb080513c017c65cf5f6aaff9ca564a2e.text: If you write a skill document (a file describing what a helper can do), you can now hand its text to the toolkit and have it checked for correctness on the spot, without the toolkit needing to go find the file on your computer first. The toolkit also gained the ability to load a list of those helpers using the same step-by-step method, which keeps everything working the same for tools that already relied on the old way of loading helpers. This is live today for anyone building or validating helper files through the toolkit.

75c94becef9f223a3266bab4840d4594ae3e8fe8.text: You'll now see ads appear a little sooner in long responses, and there will be fewer of them overall. The system now starts showing ads after about two pieces of content, then shows each next ad after three more pieces instead of two, so responses stretch out before the next interruption.

9db53d4c2136be67ada35d5716835b1bdb6fa07d.text: When you run an agent in the desktop app, it now identifies itself with a mode-specific ID (local or worktree) in addition to the original shared one, so tracing and caching work correctly per execution mode while older desktop clients still connect using the legacy ID. If you looked at the agent list, you'd see the desktop agent registered under three IDs (the original plus local and worktree variants), and each variant points to the same set of models, keeping the model picker consistent across modes.

ececbb77e5428cdaca12b67e331952f67b7fe267.text: The release of your free coding assistant was bumped to a new minor build number, so if you downloaded or updated the program, the version reported is now slightly higher than the last release. This is a behind-the-scenes version-number bump that the packaging tooling flagged as minor, meaning nothing visibly changed in how the assistant works today. If you looked for what is new, you would find the same behavior as before, since the only file touched was the description of the assistant's own release package.

185d51ce8b38a5b87b260ff2abd8c5e62afd08e4.text: The coding assistant's download bundle was rewrapped with a new internal build label; if you install or update the assistant you would simply be pulling a fresh copy that is otherwise identical in day-to-day use. The change is limited to the packaging files, contains no new features, and is being distributed now as part of the standard release flow.

af893569c95a1986af346b999206f467f2729e53.text: The project's ignore list now includes the Freebuff Desktop local runtime state, so generated files like the SQLite database, git worktrees, and built-in skills are no longer tracked in source control. This affects anyone working directly on the codebase: your project folder stays cleaner, and temporary runtime files won't show up as changes when collaborating. You would notice this if you opened a project—the runtime state is regenerated as needed without leaving behind extra files.

c26e125f40313cb18757411f71954c23c3b1cf5f.text: The inline ad banner you see in the command-line tool has been redesigned to take up two lines instead of one, with the ad title on top and the description below it. If you use the CLI and an ad appears inline with your results, you will now notice it is slightly taller and easier to read. The change makes the ad look more organized, especially on wider screens where it can also show the website address next to the description.

b01c3662b93cb30efaf48dd1e2581326fc8a31f4.text: If you're a Freebuff Web user in an outer-region (limited-tier) area, you can now create up to 3 new projects per day instead of just 1, and the counter resets at midnight Pacific time. Nothing else changes about how or when you build projects — just how many you're allowed to start in a single day.

25bcff7a78ced153e5d55e161619e48ffdb74ddb.text: When you're on the CLI installation page and copy the install command, the system now records that action. This helps track how often people intend to install the CLI, especially to see which marketing links or campaigns are working. The tracking also notes whether the copy happened from the main banner or the install section lower on the page.

633c256122a18c49ab89171fbcf977a4370c4658.text: When the assistant asks for a targeted ad, it used to always say the request came from 'chat' even when no specific place was given. Now it simply leaves that label out of the message entirely instead of sending a default value. You wouldn't notice this directly unless you were inspecting the network traffic between the app and the ad server, where the request body will now show one fewer field when no surface is provided.

081bdb229790aa903da4ba4462827ba867139ff3.text: The border around the Freebuff referral banner changed from your brand's primary color to a softer, muted tone, so the banner now blends in more subtly with the rest of the CLI's look instead of standing out with a bold accent color.
