If you're someone who opens the CLI and sees this banner, you'd notice the border looks more understated and matches the muted style already used elsewhere in the interface. This is live today and affects anyone viewing the banner during a CLI session.

05e61796b1e972e04d7ab08ff3ec77fa2d6808ce.text: When you run the assistant interactively from the command line, it now correctly counts how many tokens your conversation is using instead of falling back to a rough guess. It does this by explicitly handing over your personal API key to the token-counting step, which was previously left blank and causing that step to fail every time. The upshot: you get a more accurate read on how close you are to the conversation limit instead of the system silently switching to an estimate.

4fe98d8c048b271a57a32a41c6e79a114f39cb93.text: The free coding assistant quietly advanced to its next published version. If you checked, you'd see the version label bumped up by one, though nothing else around it visibly changed. This is just routine version housekeeping for existing users of the assistant.

9e48fc62b994946fb6f5412439bc458c0c222904.text: A new coding-focused assistant option now appears in the web model picker, so you can choose it alongside the existing list of helpers your service recommends. That new option is a premium (paid) model, and the previously free trial helper is now also treated as premium while its description changes to say its performance is being trialed. If you look at the picker, you'll see the new coding helper labeled as premium and the other helper showing the updated trial wording. A small technical allowance was also added so this new provider's model identifiers are accepted by the system's prefix checks, and that specific model is excluded from result caching.

304f8c16ed581066ab94ad28f4f3d6ab3642865f.text: If you're using the free version of the assistant with the 'no review' option turned on, the code-review step has been removed entirely. Previously, even in no-review mode, the assistant would still spawn a separate reviewer agent for free-tier users; now it skips that reviewer and runs only the type-checking and test bashers in parallel. This means a faster, leaner run when you've explicitly disabled reviews, and it's live today.

d0b938bca49fdf28e96d4a4079bcf350946b2f6f.text: If you chat with Buffy (the AI coding assistant that powers Codebuff, or Freebuff when you use it for free), its opening instructions just got tidier. The old, longer set of rules got folded into one shorter 'General guidelines' section, a leftover internal switch that wasn't doing anything finally got deleted, and a few wording tweaks were made so the message is clearer in both default and free modes. Nothing you see as a user changes today; it's just housekeeping that makes the assistant's rulebook easier to maintain behind the scenes.

6ab789012e6e8f3f43e22246828cb88f0c7a0a80.text: You can now pay for a faster version of the Tencent HY3 model instead of being limited to the free one. Behind the scenes, the app learned the exact paid model ID ('tencent/hy3') and registered it in its list of available models. Free users keep getting the free variant, but anyone on a paying plan can pick the paid one when it shows up in the model selector. The code is in place today, so the option is ready for paid users to choose.

fd36250a7af2416544869fa2694916edfd81b6d2.text: When the code-checker tool tries to verify the runner program's types, it can now find the SDK source files automatically without waiting for a compiled copy to exist first. This matters during continuous integration where the project starts fresh with no build output, because the checker follows the direct path to the SDK's live source code instead of needing a previously-built package. The change keeps the project's automated checks working smoothly from a clean start, without changing any features or behavior you'd see.

48803a249a48035e7f3c3041d5f704b233720a4c.text: When the assistant runs a command in your terminal on Windows, it now hides the extra console window that used to pop up alongside it. That stray window was letting programs like Command Prompt or PowerShell peek at the terminal's hidden input stream and print garbled codes like ^[[I^[[<35;12;7M over the screen. You would notice fewer random characters appearing on top of your terminal interface while commands run. The fix is live today and applies only to terminal commands the assistant launches on Windows.

04d67d73b9052e63dead5ad1a6cf6bbe76c4cd2e.text: The list of free AI models you can pick from just lost one option: Kimi is no longer shown alongside the others like DeepSeek and Minimax. If you open the free model picker in the app, website, or desktop, you won't see Kimi as a choice anymore. Existing conversations using Kimi, if any, are unaffected; this only changes what appears in the default list going forward.

30819406bcc40a132d363f3ac2bceb285ad06031.text: When you ask the assistant to plan or review something, it can now check whether your ChatGPT account is connected through a flexible plug-in point instead of always using the built-in account checker. This only matters for people who customize authentication flows or write tests, because most users continue seeing the same behavior as before. If you looked at the prompt logic, you would notice that two prompt-building functions and one routing function now accept optional callbacks for connection and authentication-code exchange, falling back to the normal built-in behavior when no callback is provided. The feature is live today behind the scenes, but only external test suites or advanced integrations that supply these callbacks would observe any difference.

3966fa98790b1983323c0e71526c781353ab17ea.text: The list of available AI models shown to you has been changed so that Kimi no longer appears as an option to pick, meaning you won't see it in menus or suggestion lists going forward. However, if you were already using Kimi in a saved conversation, that session can still continue using it, so your existing chats won't break. What changed is only how the availability is verified behind the scenes, ensuring that people who selected Kimi before are still admitted while new users can't pick it from the visible list.

4ea700cd6ebb12e204b37095f477a2e8fd5955b5.text: Nothing you can see changes today. The team added a new tracking label that will let them count how often people using the desktop app choose to send a queued action immediately, but that label isn't wired up anywhere yet. It's in place so the feature can be turned on later without further code changes, but right now it just sits there doing nothing.

afc82b86ff83681ec1cf4e282c9cf930f7806eac.text: The team released a new minor version of their coding assistant tool. This is a behind-the-scenes packaging update with no changes to how the tool works for users. If you looked at the tool's internal version listing, you'd see the new version number where the old one was; otherwise, nothing visible changed.

e8a95a27ac79ae26a56a5fa8d8e9904471ec4423.text: When you use the assistant for free, it no longer asks an outside service to count tokens on every step. This makes each free run a bit faster and lighter, because the assistant stops waiting for a web service to tally tokens before continuing. If you pay for the service, nothing changes and token counts stay as they were.

fe1d484e63713352e7fa5bbc033a1171fbed39c7.text: If you ever wanted to point your chat history and debug traces to a different folder than the one your project uses by default, the assistant can now do that without messing with your main setup. You'd notice this if you were running automated tests or managing multiple chat logs side by side: the system lets external tools or scripts redirect where conversation records and trace files get saved, so they don't have to share the same directory as your everyday chat data. It's already live, so anyone managing chat storage locations can take advantage of it right away.

22aa19aade611c31aff555cc55f280c653910fe7.text: When the Codebuff tool needs to find its own address while running on a remote server or in another app's backend, it now looks that address up the same standardized way every time instead of grabbing a possibly-stale address baked in at build time. This stops remote hosts (like cloud functions that include Codebuff's code) from accidentally trying to reach a developer's local machine address that they can never access. If the Codebuff team or anyone embedding Codebuff looks at the logs, the URL resolution should be more predictable and no longer silently point at a localhost address that doesn't exist in the deployed environment. It's live today, affecting only the behind-the-scenes setup for apps that bundle Codebuff's toolkit.

f67bb803bda67f875fd14647d3f3458e56e732fb.text: Behind the scenes in the agent runtime, the way the system turns a saved step template (written as text) into something the assistant can actually run has been tidied up into a single carefully labeled helper. If you were reading the logs while an agent ran, you might see the word 'deserializeHandleSteps' show up where 'eval' used to appear, but what the assistant does and how fast it does it stays the same. Nothing is live in a way you experience differently today; this is housekeeping that reduces the chance of a future mistake when building or modifying agent steps.

bfaad48713d14b4e948a6ad49a2c6f79d6cb250c.text: The referral system can now silently detect why a friend's invite code didn't work, logging the specific reason (like the friend signing up too long after being invited, or attempting to refer themselves) without flooding logs with common errors. It also tags cases where a referred user and referrer share an IP address or browser, acting as supporting evidence for fraud detection rather than an automatic block. These are new analytics events that let the team diagnose "my invite didn't count" support cases by recording failure reasons and suspicious attribution patterns that were previously invisible.

b5b0f9c223124e9746e9faa8d3d5e96978262dc9.text: The assistant's downloadable installer just got a small label update, bumping its recorded build number from 0.0.115 to 0.0.116. This is purely a version tag change, so nothing new will work or look different for you; it just marks this particular snapshot of the installer package. You wouldn't notice anything in the app itself, since no features, fixes, or behaviors changed here.

fe8de7d67497f25e3d80567e07554ae28a82a6e0.text: The app's internal number label was raised by one, so the next time you download or update it, your computer will fetch a slightly newer package than the last one. This doesn't change how the app looks or works for anyone right now; it's just a bookkeeping step the team takes each time they prepare a fresh copy to release.

e90202304629a44f84287728ac07d150354508a2.text: The free model selector that appears when you choose a model now lists the assistant from Minimax first, pushing the DeepSeek option down to second place. This reordering is live today across the web, app, and desktop versions, so you'll see Minimax's model listed at the top of the free choices without any other changes to how the models work or which ones you can access.

3f6c218fcf769874ed0dbdd7ffac50e3294db19e.text: When you ask the assistant to respond while the premium slot is already claimed by someone else, the assistant will now treat that situation the same as being rate-limited or unavailable—it will simply stop and not try to guess how long to wait. This affects anyone running the assistant from the command line who hits a premium slot contention response. You would notice that instead of receiving a delay estimate that doesn't make sense, the request just pauses until the slot is free.

03843a6a7999022e6a7cb133ae6a3d5e8bd851f5.text: If someone tries to claim a referral reward for an account that was created more than 30 days ago, the system will now reject it — a new cutoff makes sure referrers can only earn credit for genuinely recent signups. Separately, there's also a hard ceiling of 100 attributed referrals per person; this isn't a reward limit (those are already capped elsewhere) but a guardrail to stop automated abuse from creating thousands of fake referral records. Both limits are now baked into the shared referral logic, so the behavior is consistent whether you're signing up through the website, the CLI, or another entry point. It's live as part of the latest release.

79127c26ba4d555c14ad85e5f16539447f4a81b8.text: Freebuff Desktop now runs under a single shared account name for abuse tracking, the same way multiple web browser tabs can share one login, instead of needing a separate account name for each AI model you pick. If you use Freebuff Desktop and open several tabs with different models, the system still counts them as coming from one consistent source you, and the desktop tab you see in your picker now shows the full set of free models instead of being limited like the command-line version was. This is live today, so the change is already affecting how Freebuff Desktop sessions are recorded across all desktop users starting June30, 2026.

6937a4a1d869a5d878d178a2c3b57d4ae6f75562.text: The app gained a new built-in event type that tracks when a desktop thread's title is updated. This lets the developers count how often desktop users rename or edit their thread titles for analytics purposes. The change only adds a new tracking option; it does not alter how you use the app or change what you see.

90210bb6a19dd9ee6bdc4f322668619399caa166.text: If you use the Freebuff command-line tool to chat with an AI, the assistant now quietly records which subscription level you have when you send a message. Your account's access tier is sent along with your message data; if the system can't find your session or tier for any reason, it just logs 'unknown'. You won't see anything new on screen, but the people who build and improve Freebuff can now use your tier information to understand how different subscriber levels use the tool.

1576d8cceceddde2310b475e1dbe0f0f0add67d5.text: If you refer friends to get perks, the account-age requirement is now 4 months instead of 12. If you were previously blocked because your GitHub account was between 4 and 12 months old, you can now qualify using any of the referral products. The system now uses one consistent age rule instead of different ones depending on the product you choose.

00b24d0ffa5d006b4e9d830de87f5df772cbcc8e.text: The lightweight version of Codebuff now talks to a different AI model behind the scenes, MiniMax M3 instead of DeepSeek V4 Flash, and it will also ask the matching review helper to join in instead of the old one. This only changed the automated checks that confirm the lightweight setup is pointing at the right model and helper, so regular users won't see any new features or behavior today. If you looked at the lightweight setup details, you'd notice the model name and the helper name have both changed in the test expectations.

2cb4fc339e109217ef4fba773241100ee66680f0.text: If you refer a friend to the assistant through the Web, desktop app, or browser extension, that friend now needs a GitHub account that's been open for at least a year to qualify for your referral bonus—previously the Web version only required 4 months. Additionally, the number of extra free daily sessions you can earn from these referrals is now capped at 3 per day. These new limits are already in place in the system's core settings, so anyone checking referral requirements will see the updated rules today.

3c9348e961a86ace862cbc3c379eb2c2cb4fc703.text: This is a behind-the-scenes change to how the software's automated checks run, not something you would see in the product. The team that maintains the code updated some of the test scripts that make sure new changes don't break things; specifically, they adjusted conditions that decide whether certain live tests run during development. These tests now require an explicit approval flag and an API key to run against real services, and one test was simplified to use a more direct setup. Since the change only touches testing files and doesn't alter any of the shipped product code, nothing about your experience using the software is different today.

a64b9c03fd75cad359bf64f3c82b1bc7651a2bc4.text: The product now records three new milestones for its referral program: when someone uses a referral, when that referral finishes converting, and a daily snapshot of all the referrals still waiting to finish. These events are collected through the billing system and sent to the analytics store, with the snapshot event summarizing results across the entire pending list in a single report rather than logging each referral one by one. This is live today as part of the referral program server logic.

bf6d1e5e2016e11d155092e0e93ad17493db7a12.text: The software's build number ticked up to a new release identifier as part of routine packaging work, so anyone installing or updating it via standard package tools will receive this refreshed version on the next pull. If you were watching the release logs you might see the newer number show up sooner, but the day-to-day behavior stays the same - this is just keeping the behind-the-scenes bookkeeping tidy.

82827cafd83ff35bc18530e2729ccf86ee4497f4.text: A small behind-the-scenes version number was advanced for the free coding assistant tool, moving it from one internal release label to the next. This is routine housekeeping that the team bumps on each packaged release; it doesn't change what you can do with the tool today. If you were checking for the newest packaged version, you'd find the updated label, but there are no new features or fixes to notice.

d1fb7fdf239e8a306f7d31a19fd4de4fa4ab58e0.text: After you read a response from Freebuff Chat, you will now see three suggested follow-up questions appear, each phrased as something you might naturally type next — like "Show me how to..." — letting you continue the conversation with a single click instead of typing a new prompt. These suggestions are chosen for you specifically based on what you just discussed, rather than being generic prompts. The change is live today in the Freebuff Chat web interface as part of a routine weekly update.

6e8e17d890d006bf4ee5a2545d18ed9fac02f01e.text: When someone following a referral gets to the new Get Started screen, the product can now quietly count each step of their journey from seeing the page all the way through signing in, connecting GitHub, copying the install command, or clicking out to the web — and it can split those counts by whichever referrer name was passed along. The developer note clarifies this is the in-order funnel for the Freebuff referral onboarding path. The CLI also rolled forward a version number, but that's just the package release label, not a user-facing feature.

6e063e113c757309a151e1c78b52ebca7a12c0e6.text: When the service checks whether an internet address belongs to a regular person or to a shady server farm, it now listens to a label that the address database already provides. Real users sitting behind home internet, business fiber, school networks, or government lines are no longer bumped by hosting-only filters. The result, live today: fewer honest visitors get mistaken for VPN or bot traffic because the system finally trusts the ordinary-network tag.

43301d5fd2bcb9bdf1e0f3fc26a14de115359d84.text: The assistant can now be tracked when it comes from a Reddit ad. If you clicked a Reddit ad to install or sign up for the assistant, the team now records six specific steps in that journey—like when you first run it, log in, sign up, send your first message, or click the gravity ad again—plus one event that captures which ad or link originally brought you there. Nothing looks different to you on screen; this just sets up the named steps so the team can later build the parts of the product that actually report when those steps happen.

ff16426abdc93feb759df1e90f94539e877a07ca.text: The coding assistant's downloadable tool got a small version-number bump, which is how the team labels each packaged release they ship for command-line use. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping that simply prepares the next build; anyone downloading or updating the command-line tool will pull the freshly labeled version, but they won't notice any new behavior from this change alone.

feb051debac2365daf253d424385b6c6e57ec64a.text: The assistant switched to a newer version of its development toolkit, which is used behind the scenes to build and run the software. You would not notice anything different while using it; this only affects how the assistant's code is assembled internally. This kind of update keeps everything running smoothly and stays compatible with the latest tools.

637bdf14fa0443c9539f6550eeb64ae129fb55c6.text: When you type a prompt to the assistant in the CLI, it now records one analytics event each time. This event is turned on for Freebuff users only and is never skipped, so the team can count how many unique people use the CLI daily. If you are a Freebuff user, your prompts are now tracked for daily usage stats; if you are a Codebuff user, nothing changes.

0b97b6efd524e5044a6c7b31e20a7a748326feff.text: The downloadable helper application for the freebuff coding assistant received a new version number, moving from the previous build to the next one. You would see this new number if you checked the package details in your terminal or development tools before or after installing it. This is purely a behind-the-scenes numbering change that helps track versions; it does not add or remove any features. The change is live today for anyone downloading the assistant through its command-line installation process.

de1f1f716ab020ce631b126794f4de1a48daa13f.text: The referral program now gives everyone who participates more daily uses of the assistant. The base level (no referrals needed) increased from 20 to 24 standard uses and from 3 to 4 premium uses each day. Higher referral tiers received even larger increases—ranging from 30% to more than 70% more standard uses and 50% to 150% more premium uses—all taking effect today.

747abe3c717770a91c955c6e004da6e4154eb159.text: The freebuff package has been re-versioned to 0.0.110, but it does not add any new features or behavior—it is a behind-the-scenes numbering bump. If you install the assistant as a command-line tool you will now see version 0.0.110 in its metadata, but nothing else will function differently. This is housekeeping to track the release for developers packaging this tool, and it went live today.

cd4e11ce2c5b9b4f3a216ab5c0f02dcfeac333e3.text: When you open the chat, the assistant now shows suggested starter questions near the top of the screen instead of at the bottom, and only during normal first-time setup flows. If you are already past onboarding or are in review mode, those suggestions will not appear. This means the prompt list shows up earlier and stays hidden in the situations where it used to show up incorrectly.

edacbeb3609c311a58aac127c5264255149302df.text: The software now uses the name 'Freebuff' instead of the old 'Manicode' name on its official license paperwork and in the sample data sets used to test it. If you looked at the license file that ships with the software or the test files that simulate a real project setup, you'd see the copyright line now reads Freebuff, Inc. and sample database addresses or login paths that once said 'manicode' now say 'codebuff' or 'freebuff', like changing a placeholder username in a training exercise. The software itself works exactly the same way; only the paperwork and practice examples got a name tag change.

43d2681d423104d649f6809fe00414f57b212420.text: The freebuff command-line tool quietly rolled out a new version, so anyone running it will be asked to update to keep things in sync. You won't see any new features or behavior changes, just the version number ticking up under the hood.

25b6dde3bbfade9e2e2423e30c20766f5c73d2b9.text: The coding tool just rolled out a routine software update that bumps its internal version number, which is something the system uses to keep track of what's running. Nobody will see a new feature or notice anything working differently. If you checked your installation, you'd just see a new version number where these updates are tracked.

e459f2a24426424306293d667cef2ef135ed1cbc.text: If you are on the highest-tier Max plan, your advanced helper agents now use the newer Opus model instead of the older Fable model. The specialized agents that think through problems and write/review code have all been switched over, and the old Fable options have been removed. You will not see a different button or command, but if you spawn these helper agents, they are running on the updated model. This change is already live as of today.

ccac201df6fc4a1ab037a5d13c930a49e65459fe.text: If you signed up for the service through a friend's referral in a restricted country, you can still earn higher tiers and unlock watermark-free usage, but you will only get the basic free-model limit instead of the upgraded premium limit because premium models stay blocked in your region. The change only added a short note to the documentation explaining that difference, so nothing about how your account actually works today has changed; the behavior it describes is already how the system treats referral tiers in geo-gated regions.

7f85312af394fa37a87011970442a28c6c728292.text: If you pick a smart model in the assistant, it can now call on a special reasoning helper for harder problems, and that helper is triggered by a wider range of situations (not just the toughest puzzles, but also tricky bugs and uncertain approaches). Two recently added full-access models join the supported list, so more capable options can use the helper, while the fastest budget-friendly model stays excluded to keep things quick. What you'd notice: when you choose one of the newer full-access models, the assistant will offer the deeper-thinking mode more often than before.

ed764c4f8db46d834c0b0f04883fee15b35c4c55.text: When you launch the assistant on a Windows computer, the startup check used to time out because it missed the early terminal-setup signals the program sends. It now also recognizes the specific escape codes that tell the terminal to switch to full-screen mode and enable advanced keyboard handling, so the launch test can confirm the interface reached the screen instead of waiting for slower text to appear. You would only notice this if you were watching the automated startup tests, where they will stop failing intermittently on Windows servers.

4999c63158f0f57c511141ac4277be73ca153b19.text: The program that packages the free coding assistant for download has been given a new build number so the next release can be identified. This only affects people who install the tool fresh from the package repository, and you would only notice the version listed on the package page changing.

7f268e15a4c0210e7b041f3cbb2265db15d97167.text: When you use the AI assistant through certain products, the system that tracks where your usage comes from will now only look at which version of the assistant template was started at the beginning of this session. It will no longer also try to copy over an older tracking label that might have been saved from before. You wouldn't see this change directly, but if you could look at the background data being recorded for attribution purposes, it would show a single, simpler source label instead of one that could be influenced by leftover prior settings. This adjustment is live now as part of the agent runtime.

f0766573fad36c88ba482c7873e7054124140720.text: When you use the assistant, it now remembers which version of the product you're signed up for instead of resetting it on every interaction. If your account already had a specific version assigned, that stays in place; otherwise it picks one based on which assistant you're using. You won't see any visible change, but your usage will be correctly counted under the right version going forward.

778c6c18965612446c6b4fb568cba5120399fd94.text: The AI assistant will no longer summon a code reviewer after answering your questions or writing plans when no actual code was changed. This only affects the default, max, and free-tier assistants. You won't notice anything different in how responses look, but behind the scenes, the assistant is being told explicitly not to trigger that review step for non-code tasks.

be22023ea98700318566f36138d9cd5c6fe9eddb.text: The automated test that checks the web-research assistant now gives the assistant more room to work. You would not notice anything if you simply use the assistant, since this only adjusts a test, not the product you interact with.

f63541370c2725c95b8e38a776ce4c91402c2f7f.text: When you ask the web-research assistant a question, it can no longer answer from a quick search alone. It now keeps searching and reading follow-up pages until it has reviewed at least three full articles or pages (and five for trickier, multi-part questions) in parallel before giving you an answer. You'd notice it takes a bit longer to get a response, but the answer will be backed by actual page content instead of just short search summaries. This stricter behavior went into effect today.

38844c7040fd9dd3eedac0755f87c6bfe6b1f75a.text: If you start a chat at freebuff.com/chat today, the assistant can now hand your question off to a web-search helper instead of just saying it can't look anything up, so you may see it briefly check the live web and drop in sourced answers or run several searches in parallel when a topic calls for it. Behind that, the chat assistant was given permission to launch a dedicated web-research agent (now labeled Web Researcher rather than its old placeholder name), and that researcher was taught to browse for current information, run parallel searches, and cite its sources.

937787d54b56ca6ee152ff1bb454214701601916.text: The Base2 assistant can now pick a newer, higher‑thinking version of its model when you ask it to reason at maximum depth, and otherwise defaults to the current model. If you run that assistant with max‑depth reasoning turned on, it will now call the "claude‑fable‑5" model instead of the older version, which should let it work through harder problems; everyone else keeps using the standard model. The system now also recognizes both of these model names, so anything that checks or swaps models in the background will accept them without errors.

0a3669024953392e5c7b6171940113766df9c728.text: When your connection sits idle for a while during a chat with the assistant, you now see a plain-English note explaining that the network went quiet for five minutes instead of a scary technical error. The agent runtime and the SDK both catch this specific timeout and swap in friendly guidance, and the database no longer stores giant stack traces when runs fail, so records stay small and readable.

6142b8be692c47b91afbaaced3ad6e433ab47175.text: When you run the command-line tool on Windows, it previously could crash with a confusing error stack if security software blocked the helper program from starting. Now, the launcher catches that startup failure instantly and prints a clear explanation before exiting cleanly, so you see a readable message instead of a crash. This helps anyone on Windows whose antivirus or built-in Smart App Control stops the program from running. The fix is live today and also covers the free-trial version of the tool.

7715a97463b9c6609c1f9e3a5d32eaf9449fb6dd.text: New users signing up for Freebuff will now see a different AI model selected by default in their conversation picker. Instead of the previous default, the system now picks MiniMax M3, which the developers chose because it's smarter and can handle images, so routine messages don't need to use up the limited 5-per-day premium requests. If you're already using Freebuff, your currently selected or saved default stays exactly as it is. The change only affects brand-new accounts or anyone who hasn't manually picked a model yet.

7754f72e80e57678d648b9170a9bc725d31066a6.text: When you see a waiting room screen explaining that some AI models aren't available with your current connection, the wording has been reworked to explain why rather than just labeling it as a restriction. The message now specifically mentions whether your region, VPN, or unconfirmed location is the reason certain models won't appear, and it frames this as a matter of availability rather than blocked access. Only free-tier users who encounter these restrictions will see the updated notices, and the session counter now correctly labels whether you're seeing regular sessions or premium sessions based on your access level. These wording and labeling adjustments are already live in the waiting room screen.

293172345e45adda8b4ab9be0546a1b5614ad09c.text: Right now, when you ask the assistant what plan you're on while a task is running, it shows how many units you've used so far out of your total — for example, '5 of 100 used' — instead of the old '95 left'. This is the same style of number shown in the menu where you pick which model to use, so everything looks consistent. If you glanced at the status line mid-task, the number and the word 'used' replace the previous 'left' label.

ac888447c1bb269cec8476262a11cf270b02942c.text: A small behind-the-scenes update bumped the release version of the free coding assistant's packaging build, visible only to developers preparing the desktop app bundle. If you checked the project files on GitHub, you'd see one line change the version number in the packaging configuration, which is used when the app gets prepared for distribution. This update is live today, but it doesn't add new features or change how the app behaves for you.

f219b409368e128adf95153f694aabf896189c0e.text: When you open a new chat session, the assistant will now default to the Kimi model instead of the DeepSeek V4 Pro model that was used before. This change takes effect immediately for new sessions you start, so your very first message in a fresh chat will be handled by Kimi unless you manually switch to a different model. The adjustment only modifies which model is pre-selected at startup and does not affect your access to other available models or any ongoing conversations. Other smaller updates arrived alongside it, including a renaming of an ad-banner component and a replacement of an older model option in the free model picker.

2c743c61f11ee2f2df023ddf95b3268ed4737b07.text: A new artificial intelligence option now appears second in the list of available assistants, right after DeepSeek V4 Pro, and it comes with a notice saying it may collect information to help train future versions. If you open the assistant picker in either the command-line tool or the web version, you will see this assistant listed near the top instead of further down. The change is live today for anyone using the latest app.

fe118aa3f6950ee3cc04197a155e65dc87a57339.text: When you open the app without picking a specific model, it now uses DeepSeek V4 Pro as the default instead of DeepSeek V4 Flash. This applies to everyone on the web, CLI, and desktop apps. If you were not already selecting a model manually, you will notice the assistant responding with the Pro version's capabilities.

3deed7d21a3488df1deed4440a635321ec6bb445.text: When you're using the CLI and waiting for your turn in the waiting room, the summary now shows how many premium sessions you have left to use today instead of how many you've already used. Previously it displayed something like '2 of 5 sessions used today', and now it shows '3 of 5 premium sessions left'. The wording for limited-tier users also changed from 'sessions' to 'premium sessions' for consistency. This affects only the display text shown in the CLI interface.

323d5e50a72afae4df7bd73a04c94ded077e8d8c.text: The downloadable installer for the coding assistant just got its internal version number refreshed from the old release to a newer one, with no new features or behavior changes. If you download or update the installer today, you're getting this refreshed package, but nothing about how it works or what it does has changed. It's behind-the-scenes housekeeping to keep the release packaging tidy.

56b18a1960ad0c308f1b210f01aa7b0fac0b98f0.text: The coding tool got a fresh version number, the kind of routine update companies give their software to track new builds. You won't see any new features or behavior changes from this update alone. It's primarily a behind-the-scenes package version bump that doesn't affect what the tool can do.

bc2e521ae7126000175fdb40f34658c9a358d7ff.text: The free coding assistant can now be told not to automatically bring in a helper that reviews your code. This only matters if you're using the free tier of the tool and you call it with the noReview option turned on; otherwise nothing you see today changes. A couple of behind-the-scenes bits also landed at the same time: tool definitions sent to OpenAI-compatible providers now get their references resolved ahead of time so they won't fail upstream, and an optional tracking id was added that does nothing yet since nothing reads it.

ec6049895f39b81037265dc2dc4ec8ee4577161a.text: The team updated the internal checks that make sure the assistant's tools are described correctly. Specifically, they rewrote how the gravity index search feature's possible actions are listed — switching from a loose type definition to a stricter interface that now spells out a fixed set of allowed actions like search, browse, and report integration. This is a behind-the-scenes test suite update with no changes to the features themselves; users will not notice any difference in behavior today. The change ensures that only the intended gravity index actions are recognized going forward, preventing unexpected or unsupported operations.

a7e0fa38f02a212b5209e1dfcd97f866d9cba34e.text: The tagline shown for MiMo 2.5 Pro has changed from 'Smartest & Slower' to 'Smartest & Slow'. This corrects a small grammar inconsistency and only affects the text displayed next to the model name in the model picker used across the assistant's apps. You would notice the updated wording if you opened the model selection menu; the change is live today.

ce77a82c508d26c25c88f298f9d65f4ff224125f.text: When you use the assistant in its quick, streamlined mode, it can now follow up your task with suggested next steps. Previously, that mode turned follow-up suggestions off, so after a fast answer you'd just get the result and nothing else. The rule that blocked suggestions in fast mode is gone, so the same suggestions you see in normal mode now appear there too. If you ask something and get a quick reply, you may notice a short list of next things you could try appearing at the end.

9de3b7019af2014d6245280c7808e2a92afeeed1.text: The team stopped running a small internal check that verified the description next to one premium-tier AI model still read a specific phrase; nothing you see in the app changes, and the model's description itself was already updated separately. If you opened the project's test files, you would no longer find that check listed among the things they run. This is behind-the-scenes cleanup only.

87a6812a3ad19cd2f3132214ce5034886777c02d.text: The cost of running certain AI assistants just went up, so if your team or plan uses GPT-5.2, GPT-5.3 with code tools, or GPT-5.4, you will pay more for each response those assistants generate. Prices for using these assistants rose sharply, with GPT-5.4 now costing 50% more per reply and the others about 40% higher, while discounted cached input rates climbed in the same proportions. These pricing constants are already in place in the billing system, so the higher rates apply to usage from today.

89a10d6afc6fa78b3a7f001542950aae6e48307d.text: When you run a help command (like asking for instructions), the program used to accidentally clear the text from the screen because it wrongly turned off the full-screen display mode. Now it only turns off that mode after running an interactive program that actually uses a full-screen display, so help text stays visible. It also recognizes when the program crashed unexpectedly on Windows and only then performs the full cleanup.

0491f53a1259429a483e3099e04d576cbb5e5072.text: When the assistant looks around your computer to find available agent files, it now skips over folders named node_modules, scripts, skills, and anything starting with skills-, as well as folders that begin with a dot. It also does a more precise check on individual files so that type declaration files and any file named like a test or spec file are not picked up. You wouldn't see these extra files appear as agents anymore, but if you keep agent files in those now-skipped folders, they won't load at all. The change is live today wherever this version of the assistant tooling is installed.

2784b64f5e3b68033bc7c17be8184eafb65fb7bf.text: You now have two new tiers of AI model to choose from when building with the platform, and the system now knows exactly how much each one costs to run. If you open the pricing settings, you will see the standard new model charges five cents for every thousand words you ask it to read and thirty cents for every thousand words it writes back, while the premium version of the same model costs thirty cents to read and three dollars to write, with a special free rate for words that were recently looked at. The change is live today.

4642c507f8c5fe9034ddd46a98554ba964cb16db.text: When the assistant looks up a service for you to connect to (like a database or email provider), it now passes along your current session, the project repo, and the specific step you're on, so each lookup is tagged with where it came from. The service catalog information is also reorganized behind the scenes into clearer sections for searching, browsing, and getting setup details. If you use the assistant to integrate a service, you may notice the credential setup link it points you to is now the tracked signup URL, shown as a 'Get your {service name} API key' button when available. This is live today for anyone using the Gravity Index integration flow.

806e27d82f418a16f9f87c3a3e9d8af62c99d0b4.text: The assistant Buffy now shows today's date in a fresh, properly formatted way inside the system prompt that guides its behavior. Previously the date was baked in with a formatting step that lived in the wrong place, which made it static and harder to update. Now date formatting lives in the shared templating system alongside the other dynamic pieces, and the prompt references it as a placeholder that gets filled in at runtime. What you'd notice: if you look at the prompt, it reads 'Current date: <today's date>' and that date will actually match the day you're running it, instead of being a fixed value from when the code was written.

e438af55d55a845703265971145c837b820313dd.text: Starting today, if you try to use the free assistant from behind most VPNs or proxies, you won’t be turned away — you’ll be quietly moved into a stripped-down mode that gives you the cheaper, faster assistant instead of the full one. Only traffic that comes through the privacy network run by Cloudflare is still blocked completely; everything else that looks private just lands you in the budget lane. If you see a sudden downgrade in how the assistant responds rather than an error page, that is exactly why.

4c20af5ced7ab262a2098201888f8a73f5383b19.text: When you run the assistant and it can't start the helper program it needs, you now get a clearer message that tells you your operating system and setup details, and it gives Windows-specific tips if your antivirus or CPU is the likely cause. This affects anyone running the tool from the command line when the downloaded helper binary is missing or won't launch. If you looked, instead of a generic failure you'd see a short report listing your platform, Node version, where the binary is, and guidance on cleaning up stale installation files, so you can tell whether the file is genuinely gone or blocked by something on your machine.

61c1eefd5999cb4bd2d8367929e3016eb6e2d69f.text: Free users can no longer choose GLM 5.1 as their model option; it has been removed from the free service lineup across the platform. You would notice this if you previously selected GLM 5.1, as it is no longer listed among the available models. The change also affects specific agent tools (base2-free and code-reviewer-minimax), which no longer reference GLM 5.1, and documentation describing service availability hours for GLM 5.1 has been updated. This adjustment is live today.

21bb34cdb3e14f4f8bfd2eea28c3e45691483af5.text: When you've hit the free daily session limit, the screen now shows a clear explanation of when your allowance will reset, including a live countdown of the hours remaining, instead of just a generic disabled message. This only affects the free tier of users who've used up their allotted sessions; the screen tells them exactly how many they had and how long until they can start again.

4423d090bc0971f43a9c24e00c675b163ce61f38.text: When you use a free service (like web search), the system now lets you go ahead and use it without checking whether you have any paid credits on file. Before this change, even free requests were being blocked with a 'payment needed' error because the system was still checking your balance. This only applies to specific internal helpers that handle API calls, so services like web search will now work as expected for users without requiring a balance check.

84778f9c96c19f127e53384b91190eb9d0e40c3c.text: If you run a CLI command that tells the assistant to spawn a sub-agent and that sub-agent finishes without producing any output, you'll no longer see an empty or confusing error block appear in the response. The only thing you'd notice is that those silent failures are simply left out of what gets displayed. If the sub-agent did manage to produce some output before failing, that result still shows up as usual, just marked as complete instead of failed.

692b6fa2f3086116b9bf800c806b6963bd46df3b.text: When you open the browser login page during setup and the terminal never sent over a valid login code (or it already expired), the page now shows a clear 'link expired' message instead of freezing or trying to continue with a broken connection. This affects anyone running the setup flow through the terminal command, and you'd notice the helpful card telling you to return to your terminal and restart the process rather than seeing a loading spinner or error. The change is live today across both product surfaces.

565af42cfc6575e75f78e03f4ba8ad2609c4f31b.text: The assistant now mentions today's date at the start of its instructions, so you may notice references to the current date (for example, May 21, 2026) when interacting with the base system prompt. This date is generated and injected automatically each time the assistant is used, rather than being written in once and left unchanged.

d7915d1a449c1be76381e933b1237998f23e20ec.text: If you open the live stats page on Freebuff, the screen looks simpler now: the big counter no longer sits under the words "active Freebuff sessions right now," the country list no longer shows the raw two-letter codes like "us" next to the names, and the introductory sentence was shortened from "Real-time Freebuff sessions across every country we can identify, refreshed as people start coding." to just "Real-time Freebuff sessions across every country." The page still updates in real time as people start coding; only the extra text was removed. Nothing else about the page's behavior changed.

ae7713bb730569e0e4cfc464cd0e84ae5a4570c1.text: When someone tries to use the tool from a country where access isn't allowed, they will now see a clearer message that says their access was restricted because of their detected country, along with the country code. Previously, the message just said "outside available countries" without as much explanation. This only affects the text shown during the waiting-room screen, and it is live now.

f60634199133dea8a0d80c669a57cc7d750525c0.text: If you run the assistant from the command line at work, it can now route its internet traffic through your company's proxy server. When you start it, it looks for a proxy address in your system settings (HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, and lowercase versions) or in its own configuration file, and if it finds one, it sends all its web requests through that proxy instead of directly. You can still turn this off by explicitly telling it not to use any proxy, and everything works the same once the traffic reaches the proxy.

522068a877a8196bc879f2fcd71b4e4d2ccbea38.text: The live stats display on the homepage no longer shows extra text under each country and model name. It also removes the explanatory sentence below the big number that counted active sessions right now. If you open the live page today, the numbers are still there but surrounded by less clutter.

9d59c700eaa58184656fe03f362b7a04c4aee4c0.text: When you open the model selection screen in the CLI on a terminal that isn't very tall, the logo now shrinks or disappears to make room, and the list of models scrolls in a box instead of squishing everything together. The picker keeps keyboard focus visible as you move through the models, and the logo automatically downgrades to a single text line when there are fewer than six rows available. This is live today for anyone running the CLI on short terminals.

2af416b863e4aab3507c0cb19b141fd839d44871.text: If you visit Freebuff's website, the FAQ section now states clearly that the service is available in all countries, not just the full list named there, since the service operates globally in 'full' or 'limited' mode. You would notice the wording changed from implying a hard block outside those countries to explicitly confirming worldwide access with reduced functionality. This clarification affects anyone outside the named countries (or using a VPN) who previously may have wondered whether the service worked where they were.

f3d9f45431c96e2327bd28425a86a7bd853be3b4.text: The tool that builds your Windows download stopped using a stripped-down version of the Bun runtime and switched back to the full one, so the Windows release build now runs a standard build step where it previously used a stripped-down mode. If you looked, you would see the release setup label change from the reduced build to the full build in the Windows release flow and the Windows freebuff test flow. This is a behind-the-scenes change to how the Windows build is run, so most readers would not notice it directly unless they watch the build process.

982f726c537864c08fa1e238ac7eae796286d453.text: Your chat requests are now being logged with a condensed version that skips the actual conversation content (messages get omitted). Instead of saving the full chat request details until a provider finishes processing, the system now saves a summary with just the essentials like model, temperature, and message counts to the main logs, while the complete request still goes to a separate storage table upfront. This means your conversations aren't retained in the telemetry logs that were previously held until streaming completed, reducing how long full chat data lingers in the system during processing.

c3027175a0242057dd0de85ffcc835c9ad75a5e7.text: When you land on the waiting-room screen in the CLI app, you'll now see a specific reason for why you're seeing a reduced set of models instead of a generic message. For example, you might see 'hosting network detected' or 'outside available countries (FR),' which tells you exactly why your access is limited. The server now sends your country code, the specific reason your IP was blocked, and any privacy-related signals (like VPN or Tor usage) directly to the client, so the app doesn't have to figure it out locally.

e43653226f8be2c6f80ddbf0c98bcfa96cde9856.text: The homepage now shows a small live snapshot of Freebuff activity, so you can see real-time usage at a glance instead of visiting a separate page. That count now refreshes every 60 seconds (up from 15) and is served from a short-term cache, which keeps the numbers steady while reducing how often the site checks for updates.

7d451c872df79982a576bc3a1ac2906762cf1445.text: When you're using the newer DeepSeek model or OpenRouter for chat, the service now detects when your connection drops mid-response and cleanly cancels the still-running generation instead of letting it keep going and potentially getting billed for work you didn't receive. For OpenRouter, it waits about two minutes after a disconnect to give a final chance at recovery before fully cancelling, and for DeepSeek's newest Flash model it cancels immediately since that version supports it. Behind the scenes, it also keeps your message content out of error logging when you're on the restricted limited access tier, recording that it was omitted instead of the actual text. This is live today for those specific models and the telemetry changes apply to how request errors are recorded going forward.

7dc62c8e1a89fb06800c16072f4db5e169f1ddb4.text: The help page now clearly explains that people outside certain countries (or using a VPN) get a more restricted version of the service: they can only use one specific AI model, and only for up to 5 one-hour sessions per day. Visitors reading the FAQ will see a new section answering 'What is limited mode?', and the existing sections about which countries are supported and which models are offered have been adjusted to make the difference between full and limited access more obvious.

5380b97cc366aad170b24591ca16269002164dbd.text: You can now type /model:mode instead of /mode:mode to switch the assistant between different modes, and both phrases will work the same way. The system now accepts either word to reach the same command. If you looked, you would see /model:mode treated as an alternate spelling of /mode:mode in the list of available commands. This works today.

558d1fe9213d28182cede6c95c42da24b4384bb4.text: When you use the CLI to switch models or return to the start screen, your session's access tier, queue depth, and rate limits were being thrown away, causing the screen to forget important details about your tier. Now the landing logic preserves that metadata so limited-tier users see 'Back to start' and others see 'Change model', with matching loading labels. This affects CLI users switching models or returning to the landing screen in Freebuff sessions, and the fix is live as part of release 1.0.676.

7f4d431302996f59c6624a4f9eaf992dc7d413b9.text: You might notice that some buttons in the limited landing panel now have slightly better contrast when interacting with them. Instead of using the primary theme color, the text now uses the foreground color. This is a minor visual tweak aimed at improving readability. This change is live today for anyone using the CLI.

47d025ad7973d0b474df5b2f2e83d6459469d17c.text: When you're waiting to use the assistant and your premium reset timer shows up next to how many times you've used it, the screen now prints a comma instead of a dot-dot-dot symbol between those two numbers. You'd notice this if you were looking at the model selection screen while signed in with premium access and watching the countdown timer. The change only affects how that small bit of text is spaced — nothing else about how the timer counts or when it resets.

6383ae8acdef116d44f37f944b28d0f5df4b5397.text: When someone tries to log in to Freebuff using a code that doesn't look right, the system now writes down detailed information about what went wrong instead of staying quiet. Only the Freebuff team can see these notes, which helps them spot and fix problems with login links that are broken or look suspicious. You won't notice anything different when you use Freebuff, but if a login fails behind the scenes, there will now be a clear trail for the team to investigate.

8c189c305a0e72090d8eec4585136627709ce00d.text: If you run the app on your own computer in development mode, you can now flip a setting (FREEBUFF_DEV_FORCE_LIMITED) to see the restricted Freebuff experience—the one where only the DeepSeek Flash model is offered—without waiting on country checks or cached data. Developers on the team working locally will notice this limited tier kicks in right away when they set that flag to true, and turning it off takes effect immediately because the system skips reading or storing cached access results for those requests. Everyone already using the live Freebuff service is unaffected; this only matters while building or testing on localhost, and only when the environment is set to dev.

cae558b46d0c0c795fbf2c4644b5bbbfff8b2807.text: The free DeepSeek Flash assistant no longer asks a remote server to count how many words you've used before replying. Instead, it estimates that count locally on its own, which lets your request get answered faster since it skips that back-and-forth network call. This only applies if you're using that specific free assistant and you're accessing it through Codebuff. You wouldn't see this directly, but your messages would come back a little quicker.

cb88ae8074cd9a134d1a6cc2543498652b157004.text: The model picker in the CLI tool got internally reorganized so it no longer creates unnecessary intermediate lists just to sort them again. If you open the free model selection screen, you will see the exact same list of models in the same order as before. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping that makes the code simpler without changing anything you experience.

00ac6486b7f4a73b04f65ef4eec8fd5066890343.text: When you open the list of free models on Freebuff's website and in the app's help text, you'll now see DeepSeek V4 Flash listed right above MiniMax M2.7 instead of below it. Freebuff shuffled two entries in its internal settings and updated the frequently asked questions text to match, so the order stays consistent across the model picker and the help section. The change is live today for Freebuff users accessing the free model list or reading the FAQ.

7a95a981493400eb1024210de5ea59ab08e9bad7.text: The onboarding page you see when you log in to the Freebuff web app with a CLI auth code now captures more detail in its error logs when the code is invalid. If a login attempt fails, the system quietly records things like the auth code length, hash prefix, resolved token, and request headers such as host, origin, and user-agent — not for you to see directly, but so the development team can diagnose why the failure occurred. This change is live today and affects anyone attempting to onboard via an invalid Freebuff CLI auth code.

fbdf2f3ecac0bf85fe13a36b6087e65769ab3354.text: When a basher run finishes and you look at its collapsed preview, the CLI no longer shows the raw command text; instead it shows a single, width-aware line of the agent's finished output (truncated with an ellipsis if needed). You notice it only in collapsed/unstreaming branches for basher-type agents, where the preview respects the terminal width you have room for, falling back to the previous text/command output behavior when there's nothing suitable to summarize.

9f96ac1233d28d7111876e14ef5f9682669c2843.text: When you use the assistant for free, it can now run command-line tools inside a split-screen terminal window instead of just a plain shell. That means you get the same tidy, organized workspace that paying users have, where each step stays visible and separate instead of scrolling past. This only applies to the free version of the assistant today.

d885b4bc8b1f30d435472baa2f9126dd647f0cdb.text: Freebuff is now available in France, Italy, Spain, and Portugal, in addition to the countries that already had access. If you visit the site from one of these four European countries, you will now be able to use the free mode without restrictions. The FAQ page has been updated to reflect the expanded list of supported countries.

37b905688e44841274d2f3af26ae418b8e4b8b9d.text: You can now pick OpenCode MiniMax-M2.7 as a routing option when sending chat requests through the OpenCode Zen service, alongside the existing Kimi-K2.6 model. The system now uses a shared alias list and pricing table to decide which model to route to and how to charge for it, so adding this new model simply registers its name, the internal model label it maps to, and its per-token cost of 0.3 cents per million input tokens and 1.2 cents per million output tokens. If you ask for a model that isn't in that list, you'll get an error instead of it silently failing. The change is live today: the new model is accepted immediately, while unsupported names are rejected with a 400 error.

b94212ab04f5dfc15f13df05c592f633cbe9fab2.text: When you use the CLI tool and it shows you a sponsorship or partnership banner at the bottom of the screen, the banner sometimes grew taller than expected if the website address shown was especially long, which could push other content out of place or make the screen look messy. Now the tool cuts off any overflowing text in that row and stops the domain name from wrapping onto its own line, so the banner keeps a fixed height no matter how long the URL is. You'd notice the banner stays compact and aligned, instead of stretching vertically and shifting nearby text.

e798ad9c6c200fd8a54eaf99e65015dc64af4ee8.text: The assistant can no longer start a conversation using the minimax-m2.7 model through the OpenCode Zen path; that option has been removed entirely. You select a model from a fixed list rather than by typing a name starting with "opencode/", so only kim k2.6 remains available there. If you tried to request minimax-m2.7, it now comes back unchanged instead of being translated to a different model id, meaning it won't work as before. This is live now.

7d59406b7e81d940065af1a346e33a05e61584d4.text: When you pick the efficient assistant on the free service, you'll now see a notice that it saves conversations to help train future versions of the assistant. The service also updated its help page so visitors can read that same data-collection fact before they start chatting. This labeling appeared on the free model list and the website's frequently asked questions at the same time.

9e34f2500899c235232c0aab3b39452f9963b387.text: When you sign in to the service using the command-line tool, the web page now generates a random, non-readable code instead of exposing a signed authentication payload directly in the login URL. This opaque code is stored behind the scenes and resolved only once during onboarding, then deleted. This change applies to both the freebuff/web and web packages, affecting the CLI login flow and onboarding process. The change is in place today as part of the latest release, tightening how CLI authentication tokens are handled for improved security.

4987adaefa045c3255aa3ebe3be301b062c639d8.text: When you sign in to the service from the command-line tool, the system now gives you a random, scrambled code instead of a structured one that reveals internal tracking details. The scrambled code gets stored in the system's record-keeping, and when the web page confirms your login, it looks up the scrambled code to find the real internal code it needs, while still accepting the old-style codes for anything that hasn't updated yet. You'll notice no difference in how you sign in, but the codes you receive are now unreadable to anyone who might intercept them.

206d2310b08f40f9d840c8a4b7dbf682b597bca2.text: When you sign in with the CLI tool, the system now writes extra tracking details into its logs including a short, scrambled version of the login token (made by running it through a secure one-way fingerprint process), how long the token is, and where the request came from. This doesn't change how you log in or what you see, but if someone is troubleshooting a signup issue they will find more precise clues in the logs without exposing the real token. The change is live today across both the Freebuff sign-in flow and the Codebuff sign-in flow.

f14fd0cc343ecd2079f46853acc8966fee8a6449.text: When you send a message to the assistant through the free service, the system now quietly records whether your account is on the full or limited access tier as part of its routine usage analytics — but it only logs a small sample of these events so that the high volume of free requests doesn't overwhelm the analytics platform. This is live today for free-tier users, and you wouldn't notice it unless you were specifically looking at the behind-the-scenes tracking data. The tracking now includes your access level alongside basic details like whether you're streaming or using a specific agent.

1796dbd4a28fab935a1eac47ddb0fa9db83fea66.text: If you're using the Freebuff version of the assistant and you hit it too hard, it now tells you 'temporarily busy, please wait' instead of flashing a confusing error code. This only happens when the rate-limit kicks in, and it applies specifically to the Freebuff build — regular users won't see it. You'd notice it as a clean, friendly message replacing what used to look like a raw server complaint.

71b82cd473a88c3b984e5369f048ed7d9d7647aa.text: When a model sends agent-launching instructions, it sometimes wraps the settings inside a quoted block (a JSON string) instead of handing them over as a ready-made set of fields. The system now recognizes that quoted block and unfolds it into the proper settings before proceeding, so launching a helper agent no longer stalls on that formatting snag. If the block is genuinely broken or unreadable, it is left alone so the built-in checks still catch and report the problem exactly as before. You would notice this the next time you ask the assistant to spin up an inside-the-app agent with extra options.

d8395764bbe0f063c5f616efa7ca997c238aff8e.text: If you ask for a model whose name starts with the prefix "opencode/", the system will now process that request instead of turning it away with an error. You would notice that previously blocked model requests now return a real response rather than a "currently disabled" message. This affects any model request using that specific prefix going forward.

cfc3e1ae4f15d4849696cdb1437075ba154a3d0e.text: The waiting-room screen's session counter now displays the used count without zero-padding, so a number like '007' appears as '7'. This affects anyone who sees the session counter while in the waiting room, making the displayed number slightly shorter. If you looked at the screen before and after, you'd notice the 'used' count no longer has leading zeros.

3f192e006104fa3e18ee98879506805d4f0f2ea0.text: The helper that checks whether a chosen AI model belongs to the internal OpenCode Zen family now rejects anything that isn't a plain text model name before looking for the special prefix, instead of trusting that it was always given a text name. This only touches the behind-the-scenes code that runs model lookups, so nothing you see or do changes; it just prevents the program from breaking when an unexpected value is handed to that check. It's live today as part of the current release.

47ae3eb4c94fd1a79d6ec26c490b0f56b799f787.text: If you use the free version of the assistant, you can now pick the Kimi model alongside the existing free options like MiniMax, GLM, and DeepSeek V4 Pro. The free-mode model list had a small addition that makes Kimi available to free users, and a paired test confirms it. Nothing about the pricing or which accounts qualify changed — free users simply gained one more model they can switch to.

bdd8b09121cea865b3bbb7a8cf71f8b3d54a690e.text: When you land on the waiting room screen before picking a model, you'll now see how many premium sessions you've already used out of the daily total — like "2 of 5 premium sessions used today" — instead of how many were left. The count is padded with spaces so the line doesn't jump or shift width while it's loading, keeping the title centered. This affects anyone hitting the waiting room screen while premium sessions are in use.

cfd4a2c37bc0cd4a2740188a3182a5aa890deca3.text: The system was updated to properly handle a test case where it checks what happens when a free user's location can't be determined. Previously, the test relied on a special dev mode bypass that would activate when no location data was found and the request came from a local machine. Now it uses a specific fake internet address that can't be mapped to any real location, so the test accurately reflects what happens for real users whose locations can't be identified. If you looked at this test, you'd see it now sends an extra header to simulate a real unknown visitor, and it checks for the correct rejection message that matches real-world behavior instead of the old dev-only shortcut.

b51ad4b60ed674402cdfe528488e453f9929147e.text: If you use the free tier of the service, the assistant can now include a DeepSeek model when it picks which AI helper to run with. The free mode that previously only mixed Minimax and GLM models now also routes to DeepSeek alongside them, while the separate dedicated free DeepSeek and free Kimi mode sets stay the same. The change is live today in the common code that powers the free mode selection.

9d7e9e4f609d8c4af78b9b11c8943055f969aa86.text: The command-line tool used to show you a blank space where file changes should appear, and now it actually shows those changes again with colored lines marking what was added or removed. A hidden setting had been turned off, telling the tool to skip drawing the diff entirely, and that setting and its skip-check have been removed so the diff display runs normally again. If you use the CLI to review changes, you will see the expected added/removed text with the usual theme colors instead of an empty area.

5cd16cb80591c5258cdcc77501077ddd38de07b4.text: When you open the chat history list in the CLI, the button that used to say Delete now shows as a small x icon, and the row layout has been adjusted so the prompt text column expands more reliably. The spacing math now accounts for the list border, scrollbar, and button padding, so rows with emojis or wide characters no longer shift the text around. Youll notice the rows look more evenly padded and the delete button takes up less horizontal space, leaving more room for your chat titles to be visible.

247b4c84619b747079e9b166a2438087fa9ccf40.text: When the command line shows you a list of changes, it will now hide the side-by-side colored diff view and simply return nothing instead. The tool that draws those change previews now checks an internal on/off switch that has been flipped to off, so any surface that relied on it gets an empty result. If you were expecting to see the formatted additions and removals in your terminal, you will not see them anymore. The change is live today.

9342438a64ebd4276fc73ae80f54727c56b080db.text: The list of available assistants in the help section now simply spells out which ones collect data for training, and the question about session limits was removed. If you open the help page, you'll see the model names in a bulleted list instead of one long paragraph, and the note about training now states clearly that only models labeled as collecting data for training will use your conversations to teach themselves. Today, visitors to the site will read the updated help text as soon as they reload the page.

a88ccccad6a67338711b2eab5e57eb0b3f056514.text: Older client apps that still ask for the code-reviewer-lite assistant will now get served again. Those apps were built before reviewers had their own names and relied on generic provider-specific roots, so this maps the legacy request back to the matching models for MiniMax, KI, and DeepSeek. If you look, you'll see the reviewer now accepts requests from those older clients without error.

17f45a497be0e5bc95468c913c2fe0b92db4a9bb.text: When you use the command-line assistant and it spawns a helper agent, the helper's name and type now display correctly even if the name uses underscores instead of hyphens. Previously, names like 'file_picker' wouldn't match properly when looking up the agent card to show in your terminal, causing the helper to appear with the wrong or missing label. Now names are normalized during lookup and the actual agent type is passed through the whole process so the right display name shows up. This fix is live today in the CLI.

c3b019f1668af33082e689fb99254e9a3ce74d8f.text: If you ever saw the command-line assistant show your conversation history with the same helper agent listed twice, that mix-up is back: this change undoes the adjustment that had prevented duplicate reviewer agent cards from appearing, so the assistant is once again using its original method for telling agents apart and moving their message blocks into place. You, the person running the assistant in a terminal, would notice that the duplicated cards can reappear in your session log, and the assistant will resolve agent identities the way it did before this rollback. The fix is live today for anyone using the CLI as of this snapshot, including the test files that previously locked in the anti-duplicate behavior.

fdf8d94e5570efa1d48732b81b57608032d9df4e.text: If you open Freebuff today, the web app loads on the latest version of Next.js (15.5.16), which is a behind-the-scenes upgrade that keeps the site building and running correctly. The FAQ on the homepage now lists MiniMax M2.7 as an additional coding model you can pick, alongside DeepSeek V4 Pro and Kimi K2.6, with clearer notes about daily session limits and each model's trade-offs. Separately, a small fix makes the app's environment setup work the same way whether tests run on a developer's computer or on the automated servers that build and test the code.

c11a47350991d7298be950a93d1c2071dbb6ce2b.text: When the CLI runs a sub-agent (like the reviewer agent in a multi-step coding plan), it sometimes rendered two identical agent cards in the conversation panel. The CLI now carries the spawned agent's real type and ID all the way through the event-handling path, and normalizes identifiers (treating underscores and hyphens as the same) so each sub-agent matches only one UI block instead of duplicating. This fix is live today for CLI users running plans that spawn reviewer or other named sub-agents.

3df6ec9369acfcb1e7cb02288aa307c0940bbbdf.text: When your freechat session ends, a banner now appears offering you a way to start fresh. Pressing Enter begins a new same-chat session, while Esc takes you back to pick a different model. Behind the scenes, the system re-sends your request with a fallback model instead of redisplaying the old ended row, which prevents the banner from getting stuck if the original model was unavailable. This keeps the conversation flowing without leaving you waiting on a dead session.

116e456fa93f2d88a754347f5279f0633c3dd877.text: When you type a code from the Freebuff command-line tool into your browser to log in, the system now reads that code correctly even if parts of it contain dots, which previously could get it split in the wrong places. The link your browser opens is now built from the exact address the code came from, instead of a default address that sometimes sent you to the wrong version of the site (apex vs. www) during sign-in. If your code still doesn't match, the system now records a warning with details about the parts it expected versus what you entered, helping spot typos or copy mistakes. It's live today for anyone using the Freebuff CLI sign-in flow.

d313c4a1ea19bd8f6fe9f8b2e7ba25d0522cd3c8.text: When you create or edit a file, the screen no longer briefly shows a confusing before-and-after diff before the change finishes. The diff preview now waits to appear until the edit actually completes, so you will not see a misleading full-file flash during create operations. This affects anyone watching the edit process in the command-line interface.

1409cf91caa26aca496d30db773169642430a35c.text: When you open the model picker in the Freebuff CLI, paid-tier models now appear together under a single PREMIUM heading (showing one shared 0/5 quota counter) instead of each row carrying its own "Premium" or "Unlimited" label, and empty tiers are hidden so you never see an orphan header. The waiting-room screen also got layout tweaks so the landing and queued states line up neatly in their own flexible containers.

d8e01e3216f2c9976b43ad30fad7f90308f32d70.text: When the assistant asks a tool to do something, you send instructions as a list of settings. If you accidentally send that list as one long piece of text instead of structured data, the assistant has started giving you a clearer message about what went wrong. It now tells you plainly whether your instructions couldn't be read as structured data or were just plain text, and reminds you to send the full set of settings in the right format. This applies to anyone interacting with the assistant's tool use, and is live today.

992f3382112e6b710f5d76ee5226430f901aa7de.text: When you're waiting in the Freebuff CLI queue and pick from the paid model list, the remaining paid-session count (for example 3/5) now appears in the waiting-room title line instead of inside the model-selector section header. Free-tiers still just list models without any quota display, and when your paid allowance hits zero the count turns amber so it reads as you've hit the limit rather than just another number. The selector itself is now purely a list of choices grouped by tier, while the waiting-room screen imports the shared session limit and calculates the remaining quota to show in its header text. Note: the analyzer tagged this as minor, and there are several sibling changes in this snapshot that are unrelated housekeeping like fixing diff rendering and version bumps.

11fbf88499efe8ae3efd1f5b4835580e066b498f.text: If you open the command-line helper while it is already running for your account, the new one will now stop and ask you whether you want to take over the session or quit, instead of silently replacing the first one. The choice appears in your terminal before any data is sent to the server, so no work is interrupted unless you confirm. This is live today and only affects people running the command-line version locally; the web interface is unchanged.

884911e73ae7daa3131a1f3640089002400de394.text: If you use the free version, the assistant can now control a web browser for you — opening pages, clicking around, and reading what shows up, all automatically instead of you guiding it yourself. This browser automation ability was added to the list of tools that the free tier is allowed to use, backed by the same lightweight model it already uses. The change went live on 2026-05-05 and applies wherever free accounts get their settings, so right now it covers the website, the command-line tool, and the desktop app.

5a613f89b9293bbc9e93f2893301a4b475c8878c.text: When the command-line tool detects that another copy is already running, it shows a screen with two options: 'Take over' (end the other instance and use this one) or 'Exit' (quit and keep using the existing one). You can now use the left and right arrow keys, the Tab key, or Shift+Tab to move a highlighted border between those two buttons, and press Enter to confirm the one that's highlighted.
