326f91bb313f53fb16920855c6c9df7b43c325ce.text: The internal test harness for the assistant's model routing switch from one underlying model (minimax-m2p5) to another (z-ai/glm-5.1), updating both the test data and expected routing identifiers to match the current model configuration. Only developers running the verification suite observe any difference. The switch is already live in production systems, so the routing tests merely realign internal expectations with the live model selection.

af7ab3c768598a761f5b19519be416fdd9c862e0.text: The assistant that keeps your conversations from running out of space now listens to a different brain — it quietly switched from the previous thinking engine to a newer one from a different provider. You will not see settings to change this yourself, but when your chat gets long and the system summarizes what happened so far, the summary is produced by the new engine. That behind-the-scenes swap is already live today.

f3957c64105e465c713227d0b77cb0f5c42258e3.text: The service stopped offering one specific AI helper through its preferred route provider, so requests for that helper now fall back to the default provider path instead. If you were watching the configuration list, you would see that helper's custom entry turned into a comment on the line, while the other helpers remain unchanged. This is already live today.

36f9c1561ecd1d1a70aae3ec3edc914f01cb06d7.text: The free version of the assistant can now use a newer, more capable model instead of the previous one. If you use the free editor, code reviewer, or base helper tools, you'll get responses from a different AI without doing anything — it just happened automatically. The system also lets these free tools run for longer before stopping, so complex tasks have more room to complete. This change is already live for free users.

a69c4f231456107591e85132186ce0c0b82b31d6.text: When you press Escape while the assistant asks you a question in a pop-up form, the assistant now fully stops talking instead of continuing in the background. Previously, the assistant's response kept streaming even after you dismissed the form, so you had to wait for it to finish before starting over. Now, dismissing the form cleanly interrupts the assistant and lets you begin fresh immediately.

629c552090515dd8e07488eac27309ca9e6c464a.text: The token counter that determines your bill now includes the tools (functions) the assistant uses, so you're charged for the full size of your tool definitions, not just the message text. When you use OpenAI or Gemini models, an extra 30% is automatically added to the count because those systems count tokens slightly differently than Anthropic's method. If you looked at a billing estimate while using tools, you'd see the number tick up to reflect the actual size of the tool descriptions and parameters being processed.

e001224735a444eeff4190f181c1e8c775d4a0f7.text: When you run a command in the terminal, the system now only uses extra smart analysis to explain the output if you specifically ask it to focus on something. If you don’t specify what you want explained, you just get the raw result without any summary. This makes the process simpler and avoids unnecessary processing.

18283ca63e9608056a4b7fa4fce9c0b1ebf9ecca.text: When the base2 agent needs to find existing code to understand what it's changing, it now spawns a dedicated code-searcher agent instead of using a built-in search tool. This means refactoring tasks that involve updating multiple references to a function or variable will use a more specialized search approach, potentially finding more accurate matches across the codebase. If you watched this in action, you'd see it spin up a separate search-focused agent rather than performing searches inline, and the search agent now requires queries in a specific structured format with examples provided.

36c7dac32446692336ec0fed4a7d1471fb6030c8.text: If you're on the free plan and need help with something tricky, the system now saves a particularly smart assistant for the hardest questions instead of sending it for every small edit. That smart assistant also thinks a bit harder when it does show up, so it can work through tougher problems more carefully. You'd notice it only getting pulled in for the bigger, less straightforward tasks, while quick or clearly defined edits are handled faster without the extra overhead.

176eb0acaa9a773eab604411f2203f6f54953f09.text: If you are on the free plan and ask the agent to work through a multi-step problem, it will now write out a step-by-step plan for you to follow along. Previously, only paid plans got that plan-writing helper; the agent would skip it for free users. Now, whether you are on a free or paid account, the agent will break down longer tasks into a checklist it shows you before diving in, so you can see exactly what it intends to do and in what order. The change only affects how the agent organizes its work, not the quality or depth of the work itself.

52a75b23037884cbf555f87530e5442d11f62812.text: The assistant now refuses to run unless you give it a specific command to execute. Before this change, it could be started with just a description of what output you wanted, which sometimes caused it to fail. Now, every request must include the exact shell command, so the assistant won't try to run without knowing precisely what to do.

a2246d987caf879903aee6cb83886ca00eabef6f.text: The internal test that rates how well our assistant performs has been retuned to measure the assistant against a different set of benchmarks. Specifically, the test now evaluates a variant called "base2-free-evals" on a task named "server-agent-validation" instead of the previous "base2" agent and "filter-system-history" task. This only affects the behind-the-scenes scoring system used by developers; nothing you see or interact with has changed.

ff498d0692371a4a14b0a3e4c3c2d53709ba5968.text: When you ask the assistant to spin up a helper for you—say, a code search or a terminal task—it can now hand that helper a clearly labeled set of hints, like which search terms to look for or which files to read, instead of passing a freeform bag of values. The assistant can still add extra details beyond the known hints, so it doesn't lose flexibility, but the most common inputs are now described in plain language so the helper knows what you expect. If you watched a helper being started, you'd see it receive tidier, better-labeled instructions rather than a shapeless list of parameters.

8537ffbb0aa735ab6d711fc652bd11ceb0d076c8.text: When you open a very large file to look at it, the assistant now shows you the first 100,000 characters instead of stopping at just 1,000. You'll notice that the file content fills much more of your screen before hitting the cutoff, and the message that appears at the bottom now tells you how many total characters the file contains rather than repeating the old 1,000-character limit. The longer view is live today, so any large file you open will be truncated at the new, larger boundary.

284eea82b096e428c4a24de7fcf47410c8529211.text: If you use the free version of this tool to edit files, you'll now get two separate type checks during reviews: one for your recent edits and one for the entire project. This helps catch both small mistakes and bigger issues that might break other parts of your codebase. The change also slightly relaxes a coding rule, allowing type casting exceptions when a value can genuinely accept any type.

b45ead77cf75a4f4f2b4c41184295446e9309386.text: When the assistant tries to read a file that's very large, it now shows you only the first 1,000 characters instead of either skipping the file entirely or potentially failing. If a file is over 10MB in size, the assistant won't try to read it at all and will tell you it's too large to open. This change is live today and affects any large file that gets read through the assistant's file-reading capability, preventing memory problems and giving you at least a small preview instead of nothing.

975b87f312741fc6f9e815ee523b7419b2b2c801.text: When the assistant generates output that doesn't match the expected format, or when someone asks it to start another assistant with a bad prompt or settings, the error message now includes the exact text that caused the problem (cut off if it's very long, with a note that it was shortened). This means you'll see what the assistant tried to submit instead of just a generic 'something went wrong' alert, making it easier to figure out what needs fixing.

eaeec68115cdea97a0c39abb70b8025492bfe3ee.text: If you use the command-running assistant called Basher, you will now see a clearer reminder in its instructions to include the actual command inside the parameters you send it. The wording in two places that describe what Basher does was tweaked so that the AI guiding the assistant is told, in plain language, that you must specify the command within the params object, and that you shouldn’t forget that field. Nothing about how the assistant behaves has changed; this just rewrites the description so it is less easy to overlook.

d4f08ddeb63417f96c4ba9c7e30fd80e608b52a8.text: The thinker-gemini assistant (used only by free-tier users) now thinks less deeply and gives shorter answers. Before, it was told to "think deeply"; now it's told to consider the request briefly and say only what's needed to answer the question correctly. As a result, free-tier users will notice faster responses that get to the point instead of detailed explanations. This change is live today, but it only affects the free tier because the base2 agent is configured to spawn thinker-gemini exclusively for free users.

a64c5cc462ef3da1ed159b2a103a9f8e926e790d.text: If you run an automated evaluation of how well AI assistants complete coding tasks, you can now add a special command option to save a detailed record of every step the AI took while working. That record is saved as a separate file for each task and only appears when you actively turn on that option, so by default nothing changes. The new option works across all the different evaluation entry points used internally for nightly, single, and hard-task testing.

ce142ff1af0292cfac040f7e7cc82402e1424145.text: The internal testing system that scores the assistant's coding help has switched which version it grades against, moving from one evaluation setup to a newer one. This only affects the behind-the-scenes scoring used by the team that builds the assistant, so nothing you see or do changes. If you were watching the test runs, you'd see them now using the updated grading configuration instead of the previous one. It's already live for the internal tests today.

927f7722099850cff0b359c9f3f7d28be459c95c.text: When you use the free version of Codebuff to ask the assistant to do something, it will now automatically bring in a second, very capable reasoning helper before doing most of your tasks, unless your request is too simple to bother with. Previously, that helper was only brought in when a problem seemed especially complex; starting today, the free assistant treats bringing in that helper as the default move for nearly every request. If you watched the assistant work, you'd notice it pausing to gather your project details first, then deliberately spinning up that reasoning helper to plan out the best response before making any edits or suggestions. Who feels this: free-tier Codebuff users. When it started: live today, based on the April 10 snapshot.

2df5e04d4e070ae1a75a7fb195654b626c771f7a.text: When you ask the assistant to use a skill (a reusable behavior or domain guide), it now looks for skills you created yourself during this session, not just the ones bundled at startup. If the requested skill wasn't found in the program's starting cache, it scans your personal and project folders (like ~/.agents, ~/.claude, and matching local folders) for a matching skill file, checks its header information, and only uses it if the file's name matches what you asked for. You'd notice this if you had just written a new skill file on disk and the assistant suddenly recognized it in the same session instead of ignoring it as unknown.

d6769f7b647e6866397210dda0957bd180ea3b8a.text: People who use the command-running helper now have to give it both a shell command and a prompt for describing the result, instead of just the command. If you asked the helper to run something, it will now expect a second piece of instructions telling it how to explain what happened. The text telling the helper what kind of command to expect was also tweaked to remind everyone it should be a bash command.

cd1e4e16b21b0742472287db1f86af48b6acc6da.text: A developer added a missing piece of information, called STRIPE_USAGE_PRICE_ID, to a configuration file used internally for testing. This ensures that the testing setup includes all required values related to payment processing via Stripe. If you look at the configuration, you would now see this additional entry listed with the other Stripe-related settings. The change is live today and affects only the internal testing environment.

759536f390f1616d3e4f73ac9aa8e40c2d40f22c.text: If you turned on the option to hide the assistant's private thinking notes, the streaming response now actually stops showing them, instead of printing them anyway. This affects only the two sources the tool reads from for this setting, and only while the reply is being generated live. It's fixed today, so the next streamed request will honor the setting correctly.

e68a330a70788ea18964be0be64004d86c8be051.text: When you ask the service for a response from a specialized version of a model, that version occasionally fails with transient server errors that previously weren't retried properly. Now, any server-side error (such as timeout, gateway, or internal errors), not just one specific kind, will cause the request to automatically retry using the more reliable standard path. This applies internally and improves reliability for users interacting with specialized model deployments. The change is live today.

c89706ad40999ddc78d23a062d26787fd212cbbd.text: When you see a stop button in the command-line tool, you now see the word Esc instead of Stop, matching the keyboard shortcut that cancels the current action. You just notice the label change on that button; the button still does the same thing when clicked.

ecc1502818ffdeef7c0a8d074f5f02bbb5b51e97.text: The internal instructions that guide the coding assistant were updated so it now tells the assistant to look at relevant reference materials first before trying to write new code, rather than relying on what it already knows. The list of reference materials was also reformatted from clickable links to plain text file paths. At the same time, a behind-the-scenes measurement tool was extended so it can count how often the assistant opened those reference documents during a task and add up the totals across multiple attempts. The measurement change is in place today and nothing depends on it yet, so no results are visible from it right now, but the new instruction for the assistant is live and applies to anyone the assistant is helping.

caf904df1dba70f89294614c03fa39906d09fa90.text: The text next to the square stop button is now a bit darker and easier to read when you're not hovering your mouse over it. Previously, the unhovered label appeared dimmed or faded; now it displays at normal brightness. This only affects how the stop button looks in the command-line interface, and you can see the difference right away the next time you use it.

66318e6a90d7de70353f12eeaf80b2c7058b8652.text: If you visit the Freebuff landing page today, you'll see two small wording tweaks. The FAQ answer to 'How can it be free?' now says 'text ads shown in the CLI' instead of just 'ads shown in the CLI,' and the description of the 'LOADED' feature now reads '9 specialized subagents: code review, browser use, deep thinking with your ChatGPT subscription, and more.' These changes just clarify what the service means by 'ads' and that there are more specialized helpers available beyond the ones explicitly listed.

bb432101d7f49b21528f013bebf610882f5d6afb.text: When the assistant's command-line tool crashes in a way that usually leaves your terminal messed up (like frozen screens, broken cursor, or weird paste behavior), the tool now automatically fixes your terminal and prints a plain-English message explaining what likely went wrong — such as your computer's processor not being new enough to run it. You would notice the difference as a readable error message instead of a silent crash, and your terminal would no longer require manual resetting after such a failure. This behavior is live today in the released command-line versions, and it was added alongside the version 1.0.638 release.

ff5f05819b65bdfcbd25b3f67c4ec1dd8130878d.text: When you open the Freebuff website homepage, the text describing what it can do is now more detailed and easier to read. The FAQ and philosophy sections now list 9 specialized helpers that the assistant can use, including a new one called thinker-gpt that connects to your ChatGPT account for deeper reasoning. The way to do big tasks from start to finish is also spelled out more clearly with the /interview → /plan → (implement) → /review commands, and some of the text on the page uses a slightly lighter color. If you look at the homepage now, you'll see the updated descriptions with clearer bullet points and slightly brighter text.

448db9644f4e3a13231905e15d9a9faca0cb7ca7.text: The internal admin tool that tracks which free assistant users are most active now shows a much richer profile for each person, including how many messages they send per hour and per day, their token usage, and how often they benefit from cached responses. The time window it looks back at grew from 3 days to 1 week, and the default list now shows the top 50 users instead of 200, making the detailed report easier to read at a glance. You need the configurable agent ID argument (defaulting to 'base2-free') to point it at the right assistant version, and it renders ASCII bar charts so you can spot when users prefer to chat, all for internal tooling only, with no changes visible to end users.

149a328add45abd7bc11cecd4ee0bec3c2d0fdf0.text: If the assistant app gets forcefully killed while running in your terminal, the terminal can get stuck in a weird state where things like your cursor disappear or keyboard shortcuts stop working normally. Now, a background monitoring process that stays running will automatically reset your terminal to normal whenever this happens, even if the main app can't clean up after itself. You would notice this as your terminal returning to normal behavior immediately after a crash, instead of staying visually broken until you manually reset it.

ec3f863b4fc3c158a975971a5633d8f0317636d1.text: When the assistant tries to use a tool (like a calculator or a web search) and that tool call fails, you used to only see a generic error message with no context about what went wrong. Now, the error message will include the actual instruction that was sent to the tool, showing you exactly what the assistant tried to do, so you can better understand why it failed. The instruction is shown as plain text and is automatically shortened if it's very long, keeping the error messages readable while still giving helpful detail. This is live today for all users.

ae389387291f5e23faa1e1392195593ea81b49c2.text: When the CLI displays a grid of agent children, it now always sets up the data needed to group those agents before deciding whether to skip rendering entirely. Previously, that grouping step happened after early exit checks, so the order of internal setup changed depending on which path ran; now the setup always runs first, keeping the rendering logic consistent. You won't see a visual difference day to day, but this prevents crashes tied to that inconsistent ordering. This is live today in the CLI component that renders agent grids.

fa7a9595e40b9274416ac57d46ca2474b7d570a5.text: When you look at the list of AI models you can assign to an automated helper, you'll now see "Google Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview" available as an option. In everyday use, this means the special helper that judges how well other helpers are performing in our internal tests has quietly been switched to use this newer Gemini model, so those comparisons now run on more recent technology. You won't see anything different unless you're actually looking at the model-selection menu or reviewing the latest judge test outcomes.

5ca697b1fb19d7a2c270c3cd2266f920b8628f20.text: When you ask the assistant to use Fireworks, it now gives the tool instructions in a stricter, more precise format. This only affects requests sent to the Fireworks service and prevents the assistant from making up incorrect tool calls. You wouldn’t notice anything different in how the assistant responds, but behind the scenes the requests are more reliable.

bc92e426ed46b2e0e36f445d859859675e559028.text: The thinker-gpt helper no longer copies over the main set of background rules that guide it, so it now follows only its own dedicated instructions. This affects anyone who relies on the thinker-gpt helper, which will behave more narrowly since it can no longer pick up extra rules from the parent setup. If you interact with it, you may notice it gives more focused answers that stick closely to its specific task description.

571084860ec1996fc025e54911935ff59e722105.text: When you run several agents in the CLI, the small ones now crowd together on a single line while each big agent takes up the full width of the terminal. Behind the scenes, the grid logic separates agents by size before drawing them: small agents (which collapse by default) are packed into shared rows, and large agents are placed each on their own full-width line. If you are watching an agent session today, you will see this tighter packing right away when a mix of small and large agents appear together.

946dd70655b5aca3929477e67877f1d6a3fd7584.text: You're a developer who runs automated tests for the command-line tool. Tests that launch the tool with the --agent flag have been randomly failing on slow continuous-integration machines because they shut down before the tool finished starting up. The test now waits longer (up to 8 seconds) and treats a process that is still alive after that wait as a successful startup, while also catching an early exit as a failure. If you ran these end-to-end CLI tests today you would notice they no longer time out and report false failures on slower machines. This change is live today and affects only the CLI test suite, so you would notice it only when running those tests.

6bbf8ceebddb2347b03e358dba07c820f7142276.text: If you log in to the Freebuff web app using your GitHub account, the app will now prefer your Freebuff-specific GitHub credentials when they're provided, and fall back to the existing Codebuff credentials otherwise. The login configuration now accepts these new credentials and automatically picks the right one depending on whether it's running on your local machine or being deployed. You won't notice anything different unless you're setting up a Freebuff-specific GitHub integration, in which case the app will use that connection instead of the default one.

42c96674ee31177b09bc05b4483909a9690a37df.text: When the system grades coding assistants by comparing their edits to real commits, it now ignores automatically generated files like lockfiles so the grade reflects the assistant's own work instead of noise. The grading also tracks each attempted documentation improvement—including the before and after scores—and only counts an edit as a real improvement when it lifts the score by at least 0.3 points, then stops after five rounds of trying. If you were reviewing these results you'd see cleaner before/after comparisons and fewer edits that look helpful only because of file noise.

1c5d74b8b0729556a69dc6f0e8fc1c0ab2a2174c.text: When you move your mouse over the sign-in button on the Freebuff web app, the button's background now darkens slightly in addition to the existing border glow and shadow effects, giving you clearer visual feedback that the button is interactive. This is a live update today for all visitors using the Freebuff web interface, requiring no action on your part to benefit from the improved hover experience.

088ce23eb3b6e81ffe376d02ac0ccd6a9a36d7a0.text: If you visit a link like trybeluga.ai/b/abc123, the site now automatically sends you to go.trybeluga.ai/abc123 instead of showing a page or error. This affects anyone using that /b/ prefix in their web links, which redirects them to a different short link service. The redirect is not permanent, so the original path could change again later.

acef43db12096e373ff788fff9443bf01523b682.text: When you run certain command-line tools now, the output opens in a separate full-screen area instead of mixing into your regular terminal history. This means clearing the screen or exiting the tool should cleanly remove whatever was displayed without leaving leftover text behind. You wouldn't notice a difference unless you're watching how the terminal behaves when the tool starts and stops.

abe4eb8d07ac905d29a84ce6397dce7cef5c7f36.text: When you open the login page for Freebuff, the first thing you'll see is a refreshed dark background with a subtle green gradient and a frosted-glass style card where you enter your credentials. The sign-in buttons now glow softly when you hover over them and have clearer loading spinners while they work. The expired auth code screen also got the same visual treatment, so the whole flow feels consistent and modern. These updates are live today for all Freebuff web users, and no code or account changes are required to see them.

5e8ed7bfaf21a0a33ad7c498ef064239a3525c81.text: When someone signs up for the service, the system now records whether they came from CodeBuff or FreeBuff. If you watch the signup event details, you'll see a new 'signupSource' field showing 'codebuff' or 'freebuff' so the team can tell which product brought in each new user.

c1b713e625d91c6c8e60899f4235b4c3b5b71c85.text: You can now make more requests per minute, per 30 minutes, per 5 hours, and per 7 days in free mode on the web API, because the limits were raised to allow 25 per minute, 250 per 30 minutes, 2,000 per 5 hours, and 20,000 per 7 days. The per-second limit stays the same at 2. This affects how often you can call the assistant when using the web API in free mode, letting you do more in the same amount of time.

71db42d0a57ade0f25939cedd4fab6060e41232f.text: The free-tier usage limit check was miscalculating how much time had passed between requests, sometimes triggering the 5-hour cap too early. This only affected our internal testing of the limit — regular users were never impacted. The test now keeps track of elapsed time within each batch before advancing the simulated clock, so the final check correctly triggers the 5-hour limit as expected.

67c066f27636e4016d3dcea7f0b002c9f1e9a610.text: If you use an automated assistant that runs a program inside a terminal window and then types into it, that assistant can no longer tell the program to 'pause until a specific line of text shows up' — a feature called 'wait-for' has been removed. The assistant must now only use 'wait-idle', which pauses until the output stops changing for a few seconds. If you write or rely on instructions that say to wait for exact phrases to appear, those instructions will no longer work; you should switch them to wait for the screen to go quiet instead. This change is already live.

2b9c6ad7c87825fb63acc6ab00954d1bc9524bf9.text: When you open the review screen in the CLI, a new option labeled 'Changes this conversation' now appears at the top of the list, letting you review only the changes you made during the current session. Selecting it generates a review prompt scoped to that conversation's changes, and the underlying logic now recognizes this new scope alongside the existing 'Uncommitted changes' and 'This branch vs main' options. The feature is live today for anyone who opens the CLI review screen.

6ca71dc98efecf951cc96f4ac3e0b6aa560cb6f8.text: The nightly automated test run now correctly points to the right folder where the agent tests live, so it actually runs the agent end-to-end tests that it was supposed to run. A stale shortcut that looked like a folder name was cleaned up from the agent package so the test runner goes straight to the correct spot. If you were watching the scheduled nightly logs, you would see the agent tests executing properly instead of silently skipping them.

c6128f73521d191ff7f1e60047f6486a5c2918e4.text: If you use the Freebuff version of the CLI tool and sign in, the sign-in window now opens on freebuff.com instead of codebuff.com. The CLI was updated so that when it starts your browser to log you in, it sends you to the correct website depending on which product you're using. This only affects Freebuff users; standard Codebuff users will still be directed to the existing codebuff.com site.

8d0bbfb78f0ffafa963dbf606c63e57af75b31e3.text: Your computer's build tool - the software that turns the program's code into a working app on your device - got upgraded to a slightly newer version. Every file that said 'use version 1.3.5' now says 'use version 1.3.11' instead, so whether you're running the main program, its website, or special background tools, your computer will load the updated version. If you looked at the setup files, you'd just see the old number swapped out for the new one everywhere - nothing else changed.

65c4187f2e28a11c50b3c9e143f3362f328861b5.text: The get-started page on the web used to show a nav header that sat on top of everything else (using absolute positioning), and the main content below it was pushed down with extra top padding to make room. The header — including the Freebuff logo link and a GitHub link — has now been removed, and that extra top padding was reduced to match, so the page content sits higher than before. This affects anyone opening the Free-started page on the web, since the page no longer displays the nav bar at the top. The layout adjusts accordingly: on desktop viewports the main content's top padding shrinks from 8rem back to 4rem, which is the base spacing already used on mobile. No features, links, or model/data behavior changed — only the on-page header decoration and its surrounding spacing were

2d599476c5131484e22f488f306d89526df625e4.text: When you type the assistant's help command at the terminal, you'll now see a 'login' option in the basic list of available actions, and if you ask for the more advanced version you'll see both 'login' and 'publish' added at the bottom of that help text. This just makes those two actions visible in the list that pops up when you ask for help, so you don't have to guess the commands exist.

a8f35eae25cefcebf9ff85cce0fb28e7a668dc9c.text: If you run the command-line tool on Linux and ask it to open a web page, it now checks the correct settings (DISPLAY and WAYLAND_DISPLAY) to see whether it's running in an environment with a visible screen before attempting to launch your browser. Previously, this check used a direct lookup that could miss these settings in some situations, causing a crash when the tool tried to open the browser anyway. You won't notice anything different in normal use, but if you're working in a Linux terminal without a graphical desktop open, the tool will now more reliably warn you that it can't open the browser and skip that step instead of crashing. This fix is live today and applies to anyone using the CLI on Linux.

e78d48287319787a3d2a64b144bcc76c67298303.text: If you follow a link to the Freebuff get-started page, the page now reads the "referrer" parameter in the URL instead of the "ref" parameter to show who invited you. So a link like ?referrer=Alice will display "Alice invited you to try Freebuff!" in the page title and greeting. This affects anyone landing on the get-started page through a referral link. The only visible difference is the spelling of the parameter name in the link; everything else, including the 50-character limit on the name, stays the same.

953516b8f05bfc39c35b30a8ec762f68fca0e146.text: Starting today, the web assistant once again respects the 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM Eastern Time window when deciding whether to use its advanced AI model. If you open the web app before 10 AM or after 8 PM Eastern, you will automatically get the standard model instead of the premium one. This is the same time-based rule that was temporarily turned off, and it only affects people using the assistant through the website.

7d7138e1f7e4cfca6975491fdd467018717e29ea.text: If you look at the project's main guide page today, you'll see it now introduces a second, free version of the coding assistant alongside the main one. The guide explains that this free version works without any subscription or payment, and shows the simple command you type to install it on your computer before you can start using it. The main guide's title was also updated to mention both versions by name.

f2cfd899c2e71d25f69fdf3e8bdd962a4325d003.text: The system that tests how requests are routed for a specific AI provider has been simplified. Previously, tests checked whether requests were routed based on the time of day (in Eastern Time), but now they test that routing is decided by an explicit on/off switch instead. This means the tests no longer rely on simulating different times of day to verify behavior; they just check whether custom routing is enabled or disabled through a clear flag. This is behind-the-scenes cleanup that makes the tests easier to understand and maintain.

a01949c4e199540a788ea5159ae63fc7c59d6cc2.text: Starting today, the system now routes to a specific Fireworks model (accounts/james-65d217/deployments/lnfid5h9) instead of the previously tested minimax-m2p5 model, and the time-based restriction that previously limited deployment to 10 AM to 8 PM Eastern Time has been removed entirely. This change affects the agent's model selection behavior, as well as the base agent prompt which now mandates suggesting follow-ups for all user questions, even when the conversation is fast-paced. If you looked, you would notice that the model identifier in the test script has been switched from minimax-m2p5 to the new deployment ID, the time gate function always returns true, and the agent instruction now requires follow-up suggestions without exceptions for speed mode.

546904add2511685af801fb09866d5c67d229196.text: When you ask the command-line tool for help, the friendly advice box at the top now changes based on whether you've connected your ChatGPT account. If you've already linked it, you'll see a quick workflow hint showing the recommended order of commands (/interview → /plan → implement → /review). If you haven't connected yet, nothing changes and you'll still just see the existing prompt to run /connect. This only affects the help screen shown right after launching the tool.

4036f839da0e6fb7790a0288b271fabf5dc953d7.text: The system now uses a private, dedicated version of the AI model instead of the shared public one. If you were testing the connection to the AI service, you would notice requests going to a special endpoint owned by the development team rather than the default one. This only affects internal testing scripts and the part of the system that talks to the AI provider; regular users won't see any difference yet because the new setting hasn't been connected to live features.

7a2147533f1e73d451545edbd35f7238f180202b.text: If you ever noticed the system that stops heavy usage from free accounts occasionally flagging people at the wrong time, that should stop happening now. The team rewrote the checks that verify how many requests you can make per second, and they also corrected the timing logic in the test that simulates a 30-minute usage window so it advances time correctly. This is behind-the-scenes maintenance limited to the automated tests for free-mode rate limiting, so there's no new behavior you'd see today, but the checks meant to enforce the 1 request per second limit on free-tier users are now more stable behind the scenes.

2e555ff878222bcf498dade93f7cb3df2ab95112.text: The ChatGPT connection banner now shows a clickable X button to close it, instead of telling you to press the Esc key. When you see the banner while connecting, authenticating, or if it errors out, you can click the X to dismiss it and return to your normal chat view. Hovering over the X highlights it, confirming it's interactive. This change is live today for anyone using the CLI.

f6a994b95e61d9b5fe8e3eac9996eb1dd312d35a.text: Free users of the web API can now send requests twice as fast: instead of one request per second they get two, and their one-minute allowance rose from 15 to 20. If you are a free-tier caller hitting the API, you will find short bursts of requests are less likely to be throttled. The change is live today, limited to free-mode users on the web API.

ad659432d52d69c2172658c9e154c93ebaa96d8e.text: The set_output tool now accepts output fields either passed directly at the top level or wrapped inside a 'data' field, and when validation fails, it shows the error with fewer issues to help the agent retry more effectively. This is useful for AI agents that need flexibility in how they structure their outputs. Live today.

846076cc9b50bc4917ba2a020b4bf5e9f9aea00c.text: When you use the minimax-m2.5 model through the platform, it now connects to a different dedicated instance named Infid5h9 instead of the previous one. This swap only affects the internal configuration that routes requests for that one model, so most people won't notice anything different. The old instance name was qne3jo8v, and a few developer test files were updated along with it to keep notes consistent. Since the feature flag for using a custom deployment is still off, this change just updates the target address and does not alter which model you see or how it runs.

bc346d5d299af3d1c4c95a05012072c32dcd7807.text: A small internal identifier for the minimax-m2.5 model on the Fireworks provider was corrected in three places, fixing a typo that could have prevented the model from being used in a dedicated deployment. The test script that measures response speed was also updated to handle missing timing data more smoothly, so it won't error out if the model hasn't started responding yet. If you were testing model performance, you might have noticed failed requests or inaccurate timing numbers before this fix.

dae55fdfe7024589b8d7b6b03f71ac798c1b75fb.text: A new, stricter throttle was added to the free version of the AI API. If you are using the free tier, you can now send only one request per second, on top of the existing limits of 15 per minute, a maximum per 30 minutes, and a daily cap. You may notice this if you are sending rapid-fire requests; the system will briefly slow you down to enforce the new 1-second limit. The change is in the system configuration today.

8b391e482ac25b8c3eb93634e8102c2563d4cc07.text: The automated test that checks the long-form Fireworks integration now runs against the public API model (minimax-m2p5) instead of the old custom deployment. Engineers who rely on this test will see it evaluate against the same model that real users hit in production, so pass/fail results more closely mirror live behavior. The change is live in the repository today, and the old deployment reference is kept as a comment for reference.

78d22242fc0272fc1fffcb7dc8e11c65f62650ae.text: When the browser assistant runs to do tasks like clicking links or filling out forms, it now starts each session in a clean, isolated browser window that doesn't remember anything from previous runs. This means anything you did in one session won't accidentally affect the next one. You would notice this if you watched the browser open and close repeatedly while an agent works, each time behaving like a fresh start with no leftover cookies, history, or open tabs.

9a15b34b64bc4e27fc9946b1f122e3c1296089ba.text: When you send a message through the API, the system now tags whether your request used free credits, so analytics can track free vs paid usage. Free mode requests (those that cost zero credits) are now labeled with a 'freebuff' flag in the event data, and the CLI login also sends this flag instead of the old name. This is live today for anyone using the API or CLI, making it easier to see which interactions are free tier versus paid.

305645d86822a91dbc775f595fb8c46c1e938183.text: When you sign in, the app now tells its analytics system whether you're using the free assistant product instead of the main one. Previously every signed-in user was treated the same for identification tracking, so Freebuff users looked identical to regular users in the data. Now a flag named is_freebuff is included in the message the app sends when it identifies your account, which affects Freebuff users specifically, and it became live today since it comes from a constant that is already defined and read by the analytics call.

0e542543908c5aac088985127d0d9773675f35e1.text: When the app starts up, it now sets up its tracking/analytics features earlier in the startup sequence, right before it prepares the development environment tools. This prevents startup errors that happened when the environment setup tried to log activity before tracking was ready. Users on CLI v1.0.632 may notice fewer startup warnings when direnv initialization runs alongside other startup checks.

afe8895a33fc3c6d600bee9b1291bd5b1a4f279a.text: When the assistant edits a file, the system records the full result of that edit (not just a summary of what changed) so nothing gets lost when the conversation gets trimmed down. If you reviewed a long editing session, you'd now see the complete outcome of each file change instead of a shortened preview. The trimming process also stops touching a few specialized helper tools, so their work is left intact instead of being shortened.

0aa4b4a2b2640bfbe62e7db4bed3ca74bdd50aff.text: The 'connect' command now works exclusively for one specific type of customer, the same group that already had access to the 'plan' command. If you tried to use 'connect' outside that group, it would stop working. The change is live today and affects only that group's access.

d5fdfe238f9f7994e68226db45970c9e748cc435.text: The automated test scripts that check the Fireworks connection were updated to pass along a session identifier field they were missing. This fixes a build error that was caused by type mismatches in the test mocks. If you look at the project's build logs, the Fireworks tests now compile and run successfully where they previously failed.

8d5530d30f22eced4b4121fc93425741f571e3ad.text: When you run a long test chat against our internal benchmarking tool, each consecutive message now carries a shared session tag in its header so the service consistently routes all turns to the same backend machine. That machine already cached earlier prompts in the conversation, so follow-up questions reuse that cache instead of recomputing them from scratch, which is what makes longer test conversations faster and cheaper to evaluate. Separately, our internal usage stats dashboard now reports the median and peak number of requests per active client, not just the average, giving a clearer picture when a few heavy clients skew the numbers. Both changes affect only the tooling and dashboards used by our own engineers; no customer-facing behavior was altered.

436817ae59687e1e192d10213a8facf43ad3c5b2.text: You'll now see clearer answers in Freebuff's FAQ section on their website, including a new entry about 'What else is cool' that explains how the assistant can use specialized helpers for finding files, reviewing code, and controlling a browser. The FAQ answers also explain that your data won't be used for training unless you choose to opt in later, and that connecting your ChatGPT subscription gives access to a more advanced model for deep thinking. When you read any FAQ entry, line breaks will now display properly instead of running together into one block.

5e21d8a169f62b3ca201fa2e2ae2dcdda3906826.text: When you send a free-mode request to the chat API, the server now first checks two special headers from the network edge ({ "headers": {"cf-ipcountry": "Cloudflare", "x-vercel-ip-country": "Vercel"} }) that tell it your country before falling back to a slower IP-based lookup. If either header reports a real country code (anything other than the placeholder {"values": ["XX", "T1"]}), that code is used; otherwise it keeps using the old IP method. You would not see any visible change in your chat experience. The server is now also logging which country-detection method it tried, so developers can debug why a request was or was not allowed through free-mode gating. This is live today for free-mode users who hit the chat completions endpoint.

19a82f970a5661260a917e2506e679d8e440733c.text: Each time you send a message and the assistant replies, the request now includes your unique user ID as a label. This lets the system group your requests together so it can remember and reuse parts of previous conversations more efficiently. If you use Fireworks-powered features, you may notice responses feel slightly faster or more consistent because the system recognizes your session. This is active for all users today.

3615f8e093a71ed66aab77d729e223d5a43c2aaf.text: Starting today, the web-based assistant always connects to the shared Fireworks service instead of trying to reach any dedicated, custom deployments. If you use the web client, you won't notice anything change in day-to-day use, but behind the scenes the option to route requests to a separate deployment has been turned off, so all model requests now go through the standard global endpoint. Custom deployment IDs are still listed in the configuration but are no longer consulted, meaning they have no effect right now.

ba2b7f09639dd52b3455bc7d4c6cecbfc6f2865e.text: When someone in New Zealand or another newly supported region tries to use the free version of the assistant and it isn't available in their country, they will now see a message that says 'Freebuff is not available in your country.' instead of the old generic 'Free mode is not available in the United States and Canada.' message. This clearer message matches the product's branding and tells users exactly which service is restricted in their region. The change also adds New Zealand to the official list of supported countries on the website and in the project's documentation, and it updates the wording about how fast context gathering is compared to other services.

496279d0f4f8f7f026cb0e4a301a8d4b7fc865bf.text: When you type in the assistant's multiline input box and the cursor needs to figure out which line it's on for positioning and scrolling, it was reading from the wrong data field, causing the cursor to land on the wrong line. The fix corrects it to read from the right field, so the cursor now stays where it should during typing and scrolling. You'd notice the cursor no longer jumps to an unexpected line when editing text in the input box.

a967c6e936ae8cc5d880b7b03eb46f6db6f2d9bb.text: When you build the terminal tool from its source code, the build process now correctly finds the OpenTUI core package even when project dependencies are shared or moved in a monorepo setup. Previously, it only looked in one specific folder (cli/node_modules), which could fail if the package was hoisted to the top-level node_modules. Now it checks both locations and prefers the latest hashed bundle file (like index-abcd1234.js) over the generic index.js, ensuring the tree-sitter asset path patching works in all monorepo configurations. This is a behind-the-scenes fix that makes the build more reliable for developers working on the project.

0c471f89c97d1a59149f15b822325cbc83696486.text: The behind-the-scenes software that builds and ships the Freebuff release was updated to newer versions of GitHub Actions. This is internal maintenance that keeps the release pipeline compatible with current GitHub environments and security patches. If you looked at the workflow files, you'd see references to updated action versions, but there's no visible change to how Freebuff itself works for you.

cab81d0e6908fa90f377b3c6bfae2967f3649cab.text: The end-to-end tests now build the application's binary before running, so the tests no longer fail due to a missing binary. This affects the automated testing process for this software package; if you ran the e2e test suite manually you would see it compiles the binary first. This is a behind-the-scenes housekeeping change and is live today.

97841ca2cf22c0bb84d779fd7f81e0cc8cfba71c.text: When you run the CLI, it now only looks for the OpenTUI core package in one specific folder instead of searching multiple locations. This change affects the build process that packages the binary, and if you looked at the logs during a build, you'd see it skip the old fallback search entirely, going straight to patching the asset paths in the single expected file.

8ddecbc32ae834589e7c117278110b846ecca378.text: When a test session running in the terminal finishes (either successfully or by crashing), the session now stays open instead of disappearing immediately. This means you can still scroll up and read the full log output from that session after it ends, which makes it easier to figure out what went wrong when something fails. It's a behind-the-scenes tweak for the team that runs automated tests, so the change only affects internal testing setups, not anything you use directly.

a4fa669c020282e34620ce1a4bcd7183c7dec4d5.text: When Freebuff's automated end-to-end tests start up the program, they wait longer before checking the screen—up to 30 seconds instead of 15—so startup on slower machines no longer fails the test. The tests no longer look specifically for the word 'Freebuff' in the initial display; since Freebuff was forked from Codebuff, the old branding check could match the wrong program, so the checker now just confirms the startup screen actually shows something rather than being blank. If you watched a test run, you would see it wait patiently after launch and then pass even when the startup was slow, instead of rushing and failing on a half-rendered screen.

fa4fa5c6b53f6d2738346cd7687d28fba9a2ea71.text: When you publish a new version of the freebuff command-line tool, it now has to sit through a full end-to-end test run first, and only if every check passes does the release button get pressed. Previously the release could be created even if those tests hadn't finished or had failed, so this is the safety net that stops a half-baked build from going out. If you watched the process, you'd simply see an extra waiting step appear between the build artifacts and the final release, and the whole sequence would either clear that step or stop there instead of skipping to the end.

9367f31e3f5af6725e18ea8b8aefebdc1cf100e2.text: When you open the Freebuff coding assistant in your terminal, it used to greet you with a shimmering subtitle saying "The free coding agent" that animated across the screen. That subtitle and its shimmering animation have now been removed, so the logo appears cleanly without any animated text below it. Additionally, a small layout issue where a "working..." status message displayed slightly off has been corrected, making it appear properly when the assistant is actively processing your request.

0eba219ede87a8c8712489b3a5a5ab190dc19992.text: When you paste text (especially by dragging a file into the terminal from your file manager), it now reliably appears in the multiline input field instead of sometimes being ignored. This works because the input now listens for paste events even when the terminal has lost focus during a drag-and-drop, using a backup handler with a short delay to prevent the paste from being processed twice. If you paste while the terminal is not focused, the text will now correctly show up in the input area.

ac433e6920693a653d3392077d297b490779dbd9.text: When you type a slash command in the CLI, the assistant's question-gathering command now appears before the planning command in the autocomplete list. This means if you start typing a slash command, you'll see the interview option listed above the plan option. The assistant can now guide you through a series of questions to flesh out your request into a spec before you jump to planning, making it easier to start conversations that need more detail.

4afe5ddfce9ecbebda62fb155060a29a0eb6cd07.text: When you paste text into the CLI app, the app now strips out hidden formatting characters that can come along with copied content, so what you paste looks clean instead of garbled. Similarly, when something gets copied, the app tries to use the terminal's built-in copy feature first before falling back to other methods, which makes copying to your system clipboard more reliable in remote sessions. These changes affect anyone using the CLI tool, especially in SSH or remote environments.

ad37d317e83d0c2102e1e847eb5144f69d12fb2c.text: You now see a shimmering 'working...' label under any subagent that is actively running, so you can tell it hasn't frozen. The animation only appears while that specific subagent is processing, and uses a soft secondary color to match the rest of the interface. It's live today, so you'll see it immediately whenever you launch a subagent that is still thinking or working.

f994c8d1139555f94ca5ed6ba533862c7ffb03f1.text: If you collapse an agent branch so it's folded up, the little 'working...' streaming text now stays hidden instead of showing. You'd notice this only when looking at subagents in the CLI: previously the streaming indicator appeared even when the branch was collapsed, now it waits until you expand that branch first. The change is live today and affects anyone viewing agent branches in the terminal.

af302c3677798d0e10cb709b70af8983d9a93670.text: The assistant can now offer to control a web browser as one of its helper tools, but only if Google Chrome is actually installed on your computer. Before it tries to start that browser tool, it will quickly check your system and, if it can't find Chrome, it will skip that option and tell you instead. You'd only notice this new choice when you ask the assistant to do something that involves browsing the web, and you'd see it work or get a message saying Chrome is missing. This is live as of 2026-03-15.

d2ba4cef9ae65da25bed5bff3f8856a79a51fa9a.text: The automated test that checked how the assistant handles mode restrictions has been turned off in the continuous integration system. This affects only the internal testing pipeline, not any user-facing feature. If you looked at the test configuration, you would notice that the mode restriction test case is no longer listed among the scenarios being validated automatically.

34e7ba56803e2d7c0117f53603b01d8bb21ee81b.text: When you launch the software, your screen stays blank for a moment before the menus and text appear. If a test tried to interact with the screen during that split second, it could fail because nothing was visible yet. Now, before any test begins, the system pauses and waits until the screen shows enough lines of text (at least five) to confirm it's fully loaded. This prevents those premature failures and makes the tests run reliably every time. There's nothing for you to click or enable; this works automatically whenever you use the software.

8aadbbe8061e7088a6d364ae2198a5616eef1d3b.text: The CLI's text-based interface (the part you see in your terminal when you run commands) received a behind-the-scenes upgrade to its rendering library. This means the text display is now powered by a newer version of the OpenTUI libraries, which should help keep everything working correctly and compatible with future updates. There's nothing new you'd directly notice as a feature, but the terminal output may render slightly more reliably. This change is now live in the current version of the CLI.

a0acfcebfe71291893fad20243dc1878b9845fbf.text: When you open the Freebuff command-line coding tool, its startup logo now displays a short tagline — 'The free coding agent' — right below the main logo text. The word 'free' in that tagline is animated: a shimmering highlight slides back and forth across those four letters, cycling smoothly about every couple of seconds. The shimmer color automatically matches whether your terminal is set to a dark or light color scheme, so it stays visible and looks consistent. This visual tweak only appears in the Freebuff version of the tool; other builds of the CLI are unaffected.

bd2276b98669efd76b968fe3fe2253c8a249ca3a.text: When the assistant runs into an error talking to the service behind the scenes, it will now read the detailed error message that the service sends back and show that specific message to you, instead of a generic technical error. This means if something goes wrong, like trying to use a feature that isn't available in your country, the error message you see will explain the actual problem in clearer terms. The improvement is live today and affects anyone using the assistant when it runs into certain backend errors. If you looked at the error output, you'd notice a more descriptive message and an error code that points to the specific issue.

8df7b4d10604e41cdd816e0f9055b224a756b710.text: Your assistant can now show you the real reason a request was denied. When your provider says 'no' (for example, 'Forbidden'), you will see that specific message and reason code in the response instead of a generic error. Behind the scenes, a new parser reads the server's JSON error reply and pulls out the machine-readable error code and human-readable message, and the assistant passes those details along so you get a clearer explanation of what went wrong.

f2350eca2bd211bd25a64478537f2968b921be9b.text: If you log in from New Zealand, you can now use the free AI coding agent on the web without entering a payment method. The product keeps a list of countries allowed to use that free tier, and New Zealand joined it today. You wouldn't see a new button or setting for it yourself; the change just quietly lets a New Zealand IP address start a free session instead of being turned away at the door.

8d9b6c96fa37ebf843d0576046afb4bffd73abf7.text: When you use the Freebuff version of the assistant, you will no longer see an empty gap where a mode toggle used to be reserved. The assistant simply stops leaving that blank space because Freebuff never shows the toggle, so the layout now matches the rest of the interface instead of leaving a small unused strip.

70da96a9b41ca28173eda9595eecb8da4fb47a52.text: You can now tell the system, on a per-request basis, whether to try falling back to a different model version during weekday business hours, instead of letting a single global setting decide for every request. The setting still defaults to whatever the global default is, so existing behavior doesn't change unless you choose to override it for a specific request. This gives finer control over how the assistant handles traffic when the primary model is busiest.

b1e00515d7f86dbf24145f7cd8aac084d27e6fb0.text: The welcome text for Freebuff on its main pages and website now tells you plainly that it is a free coding agent that starts up in seconds, instead of calling itself the 'world's strongest.' If you open the project's home page or read its readme file today, you will see the same short bullet points about it being simple, fast, loaded with built-in web research and browser use, and the new ability to connect your ChatGPT subscription for planning and review. A small FAQ section also explains that the tool is supported by ads shown in the terminal, and that it does not train on your data, so your code stays yours.

120729c8d54f26de85bef668cc0e5da67a716fc0.text: Clicking anywhere on the ad banner in the CLI now opens the linked website, instead of only clicking a specific text button. The extra info panel that used to pop up when you clicked the ad no longer appears by default, so the banner stays compact. The 'Ad ?' label that hints at the panel only shows up for non-free-tier CLI users, keeping the banner simpler for free users.

e70d0892277b28235a2b43ef4f6b0f6fccda03d1.text: When you open the CLI assistant, the /plan command has been removed from the list of available commands. You won't see it appear in auto-complete suggestions or be able to invoke it through the regular interface. This change takes effect immediately for users without access to that specific command set.

799c317d48d98e4090f78ce52078e909aac70242.text: When you reference an agent in the CLI chat, it now uses the agent's unique ID (like @agent-123) instead of its display name (like @My Custom Agent). This means the autocomplete suggestions you see while typing also show the agent's ID as the label, and the description (which used to show the ID) is now blank. If you look at the chat now, agent mentions will appear as short IDs rather than whatever name you might have given them.

d0cc3a429f603da41749352ef1a8e78799b47cb2.text: If you use the free version of the assistant and live in Great Britain, Australia, or a number of European and Nordic countries such as Norway, Sweden, the Netherlands, Denmark, Germany, Finland, Belgium, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Ireland, or Iceland, you can now sign in and use it from your location. Previously, free access was limited to users in the United States and Canada, so visitors from these newly included regions were blocked from the no-cost tier. This matters only if you are on the free plan: the system checks the country your internet connection appears to come from, and it now counts more countries as eligible. If you tried to use the free assistant from one of these places before today and were turned away, you should be able to sign in now. Subscribers on a paid plan are not

fec627712ea8a9404bf80daa60f0d2d85e87952f.text: When you use the general-purpose assistant feature, it now taps into a newer version of its underlying large language model instead of the older one it was using before. That newer model also gets picked automatically by the system that compares multiple draft answers and selects the best one. You won't see a new button or setting, but responses routed through these features come from the updated model starting today. Other parts of the service that were already using different models continue unchanged.

1195b01792da977a0e8634fe269359802855e993.text: When you open the help screen in the command-line version of the assistant, you will now see a small Tips area near the bottom that tells you how to reference files or other agents with the @ symbol, how to cancel a reply with the Esc key, and—only if you are on the free tier and have not yet linked your ChatGPT account—a reminder to run the /connect command so you can access the /plan and /review features. That conditional line appears exclusively for free-tier users who are currently disconnected from ChatGPT, and nothing changes for paid users or anyone who has already connected their account. This is already live today, along with several other unrelated tweaks to the command-line interface such as making the advertisement banner clickable and updating the Freebuff branding.

2013d45f59d629515cc3e90393b8d938223ce755.text: The internal documentation that maps out which AI assistant handles which job has been quietly rewritten. The person who maintains or troubleshoots this setup will now see a different set of assistant assignments in the guide (for example, a different helper is now listed for code editing, reasoning, review, file hunting, running commands, and web research), and one explanatory note about how file rewrites work has been taken out. Nothing your experience as a user changes today from this; it's just an updated reference sheet behind the scenes.

aadbb4be06d0ed4a0ec75c4d2fec73b57bb412db.text: When you ask the assistant to connect to your ChatGPT account from the command-line app, it now goes straight to opening your web browser for the login step instead of showing a blank prompt where you had to paste a code. While that browser step is happening, the text area where you normally type disappears and a clearly bordered pop-up appears showing the login link and buttons you can hover over to click. The status message now reads "authorizing in browser... press Escape to cancel" so you know what to do if you change your mind. This only affects people who use the command-line tool and start the ChatGPT linking process.

b6f81763204cc7fc69346b0731035c76b92ab44c.text: You can now give the deep-thinking helper a much shorter instruction, because it automatically sees the whole conversation history you're having. Before this, you were expected to pack all the background into your prompt yourself; now the helper pulls in the context on its own, so you don't have to repeat everything. This change is live today.

0242d2d8a6e36b9bb9fc39a8a744aff446df5366.text: When the system charges you for credits you've used, it now tags each charge with a unique serial number before sending it to Stripe. That way, if the same charge gets sent twice, Stripe can tell they are the same one and won't bill you twice. The charge-recording part of your account and the part that reports your usage both add these serial numbers automatically. The change is live today and only affects how your usage is reported behind the scenes.

7f62993f7408682aea0ba3b15b6af4b510a2fa95.text: When you open the command line tool and look at the list of available actions like creating a plan or reviewing code, the short descriptions beside them now clearly state which version of the assistant they use instead of just saying GPT generically. This only affects what you see in the help text or command menu; the actual actions themselves still work the same way.

03ffe85e538b3ea5afb8a9f8943aef01c45771c0.text: Starting March 13, 2026, the `/review` command (which summons a coding review) now uses `@thinker-gpt` instead of `@GPT-5 Agent`. If you trigger `/review`, you'll be invoking a different reviewing system; the wording in prompts and help text was updated accordingly (e.g., the description now reads 'Review code changes with thinker-gpt'). Free tier users remain restricted from spawning this reviewer unless explicitly requested by you, and the system now warns that the thinker agent has no direct tool access and relies on context you provide first. If you looked at the interface today, you'd see the new naming and behavior live wherever the `/review` command or review screen appears.

ad61a1c83345d5ae36e236ea7eee50e378fad197.text: When you switch to bash mode in this CLI tool, the mode indicator in the input prompt will now show a text label "!" instead of just an icon. The label also changed from a green "success" color to a blue "info" color, and the spacing around it was widened to fit the new text label better. This makes the bash mode indicator more visually consistent with other input modes that use labels.

37a87f8e75ae11c90fc36e9660235cf4711562af.text: If you use the Codex command-line tool, you can now ask the assistant to review your code by typing a slash command, and you can link your ChatGPT account to it. Previously, both of these features were turned off and hidden from the command list. The review command has been re-added to the menu, and a setting that enables ChatGPT login has been switched from off to on. Both capabilities are active now.

0c9043e39c1ca866b9c65799fa5c494c96815d9c.text: If you use the assistant and the system tries to talk to an optional dedicated Fireworks deployment (a reserved model endpoint for specific models like minimax/minimax-m2.5), it will now always skip that reserved endpoint and use the shared public endpoint instead. The switch that could turn on the reserved endpoint is now permanently set to off, so only the standard global connection is used for those models.

d212c62159bded47a70d599b740b59d937e10318.text: When you're using the free version of the AI coding agent, you'll no longer see the message saying 'Ads are required in Free mode.' That text was meant for paid-free users but was showing up incorrectly for Freebuff, which is the free CLI tool. The assistant now checks whether it's running as Freebuff before deciding to show that warning, so the banner behaves correctly for each context.

bc4f68a015730597836bc4b56f73d564bc04b8db.text: If you use Codebuff for free from outside the United States or Canada, your chat session will now be blocked and you'll see a message telling you to upgrade to a paid plan. The service checks your internet address to guess your country, and if it doesn't recognize the address—say, because you're using a VPN—it lets you through. This filtering is enforced at the server level and surfaced through error handling in the CLI, so you'd notice it as an immediate stop to your run with a clear explanation rather than a silent failure.

0f77739bef572c0d717fd12abf2d5e75126282e8.text: Live chat answers now come back from the new AI service instead of the previous one for supported models. You won't see a name or logo change in the chat, but the behind-the-scenes system handling your streamed replies has quietly switched. Existing users on supported models automatically use the new provider today with no action needed.

44084a06cd88c1402dd962c47c1972a118358e00.text: The internal evaluation system that tests the assistant's coding ability now uses a different reference configuration when running a specific benchmark called buffbench. This only affects the behind-the-scenes testing process; nothing you see or interact with has changed.

f3083517a4d8a9e600ca5cf3854e2a2577f3ad16.text: The automated checks that make sure the command-line tool works correctly have been simplified, though you wouldn't notice anything different if you ran the tool yourself. These are behind-the-scenes tests that developers use; they now wait for each step to finish completely before moving on, instead of juggling multiple steps at once. The change is internal and only affects how the tests are written, not what the tool actually does.

a97a1c6d12bfa1d20ae8c27f2b4d8d3d4a37f12c.text: When the system that checks whether new code works runs its tests, it now builds the helper components first and only for the part of the software that lets people type commands. You wouldn't notice anything different unless you were looking at which steps the system runs, but the tests now start with a freshly built set of helpers so they stop tripping over pieces that weren't ready yet.

3a469f8e39d543e758f96bd149f2cf2922d44b32.text: The marketing text shown in your browser tab and on the Freebuff website now reads simply 'the free coding agent' instead of claiming to be 'The Strongest Free Coding Agent' or 'the world's strongest.' If you open the site today, you will see the new wording in the page title, the description below the logo, and the meta description that search engines display, with no other features or access changing.

f092bf89a849e45392c80d88dd5d02d4a0fceb19.text: When you use streaming chat (where the assistant replies piece by piece as it generates text), that conversation is now sent to CanopyWave instead of Fireworks. This affects the chat request flow used by the web API for supported models. The switch happens automatically behind the scenes, so you'd only notice if you were watching which backend service handles your request. This change is live as of March 11, 2026.

683f6d1c8eb99d8e74da94ce9e56e75f65f85925.text: When you ask for the minimax/minimax-m2.5 model with streaming enabled, the system now routes through Fireworks instead of OpenRouter. Non-streaming requests still go through OpenRouter. This mainly affects users who make real-time, streaming requests to the minimax/m2.5 model, and is live today.

cb57c6646303cca800943b0ae9d018e291b93bb6.text: The system that checks whether new account features work properly has been updated so it now includes tests for the organization billing portal, a new user billing portal checkout flow, and a logout action for the command-line tool. Anyone testing or running these newer features will now have their automated checks cover these specific areas, so previously skipped test cases for these exact paths are now included.

06250cce4548b652a0d978fcd631a3c864e093fc.text: When you click the copy button on the Freebuff landing page to copy the install command, you'll now see a burst of particles radiate outward from the button and the surrounding box will gently pulse with a soft green glow. The button itself will flash a brighter green border for about two seconds to confirm the copy happened. The page also has subtle glowing effects that intensify when you hover over certain text. This is live today for anyone visiting the Freebuff homepage.

8b107a0ab89f0bdf9950d4af8db021049885e653.text: The command-line tool was loading its built-in helpers the wrong way, causing it to fail or skip them entirely. Instead of using a complex method that tried to guess whether the helper files existed, the tool now imports them directly at startup. This means the built-in helpers load reliably every time you use the tool, with no silent gaps or errors during development.

54b1803c12a229de41ae93bf37cbd48fbf4ae781.text: The assistant can now use Fireworks models again for chat responses, after they had been turned off. This only affects requests where a Fireworks model is specifically chosen, and other model providers (SiliconFlow, CanopyWave) remain disabled. If you were to look at how requests are handled today, you'd see that selecting a Fireworks model now routes to Fireworks, while everything else still goes through OpenRouter. This change is live now.

be8555388e2dadcf95b9b51cc2ceed12252acf9e.text: The bright green accent color you see across the landing page—including the install guide toggle, the numbered step badges, the copy buttons, the animated background grid and beams, and the terminal demo prompt text—has been swapped for a slightly greener, more vivid lime (#7CFF3F) in place of the old sharp acid green (#00FF95). If you land on the site today, the first thing your eye will catch is the more vibrant glow in the background animations and the slightly different tone of the interactive teal accents while you click around the install guide. The change also quietly removes the small "Built on the Codebuff platform" credit line that used to sit below the footer links, leaving just the standard copyright notice in its place.

61dbb26699328e0d2b636c8353ca7ae6060d9787.text: When you visit the Freebuff landing page, you'll see an 'Install guide' button that you can click to reveal a step-by-step walkthrough for getting Freebuff running on your computer. The guide shows simple terminal commands like typing 'npm install -g freebuff' and 'freebuff' to install and launch the tool, and you can click to copy each command. You can expand or collapse the entire guide at any time, so it stays out of the way until you need it. This is live today — just visit the Freebuff website and look for the Install guide button below the main download section.

26887d8a5a972c250cc792e14e31b0871913f2fa.text: When the assistant generates a response, it used to stop writing once it reached 32,000 words, even if it had more to say. Now, it will keep going until it naturally finishes its answer, letting the underlying system decide how long is long enough. You might notice that very detailed explanations or long stories no longer get cut off mid-sentence.

1390d31043560aa8a653072bab2aeee4e094d7b1.text: If you use the free version of the assistant, your conversations now go through a middleman service called OpenRouter instead of connecting directly to the model provider. You won't notice any difference in how the assistant responds, but behind the scenes, the system now tells OpenRouter to use the SiliconFlow provider when handling your requests. This change affects only the free tier users who get the minimax model, while paid users continue to get their service through Amazon's cloud. The change is live today as part of the latest software update.

454dbb9eab7ab3b9a48b93b2d904a0195bc28f89.text: The app's dark-mode and light-mode switching now works correctly with React 19, the newest version of the interface library Facebook uses. If you looked at the settings today, toggling between themes would no longer break or fall back to a default; the project quietly upgraded the theming helper from an older version that was incompatible with React 19 to one that speaks it natively, and cleaned up an outdated import path so your chosen theme loads and saves the same way it always did.

8c077776cc855efa89d066e504ded3402611d0a7.text: When you set up the app on your computer, there's a sample file that shows what secret login keys to fill in for each AI provider; the project added a new line so the CanopyWave key has a spot in that file, matching how every other provider is already listed. Nothing in how the app runs actually changed yet, so you won't notice anything different when using it today.

36aa67ce5bb84e07bceb94d1173995dade9b2f9f.text: The assistant can run a terminal task that sets up its own workspace in one smooth step instead of doing it in several separate steps. Previously, the workspace tool only turned on for certain account types, but now it's available to you regardless of your account type, as long as it's turned on.

853643090200cdc81d726d5624f823b0c87011dc.text: You will now see a green, glowing outline around certain highlighted keywords on the page instead of them being plain text. When you hover your pointer over a section that contains these keywords, they light up with a bright green stroke and a soft green glow effect. This only affects the web styles and does nothing to any other part of the site.

281a5f52ef9c3a605acea7202a68a9e743d700b2.text: The Freebuff landing page has been simplified by removing the feature grids, session-based authentication UI, and external documentation links from the home page, navbar, and footer. You will notice a cleaner landing page with a updated tagline 'The free coding agent' and consolidated FAQ answers, but only on the web version. This change is live today and affects all visitors to the Freebuff website, reducing the amount of information displayed on the main landing page and navigation elements.

037ae3fe6c825b5f3d851911aad737a1e6455356.text: When you land on the Freebuff website today, you'll see a new section titled 'Philosophy' that explains how the product works in three short phrases: FAST, SIMPLE, and LOADED. The hero subtitle now says 'No subscription. No configuration. Start in seconds' instead of the old text. The FAQ answer has also been updated to reflect multiple models being used, and the question now reads 'What models do you use?' instead of 'What model do you use?' All these changes are live on the web landing page and were part of a minor update focused on improving the copy and messaging.

b872dc945f3985a845747a2981c31200227b4173.text: A small piece of the assistant's helper software was moved from one folder to another so that all of these helpers now live in the same spot. This is just tidy-up work behind the scenes; nothing you see or do changes in any way.
